Rows key on `(relpath, qualname, sha256(ast.unparse(call_node))[:12])` — NOT line numbers — so the hash changes whenever the CALL ITSELF changes, and is invariant under reindentation or edits above it. Replacing `path.write_text(...)` with a helper call therefore retires one row and mints another.

WHAT COUNTS. GOTCHA measured 2026-09-12 while planning task 5193: when two branches carry DUPLICATE copies of the same work and both land on main, the superseding fix and the superseded one's artifacts coexist, and nothing flags it. Concrete case: the ephemeral-collection lease TOCTOU in fused-memory/scripts/cleanup_test_collections.py was fixed twice — 7fce2bc9c2 (task/4775, an st_nlink `_still_linked` post-flock probe) and 91d55a7fbb (task/4502, esc-4502-5, which holds the LOCK_SH probe across the unlink in `_unlink_if_dead` and replaces the probe with `_entry_still_names`). Both merged. The result on main is green and correct (61 passed, ruff clean) yet carries: `_ACQUIRE_ATTEMPTS = 3` defined twice with two different `#:` doc comments, a `_still_linked` with no callers repo-wide, a dead `path = None`, and — worst — a `reap_dead_leases` docstring that contradicts itself, one paragraph saying the acquiring-holder window is closed from both sides and the next still asserting it is "unresolvable from this side".

TWO LESSONS. (1) Neither ruff nor the test suite catches any of it: duplicate module-level assignment is not a redefinition, an uncalled private function is not an error, and both docstring paragraphs are just prose. Only a human or an agent reading the file notices. (2) A task whose premise is stated as "measured against branch X's tip" can be stale by the time it is dispatched, because the remedy may have landed under a DIFFERENT task id. Task 5193's description quoted reap_dead_leases verbatim as still releasing its probe lock; that code no longer existed on main. Always re-verify such a premise against current main before planning — `git merge-base --is-ancestor <remedy-sha> main` plus reading the actual function — and when the answer is "already landed", also grep for the superseded lineage's leftovers rather than assuming the merge cleaned up.

GOTCHA — a repo-scan guard whose oracle is GIT-TRACKEDNESS cannot be reproduced by copying the offending file into a worktree. You get a FALSE PASS.

This is a new mechanism in the established "main-red probe reports a false green" family. It is NOT the parents[N] skip-vs-pass depth issue (topic `lock-charter-drift-guard-checkout-depth`), and NOT the dirty-working-tree-in-project_root issue (Mem0 77286e74). Those are about WHERE you run and WHAT is uncommitted. This one is about whether git knows the file at all.

MEASURED 2026-09-09, triaging esc-4576-3 (task 4576, post_merge_verify). Failing test: scripts/tests/test_design_invariants_consistency.py::test_every_enumeration_site_is_pinned, asserting docs/code-quality.md restates 4+ invariant slugs without being in PINNED_SITES. Branch task/4576 predated main's commit 7938676c28 which added that file, so the worktree did not have it.
  Attempt 1 (WRONG): `git show main:docs/code-quality.md > docs/code-quality.md` in the worktree, then run the test -> 1 PASSED in 0.38s. Byte-identical content to main, and it still passed.
  Attempt 2 (RIGHT): `git worktree add --detach /tmp/probe main`, run the test there -> 1 FAILED in 0.54s.
The delta is purely that the copy was UNTRACKED. The scan's walker considers only git-tracked markdown — task 4971's tracked-file oracle, whose own commits say "shared walker excludes untracked .md". Attempt 1's false green would have wrongly exonerated main and pinned the blame on the branch.

RULE: to ask "does this failure pre-exist on main?", build a real checkout of main and run there —
  git worktree add --detach /tmp/<probe> main && <run the single test with the probe path>
  git worktree remove --force /tmp/<probe> && git worktree prune
Never synthesize the condition by dropping files into an existing worktree. Cheap and safe: the probe worktree is detached, touches no ref, and the whole cycle here cost ~1s of test time.

GENERALISATION, and the reason this keeps recurring in different disguises: several dark-factory guards read GIT STATE (tracked set, committed blobs) rather than the filesystem, so a filesystem-level simulation of the condition silently diverges from what the guard actually sees. Mem0 77286e74 and ebe9c1a4 preach the same discipline from the other direction — "compare BLOBS, never the working file". Same principle, third mechanism.

WHY THIS ONE MATTERED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, which 4983's framing does not capture. Item 1's flake is fail-CLOSED (a passing judge reports UNVERIFIABLE, re-blocking task 3169 against a correct fix). MEASURED, and it corroborates the canonical's small-payloads-are-not-safe claim: 16 spurious failures in 3000 iterations of the item-1 pipeline on this host; a reviewer measured ~1.6%/call on a busier one, and 3 of 8 full runs of the new hermetic suite failed, each time on a DIFFERENT test. TEST SHAPE, contributed back to the pattern in canonical peer 7df6fc3b. The obvious regression test — run the real gate N times and require every run green — is PROBABILISTIC at this site's natural payload size (sub-2% per call), so at N=50 it misses a reintroduced pipe roughly half the time AND becomes suite flake itself, i.e. it reproduces the very problem it guards. scripts/tests/test_check_write_triage_flip_preconditions.py::TestVerdictReadingIsNotRaceProne instead makes it DETERMINISTIC: a stub producer emits the marker FIRST and then ~1 MB, guaranteeing a piped writer is killed before it finishes. There are TWO deterministic tests, not one: a dropped PASS marker is loud, but a dropped PASS-NEEDS-CONFIRMATION marker is silent (item 1 still PASSes, the eyeball-confirmation demand just vanishes), so each marker channel is pinned separately.

RATIONALE RECORD for task 3500's central design call (landed 2026-08-29), written to a Mem0-backed category on purpose: the conclusion alone is useless without it, and decisions_and_rationale distils reasoning away.

THE CALL: evaluating a delivered_check against a tree yields a BIT, not a VERDICT — so the same rule cannot be both an authoring gate and a corpus sweep. 3500 split them.

WHY. "expect: present and it matches" is simultaneously (a) the SUCCESS state of a landed producer and (b) a never-fires vacuous gate on a live one. Nothing in the descriptor distinguishes them. MEASURED: applying the authoring-time 2x2 to the checked-in corpus with the reference tree set to main-today flags 313/548 descriptors (57%) — 287 present/match, 203 present/nomatch, 32 absent/match, 26 absent/nomatch. The overwhelming majority of those 313 are correctly delivered work. The fold-in (esc-4545-2) had reported 104/538 (19%) and framed the 2x2 as "checkable with nothing but the manifest and git — no commit-ordering premise"; re-running it showed the reference tree is load-bearing, and that discrepancy is methodological, not corpus growth (52 vs 50 manifest files). Filed as esc-3500-1.

THE RESOLUTION THAT MADE IT TRACTABLE: at AUTHORING time the reference tree is free. commit_planning runs BEFORE the task is implemented, so HEAD at that moment IS the pre-task tree and "already green" is decisive with no history and no status. Only the RETROACTIVE sweep cannot recover it — and there the missing input is the producer's STATUS, which turns the bit into a disposition (present+nomatch is a defect on a done task, the normal forward-looking majority on a pending one). Status lives in .taskmaster/tasks/tasks.db, which is why the sweep is scripts/audit_delivered_checks.py and not a pytest gate.

THE THIRD PLACE THE SAME QUESTION LANDS, and why it got a THIRD answer: shared/tests/test_capability_manifest.py must run in any checkout, so it can read neither tasks.db nor a status. It therefore sweeps ONLY the STRUCTURAL codes (self_referential, comment_only, filename_shaped) — statements about a descriptor's SHAPE, which stay true whatever tree they are measured against — and deliberately leaves the vacuity direction alone. It is a frozen-allowlist RATCHET, not a gate, because the measured live structural debt (5 self-reference, 5 comment-only, 1 filename-only) sits in plans/ and docs/prds/ manifests outside that task's lock scope; a hard gate there would have been permanently-red and therefore ignored.

OPTIONS REJECTED, with reasons: (1) one status-blind rule everywhere — rejected on the 57% false-positive rate above; (2) the prior plan's {pre-state, still, unchanged, old, legacy, before} NAME-TOKEN vocabulary — strictly dominated and deleted entirely, because it guessed author intent from English and needed hand-tuned exclusions (installed/stillness/threshold/preflight-state-machine) to avoid false rejects on a hard-blocking gate, whereas the non-vacuity rule MEASURES the repo and subsumes the same cases; (3) adding kind='path' for MODE 3 — deferred purely on blast radius (closed Literals plus every mechanical-kind tuple in the fleet), not merit, and filed as a follow-up.

CAVEAT DELIBERATELY NOT SUPPRESSED: the corpus ratchet's allowlist is pre-existing debt the task could not repair in-scope, and the audit sweep's exit code deliberately ignores `superseded`, `inert` and `unevaluable` rows. Both are choices to keep a detector green enough to be read, not claims that those rows are fine.

GOTCHA (dark-factory, measured 2026-09-07 at HEAD=e6d5f5417469ba8844ecdf6dba0d97f708393779): when a task record claims "removing this code breaks no existing test, verified by grep", check WHAT was grepped. On task 3853 the amendment's grep searched for the audit CONTENT STRING ("Set priority override for task ...") and correctly found only synthetic extractor fixtures — but six sites in fused-memory/tests/test_scheduler_overrides_tools.py assert the audit CALL via memory_service.add_memory.assert_called_once() / .call_args, and none of them contains the content string. The miss was compounded by a path typo in FILES_TO_MODIFY: it named test_scheduler_override_tools.py (singular "override") while the real file is test_scheduler_overrides_tools.py (plural). A path-existence check reports "missing" and reads as "no coverage exists" rather than "wrong path".

RELATED, same class: deleting a function whose arguments were built by dedicated locals orphans those locals. fused-memory/pyproject.toml selects ruff rule set "F", so unused locals (F841) and the now-unused imports in the tests (F401) fail the lint gate and MUST be deleted in the same commit — they are forced, not optional tidying.

Planning task 5370 (five fused-memory fail-soft sites) surfaced four non-obvious facts about this repo's silent-fallthrough programme, all measured at HEAD=99ab62335a.

1. THE AST RATCHET GATE DOES NOT MEAN THE TREE IS CLEAN. `shared/tests/silent_fallthrough_allowlist.py` has ZERO fused-memory entries, and fused-memory's 487 `except Exception` sites produce zero hits. That is a statement about the SIGNATURE, not the tree. Signature (b) is narrowly `except (Exception|BaseException|bare): return None/{}/()/[]/set()` with NO WARN+ log and no re-raise. So it misses (a) every `except: <var> = None` ASSIGNMENT — e.g. agent_loop.py's before_state swallow — and (b) every site that already logs a WARNING before returning an empty literal — e.g. context_assembler._fetch_context. Both are genuine silent fallthroughs by the INV-11 reading. Do not cite "zero allowlist entries" as evidence a package is clean.

2. THE HOUSE FIX PATTERN, AND ITS ONE TRAP. `stages/memory_consolidator.py::_fetch_degraded_sources` is the model: per-instance list initialised in `__init__` (documented against the shared-mutable-default hazard), reset run-locally before every fetch path, appended at WARNING, surfaced via `report.stats['stage1_fetch_degraded']`. The OTHER candidate — `memory_service.py::SearchResults`, a `list` subclass carrying `degraded`/`failed_stores` in-band — is a trap wherever the consumer filters through a list comprehension: its own docstring warns the metadata does not survive slicing, sorted(), concatenation or comprehensions, so the flag is silently dropped. Prefer the instance-tracked list when the result passes through any list transform.

3. `None` IS NOT NEUTRAL IN THE LIVENESS GATE. `services/live_workflow_detector.py`'s `gate_fires = ... and corroborated is False` means a `corroborated=None` behaves IDENTICALLY to `True` on the primary arm — escalation suppressed. Any code path that degrades a corroboration probe to `None` is therefore silently asserting liveness, not abstaining. Only `False` lets a stranded-work escalation through.

4. TASK 1812 IS THE PRECEDENT AND ITS DIRECTIVE STILL BINDS. Task 1812 ("loud fetch failures + in-band search degrade channel", PRD `plans/silent-fallthrough-dedup-prd.md`) established the pattern with a STANDING DIRECTIVE worth quoting on any successor: "unify don't duplicate; RED-test-first; never suppress an escalation to degrade; file follow-up tasks for other duplication discovered." Its "fail-TOWARD-escalate" phrasing is the tie-breaker when a degraded gate could bias either way.

content: Gotcha (dark_factory, found on the task 4031 hand-carry, 2026-10-18): scripts/tests/test_inline_suppression_ratchet.py::test_the_live_tree_passes_the_gate_once_the_baseline_is_seeded keys each unowned suppression marker (`type: ignore[...]`, `noqa[...]`) by a digest of its LINE TEXT, with no path. So a new test line textually identical to an already-baselined suppression elsewhere pushes that shared digest over its count. The gate then lists EVERY site carrying the digest, including untouched files in other tasks (here test_execute_server_error_requeue.py, test_workflow_truthful_commit_stamp.py), which looks like main is red. Probe main in a detached worktree before blaming it. The fix is to remove the new suppressions, e.g. use monkeypatch.setattr instead of type-ignored attribute assignment on a workflow, or drop a kwarg the Protocol lacks. Do not add debt tags. The gate also flags a `noqa[BLE001]` that silences nothing (a logged `except Exception` already passes ruff here). Related: blessing a new task-metadata key in shared/src/shared/task_metadata.py::_BLESSED_METADATA_KEYS needs three edits, not two: the frozenset, the docs/task-authoring.md tier-a mirror fence, AND default_covers in shared/tests/test_shared_governed_lists.py (it was 52→54 under the existing Debt(TaskRef(5603)) default). THE INDEPENDENT PRE-MERGE REVIEW PAID FOR ITSELF ON DARK-FACTORY TASK 5027 (2026-09-15), and the two findings it PROVED BY MUTATION are the ones no amount of reading would have caught.

Leo's standing instruction is: do the mechanical work, independent review before merge. An opus reviewer with an explicitly adversarial brief returned DO NOT MERGE on the first pass with four blocking findings:

1. A migration replaced `tuple(e.item.request.request_id for e in worker._inflight)` with a snapshot()-based helper whose docstring asserted an invariant that does not hold: snapshot()['entries'] is PREPENDED with a finalize-head entry that is not in _inflight at all, then extended with all of _inflight regardless of verify_task, while frozen_prefix.verify_depth counts only entries WITH a verify_task. The slice is therefore neither population. PROVED by mutation (appending a non-verifying InflightEntry during recompute): the new test passed where the old one failed. The migration had silently deleted a real regression detector — and in that test's own shape the new assertion was a verbatim restatement of the next line (SPOT).
2. A 24-line file-local test double whose docstring cited `test_workflow_train_completion._ResolvingMergeQueue` — a symbol that exists NOWHERE in the tree. The real shared double, `_merge_queue_doubles.ResolvingMergeQueue`, had been created by that same task and was already imported by two sibling files. One import line replaced 24 lines of duplicate.
3. A cosmetic hoist (`registry = h._merge_inflight_registry` then two uses) banked as if it were decoupling. Two ast.Attribute nodes became one; the coupling was unchanged. The honest baseline key was 22, not 21.
4. Two false claims in the commit body.

GENERALISABLE: the reviewer's most valuable move was MUTATION — break the production code or the fixture, re-run, and check the migrated test goes RED. A test-seam migration that keeps a suite green has proved nothing about whether the migrated assertions still DISCRIMINATE. Brief a reviewer to mutate, not just to read. All four were fixed and the same reviewer re-verified at the live tip and returned MERGE.

PROCESS TRAP also surfaced: three review seats ran mutation experiments concurrently in ONE shared worktree and clobbered each other's whole-file backup/restores. RED results survive that (a wiped mutation cannot manufacture a failure) but GREEN ones must be re-established under isolation. Serialise mutation work in a single worktree, or give each seat its own.

e30e3230-9fcc-4c37-bfce-1af9f52173ba.content: INV-12 ratchet vs. the scripts/ sys.path bootstrap (task 4625): a new script that binds shared/ or fused-memory/ to its own checkout must NOT add `# noqa: E402` to the imports after the bootstrap. The ratchet (scripts/tests/test_inline_suppression_ratchet.py::test_the_live_tree_passes_the_gate_once_the_baseline_is_seeded) refuses any suppression that is not in the baseline and names no owner. The fix needs no suppression: write the bootstrap as bare module-level statements such as `sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / 'shared' / 'src'))`. Ruff's E402 exempts these, so the imports after them stay clean. A `for` loop, an `if ... not in sys.path` guard, or a `_REPO_ROOT = ...` assignment before them sets the import boundary and brings E402 back.

Two /prd decompose-time norms, both learned the hard way on the 2026-09-01 assembly-modal decompose.

**1. Bind a mechanical `delivered_check` ONLY where the PRD itself fixes the symbol; use `kind: manual` everywhere else — and verify every grep pattern matches ZERO lines TODAY before committing it.**
A `delivered_check` gates DEPENDENT task dispatch, so a guessed symbol that the implementer spells differently false-REDs and blocks downstream work (the esc-6739-1 class). Capabilities whose spelling a PRD defers to an Open Question must be `manual` with a stated reason — those are excluded from the dispatch gate by construction, which is the correct outcome, not a cop-out. Conversely a pattern that already matches on main is VACUOUS: it will read "delivered" the moment the task is done regardless of whether anything landed. On this batch, all 10 mechanical patterns were confirmed at zero matches on the base commit first (`git grep -cE <pat> -- <paths>` exit 1), and every Open-Q-deferred spelling went `manual` — 10 grep vs 47 manual across 12 leaves.

**2. Re-audit the dependency edges after wiring, mechanically, against the written plan — do not trust the running count.**
I reported "32 edges wired" while having actually issued 26: the PRD-close leaf λ was missing its edges to ε, ζ, η, θ, ι, κ because a batch of `add_dependency` calls ended mid-plan. λ would have become dispatchable once α/β/γ/δ landed and stamped the PRD **SHIPPED with six leaves still outstanding** — precisely the failure λ exists to prevent, and invisible because every individual `add_dependency` returned success. The close leaf is the highest-consequence place for this error and the last one wired, so it is the most exposed. Cheap fix: after wiring, fetch each task's `dependencies` array and diff it against the plan (a haiku subagent does this in ~4 min for 14 tasks). Do this BEFORE `commit_planning`, not after — I caught mine only while verifying the sidecar stamp.

Session summary — 2026-08-07 /prd decompose of docs/prds/jcodemunch-substrate-restoration.md (PRD committed 22472828a1). Filed 12 tasks (6106 α client session fix, 6107 β index script, 6108 γ identity+freshness gate, 6109 δ serve wrapper, 6110 ε live capstone / integration gate, 6111 ζ index timer, 6112 η retire serve unit, 6113 θ Rust-reachability spike, 6114 ι activate PDEAD, 6115 κ activate PUNTESTED, 6116 λ PLAYER activate-or-retire, 6117 μ docs truth) with planning_mode=True, wired 23 dependency edges (20 intra-batch, 3 out-of-batch), and flipped the batch in one commit_planning call which stamped all 12 labels into the YAML sidecar and copied 20 mechanical checks into producer metadata.delivered_checks. The capability manifest .md and its stamped .yaml sidecar landed together in ONE direct-on-main commit 9d08d3d3d8 via `git add` + `git commit --only` — the overlay's docs fast path behaved as documented (`verify.sh: nothing to verify (action=all scope=staged)`, main-gate logged SANCTIONED, seconds not hours). DELIVERED: 14 tasks filed, wired and LIVE (`pending`), 32 dependency edges independently re-audited (ALL MATCH), sidecar stamped 12/12 with `delivered_checks` copied into producer metadata.
IDs: α 7162 · γ 7163 · β 7164 · δ 7165 · ε 7166 · ζ 7167 · η 7168 · θ 7169 · ι 7170 · κ 7171 · λ 7172 · μ 7173. Found-during: **#7174** (port-block param defaults skip type checking entirely — root cause: `check_param_default_conformance` walks only `template.value_cells`, never `CompiledPort.members`) and **#7175** (connect direction checking skipped for every dotted sub-port connection — root cause: the `ctx.ports`-only `is_bare` lookup in `compile_connection` leaves left_dir/right_dir None, falling to the `_ => true` arm).

GATES: a four-agent substrate sweep confirmed 34/34 of the PRD's §2/§5 claims (connect/ports, mass-properties, realization channel, eigensolve/joint vocabulary). The D3 workflow then returned `blocks: true` with 31 blocking adversary findings; three would have produced fake-done leaves — β's signal was already green via the `translate()` operator, ι's drift-guard instructions would have red-ed the merge gate, and B4's completeness quantifier is false under `n_modes` truncation (default 10 at ~120 DOF). reify main is a genuinely HOT shared checkout and a /prd session must expect it to move underneath itself. During one ~2-hour authoring session on 2026-08-26/27 the following landed from concurrent sessions: the spec-conformance-suite PRD (#6758–#6791), the gui-purpose-surface PRD (#6803, #6831–#6839), an F2 solver ruling, and several merged task branches — and `git status` showed ~8 other PRD files modified plus ~30 untracked fixtures belonging to other sessions. Practical consequences: (1) task-id ranges INTERLEAVE across concurrently-filing sessions, so a commit message saying "decomposed into #6758-#6791" can span ids that belong to a different PRD — never infer ownership from a range, check metadata.prd_path; (2) `git add -A` or adding a directory would sweep other sessions' untracked work, which is why the overlay mandates listing every path explicitly and using `git commit --only`; (3) a PRD's cross-PRD table can be accurate when written and stale hours later — two sibling PRDs recorded this one as "does not exist on any branch" and "untracked in project_root" respectively, both true at authoring; (4) code anchors verified at one SHA are a DATED SNAPSHOT and should be headed as such rather than re-anchored later.

DECOMPOSE-TIME NORM (established 2026-08-27): re-check sibling-PRD decomposition state and reserved-territory rulings IMMEDIATELY BEFORE filing, never only at authoring time. Reify's project_root is worked by many concurrent sessions and a sibling batch can go from "authored, no tasks filed" to "nine pending tasks" inside one authoring session.

It was caught only because an unrelated `get_task` on #6722 happened to quote "#6741 (gui-on-demand-measurement β)" in its coordination note.

Cheap guards that would have caught it directly: `search_tasks` on the sibling PRD's slug right before submit_task, and `git log --oneline -10` right before committing. Both were run at authoring time and neither was re-run at filing time.

Corollary: `submit_task(planning_mode=True)` lands tasks as `deferred`, which is REVERSIBLE — nothing dispatches until `commit_planning` flips the batch. When a late-breaking finding is still being adjudicated, filing deferred and holding the flip is the right sequencing, not blocking the whole batch.

content:
/prd decompose mechanics observed 2026-10-13 (S6):
- **Re-stamping a held leaf is a no-op on disk.** commit_planning on a held leaf whose sidecar already carries its task_id (S9 #8741, S15 #8718) re-stamps byte-identically. The OPEN binding text must be flipped by hand. S9's manifest explicitly anticipated the releasing stream doing this.
- **A held leaf is never stamped.** It is excluded from the batch's commit_planning, so its task_id must be written into the sidecar by hand.
- **absent_overbroad warnings are benign when files=[].** commit_planning warns absent_overbroad (non-blocking) when a leaf with metadata.files=[] has absent-checks matching files it will delete.
- **Anchor new-module checks on existing files.** Point a delivered_check for a NEW module at the `mod x` line in an existing lib.rs/mod.rs, never at the not-yet-existing file (PDCHECK dead pathspec).
- **Anchor absent-checks on the definition construct.** Use `fn name\(`, not a bare token, so test fns sharing the prefix or comments cannot keep the check red.
- **Measured cost:** submitting 29 leaves plus 129 add_dependency calls in parallel batches of ~20 took one session turn per batch, with no failures.

candidates.content: solar_challenge_platform: pytest addopts in pyproject.toml include -v, so `pytest --collect-only -q` prints a <Function ...> tree rather than node IDs; use `--collect-only -qq` to get one `file::test[param]` line per test. To verify a test-file split is a faithful move (measured on task 875's amend, 2026-10-11), compare those node IDs before and after with the file path stripped (sed 's#^tests/.../test_[a-z_]*\.py::##' | sort), then reverse any renames with sed and diff the moved blocks against `git show HEAD:<old file>`.

Gotcha (solar_challenge_platform pytest): pyproject's [tool.pytest.ini_options] addopts is "-v --tb=short", so `pytest --collect-only -q` prints the <Module>/<Function> tree instead of node IDs. Use `uv run --extra dev pytest --collect-only -qq -p no:cacheprovider <paths> | grep '::'` to get bare node IDs, e.g. for a before/after test-ID diff on a behaviour-preserving refactor.

Gotcha (solar_challenge_platform, measured 2026-10-06 in task 737 on Python 3.11.15 / pytest 9.1.1): `uv run --extra dev pytest <file> -m 'not slow' --collect-only -q` prints a `<Dir>/<Package>/<Module>/<Function ...>` tree, not bare node ids, and ends with a volatile timing line such as `26/49 tests collected (23 deselected) in 0.40s`. A plan check of the form "collect-only output must diff empty against the before-file" therefore never passes with a plain `diff`. Use `diff -I 'tests collected' before after`, or compare only the `<Function ` lines. The same applies to a mypy before/after comparison after adding an import: strip line numbers first, e.g. `sed -E 's/:[0-9]+:/:N:/'`.

solar_challenge_platform gate timing, 2026-10-07 (task 806, Docker present, 4724 selected tests): `uv run --extra dev pytest -m 'not slow' -p no:cacheprovider` as 5 parallel `&`+`wait` shards in ONE foreground Bash call finished in 643 s wall — tests/integration split by alternating sorted test_*.py files (354 s / 643 s), tests/{billing,api,portal,consent,tenancy,auth,cli,schemas,models} (136 s), tests/{validation,simulator,e2e,docs} (269 s), and `tests` with an --ignore for every one of those directories (294 s) — and a --collect-only -qq node-id diff against one serial collection proved the shards select the identical set (0 duplicates, 0 gaps). When reconciling totals, passed+skipped exceeds the collected node-id count by 4 because the four Playwright e2e smoke modules (tests/e2e/test_*_smoke.py) call pytest.importorskip("playwright.sync_api") at module level, which pytest counts in "N skipped" (run header: "collected 990 items / 69 deselected / 4 skipped / 921 selected") but never lists as nodes.

solar_challenge_platform verify sizing, measured 2026-10-10 at base 1b4b448: `uv run --extra dev pytest -m 'not slow'` collects 5411 tests and ran serially in 28m42s (5388 passed, 27 skipped) at host load 100-157 on 32 cores. No pytest-xdist is in the dev extras, so it cannot be sharded with -n. That is past the ~25 min foreground limit, so background it with output redirected to a log, then wait on the pytest process's own pid. tests/integration/test_bill_account_convergence.py alone ran for several minutes, CPU-bound but not hung.

solar_challenge_platform gotcha (measured 2026-10-04 by task 526's architect at main 2838c8a): pytest-xdist is not installed in the uv dev environment, so `uv run --extra dev pytest -n 4 ...` fails at once with exit 4 ("unrecognized arguments: -n 4"). Run subsets serially; for example, tests/ingestion + tests/ops + tests/test_private_names.py (376 tests) take about 38 s. Separately, `npm --prefix frontend ci --prefer-offline --no-audit --no-fund` installs a fresh worktree's frontend/node_modules from the shared ~/.npm cache in about 4 s, with no network needed.

Gotcha (solar_challenge_platform, verified 2026-09-29, task 573): in the hermetic lane the pytest run summary's "skipped" count includes module-level skips raised at collection, which are not items. The 4 tests/e2e Playwright smokes (importorskip, playwright absent) add 4. So `pytest -m 'not slow'` reporting "3259 passed, 25 skipped, 75 deselected" against "3280/3355 tests collected (75 deselected)" is consistent (3259 + 21 item-level skips = 3280 items, plus 4 module skips = 25); it is not drift. To prove a change adds no selected tests, diff `--collect-only -qq -m 'not slow'` node ids with and without the new file rather than comparing summary totals.

Procedure (solar_challenge_platform, task 793 architect, 2026-10-10): measure who constructs a value type with some property across the whole suite before adding a __post_init__ invariant.
1. Write a throwaway pytest plugin outside the repo, e.g. /tmp/<task>-probe/naive_row_probe.py.
2. In pytest_configure, wrap the class's __init__. dataclasses.replace also goes through __init__, so the wrapper sees those copies too.

Gotcha (solar_challenge_platform tests; measured 2026-10-11 with pytest 9.1.1 by task 845's architect): pytest names each tmp_path directory after the test. It turns non-word characters into '_', keeps the first 30 characters and adds a counter. test_read_fingerprints_without_node_on_path_raises got .../test_read_fingerprints_without0. So a bare substring assertion such as 'node' in str(exc) passes vacuously whenever the message embeds a tmp path and that substring falls within the test name's first 30 characters. Match a delimited form instead, such as '`node`' or '`npm`' (backticked, as the frontend gate messages print tool names), or a hyphenated package name, since test names cannot contain hyphens.

Pytester recipe in solar-challenge-platform (pytest 9.1.1, verified by task 415's architect on 2026-09-27):
- A module-level `pytest_plugins = ["pytester"]` in a TEST MODULE is accepted with no warning. pytest only rejects `pytest_plugins` in non-root conftests.
- `pytester.inline_run(f"{__file__}::<test name>", "-p", "no:cacheprovider")` re-runs a real test from the same, already-imported module in ~0.1 s.
- `reprec.listoutcomes()` returns structured TestReports; a skipped report's reason is `report.longrepr[2]` ("Skipped: <reason>").
Two gotchas:
- The nested session inherits os.environ; pytester only swaps HOME and drops PYTEST_ADDOPTS. So set DOCKER_HOST to a dead socket inside the test before nesting any Docker-guarded slow test, because this workstation's live daemon would otherwise start the real topology.
- The nested run reuses the module imported under the OUTER env, so an env-driven skip must be an in-body `pytest.skip`. An import-time `skipif(bool)` cannot be exercised this way.

solar_challenge_platform testing gotcha (measured 2026-09-30, task 544 architect, base 8e89ef2). (1) runtime.asgi builds its graph at import time, so only the first import in a pytest process runs the build, and spies placed around a later cached import see nothing. To pin what serving scp-api constructs, execute the module afresh: spec = importlib.util.find_spec("solar_challenge_platform.runtime.asgi"); module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec); spec.loader.exec_module(module), inside db.session.repoint_scope(). This registers nothing in sys.modules. runpy.run_module emits a RuntimeWarning when the module is already imported, and importlib.reload mutates the cached module that other tests share. (2) run_settle's timescale path runs hermetically, with no Docker, over a file-based SQLite DB holding Base.metadata and no Property rows. TimescaleStore() opens no connection, property_settlement_keys returns [], and the run completes after composing its graph.

content: solar_challenge_platform pytest collect-only, measured 2026-10-12 by the task 984 architect: `pytest --collect-only --verbosity=-1` prints one node id per line, whatever verbosity pyproject's addopts (`-v --tb=short`) sets, because an explicit --verbosity after addopts overrides it. `-qq` works only while addopts carries exactly one -v. After the node ids comes a blank line, then the summary. With nothing selected, pytest exits 5 and stdout STARTS with that blank line, so read the node ids as the lines before the first blank line (itertools.takewhile(bool, ...)), not with partition('\n\n'). A collection error exits 2.

THE GOLD STANDARD IS IN task_knowledge_sync.py, NOT task_filter.py. The canonical truncation-disclosure note — the one that names the constant AND its value, the omitted count, the drop order, and says "Coverage was clipped — NOT complete", paired with a structured logger.warning — is at fused-memory/src/fused_memory/reconciliation/stages/task_knowledge_sync.py (the MAX_DONE_AUDIT_RENDERED=60 done-audit overflow note; constant + rationale defined a few hundred lines above it). TRAP 1 — "cap" is overloaded, and the collision is live. shared/src/shared/cap_markers.py has nothing to do with render/truncation caps: it is CLI USAGE-QUOTA and AUTH BANNER detection (CAPACITY_BANNER_MARKERS / AUTH_BANNER_MARKERS / BLOCKING_BANNER_MARKERS, consumed by the pytest capacity-skip guard and the legibility census). TRAP 2 — there is no shared truncation helper, but there are FOUR private ones with THREE different markers, so grepping for any single spelling finds only a quarter of them: server/write_triage_judge.py::_elide ('…[elided]', returns str), server/recon_report.py::_truncate_field ('…[truncated]', returns tuple[str, bool]), reconciliation/targeted.py::_truncate_clean (bare '…', word-boundary-aware and length-preserving — NOT a drop-in for the hard-slicing two), server/tools.py::_truncate_payload (payload-level, not text). Count-based caps have no helper at all; every site hand-rolls its f-string. Task 5365 adds fused_memory/utils/clip_disclosure.py as the single home, and a filed follow-up consolidates the rest onto it.

RULING RATIONALE (dark-factory, 2026-10-12, escalation esc-5498-3, Leo chose option A, which was the L2 watcher's recommendation). fused-memory/src/fused_memory/utils/clip_disclosure.py is the single home for truncate-and-mark. Description: Discovered during task 4519's INV-5 acceptance sweep (grep -rn 'popleft()' over shared/, fused-memory/src/, orchestrator/src/). Filed as a candidate, not a confirmed defect — it needs a design call before anyone edits it.

    while self._git_error_stamps and self._git_error_stamps[0] <= cutoff:
        self._git_error_stamps.popleft()
with an append at the call site above it and a count exposed by git_error_count_in_window() as len(self._git_error_stamps). Completed: consolidate_memories step (7c) reads member text via row.get('content'), a key Mem0 scroll rows never carry, so retain-only consolidations never seed the topic-cluster guard
Description: PRODUCTION DEFECT, verified on main 2026-09-27 by the L2 watcher (surfaced by the task-4493 architect in esc-4493-3).

WHERE: fused-memory/src/fused_memory/server/tools.py::consolidate_memories, step (7c) "TEACH THE TOPIC GUARD", introduced by 47c0827345 (task 3135 step-18). It builds `member_texts = [row.get('content') for row in member_rows ...]`.

WHY IT IS WRONG: `topic_members` comes from `memory_service.get_memories_by_metadata(...)`. That returns rows shaped by the Mem0 backend's point normaliser (backends/mem0_client.py, the single home of the scroll row shape), which is `{'id', 'created_at', 'metadata'}`. The memory text lives in `metadata['data']`, and there is NO top-level 'content' key. So every member text is None and is filtered out.

CONCRETE CONSEQUENCE: consider a retain-only call (`supersedes=[]`), which is the ratified retain-and-tag shape. It passes `texts=[canonical_content]` only. `derive_topic_cluster` needs each phrase to occur in at least two texts, so it abstains and the call reports `topic_cluster_seed={'outcome': 'skipped'}`. No data is lost. What is lost is known-topic-cluster write-guard coverage, which Leo ruled stays ON (esc-3135-8 option A′, 2026-09-27). The §10 replay that ruling rested on used canonical plus retained member texts, so production does not currently do what was ruled on.

WHY TESTS PASS: fused-memory/tests/test_consolidate_memories_tool.py::_scroll_row fakes a top-level 'content' key that real rows do not have.

FIX:
- Read the member text through the shared helper `services/memory_service.py::_mem0_content(row['metadata'])`, or an equivalent single-home reader. Do not add another inline key loop (INV-5).
- Make the test fixture `_scroll_row` produce the REAL row shape `{'id', 'created_at', 'metadata': {'data': ...}}`.
- Add a regression test: a retain-only consolidation over >=2 members sharing a phrase must seed (outcome != 'skipped').

SCOPE SPLIT: this fix is also planned inside task 4493's plan (steps 1–2, design decision 7). 4493 is low priority and lock-conflicted across ~22 files, so it is split out here deliberately so that it lands soon. Do NOT combine it into 4493. 4493's details carry a note to drop those steps if this lands first.

Reify solver tolerance inventory, measured 2026-08-26 at main 2ea72cc5e8 — useful for anyone touching #6653 (toleranced Scalar verdicts) or solver conditioning.

The dimensional path's constants are DIMENSION-BLIND ABSOLUTES applied to raw SI magnitudes: FEASIBILITY_THRESHOLD = 1e-12 (the acceptance gate, L-infinity, so 1 picometre on a metre-scale length), NM_SD_TOLERANCE = 1e-30 (argmin simplex termination on the squared-residual cost SD; deliberately <= FEASIBILITY_THRESHOLD^2 per task #4700), PENALTY_WEIGHT = 1e6, UNDEF_OBJECTIVE_PENALTY = f64::MAX/2, MAX_ITERS = 5000, FEASIBLE_OPT_ITERS_PER_DIM = 500. Inline deadbands: 1e-15 for Eq/Ne, a +1e-12 offset in comparison_violation. So a Money objective (~1e2) and a Length constraint (~1e-2) sit in the same unnormalised sum with a fixed 1e6 objective/penalty ratio regardless of physical scale.

The ONLY relative-plus-floor tolerance in the solver today is the uniqueness check's UNIQUENESS_REL_TOL = 1e-6 / UNIQUENESS_ABS_TOL = 1e-10 pair in solutions_agree. The ONLY normalisation anywhere is cost_robustness_tradeoff's normalised_blend_term. The robustness floor uses REL_MARGIN = 0.02 with ABS_FLOOR_SI = 1e-9.

The ONLY coherent tolerance HIERARCHY in the codebase is RelateTolerance::kernel_default() in crates/reify-constraints/src/relate_solve.rs — kernel_local 1e-7 m <= solver_convergence 1e-6 m <= assertion 1e-5 m, all metres, seeded from one base length. It has PRIVATE fields, exactly one constructor, no setters and no DSL knob. That ladder is the shape #6653 should generalise, and note solver_convergence (1e-6) happens to EQUAL FD_STEP, i.e. the differencing step is the same size as the convergence target.

The engine verdict fold meanwhile uses EXACT f64 equality (reify-expr eval_eq), which is why correctly-solved models report false VIOLATED at ~1e-15 residuals (probe-measured on multi_auto2/multi_auto6/auto_probe). crates/reify-core/src/scalar_tolerance.rs does not exist yet — #6653 creates it.

reify-solver-elastic gauge/convergence testing gotcha: the catenoid-tube fixtures used to calibrate form_find.rs's surfaces-path convergence criterion (crates/reify-solver-elastic/tests/tensegrity_gamma_membrane_form_find.rs build_catenoid_tube, at 16x3 / 32x6 / 8x2) are surfaces of revolution whose free nodes are all structurally identical, so their free-row norms of D are UNIFORM — measured max_row/min_row = 1.000 exactly. Any test that tries to discriminate between residual normalization schemes (ratio-of-maxes vs per-row) on these meshes is therefore VACUOUS: both schemes compute the same number there, agreeing to 10 significant digits. To get non-uniform free-row norms, add hoop cables on the free ring and make ONE of them stiff (e.g. q=30 against the others' 0.3 at n_theta=16, n_axial=2, sigma=1); measured row-norm spread then tracks the stiff q roughly linearly (q=3 -> 3.9x, q=30 -> 33.9x, q=300 -> 334x). Grading sigma per-triangle instead does NOT work — even a 10:1 sigma jump collapses triangles and the solve fails with DegenerateTriangle.

In reify's tensegrity solver, changing a convergence criterion's DENOMINATOR requires recalibrating its constant in the same change, or the fix silently loosens accuracy. Task 6119 divided the surfaces-path equilibrium residual by `d_scale = ||D||_inf` (over free rows) to make it gauge-invariant; since measured d_scale is ~8.5-9.7 at sigma~1 on the catenoid meshes, keeping the old absolute 1e-10 would have moved the stop point ~9x looser. The landed SURFACE_EQUILIBRIUM_REL_TOL = 1e-11 was chosen so the new relative bound reproduces the OLD absolute stop point to within ~10%, staying ~11.5x below the gamma catenoid golden's independent EQUIL_TOL = 1e-9. The house convention is to justify such constants against a measured quantity on the real fixtures plus an independent golden's bound, not to guess.

In reify-solver-elastic's form-finding code, any convergence or degeneracy threshold compared against a quantity built from the force-density matrix D (= C^T Q C plus the sum over triangles of sigma_T * L_T) must be RELATIVE, never absolute: D is exactly linear in the gauge pair (q, sigma), so an absolute bound makes convergence gauge-DEPENDENT. A large lambda inflates the residual so the solve never converges (loud failure); a small lambda shrinks it below tolerance so the solve stops prematurely on unconverged geometry (silent wrong answer) — a suite testing only one direction is blind to the other. The house pattern is to divide by d_scale = the infinity-norm of D restricted to the free rows, which cancels lambda exactly since numerator and denominator each pick up one factor. DEGENERATE_AREA_EPS in the same file is the older instance of the same principle ("relative so the test is scale-free"). Task 6119 applied this to the ANCHORED surfaces path (SURFACE_EQUILIBRIUM_REL_TOL, calibrated so the relative 1e-11 reproduces the previous absolute 1e-10 stop point against a measured d_scale of about 9 on the catenoid goldens). The identical absolute-threshold shape still exists on the FREE-STANDING path in form_find_free.rs (FREE_SURFACE_EQUILIBRIUM_TOL, all_node_equilibrium_residual), tracked as tasks 6413 and 6983.

geometric-relations numeric premises are NOT error-floor bounds (capability manifest numeric-floor = N/A): DOF figures (concentric removes 4, flush 3 with 2 redundant, spent 5 / free 1) are exact integer codimensions from the `coincident(X,X) removes codim(X)` law in relation_signatures.rs (relation_delta_dof). The relate-solve tolerance is one kernel-defaulted Length knob with hierarchy kernel_local ≤ solver_convergence ≤ assertion/dedup. Tests asserting "coaxial/flush within tol" must assert against the solver's own convergence tolerance (a method guarantee when SolveSpaceSolver returns Solved), never a hand-picked epsilon — a tuned epsilon would be a false numeric premise.

Measured 2026-10-14 (main 5b8a33011d): the DimensionalSolver's Nelder-Mead stops on cost-SD NM_SD_TOLERANCE=1e-30 over SQUARED residuals, so equality residuals land around 1e-15 in raw SI units regardless of dimension — e.g. `param v : Volume = auto; constraint v == 1000mm^3` solves to 1.0000000011823468e-6 m^3 (residual 1.18e-15, RELATIVE 1.2e-9). Consequence for any acceptance/verdict tolerance (task #6653): an absolute floor below ~1e-12 SI (e.g. (1um)^3 = 1e-18 m^3 for Volume) or a pure-relative 1e-9 policy turns ordinary mm^3-scale volume equalities into false Infeasible/Violated. Keep every per-dimension floor >= 1e-12 (today's FEASIBILITY_THRESHOLD), so a toleranced acceptance is never stricter than the old flat gate.

MEASURED 2026-08-26 (main 2128c3692c, reproduced independently twice): mixing an EQUALITY and an INEQUALITY on the same reify `auto` param is UNCONDITIONALLY reported infeasible, even when trivially satisfiable. `constraint L >= 8mm` + `constraint L == 10mm` (10mm satisfies both) yields "constraints could not be satisfied (max absolute residual: 5.00e-7)" and leaves L undef. The equality ALONE resolves to exactly 0.01 m.

The residual is ALWAYS exactly 5.00e-7 — verified scale-invariant, direction-invariant, order-invariant and strictness-invariant across six controls (including a x10-scaled twin). MECHANISM: the synthetic max-min-slack objective is added ALONGSIDE the equality's penalty, and minimising PENALTY_WEIGHT*d^2 - x with PENALTY_WEIGHT = 1e6 is stationary at 2*1e6*d = 1, i.e. d = 5.0e-7 exactly. That is five orders above FEASIBILITY_THRESHOLD = 1e-12.

DISPOSITION (important — do not re-file this as a new defect): the VERDICT half is ALREADY OWNED by task #6653, whose evidence names this exact probe (expr_ineq_eq.ri) and this exact residual, and whose acceptance criterion requires all four of its evidence probes to flip. DimensionalSolver (crates/reify-constraints/src/solver.rs) has a convergence-floor gotcha: solve_core's Nelder-Mead minimizes the SQUARED constraint violation (comparison_violation uses d.powi(2)) and terminates at sd_tolerance(1e-15), so its achievable L1 residual floor is ≈sqrt(1e-15)≈3e-8 — but the feasibility gate (final_max_residual > FEASIBILITY_THRESHOLD=1e-12) checks the LINEAR residual (comparison_residual). Any auto that must MOVE from its seed to satisfy an equality constraint stalls ~2.6e-8 >> 1e-12 → Infeasible. Cold solves of `param x:Length=auto` only pass when the target happens to equal extract_initial_point's 0.01 default seed (no bounds → 0.01), triggering the initially_feasible early-exit (no NM run). Task 4700 fixes this with a near-feasible polish/restart at tighter sd_tolerance.

DimensionalSolver (crates/reify-constraints/src/solver.rs) feasibility-residual floor: the Nelder-Mead cost is the SQUARED constraint violation (comparison_violation → d.powi(2)) but the feasibility check uses the LINEAR residual (comparison_residual → |d|) compared against FEASIBILITY_THRESHOLD=1e-12. With with_sd_tolerance(1e-15) on the squared cost, the linear-residual floor is ≈ sqrt(1e-15) ≈ 3e-8, so any auto param that must MOVE from an off-target seed (e.g. seed 20mm, constraint x==10mm) converges only to residual ~1e-8 >> 1e-12 and the solver returns Infeasible. Empirically confirmed (seed 0.02→target 0.01 → Infeasible residual 1.05e-8). Tightening sd_tolerance to 1e-30 (≲ FEASIBILITY_THRESHOLD²) drives the residual to ~1e-16 (Solved); full reify-constraints suite (108 lib + integration tests) still passes. extract_initial_point seeds auto params with bounds:None at a HARDCODED 0.01 — which coincidentally equals 10mm, so existing warm back-prop tests pass only because the seed already equals the solution (no movement needed).

Solver-integration landscape audit (2026-08-26, main @ 181d1ec24c, probe-verified): The production solver surface map is — reify eval/run, report, explain, GUI edit/load paths: full SolverRegistry::production() (DimensionalSolver + SolveSpaceSolver; CpSat NOT registered until PRD2 gamma #5469; Logical/CrossDomain slots fall back to Dimensional). reify build/check/test, LSP, CLI mcp-server: NO dimensional solver. relate_solve (at-auto 6-DOF pose, damped Gauss-Newton, NOT SolveSpace) is the exception on the geometry path: its single call site is Engine::build_with_geometry_output (engine_build.rs:3979, kernel-gated not solver-gated), so solved POSES reach STEP via reify build and GUI export — but never the GUI live viewport (tessellate_snapshot has no solve; eval_auto_sub_pose identity fallback) and never check. Solved VALUE autos (ctor-arg/let/param) reach no realization surface at all (#6631/#5617). Two probe-proven verdict defects: (1) engine post-solve equality verdicts compare exact f64 while the solver accepts at 1e-12 L-inf, so numerically-solved (non-exactly-representable) solutions report "constraint violated"/exit 1 from eval, and a feasible ineq+eq mix is declared infeasible at 5e-7 residual; (2) inequality-only strict autos silently resolve to a bound corner (10 m default) with no warning (Chebyshev centrality on an unbounded-above region). Constraint expressiveness is NOT a gap: min/max/clamp, if-then-else, abs, sqrt, trig, dot/cross/magnitude all work inside comparison operands (continuous residuals). The traps are: any std::distance/std::tangent/std::geo::* call classifies the constraint Geometric -> SolveSpaceSolver pattern-matcher -> inequalities/arithmetic unrecognized -> NoProgress kills the WHOLE resolve; tangent() typechecks but contributes zero residual rows anywhere (#5540 low); seed/bound derivation only understands linear-in-one-auto shapes so sqrt-algebra clearance constraints contribute no seed box.

Reify tensegrity solver — gauge-covariance testing technique (validated by measurement, task 6119). To test that a force-density form-find is invariant under scaling every q and every sigma by lambda, use a POWER-OF-TWO lambda (2^20 = 1048576). Then lambda*q and lambda*sigma are exact in IEEE-754, D = C^T Q C + sum_T sigma_T*L_T scales entrywise-exactly (triangle_cotangent_laplacian is `half_sigma = 0.5*sigma` then `w = half_sigma*cot`, so it is exactly linear in sigma; scatter_line_members adds +/-q_i directly), the partial-pivot LU multipliers a_ij/a_jj cancel lambda exactly, and solved node coordinates come out BIT-IDENTICAL (measured max|dx| = 0.0, not merely 1e-15). A non-power-of-two lambda like 1e6 only tests the identity to rounding and forfeits that signal. Corollary for convergence criteria in crates/reify-solver-elastic: any stop test on a residual built from D must divide by a norm of D (e.g. max over free rows i of sum_j |D[i,j]|), because an absolute bound on a quantity linear in q makes convergence gauge-DEPENDENT — the same structure at q and lambda*q then takes a different iteration count or reports converged == false.

Reify testing norm: a new regression fixture MUST be measured RED against the pre-fix tree before it is accepted as coverage — never infer discrimination from an architect's/plan's prose prediction that "this fails today". A fixture specified in good faith can be VACUOUS: it passes both before and after the fix and proves nothing, while looking like real coverage forever.

Measured instance (task #7186 defect B, esc-7186-1): the plan specified a rigid-platform loop-closure fixture (two +Z prismatic posts 200mm apart, closing pose = translate(200mm,0,0), bind j2=300mm) and predicted it would fail pre-fix because "the closure reduces to d2 == d1 with a 200mm x-offset that nothing can absorb". Implemented verbatim it PASSED on the pre-fix tree. Root cause: the sole free variable d1 translates only along +Z, so the unabsorbable 200mm x-residual was ORTHOGONAL to the free direction; Gauss-Newton's least-squares point was still d1 = 0.300, numerically identical to the correct post-fix answer. The defect was real but invisible in the converged value — it showed up only in the residual NORM, which snapshot() does not surface in the Snapshot Map (only is_singular is).

Generalizable rule for least-squares / Gauss-Newton solver fixtures: an error component orthogonal to the free-variable subspace is INVISIBLE in the converged value. To make a solver defect observable through the converged value, give the injected offset a component ALONG a free direction. Fix applied here: pose translate(200mm,0,0) -> translate(200mm,0,50mm), making the exact solution d1 = d2 - 0.050 = 0.250m post-fix versus the 0.300m least-squares point pre-fix — genuinely RED before, GREEN after, with an exact algebraic solution so the 1e-6 tolerance stays the solver's own NewtonConfig::default() tol_pos_m rather than a fitted threshold.

Corollary: when a fixture's discriminating power depends on a specific constant, say so IN the test's doc comment ("the 50mm z-component is load-bearing"), or a later reader will "simplify" it back to the vacuous form.

Task 4700 (esc-4700-33) root cause: the committed step-2 fix tightening DimensionalSolver NM_SD_TOLERANCE from 1e-15 to 1e-30 (crates/reify-constraints/src/solver.rs) REGRESSES crates/reify-eval/tests/auto_binding_sites_remaining_resolution.rs::example_auto_binding_sites_ri_all_four_resolve, which fails with a spurious ConstraintNonUnique error. Verified by toggling the constant: 1e-15 PASSES, 1e-30 FAILS. The escalation was mislabeled transient ENOSPC; a verify retry surfaces this real code regression. Mechanism: in the AllFourSites resolution problem there are 3 strict autos (bolt.length, m, __connector_0.gain) with current_values all None. bolt.length and m have determining constraints (==10mm) in that problem; __connector_0.gain does NOT — its determining constraint self.gain==10mm lives in EpsilonConnector's OWN scope (design D5: parent cannot name the synthesized __connector_N), so gain is genuinely underdetermined within the parent problem. verify_uniqueness perturbs all 3 to ~9m and re-solves: with the old 1e-15 tolerance the perturbed re-solve failed feasibility on bolt/m (residual ~3e-8 > 1e-12) and hit the 'perturbed solve did not converge -> assume unique' fallback, ACCIDENTALLY masking gain's non-uniqueness. With 1e-30 the perturbed re-solve now converges bolt/m to 1e-12 feasibility and lands gain at 0.158 vs the original 0.01 (diff 0.148 >> uniqueness tol) -> solutions_agree=false -> ConstraintNonUnique. So tightening the tolerance removed the accidental masking and exposed a latent problem-construction issue: connector-internal autos appear as unconstrained auto_params in the parent resolution problem. Fix is design-laden (solver uniqueness machinery or eval problem-construction); re-escalated to L1.

docs/design/geometric-relations.md is the DESIGN OF RECORD, decisions A–O locked 2026-06-08 interactively, decision log at §14. Do not re-open those decisions; read them before designing. Key sections: §2 the typed datum lattice (Direction codim 2 / Point 3 / Axis 4 / Plane 3 / Frame 6 / Scalar) and §2.2 the feature->datum trait bundle (Planar->Plane; Cylindrical->Axis+radius; Conical->Axis+apex+half_angle; Spherical->Point(centre)+radius; Linear->Axis; ArcBounded->Axis+Point+radius; Revolute->Axis; Extruded->Direction; Vertex->Point). §2.3 the tolerance coherence law kernel_local <= solver_convergence <= assertion/dedup, with a SCALE-AWARE angular tolerance ang_tol ~ lin_tol/characteristic_length (explicitly NOT OCCT's Precision::Angular). §3.1 the fundamental law coincident(X,X) removes codim(X). §3.2 three policing layers, with geometric preconditions handled BY CURATION not dependent types. §4 the three verbs — DERIVE (`let gap = distance(a,b)`), DRIVE (`relate { distance(a,b,5mm) }`), CHECK (`constraint distance(a,b) <= 5mm`) — and the rule "if it removes DOF from a pose it is a relation; if it has a truth value it is a predicate". §9 "diagnostics speak geometry, never solver internals". §12 defers geometry-in-the-loop solving to "a future PRD".

SOLVER CONSOLIDATION WAS ALREADY A NAMED FUTURE, not greenfield: docs/prds/v0_6/constrained-2d-sketch.md §11 says "Solver consolidation (three geometric solvers: relate-solve GN, sketch/libslvs, legacy pattern path) — future; breadcrumbs only here", and the same sentence is repeated verbatim in the doc comment above recognize_pattern in crates/reify-constraints/src/solvespace.rs. Leo's O3-scoped ruling REFINES it: the sketch/libslvs path is KEPT, so consolidation covers relate-solve's GN, the legacy pattern path, and DimensionalSolver's Nelder-Mead.

SPEC FRAMING: docs/reify-language-spec.md §10.3 says "The constraint engine is an orchestrator dispatching to specialized sub-solvers, not a monolithic solver", and lists a Cross-domain row ("span multiple domains simultaneously"). Unifying the continuous solvers does NOT contradict that — the orchestrator survives (CP-SAT discrete, libslvs 2D sketch, GN/LM continuous). What changes is that the Cross-domain row becomes implementable at all: a classifier PARTITIONS, it cannot SPAN.

BINDING PRIOR RULINGS NOT TO RE-LITIGATE: whole-model-objective-coupling.md §3.1 — CP-SAT outer enumeration wrapping the continuous inner solve, MINLP rejected. #5016 (done) ratified NM + alpha-clustering + deterministic multistart — but that is a ruling about the GLOBAL strategy, so replacing the LOCAL solver beneath it is not re-litigation; say so explicitly so a dispatch-time architect does not read it as such. placement-relations-belt.md §7.1 owns the world-pose substrate spec.

reify-solver-elastic: to discriminate a form_find stop criterion's normalisation (global max-row "ratio of maxes" vs per-row |(D·x)_i|/Σ_j|D_ij|), append a mechanically DECOUPLED, exactly-equilibrated stiff cable pair to the fixture: a free node at the exact midpoint of two new anchors (e.g. [0,0,0] between [0,0,±0.5]), then rescale ONLY that pair's q by 2^20. Measured by task 7046 on the 8x2 catenoid+ring-members fixture of tests/tensegrity_surface_gauge_covariance.rs: under the global max-row normaliser the membrane's solved nodes moved 7.928e-5 (iso) / 4.045e-4 (aniso), with early stops at 33 vs 99 iterations (iso) and 49 vs 396 (aniso). Under per-row the change is 0.0, bit-exact. On the 16x2 catenoid with one 1000x-stiff hoop cable, ratio-of-maxes stops with soft rows 313x above tolerance (per-row value 3.13e-9 vs 1e-11); per-row costs 183 -> 293 iterations. Healthy per-row ratio at the SOLVED geometry of solve_reduced measured <= 2.84e-16.

reify-solver-elastic Dörfler marking measurement (task 7449, 2026-10-08, θ=0.5, one refine, deterministic gmsh, aposteriori_validation.rs fixtures): feeding η_e² instead of η_e to mark_dorfler marks 2-4x fewer elements (cantilever 97 vs 192 of 761; L-shape 126 vs 495 of 2221; plate-with-hole 127 vs 425 of 2841). On the plate-with-hole fixture the squared-marked refine RAISED the Z-Z global indicator 0.0812→0.1069 (+31.6%, reads as Stalled), whereas linear marking dropped it 14.3%. Linear-on-η Dörfler provably satisfies the squared bulk criterion at the same θ (descending-prefix majorization), so it was kept deliberately; switching is deferred to ticket tkt_0RVJCTMZ98PW9DX2K0DDBG1KBT pending a pre-asymptotic-robust stall rule.

In geometric-relations ζ (task 4386), the B3 conflict case (concentric + distance(shank_axis, hole_axis, 5mm)) routes through the REMAINDER-VERIFICATION path, NOT the SolveResult::Infeasible path that step-16's text nominally describes. Reason: at the coaxial witness the two axes are coincident, so distance's perpendicular-distance Jacobian row lies entirely within concentric's perpendicular-translation span (and the origin-distance FD gradient at coincident origins is zero) → distance is rank-redundant → it lands in the remainder, and the post-solve verification finds it violated (5mm vs the 0mm concentric drives). reify-eval/src/relate_solve.rs::solve_relate_scope therefore emits the geometric conflict_diagnostic from BOTH entry points: a violated remainder relation that shares a datum operand with a driving relation (the actual B3 path), and a genuinely-infeasible driving set (minimal_infeasible_subset, plan-faithful but not exercised by any ζ test).

Task 4386 (geometric-relations ζ relate-solve) interaction with task 4651 (geometry-consumer Undef detector, now on main): `detect_unresolved_geometry_consumers` (reify-eval/src/engine_eval.rs:965) fires ONLY on the kernel-less path (`kernel_less:true`); engine.build()→check()→eval() registers a kernel so the detector is suppressed (§6 no-double-fire, engine_eval.rs:955-964). ζ's per-scope relate-solve runs at the Resolution-node BUILD pass with the OCCT kernel present — the datum-domain single-shot case that RESOLVES, the complement to 4651's deferred geometry-in-the-loop decline (E_EVAL_UNRESOLVED). An `at auto` pose cell lowers to a literal Value::Undef (ExprKind::Auto), NOT a FunctionCall, so is_geometry_consumer_call (geometry_ops.rs:3443) returns false for it — no false-positive from the new detector. Post-4651 anchors: eval_sub_pose at geometry_ops.rs:8206 (was 8140); dimensional solve call site (build_solver_problem→lookup_solver_for_module→.solve) at engine_eval.rs:~2847-2877 (was 2748-2773).

CORRECTS memory 6227ec9a (reify-solver-elastic form_find.rs, solve_reduced singularity guard). Its claim that no end-to-end test can make the residual branch decide is FALSE for a NEAR-singular, finite D_ff. Faer fixture measured 2026-09-23 (task 7046 review): a straight chain A0 -c- f0 -c- f1 =strut= f2 -c- f3 -c- A1, all cables q=1. The strut is a rank-1 update of the cable-only D_ff, singular at q_s = -1/(2+2) = -0.25. At q_s = -0.25+1e-14, form_find_anchored returns FINITE coordinates of about 7.5e13, so any_nonfinite cannot fire. The per-row residual max|(D·x)_i|/Σ_j|D_ij| is 2^-8. Rule: backward-stable LU bounds |r| ≲ eps·|D|·|x̂|, so dividing the residual by the SOLVED coordinate scale always gives ~eps (5.2e-17 here) and the branch is dead by construction. Normalise by the INPUT (anchor) scale instead: 6.5e-4 here. Caveats: the 2-free-node chain (q2 = -0.5+δ) gives an exactly-zero faer residual at every δ from 4e-16 to 1e-8, although numpy/LAPACK gives about 0.05. The x-aligned 4-node chain also gives an exact 0 at δ = 1e-11. The residual is rounding noise on huge coordinates, so measure a fixture before relying on it.

content: solver-unification ζ #6673 (dimensional scaling, PRD geometry-algebra-solver-unification §7.3/B15): under the §7.3 table's ABSOLUTE metre-row nominal tolerance (solver_convergence = 1e-6 m) with t_ang = lin_tol/L, rescaling the geometry by k multiplies the whole scaled residual r̃ by k uniformly. The GN iterates in x̃ are therefore invariant, but the stop test max|r̃| <= 1 is not. Measured 2026-10-16 on a planar analogue (L = 0.01 m, k = 1 vs k = 1024): the iteration count differed in 36/108 fixtures, and in 0/108 with an L-relative metre-row bar. Also, flooring L at kernel_local makes t_ang = 10 for direction-only relation sets (relate_solve_tests.rs b2_relations), so the convergence test passes vacuously. Filed as report_false_premise (exactness) by the ζ architect, pending re-spec.

Before the fix, an inline script that declared the renderer raised ValueError naming 'renderChart(elementId'. Now static/js/chart-renderer.js inlined into one <script> reads []. So a later call can be missed: `var quote = /'/; renderChart('chart-sankey', f);` reads []. Or a call inside a later string or comment can be counted: `var quote = /'/; var note = "it's renderChart('chart-monthly', f)";` reads ['chart-monthly']. A call from another macro inside macros.html does not count (e.g. chart_panel calling chart_container). So a change that removes a macro's last template caller must also delete that macro, or fold it into its in-file caller, in the same commit; otherwise the test fails, naming the macro. That is what happened when compare.html moved from chart_container to chart_panel.

Completed: .dockerignore's SQLite patterns (*.db, *.sqlite, *.sqlite3, *.db-journal, *.db-wal, *.db-shm) only match at the build-context root; nested ones reach the build context
Description: Follow-up from task 572 (escalation id agent-followup-572), raised by task 572's code review (reviewer_comprehensive, category robustness, location .dockerignore:47) and then measured. PROBLEM
Docker's build-context matcher (moby patternmatcher, used by both the classic builder and BuildKit) anchors any .dockerignore pattern at the context root unless it starts with `**/`. Task 572 prefixed `__pycache__/`, `*.py[cod]` and `*.egg-info/` with `**/`. The block headed "SQLite / local DB artifacts (created at runtime — never commit/ship)" in /.dockerignore still holds the bare patterns `*.db`, `*.sqlite`, `*.sqlite3`, `*.db-journal`, `*.db-wal`, `*.db-shm`, so they drop only root-level files. A runtime database written below the root, for example under tests/ or src/, is sent to the Docker daemon in the build context.

MEASURED 2026-10-01 on branch task/572 (HEAD 676962c), using the technique of tests/validation/test_container_smoke.py::received_build_context: a throwaway `FROM scratch` + `COPY . /context/` build of a copy of the tracked files plus planted files, then `docker create` + `docker cp` of /context. SUGGESTED WORK
1. Check first that no tracked file matches the SQLite patterns, as was done for dist/: `git ls-files` filtered by `*.db`, `*.sqlite*`, `*.db-*`. Widening is only safe if none does. Keep `build/`, `dist/` and `.eggs/` root-anchored: the domain library tracks src/solar_challenge/web/static/dist/style.css, so `**/dist/` would drop it from a vendored copy.
2. If none does, prefix the SQLite patterns with `**/` in .dockerignore (the `# Python` section's two-line note explains the rule; keep the file self-describing).
3. Extend the guard in tests/validation/test_container_smoke.py. `_is_python_build_artifact` and the slow probe test_the_build_context_carries_no_host_python_artifacts are Python-specific; add a sibling predicate or generalise them. The probe skips when the host holds nothing to leak (_nested_artifacts_in_received_directories), so a planted-file fixture may be needed for a deterministic RED.
4. docs/domain-library-consumption.md section B2 step 3 states which of .dockerignore's drops apply at any depth (bytecode caches and egg-info) and which only at the repo root; keep it true.

Priority is low: nothing in the repo writes a database below the root today (not measured exhaustively); this is a latent hole of the same class task 572 closed.

RE-MEASURED (steward, independently of the filer, at bf67d958da):
- `note` is WRITTEN by scripts/legibility/codebook.py::_build_sighting (schema-declared at the entry- and candidate-sighting shapes) and REQUESTED from the LLM by scripts/legibility/coder.py::build_prompt.

- The census miner reaches the LLM through that same seam (census.py::mine_to_saturation -> coder.code_digests -> build_codebook_index).

- Grep for `note` across scripts/legibility/*.py returns writes, schema declarations, and unrelated prose ("cost note") — no reader.

  (b) intended machine-read signal — in which case the wiring does not exist today and the PRD should say that plainly rather than implying it works.

Completed: coder.py: tie the trickle coder's prompt response schema to code_digest's reads so a key rename cannot silently empty every judgment
Description: Found by task 5685's amendment pass (review suggestion 1) while adding a digest-side lockstep test. It is outside 5685's scope, because scripts/legibility/coder.py is not in its lock set.

DEFECT (latent; no sighting yet). In scripts/legibility/coder.py, the trickle coder's response-schema key names ("matches", "candidates") are spelled independently in two places:
- coder.py::build_prompt's prompt text, which tells the LLM what to reply: the one-line schema example plus the empty-answer example.
- coder.py::code_digest's record assembly, which reads the reply: `"matches": judgment.get("matches") or []` and `"candidates": judgment.get("candidates") or []`. main()'s matched/candidates aggregation spells them again.
Suppose the prompt's schema is renamed (say "matches" -> "hits") and code_digest is not. Every reply then parses, `.get("matches") or []` defaults to [], codebook.validate_coding_record passes (both lists are optional), and the result is ok=True with no matches. That is "coded fine, found nothing" for every digest: exactly the silent-success failure the module docstring's never-fabricate contract (codebook lesson one-shot-subagent-contract) exists to prevent. No test ties the two together today. scripts/tests/test_legibility_coder.py's build_prompt tests check only that the prompt embeds the digest, the codebook index and the phase enum.

WHAT 5685 ALREADY DID, and why it does not cover this. scripts/tests/test_legibility_digest.py::TestCoderJudgmentPayloadClassifier::test_the_reply_the_coder_prompt_prescribes_is_recognised_lockstep reads the reply example out of coder.build_prompt and asserts digest.is_coder_judgment_payload recognises it. That test holds digest.py's CODER_JUDGMENT_KEYS in step with the PROMPT. It says nothing about whether coder.py's own consumer reads the keys its prompt asks for.

SUGGESTED FIX (the 5685 reviewer's preferred remedy, which 5685 could not take for scope reasons):
- Single-source the key set in coder.py, or in a small leaf module that digest.py could also import without inverting the digest -> coder producer/consumer layering.
- Build build_prompt's schema example and code_digest's / main()'s reads from that set.
A lighter alternative is a coder-side test: feed code_digest (with a fake invoke) the reply example taken from build_prompt's own output, populated with at least one match, and assert the record carries it.

Context: task 5685 plan design decision 4 keeps digest.py's CODER_JUDGMENT_KEYS local, and bans digest.py from importing coder.py.
Analysis: PREMISES VERIFIED (worktree .worktrees/5791 at 8b7210c220):
- scripts/legibility/coder.py (854 lines) spells the reply keys independently in three places. build_prompt (~L274-281) has a hand-written one-line schema example and the empty example '{"matches": [], "candidates": []}'. code_digest (~L489-496) does `"matches": judgment.get("matches") or []` and the same for "candidates". main() (~L803-804) reads `r.get("matches") or []` and `r.get("candidates") or []` off the records.
- The task text says digest.py holds CODER_JUDGMENT_KEYS. It has moved: the constant now lives in scripts/legibility/reingestion.py (L18), a leaf module that 'imports nothing from the legibility pipeline it serves'. The lockstep test is scripts/tests/test_legibility_reingestion.py::TestCoderJudgmentPayloadClassifier::test_the_reply_the_coder_prompt_prescribes_is_recognised_lockstep. It reads the ONE prompt line that starts with '{' out of coder.build_prompt. scripts/tests/test_legibility_coder.py::test_the_prompt_prescribes_exactly_one_json_reply_line also pins that there is exactly one such line.
- The §7.3 RECORD keys "matches"/"candidates" are a published contract (codebook.CODING_RECORD_SCHEMA, both optional, open-world). Several readers spell them literally: codebook.apply_coding_record and _reject_deletion_directive, census.py:148/1723, session_ledger.py:144-146. The reply keys and the record keys are the same names BY DESIGN, because code_digest copies the reply body into the record.

DEFECT REPRODUCED (my session, main checkout's .venv python over this worktree's code): a reply {"hits": [<valid match>], "candidates": []} gives code_digest ok=True with record["matches"] == []. That is the silent 'coded fine, found nothing'.

THE MODEL-SIDE VARIANT HAS REAL SIGHTINGS, so this is not purely latent. I scanned local transcripts: ~/.claude/projects, *.jsonl, mtime >= 2026-09-01, <= 2MB. 2660 sessions whose first user turn is the trickle-coder prompt. Of the 2466 parseable final replies:
- 2464 carry exactly {matches, candidates}.
- 0 carry only one of the two keys.
- 0 carry a non-list value.
- 2 are {"verified", "reason"}, e.g. session a3cbed47-839b-4c7f-8e85-edcf9d07b66c. Its digest quotes a census-verifier prompt and Haiku answered that prompt instead. Today code_digest turns both into ok=True empty verdicts, which is exactly the never-fabricate violation.
So requiring both keys costs ~0 real replies, and it catches real fabrications.

APPROACH (three parts):
(1) Single source in coder.py. Private _MATCHES_KEY / _CANDIDATES_KEY plus one structured _PRESCRIBED_REPLY mapping (one placeholder finding per key). build_prompt renders the schema line with json.dumps(_PRESCRIBED_REPLY) and the empty line with json.dumps({key: [] for key in _PRESCRIBED_REPLY}). I verified both are BYTE-IDENTICAL to today's literals, so the model sees no change. code_digest assembles the record from the _PRESCRIBED_REPLY keys, and main() counts through _MATCHES_KEY / _CANDIDATES_KEY.
(2) Strict read. After parse_coder_output succeeds, code_digest requires every _PRESCRIBED_REPLY key in the judgment. A missing key is an ordinary per-digest failure (ok=False, record=None, capped=False) whose reason names the missing keys and the keys the reply carried. Values pass through to validate_coding_record unchanged, with no `or []` coercion, so a null list fails as a schema violation. This makes any residual mismatch loud: a one-sided rename, or model drift.
(3) End-to-end guard test. It takes the reply line build_prompt prescribes, fills its placeholders, runs it through code_digest, then through codebook.apply_coding_record (the §7.3 consumer), and asserts one match and one candidate are applied and every filled string survives. That ties prompt keys = coder reads = record contract = merger reads, which a renamed constant would otherwise silently break downstream.

Out of scope, deliberately: reingestion.py stays untouched. Its lockstep test reads build_prompt's output, which now derives from the single source. Task 5685 decision 4 keeps it import-free. Also out: codebook.py and the other §7.3 record readers.

Running the suites: `uv run --project shared pytest scripts/tests/...` (the verify form). The main checkout's `/home/leo/src/dark-factory/.venv/bin/python -m pytest` also works from this worktree; it ran 730 legibility tests green in ~37s with a prototype of part (2) applied, since reverted.
Key decisions: Single-source the reply schema INSIDE coder.py as one private structured value (_PRESCRIBED_REPLY plus _MATCHES_KEY/_CANDIDATES_KEY). Do not use a new leaf module, reingestion.py or codebook.py.; Render the prompt's schema and empty-answer examples with json.dumps over the structured value, so the prompt text is byte-identical to today's.; Add a strict key-presence check in code_digest: a parsed reply missing a prescribed key is an ordinary uncapped per-digest failure. Drop the `or []` coercion so values reach validate_coding_record unchanged.
Steps completed: 4/4
Modules: scripts/legibility/coder.py, scripts/tests/test_legibility_coder.py
