candidates.content: In fused-memory scope.py, resolve_project_id() is deliberately a PURE, no-I/O basename derivation (relied on by ~15 hot-path callers incl. sqlite_task_backend dep-resolution equality check, pre_done_hook, server/tools) and must stay pure — do NOT add a filesystem/manifest read into it. For rename-stable project_id resolution, use resolve_project_id_for_root(root) instead: it reads the declared project_id from <root>/dark-factory-orchestrator.yaml first (via read_declared_project_id, fail-open to basename, never raises) and is wired ONLY into the two registry builders build_known_projects_map (recon-cadence registry) and ProjectPrefixRegistry.from_roots (path-scope guard). This lets a project-dir rename that preserves the manifest project_id re-point both registries under the SAME id instead of churning refiles (task 2813).

fused-memory's get_statuses (and every tool going through _normalize_project_root) hard-rejects a RELATIVE project_root with {"error": "project_root must be a non-empty absolute path, got: '.'"} — the argument is resolved by the SERVER's cwd, not the client's. scripts/legibility/census.py's CLI defaults --project-root to "." and nightly._default_census_launcher launches census.py with no arguments, so every production census get_statuses call carried "." and failed (task 3291). Always absolutise a project_root before it crosses an MCP wire boundary.
Identified that reconcile_task() incorrectly falls back to using project_id as project_root

proc_supervision.RestartPlan.__post_init__ (task 2237) raises ValueError on a non-absolute cwd. Every independent construction seam that builds a RestartPlan from a caller-supplied project_root must defensively call Path(project_root).resolve() itself — it is NOT enough to fix one caller and assume others are safe. Task 2237 needed this fix in two separate places (StaleServiceRestartCoordinator.__init__ and the module-level schedule_detached_systemd_restart) because each accepts its own project_root independently. Task 2238 (DeterministicRunner's two restart mechanisms converting to RestartPlan/EscalationSpec) will add a third such seam and should apply the same .resolve() guard at its own construction point rather than assuming an upstream caller already resolved it — an unresolved relative cwd turns every restart attempt into a ValueError that gets misclassified as a transient failure and retried forever.
Noted that both '_resolve_project_root' and '_read_project_root_from_config' already return resolved Paths
Updated '_resolve_project_root' docstring at line 30 to clarify its 'always canonical' guarantee

GOTCHA (measured on CPython 3.13.9, 2026-09-24, task 4907): pathlib's Path.resolve() in its default non-strict mode swallows OSError and does not fail on a symlink loop, but a path containing an embedded NUL still raises ValueError ("lstat: embedded null character in path"). So an audit or sweep that resolves AUTHOR-CONTROLLED paths from task metadata (for example prd_path, the way manifest_stamping.py::_stamp_capability_manifests_impl step 2 does) must catch ValueError itself, or one corrupt row aborts the whole run. In dark-factory's audit scripts this matters doubly: scripts/_task_db_scan.py::sweep_project_roots catches only sqlite3.Error, so any other exception escaping a per-project audit aborts EVERY remaining project root. For the pattern, see scripts/audit_manifest_descriptor_drift.py::_contained_sidecar_relpath: resolve, catch ValueError, return None, then containment-check with is_relative_to.

fused-memory builds its project_id→project_root registries by deriving project_id from the directory BASENAME (models/scope.py:resolve_project_id) — used by build_known_projects_map (recon-cadence registry / harness _known_projects) and ProjectPrefixRegistry.from_roots (path-scope guard). The persistent per-project root list is the DASHBOARD_KNOWN_PROJECT_ROOTS env var on the INSTALLED fused-memory systemd unit (survives fused-memory restarts; the committed service templates default to this repo only). Consequence: renaming a project directory so its basename changes breaks recon + path-guard registration for that project_id (recon reads a dead git tree → ValidationError + UNKNOWN task_count_snapshot sentinel; path-guard churns refiles) unless the id is pinned elsewhere. Task 2813 fix: resolve project_id from <root>/dark-factory-orchestrator.yaml's project_id key first (basename fallback), so a rename that preserves the manifest id re-points recon instead of churning. Verified case: my_solar_challenge renamed /home/leo/src/my-solar-challenge → /home/leo/src/solar-challenge.

GOTCHA (complements the task-3291 wire-boundary finding, does not duplicate it): fused-memory's MCP boundary rejects a non-absolute/empty project_root via server/tools.py `_normalize_project_root` -> `validate_project_root`, but INTERNAL helpers behind that boundary that build an on-disk path from project_root have no such guard. `Path('')` normalises to `Path('.')`, so a falsy project_root silently makes `<project_root>/data/orchestrator/scheduler_state.json` resolve CWD-relative — handing back whatever project the server process is rooted in instead of erroring. Measured on task 3858: `effective_lock_depth('', 2)` returned 12 (the ambient dark-factory snapshot) rather than the coarse default 2. When writing a project_root-keyed helper in fused-memory, guard falsy input explicitly and return the caller's default; a silent cross-project read is far worse than a fallback.
Completed task 'Fix: targeted.py project_root fallback silently uses project_id as path'

fused-memory gotcha: scheduler_overrides.db rows are persisted keyed on resolve_main_checkout(project_root) — set_task_priority_override funnels project_root through server/tools.py::_normalize_project_root -> resolve_main_checkout before both opening the DB and writing the project_root column. This is STRONGER than the park_eviction_requests.db contract (which uses only str(Path(project_root).resolve())): resolve_main_checkout maps any worktree subpath to the MAIN checkout, not just symlink/trailing-slash normalization. Any direct reader (e.g. the task 2781 reconciliation stale_priority_override_edge_sweep's read_live_override_state) MUST apply the same normalization before its WHERE project_root=? filter, or a non-canonical root silently matches zero rows -> returns {} -> the sweep judges every valid boost/pin/TTL edge "task absent" -> mass over-invalidation of valid edges (irreversible). Because reconciliation can't import server.tools (import cycle), replicate normalization in-module: try resolve_main_checkout (from fused_memory.models.scope), fall back to str(Path(project_root).resolve()) on ValueError so hermetic non-git temp-dir tests still run.

Current implementation of model_post_init assigns self.project_root = self.project_root.resolve()

In fused-memory, get_tasks/get_task MCP tools (server/tools.py) and the SqliteTaskBackend carry NO project provenance, while task IDs are per-project autoincrement and collide across projects (reify#1654 ≠ dark_factory#1654). Both tools funnel through the same _normalize_project_root → interceptor path, so they cannot diverge for the same project_root; cross-project 'contamination' (e.g. Stage 3's bulk get_tasks dump showing reify titles for dark_factory IDs) is therefore a CALLER passing the wrong project_root, silently undetectable because results aren't self-describing. The reconciliation harness fetches the task tree once per cycle (_fetch_filtered_task_tree, correct root) and injects it into Stage 1/2 only; Stage 3 (IntegrityCheck) does not fetch tasks in Python — its LLM agent calls get_tasks via MCP itself. Established wrong-source-read detector: task_filter.detect_census_inconsistency + FilteredTaskTree.max_task_id, recorded by stages via an overridden run() that mutates report.stats after super().run().

CORRECTION to the `build_known_projects_map` coverage-check gotcha (supersedes the id-comparison advice in memory a8dd435c-01f9-4f73-b41b-6f17b87f91b2): detecting an under-resolved `DASHBOARD_KNOWN_PROJECT_ROOTS` registry by comparing resolved project IDS is structurally blind to both degradations it claims to catch. MEASURED on real tmp roots (task 2917 amendment pass): a nonexistent/typo'd root returned "no issue", and so did a first-wins duplicate-id collision. Why: (a) `Path(raw).resolve()` is NON-STRICT, so `build_known_projects_map` does not skip a missing root — it ADMITS it under a basename-derived project_id, so the phantom id IS in the map (and downstream consumers then process a project that enumerates 0 and exits 0 — a silent green); (b) on a duplicate-id collision the DROPPED root's id is by definition still in the map, as the winner's. CORRECT PREDICATE: compare each env-named root's RESOLVED PATH against `map.values()` (catches the collision), and separately stat it with `Path(root).is_dir()`, which swallows OSError and answers False (catches the typo/moved-checkout case). Path comparison is also duplicate-proof, so it does not cry degradation when the env var lists the primary root — which the live registry does. Have the resolver return the whole `{project_id: project_root}` map rather than just ids, so coverage is judged against the builder's own single derivation and `resolve_project_id_for_root` does not re-read every `<root>/dark-factory-orchestrator.yaml` a second time. Worked example: `fused-memory/scripts/sweep_orphan_flag_markers.py::_known_projects_map` + `::_known_projects_coverage_issue`.

In reconciliation stages (post task 2146/β), BaseStage.project_id and BaseStage.project_root are read-only @property views annotated `-> str` (the NewType is widened to str). So when threading ProjectScope: a module-level helper annotated `project_root: ProjectRoot` (or `project_id: ProjectId`) must be called from stage methods with `self.scope.project_root` / `self.scope.project_id` (typed as the NewType), NOT `self.project_root` / `self.project_id` (typed str) — passing the plain-str property is a pyright reportArgumentType error. base.py is owned by β; downstream scope-threading tasks (γ task_knowledge_sync, δ targeted.py, W5) should switch helper call sites to self.scope.* rather than changing the base.py property return types.

content: Gotcha: shared.project_id.project_id_for_root does not resolve its argument, so a relative root like '.' or '..' raises ValueError (PurePath('.').name is ''). Its contract is "pass the resolved project root". Each caller resolves at the point where the root enters, e.g. project_id_for_root(Path(root).resolve()), and keeps the unresolved root for anything it renders or stores. Task 6713 did this in check_consolidation_closure._project_root, audit_combine_gate_marker_loss.resolve_project_id and census_tagger_debris.census_project. It deliberately did not do it in _task_db_scan.resolve_project_roots, which would have churned the report bytes.

a8dd435c-01f9-4f73-b41b-6f17b87f91b2.content: GOTCHA: `fused_memory.models.scope.build_known_projects_map(primary_root, extra_roots=None)` seeds its candidate list with `primary_root` BEFORE extending with the `DASHBOARD_KNOWN_PROJECT_ROOTS` roots, so an unset/unreachable env var yields a ONE-entry map, never an empty one. Any `if not known_projects_map:` degradation check is therefore unreachable in exactly the failure it looks like it guards — the caller silently narrows to the primary project and exits 0. Detect it instead by comparing resolved project IDS: `missing = [r for r in scope.known_project_roots_from_env() if scope.resolve_project_id_for_root(r) not in resolved_ids]`, and treat "env var unset" (primary-only coverage, expected on a single-project install) as a different, non-fatal case from "env var set but under-resolved". Do NOT compare COUNTS (`len(map) < 1 + len(named_roots)`): the live registry lists the primary root in the env var too, and the builder drops it as a duplicate project_id, so a count check cries degradation on every healthy run. Task 'GUI Claude assistant: wire permission-prompt UI for tool-use approval' completed. The integrated Claude assistant in the Reify GUI cannot grant the user permission to run tools that require approval (Write outside allowlisted paths, Bash, etc.). The model produces text like "It looks like I need your permission to write new files. Could you grant the write permission when the prompt appears?" but no prompt is ever shown — the GUI has no permission-prompt path on top of the sidecar.</description>
<parameter name="details">## Problem

When chatting with the integrated Claude in the GUI ChatPanel, the model surfaces text saying it needs the user to grant permission for an upcoming tool call, but no permission prompt UI ever appears, so the tool call is silently blocked.

## Root cause

`gui/sidecar/src/session.ts:142-160` invokes the Claude CLI with:

```
claude --print --verbose --output-format stream-json --include-partial-messages \
       --input-format stream-json --model ... --system-prompt ...
```

It does NOT pass `--permission-prompt-tool` (which would route permission prompts as MCP tool calls back to the host) and the GUI has no permission-prompt UI, no MCP server endpoint to receive those prompts, and no IPC channel for the host (Tauri side) to display approve/deny dialogs and forward decisions back to the sidecar.

In `--print` headless mode without a permission-prompt-tool wired, the Claude CLI defaults to denying tools that need approval (since there's no terminal to prompt on). The user sees the model's "please grant permission" prose but never sees a dialog.

## Acceptance criteria

- User chats with integrated Claude.
- Claude wants to run a tool that requires approval (e.g. Write to a path outside the workspace, Bash).
- A toast/modal/inline UI in the ChatPanel surfaces the permission request showing tool name + args.
- User clicks Allow / Deny / "Always allow this tool".
- Decision is propagated back to the sidecar → Claude CLI; the tool either runs or is denied.

## Implementation sketch

1. Run the sidecar's spawned `claude` with `--permission-prompt-tool mcp__reify-permission__approve_tool` (or similar) — Claude CLI will then route permission prompts as a tool call to that MCP endpoint instead of refusing.
2. Stand up a tiny in-process MCP server inside the sidecar that exposes `approve_tool({ tool_name, input }) → { behavior: "allow" | "deny", message?, updatedInput? }`.
3. Plumb through to the host: when the sidecar's MCP server receives an `approve_tool` call, forward to the Tauri host (new outbound message type, e.g. `permission_request`).
4. Frontend (App.tsx + ChatPanel) displays a toast/modal with Allow / Deny / Always.
5. User decision flows back: frontend → Tauri command → sidecar IPC → MCP `approve_tool` resolves with allow/deny.
6. "Always" persists per-session so we don't re-prompt for the same tool+args within a session (and possibly across sessions via sidecar layout).

Reference: Anthropic Claude Agent SDK / CLI documentation on `--permission-prompt-tool` and `canUseTool` callbacks.

## Files likely to touch

- `gui/sidecar/src/session.ts` — add `--permission-prompt-tool` arg, wire MCP listener
- `gui/sidecar/src/types.ts` — new outbound `permission_request` and inbound `permission_decision` message types
- `gui/src-tauri/src/claude_bridge.rs` — forward both directions
- `gui/src/bridge.ts` — new event subscription + send command
- `gui/src/panels/ChatPanel.tsx` (or new component) — render the prompt UI
- `gui/sidecar/src/__tests__/session.test.ts` + `gui/src-tauri/src/tests/claude_bridge_tests.rs` — coverage
- `gui/src/__tests__/ChatPanel.test.tsx` — UI test

## Out of scope

- Hardening the permission policy itself (allowlist/denylist/regex match) — start with a simple "ask the user" loop. Allowlist persistence in sidecar layout can be a follow-up.

Task 'ChatPanel: stuck "Thinking..." throbbers and streaming cursors when terminal event missing' completed. Multiple "Thinking..." throbbers and blinking streaming cursors persist in the ChatPanel after assistant turns finish or are aborted. User reported seeing 2 stuck throbbers and 3 stuck cursors in a session that hit the sidecar-crash bug (#3208). The throbber/cursor visibility logic in `ThinkingBlock` and `StreamingText` is correctly gated on `message.thinkingComplete` / `message.complete`, but multiple paths fail to flip those flags.</description>
<parameter name="details">## Root causes

Three distinct bugs combine to produce this UX:

### 1. Sidecar crash leaves orphan messages (primary)

When the sidecar Node process dies mid-turn (e.g. via #3208's missing `proc.on('error')` listener), no `done` or `error` outbound message ever reaches the frontend. The in-flight `AssistantMessage` is stuck with `complete: false, thinkingComplete: false` forever.

`gui/src-tauri/src/claude_bridge.rs:374-389` — when the reader's on_exit fires, the host sets `SidecarState::Crashed(...)` but emits **no Tauri event to the frontend**. Frontend has no way to know.

**Fix**: emit a `claude://sidecar-crashed` Tauri event from the on_exit hook. In claudeStore, register a listener that calls `cancelAndFlush()` and walks `state.messages`, marking every in-flight `AssistantMessage` (where `!complete`) as `{ complete: true, thinkingComplete: true, error: 'sidecar disconnected' }` so its throbber/cursor is hidden. Also emit a SystemMessage so the user sees what happened.

### 2. `error` outbound flips `complete` but not `thinkingComplete`

`gui/src/stores/claudeStore.ts:225-243` — the `error` case sets `m.complete = true` but does NOT set `m.thinkingComplete = true`. If the error fires while the message is still in the thinking phase, the throbber stays visible even though `complete = true` removes the cursor.

**Fix**: add `m.thinkingComplete = true` to the produce block in the error case (mirror the `done` case at line 205-206).

### 3. `claudeAbort` does not optimistically clear in-flight UI

`gui/src/stores/claudeStore.ts:274-278` — `claudeAbort()` calls `cancelAndClear`, sets sessionStatus to 'idle', and forwards onAbort. The in-flight assistant message is NOT marked complete here. The throbber/cursor only disappears IF the sidecar later sends `done`/`error`. If the sidecar crashes on abort (#3208), no event arrives → stuck UI.

**Fix**: in `claudeAbort`, locate the in-flight message via `state.currentMessageId` and flip `complete` + `thinkingComplete = true` immediately (set `m.aborted = true` if a distinct visual state for "user-aborted" is desired). The sidecar's eventual `done`/`error` should then be tolerant of an already-complete message.

## Repro

Hit Stop while Claude is mid-thinking, OR have the sidecar crash mid-turn (easy via #3208's path: send a long prompt, wait 5+ minutes for timeout). Throbber and cursor remain after sessionStatus returns to 'idle'.

## Acceptance criteria

1. After clicking Stop:
   - Throbber and cursor disappear immediately on the in-flight message.
   - Subsequent messages render cleanly.
2. After sidecar crash:
   - Frontend receives a `sidecar-crashed` event.
   - All in-flight messages get marked complete with an error note.
   - A SystemMessage appears in the chat: "Claude assistant disconnected — restart in progress" or similar.
3. After sidecar `error` outbound during thinking phase:
   - Throbber AND cursor both disappear; thinking block collapses with the partial thinking text.

## Test additions

- `gui/src/__tests__/claudeStore.test.ts`:
  - `claudeAbort` flips in-flight message to `complete: true, thinkingComplete: true`.
  - `error` outbound flips `thinkingComplete: true` (regression).
  - new `sidecar-crashed` event handler walks all in-flight messages and marks them complete.
- `gui/src-tauri/src/tests/claude_bridge_tests.rs`:
  - on_exit hook emits the new Tauri event when sidecar exits unex…[truncated, 4723 chars total]

Task 'Finance projection silently drops scenario-level SEG: _seg_export_income_gbp reads total_export_revenue_gbp, so scenario.seg_tariff_pence_per_kwh yields £0 CBS export income after Task 85' completed. POST-MERGE REVIEW FINDING (review_id 20260630T153237), surfaced by tracing the Task 85 export-revenue fix end-to-end into the board-facing finance model. Two distinct SEG inputs coexist and are NOT reconciled in the public 25-year projection, and Task 85 turned a pre-existing overstatement into a silent £0.

== THE TWO SEG INPUTS ==
1. HomeConfig.seg_tariff (per-home; added by task #2). Drives the home-sim export_revenue series -> SummaryStatistics.total_export_revenue_gbp (home.py: calculate_summary sets total_export_revenue_gbp = results.export_revenue.sum(), ~home.py:502/554).
2. ScenarioConfig.seg_tariff_pence_per_kwh (scenario-level; the field the YAML `seg:` block maps to via config.py:1713). When passed to calculate_summary it ONLY populates the SEPARATE field SummaryStatistics.seg_revenue_gbp (home.py:516-521/557); it does NOT change total_export_revenue_gbp.

== THE DEFECT ==
The CBS SEG-revenue line of the multi-year projection reads input #1, never input #2:
- finance.py: _simulate_age computes `seg_revenue = sum(_seg_export_income_gbp(s, finance, s.simulation_days) for s in per_home_summaries)` (~finance.py:1455), folded into `fleet_revenue = own_use_revenue + seg_revenue + grid_services - cbs_grid_charge` (~finance.py:1476).
- _seg_export_income_gbp (finance.py:484) reads ONLY phys.export_rev_physics = summary.total_export_revenue_gbp * scale (physics path returns it directly, finance.py:521; override path derives the rate from it, finance.py:526-532). It never reads summary.seg_revenue_gbp.
- The `calculate_summary(r, seg_tariff_pence_per_kwh=scenario.seg_tariff_pence_per_kwh)` call at finance.py:1433 therefore has NO effect on seg_revenue — the scenario-level SEG rate is silently ignored by the CBS export-income line.

== WHY TASK 85 MADE IT DANGEROUS ==
Before Task 85, a scenario with seg only at the scenario level (homes[*].seg_tariff = None, scenario.seg_tariff_pence_per_kwh set) produced total_export_revenue_gbp priced at the IMPORT rate (the old fallback) -> CBS SEG income OVERSTATED but non-zero. After Task 85 (a17acbc, landed 2026-06-30) the home-sim zeroes export_revenue when seg_tariff is None, so total_export_revenue_gbp = 0 -> _seg_export_income_gbp = 0 (both paths) -> CBS earns £0 SEG export income, SILENTLY, even though the scenario configured e.g. 6 p/kWh. Understating CBS revenue inflates the solved own-use cost-recovery rate (solve_cost_recovery_rate, public/__all__) and corrupts the ~£750k investor case.

== WHY IT IS LATENT (not caught by tests) ==
The shipped CLI is the ONLY safe caller: cli/finance.py:162-169 manually threads seg_tariff onto every home (`dataclasses.replace(home, seg_tariff=...)`) with the comment "load_fleet_config does not do this", so via the CLI both inputs are set and total_export_revenue_gbp is correctly SEG-priced. The public library functions project_multi_year / solve_cost_recovery_rate (the latter exported in solar_challenge.__all__ and consumed by the separate solar-challenge-platform repo) take homes+scenario and do NO such threading (project_multi_year just does homes = _resolve_homes(scenario)). A ScenarioConfig parsed from a YAML `seg:` block (config.py:1713) has scenario.seg_tariff_pence_per_kwh set but homes[*].seg_tariff = None -> the bug fires. The calibration test passes only because it mirrors the CLI's manual threading; no test asserts non-zero CBS SEG income via the scenario-level field alone. This exact seam was flagged as a SEAM QUESTION in task #21's description but never reconciled in the projection.

8e5ade8c-db5e-44f5-82da-450a150ea140.content: Solar Challenge sim discovery (2026-06-19, board scenario bristol-phase1-flex.yaml): the capacity-at-events grid-services model computed £0 annual income / 0.0 kW available capacity at events. Root cause is NOT a bug: under Economy-7 peak-arbitrage dispatch the battery is already fully discharging into the evening peak (16:00-18:00) at exactly the hours winter DFS events fire, so there is zero spare capacity for grid services. Arbitrage and grid-services flexibility CANNIBALISE the same battery at the same hour — they are not additive. Consequence: the consulting model's headline "£280/home/yr (£250 arbitrage + £30 grid services)" cannot be simply summed in practice; to earn grid-services revenue you must reserve battery headroom at event times, trading off arbitrage. This is hard-physics confirmation of the value+buildability model §1.1 warning "do not simply add the column maxima".

Completed: Consent check failure denies without caching the denial for the 300 s standing TTL (DecisionReason.CHECK_FAILED)
Description: DEFECT (verified on main 2085985 by the /prd lead session of 2026-09-28, while adversarially reviewing docs/prds/push-alerting-deep-health.md). consent/enforcement.py::GateConsentChecker.check_device catches every exception (e.g. a transient DB failure) and RETURNS an ordinary DeviceStanding whose decision is NO_CONSENT (property_id None). Because it returns normally, consent/enforcement.py::ConsentGuard._get_standing caches that standing like any other for consent_recheck_ttl_seconds (Settings, default 300 s). The guard's own branch 'exception-derived decisions are NOT cached' is unreachable for GateConsentChecker, since the checker already swallowed the exception. Consequence: one DB blip makes scp-ingest drop a CONSENTED home's telemetry for up to 5 minutes. This violates the review/briefing.yaml fail-safe convention: 'a transient DB failure in the consent path must deny (fail-closed) but NOT cache the denial, so the next tick retries'.

WORK
- models/consent_enums.py::DecisionReason gains CHECK_FAILED (a denial reason distinct from NO_CONSENT).
- consent/enforcement.py::GateConsentChecker.check_device returns CHECK_FAILED (not NO_CONSENT) when it catches an exception. The guard's own exception backstop in ConsentGuard._get_standing also yields CHECK_FAILED.
- ConsentGuard._get_standing caches a CHECK_FAILED standing only for a new Settings.consent_check_failure_ttl_seconds (default 15.0; validated 0 < value < consent_recheck_ttl_seconds). It is a SHORT negative cache: never-cached would put a synchronous DB checker call (up to the connect timeout) on every MQTT message on ingest's event loop during a DB fault; 15 s bounds that while recovery is seen within 15 s. Genuine NO_CONSENT / WITHDRAWN / EXPIRED standings keep the full TTL.
- The guard's dropped-row counters distinguish check_failed from no_consent, so the cause is visible.
- Every consumer of DecisionReason treats CHECK_FAILED as denied (fail-closed): grep DecisionReason usages in src (NO_CONSENT is used in ~6 places) and keep behaviour identical for them except the cache lifetime.
- Wire the new Setting through ingestion/service.py::IngestionService.from_settings (where ConsentGuard gets ttl_seconds).

CONSUMERS: scp-ingest (ConsentGuard via IngestionService.from_settings); P-Alert·η2 of docs/prds/push-alerting-deep-health.md, whose three-valued consent standing reads CHECK_FAILED as UNKNOWN.

USER-OBSERVABLE SIGNAL: with a GateConsentChecker whose session factory raises once and then recovers, a consented device's rows are dropped (counted as check_failed) for at most consent_check_failure_ttl_seconds and are accepted again after it, not after 300 s; a genuinely withdrawn consent still caches for the full TTL; tests/integration/test_consent_cross_consumer.py (the cross-consumer keystone) stays green; pytest -m 'not slow' and mypy src/solar_challenge_platform are green.

MODULES: src/solar_challenge_platform/models/consent_enums.py, src/solar_challenge_platform/consent/enforcement.py, src/solar_challenge_platform/settings.py, src/solar_challenge_platform/ingestion/service.py, tests/ingestion/test_consent_enforcement.py, tests/integration/test_consent_cross_consumer.py.

Completed: scp-ingest: the consent re-check's synchronous DB read runs on the event-loop thread, so a DB hang blocks SIGTERM handling and MQTT keepalive
Description: Follow-up filed by task 270's architect (idempotency escalation id agent-followup-270). The same observation was raised as esc-270-1 (L0, dismissed) and rolled up as esc-270-2 / esc-270-3, which are still pending at L1/L2. esc-270-1 suggested exactly this follow-up task. Task 270 does not fix this: its scope is the store-write thread that asyncio.run and the interpreter joined at exit.

OBSERVED IN CODE (main e964a4a):
- scp-ingest runs with consent enforcement on by default. src/solar_challenge_platform/settings.py sets ingestion_consent_enforced = True and consent_recheck_ttl_seconds = 300.0. src/solar_challenge_platform/ingestion/service.py::IngestionService.from_settings then attaches a ConsentGuard backed by GateConsentChecker.
- src/solar_challenge_platform/ingestion/subscriber.py::Subscriber._accept calls ConsentGuard.filter_rows (src/solar_challenge_platform/consent/enforcement.py) directly on the event-loop thread for every message.
- On each per-device cache miss (one per device every 300 s), filter_rows calls GateConsentChecker.check_device, which does synchronous DB reads.
- While the database hangs, that read blocks the whole event loop until the hardened engine's bounds end it (src/solar_challenge_platform/db/session.py: statement_timeout 60 s, connect_timeout 10 s, TCP keepalives 30 s idle + 3 x 10 s). Two things wait with it:

- The validation supervisor's stop grace is 5 s and docker stop's is 10 s. A stop during a DB incident can therefore still end in SIGKILL (exit 137), and a long read can also make the broker drop the connection.

Hypothesis, not measured: under a hung DB with enforcement on and devices whose cache entries have expired, a SIGTERM waits for the in-flight consent read before serve() can cancel Subscriber.run.

For example, run filter_rows's cache-miss DB reads on a thread the stop does not wait for, the way task 270 runs store writes on daemon threads (ingestion/subscriber.py _to_daemon_thread once task 270 lands). _accept would become awaitable on the run() path, and the sync handle_message path would stay as it is.
(b) Bound the consent read well below the stop grace, e.g. with a per-statement timeout on the consent query only. Failing closed is already the documented posture.
(c) Accept and document it.

Whichever is chosen, add a stop-time test with a hung consent read and enforcement on: the process should exit within the 5 s grace.

Priority: low, unless a DB-incident restart is observed to take the full grace.

Task 309 (scp-ingest consent re-check blocks the event loop) architect pre-analysis, 2026-09-25, main 4597c4c. MEASURED: a Subscriber under serve() with a ConsentGuard whose checker never returns runs check_device on MainThread and is still alive 8 s after SIGTERM (SIGKILLed); probe at /tmp/scp309/hung_consent_probe.py. Coordination for task 617 (PLATFORM_OPERATION becomes contract-basis). Task 583's plan (2026-10-09) changes how ingest handles a failed consent check: a CHECK_FAILED row is deferred in StoreForwardBuffer's deferred lane and re-judged on a later flush, instead of being dropped. Design constraints found:
(1) In Subscriber.run, every flush runs _write_pending on an abandonable 'ingest-store-write' daemon thread under _flush_lock. The guard's cache, counters and logging must stay on the event loop (the 270/309 invariant). So re-judge pending rows on the loop, before rows go to the write thread, never inside _write_pending or StoreForwardBuffer.flush.
(2) Pending rows must share StoreForwardBuffer's one drop-oldest max_depth cap: Settings.ingestion_buffer_max_depth = 2_000_000, with evictions counted in .dropped.
(3) Task 617 makes PLATFORM_OPERATION contract-basis: ConsentGate.check then returns OTHER_LAWFUL_BASIS without reading a row. After that, withdrawing platform_operation consent no longer refuses ingest. A keystone 'withdrawn device' must then be modelled differently, e.g. as a device whose Account is no longer ACTIVE, which GateConsentChecker denies as NO_CONSENT.

Consent-test gotcha (solar_challenge_platform, verified 2026-10-11): ConsentGate.check never reads a grant's ts. It decides on the ConsentCurrent row's status, scope and expiry against its clock `at`. The ts that record_event(..., ts=None) stores only orders the events of one (customer, purpose): the latest ts wins, and created_at breaks ties. A test that grants consent need not pin ts unless it records several events for one purpose and relies on their order. record_event already defaults ts to utcnow() and ends with session.flush(), so a trailing flush after it is redundant.

Gotcha (consent/enforcement.py): ConsentGuard._get_standing wraps every ConsentChecker.check_device call in a fail-closed `except Exception` backstop. The backstop returns an UNCACHED NO_CONSENT standing and only WARN-logs 'consent guard check raised', so a broken ConsentChecker test double never raises in the test. Examples: a TypeError or ImportError inside the double, or (from task 261) the ValueError DeviceStanding.__post_init__ raises for a roster-checked grant with property_id=None; a double that keeps no roster must pass roster_checked=False. The breakage shows up instead as rows counted in guard.refused, or as extra check_device calls, because the denial is never cached. When a guard test's refused or call_count assert fails unexpectedly, look for that WARN line in caplog first.

MEASURED 2026-08-28 (task 4537 revalidation): the escalation `category` vocabulary listed in the prose comment on `escalation/src/escalation/models.py::Escalation.category` is NOT the real vocabulary, and its "REFACTOR TRIGGER (task 3709): the NEXT category addition promotes this comment to an enum" note does NOT fire for most new categories. The comment enumerates 9 categories; a grep for `category='...'` literals across orchestrator/src, escalation/src and fused-memory/src returns 55+ distinct values actually in use — including the whole `verify_*` detector family (`verify_drift_divergence`, `verify_cross_check_mismatch`, `verify_host_unreachable`) and the `merge_*` family, none of which are in the prose list. So the trigger is scoped to additions that would GROW THAT COMMENT'S LIST ("instead of growing another line"), not to any new category string anywhere; a detector-local category filed by an orchestrator module follows the established precedent and needs no change to `escalation/`. Practical consequence: adding a new detector category does not require widening a task's file locks into the escalation package — but do say so explicitly in a design decision, because a reviewer reading models.py will otherwise flag the trigger as unhonoured.

Escalation `category` alone is NOT a safe discriminator for identifying a specific escalation class in dark-factory: `category='infra_issue'` has 20+ distinct filing sites (scheduler.py, merge_queue.py, workflow.py, deterministic_runner.py), several of them human-routed `escalate_to_human=True` failures. The established house pattern for pinning one class is the (agent_role, category, unique-summary-substring) triple — see `harness._is_scope_divergence_orphan` and `_is_done_step_commit_orphan` — and note that `suggested_action` is only a unique discriminator for the done-step-commit class, not the plan.files/metadata.files divergence class. Any veto/skip predicate keyed on category alone risks admitting a human-concern escalation.

Escalation revalidation-sweep category blind spot (found 2026-08-10, info-L0→blocking-L2 investigation): L2s minted by promote_to_l2 default to category='design_concern' (escalation/src/escalation/server.py:1299), but the terminal-subject revalidation sweep `_revalidate_open_l2` (orchestrator/src/orchestrator/harness.py:12229-12320) only closes categories in `escalation_revalidation_allowlist`, default frozenset({'task_failure','stranded_blocked'}) (config.py:3608-3610). Any fix that relies on the existing sweep must either widen the allowlist (risky for genuine design concerns) or use task 3587's flag-into-triage-bucket design, which covers arbitrary categories without auto-dismissal. Pattern for filing in-process escalations from orchestrator code (not the MCP tool): use the injected escalation_queue — dedup via escalation_queue.get_by_task(sentinel_task_id, status='pending'[, level=N]), build escalation.models.Escalation(id=escalation_queue.make_id(sentinel), task_id=sentinel, agent_role='orchestrator-...', severity=..., category=..., summary, detail, level=...), then escalation_queue.submit(esc). Born-at-L2 = severity in {critical,urgent}; the 'orchestrator-'/'harness-' agent_role prefix marks a harness sentinel so the server never downgrades severity. GOTCHA (orchestrator/src/orchestrator/deterministic_runner.py): the escalation CATEGORY and the `gate_escalated_at` STAMP are coupled inside the `_file_*_and_block` family, so "just change which category this leg files" is never a one-word change. `_file_milestone_check_failed_and_block` files `milestone_check_failed` AND stamps `gate_escalated_at` (arming section-1's resume fork); `_file_infra_issue_and_block` files `infra_issue` and deliberately stamps NOTHING, which is what lets a read-only predicate be re-attempted on the next dispatch. Task 4065 made that no-stamp property load-bearing for `_run_predicate`'s three no-verdict arms (outer wall-clock guard, the default runner's inner `ScriptTimeout`, unexpected `run_fn` error) and pinned it with `scheduler.update_task.assert_not_awaited()`. So a task asked to move one of those legs to a different category must widen the *infra* helper with a `category` argument, NOT re-point the leg at the milestone helper — the latter silently smuggles in the stamp and changes resume semantics. Two further traps at the same site: the three no-verdict arms are documented as distinguishable ONLY by their summary/detail wording (tests pin `esc.summary` by exact equality, so keep summaries byte-identical when you change a category), and the `ScriptTimeout` arm's detail literally says "this is an INFRA fault, deliberately not milestone_check_failed" — prose that contradicts the record if the category moves and must be updated with it.

`Escalation` records do NOT persist a `project_id` field — the recon gate-backlog path recovers it only from the first line of `detail` (`f'project_id: {project_id}'`). The reconciliation escalation queue at `data/reconciliation/escalations/` is SHARED ACROSS PROJECTS (7 observed live: dark_factory, reify, autopilot_video, know_live, solar_challenge_platform, pump_web_ui, solar_challenge) and task ids are small per-project integers. Any dedupe/identity key for that queue must therefore include project_id; a `(category, task_id)` key would cross-fold different projects' escalations and silently drop one.

Escalation closer matrix (verified 2026-08-23, epsilon investigation): only ONE closer consults authority.py — the HTTP resolve_issue endpoint; every other closer calls EscalationQueue.resolve() in-process. Closers reaching a foreign born-at-L2: (1) header-less resolve_issue (humans — unrestricted by design); (2) watcher-auto via l2_auto_close_class — defeated by L2_AUTO_CLOSE_DENY_ROLES ('orchestrator-deterministic') or L2_AUTO_CLOSE_DENY_CATEGORIES ({design_concern, milestone_gate, milestone_check_failed}), denylist-first; note stale_task_scoped matches the RESOLUTION string supplied at close time, not the record's own evidence; (3) Harness._revalidate_open_deterministic_escalation — requires category=='infra_issue' AND role in sentinel roles AND scheduler.get_task(task_id) resolving AND a deploy-stranded metadata shape (before_done.target_unit) AND a healthy unit probe (triple-gated, not spelling-only); (4) _revalidate_open_l2 — category allowlist (default {task_failure, stranded_blocked}, hot-reloadable) AND subject task terminal AND resolvable task_id. FULLY-ESCAPED shape: non-infra_issue category + 'orchestrator-deterministic' role + non-numeric (dunder) sentinel task_id — each property independently defeats one closer class; only humans can close it. DEDUP KEYS: the dedicated root_cause field + find_pending_l2_by_root_cause is the superior sentinel discriminator (the watcher-outage pair's key); get_by_task is the common sentinel idiom; has_open_l1 is hardcoded level=1 and can never see an L2. The watcher-outage precedent (_file_watcher_outage_l2/_resolve_watcher_outage_l2) has NO N-consecutive-clean-passes counter — it resolves ONLY on a positive liveness event (a healthy rotation completing), so it distinguishes clean-from-blind by construction; the claimant-enforcement PRD's D5 fused that record shape with an auto-resolve semantics that exists nowhere in the tree, which is what created the blind/clean hazard. Also: milestone_check_failed records have a fully clean closer walk, and Harness._recover_stranded_deterministic_gate (Source A) re-files a lost deterministic gate escalation byte-identical — the only self-healing alarm-record path in the system. Novel escalation categories are established practice despite the models.py enum-promotion rule (verify_worktree_contention, candidate_key_residual_duplicates both live).

Born-at-L2 filing mechanics (verified on main 2026-07-13, escalation/server.py:298-334): an escalation is stamped level=2 iff severity ∈ BORN_AT_L2_SEVERITIES ({critical, urgent}) AND agent_role passes _is_harness_sentinel_role (harness-*/orchestrator-* prefixes) — the role does NOT need to be 'orchestrator-deterministic'; 'orchestrator-scheduler' qualifies. A critical/urgent filed by a NON-sentinel role is silently DOWNGRADED to severity='blocking' with a '[downgraded:<orig>]' suffix appended to the summary (suffix placement preserves the 3-token dedupe key) and routes through the normal L0 path. escalation category is a free-form str (models.py:55) — new category strings like 'dependency_capability' need no enum change; watcher urgency keys off severity (watcher.py:110), not category.

content: Since task 5257, the escalation category vocabulary is a checked contract, so the 2026-08-28 note that new detector categories need no escalation-package change no longer holds. Every filed category must be a member of escalation/src/escalation/categories.py::EscalationCategory, and a task that adds a category must add the member in the same change and list categories.py in its files lock. Otherwise EscalationQueue.submit/submit_resolved raise UnregisteredEscalationCategory, escalate_blocker/escalate_info/promote_to_l2 return {'error': ...}, and escalation/tests/test_category_census.py fails verify. Rehydrated legacy records are never checked.

candidates.content: The normative strict-auto uniqueness contract for the Reify constraint solver lives at docs/reify-implementation-architecture.md:1140 (§11.6): a strict `auto` is well-determined iff it is EITHER "uniquely determined by constraints" OR "uniquely optimal under the applicable objective" — two disjunctive tests. crates/reify-constraints/src/solver.rs's verify_uniqueness historically implemented only the first (comparing PARAMETER values via solutions_agree) and applied it to problems governed by the second, which is the root of both the near-inert-check and the suboptimality-conflation defects in task #5711. Read §11.6 before changing anything about uniqueness, ConstraintNonUnique, or auto(free) semantics.

Two reify solver behaviours that any new hard-domain feature inherits (measured 2026-10-07):
(1) On the CP-SAT path, a STRICT auto with several feasible solutions silently returns the first enumerated one, with unique:false and NO diagnostic. Example: strict Bools a and b with `constraint a or b` print a=true, b=true, exit 0. #6554 owns making this the P3 §3.4 non-uniqueness Error.
(2) Guarded (`where`-block) constraints never reach the COLD solve: build_solver_problem filters only template.constraints. `x >= 1mm`, `x <= 9mm` plus `where flag { constraint x == 7mm }` resolves x = 5mm silently. #7489 and #6572 own the cold side; the warm edit paths include every guarded arm unconditionally (#8045). The catalog-membership PRD (β #8356 depends on #6554) scopes its no-silent-non-member invariant I1 to unguarded constraints for these reasons.

REIFY DETERMINISM, measured manifestation (2026-09-01, task #5469 PRD2 γ): the SubProblem.auto_params HashSet axis-order leak documented on 2026-08-26 is NOT merely a latent BT5/D4 claim — it changes user-visible `reify eval` output the moment CpSatSolver occupies a registry slot. With CpSat wired into `logical` + a DiscreteFirstFallback in `fallback`, two consecutive runs of docs/prds/v0_6/fixtures/discrete_balance_lets.ri returned the two DIFFERENT balanced Bool configs, because CP-SAT's variable order IS ResolutionProblem.auto_params order and its search is fixed depth-first. DimensionalSolver was order-tolerant enough to hide it. FIX ADOPTED (5/5 runs bit-identical after): in SolverRegistry::solve_inner build sub_auto_params as `problem.auto_params.iter().filter(|ap| component.auto_params.contains(&ap.id)).cloned().collect()` — filter the caller's Vec rather than sort, because PRD2 §3 decision 10 specifies *declaration* order, and this mirrors the adjacent sub_dependent_cells discipline ("filter over the original slice, never a rebuild from a set"). It also makes the pre-existing `param_lookup` binding dead, which fails the workspace's -D warnings gate if left. A registry-level regression test CAN catch this in-process: each solve rebuilds the component HashSet with a fresh RandomState, so ~20 fresh ResolutionProblems suffice.

In reify, let-indirected auto constraints are dropped by FOUR one-hop-blind layers, not three: filter_constraints_reading_autos (engine_eval.rs:1415), decompose_into_components (decompose.rs:90), CP-SAT's forward-check (cpsat.rs:127-194, which never folds dependent_cells), and — the one usually missed — detect_underdetermined (engine_eval.rs:666). The fourth is what emits W_UNDERDETERMINED for a `let`-indirected auto; it runs OUTSIDE the has_active_solver gate and never reads the ResolutionProblem, so no solver-side fix clears it. Any task whose acceptance signal is "no W_UNDERDETERMINED" must fix detect_underdetermined explicitly.

DISCOVERY (2026-07-24 discrete-solve investigation): the reify let-tracing gap (constraints on let-cells that read autos silently disconnect) is THREE one-hop-blind layers, not one: (1) filter_constraints_reading_autos (crates/reify-eval/src/engine_eval.rs:1410) keeps a constraint only if its expr DIRECTLY reads an auto id — let-indirected constraints are dropped from ResolutionProblem before any solver runs (autos report "awaiting solve"); (2) decompose_into_components (crates/reify-constraints/src/decompose.rs) builds connectivity edges only from direct ValueRefs intersected with auto params; (3) no solver folds dependent_cells per trial — the task #5188 machinery (topo-ordered coupled non-auto cell list in ResolutionProblem.dependent_cells) is consumed ONLY by reify-eval's post-solve write-back (engine_eval.rs:4799/6250), never by DimensionalSolver residual eval or CpSat forward-check, and SolverRegistry::solve_inner passes dependent_cells: Vec::new() into every sub-problem. Fix is mechanical: transitive closure in (1)+(2) reusing build_dependent_cells, per-trial fold in both solvers, thread the field through the registry. Verified empirically: wiring CpSat does NOT fix the let variant (n2 probe still all-undef) — the gap is upstream of solver choice.

Reify solver-uniqueness reporting — the four measured wrongs (verified 2026-08-26 at main 2128c3692c by direct `reify eval` probe; fixtures landed at tests/prd-gate/fixtures/ssc_*.ri in commit d8bf51af15). The root cause of all four is one type error: `SolveResult::Solved.unique` is a BOOL, and a bool cannot distinguish proved-exactly-one / proved-two / found-one-and-proved-nothing / found-two / proved-none-exist.
(1) `auto(free)` with two genuine roots commits to one silently. finalise_uniqueness skips verification entirely for all-free problems and reports unique:false UNCONDITIONALLY, rendered as the code-less "Parameter `x` resolved via auto(free) -- result is not uniquely determined." from FIVE byte-identical sites (push_merged_cluster_nonunique_warnings + the cold arm in engine_eval.rs, the eval_cached arm, two arms in engine_edit.rs). DECISIVE EVIDENCE: ssc_two_roots_free.ri (two roots) and ssc_single_root_free.ri (ONE root) emit BYTE-IDENTICAL output — exit 0, length = 0.01 m, same warning. The signal carries no information. It also carries no DiagnosticCode (live INV-SF-6 violation), and for a merged cluster one cluster-wide flag is fanned out to every free auto, so it can name a parameter that is not the culprit.
(2) Strict `auto` with two genuine roots is reported as INFEASIBILITY, not multiplicity. finalise_uniqueness demotes the whole result to SolveResult::Infeasible with DiagnosticCode::ConstraintNonUnique and "strict auto parameter resolution is not uniquely determined — consider using auto(free) for exploration"; the cell goes undef with UndefCause::SolveFailed{detail:"infeasible"}. A model with TWO answers is told it has NONE, and neither root is ever named. So the gap is NOT "reify silently picks one" — reify NOTICES and then throws the information away.
(3) When the uniqueness probe fails to converge, verify_uniqueness returns TRUE ("conservatively assume unique") — conservative in the WRONG direction: it converts no evidence into a claim. And it is not a rare path: build_auto_param_list sets bounds:None UNCONDITIONALLY, so effective_bounds always degrades to default_bounds_for and the reflected anchor always lands outside any real bracket (#5711). Measured: ssc_ineq_bracketed_strict.ri (strict auto, 8mm <= L <= 40mm) resolves to 0.024 m with NO diagnostic at all.
(4) Two production drivers assert completeness they never computed: SolveSpaceSolver::solve hardcodes unique:true on every libslvs Ok arm (and it IS in SolverRegistry::production()'s Geometric slot), and relate_solve::solve_frame sets unique from LOCAL Jacobian rank. Neither ever reaches verify_uniqueness, which is private to solver.rs.
UNDERNEATH ALL FOUR: the alternatives are ALREADY COMPUTED and discarded. DimensionalSolver::solve_ranked_impl runs K = 2*(dim+1) starts and returns them ranked; both engine consumption seams call candidates.swap_remove(0) and drop candidates[1..]. RankedSolveResult/RankedCandidate appear in NO crate outside reify-ir/reify-constraints/reify-eval — no CLI, GUI or MCP surface has ever seen an alternative optimum. The candidates are also NOT deduplicated, so "K candidates" is not "K solutions".

DISCOVERY (jun7, red-team of Option A): a geometry-backed constraint that constrains an AUTO cell is a SILENT false-negative, NOT a statically detectable cycle. For `w = auto; part reads w; constraint fits_build_volume(bounding_box(part), build_vol)`, build_solver_problem (engine_eval.rs:603) filters constraints by extract_dependency_trace(c.expr).reads ∩ auto_ids — the constraint reads {part, build_vol}, NEVER the auto `w` (read by part's realization, not the constraint expr), so it is dropped from the solver. The only auto<->Resolution coupling is the runtime solver WRITE (engine_eval.rs:2422-2429), never a static read edge, so no Tarjan SCC over the static node graph can contain it. Therefore any "this loop is a static Resolution-involving SCC caught before solve" claim is structurally false for this class. The honest contract: compute a transitive auto-read closure (constraint.reads -> backing Realization -> that realization's reads, with the deps.rs:394 Boolean-operand drop fixed) and emit an E_EVAL_UNRESOLVED diagnostic declining to solve that class, preserving the no-hang guarantee. A pure legacy-vs-unified differential corpus will NOT surface this because legacy degrades identically. (Genuine geometry-in-the-loop solving would need a real fixpoint round, contradicting "one forward pass per scope.")

reify engine seam gotcha (measured 2026-08-30, task 6706): a solver mock's `unique: false` is OBSERVABLE at `Engine::eval` only when the model's auto is `auto(free)`, not strict `auto`. engine_eval.rs's per-template resolution arm emits "Parameter `X` resolved via auto(free) -- result is not uniquely determined." inside `if !unique { for ap in &problem.auto_params { if ap.free { ... } } }`, so under strict `auto` the flag reaches no diagnostic on that path and changes no resolved value. Consequence for tests: an engine-level test that means to pin "the engine does not derive/promote `unique`" is VACUOUS on a strict-`auto` fixture — verified by mutating the seam to `unique: candidate.unique || completeness.derived_unique(candidates.len())`, which the strict-`auto` fixture still passed and the `auto(free)` fixture reds on. Also note the ranked seam is entered only when `problem.objective.is_some()` (a `minimize`/`maximize` in the source); objective-less models take the `.solve()` path and never see `RankedSolveResult` at all. So an engine test targeting the ranked seam needs BOTH properties: an objective AND `auto(free)`.

Reify auto-param solver surface, probe-established 2026-08-26 (task #6631 carries the full evidence; probes preserved at ~/.claude/fleet/sessions/dogfood-reify-3312231/probes/): `reify eval` SOLVES autos — including a ctor-arg auto constrained EQUAL to a derived self.<sub>.<member> read (solved to ~1e-13), which means once realization consumes solved autos, the idiom `sub x = Leaf(length: auto)` + `constraint self.x.length == <derived cell>` replaces the whole #6586 pinned-literal workaround and re-solves on resize instead of failing pins. But TODAY no surface realizes solved geometry: `reify build`/`check` are deliberately solver-free (cmd_build comment, crates/reify-cli/src/main.rs ~:987 — provenance of that posture questioned by Leo, being investigated); the GUI realizes child DEFAULTS despite wiring SolverRegistry::production(); even eval-with-solver realizes the default body; and `reify check` reports the unresolved autos' indeterminate constraints as "No constraints violated" — a design whose autos silently failed GREENS the gate (same vacuity shape as #6592). Related live tasks: #5617 (instance-path write-back), #5388 (strict-auto multimodality), #5416 (capability envelope). Practical rule until #6631 moves: treat auto as an eval-layer calculator only; never trust check/build/GUI output of a design containing autos.

reify gotcha (measured 2026-10-13, task #6554): an objective that reads kernel geometry (e.g. `minimize volume(body)` in tests/prd-gate/fixtures/mwaste_coupled_bool.ri) is UNSCORABLE inside CP-SAT's solve_ranked, so it takes the nothing-scored fallback (feasibility decides) rather than a real argmin. Don't cite such a fixture as a 'unique argmin' case. Since #6554, a strict Bool auto there yields a ConstraintNonUnique Error naming both models on cold `reify eval` (rc 1), where it was a silent `wide = true` before.

REIFY DETERMINISM: the BT5 bit-identity claim in docs/prds/v0_6/whole-model-objective-coupling.md ("two reify eval runs produce bit-identical resolved values + identical RankedSolveResult candidate ordering") IS NOT ACTUALLY HELD on the production registry. Established 2026-08-26.

MECHANISM: decompose_into_components_with_reads (crates/reify-constraints/src/decompose.rs) carries SubProblem.auto_params as a HashSet<ValueCellId>, and SolverRegistry::solve_inner collects it into the Vec that becomes ResolutionProblem.auto_params — the solver's AXIS ORDER. im::HashMap/HashSet over std RandomState iterate differently PER INSTANCE, not merely per process (verified by EXECUTING a standalone program: three HashSets built from the same six keys, one process, one thread, iterated in three different orders). Axis order fixes the start-index-to-axis map in multistart_points, and start index is the multistart TIE-BREAK key, so two equal-scoring starts in different basins hand the win to whichever got the lower index. Separately component_map is an unsorted HashMap-derived Vec and solve_inner EARLY-RETURNS on the first failing component, so which diagnostic surfaces and which component receives the objective are both nondeterministic.

WHY THE EXISTING TESTS MISS IT: merged_cluster_auto_param_ordering_is_deterministic_across_runs uses a SPY solver; solve_ranked_multistart_is_deterministic_across_calls and multistart_points_is_deterministic_across_calls call DimensionalSolver DIRECTLY, bypassing SolverRegistry entirely. No test exercises the registry's own ordering.

THE HOUSE PATTERN ALREADY EXISTS ELSEWHERE and is the model for the fix, not new invention: resolve_order.rs (explicit sort_unstable, clusters.sort_by_key), engine_fixpoint.rs (a BTreeSet<DebugOrd> ready set described in-source as "the SINGLE source of determinism ... so no HashMap iteration order ever leaks"), engine_constraints.rs (BTreeMap bucketing with an original-index weave). decompose.rs and engine_edit.rs simply do not follow it. ValueCellId already implements Ord, so the sort key exists.

ALSO: the `#deterministic` MODULE PRAGMA IS A DEAD FLAG — apply_deterministic_pragma (crates/reify-compiler/src/module_pragmas.rs) sets module.deterministic and NOTHING READS IT. It is named as the cross-machine reproducibility escape hatch in docs/prds/v0_3/structural-analysis-fea.md, so that escape hatch does not currently exist.

reify CP-SAT gotcha (crates/reify-constraints/src/cpsat.rs backtrack_all): do NOT assume a dependent cell whose autos are not all assigned evaluates to Undef. reify-expr's And/Or/Implies are Kleene with short-circuit (eval_and in reify-expr/src/lib.rs returns Bool(false) as soon as its left operand is false; kleene_and(_, False) = False). So a partial fold can yield a DEFINED, sound Bool, and CP-SAT's forward-check uses it to prune at shallow depths. Removing or skipping not-yet-exact cells to save fold work forfeits that pruning; a let-conjunction over n Bool autos goes from ~2n nodes to ~2^(n+1). The safe saving is to skip cells whose autos were ALL assigned at a shallower depth (task #6967, esc-6967-5). Arithmetic and comparisons, by contrast, propagate Undef strictly.

REIFY SOLVER WIRING GOTCHA (verified 2026-08-26): `SolverRegistry::production()` and a bare `Box::new(DimensionalSolver)` ARE NOT INTERCHANGEABLE — they behave differently on an `auto` that NO CONSTRAINT TOUCHES.

- SolverRegistry::production(): decompose_into_components_with_reads DROPS the untouched auto, solve_inner returns Solved{values:{}} (an EMPTY map), and the engine's write-back loop only writes ids present in that map — so the cell stays Undef.
- A bare DimensionalSolver: build_solved_values covers ALL auto_params, the residual folds to 0.0, and the `initially_feasible && objective.is_none()` early return hands back the SEED value — so the cell resolves.

Measured consequence: seven currently-passing reify-cli tests depend on the REGISTRY behaviour (check_strict_purpose_indeterminate_exits_failure, check_underdetermined_free_param_exits_success_with_warning, the four cli_purpose_stdlib determinacy tests, check_integration_full_v01_succeeds) and would break under a bare solver. Wiring the wrong one roughly DOUBLES the blast radius of the build/check solver flip.

The correct production wiring line is:
  engine.with_solver(Box::new(reify_constraints::SolverRegistry::production()))
and NOT by reusing configured_eval_engine, which additionally attaches the persistent cache — a STALENESS choice a driver must make deliberately rather than inherit.

RELATED FIXTURE-AUTHORING RULE, same measurement: a `.ri` fixture intended to stay unresolvable under `--strict` must contain ZERO `auto` params. An undef-operand constraint that ALSO reads an auto poisons the solve — comparison_residual's `_ => 1.0` fallback arm is a flat residual far above FEASIBILITY_THRESHOLD = 1e-12, so the component is declared Infeasible and emits Severity::Error, flipping `reify build` to exit 1. With no autos, filter_constraints_reading_autos removes the constraint from the problem entirely and build's exit-0 contract is preserved.

Reify solver honesty vocabulary — what exists, and the two naming collisions that will bite a PRD in this area (verified 2026-08-26 at main 2128c3692c).

EXISTS. `reify_ir::ranked::OptimalityStatus` = ProvenOptimal | BestFound{reason: BestFoundReason} | FeasibilityOnly; BestFoundReason = IterationLimit | ConvergedWithinBudget | Unreported. Invariant I3 reserves ProvenOptimal for a real proof. Its ONLY construction site is CpSatSolver::solve_ranked_with_budget when `complete` — and CpSat is NOT in SolverRegistry::production() (logical slot None), so **ProvenOptimal is unreachable in production today**. `FeasibilityOnly` says nothing about HOW MANY feasible points exist — that is the orthogonal hole. `W_SOLVER_OPTIMALITY_UNPROVEN` is shipped and fires from reify eval/check, gated on a variant match against BestFoundReason::IterationLimit. `cpsat::SolveAllResult` = Enumerated{solutions, complete} | NotEnumerable{reason} is the repo's ONLY explicit "did I exhaust the space" flag, and its doc is the cleanest existing statement of the doctrine: an empty set with complete:true is a PROOF of unsatisfiability, an empty set with complete:false proves nothing, and every honesty claim is CONJOINED with the flag rather than asserted.

ABSENT. No SolveStatus / ConstraintStatus / Verdict type exists. No interval arithmetic, contractor, box consistency, HC4 or branch-and-bound anywhere in crates/ (`DerivedInterval`/`derive_param_intervals` is a one-pass syntactic bound miner over four linear-in-one-auto shapes with a constant far side; Eq, Ne, Or and every nonlinear or multi-auto shape are silently skipped). `DeterminacyState` has NO "locally unique / globally unverified" state — every solved auto is written `Determined` regardless of `unique`. No CLI surface reports more than one solution: no `reify solve` subcommand, and zero flags matching rank/ranked/solutions/enumerate/optimal/uniqueness. `reify explain` prints per-cell objective provenance and carries NO optimality, uniqueness, solver-identity or completeness token — it is the natural, already-shipped home for a solve-quality field.

COLLISION 1 — "cluster". `whole-model-objective-coupling.md` and its landed leaf #5016 use "cluster" for a coupled SCOPE SCC, and its "NM + clustering + deterministic multistart" is best-of-K over merged SCOPES, not basins. A multimodality PRD's basin clustering is a DIFFERENT thing; do not reuse the word.

COLLISION 2 — "strict". `reify check --strict` means "treat unevaluated as failure", NOT "require a unique solution". It produces IDENTICAL output for a uniquely-solvable design, a genuinely bimodal one, an infeasible one and a fully determined one, because `check` never solves at all — the "indeterminate" it flags is check's own refusal to run the solver.

Determinism is a HARD house constraint, not a preference: whole-model-objective-coupling.md §3 decision 2 chose a fixed deterministic start set with no RNG, no clock and no seed, and explicitly declined to take on a seeded global optimiser's determinism obligations. Any new multistart must be deterministic too.

Reify .ri gotcha (measured 2026-10-07, post-#5469): a `param b : Bool = auto(free)` with NO constraint reading it (directly or via a `let`) is never solved. `reify eval` exits 0 with b undef and a note "b awaiting solve", and no W_UNDERDETERMINED (that warning fires only for STRICT `auto`). Any constraint over the let-mapped value brings b into the solve, even a tautology like `constraint s * s == 1` for `let s = if b then 1.0 else -1.0`. CP-SAT then resolves it exactly; a discriminating constraint such as `s < 0` pins the alternative.

Tests cover underdetermined resolution with mock/real solvers, strict auto infeasibility, per-param warning diagnostics, unique-flag suppression, mixed free/strict filtering, tight-range narrowing, near-equality pinning, minimize objectives with/without upper bounds, snapshot determinacy state, and dependent let-binding re-evaluation

In reify-constraints, the canonical source for the strict-`auto` §11.6 uniqueness contract is `verify_uniqueness`'s doc comment in crates/reify-constraints/src/solver.rs (task #5711). It records the four-branch `classify_uniqueness` rule, the per-fixture measurement table for the six fixtures the #5618 derived-anchor box flips, the A/B evidence table for the γ `cost_robustness_tradeoff` path, and two explicit "Do NOT" guards whose violations were each MEASURED to silently break a fixture: do not add `.or(build_centrality_objective(..))` to the objective scoring (the synthetic centrality objective's better score elsewhere is evidence FOR non-uniqueness, and wiring it in flips `strict_auto_non_unique_returns_infeasible` to a false `Solved`), and do not simplify the γ branch to a blanket `return true` (measured to turn a loud `ConstraintNonUnique` into a silent `thickness = 10 m`, i.e. `default_bounds_for`'s Length ceiling). Read that doc before touching uniqueness, the perturbation anchor box, or the `floor_applied` clamp gate in `solve_core_with_sd_tolerance`.

reify silent-wrong-answer baseline (2026-10-10, fixture tests/prd-gate/fixtures/mwaste_coupled_bool.ri): when a FINITE auto (Bool) drives geometry that a `minimize volume(body)` objective reads, CP-SAT's solve_ranked finds the objective unscorable (geometry is Undef inside the solver) and returns its FIRST enumerated model as feasibility-only. `wide = true` (the LARGER volume) is resolved with exit 0 and zero diagnostics for a strict auto; auto(free) gets only the generic not-uniquely-determined warning. A CONTINUOUS auto in the same shape instead gives NoProgress 'objective expression evaluated to undefined' and undef (mwaste_coupled_continuous.ri). M-WASTE α fixes both via a classification pass.

Measured 2026-10-01 at main 107171c475 (after PRD2 γ #5469): `reify eval` routes an all-Bool component to CP-SAT and honours `minimize`/`maximize` end to end (discrete_balance_min.ri flips its config when the objective flips). A Bool auto sharing a component with a continuous auto still falls through to DimensionalSolver and fails with "constraints could not be satisfied (max absolute residual: 1.00e0)" until ζ #5472. A STRICT `auto` Bool with two feasible models resolves silently to the first model with no non-unique diagnostic; that is owned by #6554. Gotcha for scratch probes: a .ri's `module` name must equal its file basename, or eval fails with E_MODULE_PATH_MISMATCH.

Architecture fact (reify auto-type-param resolution, confirmed jun9-2026): the v0.3 completion lands incrementally-safe because β/γ/δ are behavioural no-ops on the stub path. The real SimpleConstraintChecker (reify-constraints/src/lib.rs:47) cannot be constructed inside reify-compiler (no dep on reify-constraints — a prod edge would cycle since constraints dev-deps compiler) or reify-eval prod (reify-constraints is dev-dep only, reify-eval/Cargo.toml:64); it's injected as &dyn ConstraintChecker from the top-level binary (gui/src-tauri/src/main.rs:651 constructs it). The default is the kept stub CompileTimeIndeterminateChecker (auto_type_param_phase.rs:52-66) which returns Indeterminate(=feasible) for every constraint. So per-candidate ValueMaps (β) change no verdict, the BFS joint-recheck (γ) never finds a Violated, and a module without auto: or compiled with the stub is byte-identical to pre-PRD main. The real checker is opt-in PER-CALL-SITE: only the structure sub-component resolution path uses it; enum (generic-data-carrying-enums 4031) and fn-generics (generic-user-functions, uses type erasure D1) consumers of the shared resolver keep the stub. Also: EvaluationGraph::from_templates (reify-eval/src/graph.rs:278) inserts one shared template per name and find_template (reify-compiler/src/types.rs:789, called graph.rs:365) looks up by structure_name ignoring type_args — which is WHY monomorphization (α) must synthesize a per-(name,type-args) clone name (e.g. Bearing$GasketSeal) and rewrite SubComponentDecl.structure_name to it.

content: reify gotcha (discrete uniqueness rules): deciding "is a STRICT auto determined?" by comparing the first few FULL solver models is order-dependent whenever strict and auto(free) params share a component — the leading models can differ only on a free auto while a later model contradicts the strict one (e.g. strict a declared before free b with `a or b`: DFS yields (T,T),(T,F) before (F,T)). Compare STRICT PROJECTIONS and look past the prefix (first witness + first later witness with a different strict projection, or a nogood-pruned probe); the same blind spot hits any top-N carrier (CP-SAT RANKED_CANDIDATE_CAP=16) that evicts tied models. Found in review of task 6554's cpsat.rs strict-auto rule.

Completed: Treat an empty INTAKE_PUBLIC_URL or INTAKE_DATA_DIR as unset, and refuse a public URL without a scheme and host (cli.py)
Description: Found while planning task 9 (follow-up id agent-followup-9); read in the code, not reproduced. src/scoping_intake/cli.py reads two settings with os.environ.get(name, default). After task 9 these reads are environment.get inside sites_for and _data_dir. A variable that is set but empty, such as a blank `INTAKE_PUBLIC_URL=` line in an env file, is used as a value, not as unset:

(1) INTAKE_PUBLIC_URL="" makes the public URL "", and urlsplit("").netloc is "", so "" joins the prospect site's Host allow-list. web.py's check, `self.headers.get("Host", "") in site.hosts`, then answers a request that sends no Host header, and the operator page offers a relative private link ("/s/<token>"). A value with no scheme, such as "intake.example", has the same effect, because urlsplit puts it in the path and leaves the netloc empty.
(2) INTAKE_DATA_DIR="" gives Path(""), which is the current working directory, so session data would be written under ./sessions wherever serve, calibration or purge is run. That breaks the briefing's rule that session data lives outside every git repository. The deploy unit sets the variable explicitly, so the installed service is not affected.

candidates.content: Gotcha (solar_challenge): config.load_fleet_config() returns HomeConfigs with seg_tariff=None even when the scenario YAML has a top-level `seg:` block. The finance CLI attaches SEG afterwards with dataclasses.replace (cli/finance.py:161-169), and project_multi_year reconciles it. Any CLI command or ad-hoc fleet measurement that needs SEG-priced export must do the same: parse the `seg:` block, then dataclasses.replace(home, seg_tariff=SEGTariff(...)) on each home before simulate_fleet/simulate_home. Otherwise export revenue is 0 and a UserWarning fires. Task 185 tracks `fleet run` ignoring the block; task 186 tracks collapsing the duplicated finance/optimize loading blocks.

In solar_challenge, `load_fleet_config` (config.py) historically does NOT thread scenario-level pricing onto `fleet_distribution` homes: SEG is threaded post-load in cli/finance.py:114, and each distribution home's `tariff_config` was hardcoded `None` (config.py:1579) until task #53 (W1 β). `generate_homes_from_distribution` builds each HomeConfig/BatteryConfig fresh in a loop, so new per-home config is best passed via keyword-only params (e.g. `*, fleet_tariff=None, fleet_grid_charging=None`) and applied by direct construction — keeping the four existing 2-positional-arg callers (load_fleet_config, cli/fleet.py sweep x2, web/api.py) bit-identical. The canonical θ calibration scenario scenarios/bristol-fin-calibration.yaml has NO top-level `tariff:` and no battery.grid_charging, so any fleet-pricing change must default to None to stay calibration-safe.

No FleetResults is needed, and each run takes well under a second. The CliRunner result tells three outcomes apart:
- result.exception is the sentinel: the command reached simulation; optimize's first call is asked for the sweep's SimulationPeriod timestamps.
- result.exception is SystemExit(1): handle_errors refused, and its "Configuration error: ..." text is in result.output, stderr included.
- result.exception is a raw exception such as AttributeError: an unhandled crash.

tests/api/conftest.py is a MODULE-scoped HTTP harness (introduced by the consent/task-13 work): db_engine (StaticPool in-mem SQLite) seeds Customers A/B + their CUSTOMER Users + one ADMIN User and COMMITS; app_client is a module-scoped TestClient over create_app() with get_session+get_settings overridden; auth_headers mints a Bearer header for ANY (user_id, role, customer_id) via JwtAuthProvider.issue_token. Two gotchas for new tests/api tests: (1) auth is STATELESS — current_principal decodes claims and never re-fetches the User row, so you can mint admin/operator/customer tokens with arbitrary UUIDs without seeding User rows.
