Ordered by operational severity, highest first. The first two are correctness-of-ACTION bugs in an operator console - they can make a click act on the wrong record - and should be treated as the real content of this task; the last three are latent or housekeeping.

1. tab_escalations.jsx renders rows with a null React key.
   Live console error on the Escalations tab: 'Each child in a list should have a unique "key" prop ... Check the render method of EscalationsTab ... at tr'. The code says `<tr key={row.id}>`, so the cause is the DATA: 2 of 300 escalation rows in the live payload carry `id: null` (one from /home/leo/src/dark-factory, one from /home/leo/src/reify). Those rows fall back to index keys, so a reorder between polls can hand the row click handler a different row than the one clicked. Fix needs a decision on both ends: why the server emits a null escalation id, and a stable client-side fallback key that does not collide.

2. findEscalationRow returns the first cross-project match.
   tab_escalations.jsx::findEscalationRow searches every subsection and returns the first hit, but escalation ids are only unique WITHIN a project. The live payload has esc-3169-1, esc-7603-1, esc-652-1 and roughly 20 others appearing in two different project subsections. A cross-tab focus link (e.g. from tab_memory_evals.jsx) can therefore open the wrong project's escalation. The lookup key must be (project, escalation_id), not escalation_id alone.

3. tabs.jsx::ChipList calls hooks conditionally.
   `persistKey ? usePersistedState(persistKey, false) : uS(false)` - two hooks on one branch, one on the other. Harmless today only because persistKey happens to be stable per instance. The first caller that makes persistKey conditional gets a 'Rendered fewer hooks than expected' crash. Call the hook unconditionally and branch on the value instead.

4. __DF_PAUSE does not suppress chip-driven refreshes.
   Only data.js::pollTick consults window.__DF_PAUSE. app.jsx's `uE(() => window.DF_REFRESH(win), [win])` calls refreshDFData directly, bypassing the check. Measured: with __DF_PAUSE = true, six window-chip clicks produced two extra full 14-endpoint refreshes. 'Pause live' should mean paused.

5. Unbounded, never-pruned localStorage keys.
   tabs.jsx::usePersistedState (via ::ChipList, ::DepsCell, ::LocksCell) writes one `df.deps.<task_id>` and one `df.locks.<task_id>` key per task row rendered, on MOUNT as well as on change, and never prunes them. QuotaExceededError is swallowed by a bare `catch (e) {}`, so the failure mode is silent loss of every persisted UI preference. Completed: Poll only the ACTIVE tab's endpoints, using the TAB_ENDPOINTS map that already exists
Description: data.js fetches all 14 dashboard endpoints every 3000ms regardless of which tab is open, but only ONE tab is ever mounted: app.jsx's renderTab() is a switch returning a single component, and the body wrapper carries key={tab} so a tab change tears the old subtree down entirely. So the dashboard continuously fetches and parses data for twelve tabs nobody is looking at.

The mapping needed to fix this ALREADY EXISTS and is already maintained. endpoint_staleness.js::TAB_ENDPOINTS maps every tab id to the endpoints that tab actually consumes, and endpoint_staleness.test.mjs machine-checks BOTH directions - every path is a real endpointsFor() key, and every app.jsx tab id has an entry - precisely so it cannot silently drift. It says, for example, scheduler maps to a single endpoint.

Concrete saving, from live measurement 2026-09-23: sitting on the Scheduler tab currently costs about 22 MB per poll cycle across 14 endpoints; that tab needs /api/v2/dashboard/scheduler alone, 3.1 MB. The server-side cost is the real prize - 99.4% of each endpoint's wall clock is the server building the payload via MCP fan-out across 9 project roots (tasks: ttfb 3.886s of 3.910s total), on the same host as the orchestrator fleet.

So today /api/v2/dashboard/tasks - the single most expensive endpoint - is required on every tab just to render one number in a badge. Scoping the poll set without first giving the rail a cheap counts source would either blank the badges or keep the expensive endpoint polling everywhere, which forfeits most of the win.

That is what the dependency on task 5587 is for: its task snapshot unit is the natural cheap source. get_statuses (a compact id-to-status map, roughly 95% smaller than get_tasks) is the other candidate.

Completed: Consolidate the five near-duplicate known-project-roots walks in the dashboard
Description: Discovered while planning task 5586 (the dashboard app.py handler/loop extraction, PRD plans/dashboard-one-datum-one-path-prd.md leaf alpha2); explicitly OUT OF SCOPE there because 5586 is a no-behaviour-change mechanical move and this is a logic change.

The dashboard has FIVE independent implementations of the same walk — "primary config.project_root first, then config.known_project_roots, de-duplicated" — each re-spelling the `seen: set[Path] = {config.project_root}` idiom:

1. dashboard/src/dashboard/app.py::_project_scoped_dbs (lines 1274-1286 as of base c11a958300)
2. dashboard/src/dashboard/app.py::_project_scoped_dbs_labeled (1289-1301) — same walk, returns (str(root), conn) pairs
3. dashboard/src/dashboard/app.py::_performance_resources (1312-1326) — same walk, hand-builds root/'data'/'orchestrator'/'runs.db' and root/'data'/'escalations' instead of taking a rel_path
4. dashboard/src/dashboard/app.py::_analytics_project_dirs (2341-2361) — same walk, returns (root.name, escalations_dir, runs_db) triples; its own docstring says it "Mirrors build_escalation_queues' primary-first, de-duped root iteration"
5. dashboard/src/dashboard/data/active_tasks.py::_all_project_roots — the same enumeration for the task fan-out

and dashboard/src/dashboard/data/escalations.py::build_escalation_queues does the iteration a sixth time (per item 4's own docstring). This is a SPOT violation (docs/code-quality.md heuristic 11) with a real failure mode: a change to root resolution — a new env override, a different de-dupe key, an ordering fix — has to be found and applied in five or six places, and a missed one diverges silently because each site returns a different shape.

NOTE ON LOCATION: task 5586 moves items 1 and 2 (plus _cost_dbs and _burndown_dbs) into a new dashboard/src/dashboard/project_dbs.py, and leaves items 3 and 4 in app.py. Re-read the tree before planning — do not assume the line numbers above. Also check whether PRD leaves beta/eta (which rework data/active_tasks.py, data/tasks.py and data/escalations.py) have already collapsed item 5 or 6; if so, scope this to whatever remains.

Suggested shape: ONE root enumerator returning the ordered, de-duped roots, with the per-consumer path/label derivation layered on top as thin mappers — i.e. separate "which roots" (one implementation) from "what do I want per root" (per-consumer), rather than five copies of both fused together. Heuristic 3 (orthogonal dimensions of variability) is the argument for that split.

Do this AFTER PRD plans/dashboard-one-datum-one-path-prd.md has landed, or at least after its beta and eta leaves: those rework the same call sites and an early refactor would collide with their lock sets. No escalation was filed for this — it is a latent quality issue, not a defect with an observable symptom.
Analysis: REVALIDATED 2026-10-15 against base 344897b905 (main tip). Since the original base 8b7210c220, main changed only api/invariants.py, data/active_tasks.py, data/escalation_corpus.py, test_active_tasks.py and test_app.py among this plan's files, and none of those changes touches the root walk:
- api/invariants.py (task 4679) now also reads the escalation corpus via corpus_queues(config) / acquire_corpus (module-level TTL cache keyed on the queue tuple) and still enumerates roots with project_dbs.project_roots(config). The step-3 invariants contract case now clears that cache, mirroring test_api_invariants.py's autouse fixture.
- data/active_tasks.py (task 5761) deleted collect_active_tasks; _all_project_roots, project_roots_for_label, _rotated_project_roots and collect_tasks_with_counts are unchanged.
- data/escalation_corpus.py added PendingEscalations / pending_escalation_ids; corpus_queues still re-spells the walk with an inline dict.fromkeys.
- test_app.py: only docstring edits. The six patch('dashboard.api.tasks._all_project_roots') sites remain at ~530, 569, 645, 771, 979, 2487.

Tasks 6722 (kappa) has not landed: app.py still spells root / 'data' / 'orchestrator' / 'runs.db'.

ORIGINAL ANALYSIS (still accurate). The task text predates PRD leaves alpha2 (5586), beta/eta and task 4670, so its five-item list is stale:
- Items 1+2 (_project_scoped_dbs / _project_scoped_dbs_labeled) moved to dashboard/src/dashboard/project_dbs.py (5586). Task 4670 then added project_dbs.py::project_roots(config) = list(dict.fromkeys([config.project_root, *config.known_project_roots])) and rebuilt both helpers on it. The project_dbs module docstring says it is "the canonical home ... but not yet its only copy" and names the remaining hand-rolled sites.
- Item 4 (app.py::_analytics_project_dirs) is GONE: the escalation-corpus leaf replaced it with data/escalation_corpus.py::corpus_queues, which re-spells the walk a third way (dict.fromkeys inline).
- Item 6 (data/escalations.py::build_escalation_queues) no longer walks roots at all: it iterates corpus scans. Nothing to do there.
- Item 3 app.py::_performance_resources (~line 908) still hand-rolls `seen: set[Path] = {config.project_root}`.
- Item 5 data/active_tasks.py::_all_project_roots (line 251) still hand-rolls the same idiom. It is imported privately by api/tasks.py (terminal-window label lookup + total_roots) and data/scheduler.py (roots_to_query), and feeds project_roots_for_label, _rotated_project_roots and collect_tasks_with_counts. test_app.py patches it by dotted path at six sites, listed as a private_patch_target in plans/quality-metrics/review-all-dark_factory-20261008.json.
- Sites the task did not list: data/metrics.py::fan_out_list_tickets (~line 102, str-keyed seen-set), api/orchestrators.py (line 49, un-deduped [project_root, *known] fed to shape_orchestrators, which de-dupes itself), and DashboardConfig.__post_init__ (un-deduped list fed to _discover_escalation_urls, so a duplicated root is probed and WARNed about twice).
- NOT this walk: data/burndown.py::collect_snapshot and data/metrics.py::_sample_orchestrators walk a different population (primary, then live-orchestrator-discovered roots, then known roots). Out of scope.

APPROACH (heuristic 3: separate "which roots" from "what per root"). Put the ONE enumerator on DashboardConfig as a read-only property `all_project_roots -> tuple[Path, ...]` = tuple(dict.fromkeys((self.project_root, *self.known_project_roots))). It lives beside __post_init__, whose symlink canonicalisation is the premise the de-dupe depends on (heuristics 10/11). Every consumer already holds a DashboardConfig and imports dashboard.config, so no new import edge is created; homing it in project_dbs instead would make data/* import a module above them (project_dbs imports data.db), heuristic 13. Delete project_dbs.project_roots and active_tasks._all_project_roots outright: no re-export shim. Every consumer becomes a thin per-root mapper over config.all_project_roots. Per-root PATH spellings (data/orchestrator/runs.db, data/escalations) are a different axis owned by pending task 6722 (S14 kappa), so they are kept verbatim here.

The only observable behaviour change is that escalation-URL discovery probes, and WARNs about, each distinct root once. Everything else is a pure refactor, and its RED test is a contract test: a DashboardConfig subclass whose all_project_roots answers a different policy (reversed), handed to each consumer through its ordinary config parameter. A consumer that still hand-rolls primary-first fails. That is the executable form of the SPOT claim and uses no private patching. test_app.py's six private patches move to the public seam, installing a config naming the roots on client.app.state.config (the swap pattern loops.py::_metrics_loop documents ~25 tests rely on).

PRD GATE: the escalation corpus (decision 13) and the api/ + project_dbs extraction (5586) have both landed. Pending tasks 5760 and 6722 overlap some files at lock level only, with no semantic conflict.
Key decisions: The single root enumerator is a read-only property on DashboardConfig (config.py). It is not project_dbs.project_roots, and not a new module.; Name it all_project_roots, returning tuple[Path, ...].; Per-root path spellings (data/orchestrator/runs.db, data/escalations) are left verbatim; this task changes only WHICH roots are walked.

candidates.content: In reify, a bash helper that allocates a temp file/dir and registers it in a caller-scoped cleanup array (`_TMPFILES+=("$f")`) silently leaks when the helper is invoked through command substitution (`f="$(_scan_file ...)"`), because the substitution runs in a subshell and the array append mutates a copy that dies with it — the EXIT trap then always sees an empty array. Measured 32 leaked entries per run of tests/infra/test_cited_test_paths_resolve.sh before the fix. Allocate everything under ONE run-private `mktemp -d` and `rm -rf` just that directory in the trap; this removes the failure mode by construction instead of requiring every helper to register correctly. Same subshell hazard test_helpers.sh documents for assert() (esc-4959-57).

In reify's tests/infra bash suites, a helper called as `X="$(make_helper ...)"` runs its body in a command-substitution SUBSHELL, so any `_TMPDIRS+=("$dir")` registration inside it is silently discarded and the dir leaks. Anchor cleanup on a single per-run root dir mktemp'd and registered in `_TMPDIRS` once in the main shell (the helper then mktemps beneath it), or make the helper an out-param (`printf -v "$1"`) that runs in the current shell.

Reify shell test suites leak /tmp fixtures in three distinct shapes, and only the third was previously documented. (1) NEVER REGISTERED: a mktemp'd var missing from a hand-maintained cleanup enumeration (test_reify_audit_ptodo.sh's cleanup_all listed 10 vars but not FIX_F/FIX_F2). (2) TRAP REPLACEMENT: N successive `trap ... EXIT` registrations in one file — bash EXIT traps do NOT stack, so each replaces the previous and only the last temp is ever removed (test_setup_worktree_debug_port.sh had 10 mktemps and 10 traps, leaking 9 per run). (3) SUBSHELL REGISTRATION DISCARDED: a factory doing `dir=$(mktemp -d); _TMPDIRS+=("$dir")` invoked via `$(...)`, so the append dies with the subshell (test_main_gate_worktree_config.sh, 7 leaks/run). All three leak on a fully GREEN run. Fix for all three is the same: ONE parent-registered root plus a single EXIT trap, per tests/infra/test_git_rerere_guard.sh.

reify tests/infra gotcha: making a test_*.sh sourceable exposes its fixture helpers to callers that never built a fixture, and `git -C ""` resolves to the CURRENT directory. A sourced helper like test_verify_scope.sh's plan_for (`git -C "$FIX" add ...; git -C "$FIX" reset -q -- .`) with an empty FIX would silently unstage the caller's own index, and plan_for_branch would checkout -b/commit/branch -D in the caller's real worktree. `set -u` catches only an UNSET var, not an empty or wrong one. Guard each helper by checking that the fixture path is one the suite's constructors registered (e.g. membership in _TMPDIRS) before any git call (task 8476 plan).

In tests/infra shell suites, a `_TMPDIRS+=("$dir")` inside a factory function is only a leak when that function is invoked via a SUBSHELL — `x="$(fn)"`, backticks, `<<< "$(fn)"`, or a pipeline. A grep for `_TMPDIRS+=` inside function bodies is NOT evidence of a leak: an audit of all 166 tests/infra/*.sh (task 6293, 2026-08-20) found 23 of 25 grep-flagged files were false positives — factories called as plain statements, main-shell-only helpers whose only apparent `$(fn)` site is inside a comment warning against it, bodies already rooted under $_LANE_ROOT via make_isolated_lane, and a `printf -v` write-back helper whose single subshell call site returns before mktemp. The canonical safe idiom in this tree is to root every throwaway path under ONE parent-shell-registered variable — either `mktemp -p "$WORKDIR"` with WORKDIR registered at top level (test_cpu_admit.sh), or the test_helpers.sh init/make split (init_isolated_lane_root + make_isolated_lane) where the factory registers nothing at all.

Reify tests/infra convention for a test that must temporarily replace a REAL repo file (not a fixture): never back it up inside the tracked source tree. tree-sitter-reify/.gitignore covers src/parser.c but NOT src/*.bak, so an in-tree `parser.c.bak` is untracked-and-not-ignored (`git check-ignore -v` exits 1) and the lane cleanliness guards, warm-lane-audit and scripts/land.sh all read `git status --porcelain` as a dirty worktree for the test's whole duration. Correct shape (both call sites in tests/infra/test_tree_sitter_pipeline.sh use it as of task 5629): `bakdir=$(mktemp -d) || return 1`; register CLEANUP_ACTIONS BEFORE the copy so an interrupt in the gap leaks nothing; register the restore AHEAD of the bakdir `rm -rf` because cleanup replays in insertion order; restore with atomic self-consuming `mv -f`, never cp+rm — a failed cp-restore that still runs `rm -f` destroys the only copy. Always append `|| return 1` to the backup copy: set -e is DISABLED inside test bodies (the runner invokes them as `if "$t"; then`), so an unchecked cp fails silently and the subsequent `rm -f` deletes the original with no usable copy.

The /tmp fixture EXIT-trap cleanup reference implementation is tests/infra/test_git_rerere_guard.sh, and it uses an INLINE triple — `_TMPDIRS=()` + `cleanup()` + `trap cleanup EXIT` with every fixture rooted under one parent-registered `_SUITE_TMP="$(mktemp -d)"` — NOT shared helper functions. Task descriptions in this cleanup cluster (e.g. 7218) name `init_suite_tmp_root`/`make_suite_tmpdir`/`make_suite_tmpfile` in tests/infra/test_helpers.sh as though they already exist; as of 2026-09-14 they exist in no ref (`git log --all -S` returns nothing) and are unbuilt deliverables of still-pending task 6606, alongside tests/infra/tmp-fixture-cleanup-baseline.txt and tests/infra/test_tmp_fixture_cleanup_guard.sh. Verify these three before planning any suite in this cluster.

To measure whether a reify shell test suite leaks /tmp fixtures, run it with a private TMPDIR and count the residue: `T=$(mktemp -d); TMPDIR="$T" bash tests/infra/<suite>.sh; ls -A "$T" | wc -l; rm -rf "$T"`. mktemp honours $TMPDIR, so this captures the suite's own leaks exactly. Never measure against the real /tmp — it is shared across ~253 warm lanes and was measured drifting by 4 entries during a single suite run, which makes any real-/tmp assertion flaky and liable to red for another lane's defect.

reify tests/infra — MEASURED 2026-09-14 (task 7209, git 2.43.0, throwaway mktemp dirs): `git init` is ALSO redirected by a poisoned repo environment, and it fails SILENTLY. Under `GIT_DIR=<other>/.git`, BOTH fixture-construction forms — `git -C "$FIX" init -q` and the path-arg `git init -q "$FIX"` — leave `$FIX/.git` ABSENT and instead re-run init against the repository GIT_DIR names, rewriting its config. That is the `bare = true`-into-the-shared-config half of esc-7106-1 (memory 0afa9fa5 covers the complementary `git add` -> real-index corruption via the hook-exported RELATIVE GIT_INDEX_FILE). Consequence when diagnosing: a fixture test failing with "not a git repository" or an empty `ls-files` is the expected symptom of an unscrubbed `init`, not a broken fixture — GIT_INDEX_FILE does NOT affect init, GIT_DIR does, so the two verbs fail in visibly different ways. Correct route for a fixture call is `fixture_git` from tests/infra/test_helpers.sh (one-line delegation to `reify_git_env_scrub`); never hand-write an `env -u` list — the two pre-7209 precedents named only 4 and 3 of the canonical 8 vars. For scrubbing a SUITE'S OWN shell rather than a child command see memory 46d8f890 (including its exported-source-guard trap, which also bites any file that sources scripts/lib_git_env_scrub.sh to define a wrapper). The regex `(^|[^_[:alnum:]])git( +-[^ ]+( +[^ ]+)?)* +init` is the census form that finds raw sites while structurally exempting `_fixture_git`/`_clean_git`/`fixture_git` wrappers.

tests/infra harness gotcha (task 5629): any suite that PATH-stubs cargo and then executes scripts/verify.sh must also export REIFY_TS_FRESHNESS_TARGET_DIR at a per-run tmpdir, alongside the REIFY_PSI_GATE_DISABLE / REIFY_COMPILE_GATE_DISABLE knobs. verify.sh emits scripts/tree-sitter-freshness.sh `ensure` before the cargo wave and `check` after it; with cargo stubbed nothing is ever compiled, so against the real ./target (a) `check` asserts its post-condition over archives the run never built — measured RED "STALE — the archive cargo will link was NOT built from the sources now on disk", failing the suite wholesale, and (b) `ensure`'s repair path bumps mtimes on the worktree's TRACKED tree-sitter sources (grammar.js, src/scanner.c, src/tree_sitter/*.h), which in a CoW-seeded warm lane is precisely the rebuild signal that mechanism reads. An empty target dir scans as TS_SCAN_STATUS=none and returns BEFORE ts_force_touch, so both leaves degrade to clean no-ops ("no built archive under <dir>; nothing to force/check", exit 0) — note the corollary that a throwaway target dir also means `ensure` performs NO repair, so never use one in a cleanup path that is supposed to leave the real archive scheduled for recompile. Fix HARNESS-side only: verify.sh cannot distinguish a stubbed cargo from a real one, so relaxing `check` or special-casing REIFY_INFRA_SUITE_ACTIVE inside the guard would weaken the post-condition that closes the stale-archive false-GREEN class in the real merge gate. Canonical implementation: apply_hermetic_env in tests/infra/test_verify_semaphore_e2e.sh; pinned from the guard's side by test_freshness_target_dir_override_is_a_clean_noop and test_semaphore_e2e_harness_isolates_the_freshness_guard in tests/infra/test_tree_sitter_pipeline.sh. Extends the base hermetic-execute recipe in memory de69b397-6229-44b4-858e-dff6e66ccb2b.

Bash gotcha measured twice in reify tests/infra static guards (task 6247): a `trap 'cleanup' RETURN` registered INSIDE a function, where `cleanup` reads that function's `local` variables, runs AFTER those locals are popped — so under `set -u` the handler aborts on the first unbound name and never reaches its `rm -f`. The construct in tests/infra/test_no_new_wallclock_upper_bounds.sh (`local _viof=$(mktemp)`, `local _detector_cleanup_done=0`, `_detector_cleanup(){ ... }`, `trap '_detector_cleanup' RETURN`) is symptom-free ONLY because every call site invokes the detector at TOP LEVEL, where the flag still resolves; measured 0 temp survivors under a private TMPDIR. Copied verbatim into test_no_bare_holder_sleep_grace.sh and wrapped one level down in a helper function, the identical code printed "_detector_cleanup_done: unbound variable" on every call and leaked 9 temp files per run. So the correctness of a RETURN-trap cleanup silently depends on the CALL SITE's nesting depth, which nothing states and nothing enforces — the next refactor that factors a call into a helper reintroduces the leak. Fix that removes the class rather than repairing the handler: accumulate into a `local -a` array and `printf '%s\n' "${arr[@]}"` at the return points, so no temp file exists and there is no cleanup path to get wrong (guard the empty case under `set -u` with `[ "${#arr[@]}" -gt 0 ]`).

In reify's tests/infra, any test that forces a finite-WAIT slot_acquire deadline (rc=75) MUST redirect the child's stderr to a temp file. Since task 6024, scripts/lib_slot_acquire.sh emits a column-0 `@@REIFY_SLOT_TIMEOUT@@` sentinel on every such deadline, and run_all.sh's Phase-3 re-emission sanitizer (_RA_CLOCK_SANITIZE, run_all.sh:368) is prefix-scoped to `@@REIFY_CLOCK_` only — so an unredirected sentinel survives verbatim into the merge-gate verify log and makes dark-factory's line-anchored classifier mark the ENTIRE merge verify as SEMAPHORE_TIMEOUT. Two leak channels exist: an unredirected child stderr, and an assert description interpolating an unfiltered `$(cat "$X_ERR")` (test_helpers.sh prints $desc raw, so line 2+ of a multi-line interpolation starts at column 0 — on PASSING asserts too). Indenting is NOT a defence; the consumer's anchor is `^[ \t]*`. The sanctioned escape hatch when you must dump a capture is the prefix filter `$(sed 's/^/  | /' "$X_ERR")` — `| ` is non-whitespace and breaks the anchor. When writing a test that handles the sentinel, assemble the token at runtime (`SP='@@REIFY_SLOT_'` then "${SP}TIMEOUT@@") so the literal never appears in the file. Guards: Sections D and E of tests/infra/test_slot_timeout_marker.sh.

Reify temp-dir test hygiene, as landed by task 5640 in crates/reify-test-support/src/temp_dirs.rs (complements the earlier binding-rule note): (1) Post-mortem knob — `REIFY_KEEP_TEMP_DIRS=1 cargo test ...` makes every `prefixed_tempdir` guard RETAIN its directory (tempfile `Builder::disable_cleanup`) and echo the path to stderr, so a RED run's artifacts survive for inspection. Nothing removes them afterwards; delete by hand. Use it when the artifact under test IS the directory contents (e.g. `reify doc --out <dir>` writing index.html in crates/reify-cli/tests/harness_cli/cli_doc.rs). (2) A source scanner, `find_unguarded_temp_dir_sites` / `check_temp_dir_hygiene` / `assert_no_unguarded_temp_dir_sites`, flags BOTH hand-rolled `env::temp_dir()` construction AND the unbound-guard one-liner `prefixed_tempdir("x-").path().to_path_buf()`. Regular `//` comments are NOT skipped (only `///` and `//!`), so a prose mention of the call in a plain comment fails a ratchet test in reify-test-support rather than in the crate you edited — move the mention into a `///` doc comment or annotate the line `// temp-dir:allow — reason`, mirroring the house `// ptodo:allow` convention. (3) Enforcement is a hard-coded six-file ratchet at the bottom of temp_dirs.rs, NOT a workspace sweep, so a new leaking test elsewhere gets no signal; extending it to a sweep needs `walk_test_rs_files` in ignore_hygiene.rs to grow a path filter (it excludes `src/` files today) and is filed as follow-up work.

Bash gotcha in reify's tests/infra/*.sh hermetic test harnesses (task 5590, verified empirically): a bash ARRAY append (`ARR+=("$x")`) made inside a backgrounded `( ... ) &` subshell is silently discarded when the subshell exits — the parent shell's array is unaffected. Probe: `HITS=(); note main; ( note bg1; note bg2 ) & wait` yields `count=1 elems=main`. This blinds any runtime detector/recorder fed from inside a backgrounded fixture (e.g. tests/infra/test_seed_warm_lane.sh's H5d/H9, which run `run_helper_real` inside `( ... ) &` to test blocking-lock behaviour) — the detector silently reports all-clear even when the backgrounded invocation truly hit the condition being watched for. Fix: back the detector's state with an append-only FILE instead of an array (e.g. `printf '%s\n' "$x" >> "$STATE_FILE"`) — a `>>` append performed inside a subshell IS visible to the parent, because it's a kernel-level write to a shared inode, not a shell-variable mutation. Anchor the file under the suite's existing per-run tmpdir-root (reclaimed by the EXIT trap) so no new cleanup registration is needed. Single-line `printf` appends to an O_APPEND file are atomic well below PIPE_BUF (4096), so concurrent appends from a background job and the main shell's own use cannot corrupt a record. Non-vacuity discipline: pair the fix with a mechanism-guard test that constructs its own `( ... ) &` around the real recorder function and asserts the append survives — an end-to-end assert against real backgrounded call sites alone can go vacuous if those call sites are ever un-backgrounded.

When a tests/infra suite asserts on an orchestrator-parsed marker (@@REIFY_CLOCK_*@@, @@REIFY_SLOT_TIMEOUT@@, @@SEMAPHORE_*@@), the leak surface is not just the assert DESCRIPTION — test_helpers.sh's assert() also dumps `tail -50` of the checker's captured stdout/stderr on FAIL (esc-4959-57). So a checker that prints the captured file (cat/echo/grep without -q) leaks live marker tokens into run_all.sh's .out re-emission on red runs, where only the `s/@@REIFY_CLOCK_/@@REIFY_QUOTED_CLOCK_/g` rule applies. Use silent `grep -q*` checkers (they produce no output, so the FAIL-dump branch stays empty) plus the runtime split-token idiom (test_run_all_clock_marker_sanitize.sh:38-42) and the assert_marker helper (test_verify_semaphore_e2e.sh:260-273), which together close the leak without touching run_all.sh's sanitizer.

reify tests/infra gotcha: `git -C ""` and `cd ""` both resolve to the CALLER's cwd rather than failing (measured 2026-10-11). So a fixture-driven infra helper like `git -C "$FIX" ...` / `rm -f "$FIX/$f"` that runs with an unset fixture variable (e.g. after sourcing a test file without strict mode) operates on the caller's own checkout, or on `/`. Guard fixture variables explicitly before use; `set -u` alone does not catch a var that is set but empty.

Fixed subshell resource leak in tests/infra/test_test_helpers.sh

reify tests/infra — a PATH-stub CALLS_FILE probe for "did helper X run?" is DISPATCH-INDEPENDENT and cannot pin WHICH subcommand was passed. Measured on Block W of tests/infra/test_seed_warm_lane.sh (task #6889).

These suites detect a delegated helper by grepping CALLS_FILE for a git invocation only that helper makes. For scripts/git-rerere-guard.sh the probe is `--is-inside-work-tree`, emitted at git-rerere-guard.sh:182 — which sits BEFORE the subcommand dispatch at :951-953. So it fires identically for `arm` and for `check`, and identically whatever target was passed. Demonstrated end-to-end: downgrading seed's call from `arm` to `check` left ALL nine CALLS_FILE-based asserts GREEN. That matters because `check` merely REPORTS the drift while leaving the whole fleet armed — the exact regression the block existed to catch.

Such a probe proves only "some helper-shaped call happened somewhere". Close the two halves it cannot reach:
- ARGUMENT half — still doable from CALLS_FILE: the recorded line is literally `git -C <TARGET> rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree`, so extract the FIELD after `-C` (awk) and compare it to the expected dir. Match the field, never a substring of the line: a substring grep for the lane path is also satisfied by a call that passed a CHILD of it, and one for a parent is satisfied by the lane itself.
- SUBCOMMAND half — structurally unreachable from CALLS_FILE; use a SHIM. Copy the script under test to a temp dir, drop an executable helper of the same name beside it that appends "$@" to a log and exits 0, point the suite's $SCRIPT global at the copy, run through the UNCHANGED run_helper (it does `bash "$SCRIPT" "$@"`, so BASH_SOURCE[0] and hence the script's _SCRIPT_DIR resolve to the temp dir), then RESTORE $SCRIPT in the same sub-block and assert the restoration — these suites are long-lived and every later block reads that global. Check first that the script derives its sibling paths from exactly one BASH_SOURCE-rooted var and sources no sibling lib, or the copy is not faithful.

TWO SHIM CAVEATS. The shim MUST be chmod +x and that must be ASSERTED: an `-x` existence gate in the caller silently takes its warn branch for a non-executable shim, so every downstream assert passes vacuously against a never-created log. And keep shim-based asserts ADDITIVE — do not convert the existing asserts to the shim. A real helper that exits non-zero under the stub `git` is what gives the caller's fail-open assert its teeth; a shim exiting 0 would make that one vacuous, reintroducing the defect. Bonus: because the shim DOES exit 0, it also reaches the helper-success branch, which the real helper never reaches under a stub git.

Reify: when a task fixes a SEMANTICS defect (not just a bug in one function), deriving the plan's file scope from static callers of the changed function systematically under-counts. Fixtures that encode the OLD contract as their premise are invisible to a caller grep — they surface only by RUNNING the suites. On task 7186 (loop-closure closing-joint double-count) the caller-derived plan.files missed: 6 files the handler later granted (2 e2e harnesses stating the pre-fix chain shape verbatim in doc comments, examples/kinematic/four_bar_singular.ri, examples/dynamics/closed_2prismatic_idyn.ri whose stale header passed either way because reduce_constraint_rank projects the row out, plus the .ri's driver test) and crates/reify-stdlib/src/sweep.rs's in-crate `mod tests` fixture. Plan for this: budget an explicit post-fix cross-crate sweep STEP that re-runs every touched suite, and expect it to expand scope. A fixture whose assertion still passes after the fix but whose comment states the pre-fix contract is the most dangerous case — nothing will ever catch it.

content: In reify, a fixture helper that registers cleanup by appending to an array (e.g. `CLEANUP_ACTIONS+=(...)`) silently leaks when it is called as `x=$(helper)`: the command substitution is a subshell, so the append is discarded. Measured in tests/infra/test_tree_sitter_pipeline.sh, where mk_ts_generate_fixture, mk_ts_build_fixture, ts_masked_path_dir and mk_verify_fixture leaked every run (task 8725). The fix is a run- or case-scoped temp root inherited by subshells (the test_helpers.sh make_isolated_lane reasoning). Register only main-shell restores of real-tree files.

8e5ade8c-db5e-44f5-82da-450a150ea140.content: Solar Challenge sim discovery (2026-06-19, board scenario bristol-phase1-flex.yaml): the capacity-at-events grid-services model computed £0 annual income / 0.0 kW available capacity at events. Root cause is NOT a bug: under Economy-7 peak-arbitrage dispatch the battery is already fully discharging into the evening peak (16:00-18:00) at exactly the hours winter DFS events fire, so there is zero spare capacity for grid services. Arbitrage and grid-services flexibility CANNIBALISE the same battery at the same hour — they are not additive. Consequence: the consulting model's headline "£280/home/yr (£250 arbitrage + £30 grid services)" cannot be simply summed in practice; to earn grid-services revenue you must reserve battery headroom at event times, trading off arbitrage. This is hard-physics confirmation of the value+buildability model §1.1 warning "do not simply add the column maxima".

solar_challenge_platform gotcha (task 444 planning, 2026-10-13): runtime/roles/_common.py is a private submodule of the runtime.roles package, and tests/test_private_names.py forbids any module outside runtime.roles from importing it — domain modules (control/, optimiser/) AND tests alike (checked with its private_reaches()). So bootstrap_role (P-Ops·β, extended by P-Gate·β1) can be called only from runtime.roles modules, and tests must drive it through console-script entrypoints (e.g. a subprocess per script), never by importing _common. Task 444's plan moves the control-plane-service and optimiser-service console scripts into runtime/roles for this reason.

CONVENTION (task 375, 2026-09-26): tests/test_entrypoints.py::test_console_scripts_are_the_roles_and_the_ops_debug_one_shots pins pyproject [project.scripts] to EXACTLY {f"scp-{role}" for role in ROLES} | OPS_DEBUG_ONE_SHOTS, where OPS_DEBUG_ONE_SHOTS = {control-plane-service, optimiser-service}, the standalone CLIs that D2 (docs/prds/productionization-composition-root.md §4) keeps as ops/debug one-shots. Adding any console script therefore requires a deliberate edit: to ROLES for a new scp-<role>, whose target must be runtime.roles.<role>:run_<role>, or to OPS_DEBUG_ONE_SHOTS only for a D2-sanctioned one-shot. A second name for a long-running loop is refused by design, which is why task 375 retired ingestion-service, a duplicate of scp-ingest with no serve()/SIGTERM drain and no configure_logging. A call is a lookup only when it is made by getattr, hasattr, setattr, delattr or object (so monkeypatch.setattr/delattr and patch.object), not any call whose second positional argument is a private string; the _AWAITING_PUBLIC_READ keys are therefore spelled positionally, InstanceReach("tests/x.py", "_optimiser"), with no keyword arguments, and a constructor or pytest.param handed a private-named string looks nothing up. Completed: Interceptor terminal-status claimant clearing, blessed exception stamp, and recurrence-carrier minting
Description: Three PRD-decomposed tasks from two different PRDs (claimant-invariant-enforcement, claimant-invariant-detection, and recurring-deterministic-tasks) all need to edit the same choke point -- TaskInterceptor._apply_status_transition's terminal-status handling -- and two of them formally declare a dependency on the third. Resolution: the successor title is the chain's base title plus a structured run label composed from the successor's own milestone.at. That keeps the store's dedup index intact and makes successive links distinct. Completed: Ground Stage 2's tasks_created counter in an actually-consulted journal (reconfirmed cross-project via solar_challenge run f9e49aef, task 105), and split curator "combine" outcomes into a separate tasks_combined stat
Description: Umbrella effort to stop trusting Stage 2's (task_knowledge_sync) LLM-self-reported cycle counters and instead ground/correct them against actual code-side evidence, covering both known accuracy-bug classes on the tasks_created counter: (1) undercounting because task_created_records lacks a code-side writer on remediation/ticket-curator paths (from task 3051, 3rd recurrence after done tasks 1199 and 3046; now independently reconfirmed a further time — see evidence below), and (2) miscounting because the "Verifying Task Operations" convention increments tasks_created for actions that are actually curator/combine outcomes rather than new-task creations. Fixing both requires the same corroborate-against-ground-truth mechanism (get_task lookups feeding an actually-consulted task_created journal) across the same task_knowledge_sync code paths, so they are planned and implemented together.

NEW EVIDENCE (cross-project routing, low-priority candidate folded in): reconciliation run f9e49aef-7233-4c0e-abe7-b63c6feede06 (stage=task_knowledge_sync, project=solar_challenge) self-reported stats.tasks_created=1 but stats.task_created_records_valid=0 in the same cycle, even though get_task(105) in solar_challenge confirms task 105 was in fact created — i.e. the task_created_records entry for a real, successfully-created task was omitted. This is the same accounting gap as bug class (1) (task_created_records missing a code-side writer on a task-creation path), now confirmed in a third project. Routed from solar_challenge Stage 1 finding f1656384-6fab-46e2-a12f-44479b113a04 via reconciliation run 5e85f3a1-6c8c-48e7-8697-00b249c5007c, itself carried forward from a prior Stage 3 integrity check. Use this run/task pair as an additional corroboration fixture when implementing the get_task-backed journal fix.
Analysis: PREMISES VERIFIED on branch tip 27fb2a0bee (== main tip): every file in the task's FILES_TO_MODIFY exists; the 3051 landing is present (task_knowledge_sync.py::_action_record_keys, ::_corroborate_record_keys, ::_coerce_tasks_created_count, ::_count_valid_task_created_records, ::_TASK_CREATED_SUCCESS_STATUSES = {'created','combined'}; TaskKnowledgeSync._apply_post_flight_guards publishes task_created_records_valid/_corroborated/_uncorroborated/_unresolvable); flag_dedup.safe_get_task/confirm_task_present/_cited_task_corroborated/filter_false_phantom_task_creation_flags exist; TaskInterceptor emits EventType.task_created in _process_add_ticket, _process_add_tickets_batch_prepared and _submit_task_planning_mode. Coalesced members read with get_task: 3573 (journal submit_task/resolve_ticket so tasks_created is journal-derived; hard-coded agent_id), 4018 (tasks_hints_updated parity: action-record list + get_task corroboration with a superset predicate), 4140 (_coerce_tasks_created_count raises on NaN/inf float and 'inf'/'1e400' strings), 3916 item 2 (false "unlike the flag counters above" clause in _apply_post_flight_guards' docstring), 3487 (project-agnostic code-side drop of Stage-3 findings that pair a task_count_snapshot* stat with a missing Graphiti temporal_facts edge; stage3.py note currently says "prompt-only for now").

ROOT CAUSE OF THE UNDERCOUNT. Every evidence run (f9e49aef/task 105, 90d762d0/task 4745, 507bc25b/task 3045) is an LLM omission: the agent did not append a task_created_records entry. Nothing code-side records which run created which task: submit_task/resolve_ticket are not journaled, the ticket store row has no submitter identity, and the EventType.task_created events carry no agent/run attribution (they are drained by the recon event buffer and cannot tell a Stage-2 filing from a concurrent orchestrator agent's).

ATTRIBUTION THAT ALREADY EXISTS. stages/base.py injects "For every fused-memory write call include agent_id='recon-stage-<stage>' and metadata._causation_id=<run_id>" into every stage prompt; stats_verifier/derive_stage_stats already treat causation_id+agent_id write_ops rows as computed ground truth. Measured on the live dark_factory store: task 4745 (evidence run 90d762d0, filed via resolve_ticket) carries metadata._causation_id == '90d762d0-...', and so does 1594 (run 1bae8fe2). The submitter's causation therefore reaches TaskInterceptor.submit_task inside metadata today; it is simply never journaled with the outcome. Stage 1 and Stage 3 are denied submit_task/resolve_ticket/commit_planning (cli_stage_runner.DISALLOW_TASK_WRITES), so within one run's causation only Stage 2 can mint creations.

DESIGN.
(1) New leaf module fused_memory/middleware/task_creation_journal.py owns the creation-journal ROW CONTRACT both ways: frozen CreationAttribution (agent_id, causation_id) parsed once at the submit boundary from (metadata._causation_id, resolved agent_id) and round-tripped through the ticket blob; operation constants TASK_CREATED_OPERATION='task_created' / TASK_COMBINED_OPERATION='task_combined' and creation_operation_for(status) (created->task_created, combined->task_combined, anything else->None); frozen CreationOutcomes(created, combined: frozenset[(project_id, task_id)]); and async read_run_creation_outcomes(write_journal, run_id) -> CreationOutcomes | None over WriteJournal.get_ops_by_causation (None = journal unavailable: no journal, raising read, or non-list result).
(2) TaskInterceptor writes one write_op row per creation OUTCOME at the moment it is decided, through the existing single Layer-1 writer _log_write_op_row (gains a causation_id kwarg): planning mode (created, or combined on DuplicateCandidateKeyError) directly; every curator-worker terminal (create / drop / combine / candidate_key_collision / within-batch drop / R4 idempotency hit, single and batch, incl. the cancel path) via _persist_worker_terminal, which gains project_root + attribution kwargs and journals after mark_resolved regardless of its bool (the backend write happened even if a concurrent cancel won the ticket row). The two idempotency-hit paths that call mark_resolved directly are routed through _persist_worker_terminal so there is one terminal chokepoint. Attribution rides the ticket blob under a top-level 'creation_attribution' key (never inside kwargs, never forwarded to tm.add_task); _PreparedTicket gains an attribution field. refused/failed/cancelled outcomes write no creation row.
(3) New module fused_memory/reconciliation/stage2_counter_grounding.py receives the 3046/3051 accounting helpers moved out of task_knowledge_sync.py (public names: coerce_count, action_record_keys) plus the new grounding: for each grounded Stage-2 counter it builds evidence = journal keys (code truth, trusted, never re-looked-up) ∪ LLM record keys (claims, each corroborated with get_task in its own project), repairs the self-reported counter UPWARD ONLY to |confirmed evidence| (W5-mu stance unchanged), and RETURNS stat updates (no in-place mutation). Three counters, one mechanism: tasks_created (records status 'created' + journal created), tasks_combined (records status 'combined' + journal combined — scope 2), tasks_hints_updated (task_hints_updated_records with a memory_hints SUPERSET predicate — 4018). Published per counter: <counter> (coerced int, always present), <counter>_reported (raw, only on repair), <prefix>_valid (confirmed creations: journaled + corroborated record-only — the meaning the task text asks for), <prefix>_journaled, <prefix>_uncorroborated, <prefix>_unresolvable (the last two partition the record-only claims). Warning event names keep their current spellings for tasks_created (reconciliation.stage2_tasks_created_undercount / reconciliation.stage2_task_created_records_uncorroborated) by deriving them from the counter/prefix; plus reconciliation.stage2_creation_journal_unavailable when the journal cannot be read.
(4) SPOT fold (review note): flag_dedup gains public frozen TaskLookup(project_id, task_id, accept) + LookupVerdict + async corroborate_task_lookups(taskmaster, known_projects, lookups) — the single resolve-root -> one flat plain gather of safe_get_task -> classify loop; filter_false_phantom_task_creation_flags and the grounding module both call it (task_knowledge_sync._corroborate_record_keys/_RecordCorroboration/_normalize_record_keys are deleted).
(5) 4140 fix lands in coerce_count (math.isfinite gate; string branch also catches OverflowError). 3916 item 2 is closed by rewriting _apply_post_flight_guards' docstring around the new journal truth. _count_valid_task_created_records (dead) is deleted with its duplicate test class after porting any case TestActionRecordKeys lacks.
(6) 3487: flag_dedup.filter_snapshot_stat_edge_findings (project-agnostic, fail-open, per-drop logger.debug) wired as a 4th gate in IntegrityCheck.run() with stat snapshot_stat_edge_findings_dropped; stage3.py's "prompt-only for now" paragraph updated.
(7) Prompts: stage2.py (## Creating Tasks says the framework journals each curator outcome against the _causation_id in submit_task metadata; ## Verifying Task Operations routes combined to tasks_combined; Per-Cycle Counter Schema adds tasks_combined and task_hints_updated_records), recon_self_model.py (accounting section updated; new render_task_hints_update_accounting_section wired once), stage3.py (cross-project corroboration section explains task_created_records_journaled and that tasks_combined is never a phantom creation).

NOT MODIFIED: reconciliation/stage_stats.py and reconciliation/stats_verifier.py (see design decision: their full-override contract would clobber the upward-only grounding; the creation rows use operation names absent from _OP_TO_STAT so derive_stage_stats ignores them).
Key decisions: Code-side ground truth is a write_journal row per creation OUTCOME, written by TaskInterceptor where the outcome is decided and attributed by the submitter's metadata._causation_id + resolved agent_id. The existing EventType.task_created events are not consumed.; Journal keys are trusted and never re-checked with get_task. get_task corroboration applies only to LLM record claims that the journal does not already cover. The counter repair stays UPWARD-ONLY.; task_created_records_valid changes meaning to CONFIRMED creations (journaled + corroborated record-only claims), and task_created_records_corroborated is no longer published. Reify has TWO established conventions for a symbol that must be reachable from a test in another compilation unit without being advertised as crate API, and they are not interchangeable. (2) A cargo feature gate — `test-fixtures = []` / `test-utils = []` in Cargo.toml plus `#[cfg(any(test, feature = "..."))]`, precedent crates/reify-runtime/Cargo.toml:18 — which removes the symbol from non-test builds entirely and is strictly stronger. Choose (2) only when you can edit BOTH manifests: the consumer crate has to enable the feature on its dependency. When the consumer is another crate's in-lib unit test (`mod foo { mod tests }`) reached via a dev-dependency, or when file locks forbid touching Cargo.toml, (2) is unavailable and (1) is the correct fallback. Fact (scoping_intake, verified 2026-10-14 on main f628a00): web.py::route compiles the path as a regex and _dispatch uses fullmatch, so a literal path like "/confidentiality" routes with no token; a Handler may ignore both the match and the form (tests/test_web.py already does). wording.py::wording_html is called only from cli.py::sites_for, substitutes only {{retention_days}}, html-escapes each blank-line chunk into

, and cannot render headings, lists, links or line breaks; markdown markers come out literally. A copy/*.md file therefore cannot carry an anchor, so a link from the notice page must be added in prospect_pages.py::_notice_page. The CSP (default-src 'none') governs resource loads, not navigation, so a same-origin needs no header change. Referrer-Policy same-origin sends the token-bearing URL on a click to our own handler, which never logs paths. tests/test_serve.py::answer dispatches against a Site without binding a port; tests/test_session_flow.py::Browser serves a route list over real HTTP with Host set.

Completed: Check Host, Origin and password before reading a POST body: one ordered refusal chain (web.py RequestHandler)
Description: In src/scoping_intake/web.py, a POST's refusals are applied in two places, in an order that reads the body before deciding whether the request may be answered at all.

do_POST (web.py:111-117 at main 368e171; after task 7 lands, RequestHandler.do_POST at module level) does these steps in order:
1. Checks the Content-Length header.
2. Reads the body: self.rfile.read(...), up to MAX_FORM_BYTES = 256,000 bytes.
3. Calls _respond, which only then runs _refusal(): Host allow-list (refused.host), same-origin via Sec-Fetch-Site/Origin (refused.origin), then the operator password (refused.password).

Consequences:
(a) A POST with a foreign Host, from another website, or without the operator password still makes the server read up to 256 KB before refusing it.
(b) A foreign-Host POST with a bad Content-Length is answered with the length refusal instead of the Host refusal.
(c) The refusal policy has two homes: the inline length checks in do_POST and the _refusal() chain. This is docs/code-quality.md heuristic 10, 'uniformly enforced': one mechanism everywhere, and the invariant's definition has one home.

Proposal: one ordered refusal chain run before any body is read. The order is Host, then origin, then password, then length (missing or unreadable as malformed, over the limit as too long), then read the form. Keep every refusal's route name, status and page.

Tests: through make_server with a bare socket client, as tests/test_web.py does after task 7. A foreign-Host POST with a bad length is refused as refused.host (421), and a refused request's body is never read. One way to show the second: declare a Content-Length larger than the body sent and confirm the refusal still arrives at once, before the 30-second socket timeout.

Found while planning task 7 (review run review-scoping_intake-20261007, findings fk-da190964bd10 and fk-d79ef903b73e). Task 7 deliberately keeps the existing order: reordering is a behaviour change outside its brief. Depends on task 7, which moves RequestHandler to module level and splits the length refusal into refused.malformed and refused.too-long; rebase on it. Low priority: both listeners bind loopback, the prospect listener is published only through Tailscale Funnel, and the read is bounded by MAX_FORM_BYTES and the socket timeout.

Security observation recorded as take-out PRD decision 11 (2026-10-15): a file a browser saves from GET /s/<token>/p/<n>/take-out may carry its download URL, token included, in OS metadata (macOS kMDItemWhereFroms, Windows Zone.Identifier HostUrl), and the PRD invites the prospect to share the file. Accepted for now as the same exposure as the prospect's browser history holding the link; email and most sync tools strip the attribute. The mitigation, if Leo wants it closed, is a POST that redirects to a token-free one-time download path (needs a nonce store). The question is in the PRD's §Wording for Leo.

Smoke-testing gotcha for scoping-intake (current as of task 20, replaces the task-7 text that named do_POST as the length refuser): web.py's RequestHandler._refusal() decides every refusal before any body is read. It checks Host (refused.host, 421), then a POST's origin (refused.origin, 403), then the password (refused.password, 401), then a POST's Content-Length; only when none refuses does _respond() read the form, so a refused POST's body is never read. A Content-Length that is missing or not a decimal is refused under the route name refused.malformed with the page 'Malformed request'. A decimal length over MAX_FORM_BYTES, or with more digits than MAX_FORM_BYTES has, is refused under refused.too-long with the page 'Too long'. Both are HTTP 400, and the log line records only method, route name and status. Because the length is judged last, a POST that also breaks an earlier rule gets that rule's status instead: an operator-listener POST without credentials and without Content-Length is 401, not 400, and a foreign-Host POST with a bad length is 421. Before task 7 every length case was one refused.length / 'Too long' refusal, which misled the first smoke pass of review-scoping_intake-20261007 (finding R8, fk-d79ef903b73e). curl -X POST with no --data sends no Content-Length, so a curl-driven walk of the flow is still refused (as malformed, once Host, origin and password pass) on consent, write-up and delete: pass --data '' (or use urllib, which sends Content-Length: 0). A working smoke script follows the review session's scratchpad pattern: synthetic backend, mktemp INTAKE_DATA_DIR, free loopback ports, curl with Host matching 127.0.0.1:<port>.

To try a change to scoping-intake's Host allow-list before and after without a browser (task 35, 2026-10-08): run `.venv/bin/scoping-intake serve --backend synthetic` as a subprocess with env {PYTHONPATH: <src tree>, PATH: /usr/bin:/bin, throwaway HOME and INTAKE_DATA_DIR, INTAKE_PUBLIC_URL: <case>} on two ports from bind(('127.0.0.1', 0)), taking the unchanged tree from `git archive HEAD src` and the changed one from the worktree's src, and terminate the server in a finally. POST /invite on the operator port needs no Origin header (a client that sends neither Origin nor Sec-Fetch-Site passes web.py's same-origin check); read `https?://.../s/<32 characters>` off the session page, then GET /s/<token> on the prospect port with http.client putrequest(..., skip_host=True) and putheader('Host', <the Host Chrome sends, see the browser-host-header entry>). Measured: the unchanged tree answered 421 refused.host and the fixed one 200 prospect.show for https://Intake.Example, http://intake.example:80 and http://Intake.Example:<prospect port>, while https://intake.example:8443 got 200 on both.

Completed: serve: Host allow-list entries that still differ from the Host a browser sends (non-canonical INTAKE_PUBLIC_URL hosts; loopback entries on port 80)
Description: Found while planning task 35 (follow-up id agent-followup-35). Task 35 makes src/scoping_intake/cli.py derive the prospect site's Host allow-list entry from INTAKE_PUBLIC_URL the way a browser writes Host: the host in lower case, no port when it is the scheme's default (80 for http, 443 for https) or empty, any other port kept, and an IPv6 address in brackets. The derivation lives in a helper, cli._host_header(scheme, hostname, port), which _public_url calls. web.py RequestHandler._admission_refusal answers only a Host header that is in site.hosts by string equality, and otherwise replies 421 'Not found'. Two cases are left. Both are outside task 35's scope and unlikely in the deployed setup: deploy/README.md sets INTAKE_PUBLIC_URL=https://<machine>.<tailnet>.ts.net, and the units use ports 8471 and 8472.

(1) Host spellings a browser rewrites beyond case and port. Measured on 2026-10-08 with headless Chrome 151 and a capture server: http://[0:0:0:0:0:0:0:1]:P/ is sent as Host [::1]:P. Per the WHATWG URL standard but NOT measured: a non-ASCII name such as https://bücher.example is sent in punycode (xn--bcher-kva.example), and IPv4 shorthand such as http://127.1:P/ is sent as 127.0.0.1:P. urllib.parse.urlsplit keeps all three as typed (CPython 3.14.4, the project venv). The allow-list entry therefore never matches, and every prospect request gets 421. The fix is either to derive the entry the way the browser does (IPv6 compression via ipaddress, IDNA/UTS-46, IPv4 parsing) or to refuse such values at start with UnusablePublicUrl, naming the variable.

(2) cli._loopback_hosts(port) always writes the port: {127.0.0.1:P, localhost:P}. A browser leaves out port 80 for http; measured in Chrome 151, http://intake.example:80/ is sent as Host intake.example. So with --prospect-port 80 or --operator-port 80, a browser at http://localhost/ sends Host 'localhost' and gets 421. The operator site would also refuse http://127.0.0.1/. cli._host_header from task 35 could build these entries too.

SIGHTING of the stale-base silent-semantic-break pattern (task 4286, 2026-09-09) — a NEW shape, outside the dashboard structural/regex class the canonical enumerates: RETURN-ARITY WIDENING caught by a test double, not by a source-text assertion.

THE CASE. task/4286 was 99 commits stale. `git merge-tree --write-tree main task/4286` returned rc=0 with a bare tree OID — no conflicts — and the merge landed clean. But main had meanwhile widened `orchestrator/src/orchestrator/agents/briefing.py::filter_foreign_project_results` from `(text, dropped)` to `tuple[str, int, int]` (top-level vs nested drops split into separate quantities, task 4008 amendment). The branch's new test patched that function with `side_effect=[('', 1), RuntimeError(...)]` — a 2-tuple stub written against the old contract. Post-merge the first patched call raised `ValueError: not enough values to unpack (expected 3, got 2)` INSIDE the production code's own try block, which caught it, logged a WARNING, and fell through; the drop counter never incremented and the drop-clause variant rendered bare. Fix was one character class: `('', 1, 0)`.

WHY IT EVADES THE CANONICAL'S CHECK. The canonical's verify recipe greps definition-vs-use for helpers (`grep -n "def X\|X("`). That would NOT have caught this: definition and call site were both consistent — main updated them together. The stale thing was the MOCK's return value, which no static grep relates to the real signature, and which pyright does not type-check either (`side_effect` is untyped). Both `ruff` and `pyright` were clean on both prefixes with the bug present.

THE ADDED RULE. After a stale-base merge, the at-risk set is not just tests asserting on another file's source text — it is every TEST DOUBLE standing in for a function main may have re-signatured: `patch(..., return_value=/side_effect=)`, fakes, and stubs. For each one your branch introduces or touches, re-read the CURRENT signature of the patched target in the merged tree and confirm the double still satisfies it. Grepping `patch\(` for targets whose module main touched (`git log --oneline <base>..main -- <path>`) finds these cheaply.

AND THE LOUDER LESSON: an exception-swallowing `except` around the call site converts a contract break into a passing-looking degraded path. Here the only surface signal was one WARNING line in captured logs. Do not treat merge-tree rc=0 plus green lint/type as evidence a refresh was inert — run the tests.

GOTCHA (measured 2026-09-04, task 4377 debugger): the orchestrator's SERIAL RE-RUN path silently changes pytest collection semantics, and for the `scripts` module it turns a green suite red with 2 collection errors.

MECHANISM. `orchestrator/src/orchestrator/verify.py::_serial_pytest_str` (:1374) appends `-p no:xdist -o addopts=` to force serial pytest. Its docstring says the `-o addopts=` exists to clear `-n auto` (task 2045's shared-venv-mutation workaround). But root `pyproject.toml:66` is the SOLE carrier of `--import-mode=importlib`, so blanking addopts drops the import mode too — collateral, not intended. Under pytest's default `prepend` mode, `scripts/orchestrator.yaml:22`'s deliberate two-directory union (`pytest tests/scripts/ scripts/tests/`, task 3384) collides on the basenames shared by both dirs — today `test_restart_all_orchestrators.py` and `test_reviewer_redundancy_diagnostic.py` — because neither directory has an `__init__.py`. Result: `import file mismatch`, rc=2, "2 errors", ZERO test failures.

`dark-factory-orchestrator.yaml:105-110` states the dependency outright ("collision across the two directories' few shared basenames is safe because the root pyproject.toml sets addopts = --import-mode=importlib and neither directory has an __init__.py") — so the union command is only collision-free WHILE addopts survives, and the serial re-run is the one path that removes it.

A/B THAT PROVES IT (single variable): the recorded verify cmd `uv run --project shared pytest --tb=short -q --timeout=300 -p no:xdist -o addopts= tests/scripts/ scripts/tests/` → 2 collection errors, rc=2. Same command + `--import-mode=importlib` → 4216 passed, 2 skipped, rc=0 in 290.64s.

HOW TO RECOGNISE IT AS A DEBUGGER. Symptom is COLLECTION errors ("import file mismatch ... which is not the same as the test file we want to collect"), never assertion failures, and the failing leg's recorded `cmd` in `.task/verify/*.summary.json` contains `-o addopts=`. Before touching any code, re-run that exact cmd with `--import-mode=importlib` appended. If it goes green, the defect is the invocation, not your branch — check `git diff --name-only main...HEAD` to confirm your branch touched neither colliding directory, then escalate rather than renaming test files or adding `__init__.py` (the missing `__init__.py` is DELIBERATE and load-bearing per the yaml comment above).

THE CORRECT FIX SHAPE, already precedented in-repo: `cockpit/tests/test_root_config_smoke_deselection.py::_addopts_without_marker_filter` (:202) DERIVES an addopts override from root pyproject.toml and strips only the one token it means to strip, instead of blanking addopts wholesale. That file (:365) had already named this exact hazard in prose — "a bare `-o addopts=` ... would silently run collection under different semantics than every real root-bound run" — a year before it bit a real verify run.

BLAST RADIUS: any task whose scope resolves to the `scripts` module config and reaches the serial confirm re-run hits this deterministically; nothing about the triggering task is special beyond having touched some `scripts/*.py`. Filed as esc-4377-3.

REFINEMENT (measured 2026-09-02, task 4345) of the existing note that "--import-mode=importlib does not put a test file's own directory on sys.path". The truth is ASYMMETRIC, and the asymmetry is the trap:

* `cd escalation && uv run pytest tests/...` — the tests dir IS `sys.path[0]`. A bare `from _sibling import X` WORKS. Conftest is named `'conftest'`.
* Repo-root MULTI-package run (`pytest escalation/tests/x.py orchestrator/tests/y.py`) — `sys.path[0]` is some OTHER subproject's tests dir; escalation/tests is absent entirely. The same import raises `ModuleNotFoundError` at COLLECTION time. Conftest is named `'escalation.tests.conftest'`.

Why this hides: dark-factory's verify `test_command` runs each subproject SEPARATELY (`cd shared && pytest tests/ && cd ../escalation && pytest tests/ && ...`). So a sibling-module import with no conftest sys.path insert is fully green in verify and breaks only for a human running pytest from the repo root. Never conclude "the sibling import works" from a single subproject-scoped run — test both shapes.

THE FIX IS AN ENFORCED HOUSE CONVENTION, not an ad-hoc insert. `tests/scripts/test_pytest_workspace_collection.py` states it ("each subproject exports its non-fixture helpers under a uniquely-named sibling module") and enforces it: `test_subproject_conftests_add_tests_dir_to_sys_path` iterates `_SUBPROJECTS_WITH_CONFTEST` and requires `sys.path.insert(0, str(_TESTS_DIR))` (Path form) or `sys.path.insert(0, _tests_dir)` (os.path form) — the regex accepts ONLY those two spellings, positioned after the `_SRC` insert and before the first non-stdlib import. Existing sibling helpers: `_fm_helpers.py`, `_orch_helpers.py`, `_dashboard_helpers.py`, `_dt_helpers.py`, `_merge_queue_harness.py`.

`_SUBPROJECTS_WITH_CONFTEST` is a HAND-MAINTAINED registry and was `['dashboard', 'fused-memory', 'orchestrator', 'shared']` — escalation had a tests/conftest.py but was absent from the list AND missing the insert. So "escalation can't use a sibling helper" was never a property of importlib mode; it was an un-enrolled subproject. If you hit this for a subproject, check the registry before concluding the option is closed. Adding the insert to escalation left the full suite green (1511 passed, 2 xfailed, 84s).

Corollary for planning: "a conftest helper is reachable only as a fixture, so folding it needs a fixture parameter on every test" is only true when the sibling-module route is genuinely unavailable. Check the registry first — it can turn a ~90-call-site mechanical conversion into a 6-file edit with zero test-signature changes.

NORM (dark-factory, task 5444, steward-verified 2026-09-14): a TEST-ISOLATION hardening fixed in one subproject's conftest has NO mechanism to reach its siblings, and the gap is invisible because every gate stays green. When you harden one subproject's test isolation, check the siblings in the same commit or file the propagation explicitly — do not assume an RCA'd-and-fixed class is fixed repo-wide.

THE INCIDENT THAT ESTABLISHED IT. `orchestrator/tests/conftest.py::_isolate_orch_config` pins `ORCH_CONFIG_PATH` to a canonical ABSOLUTE path, added under task 2719 after task 2957 RCA'd the leak class (plans/eval-metric-collector-orch-config-leak-rca-2026-07-22.md). fused-memory had only `preserve_config_path`, which save/restored `CONFIG_PATH` but never PINNED it — so it guarded intra-suite pollution and was blind to ambient inheritance and to the CWD. Nothing propagated the orchestrator's fix. Consequence: a fused-memory test's outcome was a function of the pytest CWD, because `FusedMemoryConfig` is a pydantic-settings `BaseSettings` whose `settings_customise_sources` defaults `CONFIG_PATH` to the RELATIVE `config/config.yaml`, and `YamlSettingsSource.__call__` returns `{}` SILENTLY when it misses. Same commit, same test: green via `uv run --directory fused-memory pytest ...` (the gate's invocation), red from the repo root.

WHY IT COST SO MUCH. The divergence manufactured a PHANTOM main-red. A steward measured the root-CWD failure, concluded a test had been born red and sat red 18 days, fixed a test that was never broken (commit a484d16588), and filed task 5444 on a false premise. An independent read-only agent re-derived the same wrong conclusion from the same evidence. Both experts read `Field(default=None)` without reading `settings_customise_sources`. The gates were never wrong — there was no red to catch.

THE TWO TRANSFERABLE LESSONS.
1. For a pydantic-settings `BaseSettings`, a field's declared default is NOT what a test reads. Env settings and the YAML layer both outrank it, and `env_prefix=''` makes any bare variable named after a top-level field an unprefixed override. Before concluding "this default is None so the test must fail", check the settings sources and the tracked config file.
2. A per-subproject conftest fixture is invisible infrastructure with no cross-subproject owner. Ask "does the sibling subproject have this?" — the answer was no for three years of `CONFIG_PATH` and nothing ever reported it.

THE REMEDY SHAPE THAT IS FREE vs THE ONE THAT IS NOT — worth reusing. Pinning an env var to a tmp path changes what every currently-green test reads (here ~20k of them) and so carries real collateral; DELETING an inherited variable that is already unset under every registered verify command is free. Task 5444 therefore deleted `PROJECT_ROOT`/`QUEUE_DATA_DIR`/`RECONCILIATION_DATA_DIR` (the YAML's `${VAR:default}` interpolation surface, which pydantic never sees, so a `model_fields`-derived scrub misses it) while filing the pin-the-leaves half as task 5481. When a reviewer proposes a setenv analogue, check whether a delenv gets the ambient half for zero collateral first.

AND THE ANTI-PATTERN THIS FIX ITSELF AVOIDED, which is the incident's own shape recurring: `model_dump()` equality across a `chdir` is NOT semantic equality when the leaves are relative strings — two identical dumps denoted different directories. Reading dump equality as "config does not depend on CWD" would have been the same false assurance that produced the phantom red. State the weaker invariant executably (a companion test asserting the same relative leaf resolves to two different directories) rather than letting a strong-sounding assertion imply more than it checks.

Structural follow-ups: task 5480 (extract a shared settings-isolation fixture factory into df_pytest_isolation.py so the two conftests stop hand-copying it) and task 5481 (the un-propagated path-leaf half).

Completed: _serial_pytest_str's bare `-o addopts=` silently drops root addopts tokens it never meant to strip (import mode AND the smoke/integration/warm_lane_bash deselection)
Description: orchestrator/src/orchestrator/verify.py::_serial_pytest_str rewrites every pytest invocation to run serially by appending `-p no:xdist -o addopts=`. Its own docstring states the INTENT of `-o addopts=` narrowly: clear the pyproject-level `-n auto` per task 2045's shared-venv-mutation recovery. But `-o addopts=` is a WHOLESALE BLANK, not a targeted removal, so it also drops every other token the root addopts carries. Root pyproject.toml:66 carries two more, both load-bearing:

    addopts = "--import-mode=importlib -m 'not smoke and not integration and not warm_lane_bash'"

TWO DISTINCT CONSEQUENCES, the second worse than the first.

(1) COLLECTION MODE. Dropping --import-mode=importlib reverts pytest to prepend mode, which breaks any command whose collection depends on importlib. Measured on the task/4377 worktree, single variable, HEAD=40204bf476:
    `uv run --project shared pytest --tb=short -q --timeout=300 -p no:xdist -o addopts= tests/scripts/ scripts/tests/`
      -> 4197 collected + 2 collection errors ("import file mismatch"), rc=2
    same command + `--import-mode=importlib`
      -> 4218 collected, 4216 passed / 2 skipped, rc=0
The scripts module test_command is a deliberate UNION of tests/scripts/ and scripts/tests/ (task 3384/3460); the two dirs share three basenames (conftest.py, test_restart_all_orchestrators.py, test_reviewer_redundancy_diagnostic.py) and neither has an __init__.py. dark-factory-orchestrator.yaml:105-110 states the safety argument in as many words and rests it explicitly on root addopts setting importlib. This surfaced as esc-4377-3, which red-legged task 4377's verify for a defect entirely outside that task.

(2) MARKER SELECTION -- the wider hazard, and NOT fixed by the narrow unblock. Blanking addopts also drops `-m 'not smoke and not integration and not warm_lane_bash'`, so a serial re-run COLLECTS AND RUNS the smoke, integration and warm_lane_bash buckets that every normal run deselects. A serial recovery re-run therefore does not execute the same test set as the run it is recovering, and can go red on tests the primary path never intended to run. cockpit/tests/test_root_config_smoke_deselection.py:365-367 already records this in-repo: "A bare `-o addopts=` with nothing carried over also works today but would silently run collection under different semantics than every real root-bound run."

PROPOSED FIX. Stop blanking. Emit `-o addopts=<root addopts minus the xdist tokens>` -- derive the override from root pyproject.toml and strip only the token(s) actually targeted. The in-repo precedent for exactly this shape already exists: cockpit/tests/test_root_config_smoke_deselection.py::_addopts_without_marker_filter (:202). Note `-p no:xdist` is already appended independently and disables the plugin outright, so the `-n auto` removal is belt-and-suspenders -- task 2045's intent is preserved.

REGRESSION COVERAGE. Assert a serial-rewritten command still carries the root import mode AND the root marker deselection. Both directions matter: importlib is what keeps the two-directory scripts union collectable, and the marker filter is what keeps the recovery run's test SET equal to the primary run's.

RELATED, ALREADY LANDED: scripts/orchestrator.yaml now pins --import-mode=importlib explicitly on its test_command (steward fix for esc-4377-3, commit 9c657d48ca on task/4377). That is a narrow per-module unblock only -- it does nothing for consequence (2), and nothing for any other module whose collection or selection depends on a root addopts token. This task supersedes it as the general fix; the explicit flag becomes redundant but stays correct.

BLAST RADIUS: every module whose verify leg reaches the serial confirm/recovery re-run, which is the ENV_TRANSIENT retry path for the whole fleet.

Completed: escalation/tests/conftest.py's hand-mirrored CheckpointResult stub is stale (2 fields vs the real 3), poisoning orchestrator/tests/test_sqlite_pragmas.py collection
Description: Discovered incidentally while running verification for task 5504 (warm-lane GC; unrelated code). Not fixed there — out of that task's scope.

OBSERVED. `uv run --project orchestrator pytest -m warm_lane_bash -q` from the repo root (worktree .worktrees/5504) aborted with 13 collection errors. One of them is NOT a missing-dependency error and is a genuine defect:

    ERROR collecting orchestrator/tests/test_sqlite_pragmas.py
    orchestrator/tests/test_sqlite_pragmas.py:413: in <module>
        _SENTINEL_RESULT = CheckpointResult(busy=0, log=0, checkpointed=0)
    E   TypeError: CheckpointResult.__new__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'busy'

MECHANISM (verified by reading both sites, not inferred):
* `shared/src/shared/async_sqlite_base.py::CheckpointResult` is a 3-field NamedTuple: `busy: int`, `log: int`, `checkpointed: int`. `shared/src/shared/sqlite_sync_base.py` re-exports it and its own comment says "single definition, no duplication".
* `escalation/tests/conftest.py` (around lines 64-86) stubs `shared` and `shared.async_sqlite_base` into `sys.modules` at MODULE IMPORT time (not in a fixture) so escalation's project-scoped venv need not carry aiosqlite. Its stub is hand-written as a namedtuple with only TWO field names, 'log' and 'checkpointed'. It is missing 'busy'.
* Because the stub is installed unconditionally into `sys.modules` and guarded only by an `if 'shared.async_sqlite_base' not in sys.modules` check, any collection that imports escalation's conftest BEFORE orchestrator/tests/test_sqlite_pragmas.py hands the latter the 2-field stub instead of the real 3-field type, and its module-level construction raises.

SCOPE / SEVERITY. This does NOT fire on the documented per-package run (`cd orchestrator && uv run pytest -q`), which is the established norm, so it is latent rather than breaking CI. It fires on a root-scoped collection, where it reads as a regression in sqlite pragma code that is in fact untouched. Low priority accordingly.

RATIONALE FOR FILING RATHER THAN FIXING INLINE. The stub is a hand-mirror of a type defined in another package — the drift-prone shape that code-quality heuristic 11 (SPOT) and heuristic 10 (invariants uniformly, redundantly enforced) both name. It has already drifted once. The minimal fix is to add 'busy' as the first field so the stub matches the real NamedTuple's order; the better fix is to derive the stub's field list from the real definition, or to assert at stub-construction time that the two field tuples agree, so a future field addition fails loudly at the stub instead of silently at an unrelated test module's import.

FILES: escalation/tests/conftest.py (the stale stub, ~line 76); shared/src/shared/async_sqlite_base.py (the authoritative 3-field NamedTuple, ~line 29); orchestrator/tests/test_sqlite_pragmas.py (~line 413, the victim).
Analysis: Stub had 2 fields vs real 3. Parse real NamedTuple fields via ast from shared/src/shared/async_sqlite_base.py so the stub cannot drift.
Steps completed: 1/1
Modules: escalation/tests/conftest.py

5221e59f-d26d-4324-ba33-e8a5af4cf595.content: On a stale-base branch merge, the CLEANLY auto-merged files are often the dangerous ones — a conflict marker is a warning you get; a silent semantic break is not. The high-risk class in this repo is dashboard's structural/regex tests, which assert on ANOTHER file's source text: git sees no coupling between them, so a refactor on main breaks them with zero conflict. Two live instances found merging task/3517 (4851 commits behind) into main: (1) main promoted the file-local `_extract_function_body` to `_dashboard_helpers.extract_function_body`, so the merged test_tab_tasks_runtime.py IMPORTED one name and CALLED the other — parses fine, NameError at fixture time, 5 tests erroring; (2) main moved the literal `data-testid="tasks-offline-banner"` out of tab_tasks.jsx into a `bannerTestIds` kind->testid map rendered as `data-testid={bannerTestIds[notice.kind]}`, so a test grepping for the double-quoted literal fails. A third, subtler shape: an assertion can go TOOTHLESS rather than red — ours asserted `'tasksOffline' not in <guard>` for a binding main had deleted, so it could no longer fail for any implementation. VERIFY BEFORE COMMITTING the merge: `T=$(git merge-tree --write-tree main HEAD | head -1)`, extract each auto-merged blob with `git show "$T:<path>"`, and grep definition-vs-use for every helper (`grep -n "def X\|X("`). Do this for the NO-conflict files specifically — the conflicted ones you will read anyway. Same discipline applies to absence assertions: dashboard's own idiom (test_tab_tasks_status_counts.py:46-56) runs them against `strip_js_comments(body)`, because the comment explaining an absence otherwise defeats the assertion checking it.

candidates.content: Adding any `source "$SCRIPT_DIR/<lib>.sh"` line to scripts/verify.sh reds SIX infra suites at once with `copy-list drift: missing <lib> (transitive source closure of verify.sh)`: test_verify_scope.sh (2 cp-sites), test_compute_trampoline_registration_wired.sh (2), test_scope_boundary.sh, test_verify_throughput.sh, test_verify_pipeline_guard.sh, test_verify_release_delta_skip.sh.
