Budget those 6 files into the plan's scope BEFORE writing the source line. Note copy_list_preflight_lib.sh's parser only captures double-quoted literal `/<name>.sh"` paths, so sourcing via a bare variable or a child `bash -c` silently evades the guard — that is evasion, not a fix.

Reify gotcha: scripts/lib_slot_acquire.sh cannot hard-require a new sibling lib. Eight verify.sh --print-plan fixtures copy a hand-picked scripts/ subset that includes it: test_verify_throughput, test_scope_boundary, test_verify_gui_feature_check, test_verify_release_delta_skip, test_run_all_tiering, test_verify_pipeline_guard, test_compute_trampoline_registration_wired, and test_verify_scope (twice). verify.sh:437 sources lib_test_semaphore.sh, which sources lib_slot_acquire.sh, unconditionally. A literal double-quoted `source ".../x.sh"` grows copy_list_preflight_lib's closure, and every fixture then reds by name. A variable-path `source "$v"` is invisible to that preflight, but a hard existence check behind it still exits 1 in every fixture. Either make the sibling optional or update every copy list.

Several hermetic tests/infra/*.sh fixtures (test_scope_boundary.sh, test_verify_gui_feature_check.sh, test_verify_scope.sh, test_verify_throughput.sh) build isolated fixture dirs by hand-copying a curated allowlist of scripts/*.sh libs alongside their copy of verify.sh, rather than deriving the list dynamically. When verify.sh gains a new `source "$SCRIPT_DIR/<newlib>.sh"` line, ALL of these fixture-builder functions (make_fixture/make_branch_fixture) must also get a `cp "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/<newlib>.sh" "$dir/scripts/<newlib>.sh"` line added, or their fixture's verify.sh copy fails to source it and the test breaks. This bit task 4915/A4 when verify.sh was made to source scripts/heavy-test-filter-lib.sh: 4 of these fixtures broke and needed the one-line cp added (fixed in commit fcb32af60d). scripts/verify-pipeline-guard.sh's own --list is dynamically auto-derived from verify.sh's source lines so it does NOT need manual updates, but these 4 test fixtures are a separate, manual-allowlist mechanism and DO. When adding any new `source` line to scripts/verify.sh, grep tests/infra/*.sh for existing `cp .../gen-nextest-config.sh` lines to find all fixture-builders that need the matching addition.

The copy-list-drift preflight for verify.sh sandbox meta-tests (tests/infra/test_verify_scope.sh, test_scope_boundary.sh, test_verify_throughput.sh) is factored into a shared helper tests/infra/copy_list_preflight_lib.sh. Any new `--print-plan` sandbox fixture that cp's a subset of scripts/ must, after its cp block and before `git init`, call: `assert_source_closure_copied "$REPO_ROOT/scripts" "$dir/scripts" verify.sh || exit 1`. It walks verify.sh's FULL transitive `source`/`.` closure (not just direct sources) and fails loudly with "copy-list drift: missing <lib>". Wiring is proven behaviorally (not source-grep) via the fault-injection seam REIFY_COPY_LIST_PREFLIGHT_INJECT_PHANTOM (inert by default). Pure-variable-indirection libs like lib_clock_stop.sh (`source "$var"`) are a documented parser exclusion and stay hand-copied.

When adding a new directly-sourced lib to scripts/verify.sh (a `source "$SCRIPT_DIR/<lib>.sh"` line), you must `cp` it into ONLY the 9 infra tests that build an isolated verify.sh fixture — the same set that already copies lib_test_semaphore.sh: test_scope_boundary, test_slot_event_log, test_test_run_semaphore, test_verify_gui_feature_check, test_verify_pipeline_guard, test_verify_scope, test_verify_semaphore_e2e, test_verify_semaphore_wiring, test_verify_throughput. Tests that invoke the REAL $REPO_ROOT/scripts/verify.sh (e.g. test_verify_failfast_order, test_occt_gated_scope, test_release_scoped_scope, test_verify_compile_gate, test_verify_role_prio, test_occt_flock_gate) self-heal and need no change. make_branch_fixture's preflight (test_verify_throughput.sh:64-82) fails loudly on any missed cp. A directly-sourced lib is auto-derived as load-bearing by scripts/verify-pipeline-guard.sh, so NO scripts/verify-pipeline-paths.txt manifest entry is needed (only TRANSITIVELY-sourced libs need a manifest entry).

Writing a synthetic scripts/verify.sh fixture: a bare `cp scripts/verify.sh $tmp/verify.sh` is READABLE but NOT RUNNABLE. verify.sh resolves its libs relative to its own directory, so a lone copy hard-fails immediately with "verify.sh: ERROR — scripts/occt-scope-lib.sh not found next to verify.sh" (measured: exit 1 in 0.028s, empty stdout). That is fine for a test that only greps the copy's source text, but any test that actually EXECUTES it (e.g. --print-plan) must materialize $dir/scripts/ with the whole sibling set plus $dir/.config/nextest.toml. The maintained list lives in tests/infra/test_verify_throughput.sh's make_branch_fixture, and its companion guard is assert_source_closure_copied from tests/infra/copy_list_preflight_lib.sh, which turns a future source-line addition into a precise "copy-list drift: missing <lib>" error instead of an opaque downstream failure. reify tests/infra gotcha: making a test_*.sh sourceable exposes its fixture helpers to callers that never built a fixture, and `git -C ""` resolves to the CURRENT directory. A sourced helper like test_verify_scope.sh's plan_for (`git -C "$FIX" add ...; git -C "$FIX" reset -q -- .`) with an empty FIX would silently unstage the caller's own index, and plan_for_branch would checkout -b/commit/branch -D in the caller's real worktree. `set -u` catches only an UNSET var, not an empty or wrong one. Guard each helper by checking that the fixture path is one the suite's constructors registered (e.g. membership in _TMPDIRS) before any git call (task 8476 plan).

Siting gotcha, measured 2026-10-07 at reify main 90b846861f: a shared ASSERTION helper for tests/infra gates placed under scripts/ is outside the full-gate admission oracle. `bash scripts/verify-pipeline-guard.sh requires-full-gate scripts/prd-gate-substrate-guard.sh` (and any new scripts/*.sh) exits 1, while tests/infra/<name>_lib.sh exits 0 via the open-ended tests/infra/*.{sh,py} glob. So extracting duplicated gate logic OUT of tests/infra/test_*.sh INTO scripts/ silently lets a later helper-only edit fast-path with no gate run, the same guard-goes-quiet shape as #7626's .sh->.py port. Site test-assertion libraries (anything using test_helpers' PASS/FAIL/test_summary) at tests/infra/*_lib.sh, and add a verify-pipeline-infra-tests.txt row (lib -> its consumer glob) for branch-scope selection.

72ebfa7a-ce14-4b11-a796-07fe8a031511.content:
To prove what reify's pre-commit gate actually plans for a given staged changeset WITHOUT touching the shared main checkout's index, reuse tests/infra/test_verify_scope.sh's OWN hermetic harness rather than writing a fixture by hand. verify.sh's scope picker needs only a git repo plus a handful of sibling scripts — no cargo workspace — so a throwaway repo answers the question exactly.

Recipe (used 2026-08-19 to settle esc-6077-3):
  source tests/infra/{test_helpers,plan_capture_lib,copy_list_preflight_lib}.sh
  eval "$(sed -n '/^make_fixture() {/,/^}/p' tests/infra/test_verify_scope.sh)"
  eval "$(sed -n '/^plan_for() {/,/^}/p'    tests/infra/test_verify_scope.sh)"
  FIX=""; make_fixture FIX; plan_for staged <paths...>; echo "$PLAN_OUT"

EXTRACTING the two functions with `sed` (rather than retyping them) is the load-bearing part: make_fixture's copy list is long and drifts, and it runs assert_source_closure_copied, so a hand-rolled clone silently rots the moment verify.sh gains a new sourced lib. Note make_fixture also copies scripts/verify-pipeline-infra-tests.txt into the fixture, so manifest-row experiments work by appending to "$FIX/scripts/verify-pipeline-infra-tests.txt".

For rename/delete scenarios plan_for is not enough — it only stages NEW files. Seed and commit the file in the fixture first (`git -C "$FIX" -c commit.gpgsign=false commit`), then `git mv` / `git rm` and capture the plan, so the diff carries a real R/D entry.

Read the result from two places: the `# scope decision — RUN_RUST=… RUN_GUI=… RUN_OCCT_GATE=…` line, and plan_count_noncomment_lines "$PLAN_OUT" for the emitted command count (a docs-only stage legitimately yields 0 and `# (no commands — nothing to verify for this action/scope)`).

This is strictly better than reasoning from verify.sh's source or from a script header: hooks/project-checks' own header claims a docs-only stage "produces an empty plan and exits 0", which is true today but says nothing about which manifests can still inject a pole — the measured plan does.

a95e43c6-0f07-4f15-8071-c0b4d32650c7.content: reify tests/infra gotcha: `git -C ""` and `cd ""` both resolve to the CALLER's cwd rather than failing (measured 2026-10-11). So a fixture-driven infra helper like `git -C "$FIX" ...` / `rm -f "$FIX/$f"` that runs with an unset fixture variable (e.g. after sourcing a test file without strict mode) operates on the caller's own checkout, or on `/`. Guard fixture variables explicitly before use; `set -u` alone does not catch a var that is set but empty.

candidates.content: solar_challenge Python gotcha (task 850 architect, measured 2026-10-17 on CPython 3.11.15 and 3.12.3, main 7a47ab4): a dataclass field whose default is a MappingProxyType, e.g. `cache_usage: Mapping[str, int] = MappingProxyType({})`, imports on the 3.12 pin but raises ValueError("mutable default <class 'mappingproxy'> for field ... is not allowed: use default_factory") at class definition on 3.11. The reason: 3.11's dataclasses rejects a default whose class has __hash__ None, and 3.12 gave mappingproxy a __hash__ (although hash(MappingProxyType({})) still raises TypeError, because the dict inside it is unhashable). The per-task verify runs only on the pin, so only the offline lane's interpreter matrix catches this. In the 3.11 run, pytest stops at collection, so the whole matrix case fails within about a minute. Fix: `field(default_factory=lambda: MappingProxyType({}))`. To reproduce in a minute: UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT=/tmp/<dir> UV_PYTHON=3.11+gil UV_OFFLINE=1 uv run --locked --extra dev --extra web pytest -m 'not slow and not e2e' --ignore=tests/e2e --ignore=tests/interpreter_matrix --collect-only -q

Python dataclasses field(init=False) gotchas for solar_challenge's tests/_surface_forms.py. Measured by task 550's architect on 2026-10-08 (main 460f9a1), identical on CPython 3.11.15, 3.12.3, 3.13.9 and 3.14.4.
(1) A plain default, e.g. `x: float = field(init=False, default=0.0)`, stays in vars(cls), so a vars()-based member scan reads the field as a class constant ('float').
(2) A default_factory or no-default init=False field is deleted from vars(cls). Instances read a plain default from the class and get a factory value from the generated __init__. They lack a no-default field until the source sets it, e.g. object.__setattr__ in __post_init__.
(3) field.init is only the field-level flag. Under @dataclass(init=False) with a hand-written __init__, every field keeps init=True even when the constructor omits it. So read 'which fields the class form pins' from inspect.signature(cls).parameters, not field.init.
(4) Probe fixtures whose source inspect.getsource must read (e.g. through _attributes_set_on_self) must be loaded from a real file via importlib.util.spec_from_file_location. Exec'ing their text under a fake filename raises OSError: 'could not find class definition' on 3.11/3.12, 'lineno is out of bounds' on 3.13/3.14.

Python dataclass-parameter gotchas for solar_challenge's frozen-surface lock (tests/_surface_forms.py), measured by task 567's architect on main 5da62aa, 2026-10-12. (1) cls.__dataclass_params__ (dataclasses._DataclassParams) records only init, repr, eq, order, unsafe_hash and frozen on CPython 3.11.15; 3.12.3, 3.13.9 and 3.14.4 also record match_args, kw_only, slots and weakref_slot. So a surface form that must read alike on every admitted minor (3.11-3.14) can read only those six from it. The locked mypy's typeshed declares no __dataclass_params__: read it with a scoped `# type: ignore[attr-defined]`, as task 631 did for other typeshed gaps. An undecorated subclass inherits its base's record through attribute lookup. (2) To prove the lock catches a frozen flip, do not un-freeze Location, or any class whose instance is another dataclass's field default. HomeConfig's location default would become unhashable, and dataclasses on 3.11+ then raises ValueError ('mutable default ... use default_factory') when solar_challenge.home is imported, so the lock never runs. Flip BillBreakdown (finance.py) or add order=True/eq=False to TariffPeriod or GridChargeConfig instead.

solar_challenge tests/_surface_forms.py gotcha, measured by the task 550 implementer on CPython 3.11.15, 3.12.3, 3.13.9 and 3.14.4 (task/550, 2026-10-08): in a @dataclass(slots=True) every field's entry in vars(cls) is a member_descriptor, fields the constructor takes included. _declared_attributes computes its class values as vars(cls).keys() - _fields(cls).keys(), so a field(init=False) in such a class is still spelled 'attribute <annotation>' (e.g. 'attribute list[float]'), and unset_attributes ignores it when it has a default or default_factory. Without that subtraction it would read 'member_descriptor'. No test pins this and src has no slots=True dataclass yet, so keep the subtraction when refactoring _declared_attributes or _own_members.

solar_challenge tests/_surface_forms.py gotchas for reading dataclass bodies (task 551 architect, 2026-10-08, main 2cc2ff3). (1) A defaulted InitVar's default stays in vars(cls) as a class attribute, e.g. `floor: InitVar[float] = 0.0` leaves Reading.floor == 0.0, measured on 3.12.3. dataclasses replaces only Field objects, and dataclasses.fields() omits InitVars. So any vars(cls)-based 'defined names' set sees an InitVar's default as a class value. (2) dataclasses.is_dataclass(cls) is True for an UNDECORATED subclass of a dataclass, so a rule keyed on is_dataclass plus the subclass's own annotations can misread a plain annotated attribute. Task 551's plan defines an init-only variable once, in _init_only_variables(cls): the names cls's own body annotates that its constructor takes but that are no dataclass fields. _own_members drops those names, so member_forms, named_classes and undeclared_attributes all inherit the rule.

solar_challenge gotcha, measured 2026-10-02 on task/339 (ce5fd8d + dfee847, pending merge): web/storage.py's stored-config decoder no longer reloads BatteryConfig.dispatch_strategy / grid_charging as dicts. A new _field_types(cls) resolves field annotations in the defining module's namespace merged over solar_challenge.config's, and the old `except NameError` fallback to raw f.type is gone. Consequence: if you give a RunStorage-stored dataclass a TYPE_CHECKING-only annotation whose type is defined in neither its own module nor solar_challenge.config, every load of that class raises NameError naming the type. It no longer degrades silently to a dict. history_export_yaml's decode guard now also catches ConfigurationError, so a stored sub-config its class refuses answers JSON 500 "Invalid config data: ...". This supersedes the 2026-10-01 memory about the dict reload once task 339 merges.

solar_challenge review norm (task 436 amendment, commit c537877): each behavioural claim in an '**Unreleased on main**' line of docs/domain-library-consumption.md needs a behavioural test in the same task that fails if the claim stops holding. The reviewer flagged the task-436 line's untested "`hash(results)` still raises `TypeError`" (a frozen dataclass with eq=True hashes its fields, and pd.Series is unhashable). The fix was tests/unit/test_home.py::TestSimulationResults::test_results_stay_unhashable_though_frozen, which a temporary `@dataclass(frozen=True, eq=False)` edit (identity hash) turns red. Test the behaviour the line claims, never the doc's wording.

solar_challenge test-design convention (task 200 amendment, mutant-verified 2026-09-30): to pin that a stored config dataclass such as TariffConfig stays run-storage compatible, assert it rebuilds through its constructor from its fields — `Cls(**{f.name: getattr(x, f.name) for f in dataclasses.fields(x)}) == x`. Do NOT pin the exact field-name list, which breaks on any legitimate new constructor field. Do NOT import web/storage.py's private _serialize_dataclass/_deserialize_dataclass (Tests stance). RunStorage's load passes every annotated field back to the constructor. So a derived value made a field(init=False) fails both that rebuild test and tests/unit/test_web_storage_roundtrip.py::TestTupleFieldRoundtrip with "TypeError: __init__() got an unexpected keyword argument", while a functools.cached_property value passes both.

solar_challenge tests/_surface_forms.py gotcha, measured by task 620's amendment on CPython 3.11.15, 3.12.3, 3.13.9 and 3.14.4 (task/620 a8dd6d6, 2026-10-11): _holds_generated_init must test isinstance(init, types.FunctionType) after inspect.unwrap, before it reads __code__. A callable object a dataclass body assigns to __init__ (`__init__ = Caller()`, Caller.__call__ annotated) gives inspect.signature(cls) == (valve: 'Valve') -> None on all four minors but has no __code__, so named_classes raised AttributeError. Other forms make poor test fixtures: `__init__ = object.__init__` gives the empty signature, so no annotation reaches the check, and functools.partial shows self on 3.11-3.13 but not on 3.14 and warns FutureWarning on 3.13.

solar_challenge gotcha (task 195, measured 2026-10-02 at task/195 dc0cf2d): web/storage._deserialize_dataclass, used by stored_home_config, RunStorage.load_home_run/load_fleet_run and Export YAML, skips a stored key that is not a dataclass field only when its value is non-null. A non-field key stored as null raises TypeError (unexpected keyword argument), because the None shortcut runs before the field lookup. Stored runs are asdict field trees, so retiring an Optional field (default None, e.g. PVConfig.custom_module_params) would break loading every saved run until that order is fixed; follow-up ticket tkt_0RVB7JBE5XB3B4AE53B61RCJNZ. Retiring a field that was always non-null, as task 195 did with PVConfig.module_efficiency and temperature_coefficient, is safe.

solar_challenge, amendment to 23410657 (task 350's gotcha on moving a frozen-surface name to another module), from task 719 (task/719 b028f6e..a90b42f, 2026-10-14; applies once task/719 merges). test_every_name_resolves_and_caches is gone. solar_challenge convention (task 700, task/700 commits fc0cf66..8221b63 on base c1859d5, 2026-10-17; holds once task 700 merges): tests/_surface_forms.py's undeclared_attributes and unset_attributes read only the __init__ and __post_init__ a class body itself defines, through their first parameter. They raise TypeError naming the class and each write to self whose attribute name is no string constant, e.g. setattr(self, name, v), object.__setattr__(self, f'...', v), or any self.__dict__ / vars(self) reach. So a pinned class whose __init__ or __post_init__ sets an attribute under a computed name fails test_pinned_classes_declare_the_public_attributes_they_set_on_self until a reviewer checks that every name it sets is declared and pastes the write's text into tests/unit/test_public_api_surface.py's REVIEWED_COMPUTED_NAME_WRITES, under the class path, with the reason. The text must be exactly as the TypeError prints it (ast.unparse). An entry the class no longer makes raises ValueError, so drop it then. A constant name, e.g. object.__setattr__(self, "name", value), needs no review. The two reviewed classes are FinanceConfig and home.SimulationResults.

solar_challenge, correction to a06c20c9 (task 719's note on what checks a frozen-surface re-point), from task 719's amendment pass (task/719 876d98c on base ad42de8, 2026-10-14; applies once task/719 merges). (1) tests/unit/test_init_lazy_surface.py::test_every_name_resolves_to_its_type_checking_import checks that each __all__ name resolves to the object __init__.py's top-level `if TYPE_CHECKING:` block imports under that name, and stays that object across accesses. It does NOT check a name's first access, as a06c20c9 says. solar_challenge.__getattr__ caches each resolved object into the package's globals(), and the package is imported once per pytest session. So once any earlier test reads a name, every later in-session access is a cache hit, and only a subprocess (as test_import_is_pvlib_free does) sees a true first access. The check still catches a wrong mapping, because the cached value came from the same __getattr__. Measured: with a scratch -p plugin pre-caching all 69 names after setting _SYMBOL_MODULE['TariffPeriod'] = 'dispatch', the test failed with "solar_challenge.TariffPeriod is not solar_challenge.tariff.TariffPeriod". (2) a06c20c9's commit range b028f6e..a90b42f is pre-rebase and not on task/719; the branch's commits are aadd4ad..876d98c.

solar_challenge convention (task 775, task/775 at fa57ad6 on base 70f3f00, 2026-10-17; holds once task 775 merges): no solar_challenge module imports another inside a function unless tests/unit/test_import_structure.py's ALLOWED_FUNCTION_LOCAL_IMPORTS lists the (importing module, imported module) pair as Permanent(contract) or Transitional(owner). The test checks both ways, so the commit that removes a pair's last function-local import deletes its entry, and one that adds an import hoists it or adds an entry. Its seeded violation imports load_scenarios, never ConfigurationError: the capability manifest's importers-repointed-to-errors check (docs/prds/errors-leaf.capability-manifest.yaml) greps src/ and tests/ for the text `from solar_challenge.config import ConfigurationError` and expects it absent, so do not write that text anywhere in tests/, even inside a string.

Amendment to the solar_challenge FinanceConfig "appended-default field" recipe, step 4 (task 293, branch task/293, final commit b35c22a, 2026-10-01; applies once merged to main): a new defaulted FinanceConfig field needs one row in TestFinanceConfig._DECLARED_DEFAULTS (tests/unit/config/test_finance_block.py), NOT a new test_defaults_<field> method. test_declared_defaults_cover_every_optional_field fails until the row exists, and test_declared_default[<field>] then pins it. The parser's omitted-key default needs no per-field test either: TestFinanceConfigParsing::test_minimal_dict_uses_defaults asserts parse_finance_config({"standing_charge_pence_per_day": 60.0}) == FinanceConfig(standing_charge_pence_per_day=60.0), and FinanceConfig's generated __eq__ compares every field, so the dataclass default and the parser's .get() fallback must agree.

solar_challenge procedural gotcha (task 491 architect, measured 2026-10-08 on main 23c019e, CPython 3.12.3). For a task-455-style byte-identity probe, you write `git show HEAD:src/solar_challenge/web/charts.py` to /tmp and load it with importlib.util.spec_from_file_location + module_from_spec. Set sys.modules[spec.name] = module BEFORE spec.loader.exec_module(module). Without it, exec_module raises AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute '__dict__' inside dataclasses: charts.py defines a @dataclass under `from __future__ import annotations`, and dataclasses looks the class's module up in sys.modules. To prototype a whole change without touching a worktree, rsync the tree (minus .venv, .git, .task) to /tmp and run the worktree's .venv/bin/python -m pytest there with PYTHONPATH=<copy>/src. The venv's editable install is a plain __editable__ .pth path entry, so PYTHONPATH shadows it. For mypy, run the venv's mypy from the copy's root.

solar_challenge web/fleet_config.py after task 278's amendments (branch task/278, commits 415641d and f7df798, 2026-10-01; applies once merged): the shape helpers are _require_dict(value, field) and _dict_list(spec, key), formerly _require_mapping/_mapping_list. The user-facing text stays "<field> must be a mapping, got <type>". sample_distribution now normalises params through _build_distribution_dict({**params, "type": dist_type}) and samples from the spec that comes back. So every per-type default and every row conversion, including int(count), lives only in _build_distribution_dict. Pending task 312's text is stale on two points. It cites _require_mapping/_mapping_list, and it says a shuffled_pool count is converted both in _build_distribution_dict and in sample_distribution. Its Infinity-count OverflowError fix now has that one site, and it covers both routes.

Python dataclasses InitVar gotchas for solar_challenge's tests/_surface_forms.py. Measured by task 546's architect on 2026-10-07 (main ae29b86), identical on CPython 3.11.15, 3.12.3, 3.13.9 and 3.14.4 unless noted.
(1) dataclasses.fields() omits InitVars, but the generated __init__'s inspect.signature(cls) carries every one. That includes a string-annotated InitVar: dataclasses resolves 'InitVar[...]' against sys.modules[cls.__module__], so InitVar must be imported at module level there.
(2) An InitVar's default (e.g. `floor: InitVar[float] = 0.0`) stays in vars(cls) as a plain class attribute. A vars()-based member scan therefore reads it as a class constant ('float').
(3) An evaluated InitVar[T] has no typing origin and is not a class. Its repr is 'dataclasses.InitVar[...]' with T unrespelled: InitVar[Optional[float]] reads 'dataclasses.InitVar[typing.Optional[float]]' on 3.11-3.13 but 'dataclasses.InitVar[float | None]' on 3.14. Respell InitVar.type instead; task 546 plans exactly that.

content: solar_challenge (task 850 implementer, branch task/850 at fd55163, base main b3d45a3, 2026-10-17; holds once 850 merges): an unhashable dataclass field default such as MappingProxyType({}) is now caught in every per-task verify on the 3.12 pin by tests/unit/test_dataclass_defaults.py, not only by the offline lane's 3.11 interpreter-matrix case. The test imports every solar_challenge module through tests/_package_modules.py::package_modules, the walk test_docstring_examples.py also uses. It hashes every field default of each module-level dataclass and fails naming module.Class.field with the default's repr; the fix is dataclasses.field(default_factory=...). Known gap, measured on CPython 3.11.15 and 3.12.3: a default that hashes on 3.12 but whose class 3.11 judges unhashable, e.g. slice(1, 2), passes the census on the pin but raises ValueError at class definition on 3.11, so only the matrix catches it.

00bae4c9-b0ca-470c-8e68-0bcb474a2fc4.content: solar_challenge measurement (task 700 planning, main 0a5ab70, 2026-10-15, CPython 3.12.3). I ran a prototype receiver-based version of tests/_surface_forms.py::_attributes_set_on_self over the 41 classes that tests/unit/test_public_api_surface.py::_pinned_classes() pins. The prototype takes each non-static method's first parameter as the receiver, skips nested classes, and counts constant-name setattr and __setattr__ calls. It finds exactly the attributes the current self-only ast.walk finds. No pinned class uses another receiver name, setattr(), self.__dict__, vars(self) or a nested class. Only two pinned classes set an attribute under a computed name: FinanceConfig.__post_init__ calls object.__setattr__(self, field_name, whole_years) in a loop over the literal tuple ("loan_term_years", "asset_life_years"), and home.SimulationResults.__post_init__ calls object.__setattr__(self, name, series.rename(column)) in a loop over self._series_columns(). So task 700's proposal to raise TypeError on every computed-name set would make test_pinned_classes_declare_the_public_attributes_they_set_on_self error on main, unless the plan also handles those two classes. Once task 670 merges, undeclared_attributes' rule tests live in tests/unit/surface_forms_helper/test_undeclared_attributes.py and unset_attributes' in test_unset_attributes.py, not in tests/unit/test_surface_forms_helper.py.

23410657-69f0-4522-ac61-50450bfc5aca.content:
solar_challenge gotcha (verified 2026-10-08, task 350 planning): moving a frozen-surface name (anything in solar_challenge.__all__) to another module is safe only if two things hold.
1. The annotation text stays byte-identical. tests/unit/test_public_api_surface.py FROZEN_SURFACE pins the signature text, quotes included, e.g. scenario: 'ScenarioConfig'.
2. Every name an annotation spells is bound in the NEW module's globals or in its top-level `if TYPE_CHECKING:` imports. tests/_surface_forms.py::_evaluated resolves string annotations there to compute FROZEN_CLOSURE, and raises NameError otherwise.
The test pins no origin module. So re-pointing __init__._SYMBOL_MODULE and the TYPE_CHECKING `from solar_challenge.<new> import X as X` line is enough; test_every_name_resolves_and_caches checks the re-point.

candidates.content: solar_challenge_platform test convention (on main since task 597, verified at 650127d on 2026-10-08): tests/_alembic.py is the one public Alembic helper for tests. alembic_config(url) returns the repo's Config with script_location set absolutely, and upgraded_sqlite(db_file, revision) returns (cfg, engine) for a temp-FILE SQLite upgraded to a revision. New migration test modules should import these rather than copy a private _alembic_config, which test_private_names.py would forbid importing anyway. Use alembic_config("sqlite://") for a static ScriptDirectory chain-link check (tests/control/test_refresh_tick_store.py), and alembic_config(engine.url.render_as_string(hide_password=False)) to downgrade or upgrade a Timescale test database. tests/_migrated_engine.py::migrated_engine still yields an engine already at head.

Correction (solar_challenge_platform, measured on main 71793bd, 2026-10-13): tests/integration/test_rls_postgres.py does NOT yet take its Alembic Config from tests/_alembic.alembic_config on main. Its pg_rls_db fixture still builds Config(alembic.ini) + script_location + sqlalchemy.url itself. Only task 707's unmerged branch (commit e29a5ba) makes that change. Task 374's plan moves it, and every other copy in tests/, onto tests._alembic, and adds a one-home guard (tests/test_alembic_config_home.py). Check `git merge-base --is-ancestor <sha> main` before trusting a remembered "file X uses helper Y".

When testing Alembic `upgrade head` in-process (via alembic.config.Config + alembic.command.upgrade) in solar_challenge_platform, the test DB MUST be a temp FILE (pytest tmp_path_factory + sqlite:///<file>), never sqlite:///:memory:. Alembic opens its own connection for the upgrade and discards it; a separate reflection/ORM engine on :memory: would see an empty schema. PRACTICE: before a committed doc cites a follow-up, check list_tickets until the ticket shows status=created, then cite the task id rather than the tkt_ id. If the ticket failed, find the recovered task with search_tasks(query=<the title>, score_threshold=0.5) before you re-submit; re-submitting would duplicate the recovered task.

When a fused-memory ticket fails (status failed, reason server_restart), the candidate payload survives in the LIVE tickets store at data/reconciliation/tickets.db, table tickets. Columns: ticket_id, project_id, candidate_json, status, task_id, reason, result_json, created_at, resolved_at, expires_at, escalated_at. candidate_json is {project_root, kwargs: {title, description, details, priority, dependencies, tag, prompt}, metadata}. fused-memory/data/tickets.db is a 0-byte decoy. Ticket-to-task lookup mechanics (dark-factory fused-memory), learned 2026-08-17 chasing `tkt_0RS82XDT4WMAZHPA9H5P1KVAG5`:

The CHEAPEST way to find out what a ticket became is to call `resolve_ticket(ticket=..., project_root=...)` directly. If the ticket is already terminal it returns IMMEDIATELY with its final status — no blocking, no timeout risk, no worker involvement. `tkt_0RS82XDT4WMAZHPA9H5P1KVAG5` returned `{"status": "created", "task_id": "3918"}` in one call.

This is strictly better than reaching for `list_tickets` first, and avoids a trap: `list_tickets` defaults to a LAST-7-DAYS window. This ticket was filed 2026-08-09 and looked up on 2026-08-17 — 8 days old, so the default window would have returned nothing and read exactly like "no such ticket". You would have to pass an explicit `since` to see it at all. (Separately, `list_tickets` rows key the id as `ticket_id`, not `ticket`.)

So the order is: `resolve_ticket` first (works for terminal AND pending, returns the answer either way); fall back to `list_tickets(since=<well before the filing date>)` only when you need to enumerate or you don't have the ticket id.

Extends the existing lesson that "filed as ticket tkt_…" is not evidence work is tracked — resolve_ticket is the one-call way to discharge that check.

A non-planning_mode `submit_task` in dark-factory returns a TICKET id (`tkt_…`), not a task id — the curator decides create-vs-combine asynchronously — so filing is not complete until the ticket resolves. Do not conclude either success or failure from the immediate return. Verify with `list_tickets`: a resolved ticket shows `status: "created"` (or `"combined"`) with a non-null `task_id`; `status: "pending"` with `task_id: null` means still in flight. Timing observed 2026-08-12: one ticket sat `pending` for ~12 seconds while four sibling tickets in the same window resolved in 1-3 seconds — so a `pending` read is NOT evidence of failure, poll it rather than re-submitting (re-submitting risks a duplicate). After it resolves, `get_task` the returned id and check `metadata.curator_action`: `None` means it was created clean, whereas a `combine` means the curator folded your text into an EXISTING task and may have rewritten it — verify the description survived intact, since combine overwrites title/description/details wholesale. This matters more than it looks: 595 of 640 historical combines changed the target's description.

A resolve_ticket TIMEOUT is not a filing failure. On 2026-08-19 a submit_task followed by resolve_ticket(timeout_seconds=115) raised "The operation timed out", but the ticket was durable and the curator created the task anyway — tkt_0RSN703XVFRCXVMR4VWG1116XR resolved to task_id=4462, status=created, visible via list_tickets moments later. The ticket is persisted at submit time; resolve_ticket only BLOCKS on the curator's decision. ALWAYS confirm via list_tickets before re-filing, or the retry mints a duplicate task. Related curator behaviour observed the same day: submitting a candidate that duplicates in-flight work is correctly DROPPED with a reason naming the existing task (a candidate to fix the capability-manifest schema was dropped because task 4471 was already in-progress doing exactly that), so the two-phase flow also acts as a duplicate-detection pass and its refusals are successes, not errors.

mcp__fused-memory__resolve_ticket timing out does NOT mean the task filing failed — the curator may already have created the task. Observed 2026-08-05: submit_task returned tkt_0RS3JB7ZQZ4V3SAYMZNQPBGW2F, resolve_ticket then returned "The operation timed out", but the task (3655) had in fact been created. The way to find out safely is cancel_ticket, which returned {"status": "created", "no_op": true} — i.e. it refused to cancel because the ticket was already terminal, and reported the terminal status. A second resolve_ticket with an explicit short timeout_seconds then returned {"status": "created", "task_id": "3655"} immediately. So on a resolve_ticket timeout: call cancel_ticket to learn the true state before re-filing, otherwise a blind retry creates a duplicate task. Related: when all Claude accounts are usage-capped the curator cannot make LLM calls and legitimately stalls — get_curator_state reports paused=false with a soonest_open_at timestamp (13:00 UTC in this instance), which is a GATE, not a hang. Do not restart it.

GOTCHA (dark-factory, task 4484): an agent-authored ledger, gate, or plan step that requires a TASK ID for filed follow-up work is UNSATISFIABLE by an agent at filing time. `submit_task` is two-phase and returns `{"ticket": "tkt_..."}` only; the curator decides create/combine/drop asynchronously; and the agent operating instructions explicitly forbid calling `resolve_ticket`. So no task id exists when the agent writes the record.

DISTINCT from the existing `resolve-ticket-timeout-discriminator` topic, which is about how to interpret a resolve_ticket TIMEOUT. This is about the id-AVAILABILITY contract for agent-side records: the id is simply not available yet, timeout or not.

Eleven `submit_task` calls returned eleven tickets and zero task ids, so flipping the rows would either turn the gate red or bless a row pointing at a decision the curator had not made.

PRACTICE when you hit this shape:
1. Keep the pre-filing disposition (`to_file`, `pending`, whatever the vocabulary calls it) and record the TICKET id in the row. A ticket is durable and greppable; it is a real pointer, just not a task pointer.
2. State the reason ONCE — in a module docstring or schema comment — rather than repeating it per row; INV-9 (one-fact-one-home) applies to the explanation as much as to the data.
3. Name "flip to `filed` with the task id when the ticket resolves" as explicit follow-up work in the artifact, so the intermediate state is a recorded step and not drift.
4. File an `escalate_info` recording the deviation (task-3890 precedent): the plan text stays frozen in plan.json, so a reviewer diffing plan against code otherwise reads it as an oversight.

FOR PLAN AUTHORS: do not write a step that requires an agent to record a task id for work it files itself. Write "record the ticket id" instead, or make the gate accept either shape.
Involved with submit_task and resolve_ticket processes

How a machine-filed task is actually deduplicated in dark-factory's fused-memory (read from code 2026-09-18) — it is NOT "identical title". Three mechanisms sit on the `submit_task` (planning_mode omitted) path: (i) a store-level UNIQUE index `ux_tasks_candidate_key ON tasks(tag, candidate_key) WHERE candidate_key IS NOT NULL AND status != 'cancelled'`, where `fused_memory/middleware/candidate_key.py::compute_candidate_key(title, files)` hashes the normalised title AND the sorted files_to_modify; a collision raises a typed DuplicateCandidateKeyError. Consequences: changing the file list changes the key, and because only `cancelled` is excluded, a finding closed as `done` can never be re-filed with the same title+files even if the condition persists. (ii) `task_curator.py::TaskCurator._pre_llm_exact_match` consults the same key only through an in-process `_recent_creates` cache with a 600-second TTL, so a nightly filer never hits it. (iii) the LLM curator itself, best-effort (any failure degrades to `create`), whose candidate pools exclude only `cancelled` and whose `_STATUS_RANK` ranks `done` — so a `drop` can legally target a DONE task; only `combine` is restricted to pending. A sweep that files "owner task N is dead" findings can therefore have the finding dropped onto the very done task N it reports, leaving no task and a silent violation. Design consequence adopted for the INV-12 owner-liveness sweep: a periodic filer must carry its OWN idempotence key in task metadata (Tier-C `x_` key, accepted by `shared/src/shared/task_metadata.py`) and look it up read-only before filing, treating the curator as a backstop only. Also: `submit_task` returns a ticket (`tkt_…`), not a task id, unless planning_mode=True; no agent role in `orchestrator/src/orchestrator/agents/roles.py` holds `resolve_ticket` (architect, implementer, steward and deep reviewer hold `submit_task`; debugger, judge, merger, simple-task hold neither), so an agent can never learn the id of a follow-up it files. Tickets persist indefinitely (`ticket_store.py` has no delete path; expires_at is a 365-day placeholder), but a ticket can resolve `failed` with no task_id — `flush_pending_on_startup` fails every pending ticket with reason `server_restart` on each fused-memory restart.

Tool quirks met while operating the dark-factory task store and memory on 2026-10-11/12. (1) resolve_ticket can time out at the MCP transport while the curator still resolves the ticket; read data/reconciliation/tickets.db read-only (status, task_id) instead of re-submitting. A submission may come back `combined` into an existing task. (2) update_task refuses append=True together with metadata_mode='merge'; send the details append and the metadata write as two calls. (3) add_memory rejects a declared `entities` list unless each declared task is named in the content, and its completion-claim check reads a future action phrased as done ("task N cancelled as superseded") as a claim and files an unverified-claim L0. (4) scripts/cgroup-stall-ratio.py --json prints a table and then JSON, and its JSON headline reported null for the dark_factory verify-worker classes in six windows, because it counts only processes classified xdist-worker; read the per-scope table rows. That headline defect has no owner task.

Operational note confirmed again 2026-08-20: a `submit_task` -> `resolve_ticket` that times out is NOT a terminal failure and must be RETRIED, not treated as an error or re-submitted as a new ticket. Observed live this session: filing dark-factory task 4503 returned "The operation timed out" on the first resolve_ticket(timeout_seconds=115); an immediate retry with the SAME ticket id returned {"status":"created","task_id":"4503"}. Re-submitting instead of retrying would have created a duplicate. This is the expected behaviour whenever curation latency exceeds the caller's wait — and it commonly does, because curator p99 is ~156.7s while resolve_ticket's default wait is 115s. A historical instance of exactly this being MISREAD is recorded in esc-task-curator-3's resolution: a watcher cited a 110s resolve_ticket timeout as "a live reproduction of the cap", but the ticket ledger later showed the curation completed in ~118s — the call expired roughly 8 seconds before the curator decided, and the "capped curator" claim was fabricated from an unlucky timeout boundary. Check the durable ticket row (data/reconciliation/tickets.db) before concluding anything systemic from a single resolve_ticket timeout.

content: To tell whether an old submit_task ticket's owner is still live without holding resolve_ticket, read the ticket store read-only. The live file is /home/leo/src/dark-factory/data/reconciliation/tickets.db, table `tickets`, whose columns include ticket_id, status, task_id and reason. Two traps sit beside it: fused-memory/data/tickets.db and data/reconciliation/escalations/tickets.db are empty decoys with no `tickets` table. status 'created' or 'combined' gives the resolved task_id. Then read that task's metadata.x_coalesced_into, because a deferred task is often coalesced into a live successor. Graphiti curation gotchas learned executing curator gate 5325 (reify graph): (1) The entity resolver FOLDS a "DF Task NNNN" subject into an existing "Task NNNN" node on every extraction round — a distinct cross-project entity node cannot be created via add_memory; there is no create-entity or edge-endpoint-reassign primitive. Accepted pattern (per the f02a32ea god-node precedent): keep the fact on the folded node but make the fact TEXT self-disambiguating ("DF Task NNNN (dark_factory project's task NNNN — a DIFFERENT task from reify's task NNNN)"). (2) Re-adding a deleted/corrected fact can make the extraction pipeline RE-CREATE the very conflation you just removed: literal tokens like branch names ("task/2854") or "pre-renumber id NNNN" in the fact text get re-derived into wrong-subject edges. Write curation re-adds with extraction-safe wording — drop literal branch/old-id tokens from the fact body and keep that provenance in the task record or a decisions memory instead — then verify the derived edges after ingestion and delete any wrong-subject derivations before refreshing the entity summary.

fused-memory API quirks found 2026-09-30. get_task returns `id` as an int, while get_tasks pages return string ids, so compare with str(). update_memory and delete_memory require a `store` argument ('mem0'). In-place update_memory content amendment is refused unless agent_id starts with 'recon-stage-' or 'curator-' (Mem0UpdateNotAuthorized); to fix a wrong memory you wrote, add_memory a corrected copy, verify it, then delete_memory(store='mem0') the old one. submit_task(planning_mode=True) returns {task_id, status:'deferred'} synchronously; commit_planning(task_ids='N') then flips it to pending.

update_task METADATA WRITES CLOBBER memory_hints, not just the defer-to-edit path. Confirmed 2026-08-20 on reify task 5627: a plain `mcp__fused-memory__update_task(id=..., metadata={...})` call passing ONLY delivered_checks replaced memory_hints wholesale — the original {entities: ["Task 5847","Task 5758","Task 5412"], queries: [3 specific topic queries]} came back as {entities: [], queries: ["resolution for: <task title>"]}, an auto-generated LLM-backfill placeholder. This is the same class as the known defer-to-edit clobber but triggered by an ordinary metadata update. MITIGATION: always read back the full task record after any update_task metadata write and re-send memory_hints verbatim in a follow-up call if it was replaced; a backfilled placeholder LOOKS populated, so a shallow "the field is non-empty" check will not catch it (this is the wiped-field-refilled-masks-corruption failure mode).

ROOT MECHANISM of the fused-memory prose path-matcher false-positive class (established 2026-07-28 by reading the actual task records, not inferred): the matcher fires on ENGLISH SLASH-ALTERNATIONS of the form "X/Y" where Y is a lowercase English word, not a path component. Prior escalations repeatedly claimed "the token appears nowhere in the text" — in every case checked, it DID appear, just not as a path. Five witnesses:
- reify 5667, stamped corpus/ ← "already hosts corpus/compile helpers" (means "corpus or compile")
- reify 5678, stamped backend/ ← "found=false, not a backend/timeout error" (means "backend or timeout")
- reify 5679, stamped backend/ + tools/ ← self-referential: the task quotes 5678's own stamp
- dark_factory 2434, stamped memory/ ← "re-cite the existing memory/edges"
- dark_factory 3102, stamped crates/ ← cites a real reify path but only as EVIDENCE, not as a file it modifies
Note the last is a different failure from the first four: a genuine path correctly matched but wrongly read as ownership. Only the first four are a lexing bug. Corollary: a task ABOUT the path guard trips the path guard by quoting its tokens — that self-reference, not a new defect, explains the "ambiguous multi-owner match with no suggested_project" variant seen in esc-task-path-guard-27.

Completed: Pass the claude-code backend's prompt on stdin: a transcript over 128 KiB exceeds Linux's per-argument limit (claude_code.py::ClaudeCodeScopingModel._run)
Description: Found while planning task 8 (translate backend failures at the ScopingModel seam). src/scoping_intake/claude_code.py::ClaudeCodeScopingModel._run passes the whole prompt (NEXT_MESSAGE_INSTRUCTION plus transcript_document(transcript) for a reply, or transcript_document(transcript) for an analysis) as ONE argv element after `-p`. Linux caps a single argument at MAX_ARG_STRLEN = 32 pages = 131,072 bytes on this host (PAGE_SIZE 4096), while intake.py allows a transcript of up to MAX_TRANSCRIPT_CHARS = 300,000 characters. Measured 2026-10-08 with the worktree's Python: subprocess.run(['/bin/true', '-p', 'x' * 140_000]) raises OSError errno 7 'Argument list too long'; 100,000 characters succeed. So once a claude-code trial session's transcript document passes roughly 131 KB, every reply, retry and write-up fails with OSError(E2BIG). That error escapes the seam untranslated and the prospect page shows the generic 500 'Something went wrong on our side'. The session cannot recover, because retrying resends the same transcript. The other long arguments are small: analyst prompt 16,828 bytes, interviewer prompt 12,364 bytes, record schema JSON 8,556 bytes.
Analysis: ## Current state (base 57ecf41, task 8 merged; 59 tests green, measured in this worktree)

- `src/scoping_intake/claude_code.py::ClaudeCodeScopingModel._run` builds the command `[executable, "-p", prompt, "--system-prompt", system_prompt, "--tools", "", "--restricted", "--model", model, "--output-format", "json"]`, adding `"--json-schema", schema` for an analysis.
- It then calls `subprocess.run(command, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=..., cwd=..., env=..., check=False)` with no stdin, so claude inherits the server's stdin.
- `reply` passes `f"{NEXT_MESSAGE_INSTRUCTION}\n\n{transcript_document(transcript)}"` and `analyse` passes `transcript_document(transcript)`.
- `intake.py` lets a conversation grow to MAX_TRANSCRIPT_CHARS = 300,000 characters, in messages of at most MAX_MESSAGE_CHARS = 20,000.

## Facts measured for this plan

1. **The argument limit.** With 4096-byte pages, an argument of 131,071 bytes runs and one of 131,072 bytes raises OSError errno 7 (E2BIG) in the parent, before the child starts. A 300,000-character transcript gives a 300,056-character document and a 300,179-byte reply prompt.
2. **`claude -p` reads its prompt from stdin.**
   - `claude --help` (2.1.294) gives the usage as `claude [options] [command] [prompt]`.
   - `-p, --print` is a flag ("Print response and exit (useful for pipes)"), so the prompt is the positional argument, not the value of -p.
   - `--input-format` is "(only works with --print): text (default), or stream-json".
   - The installed binary was also read statically with grep -a and dd. Nothing was executed and nothing was spent.
   - Its getInputPrompt reads stdin when stdin is not a TTY. It decodes it as UTF-8 (`process.stdin.setEncoding("utf8")`) up to 10 MiB. Once data arrives it waits for EOF; its 3-second timer fires only when no data arrives at all.
   - It returns `[promptArgument, stdin].filter(Boolean).join("\n")`. The no-input error reads "Input must be provided either through stdin or as a prompt argument when using --print".
   - So with no positional prompt, claude's prompt is exactly what we write to stdin.
3. **No hang in the RED run.** Under pytest's default fd capture, which verify uses through plain `uv run pytest`, a child's fd 0 is /dev/null (measured). A stand-in that reads stdin therefore gets '' at once against today's code.
4. **Throwaway-copy trial.** The setup: `git archive HEAD` into /tmp, run with PYTHONPATH=<copy>/src.
   - With the planned test file, today's code fails exactly two tests, in 2.6 s: the reply test, because stdin is '', and the new long-conversation test, with OSError [Errno 7] Argument list too long.

Description: Agent follow-up found while planning task 195 (escalation id agent-followup-195). OUT OF SCOPE for task 195. That task removes PVConfig.module_efficiency and PVConfig.temperature_coefficient and refuses them in scenario YAML. It does not touch the inverter.

CODE FACT (main d4a416d): src/solar_challenge/pv.py::_inverter_and_wiring sets inverter_params["Pdco"] = Paco / config.inverter_efficiency only when config.inverter_efficiency != 0.96.
- The default, and an explicit 0.96, both keep the voltage-matched CEC inverter's own Pdco.
- Any other value overrides it.
- The PVConfig docstring documents the field as "Inverter efficiency as fraction (default 0.96 = 96%)". This is the same default-sentinel pattern that made temperature_coefficient a no-op (task 195).

MEASURED on 2026-09-30, worktree task/195 at d4a416d, CPython 3.12.3, pvlib 0.15.1. Paco/Pdco of the system create_pv_system builds with inverter_efficiency=0.96 (default or explicit):
- 3.0 kW: 0.9547
- 3.68 kW: 0.9406
- 4.0 kW: 0.9667
- 5.0 kW: 0.9711
- 6.0 kW: 0.9727
With inverter_efficiency=0.9601, every capacity gives exactly 0.9601.

EFFECTS:
- The documented 96% default is not what the model uses.
- A fleet diversity distribution over pv.inverter_efficiency (src/solar_challenge/config.py PVDistributionConfig.inverter_efficiency) has a discontinuity at exactly 0.96. A home sampled at 0.96 keeps the catalogue efficiency, while its neighbours get the sampled value.

WORK (suggested): decide the semantics. Options:
- inverter_efficiency: Optional[float] = None, meaning "the catalogue inverter's own", with any value always overriding Pdco;
- always apply the configured value.
PVConfig is in solar_challenge.__all__, so a signature or default change falls under review/briefing.yaml's frozen-surface rule (version bump plus a note in docs/domain-library-consumption.md; task 195 bumps to 0.6.0). Add a test that an explicit 0.96 yields Paco/Pdco == 0.96, or whatever the chosen semantics give.

candidates.content: solar_challenge_platform technique, measured by the task 1039 architect on 2026-10-15 at main 314e8ea: you can test a package __init__ reduction (re-exports removed) against the whole suite without editing the tree. Write a pytest plugin module in a temp dir that, at import, does `spec = importlib.util.spec_from_loader("<pkg>", loader=None, is_package=True)`, builds the module from it, sets `module.__path__` to the real package directory, and assigns it to sys.modules["<pkg>"]. Then run `PYTHONPATH=<tempdir> .venv/bin/python -m pytest -p <plugin> -m 'not slow' --collect-only -q`, plus a targeted functional run. `-p` loads the plugin before any conftest. A fresh-interpreter probe of sys.modules (subprocess with sys.executable -c) shows what each import loads before and after the change.

solar_challenge_platform architect recipe, used by task 983 on 2026-10-14. It proves a planned test is RED against current code and GREEN against a candidate implementation, without copying the tree or touching the worktree, and git status stays clean.
1. Write the modified test module to /tmp/<task>-probe/test_x.py.
2. Write the candidate function to /tmp/<task>-probe/candidate.py as a standalone module.
3. From the worktree root, run `PYTHONPATH=<worktree> uv run --extra dev pytest -c pyproject.toml --rootdir=<worktree> -p no:cacheprovider /tmp/<task>-probe/test_x.py > log 2>&1`.
4. For GREEN, change the test copy's one import line to `from candidate import ...`. pytest's prepend import mode puts /tmp/<task>-probe on sys.path, so that import resolves.
PYTHONPATH makes `tests._timescale_container` and `tests._migrated_engine` importable. tests/conftest.py is not loaded for a file outside tests/. For src changes that span modules, use the whole-tree git-archive copy instead (memory faa3da26).

solar_challenge_platform architect technique (task 810, 2026-10-14): to run the real test suite, Docker lane included, against a candidate change without editing the task worktree, use a scratch copy. Tar the worktree into /tmp, excluding .venv, .git, node_modules and .task. Apply the candidate files there. Run the worktree's own .venv/bin/python -m pytest from the copy's root with PYTHONPATH=<copy>/src. PYTHONPATH outranks the editable install's .pth entry, so the copy's package is imported, and tests/_alembic.py resolves alembic.ini and migrations/ relative to the copy.

Procedure (solar_challenge_platform, task 793 architect, 2026-10-10): measure who constructs a value type with some property across the whole suite before adding a __post_init__ invariant.
1. Write a throwaway pytest plugin outside the repo, e.g. /tmp/<task>-probe/naive_row_probe.py.
2. In pytest_configure, wrap the class's __init__. dataclasses.replace also goes through __init__, so the wrapper sees those copies too.
3. Each call records the property, the current test nodeid (set by a pytest_runtest_protocol hookwrapper) and the first caller frame outside the plugin and dataclasses.py.
4. In pytest_sessionfinish, dump the records as JSON.
5. Run it with `PYTHONPATH=/tmp/<task>-probe uv run --extra dev pytest -p naive_row_probe -m 'not slow'`.
Task 793 found 15 naive TelemetryRows among 1,469,599 this way: 9 tests, and one src site, raw_telemetry.read_raw_rows on SQLite. Tests that a nested pytest or a subprocess runs are not seen.

To verify a test-file split is a faithful move (measured on task 875's amend, 2026-10-11), compare those node IDs before and after with the file path stripped (sed 's#^tests/.../test_[a-z_]*\.py::##' | sort), then reverse any renames with sed and diff the moved blocks against `git show HEAD:<old file>`.

solar_challenge_platform testing gotcha (measured 2026-09-30, task 544 architect, base 8e89ef2). (1) runtime.asgi builds its graph at import time, so only the first import in a pytest process runs the build, and spies placed around a later cached import see nothing. To pin what serving scp-api constructs, execute the module afresh: spec = importlib.util.find_spec("solar_challenge_platform.runtime.asgi"); module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec); spec.loader.exec_module(module), inside db.session.repoint_scope(). This registers nothing in sys.modules. runpy.run_module emits a RuntimeWarning when the module is already imported, and importlib.reload mutates the cached module that other tests share. solar_challenge_platform pytest collect-only, measured 2026-10-12 by the task 984 architect: `pytest --collect-only --verbosity=-1` prints one node id per line, whatever verbosity pyproject's addopts (`-v --tb=short`) sets, because an explicit --verbosity after addopts overrides it. `-qq` works only while addopts carries exactly one -v. With nothing selected, pytest exits 5 and stdout STARTS with that blank line, so read the node ids as the lines before the first blank line (itertools.takewhile(bool, ...)), not with partition('\n\n'). content: solar_challenge_platform technique (task 967 architect, 2026-10-17): to show a refactor of test fixtures leaves each test's inputs as they were, record what every test builds, then diff before and after. Write a throwaway pytest plugin module in a /tmp directory. It wraps the library constructor, e.g. solar_challenge.BatteryConfig.__init__, and stores the first instance built per item.nodeid, setting the current nodeid in a pytest_runtest_call hookwrapper. pytest_sessionfinish dumps the records to JSON. Load it with PYTHONPATH=<that dir> and `-p <module>`, once on the original tree and once on a scratch copy with the refactor, then compare per node id. Only the first instance per test is the test's own input: dataclasses.replace inside the code under test constructs further instances through the same __init__. Applied to task 967, this showed no SoC band change in any of the 21 test_param_search cases, and that only build_candidate_set-only cases changed capacity.

CONVENTION + CORRECTION for dark-factory tests/scripts guards that read a marked span of a document. Measured 2026-09-23 in task 5690's amendment pass.

The loud marker-extraction mechanic already has ONE home: `tests/scripts/verify_command_invariants.py::marked_span` (task 4108).
