Add an is_file() sentinel so a mis-resolved root fails loudly instead of scanning nothing, per silent_fallthrough_scan.py / test_safe_io.py.
2. Pair the byte scan with an anti-vacuity assertion, because "contains no raw literal" is trivially satisfiable by DELETING the text. Read the docstring back with ast.get_docstring(ast.parse(source)) on the SAME text the scan read — not via module.__doc__, which reintroduces trap 1 — and assert the decoded docstring still contains the specimens. Raw-bytes-absent AND decoded-specimens-present is jointly satisfiable only by escaping.

Also: re-spelling an existing hand-written drift-guard tuple with `\x3c` does NOT weaken it — the escape is byte-identical at runtime, so the tuple stays an independent pin. Do not "modernise" such a tuple by deriving it from the constant it guards; that turns its drift test into a tautology. Precedent: shared/tests/test_toolcall_markup.py::_TRIPWIRE_TUPLE_TODAY.

CORRECTION to the "sanctioned STRUCTURAL drift guard" carve-out recorded in mem0 b80b78c4 (which cites tests/scripts/test_contributing_lint_command_drift.py and its HTML-comment-marker convention as the approved way to pin a doc against live code). That carve-out is NOT reliably sanctioned and should not be planned as a safe pattern. On task 3465 an architect followed it exactly — bare `<!-- name:begin/end -->` marker spans in skills/escalation-watcher-auto/SKILL.md and OPERATIONS.md, values derived from live producer constants via stdlib `ast` rather than hardcoded, loud-failing extractors that raise instead of returning empty, explicit STRUCTURE-NEVER-WORDING discipline — and reviewer_comprehensive still blocked the whole 769-line module as a documentation/introspection meta-test and mandated deletion. That is the second such data point: task 3544 (mem0 3c294ce3) had a mermaid-vs-TRANSITIONS parity test deleted despite a live in-code oracle. Two independent blocks means the reviewer treats "derived from code at runtime" and "anchored on markers" as insufficient — what it keys on is that the ASSERTION TARGET is doc prose, a module-level/function-body string literal, or a parameter name recovered by introspection. Practical rule for architects: before planning any producer→consumer mirror guard, first check whether the producer's OWN package already asserts those tokens against real produced OUTPUT; on 3465 fused-memory/tests/test_scope_violation_escalator.py already called the real report_rejection() and asserted category/agent_role/severity on the escalation JSON that landed on disk, so the entire guard was redundant with existing behaviour coverage. Same held for its two "premise guard" tests: escalation/tests/test_server.py, escalation/tests/test_queue.py and orchestrator/tests/test_workflow_status_on_resume.py already cover the granted_files grant end-to-end, so an introspection check on the parameter NAME was both redundant and strictly weaker. Also: when deleting such a guard, the doc-side marker spans and any prose sentence claiming the tokens are "pinned by <test file>" must be deleted with it — a SKILL.md is read verbatim as an LLM system prompt, so a dangling reference to a deleted test tells the executing agent a mechanism exists when it does not.

MCP tool-call envelope markup can still leak into a task description as of 2026-08-18, DESPITE the containment guard having shipped — there is a live bypass, and it silently corrupts a field value.

WHAT WAS OBSERVED (recon Stage 2, run d0f2b5dc-84c1-4060-91df-7c8b84476b73, by direct get_task against the live task store): an in-progress dark_factory task's description column carried a trailing leaked envelope fragment — a stray closing description tag followed by a serialized parameter element naming priority with the value "low". (Described in prose deliberately; spelling the raw literals re-triggers the write-time tripwire and reproduces the truncation bug. Escaped conventions live in shared/src/shared/toolcall_markup.py and docs/mcp-toolcall-xml-leak.md.)

THE PART THAT MATTERS IS THE SILENTLY WRONG VALUE, not the stray text: the fragment declared priority "low" while the task's actually-stored priority was "medium". The intended field value was absorbed into description prose and a different value persisted. That reproduces the exact failure mode task 3141 cites as its motivating incident (DF 3083: task 3210 filed priority=high, stored as medium).

WHY THIS READS AS A BYPASS RATHER THAN A KNOWN-UNFIXED INSTANCE: the three tasks owning this defect class are all in terminal state — 3141 (markup_tripwire rejecting raw envelope markup at the add_memory / add_episode / submit_task / update_task boundaries), 2939 (read-only detector scripts/scan_task_toolcall_leaks.py), 2944 (sweep over ~32 affected tasks). The specimen task's routing history begins 2026-08-17, after all three. So the guard exists and the corpus was swept, yet a fresh instance still landed.

PRIMARY HYPOTHESIS, UNVERIFIED — CONFIRM BEFORE FIXING: the filing PATH avoids the guard rather than the guard's pattern list being wrong. The specimen carries source="agent-followup" / spawn_context="agent_followup" and was not filed through an interactive curator submit_task call. Task 2563 documents this hole's general shape for a different writer: "planning_mode (PRD batches — the dominant filing path) bypasses all of them."

GENERALIZABLE LESSON WORTH CARRYING FORWARD: a write-time tripwire is only as good as the set of writers routed through it. When a guard task reaches done, "this defect class is contained" is a claim about the ONE boundary that was instrumented — not about the column it protects. Verify coverage per WRITER, not per guard, and prefer the unbypassable shared chokepoint every caller passes through (the argument task 3588 makes for the submit_task boundary). The same reasoning applies to any future guard filed against a corpus-corruption class.

TRACKING: dark_factory task 4419 (execution_class=code_tdd) is intended to own the guard gap and a fresh corpus re-scan. Task 4228 concerns only markup_tripwire.py's docstring spelling literals raw and is unrelated to enforcement coverage.

Task 4659 (architect, 2026-08-24) is a THIRD data point for the anti-doc-meta-test norm in mem0 48e2b53d/b80b78c4 — this time caught at PLANNING time rather than by a review block. The task description itself instructed building a `skills/*/SKILL.md`-grepping guard ("a three-line addition to that _GUARDED_DOCS tuple", "cheap"); the plan was drafted with that guard, then revised to impl-only after finding `orchestrator/tests/test_roles_ancestry_check.py:33-37` rejects the identical construction by name as "a documentation meta-test". Practical lesson for architects: a task DESCRIPTION recommending a doc-grepping structural guard is not evidence the pattern is sanctioned — tasks 4095 (guard is this shape, stranded in-progress) and 4400 both still point at it. Check the norm before planning, not after. Tracked for reconciliation as task 4666.

Separate concrete gotcha from the same task: a doc's negative-example escape marker MUST be copied from the consuming guard's own `_NEGATIVE_MARKER` constant, never invented. Commit 9fd6895ccc shipped `<!-- provenance-derivation:negative-example -->` into three SKILL.md files while task 4095's guard defines `_NEGATIVE_MARKER = "provenance-guard: negative"` — mismatched, so the markers suppressed nothing and the docs' own stated prohibitions would have been flagged as violations. When the guard lives on an unmerged branch, read it with `git show <branch>:<path>` rather than guessing the spelling.

CONVENTION for the dark-factory module-config guard tests (tests/scripts/test_scripts_module_config.py and siblings) that parse a declared lint/type/test command: (1) Distinguish WRAPPER flags from CHECKER flags by ANCHOR POSITION, and take the split from the shared `_anchor_split` helper (`_pre_anchor_tokens` / `_post_anchor_tokens`) rather than hand-rolling `shlex.split(_segment(cmd, kw))` + `tokens.index(kw)` at the call site — duplicate copies of that logic are the drift the helper exists to end, and the hand-rolled form raises a bare ValueError instead of the helper's diagnostic when the anchor is absent. (2) Any helper reading a flag VALUE must accept BOTH spellings, `--flag value` and `--flag=value`: `uv run --project=shared pyright scripts/` is an exactly equivalent uv invocation, so an exact-token scan yields a FALSE RED whose message claims the command selects no environment at all. `_narrowing_flag_args` already prefix-matches for this reason; `_uv_project_member` (task 4358) folds both spellings plus the three no-usable-selector cases into a `str | None`. (3) Read tables out of the root pyproject.toml with a guarded `.get` chain (the `_load_root_pyright_config` shape), never raw chained indexing — a restructured table should fail naming the missing table, not as a bare KeyError that reads as a broken test.

No test in dark-factory asserts on CLAUDE.md *content* — its ~15 .py references are all docstring/comment pointers (e.g. shared/tests/test_task_metadata.py:526 citing "CLAUDE.md field-combo presets"), so CLAUDE.md doc tasks are impl-only with no meta-test. Keeping it short is a measured cost constraint rather than style: CLAUDE.md is auto-loaded into every agent call from cwd, and fused-memory/tests/test_config_schema.py:737-752 records that "filing-project CLAUDE.md growth" eroded the path-scope adjudicator's budget floor until it returned error_max_budget_usd and became a silent no-op. New Task Routing subsections should match the density of the existing "Deterministic task kind" section and cross-reference the PRD for rationale.

SIGHTING under topic `vacuous-test-guard` (task 4108 amendment pass, 2026-09-07) — a NEW LOCATION for the canonical entry's "PARAMETER SUPPLIES THE DISCRIMINATOR" shape, plus a detection route the canonical entry does not name.

THE SHAPE: A GUARD'S "THE MESSAGE NAMES THE ARTIFACT" ASSERTION SATISFIED BY A CALLER-SUPPLIED STRING. `tests/scripts/test_contributing_type_check_command_drift.py` asserts that every extractor failure message contains `"CONTRIBUTING.md"` and the marker literal — the whole vacuity contract of a tier-2 INV-10 mirror guard. It passed. But the begin-marker-count message named no artifact at all; the assertion was satisfied because the caller happened to spell "CONTRIBUTING.md" into a `label` argument that the message interpolated. Nothing in the message-FORMATTING code contributed the token the test was checking for. Same shape as the canonical entry's parametrized-discriminator bullet, one level down: the discriminator arrived through an argument, so the test proved a property of its own call site rather than of the code.

THE DETECTION ROUTE, distinct from the canonical entry's mutation test: EXTRACT THE HELPER AND UNIT-TEST IT WITH NEUTRAL ARGUMENTS. Lifting the four marker assertions into `tests/scripts/verify_command_invariants.py::marked_span` and testing it with a synthetic `label` that did NOT contain the filename made the gap fail immediately. Deduplication and vacuity-detection turn out to be the same operation here: a copy tested only through its real caller can never distinguish "the code supplies this" from "my caller does". Worth reaching for when the mutation test is awkward because the thing to mutate is a message string rather than a constant.

THE FIX, generalised: a shared assertion helper must put every identifying token — artifact, marker, task id — into EVERY message itself, never rely on a caller having stuffed one into a label. And a message test should assert against a fixture whose caller-supplied strings are deliberately neutral.

ACCRETION: appended as a peer under `vacuous-test-guard`; see the canonical entry for the other shapes and the mutation test.

CANONICAL (consolidates c80cb400-be6b-40c3-a2cf-d76e3f959f01 [2026-08-16, same task-3471 review] into this entry). In dark-factory tests, do NOT enforce test-authoring conventions by having a test read its OWN module source (`Path(__file__).read_text()`) and regex-match the syntactic spelling of sibling call sites. Originally surfaced in the dashboard source-as-text suites, but the rule is general.

Task 3471 shipped three such "every table entry must be consumed via this exact call shape" guards and ALL THREE were blocking review findings (reviewer_comprehensive, meta-test class). Three independent reasons:
1. They assert the FORMATTING of test code rather than production behaviour.
2. They fail on semantically identical refactors — e.g. binding a pattern to a local before searching.
3. They cannot close the hole they claim to: iterating an EXISTING contract table never sees a freshly written non-conforming assertion, so they never deliver the "front door" guarantee they advertise.

INSTEAD: state the convention as prose/a comment above the table and rely on code review to enforce it; keep the executable guard pointed at the REAL artifact (e.g. mutation-testing the tabled regexes against the actual .jsx) rather than at the test module's own text.

GOTCHA for anyone asked to "add a class / action / gate to docs/escalation-standing-policy.md" (task 5374 wrote it; task 5723 is the first follow-on, and there will be more). THREE of that document's `## ` sections are MACHINE-BOUND VOCABULARIES, not prose lists — "Reversible actions", "Human-forever gates" and "First-tranche candidate classes". tests/scripts/test_shadow_ruling_doc_contract.py::test_documented_slugs_equal_the_live_vocabulary holds the leading backticked token of every bullet under each heading equal, IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, to REVERSIBLE_ACTIONS / HUMAN_FOREVER_GATES / FIRST_TRANCHE_CLASSES in escalation/src/escalation/shadow_ruling.py. So adding a bullet under one of those three headings is a CODE change, not a docs change: it goes red until the matching frozenset is edited too.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE RED. Membership in FIRST_TRANCHE_CLASSES is exactly what makes a class STAMPABLE — ShadowRuling.__post_init__ rejects any ruling_class outside it. A class that is a constraint on how a record may be CLOSED (a policy statement binding everyone) becomes, if parked in that list, a candidate for an L2 session to close one AUTONOMOUSLY. That is an inversion of intent, and the guard that catches it is the drift test, not anything semantic. Check what a list is bound to BEFORE choosing where a new item goes.

TWO MECHANICAL FACTS measured at main a98e83cde1 while planning 5723:
- The extractor is `^- \`([a-z0-9_]+)\`` scoped by exact heading, so it sees UNDERSCORED leading tokens only. A hyphenated slug (`scope-not-delivered`) is structurally invisible to it and is also rejected by the live parse_shadow_ruling — hyphen-vs-underscore is usable as a checkable mark of "policy vocabulary, not codec vocabulary" in the same file.
- `_section(text, heading, level="### ")` INCLUDES any `#### ` subsections, because `"#### x".startswith("### ")` is False (the fourth char is `#`, not a space). Relied on to extract skills/escalation-watcher/SKILL.md's `### \`design_concern\`` body together with its `#### Standing rule ...` subsection.

The contract file's own docstring states its scope as "STRUCTURE ONLY, NEVER PROSE" — honour that. A presence guard for a new documentation policy belongs on structural anchors (a `<!-- slug:begin/end -->` marked span, a leading backticked token, a repo-relative path), the shape tests/scripts/test_line_pin_policy.py already records for a two-home policy.

CORRECTION + EXPANSION of memory 691895ed-d0b6-4298-9f0d-5d202c6f5f45 (the "claude CLI resolved from bare PATH at one site" note). That entry is still right about the SITE but WRONG about the blast radius, and its line pins have drifted. It could not be amended in place (content_amend is restricted to recon-stage-/curator- agents), hence this superseding note. Re-measured 2026-09-11 during task 4448 plan revalidation.

THE SITE (unchanged, now cited by symbol): `shared/src/shared/cli_invoke.py::build_claude_argv` builds `cmd = ['claude', '--print', '--output-format', 'json']`. Since task 2465 BOTH spawn paths route through it — `orchestrator/src/orchestrator/agents/invoke.py` imports it rather than keeping its own literal — so this one line governs sandbox and non-sandbox agent spawns alike.

THE CORRECTION. The old note said only two assertions pin the literal `'claude'` as argv[0]. There are FIVE, across TWO files. Grep both; do not trust a remembered count:
- `shared/tests/test_build_claude_argv.py` — two golden-argv lists, PLUS a provenance test (task 3147) that pins `'claude'` in its `supplied` token set AND separately asserts `cmd[0] == 'claude'` in its structural walk. Do not weaken that one to `.endswith('claude')`: exact provenance of every non-flag token is its entire purpose.
- `shared/tests/test_cli_invoke_sandbox_wrap.py` — asserts `argv[0] == 'claude'` on argv captured through `invoke_claude_agent`. Its intent is "no sandbox wrapper was prepended", not "argv[0] is a bare name".

THE OVER-REPORT, which is why the naive grep misleads in the other direction too. A plain `grep "'claude'"` also returns ~15 hits that are NOT affected, because they pin a backend NAME rather than argv[0]: every `orchestrator/tests` hit is `kwargs['backend'] == 'claude'` / `cfg.backends.architect == 'claude'`, or mocks `build_claude_argv` outright. And the `['claude','--x']` assertions in `test_cli_invoke.py` are on `_run_subprocess`, which receives `cmd` as a parameter and never calls the builder. Backend-name-vs-argv[0] is the discriminator.

RELATED CONSTRAINT for anyone changing this. A `resolve_claude_binary`-style helper must NOT raise. Several suites reach `build_claude_argv` in environments with no `claude` on PATH (`test_cli_input_rejected.py`, `startup_completion_probe.py`, fused-memory's `test_judge.py` and `test_recon_amend_tool_advertisement.py`), so a raising resolver turns a curator-only defect into a fleet-wide spawn outage. Resolve fail-open; enforce separately at startup.

content: As of 2026-10-12 (task 5840), all three CLAUDE.md bullet-recipe guards in tests/scripts/ wrap verify_command_invariants.marked_span through an identical private _marked_command: test_checkout_root_anchor_convention.py, test_package_source_lookup_convention.py and test_tasks_db_schema_convention.py. The only differences are source and task. Ticket tkt_0RVQF1J7RWBXQK493E8Q5RWAV7 proposes a shared vci.marked_bullet_command(text, *, slug, bullet_label, source, task). Before writing a fourth bullet guard, check whether that helper has landed and use it rather than copying the wrapper.

candidates.content: Reify orphan-audit G-allow pin gotcha for DELETION tasks (distinct from the consumer-wiring case): the new_orphans_<date>_g_allow.rs / engine_seam_orphans_g_allow.rs pins in crates/reify-audit/tests/ also break when a task DELETES the source file that hosts a `// G-allow:`-marked pub fn. The fn then vanishes from the tree, landing in NEITHER orphans[] nor allowed[], so assertion (b) trips "expected exactly 1 entry in allowed[]; 0 entries". Two traps: (1) the pin lives in reify-audit, a DIFFERENT crate than the deleted src, so a task scoped to other crates hits it only at verify time; (2) a workspace grep of the deletion's own target symbols will MISS it when the pinned fn name is an incidental G-allow orphan unrelated to those symbols (e.g. task ο #5065 deleted reify-runtime/src/concurrent.rs whose `default_populate_priorities` was pinned, unrelated to the ConcurrentScheduler/ConcurrentEdit* stack being removed). Fix: any task deleting files under crates/reify-*/src must also `rg -F <deleted-file-path>` AND grep pinned fn names across crates/reify-audit/tests/*_g_allow.rs, and delete the matching PINS row (+ its header-doc bullet + bucket count) in the same change. Per the file's removal contract a pin whose fn no longer exists must be removed.

Moving a reify `pub fn` (or a whole file) to a new module path can red gates in OTHER crates that pin source paths. (1) Any fn carrying a `// G-allow:` marker is pinned by exact `file.ends_with(<old path>)` in a crates/reify-audit/tests/new_orphans_*_g_allow.rs / engine_seam_orphans_g_allow.rs pin row, which must be repointed in the same diff (e.g. reify-lsp compute_document_symbols in new_orphans_2026_06_09_g_allow.rs). (2) crates/reify-compiler/tests/harness_ctor_conformance_survey/sweep.rs INLINE_FIXTURE_PINNED_HOSTS pins named .rs files to a floor of admitted raw-string Reify snippets (crates/reify-lsp/src/analysis.rs floor 8), so moving test fixtures out of a pinned host can drop it below its floor. Before moving, find these pins with `git grep -n '<old/path.rs>' -- crates tests scripts`.

Adding a new `pub fn` under crates/reify-audit/src/ fails `cargo test -p reify-audit --test g_allow` unless it has a non-test caller in a DIFFERENT file: scripts/audit-orphan-producers.sh excludes tests, the defining file itself, and `pub use` re-exports when counting callers. So a pub fn called only by a same-file wrapper (e.g. `check` delegating to `check_with_stats`) still counts as an orphan and needs a `// G-allow: <reason>` comment on the line immediately above the declaration — same situation as the existing `tasks_db_path`/`is_swept_ext` markers in src/ptodo.rs.

Reify reify-audit live G-allow gates only scan `// G-allow:` marker lines via `g_allow_marker_body` (plain `///`/`//!`/`//` comments citing #NNNN are NOT flagged). EXCEPTION: `engine_seam_g_allow_cites_live.rs::scan_pins_blocks` also scans the plain `//` comment blocks AFTER `const PINS` in `engine_seam_orphans_g_allow.rs` and extracts owner cites from them — so bare terminal cites in those PINS provenance comments DO fire g-allow-orphaned in the engine-seam Test B (real DB), even though the repo-wide `check()` gate allowlists all of crates/reify-audit/. Repo-wide gate does scan crates/reify-*/tests/*.rs that are NOT under reify-audit (e.g. mesh-morph tests/), but again only `// G-allow:` lines. Two orphan-producer pin tests (`engine_seam_orphans_g_allow.rs`, `stats_g_allow.rs`) require a still-orphan pub fn to KEEP its marker; `diagnostics_g_allow.rs` was already inverted to assert its 4 recorders are wired (markers vestigial, safe to delete).

reify-audit's tests/g_allow.rs (via scripts/audit-orphan-producers.sh, PUB_FN_RE = `^\s*pub(\([^)]*\))?\s+...fn`) treats `pub(crate) fn` exactly like `pub fn`. Any such fn whose ONLY callers are tests, its own defining file, or a `pub use` re-export is an orphan and reds the test unless it carries a `// G-allow:` marker; a fn with a real non-test caller in another src file needs no marker (that is why scan_util.rs's pub(crate) fns carry none). TDD consequence: introduce a new pub(crate) helper in the SAME impl commit that wires its first non-test caller, or the intermediate commits leave g_allow red.

CORRECTION to memory d70c7477-13d3-4338-b84e-0bc66a643def, which says reify-audit's orphan-audit counts "only inter-crate (external file) call sites". The operative granularity is the FILE, not the crate, and the parenthetical is the accurate half. Measured 2026-09-18 in task 7550 by running `bash scripts/audit-orphan-producers.sh --scope crates/reify-audit/src` and reading its PUB_FN_RE.

What the script (scripts/audit-orphan-producers.sh, driven by `cargo test -p reify-audit --test g_allow`, asserts orphan_count==0) actually does:
- PUB_FN_RE is `^\s*pub(\([^)]*\))?\s+...fn\s+(\w+)`, so the optional visibility-qualifier group DOES match `pub(crate) fn`, `pub(super) fn`, `pub(in path) fn`. Those are scanned exactly like `pub fn`. A bare `fn`, and trait-method / trait-impl declarations, are not scanned.
- A call site in any file OTHER than the declaring one counts as a caller. So a `pub(crate)` helper called from a sibling module of the SAME crate has callers and passes with no marker. Only a fn whose sole callers live in its own declaring file — typically its own inline `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` — is reported as an orphan.

Both halves were exercised in one diff:
- Widening two private ptodo.rs helpers (`path_present_in_tracked`, `is_terminal_status`) to `pub(crate)` and calling them from a NEW pdcheck.rs needed no G-allow marker; they never appeared in the report.
- Two `pub fn`s in pdcheck.rs whose only callers were that same file plus its inline test module were flagged (orphan_count 2, failing both `reify_audit_pub_fns_are_g_allow_marked` and `orphan_audit_survives_ambient_hook_git_env`).

PREFER NARROWING OVER MARKING. For that second case the correct fix was dropping them to private `fn`, not adding a marker — an inline `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` reaches private items via `super::`. Reach for `// G-allow: <reason>` only when a SEPARATE crate genuinely needs the item public, which in this crate means a tests/*.rs integration binary (it cannot see crate-private items). The marker must sit on the line IMMEDIATELY above the declaration: the script reads lines[idx-1], so a doc comment between marker and fn breaks it.

In reify, `pub fn`s in crates/reify-test-support need NO `// G-allow:` orphan-producer marker, unlike other crates: scripts/audit-orphan-producers.sh lists `reify-test-support` in EXCLUDE_CRATES (mirrored in Rust as crates/reify-test-support/src/orphan_audit.rs's own EXCLUDE_CRATES const) and discover_sources skips any path containing that segment, so neither the literal-scope nor the glob-scope sweep reaches it and a marker there is dead ceremony. Consequences when moving a `pub fn` across that boundary: moving one INTO reify-test-support means dropping its marker and justifying the `pub` by its callers in a doc comment instead (no sweep will flag it if the last consumer disappears); moving one OUT of crates/reify-audit/src must keep tests/g_allow.rs's `orphan_count == 0` green. A `pub use` re-export never needs a marker either — the script's PUB_FN_RE matches only `pub ... fn ...` declarations, never `pub use` lines.

Reify orphan-producer audit gotcha (crates/reify-audit/tests/engine_seam_orphans_g_allow.rs): when a task wires a real (non-test) consumer for a `pub fn` that was a G-allow-marked orphan, that function leaves the audit's allowed[] set and the test engine_seam_orphans_are_g_allow_marked fails assertion (b) "expected exactly 1 entry in allowed[]; 0 entries". Per the file's removal contract, the OWNING task (cited in the source `// G-allow:` marker) must DELETE its PINS row in the consumer-wiring commit. Before deleting, confirm a real call edge with `rg '\bFN_NAME\b' crates/reify-*/src` (the wide scope means a same-name token elsewhere can also push callers>0 — `eligible` is the canonical collision risk). SEPARATELY, the now-stale `// G-allow:` markers in the source remain harmless while the owner task is non-terminal, but become g-allow-orphaned (High) terminal-cites once the task is marked done — remove/re-home them at task closure or they ambush the next Rust verify.

Splitting a reify test harness (tests/harness_X.rs + its #[path] module dir) trips two gates that a plain `cargo test --no-run` does NOT surface. (1) clippy::doc_lazy_continuation, denied via -D warnings: a `//!` paragraph that runs straight on from a bullet list with no blank `//!` separator is read as a lazy continuation and fails the build — always finish with `cargo clippy -p <crate> --test <new_root> --test <old_root>`, not just a build. (2) The reify-audit PTODO fingerprint ratchet (tests/infra/test_reify_audit_ptodo.sh) is severity-blind and matches PHANTOM_PHRASES like "tracked separately" / "tracked by its own follow-up" in ANY tracked file including shell comments — so a new-root or guard comment claiming work is tracked elsewhere reds the gate unless backed by a live `#NNNN`. submit_task returns a ticket id, not a task number, so at authoring time there is usually no cite available: drop the claim rather than invent one.

reify G-allow marker edits are constrained on two sides: markers must stay SINGLE-LINE immediately above the fn (scripts/audit-orphan-producers.sh reads only lines[idx-1]; ptodo.rs scan_g_allow_markers is per-line), and for symbols pinned in crates/reify-audit/tests/new_orphans_2026_05_16_g_allow.rs the marker must NOT be deleted and must keep a `#NNNN` cite — that test asserts the symbol is absent from orphans[], present exactly once in allowed[], with a task-citing allow_reason. So a "delete the stale marker" cleanup on a pinned symbol silently breaks a test in a different crate.

crates/reify-audit enforces an orphan-pub-fn gate: `cargo test -p reify-audit --test g_allow` shells `scripts/audit-orphan-producers.sh --scope crates/reify-audit/src` and asserts orphan_count==0 (landed commit e54edf4377). Any NEW inherent `pub fn` in crates/reify-audit/src/ with only test callers (no non-test src caller yet) MUST carry the verbatim marker `// G-allow: F-infra T-4 CLI consumer (crates/reify-audit-cli) — design pinned in docs/architecture-audit/f-infra-design.md` on the line IMMEDIATELY above the `pub fn` (no doc comment between marker and fn — the script checks lines[idx-1]). Trait method declarations and trait-impl methods (bare `fn`, no `pub`) are NOT scanned and need no marker. MockGitOps is gated by `#[cfg(any(test, feature="test-support"))]` which the script's `#[cfg(test)]`-only mask does NOT cover, so its inherent `pub fn` setters each need the marker.

The reify-audit / reify-test-support duplicate-and-pin convention has been SUPERSEDED by single-sourcing, and task descriptions still cite the retired version. `repo_redirect_vars_matches_reify_test_support_orphan_audit_copy` no longer exists: `crates/reify-audit/src/git_env.rs` now does `pub use reify_test_support::git_env::{REPO_REDIRECT_VARS, sanitize};`, deleting the copy and retiring the pin. The surviving rule is stated at `crates/reify-test-support/src/orphan_audit.rs` next to `EXCLUDE_CRATES`: duplicate-and-pin "is the last resort, not the default: where a value CAN be single-sourced it should be." Only a genuine cross-language boundary (the Rust `EXCLUDE_CRATES` copy of `scripts/audit-orphan-producers.sh`'s set literal) still earns an equality pin. Items shared between the two crates belong in reify-test-support (the LOWER crate), because the edge runs reify-audit -> reify-test-support and only that direction avoids inverting it.

Reify: a task branch that verifies `file.rs:NNNN` line pins in a commit is only verified against the base it was authored on. Orchestrator dispatch replays task branches onto a newer main, so pins into churny files (e.g. `crates/reify-eval/src/engine_build.rs`) silently drift by whatever main inserted ahead of them — task #5951 shipped a commit explicitly asserting `engine_build.rs:4619`/`:4246` were CORRECT, and both were 29 lines stale in the tree at HEAD after the replay. Repo policy already prefers dropping the number and symbol-anchoring (name the fn/const/`// ── Phase N` block); treat that as mandatory, not optional, for any pin a branch introduces. Same trap for file PATHS: moving a test under a harness root (e.g. `tests/x.rs` -> `tests/harness_engine/x.rs`) to satisfy `check-harness-baseline-registration.sh` / `test_harness_kloc_cap.sh` invalidates every in-tree citation of the old path. Before finalizing, re-read every branch-introduced citation target in the CURRENT tree, not the one you authored against.

Reify architecture-audit has TWO orphan-producer detector paths that are meant to stay in lockstep: the live P1 detector (crates/reify-audit/src/p1_producer_orphan.rs) and the offline G-tool script (scripts/audit-orphan-producers.sh, snapshotted to docs/architecture-audit/g-tool-baseline-report.md). The G-tool script has NO crates/reify-stdlib scope-exclude — it scans crates/reify-*/src and relies solely on the `// G-allow:` marker convention. P1 historically diverged with a hardcoded `symbol.file.starts_with("crates/reify-stdlib/")` exclude (its `.ri structure_def` rationale is inapplicable — reify-stdlib is all .rs and jcodemunch indexes Rust). Both detectors already honor the marker convention (#[allow(dead_code)] / #[cfg(test)] / non-blank `// G-allow:`), so the marker is the correct false-positive guard for in-flight stdlib producers, not a blanket crate exclude.

In crates/reify-audit, AuditContext and TaskMetadata are shared structs constructed via plain literals (no Default — AuditContext holds references). Adding ANY field to either breaks every construction site across ALL detector test files (tests/p5.rs, tests/p2.rs, and the api_surface_pin in p5.rs that destructures every TaskMetadata field by name). Additionally, tests/g_allow.rs shells `scripts/audit-orphan-producers.sh --scope crates/reify-audit/src` and asserts orphan_count==0, so every new `pub fn`/`pub` method in src/ MUST carry a verbatim `// G-allow: F-infra T-4 CLI consumer (crates/reify-audit-cli) — design pinned in docs/architecture-audit/f-infra-design.md` marker or `cargo test -p reify-audit --test g_allow` fails. New detectors should clone the p2_consumer_stub.rs structure and copy its private is_test_path verbatim to keep cross-detector test-path semantics identical.

scripts/audit-orphan-producers.sh (the orphan-producer audit behind reify_test_support::run_orphan_audit and the new_orphans_*_g_allow.rs tests) uses DIRECT external non-test caller counting (callers==0 => orphan), NOT transitive reachability from roots. Consequence for consumer-wiring tasks: a `// G-allow:`-marked scaffolding `pub fn` leaves the allowed[] list the instant ANY non-test caller in a DIFFERENT file references it — even if that caller is itself not yet reachable from a public root. So the PINS-row deletion in new_orphans_*_g_allow.rs AND removal of the source `// G-allow:` + TODO(#NNNN) markers MUST land in the SAME commit as the consumer wiring, or new_orphans_*_are_g_allow_marked goes RED ("found 0 entries in allowed[]").

In reify, `pub` items in crates/reify-test-support have NO orphan-producer gate: scripts/audit-orphan-producers.sh lists reify-test-support in EXCLUDE_CRATES and discover_sources skips any path containing that segment, so neither the literal-scope nor the glob-scope sweep reaches it and a `// G-allow:` marker there is dead ceremony. The script's stated premise for that exclusion — that a test-support crate's publics are reached only from test files — is no longer strictly true: reify_test_support::git_env::{sanitize, REPO_REDIRECT_VARS} (via the re-export in reify-audit/src/git_env.rs) and reify_test_support::ignore_hygiene::extract_ignore_reason are both reached from reify-audit's PRODUCTION path, which is why reify-test-support is a normal rather than a dev dependency in reify-audit/Cargo.toml. Consequence when adding a public item there: nothing will flag it if its consumer disappears, so justify the `pub` in the item's own doc and demote or delete it in the same change as its last caller.

reify-orphan-audit-g-allow-marker-line-placement: scripts/audit-orphan-producers.sh detects a `// G-allow:` marker only on the single source line immediately preceding the `pub fn` declaration (the script inspects lines[idx-1]). See same-topic peers for distinct added detail: multi-line rationale must end in the G-allow line and re-export aliases go untraced (4b6e6989); cfg(any(test,...)) placement and same-file caller exclusion (453ad00d); the allowed[] list contains only zero-caller fns (e966949f); #[cfg(test)] masking behavior (6e1c3aab); and a 2026-09-18 correction fixing file-vs-crate granularity (614baa77).

Reify siting shortcut for a NEW repo-wide anti-drift guard: put it in crates/reify-audit/tests/ as a plain cargo integration test, not tests/infra/test_*.sh. Two measured reasons (2026-08-03, HEAD=20d029a5b2). (1) reify-audit is NOT among the 5 consolidatable crates enumerated at tests/infra/harness-layout-lib.sh:81 (reify-cli reify-syntax reify-kernel-occt reify-eval reify-compiler), so a new standalone crates/reify-audit/tests/<f>.rs does NOT trip check-harness-baseline-registration.sh's `reason=unregistered-standalone` and needs no harness_<subsystem>/ nesting and no baseline-manifest row. (2) It stays crate-scoped in verify, whereas any new tests/infra/*.sh forces the full `--scope all --profile both` gate (`scripts/verify-pipeline-guard.sh requires-full-gate tests/infra/<anything>.sh` exits 0). Existing shape to copy: crates/reify-audit/tests/g_allow_repo_wide_hard_gate.rs Test B — scans the real repo via AuditContext, graceful-skips in <1 ms when git or tasks.db is absent, so it is green in task worktrees and enforcing on the main checkout. Choose tests/infra/ only when the guard genuinely needs shell/filesystem/process semantics that a Rust test cannot express.

In crates/reify-audit, every inherent `pub fn` visible to the compiler (including those gated by `#[cfg(any(test, feature="test-support"))]`) must carry a `// G-allow: F-infra T-4 CLI consumer (crates/reify-audit-cli) — design pinned in docs/architecture-audit/f-infra-design.md` comment on the line immediately above the `pub fn` declaration. The gate is enforced by `cargo test -p reify-audit --test g_allow`, which shells `scripts/audit-orphan-producers.sh --scope crates/reify-audit/src --quiet --format json` and asserts orphan_count==0. Trait method decls and trait-impl methods (bare `fn`, no `pub`) are invisible to the scanner and need no marker.

content: Splitting a reify source file can break a G-allow pin even though the change only moves code. scripts/audit-orphan-producers.sh counts a pub fn's callers from OTHER files only, and it matches pub(super)/pub(crate) fns too. Once a pub fn and its callers land in different files, a fn pinned as a "same-file caller" false positive gains real cross-file callers and leaves allowed[]. Its crates/reify-audit/tests/*_g_allow.rs pin then reds with assertion (b) "0 entries". That file's removal contract requires deleting the pin row and the now-false `// G-allow:` marker in the same commit. The pin also matches by path suffix, so renaming the file breaks it too. reify-lsp changes do not make reify-audit an affected crate, so only the merge gate's --scope all run catches this. Run `cargo test -p reify-audit --test <pin file>` yourself after a split. Example: task 8757, collect_references in reify-lsp references.rs.

content: Security observation recorded as take-out PRD decision 11 (2026-10-15): a file a browser saves from GET /s/<token>/p/<n>/take-out may carry its download URL, token included, in OS metadata (macOS kMDItemWhereFroms, Windows Zone.Identifier HostUrl), and the PRD invites the prospect to share the file. 939af9fc-a18f-4c60-ad3b-098797557110.content: solar_challenge / dark-factory ordering gotcha (task 273 planning, 2026-10-01): a follow-up filed via submit_task with spawned_from=<parent> gets no Taskmaster dependency on its parent. So when an orchestrator restart cancels the unmerged parent back to pending (task 263 was cancelled at 04:54Z with all 5 plan steps committed), the follow-up can take the shared file locks first (273 did at 04:55Z). When the follow-up must edit lines the parent rewrites, have its architect call report_blocking_dependency on the parent rather than plan on main, because whichever task lands second then hits a guaranteed merge conflict. While the parent is non-terminal, dark-factory's workflow.py _handle_blocking_dep_report registers the dependency and requeues the follow-up; if the parent is cancelled, the follow-up dispatches again.

GOTCHA (measured in task 345, CPython 3.11): `dt.utcoffset() == timedelta(0)` does NOT mean "written in UTC". A zero-offset DST zone such as ZoneInfo('Europe/London') in winter passes it. Python's `datetime + timedelta` on a ZoneInfo datetime runs on the WALL CLOCK: London noon GMT on 2026-03-28 plus 24h is 2026-03-29 11:00Z, only 23h elapsed. To test that the ZONE is UTC, use `dt.tzinfo.utcoffset(None) == timedelta(0)`. A zone states its offset without a date only if that offset never changes. timezone.utc, ZoneInfo('UTC'/'Etc/UTC'), pytz.utc, dateutil tz.UTC and pandas' UTC (which is datetime.timezone.utc) answer timedelta(0). Europe/London and even Africa/Abidjan answer None, the latter because of pre-1912 history. In this repo, rollups.require_utc_hh_aligned (strict, used by OptimiserService.run_window) applies this check via the private rollups._is_utc. rollups.as_utc_hh_aligned is the lenient counterpart: it refuses a naive time, converts to UTC, checks the half-hour grid and returns the UTC datetime. Both ForecastProvider bindings read t0 through it, and a new binding should too.

solar_challenge_platform gotcha (verified 2026-10-07, task 209 planning): SQLAlchemy's DateTime(timezone=True) on SQLite binds a tz-aware datetime by its wall-clock fields and drops the offset, so a non-UTC instant is stored wrong. Every store converts to UTC before binding (as DispatchLivenessStore.write_refresh_tick does) and re-attaches UTC to the naive values SQLite reads back. The repo had no portable upsert: on_conflict_do_update exists only on the dialect-specific constructs (sqlalchemy.dialects.postgresql.insert / sqlalchemy.dialects.sqlite.insert). A store that must run on both the hermetic SQLite suite and Postgres picks one by session.get_bind().dialect.name.

Completed: rollups.settlement_hh sorts and integrates rows written in a DST zone on their wall clock, so a half-hour whose sample window spans the autumn clock change settles wrong
Description: Follow-up from task 776 ("rollups.settle_half_hours keys half-hours on each sample's own clock (hh_floor), so samples written off UTC settle off-grid half-hours"), found by its architect on 2026-10-03 at main 5ceee69. Idempotency key: agent-followup-776. There is no escalation record. Start this only after task 776 lands: both edit src/solar_challenge_platform/timeseries/rollups.py.

OBSERVED (scratch probe, not committed, at main 5ceee69):
- src/solar_challenge_platform/timeseries/rollups.py::settlement_hh builds `sorted(Sample(r.ts, r.value) ...)` from its rows exactly as they are written. Python compares and subtracts two aware datetimes that share a tzinfo on their wall clock, ignoring fold. On 2026-10-25 at 01:00Z London's clocks go back, so its wall clock reads 01:00-01:59 twice. Rows written in Europe/London (one ZoneInfo) across that change are therefore mis-ordered, and rollups._settle_flow subtracts them on the wall clock.
- Input: 121 pv_power rows, 1000 + 10*m W at minute m from 2026-10-25T00:00Z, each written with .astimezone(ZoneInfo('Europe/London')). Compared with the same instants written in UTC, settlement_hh at the UTC hh_starts 00:00Z, 00:30Z, 01:00Z and 01:30Z gave [equal, NOT equal, equal, equal]. The 00:30Z half-hour differs; its settlement_sample_window reaches 01:01:30Z, past the change.
- Task 776 fixes the same defect in rollups.settle_half_hours by reading every sample as its UTC instant on entry. Before that fix, settle_half_hours on this input returned two London-keyed half-hours with sample_count 62 and 61 instead of four UTC half-hours of 31. A fix that only keyed on utc_hh_floor raised ZeroDivisionError in rollups._power_at.

WHY IT MATTERS: settlement_hh is MemoryStore's SETTLEMENT_HH path (the hermetic default backend). It is also the audit reference that TimescaleStore's materialiser is checked against. MemoryStore.write does not normalise timestamps to UTC (see task 749's description). So a caller writing Europe/London readings silently gets a wrong settlement around the October change. Heuristic 10 (clear invariants, uniformly enforced) in /home/leo/src/dark-factory/docs/code-quality.md applies. After task 776, settle_half_hours and settlement_hh disagree on such input, although settle_half_hours' docstring calls it "the same arithmetic as settlement_hh".

SUGGESTED FIX: settlement_hh writes each in-window row's ts in UTC as it builds the Sample, through the same naive-refusing conversion task 776 adds to rollups (planned as the private rollups._as_utc). Convert AFTER the home/metric/window filter, so rows outside the window get no new per-row work. This matters because of the task 273 gotcha: MemoryStore calls settlement_hh once per half-hour with every row of the home. Test in tests/timeseries/test_settlement_reference.py: using the London ramp above, settlement_hh at each UTC hh_start equals its value for the same instants written in UTC, and equals settle_half_hours' value for that half-hour. Use public names only (tests/test_private_names.py).

content: Coordination note for S26 (solar_challenge_platform, task 979 architect, 2026-10-17, plan confirmed at main 02be628, not yet implemented). Task 979 adds src/solar_challenge_platform/timeseries/store.py::window_in_utc(t0, t1) -> (t0_utc, t1_utc). It is the single check of a TelemetryStore query window. It refuses a naive bound and refuses a t0 that is not strictly before t1 compared in UTC. It returns both bounds written in timezone.utc. MemoryStore.query, TimescaleStore.query and TimescaleStore.refresh_continuous_aggregates call it, replacing their old `t0 >= t1` guards, which compared same-ZoneInfo bounds on their wall clocks and ignored fold. Because utc.py is not yet on main, the naive refusal goes through a private store._in_utc(name, dt). That function has exactly S26 utc.in_utc's contract: predicate utcoffset() is None, D4 wording, D5 semantics. Once S26-alpha (task 1078) lands utc.py, S26-delta (task 1086) should replace store._in_utc with an import of utc.in_utc. Delta's no-second-aware-predicate grep over timeseries/ will flag it. Measured for that work: a probe wrapping all three methods over the 81 store-using test modules (-m 'not slow') saw 2525 window calls, none with a naive bound and none whose wall-clock order differs from its instant order.

824aea97-bdc3-4256-a027-66feb8afaafc.content: solar_challenge_platform convention (task 588, branch task/588; holds once merged). Type every datetime instant a response model serves as schemas.serialization.UtcInstant, an Annotated[datetime, AfterValidator] that reads a naive value as UTC via config.contract.as_utc and converts an aware one to UTC. pydantic-core then serves RFC3339 UTC with a trailing Z on SQLite too, and the OpenAPI schema stays a plain date-time. tests/schemas/test_wire_serialization.py::test_every_instant_the_api_serves_is_utc_with_a_trailing_z walks every router's response models, so a served field left as plain datetime fails there. dc07cd37-d511-470e-86ff-69bb1b23d01d.content: GOTCHA (solar_challenge_platform, measured 2026-10-11 at main 1b647d3 by task 941's architect): Python's == between two aware datetimes with DIFFERENT tzinfos returns False whenever either one's UTC offset depends on fold, i.e. it lies in a clock change's repeated hour or gap (PEP 495), even when both name the same instant. Ordering comparisons (<, <=, >, >=) and subtraction stay instant-correct. So bucket_grid.ceil_to_bucket's `floored == ts` misreads such a ts: ceil_to_bucket(datetime(2026,10,25,1,0,tzinfo=ZoneInfo('Europe/London')), 30 min) returns 00:30Z, not 00:00Z; with width 1 day it returns 2026-10-26T00:00Z, not 2026-10-25T00:00Z. To test 'same instant' across zones, compare in UTC (a.astimezone(timezone.utc) == b) or use ordering; floor_to_bucket is unaffected (it subtracts).

candidates.content: When retiring or renaming a fused-memory symbol (model, method, return shape), also grep fused-memory/scripts/: fused-memory's pyproject pyright include is ["src","tests","scripts"], and manual diagnostics there (e.g. scripts/probe_schema_max_turns.py, which drives the real Judge.review_run over a synthetic run) import production models but are imported by no test. So a stale import or stub only shows up as a pyright failure, and a stub of a retired reader silently stops feeding the code under measurement. Also check scripts/legibility/digest.py, whose docstrings describe the judge prompt headings.

The task-3223 atomic-write anti-regrowth guard (_SRC_TREES / _ALLOWED_RENAMERS / _find_renamers / TestNoRegrownAtomicWriters) enumerates its exempt sites as (repo-relative path, qualname) pairs, and any prose list of those sites rots fast. Task 3388's task description named six sites in fused-memory/ and scripts/; running the guard's own _find_renamers over those trees at base main aab5322588 reported seventeen (fused-memory/src 6, fused-memory/scripts 3, scripts 8), including a non-delegating helper literally named _atomic_write_text at fused-memory/scripts/bake_off_storage_shape.py:2539. Always re-derive the inventory by executing _find_renamers at HEAD rather than trusting any written enumeration. Two detector properties explain part of the gap: it uses ast.walk, so an outer function is reported alongside a nested closure that does the rename, and it matches four spellings (os.replace, os.rename, and arity-1 Path.replace/Path.rename).

GOTCHA (dark-factory, measured task 4881): a mechanical rename that strips a leading underscore from a HELPER can silently eat the underscore in a TEST FUNCTION'S OWN NAME, and pytest will not tell you. Renaming `_find_script_position` -> `find_script_position` across dashboard/tests with a plain textual substitution turned `def test_find_script_position_returns_document_order` into `def testfind_script_position_returns_document_order`.

WHY IT IS INVISIBLE: pytest's default `python_functions = test*` is a PREFIX GLOB, not `test_*`. `def testfoo` is still collected and still passes, so nothing turns red, no warning is emitted, and the diff reads as a correct rename. It survived a full-suite run, a verify pass, and .pytest_cache nodeids confirmed all five parametrizations were executing.

WHY IT STILL MATTERS: it is a latent trip-wire. The day anyone sets `python_functions = test_*` in a root or package `[tool.pytest.ini_options]` — a plausible tightening — those tests stop being collected and the coverage loss is silent in both directions.

DETECTION, cheap and exact: `grep -rn 'def test[^_]' <tests-dir>/*.py`. On the dashboard suite that returned exactly one hit, which was the defect. Run it after any bulk rename that touches identifiers appearing inside test names; a passing suite is not evidence of absence here.

GENERAL FORM: when a rename's search string is a substring of test function names (helper names usually are, since tests are named after what they test), the substitution hits the `def test_<helper>` line too. Prefer an anchored/word-boundary pattern, or grep the diff for changed `def test` lines before committing.

The atomic-write anti-regrowth guard (tests/scripts/test_atomic_write_regrowth.py::TestNoRegrownAtomicWriters::test_no_unapproved_renamers_in_source_trees) also scans TEST modules such as scripts/tests/*.py, not only production code. A test helper that simulates a swapped or corrupted store with Path.rename/Path.replace trips it in the full-suite verify, even though the module's own tests pass. In a test, simulate the swap with byte copies instead: aside.write_bytes(store.read_bytes()), overwrite the store in place, then write the saved bytes back. That needs no _ALLOWED_RENAMERS entry (found in task 4625).

GOTCHA (dark-factory, found 2026-09-04 planning task 4564): renaming a field in a JSON sidecar can DELETE it downstream with no error and no failing test, when the consumer copies keys through a whitelist guarded by `if key in <source>`.

The concrete instance: `fused-memory/scripts/read_transform_selection.py::production_query_provenance` copies the harvest sidecar into `block['harvest']` via a literal key-name tuple filtered by `if key in sidecar`. A reviewer suggestion to rename `HarvestResult.family_share` -> `four_template_share` in `harvest_production_queries.py` would have made that key silently vanish from `plans/read-transform-selection-report.json` — the guard turns "key renamed" into "key absent" rather than into a KeyError, and no test asserts on `harvest.family_share`.

THE GENERAL SHAPE, worth checking before accepting any rename of a serialized field: grep for the OLD name in consumers and classify each hit as (a) a dereference, which fails loudly, or (b) a membership-guarded copy / `.get(name)` / `getattr(obj, name, default)`, which fails SILENTLY. Only (a) is caught by tests. A rename is only as safe as its loudest consumer.

SECOND, INDEPENDENT REASON THE RENAME LOSES HERE, also generalizable: the same quantity was already published under the same name by a DIFFERENT producer — `production_queries.family_share` is computed independently as the sum of the four template shares, and only the harvest-sidecar copy would have been renamed. A one-sided rename leaves two spellings for one number inside a single JSON object, which is strictly worse legibility than the ambiguous-but-consistent name it set out to fix. When a field name is merely ambiguous and the VALUE is correct, documenting the numerator beats renaming.

Atomic-write anti-regrowth guard, inventory re-derived at main 1d7532221803d46a97a5d4aedf73b01981a08408 (task 4267 architect, 2026-08-29). Running the guard's OWN _find_renamers AST detector (currently in shared/tests/test_safe_io.py) over the trees outside _SRC_TREES yields: cockpit/src = 2 — cockpit/src/cockpit/priority.py::save_priorities and cockpit/src/cockpit/ui_config.py::save_ui_config; dashboard/src = 0; sampler/src = 0; skills = 0. This CONFIRMS task 4267's prose enumeration, unlike task 3388's description which claimed six sites where the detector reported seventeen. Cheap way to re-derive without importing the whole test module (it has package-import side effects): ast.parse the test file, exec only the _find_renamers FunctionDef node into a fresh namespace, then walk each tree's *.py with it — about 10 lines, runs in under a second. Do this rather than trusting any prose list; the guard's four rename spellings (os.replace, os.rename, Path.replace, Path.rename, the last two disambiguated from str.replace by single-positional-arg arity) are easy to under-count by grep.

Meta-tests that assert over the SOURCE TEXT or IDENTIFIER NAMES of sibling test modules (pinning a function name like `_falkor_available`, which identifiers appear in an ImportFrom, or a string literal) are rejected in /review as name-pinning: a copier who renames evades them, so they buy no coverage while implying duplication cannot return. A de-duplication migration guard should assert only RUNTIME properties — e.g. "each migrated module still applies the shared skip marker in a position pytest honours (a pytestmark entry or a class/function decorator)", not "no module defines a function with this name". Note that `fused-memory/tests/test_gather_idiom_helper_routing.py` IS an accepted in-repo precedent for the name-pinning species; citing it to defend a new guard was heard and explicitly overruled on task 3502 (esc-3502-2), so it is not a valid defence. Do not respond to such a finding by hardening the name lists — that deepens the same hole.

MEASURED (dark-factory, 2026-09-18, HEAD 976ed91ae2): a leading underscore in `fused-memory/src/fused_memory` does NOT mean "module-private / never crosses a module boundary". An AST ImportFrom census counted 47 cross-module underscore imports across 17 modules: reconciliation.prompts 8, utils.referent_verification 7, utils.validation 5 (`_safe_repr` alone reaches five modules), middleware.task_interceptor 4, reconciliation 3, reconciliation.flag_dedup 3, then singles and pairs. Locally the underscore reads "not part of the public MCP/server tool surface", which is a different claim.

WHY THIS IS WORTH KNOWING BEFORE FILING OR ACTIONING A NAMING REVIEW. A reviewer looking at any one module sees underscore-prefixed names in an import block and correctly reads it as a smell under the standard Python reading; the fix that follows ("drop the underscore, these ARE the interface now") then makes that module the single outlier against 16 others, which raises the cost of the next change in it — the thing docs/code-quality.md defines quality AS. This happened on task 5262 (esc-5262-3) and the sweep was declined on that basis plus a hard runtime collision. An older stray memory (c8fafe9c, task 694, "The leading underscore marks it module-private") states the standard reading without the repo-local measurement; prefer this census over it for dark-factory.

`__all__` is NOT the established alternative either: present in 37 of 177 .py files under fused-memory/src, a real but minority pattern.

IF YOU DO DECIDE TO DE-PRIVATIZE a module-level name anywhere, AST-scan the calling functions for a Store or arg binding of the NEW (unprefixed) name FIRST. The private and public spellings differ by one character, and the unprefixed spelling is exactly what a local holding that function's RESULT would be called — so the collision is the normal case, not the exotic one. Python makes a name assigned anywhere in a function local throughout it, so the call raises UnboundLocalError rather than failing at import, and a grep for the old name cannot see it.

CORRECTION superseding memory 48fe36f7-ed33-43f4-9b92-2ab409af17b8 (same bash-function-under-test pattern; that entry could not be amended in place — the content_amend arm of update_memory is restricted to recon-stage-* agents by design).

When extracting a bash function for test with an anchored regex like `r'^name\(\)\s*\{\n(?:.*\n)*?^\}$'` under re.M (reference impl: `_bash_encode_cwd_source` in scripts/tests/test_legibility_inventory.py), do NOT claim it breaks when the function is renamed "or moved". MEASURED in dark-factory task 3464's amendment pass against the real file: extraction breaks ONLY on a rename, on the `function name {` form, or on a definition that stops starting at column 0. It does NOT break when the function is MOVED anywhere in the file (re.search scans all of it), nor when `()` and `{` are split across lines (`\s*` spans newlines). The body must end at a bare column-0 `}`; an earlier column-0 `}` truncates the match, since the middle is non-greedy.

Two guards the pattern needs beyond the extraction assert, both surfaced by code review: pass `timeout=` to subprocess.run (an unavailable or wedged bash otherwise HANGS the suite instead of failing it — the one silent-degradation path in an otherwise fail-loud bridge), and check `returncode` explicitly rather than using `check=True` (CalledProcessError's default message omits captured stderr, so a bash syntax error surfaces as a bare "returned non-zero exit status 2" with the real diagnostic hidden in an unprinted attribute).

Measurement gotcha that produced the original false claim: a `src.replace('name() {', ...)` probe can hit the script's own COMMENT quoting that string before reaching the definition, so the variant under test is not the one you think you built. Anchor probes on the extracted function text, never on a substring that also appears in prose.

MEASURED 2026-08-28 (task 4810 architect, main f474347580): in fused-memory/src/fused_memory/server/write_triage_judge.py, `select_judge_candidates` does NOT always return the attach target at index 0. Its winner-rescue branch APPENDS the rescued winner — `selected = [*selected[: max(n - 1, 0)], winner]` — so when `decision.canonical_id` is a HOISTED parent id that never appeared as a search result of its own, the child carrying the evidence (found via grouped_read.PARENT_ID_KEY) is kept and lands LAST. Direct probe: select_judge_candidates(results, 3, canonical_id='parent-1') returned slate ids ['m0','m1','child-1'] — target-is-first False, target-is-last True.

WHY THIS MATTERS: any fix for the write-triage judge's attach-target defect that identifies the target POSITIONALLY (e.g. "candidates[0] is the attach target, candidates[1:] are context") is wrong on that path — it tells the model m0 is the target while the attach touches parent-1 via child-1, which is the same wrong-memory harm the fix exists to prevent, just relocated. Identify the target BY ID: pass the band's canonical_id into build_judge_prompt (judge_write already holds `decision.canonical_id` at the call site, so this stays inside write_triage_judge.py plus its test file and needs none of the cross-module option-(a) refactor).

HOW IT WAS MEASURED, reusable: `git archive <ref> fused-memory/src | tar -x -C <tmpdir>`, then run the repo-root .venv python with PYTHONPATH=<tmpdir>/fused-memory/src. This executes the code AT A GIT REF rather than the working tree; assert `module.__file__` starts with the tmpdir to confirm PYTHONPATH shadowed the installed package. Candidate doubles can be plain objects with .id/.content/.metadata — near_duplicate_guard._cosine_of just reads metadata['store_score'] — so no MemoryResult import is needed. Whole probe ran in about 2s. git archive is read-only and touches no .git state, unlike `git worktree add`.

CONVENTION (dark-factory, established task 2610 Group B, reapplied by task 4384): when promoting a test helper into orchestrator/tests/_workflow_helpers.py, CHECK whether the name is already a common module-local spelling elsewhere under orchestrator/tests/, and QUALIFY it if so.

The file documents this about itself. Its Group B section header reads: "renamed from the bare `_make_workflow` since that name is reused ~30x across the tests dir with different signatures" — hence `_make_warmlane_workflow`. Re-measured 2026-09-03: 42 modules under orchestrator/tests/ define a local `_make_workflow`. Task 4384's first pass promoted a bare `_make_workflow` into that same file, ~500 lines below the header recording the retirement of exactly that name; it was renamed to `_make_transcript_workflow` before landing.

HOW TO CHECK: `grep -rlc '^\s*\(async \)\?def <name>' orchestrator/tests/ | wc -l` before choosing. A count in the dozens means qualify.

THE HAZARD IS NOT A LIVE BUG. Imports from _workflow_helpers are explicit by name and nothing star-imports it, so a colliding shared name breaks nothing at runtime. It is (a) a shadowing hazard at every call site — a reader cannot tell which `_make_workflow` a line means without checking the imports — and (b) a guaranteed coherence finding for the next reviewer, since the contradicted decision is recorded in the same file.

WHERE THE LINE IS DRAWN: qualify only names with a real collision population. Task 4384 renamed `_make_workflow` and deliberately left `ENC`, `_config`, `_make_git_ops`, `_config_dir`, `_write_transcript` and `_archived` alone — the latter four are transcript-distinctive and `_config` has only 5 local definitions with no importer overlap. Renaming for symmetry inflates a behaviour-preserving diff across every consumer for no measured hazard.

WHEN A CONSUMER'S OLD LOCAL NAME MUST SURVIVE, the established escape hatch is an alias at the IMPORT site, not a second definition: `from _workflow_helpers import _make_warmlane_workflow as _make_workflow` (test_workflow_warm_lane_requeue.py), with the identity guard asserting `wr._make_workflow is _make_warmlane_workflow`.

GOTCHA — the ASSERTION side of the by-path importlib seam (measured 2026-08-21, dark_factory task 4583; complements mem0 443c3bc5 which covers the clobbering mechanism, and CORRECTS the advice in mem0 d2785d01). Do NOT pin a cross-script reuse seam with object identity (`assert mod._cell is _bake_off()._cell`) when the TEST also loads the sibling by path: fused-memory/tests/test_read_transform_selection.py::_load_script has no sys.modules reuse guard and overwrites the registered module, while read_transform_selection._load_script has one, so the two sides hold different instances of one source file and `is` fails. Assert PROVENANCE instead: `(fn.__module__, fn.__qualname__) == ('<sibling_module>', name)`. It is order- and instance-independent AND strictly stronger for a "no second implementation" invariant — a local `def name` would shadow the PEP 562 __getattr__ entirely and report the WRONG __module__, so the re-implementation is still caught. Add a value-level cross-check on a plain str/int constant (e.g. `mod._cell(None) == bake._NO_MEASUREMENT`), which crosses instances safely. TESTING TRAP: under fused-memory's `addopts = "-n auto --dist loadgroup"` such a test is SCHEDULE-DEPENDENT, so file-level green does NOT prove it fixed — measured on one unmodified tree, the same test gave 1 failed selected alone, 3 passed at class level, and 216 passed at file level. Always re-run the single test id in isolation, and make the reproduction deterministic in-process by clobbering sys.modules before EACH check (one clobber only reddens the first check — the first check's own loader call re-syncs sys.modules with the functools.cache'd test helper, so a later check then passes).

MAINTENANCE-SCRIPT WRITE ATTRIBUTION IN FUSED-MEMORY HAS **TWO** CHANNELS, KEYED ON DIFFERENT FIELDS, AND SETTING ONLY `_source` LEAVES HALF THE JOURNAL ANONYMOUS (measured 2026-08-29, task 4610).

The sibling-script convention (retro_stamp_topics.py's WRITE_SOURCE comment, copied by every later sweep) teaches `_source=WRITE_SOURCE` and stops there. That covers ONE consumer:

* `_source` → the write journal and the AMENDMENT STORM ALARM. This is the field the "a bulk rewrite under the default `mcp_tool` source would look exactly like the runaway rewrite that alarm exists to catch" comment is about.
* `agent_id` → a DIFFERENT consumer, reached only when the call carries a `metadata_patch`. `MemoryService.update_memory` then runs `_apply_memory_metadata_validation`, which forwards `agent_id` to `emit_schema_warnings`, `UnknownKeyStormDetector.record(project_id, agent_id, keys)` and `file_unknown_key_storm_escalation`. `agent_id` defaults to None, so every census line and storm bucket a patch-carrying sweep produces is keyed to a NULL agent while `_source` correctly names the sweep — the two views of the same write disagree about who did it.

MEASURED: `retro_stamp_topics.py:1334` passes `metadata_patch` and `_source` but no `agent_id` (memory 14752d2e independently recorded, 2026-08-12, that its writes are storm-counted under the `<unattributed>` key). `amend_stale_resume_cwd_records.py` (task 4610) sets both to the same constant.

PRACTICE for any script reaching `MemoryService.update_memory` directly: if the call carries a `metadata_patch`, pass `agent_id=WRITE_SOURCE` alongside `_source=WRITE_SOURCE`. One constant, both channels, and the census/storm rows match the write journal. There is no authz consequence — the mem0_update prefix gate is MCP-tool-layer only, and `agent_id` at the service seam is pure attribution, so naming the script does not gate or unblock anything.
