GOTCHA (dark-factory, measured task 3659, 2026-09-14): renaming a markdown heading that BriefingAssembler renders silently degrades scripts/legibility/digest.py's harness-turn classifier, and nothing reports it.

MECHANISM. `is_harness_injected_turn` lowercases the turn, splits it into a SET OF STRIPPED LINES, and tests `heading in lines` — whole-line equality, not substring or prefix. So HARNESS_BRIEFING_SUBHEADINGS' '## conventions' does NOT match a rendered '## Conventions & Gotchas'. A briefing turn needs one anchor plus one corroborator (>=2 total) to be filtered out of the digest's "gold" User Corrections section; lose the corroborator and a machine-generated briefing is presented to a human as gold human input — the exact fabrication class the 07-31 confusion census (cluster 1.1(b)) found.

WHAT TO DO when you rename or retire a briefing heading: ADD the new spelling to HARNESS_BRIEFING_SUBHEADINGS and KEEP the old one. The filter reads ARCHIVED transcripts, so the retired spelling is still live data — pruning it un-classifies every historical briefing turn. Task 3659 added '## conventions & gotchas' beside the pre-3659 '## project context' / '## conventions' / '## recent decisions'.

WHY IT IS EASY TO MISS: digest.py lives under scripts/, is not imported by the orchestrator, and its tests (scripts/tests/test_legibility_digest.py, run via `uv run --project shared pytest scripts/tests/`) stay green on the rename because they exercise the constant's own literals rather than briefing.py's output. There is no cross-file drift guard; the coupling is prose-only. Grep scripts/legibility/digest.py for the heading literal whenever you touch a rendered '## ' heading in orchestrator/src/orchestrator/agents/briefing.py.

candidates.content:
data/verify-logs/ IN REIFY IS A WRITE-ONLY ARCHIVE — nothing has ever read it back. Surveyed 2026-08-19: 589 directories, 828 files, 271 MB. Contents are (a) per-task raw verify output and DF-written classifier summary JSON, both written by dark-factory not reify; (b) flaky-ledger.jsonl, written by tests/infra/run_all.sh via REIFY_RUN_ALL_FLAKY_LEDGER; (c) run-all-skip-state.json, the one artifact that IS self-consumed (run_all.sh reads its own content-addressed skip state across merges). A sweep of scripts/, tests/, crates/ and .claude/ found zero post-hoc analysis consumers. The only mining that has ever happened was ad-hoc and agent-driven (the 12-agent survey recorded in docs/notes/merge-verify-cpu-survey-2026-07.md).

This is a standing opportunity: run_all.sh already computes and prints its Phase-1 peak concurrent worker-shell count into that archive on every merge verify, and nobody has ever read it. Any "how concurrent did we actually get" question is answerable from data already on disk.

KNOWN FAILURE MODE TO AVOID when wiring a new verify-logs artifact: the flaky ledger was "amnesiac" for months because its path defaulted to the RUNNING CHECKOUT rather than the main checkout, so every warm-lane reseed wiped it (docs/notes/merge-verify-cpu-survey-2026-07.md). Point any new path at the main checkout from day one, and pin it with an assertion in the style of tests/infra/test_run_all_content_skip.sh, which guards the durable absolute path.

RELATED CONSTRAINT on adding a new runtime check to tests/infra/: the `host-exclusive` bucket in tests/infra/run-all-classification.manifest is EXCLUDED from every merge verify (scripts/verify.sh sets REIFY_RUN_ALL_EXCLUDE_HOST_INFRA=1) and runs only in the `--scope host-infra` cold lane — which per the same survey note has never actually run. A check classified host-exclusive may therefore never execute at all; to fire on real verifies it must be `pool`-classified, which means generating its own load hermetically rather than observing the ambient verify.

reify gotcha (task 7423): any tests/infra member that runs scripts/verify.sh in EXECUTE mode (not --print-plan) under DF_VERIFY_ROLE=background must export REIFY_BACKGROUND_SWEEP_LEDGER to a scratch path. Otherwise verify.sh's EXIT-trap _record_background_verdict appends a synthetic sweep record to the MAIN checkout's live ledger data/orchestrator/verify-background-sweeps.jsonl, which resolves via lib_main_checkout.sh even from a lane. test_verify_semaphore_e2e.sh Section H did exactly this and left 2 polluted records at ec35141500 (fixed in a612418e0a).

reify verify.sh admission knobs: dark-factory-orchestrator.yaml's `verify_env` block reaches ONLY the verify subprocesses the orchestrator spawns. Every other verify.sh invocation — the /unblock manual full gate (`verify.sh all --scope all --profile both`), a hand-run gate, a fixture — sees none of it and falls back to the in-repo `:-` default. Root-caused 2026-08-20 (task 6393) from an exit-75 "test-run semaphore acquire" on a manual /unblock gate in /home/leo/src/reify-unblock-5481 (2026-08-19 13:08:47): leaf epsilon (task 4838) activated the clock-stop seam on 2026-06-27 by setting REIFY_TEST_SEMAPHORE_WAIT / REIFY_PSI_GATE_MAX_WAIT to "unlimited" in verify_env ONLY, leaving the in-repo defaults at the pre-seam 1800s for ~7 weeks. Orchestrator verifies waited gracefully; manual ones burned a finite 1800s deadline and died at the semaphore after ~55min of completed compile (clippy 35m20s + gui check 19m38s), with the test suite never running. GENERAL LESSON: any reify knob whose correct value must hold for EVERY verify.sh caller has to live in the script's `:-` default, not only in verify_env — a config-only flip covers the orchestrator population and silently leaves everyone else on the old behaviour. verify.sh's apply_env() re-bakes verify_env for exactly this reason (RUSTC_WRAPPER, CARGO_INCREMENTAL, CARGO_MAKEFLAGS, LD_LIBRARY_PATH) but was never extended to the admission knobs.

Reify: `data/verify-logs/<task_id>/` is an underused ground-truth source for what a verify ACTUALLY ran. Two file shapes. (1) Task-side `attempt-N.summary-<ts>.json` — keys category, cause_hint, rc, timed_out, cmd, started_at, duration_secs, commands[]; the commands[] array quotes the literal command line. Across all such files the task-side commands are 100% uniform: `./scripts/verify.sh test --scope branch --include-infra` (217), `./scripts/verify.sh lint --scope branch --include-infra` (222), and type = the literal `true` (217, i.e. type-checking is a no-op for reify). NOTE these summaries are written on FAILURE, so they are not a sample of all verifies. (2) Merge-side `attempt-N.remote-laptop.pass-summary-<ts>.json` — keys category, duration_ms, merge_sha, passed, runner, scope{merge_verify_breadth, merge_verify_workspace, task_files}. Caveat: `merge_verify_breadth: "scoped"` / `merge_verify_workspace: false` there are the DF-side staged-rollout knobs (reify leaves both at their defaults), NOT the reify-side verify.sh --scope; do not read them as "the merge gate was scoped". dark-factory's own project sets merge_verify_breadth: "full"; reify does not.

Reify verify-pipeline extension mechanics, mapped 2026-08-26 (symbol-level; for anyone adding a new verify step or test tier): (1) verify.sh steps are strings appended to a flat PLAN array inside build_plan() via add() (cargo lines, each requiring a trailing '# ld-ok: <reason>' marker enforced by test_verify_ld_library_path_scope.sh) or add_tool() (non-cargo lines, LD-scrubbed). (2) A new tests/infra/test_*.sh needs its run-all-classification.manifest row in the SAME diff or plan step #1 (scripts/check-infra-classification-manifest.sh) fails immediately. (3) The cleanest diff-keyed hook is scripts/verify-pipeline-infra-tests.txt — one row '<artifact-path> <infra-test-glob>' makes edits to that artifact run that test at task role; merge/background roles run the full run_all.sh pool instead (INV-5 exactly-once). (4) The _RUST_COUPLED_RI_FIXTURES arm in decide_scope is the precedent for escalating a docs-classified file out of the no-heavy-checks arm. (5) Heavy-tier membership is the single expression REIFY_HEAVY_NEXTEST_FILTER in scripts/heavy-test-filter-lib.sh (offline role selects it positively with --run-ignored all; task/merge negate it when REIFY_GATE_EXCLUDE_HEAVY=1, currently ON) — and two guards pin the atom count exactly (test_heavy_filter_atoms.sh assertion E, test_verify_offline_partition.sh assertion e, both currently 8), so adding an atom means updating both same-diff. (6) C1/C2 harness-layout: new standalone tests/*.rs binaries are ratchet-banned in the 5 consolidatable crates (reify-cli, reify-syntax, reify-kernel-occt, reify-eval, reify-compiler) per esc-5056-11 — but a NEW crate is outside C1/C2 scope entirely, which is a real factor favoring dedicated-crate designs for new test suites.

How to measure reify verify phases when there is no telemetry (learned 2026-09-10): scripts/verify.sh persists NO per-phase timings (its only `date` call writes target/reify-verify-attempt.json, a tree pin; the executor trace line `verify.sh: + $_cmd` is untimestamped) and dark-factory archives verify logs to data/verify-logs/<task_id>/ ONLY on failure (verify.py _should_archive_category), so there is no artifact at all for a passing gate. Recoverable per archived failed log: dark-factory's attempt-N.summary-*.json → commands[].duration_secs for the three legs (test/lint/type); cargo-nextest's `Summary [NNN.NNNs] N tests run` and per-test `PASS [ X.XXXs]` lines (awk over `PASS [ Xs] (i/N) <package[::binary]> <test>` gives per-binary and per-test CPU-seconds); run_all.sh's `INFO: run_all.sh pool progress: X/Y complete, elapsed Ns` every 30 s (concurrent phase only — the serial phase has no timestamps); npm `audited N packages in Xs` and vitest `Duration Xs`. Merge-role logs are identified by the `cargo build --release -p reify-audit` + `cargo nextest run --workspace` (no -p) plan lines (39 of 475 archived files on 2026-09-10). Do NOT read a `--scope branch` cmd string in a summary JSON as evidence the run narrowed — verify.sh forces --scope all internally for DF_VERIFY_ROLE ∈ {merge, background}. Merge-verify durations: runs.db events, event_type='merge_verify', json_extract(data,'$.duration_ms') (the events.duration_ms column is NULL on 100% of rows); $.runner, $.passed, $.speculative, $.depth, $.chain_items are also in the payload. Task-leg verify duration is persisted ONLY as rebase_verify_cost.next_verify_wall_secs (the post-rebase verify); in-loop task verifies have no recorded command wall (phase_enter/phase_exit 'verify' spans the whole phase incl. review/debug loops — do not read it as verify wall). The 30-day window had a 4-day telemetry gap (2026-08-14..17): use active days as the denominator. The `RELEASE-PASS: skipped (delta-clean)` marker goes to stdout of passing gates and is never archived, so REIFY_RELEASE_DELTA_SKIP's firing rate is unmeasurable today (reify 5376, deferred, would record it).

The reify verify pipeline injects env vars into the run_all.sh pool (~103 tests) ambiently from TWO sources that must be considered together: (1) scripts/verify.sh's run_all.sh plan-line prefix env (verify.sh:1430, e.g. REIFY_AUDIT_NO_COLD_BUILD=1 REIFY_RUN_ALL_EXCLUDE_HOST_INFRA=1) and (2) orchestrator.yaml's verify_env block (REIFY_RUN_ALL_EXCLUDE_HOST_INFRA, REIFY_GATE_EXCLUDE_HEAVY, RUSTC_WRAPPER, CARGO_INCREMENTAL). A var that changes test behavior (esp. REIFY_AUDIT_NO_COLD_BUILD, which maps to SKIP/exit-0 at verify.sh:1410-1412) can mask coverage silently. The robust guard pattern (task 5152): derive the live injected set from both sources (merge-role `verify.sh --print-plan` prefix-env extraction + the verify_env_exports awk parser at test_verify_env_ambient_isolation.sh:59-85) and cross-check it for SET EQUALITY against a checked-in keys-only ledger (tests/infra/run-all-ambient-vars.manifest, registered in scripts/verify-pipeline-paths.txt) so any new/removed injected var RED-fails by construction.

Reify verify runs cannot persist anything through .task/verify/ that must survive a PASS. dark-factory's `FailureCategory.PASSED` policy is `archive=False` (verify_categories.py:334-338) and the merge path is gated `... and not passed` (verify.py:6221), so nothing is archived on green; `.task/` is then destroyed in the lane by `git clean -xfd -e target` and an explicit rmtree (git_ops.py:7248); and `attempt-N.summary.json` is built by DF from its own subprocess bookkeeping through an explicit key whitelist (verify.py:1804-1806), so reify cannot add keys to it — it is also excluded from archiving even on FAIL. The working pattern for durable reify-side verify telemetry is an append-only .jsonl ledger under the MAIN checkout's data/verify-logs/, resolved via `reify_main_checkout()` (scripts/lib_main_checkout.sh:124) so it never defaults to a lane-relative path that a reseed wipes.

scripts/verify.sh derives REPO_ROOT from its own BASH_SOURCE location ($SCRIPT_DIR/..), NOT from cwd — so a real `verify.sh test` always operates on the real repo and cannot be redirected to a throwaway workspace. To test verify.sh behavior, either drive it hermetically via `--print-plan` (the established pattern in tests/infra/test_verify_role_prio.sh and test_occt_gated_scope.sh, which `grep -v '^#'` the printed plan), or expose a lightweight standalone action that runs only the unit under test. Adding a side-effecting feature (e.g. the PSI gate, task 4054) is best done as a dedicated action invoked as a plan step, so it can be exercised in isolation while still printing faithfully in the plan oracle.

Reify has TWO sanctioned wiring patterns for a new verify-pipeline lint/gate script, and the lighter one is often correct. (A) scripts/verify.sh add_tool line — used by check-nan-safe-ordering.sh and check-compute-trampoline-registration.sh; requires editing verify.sh, the most contended file in the repo. (B) NO verify.sh edit at all — the gate is driven solely by its own tests/infra/test_*.sh, which tests/infra/run_all.sh auto-discovers and verify.sh runs; scripts/spec-anchor-lint.sh (task #6758) does exactly this, and `grep -rn spec-anchor-lint scripts/verify.sh` returns empty. Pattern B still runs on every verify provided the infra test carries a LIVE CONTROL block asserting the shipped corpus scans clean against the real repo root (test_spec_anchor_lint.sh block (b)). Prefer B for corpus/doc lints: same coverage, no verify.sh churn.

scripts/verify.sh (landed 2026-05-26, merge 31df17e8d7, task 3766 Stage 1) is now the SINGLE source of truth for Reify verification, called by BOTH orchestrator.yaml (test_command/lint_command/type_check_command are thin `./scripts/verify.sh <test|lint|typecheck> --scope all [--include-infra]` calls) AND the git hooks (hooks/project-checks = `verify.sh all --profile debug --scope staged --include-infra`; new hooks/pre-merge-commit = `verify.sh all --profile debug --scope all`). Signature: `verify.sh <test|lint|typecheck|all> [--profile debug|release|both] [--scope all|staged] [--include-infra] [--print-plan]`. Env (sccache, CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0, jobserver-when-FIFO-exists, OCCT LD_LIBRARY_PATH, . ~/.cargo/env) is baked into verify.sh, so the hook no longer depends on ambient shell env. OCCT crate set shared via scripts/occt-scope-lib.sh.

To run a faithful standalone reify merge-gate verify (e.g. for benchmarking), outside the orchestrator: `DF_VERIFY_ROLE=merge RUSTC_WRAPPER=sccache CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 ./scripts/verify.sh all --profile both --scope all` in a detached worktree with empty target/. Facts confirmed jun9 2026: verify.sh BAKES IN the OCCT LD_LIBRARY_PATH itself (scripts/verify.sh ~lines 414-423, mirrors .cargo/run-with-occt.sh: /snap/freecad/current/usr/lib + /opt/reify-deps/lib) so no manual LD setup needed; the cargo jobserver FIFO is owned by a SEPARATE systemd unit `reify-jobserver.service` (not orchestrator-reify), CARGO_MAKEFLAGS=--jobserver-auth=fifo:/tmp/reify-jobserver — leave CARGO_MAKEFLAGS UNSET for a solo run so cargo uses -j(nproc) on an idle box (equivalent to a solo merge verify, avoids depending on the possibly-stale FIFO; the reify-jobserver-canary unit was observed failed). verify.sh wraps cargo in CARGO_PRIO = `nice -n 5` for merge role, `nice -n 15 ionice -c2 -n7` for task role. `verify.sh --print-plan` emits the exact ordered command list. Reify has TWO deliberate registries that make a file load-bearing to the verify pipeline, at two different cost points: scripts/doc-sync-paths.txt is BLUNT (any edit routes the whole diff to the full --scope all gate, via verify-pipeline-guard.sh's doc-sync clause), while scripts/verify-pipeline-infra-tests.txt is SURGICAL (an edit SELECTS just the guarding infra test at task scope, via verify.sh's select_infra_tests()). A row in the surgical registry is a first-class registration, not a lesser one — for a prose note whose only coupling is one grep, it is the proportionate choice, and `verify-pipeline-guard.sh requires-full-gate <path>` correctly returns rc=1 for such a path. Measured 2026-08-30: docs/notes/spec-anchor-contract.md, docs/reify-language-spec.md and scripts/prd-capability-check.py are all surgical-only keys with rc=1.

Fact about the reify verify pipeline (confirmed 2026-06-09): there is a deliberate-looking but consequential ASYMMETRY in who runs the infra shell-test suite. The orchestrator's test_command (`verify.sh test --scope branch --include-infra`) runs tests/infra/run_all.sh on EVERY task verify — and run_all.sh executes ALL 39 infra scripts regardless of branch scope — while the pre-merge-commit hook (`verify.sh all --profile both --scope all`, no --include-infra) does NOT. Consequence: a change that breaks any infra test can merge GREEN through the gate and then red every subsequent orchestrator task verify (exactly what task 4451 did to test_verify_failfast_order.sh on 2026-06-09). When triaging 'every task verify suddenly fails at run_all.sh', diff the infra tests against the last merge to main, not the task branches. Also note merge-role post-merge verifies export DF_VERIFY_ROLE=merge into the infra tests' environment — infra tests that shell out to verify.sh --print-plan must pin DF_VERIFY_ROLE=task or the C2 role-guard forces scope=all and narrowing assertions fail (the esc-4450-10 class; fix in-flight on branch task/verify-throughput-role-iso as of session end).

Reify verify facts verified 2026-09-11 during the verify-speed synthesis. (1) The `sccache-redis` docker container (port 6380, tailscale + localhost) runs `redis-server --maxmemory 16gb --maxmemory-policy allkeys-lru` and is EMPTY (dbsize 0, ~1 MB used, 10 MiB container RSS): the sccache SERVER user unit (`systemctl --user cat sccache.service`) carries only SCCACHE_CACHE_SIZE=100G and SCCACHE_IDLE_TIMEOUT=0, so the server's backend is local disk (100 GiB of 100 GiB, continuously evicting) and the yaml's `sccache.backend_env.SCCACHE_REDIS` reaches clients only. Leo ruled 2026-09-11: NO Redis backend (Redis is RAM-resident; a shared cache there is a 16 GB RAM cache); raise the disk cap instead (task 7425); a disk-backed shared cache, if ever justified by the laptop's measured miss cost, is sccache's S3 backend against MinIO/Garage on the workstation NVMe as a two-level L1+L2. Lifetime stats: 1.88M requests, 87.6% non-cacheable, 58% hit on the eligible rest. (2) Reify's verify pipeline NEVER runs doctests: no `--doc` anywhere in scripts/verify.sh and nextest does not run doctests; 158 files under crates/ carry doc code fences (329 unmarked ```/```rust blocks that would compile as doctests, 285 marked ignore/no_run/text). The comments-only merge-gate class (dark-factory task 5411) runs `cargo test --doc -p <touched crates>`, which is therefore a coverage INCREASE. (3) The GUI vitest lane runs on every Rust change (`RUN_GUI=$(( rust | gui ))` at verify.sh ~1391); Leo rejected a path-based narrowing because a Rust change to a Tauri command, event-channel type or wire format can break the frontend; the ruled predicate is "reify-gui in the affected-crates rdeps closure ⇒ run the lane", tsc always kept (task 7427). (4) Reify tasks 3188/3189 are OLD DONE Rust cleanups (persistent_cache slab helpers, mid_surface.rs); the "canary 3189" and "telemetry 3188" in the deep-chain PRDs are DARK-FACTORY task ids.

In reify's scripts/verify.sh, a new plan leaf must be emitted with add_tool() (not plain add()) unless the line actually reaches cargo — /opt/reify-deps/lib is a conda prefix that shadows hundreds of system sonames and outranks DT_RUNPATH, so shell/npm/git/node tool lines need the LD_LIBRARY_PATH scrub. tests/infra/test_verify_ld_library_path_scope.sh Section E ENUMERATES every plain-add() site and fails any that lacks a trailing `# ld-ok: <reason>` marker, so it catches a new unscrubbed tool line by shape even though it has never heard of its name. That guard is routed from scripts/verify.sh via the `tests/infra/test_verify_*.sh` glob row, and it runs unconditionally at merge tier — so an unmarked add() can pass a task-scope verify and then red the merge gate.

reify verify signature: tests/infra/test_verify_background_sweep_ledger.sh failing exactly A4/A5/A9/D3/E1/F4 (22 passed / 6 failed) is task #8278, not the branch under test. Its stub-cargo "passing" `DF_VERIFY_ROLE=background verify.sh typecheck` runs end with `tree-sitter-freshness.sh check` against the lane's REAL target/. When the newest-marker tree-sitter-reify build dir is stale (seeded archive target/release/build/tree-sitter-reify-02cc16f2fe233fdc, "first differing input: src/parser.c"), check exits 1 and the stub cargo can never rebuild it. It passes once any real cargo leaf (e.g. lint's clippy) rebuilds a live dir. Diagnose with `bash scripts/tree-sitter-freshness.sh check`. Durable fix (#8278): export REIFY_TS_FRESHNESS_TARGET_DIR to an empty per-run dir, as test_verify_semaphore_e2e.sh's apply_hermetic_env does. Reproduced in _lane-30 on 2026-10-12 (task 7491, esc-7491-12).

Reify scripts/verify.sh resolves REPO_ROOT from its OWN script location (`SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"; REPO_ROOT="$SCRIPT_DIR/.."`) and `cd "$REPO_ROOT"` (lines ~51-53,153). Consequence: if you run `cd <worktree> && bash scripts/verify.sh` but the `cd` SILENTLY FAILED (e.g. the worktree was reaped out from under you), verify.sh resolves `scripts/verify.sh` relative to the fallback cwd (main checkout) and verifies MAIN, not your worktree — a green result that validates nothing. Tell-tale in the log: compile paths show `/home/leo/src/reify/crates/...` (main) instead of your worktree path. ALWAYS grep the verify log to confirm it's building the intended worktree path before trusting the result. (Discovered 2026-05-29 during task 3958 recovery: a release-profile re-run silently verified main for ~25min after the worktree was reaped.)

content: Reify verify instrumentation ledger (task 7424): every top-level executed scripts/verify.sh run appends one reify.verify-run/1 JSON line to <main checkout>/data/verify-logs/verify-runs.jsonl (override REIFY_VERIFY_LEDGER_DIR). It carries per-step walls, sccache/concurrency pairs, the nextest JUnit split, the run_all block and a lane_seed block read from <lane>.seed-stamp.json. efb08054-2056-4cc3-a75b-33d7a0e3f9b7.content: tests/infra harness gotcha (task 5629): any suite that PATH-stubs cargo and then executes scripts/verify.sh must also export REIFY_TS_FRESHNESS_TARGET_DIR at a per-run tmpdir, alongside the REIFY_PSI_GATE_DISABLE / REIFY_COMPILE_GATE_DISABLE knobs. verify.sh emits scripts/tree-sitter-freshness.sh `ensure` before the cargo wave and `check` after it; with cargo stubbed nothing is ever compiled, so against the real ./target (a) `check` asserts its post-condition over archives the run never built — measured RED "STALE — the archive cargo will link was NOT built from the sources now on disk", failing the suite wholesale, and (b) `ensure`'s repair path bumps mtimes on the worktree's TRACKED tree-sitter sources (grammar.js, src/scanner.c, src/tree_sitter/*.h), which in a CoW-seeded warm lane is precisely the rebuild signal that mechanism reads. An empty target dir scans as TS_SCAN_STATUS=none and returns BEFORE ts_force_touch, so both leaves degrade to clean no-ops ("no built archive under <dir>; nothing to force/check", exit 0) — note the corollary that a throwaway target dir also means `ensure` performs NO repair, so never use one in a cleanup path that is supposed to leave the real archive scheduled for recompile. Fix HARNESS-side only: verify.sh cannot distinguish a stubbed cargo from a real one, so relaxing `check` or special-casing REIFY_INFRA_SUITE_ACTIVE inside the guard would weaken the post-condition that closes the stale-archive false-GREEN class in the real merge gate. Canonical implementation: apply_hermetic_env in tests/infra/test_verify_semaphore_e2e.sh; pinned from the guard's side by test_freshness_target_dir_override_is_a_clean_noop and test_semaphore_e2e_harness_isolates_the_freshness_guard in tests/infra/test_tree_sitter_pipeline.sh. Extends the base hermetic-execute recipe in memory de69b397-6229-44b4-858e-dff6e66ccb2b.

Completed: Version the stored draft and release records so a schema change does not break existing sessions (store.py::Stored)
Description: Draft and Released embed Analysis with extra="forbid" (record.py:11, store.py) and are re-validated on every read (store.py::_read), with no version field and no migration. Intake.prospect_view reads both on every prospect page load, and a ValidationError matches no case in error_pages.session_error_page, so after any schema change or tightened validator an existing session's whole page, chat included, becomes a 500 (web.py:95-100), and the operator page likewise. Tasks 10, 14, the criterion-to-system link and the T3 validator all change the schema or tighten validation. Found in the R13 discussion on 2026-10-07; agreed with Leo.
Analysis: PREMISES, checked on base 0a7cf7c (main = branch tip).
- The task title names store.py::Stored. That class no longer exists: an earlier task folded it into record.Frozen (record.py:12-13, ConfigDict(frozen=True, extra="forbid")). Draft (store.py:35-46) and Released (store.py:49-53) now derive from Frozen directly and embed Analysis, so the defect stands as described.
- SessionStore._read (store.py:177-179) runs kind.model_validate_json on every read. No version field exists and nothing migrates.
- Intake.prospect_view (intake.py:64-72) reads the draft and the release on every prospect page load. The /criteria and /report routes go through it too (prospect_pages.py:80-84, 102-109).
- Intake.operator_view (intake.py:125-137) reads the draft, the operator placement and the release. request_write_up, place, rewrite and release read the draft (intake.py:101-158, 204-212).
- error_pages.session_error_page (error_pages.py:11-30) has no case for ValidationError, so web._dispatch (web.py:92-104) answers 500 "Something went wrong". Any Analysis change or tightened validator therefore turns an existing session's chat page into a 500, and its operator page likewise.
- purge_unused/_last_used (intake.py:228-248) read the release for its time and leave a session whose release cannot be read in place, reporting it. tests/test_session_flow.py:347-363 pins that. A naive versioning would make every session released before a schema change "unreadable" to the purge, so no such session would ever be deleted: the 90-day promise would break.
- Deletion never reads the draft. The prospect route goes intake.delete -> _locked -> store.get (session.json only) -> shutil.rmtree. The operator route goes through by_prospect_id/readable(), which reads session.json only. So deletion already survives an unreadable draft; this task pins that with a test.

POLICY CHOSEN: an operator-facing state, not a migration table (see design decisions).
- store.RECORD_FORMAT = 1 is the record format this version writes drafts and releases in, and the only one it reads.
- Draft and Released derive from a small base, StoredWriteUp(Frozen), holding record_format: int = RECORD_FORMAT and analysis: Analysis. The format is therefore written on save by the record's own serialisation.
- On read, the store first reads only the declared format: a Frozen model _DeclaredFormat(record_format: int = 1), validated with pydantic 2.13.5's per-call model_validate_json(..., extra="ignore"). A record from before formats were numbered declares none and is format 1, so Leo's existing trial sessions keep working.
- Only a record declaring RECORD_FORMAT is validated in full. Every other outcome is returned, never raised, as UnreadableWriteUp(record_format=<declared> | None): another format, unparseable bytes, or a current-format record that fails the record's rules.
- draft() and released() return Draft/Released | UnreadableWriteUp | None.
- A new SessionStore.released_at(token) reads only released_at (a Frozen _ReleaseTime, again extra="ignore" per call) from a release in any format. A damaged release still raises there, so the purge keeps counting a release made in an older format and keeps leaving a damaged one in place.

Completed: serve: Host allow-list entries that still differ from the Host a browser sends (non-canonical INTAKE_PUBLIC_URL hosts; loopback entries on port 80)
Description: Found while planning task 35 (follow-up id agent-followup-35). Task 35 makes src/scoping_intake/cli.py derive the prospect site's Host allow-list entry from INTAKE_PUBLIC_URL the way a browser writes Host: the host in lower case, no port when it is the scheme's default (80 for http, 443 for https) or empty, any other port kept, and an IPv6 address in brackets. The derivation lives in a helper, cli._host_header(scheme, hostname, port), which _public_url calls. web.py RequestHandler._admission_refusal answers only a Host header that is in site.hosts by string equality, and otherwise replies 421 'Not found'. Two cases are left. Both are outside task 35's scope and unlikely in the deployed setup: deploy/README.md sets INTAKE_PUBLIC_URL=https://<machine>.<tailnet>.ts.net, and the units use ports 8471 and 8472.

(1) Host spellings a browser rewrites beyond case and port. Measured on 2026-10-08 with headless Chrome 151 and a capture server: http://[0:0:0:0:0:0:0:1]:P/ is sent as Host [::1]:P. Per the WHATWG URL standard but NOT measured: a non-ASCII name such as https://bücher.example is sent in punycode (xn--bcher-kva.example), and IPv4 shorthand such as http://127.1:P/ is sent as 127.0.0.1:P. urllib.parse.urlsplit keeps all three as typed (CPython 3.14.4, the project venv). The allow-list entry therefore never matches, and every prospect request gets 421. The fix is either to derive the entry the way the browser does (IPv6 compression via ipaddress, IDNA/UTS-46, IPv4 parsing) or to refuse such values at start with UnusablePublicUrl, naming the variable.

(2) cli._loopback_hosts(port) always writes the port: {127.0.0.1:P, localhost:P}. A browser leaves out port 80 for http; measured in Chrome 151, http://intake.example:80/ is sent as Host intake.example. So with --prospect-port 80 or --operator-port 80, a browser at http://localhost/ sends Host 'localhost' and gets 421. The operator site would also refuse http://127.0.0.1/. cli._host_header from task 35 could build these entries too.

solar_challenge procedure for auditing `# type: ignore` comments in tests/. Measured by task 493's amendment pass on 2026-10-13 with mypy 2.1.0. Nothing gates this: type_check_command covers src/solar_challenge only, and mypy over tests/ prints about 1,900 lines of errors.
(1) From the checkout root, run `UV_OFFLINE=1 uv run --locked --extra dev --extra web mypy --cache-dir /tmp/<dir> --warn-unused-ignores --no-error-summary <test files>`. Every tests dir is a package, and pyproject's strict [tool.mypy] applies. Each unused ignore prints as `path:line: error: Unused "type: ignore" comment [unused-ignore]`. For a multi-code ignore with one unused half, the message names that half, e.g. `Unused "type: ignore[name-defined]"`. Removing only a trailing comment moves no line, so diff the before and after output line for line.
(2) mypy hides the error an ignore suppresses. To see which name a kept `[name-defined]` ignore still covers, read ruff's F821 on that line: `uv run --locked --extra dev ruff check --no-cache --isolated --select F <file>`.
(3) Before deleting an unused ignore of another code, rerun with `--disallow-any-expr`. If the line holds an Any-typed expression, the ignore may be unused only because of that Any, from an unannotated fixture or an unresolved annotation (memory ce0bb8fb). Resolve the type, or keep the ignore.
(4) To compare against a base commit, `git archive <base> | tar -x -C /tmp/<dir>`, then run the worktree's `.venv/bin/mypy` with that dir as cwd. It reads that tree's pyproject.

mypy gotchas for a test that runs mypy as a subprocess, measured on mypy 2.1.0 (solar_challenge uv.lock, CPython 3.12.3) by task 631's architect on 2026-10-11. (1) `--output=json` is not pure JSON on stdout: the warn_unused_configs note ("pyproject.toml: note: unused section(s)...", which a one-file run under solar_challenge's pyproject always prints) and the blocking-error summary ("Found 1 error in 1 file (errors prevented further checking)") are printed as plain text among the JSON lines, and a clean run prints one empty line. JSON output also needs mypy >= 1.11, while the dev extra admits mypy>=1.0.0. The default text lines `path:line: error: message  [code]` work on every admitted mypy. (2) Exit codes: 0 means no errors, 1 means errors, and 2 means it could not check (an unreadable file, or a syntax error, which still prints its error line). `python -m mypy` with mypy not installed also exits 1, with nothing on stdout. (3) `--shadow-file <real.py> <probe.py> <real.py>` type-checks the probe under the real file's path and module name, so per-module overrides apply and errors are reported against the real path. It is mypy's equivalent of ruff's --stdin-filename for a probe of known verdict. (4) `--cache-dir=/dev/null` (os.devnull) turns the cache off. A run of tests/_surface_forms.py with no cache took 2.6-3.2 s at host load ~160 on 32 cores, and 0.8-1.3 s with a warm cache. The verify's type leg runs at the same time as its test leg in the same worktree, so a test should not share the worktree's .mypy_cache.

solar_challenge technique (measured 2026-10-11 on task/597 at 3a87401, mypy 2.1.0 from uv.lock): to confirm that mypy catches an injected mutation in one src module without editing the worktree, write the mutated copy to /tmp, e.g. with sed, and run `uv run --locked --extra dev --extra web mypy src/solar_challenge --shadow-file src/solar_challenge/web/api.py /tmp/<mutated>.py`. mypy checks the shadow file in place of that path and reports errors under the real path and line numbers. With "completed" sed-changed to "complete" in api.py's two state.status comparisons, it reported exactly 2 [comparison-overlap] errors. The real file stayed untouched, so this is safe while that file holds uncommitted edits. It is lighter than memory 293c5ff3's scratch-tree copy when only mypy needs to see the mutation; pytest still needs the scratch tree.

(1) mypy 1.4.0 is the first release that prints the [unused-ignore] code on an unused `# type: ignore`. 1.0.0 and 1.3.0 print the same line with no code. mypy's CHANGELOG, Mypy 1.4: "make it a real error code".

solar_challenge procedural tip (task 295 architect revalidation, verified 2026-10-02): to test a src patch without touching the task worktree, copy src/solar_challenge to /tmp/<dir>, patch the copy, then from the worktree run `PYTHONPATH=/tmp/<dir> uv run --extra dev --extra web pytest <files> -p no:cacheprovider`. PYTHONPATH precedes the editable install, so the copy is the module under test, which you can confirm from the /tmp paths in its warnings. Run `uv run --extra dev --extra web mypy --config-file pyproject.toml --cache-dir /tmp/<dir>/.mypy_cache /tmp/<dir>/solar_challenge` for strict typing on the copy. pyproject's pytest config has no filterwarnings=error, so a test-file copy run from /tmp behaves the same as it does in tests/.

solar_challenge review procedure (verified 2026-10-02, HEAD 0669545): when review Phase 1 reports "Failed to spawn pytest/mypy", get a real baseline by running the orchestrator's configured commands verbatim in a detached scratch worktree (git worktree add --detach /tmp/<id>-wt HEAD; uv builds its own .venv there). solar_challenge gotcha (measured 2026-10-01): the project's pytest addopts make `pytest --collect-only -q` print a <Module>/<Function> tree, not one node id per line. Grepping for '::' therefore counts 0. To compare test counts across branches, e.g. to check that an auto-merge lost no tests, read the 'N tests collected' summary line from `uv run --extra dev --extra web pytest <files> --collect-only -p no:cacheprovider`.

solar_challenge technique for checking a src refactor without touching the worktree (task 372 architect, 2026-10-08). Copy src/ and pyproject.toml into a /tmp root and swap in the patched module. Then:
- `cd /tmp/root && uv run --project <worktree> --locked --extra dev --extra web mypy src/solar_challenge` type-checks the patched tree;
- `PYTHONPATH=/tmp/root/src uv run --locked --extra dev --extra web pytest <worktree tests>` runs the worktree's tests against it, because PYTHONPATH precedes the editable install.
Confirm the swap with `python -c 'import solar_challenge.config as c; print(c.__file__)'`. For an equivalence probe, load the old module by path with importlib.util.spec_from_file_location. Compare exceptions by type NAME and message: a module loaded by path has its own ConfigurationError class.

solar_challenge scratch-prototype gotcha (task 667 architect, measured 2026-10-13 on a git-archive copy of main 1fb95da, run with the worktree's .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/unit and PYTHONPATH=<copy>/src). Running the WHOLE unit suite from such a copy gives 7 false failures plus 7 setup errors, none caused by the change under test:
- tests/unit/test_per_task_verify.py (2)
- tests/unit/test_offline_lane_contracts.py::test_the_job_collects_its_suite_and_nothing_else (4 ids)
- tests/unit/test_interpreter_matrix_lane.py (1)
These tests shell out to `uv run --locked ...` inside the copy, which has no .venv. uv then tries to build one from PyPI and fails behind the sandbox proxy with "tunnel error: unsuccessful". solar_challenge procedure (task 576 architect, measured 2026-10-10 at main 1a13669): to try a planned edit without touching the worktree, export a copy with `git archive HEAD | tar -x -C <dir>`. Run the worktree's .venv/bin/python with PYTHONPATH=<dir>/src from a directory outside the repo, so the copy shadows the editable install. Run pytest and mypy from <dir> too, so they pick up its pyproject.toml and tests/. Do NOT add `python -I`: isolated mode ignores PYTHONPATH, so the editable install's worktree src is imported instead, silently. Confirm with `print(module.__file__)`.

solar_challenge gotcha when checking a change to a tests/ helper (e.g. tests/_css_classes.py) against a scratch copy of tests/ (measured 2026-10-10 by the task 596 architect, task/596 at 86eb58b, CPython 3.12.3). From the worktree root, `PYTHONPATH=/tmp/<copy> uv run ... python -c "import tests..."` imports the WORKTREE's tests package: -c puts the cwd first on sys.path, ahead of PYTHONPATH. A before/after comparison run that way compares the worktree with itself and comes out identical whatever the copy holds. Run a script FILE under /tmp instead: its own directory, then PYTHONPATH, comes first, so `tests` resolves to the copy. Confirm it by printing tests._css_classes.__file__. For pytest, copy pyproject.toml into the copy's root and run from there, so rootdir is the copy (the header's 'rootdir:' line shows it). Copies of src/ are not affected, because src/ is not under the cwd.

solar_challenge procedural gotcha (task 491 architect, measured 2026-10-08 on main 23c019e, CPython 3.12.3). For a task-455-style byte-identity probe, you write `git show HEAD:src/solar_challenge/web/charts.py` to /tmp and load it with importlib.util.spec_from_file_location + module_from_spec. Set sys.modules[spec.name] = module BEFORE spec.loader.exec_module(module). Without it, exec_module raises AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute '__dict__' inside dataclasses: charts.py defines a @dataclass under `from __future__ import annotations`, and dataclasses looks the class's module up in sys.modules. To prototype a whole change without touching a worktree, rsync the tree (minus .venv, .git, .task) to /tmp and run the worktree's .venv/bin/python -m pytest there with PYTHONPATH=<copy>/src. The venv's editable install is a plain __editable__ .pth path entry, so PYTHONPATH shadows it. For mypy, run the venv's mypy from the copy's root.

solar_challenge gotcha (task 319 architect, measured on main f979422, 2026-10-01). The shared test helpers tests/_pyproject.py and tests/_interpreters.py layer one way only: tests/_interpreters.py line 14 imports load_project_table from tests._pyproject. So tests/_pyproject.py, home of declared_floor, must never import from tests/_interpreters.py; that would be an import cycle (heuristic 13). A second reason not to reuse tests/_interpreters.py::minor_versions_where_marker_holds for 'every environment' reasoning: it varies only python_version/python_full_version and evaluates every other marker variable (platform_machine, sys_platform, ...) at THIS host's value.

solar_challenge gotcha (extends memory d0e9334a): to run a test file that exists only on another unmerged task branch, do NOT extract just that file with `git show task/<N>:<path> > /tmp/x.py`. It fails with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'tests'` when the guard imports sibling helpers that also live only on that branch (task/176's guard needs tests/_synthetic_weather.py and tests/integration/_peak_rate_energy.py). Extract the whole tests tree with `git archive task/<N> tests | tar -x -C /tmp/x`, then run `PYTHONPATH=/tmp/x uv run --extra dev pytest -c pyproject.toml --rootdir /tmp/x -o addopts="" /tmp/x/tests/<path> -p no:cacheprovider`. `solar_challenge` still resolves to the worktree's editable src (check with `uv run --extra dev python -c "import solar_challenge.flow as f; print(f.__file__)"`). solar_challenge refinement of memory b212a70b's base-vs-refactored mutation check (task 585 amend pass, 2026-10-11): the base copy of the test module can live in /tmp instead of tests/unit, so the worktree is never written. Extract it with `git show HEAD:<test file>` into /tmp/<dir>/, then from the worktree root run `PYTHONPATH=/tmp/<dir> uv run --locked --extra dev --extra web python -m pytest -p <mutation plugin> --rootdir=. -c pyproject.toml -o addopts= --tb=no -q -rA /tmp/<dir>/test_old.py tests/unit/<refactored module>`; `python -m` puts the worktree root on sys.path, so the /tmp module's `tests.*` imports resolve. solar_challenge: to dry-run a planned src+test change without editing the task worktree (e.g. to prove a RED/GREEN premise while a background pytest run is using the worktree), copy src/, tests/ and pyproject.toml to a scratch dir, apply the edits there, and run `PYTHONPATH=<scratch>/src:<scratch> <worktree>/.venv/bin/python -m pytest ...` from the scratch dir (and `<worktree>/.venv/bin/mypy --config-file pyproject.toml src/solar_challenge` for types). PYTHONPATH takes precedence over the editable install, so `solar_challenge` resolves to the scratch copy; drop the `<scratch>/src` entry to run the edited tests against the worktree's original source (the RED check). Verified 2026-09-30 on task/171 at 3d769a9 by printing `solar_challenge.web.assistant.__file__` in both modes.

solar_challenge procedure (task 555 step-1, 2026-10-08, commit 00b24e6; complements the architect's scratch-copy entry on the same topic): to record OLD vs NEW for a characterization pin that passes on its first run, drive the transient mutations from a script under /tmp. For each mutation it writes the mutated module into the worktree, runs ONE pytest call over the edited test file plus an untracked copy of HEAD's version (git show HEAD:<file> > tests/unit/<name>_old<task>.py, unlinked in a finally block), then restores the module with git checkout -- <module>. OLD shows no failure and NEW shows exactly the named test, with the summary count ('1 failed, 109 passed' = 56 edited + 54 old tests). Pass --tb=line to get each failure's file:line and message on one line. Gotcha: on this host `uv run` prints a 'VIRTUAL_ENV ... does not match the project environment path' warning on stderr, so with stderr merged into stdout the last output line is that warning, not pytest's summary; take the summary with a regex such as r'^=+ (.*?) in [0-9.]+s'.

solar_challenge doc-only change recipe (task 368, measured 2026-10-02): to prove a docstring/help-string diff changed no executable line, parse the HEAD version (`git show HEAD:<path>`) and the working-tree version with `ast`, strip each Module/Class/Function docstring, blank the one permitted help= kwarg if any, and compare `ast.dump` of the two trees; keep the script in /tmp, uncommitted. The verify set `tests/unit/test_optimize_enumerate.py tests/unit/test_optimize_rank.py tests/integration/test_optimize_cli.py tests/unit/test_docstring_examples.py -m 'not slow and not e2e'` runs 98 passed, 1 deselected in about 35 s wall (510 MB max RSS), and `mypy src/solar_challenge` (47 files) is clean, so neither needs a long timeout.

content: solar_challenge mypy-over-tests gotcha (task 688 architect, measured 2026-10-13 at main 7dfea36, mypy 2.1.0 from the worktree's .venv). The `warn_unused_configs` note line `pyproject.toml: note: unused section(s): module = ['flask.*', 'plotly.*', 'richardsonpy.*', 'solar_challenge.web.*']` depends on WHERE mypy runs, not on the code. Run from the worktree root over 20 test files, mypy printed it. Run from a `git archive HEAD | tar -x` copy in /tmp over byte-identical files, it did not, with the same fresh --cache-dir, the same binary and the same 116 errors. So when you compare base and branch with mypy over tests/, run both sides from the same checkout root (baseline first, then edit, then rerun), or strip that note line before diffing. Otherwise the archive-copy route in the tests-type-ignore-audit procedure shows a spurious one-line difference.

solar_challenge procedure (task 615 architect, measured on main 758f36e, 2026-10-10): to prototype test edits, or run transient src mutations, without touching a task worktree, use a scratch copy.
1. Copy: `git archive HEAD | tar -x -C /tmp/<scratch>`.
2. Run the worktree's own interpreter from the scratch copy: `<worktree>/.venv/bin/python -m pytest <paths> -p no:cacheprovider -o addopts=`. pytest imports tests.* from the scratch copy, and solar_challenge from the worktree's editable install.
3. To mutate src as well, prefix PYTHONPATH=<scratch>/src so the scratch package is imported ahead of the editable install.
Never run `uv run` inside the scratch copy against the worktree's .venv: that re-points the editable install at the scratch tree.
For node ids use `pytest --collect-only -q`; `-qq` prints only per-file counts.

b212a70b-67bb-46a2-bf10-0c833e1632f1.content: solar_challenge procedure (task 615 implementer, 2026-10-10): to show that a test-only refactor still fails where the base test did under a transient src mutation (e.g. of src/solar_challenge/web/charts.py), run the base version of the test module beside the refactored one. Write `git show <base-sha>:tests/unit/test_x.py > tests/unit/test_zz<task>base_x.py`; tests/unit is a package, so the copy imports as a module of its own with no name clash. Apply each mutation to the src file, run both files, then restore the src file from a saved copy and delete the test copy in a `finally`. A /tmp scratch tree (task 551's recipe) does not work for src mutations: the package is installed editable from the worktree's src, so the scratch tree would import the unmutated worktree code. Afterwards confirm `git diff --quiet -- src/` and `git status --short --untracked-files=all`.

ce0bb8fb-2c0f-4f7d-aee6-6fa4408ca771.content:
solar_challenge mypy gotcha for tests/ (measured 2026-10-03, task 352 architect, main 9fa9dd5). A `# type: ignore[misc]` on a deliberate frozen-dataclass assignment can be reported as `[unused-ignore]` only because the variable's type is an unresolved string annotation. Example: `yp.year = 99` in a method annotated `-> "YearPoint":  # type: ignore[name-defined]` when the module never imports YearPoint. That annotation is pyflakes F821, and mypy then treats yp as Any.

Resolve the annotation instead of deleting the misc ignore: `if TYPE_CHECKING: from solar_challenge.finance import YearPoint`. The misc ignore becomes needed and the name-defined ignore becomes unused. In tests/unit/test_finance_multi_year_curve.py this applies to L54/L209 (misc) and L22/L161/L174 (name-defined). Deleting the misc ignores would plant errors that resurface once task 300's F821 sweep resolves the names.

Completed: Bound DB I/O on the dispatch loop: set tcp_user_timeout/keepalives on the engine so a network partition to the DB cannot stall keep-alive for ~15 min
Description: FINDING (review 20260928T154500, control deep read; PLAUSIBLE — mechanism read in code at HEAD 417e306, partition timing from kernel defaults, not measured).

WHAT'S WRONG: every actuation, including every ~20 s refresh, does a synchronous feedback write on the dispatch loop thread (control/controller.py ~L348 → control/feedback_store.py ~L111). src/solar_challenge_platform/db/session.py (~L95-109) sets statement_timeout and connect timeout but no tcp_user_timeout / TCP keepalives. On a network PARTITION (packets dropped, not connection refused) the pool pre-ping or an in-flight write blocks for the kernel retransmission timeout (~15 min); each reconnect then costs the 10 s connect timeout. Keep-alive stalls fleet-wide; devices fail safe to Passthru, but a DB outage becomes a control outage (and alerts see a dispatch wedge).

FIX: add libpq tcp_user_timeout (e.g. 5 s) and keepalives_idle/interval/count to the Postgres connect args for all roles; make feedback-log writes best-effort off the refresh critical path (bounded queue drained by a worker, drop-and-count on overflow) so actuation never waits on the audit DB. Any new `--print-plan` sandbox fixture that cp's a subset of scripts/ must, after its cp block and before `git init`, call: `assert_source_closure_copied "$REPO_ROOT/scripts" "$dir/scripts" verify.sh || exit 1`. It walks verify.sh's FULL transitive `source`/`.` closure (not just direct sources) and fails loudly with "copy-list drift: missing <lib>". Pure-variable-indirection libs like lib_clock_stop.sh (`source "$var"`) are a documented parser exclusion and stay hand-copied.

Adding any `source "$SCRIPT_DIR/<lib>.sh"` line to scripts/verify.sh reds SIX infra suites at once with `copy-list drift: missing <lib> (transitive source closure of verify.sh)`: test_verify_scope.sh (2 cp-sites), test_compute_trampoline_registration_wired.sh (2), test_scope_boundary.sh, test_verify_throughput.sh, test_verify_pipeline_guard.sh, test_verify_release_delta_skip.sh. GOTCHA: adding a line to `scripts/verify.sh`'s plan (e.g. a new lint-block entry beside check_event_inventory.sh) bumps the non-comment plan-line count, which `tests/infra/test_verify_throughput.sh`'s note↔oracle sync-drift guard enforces against `docs/notes/verify-scope-throughput.md`'s `<!-- THROUGHPUT-COUNTS:BEGIN/END -->` sentinel (a markdown table of per-shape × per-scope counts). You MUST bump the note to match: both the prose "Plan-Step Counts" table AND the machine sentinel, plus a "_Counts bumped YYYY-MM-DD (task N):_" changelog entry. The count appears in scope=all for every shape, and scope=branch only for RUN_RUST shapes (reify-doc, reify-eval); docs-only branch stays 0 and gui-only branch stays a fixed small number (the Rust-infra lint block isn't emitted there). BROADER LESSON: before merging any verify.sh plan change, run the FULL hermetic infra pool locally — `REIFY_AUDIT_NO_COLD_BUILD=1 REIFY_RUN_ALL_EXCLUDE_HOST_INFRA=1 bash tests/infra/run_all.sh` (112 tests, ~minutes) — not just the tests you think are relevant. Task 5093's first merge-verify FAILED on this because local checks only ran the gate/wiring/drift-guard, not the full pool; it cost a full merge-queue round-trip.

verify-pipeline-guard.sh auto-derives load-bearing libs ONLY from verify.sh's DIRECT `source "$SCRIPT_DIR/<lib>"` lines. A lib sourced TRANSITIVELY (e.g. lib_test_semaphore.sh sources a helper, which verify.sh sources) is invisible to the guard — so editing that helper alone can take the merge-worker config fast-path and ambush the next Rust task. Description: Draft and Released embed Analysis with extra="forbid" (record.py:11, store.py) and are re-validated on every read (store.py::_read), with no version field and no migration. Intake.prospect_view reads both on every prospect page load, and a ValidationError matches no case in error_pages.session_error_page, so after any schema change or tightened validator an existing session's whole page, chat included, becomes a 500 (web.py:95-100), and the operator page likewise. Tasks 10, 14, the criterion-to-system link and the T3 validator all change the schema or tighten validation. Found in the R13 discussion on 2026-10-07; agreed with Leo.
Analysis: PREMISES, checked on base 0a7cf7c (main = branch tip).
- The task title names store.py::Stored. That class no longer exists: an earlier task folded it into record.Frozen (record.py:12-13, ConfigDict(frozen=True, extra="forbid")). Draft (store.py:35-46) and Released (store.py:49-53) now derive from Frozen directly and embed Analysis, so the defect stands as described.
- SessionStore._read (store.py:177-179) runs kind.model_validate_json on every read. No version field exists and nothing migrates.
- Intake.prospect_view (intake.py:64-72) reads the draft and the release on every prospect page load. The /criteria and /report routes go through it too (prospect_pages.py:80-84, 102-109).
- Intake.operator_view (intake.py:125-137) reads the draft, the operator placement and the release. request_write_up, place, rewrite and release read the draft (intake.py:101-158, 204-212).
- error_pages.session_error_page (error_pages.py:11-30) has no case for ValidationError, so web._dispatch (web.py:92-104) answers 500 "Something went wrong". Any Analysis change or tightened validator therefore turns an existing session's chat page into a 500, and its operator page likewise.
- purge_unused/_last_used (intake.py:228-248) read the release for its time and leave a session whose release cannot be read in place, reporting it. tests/test_session_flow.py:347-363 pins that. A naive versioning would make every session released before a schema change "unreadable" to the purge, so no such session would ever be deleted: the 90-day promise would break.
- Deletion never reads the draft. The prospect route goes intake.delete -> _locked -> store.get (session.json only) -> shutil.rmtree. The operator route goes through by_prospect_id/readable(), which reads session.json only. So deletion already survives an unreadable draft; this task pins that with a test.

POLICY CHOSEN: an operator-facing state, not a migration table (see design decisions).
- store.RECORD_FORMAT = 1 is the record format this version writes drafts and releases in, and the only one it reads.
- Draft and Released derive from a small base, StoredWriteUp(Frozen), holding record_format: int = RECORD_FORMAT and analysis: Analysis. The format is therefore written on save by the record's own serialisation.
- On read, the store first reads only the declared format: a Frozen model _DeclaredFormat(record_format: int = 1), validated with pydantic 2.13.5's per-call model_validate_json(..., extra="ignore"). A record from before formats were numbered declares none and is format 1, so Leo's existing trial sessions keep working.
- Only a record declaring RECORD_FORMAT is validated in full. Every other outcome is returned, never raised, as UnreadableWriteUp(record_format=<declared> | None): another format, unparseable bytes, or a current-format record that fails the record's rules.
- draft() and released() return Draft/Released | UnreadableWriteUp | None.

Gotcha: solar_challenge's review/briefing.yaml POSTURE header + deferred-task tally recur (3 occurrences: task 91 fix -> task 92 cancelled/redundant -> task 96 third recurrence) because the fix approach commits a STATIC point-in-time snapshot count inside a slow-moving task branch, while reconciliation cycles file new tasks faster than that branch can land — a merge-latency-vs-churn-rate race, not a defect in any individual fix (task 99's 2026-07-29 addendum: briefing.yaml still read "96 tasks" while the live tree was already at 99). Task 96 landed 2026-09-16 (commit c17adbba0c8108e8ddb087e1d3a9cf52bf6b4982), closing the third occurrence — but it was itself just another static point-fix, not a switch to dynamic generation, so the underlying race is unresolved and a 4th occurrence remains plausible. FIX: generate the POSTURE header / deferred-task tally DYNAMICALLY at merge time or read time instead of hand-editing a static count into a task branch. Distinct from the sibling gotcha at memory 7295f77e-6f96-477b-9f2a-ab688144e62b (which covers briefing.yaml's OTHER stale-section classes and the "file-content-looks-landed is not proof of a commit" lesson) — that entry addresses sweep SCOPE, this one addresses the generation-time ROOT CAUSE. Promoted from observation ba1b3990-3a23-4775-82ac-e08d8c0f16ac (2026-07-30), which remains the fuller incident-history record.

RESOLUTION (2026-09-18, task 107, commit 3f4a1c1002850783480b6d52002fc30e6458639c; CORRECTED 2026-09-18 per solar_challenge_platform memory 0209553a-227e-47b9-9e41-96b970aeabd1 / task 183 / esc-183-1): the 4th occurrence did NOT switch to dynamic generation as the FIX above proposed. It DELETED the derived tally/POSTURE-header counts from review/briefing.yaml entirely, replacing them with an explicit "re-derive live via get_statuses" instruction, and relies solely on a `# human-edited` marker comment convention (preserved by the /review-briefing regenerator per briefing-schema.md) to prevent reintroduction via regeneration. An offline pytest guard (tests/unit/test_review_briefing.py) was added mid-branch (commits 2b4c6a0, 61c57c4, eeb741c) but was DELETED by commit b435273 before merge — to resolve two blocking review issues, since it covered nothing executable and was trivially bypassable (e.g. "2 in progress", "96 total tasks" slipped its regex). The guard did NOT land; the merged commit touched review/briefing.yaml only. There is therefore NO automated build-time enforcement against a hand-maintained count reappearing — only the delete + `# human-edited` marker documentation convention guards against recurrence, so a 5th occurrence is not structurally foreclosed the way the original (uncorrected) account of this resolution claimed. See ba1b3990-3a23-4775-82ac-e08d8c0f16ac and observation 89939e89-5159-4b9f-bd93-52bcfaece322 for full detail.

9e0097a9-9060-4839-a7c0-78743ecefcaa.content: solar_challenge test gotcha, measured 2026-10-14 by task 674's architect at ad42de8. tests/unit/test_web_template_macros.py::test_every_library_macro_is_called_by_some_template counts a components/macros.html macro as used only if some template imports it by name with {% from %} and calls it. A call from another macro inside macros.html does not count (e.g. chart_panel calling chart_container). So a change that removes a macro's last template caller must also delete that macro, or fold it into its in-file caller, in the same commit; otherwise the test fails, naming the macro. That is what happened when compare.html moved from chart_container to chart_panel.

candidates.content: Reify monomorph clones (Bearing$GasketSeal, built in compile_builder/auto_type_param_phase.rs) keep the ORIGINAL ValueCellId structure component — their cells are still keyed ValueCellId("Bearing","seal"), not ("Bearing$GasketSeal","seal"). Because monomorphs are APPENDED to ctx.templates, reify-eval/src/graph.rs inserts them after the generic and the substituted cell overwrites the generic template's unsubstituted TypeParam cell in graph.value_cells. That insert-order accident is the only reason the debug-only assert_value_cell_types_representable (engine_eval.rs:210) does not fire on the generic's own cells; an uninstantiated generic panics, and two monomorphs of one generic collide last-write-wins on the same id.

In reify, a generic `structure def Foo<T> { param x : T }` reaches `EvaluationGraph::from_templates` verbatim: the generic template SURVIVES monomorphisation in `CompiledModule.templates` still carrying `cell_type = Type::TypeParam("T")`. A successful `auto:` resolution is nevertheless safe only because the synthesized `Foo$Bar` monomorph re-uses the SAME `ValueCellId` (`Foo.x`, not `Foo$Bar.x`) with the substituted type, and `graph.value_cells` is a map — last writer wins. Consequence: scanning `compiled.templates` for `Type::TypeParam` cells is NOT a valid detector for the debug-build `assert_value_cell_types_representable` panic; it over-fires on every successful generic instantiation. The exact detector is to build `reify_eval::graph::EvaluationGraph::from_templates(&compiled.templates)` and test each `value_cells` entry with the public `reify_eval::is_representable_cell_type` — the same graph and the same predicate the assertion itself uses.

reify-eval instance-scope gotchas (measured 2026-10-07, HEAD 3bae3c7bda): (1) `where`-guard cells (`T.__guard_N`) exist only at template scope; sub-instance elaboration never materializes `Root.t.__guard_N`, so instance-scoped code must evaluate the rescoped `CompiledGuardedGroup::guard_expr` itself. (2) reify-expr's DeterminacyPredicate (`determined(x)` etc.) hits `debug_assert!(false)`, a debug-build PANIC, when its cell is absent from the determinacy snapshot, while a plain ValueRef to an absent cell safely yields Undef. Any rescoped expr containing determined() needs its cell present in the determinacy map. (3) The collapsed `Value::StructureInstance` at a sub cell (`Root.u = Cube { body: undef, vol: undef, w }`) keeps stale `undef` for geometry-derived lets, even after the per-member cell `Root.u.vol` is folded post-geometry. Compare PARAM fields, never collapsed let fields, when deciding whether an instance matches template defaults.

FACT/DISCOVERY (jun8, reify auto-type-param): the M-013 "no production code applies Type::TypeParam→StructureRef to cells/IR" gap and the eval representability invariant are two views of the SAME unreached cell. crates/reify-eval/src/engine_eval.rs:144 assert_value_cell_types_representable PANICS (debug) on a value cell typed Type::TypeParam (is_representable_cell_type :68-72; StructureRef is permitted Undef-only). Today NO .ri reaches it because zero .ri files use a type-param in a value position (`param x : T`) — verified by grep; the only such construct lives in reify-compiler unit tests (trait_bounds_tests.rs) on the compile_source path that never builds an EvaluationGraph. So the audit's "eval sees the abstract param → Real/Undef" describes what WOULD happen, guarded by that panic. Consequence: the M-013 substitution pass is NET-POSITIVE for the invariant (it removes the only construct that could trip it, replacing TypeParam with representable StructureRef) — and the invariant is precisely what FORCES the substitution to exist before any T-in-body cell may reach eval.

Reify: `reify eval <file.ri>` prints every top-level value cell keyed exactly as `ValueCellId::new(entity, cell)` (e.g. `Fairlead.stroke = 0.063 m`), including `param`s and cells of nested `sub`s under both the bare template key and the composed `Assembly.sub.cell` path. That makes it a seconds-scale oracle for "will a Rust e2e test's `result.values.get(&ValueCellId::new(E, C))` resolve?" — check it before writing the test instead of rebuilding the test binary. GOTCHA on the sibling `reify check` path: geometry-consumer builtins are unresolvable there, so any file using `volume()`/similar emits `error: \`volume\` could not be resolved: ... only resolvable on the build()/tessellate() path` as PRE-EXISTING baseline noise (prj/printer_v01/dev_capstan.ri emits two). Diff against an untouched baseline run before treating those as your regression.

reify-compiler integration tests can drive full compile→eval and inspect evaluated cell Values: use reify_test_support::eval_source(source) (gated by the `eval-helpers` feature, which reify-compiler's dev-deps already enable in crates/reify-compiler/Cargo.toml) and look up a cell with result.values.get(&reify_core::ValueCellId::new("StructureName","cell")), then match reify_ir::Value. This is the way to pin VALUE facts (e.g. composition order) that typing tests can't — both a∘b and b∘a type identically as AffineMap(3). Pattern reference: crates/reify-eval/tests/stdlib_constants_e2e.rs:16-21.

Reify generics substrate, measured 2026-09-25 with target/debug/reify: (1) `structure def G<T: HasShaft> { sub m : T }` -> `error: sub-component "m" references unknown structure "T"` — entity.rs lowers MemberDecl::Sub to Type::StructureRef(name) and conformance/sub_component_validation.rs::check_sub_structure_existence checks only prelude+local templates, never the enclosing type_params; trait-typed subs (`sub motor : NemaMotor`) fail the same way. (2) `param m : T` in an UNinstantiated generic makes debug `reify check` panic (engine_eval.rs:210 unrepresentable cell_type TypeParam) — tracked #7225. (3) `auto` type params DO monomorphise (eval shows `MotorMount$Nema23`) and pick correctly via trait-required params, but member reads through the slot afterwards are INDETERMINATE. (4) explicit `Foo<Bar>()` is never monomorphised (#6853). Note: spec §3.9.1/§3.9.2 type-ERASURE applies to generic fns/enums, NOT structure type params — do not conflate.

Reify gotcha (task #6851): injecting a real ConstraintChecker into a compile entry point is what makes `auto:` type-param resolution genuinely FAIL, and `phase_auto_type_param_resolution` gates all substitution behind `if !sigma.is_empty()` — so a failed resolution synthesizes no monomorph and a `param x : T` member keeps `cell_type = Type::TypeParam("T")` into the evaluation graph, where reify-eval's debug-only `assert_value_cell_types_representable` PANICS (and in release yields a silently wrong TypeKindMismatch/Undef). Any caller adopting `compile_with_stdlib_checked` must pair it with a containment guard. Detect the hazard structurally via `EvaluationGraph::from_templates` + `reify_eval::is_representable_cell_type`, NOT by matching AutoTypeParam* DiagnosticCodes: on a SUCCESSFUL resolution the generic template survives carrying a TypeParam-typed cell and only the monomorph's substituted type wins the shared ValueCellId in the graph, so a flat template scan over-fires on every successful generic instantiation.

Reify gotcha (measured 2026-10-03, main 7da9051b0e): explicit sub type-args and type-param defaults never reach the compiler as Type::Applied or Type::Error. entity.rs's two sub type-arg arms (~3281, ~5674) and convert_type_params' default arm (type_resolution.rs ~4518) match `Named { name, .. }`, which drops nested args, so `Box<SealA>` becomes StructureRef("Box") and `List<Real>` becomes StructureRef("List"). Any unknown name falls back to StructureRef(name) with no diagnostic unless the type param has a bound. A quick way to probe compile+eval behaviour without building tests is the warm lane's prebuilt `target/debug/reify check|eval <file.ri>`.

In reify, `compile_source_with_stdlib` CANNOT detect a leaked `Type::TypeParam` in a compiled module — you must use `reify_test_support::check_source_with_stdlib` (available to any crate with the `reify-test-support` `eval-helpers` dev-dependency). The debug-only `assert_value_cell_types_representable` at crates/reify-eval/src/engine_eval.rs:210 runs over the HYDRATED GRAPH, not over `compiled.templates`, so a generic template carrying `Type::TypeParam` cells is inert while nothing points at it and only panics once a `SubComponentDecl.structure_name` drags it into the graph. Consequence: a compiler-only test that asserts over `compiled.templates` can pass while the same source panics at eval. In release builds the assert is `#[cfg(debug_assertions)]`-gated (engine_eval.rs:4992), so the same graph degrades silently to `Value::Undef` / `EngineError::TypeKindMismatch`.

Reify compiler: a builtin-call typing arm in expr.rs's NoUserFunctions ladder can safely set a value-cell's type to Type::StructureRef("Nominal") even when the builtin evaluates to a concrete Value::Map/Int/List (not Value::Undef). Reason: the only value-vs-type check, value_type_kind_matches (reify-eval/src/lib.rs:215), is invoked ONLY on param-override/admin-edit paths (engine_admin.rs:127, engine_edit.rs) — NOT on the Engine::eval cold-start for let-cells; and the debug-only invariant that DOES run during normal eval, assert_value_cell_types_representable (engine_eval.rs:144), explicitly permits Type::StructureRef (engine_eval.rs:122-124). Confirmed empirically: §13 joint builtins (prismatic/couple/bind/…) already carry a first-arg-fallback cell type that mismatches their stored Value::Map today, yet mechanism eval tests pass. This is the load-bearing premise behind the constructor-signature-family pattern (math_signatures.rs, dynamics body_mass_props→StructureRef("MassProperties"), and task 4311's joint_signatures.rs) and the planned B1/B2 follow-ups (tolerancing, geometry Plane/Axis).

EvaluationGraph::from_templates (crates/reify-eval/src/graph.rs:320) hydrates value cells from EVERY compiled template with no filter on template.type_params, so an abstract generic like `structure def Bearing<T: Seal> { param seal : T }` injects `Bearing.seal : TypeParam("T")` into graph.value_cells and trips assert_value_cell_types_representable (engine_eval.rs:208) in debug builds — even when the generic is never instantiated. Successful `auto:` resolution masks this only by accident: a monomorph clone keeps the ORIGINAL entity name in its cell ids (mono.name becomes "Bearing$GasketSeal" but cell ids stay "Bearing.seal") and monomorphs are ctx.templates.extend-ed AFTER the generic, so the substituted StructureRef cell overwrites the TypeParam cell in the map.

Reify has TWO distinct ValueCellId entity scopings that are easy to conflate, and mixing them silently produces no-op code rather than an error. (1) STRUCTURE-NAME scoping: every `TopologyTemplate.value_cells` id is minted `ValueCellId::new(&structure.name, ..)` by the compiler (reify-compiler/src/entity.rs:6066 for params, :6197 for lets). Anything that walks `templates[*].value_cells` — e.g. resolve_order's auto_owner map — is keyed this way. (2) INSTANCE-PATH scoping: `{parent}.{sub}.{member}` ids exist only in the runtime ValueMap, created by `elaborate_child_instance` (reify-eval/src/engine_eval.rs:4204). These are produced by structural-query expansion (`apply_cost_aggregation`, reify-eval/src/structural_query.rs:686, over `enumerate_descendants` paths `{prefix}.{sub}` / `{prefix}.{sub}[{idx}]` seeded at `template.name`) AND by the compiler for sub-member accesses (`format!("{}.{}", scope.entity_name, sub_name)` at reify-compiler/src/expr.rs:843, :1211, :3904, :3935, :5595). Consequence: looking up a structural-query-expanded or sub-member-access id in any template-derived map always misses. Because such lookups are usually `if let Some(..)`, the miss is silent — the feature just does nothing. Task #5334's delta cluster formation shipped green over exactly this bug: the hand-built test fixtures used `TopologyTemplateBuilder::new("Child")` while naming that template's own cells with the instance path `"Parent.childinst"`, a shape the compiler cannot emit, so the tests passed while real .ri modules formed zero clusters. When a test fixture's cell-id shape is load-bearing, build it from real source via `reify_test_support::parse_and_compile_with_stdlib` rather than `TopologyTemplateBuilder`. Note that reify-test-support is a dev-dependency of reify-eval, so in-crate `#[cfg(test)]` modules under src/ can use the real compiler AND still see pub(crate) internals.

Reify vacuity trap: a `compile_with_stdlib`-clean assertion can NEVER prove a stdlib function is registered as a language-level built-in. `crates/reify-compiler/src/expr.rs` (~line 952-968) falls ANY unknown function-call name through to a generic `CompiledExpr::FunctionCall` typed as `compiled_args.first().result_type`, emitting no undefined-name diagnostic. Measured 2026-08-26 on main-ancestor fb265292f2: `examples/topology_selectors/block_inertia.ri`, calling the entirely unregistered `moment_of_inertia`, compiled with ZERO diagnostics. The non-vacuous observable is the compiled value cell's `cell_type`: an unregistered selector yields `Type::Geometry` (the first-arg fallback), which `reify_eval::engine_eval::is_representable_cell_type` rejects and `assert_value_cell_types_representable` turns into a hard debug-build panic inside `Engine::eval`. Assert on cell_type, not on "no error diagnostics".

reify structural facts measured 2026-09-03 at main c8bfba6087, each a named blast-radius item for work touching the FEA result structs or the solver test surface. (1) `BucklingResult` is pinned at EXACTLY 4 param cells by crates/reify-compiler/tests/buckling_stdlib_compile.rs ("BucklingResult should have exactly 4 param cells"), and `ModalResult` at EXACTLY 6 by crates/reify-compiler/tests/modal_options_validation_tests.rs ("ModalResult should have exactly 6 param cells") — adding a field to either moves the assertion, its message and the required-param name list beside it. (2) crates/reify-solver-elastic test binaries are GATE-RESIDENT BY DEFAULT: scripts/heavy-test-filter-lib.sh's REIFY_HEAVY_NEXTEST_FILTER excludes only {determinism, analytical_validation, modal_benchmarks} from that package (plus buckling_smoke and fea_diagnostics_e2e from reify-eval-fea-tests), so a NEW solver test binary joins the merge gate immediately and inherits .config/nextest.toml's default 1200s slow-timeout unless given its own [[profile.default.overrides]]. (3) `@optimized` is well-worn substrate — 55 uses across crates/reify-compiler/stdlib/*.ri — so converting a pure `.ri` stdlib helper into a Rust trampoline (needed whenever a helper must raise a diagnostic, since Reify `constraint` clauses express only scalar predicates over a struct's own cells and cannot express "this call is invalid") is a port of a live shape, not a new seam.

Reify: a user `structure def`'s runtime Value::StructureInstance is built at FOUR independent sites, so any change to what an instance carries must cover all of them: (1) reify-expr eval_structure_instance_ctor (lowered in reify-compiler expr.rs from the authoritative template for entity-scope ctors, and from build_structure_def_skeleton templates for fn-body ctors); (2) engine_eval.rs plain-sub collapse (writes ValueCellId(parent, sub) and the "{parent}.{sub}"/__self alias); (3) engine_eval.rs keyed-sub per-key collapse; (4) unfold.rs nested-sub collapse. The three engine collapses gather fields from child_template.value_cells scoped cells only. Sub elaboration (unfold.rs elaborate_child_instance_nested) does NOT evaluate the child template's guarded_groups at all, so `Test.s.g` scoped cells never exist for where-guarded members (measured 2026-09-29, task #5935).

Description: Discovered by task #7008's architect (out of scope there). OBSERVED on the warm-lane debug binary (target/debug/reify, built 2026-10-05) with this file:

`reify check` panics: "thread 'main' panicked at crates/reify-eval/src/engine_eval.rs:210:9: unrepresentable cell_type: value cell `S.v` has cell_type TypeParam("T") post-compilation".

LOCATION: crates/reify-compiler/src/expr.rs, the OverloadResolution::NoMatch arm's default-padding branch (`try_default_padding` → `let result_type = padded_fn.return_type.clone();`, ~line 3263). It copies the generic return type verbatim. The OverloadResolution::Resolved arm (~lines 3159-3232) instead unifies params against arg types and calls type_resolution::substitute_type_params. try_default_padding admits generic candidates through reify_core::overload::slot_matches_wildcard_tier (is_generic disjunct), so this path is reachable for any generic fn with a trailing defaulted param.

SUGGESTED FIX: extract the Resolved arm's generic return instantiation (unify → conflict diagnostic → substitute → bare-unbound check) into one pure helper returning Result<Type, Diagnostic>. Route the padding branch through it with the provided arg types; a type-param slot cannot carry a valid default, since fn_param_default_compatible is strict equality. For uniformity also route the selector-coerced branch (~3293) and the trait-static Resolved arm (~6628, `matched_fn.return_type.clone()`). The trait-static arm is currently unreachable with a generic callee because generic trait fns fail trait lowering with "unresolved type in trait". Add a compile-level test in crates/reify-compiler/tests/harness_traits/fn_generic_call_inference_tests.rs asserting keep(5mm) types as Length, plus a no-panic check.

reify fact (2026-10-05): there is NO IR-side value-cell declaration. reify-eval reads reify-compiler's `ValueCellDecl` (types.rs) directly, and `build_auto_param_list` (reify-eval engine_eval.rs) is where per-cell compiler data such as `solver_hints` becomes `reify_ir::AutoParam`. A `@solver_hint("discrete_set", X)` collection is a BARE fn name. `validate_solver_hint_collections` (reify-compiler annotations.rs) only checks that X is an in-scope member name OR any CompiledFunction with `name == X`; it does no type or arity check. Stdlib catalogs (stdlib/standard_stock.ri) are zero-arg `pub fn … -> List<Length>`. They evaluate via `CompiledExpr::user_function_call(X, vec![], ty)` plus `reify_expr::eval_expr` over `ResolutionProblem.functions`, which already includes prelude fns. The edit-path re-solves (engine_edit.rs) instead build AutoParams from graph `ValueCellNode`, which carries no hints.

Architecture fact (reify auto-type-param resolution, confirmed jun9-2026): the v0.3 completion lands incrementally-safe because β/γ/δ are behavioural no-ops on the stub path. The real SimpleConstraintChecker (reify-constraints/src/lib.rs:47) cannot be constructed inside reify-compiler (no dep on reify-constraints — a prod edge would cycle since constraints dev-deps compiler) or reify-eval prod (reify-constraints is dev-dep only, reify-eval/Cargo.toml:64); it's injected as &dyn ConstraintChecker from the top-level binary (gui/src-tauri/src/main.rs:651 constructs it). The default is the kept stub CompileTimeIndeterminateChecker (auto_type_param_phase.rs:52-66) which returns Indeterminate(=feasible) for every constraint. So per-candidate ValueMaps (β) change no verdict, the BFS joint-recheck (γ) never finds a Violated, and a module without auto: or compiled with the stub is byte-identical to pre-PRD main.
