AMENDMENT-PASS PRECEDENT, task 5322 (commit a34fb48784) — a SIXTEENTH rung under topic `amendment-pass-precedent-ladder`, and the first one where the resolution was "the scope rule's own escape hatch makes the preferred remedy legal". Read the canonical index for the other fifteen.

THE FORK. A reviewer found ~120 lines of `shared/src/shared/uuid_prefix_guard.py` were near-verbatim copies of `shared/src/shared/mcp_markup_middleware.py` (78 identical stripped lines in runs of >=6, including one 34-line contiguous identical block covering the whole of `_record_storm`) — INV-5 lock-step duplication. The obvious de-duplication is to unify the two guards, but `mcp_markup_middleware.py` was NOT in the task's lock list, and the amendment-pass rules say a suggestion requiring an edit to an out-of-lock EXISTING file must be skipped and noted.

THE TEST THAT DECIDED IT. The amendment-pass scope rules distinguish EDITING an existing out-of-lock file (forbidden) from CREATING a new file (explicitly allowed — "a path that did not exist cannot collide with another task's concurrent edits"). So the question is not "may I de-duplicate?" but "is there a de-duplication whose diff touches only my locked files plus new ones?" There was: extract the shared mechanism into a NEW `shared/boundary_storm_escape.py` and have ONLY the in-scope guard compose it. The other guard keeps its copies untouched, so its file is not in the diff at all. One call site migrated is already SPOT for the extracted code; the second migration is a follow-up task.

GENERALISED: when a duplication finding spans an in-scope and an out-of-scope file, an EXTRACT-AND-MIGRATE-ONE lands inside scope where an INLINE-UNIFY does not. Prefer it over the reviewer's own fallback ("if extraction is deferred, at least name the duplication in the docstring"), and take the fallback only for the members that genuinely cannot be extracted without editing the other file.

TWO OBLIGATIONS THAT COME WITH IT, both applied here. (1) File the second migration as a `submit_task` follow-up carrying the details a fresh agent could not re-derive — here, that the other guard's ERROR log has a trailing clause the extracted formatter does not reproduce, and that its `_call_sink` RETURN VALUE is load-bearing (an escalation id reaches the caller). (2) Update the in-scope module's honesty note: it had said only ONE member was knowingly duplicated while five were. After extraction, name the residual members IN FULL and state WHY they are different (they cannot be extracted without editing the other file), so a reader is never told a file is INV-5-clean when part of it is not.

Escalation dedup convention (verified 2026-08-26 against escalation/src/escalation/queue.py:683): EscalationQueue.has_open_l1(x, category=...) delegates to get_by_task(x, status='pending', level=1), which filters on esc.task_id == x. Therefore any non-task-scoped escalation MUST put its dedup key in the task_id slot, not only in the minted id. Filing with task_id='' while deduping on some other key (e.g. entity_uuid) means the dedup NEVER fires and a fresh L1 is filed every cycle. Existing precedents that do it correctly: merge_liveness.py task_id=sentinel, verify_runner.py task_id=_DRIFT_SENTINEL. Also honors the documented id == "esc-{task_id}-{seq}" relation; offline_lane.py already calls an empty task_id escalation "meaningless". Applies to the in-flight task-2896 maybe_escalate_suppression_storm work in fused_memory/reconciliation/flag_dedup.py, where a reviewer found exactly this defect.

Convention for deduped escalation filers (established task 4505, fused_memory/server/markup_tripwire.py::emit_markup_storm_escalation): when a filer folds later events into ONE open record via an anchor dedup, the record must disclose the fold rather than read as a running total — its summary says the count/outcome describe the FIRST occurrence observed and that later ones fold in until it is resolved — and a fold whose material fields DIFFER from the open record's is logged at ERROR (not INFO), naming what was suppressed and the record it folded into, under the same grep token the record's own suggested_action points the triager at. Rationale: an outcome-agnostic dedup otherwise lets the first, milder burst be the only one an operator ever sees while a later, more serious one (e.g. 'unrepairable', which loses caller data) is named nowhere. The open record's own field is read back off its detail line via a key constant shared by writer and reader, so the two spellings cannot drift.

When submit_task/resolve_ticket returns status='combined', READ THE FOLDED TASK BACK AND VERIFY YOUR CONTENT PER FIELD — the curator rewrites, and it can replace a verified root cause with a plausible but WRONG mechanism. Observed dark-factory 2026-08-10: a candidate describing L2 co-parent orphaning (mechanism located in escalation/src/escalation/queue.py + server.py) was folded into task 3587, and the curator's rewrite re-attributed it to "the sweep's terminal-subject check is keyed off a co-parent/task-id relationship that doesn't resolve to the true terminal task for L2 records" — a mechanism that does not exist (the escalation's task_id was unambiguous throughout) — while DROPPING both escalation-package files from files_to_modify, so an implementer would have gone straight to the wrong module. Fixed with an explicit update_task carrying a "CORRECTION TO AN EARLIER DRAFT" block plus the restored file list. The combine decision itself was correct (3587 genuinely owned the problem space); it is the rewritten prose that needs auditing. Related: a curator combine can also silently WIDEN a task's charter, which matters because a lock is taken over the declared charter.

SUPERSEDED IN PART by task 3891 (2026-08-20): the historical measurement below still holds, but its closing advice REVERSES. Kept in place (not re-added) because three code sites cite this exact memory id: task_filter.py:270, task_filter.py:326, tests/test_task_filter.py:3245.

HISTORICAL (task 3098, 2026-07-31). Reusing fused_memory.reconciliation.task_filter's clause-level idiom (find_conflicting_task_status_ids / find_present_tense_completion_claim_task_ids) on real recon-authored memory content silently yielded nothing. _CLAUSE_SPLIT_RE then split on '[.;\n!?]', so ordinary technical prose was shattered mid-sentence at every filename and path ("dark-factory-orchestrator.yaml", ".envrc", "CLAUDE.md:95"), separating a task reference from the live-status fields in its own sentence. Compounding it, TASK_REF_RE (r'(?:\btask\b|\bdf\b|#)\s*#?\s*(\d+)\b') did not match the common "task/94" slash form, only "task 94" / "df 94" / "#94". Probed against four real solar_challenge liveness-snapshot memories: whole-content TASK_REF_RE.findall returned the right ids, while clause-scoped association returned the empty set for all four. That measurement is why task 3403 exists.

CURRENT ADVICE (task 3891). Task 3403 narrowed _CLAUSE_SPLIT_RE to r'\.(?!\w)|[;\n!?]' — a dot ends a clause only when not followed by a word character, so filenames and paths no longer shatter — and widened TASK_REF_RE's separator to r'\s*[#/]?\s*', which matches "task/94". Task 3891 re-MEASURED the clause technique against the SAME four records (6b245659, 08aa0017, 68dd5f93, 1eef7df7) rather than assuming, and it now yields the correct per-subject association: subjects 94 and 96 each key STRANDED (claimant_run_id=null|heartbeat_at=null|status=in-progress) from their OWN clause, and the two real groups are preserved. So clause scoping IS the right idiom for this corpus now. Ship it with a whole-record-union FALLBACK for any subject carrying no clause-level evidence — a metadata-only ref, a prose ref in an assignment-free clause, or a clause boundary landing inside a quoted value — which is byte-identical to the pre-rescope key and so can only ADD recall, never remove it. Reference implementation: scripts/audit_duplicate_memories.py::liveness_snapshot_subject_facts.

CAVEAT FOR THE NEXT IMPORTER. _CLAUSE_SPLIT_RE is module-private BY CONTRACT: tests/test_task_filter.py::test_clause_split_re_has_no_out_of_module_consumers AST-scans fused-memory/src and fused-memory/scripts against an explicit allowlist and asserts equality in BOTH directions, so a new import and its allowlist entry must land in the SAME commit or the tree is red either way. A new importer must first show its fail-safe direction matches the two soft-block consumers'; if an over-long clause would cost anything that does not self-heal next cycle, take the public STRICT_CLAUSE_BOUNDARY_RE (r'[.;\n!?]') instead.

escalation.dedupe.compute_content_fingerprint keys ONLY on (category, kind, sorted+\x1f-joined affected_ids) — summary/detail/suggested_action are NOT inputs (dedupe.py:103-111). So rewording an escalation's prose is always dedupe-safe, but adding or changing ANY affected_ids token changes the digest. Gotcha when adding a discriminator to an EXISTING compute_content_fingerprint call site (learned task 3119, pattern used by fused_memory.middleware.scope_violation_escalator._ADVISORY_FINGERPRINT_TOKEN): append the new token ONLY on the new/narrower branch, never on both — adding any token to the pre-existing branch changes its digest, and since submit_or_dedupe/find_dedupe_parent fold only into PENDING parents keyed on that digest, every live pending parent is silently orphaned and the operator queue re-floods with events that used to fold. The resulting asymmetry (e.g. a 'mode:advisory' token with no 'mode:rejection' counterpart) reads as an oversight to the next reader, so record why in a comment at the token, and pin the legacy digest with a test that recomputes it independently via compute_content_fingerprint rather than reading it back from production code.

Full anatomy of the escalation-id vs stored-task_id divergence in dark-factory, measured 2026-08-20 at HEAD ca7459b0a9. EscalationQueue.make_id(self, task_id: str) at escalation/src/escalation/queue.py:1642 does NOT take a task_id — it takes an arbitrary id-NAMESPACE key, and callers may store a different task_id on the record. By AST scan of every production Escalation(...) construction (tests and evals excluded): 102 take their id from make_id; 97 pass the identical expression for both the key and task_id; exactly 5 diverge, confirming a previously unverified claim of "5 sites". The five: curator_escalator.py:422, :493, :603 all pass make_id('curator') with task_id='task-curator'; ticket_janitor.py:284 passes make_id('ticket-janitor') with task_id='task-curator'; ticket_janitor.py:491 passes make_id('ticket-janitor') with a real numeric task id. content: GOTCHA for escalation/src/escalation/dedupe.py::file_or_fold_l1 (task 5466): `subject` is three things at once — the stored task_id, make_id's id-namespace key (it names the counter file `esc-{subject}.seq` and the id stem), and the fingerprint body `project_id:subject`. So a subject must be filename-safe: a raw path or free text cannot go there, so hash it (e.g. a sha256 prefix) and put the readable value in summary/detail. And a fold never writes the child record: attach_or_submit only appends the child's id to the parent and bumps dedupe_count. So if two distinct conditions share one subject, the second one's summary/detail is lost. Give each condition the operator must see its own subject. Found while revalidating task 3166's per-asserted-root mismatch storm escape.

44c58990-26a4-4e7c-b4ab-548aec475006.content:
MEASURED CORRECTION (task 5354, 2026-09-17, read-only census over all 4,858 live data/escalations/**/*.json): a "field X is empty on N% of all escalation records" sweep finding is NOT by itself evidence that X's mechanism is broken, and on the one case audited end-to-end the causal inference was false. Treat field-emptiness census rows as a PROMPT TO MEASURE THE CONSUMER, never as a defect.

WHY EMPTINESS IS THE DEFAULT, NOT A SYMPTOM. `Escalation.to_dict()` is a bare `dataclasses.asdict` (escalation/src/escalation/models.py:683-687), so EVERY dataclass field is emitted on EVERY record. Any optional field owned by a narrow set of emitters therefore reads "present and ~100% empty" corpus-wide BY CONSTRUCTION. Confirmed for five fields at once: `dedupe_fingerprint` 99.0% empty, and `citation_sha`/`refiles_suppressed`/`train_state`/`index_health` 100% empty — and those four share NO writer with each other or with dedupe_fingerprint (citation_sha -> orchestrator/landing_evidence.py:2300,2383; train_state -> orchestrator/workflow.py:12160-12444, train tasks only; index_health -> fused-memory/.../harness.py:3649-3737 + index_drift_detector.py:186; refiles_suppressed -> no writer outside queue.py's increment). Each is empty because its narrow trigger has not fired. This is the INVERSE consequence of the asdict property already recorded in memory 3227cab0 (which covers asdict putting new fields on the read surface for free).

THE THREE CHECKS THAT DECIDE IT, in order — each one independently falsified the 5354 premise:
1. Does any consumer READ the field on the records that are empty? The agent-facing MCP tools `escalate_info`/`escalate_blocker` (escalation/src/escalation/server.py:1532,1617) forward a fixed field set that excludes dedupe_fingerprint, but the server's stock DedupeConfig folds on `summary_dedupe_key`, which never reads it. Field neither written nor read on that path => empty is CORRECT.
2. Is the mechanism observably working anywhere? 49 records carry a fingerprint; of the 6 with dedupe_count>0, three (esc-4941-4, esc-5063-7, esc-4259-1, all preexisting_main_break) folded via a stamped one. "Cannot be folding anything" was falsified by the corpus the sweep itself cited.
3. Would populating the field actually change the outcome? Group records by (category, task_id, normalised summary): 4,773 identities, only 85 repeats (1.7%). Of those 85, ZERO could have folded with a perfect key — 62 short-circuit at `submit_or_dedupe`'s Gate 2 because their category is in no dedupe tuple (stock ('infra_issue',), for_recon ('recon_integrity_issue',), for_gate_backlog ('reconciliation_stale_gate_backlog',)), and the 23 infra_issue ones all missed the 600s window (measured gaps 3,746s-796,144s; the window filter at dedupe.py:525 runs AFTER the key match). Only 8 of 85 had any open parent at all, because `find_dedupe_parent` scans `get_pending()` only.

THE TRAP IF YOU "JUST STAMP IT". Universally populating an optional dedupe key is not a safe no-op: it flips `content_fingerprint_key`'s documented "None => never fold" contract (dedupe.py:144-152 plus the falsy-key short-circuit at dedupe.py:485) into "fold" for every config using that key fn, and defeats `gate_backlog_fingerprint_key`'s legacy fast path (`if esc.dedupe_fingerprint: return it`, dedupe.py:232) which exists precisely so unstamped legacy parents fall through to prose recovery. A `__post_init__` stamp is worse still, because `from_dict` would then stamp records read off disk that were persisted as None.

GENERAL LESSON: escalation dedupe non-folding is dominated by the fold WINDOW, the CATEGORY tuple, and the pending-only parent scan — not by key presence. Measure those three before attributing an undercount to a missing key.

candidates.content: Two reify-audit facts that PRD prose gets wrong (both measured 2026-08-31). (1) `--format markdown` is NOT a reify-audit binary flag. `parse_args` accepts only --task, --pre-done, --since, --pattern, --tasks-file, --fused-memory-url, --runs-db, --project-root, the --jcodemunch family, --no-jcodemunch, --help, --version, and hard-rejects anything else as "unknown flag". `--format markdown` is an argument of the /audit SKILL, which renders the report itself. The binary emits a JSON Finding array on stderr and a human summary on stdout. (2) PTODO's task-liveness lane does NOT use `crates/reify-audit/src/fused_memory_client.rs`, despite PRDs citing it. It opens the task store directly READ-ONLY via rusqlite — `tasks_db_path` (honoring a REIFY_PTODO_TASKS_DB env override) and `open_tasks_db` with SQLITE_OPEN_READ_ONLY — and queries status+metadata for one id under the master tag. Both mechanisms exist in the crate; a new detector copying "the same mechanism PTODO uses" must copy the rusqlite one, reusing `is_terminal_status` (done or cancelled are terminal; every other present status is live) and its fail-soft contract (missing store degrades the lane with one stderr breadcrumb, exit class untouched, never exit 125).

Reify audit skill (`.claude/skills/audit/`) on main still references the deleted `.taskmaster/tasks/tasks.json` path for `--tasks-file` in cli-invocation.md, modes.md (4 sites), and output-format.md. Task 3731 (in-progress) introduces a `scripts/reify-audit-predone-wrapper.sh` + `scripts/reify-audit-snapshot-filter.jq` snapshot-materializer pattern using `mcp__fused-memory__get_tasks` instead. Until 3731 merges, the audit skill is non-functional on a fresh checkout. Don't file a duplicate — 3731 covers all five reference sites and the binary's removal of the dead default.

To run reify-audit (e.g. `--pattern PPRDSTATUS`) offline from a reify warm lane, use the prebuilt target/debug/reify-audit with LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/opt/reify-deps/lib:/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu. Without it the binary exits 127 with "libopenvdb.so.13.0: cannot open shared object file". Pass `--no-jcodemunch --project-root . --tasks-file <json array of TaskMetadata> --runs-db <sqlite file with CREATE TABLE events (task_id TEXT, event_type TEXT)>`. A synthetic --tasks-file that sets `prd` on a PRD's leaves lets you check whether the stale-status-header lane would fire. You need it for legacy leaves that carry no metadata.prd, which the live detector cannot see. Fixture shape: crates/reify-audit/tests/pprdstatus_cli.rs.

When reify-audit is invoked without --tasks-file, it connects to fused-memory MCP to load tasks. Under verify-pipeline load, this can fail with EMFILE ("too many open files"), causing the binary to exit 125 instead of the expected High-finding count. Fix: always pass --tasks-file pointing to an empty JSON array ([]) in hermetic test invocations that don't need liveness checking. reify's .taskmaster/tasks/tasks.db runs in WAL mode with a live -wal sidecar, so a plain `cp` of the .db alone silently drops recent commits and yields a torn corpus census that still looks authoritative. Snapshot it with sqlite3 "file:<db>?mode=ro" ".backup /tmp/snap.db" (or VACUUM INTO). reify-audit's REIFY_PTODO_TASKS_DB env var (ptodo.rs tasks_db_path) then points the detector at that snapshot while --project-root still targets the real checkout, so git ops resolve against the true tracked set — which is how you run a positive control on a perturbed copy without ever writing the live DB.

solar_challenge procedure (task 252 architect, 2026-10-09): to prototype a change and run the full verify suite without dirtying the task worktree, add a scratch detached worktree. Commands:
- `git worktree add --detach /tmp/<dir>/tree HEAD`
- in that tree, `UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT=/tmp/<dir>/venv UV_OFFLINE=1 uv sync --locked --extra dev --extra web` (succeeded offline from uv's cache)
- `uv run --locked --extra dev --extra web pytest -m 'not slow and not e2e' --ignore=tests/e2e -p no:cacheprovider` with the same env vars, backgrounded
- afterwards, `git worktree remove --force /tmp/<dir>/tree` and `git worktree prune`
The suite runs serially (addopts has no -n): 4512 tests took 14 min 18 s on main cf6af55. For real-TMY measurements outside pytest, copy /home/leo/src/solar-challenge/.cache/weather and pass the copy to set_weather_cache(WeatherCache(copy)). Its tmy_f8a4df0259c4 entry is Bristol's scaled v2-key TMY (GHI 1069.46 kWh/m2); tmy_5dc8c8bca218 is the pre-285 raw one, which is never read.

solar_challenge: how to profile or prototype simulate_home from a task worktree using the real Bristol TMY. Worktrees have no .cache/weather. Call set_weather_cache(WeatherCache(Path('/home/leo/src/solar-challenge/.cache/weather'))) to reuse the main checkout's cache read-only, with no PVGIS call; tmy_5dc8c8bca218 is Bristol, indexed UTC for 1990, 8760 rows. Gotcha: if you run the suite against a scratch source copy via PYTHONPATH=<copy>/src, tests/integration/test_external_install.py::test_isolated_install_resolves_and_calls_every_symbol fails spuriously. PYTHONPATH leaks into its `uv run --isolated` probe, which asserts that solar_challenge loads from site-packages; ignore that one failure in scratch-copy runs (measured task 164, main efe3145).

solar_challenge: to run the @pytest.mark.slow suite offline from a task worktree, first run `mkdir -p .cache && cp -r /home/leo/src/solar-challenge/.cache/weather .cache/`. solar_challenge.weather caches at the cwd-relative Path(".cache/weather"), and worktrees have none, so otherwise get_tmy_data calls PVGIS. COPY, do not symlink: the .gitignore pattern `.cache/` only matches directories, so a `.cache` symlink shows up untracked and can be committed. Delete the copy afterwards. Command: `uv run --extra dev --extra web pytest -m 'slow and not e2e' --ignore=tests/e2e --ignore=tests/unit/web_assistant -p no:cacheprovider -o addopts=""`. The web_assistant slow tests call the live Anthropic API. It collected 103 tests and took 8-10 min wall clock on main 4c489d5 (2026-09-30, task 166). On unmodified main, 1 fails: tests/integration/test_tou_dispatch.py::TestTOUDispatchComparison::test_tou_dispatch_reduces_costs (follow-up ticket tkt_0RV7VMWKRZVV9R3JDN4S4G9GBM).

solar_challenge gotcha, measured 2026-10-02 by the task 344 architect (uv 0.11.6, main 3ba0132): a fresh UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT does NOT catch a configured command that drops the extra providing pytest. `uv run ... pytest` prepends the fresh venv's bin to PATH and, finding no pytest there, runs the next PATH entry's pytest: inside the verify that is the worktree's shared .venv, in a bare shell dark-factory's venv. It DOES catch a dropped extra the suite imports: removing --extra e2e (17 collection errors) or --extra web (tests/e2e/conftest.py importorskip('werkzeug')) from the e2e lane job fails collection in a fresh venv but passes in the shared .venv. Cost of a fresh venv for the e2e lane job's collect-only: ~15 s vs ~5-8 s shared; the sync is ~1 s (hardlinks from ~/.cache/uv) and the rest is first-import byte compilation; with UV_LINK_MODE=copy it is ~24 s and ~788 MB.

- tests/unit/test_web_jobs.py::TestJobCompletion (2 tests): a real create_app JobManager job, in-process.

solar_challenge: to test an entry point that fetches weather itself and takes no weather_data argument (config.run_parameter_sweep, simulate_fleet) offline in a unit test, seed a throwaway cache. In a fixture: `cache = WeatherCache(cache_dir=tmp_path / "weather")`, then `cache.put(tests._synthetic_weather.synthetic_june_weather("2024-06-21"), "tmy", Location.bristol())`, then `set_weather_cache(cache)`, yield, and teardown with `set_weather_cache(None)`. WeatherCache and set_weather_cache are frozen public surface, not a dotted-path monkeypatch. The cache's CSV round trip turns the index tz into a fixed UTC+01:00 offset. A sweep point's generation still exactly equals simulate_home of dataclasses.replace(base_pv, <field>=value) read through the same cache (pd.testing.assert_series_equal). A 1-day simulate_home with use_stochastic=False takes about 0.1 s, plus about 0.7 s pvlib warm-up. Measured by the task 175 architect on main 9e9ab8f. Scripts outside pytest that import tests._synthetic_weather need PYTHONPATH=<worktree>.

Probe technique for solar_challenge multiprocessing/weather behaviour without a Python 3.14 env: on the 3.12 .venv (main checkout .venv/bin/python has solar_challenge editable), call multiprocessing.set_start_method('forkserver', force=True) to reproduce 3.14's Linux default. Set HTTP(S)_PROXY/http(s)_proxy to http://127.0.0.1:9 and NO_PROXY empty, and chdir to an empty temp dir, so any live PVGIS fetch fails fast with ProxyError instead of hitting the network. Seed weather with tests/_synthetic_weather.synthetic_june_weather via WeatherCache.put.

solar_challenge gotcha (task 649 implementer, 2026-10-12, uv 0.11.6): after a requeue, the task worktree's .venv had lib/python3.12/site-packages but no bin/ and no pyvenv.cfg. Every `uv run --locked ...` then failed with "Project virtual environment directory `<worktree>/.venv` cannot be used because it is not a valid Python environment (no Python executable was found)". uv will not repair or replace such a directory. Fix, inside the worktree: `rm -rf .venv && uv sync --locked --extra dev --extra web --extra e2e`. That rebuilt it from the uv cache, offline, with nothing lost. The same requeue had also deleted tracked files (README.md, .envrc, scenarios/*.yaml), and the harness's WIP auto-commit committed those deletions (escalation esc-649-1). So check `git show --stat` on a "save WIP before requeue rebase" commit before trusting it.

solar_challenge recipe (task-256 implementer, measured 2026-10-01, uv 0.11.6, pytest 9.0.3, factory host): to check ONE test file on another admitted Python minor without the 6-10 min tests/interpreter_matrix run, use a private env under /tmp: `env -u VIRTUAL_ENV UV_PYTHON=3.13+gil UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT=/tmp/<unique>-venv-py313 uv run --extra dev --extra web pytest <file> -p no:cacheprovider > <log> 2>&1`. Request 3.14+gil, never plain 3.14, which selects the free-threaded build. The worktree's .venv and git status stay untouched, and the venv is hardlinked from the uv cache, so a cold env plus a 13-test file took 0:08.6 wall on 3.13. Measured: tests/unit/test_web_app.py (13 tests, including the in-process package-copy seam for a web package lacking templates/ or static/) passed on 3.11.15, 3.12.3, 3.13.9 and 3.14.4. Delete the /tmp venv afterwards.

solar_challenge procedural note (task 489 architect, 2026-10-05, uv 0.11.6). ~/.cache/uv holds the pytest 9.1.1 wheel, so a "newest pytest" check runs WITHOUT network: `UV_OFFLINE=1 uv run --no-project --isolated --with-editable '.' --with 'pytest==9.1.1' --with flask --with plotly --with pyarrow --with anthropic --with pytest-cov pytest <paths> -o addopts= -W error::pytest.PytestRemovedIn10Warning -p no:cacheprovider`. The locked pytest 9.0.3 defines PytestRemovedIn10Warning but lacks 9.1's parametrize-iterator and class-fixture-instance-method checks, so only the 9.1.1 run can show those. Separately: tests/integration/test_cost_recovery_calibration.py mixes in a @pytest.mark.slow class, TestPhysicsReconciliationColumn, that fetches the live PVGIS TMY. Any command naming that file without -m 'not slow' needs PVGIS, and it writes .cache/weather/tmy_*.csv under the cwd (gitignored).

solar_challenge recipe (measured 2026-10-01, task 251, uv 0.11.6, pytest 9.0.3): to exercise a test's "tool not on PATH" skip path, run the worktree venv's python directly with a trimmed PATH, e.g. `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:/usr/bin:/bin" .venv/bin/python -m pytest <file> -rs --basetemp=/tmp/<unique>`. `uv run` would re-add its own paths. On this host uv lives only in ~/.local/bin and git only in /usr/bin and /bin, so either tool can be dropped independently. For a "not a git checkout" case, run the venv python from a git-listed copy of the tree under /tmp, since /tmp is not inside a repo. pytest creates --basetemp lazily, so if that directory is absent after the run, the skip fired before any tmp_path_factory use (i.e. before any copy or build).

solar_challenge gotcha (task 183, 2026-09-30): a scratch script run as `uv run --extra dev python /tmp/x.py` cannot import the repo's test helpers (e.g. `from tests._synthetic_weather import synthetic_june_weather` fails with ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'tests'). The editable install exposes only src/solar_challenge, and plain python puts the script's own directory, not the repo root, on sys.path; pytest makes `tests` importable through its rootdir handling. Prefix the command with PYTHONPATH=<worktree root>, which adds the root without shadowing the editable solar_challenge.

Timing/how-to: a full board-scenario finance run (`solar-challenge finance run scenarios/bristol-phase1.yaml --assumptions physics --project --cost-recovery`) runs offline with UV_OFFLINE=1 from the repo root (it reads the repo-relative .cache/weather TMY cache) but takes 1h20m-1h50m wall clock (100 homes, ~7 sampled ages, project then cost-recovery). To measure a src change against it without touching the repo, `git archive HEAD src tests pyproject.toml scenarios` into a scratch dir, edit there, and run the repo's environment with PYTHONPATH=<scratch>/src (it shadows the editable install); for pytest in the scratch tree also copy dark-factory-orchestrator.yaml (tests/unit/test_stale_uv_lock.py reads it at collection) and use `python -m pytest`.

solar_challenge gotcha, measured 2026-09-30 with uv 0.11.6 by the task 254 architect: `uv run` syncs INEXACTLY by default. It installs what the requested extras need but never removes packages; only `--exact` removes extraneous ones. For example, flask stayed importable after `uv run --extra dev` in a venv that already had it. Consequence: tests/unit/test_e2e_lane.py's nested `uv run --extra dev --extra web --extra e2e` installs the web and e2e extras into the worktree's shared .venv mid-verify. Any test that runs a configured command to check which extras it provides must therefore set UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT to a fresh dir such as tmp_path/'venv'. Otherwise it still passes after the extra is dropped. A fresh env costs about 3 s here, because uv hardlinks from ~/.cache/uv on the same filesystem.

Running 'uv run --locked --extra dev --extra web --extra e2e …' in /home/leo/src/solar-challenge syncs the project's .venv to include those extras: it installed 7 packages on 2026-10-16. The environment is still the locked one, so this is harmless, but a later plain 'uv run --locked --extra dev' re-syncs and removes them. The locked Playwright's chromium-headless-shell was already installed under ~/.cache/ms-playwright and ran fine for an ad-hoc EventSource probe.

Completed: Merge lane never un-stacks a train member whose predecessor leaves the queue without landing — the orphan's conflicts are then reported as the member's own
Description: MEASURED 2026-09-18 while resolving esc-4137-3/esc-4137-4 (steward). Task 4137's merge was blocked for reasons that had nothing to do with task 4137.

THE DEFECT. When a train is formed, an order>0 member is rebased onto its predecessor's branch tip rather than main (orchestrator/src/orchestrator/git_ops.py::_resolve_predecessor_tip, "train-predecessor tip or main"). That is correct at formation. But if the predecessor subsequently leaves the merge queue WITHOUT LANDING, nothing un-stacks the member. The member's branch silently keeps carrying every one of the predecessor's commits, and its next merge_request therefore reports the PREDECESSOR's conflicts against main as its own.

THE SIGHTING. task/4137 (7 own commits, all dashboard) was stacked behind task/4480 at 2026-09-08 21:49 (reflog task/4137@{0} = 'rebase (finish) onto 9788a34b13'). Task 4480 then went to status=pending and left the queue, never merged; merge_status(task_id=4480) = unknown. Ten days later 4137's merge attempt reported 15 conflicts — of which 14 were 4480's fused-memory test refactor vs main's task-3895 load_script_module migration. Replaying only 4137's own delta (`git merge-tree --merge-base=9788a34b13 main <tip>`) conflicts in exactly ONE file, its own index.html cache-buster.

WHY THIS IS WORSE THAN A STALE BRANCH. The failure is mis-attributed by construction. The canonical ancestry check then read rc=1 (branch ref present, commits genuinely not on main), which means "not landed YET", not a stale record, and under rc=1 the tip-marker and task-status landing signals are NOT consultable (they apply only under rc=128-with-empty-marker). Correct handling throughout was to keep polling the branch handle and never resubmit, since the re-drive already had. Useful incidental: the train id encodes the tip task id as coalesce-<TIP_ID>-<hex>, so `coalesce-3543-...` meant 3543 was the train's tip and would therefore carry its own "Merge task/3543 into main" marker if the train landed.

Two corrections:

(1) WHY IT HELD HERE: task 3543 was the train's TIP (`coalesce-3543-...`), and a tip that has not yet landed genuinely is not on main — so rc=1 correctly meant "not landed YET" in this specific case. The reading was right; the generalisation is not.

(2) WHERE IT FAILS: for a NON-TIP member of a coalesce train, `git merge-base --is-ancestor task/<ID> main` returns rc=1 PERMANENTLY on work that DID land. Task 'merge queue: release per-branch in-flight slot on FAILED/abnormal finalize + reconcile merge_request coalesce gate with live snapshot (resubmit attaches to dead request_id)' completed. Bug surfaced during the reify task 4577 merge attempts (2026-06-15). After a merge verify finalized FAILED (passed=False — e.g. mr-4cd91bea, mr-649dd4ba), a subsequent merge_request(branch=4577) returned status="attached"/"in_flight" coalesced onto the now-DEAD request_id, while get_merge_queue (reading the live worker snapshot) showed NO entry for that branch — i.e. merge_request and get_merge_queue disagree. merge_cancel on the dead id later reported state:"blocked", reason:"Request already finalized". Net effect: a resubmit silently attaches to a finalized-dead request, so the operator/agent waits on a merge that will never run instead of enqueueing a fresh one — wasted long verify cycles and a misdiagnosis (looked like an infra "drop").

ROOT-CAUSE HYPOTHESIS: the per-branch in-flight slot (orchestrator/src/orchestrator/merge_queue.py — InFlightMergeRegistry._slots, keyed by bare branch name; and/or the multi-waiter Entry model from task 1639) is auto-released via Future.add_done_callback when the request future resolves (registration landed in task 1628's enqueue_merge_request). On an abnormal/FAILED finalize the slot evidently is NOT cleared (or a stale entry survives), so the branch's dedup slot keeps pointing at the finalized-dead request_id, and merge_request's coalesce/attach gate (escalation/src/escalation/server.py) matches it. This is distinct from the model-building tasks 1604/1639/1641/1628 (which created the dedup/multi-waiter/retention machinery) and from 1741 (live-entry VISIBILITY in the status surfaces) — this is a bug in the FINALIZE-RELEASE path of that machinery.

FIX (two parts):
1. Release the per-branch in-flight slot/waiter on EVERY terminal outcome — done / conflict / blocked / abandoned / failed / abnormal-finalize — not just clean success. Audit the add_done_callback / finalize path so a FAILED or exceptionally-finalized future still clears the slot (and detaches any waiters) atomically.
2. Make merge_request's coalesce/attach gate consistent with the live worker snapshot: before attaching to an existing in-flight entry, confirm that entry is actually live in worker.snapshot() (the same source get_merge_queue reads), so the two surfaces cannot disagree. A slot with no live snapshot entry must NOT absorb a resubmit — enqueue fresh instead.

User-observable signal: a regression test drives a merge to a FAILED finalize for branch B, then asserts (a) get_merge_queue shows no entry for B, (b) the per-branch in-flight slot is clear, and (c) merge_request(branch=B) returns a FRESH request_id (enqueued) rather than status="attached"/"in_flight" on the dead id. End-to-end: after a failed merge verify, a resubmit re-runs the merge instead of hanging on a dead request.

Consumer: the /merge-queue and /unblock skills (submit→poll callers) and operators reading get_merge_queue / merge_status.

Modules: orchestrator/src/orchestrator/merge_queue.py (InFlightMergeRegistry / multi-waiter entry release on finalize), escalation/src/escalation/server.py (merge_request coalesce gate ↔ live-snapshot reconciliation).

Relationship: sibling-incident to the merge-status-false-unknown batch (1748/1749/1750) — same reify 4577/4352 saga, but a DISTINCT code path (in-flight dedup release vs terminal-status lookup tiers). No hard dependency; note the shared files (merge_queue.py, server.py) for lock-contention awareness with 1749.

Completed: Merge-worktree reaper deletes the tree without clearing its `locked` marker — the unprunable admin entry then hard-fails EVERY subsequent merge_request enqueue
Description: MEASURED 2026-08-28 01:36-01:45 UTC during the reify stranded-branch recovery session. This is a live merge-queue OUTAGE shape: one stale git worktree admin entry hard-failed every new `merge_request` enqueue until cleared by hand.

## Symptom
`mcp__escalation__merge_request` (reify, port 8100) returned, for every task, regardless of branch:

    Error calling tool 'merge_request': Worktree missing: /home/leo/src/warm-lanes/worktrees/_merge-8e69447b

Existing queue entries kept verifying and landing normally; only NEW enqueues failed. Three retries over ~9 minutes all failed identically, so it was not transient.

## Root cause (verified, not inferred)
1. The merge worker created `_merge-8e69447b` at 2026-08-27 19:58:03 and marked its git admin entry LOCKED with reason `initializing` — `.git/worktrees/_merge-8e69447b/locked` contained the literal string `initializing`.
2. Something killed it mid-init (the orchestrator was restarting around that window).
3. The periodic reaper later deleted the on-disk directory. The queue's own `resource_audit.worktree_ledger` had been reporting it for hours as `unregistered on-disk merge worktree ... absent from owned ledger — possible leak — scheduled for automatic reclaim by the periodic reaper once it passes age 21600s`, and the reclaim duly happened.
4. **`git worktree prune` SKIPS locked entries.** So the admin entry outlived its own directory: `gitdir` pointed at `/home/leo/src/warm-lanes/worktrees/_merge-8e69447b/.git`, which no longer existed, while `git worktree prune --dry-run -v` printed NOTHING because of the lock.
5. `merge_request`'s enqueue path evidently enumerates/validates registered worktrees, hits the dangling one, and raises `Worktree missing: <path>` — poisoning every enqueue for the whole queue, not just the affected task.

The reaper deleting the DIRECTORY without first clearing the `locked` MARKER is the defect. Removing a locked worktree's tree is exactly the case git refuses to clean up afterwards.

## Evidence
- `.git/worktrees/_merge-8e69447b/` present, birth 2026-08-27 19:58:03, containing `locked` (6 bytes, `initializing`), `gitdir`, `HEAD`, `ORIG_HEAD`, `index` (473443 bytes), `commondir`, `config.worktree`, `logs/`.
- `ls -d /home/leo/src/warm-lanes/worktrees/_merge-8e69447b` -> `No such file or directory`.
- `git worktree prune --dry-run -v` -> NO OUTPUT (skipped: locked).
- It was the ONLY one of 242 registered worktrees whose directory was missing (scanned every `.git/worktrees/*/gitdir` and stat'd the parent).
- No live process referenced it — checked both `/proc/*/cmdline` and `/proc/*/cwd`.

## Remediation applied by hand (for reference; NOT the fix)
Removed the stale `locked` file, then let git do the removal itself:

    git worktree prune -v
    # Removing worktrees/_merge-8e69447b: gitdir file points to non-existent location

242 -> 241 worktrees, zero missing-directory entries remaining, all 112 `_lane-*` worktrees intact. `merge_request` succeeded immediately afterwards (mr-5497c23f).

## Why this is not covered by the existing merge-worktree lifecycle family
Tasks 2922 / 2924 / 2925 / 3251 (all done) cover teardown half-completion, lease-guarded removal, the C2 namespace invariant, and the RunnerUnavailable ledger leak. Task 2922 explicitly says of this exact inverse shape: "A transient inverse shape (admin dir without tree) also occurs and is handled by prune/name-reuse." **That claim is FALSIFIED for the locked case** — prune cannot handle it, by design, and the entry is therefore permanent rather than transient. 2922's sentence should be corrected as part of this work so the next reader does not re-derive the same false assurance.

## Suggested fix directions (not prescriptive)

Completed: Retroactive coalescing absorbs workflow-less merge_request singles into trains that can never complete (no awaiting workflow ⇒ member never reaches merge-deferred)
Description: MEASURED 2026-08-29/30 during the category-B/C stranded-branch recovery (session recover-dark_factory-3323308). 24 verified-green branches were eaten by this, twice, and one branch was QUARANTINED out from under a live queue entry (NOT destroyed — the original filing said "destroyed"; see CORRECTION 1 at the top of details).

THE DEFECT. `SpeculativeMergeWorker._maybe_coalesce_waiting_singles` absorbs >=2 waiting single MergeRequests into a `coalesce-*` GroupMergeRequest, resolving each absorbed single's ORIGINAL future as `superseded`. For an ORCHESTRATOR-DISPATCHED task that is fine: its `TaskWorkflow` is awaiting that future, and `workflow.py::TaskWorkflow._handle_superseded` (workflow.py:1532, reached from :10943) parks the task at `merge-deferred`, which is the precondition `_do_train_merge` then checks.

A request submitted through the `mcp__escalation__merge_request` MCP surface has NO TaskWorkflow awaiting it. Nothing consumes the `superseded` outcome, so the task stays `pending` forever and the train can NEVER satisfy "all members merge-deferred". The train sits until it is dequeued, then dies.

ROOT CAUSE, verified in code: the ONLY production writers of `merge-deferred` are two `TaskWorkflow` methods — `workflow.py:1515` (`_park_train_member`) and `workflow.py:1544` (`_handle_superseded`). There is no workflow-less path to that state. And `_default_coalesce_exclusion_reason` (merge_queue.py:15097) — the predicate that decides which waiting singles may be coalesced — implements exactly TWO signals: (1) the in-memory one-strike registry `_coalesce_derailed_task_ids`, (2) event-store recent-terminal `blocked`/`error`. NEITHER asks whether a workflow is awaiting the request, i.e. whether this member is even CAPABLE of reaching merge-deferred.

CONFIRMED LIVE 2026-08-31 with both sides of the seam visible in one two-member train: `coalesce-2930-fc18dcb1` had member 3187 (orchestrator-dispatched, awaiting workflow) reach `merge-deferred`, while member 2930 (MCP-submitted, no workflow) stayed `pending`. The all-members precondition was unsatisfiable from the moment the train formed.

OBSERVED, TWICE, on 2026-08-29/30:
- 01:31 UTC — eight trains, all rejected with `Train merge rejected: not all members are merge-deferred: member '<id>' is 'pending' (expected merge-deferred)` (the `TRAIN_INCOMPLETE_REASON_PREFIX` at merge_queue.py:498), then `Coalesce one-strike: marked N task(s) after coalesce-train derail`.
- 07:01 UTC — seven more, all returning `merge_attempt {outcome: 'train_incomplete'}` within four seconds of each other, then dropped from the queue.
- A THIRD derail shape was observed 2026-08-31 and is described in CORRECTION 2 at the top of details: the pass leaves a replacement queue entry that no caller can cancel.

MEASURED SPLIT across the session: single-entry submissions landed 7 of 7; coalesce-train members landed 0 of 15.

TWO COLLATERAL DAMAGE MODES, both measured:
1. Building the atomic tip REWRITES the leader's branch ref and the derail does NOT undo it. 18 of 28 branches were rewritten after the first derail and 12 more after the second: `task/3123` went 17 -> 26 commits ahead carrying task 4668's entire branch; `task/3550` 16 -> 42; `task/4006` 41 -> 62. Two then conflicted with main on files neither task owns. Resubmitting a rewritten leader lands three tasks' work under one task's name, on a tree nobody reviewed. RECONFIRMED 2026-08-31: `task/2930` went 12 -> 30 ahead carrying task 3187's entire branch.
2. `task/3550`'s branch was RENAMED and its worktree MOVED to `.worktrees-orphaned/` by `orchestrator/src/orchestrator/git_ops.py::GitOps.quarantine_worktree` while a queue entry was live; its entry then came back `merge_attempt {outcome: 'unknown_branch'}` ("tried 'task/3550' and '3550'"). CORRECTED 2026-08-31 — the original filing said the ref and worktree were DELETED and that recovery required the object store. Neither is true: nothing was deleted, the worktree is still a registered worktree at `.worktrees-orphaned/3550-20260830T043338Z`, and the ref was reachable the whole time under its parked name `task/3550-20260830T043338Z`, sitting at exactly the verified tip. See CORRECTION 1 at the top of details before planning this half.

THIRD SYMPTOM, same root cause: because the task stays `pending`, the SCHEDULER also re-dispatches it. Four already-verified, already-queued branches were re-dispatched to fresh agents mid-flight, racing a queued entry that had vouched `verified_green` for a specific tip.

NOT A DUPLICATE — checked against the whole owning family before filing:
- 1867 (done) covers a train that DERAILS after its members REACHED merge-deferred, and re-drives them. Members here never reach it.
- 4737 (pending) covers members STRANDED IN merge-deferred that 1867's re-drive misses. Opposite state.
- 4497 (pending) covers a merge-deferred member already on main being re-driven through a full solo merge. Opposite state.
- 4630 (deferred) is unblock SKILL.md prose about a coalesce non-tip member.
- 3860 (pending) covers FINALIZED entries never retired from the live queue; CORRECTION 2's uncancellable entry is a LIVE `queued` one, a different state.
- 1519-1530 built the atomic-train feature; 1523/1526 are the merge-deferred transition and the all-members-ready enqueue, both done and both workflow-mediated by design.
None of them contemplates a queue entry with no workflow behind it.
Analysis: PREMISES VERIFIED on this branch (base 3061f908e7, dependency 5036 done; merge_queue.py is now a sys.modules alias of orchestrator/src/orchestrator/merge_lane/worker.py):
- merge_lane/worker.py::SpeculativeMergeWorker._maybe_coalesce_waiting_singles builds candidates from _lane_buffers['normal'], filters each through `self._merge_ready_predicate or self._default_coalesce_exclusion_reason` (production never injects a predicate, but the seam would REPLACE the default wholesale), stacks via git_ops.stack_train_branches, then resolves every absorbed single's original future MergeOutcome('superseded') and retires it. _default_coalesce_exclusion_reason has exactly two signals (one-strike registry, recent terminal blocked/error). Nothing asks whether a TaskWorkflow awaits the future.
- MergeRequest (merge_lane/types.py) has no field that says who awaits it. Construction sites: workflow.py::TaskWorkflow._submit_to_merge_queue (awaited by the workflow, whose _handle_superseded parks merge-deferred); escalation/server.py merge_request (MCP, nobody parks); stranded_verified_green.py (reaper, nobody parks); merge_lane/queue_store.py::reconstruct_merge_request (journal recovery; the workflow died with the process); worker.py solo-verify helper (never buffered).
- Option (b), the waiter registry, is not worker-reachable (the worker holds no InFlightMergeRegistry) and its labels lie: worker.py::register_and_enqueue_merge_request (the WORKFLOW path) calls registry.acquire without source=, so workflow submissions are recorded source='mcp'.
- Collateral 1 mechanism: git_ops.py::GitOps.stack_train_branches -> _stack_member rebases every successor onto its predecessor (after 5618's unstack_from_unlanded_base); _do_train_merge then rebases the tip onto main. On a non-'done' coalesce outcome the merger loop (worker.py, the `req.train_id.startswith(_COALESCE_TRAIN_ID_PREFIX)` block after `await _do_train_merge`) only one-strikes and calls _redrive_coalesce_members, which re-drives merge-deferred members only (5618 un-stacks those onto main, which is NOT byte-identical and conflicts when main moved). _dissolve_coalesce_train (admission halt) has the same shape. Nothing records or restores the pre-stack tips.
- Correction 2's "uncancellable ghost entry" is the coalesce train's own GroupMergeRequest (task_id/branch = tip, fresh mr- id, no MCP waiter). Once MCP singles are never absorbed, an MCP submitter's handle is never replaced; the general waiter-less-cancel gap is task 5248 (pending). Correction 1's quarantine (git_ops.py::GitOps.create_worktree identity-mismatch -> quarantine_worktree parking a branch that has a live queue entry) is a different mechanism in a different module; it is filed as a follow-up, not done here.

APPROACH
Part A (admission): add MergeRequest.awaited_by_workflow (kw_only, default False, i.e. fail-safe: a construction site that forgets loses coalescing, never correctness). Only workflow.py::_submit_to_merge_queue sets True; the MCP, reaper and recovery sites need no edit. In the coalescing pass, a non-awaited candidate is excluded with reason 'no_awaiting_workflow' BEFORE the injectable risk predicate runs, so no injected predicate can readmit it; it appears in the 'Coalesce exclusion' log and in train_coalesced data['exclusions'] beside coalesce_derailed_one_strike / recent_terminal_*.
Part B (unwind): stack_train_branches reports, per stacked survivor, the tip it had immediately before the rebase onto its predecessor (PreStackTip, in branch_stack.py); a member whose tip cannot be read is ejected (no stack without a restore point). The coalescing pass carries them on GroupMergeRequest.member_pre_stack_tips. On every non-'done' coalesce outcome AND on admission-halt dissolution, one worker method _unwind_coalesce_train first restores tips, then runs the existing 1867 re-drive. Restore: skipped wholesale when the tip branch is already an ancestor of main (the train landed); per member only when status_check says no live agent can own the branch (merge-deferred / pending / blocked); the GitOps primitive restore_pre_stack_tip does a compare-and-swap `git update-ref <branch> <pre> <observed>`, then `git reset --hard` in the holding worktree, refuses a dirty worktree / landed tip / moved ref / missing branch, and forgets the member's stack-base record. Never raises: the derail path must always reach the re-drive.

TESTS drive public seams only (make_lane/running_lane or SpeculativeMergeWorker+running_merge_worker over real tmp git repos, injected TrainCallbacks, EventStore.fetch_events_by_type, request futures, git rev-parse), so the new files add no private reads or patch targets to the ratchet. Every impl step regenerates orchestrator/tests/merge_lane_ratchet_baseline.json (worker.py, types.py and git_ops.py are cluster files) with `uv run --project orchestrator python scripts/merge_lane_metrics.py --write-baseline orchestrator/tests/merge_lane_ratchet_baseline.json --authorize-raise 4953 --reason "..."` when a measure rises, so each commit is green.

OUT OF SCOPE (recorded): quarantine of a branch with a live merge entry (follow-up filed); merge_cancel of waiter-less entries incl. coalesce trains (task 5248); members stranded in merge-deferred when a workflow parks after the re-drive's status read (task 4737); declared trains (their tip workflow re-fires them); skills/*.md (the unblock runbook's 'the re-drive lands it' becomes true again once MCP singles are never absorbed).
Key decisions: Use option (a): a typed flag `MergeRequest.awaited_by_workflow` (default False) is the coalescing-capability signal. Reject (b) the waiter registry, (c) MCP-side merge-deferred parking, and the alternative of having the coalescer park members itself.; Check the capability precondition in the coalescing loop BEFORE, and outside, the injectable merge_ready_predicate, and report it as an ordinary exclusion reason, 'no_awaiting_workflow'.; The restore point is captured by the code that overwrites it. stack_train_branches/_stack_member reads each successor's tip immediately before the rebase onto its predecessor and returns it as PreStackTip in TrainStackResult. A member whose tip cannot be read is ejected. The tips travel in memory on GroupMergeRequest.member_pre_stack_tips, not in a durable ref.
Steps completed: 8/8
Modules: orchestrator/src/orchestrator/branch_stack.py, orchestrator/src/orchestrator/git_ops.py, orchestrator/src/orchestrator/merge_lane/types.py, orchestrator/src/orchestrator/merge_lane/worker.py, orchestrator/src/orchestrator/workflow.py, orchestrator/tests/merge_lane_ratchet_authorized_raises.json, orchestrator/tests/merge_lane_ratchet_baseline.json, orchestrator/tests/test_coalesce_integration_gate.py, orchestrator/tests/test_git_ops_unstack.py, orchestrator/tests/test_merge_lane_coalesce_admission.py, orchestrator/tests/test_merge_lane_coalesce_unwind.py, orchestrator/tests/test_merge_lane_restart_drain.py, orchestrator/tests/test_merge_queue_coalesce.py, orchestrator/tests/test_merge_queue_lifecycle_registry.py, orchestrator/tests/test_workflow_first_enqueue_stamp.py

DERIVATION RECIPE that finds them without drowning in prose: match quoted `"(\.\./)*docs/[A-Za-z0-9_./-]+\.[a-z]+"` literals in tracked *.rs, resolve (relative forms against the containing file's dir, anchored forms against repo root), and KEEP ONLY those that resolve to a tracked file. Calibrated on main this yields exactly 6 candidates — the 4 real couplings, the dormant one, and ONE false positive (crates/reify-audit/src/pdoccover.rs:3231, a #[cfg(test)] path-classifier assertion with no I/O). The 11 synthetic `docs/x.md` / `docs/foo.md` / `docs/unrelated.md` literals in reify-audit's unit tests drop out for free because they resolve to nothing.
TWO TRAPS: (a) do NOT anchor the regex on the line containing include_str! — uniform_member_path_tests.rs puts `include_str!(` and the path on DIFFERENT lines, so a line-anchored `include_str!.*docs/` finds only 1 of the 4. (b) the "resolves on disk" filter is a graceful-skip vacuity hole ON ITS OWN — pair it with the reverse assertion (every REGISTERED docs path still resolves to a tracked file), which is what actually catches a delete/rename.

reify PRD fixture corpora have TWO different coupling regimes, and confusing them changes whether committing a deliberately-failing fixture can redden main. Verified 2026-08-20.

`docs/prds/v0_6/fixtures/*.ri` — read ONLY by explicit `include_str!` from named test files (as of 2026-08-20: harness_langcore/enum_ctor_param_binding_tests.rs reads member_enum_ctor.ri; harness_langcore/uniform_member_path_tests.rs reads member_chain_scalar.ri, member_let_read.ri, member_sub_geom_baseline.ri). There is NO glob sweep over that directory. Consequence: a PRD may commit a probe fixture that produces a hard compile Error on today's main — e.g. enum-shadow-coherence's shadow_oblig_redeclared.ri and shadow_oblig_required.ri, which are supposed to be RED until leaf γ lands — without any gate turning red, because nothing compiles them until a leaf wires them in. Because the coupling is `include_str!` (a compile-time input), once a fixture IS wired, editing it rebuilds the reading test automatically, so there is no stale-fixture hazard either.

`tests/prd-gate/fixtures/*.ri` — the same directory-level docs carve-out in scripts/verify.sh's `decide_scope` applies (task #5536), BUT a named subset is Rust-coupled and excluded from it: `_RUST_COUPLED_RI_FIXTURES` in scripts/verify.sh. Editing one of those escalates a staged commit to the full workspace suite by design. Membership's source of truth is behavioural, derived in tests/infra/test_verify_scope.sh's PG-DRIFT scenario from a real grep over all tracked *.rs — so adding a new Rust reference without listing it goes RED.

Latent gap worth knowing (not filed as a task, not this session's to fix): `_RUST_COUPLED_RI_FIXTURES` covers only tests/prd-gate/fixtures/. `docs/prds/**` classifies as docs unconditionally in decide_scope, so a Rust-read fixture living under docs/prds/v0_6/fixtures/ gets no equivalent escalation. The `include_str!` coupling makes that mostly harmless — a changed fixture forces a rebuild of its reader — but the asymmetry is real.

Reify's cross-repo code citations rot near-totally and must never be "refreshed". Critically it also forbids re-anchoring a dated snapshot and warns that retro-stamping an as-of SHA the anchors were never re-located against manufactures false provenance — so the fix for a stale dated record is a dated-evidence label, never new numbers. reify's INV-EVAL-1 commit-primitive migration leaves (tasks 5056, 6373, 6423 and successors) follow a fixed three-commit shape on crates/reify-eval/src/engine_edit.rs: `test(N): RED — pin <site> onto commit_cell_result`, `fix(N): GREEN — route <site> through commit_cell_result`, `doc(N): make edit_param/edit_source sync-pair cross-reference bidirectional`. The RED test must live INLINE in engine_edit.rs's #[cfg(test)] mod tests because crate::cell_commit is pub(crate) (lib.rs:13), so an integration test under crates/reify-eval/tests/ cannot name the typed TraceSource slug. Reuse the shared helper assert_recorded_via_commit_primitive rather than open-coding the ~40-line journal/snapshot/cache assertion block, and name the test `<surface>_<site>_routes_through_commit_primitive` so the whole migration roster stays greppable by that one substring.

reify main is a genuinely HOT shared checkout and a /prd session must expect it to move underneath itself. During one ~2-hour authoring session on 2026-08-26/27 the following landed from concurrent sessions: the spec-conformance-suite PRD (#6758–#6791), the gui-purpose-surface PRD (#6803, #6831–#6839), an F2 solver ruling, and several merged task branches — and `git status` showed ~8 other PRD files modified plus ~30 untracked fixtures belonging to other sessions. Practical consequences: (1) task-id ranges INTERLEAVE across concurrently-filing sessions, so a commit message saying "decomposed into #6758-#6791" can span ids that belong to a different PRD — never infer ownership from a range, check metadata.prd_path; (2) `git add -A` or adding a directory would sweep other sessions' untracked work, which is why the overlay mandates listing every path explicitly and using `git commit --only`; (3) a PRD's cross-PRD table can be accurate when written and stale hours later — two sibling PRDs recorded this one as "does not exist on any branch" and "untracked in project_root" respectively, both true at authoring; (4) code anchors verified at one SHA are a DATED SNAPSHOT and should be headed as such rather than re-anchored later.

reify PREMISE-VERIFICATION GOTCHA for architects: a task description or PRD that cites a test file as `crates/<c>/tests/<stem>.rs` may be quoting a PRE-CONSOLIDATION path. The merge-gate-compile-cost W1 consolidation moved most standalone binaries into `crates/<c>/tests/harness_<sub>/<stem>.rs`, so `git ls-files -- crates/<c>/tests/<stem>.rs` returns EMPTY for a file that very much exists. Do NOT read that empty result as a missing premise and fire report_blocking_dependency / escalate_blocker(missing_premise) — always re-resolve by stem first: `find crates -name '<stem>.rs'` or `git ls-files '*/<stem>.rs'`. Seen on task #6266, whose description cited `crates/reify-compiler/tests/examples_smoke.rs` and `crates/reify-eval/tests/best_practices_constraint_gate.rs`; both live under `harness_compilation_surface/` and `harness_corpus_gates/` respectively. A stale cited path is a doc-rot artifact, not grounds for a rejection exit.

Reify's cited-test-path ratchet (tests/infra/test_cited_test_paths_resolve.sh via tests/infra/cited-test-path-lib.sh::cited_test_path_scan) flags a citation of crates/<crate>/tests/<x>.rs only when the cited path no longer resolves BUT a file with the same basename still exists under the SAME crate's tests tree (index key `<crate>/<basename>`). So moving a test file into a different crate's tests/ never reds that gate. Stale cross-crate citations go undetected and have to be fixed by hand. Moving a file within a crate (e.g. flat -> harness_*/) does red it unless the citation is repointed.

Stale crates/<crate>/tests/**/*.rs prose citations ARE gated in reify now. The 2026-08-31 observation that there is "no gate" is outdated. tests/infra/test_cited_test_paths_resolve.sh (task #7095) ratchets live stale citations ⊆ tests/infra/cited-test-path-baseline.manifest, and its `--list` flag prints (file, cited, verdict, suggested target) records. The sanctioned burn-down is two commits: first drain the rows from the baseline (RED), then repoint by running a literal substitution driven by `--list` (GREEN), as #6468 did (b376faca03, 1754c8d7e6) and #7501 does. The gate deliberately ignores citations whose basename resolves nowhere (deleted tests, fixtures, forward refs), so renamed-and-moved targets such as money_force_diag_tests.rs -> harness_units_materials/money_force_diagnostic_tests.rs need a manual check.

Reify's docs/prds/v0_6/fixtures/*.ri directory is consumed by Rust test crates two ways — compile-time include_str! (crates/reify-compiler/tests/harness_langcore/{enum_ctor_param_binding_tests,uniform_member_path_tests}.rs) and runtime disk reads (crates/reify-eval, via task #5467's let_tracing_transitive_e2e.rs) — but is NOT listed in scripts/verify-pipeline-paths.txt. Because CLAUDE.md routes docs-only changes through a hooks/pre-commit run on main that scopes docs/ to no-heavy-checks, renaming/moving/deleting a fixture there lands GREEN and then breaks an unrelated crate's build or tests. Before touching a .ri under docs/prds/, run `git grep -n "prds/v0_6/fixtures" -- ':!docs/'` to find its code consumers.

reify's cited-test-path gate (tests/infra/test_cited_test_paths_resolve.sh, task #7095) SUPPLEMENTS memory 0c1a520e-6eac-4ccd-9b3d-cb395148cb5e with its scan GRAMMAR, which decides whether a citation is guarded at all: CITED_TEST_PATH_REGEX='crates/[a-z0-9-]+/tests/[A-Za-z0-9_./-]+\.rs' (tests/infra/cited-test-path-lib.sh:53). Only the FULL repo-relative form is scanned — a bare stem (`examples_smoke.rs`) and, the non-obvious one, a HALF-PATH (`harness_compilation_surface/examples_smoke.rs`) both match nothing and are completely invisible to the gate. So when repairing a stale citation, writing the half-path looks like a fix, reads like a fix, and leaves the citation just as unguarded as the bare stem was; it is also unresolvable for a human reader whenever the citing file lives under a different crate. Measured first-hand on task #7015 (branch tip vs base main 362adf9bd3): the two files it repaired carried 0 guard-visible citations on base and 8 on HEAD (7 in crates/reify-eval/tests/harness_corpus_gates/best_practices_constraint_gate.rs, 1 in .claude/skills/reify-design/SKILL.md) — i.e. the repair's real payoff was moving citations from human-only to machine-enforced, and two review-driven amendment commits were needed precisely because the first drafts used the half-path. Pair this with the standing preference for symbol-name anchors (`foo.rs::some_fn`) over line numbers (`foo.rs:248`): line numbers are what rot, and nothing in the tree gates them (1890 `<file>.rs:<N>` citations across 452 tracked .rs files on that same tree).

reify gotcha: in a PRD, a `path:line` cite that sits under a section stamped "Against main <sha>" is dated provenance, not a dangling cite, even when the target has since been deleted. Check it with `git show <sha>:<path>`. Fix staleness by adding a forward pointer by section-banner name, never by replacing the line range. This follows dark-factory's /prd author-mode rule "Never re-anchor a dated snapshot". Example: docs/prds/jcodemunch-substrate-restoration.md §2.1, task 7367.

Reify mechanism confirmed working (2026-06-30): a docs-only / PRD-only change can be landed DIRECTLY on main with a plain `git commit` (NO --no-verify, NO land.sh). hooks/pre-commit runs hooks/project-checks → `scripts/verify.sh all --profile debug --scope staged --include-infra`, which for a docs-only stage produces an empty plan and exits 0 fast ("verify.sh: nothing to verify (action=all scope=staged) — no commands in plan."). On success hooks/pre-commit calls main_gate_mark (hooks/main-gate-lib.sh) which marks the sentinel, so hooks/reference-transaction records the refs/heads/main move as SANCTIONED ("main-gate ...: sanctioned main move <old> -> <new>"). At time of writing REIFY_MAIN_GATE_ENFORCE was unset (tripwire warn-only) but the commit was still recorded sanctioned. Used to land PRD edit commit de21fb8084. This is cleaner than land.sh (which is for --no-ff task-branch merges and runs the full --scope all gate).

Refinement to the reify PG-DRIFT / _RUST_COUPLED_RI_FIXTURES rule (measured on task 6093, 2026-08-29): the trigger is a raw SOURCE-TEXT match, not an actual file read. tests/infra/test_verify_scope.sh derives the referenced set with `git grep -h -o -E 'tests/prd-gate/fixtures/[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+\.ri' -- '*.rs'`, which matches DOC COMMENTS and ordinary comments just as readily as include_str!/runtime opens. So merely CITING a fixture path in a /// docstring — e.g. naming which corpus sites a new test guards — makes verify.sh demand that basename in _RUST_COUPLED_RI_FIXTURES, and omitting it fails PG-DRIFT with test_verify_nextest_absent_suites.sh's S5 failing downstream. This is exactly how task 6093's post-merge verify went red (head f4d18741fd): a doc comment added by the test commit named r3b_displacement_at_selector_grammar.ri and nothing opened it. verify.sh's own comment block already anticipates this — it flags compiler_type_hygiene_trait_args_silent_accept.ri and stdlib_ns_mode_member.ri as "doc-comment-mentions-only" entries — so extending the list IS the sanctioned fix for this shape, and a citation-by-symbol rewrite to dodge the guard would trade real traceability for a lint dodge. Practical rule: after adding any prd-gate fixture path to a .rs file for ANY reason, re-run `bash tests/infra/test_verify_scope.sh` before committing.

candidates.content: Capability-manifest sidecar validation recipe used for solar-challenge PRDs: load the YAML with dark-factory's loader via /home/leo/src/dark-factory/.venv/bin/python, with sys.path including /home/leo/src/dark-factory/shared/src, calling shared.capability_manifest.load_capability_manifest(path). Then check polarity by running `git grep -qE <pattern> -- <paths>` in the target repo for each kind: grep delivered_check, confirming it FAILS on current main: an expect:present pattern is absent now, an expect:absent pattern is present now. A check that already passes on main delivers nothing. The S11 sidecar (5 tasks, 22 grep checks) passed both.

You can pre-check a capability-manifest sidecar before commit_planning, so a polarity violation does not reject the whole batch. Load it with dark-factory's shared.capability_manifest.load_capability_manifest. For each label, build its mechanical checks as DeliveredCheckMeta(name=cap.name, kind, pattern, expect, paths, ...).model_dump() plus 'manifest_path', then call shared.delivered_check_polarity.lint_delivered_checks(checks, files=<the task's metadata.files>, repo_root=<project>, ref=GATE_REF). Run it with /home/leo/src/dark-factory/.venv/bin/python -I. An empty findings list means commit_planning will copy every check. kind 'path' (expect present/absent on a file) is a valid mechanical kind beside grep and script. For a held leaf left out of commit_planning, the block keeps task_id: null in the sidecar until the releasing stream's commit stamps it (S10's η and S2's ε both do this).

The dark-factory capability-manifest sidecar schema (shared/src/shared/capability_manifest.py, DeliveredCheck) accepts four check kinds: grep, script, path and manual — `kind: path` (with paths + expect present/absent) is valid even though the /prd decompose-mode reference text mentions only grep/script/manual. Mechanical kinds (grep, script, path) are copied into the producer task's metadata.delivered_checks by commit_planning; manual stays sidecar-only. commit_planning's polarity gate rejects a batch whose checks are already satisfied on main, so verify each check fails on main before committing (git grep -E -c <pattern> main -- <paths>; git ls-tree main -- <path>).

PRD sidecar authoring tip (from authoring solar_challenge's errors-leaf PRD, 2026-10-14). Validate a capability-manifest YAML sidecar before decompose by running dark-factory's own code from /home/leo/src/dark-factory/.venv/bin/python:
- shared.capability_manifest.load_capability_manifest(path) checks the schema.
- shared.delivered_check_polarity.lint_delivered_checks(checks, files=<task metadata.files>, repo_root=<target repo>, ref="HEAD") checks polarity. Each grep/path check must FAIL on main now and PASS after its producer lands.
An `expect: absent` grep whose matches lie in files outside the task's declared files yields a WARN (absent_overbroad). It clears once the task's metadata.files lists those files. A 'path' kind check is the way to assert a new file exists; a grep cannot.

To pre-flight a capability-manifest sidecar before commit_planning, run dark-factory's own validators from its venv: /home/leo/src/dark-factory/.venv/bin/python with shared/src on sys.path. Load the sidecar with shared.capability_manifest.load_capability_manifest. For each task's checks whose kind is in MECHANICAL_CHECK_KINDS, call shared.delivered_check_polarity.lint_delivered_checks(checks, files=None, repo_root=<project>, ref='main'). git grep is invoked with -e, so a pattern starting with '--' is safe. The finding-key lookup (quality-findings-contract §8 step 1) has no MCP tool yet. Use a read-only sqlite query on <project>/.taskmaster/tasks/tasks.db that matches json_each(metadata,'$.x_finding_key') or the scalar json_extract. It works, and was sanity-checked against fk-998f0cb69410, which is on task 284.

You can pre-lint a capability-manifest sidecar's delivered_checks before commit_planning by reproducing its polarity gate offline with dark-factory's own modules. From /home/leo/src/dark-factory, run .venv/bin/python with:
- shared.capability_manifest.CapabilityManifestDoc.model_validate(yaml) to validate the sidecar;
- shared.delivered_check_polarity.lint_delivered_checks(checks, files=<leaf metadata.files>, repo_root=<project root>) on each label's non-manual checks, each given name=<capability name>.
An empty findings list means commit_planning will not reject the batch with DeliveredCheckPolarityViolation. The S21 decompose (2026-10-16) used this, and its commit_planning went through clean.

The review-all program's capability-manifest sidecars in solar_challenge (docs/prds/*.capability-manifest.yaml) had no signal_leaves field until 2026-10-17. Without it, the dashboard reads each PRD as 'names no signal leaf'. The S4 decompose added signal_leaves: ["ι"] (the integration-gate leaf, task 872) to docs/prds/finite-quantities.capability-manifest.yaml and confirmed it loads under dark-factory's CapabilityManifestDoc. The schema also supports a `kind: path` delivered_check (paths + expect present/absent) besides grep/script/manual. A decompose session can validate a sidecar with `uv run --directory /home/leo/src/dark-factory/shared python -c 'from shared.capability_manifest import CapabilityManifestDoc; ...'`.

Validating a /prd capability-manifest YAML sidecar for solar_challenge before decompose: from /home/leo/src/dark-factory run `uv run --directory shared python` with shared.capability_manifest.load_capability_manifest(<sidecar>) for schema, and shared.delivered_check_polarity.lint_delivered_checks(checks, files=<task files or None>, repo_root=/home/leo/src/solar-challenge) per task for polarity (a check must fail on main and pass after the leaf). With files=None every expect=absent check reports a non-blocking 'absent_overbroad' warning because nothing is declared in scope; those clear once metadata.files lists the edited files. Vacuous checks (expect=present already matching main, expect=absent already absent) are the blocking class.

Capability-manifest convention used by the S12 PRD: when a leaf's upstream producer belongs to another stream that has not yet filed (here S11 δ, S13's hand-off leaf, S21 δ/α), the binding's verdict is OPEN with a manual delivered_check whose reason says it turns PASS once the lead hands back the id and the edge is wired. The batch verdict is then OPEN, which blocks decompose. This is the honest form of G3 for unfiled cross-stream producers, rather than writing PASS. The sidecar validated with dark-factory's shared.capability_manifest.load_capability_manifest, run via `cd /home/leo/src/dark-factory/shared && uv run python -I`.

Validating a /prd capability-manifest YAML sidecar from the solar-challenge repo: run `cd /home/leo/src/dark-factory && uv run --directory shared python -I -c "import yaml,sys; sys.path.insert(0,'src'); from shared.capability_manifest import parse_capability_manifest; parse_capability_manifest(yaml.safe_load(open('<abs path>.yaml')))"`. The verdict vocabulary is PASS|FAIL|OPEN. A block has exactly one of task_id or external_task_id. Before committing delivered_check grep patterns, baseline them with `git grep -E -c` against main: e.g. '(^|[^a-z-])amber-[0-9]' misses 'bg-amber-50' because the char before 'amber' is a hyphen; plain 'amber-[0-9]' is correct.

The capability-manifest sidecar for a solar_challenge PRD can be validated before filing from the dark-factory checkout: `cd /home/leo/src/dark-factory && uv run --project shared python -c "from pathlib import Path; from shared.capability_manifest import load_capability_manifest; load_capability_manifest(Path('<abs sidecar path>'))"`. A pre-filing polarity check (every grep delivered_check must be red on HEAD: an expect=present pattern has 0 hits, an expect=absent pattern has hits) can be run with `git grep -n -E <pattern> HEAD -- <paths>`. content: The capability-manifest sidecar schema (dark-factory shared/src/shared/capability_manifest.py) does not allow a 'note' field on a capability. ManifestCapability has only name, binding, verdict and delivered_check, and extra fields are forbidden, so a sidecar carrying one fails to load. Only the task block (ManifestTask) has a 'note'. Rationale for a single capability belongs in its binding string. delivered_check kinds are grep, script, path and manual; 'path' (with paths and expect) is valid and is copied into metadata.delivered_checks as a mechanical check. Validate a sidecar before filing with: cd dark-factory/shared && uv run --frozen python -c "from shared.capability_manifest import load_capability_manifest; load_capability_manifest('<path>')".
