candidates.content: Addendum (task 672, measured 2026-09-30 with a stand-in BatterySpec subclass) to the gotcha about tests/config/test_store.py::_governed_spec_values and BatterySpec fields the library lacks: TWO tests break when BatterySpec gains a platform-only field (task 596's commissioned_max_charge_current_a / commissioned_max_discharge_power_w), not one. Besides test_battery_spec_defaults_match_solar_challenge_battery_config, test_non_default_spec_leaves_no_field_at_its_library_default also raises AttributeError, because it too reads every BatterySpec field off a solar_challenge.BatteryConfig through _governed_spec_values. The round-trip tests test_battery_spec_to_battery_config_reconstructs_lib_type and test_set_battery_write_and_reconstructed_reads keep passing, because they build the expected battery with _library_battery_from(spec), which passes BatteryConfig only the fields it has. So task 596 needs the library-side restriction in exactly those two tests and no other edit to the file.

Gotcha (config governance): a frozen value-object that mirrors a solar_challenge library dataclass (e.g. config/contract.py BatterySpec ↔ solar_challenge.BatteryConfig) MUST replicate the library's FULL __post_init__ validation set, not a subset. Under-validation is latent data corruption: set_battery() persists the BatterySpec fields directly (no to_battery_config() guard, no ORM CheckConstraint), so an invalid value flushes fine but every later current_battery()/battery_as_of() read raises ValueError inside to_battery_config()/the lib constructor — the row is permanently unreadable. solar_challenge.BatteryConfig.__post_init__ rejects capacity_kwh<=0, max_charge_kw<=0, max_discharge_kw<=0, and (via battery._validate_soc_and_efficiency) requires 0<=min_soc<max_soc<=1, 0<charge_efficiency<=1, 0<discharge_efficiency<=1. BatterySpec is the documented validation boundary, so all of these belong in its __post_init__.

Gotcha (config governance tests; measured 2026-09-29 at task 561 HEAD a55a5ac): tests/config/test_store.py::_governed_spec_values does getattr(battery, name) for EVERY name in dataclasses.fields(BatterySpec) on each mirror, including a solar_challenge.BatteryConfig, so adding a BatterySpec field the library does not carry makes test_battery_spec_defaults_match_solar_challenge_battery_config raise AttributeError (simulated with a stand-in subclass: 'BatteryConfig' object has no attribute 'commissioned_max_charge_current_a'). Pending task 596 adds exactly two such non-physics nullable fields (commissioned_max_charge_current_a, commissioned_max_discharge_power_w) and does not list tests/config/test_store.py in its files, so its implementer should add that file and restrict the library-side comparison to library-carried fields (for example an explicit exclusion set naming the two commissioned fields, so an unlisted physics field still fails loudly) while keeping the ORM-side comparison whole.

Completed: test_battery_spec_to_battery_config_reconstructs_lib_type should round-trip every governed field and read the library defaults, not pin literals
Description: Found by task 561's architect while planning task 561 (follow-up id agent-followup-561; no escalation was filed).

OBSERVED: tests/config/test_store.py::test_battery_spec_to_battery_config_reconstructs_lib_type has the docstring "Governed fields round-trip exactly; degradation fields (not governed by P10) take the library's own defaults." Its body builds BatterySpec(capacity_kwh=8.0, name="X").to_battery_config() and asserts capacity_kwh == 8.0, name == "X", system_age_years == 0.0 and soh_floor == 0.5. Six of the eight governed fields (max_charge_kw, max_discharge_kw, min_soc_fraction, max_soc_fraction, charge_efficiency, discharge_efficiency) stay at their defaults, and those equal the library's. So a BatterySpec.to_battery_config() (src/solar_challenge_platform/config/contract.py) that dropped any of those keywords would still pass. The degradation defaults are pinned as literals rather than read from solar_challenge.BatteryConfig.

NO OTHER TEST CATCHES IT: a grep of tests/ on 2026-09-29 (base 4139aa3) found no test that round-trips non-default governed values through to_battery_config(), or through ConfigGovernanceStore.current_battery / battery_as_of, which both return BatterySpec.from_orm_row(row).to_battery_config(). tests/runtime/test_scp_seed.py::test_seed_golden_fleet_rerun_keeps_a_later_board_battery_edit asserts store.current_battery(home_0) == resized.to_battery_config(), which puts to_battery_config on both sides. tests/config/test_store.py::test_set_battery_write_and_reconstructed_reads also pins current.system_age_years == 0.0 as a literal.

WHY IT MATTERS: the optimiser plans with the battery that store.current_battery(...) returns. If to_battery_config dropped a mapping, a board-governed 5 kW battery would be planned at the library's 2.5 kW with no error. The docstring claims more than the body checks (heuristic 1), and the round-trip invariant is not enforced (heuristic 10).

SUGGESTED FIX (test-only, no production change): build a BatterySpec with every governed field set to a non-default value, then assert spec.to_battery_config() == solar_challenge.BatteryConfig(**dataclasses.asdict(spec)). That one assertion checks both that every governed field crosses over and that every ungoverned field takes the library's own default. Optionally, have test_set_battery_write_and_reconstructed_reads use non-default governed values and compare current_battery(...) with the library battery built the same way. The test passes as soon as it is written. To show it is not tautological, temporarily delete one keyword (e.g. max_charge_kw=self.max_charge_kw) from to_battery_config(), watch the test fail, then revert.

SEQUENCING: task 561 rewrites the neighbouring defaults test in the same file and adds a _governed_spec_values helper there, so land this after task 561.
Analysis: Test-only change in tests/config/test_store.py: use non-default governed values and compare to solar_challenge.BatteryConfig(**asdict(spec)).

solar_challenge_platform gotcha (code reading, 2026-10-04, main 2838c8a, task 542): PhysicsDeviceEnd's delivered feedback, and therefore control_command_log, does NOT depend on the battery_factory's battery capacity. The DVCC clamp is the fixed-W dvcc_max_setpoint_w (None in validation/run.py::drive_dispatch), and _apply_to_battery's min-SOC guard compares only against max_soc_fraction (0.9 for both BatteryConfig.default_5kwh() and the simulator's per-slot BatteryConfig). A wrong per-home battery in the device end is visible only through battery_for(home), i.e. once something steps that Battery (task 529's coupled physics, P-Fleet δ F26). So a command-log or determinism assertion cannot detect it; assert on battery_for(home).config instead.

Import-cycle gotcha (measured 2026-09-30, task 684, base b392a1a): a shared-defaults module placed anywhere under the solar_challenge_platform.config package cannot be imported from models/battery_config.py. config/__init__.py eagerly imports config.store, which imports models.battery_config at module scope. So when `models` is imported first, as tests/config/test_store.py's db_session fixture does, the import fails with "ImportError: cannot import name 'HomeBatteryConfig' from partially initialized module". This was simulated with an in-memory leaf via a meta-path finder; importing `config` first happens to succeed, so the failure depends on import order. A single source of the battery-spec defaults that both BatterySpec and HomeBatteryConfig read must therefore live outside config/, for example in models/ or in a project-import-free leaf, or be derived from solar_challenge.BatteryConfig.

Gotcha (optimiser): the governed battery band can be narrow, and deriving a BatteryConfig from it can crash. solar_challenge.BatteryConfig requires 0 <= min_soc_fraction < max_soc_fraction <= 1 (strict) and raises ValueError('Invalid SOC limits: min=..., max=...') otherwise. The platform's BatterySpec (config/contract.py) accepts narrow governed bands such as [0.10, 0.20]. So any code that derives a config with dataclasses.replace(battery_config, min_soc_fraction=F), e.g. planner reserve floors or β3a's standing_floor, must keep F strictly below the governed max_soc_fraction or it crashes. The device-end simulator likewise rejects a min_soc_pct outside [0, max_soc_fraction) (simulator/device_end.py ~L388-397). Measured 2026-09-29 on main 0cbb6a6 (task 563).

solar_challenge_platform gotcha (task 542, 2026-10-04): PhysicsDeviceEnd() with no battery_factory gives EVERY home a 5 kWh battery (BatteryConfig.default_5kwh()). Code that fronts the simulated golden fleet must pass battery_factory=SimService.build_battery_factory(n) (simulator/service.py). That gives home build_registry(n)[i] a fresh Battery of build_fleet_config(n).homes[i].battery_config: (8 + i) kWh, the same battery scp-seed commissions as the governed battery. It raises LookupError naming any home outside the n-home fleet. validation/run.py::build_fleet_device_end(config) wraps it for drive_dispatch, and the scp-sim-modbus role (task 489) should reuse SimService.build_battery_factory. This supersedes the final clause of memory 106be145 ("device_end still uses a 5 kWh battery").

Gotcha (solar_challenge_platform, measured 2026-10-14 by the task 1123 architect at base 2db33ae): dropping an ORM column's Python-side default makes "rejects …" constraint tests pass VACUOUSLY, because a row built without that column now hits NOT NULL before the partial-unique index or CHECK the test means to exercise. For HomeBatteryConfig this hit three tests in tests/config/test_models.py: rejects_second_open_row_same_property, rejects_bad_effective_window and the migration-0014 constraints test. Before removing any column default, repoint every direct constructor in tests to supply the column; for battery rows, use **dataclasses.asdict(BatterySpec(...)).

solar_challenge.BatteryConfig fields (probed live from the pinned lib 2026-06-30, for the P10 per-home battery ORM): capacity_kwh (REQUIRED, no default), max_charge_kw=2.5, max_discharge_kw=2.5, name="", min_soc_fraction=0.1, max_soc_fraction=0.9, charge_efficiency=0.975, discharge_efficiency=0.975, plus a degradation model (system_age_years, calendar_fade_rate_per_year, cycle_fade_per_equivalent_full_cycle, soh_floor, soh) and optimiser-owned nested configs (dispatch_strategy, grid_charging). BatteryConfig.default_5kwh() returns capacity_kwh=5.0/charge=discharge=2.5. The P10 governed table stores the PHYSICAL SPEC (capacity, charge/discharge, SoC bounds, efficiencies, name); resolve() reconstructs a valid BatteryConfig from those columns; the degradation model defaults to lib defaults (SoH governance deferred). The optimiser obtains it at optimiser/identity.py:165 (currently hardcoded default_5kwh()); the simulator also uses default_5kwh() in simulator/device_end.py and physics.py.

P3 simulator gotcha: solar_challenge.FleetConfig.create_heterogeneous(pv_capacities_kw, battery_capacities_kwh, annual_consumptions_kwh, location=Bristol) yields HomeConfig objects whose battery_config is None whenever the corresponding battery_capacities_kwh entry is None (PV-only homes). simulator.physics.SimHome REQUIRES a non-None BatteryConfig (it unconditionally builds Battery(battery_config, ...)). So simulator/fleet.py Fleet.from_config must narrow/reject None battery_config (raise a clear ValueError naming the home index) before constructing a SimHome — do not substitute a default battery (would violate D2 'every metric derives from a solar_challenge call'). Verified 2026-06-21 on task/37.

Completed: Fleet simulator seeds SimHome's battery at a fraction of NOMINAL capacity, which raises once SoH < 1 (same latent bug class as task 849)
Description: Filed as a follow-up from task 849 ("Optimiser.plan() clamps the initial SoC with nominal capacity but Battery validates against SoH-derated capacity"). Escalation id: agent-followup-849.

WHAT: src/solar_challenge_platform/simulator/fleet.py line 336 (the per-home loop that builds SimHome, in the classmethod that takes initial_soc_fraction, default 0.5) passes initial_soc_kwh=initial_soc_fraction * battery_config.capacity_kwh. That is a fraction of the NOMINAL capacity. SimHome hands it straight to solar_challenge's Battery(battery_config, initial_soc_kwh=initial_soc_kwh) (src/solar_challenge_platform/simulator/physics.py line 287). In solar_challenge 0.5.0, Battery validates initial_soc_kwh against min/max SoC fractions of the SoH-DERATED effective capacity (capacity_kwh * SoH). Its own soc_fraction is also a fraction of effective capacity, not nominal.

MEASURED (2026-10-07, worktree of task 849, solar_challenge 0.5.0), evaluating fleet.py's expression against Battery directly:
- BatteryConfig(capacity_kwh=5.0, soh=0.9), fraction 0.9: "ValueError: Initial SOC 4.5 kWh outside allowed range [0.45, 4.05]".
- BatteryConfig(capacity_kwh=5.0, soh=0.5) (0.5 is the library's default soh_floor), fraction 0.5 (the default): "ValueError: Initial SOC 2.5 kWh outside allowed range [0.25, 2.25]".

(b) Reuse battery_at_clamped_soc. Check layering first: the simulator would then import from optimiser.planner.

solar_challenge 0.5.0 gotcha, measured 2026-10-05 on main d8982d6 for task 764. Battery's floor, max and initial-SoC check all use effective_capacity_kwh = capacity_kwh × SoH. But simulate_timestep hands strategies config.capacity_kwh, the nominal capacity, so grid-charge targets are measured against nominal capacity. solar_challenge 0.5.0 Battery seeding gotcha (verified 2026-10-07, task 849). Battery(config) WITHOUT initial_soc_kwh seeds the midpoint and validates no SoC, so it never raises for a valid BatteryConfig. Battery has no public SoC setter (soc_kwh is read-only). To seed a simulation at a live reading that may lie outside the SoH-derated range, read min_soc_kwh/max_soc_kwh from a SoC-less Battery(config), clamp the reading into them, then build Battery(config, initial_soc_kwh=clamped). Task 849 adds this as planner.battery_at_clamped_soc. Never clamp with fraction * config.capacity_kwh: that is nominal capacity, and it equals the derated bounds only at SoH 1.0. To read effective capacity alone, use Battery(config).effective_capacity_kwh.

solar_challenge_platform test technique (task 878, verified 2026-10-07): to read the SoC that Fleet.from_config seeded into a home's battery, use only public seams. Pass from_config(profile_source=...) a ProfileSource whose sample() returns (0.0, 0.0). With zero generation and zero demand, simulate_timestep calls neither Battery.charge nor Battery.discharge, so the first tick's battery_soc_kwh equals the seed bit-exactly. Read that tick via fleet.sources[i].encode_tick(clock.tick()), then ingestion.wire.decode, then take the Metric.battery_soc_kwh row. Never read SimHome._battery.

Structural fact behind the "uncloseable consolidation gate" trap (dark_factory, verified 2026-09-07 planning task 4878): the topic-slug migration recipe recorded in memory c7768b64 spans TWO DIFFERENT STORES, which is why gates 4220 and 4774 each needed hand work rather than one bulk operation.

- The member records are Mem0 memories; their `topic` moves via a metadata-only `MemoryService.update_memory(metadata_patch={'topic': new}, metadata_mode='merge')`.
- `x_recon_consolidation_gate` is NOT Mem0 metadata. It is a Tier-C block on TASK metadata, written by `build_consolidation_gate_task`, read by `fused_memory/reconciliation/consolidation_gate.py`, and enforced by `fused_memory/middleware/task_interceptor.py` on the `status='done'` transition (only for a task carrying `operational_mode == 'gate'` AND that block). Moving its `topic` is an `update_task` call through the MCP server — the route `scripts/migrate_task_metadata_to_x_namespace.py` established, loading `FusedMemoryClient` by importlib path from `scripts/strip_leaked_control_keys.py` ("there is one JSON-RPC handshake in this repo").

Consequence for anyone automating this: the two halves must be held as a PAIR. Renaming the memories alone leaves the gate's closure check scrolling a slug no record carries any more — re-creating the uncloseable-gate trap at a NEW address, which is strictly worse than leaving the snake_case slug alone, because the operator must now also discover the migration caused it.

Two more traps on the same path: (1) `update_task` reports some rejections by RETURNING an error envelope rather than raising, so guard it with `assert_write_accepted(result, tool='update_task')` — the same is true of `update_memory`. (2) Folding `foo_bar` -> `foo-bar` when records already carry `foo-bar` is a namespace MERGE, not a normalization; since `topic` scopes canonical uniqueness (`_check_canonical_uniqueness` probes `{'topic': T, 'canonical': True}`) and that seam warn-fails OPEN under the shipped `memory_metadata.enforce=false`, merging two clusters that each hold a canonical creates a second canonical silently. Check for an incumbent before every rename.

ARCHITECT TRIAGE RULE for any "consolidate the N duplicate memories about X" task: BEFORE planning, run a DETERMINISTIC topic re-query, not a semantic search. A corpus-hygiene follow-up is often already satisfied by a consolidation gate that closed AFTER the follow-up was filed, and its prescribed remedy may now be FORBIDDEN rather than merely redundant.

MEASURED at task 4288 (2026-08-29, HEAD 09e589e0a1). 4288 was filed 2026-08-16 as an agent follow-up naming 8 duplicate entry ids and prescribing "collapse into one canonical, then delete the superseded entries with delete_memory". THE PART THAT MAKES THIS MORE THAN STALENESS: the deletes were the one step still "undone", and they are undone ON PURPOSE. Gate 3417 executed in the gate-3200 ratified RETAIN-AND-TAG shape — a SHORT canonical index claim plus every member retained in place via metadata-only patch, so Qdrant point ids and created_at survive and nothing citing them dangles — closing with "retained=30 | deleted=0 ... ZERO deletes, so no citation dangled and the citation-repoint gate was never engaged". Executing the follow-up as written would have destroyed 7 records a ratified decision deliberately kept. A task that looks 7/8 done can be 100% done plus one actively harmful step.

A gate task names its cluster by member UUID and NEVER by topic, so a pre-existing topic over the same subject is invisible unless you go looking. Two mechanical findings from the 2026-08-27 consolidation-gate curation sitting, both of which blocked execution until worked around.

1. TOPIC SLUGS: snake_case topics are UNCLOSEABLE BY CONSTRUCTION. Gate 4774's topic was mem0_tombstone_coverage, which fails topic_slug.py::TOPIC_SLUG_RE. Topic WRITES are warn-mode — which is how its members got stamped in the first place — but consolidate_memories validates its topic ARGUMENT hard, so the first call was refused and no canonical could ever be written under that spelling by any legal route. The gate could not be closed without migrating the slug. Resolution: migrated both peers and the gate block in lockstep to mem0-tombstone-coverage, content-neutral, UUIDs preserved; the old slug now scrolls zero. topic_slug.py's own docstring names this normalization as the intended remedy for its 98 known snake_case values, so expect this to recur on any of those.

Gate 4750 enumerated 6 candidates in its metadata while the LIVE topic scroll returned 8 — and the metadata block says so itself, carrying authoritative:false. Always take the working list from the live metadata.topic scroll, never from a hand-written or gate-recorded enumeration.

Same key, two incompatible meanings, no discriminator in the value.

WHY IT BITES ASYMMETRICALLY. Reading it off a STORED row is safe if you also require the row to be what you're looking for — `recurring_gate_guard.find_open_gate` additionally requires `execution_class=='operational'` and gate mode, so the three code_tdd/decision rows can never be mistaken for gate carriers. Reading it off an INCOMING submission has no such fallback: the submission is already known to be a gate (that is how it reached subject resolution), so a see-also pointer silently becomes the dedupe subject and the write is hard-rejected against an unrelated record, with the rejection prose asserting the two share a subject. If you resolve a key on both sides, the two alias orders are NOT interchangeable — `recurring_gate_guard.py` now keeps `GATE_SUBJECT_ALIASES` (stored, wide) separate from `GATE_SUBJECT_SUBMISSION_ALIASES` (incoming, narrow) for exactly this reason.

RELATED KEYS, for anyone writing a carrier->subject join: `gate_subject` is the canonical spelling introduced by task 3588 (1 row at time of measurement); `stranded_task_id` is unambiguous (only ever a subject) but has 0 rows in dark-factory — that population lives in the reify project. So a census run against the wrong corpus will conclude the key is unused. This sits alongside the task-3201 gotcha about curator gates not sharing an id-enumeration convention: task metadata key semantics in this store are per-filing-agent conventions, not a schema, so measure the live corpus before joining on any of them.

NORM for executing a Mem0 duplicate-cluster gate (reinforced 2026-08-24, esc-4640-1). Three mechanical facts that the escalation records' own EXECUTION CONTRACT sections do not mention, each of which bites at execution time:

1. THE CONTENT-AMEND ARM OF `update_memory` IS GRANT-GATED. Authorized agent_id prefixes are ['recon-stage-', 'curator-'] (config `mem0_update.content_amend_allowed_agent_prefixes`). An ordinary `agent_id="claude-interactive"` is refused with `error_type=Mem0UpdateNotAuthorized` — "in-place amendment is a silent-rewrite primitive, so the default bar is deliberately narrow". Use `agent_id="curator-<escalation-or-sitting-id>"` for curation work. METADATA-ONLY patches are NOT gated, so retain-and-tag topic stamping works from any agent id.

2. A GATE TASK IS A LIVE CITER OF EVERY UUID IT ENUMERATES, so its own delete will refuse. `_citation_repoint_gate` computes `live_citers = [c for c in citers if not c['terminal']]` (fused-memory/src/fused_memory/server/tools.py:1949), and a gate task sitting at `blocked` is non-terminal. Measured on task 4640: it was the ONLY task in tasks.db citing either clustered UUID, so 100% of the citation exposure was its own bookkeeping. The fix inverts the normal order — CLOSE THE GATE TASK BEFORE RUNNING ITS DELETES — and then the guard becomes a precise detector of genuine third-party exposure. This is the sequencing trap documented in skills/curate-fused-memories and task 3625.

3. THE REPOINT GATE COVERS TASK CITATIONS ONLY, NOT MEMORY PROSE. `_scan_task_citations` scans tasks. A memory whose TEXT cites another memory by 8-char UUID prefix (a common house style — e.g. c2333fe9 cites "mem0 9988ed0e, 15019144, 254ff143, 5f413f86") will be left with a dangling reference by any delete, silently, with no refusal. Check for prose citations separately, and note that this exposure is usually symmetric across candidate survivors and therefore NOT a tiebreaker.

RELATED: do not try to verify prose citations with `scan_memory_content` — its `matches` field is unusable for arbitrary needles (see the standing entry on that, and task 3898 which owns the fix).

Resolved the same way as 4220 — migrate the members onto the conformant hyphenated spelling (`mem0-tombstone-coverage`) — which is now the established remedy across two independent gates.

THE MECHANISM, which a52b7919 does not state and which makes this predictable rather than surprising: the asymmetry is between the WRITE path and the OP-ENTRY path. `metadata.topic` writes are validated in WARN MODE (memory_metadata.enforce=False), so stamping a snake_case topic succeeds, emits a census line, and proceeds — which is how these clusters come to exist, including via recon Stage 1's own stamping. But `consolidate_memories` validates its `topic` ARGUMENT HARD at op entry through `server/consolidation.py::validate_consolidate_args` -> `topic_slug.py::is_valid_topic_slug`. So the corpus can freely ACQUIRE a topic that the sanctioned consolidation op can never WRITE to.

CONSEQUENCE FOR CONSOLIDATION GATES SPECIFICALLY: such a gate is UNCLOSEABLE BY CONSTRUCTION, not merely awkward. No canonical can be written under the bad spelling by ANY legal route — hand-writing one via add_memory hits the same shared predicate, and promoting an existing peer to canonical is what the Option-C end state forbids. The gate can never reach "exactly one canonical" until the slug is migrated. Note `build_consolidation_gate_task` DOES raise on a malformed topic, so a gate filed through that constructor cannot hit this; the exposure is gates whose cluster was stamped by some other path.

MIGRATION RECIPE (content-neutral, used on both 4220 and 4774): metadata-only `update_memory` patch of `topic` on each member (UUIDs preserved, zero content amends, zero deletes), and — for a gate task — move `metadata.x_recon_consolidation_gate.topic` IN LOCKSTEP, because that block's topic is what the closure check scrolls. Verify afterwards with count_memories_by_metadata on the OLD slug expecting 0, so nothing is stranded.

`topic_slug.py`'s own module docstring names this normalization as the intended remedy for its ~98 known non-conforming values, so this is sanctioned cleanup, not improvisation. The corpus-wide slug-conformance migration remains UNOWNED — this is now the second gate to pay for it individually.

THE ESTABLISHED SHAPE FOR THIS CLASS IS A BATCH RULING, not one-at-a-time: esc-3524-1 batch-ruled FOURTEEN open consolidation gates on 2026-08-02, and that batch is what produced skills/curate-fused-memories and the curator- grant. GOTCHA (dark-factory, measured 2026-09-07 while planning task 4643): when you are asked to build a guard over a set of METADATA KEY NAMES, check whether those key names actually occur in THIS repo before writing an allowlist — for the agent-invented memory-id key family they usually do not, and the allowlist ships empty-by-construction and passes everything silently.

THE TRAP, ALREADY MEASURED AND RECORDED ONCE. `fused-memory/src/fused_memory/reconciliation/citation_verifier.py::find_citation_occurrences` states it verbatim in its docstring: "the known citation key names from that incident (`mem0_canonical_entry`, `mem0_cluster_entries`, `x_memory_write_caution`) are *reify-project* task-DB keys with ZERO occurrences in this repo, so an allowlist built from them would be empty-by-construction and would silently pass every delete." That module answers the question with a mechanical all-keys/all-positions scan instead of a key list. Task 4643 hit the identical trap from the other direction: its task description proposed an allowlist whose headline member, `cluster_memory_ids`, is a reify key with zero occurrences here — so the guard would have missed the very instance that motivated it.

WHY THE FAMILY IS OPEN. These keys have no code writer. The writers are recon Stage 1/2 PROMPTS and hand-authored gate tasks, so the population drifts freely. Measured live spellings: `memory_ids` (invented by DF gate 3036, repudiated in `reconciliation/consolidation_gate.py`), `related_memory_ids` (the canonical Tier-A blessed spelling, `reconciliation/prompts/__init__.py::FINDING_MEMORY_IDS_METADATA_KEY`), `stale_cluster_memory_ids` + `canonical_fact_memory_ids` (`scripts/retro_stamp_topics.py`), `cited_memories`, `duplicate_memory_ids` + `cited_memory_ids` (`reconciliation/flag_dedup.py`), `origin_memory_ids` (docs/task-authoring.md), plus reify's `cluster_memory_ids`, `mem0_canonical_entry`, `mem0_cluster_entries`. Grepping for a CODE writer and finding none is not evidence the key is dead — docs/task-authoring.md §8 says this explicitly for `related_memory_ids`.

WHAT TO DO INSTEAD, and the two spellings that are NOT interchangeable. Use a key-NAME SHAPE rule, but anchor it on the SUFFIX, never on a substring. A substring rule like "name contains 'memor'" has a measured false positive: `memory_hints` is a REGISTERED `TaskMetadata` submodel whose values are prose search queries, so it would acquire a UUID rule. A suffix rule (`memory_ids`/`memory_id`/`memories`/`entries`/`entry`, plus the literal `supersedes`) covers every spelling above INCLUDING the cross-project ones, and collides with nothing code-written.

THE HAZARD THE SUFFIX ANCHOR EXISTS TO AVOID, which is the part that bites hardest: several task-metadata keys legitimately carry SHORT HEX that is not a memory id — `branch_base_sha`, `done_provenance.commit`, `suggestion_hash`, `retry_ledger.merge_outcome_signature`, `merge_retry_pending.base_sha`/`branch_head`. A UUID-shaped-value rule applied over the whole blob would reject an abbreviated commit sha and block `done` writes, stalling the merge lane. Git SHAs and UUID prefixes are indistinguishable by value shape alone, so the key rule — not the value rule — is what has to keep them apart. None of those names matches the suffix anchor.

VERIFY THE NON-COLLISION AS A TEST, not by inspection: assert no `shared.task_metadata.TaskMetadata.model_fields` name, no registered-submodel key (`milestone`, `routing`, `merge_retry_pending`, `recurrence`, `delivered_checks`, `deploy_state`), and no `_BLESSED_METADATA_KEYS` member other than the intended one satisfies the rule. That way a future typed field named e.g. `deploy_entry` fails the suite instead of silently inheriting a UUID rule.

Two gotchas for any code that writes around a Mem0 topic cluster or files recurring gates through the raw SqliteTaskBackend (found while planning task 5240).
1. A record that carries a top-level metadata.topic JOINS that topic's scroll. That scroll is get_memories_by_metadata({'topic': T}), which consolidation_gate.py::evaluate_closure and the topic-anchor pin both read. So an audit or system record ABOUT a topic must nest the topic under an x_ key (e.g. x_auto_consolidation.topic). Otherwise, after a reversal it is left as a topic member with no canonical, which is an orphan.
2. SqliteTaskBackend.add_task's candidate-key guard (title + metadata files) rejects a match against ANY non-cancelled row, done rows included. A gate filed with a fixed per-topic title therefore can never be re-filed once an earlier gate for that topic is done. Make the title unique per filing (e.g. include the proposal run id) and handle DuplicateCandidateKeyError.existing_id.

Bulk-filing a /prd decompose batch exactly (worked 2026-10-11, M-WASTE, 18 long task texts):
1. Render every task record (title, description, priority, metadata) to a JSON file with a script.
2. Call submit_task(planning_mode=True) and add_dependency over a small Python urllib MCP client against fused-memory :8002 (initialize → mcp-session-id → notifications/initialized → tools/call), so nothing is hand-transcribed.
3. Read every task back with get_task and diff the description, prd_task_label and dependencies against the source.

Behaviour observed on readback:
- metadata.execution_class='decision' leaves are converted at submit to task_kind='deterministic' plus always_escalates=true.
- An add_dependency client_op_id makes the edge writes idempotent.

For delivered_checks:
- Use kind='path' to assert that a new file exists. A grep for a filename never goes green.
- Avoid a visibility-change grep such as `pub(crate) fn X` when the change could legitimately be skipped. Such a check can stay red after a correct delivery and wedge dependents.

Bulk fused-memory work is best scripted through ~/.claude/fleet/recovery/mcpcall.py (a streamable-HTTP MCP client to 127.0.0.1:8002) even while the session's own MCP connection works, because it keeps large payloads out of the conversation. Measured 2026-09-30: paging all 8008 reify tasks via get_tasks(page_size=50) took ~8.5 min (~3 s per page), and the statuses=[pending,deferred,in-progress] filter (1615 tasks) was far faster. get_task/update_task round-trips were ~0.15 s (132 stamps with pre-read and read-back in 58 s). Snapshot then: 5788 done, 1349 pending, 606 cancelled, 241 deferred, 24 in-progress.

Bulk task filing for a large /prd decompose: generate each leaf record (title, description quoting the PRD §8 row, metadata from the manifest) into a JSON plan with a script, then submit through a small Python MCP streamable-HTTP client against fused-memory at 127.0.0.1:8002 (initialize → mcp-session-id header → notifications/initialized → tools/call, parse SSE data: lines). On 2026-10-08 this filed 22 planning_mode leaves and 77 add_dependency edges (with client_op_id for idempotency) without hand-copying ~36k characters into tool calls; stop on the first response without a task_id and never retry blindly, since a timed-out submit may still have landed. Read the dependency lists back afterwards and diff them against the plan.

Procedural (contract §8 dedup step 1 on reify, 2026-10-13): the paginated get_tasks key-index scan is cheap via the streamable-HTTP MCP client against fused-memory :8002 (initialize → mcp-session-id → notifications/initialized → tools/call, parse SSE data: lines): page_size 200 over ~8,850 tasks finishes in about a minute; collect metadata.x_finding_key into an index and assert examined == pagination total. The same paging pass can record dependencies and spawned_from/x_superseded_by/x_replacement to find a task's DEPENDENTS and CHILDREN — get_task returns neither, and both must be checked before cancelling a task as subsumed (a cancelled dependency counts as satisfied, so its dependents dispatch early unless re-pointed).

Procedural technique for scanning the whole reify task corpus without flooding context: an MCP tool result that exceeds the response token limit is NOT lost — the harness saves the full payload to a file under the session's tool-results/ directory and returns the path plus the JSON schema. So `mcp__fused-memory__get_tasks(project_root=..., statuses=["pending","in-progress","blocked","deferred","infra-hold"])` (2.5 MB, 507 tasks on 2026-08-05) can be called deliberately and then queried with jq. Used on 2026-08-05 to answer "does anything depend on task X" exhaustively: `jq -r '.tasks[] | select(.dependencies // [] | map(tostring) | index("5717")) | "\(.id)\t\(.status)\t\(.title)"' <file>`. This is the only practical way to enumerate reverse dependency edges — fused-memory exposes add_dependency/remove_dependency but no reverse-edge query — and it stays within the rule that .taskmaster/tasks.db must never be read or written directly.

Bulk decompose filing over HTTP: for an 18-leaf /prd batch, a ~40-line stdlib python streamable-HTTP MCP client against fused-memory (http://127.0.0.1:8002/mcp: initialize → mcp-session-id header → notifications/initialized → tools/call, parse SSE data: lines) filed every submit_task, add_dependency (with client_op_id idempotency keys), update_task and set_task_status from a structured spec file. This keeps descriptions byte-exact with the spec and keeps them out of the agent's context. Stop on the first error and never retry a submit_task that returned no task_id; check by title instead. update_task(details=..., append=True) appends correctly, while description is replace-only. Read back lengths to confirm descriptions were untouched.

Tool quirks seen in the reify L2 watcher session of 2026-10-08 to 10-10:
- fused-memory get_tasks called without pagination returned a response over 16MB that the client could not read. Use page_size <= 200 with offset, plus a status filter. An exhaustive reverse-dependency scan (who depends on task X) must page get_tasks and check examined == pagination.total. search_tasks is semantic and cannot see dependency edges.
- update_task and get_task echo the FULL task record, which can be very large (e.g. 6925, 6155, 5380). For context-sensitive sessions, delegate bulk task writes to sub-agents.
- The completion-claim gate (fused_memory completion_claim_gate) false-positives on imperative, forward-looking or quoted phrasing about a task landing, e.g. "check #8246's status for whether it has landed". There were 3 instances in 3 days (7407-3, 5471-4, 8246-5); filed as dark-factory #6677.

PROCEDURE/GOTCHAS for the fused-memory task API when the MCP is disconnected (2026-09-23): the streamable-HTTP fallback client at the spawn-brief path (mcp.py <port> <tool> '<json>') works for submit_task / resolve_ticket / update_task / get_task / search_tasks against port 8002 and get_merge_queue against 8100; it pretty-prints JSON, so parse the whole stdout, not the last line. submit_task rejects metadata.milestone=true — `milestone` is a RESERVED schedule shape ({'mode':'dated','at':ISO} or {'mode':'delayed','after_secs':N}); tag a decision-gate task with another key (used decision_gate=true) and put [MILESTONE] in the title. submit_task's `dependencies` string is comma-separated ('7834,2952') and lands as real edges (read back showed deps [2952, 7834]). Escalation resolve_issue rejects free-form resolution_class — allowed: actionable, benign, moot-terminal-subject, stale-strand. update_task with description+details+dependencies+metadata in one call works; metadata merges shallowly (files list overwrites wholesale).

fused-memory MCP access quirk (2026-06-23): the full get_tasks call (reify has ~4700 tasks, ~25MB payload) reliably returns 'session expired' through the Claude Code harness MCP client, but get_task/submit_task/update_task/set_task_status (small payloads) work fine. Reliable workaround for bulk reads/writes: POST JSON-RPC directly to http://127.0.0.1:8002/mcp with headers 'Content-Type: application/json' and 'Accept: application/json, text/event-stream', method tools/call. The server is effectively stateless — no Mcp-Session-Id handshake needed; a bare initialize returns no session header and tools/call works immediately. result.content[0].text holds the JSON-stringified payload.

Reify reconciliation — bulk task listing limitations (revised 2026-07-26, run bdfdd837): full/unfiltered bulk endpoints remain unreliable for the reify project at current scale (~5518 tasks), but PAGINATED and ID-FILTERED variants are confirmed reliable and should be preferred over ad-hoc get_task loops.

1. get_tasks, UNPAGINATED/full-dump call → persistent "MCP server session expired" failures on every call (historical, confirmed recurring through run 2690c3db). Do not retry the full-dump form.
   CARVE-OUT (confirmed run 06a4466d): get_tasks(project_root=..., page_size=10, offset=X) succeeds reliably at reify's current 5518-task scale — Stage 3 made three separate paginated calls (offset=0, a mid-range offset, and offset=5508 at the far end of the task range) and all three succeeded. Use paginated get_tasks for bulk enumeration, not the full-dump form.

2. get_statuses, UNFILTERED/full-population call → previously silently truncated at ~3414 task IDs with no error signal (confirmed 2026-05-14). As of 2026-07-26, with reify at 5518 tasks, the unfiltered call now fails OUTRIGHT with "result (79,357 characters) exceeds maximum allowed tokens" instead of silently truncating — the failure mode escalated from silent truncation to a hard transport error as task count grew past the tool's tested envelope. Confirmed by Stage 3 in reconciliation run 06a4466d-cdc0-49ac-8e99-e6723be39392, blocking full-population status enumeration for spot-check sampling.
   CARVE-OUT (confirmed run 06a4466d): get_statuses already supports an `ids` list filter, and this filtered mode was confirmed working this cycle at reify's current scale. Only the unfiltered/full-population call fails.

3. search_tasks → returns STALE title/description text at recycled IDs (confirmed 2026-05-26); status field is live-enriched but title/updated_at are from a corpus snapshot. Always confirm identity via get_task(id) before concluding a task "already exists" or is a duplicate.

RECOMMENDED STAGE 3 PROCEDURE (revised in run bdfdd837, 2026-07-26): Prefer paginated get_tasks(page_size=..., offset=...) for bulk enumeration at reify's current scale — confirmed reliable end-to-end including the far-end offset. Prefer get_statuses(ids=[...]) for targeted status checks against a known id set — confirmed reliable. Reserve individual get_task calls for identity confirmation and small hand-picked samples. Treat ONLY the unpaginated get_tasks call and the unfiltered/full-population get_statuses call as unusable at current scale; treat search_tasks results as hints only pending get_task confirmation.

Over-wide module-lock remediation sweep (2026-06-18, requested by Leo: "if you have any directory level metadata.files, delete them. Only use specific files that you're confident of"). Of 178 NON-TERMINAL reify tasks (pending/in-progress/blocked/review), 85 (~half the backlog) carried ≥1 directory-level metadata.files entry. Completed: Assistant trigger tools: list start/end in run_home_simulation's and run_fleet_simulation's input_schema, so the model can ask for a window other than days from 2024-06-01
Description: Agent follow-up found during task 524's amendment pass (escalation id agent-followup-524). OUT OF SCOPE for task 524. That task makes simulation_params.parse_date_range refuse a body that sends days together with start/end, and makes the assistant's trigger tools apply their 7-day default through simulation_params.with_default_days only when the model sends no window. It deliberately left the tool schemas unchanged. Land after task 524 merges.

OBSERVED on branch task/524 at b389d86 (2026-10-08), by reading src/solar_challenge/web/assistant.py:
- In TOOLS, run_home_simulation's input_schema lists pv_kw, battery_kwh, consumption_kwh, occupants, location and days. run_fleet_simulation's lists n_homes, pv_kw, battery_kwh, location and days. Both days descriptions read "Simulation duration in days (default 7)." Neither schema lists start or end.
- The handlers now read an off-schema start/end as POST /api/simulate/home reads it. They also refuse days sent with start/end, e.g. "Invalid simulation parameters: days must not be sent with start or end, got days 30 with start '2024-03-01' and end '2024-03-05'". Tests: tests/unit/web_assistant/test_tool_handlers.py::TestRunHomeSimulation::test_start_and_end_sent_run_that_window_not_the_7_day_default, ::test_days_sent_with_start_and_end_returns_the_refusal_naming_what_was_sent, and TestRunFleetSimulation::test_fleet_start_and_end_sent_run_that_window_not_the_7_day_default.
- So the model is only told about days, which runs N days from 2024-06-01, or the full 2024 year for 365. A user who asks the assistant for, say, a January or winter run cannot get one unless the model sends fields its schema does not list. The days description does not say that days excludes start/end.

The task 524 comprehensive review offered two fixes. (a) Add start/end, ISO dates mutually exclusive with days, to both tool schemas. (b) Leave the schemas and document start/end as off-schema. Task 524 took (b), in commit b389d86, run_home_simulation's docstring: "an off-schema start/end is read as that endpoint reads it". It did so to keep the model-facing API and the cached prompt prefix unchanged. This task is option (a), a product decision on whether the assistant should offer date windows.

SUGGESTED CHANGE: add "start" and "end" (type string, ISO 8601 YYYY-MM-DD, end inclusive; one not sent reads as 2024-01-01 / 2024-12-31, as parse_date_range reads it) to both trigger tools' input_schema. Say in days' description that it is not sent with start/end, and that 365 means the full 2024 year. Then drop "off-schema" from run_home_simulation's docstring. TOOLS renders ahead of the cached system block, so any schema change misses the prompt cache once. Keep the tool order: tests/unit/web_assistant/test_tool_use.py::TestToolSurface pins it.
Files: src/solar_challenge/web/assistant.py, tests/unit/web_assistant/test_tool_use.py, tests/unit/web_assistant/test_tool_handlers.py. Pending task 440 also edits assistant.py, in run_fleet_simulation's n_homes block and dispatch_tool, not TOOLS.

Completed: Billing push: a provider refusal leaves a dangling Stripe invoice and crashes scp-bill --account; the collected-payment cancel differs between fake and real
Description: FINDING (review 20260928T062907). Traced by a review sub-agent at HEAD 3d74313, with file:line evidence. Re-verify the line numbers before editing.

1. NOTHING CATCHES ProviderRefusal. A repo-wide grep finds no `except ProviderRefusal`. runtime/roles/bill.py::_bill_single_account (≈:327-374) turns ConsentDenied, BillingOrderError and PropertyOfRecordMismatch into tagged `[TAG] … nothing persisted` lines. A refusal from dd.schedule() instead escapes as a raw traceback. The fleet close is fine: fleet_run.py:203-215 catches Exception per account.

2. PUSH ORDER BREAKS "pushes NOTHING". billing/status.py (≈:386-391) creates the Stripe invoice before it schedules the GoCardless DD, and store.put (≈:301-303) comes after both. When the DD is refused, the Stripe invoice already exists but no BillingRun is persisted. One reachable trigger: dd._require_collectable (billing/dd.py:33-40) checks only amount > 0, and the real GoCardless £1.00 minimum is "not modelled" (billing/cassettes/README.md:27-31). A 1-99p amount due therefore passes locally and is refused by the real rail. Suggested fix: check collectability, including a governed or constant rail minimum, before any provider call, and hold or skip with a typed reason. Alternatively, void the Stripe invoice when the DD is refused. Add a fake-lane test showing that a refused DD leaves no Stripe invoice.

3. cancel_payment IGNORES COLLECTED STATUS, AND FAKE AND REAL DIFFER. DirectDebit.recalculate (dd.py:70-96) cancels `current` with no status check. FakeGoCardless.cancel_payment (billing/providers/fakes.py:293-302) quietly turns a CONFIRMED (collected) payment into CANCELLED. The real GoCardlessDirectDebit.cancel_payment (billing/providers/gocardless.py:185-187) lets gocardless_pro InvalidStateError through untranslated, unlike create_payment, which maps errors to ProviderRefusal. Make both refuse a collected payment the same way, through the contract.ProviderRefusal port. Note that recalculate has no production caller: status.py only calls schedule(). Keep it, since task 347 pins it, but its refusal of a negative revision should be a named exception, not a bare ValueError (dd.py:33-40).

Out of scope (latent, noted only): Stripe item, invoice and meter-event keys come from reference_key(account, period) with no revision component (billing/providers/stripe.py:167,172,202,259). A re-price of an already-pushed period would silently reuse the original items. No production path re-prices today.

Leo's 2026-09-28 ruling on esc-404-2 ("A + milestone"): task 404 is CANCELLED as working-as-designed.

WHY. The IdempotencyError on a changed re-push of an already-invoiced period is the PRD-intended loud failure. Restatement is deferred per docs/prds/billing-engine-s4-s5.md §12: the pilot ships immutable first-run statements plus a back-billing guard, and a corrections/credit-note workflow comes later. Persisted statements are never re-derived. billing/statement.py:894-904 is an idempotent read-through, and runtime/roles/bill.py:174-177 checks the store before any push. So a changed re-push needs a manual DB edit. Stripe idempotency keys expire after about 24h, so statement immutability is the lasting guard.

Both proposed fixes double-charge.
- (a) Content-digest item keys: the invoice call replays the original, so new items sit beside stale lines or get swept into next month. Digesting the invoice key creates a second invoice. Task 315's design record already rejected this.
- (b) A versioned reference_key creates a second invoice while the first is open or paid, and breaks the payment<->invoice<->statement join (billing-provider-integration-s5.md §E lines 309-310, §G line 324).

The correct future design is void-and-reissue: a durable revision, a {acct}:{period}:r{n} key, the old invoice voided or credit-noted, and the DD cancelled or refunded.

Do not re-file on the strength of this cancellation; re-file only if statements become re-derivable after push, or the milestone task is cancelled.

Hotspot survey 2026-10-13 (verified at 40a6556) — billing push lifecycle and composition gaps: billing/status.py::run_and_persist writes the first durable billing_run_status row only AFTER every Stripe/GoCardless call; BillingRunState declares PUSHED/INVOICED/DD_SCHEDULED but never produces them, there is no transition table, and SqlAlchemyBillingRunStore.put upserts any state over any state; the only double-push guard is bill_account's store.get. billing_statements has no unique constraint (only billing_runs is unique on account/start/end), so concurrent runs over different periods both pass the R3 contiguity guard, and R3 has no base case (first bill can drop opening days, task 519). Idempotency/join keys are f-strings built in five places; a revision key '<ref>:r1' neither matches PaymentMatcher nor parses in parse_reference_key. Providers are hard-coded to FakeStripeInvoicing/FakeGoCardless at four construction sites (runtime/roles/bill.py, validation/run.py, dropped_readings.py, ...); the real adapters are built only by billing/slow_lane.py, whose BillingDriftExecutor.run labels every adapter exception (even KeyError) as infra 'NOT billing drift'. POST /billing/run builds its own BillingService without as_of, so it skips the back-billing guard. Survey advice: extend the approve-issue-gate PRD's billing/lifecycle.py LEGAL table (task 466) with an ISSUING state committed before provider calls plus lookup-before-create, rather than a second table; one providers_for(settings) that refuses fakes in production.

Stripe push idempotency vs restatement (task 404 architect, 2026-09-28, verified against main 09e3ee7): StripeInvoicing's keys do not depend on content (invoice = reference_key(account_id, period); item = f"{ref_key}:item:{position}"). So a CHANGED re-push for an account+period that was already pushed fails loudly with stripe.IdempotencyError inside Stripe's 24h key window. This is by design, not a defect. Statements are immutable after their first run: docs/prds/billing-engine-s4-s5.md §12 lists "Re-billing / credit notes / statement supersession workflow" as out of scope for the pilot. PRD billing-provider-integration-s5 §G also requires that a retried push never creates a second invoice. Two proposed fixes were rejected. (a) Folding a content digest into the item or invoice keys lets a changed view create a second set of Stripe charges: stale items beside new ones on one invoice, or a second invoice for the period. (b) Minting a revised reference_key does the same unless the superseded invoice is voided or credited, and nothing produces a revision (Statement has none; DirectDebit.recalculate has no production caller). Either belongs only inside a designed corrections workflow: void or credit note, DD recalculate wiring, a persisted statement revision, and updates to every consumer of reference_key as a join key (matching.py, arrears.py via parse_reference_key, status.py InMemoryBillingRunStore, gocardless.py payment metadata). It is never a standalone key change.

Billing push architecture (review 20260928T062907):
- No flow re-prices an already-billed statement. DirectDebit.recalculate (billing/dd.py) has no production caller; status.py only calls schedule().
- scp-bill's idempotency pre-check returns the existing BillingRun without a re-push.
- status.run pushes the Stripe invoice BEFORE it schedules the GoCardless DD, and persists only after both. A DD refusal therefore strands a Stripe invoice.
- ProviderRefusal is caught nowhere except the fleet close's per-account Exception guard.
- Stripe idempotency keys are reference_key(account, period) with no revision component.
Treat any future "revise a bill" feature as needing a revision-namespaced key and a persisted payment ledger.

candidates.content: Orchestrator MCP role-config reference (verified 2026-07-12 @ main 7b6c1f829c): there are TWO role gates in workflow.py. `_MCP_CONFIG_ROLES` (workflow.py:116-118 = architect/implementer/debugger/merger/judge/simple_task) gates whether the HTTP mcp_config (fused-memory + escalation) is built. `_PLAN_TOOLS_ROLES` (workflow.py:125 = architect/implementer/debugger/simple_task) gates the per-worktree stdio plan-tools server. reviewer and triage are in NEITHER gate — their `mcp__jcodemunch__*` grant (roles.py:426, :22) is INERT because no MCP config is injected for them. judge and merger are in _MCP_CONFIG_ROLES only. There is NO on-disk .mcp.json from the orchestrator — the config is an in-process dict → tempfile → `--mcp-config` (cli_invoke.py:1270-1275). Crucially, `_inject_plan_tools_mcp` (workflow.py:142-175) creates a `{'mcpServers':{}}` skeleton when mcp_config is None, so a role NOT in _MCP_CONFIG_ROLES can still receive a per-worktree stdio server without joining that gate. To add a new stdio MCP server for a role: mirror _PLAN_TOOLS_ROLES + _inject_plan_tools_mcp + plan_tools_mcp_server (mcp_lifecycle.py:69-144) + a tool-grant family in roles.py (like _PLAN_CREATOR_TOOLS roles.py:80-104), gated `role.name in <ROLES> and cwd` at the _invoke spawn site (workflow.py:7397).

GOTCHA (verified 2026-09-09 by the capacity-study critic): "read-only by construction" or "isolation-safe by construction" is FALSE for any eval, sweep or role invoked through shared/src/shared/cli_invoke.py under its default permission_mode='bypassPermissions'. The Claude CLI ambient-merges the project-scoped .mcp.json found at cwd (live escalation 8102 + live fused-memory 8002), so a role's narrow tool grant (e.g. reviewer_comprehensive holding only verdict_tools) does NOT prevent live writes. Only --strict-mcp-config (emitted solely when mcp_config= is passed together with strict_mcp_config=True) and --disallowed-tools are load-bearing; --allowed-tools does not restrict. Concrete instance: orchestrator/src/orchestrator/evals/reviewer_trial/runner.py passes mcp_config= but never strict_mcp_config=True, so the reviewer-corpus campaign is NOT isolated until that one kwarg is added. Same class as task 4757 (the v2 fable campaign wrote 36 add_memory / 7 escalate_info / 3 submit_task into live stores). How to apply: before asserting isolation, grep the invocation path for strict_mcp_config and disallowed_tools and read cli_invoke.py::build_claude_argv; never infer isolation from the role definition.

GOTCHA: the orchestrator's 'orchestrator' MCP family is an all-or-nothing bundle. `MCPLifecycle.mcp_config_json` (orchestrator/src/orchestrator/mcp_lifecycle.py:1030-1051) hardcodes BOTH `fused-memory` (http) and `jcodemunch` (a stdio subprocess) in the same dict, and `AgentRole.__post_init__` forces `mcp_families |= {'orchestrator'}` the moment any `mcp__fused-memory__*` tool enters `allowed_tools`. So you cannot grant a role memory access without also attaching the jcodemunch subprocess (cold-start plus the 0-turn MCP-startup wedge class, reify esc-4415-232). Splitting a memory-only family out of `'orchestrator'` is the real precondition for granting memory to any currently-memoryless role.

In shared/src/shared/cli_invoke.py's build_claude_argv, `--strict-mcp-config` is emitted ONLY inside the `if mcp_config:` block, so passing `mcp_config={}` is a silent no-op that emits neither `--mcp-config` nor `--strict-mcp-config` — a scoping config MUST stay truthy (use `{'mcpServers': {}}`). This matters because when an `output_schema` is present the `disallowed_tools=['*']` wildcard is stripped and replaced by `_REAL_BUILTIN_TOOLS_DENYLIST`, which names BUILT-IN tools only; MCP tools are therefore NOT denied, and a caller whose `cwd` carries a `.mcp.json` (e.g. explore_codebase_root = project root) ambient-merges real MCP servers under bypassPermissions. Denying built-ins alone does not close MCP access.

In shared/cli_invoke.py, passing disallowed_tools=['*'] does NOT block MCP tools when an output_schema is also set: the wildcard is expanded into _REAL_BUILTIN_TOOLS_DENYLIST, which lists built-in tool names ONLY and carries no MCP tool pattern. Any such caller whose cwd holds a live .mcp.json (e.g. explore_codebase_root = the project root) has those servers ambient-merged by the CLI and reachable — under permission_mode='bypassPermissions' that is unreviewed access.

TWO WAYS TO CLOSE IT: (1) mcp_config=NO_MCP_SERVERS_CONFIG plus strict_mcp_config=True — note the --strict-mcp-config emit is gated on `if mcp_config:` in build_claude_argv, so a bare {} silently no-ops and the scoping config MUST stay truthy; or (2) run from a neutral_cli_cwd() that carries no .mcp.json at all, which removes the ambient merge at its source rather than denying it after the fact.
