candidates.content: Pattern for testing TaskWorkflow.run()'s ESCALATED branch end-to-end without driving real agents: (1) pre-create worktree via git_ops.create_worktree, optionally add a marker commit so the branch is one commit ahead of main (otherwise wt_head == main_sha and the already-on-main short-circuit fires before whatever you're testing); (2) build TaskWorkflow with workflow.initial_plan = PLAN to skip PLAN phase, and pre-set workflow.worktree (triggers eval-mode `_worktree_external = True`, which skips the MERGE phase block); (3) submit an L0 escalation directly to the EscalationQueue before run() so _ensure_steward_started() finds it; (4) monkeypatch workflow._execute_verify_review_loop to AsyncMock returning [ESCALATED, DONE]; (5) use _make_status_setting_steward(queue, scheduler, task_id, status) factory to drive the steward's behavior; (6) mock workflow._invoke (resume implementer) so its call count is observable. See orchestrator/tests/test_workflow_status_on_resume.py for the canonical example.

To unit-test orchestrator TaskWorkflow._setup_worktree_and_artifacts directly (all existing tests fully MOCK it), drive the REAL method via its external-worktree branch: pre-set `wf.worktree` to a real git repo (with ≥1 commit so `git rev-parse HEAD` succeeds → sets `_worktree_external=True`, skipping create_worktree + venv sync), stub `scheduler.get_status` (non-terminal, e.g. 'pending'), `set_task_status`/`update_task`/`set_task_claimant` as AsyncMocks, set `config.claimant_heartbeat_interval_secs` to a large number so the background heartbeat task sleeps, and cancel `wf._claimant_heartbeat_task` in a finally (awaiting with contextlib.suppress(asyncio.CancelledError)). See test_workflow.py::TestSetupWiresLanePlanSymlink (task 2763).

RED-MAIN RCA (2026-07-10, esc-2367-4): 53-fail/31-err deterministic red-main in orchestrator workflow-state-machine suite (tests/test_repend_state_machine.py + tests/test_workflow_e2e.py), symptom "Task 42: architect produced no plan.json (success)" → workflow BLOCKS at planning before MERGE-entry gate. ROOT CAUSE: commit e168feb80b relocated the workflow's artifacts root from legacy <worktree>/.task to the SIBLING <worktree_base>/.task-meta/<name> via TaskArtifacts(self.worktree, _meta_root_for_worktree(self.worktree)) (ε1/task 2258 design — meta_root outside worktree survives git clean). But the e2e test DOUBLES that hand-roll plan.json paths were NOT migrated: AgentStub._architect writes cwd/.task/plan.json directly (bypasses TaskArtifacts, so the autouse _derive_meta_root_like_production constructor-patch fixture CANNOT reach it); direct-body seeds at test_workflow_e2e.py:1114/1220/1354/1386 use task_dir=cwd/'.task'; and test_repend_state_machine.py imports AgentStub but LACKS the autouse fixture entirely (fixture is file-local to test_workflow_e2e.py, not in conftest). The 31 ERRORS are secondary (blocked workflow fires run_dry_run_unblock → _dry_run_unblock_e2e_guard teardown error). FIX: hand-rolled plan.json writers must target TaskArtifacts.meta_root_for(cwd.parent, cwd.name) (== workflow's self.artifacts.root), fixture-independently. Classic dropped-rebase-companion (e168feb80b is a 'save WIP before requeue rebase' commit — the _architect/test-body migration vanished in a requeue rebase, same failure mode as task 2403).

In the dark-factory orchestrator, core TaskWorkflow contracts (e.g. `_mark_blocked`'s `merge_phase` status-write suppression) are pinned not only in the obviously-named test files but as incidental TAIL assertions inside tests whose real subject is something else — task 3537 found `tests/test_workflow_dry_run_hook.py` asserting `'blocked' not in scheduler.statuses` purely as a "contract intact" afterthought in two dry-run-hook tests. Grepping only the neighbour files an architect's plan names will miss these. When changing a workflow-spine contract, run the FULL orchestrator suite (`cd orchestrator && uv run pytest tests/ --timeout=300`, ~16k tests, 6-12 min under the default xdist addopts) before declaring the step green.

MEASURED PREMISE FAILURE worth knowing before planning any "move these private writes into the constructor" test migration (dark-factory, task 5025, branch task/5025, HEAD 2467fc528b, 2026-09-12).

THE PLAN STEP said: move test_workflow_e2e.py's 11 `workflow._steward_factory = ...` and 2 `workflow._cancel_event` writes into the TaskWorkflow constructor, "a pure relocation with zero production change", because both ARE real TaskWorkflow parameters — which they are (`steward_factory` workflow.py:1173 stored :1240; `cancel_event` :1179 stored :1232).

WHAT THE STEP MISSED, and what to check next time: WHERE the object is constructed. test_workflow_e2e.py contains exactly TWO direct `TaskWorkflow(` call sites (:373, :1141) and neither serves those 13 writes. All 11 steward sites build through `_build_workflow_no_merge_worker` (a local delegate at :1497) which forwards to `_build_workflow_with_escalation`, and both cancel-event sites through `_build_workflow`; both builders live in orchestrator/tests/_workflow_helpers.py and construct the TaskWorkflow themselves (:1172-1182) with no steward_factory/cancel_event passthrough. TaskWorkflow offers no public alternative either — its only public methods are the `state` property/setter (:1514/:1525) and `run()`; there is no cancel()/soft_cancel()/set_steward_factory().

So "the class takes the parameter" does NOT imply "the test can pass it". The cheap check is `grep -c '<ClassName>(' <test file>` and then following each helper the sites actually call, BEFORE writing the step or the RED baseline number.

CONSEQUENCE HERE: the 13 sites were recorded as measured residual and filed as esc-5025-4 (scope_violation, non-blocking) rather than edited, because _workflow_helpers.py is not among task 5025's 12 assigned files and is shared with test_repend_state_machine.py — editing a shared helper during a nine-sibling concurrent rebase is exactly what the per-path-key ratchet method exists to avoid. The RED baseline was lowered only to the reachable target (patch_targets 2 -> 1, private_reads left at 188) rather than to the step's stated 175.

THE FIX, for whoever picks this up (routed to task 5446): optional `steward_factory=` / `cancel_event=` passthrough kwargs on `_build_workflow_with_escalation` and `_build_workflow`. It is measure-neutral for the merge-lane ratchet — a keyword argument is not an ast.Attribute, so _workflow_helpers.py's own entry stays at {"patch_targets": [], "private_reads": 0} — and it would retire all 13 sites at once.

FACTS for anyone building on the harness event/artifact seams (verified 2026-09-10 at main 32d0f6d1a7, for the live shadow eval PRD): EventType.phase_enter / phase_exit are emitted from workflow.py with (task_id, phase); EventType.merge_finalized (merge_queue.py) carries request_id, branch (bare_id), state, snapshot_tip, merge_sha, superseded_by, generation, reason, landed_via_chain; EventStore exposes latest_merge_finalized(branch=) and fetch_events_by_type. The accepted plan is durable at .task-meta/<task>/plan.json (artifacts.py::TaskArtifacts.write_plan, called from mcp/plan_tools.py; the lane copy is a symlink). The task record carries metadata.branch_base_sha (dispatch base). Eval worktrees are created by evals/snapshots.py::create_eval_worktree under <project_root>.parent/<name>-eval-worktrees, i.e. OUTSIDE .worktrees/. TaskWorkflow exposes exactly one callback (on_soft_cancel); any other observer needs a new seam. The harness _maybe_auto_eval sibling-task redo hook (config auto_eval_enabled default True, $50/day) has fired 0 times ever and only triggers on BLOCKED optimistic-path tasks — it is not a general paired re-run mechanism. The load gate is scheduler.py::_phase_psi_gate over shared.psi::saturated(cfg).

When TaskArtifacts gained the meta_root param (TaskArtifacts(worktree, meta_root=None), artifacts.py), production call sites (workflow.py self.artifacts, plan_tools.py) were updated to pass the derived sibling `.task-meta/<name>` root via `_meta_root_for_worktree`, but tests/test_workflow_e2e.py has ~50 agent-side doubles (AgentStub._architect/_implementer etc.) that hand-construct `TaskArtifacts(worktree)` with no meta_root. That created a read/write split-brain: production's self.artifacts pointed at the NEW sibling root while doubles wrote step status to the legacy `worktree/.task` root, so get_pending_steps() never saw completion and workflows blocked with 'Execution iterations exhausted'. Fix (task 2258): an autouse pytest fixture that monkeypatches TaskArtifacts.__init__ to default meta_root to `TaskArtifacts.meta_root_for(worktree.parent, worktree.name)` whenever omitted, mirroring production's derivation for every call site at once. Lesson: when a shared value-object gains a new optional constructor param with a legacy-compat default, audit hand-rolled test doubles that bypass the real constructor call sites — they silently keep old behavior and can desync from relocated production state.

Gotcha (orchestrator tests, task 6051): run()-exit-contract assertions (store_unavailable / violation records) are only observable in a run() whose worktree is NOT external. workflow.py::TaskWorkflow._exit_status_facts returns (None, None) when self._worktree_external (eval mode) or after a hard cancel, so judge_exit sees no status row and no write failure and records nothing. test_workflow_status_on_resume.py's _build_workflow(config, git_ops, task_assignment, queue, wt) passes a worktree and runs in that eval mode. Drive exit-contract tests through _workflow_helpers.py::_build_workflow (no external worktree) or _make_warmlane_workflow instead, as test_workflow_state_machine_boundary.py's row-6 tests do.

ROOT CAUSE (VERIFIED 2026-08-05, still live): a warm lane can be handed to an architect carrying an uncommitted half-finished implementation WITHOUT any warm-lane reseed failure. orchestrator/src/orchestrator/workflow.py:2559-2567 — when a `simple_task` agent returns the fall-through sentinel, the handler unlinks ONLY plan.json and plan.lock ("drop the plan so the architect path runs cleanly") and never reverts the working tree. The SIMPLE_TASK role contract (agents/roles.py:1508) is explicitly explore -> plan -> EDIT THE FILES -> commit, so any mid-implement death leaves partial source edits that pass straight to the architect. Consequence: every TDD RED step the resulting plan schedules starts from a tree where the implementation already exists, so RED steps come up spuriously GREEN and the TDD gate proves nothing. Diagnosed from reify esc-5985-2, whose OWN filed hypothesis ("a retry inherited the dirty tree rather than a fresh reseed") is REFUTED — runs.db showed a single run, a single lane acquire that reseeded correctly (HEAD == branch_base_sha), a simple_task killed at 11:14:31Z by subtype=error_max_budget_usd, and the architect entering the SAME worktree 10 s later with no lane release/re-acquire. Scale: ~78 failed simple_task invocations across reify + dark-factory runs.db (~16-20% of all simple_task dispatches). Filed as dark_factory task 3652. Fix: dump `git diff HEAD` to artifacts for forensics, `git reset --hard HEAD` (NOT to base — the branch may carry legitimate committed WIP), then clear untracked strays via GitOps._clean_lane_retaining_artifacts (git_ops.py:6729) so target/ survives.

Recipe for unit-testing orchestrator `TaskWorkflow._review` directly (it had ZERO direct test coverage until task 3639 added TestReviewMirrorCarriesSalvagedVerdict in orchestrator/tests/test_reviewer_verdict_routing.py). Build the fixture with `_workflow_helpers._make(worktree=..., project_root=...)`, then stub four things: `wf.briefing.build_reviewer_prompt` -> AsyncMock; `wf.git_ops.get_diff_from_base` AND `get_diff_from_main` -> AsyncMock (which of the two `_review` calls depends on whether `artifacts.read_base_commit()` is set — `_make` calls `artifacts.init(..., base_commit='oldbase')`, so the base branch is taken; this is the known bare-MagicMock-not-awaitable gotcha); and CRITICALLY `wf.config.reviewer_stagger_secs` and `wf.config.max_reviewer_retries` to real numbers. The latter two are the non-obvious part: `_make` builds config as `MagicMock(spec_set=pydantic_spec(OrchestratorConfig))`, so unset fields return MagicMocks that reach `asyncio.sleep(idx * stagger)` and `range(max_reviewer_retries)` and blow up. Set stagger to 0 to keep the test fast, and retries to a small int to make the exhaustion path (initial + N retries) countable via `wf._invoke.call_count`. `_review` returns `artifacts.aggregate_reviews()`, and the on-disk mirror it wrote is at `artifacts.root/'reviews'/f'{role}.json'`.

Writing an orchestrator INTEGRATION GATE that drives real dispatches with a fake agent runner: the injection seam is NOT a constructor param. `TaskWorkflow.__init__` has no `invoke_fn`; production `_invoke` (workflow.py:12179) passes the module-global `orchestrator.workflow.invoke_agent` as `invoke_fn=` to `invoke_with_cap_retry` (:12385). So the ONLY patch that leaves the real `_invoke` running (resolve_route, ceiling spend query, `_record_routing_decision`, the `metadata.routing` merge-write, MCP injection, session/sidecar lifecycle) is `monkeypatch.setattr('orchestrator.workflow.invoke_agent', fake)` — with per-module twins `orchestrator.steward.invoke_agent`, and the same shape in review_checkpoint.py / dry_run_unblock.py. Coarser seams silently defeat the gate: `patch.object(TaskWorkflow, '_invoke')` skips route resolution entirely; patching `invoke_with_cap_retry` means no runner runs so nothing proves the resolved model reached the CLI argv; patching `resolve_and_record_route` mocks out the very behaviour an out-of-band parity test asserts. Fake signature that survives kwarg drift: `async def fake(*, cwd: Path, **kwargs) -> AgentResult` (only `success`/`output` are required on AgentResult). Three rig gotchas: (1) `_workflow_helpers._derive_meta_root_like_production` is an AUTOUSE fixture that only activates if you import it BY NAME — without it a bare `TaskArtifacts(worktree)` resolves the legacy `.task` root, not the production `.task-meta` sibling, and writes land where the workflow never reads; (2) `_build_workflow(config, git_ops, assignment, agent_stub)` accepts the stub but does NOT wire it — you still monkeypatch yourself; (3) a REAL `OrchestratorConfig` is mandatory (not `_workflow_helpers._make`'s MagicMock) because `resolve_route` does membership/dict ops over `config.routing.*`, and `sandbox=SandboxConfig(enabled=False)` is required against fake worktrees or `compute_write_set` raises. Canonical precedents: test_verdict_servers_integration_gate.py (task 2488), test_config_reload_integration_gate.py (task 2008), test_workflow_e2e.py.

In dark-factory, TaskWorkflow builds its TaskArtifacts with meta_root=_meta_root_for_worktree(worktree) (workflow.py:2384), so plan.lock lives at <worktree_base>/.task-meta/<worktree_name>/plan.lock — a SIBLING of the worktree. Only plan.json is symlinked back into the lane as <worktree>/.task/plan.json (artifacts.py ensure_lane_plan_symlink); plan.lock is NOT. Any code that reads plan.lock via a bare TaskArtifacts(worktree_path) will look in the legacy <worktree>/.task/ and find nothing.

Integration gates that fake at `build_workflow`/`invoke_with_cap_retry` (e.g. orchestrator/tests/test_session_resume_integration_gate.py) never execute `TaskWorkflow.run()`, so `_on_terminal_cleanups` and the warm-lane `git clean` reset are invisible to them. A feature can be fully green at that gate and 0% functional in production if its defect is in teardown or lane preparation. When a gate proves "A's output is B's input", check separately whether anything destroys the artifact between A and B.

dark-factory: the SIMPLE_TASK "simple" label is retired on only ONE of the fall-through paths, so a failing task can loop forever. _run_simple_task in orchestrator/src/orchestrator/workflow.py returns WorkflowOutcome.REQUEUED from several arms, but only the MAX_TURNS arm (~:5178) calls _stamp_simple_saturated(), which is what sets metadata.routing.simple_saturated and makes every subsequent dispatch take the full architect path. The two artifact-shaped arms stamp nothing: ~:5201 "SIMPLE_TASK wrote no plan — falling through" and ~:5218 "SIMPLE_TASK plan has no steps marked done". On those paths simple_saturated stays False, so _should_run_simple_task() (~:5106) returns True again on the very next dispatch and SIMPLE_TASK re-runs against a task it has already demonstrably failed. Combined with the ownership-blind plan unlink in the same fall-through, this produces a self-erasing loop: dispatch -> SIMPLE_TASK fails -> delete the previous architect plan -> architect re-plans (opus/max/$25/180 turns) -> workflow ends -> repeat. THE WORKING MANUAL LEVER is metadata.force_full_path=true, which _should_run_simple_task() hard-checks; setting it skips Lever C entirely so plan.json is no longer unlinked. Measured over two full cycles on reify task 5921, 2026-08-27.

Task 2372 (harden pre-EXECUTE found_on_main recovery against trivial-ancestor fresh-worktree false-DONE) is fully implemented across all 6 plan steps: Layer A (_iteration_entry_is_work per-entry classifier in workflow.py, replacing the naive agent-in-(implementer,debugger) predicate), Layer C (branch-content-diff gate via get_merge_diff_files in _recover_before_execute, replacing the spoofable iteration-log fallback and stamping real metadata.files evidence), and Layer B (TaskArtifacts.clear_iteration_log() wired into _setup_worktree_and_artifacts, wiping iterations.jsonl on a definitive re-dispatch onto a new fork point). All steps committed on task/2372; full workflow+artifacts test suite (852 tests) green. Two follow-ups were deliberately deferred by the architect and NOT filed as new tasks by the implementer (out of scope for a code-writing TDD implementer role): (1) a reconciliation/scheduler-subsystem task for the backward found_on_main citation-mismatch audit sweep (ACTION #4, excluding tasks 2082/2315) plus stamping metadata.done_provenance_invalidated on reopen (ACTION #5); (2) a task_kind='deterministic' restart of orchestrator-dark-factory.service depending on 2372, since workflow.py is orchestrator code that won't hot-reload on merge alone. A human or the orchestrator's post-merge process should file both.

Fact (2026-07-19): dark-factory has TWO distinct auto-file mechanisms that must not be conflated. (1) The offline-lane RED PATH (offline_lane.py) files a fix task on a CONFIRMED HARD FAILURE of an off-hot-path run: build_offline_lane_fix_task_arguments files status=pending, priority='high', metadata.merge_lane='normal' (routes through the standard TDD→PR→merge gate, NOT the B3 red-main fix-forward path), plus an L0 INFO escalation; it only escalates born-at-L2 (escalate_blocker) after config.git.offline_lane_red_advances_before_blocker consecutive same-fingerprint red advances without the fix landing. It is content-agnostic — pytest node-ids dedup exactly like reify test IDs. (2) chronic_flake.py (ChronicFlakeConfig, TaskWorkflow._maybe_file_chronic_flakes) files a medium-priority De-flake task for tests that are FLAKY-BUT-PASSING (retry-once absorbed them); it reads reify's flaky-ledger.jsonl + CHRONIC-FLAKY markers (reify task 5142), is enabled:false, and is a different mechanism for a different signal. The integration-test-lane PRD reuses (1) and leaves (2) out of scope. Key reused helpers: verify._extract_failing_test_ids (verify.py:545), workflow.compute_failing_test_set_fingerprint (workflow.py:467), verify_cmd.serial_pytest (verify_cmd.py:545).

GOTCHA (dark-factory, measured task 4389): a `MagicMock(spec_set=pydantic_spec(OrchestratorConfig))` config makes every nested gate attribute TRUTHY by default — `config.transcript_archive.enabled`, `config.chronic_flake.enabled` and friends all read as True. So the "disabled by default" reasoning you would apply to a real config does NOT hold in these tests: the only thing keeping a mkdir-capable branch from firing is that the branch is not exercised, not that its gate is off.

WHY IT MATTERS. `TaskWorkflow` reads `self.config.project_root` at ten sites in orchestrator/src/orchestrator/workflow.py, and four of them can `mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)` through it: :8488 and :13387 (transcript archive), :9458 (verify archive), :9568 (chronic-flake ledger). Sixteen workflow test factories set `config.project_root` to an absolute `/tmp` sentinel that nothing ever creates, so a leak was structurally possible.

HOW TO CHECK IT CHEAPLY, rather than reasoning about gates: `ls /tmp/<the-sentinel>`. If the directory is ABSENT on a machine that has run the suite thousands of times, no mkdir-capable path has ever been reached under those mocks. That one `ls` is worth more than reading every gate, and it is what settled 4389's classification. The check is monotone — nothing removes the directory — so an absence is strong evidence and a presence is proof of a live leak.

RELATED, and easy to get backwards: `ReviewCheckpoint._run_review` (orchestrator/src/orchestrator/review_checkpoint.py:148-155) raises ValueError on any project_root containing '/tmp/pytest', but that guard is in `_run_review` ONLY — `_build_prompt` has none — and `ReviewCheckpoint` is not on the `TaskWorkflow` path at all (workflow.py:273 says so). Measured: flipping all 16 workflow sentinels to a pytest-shaped path left 327 tests passing. So the 3551 "cannot sandbox review configs" trap does not generalise to workflow configs; check which class you are actually constructing before assuming it applies.

dark-factory test-double drift, the option to check BEFORE writing a fidelity test: when a test double hand-reimplements a production RULE that is a pure function of its arguments (a validation guard, a precedence resolver, a rejection condition), the strongest fix is not a mirror test or a fidelity test — it is to delete the copy and have the double CALL production's own helper, so it mirrors by construction. Task 3890 (amendment pass, reviewer_comprehensive "duplication" finding) did this: `Scheduler.update_task`'s contradictory-pair rejection had been hand-copied into `FakeMetadataBackend` (orchestrator/tests/_workflow_helpers.py) with slightly different prose, and the two tests covering it pinned only today's single cell — so a future narrowing/widening of the production condition would have left the fake silently over-permissive again. Remedy: extract a module-level `_reject_contradictory_metadata_mode(metadata_mode, append)` into orchestrator/src/orchestrator/scheduler.py, called by BOTH `Scheduler.update_task` and the fake. Tests reduce to one cheap identity assert (`_workflow_helpers._reject_contradictory_metadata_mode is orchestrator.scheduler._reject_contradictory_metadata_mode`) plus behavioural cells confirming the double calls it at the right MOMENT (before recording the call / mutating its blob).

WHEN THIS APPLIES vs. the existing task-4096 guidance. 4096's fidelity-test recipe (drive the real object and the double through the same scripted inputs, assert observable calls agree) is for doubles that MUST reimplement — a MagicMock modelling stateful dispatch, where calling production would drag in the very machinery the double exists to avoid. Delegation is available only for the pure-function slice. Prefer delegation where it fits, fall back to a fidelity test where it doesn't, and treat a bare mirror test that restates the double's own body as the weakest of the three. Same spirit as task 3495's hand-copied-config rule (duplicate the drift guard per copy) — but here the better move is having no copy to guard.

Tests importing from `orchestrator.scheduler` in orchestrator/tests/ is already established (`_workflow_helpers.py` imports `TaskAssignment` from it), so the delegating import costs nothing new.

In dark-factory's orchestrator, `TaskArtifacts(worktree)` constructed WITHOUT the second `meta_root` argument silently falls back to the legacy `<worktree>/.task` root (artifacts.py:260), which no production code has written since the meta-root migration (commit 5067b2d230, 2026-07-06). Since that migration, artifacts live in the `<worktree_base>/.task-meta/<worktree_name>` SIBLING, derived by `TaskArtifacts.meta_root_for(worktree.parent, worktree.name)` — the single owner of that path shape. A bare `TaskArtifacts(path)` in non-test code is therefore a reader/writer path-drift bug, not a valid default: it reads a location nothing populates and returns None forever while looking like a live signal. When auditing this, note that `TaskWorkflow.artifacts` is assigned at exactly one site (workflow.py:2397) with a real meta_root, so tracing any artifact write means tracing that one assignment rather than the individual `lock_plan`/`write_*` call sites.

Gotcha for any change that makes TaskWorkflow._try_narrow_plan (or another merge-path step) reconcile scope: orchestrator/tests/test_workflow.py::_make_workflow wires a bare MagicMock() scheduler with only get_task stubbed (AsyncMock -> None). So an awaited scheduler.handle_blast_radius_expansion / update_task raises TypeError in TestSubmitToMergeQueuePlanTightening's accepted-narrow tests. Root-level fixture files like a.py derive module 'a.py', not the assignment's 'mod_a', so the reconcile is never a no-op there. Opt each test in via _workflow_helpers.wire_metadata_backend rather than changing _make_workflow. Wiring it globally would turn the deliberate get_task->None fail-safe into a live _check_scope_invariant read for ~80 unrelated tests.

content: dark-factory test gotcha (task 6052): when a test drives the REAL TaskWorkflow.run() on a hand-built workflow (e.g. test_workflow_ready_to_merge.py::_make, which pre-sets wf.artifacts to a legacy TaskArtifacts(worktree)), run()'s setup replaces wf.artifacts with a meta_root-relocated instance. An _invoke stub that writes an exit artifact (ready_to_merge.json, already_done.json) through the fixture's pre-run artifacts object is then invisible to the dispatch chain: the architect logs 'produced no plan.json' instead of reaching the handler. Inside the stub, write through f.wf.artifacts, read at call time. Tests that call _plan()/_run_simple_task() directly are unaffected.

candidates.content: The ONE Rust-source mini-lexer in reify (comment-, char-literal- and raw-string-aware) is `strip_comments_and_collect_literals` in crates/reify-builtins/tests/common/seed_name_scan.rs:152, with `char_literal_end`:113, `blank`:97 (blanks to spaces but PRESERVES newlines, so byte offsets and line numbers both survive) and `line_of`:1134. Its raw-string branch (:185-222) correctly handles `r` + N`#` + `"` with a `prev_is_ident` guard against raw identifiers (`r#type`) and an N-hash close — but it BLANKS raw strings rather than collecting them. It is `pub(crate)` in a `#[path]`-included test module of reify-builtins, so it is not importable from another crate. crates/reify-audit/src/pdoccover.rs is line-oriented and raw-string-UNAWARE (`blank_literals`:489 handles only `"…"` and `'x'`); pdiag.rs explicitly tolerates literal confusion. scripts/check-nan-safe-ordering.sh has the same lexer in awk. The workspace has NO `syn`/`proc-macro2` dependency, so a Rust-text scanner must be hand-rolled from one of these.

Writing a grep-based Rust drift guard (scripts/check-*.sh) in reify: reduce each line to production code with a SINGLE left-to-right awk lexer, and count the braces that drive `depth` from that LEXED view, never from the raw line. A two-regex chain fails in EITHER order — strip comments first and a `//` inside a STRING truncates the code after it (11 lines of the ~562-file crates/*+gui/src-tauri scan set change brace balance under that, e.g. crates/reify-audit/src/ptodo.rs:90 `if line.trim_start().starts_with("//") {`); blank strings first and a quote inside a COMMENT mis-blanks the code after it. Counting raw-line braces lets a brace living only in a comment/string/char-literal/raw-string move `depth` and silently mis-drive the `#[cfg(test)] mod` skipper: a stray `{` over-extends it until the scan goes blind (under-flag), a stray `}` releases it early until any positive/pin assertion goes vacuous (false green). Both are live shapes, not hypotheticals — 4 unbalanced brace char literals sit in that scan set (crates/reify-kernel-occt/src/lib.rs:4930,4948,9167; crates/reify-test-support/src/orphan_audit.rs:778) and 277 of its files carry raw strings. Also: make the cfg(test) skipper require the opening line to declare a `mod` — check-nan-safe-ordering.sh:106-120 does NOT, so a bare `#[cfg(test)] use …;` (gui/src-tauri/src/engine.rs:21,:102,:104 each have one) leaves it armed until an unrelated production item. Worked reference implementation: scripts/check-compute-trampoline-registration.sh's `_AWK_PRODUCTION_PROLOGUE` / `_strip_line` (task 5076), POSIX-awk only (substr/index/length/match, no gensub) so the gate is not silently gawk-only; keep the inline `:allow` escape check and the violation printf on RAW $0, since the escape lives in a `//` comment the lexer drops and violation output must show the source as written.

reify: a new grep-style Rust-source gate should lex through scripts/lib_rust_production_view.sh's RUST_LEXER_AWK export (_strip_line/_lexer_open_state/_lexer_reset). The repo norm is "no second Rust lexer" (lib header, verify-pipeline-infra-tests.txt, tooling-front-end.md). A Python tool can spawn it via `bash -c 'source "$1" && prog="$RUST_LEXER_AWK\n$2" && shift 2 && awk "$prog" "$@"'`; with gawk this lexed all 683 workspace .rs files in ~6 s with zero files unbalanced at EOF (2026-10-12, task 8673). The lib is itself a verify-pipeline path, so editing even its header comment forces the full --scope all gate.

Reify's grep-based source gates (scripts/check-nan-safe-ordering.sh, scripts/check-compute-trampoline-registration.sh) share a hand-ported awk Rust lexer, `_AWK_PRODUCTION_PROLOGUE`, that reduces each line to production code (comments dropped; string/char/raw-string contents blanked, delimiters kept; `/* */`, `"…"` and `r#"…"#` state carried across lines; char literal distinguished from lifetime) and — critically — counts the braces driving `depth` from that LEXED view, never from the raw line. A two-regex strip-comments/blank-strings chain is wrong in EITHER order and was replaced, not reordered. When writing a new gate of this shape, port the prologue from check-nan-safe-ordering.sh's copy on main verbatim (change only the escape token and the matched patterns) rather than re-deriving it.

Reify convention: a shell command embedded in a Rust doc/`//` comment must stay on ONE line — never wrap it with a trailing `\` continuation. These doc invocations exist to be hand-copied (for an `#[ignore]`d test the typed command is its entire operational access route), and a verbatim two-line paste joins the second line's `//` comment prefix into the command, e.g. `cargo test ... --test harness_fea_solver_e2e // -- kinematic_sweep_closed_chain::`, where `//` becomes a stray positional test filter. Current libtest ORs multiple filters so it may still appear to work, which makes the breakage silent. There is no rustfmt gate in this repo and over-long comment lines are already common, so length is not a reason to wrap. Observed and fixed at crates/reify-eval/src/engine_hash_algo.rs:322 (task 5687); the other nine sites in that sweep were already single-line.

reify merge-gate tripwires that repeatedly caught stranded branches during the 2026-08-27/28 recovery, worth checking on any branch before submitting it. (1) HARNESS-LAYOUT RATCHET: a new standalone `crates/*/tests/*.rs` in one of the 5 consolidatable crates (reify-cli, reify-syntax, reify-kernel-occt, reify-eval, reify-compiler) must be `#[path]`-declared from a `harness_<subsystem>` root; adding a `tests/infra/harness-layout-baseline.manifest` row is SUPERSEDED as a remedy (Leo 2026-07-22, esc-5056-11 — the manifest is a shrinking ratchet). reify-solver-elastic and reify-eval-fea-tests are deliberately OUT of that contract. (2) `_RUST_COUPLED_RI_FIXTURES` at `scripts/verify.sh:1080`: a new `tests/prd-gate/fixtures/*.ri` that a compiled Rust test READS must be listed there, or `tests/infra/test_verify_scope.sh`'s PG-DRIFT scenario reds. (3) `clippy::neg_cmp_op_on_partial_ord`: `!(x > 0.0)` guards fail the gate's `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`; the in-tree idiom is to bind a bool first (`crates/reify-eval/src/engine_build.rs:12718` names the lint in its comment). (4) PTODO fingerprint ratchet: a literal `TODO(`/`FIXME:`/`HACK(` in a comment with no `#NNNN` cite and no `// ptodo:allow` escape is a NEW untracked fingerprint and reds the severity-blind subset check — note `TODO)` does NOT match the regex, only `TODO(` or `TODO:`. (5) `scripts/release-sensitive-crates.txt`: the FIRST `#[cfg(not(debug_assertions))]` in a crate makes it release-sensitive by grep derivation, and if it is not DECLARED there, `tests/infra/test_release_scoped_scope.sh` Test 3 reds AND the release pass stays `-p`-scoped so the new release-only test never runs anywhere.

PG-DRIFT (tests/infra/test_verify_scope.sh) derives its "read by a compiled test target" set from a deliberately COMMENT-INCLUSIVE grep: `git grep -o -E 'tests/prd-gate/fixtures/[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+\.ri' -- '*.rs'`. So a plain `//` comment that spells a fixture as one joined path makes the checker believe a Rust target reads it, even when nothing does.

This has now bitten twice with the SAME ironic shape, where the tripping comment was a sentence asserting the fixture is NOT rust-coupled:
- reify task 5540 (commit e34e0d9e01) — the comment's whole point was that the fixture has no automated consumer.
- reify task 6249 (commit 238c380ea4) — a SCOPE FENCE comment in crates/reify-compiler/tests/math_transcendental_signatures.rs explaining that dcr_langsurface_crossdim_silent.ri is GUI-only, registered in _GUI_COUPLED_RI_FIXTURES and deliberately not in _RUST_COUPLED_RI_FIXTURES pending task #5809's leaf kappa.

In BOTH cases adding the _RUST_COUPLED_RI_FIXTURES row would have been FALSE, and would have falsified the very sentence one paragraph below it. THE CORRECT FIX is to reword so the path cannot be reassembled: spell the fixture NAME first and its DIRECTORY second, with an inline note saying the split is deliberate so a later editor does not "tidy" it back.

THE DISCRIMINATOR, always: does a compiled target actually READ the fixture (read_to_string, include_str!, a path built with concat!/env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"))? Task 6093 was the genuine case — crates/reify-eval-fea-tests/tests/r3b_modal_selector_displacement.rs:674 really does read its fixture — and there the row IS the right fix, plus a bump of the adjacent member-count NOTE. Same assertion, opposite correct remedies; measure, never pattern-match.

Reify corpus sweeps over Rust test-fixture strings (embedded `.ri` snippets in `crates/**/*.rs`) must use a STRING-LITERAL-AWARE comment stripper, not a naive trailing-comment stripper that truncates at the first `//` not preceded by `:`. The naive form also truncates at a `//` INSIDE a Rust string literal, so a fixture whose embedded snippet opens with a doc/line comment (e.g. `let src = "/// A bracket.\nstructure Bracket { param w: Length = 1 }";`) has its whole payload discarded before the regex runs — a silent FALSE-NEGATIVE / under-counting class. Found in task 5756's category-C sweep: this under-counted by 3 sites (57 raw hits → 60 corrected), all in `crates/reify-syntax/src/ts_parser.rs`'s doc-comment-extraction tests (lines :6466, :6477, :6499). The fix is monotone (removes no hits) and does not affect `.ri`-tree sweeps, where `//` inside a string literal is essentially absent. Fix: walk chars tracking `"`-toggled in-string state with `\` escaping, treat `//` as a comment start only outside a string, keep the `:` guard. Reference implementation and the buggy original side-by-side: `/tmp/5756-scratch/cat_c_scan4.py`; documented normatively in `docs/notes/dimensioned-construction-blast-radius-2026-07-29.md` §2.2.1/§2.2.2(3).

reify gotcha for source-scanning test gates: a per-line-reset Rust lexer (as in crates/reify-eval/tests/version_id_discipline_gate.rs) cannot reliably mask a big `#[cfg(test)] mod tests`. Files like crates/reify-kernel-occt/src/lib.rs hold `'}'` char literals and dozens of backslash-continued multi-line strings inside that module, so brace counting desyncs and test lines leak into the "production" scan. Use a whole-file stateful lexer modelled on crates/reify-builtins/tests/common/seed_name_scan.rs (strip_comments_and_collect_literals, char_literal_end, attr_gates_test_code, mask_cfg_test_blocks), which is test-private there, so it is a model, not a call.

Reify rejects comment-content meta-tests: do NOT add regex/substring tests that scan .ri or .rs comment prose to guard documentation claims. Commit 593aaeb4f0 deleted crates/reify-compiler/tests/harness_stdlib_hygiene.rs and its stdlib_citation_hygiene module as a blocking review finding named `comment-content-meta-test`, and explicitly rejected "harden the matcher" as the remedy — the guard had certified a false invariant over a corpus holding 11 stale cites because line-wrapped and prose-form citations were structurally unmatchable. The sanctioned home for comment-content invariants is crates/reify-audit (e.g. the PTODO detector, ptodo.rs, which does scan .ri comments), not a per-crate meta-test. Related gotcha: a malformed .ri comment is NOT observable as a test diagnostic — crates/reify-compiler/src/stdlib_loader.rs:499-514 hard-asserts no Error diagnostics, so it panics the loader and fails every test in the binary instead.

G-allow marker syntax: the two enforcement paths DISAGREE on triple-slash. reify-audit's Rust detector parses the marker in extract_g_allow (crates/reify-audit/src/jcodemunch_client.rs:739-749) as strip_prefix("//") then trim_start then strip_prefix("G-allow:"), so a doc-comment marker leaves a stray leading slash, returns None, and the symbol is SILENTLY still flagged as a producer-orphan. scripts/audit-orphan-producers.sh uses an unanchored re.search for //\s*G-allow:, which happily matches inside a triple-slash line. So a marker that looks correct and passes the script can still fail the Rust detector. Always write the marker as a plain two-slash line comment. The positional rules also differ: the Rust side walks upward over the contiguous attribute/comment block and stops at the first blank or code line (extract_suppression, same file 687-728), while the script inspects only the single line immediately above the declaration. No test pins the triple-slash case in either path. Confirmed 2026-08-31 while planning task #6205, whose commit b14cc32985 exists solely to convert four such markers back to plain comments.

Documented-grammar-vs-implementation gap: both p1_producer_orphan.rs:70 and jcodemunch_client.rs:738's own doc comments describe the grammar as regex G_ALLOW_RE = //\s*G-allow:\s*(.+), which — unlike the actual strip_prefix-based Rust implementation — would match a triple-slash line literally if taken as a literal regex search; the documented grammar and the real Rust detector diverge on this exact edge case. Correct precedent showing the fix: crates/reify-kernel-gmsh/src/ffi.rs:268 (gmshModelMeshSetSize) — its /// doc block ends, then a separate plain // comment (including the G-allow line) sits directly above pub fn.

Reify norm: do NOT add a test that greps `.ri`/source COMMENT PROSE for a formatting pattern (a "comment-content meta-test") — e.g. a guard failing on stale `foo.rs:472` line citations. Task 5856 added exactly this (tests/harness_stdlib_hygiene/stdlib_citation_hygiene.rs, a shrinking `PENDING_SWEEP` ratchet guarding against stale hard line cites in stdlib/*.ri) and review rejected it as a blocking finding (`comment-content-meta-test`): a substring matcher requiring a digit right after `.rs:`/`.ri:` on the same line is structurally blind to line-WRAPPED cites (e.g. `…(structural_physical.ri:` + `67-68 documents…` split across two comment lines) and to prose spellings (` <file> lines NNN-NNN` / ` (line N)` / `foo.rs line 472`) — so it reported green while ~11 stale cites (drift 4-35 lines) sat unswept, actively certifying a false invariant while its own module doc claimed full coverage. Hardening the matcher is explicitly NOT the sanctioned remedy: each new spelling (`#L472`, `foo.rs @ 472`, a three-line wrapped cite) evades the next matcher while adding prose-pinning surface. The remedy is to sweep the stale cites once (cite by symbol name / stable anchor, keep the crate-relative path, drop the `:<line>`) and rely on human review — not a mechanical grep gate. A general reify-audit detector for this class of drift stays deferred pending a scope decision across `docs/` and `crates/*/src`.

reify — FIFTH variant of the self-matching-grep hazard class (siblings: a56545ed manifest-vs-meta-test, 07b67efe same-file static source scan, bc2826b0 parent-greps-child-script, a97e85e2 sub-shell assert-description self-match). Here the self-match is in a MEASUREMENT quoted inside a comment: crates/reify-audit/src/ptodo.rs's `prd_relative_cite_negatives` documented "family 1 has ZERO live four-digit exposure" and quoted `git grep -nEi '(§[0-9.]*|\b(OQ|DD|Q|T))#[0-9]{3,}' -- '*.rs'` as the proof — but the five synthetic controls sitting directly beneath that comment (`§7#4553`, `T#4553`, `Q#4553`, `OQ#4553`, `DD#4553`) ARE tracked source, so re-running it in Aug 2026 returned 5, not 0. RULE: any `git grep` corpus measurement about PTODO/marker/cite grammar must add `':!crates/reify-audit/*'` — that crate is the detector's own §6.8 ALLOWLIST_PREFIXES entry, so its fixtures and test string-literals are invisible to the live sweep but fully visible to a bare `git grep`, i.e. the grep and the detector disagree by construction. Same trap applies to `crates/reify-test-support/src/ignore_hygiene.rs` and `crates/reify-test-support/tests/ignore_reason_hygiene.rs`, the other two allowlist entries. Corollary: prefer the file path WITHOUT a line number in provenance comments (`// crates/reify-eval/src/detectors.rs`, not `:671`) — nothing verifies a line number and no test enforces it; task #6103's own diff shipped a `:671` citation whose quoted text that same branch had already rewritten.

Reify's grep-based lint gates (scripts/check-*.sh) skip `#[cfg(test)] mod` bodies with an awk brace-depth counter, and the copied-around version counts braces from the RAW `$0` before any comment/string stripping — so a brace inside a comment, string, char literal or raw string silently moves `depth` and mis-drives the skipper (a stray `{` over-extends it into an UNDER-flag, a stray `}` releases it early into a FALSE RED). Measured over reify's 562-file production scan set: 22 files drifted at EOF, 14 with the skipper stuck ON. The fix is in scripts/check-compute-trampoline-registration.sh (`_strip_line`, task 5076): a single POSIX-awk left-to-right lexer that carries nested `/* */`, `"…"` and `r#"…"#` state across lines and tells a char literal from a lifetime, with the brace counts taken from its output. Do NOT "fix" it by reordering a strip-comments/blank-strings regex chain — both orderings are wrong in one direction (comment-first truncates a `//` that lives inside a string; 11 lines of reify's scan set change brace balance under it). Validate any such lexer by dumping every scan-set file's EOF depth/in_str/in_raw/in_block: all must be zero.

reify's PTODO gate has a structural blind spot, and it is the MARKER VOCABULARY, not the citation grammar (established 2026-08-07). crates/reify-audit/src/ptodo.rs:762 classifies a line ONLY inside the find_comment_marker(line).is_some() branch, so a line with no TODO/FIXME/HACK token, no todo!()/unimplemented!(), no #[ignore] and no "// G-allow:" is never examined at all — even when it carries a perfectly canonical #NNNN cite pointing at a terminal task. PROOF: crates/reify-eval/src/engine_build.rs:12891 reads `#[allow(dead_code)] // production wiring pending task #4744` and task 4744 is terminal; written as `// TODO(#4744):` it would fire `orphaned` at High and hard-fail the merge gate, but as an allow-attribute rationale it is silent. Likewise crates/reify-core/src/diagnostics.rs:3991 and :4046 cite #2947, a CANCELLED task — a dead-task cite, equally invisible. So fixing the Greek-letter/alias convention alone would NOT have caught either. Measured surface over tracked crates/**/*.rs + gui/src-tauri/src/**/*.rs (1741 files): 300 `#[allow(dead_code)]` occurrences vs 249 `#[ignore]`; 69 of the 300 carry a trailing rationale comment, and only 4 of those 69 cite a #NNNN at all. Separately: a full detector run (reify-audit --pattern PTODO, exit 0) returned zero untracked, zero orphaned, zero bare-ignore and zero malformed-cite findings, so promoting malformed-cite from Medium to High (one line at crates/reify-audit/src/ptodo.rs:684) has a blast radius of ZERO — though it is largely redundant because ptodo-baseline.txt is 0 bytes and the baseline generator fingerprints every source-marker finding regardless of severity, so a new malformed-cite already fails the merge ratchet at Medium.

Any Rust test file under crates/**/*.rs is itself scanned by the corpus-cleanliness guard crates/reify-cli/tests/harness_cli/corpus_no_bare_scalar.rs (its only exclusions are the file corpus_no_bare_scalar.rs by basename, crates/reify-syntax/tests/, crates/reify-ast/tests/, and crates/reify-spec-conformance/fixtures/). So writing a literal bare `: Scalar` / `-> Scalar` example on a NON-comment line in a new test — e.g. as a unit-test input string — turns that guard RED for real. Splice the keyword in at runtime instead (e.g. `parts.join("Scalar")`); doc/`//` comment lines are safe because the predicate skips pure-comment lines and strips trailing `//` comments.

EXTENDS the existing entry "Any grep/architecture test over gui/src-tauri/src/debug_server.rs MUST strip comments before matching" (Mem0 230358ce): stripping comments is NECESSARY BUT NOT SUFFICIENT — string LITERAL contents are a second false-GREEN path, and it was found live in task #5100's INV-GUI-2 gate (gui/src-tauri/src/tests/debug_write_tool_routing_tests.rs) after that gate had already landed its comment-stripping step. Reproduced, not reasoned about: a handler body of `run_on_engine(...)` plus `tracing::debug!("bypassing write_on_engine_and_refresh_baseline for speed")` — a real bypass — satisfied the routing check and the gate went green; symmetrically a compliant handler mentioning `.emit(` in a log string false-RED. A tracing span name, an error message, or a `json!` field naming the seam while the call is being removed is an ordinary agent edit, not a contrived one.

THE FIX IS TWO VIEWS OF THE SAME BYTES, NOT ONE WIDER STRIP, and that is the non-obvious part. A gate of this shape usually has two consumer families needing OPPOSITE things: the tool/name ENUMERATIONS read identifiers OUT of string literals (`"reify_export" =>` dispatch arms, `name: "reify_export"` registry rows), while the BEHAVIOURAL checks (does this fn call the seam / does it emit) must not see literal contents at all. One stripped view cannot serve both. Blanking must be equal-LENGTH (replace each stripped char with spaces, keep newlines) so a byte offset means the same thing in either view and fn-body slices found in one line up in the other.

This matches the design reify's awk-based gates already use (Mem0 1b0e5c7f: `_AWK_PRODUCTION_PROLOGUE` blanks string/char/raw-string CONTENTS while keeping delimiters), and crates/reify-builtins/tests/common/seed_name_scan.rs already handled literals correctly — so the hole existed only because each gate hand-rolls its own scanner. Before writing a new Rust source-scanning gate, port an existing literal-aware scanner rather than re-deriving one; the shared-primitive extraction is filed as a follow-up from #5100 (ticket tkt_0RTQ6NPHP5KR44Q1ZSJ64B5PRC).

Reify shell COUNTING guards over a script's own source (e.g. tests/infra/test_infra_git_env_isolation.sh arm F, which asserts every member-spawn / `git -C` site in tests/infra/run_all.sh is wrapped in reify_git_env_scrub): normalize in this ORDER — fold line continuations FIRST (`sed -e :a -e '/\\$/N; s/\\\n//; ta'`), THEN drop comment lines (`grep -v '^[[:blank:]]*#'`). Folding first is needed so a wrapper sitting on the preceding physical line counts as one logical statement; stripping comments is needed because run_all.sh is heavily commented and a comment that quotes the invocation shape verbatim otherwise scores as a real, unscrubbed call site. MEASURED and self-inflicted on task #7106: the explanatory block comment added alongside the fix contained `git -C "$FIX"`, which took the guard from 7-of-7 to 7-of-8 and would have redded the merge gate on pure prose. Prefer the comment strip over anchoring the pattern to a leading `bash `/`reify_git_env_scrub` token — narrowing the pattern also stops it matching a legitimately reshaped call site (e.g. inside a command substitution), turning a real coverage hole into a silent pass, and a `>= N` floor only catches sites DISAPPEARING, never ones the pattern was narrowed past. Same family as memories 07b67efe (self-matching static source-scan guard) and fb0ff32e (header comment over-counting a manifest grep).

Reify gotcha: crates/reify-cli/tests/fixtures/*.ri files are real DSL source parsed by `reify check`, not inert text — so even a comment-only edit to a fixture header is a functional change that can break parsing. There is no prose-assertion test guarding them and none should be added; the existing OCCT-gated consumers are the real gate. For dfm_with_repr_within.ri that is `cargo test -p reify-cli --test harness_cli -- check_dfm_plus_repr_within_combined_arm check_both_kinds_yield_real_verdicts_under_occt` (expect PASS 2), plus `cargo test -p reify-eval --test representation_within_assertion` (expect PASS 8) for the paired .rs doc block. Run both after any fixture comment edit.

Splitting a reify test harness (tests/harness_X.rs + its #[path] module dir) trips two gates that a plain `cargo test --no-run` does NOT surface. (1) clippy::doc_lazy_continuation, denied via -D warnings: a `//!` paragraph that runs straight on from a bullet list with no blank `//!` separator is read as a lazy continuation and fails the build — always finish with `cargo clippy -p <crate> --test <new_root> --test <old_root>`, not just a build. (2) The reify-audit PTODO fingerprint ratchet (tests/infra/test_reify_audit_ptodo.sh) is severity-blind and matches PHANTOM_PHRASES like "tracked separately" / "tracked by its own follow-up" in ANY tracked file including shell comments — so a new-root or guard comment claiming work is tracked elsewhere reds the gate unless backed by a live `#NNNN`. submit_task returns a ticket id, not a task number, so at authoring time there is usually no cite available: drop the claim rather than invent one.

content: reify gotcha: tests/infra/adoption_ratchet.py (adoption-ratchet.manifest, #8678) treats only lines whose first non-blank char is '#' as comments. That rule is shell-only, so it is unfit for Rust-source ratchets: it counts `//`/`///` prose as code and drops `#[cfg(..)] foo!(..)` lines as comments. A Rust grep-style gate should read source through scripts/lib_rust_production_view.sh's RUST_PRODUCTION_VIEW_AWK (one awk process per file, escape matched via `comment_tail`), as check-nan-safe-ordering.sh and task 7556's tests/infra/reify_lsp_stderr_scan.py do.

Measured 2026-10-14 at solar-challenge main 9d7b67e: the board scenario scenarios/bristol-phase1-flex.yaml earns £0 capacity-at-events grid-services income. Probe: first 3 battery homes, simulate_fleet over 2024-01-08..21, compute_grid_services_at_events with the scenario's own events config, at battery SOH 1.0 and 0.8 → annual_income_gbp 0.000, per_window_avail_kw (0.0,). Work (src/solar_challenge/gridservices.py):
- compute_fleet_spare_capacity_kw(fleet_results, windows) -> tuple[float, ...] (one avail_kW per window).
- Per home, per window w=[t0,t1] with event_hours=t1-t0:
  P_spare = max_discharge_kw - max_{t in w} battery_discharge(t)   # inverter headroom, firm

Process lesson from the 2026-10-16 solar_challenge grid-services firmness investigation: a /prd G6 measurement on a small slice can mislead. The S9 PRD's §2.2 probe (first 3 battery homes of the board scenario, two January weeks) reported £0 event income and the PRD framed the whole stream around it; the full 100-home, full-year measurement found three homes that never touch the floor (£3/yr) and, more importantly, that 64% of event days never reach the floor in-window, which changed the modelling conclusion (an artefact of the firmness rule, not an absence of capacity). Norm: when a PRD's premise rests on a measured figure for "the board scenario", measure the actual board fleet over the actual window population (all homes, the whole season), and report the distribution (fraction of days/homes affected), not only the aggregate. A 100-home full-year run costs ~11 min here, which is cheap against a mis-framed stream.

PRD gap in grid-services-pricing-model §5.8 (the surface ledger): gridservices.compute_fleet_spare_capacity_kw is on solar_challenge's frozen surface (FROZEN_SURFACE in tests/unit/test_public_api_surface.py) with the form (fleet_results, windows) -> tuple[float, ...]. It cannot compute either delivery baseline without receiving the baseline. Task 837 therefore expects it to gain a last parameter, delivery_baseline: str = "operational". G6 premise error found in grid-services-pricing-model PRD §9 P8 (displaced self-use), corrected on task 837. P8 extends the P6 fixture, in which home A sits at its SOC floor for one minute on day 1, so A's day-1 availability is 0 and A displaces nothing that day. The fleet's daily displaced energies are therefore (1.5, 3.0) kWh, a mean of 2.25 kWh per event, not the PRD's "1.5 kWh per home per event × 2 homes" (3.0). Displaced self-use per home-day is min(avail × h, post-window discharge energy), so it is zero whenever that day's availability is zero.

candidates.content: Discovery (2026-10-16, solar_challenge board fleet, tou_optimized dispatch with Economy-7 grid charging to 90%): almost no battery capacity escapes time arbitrage. The ~0.9 kWh above floor left at 19:00 on winter event days is used for the home's own evening load before the 00:30 recharge (0.81 kWh discharged 19:00–00:29; 88% of days end at the floor). So an event discharge at 16:00–19:00 displaces ~0.8 kWh of 25p peak import per home per event (~£0.20) against a net central-band grid-services payment of ~£0.25 per home per event. Under the operational (DFS) baseline the CBS books ~£300/yr while householders lose ~£240/yr of import savings (community net ~£50); under the NGED capacity baseline gross ~£920, community net ~£680. The current gridservices.py books gross income to the CBS and ignores the displaced import, which lands on the householder bill. This incidence question dominates the firmness question and motivates the successor counterfactual-event-simulation PRD. Also: the consulting £30/home/yr grid-services figure cannot be reached under any rule, because a 5 kWh battery sustains 1.33 kW over a 3 h event, not the 2.5 kW nameplate the flat rate prices; even full reservation reaches 44% of the flat figure.

Solar Challenge grid-services flexibility value (researched 2026-06-16, for a ~100-home / ~0.3 MW firm / ~1 MWh / ~0.6 MWh-usable fleet) is MODEST and a MINORITY of total value: net of a ~25% aggregator share, roughly £4 (low) / £38 (central) / £120 (high) per home/yr, with a ~£0 FLOOR if the fleet is not in an active NGED Constraint Management Zone (CMZ). The real economic anchor is wholesale/TOU arbitrage + PV self-consumption (~£250–400/home/yr); grid services add only ~10–25% on top. Best realistic stack = NESO DFS + NGED DNO local flex (location-dependent), accessed via ONE partnered aggregator — self-registering as a VLP is NOT viable at 100 homes (below ~1 MW practical floors), and standalone Balancing Mechanism, Capacity Market and frequency-response are not worth chasing at this scale. P483 (Ofgem-approved 22 Aug 2025, live 27 Nov 2025) is the DECISIVE enabler: it lets an aggregator trade domestic flexibility via a separate ASSET METER without full MHHS — so the pilot must install asset meters and pick a P483-capable aggregator. This refines the earlier rougher "flexibility ≈ several × surplus" note: the multiple comes mostly from arbitrage/self-consumption optimisation, not pure grid services.

Facts about the solar_challenge simulator learned 2026-10-16 while measuring grid-services firmness: (1) SimulationResults.self_consumption already INCLUDES battery discharge (flow.py ~294 and ~412), so "demand − self_consumption" is grid import, not own-load-serving discharge; own-load discharge = total discharge minus any discharge coincident with export (zero on the board fleet). (2) On the board fleet there is zero battery charging of any kind between 19:00 and 00:29, and the first grid-charge minute is exactly 00:30 (Economy-7 off_peak_start) on every home-day. (3) The SOC balance soc(t1) − soc(t2) = discharge/0.975 − charge×0.975 closes to 3e-14 over 1-minute series. (4) A 100-home full-year simulate_fleet run takes ~11 min via `uv run --locked --extra dev python` with a warm .cache/weather; the repo's venv/bin/python is a free-threaded 3.14 interpreter without the package installed and its ProcessPool crashes, so use uv. (5) Two-period (Jan–Feb + Nov–Dec) and full-year runs give identical in-window figures to all printed digits.

Solar Challenge finance/physics facts verified 2026-06-17 (load-bearing for the flex work): (1) home.py:322 prices grid import PER-TIMESTEP at the TOU rate (`r.grid_import * rate`), so cheap-rate grid charging genuinely lowers total_import_cost_gbp — the arbitrage time-shift reaches the householder bill correctly today. (2) project_multi_year computes fleet_revenue = Σ(self_consumption_saving + seg_export) ONLY (finance.py:864-877) — it does NOT include the arbitrage import-cost reduction; the time-shift only leaks into project surplus via self_consumption counting grid-charged battery DISCHARGE as self-consumption (flow.py:276) valued at full retail, which OVERSTATES it (the 'self-consumption-inflation'; the W2 cost-recovery CR2 task now owns a cbs_grid_charge_cost correction that reassigns the off-peak grid-charge cost from householder import to a CBS outgoing). (3) Fleet-distribution homes are hardcoded tariff_config=None (config.py:1579 in generate_homes_from_distribution), so the canonical fleet sees ZERO arbitrage value until a fleet-wide TOU tariff is threaded (W1 task β). (4) max_discharge_kw is a real BatteryConfig field (config.py:264, default 2.5 kW), exposed on home.battery_config like capacity_kwh — used as the per-kW grid-services multiplier.

UK flexibility product firmness semantics, web-sourced 2026-10-16 (for solar_challenge grid-services modelling): NESO Demand Flexibility Service declares volume per event per settlement period, pays utilisation only (£/MWh), scales pay by delivery factor K (0 below 25% delivery, linear to 1.2 at ≥120%), deregisters only for persistent K<50% (5 consecutive or 10 in 3 months); minimum cut to 0.1 MW in 2026 so a 100-home × 2.5 kW fleet (0.25 MW) qualifies via an aggregator; baseline is an operational baseline (only the increment over it counts). NGED Flexible Power (Bristol's DNO): annual tenders plus day-ahead trading since 31 Mar 2026 (gate 12:00 D-1), availability (£/MW/h) + utilisation (£/MWh), under-delivery clawback with 5% grace and ×2–3 multiplier, and for domestic stored-energy assets the calculated baseline = asset capacity (pre-existing discharge is NOT netted); Bristol postcodes BS1/BS4/BS5/BS14 are in active CMZ_T8A_SWE_0039. Capacity Market DSR: per delivery year, 79% de-rating, likely needs pooling above ~1 MW. Aggregators (Axle): per-event, ~£1/kWh exported, owners report £120–240/home/yr. No product requires season-long firmness; the closest analogues are per-window declared capacity with proportional penalty (NGED) or per-event performance factor (DFS). Unconfirmed: DFS Schedule 3 baseline text, NGED zone ceiling prices and window shapes, CM thresholds.

candidates.content: solar_challenge_platform test convention (task 1093, branch task/1093; holds once merged): read what an engine hands its driver's connect() with tests/_driver_connect.py::driver_connect_args(target, connect). It listens on SQLAlchemy's do_connect, refuses the connection before the driver runs (no socket, no DNS), fails the test if connect() never connects, and removes its listener on return. Pass target=sqlalchemy.Engine (the class) to see an engine that code under test builds internally, e.g. driver_connect_args(Engine, lambda: command.upgrade(alembic_config(pg_url), "head")) for migrations/env.py; pass an engine and its .connect for an instance. For a Timescale-lane database whose default TimeZone is not UTC, use tests/_scratch_database.py::scratch_database(server_url, *, time_zone): it takes timescale_url()'s URL, so it is not enrolled by tests/validation/test_reaper.py, and drops the database however the block exits. The PostgreSQL session-zone pin is db/dialects.py::PG_SESSION_TIMEZONE_OPTION ("-c timezone=UTC"), read by db/session.py and migrations/env.py; db/session.py's DB_SESSION_TIMEZONE no longer exists.

solar_challenge_platform testing technique (verified 2026-10-14 by the task 1036 architect, SQLAlchemy 2.0.51, main 295b6cb). Use it to reach an unsupported-dialect refusal, such as db/dialects.py::dialect_insert's ValueError, through a public seam that runs real queries first. A stand-in session cannot do that.
1. Subclass sqlalchemy.dialects.sqlite.pysqlite.SQLiteDialect_pysqlite. In the subclass's own body, set a fictional `name` such as 'elsewhere' and `supports_statement_cache = True`; without the latter SQLAlchemy warns with code cprf.
2. Register it with sqlalchemy.dialects.registry.register(name, __name__, cls.__name__).
3. Build it with create_engine(f'{name}://', poolclass=StaticPool), then Base.metadata.create_all. The full schema builds: the property after_create listener just skips its SQLite trigger, and RLS does nothing.
Never register a real dialect name such as 'mysql': the registry is process-wide and would shadow SQLAlchemy's own dialect.

solar_challenge_platform gotcha (measured 2026-10-07, SQLAlchemy 2.0.51 + psycopg 3): a refused Postgres connection surfaces as sqlalchemy.exc.OperationalError with connection_invalidated=False and statement=None. The psycopg dialect's is_disconnect returns False when there is no connection yet. So a retry predicate keyed only on connection_invalidated misses a DB restart; it must also check the OperationalError/InterfaceError type. On SQLite, a missing table ("no such table: ...") is ALSO an OperationalError, so a type-based transient check retries schema errors there.

solar_challenge_platform test convention (task 453, branch task/453; holds once merged): two shared non-test modules serve SQL store and migration tests. tests/_sql_executions.py::executions_naming(engine, table) records every execution naming a table, each an Execution(statement, executemany); attach it before the call to pin "one statement, not executemany". tests/_schema_state.py::table_shape(engine, table) returns a TableShape (column nullability, PK columns in order, index names, foreign keys); compare the migrated SQLite head with make_in_memory_engine()'s ORM schema. Import these rather than writing private copies: tests/test_private_names.py forbids importing another test module's private helpers. SQL-portable upserts use db/dialects.py::dialect_insert(session, Model), and reads of stored timestamps use db/dialects.py::stored_utc.

Hermetic DB-engine config testing (solar_challenge_platform): a `postgresql+psycopg://…` engine can be built in the fast unit suite WITHOUT a live database — `sqlalchemy.create_engine` is lazy (no connection until first checkout) and `psycopg[binary]` is a declared dep. To verify `pool_pre_ping=True` wiring reached the engine, assert `engine.pool._pre_ping` (True for PG QueuePool, False for `sqlite:///:memory:` SingletonThreadPool). For deterministic assertions on connect_args/timeouts, factor a pure `_engine_kwargs(url) -> dict[str, Any]` helper and test that (introspecting connect_args off a live engine is fragile). The `create_engine(url, **_engine_kwargs(url))` splat passes mypy --strict.

GOTCHA (measured 2026-09-26, psycopg 3.3.4 / SQLAlchemy 2.0.51): PLATFORM_TEST_TIMESCALE_URL holds a SQLAlchemy URL (postgresql+psycopg://user:pw@host:port/db), and libpq rejects that scheme. psycopg.connect(url) and psycopg.conninfo.conninfo_to_dict(url) raise ProgrammingError: missing "=" after "postgresql+psycopg://..." in connection info string. To hand such a URL to plain psycopg, derive a libpq URI with sqlalchemy.engine.make_url(url).set(drivername="postgresql").render_as_string(hide_password=False). That keeps percent-encoded passwords and query parameters such as ?sslmode=require intact. Before task 336, tests/timeseries/test_timescale_smoke.py passed the variable to psycopg.connect verbatim, so that smoke test failed whenever the variable was set.

solar_challenge_platform conventions confirmed while planning P1·β (S7 models): (1) the orchestrator verify runs `mypy --strict` on src/solar_challenge_platform ONLY — test files under tests/ are NOT type-gated, so test code can be loosely typed but every src/ symbol must be mypy-clean. (2) Cross-module SQLAlchemy 2.0 ORM relationships should use TYPE_CHECKING imports + string forward refs (Mapped[list['Account']]) and declare FKs via 'table.id' strings — SQLAlchemy resolves targets from its class registry, so no runtime imports between mutually-referencing entity modules are needed (avoids import cycles) while staying mypy --strict clean. models/__init__.py must import every entity module so Base.metadata is fully populated for create_all and Alembic autogenerate. UUID PKs use sqlalchemy.Uuid + default=uuid.uuid4 (portable SQLite/Postgres); money uses Numeric/Decimal.

solar_challenge_platform test gotcha, measured on task 516's probes at main 40a6556, 2026-10-13. To make the database reject ONE statement for one home, attach a before_cursor_execute(retval=True) listener to the test's engine. It replaces the first statement whose bound values equal the home's UUID with "SELECT * FROM no_such_table" and returns type(parameters)().
- Match the UUID against a tuple of (uuid, str(uuid), uuid.hex) using ==. Do not use a set: some bound values are unhashable. psycopg binds uuid.UUID values in dicts, while SQLite binds 32-char hex strings in tuples.
- SQLite raises OperationalError; Postgres raises ProgrammingError (UndefinedTable) and aborts the transaction.
- On Postgres, without a savepoint (session.begin_nested()) the next home's read in the same Session fails with InFailedSqlTransaction. SQLite never aborts the transaction, so only a timescale-lane test can prove a per-home savepoint.

solar_challenge_platform SQLite write-side gotcha, measured 2026-10-10 at main 3751150 with TestClient probes on tests/_sqlite_engine.make_in_memory_engine. SQLAlchemy's SQLite DateTime(timezone=True) stores an aware non-UTC datetime at its wall clock and drops the offset without converting. Two cases: a consent expiry sent "2027-06-14T11:02:11+01:00" read back as naive 11:02:11, and a config effective_from sent "2026-09-01T01:00:00+01:00" was served as "2026-09-01T01:00:00Z". So a read-back fix (naive means UTC) alone serves such instants an hour off. Convert request datetimes to UTC before they reach an ORM column. PostgreSQL timestamptz stores the right instant.

solar_challenge_platform gotcha, measured 2026-10-11 by a probe in task 793's amendment pass. Python compares and hashes two aware datetimes that share one tzinfo object by their wall clock. So two TelemetryRows at 00:30Z and 01:30Z on 2026-10-25, otherwise equal and both written in one ZoneInfo("Europe/London") (01:30 fold=0 and fold=1), are == and hash-equal, and set or dict membership merges them; their in_utc() forms differ. psycopg returns every timestamptz in one cached ZoneInfo per session zone name (psycopg/_tz.py get_tzinfo). So rows read through an engine without db/session.py's "-c timezone=UTC" pin are exposed. One such engine is the dropped-readings drill's bare sa.create_engine(live_config.database_url), whose rows reach dropped_rows' set(survivors). Write such read-backs in UTC (astimezone(timezone.utc)) before comparing, sorting or hashing them, as timescale_store._to_utc does. Follow-up ticket tkt_0RVNM13HJNP7Y8F7ACA453CJWH covers read_raw_rows.

solar_challenge_platform gotcha (verified 2026-10-07, task 209 planning): SQLAlchemy's DateTime(timezone=True) on SQLite binds a tz-aware datetime by its wall-clock fields and drops the offset, so a non-UTC instant is stored wrong. Every store converts to UTC before binding (as DispatchLivenessStore.write_refresh_tick does) and re-attaches UTC to the naive values SQLite reads back. The repo had no portable upsert: on_conflict_do_update exists only on the dialect-specific constructs (sqlalchemy.dialects.postgresql.insert / sqlalchemy.dialects.sqlite.insert). A store that must run on both the hermetic SQLite suite and Postgres picks one by session.get_bind().dialect.name.

Task 'M1·F3: harden DB engine vs half-dead sockets (timeouts + keepalives + pre-ping) — silent dispatch wedge' completed. Witnessed 2026-07-03: a scp-dispatch process wedged silently mid-optimiser-tick — main thread parked in epoll on a sync psycopg socket wait while Postgres showed its sessions idle 15+ min; process stayed alive so systemd Restart=on-failure can never fire; only the device-side watchdog protected the fleet. Document the systemd-level liveness recommendation (WatchdogSec) in docs/examples/scp-dispatch.service comments.

solar_challenge_platform hermetic test pattern, measured 2026-10-10 by the task 778 architect. To prove a TimescaleStore method refuses its input before any I/O, with no database, build TimescaleStore(engine=sqlalchemy.create_engine("postgresql+psycopg://", creator=f)) where f raises. A postgres engine opens nothing until first use. SQLAlchemy lets a non-DBAPI exception raised by the creator propagate unwrapped: an AssertionError arrived as AssertionError. So the test sees either the method's own ValueError or the creator's sentinel, and a sentinel can also pin that an accepted input goes on to the database. Precedent: tests/timeseries/test_timescale_store_write.py.

AMENDMENT to 19e9f71c (the task-421 engine-guard convention), CORRECTING amendment d6856901 (task 576's first amendment), from task 576's reviewer amendment pass, commit 372df8d, written 2026-09-30 on branch task/576 and effective on main when that task merges. The guard's predicate no longer matches two literals by exact equality: tests/test_sqlite_engine_home.py's _is_an_in_memory_url asks SQLAlchemy, so EVERY spelling of the in-memory SQLite URL counts, "sqlite:///" and "sqlite+pysqlite://" included. It parses a literal first argument with sqlalchemy.engine.make_url and accepts the sqlite backend on a database of None, "" or ":memory:" (SQLite's dialect opens exactly those as :memory:, via url.database or ":memory:"). So "sqlite:///:memory:", "sqlite://", "sqlite:///", "sqlite+pysqlite://", "sqlite+aiosqlite://" and a query string on the in-memory URL are all flagged when built with StaticPool and a connect_args that may turn check_same_thread off. The database match stays exact, so a file URL such as "sqlite:///scp.db", another backend's URL such as "postgresql://", and a named shared-cache URI ("sqlite:///file:foo?mode=memory&cache=shared&uri=true", database "file:foo") are different databases and are not flagged. Two statements in d6856901 are superseded: "matches those two literals by exact equality" and "no other spelling is read". Everything else in d6856901 stands: _roster_engine is migrated onto make_in_memory_engine(), the repo scan reports only the helper and the three _AWAITING_MIGRATION files (task 560), and tests/validation/test_waits.py's default-pool create_engine("sqlite://") is still not flagged. Gotcha: make_url raises ArgumentError for text with no URL shape and ValueError (not ArgumentError) for a non-numeric port, and the scan feeds it every string literal that is the first argument of any create_engine call under tests/; the helper _literal_url catches both and treats the literal as no URL. Reader cases pin each in-memory spelling and each not-counted condition (file, other backend, no URL, bad port), and mutating any condition of the predicate fails one of them.

solar_challenge_platform gotcha (updated 2026-10-07, task 807 amend b309dec; supersedes the 2026-10-06 note that the drill's raw-row helpers were Postgres-only): the dropped-readings drill's raw-row access now lives in the public validation/drills/raw_telemetry.py (read_raw_rows / delete_raw_rows, formerly the private _read_raw_rows / _delete_rows in dropped_readings.py). Gotcha in solar_challenge_platform tests: with SQLAlchemy 2.x, an engine for 'sqlite:///:memory:' that has no StaticPool (for example db.session.init_db(url='sqlite:///:memory:')) uses one connection per thread. Each thread therefore sees its own empty database. Since task 309, Subscriber.run() runs consent checks on an 'ingest-consent-check' daemon thread, so a database seeded on the test's thread is invisible to them. Use tests/_sqlite_engine.make_in_memory_engine() (StaticPool, check_same_thread=False) with GateConsentChecker(session_factory=lambda: Session(engine)), or a file-backed SQLite under tmp_path. handle_message runs its checks on the calling thread and is not affected.

content: solar_challenge_platform convention (task 1093 amendment, branch task/1093 tip 23433d0; holds once merged): src/solar_challenge_platform/db/dialects.py::is_postgresql(url) is the one predicate for "this SQLAlchemy URL names PostgreSQL, whatever its driver". It is built on make_url(url).get_backend_name(). db/session.py::_engine_kwargs and migrations/env.py::_connect_args both call it before adding the libpq options pin db/dialects.py::PG_SESSION_TIMEZONE_OPTION ("-c timezone=UTC"). 0cee50f5-1131-45f4-b72f-9105083c92d1.content: solar_challenge_platform test convention (task 426, branch task/426; holds once merged): tests/_schema_state.py is the shared reader of what migrations leave in a database. alembic_revision(engine) returns the alembic_version row's revision. chunk_time_intervals(engine) returns a dict mapping relation name to its new-chunk interval (a timedelta). 19e9f71c-ac97-4c8b-a981-1fb760ec9cca.content: Convention (machine-enforced since task 421): a test that needs the whole-schema in-memory SQLite engine (create_engine("sqlite:///:memory:", poolclass=StaticPool, connect_args={"check_same_thread": False}) + Base.metadata.create_all) must call tests._sqlite_engine.make_in_memory_engine() via a module-level import, never build its own copy. tests/test_sqlite_engine_home.py is an AST guard that fails on any such copy outside the helper; its _AWAITING_MIGRATION set holds three files (test_billing_boundary.py, test_dropped_readings_drill.py, test_integration_e2e.py) until task 560 migrates them. Default-pool engines (create_engine("sqlite:///:memory:"[, echo=False])), JWT-mint engines and StaticPool engines without check_same_thread are deliberately different and are not flagged.

9b6e2e3f-6513-4edb-b76e-96a972c15a80.content:
Gotcha + technique (probed 2026-09-28, task 516):
- On Postgres, one failed statement aborts the Session's transaction, and every later statement on that Session raises psycopg InFailedSqlTransaction until ROLLBACK or ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT. SQLite never aborts, so a test proving per-item savepoint isolation must run on the timescale lane (tests._timescale_container.timescale_url + tests._migrated_engine.migrated_engine, about 11 s; Docker is present, so the lane runs in verify).
- To inject a genuine DB error hermetically, listen for before_cursor_execute with retval=True on the test's own engine. Swap the first statement whose bound params name a value for ("SELECT * FROM no_such_table", type(parameters)()).
- Match the value against the tuple (uuid, str(uuid), uuid.hex) using ==, never a set, because params can be unhashable. psycopg binds uuid.UUID in dicts; SQLite binds 32-char hex in qmark tuples.
- session.get() calls answered from the identity map emit no SQL, so they cannot be targeted this way.
