Completed: Dashboard client: five incidental defects found during the 2026-09-20 crash investigation
Description: Five unrelated client-side defects surfaced by the 2026-09-20 /team investigation into the dashboard renderer crash. None causes the crash (that is task 5705); all were found while auditing the cross-cutting client bundle and are filed together because each is a small, independent fix in the same area.

Ordered by operational severity, highest first. The first two are correctness-of-ACTION bugs in an operator console - they can make a click act on the wrong record - and should be treated as the real content of this task; the last three are latent or housekeeping.

1. tab_escalations.jsx renders rows with a null React key.
   Live console error on the Escalations tab: 'Each child in a list should have a unique "key" prop ... Check the render method of EscalationsTab ... at tr'. The code says `<tr key={row.id}>`, so the cause is the DATA: 2 of 300 escalation rows in the live payload carry `id: null` (one from /home/leo/src/dark-factory, one from /home/leo/src/reify). Those rows fall back to index keys, so a reorder between polls can hand the row click handler a different row than the one clicked. Fix needs a decision on both ends: why the server emits a null escalation id, and a stable client-side fallback key that does not collide.

2. findEscalationRow returns the first cross-project match.
   tab_escalations.jsx::findEscalationRow searches every subsection and returns the first hit, but escalation ids are only unique WITHIN a project. The live payload has esc-3169-1, esc-7603-1, esc-652-1 and roughly 20 others appearing in two different project subsections. A cross-tab focus link (e.g. from tab_memory_evals.jsx) can therefore open the wrong project's escalation. The lookup key must be (project, escalation_id), not escalation_id alone.

3. tabs.jsx::ChipList calls hooks conditionally.
   `persistKey ? usePersistedState(persistKey, false) : uS(false)` - two hooks on one branch, one on the other. Harmless today only because persistKey happens to be stable per instance. The first caller that makes persistKey conditional gets a 'Rendered fewer hooks than expected' crash. Call the hook unconditionally and branch on the value instead.

4. __DF_PAUSE does not suppress chip-driven refreshes.
   Only data.js::pollTick consults window.__DF_PAUSE. app.jsx's `uE(() => window.DF_REFRESH(win), [win])` calls refreshDFData directly, bypassing the check. Measured: with __DF_PAUSE = true, six window-chip clicks produced two extra full 14-endpoint refreshes. 'Pause live' should mean paused.

5. Unbounded, never-pruned localStorage keys.
   tabs.jsx::usePersistedState (via ::ChipList, ::DepsCell, ::LocksCell) writes one `df.deps.<task_id>` and one `df.locks.<task_id>` key per task row rendered, on MOUNT as well as on change, and never prunes them. Same shape for `df.curator.files.<ticket_id>` (tab_curator.jsx) and `df.memevals.prov.<eval_id>` (tab_memory_evals.jsx). Measured growth: 3 -> 109 keys on a single Orchestrators visit (53 rows); 117 -> 217 keys across four page loads in ~15 minutes. Over days this converges on the full task corpus (~7,000 keys). QuotaExceededError is swallowed by a bare `catch (e) {}`, so the failure mode is silent loss of every persisted UI preference. Needs pruning (or a single keyed object rather than a key per entity), and the bare catch should at minimum be observable.

Completed: LineChart/StackedAreaChart: snap the count-axis maximum to a whole multiple of the tick count (niceCountMax)
Description: Follow-up from task 4232 (LineChart integer-count y-axis tick labels), filed during that task's amendment pass at the reviewer's own suggestion. NOT in-scope work that was skipped — a deliberate deferral recorded in the source and now carried here.

WHAT 4232 SHIPPED. dashboard/src/dashboard/static/redux/spark_path.js gained `formatCountTick(v)`, a y-tick label formatter for integer-COUNT axes that returns String(v) for a whole tick and '' otherwise. It is wired at three LineChart call sites (dashboard/src/dashboard/static/redux/tabs.jsx MemoryTab reads/writes and MergeTab attempt-depth; dashboard/src/dashboard/static/redux/tab_escalation_analytics.jsx WorkflowPanel churn). It deliberately BLANKS rather than rounds, because LineChart's ticks are (maxV * i) / 4 and Math.round on those fabricates duplicate labels at small maxima (measured: maxV=1 renders 0/0/1/1/1, and maxV=1 is the plottableMax(values, 1) seed floor every idle count series reaches).

THE RESIDUAL DEFECT. Blanking is better than fabricating but leaves gridlines unlabelled, because both options take the axis maximum as given. Measured over every integer maxV in 1..200: 100 axes label only 2 of 5 ticks (floor + peak), 50 label 3, and only 50 label all 5. So on arbitrary count data — memory reads/writes per hour, merge attempts per 15-minute bucket — roughly half of all renders lose three gridline labels, and maxV=999 reads "0 ... 999" with three bare gridlines.

THE WORK. What charting libraries do instead is snap the axis maximum UP to a multiple of the tick count (7 -> 8, 999 -> 1000) so every tick is whole and nothing is either fabricated or omitted. Add a `niceCountMax(maxV, ticks)` to spark_path.js and have the count axes scale to it.

WHY IT WAS NOT DONE IN 4232. It is not a label change and could not be reached from formatCountTick, which only sees the tick it is handed. LineChart computes `plottableMax(all, 1)` internally, so snapping means changing LineChart's own scale — its range, its gridline positions, and the height every plotted point maps to. That is a chart-GEOMETRY change across all eight LineChart call sites (and StackedAreaChart's, which has the same latent shape), not a label change, and 4232's plan explicitly froze LineChart's tick generator because task 4059's pin `test_line_chart_hands_format_y_the_raw_tick` guards it.

- Snapping must be OPT-IN per axis, not a new default. tab_escalation_analytics.jsx's WorkflowPanel esc-per-done chart plots a genuine `filings / done` ratio (escalation_analytics.py::_esc_per_done) through LineChart's default and must not be snapped to whole numbers; that same asymmetry is what ruled out a rounding default in 4232.
- formatCountTick is forward-compatible and should NOT need changing: under a snapped maximum every tick is already whole, so it labels all five and its blank branch simply stops being reached.
- Task 4059's pins must stay green: test_line_chart_hands_format_y_the_raw_tick, test_default_format_y_callers_keep_integer_count_axes, test_stacked_area_chart_does_not_pre_round_the_tick_before_format_y (dashboard/tests/test_charts_axis_labels.py).

Description: PROBLEM
A scheduler park reserves modules for an owner that will dispatch once they free. orchestrator/src/orchestrator/scheduler.py::Scheduler._park_gc_reason expires an owner's parks in only three cases: the owner is terminal, it is missing from the active fetch, or it has an unsatisfied LOCAL dependency. That leaves three gaps:

1. An owner whose status is blocked, deferred, review or merge-deferred keeps its parks until it goes terminal or the orchestrator restarts. It cannot dispatch, so the parks reserve for nobody. A day-old park:

   - refuses running tasks that try to widen into it;
   - can be shadowed only by a pin reservation when it is critical.
2. Park GC ignores cross-project dependencies (metadata.external_deps). Task 1580 (7f8540b892, design decision 4) kept GC on the legacy local-only call. A critical owner whose external dep is not done therefore keeps its parks for as long as the other project takes, potentially weeks, while it cannot dispatch.

Description: PROBLEM
A pin today buys exactly one thing: on each scheduler tick, the pinned task gets the first try at acquiring ALL of its module locks at once (orchestrator/src/orchestrator/scheduler.py::Scheduler._phase_select_pins). If that try fails, the pin earns nothing. No skip count, no park, no event.

Fairness parks go only to the scored loop's single strict-top candidate (::Scheduler._phase_select_scored -> ::Scheduler._bump_skip_and_maybe_park). orchestrator/src/orchestrator/config.py::TIER_BASE makes every critical candidate outscore every high one. So a non-critical pin can never earn a park while any critical candidate is eligible, and one always is: in the 7 days to 2026-09-28, all 390 task_skipped events went to six critical tasks.

A pinned task whose footprint touches a contended file therefore dispatches only on a tick where every one of its files happens to be free of both holders and parks. Meanwhile, the files it needs free up one at a time and are taken by lower-tier scored candidates in the same tick. The pin fails exactly the class the scheduler PRD says pins exist for: plans/scheduler-dispatch-scoring-and-lock-layer-prd.md §C4 says "never top-scored — this is what the pin is for".

Completed: Scheduler heatmap: stranded-park and held-module columns are unreachable at live scale — the column slice crowds out its own carve-outs
Description: Discovered by task 5705's implementer during its amendment pass; see escalation esc-5705-3 for the full observation. Task 5705 bounded the Scheduler contention heatmap's rows x modules render; this is a residual defect in the column axis it introduced, filed rather than fixed because the remedy is a design choice, not an amendment.

FILE: dashboard/src/dashboard/static/redux/scheduler_heatmap_bounds.js (function boundHeatmapAxes, and the moduleEarnsColumn predicate above it). Test suite: dashboard/tests/js/scheduler_heatmap_bounds.test.mjs. Consumer: dashboard/src/dashboard/static/redux/scheduler_heatmap.jsx (the .sched-heatmap-cap truncation caption).

THE DEFECT. Column selection is `allModules.filter(moduleEarnsColumn).slice(0, MAX_HEATMAP_COLS)` with MAX_HEATMAP_COLS = 60. moduleEarnsColumn carries two rescue clauses beyond `contention > 1`: a `park_stack` disjunct (task 5705 design decision 2 — dashboard/src/dashboard/data/scheduler.py injects an entry for every park-stack key at contention 0 so a fully-stranded module still gets one) and a `holder` disjunct (added for a reviewer finding — a stale current_holders entry leaves a genuinely-blocked waiter at contention 1). Both rescue modules at contention 0 or 1. The server returns modules sorted `(-contention, path)` (scheduler.py::_module_contention_counts), so both rescued classes sort to the END of the list, and the positional slice takes a PREFIX. At production scale the 60-column budget is exhausted by high-contention modules long before the slice reaches either, so neither rescue clause can ever fire.

MEASURED (HEAD 62aa61a5b3, worktree .worktrees/5705). A 4,304-module live-shaped fixture — 4,302 modules with ~43% at contention > 1 matching the 2026-09-20 snapshot, plus one fully-stranded park module at contention 0 and one stale-holder module at contention 1, sorted as the server returns them — yields: 1845 modules at contention > 1; 60 columns out; minimum contention among survivors 6; stranded-park column survived false; stale-holder column survived false. On a small or quiet deployment, where the budget is not exhausted, both clauses work as written.

WHY IT WAS NOT FIXED IN 5705. This is structurally the same defect a reviewer found on that task's ROW axis ("the filter honours parked rows, the slice then takes a positional prefix of the ORIGINAL server order"), and the row axis was fixed by partitioning parked rows ahead of touching rows before the slice. That remedy does not transfer: applied to columns it would put contention-0 and contention-1 columns leftmost, which falsifies the truncation caption the same review pass corrected — the "most contended" superlative was deliberately moved onto the COLUMN axis because filter+slice yields a prefix of the server's sort, and the row axis was given a plain count instead. Making both true at once needs a reserved-slot design (budget k of the 60 columns for carve-outs, fill the remainder from the contention prefix, then decide the render order and what the caption claims). That is a design decision plus new copy, outside an amendment pass's remit.

NOT A REGRESSION. Before task 5705 the grid rendered all 4,302 columns and killed the browser renderer, so nothing got worse. The Scheduler tab's red stranded-parks banner and ParkStacksSection surface stranded parks independently of the heatmap; what is missing is the stranded module's COLUMN in the grid.

ACCEPTANCE. Pick and implement a column budget that lets both carve-outs reach the rendered set at live scale; add a cap-scale JS test mirroring the row-axis one already in scheduler_heatmap_bounds.test.mjs ('BOUND: a parked row survives the cap even when ordinary rows would fill it'); and update the .sched-heatmap-cap caption in scheduler_heatmap.jsx so whatever it claims about column ordering stays true under the new selection. Closing this as won't-fix is a legitimate outcome if the conclusion is that the banner and ParkStacksSection already cover the stranded case adequately — record that reasoning rather than leaving the rescue clauses in place unexplained.
Analysis: PREMISES VERIFIED on base ad1e604fe9, RE-VERIFIED on main 8dce6f53b4 (2026-10-12 revalidation). scheduler_heatmap_bounds.js, scheduler_heatmap.jsx, scheduler_heatmap_bounds.test.mjs, test_index_html.py and _cache_buster_helpers.py are byte-unchanged since ad1e604fe9 (git diff --quiet rc=0), and the bounds suite is still 25/25 green. scheduler_heatmap_bounds.js::boundHeatmapAxes selects columns as `allModules.filter(moduleEarnsColumn).slice(0, MAX_HEATMAP_COLS)`. moduleEarnsColumn = contention>1 || park_stack non-empty || (holder && contention>0). The server sorts modules (-contention, path) (scheduler.py::_module_contention_counts), so both rescue classes sort to the tail and a positional prefix never reaches them. The JSX caption (.sched-heatmap-cap) claims "the N most contended of M modules". The comment above moduleEarnsColumn ("Neither rescue can crowd the contended columns out...") states the true-but-irrelevant direction and hides the defect.

CHANGES ON MAIN SINCE THE FIRST PLAN, ALL COMPATIBLE: (1) task 4889 changed scheduler.py::collect_scheduler_state. It now reads collect_tasks_with_counts, adds degraded_projects as an 8th return element, and withholds a degraded project's park stacks. A degraded project contributes no rows, so it emits no module entries at all. _module_contention_counts and _merge_module_lists are unchanged, so steps 1-2 apply as written (see the degraded-project design decision). (2) index.html: the redux cache-buster is now ?v=82 on all 45 tags (it was 79). pre-1 bumps it to 83. (3) test_tab_scheduler.py: one test was appended (degraded_projects wiring). _heatmap_body, test_scheduler_heatmap_consumes_the_shared_bound and test_scheduler_heatmap_discloses_what_it_is_not_showing are intact. (4) test_scheduler_page.py grew to 3,531 lines, which strengthens the case for putting holder_live tests in a new file. (5) classic_script_scope.test.mjs registered invariant_chip.js only. No name collision with this plan's new top-level functions.

LIVE MEASUREMENT (GET http://127.0.0.1:8080/api/v2/dashboard/scheduler, 2026-10-12; context: the running dashboard process, not this worktree): 7,185 modules, 4,266 rows, 2,977 at contention>1, server-sorted. The two rescue clauses match far more modules than their stated targets:
- park_stack clause: 99 modules have a park stack, ALL with live owners, 0 has_dead_park. Its stated target (a fully-stranded module, the banner's has_dead_park) is 0 modules today.
- holder clause: 204 modules have holder && contention==1. In 203 of them the holder is itself a live row whose own lock_set contains the path, so the "1" is the holder and nobody waits. Only 1 is the stated target. Its comment ("requiring a waiter keeps a merely-held module out") is false: contention cannot tell the holder from a waiter.
- Narrowed targets: 5 modules, all held by one departed holder (scoping-intake T-29, absent from active tasks), at contention 15/9/7/6/1. Each ranks 179th or lower among contended modules (the head of 60 bottoms out at contention 33).
So a reserved-slot budget over the CURRENT predicates would fill with noise (303 candidates). The predicates must be narrowed first.

SECOND-ORDER DEFECT (found by simulating a reserved-slot column design against the live payload): rescuing a column is hollow if no row that colours it survives the 60-row cap. With the current row tiers (parked first, then touching rows in server order), 5 rescued columns would render but only 1 would have a coloured cell. Their waiter rows sit around index 2,208 of 2,223 touching rows. This is the same "carve-out survives the filter but not the slice" shape, moved to the row axis. Adding a tier for rows waiting on a rescued column costs 15 rows on live data (8 parked + 15 waiting + 37 ordinary = 60).

DESIGN (not won't-fix): the banner and ParkStacksSection do cover stranded parks, but NOTHING on the tab flags a departed holder (ModulesView prints "held by T-29" with no liveness), and live data has one blocking 15 rows. Implement:
1. Server: `holder_live: bool|None` on each module entry in scheduler.py::_module_contention_counts (True/False iff a holder exists AND live_task_ids was supplied; None otherwise), carried with `holder` in _merge_module_lists. This mirrors parked_owner_live; the server owns live_task_ids, so liveness stays single-sourced.
2. Client predicate `lockIsStranded(m)` = m.has_dead_park || (m.holder && m.holder_live === false && contention > 0). Column eligibility = contention>1 || lockIsStranded. Live parks and live-held modules at contention<=1 no longer earn a column (one coloured cell is not contention, which is the rule the existing 'held module with NO live waiter' test already pins).
3. Column budget: a contended HEAD (prefix of the contention>1 modules in server order) plus a RESCUED TAIL (stranded modules the head did not reach, at most MAX_RESCUED_COLS=10, in server order). Slots are reserved only on demand: the head shrinks one slot per rescued module. The head length is a fixed point, because shrinking the head can push a stranded module out of it. Render order = head then tail = server order throughout, so columns stay contention-descending left to right.
4. Rows: three tiers (parked, then rows touching a rescued-tail column, then rows touching any other kept column), then slice 60.
5. Caption: composed by a new exported `describeHeatmapCap(bounded)` in the .js (executable under node), reading a new `modulesRescued` count on the return value; the JSX only renders it. Copy: no rescues -> unchanged sentence; with rescues -> "..., and the N most contended of M modules, then R stranded (dead park owner or departed holder)."; no contended columns -> "..., and R of M modules, all stranded (dead park owner or departed holder)."
6. Bump every /static/redux/*?v= in index.html (82 -> 83 on 8dce6f53b4; base-relative cache-buster rule enforced by test_index_html.py::test_redux_cache_buster_bumped).

Tests:
- JS behaviour in dashboard/tests/js/scheduler_heatmap_bounds.test.mjs: cap-scale column tests mirroring 'BOUND: a parked row survives the cap even when ordinary rows would fill it', a live-shaped 4,302-module fixture with both carve-outs, the fixed-point edge, the flood cap, the row tier, and the caption strings.
- Python unit tests for holder_live in a NEW file dashboard/tests/test_scheduler_holder_live.py. test_scheduler_page.py is now 3,531 lines, past the heuristic-14 alarm, so it is not grown.
- One rewritten source-WIRING probe in dashboard/tests/test_tab_scheduler.py: the JSX calls describeHeatmapCap and no longer hand-writes the copy.

Run JS with `node --test dashboard/tests/js/scheduler_heatmap_bounds.test.mjs` from the worktree root, and Python from dashboard/ with `uv run pytest tests/<file>`. classic_script_scope.test.mjs must stay green: new top-level names in the classic script must be distinctive `function` declarations or non-JSX-bound consts.
Key decisions: Fix rather than close as won't-fix: reserve column slots for stranded locks, on demand, as a contended HEAD plus a rescued TAIL (MAX_RESCUED_COLS = 10 of the 60), rendered in server order.; Narrow both rescue clauses to their stated targets before budgeting for them: stranded = has_dead_park OR (holder AND holder_live === false AND contention > 0). Live parks and live-held modules at contention <= 1 no longer earn a column.; Holder liveness is computed on the SERVER as a new `holder_live: bool | None` module field in scheduler.py::_module_contention_counts (None when there is no holder or live_task_ids was not supplied), carried with `holder` in _merge_module_lists. The client does not derive it from rows.

SCHEDULER SCORING EVIDENCE — figures MEASURED first-hand 2026-09-20 while planning task 3819 (PRD plans/scheduler-dispatch-scoring-and-lock-layer-prd.md). Four things that are not derivable from the PRD prose and that a later agent would otherwise re-derive or get wrong.

(1) UNITS GOTCHA. `Scheduler._compute_age(task_id, max_id)` returns "newer-task-count" (`max_id - pending_anchor`), NOT seconds — it is an id-distance proxy. `_compute_score` is a PURE SCALAR function `(tier, age, transitive_count)` that never receives the task dict. Anything wall-clock must come from elsewhere. The seam already exists: `self._wall_now()` / `_resolve_wall_time_source` (scheduler.py::_resolve_wall_time_source) returns a `datetime` and is injectable as `Scheduler(config, wall_time_source=...)` — this is the preferred clock seam, and a few legacy sites still call `datetime.now(UTC)` inline instead.

(2) THE BASELINE CSV. plans/evidence/scheduler-scoring-2026-08-06/candidates_scored.csv recomputes over all 294 rows to 47 DISTINCT scores / max tie group 117 at 2999.0 / 251 CAPPED; 4 tiers (critical 1 / high 56 / medium 90 / low 147); 51 rows with D>=1, maxD 31. The PRD §10 prose's "46-distinct / 249-masked" are NOT reproducible from this file (they come from an unrecorded 291-row scoping); only the 117-way tie reproduces exactly. Recomputing the legacy formula from (tier, age, D) matches the committed `score` column on all 294 rows within 1e-3 — the only deltas are the CSV's 4-decimal truncation, so the column is faithful and can be trusted directly.

(3) TIER_BASE IS NOT UNIFORMLY SPACED, despite the comment above it in config.py saying "uniform TIER_WIDTH between adjacent tiers". Actual: critical 16000 / high 8000 / medium 4000 / low 2000 / polish 1000 — gaps of 8000/4000/2000/1000. TIER_WIDTH (1000) is purely the bonus CAP, and it happens to equal the SMALLEST adjacent gap (low->polish), which is what actually makes the no-tier-crossing property hold. Do not reason from the comment.

(4) ALPHA'S BACK-FILL HAS RUN. On the live dark-factory store: 1057 pending tasks, `metadata.pending_since` coverage 1.0, 1056 carrying `pending_since_backfilled`, values ms-precision ISO-8601 with a trailing `Z` (e.g. `2026-07-16T20:49:48.531Z`). 210 of those have D>=1, maxD 188 (so a CPM cap of 32 genuinely clips). Consequence: the D12 anchor-coverage arming gate is already self-cleared in production and is a deployment-window safety net, not the steady state.

Completed: Refuse a relative INTAKE_DATA_DIR at start (cli.py _data_dir)
Description: Found while planning task 22 (follow-up id agent-followup-22). Read in the code, not reproduced.

Task 22 makes src/scoping_intake/cli.py's _data_dir treat an empty INTAKE_DATA_DIR as unset. Any other relative value, such as `INTAKE_DATA_DIR=data`, is still used as given and resolves against the working directory of whichever command runs it. serve (through sites_for), calibration and purge each call _data_dir(os.environ). That has two consequences:

(1) Run from the repository root, `data` puts the session directories under ./data/sessions, inside the git repository. .gitignore ignores only data/escalations/, data/orchestrator/, data/queue/ and data/reconciliation/, so session data could be committed. This breaks review/briefing.yaml's rule that session data lives outside every git repository.

(2) A purge run from a different working directory than serve builds a SessionStore on a different, empty directory (SessionStore mkdirs it at construction) and prints 'purged 0 sessions: none'. The retention promise can therefore fail without any sign.

The deploy units (deploy/scoping-intake.service, deploy/scoping-intake-purge.service) and every README example use absolute paths, so the installed service is not affected. The exposure is a hand-typed relative path.

Proposal, for Leo's judgement: refuse a relative INTAKE_DATA_DIR at start, with a message naming the variable and quoting the value. Do it in serve, calibration and purge alike, reusing the UnusableIntakeVariable refusal type that task 22 introduces in cli.py. calibration and purge would need the same refusal-to-exit translation that _serve has. Test through cli.sites_for and through cli.main() in tests/test_serve.py or a sibling test module. Never let a test resolve the real ~/.local/share/scoping-intake: patch HOME into tmp_path and chdir into a tmp directory, as task 22's data-directory test does.

Rationale: docs/code-quality.md heuristic 10 (an invariant enforced where the value enters, and named when violated), and the briefing convention on where session data lives. Depends on task 22 having landed.

Description: Agent follow-up from task 255 (escalation id agent-followup-255). OUT OF SCOPE for task 255, which only rewords the printed label and docstrings of tests/integration/test_cost_recovery_calibration.py::TestPhysicsReconciliationColumn and must not change product behaviour.

CODE FACTS (main 270864e, 2026-10-01):
- src/solar_challenge/finance.py::project_multi_year (inner _simulate_age): own_use_revenue = own_use_rate_pence_per_kwh x fleet_sc / 100, where fleet_sc = sum over homes of (demand - import) over scenario.period. It is NOT annualised. seg_revenue = sum of _seg_export_income_gbp(s, finance, s.simulation_days), which IS annualised (x 365/days when days < 360). grid_services is an annual GBP figure. YearPoint.fleet_self_consumption_kwh carries the same un-annualised window total.
- project_economics subtracts an annual fleet opex and annual debt service. solve_cost_recovery_rate drives the per-home-per-year mean surplus to the annual retained-cash floor; its slope is mean(fleet_sc)/100/n_homes.
- So when scenario.period is shorter than about a year, the solve and the project economics set N days of own-use against a year of opex, debt and floor. The only warning raised comes from bill_distribution (solve step 6): "Simulation period is only N days (<360); scaling financial outputs to 365-day annual basis". That warning describes the outlay path, not the solve, and reads as though the solve were annualised too.
- project_multi_year's docstring Note says "fleet_revenue_gbp is annualised by householder_bill". Since CR3 project_multi_year no longer calls householder_bill (see the comment above own_use_revenue in _simulate_age), and only the SEG part of fleet_revenue_gbp is annualised. The Note's conclusion (use about one full year) still holds; its mechanism sentence is stale.

solar_challenge test gotcha (task 749 amendment, measured 2026-10-14 on task/749, pandas 3.0.3): the day count (index[-1] - index[0]).days + 1 overcounts a window crossing the autumn clock change only on an index of whole local days, built the way load.py indexes a period: pd.date_range(first_day, f"{last_day} 23:59", freq="1min", tz="Europe/London"). Built that way, October 2024 is 745 hours and counts 32 days; March 2024 is 743 hours and counts 31. An index built with periods=days*1440, as tests/unit/test_validation.py's _create_minute_index builds one, always spans days*1440-1 minutes, so it counts exactly `days` across either clock change and cannot reproduce the overcount. A RED test for the S10 covered-days fix needs the whole-local-days index.

solar_challenge finance gotcha (measured on main 270864e, 2026-10-01, task 271 architect). Since CR2 (commit 240666d), project_multi_year sums basis-C own-use, export, import and battery discharge over the raw simulated window and does NOT annualise them. Only SEG is annualised (×365/days below 360 days). On a short window, solve_cost_recovery_rate and project_economics therefore set N days of own-use against a year of opex, debt and floor. The older advice "use --start/--end for exploratory optimize/finance runs" (also printed by `optimize configs`) gives every config infeasible_above_retail at the retail clamp today. Measured: a 3-day copy of a fleet that solves at 18.96p on a full year returns 30p infeasible_above_retail. Task 271 plans to annualise all four aggregates through one shared `_annualisation_scale` rule. Until it merges, use full-year windows for any solve or projection.

9b696a27-f127-48ed-a990-d922c6e48ad6.content: Amendment to the solar_challenge FinanceConfig "appended-default field" recipe (task 374, branch task/374, 2026-10-10; applies once merged to main). (1) In FinanceConfig.__post_init__, a new >= 0 float field is one entry in the _non_negative_fields dict, checked as `0 <= v < math.inf` ("<f> must be >= 0 and finite, got <v>"); a strictly positive field is one entry in _positive_fields (`0 < v < math.inf`). (2) Its config.py _FINANCE_SCALAR_COERCIONS row is `_number` (or `_number_or_none` for an Optional[float] where null means unset), not `float`: _number refuses a YAML boolean, which float() reads as 1.0/0.0. FinanceConfig refuses a bool, non-finite or fractional year with "<f> must be a whole number, got <v>" and holds a whole float as an int: LoadConfig.household_occupants' rule. (4) parse_finance_config's three coercion wrappers catch (ValueError, TypeError, OverflowError), so a 10**400 is a ConfigurationError. tests/unit/config/test_finance_block.py's tests parametrized over _NUMERIC_FIELDS (non-finite, boolean and 10**400 refusals) cover a new numeric field automatically.

Docker's build-context matcher (moby patternmatcher, used by both the classic builder and BuildKit) anchors any .dockerignore pattern at the context root unless it starts with `**/`. content: Running /hotspot-survey from a fleet child session — procedural lessons (2026-10-13): (1) To pin the run to an as_of sha while main moves, `git worktree add --detach <scratchpad>/tree <sha>` gave every agent one read-only tree with working git history; remove it with `git worktree remove --force` afterwards. (2) Reviewers told the tree was READ-ONLY still dropped pip-downloaded wheels (aiomqtt, paho) into its root to read library source; give agents an explicit scratch dir for downloads and expect untracked junk. (3) `cd` into another session's worktree (e.g. .claude/worktrees/review-all-*) makes the harness switch the session's primary working directory to it; use `git -C <path>` and absolute paths instead. (4) The Workflow tool's task .output file is a wrapper {summary, agentCount, logs, result, workflowProgress, totalTokens, totalToolCalls}; the script's return value is under 'result'. (5) Even with path::Class.method anchors, two distinct findings at the same method with the same fixed primary tag collide on key (3 of 92 here); the digest must detect collisions and re-anchor to a finer or more accurate symbol before the conformance check. reify-audit's tree-coupled baseline manifests (crates/reify-audit/pdiag-baseline.txt, ptodo-baseline.txt) pin per-file counts against the WHOLE worktree, so they go stale on every rebase of a long-lived branch — and the always-on Rust test tiers do not catch it. Staleness surfaces only in the #[ignore]d whole-repo ratchet (`cargo test -p reify-audit --test pdiag_baseline -- --ignored`) and the infra shell gate (`bash tests/infra/test_reify_audit_pdiag.sh`, scenario (a)). Fix by regenerating with the canonical generator — `cargo run -p reify-audit --bin pdiag-baseline-gen -- --project-root . > crates/reify-audit/pdiag-baseline.txt` — never by hand-editing rows, which is what keeps generation and enforcement structurally in sync. Critically, a row that ROSE must be attributed before it is blessed: if `git diff <merge-base> HEAD -- <file>` is EMPTY the drift arrived from main and absorbing it is sanctioned (PRD §6 decision 3 makes backlog migration opportunistic; enforcement is only for sites the diff itself adds), but if it is NON-EMPTY the branch added a code-less Diagnostic::error/warning and that is a real INV-SF-6 violation to remediate per docs/notes/diagnostic-severity-policy.md §3. A bare regenerate blesses both cases identically, which is why the attribution check cannot be skipped. Cheap pre-check before a full verify: `cargo run -p reify-audit --bin pdiag-baseline-gen -- --project-root . | diff - crates/reify-audit/pdiag-baseline.txt`.

reify-audit PDIAG (task #5405, crates/reify-audit): the two whole-repo ratchet checks in crates/reify-audit/tests/pdiag_baseline.rs — `live_counts_are_within_the_committed_baseline` and `regenerating_the_committed_baseline_is_a_no_op` — are `#[ignore]`d as on-demand checks that need a real git checkout. So a plain `cargo test -p reify-audit` reports FULLY GREEN (79 lib + 69 cli + 22 pdiag_baseline passing) while the committed crates/reify-audit/pdiag-baseline.txt is stale against the tree. You must run `cargo test -p reify-audit --test pdiag_baseline -- --ignored` to see it. The merge gate does catch it, via tests/infra/test_reify_audit_pdiag.sh scenario (a), which runs `reify-audit --pattern PDIAG` and expects exit 0 — but only after a release build, so the fast feedback loop is the `--ignored` run. Measured 2026-09-10 on task/5405 rebased onto main b42c7dd: six baseline rows had drifted from main's movement alone (auto_type_param_phase.rs 1->2, geometry_ops.rs 136->138, modal_ops.rs 21->25 up; engine_admin.rs 3->2, engine_compute.rs 2->1, engine_eval.rs 23->21 down), none of those files touched by the branch. This is the esc-5405-17 bootstrap drift and is self-limiting once PDIAG is enforced on main. Remedy is always regeneration, never a hand-edit: `cargo run -p reify-audit --bin pdiag-baseline-gen -- --project-root . > crates/reify-audit/pdiag-baseline.txt`.

Topic: PDIAG/PTODO baseline-ratchet staleness. reify-audit's committed baseline manifests (crates/reify-audit/pdiag-baseline.txt, ptodo-baseline.txt) are tree-coupled per-file-count/fingerprint ratchets that go stale whenever an unrelated task lands on main while a branch is in flight. See peer procedural_knowledge entries for: the risen-row attribution check (empty vs non-empty `git diff <merge-base> HEAD -- <file>`); the regenerate-as-last-step-before-landing-and-after-every-rebase timing rule; the general landing-race diagnosis/remedy recipe (`git diff --name-only main...HEAD -- <path>`, regenerate-and-absorb as a solo chore); and the task-5887 stale-release-binary + absolute-per-file-count incident.

A warm lane's seeded `target/` is built from `main`, not from your task branch, and `scripts/reify-audit-freshness.sh` does NOT catch that cross-branch staleness — its guard only compares binary MTIME against the last git commit epoch of crates/reify-audit/, so it judges a base-built binary FRESH whenever the lane's target/ was built later in wall-clock than the branch's own reify-audit commits, even though that binary contains none of the branch's detector changes. Always run `cargo build --release -p reify-audit` (rebuilds both `reify-audit` and `ptodo-baseline-gen`) before running `tests/infra/test_reify_audit_ptodo.sh` or `ptodo-baseline-gen` on a branch that changes the detector — otherwise the binary under test is main's. This bites in BOTH directions: a new hermetic scenario fails spuriously with 0 findings, and the §6.6 `live ⊆ baseline` ratchet scenario (a) passes VACUOUSLY against a main-built binary (main's smaller/older live set is trivially a subset of the branch's grown baseline), so a green ratchet is not evidence on a stale binary. Measured on task/6103: 2026-08-31 rebuild flipped the gate 24 passed/1 failed → 25 passed/0 failed; a 2026-09-04 recurrence cost a false FAIL before the same rebuild fixed it again. NOTE: this exact lesson was independently rediscovered THREE times on task 6103 alone (2026-08-31 architect, 2026-09-04 architect, 2026-09-04 implementer) — treat as a standing gotcha to check FIRST, not something to re-derive.

Reify's PDIAG ratchet (crates/reify-audit/src/pdiag.rs + crates/reify-audit/pdiag-baseline.txt, landed on main 2026-09) counts per-file code-less `Diagnostic::error(...)` / `Diagnostic::warning(...)` construction sites and allows counts only to DECREASE, so any task that adds a diagnostic must attach `.with_code(...)` or it reds its file's row. To check a branch cheaply before committing, run `cargo run -q -p reify-audit --bin pdiag-baseline-gen -- --project-root . > /tmp/pdiag-live.txt` and diff it against the committed baseline ignoring `#` lines — rows going DOWN are green and need no baseline regen. [STALE as of 2026-09-19, see marker above:] As of 2026-09-16 pdiag is NOT referenced by scripts/verify.sh (only ptodo is), so it is not yet a merge-gate check.

crates/reify-audit/ptodo-baseline.txt fingerprints are line-number-erased and deduped (format "{path} :: {kind} :: {text}", separator is space-colon-colon-space), so ONE baseline entry can stand for MANY source lines — the 5 entries seeded by task #6087 cover 14 lines, and the T12 layer-B seam entry alone covers 8 identical lines that must ALL be fixed or the entry survives. The section 6.6 ratchet is a SUBSET oracle (comm -23 live baseline), so shrinking SOURCE keeps it green while shrinking the BASELINE first turns it red: always land source fixes BEFORE regenerating the baseline. Regenerate only via target/release/ptodo-baseline-gen with REIFY_PTODO_TASKS_DB pointed at the real tasks.db (a DB-present run is a strict superset of the degraded run the ratchet performs); never hand-edit or sed it. An empty 0-byte baseline is the valid PRD section 6.4 zero-residual-debt end state, pinned by tests/ptodo_baseline.rs validate_accepts_empty_baseline, but the file must stay tracked and present because baseline_is_well_formed asserts path.exists().

In reify, a docs/notes/ decision record that pastes verbatim measurement stdout must anchor provenance to the branch's merge-base with main (e.g. "measured at merge-base 2e3f228d2d"), never to a branch-tip SHA. Task branches get rebased before landing, which orphans any tip SHA cited inside the note (task #6290's record cited 94aaecff43, a real commit that is not an ancestor of the rebased tip). 35e0187a-2a81-436f-892f-0fa980fc70eb.content:
GOTCHA — reify-audit's PTODO ratchet (test_reify_audit_ptodo.sh) has a "phantom-tracking" heuristic (crates/reify-audit/src/ptodo.rs §8.3, PHANTOM_PHRASES ~line 1719) that flags ANY source line — including plain `///` doc comments, not just TODO/FIXME/HACK markers — containing one of four phantom phrases ("tracked separately", "tracked as a follow-up", "tracked in project memory", "follow-up task will") with no canonical `#NNNN` cite on that SAME line, as a Medium-severity structural finding. The check fires per-LINE, independent of the TODO/FIXME/HACK marker regex and with NO above-line lookback: in a multi-line `//` comment block, a properly-cited `TODO(#NNNN)` on one line does NOT protect a later line in the same block that happens to contain a phantom phrase without its own same-line cite. Because crates/reify-audit/ptodo-baseline.txt is committed empty (zero-residual-state policy), ANY new PTODO-pattern fingerprint fails the ratchet and blocks merge.

Confirmed trigger in the wild: a doc comment using "Tracked separately from `other_field`" (added by task 4636 in engine_build.rs) tripped this heuristic on an otherwise unrelated code comment.

FIX POLICY — RATIFIED 2026-08-20 (curator gate 5821). Choose by whether a real follow-up actually exists:
1. A REAL, live, non-terminal follow-up exists → CITE IT: `#NNNN` on the same line. This is the primary fix. It is also what the project's hard convention requires for every TODO/FIXME/HACK marker, todo!()/unimplemented!() stub, and blocker #[ignore] (CLAUDE.md "TODO citation convention"; grammar in docs/prds/reify-audit-ptodo-detector.md §8). Rewording away a genuine pointer destroys information and is the wrong fix here.
2. NO real follow-up exists — the phrase is incidental prose and no citation would be meaningful → REWORD (comment-only, no logic change): "Distinct from X" / "Not the same set as X" instead of "Tracked separately from X".
3. A cite you added later goes terminal (done/cancelled) → it becomes an `orphaned` High-severity finding. Re-point it at a live task, or, if no follow-up remains, reword per (2). Cited != tracked.
Escape hatch for a legitimate pattern string that is neither: append `// ptodo:allow — reason`.

To debug/find the exact offending fingerprint: run `env -u REIFY_PTODO_TASKS_DB target/release/ptodo-baseline-gen --project-root $PWD` and inspect the `path :: kind :: text` output.

[CURATOR CORRECTION 2026-08-20, gate 5821.] This entry previously carried a BLANKET "Do NOT fix by adding a `#NNNN` cite ... that opts the line into the β liveness resolution lane and can itself become an `orphaned` High-severity finding instead." That was read fleet-wide as "never cite", which conflicts with the project's own hard gate and with the lesson drawn from /unblock of task 5566 (Graphiti decisions_and_rationale episode 16e38e28-819d-4293-8656-ba5c1f5e81bd, 2026-07-29: cite a real live task instead of rewording, because "rewording destroys a real pointer"). The two were never truly contradictory — this entry's clause was about a NON-MARKER doc comment where no citation would apply, while 16e38e28 is about a line with a genuine follow-up — but the unscoped wording made them read as opposed. The orphaning risk is real and is now handled as case (3) above rather than as a reason to avoid citing. Mem0 0431790f-4e4e-4a8a-b0dd-f78656819384 (with 85c1120b-6e81-4bc9-890c-521d07ed25cf), which already listed citing a live non-terminal task among three legitimate fixes, is consistent with this ratified policy.

(Consolidation, 2026-07-17, Stage 1 run a0318deb-afac-4667-86fb-f33427061f84: merges 3 rediscoveries of the same PHANTOM_PHRASES/phantom-tracking gotcha: b68c69b4, c734b74b, 0daf5014. This is the SOLE canonical entry for this topic — if about to write a new memory documenting the PTODO "tracked separately"/phantom-tracking phrase gotcha, append to this entry or write a stamped peer under topic `ptodo-phantom-tracking-phrases`; do not write a new unstamped entry.)

395d6a09-665a-419c-b255-40f64e3e0d37.content: Regenerating crates/reify-audit/ptodo-baseline.txt is asymmetrically expensive by DB mode. `ptodo-baseline-gen --project-root <root>` under `env -u REIFY_PTODO_TASKS_DB` (degraded/structural-only, the mode the ratchet gate runs in) finishes in seconds; the same binary with REIFY_PTODO_TASKS_DB pointed at a real tasks.db exceeded 5 minutes without completing, because the ζ inverse lane walks git history per finding (51 task-cites-deleted-path findings on main as of 2026-08). Budget a long foreground timeout or background+poll for a correct (DB-present, superset) regen — and note that a task worktree has no .taskmaster/, so a correct regen is not available there at all: regenerating in a lane silently drops the DB-dependent `orphaned` fingerprints, yielding a baseline that then fails the `comm -23` subset check wherever the DB IS present.

3c58aef6-7664-4541-9313-dded8592ce38.content: PDOCCOVER's ratchet baseline (crates/reify-audit/pdoccover-baseline.txt) is INERT until `git add`ed: pdoccover.rs's `load_inputs` gates every read — units.rs, the chunks/*.md corpus and the baseline itself — on `ctx.git.ls_files()` membership, reading content from std::fs only for tracked paths. Writing the file and re-running `reify-audit --pattern PDOCCOVER` without staging it looks exactly like the file having no effect. Same trap applies to any hermetic tempdir fixture for this detector: `git init` plus `git add -A` is mandatory, not decoration.

4ec04e82-a134-46ab-91dc-30f6bc960b8f.content: Reify PTODO baseline seeding: regenerate `crates/reify-audit/ptodo-baseline.txt` WITH the task DB set (`REIFY_PTODO_TASKS_DB=/home/leo/src/reify/.taskmaster/tasks/tasks.db target/release/ptodo-baseline-gen --project-root . > ...`), never in degraded mode. A cited line yields an `orphaned` fingerprint only when the DB is reachable, so degraded_live is a strict subset of db_present_live; `tests/infra/test_reify_audit_ptodo.sh` scenario (a) runs the generator under `env -u REIFY_PTODO_TASKS_DB` (task worktrees have no `.taskmaster/`) while `/audit` runs in the main checkout WITH the DB. Seeding from a DB-present run makes the baseline a superset of both so `comm -23 live baseline` stays empty in either context; seeding from a degraded run leaves the main-checkout ratchet red.

d0dcf25a-0d12-4ae6-9355-cadd8e82de49.content: PTODO ratchet gotcha: `target/release/ptodo-baseline-gen` run WITHOUT `REIFY_PTODO_TASKS_DB` degrades its liveness lane to structural-only, so it emits a strict SUBSET of the real fingerprint set — `orphaned` / `unknown-id` kinds are simply not classified and silently vanish from the output. Never regenerate `crates/reify-audit/ptodo-baseline.txt` wholesale from a DB-less run: that drops live orphaned grandfather entries and hands future findings free immunity. For a targeted burndown, delete only the one line you resolved, and only if its kind is structural (`untracked` / `malformed-cite` / `bare-ignore` / `phantom-tracking`), whose absence from a DB-less live set IS conclusive. Point it at the real DB with `REIFY_PTODO_TASKS_DB=/home/leo/src/reify/.taskmaster/tasks/tasks.db` when you need the liveness lane.

Completed: serve: Host allow-list entries that still differ from the Host a browser sends (non-canonical INTAKE_PUBLIC_URL hosts; loopback entries on port 80)
Description: Found while planning task 35 (follow-up id agent-followup-35). Task 35 makes src/scoping_intake/cli.py derive the prospect site's Host allow-list entry from INTAKE_PUBLIC_URL the way a browser writes Host: the host in lower case, no port when it is the scheme's default (80 for http, 443 for https) or empty, any other port kept, and an IPv6 address in brackets. The derivation lives in a helper, cli._host_header(scheme, hostname, port), which _public_url calls. web.py RequestHandler._admission_refusal answers only a Host header that is in site.hosts by string equality, and otherwise replies 421 'Not found'. Two cases are left. Both are outside task 35's scope and unlikely in the deployed setup: deploy/README.md sets INTAKE_PUBLIC_URL=https://<machine>.<tailnet>.ts.net, and the units use ports 8471 and 8472.

(1) Host spellings a browser rewrites beyond case and port. Measured on 2026-10-08 with headless Chrome 151 and a capture server: http://[0:0:0:0:0:0:0:1]:P/ is sent as Host [::1]:P. Per the WHATWG URL standard but NOT measured: a non-ASCII name such as https://bücher.example is sent in punycode (xn--bcher-kva.example), and IPv4 shorthand such as http://127.1:P/ is sent as 127.0.0.1:P. urllib.parse.urlsplit keeps all three as typed (CPython 3.14.4, the project venv). The allow-list entry therefore never matches, and every prospect request gets 421. The fix is either to derive the entry the way the browser does (IPv6 compression via ipaddress, IDNA/UTS-46, IPv4 parsing) or to refuse such values at start with UnusablePublicUrl, naming the variable.

(2) cli._loopback_hosts(port) always writes the port: {127.0.0.1:P, localhost:P}. A browser leaves out port 80 for http; measured in Chrome 151, http://intake.example:80/ is sent as Host intake.example. So with --prospect-port 80 or --operator-port 80, a browser at http://localhost/ sends Host 'localhost' and gets 421. The operator site would also refuse http://127.0.0.1/. cli._host_header from task 35 could build these entries too.

Files: src/scoping_intake/cli.py and tests/test_serve.py. Test through tests/test_serve.py's composed() / cli.sites_for, asserting sites.prospect.hosts and sites.operator.hosts.
Analysis: STATE ON MAIN (8541f87, task 35 merged; this worktree's baseline `uv run pytest` = 184 passed).
- cli._public_url checks INTAKE_PUBLIC_URL with urlsplit, then derives PublicUrl.host with cli._host_header(scheme, hostname, port). That helper puts an IPv6 address in brackets and leaves the port out when it is DEFAULT_PORTS[scheme]; urlsplit has already lower-cased the host.
- Commit 99258fd already refuses a non-ASCII host and port 0. So the IDNA half of case (1) is done, and the remaining work is IPv6, IPv4 and other host spellings.
- cli._loopback_hosts(port) always writes f"{LOOPBACK}:{port}" and f"localhost:{port}".
- web.RequestHandler._admission_refusal answers only a Host that is in Site.hosts, by string equality, and otherwise replies 421.

MEASURED WHILE PLANNING. Headless Chrome 151.0.7922.169, 2026-10-08, through a capture proxy on an ephemeral loopback port. No service port was touched. The recipe is in memory topic browser-host-header.

Completed: Check Host, Origin and password before reading a POST body: one ordered refusal chain (web.py RequestHandler)
Description: In src/scoping_intake/web.py, a POST's refusals are applied in two places, in an order that reads the body before deciding whether the request may be answered at all.

do_POST (web.py:111-117 at main 368e171; after task 7 lands, RequestHandler.do_POST at module level) does these steps in order:
1. Checks the Content-Length header.
2. Reads the body: self.rfile.read(...), up to MAX_FORM_BYTES = 256,000 bytes.
3. Calls _respond, which only then runs _refusal(): Host allow-list (refused.host), same-origin via Sec-Fetch-Site/Origin (refused.origin), then the operator password (refused.password).

Consequences:
(a) A POST with a foreign Host, from another website, or without the operator password still makes the server read up to 256 KB before refusing it.
(b) A foreign-Host POST with a bad Content-Length is answered with the length refusal instead of the Host refusal.
(c) The refusal policy has two homes: the inline length checks in do_POST and the _refusal() chain. This is docs/code-quality.md heuristic 10, 'uniformly enforced': one mechanism everywhere, and the invariant's definition has one home.

Proposal: one ordered refusal chain run before any body is read. The order is Host, then origin, then password, then length (missing or unreadable as malformed, over the limit as too long), then read the form. Keep every refusal's route name, status and page.

Tests: through make_server with a bare socket client, as tests/test_web.py does after task 7. A foreign-Host POST with a bad length is refused as refused.host (421), and a refused request's body is never read. One way to show the second: declare a Content-Length larger than the body sent and confirm the refusal still arrives at once, before the 30-second socket timeout.

Smoke-testing gotcha for scoping-intake (current as of task 20, replaces the task-7 text that named do_POST as the length refuser): web.py's RequestHandler._refusal() decides every refusal before any body is read. It checks Host (refused.host, 421), then a POST's origin (refused.origin, 403), then the password (refused.password, 401), then a POST's Content-Length; only when none refuses does _respond() read the form, so a refused POST's body is never read. A Content-Length that is missing or not a decimal is refused under the route name refused.malformed with the page 'Malformed request'. A decimal length over MAX_FORM_BYTES, or with more digits than MAX_FORM_BYTES has, is refused under refused.too-long with the page 'Too long'. Both are HTTP 400, and the log line records only method, route name and status. Because the length is judged last, a POST that also breaks an earlier rule gets that rule's status instead: an operator-listener POST without credentials and without Content-Length is 401, not 400, and a foreign-Host POST with a bad length is 421. Before task 7 every length case was one refused.length / 'Too long' refusal, which misled the first smoke pass of review-scoping_intake-20261007 (finding R8, fk-d79ef903b73e). curl -X POST with no --data sends no Content-Length, so a curl-driven walk of the flow is still refused (as malformed, once Host, origin and password pass) on consent, write-up and delete: pass --data '' (or use urllib, which sends Content-Length: 0). solar_challenge: why the Bristol PVGIS TMY reads low (measured by the task 285 architect on 2026-10-01, main abd0bcc, pvlib 0.15.1).
- Database: pvlib's unversioned PVGIS URL serves v5.3 (PVGIS-SARAH3 + ERA5). The cached tmy_5dc8c8bca218 equals a fresh v5_3 TMY.
- Bristol TMY GHI is 992.3 kWh/m². The 2005-2020 seriescalc annual totals run from 1006.3 to 1141.6, mean 1069.5. SARAH2 (v5_2) shows the same gap: 990.8 vs 1072.3.
- Cause: every TMY month is an unaltered real month (within 0.4%). ISO 15927-4 picked a darker-half month (rank 1-8 of 16) in 11 of 12 calendar months. August 2008 is -23%, and July-September come from 2008, the darkest year.
- The project's ModelChain on a 4 kW south 35° system gives 4328 kWh AC from the raw TMY vs a mean of 4677 over the 16 real years (-7.5%).
- Scaling the whole TMY's ghi/dni/dhi by one factor to the 2005-2020 mean GHI lands within -1.9..+0.4% of the 16-year mean AC at 7 UK sites. Monthly factors are no better and push Bristol's August peak GHI to 1088 W/m² (16-year record 944).

Description: FINDING (review 20260928T154500, control deep read; PLAUSIBLE — mechanism read in code at HEAD 417e306, partition timing from kernel defaults, not measured).

On a network PARTITION (packets dropped, not connection refused) the pool pre-ping or an in-flight write blocks for the kernel retransmission timeout (~15 min); each reconnect then costs the 10 s connect timeout. Completed: _serial_pytest_str's bare `-o addopts=` silently drops root addopts tokens it never meant to strip (import mode AND the smoke/integration/warm_lane_bash deselection)
Description: orchestrator/src/orchestrator/verify.py::_serial_pytest_str rewrites every pytest invocation to run serially by appending `-p no:xdist -o addopts=`. Its own docstring states the INTENT of `-o addopts=` narrowly: clear the pyproject-level `-n auto` per task 2045's shared-venv-mutation recovery. But `-o addopts=` is a WHOLESALE BLANK, not a targeted removal, so it also drops every other token the root addopts carries. Root pyproject.toml:66 carries two more, both load-bearing:

    addopts = "--import-mode=importlib -m 'not smoke and not integration and not warm_lane_bash'"

TWO DISTINCT CONSEQUENCES, the second worse than the first.

(1) COLLECTION MODE. Dropping --import-mode=importlib reverts pytest to prepend mode, which breaks any command whose collection depends on importlib. Measured on the task/4377 worktree, single variable, HEAD=40204bf476:
    `uv run --project shared pytest --tb=short -q --timeout=300 -p no:xdist -o addopts= tests/scripts/ scripts/tests/`
      -> 4197 collected + 2 collection errors ("import file mismatch"), rc=2
    same command + `--import-mode=importlib`
      -> 4218 collected, 4216 passed / 2 skipped, rc=0
The scripts module test_command is a deliberate UNION of tests/scripts/ and scripts/tests/ (task 3384/3460); the two dirs share three basenames (conftest.py, test_restart_all_orchestrators.py, test_reviewer_redundancy_diagnostic.py) and neither has an __init__.py. dark-factory-orchestrator.yaml:105-110 states the safety argument in as many words and rests it explicitly on root addopts setting importlib. This surfaced as esc-4377-3, which red-legged task 4377's verify for a defect entirely outside that task.

(2) MARKER SELECTION -- the wider hazard, and NOT fixed by the narrow unblock. Blanking addopts also drops `-m 'not smoke and not integration and not warm_lane_bash'`, so a serial re-run COLLECTS AND RUNS the smoke, integration and warm_lane_bash buckets that every normal run deselects. A serial recovery re-run therefore does not execute the same test set as the run it is recovering, and can go red on tests the primary path never intended to run. cockpit/tests/test_root_config_smoke_deselection.py:365-367 already records this in-repo: "A bare `-o addopts=` with nothing carried over also works today but would silently run collection under different semantics than every real root-bound run."

PROPOSED FIX. Stop blanking. Emit `-o addopts=<root addopts minus the xdist tokens>` -- derive the override from root pyproject.toml and strip only the token(s) actually targeted. The in-repo precedent for exactly this shape already exists: cockpit/tests/test_root_config_smoke_deselection.py::_addopts_without_marker_filter (:202). Note `-p no:xdist` is already appended independently and disables the plugin outright, so the `-n auto` removal is belt-and-suspenders -- task 2045's intent is preserved.

REGRESSION COVERAGE. Assert a serial-rewritten command still carries the root import mode AND the root marker deselection. Both directions matter: importlib is what keeps the two-directory scripts union collectable, and the marker filter is what keeps the recovery run's test SET equal to the primary run's.

That is a narrow per-module unblock only -- it does nothing for consequence (2), and nothing for any other module whose collection or selection depends on a root addopts token. This task supersedes it as the general fix; the explicit flag becomes redundant but stays correct.

BLAST RADIUS: every module whose verify leg reaches the serial confirm/recovery re-run, which is the ENV_TRANSIENT retry path for the whole fleet.

Completed: Train landing path: any move of main under a train verify (e.g. a direct docs commit) derails the train and can strand its members until manual rescue; retry the CAS via reverify_on_rebase instead
Description: PREMISE CORRECTED 2026-09-23 (interactive session, re-read of current code + runs.db). The original 2026-09-03 description claimed a moved main makes the train land an UNVERIFIED re-merged tip. That cannot happen, and the real defect is the inverse: the train DERAILS and discards its verify. The fix direction (option (a) below) is unchanged.

=== MECHANISM (verified in code) ===
`orchestrator/src/orchestrator/merge_queue.py::_do_train_merge` reads `main_sha = await git_ops.get_main_sha()` BEFORE the train verify and passes it as `expected_main=main_sha` to `_journal_landed_then_advance` WITHOUT `reverify_on_rebase=True`. If main moved during the verify, `git_ops.py::GitOps.advance_main`'s attempt loop rebases/re-merges the tip onto the new main (`rebased = True`), skips the "Reverify-on-rebase gate" (flag unset), and reaches `git update-ref refs/heads/main <rebased> <expected_main>`. `expected_main` is the stale pre-verify value, so the CAS is certain to fail → `AdvanceOutcome('cas_failed')` → `_do_train_merge` emits `train_derailed` ('Train merge advance failed: cas_failed') and returns blocked; members are re-driven as singles. The rebased sha can never land, so there is NO unverified-landing hole. The task-2154 "Correctness (amendment)" comment after the advance call ("can transparently rebase merge_commit onto a moved main and land the REBASED sha directly") describes an unreachable path whenever expected_main is passed, and it always is here. The `_await_unadvanced_predecessor` docstring states the correct behaviour ("For a TRAIN it is terminal").

Contrast: the single-branch site (`SpeculativeMergeWorker._finalize_inflight`) passes `reverify_on_rebase=True`, gets `rebased_pending_reverify`, runs `merge_gates.py::_reverify_rebased_tree` (disjoint delta → advance with no re-verify; overlap → re-verify), re-anchors base_sha, and retries the CAS. A direct docs commit during a solo verify is therefore absorbed in ~2 min (measured 09-18, task 5578); during a train verify it costs the whole train.

=== MEASURED COST (runs.db `data/orchestrator/runs.db`, read-only, 2026-09-23) ===
train_merged 37, train_derailed 29 all-time; 5 derails are `cas_failed`: coalesce-3215 (07-31, 27 min verify lost), 3146 (07-31, 27 min), 4097 (08-16, 29 min), 4545 (09-06, 53 min), 4574 (09-16, 72 min; the mover was a direct docs commit 4 s after the train read main). Each also re-drives every member solo, and 4574's derail re-pended the tip with a stacked branch carrying the other member's commits (see memory feedback-a-lost-cas-train-derail-repends-the-tip-with-a-stacked-branch). Operational side-effect: interactive sessions are now deferring direct-to-main docs commits whenever the queue is live, because the train case is not separable from the harmless solo case.

=== FIX ===
INVARIANT (unchanged): a train never advances main to a tree no gate verified. NEW GOAL: a moved main does not discard a green train verify when the intervening delta cannot interact with the train.

candidates.content: Reify gotcha (measured 2026-10-12): a top-level user `fn` whose name is a compiler builtin (e.g. `clamp`, `von_mises`; check with `reify_compiler::is_known_builtin`) silently REPLACES the builtin for the whole module, with no warning. Example: `fn clamp(x: Real, lo: Real, hi: Real)` makes `clamp(5mm, 0mm, 3mm)` fail "no matching overload". So doc examples and fixtures that declare fns must use non-builtin names. Also, Tensor component access `t.xx` is not implemented ("member access not yet supported: .xx").

Reify user `fn` declarations resolve calls in SOURCE ORDER only: crates/reify-compiler/src/compile_builder/functions_phase.rs:74-92 passes `&ctx.functions` (prior-compiled fns only) to compile_function, so a fn is absent from its own resolution table while its body compiles. Consequence: self-recursion, mutual recursion and forward references all fall through OverloadResolution::NoUserFunctions (type_compat.rs:1161-1165) to a `std::<name>` stdlib FunctionCall (expr.rs:3139, result type guessed as the first arg's type at expr.rs:3582-3599 with no diagnostic for >=1-arg calls) and evaluate to silent Undef via reify_stdlib::eval_builtin. The MAX_RECURSION_DEPTH=256 guard at crates/reify-expr/src/lib.rs:1615 is therefore DEAD for self-recursion — the self-call never becomes a UserFunctionCall. Base-case-only calls appear to work because Conditional is lazy (reify-expr/src/lib.rs:674-686), which masks the defect.

Reify compiler resolves unknown function-call callees PERMISSIVELY: a call to a name with no user `fn` (e.g. a stdlib builtin like `complex_mul` or a brand-new `complex_exp`) is NOT rejected — resolve_function_overload (reify-compiler/src/type_compat.rs) returns NoUserFunctions and expr.rs falls to a first-arg-type fallback emitting a `std::<name>` FunctionCall with no Error diagnostic; runtime dispatch goes to reify_stdlib::eval_builtin. Consequence: adding a new stdlib builtin requires touching ONLY its eval_* module (e.g. complex.rs); .ri examples calling it compile clean and pass crates/reify-compiler/tests/examples_smoke.rs. There is no compiler-side builtin signature registry.

Reify: the "unrecognised function name compiles silently / green check" defect (a bareword call to a nonexistent name with >=1 arg gets ZERO diagnostics; expr.rs terminal first-arg-type fallback, ~expr.rs:3851) is ALREADY OWNED by a three-task chain — #5371 (warn-mode closed-world manifest, in flight on branch task/5371, creates crates/reify-compiler/src/unresolved_function.rs), #5997 (flip Warning -> Severity::Error), #6014 (delete the fallback). Evidence base: docs/notes/fallback-soundness-analysis-2026-08-03.md (regime (b)) + PRD docs/prds/v0_6/builtin-signature-registry.md boundary test #8. Before planning any "unknown builtin/function name should be an error" work, check that chain first — a standalone fix collides head-on with task/5371's file set (expr.rs, units.rs, reify-core/src/diagnostics.rs).

Generic-user-fns call-site testing (tasks 4231-β/γ/δ): `reify_test_support::compile_source` (NO stdlib) already resolves `5mm`, `Length`, and `List<…>`, so generic-fn call-site tests like `fn id<T>(x:T)->T{x} structure S{ let v = id(5mm) }` need no stdlib. Inspect the call's compile-time type via `module.templates[0].value_cells[].default_expr.result_type` and eval it via `reify_expr::eval_expr(expr, &reify_expr::EvalContext::new(&reify_ir::ValueMap::new(), &module.functions))`. Gotchas: (1) whole-number literals like `42.0`/`3.0` lex as `Int`, not `Real` — use `42.5`/`1.5` for a guaranteed Real; (2) `compile_function` does NOT type-check a fn body against its declared return type, so trivial/mismatched bodies (`{ value }`, `{ 0 }`) compile cleanly; (3) `DiagnosticCode` (reify-core/src/diagnostics.rs) derives Debug+serde and is `#[non_exhaustive]` with no manual `as_str`/Display match — adding a variant needs only the variant + doc comment, no exhaustive-arm updates; attach to a diagnostic via `.with_code(DiagnosticCode::X)`.

reify-compiler compile_builder has a load-bearing asymmetry in which function table each body kind compiles against: `fn` bodies (functions_phase.rs) compile against `&ctx.functions` — the user-only table built up in source order — while entity/field/post-pass bodies get `&ctx.resolution_functions` (merged with prelude afterward at functions_phase.rs:105); imported user modules are not special-cased, since module_dag.rs feeds each import's CompiledModule into the prelude slice via compile_with_prelude_refs, so imported fns behave like prelude fns everywhere. Static fns inside trait bodies hit the same hazard from a different cause: traits_phase.rs:173 passes None for compile_function's prelude_template_registry, so struct-constructor calls there also miss the merged table (regular fn bodies are fine — functions_phase passes Some(&merged_registry)). Consequence, measured 2026-09-15: a `fn` body call to a LATER-declared sibling, or either half of a mutually-referential pair, resolves to `OverloadResolution::NoUserFunctions` and falls through to the terminal first-arg fallback in expr.rs — a wrong-arity call is silently mistyped from arg0 — while the identical call from an entity body is a hard "no matching overload" error (entity forward-reference is pinned by boundary2_producer.rs's `compile_function_forward_reference`, which is why the inconsistency is easy to miss). Any diagnostic added at the FunctionCall fallback must gate on the module's declared names, not just builtin membership.

Reify stdlib-vs-user fn name collisions are resolved silently by `merge_prelude_functions` (crates/reify-compiler/src/lib.rs:268): a local user `fn` SHADOWS a stdlib `pub fn` when their `(name, arity, param_types)` triple matches (first-wins, user-first, no diagnostic). Consequence: adding a `pub fn constant_field<D,C>(value:C)` to stdlib/fields.ri does NOT break examples/generics/unbound_param.ri, whose local `fn constant_field<D,C>(value:C){value}` stub shadows the stdlib version in that file. `resolve_function_overload` (type_compat.rs:735) returns Ambiguous only when ≥2 *surviving* same-name candidates match — the prelude dup is excluded before resolution.

Reify compiler gotcha (measured 2026-10-09, task 8393 σ): `names_phase::build_resolution_names` puts every PRELUDE fn name into `ctx.declared_fn_names`, so `expr.rs`'s terminal first-arg fallback never warns "unresolved function" for a stdlib name. Before σ, user fn bodies (and fn param defaults and trait-static fn bodies) compiled against the user-only `ctx.functions`, so a stdlib .ri call there silently lowered to a generic `FunctionCall` and evaluated to Undef (OpContractViolation) with no diagnostic. When debugging a silent Undef from a call inside a fn body, check which function table that body compiled against before blaming eval.

Reify gotcha (stdlib): a `.ri` fn declaration with a body shadows the same-named eval builtin. resolve_function_overload returns UserFunctionCall for any fn with a `.ri` body, so the evaluator runs the body and NEVER reaches eval_builtin/eval_trajectory. Therefore an unwired stub body with a numeric placeholder (e.g. `{ [0.0] }` or `{ 0.0 * 1s }`) returns plausible-but-wrong values with NO diagnostic — a silent-wrong-value defect class. The fix pattern (used by gcode_import->gcode_import_lower, input_shape->input_shape_apply, and the EndEffectorTrack *_at accessors): make the `.ri` body delegate to an UNDECLARED `*_at` intrinsic, which resolves NoUserFunctions->FunctionCall->eval_builtin->eval_trajectory; wire eval_trajectory to route both the public and `*_at` names to the impl. Prefer returning Value::Undef (loud) over a numeric placeholder for any unwired stdlib stub.

Measured enumeration of the reify compiler's terminal first-arg-type fallback (crates/reify-compiler/src/expr.rs:3568-3584), against main 36738b9b92, from the 2026-08-03 fallback-soundness investigation (session investigate-reify-995019; per-name data in xref.json beside analysis.md): 231 eval-dispatchable builtins; 110 typed explicitly by the NoUserFunctions ladder; 121 ride the terminal fallback; 93 are MISTYPED; 16 are coincidentally first-arg-correct; 5 dimension-dependent; 7 shadowed by typed stdlib .ri decls. The LSP BUILTIN_FUNCTIONS table advertises 35 signatures the compiler contradicts. Crucially it is not only a typing defect — it produces WRONG VALUES: floor(2.5mm) returns Int(0), the floor of the SI-erased f64. Initial triage from a single escalation had estimated five affected builtins; the true count is 93, i.e. a genuine soundness hole rather than a handful of missing registrations. This motivated PRD docs/prds/v0_6/builtin-signature-registry.md, whose task omega deletes the fallback outright.

In reify-compiler, a fn body's own call expressions resolve overloads only against ctx.functions (prior sibling user-defined fns in source order) — NOT the prelude-merged ctx.resolution_functions. Only a structure's value-cell expressions (compiled in entities_phase.rs) resolve calls against ctx.resolution_functions, which includes stdlib/prelude functions. So a test that needs a user-defined generic overload (e.g. unwrap_or<T,E>(r: Result<T,E>,..)) to compete against a stdlib overload (e.g. option_recovery.ri's unwrap_or<T>(o: Option<T>,..)) must place the competing call inside a structure's `let`/value-cell, not inside another fn's body — a call inside a fn body would never see the stdlib candidate and any overload-disambiguation signal there is vacuous. Discovered while implementing task 4991 (Option/Result overload disambiguation); see crates/reify-compiler/tests/result_combinator_overload_tests.rs doc comments for the concrete example.

Reify stdlib pattern for wiring an evaluator-backed intrinsic WITHOUT a compiler change (used by gcode_import->gcode_import_lower, input_shape->input_shape_apply, and trajectory evaluate_profile/_dot/_ddot/profile_duration -> *_at, task 4539): declare the user-facing `fn foo(args) -> T { foo_at(args) }` in the .ri stdlib, where `foo_at` is an UNDECLARED name. Dispatch: (1) the .ri `foo` shadows any same-named eval_builtin so it resolves Resolved->UserFunctionCall; (2) its body calls undeclared `foo_at`, which resolves NoUserFunctions->FunctionCall->eval_builtin; (3) the crate's eval_<module> router (e.g. reify-stdlib/src/trajectory/mod.rs::eval_trajectory) routes BOTH `foo` and `foo_at` to the same Rust composer. The compiler's first-arg type-fallback gives the undeclared `*_at` call an inferred type that is discarded (the outer UserFunctionCall uses the declared return type); compile_function applies no body-vs-return-type check, so no compiler edit is needed. Composers return Value::Undef (loud not-computed) on unmarshalable input, never a numeric placeholder.

Fallback-closure program baseline (measured 2026-08-03, main 36738b9b92, agent-team enumeration): the reify compiler NoUserFunctions ladder (expr.rs:3066-3604) explicitly types 110 of 231 eval-dispatchable builtins; 121 ride the terminal first-arg-type fallback (expr.rs:3568-3584); 93 of those are MISTYPED (incl. floor/ceil/round, which return Value::Int of the SI-erased f64 — silently wrong VALUE for dimensioned args, probe: floor(2.5mm) evals Int(0)); 16 are correctly first-arg-typed (transform_compose/orient_slerp/complex_* class); 5 vary by arg dimension (sinh/cosh/tanh/log10/remap); 7 are shadowed by typed stdlib .ri decls. The LSP BUILTIN_FUNCTIONS table advertises 35 signatures the compiler contradicts. Reify gotcha (measured 2026-10-09, task 8232 branch 7c98a0ba63): a generic trait assoc fn, either fn-level `fn pick<T>(self, x: T) -> T` or trait-level `trait Boxed<T>`, never compiles cleanly, because traits.rs assoc_fn_sig resolves its signature with empty type-param sets and emits UnresolvedType. The expr.rs instance TraitMethodCall arm nonetheless lowers `obj.(Trait::f)(5mm)` to a UserFunctionCall whose result_type and value-cell cell_type are a raw TypeParam("T"): it clones CompiledAssocFnSig.return_type, and the free-fn helper instantiate_call_return_type (which takes &CompiledFunction) is not applied there. The leak is masked only by those definition-site errors, so whoever lands #7866 (generic trait assoc fns end-to-end) must instantiate the return type on that arm too, or reify-eval's assert_value_cell_types_representable panics (follow-up ticket tkt_0RVKFWRB3TXGJXH58XD83M5ZJQ).

Reify compiler gotcha (measured 2026-10-01, main 15634a417f): inside a trait INSTANCE assoc-fn body, every `self.member` / bare member read types as dimensionless Real, regardless of the member's declared type. Cause: crates/reify-compiler/src/functions.rs compile_assoc_function builds its body scope without set_template_registry, so expr.rs member_access_on_structure_like hits its registry-miss permissive fallback for the StructureRef(conformer) receiver. E.g. `fn lateral_area(self) -> Scalar<Area> { pi * diameter * length }` compiles its body to Real. Any static check on assoc-fn body types (comparison guards, body-vs-return reconciliation) will false-positive or false-negative there. Tracked as #8118; sibling #7855 is the same erase-to-Real class for trait-typed fn params.

Reify compiler limitations on fn signatures (as of 2026-05-11 main): (1) fn_param grammar at tree-sitter-reify/grammar.js:83-87 is `seq(name, ':', type)` with NO default-value slot — `param: T = expr` does not parse; (2) compile_function at crates/reify-compiler/src/functions.rs:11-15 hardcodes `empty_structs: HashSet<String>` and `empty_traits: HashSet<String>` passed to resolve_type_expr_with_aliases, because "functions are compiled before the trait/structure registries are built". Net effect: fn signatures CANNOT reference any user-defined trait/structure name (including stdlib types like ElasticMaterial, ElasticOptions, ElasticResult, Solid) — they resolve to Type::Real with an "unresolved type" Error diagnostic. Anyone filing a task that adds a fn declaration to the stdlib must either use builtin-only types in the signature OR depend on task 3440 (resolve stdlib trait/structure names in fn signatures, two-pass compile).

In reify-compiler, FUNCTION/builtin call arguments are matched by EXACT type equality in resolve_function_overload (type_compat.rs:288-312) — NO trait-conformance widening; failure emits "no matching overload" (not E_TypeMismatch). Nominal trait-conformance ARG checking (check_trait_arg_conformance / emit_leaf_conformance_for_arg_type, conformance/mod.rs:130-411) fires ONLY for STRUCTURE-CONSTRUCTOR args, requires the arg already typed StructureRef/TraitObject, and emits DiagnosticCode::TypeNotConformingToTrait ("type X does not conform to trait Y required by param Z"). Bare Rust eval_builtins (bind/couple/prismatic in reify-stdlib/joints.rs + snapshot.rs) have NO compile-time signature; expr.rs NoUserFunctions arm types them via per-name geometry hooks else first-arg fallback with zero arg checking. Consequence: passing a non-conforming value to a lowercase builtin (e.g. bind(coupling,...)) CANNOT raise a compile-time type error without new machinery (typed builtin signatures + joint-builtin→structure typing + function-call conformance path). KINEMATIC_FUNCTION_OVERRIDES does not exist in code (PRD prose only); kinematic_query_result_type has 1 caller (expr.rs:1408) for geometry queries interferes/min_clearance, unrelated to DrivingJoint.

Reify trait associated-fn instance dispatch (task ζ/3941): the `self` receiver is bound by passing the receiver object as the first arg to a UserFunctionCall (Design A), NOT by inlining. A `sub pin : Pin` Ident evaluates to a `Value::StructureInstance` at `ValueCellId(parent, sub_name)` (materialized by task 3540 SIR-α), and member access on a `Type::StructureRef`-typed value compiles to `CompiledExprKind::IndexAccess(obj, Literal(String(member)))` which evals via `Value::StructureInstance.fields.get(k)` (reify-expr/src/lib.rs ~1095). So `self.diameter` inside an assoc-fn body works with zero new evaluator entry point. Key naming constraint: a CompiledFunction's body references params/lets via `ValueCellId(func.name, ...)`, and eval binds args under the same `func.name`, so a function MUST be compiled under the exact name it is registered/called by — you cannot rename a CompiledFunction after compilation without rewriting its body's ValueCellIds. Trait-static fns (task η) follow this by cloning+renaming the FnDef BEFORE compiling (trait_static_fn_symbol = "Trait::method"); instance fns need a per-conformer symbol compiled the same way.

content: Discovery (reify, probed 2026-10-13, fixture tests/prd-gate/fixtures/s8_user_fn_shadows_builtin.ri): a user `fn map_or(a: Real, b: Real, c: Real) -> Real { 222.0 }` called as map_or(1.0, 2.0, 3.0) evaluates to undef — reify-expr's UserFunctionCall arm intercepts map_or/3 (and map_err/2, the ten option_recovery combinators, solve_load_cases/5|6) by BARE NAME and arity, swallowing the user's function. Description: simulate_home simulates a home AND prices it: in one 180-line body (home.py:292-472, radon cyclomatic 32 = grade E, complexipy cognitive 37) it fetches weather, validates heat-pump weather length, runs PV, expands it, generates load, adds heat-pump load, aligns, builds the battery, chooses between the two dispatch paths with a three-flag predicate and re-branches on it every timestep (home.py:374-415), then prices import cost, grid-charge cost and SEG export revenue with its own warning policy (home.py:424-454) before assembling results. The pricing is the briefing's SEG-valuation convention's enforcement point, so a change to physics orchestration and a change to pricing edit the same function.

Proposal: Split into private steps with one purpose each - demand assembly (load + heat pump), dispatch-path selection returning one per-timestep callable, the timestep loop, and a pricing step that turns flows into import cost, grid-charge cost and SEG revenue - leaving simulate_home a short composition; no public signature changes.
