solar_challenge load.py gotcha (measured 2026-10-14 on main e5d7e80, task 711 architect, CPython 3.12.3): both load paths step through the window's days by adding an absolute pd.Timedelta(days=1) to a tz-aware Europe/London midnight. (1) If the window starts in BST and crosses the autumn clock change, every later day is labelled 23:00 on the previous date, so its month (and richardsonpy's day_of_year/weekday) is a day early. A deterministic 2024-07-01..2025-06-30 profile (3,400 kWh) totals 3,323.6 kWh instead of 3,325.0. (2) _generate_elexon_profile's `while current_date <= end_date` drops the last day of a window that starts in GMT and ends in BST, because that day's label is 01:00 BST, after the 00:00 end. The trim/pad block then fills that day with the previous day's mean power: 2024-03-30..04-01 gives 30.3128 kWh, with April 1 at March's seasonal factor. Calendar-year windows (Jan 1-Dec 31) label every day correctly. Review finding R6 (fk-1d920c89e872) covers DST placement in these loops. Cost for test design: a seeded stochastic full calendar year takes about 25 s (365 richardsonpy days); a deterministic Elexon year takes about 0.1 s.

content: solar_challenge test gotcha, measured 2026-10-17 by task 795's architect on main cafd8b7 (CPython 3.12.3), offline with HTTP(S)_PROXY pointed at a dead port. A full synthetic UTC 1990 TMY year round-trips exactly through WeatherCache: 8760 hourly rows built like tests/unit/test_home_heat_pump.py::_dark_tmy_year, stored with weather_cache.put(frame, "tmy", Location.bristol()). get_tmy_data returns it with pd.testing.assert_frame_equal holding, tz UTC, freq h. So a heat-pump simulate_home called with no weather_data runs offline from that cache, at 0.6-1.9 s per one-day run. A dark year generates 0.0, so a test asserting PV generation needs irradiance on its simulated day. Diffuse light alone works: ghi = dhi = 100 W/m², dni 0, on 1990-01-15 09:00-15:00 UTC gave 2.13 kWh from a 4 kW array on 2024-01-15.

75c663e5-6cf6-471b-be93-a70dd81e7340.content: solar_challenge CLI test technique (task 731, measured 2026-10-15 on task/731 at 3d067d2, based on main ece941b, pandas 3.0.3): check what a command simulated through its `-o` CSV, with no seed and no spy on cli.home.simulate_home. LoadConfig's default stochastic load is random minute to minute, but load._try_richardsonpy_profile rescales the window to the sum of annual/365 x SEASONAL_FACTORS[month], so pd.read_csv(csv, index_col=0, parse_dates=True)["demand_kw"].sum() equals generate_load_profile(LoadConfig(...), day, day).sum() under pytest.approx (tests/unit/test_cli_home_quick.py; six repeat runs green; reintroducing the old 3400 default, or dropping the -c value, fails exactly its own case). A time of day on the start timestamp does not reach the CSV: the load generators normalise the window to whole days, and `home quick` mutated to start at 2024-06-01 06:00 still saved a CSV from 00:00.

candidates.content: solar_challenge_platform test convention (on main since task 597, verified at 650127d on 2026-10-08): tests/_alembic.py is the one public Alembic helper for tests. alembic_config(url) returns the repo's Config with script_location set absolutely, and upgraded_sqlite(db_file, revision) returns (cfg, engine) for a temp-FILE SQLite upgraded to a revision. New migration test modules should import these rather than copy a private _alembic_config, which test_private_names.py would forbid importing anyway. Use alembic_config("sqlite://") for a static ScriptDirectory chain-link check (tests/control/test_refresh_tick_store.py), and alembic_config(engine.url.render_as_string(hide_password=False)) to downgrade or upgrade a Timescale test database. tests/_migrated_engine.py::migrated_engine still yields an engine already at head.

solar_challenge_platform test convention (task 426, branch task/426; holds once merged): tests/_schema_state.py is the shared reader of what migrations leave in a database. alembic_revision(engine) returns the alembic_version row's revision. chunk_time_intervals(engine) returns a dict mapping relation name to its new-chunk interval (a timedelta). It covers every hypertable and continuous aggregate; an aggregate is keyed by its VIEW name through the timescaledb_information.dimensions-to-continuous_aggregates join, so never hardcode _materialized_hypertable_N. Migration tests (e.g. task 728's telemetry_hh chunk/compression test) should import these rather than write a private _revision or chunk-interval query. tests/integration/test_timeseries_compression.py still has private copies until follow-up ticket tkt_0RVJRF69WPRETSY4DCVFGRDSYX switches it.

When testing Alembic `upgrade head` in-process (via alembic.config.Config + alembic.command.upgrade) in solar_challenge_platform, the test DB MUST be a temp FILE (pytest tmp_path_factory + sqlite:///<file>), never sqlite:///:memory:. Alembic opens its own connection for the upgrade and discards it; a separate reflection/ORM engine on :memory: would see an empty schema. Also set script_location ABSOLUTELY on the Config (cfg.set_main_option) so it doesn't resolve relative to cwd. The Alembic env.py/migration files and tests/ are outside the mypy target (mypy only checks src/solar_challenge_platform), so they aren't strict-type-checked by the verify command.

solar_challenge_platform probe technique (verified by task 588's implementer, 2026-10-11, branch task/588 at 75c229c): a throwaway TestClient probe can reuse the tests/api SQLite harness unchanged (app_client, auth_headers, the seeded Customer A/B) without putting a file in the repo. Write the probe as a pytest test under /tmp/<task>/ and load the harness's conftest as a plugin, from the worktree root: `uv run --extra dev python -m pytest -p tests.api.conftest /tmp/<task>/test_probe.py --rootdir=. -s -p no:cacheprovider`. Use `python -m pytest` because it puts the current directory on sys.path, so `-p tests.api.conftest` imports. Give each case its own consent purpose, because the engine is module-scoped. This measured POST /consent expiry spellings on SQLite in about a minute.

Test convention (solar_challenge_platform, task 909, branch tip 68ca296, pending merge; amends 0cee50f5): a test that reads a database's Alembic revision through an Engine calls tests/_schema_state.alembic_revision(engine), binds the result as `revision` and asserts `revision == X` with a message naming the phase (e.g. "after re-upgrade"), or writes `assert alembic_revision(engine) == CHAIN_HEAD` when there is no message; it no longer inlines SELECT version_num FROM alembic_version. Only 8 inline reads are left, on purpose, so do not copy them: six that keep the same connection for later reads (four back-fill tests in tests/test_billing_migration.py, plus test_full_chain_upgrade_from_empty and test_cbs_amount_due_backfills_a_populated_database in tests/integration/test_full_migration_chain.py), tests/integration/test_migrated_engine.py (it inspects the pooled DBAPI connection) and tests/validation/test_container_smoke.py (psql in a subprocess).

solar_challenge_platform (task 784, branch task/784; holds once merged): no revision under migrations/versions may import solar_challenge_platform, at any depth. tests/test_migrations_frozen.py enforces this via an AST scan. Spell the values as literal SQL in _UPGRADE/_DOWNGRADE tuples, the way 0005 and 0021 now do. 0005's four retention windows are frozen (telemetry 90 d, telemetry_1min 180, telemetry_hh 1095, telemetry_daily 3650). tests/integration/test_retention.py::test_retention_policy_catalog binds the database's (relation, drop_after) jobs to timeseries/retention.py::drop_policies(). So changing a retention window or adding a relation means a new migration plus the catalogue edit, or that Timescale test fails.

Test convention (solar_challenge_platform, task 374 amendment, branch tip 4ef1ea8, pending merge; amends 1b8ee28e and its amendment bd121fb6): tests/_alembic.py adds script_directory() -> ScriptDirectory, the repository's migration scripts read without opening a database, and alembic_config_for(engine) -> Config, pointed at an engine's database with the password kept. Once that merges, a static chain-link check is script_directory().get_revision("NNNN") or script_directory().get_heads(), not ScriptDirectory.from_config(alembic_config("sqlite://")); a Timescale downgrade or upgrade test takes cfg = alembic_config_for(timescale_engine), not alembic_config(engine.url.render_as_string(hide_password=False)). Six files outside task 374's locks (test_feedback_store, test_refresh_tick_store, test_property_never_deleted_schema, test_ingest_health_store, test_signal_last, test_minute_aggregate_chunk_interval) keep the old spellings until follow-up ticket tkt_0RVS0VPMFZ8R6HVMX90GS71DYP moves them, so do not copy those.

Schema in solar-challenge-platform is migration-managed (migrations/versions/0001–NNNN). Any new SQLAlchemy ORM model MUST ship a paired Alembic migration in the same task — adding a model alone is incomplete. Tests use Base.metadata.create_all (e.g. tests/api/conftest.py) which builds tables directly and MASKS a missing migration: the suite passes green while a migration-managed (Postgres) DB lacks the table and raises ProgrammingError at runtime. Pattern to copy: 0008_control_command_log.py (portable op.create_table on all dialects, no dialect guard) — and a new migration advances the chain head, so you must also bump the '0008'-style head-pin assertions in tests/test_migrations.py, tests/test_consent_migrations.py, and tests/integration/test_full_migration_chain.py in the SAME commit (single-head + down_revision chain-tail checks).

Test convention (solar_challenge_platform, task 374, branch tip 9f41ab0, pending merge): tests/test_alembic_config_home.py fails on any call outside tests/_alembic.py whose callee resolves through the module's imports to alembic.config.Config, with no exception set. A new migration test must therefore build its Config with tests._alembic.alembic_config(url): alembic_config("sqlite://") for a static ScriptDirectory chain-link check, or upgraded_sqlite(db_file, revision) for a SQLite file upgraded to a revision. tests/_import_paths.py now also exports import_bindings(tree, package) and dotted_target(expr, bound), the import-binding resolver test_private_names.py uses, so a new AST guard that must resolve a callee through a module's imports should import these rather than write its own.

Correction (solar_challenge_platform, measured on main 71793bd, 2026-10-13): tests/integration/test_rls_postgres.py does NOT yet take its Alembic Config from tests/_alembic.alembic_config on main. Its pg_rls_db fixture still builds Config(alembic.ini) + script_location + sqlalchemy.url itself. Only task 707's unmerged branch (commit e29a5ba) makes that change. Task 374's plan moves it, and every other copy in tests/, onto tests._alembic, and adds a one-home guard (tests/test_alembic_config_home.py). Check `git merge-base --is-ancestor <sha> main` before trusting a remembered "file X uses helper Y".

solar_challenge_platform (observed on main b4a12f5, task 584 architect, 2026-10-13): telemetry_settlement_hh is read directly, bypassing TelemetryStore.query, by ops/reads.py::_read_settlement_coverage (portable SQL, run on SQLite in tests/ops/test_reads.py via settlement_table.metadata.create_all) and validation/run.py::query_smoke_summary (raw SUM/AVG). It is written directly by test fixtures: tests/ops/test_reads.py::_insert_settlement, tests/integration/test_ops_reads_timescale.py, tests/integration/test_ops_dashboard_e2e.py (via settlement_table.insert()) and tests/integration/test_retention.py (raw INSERT). So a schema change to the table (e.g. a new NOT NULL column or a new unique key) must update all of them in the same commit as the migration. Capability manifests cite timescale_store.py::settlement_table, so moving that Table breaks tests/docs/test_capability_manifest_pointers.py.

solar_challenge_platform test gotcha, measured on task 516's probes at main 40a6556, 2026-10-13. To make the database reject ONE statement for one home, attach a before_cursor_execute(retval=True) listener to the test's engine. It replaces the first statement whose bound values equal the home's UUID with "SELECT * FROM no_such_table" and returns type(parameters)().
- Match the UUID against a tuple of (uuid, str(uuid), uuid.hex) using ==. Do not use a set: some bound values are unhashable. psycopg binds uuid.UUID values in dicts, while SQLite binds 32-char hex strings in tuples.
- SQLite raises OperationalError; Postgres raises ProgrammingError (UndefinedTable) and aborts the transaction.
- On Postgres, without a savepoint (session.begin_nested()) the next home's read in the same Session fails with InFailedSqlTransaction. SQLite never aborts the transaction, so only a timescale-lane test can prove a per-home savepoint.

solar_challenge_platform Timescale-lane test placement (observed 2026-10-01, main e277546): tests/integration/test_timescale_store.py's module fixture pauses EVERY policy job (refresh, retention and 0021's compression) via tests/_migrated_engine.migrated_engine(pause_policy_jobs=True), so it is the safe home for a probe that writes fixed historical telemetry and reads a continuous aggregate. tests/integration/test_retention.py runs its jobs live, and test_timeseries_compression.py compresses and downgrades its private DB. Each new module that calls tests/_timescale_container.timescale_url() starts its own container, unless PLATFORM_TEST_TIMESCALE_URL is set. The CAs (telemetry_1min/_hh/_daily) group rows by (bucket, home_id, metric). The module's fresh-home UUID prefixes in use: 11220000, 27300000, 38900000, aaaaaaaa–eeeeeeee, ee000000, ff000000.

Adding any new ORM table + alembic migration in solar_challenge_platform requires bumping the alembic head-pin assertions in tests/test_migrations.py. That file is intentionally NOT slow/integration-marked (so it runs under `pytest -m 'not slow'`) and hard-asserts `alembic upgrade head` lands on a specific revision string (e.g. "0016") in ~6 places (test_upgrade_head_creates_all_s7_tables, test_downgrade_round_trip, test_upgrade_head_reaches_0002, test_0002_downgrade_roundtrip, test_0004_timeseries_ddl_skipped_on_sqlite). A new migration NNNN must update every one of those literals to the new head or the fast suite goes red on an assertion unrelated to the new table. Its test_schema_matches_orm_metadata drift check is scoped `only=set(_S7_TABLES)`, so brand-new non-S7 tables do NOT trip drift. Hermetic tests build schema via `import solar_challenge_platform.models; Base.metadata.create_all(engine)`, so a new model must also be registered in models/__init__.py (import + __all__).

solar_challenge_platform gotcha, measured 2026-10-11 by a probe in task 793's amendment pass. Python compares and hashes two aware datetimes that share one tzinfo object by their wall clock. So two TelemetryRows at 00:30Z and 01:30Z on 2026-10-25, otherwise equal and both written in one ZoneInfo("Europe/London") (01:30 fold=0 and fold=1), are == and hash-equal, and set or dict membership merges them; their in_utc() forms differ. psycopg returns every timestamptz in one cached ZoneInfo per session zone name (psycopg/_tz.py get_tzinfo). So rows read through an engine without db/session.py's "-c timezone=UTC" pin are exposed. One such engine is the dropped-readings drill's bare sa.create_engine(live_config.database_url), whose rows reach dropped_rows' set(survivors). Write such read-backs in UTC (astimezone(timezone.utc)) before comparing, sorting or hashing them, as timescale_store._to_utc does. Follow-up ticket tkt_0RVNM13HJNP7Y8F7ACA453CJWH covers read_raw_rows.

scp-migrate (task 85) cannot be unit-tested by running `alembic upgrade head` on the SQLite fast-suite backend: migrations 0002_rls_policies and 0004_timeseries emit Postgres-only DDL (RLS policies, Timescale hypertables) that fails on SQLite. Test the thin migrate CLI by monkeypatching alembic.command.upgrade and asserting it is called with revision "head"; the real migrate-then-serve proof is the η @timescale capstone.

solar_challenge_platform testing gotcha (measured 2026-09-30, task 544 architect, base 8e89ef2). (1) runtime.asgi builds its graph at import time, so only the first import in a pytest process runs the build, and spies placed around a later cached import see nothing. To pin what serving scp-api constructs, execute the module afresh: spec = importlib.util.find_spec("solar_challenge_platform.runtime.asgi"); module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec); spec.loader.exec_module(module), inside db.session.repoint_scope(). This registers nothing in sys.modules. runpy.run_module emits a RuntimeWarning when the module is already imported, and importlib.reload mutates the cached module that other tests share. (2) run_settle's timescale path runs hermetically, with no Docker, over a file-based SQLite DB holding Base.metadata and no Property rows. TimescaleStore() opens no connection, property_settlement_keys returns [], and the run completes after composing its graph.

solar_challenge_platform SQLAlchemy gotcha for telemetry_settlement_hh. It was measured 2026-10-12 by task 698's architect with throwaway probes at main 553f437. On SQLite, a raw sa.text() SELECT returns home_id as 32-char hex text and hh_start as the storage string '2026-07-01 08:30:00.000000'. A typed Core select over timescale_store.settlement_table, or over a Subquery built from it, returns uuid.UUID and a NAIVE datetime holding the UTC wall clock instead. Wrap it in config.contract.as_utc to make it aware. A derived table select(settlement_table).where(...).subquery() names every column, so renaming ANY table column raises OperationalError, even a column the outer query never selects. On the pinned TimescaleDB image, Postgres pulls such a derived table, including a correlated MAX(method_version) scalar subquery, up into its caller. It plans the same index scan on uq_settlement_home_metric_start_version as the flat form, with one Index Only Scan Backward per candidate row, about 4.8 µs each (64,640 rows ANALYZEd).

solar_challenge_platform architect technique (task 810, 2026-10-14): to run the real test suite, Docker lane included, against a candidate change without editing the task worktree, use a scratch copy. Tar the worktree into /tmp, excluding .venv, .git, node_modules and .task. Apply the candidate files there. Run the worktree's own .venv/bin/python -m pytest from the copy's root with PYTHONPATH=<copy>/src. PYTHONPATH outranks the editable install's .pth entry, so the copy's package is imported, and tests/_alembic.py resolves alembic.ini and migrations/ relative to the copy.

In solar_challenge_platform's migration tests, only two kinds of site are HEAD pins that must move when a migration moves the Alembic head: (a) an alembic_version read-back taken after command.upgrade(cfg, "head") (or after scp-migrate), and (b) script.get_heads() == [...]. Three kinds of site are REVISION pins that must stay literal: `script.get_revision("00NN")` + `.down_revision == "00MM"` link blocks (true forever — rewriting "0018" there as the head would make the paired "0017" go stale at the next bump); tests that upgrade TO a specific revision, e.g. tests/test_billing_migration.py::test_meter_evidence_backfills_rows_that_predate_it; and tests/register_seed.py's LEDGER_COLUMNS / METER_EVIDENCE_* ("what migration 0018 puts on disk"). So register_seed.py is NOT a head-pin site, and there are ten such files, not eleven. Task 195 (planned 2026-09-22) routes every head pin through tests/_migration_head.py::CHAIN_HEAD, guarded by tests/test_migrations.py::test_chain_head_is_the_single_script_head. Once it merges, a migration that moves the head bumps only CHAIN_HEAD plus its own tests.

content: solar_challenge_platform test technique (verified 2026-10-15, task 1093 planning, alembic 1.18 on SQLite and the Timescale lane). Then call cfg.set_main_option("version_locations", str(tmp_dir)) and command.upgrade(cfg, "head"). script_location stays the repo's migrations/, so env.py runs in place and only the probe executes; alembic_version holds the probe's id. 656c17e3-2a6a-4410-9b71-a02fe2df51d6.content: solar_challenge_platform (task 597 amend, branch task/597; holds once merged): dispatch provenance is split across two modules, unlike PRD fleet-dispatch-policy-and-config-freshness §9.4's sketch. control/provenance.py holds only the pure values LimitAction and CommandProvenance and imports no SQLAlchemy; tests/control/test_provenance.py::test_importing_the_provenance_value_loads_no_sqlalchemy pins that. control/command_log_provenance.py holds ProvenanceColumns (of/of_row/provenance), last_limit_writes and last_override_write, which is where β3b and δ1 should import the readers from. tests/_alembic.py provides public alembic_config(url) and upgraded_sqlite(db_file, revision) for migration tests; pending task 374 tracks moving the other Alembic Config copies onto it.

Gotcha + technique (probed 2026-09-28, task 516):
- On Postgres, one failed statement aborts the Session's transaction, and every later statement on that Session raises psycopg InFailedSqlTransaction until ROLLBACK or ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT. SQLite never aborts, so a test proving per-item savepoint isolation must run on the timescale lane (tests._timescale_container.timescale_url + tests._migrated_engine.migrated_engine, about 11 s; Docker is present, so the lane runs in verify).
- To inject a genuine DB error hermetically, listen for before_cursor_execute with retval=True on the test's own engine. Swap the first statement whose bound params name a value for ("SELECT * FROM no_such_table", type(parameters)()).
- Match the value against the tuple (uuid, str(uuid), uuid.hex) using ==, never a set, because params can be unhashable. psycopg binds uuid.UUID in dicts; SQLite binds 32-char hex in qmark tuples.
- session.get() calls answered from the identity map emit no SQL, so they cannot be targeted this way.

a932e9b3-00b0-49f0-9408-38a2458b1622.content: solar_challenge_platform remedy for raw sa.text() reads on SQLite. Measured 2026-10-11 by the task 685 architect at main 6d7c06a, sqlalchemy 2.0.51. Declare result types on the text clause, e.g. `sa.text(sql).columns(hh_start=sa.DateTime(timezone=True), home_id=sa.Uuid())`. SQLAlchemy's SQLite dialect then parses its own stored text ('2026-07-01 08:30:00.000000') into a naive datetime and its hex UUID text into uuid.UUID, while Postgres/psycopg values pass through unchanged, so no fromisoformat or isinstance(str) sniff is needed. The keyword form matches columns by name, so untyped columns and the :since/:limit binds keep working; then apply config.contract.as_utc (naive means UTC) to the datetime.

solar_challenge_platform procedure (task 761, 2026-10-07): to prototype a change without touching the task worktree, reuse the worktree's venv.
1. Export a clean copy: `git archive HEAD | tar -x -C /tmp/<scratch>`.
2. From /tmp/<scratch>, run tests with `PYTHONPATH=/tmp/<scratch>/src:/tmp/<scratch> <worktree>/.venv/bin/python -m pytest ...`. Run strict mypy with `MYPYPATH=/tmp/<scratch>/src <worktree>/.venv/bin/mypy --config-file pyproject.toml src/solar_challenge_platform`.

candidates.content: To answer "did the orchestrator restart, and when?" from runs.db, read the `runs` table: Harness.run writes exactly one row per startup via RunStore.start_run(run_id, project_id, started_at), with the same run_id EventStore uses. Do not use `service_restart` events: service='orchestrator' rows are only the merge-landed coordinator's restart REQUESTS, stamped minutes to hours before the startup, and watchdog, fleet-sweep and manual restarts emit none. Measured 2026-10-17: 0 such rows between 09-04 and 10-12 against 15 `runs` startups. runs.started_at precedes a run's first event by 0.01–43 s.

AMENDMENT to the gotcha "count service_restart events BY SERVICE to judge a restart-tier leaf" (task 5440). Measured 2026-09-26 by task 5441: service_restart is NOT a complete orchestrator-restart witness, so counting by service can still answer wrongly.

MEASURED.
- In the D6 window [2026-09-12T06:43:16Z, 2026-09-26T06:43:16Z), every service_restart row is fused-memory or dashboard, with none for the orchestrator.
- Yet routing_decision events carry SIX distinct orchestrator run_ids in that window. orchestrator/src/orchestrator/harness.py::Harness.run mints a fresh run_id at every startup. The first startup after the 2026-09-12T07:00:51Z config_reload, whose restart_required named usage_cap.scoped_cap_models, is run-063e9795fcf6: its first routing decision was at 2026-09-12T10:11:50Z.
- A Fable-scoped cap_hit (details carrying a `scope` key, max-e, 2026-09-14T14:05:01Z) proves scoped_cap_models WAS live.
- So the parent's worked example ("scoped_cap_models configured but inert", measured 2026-09-13) was most likely already false when it was written.

PRACTICE. To ask "has the orchestrator restarted since config_reload X flagged a leaf restart_required?", use the first-seen timestamp of each distinct events.run_id after X (e.g. `SELECT run_id, MIN(timestamp) FROM events WHERE event_type='routing_decision' AND timestamp >= X GROUP BY run_id`). Do not use service_restart rows.

Hypothesis: the watchdog and fleet-redeploy restart path emits no service_restart event.

Follow-up ticket for scripts/audit_model_admission.py's restart table: tkt_0RV3ER6SYR76TM3XWEMB0RAZZ1.

The dark_factory orchestrator's restart cadence REGRESSED starting 2026-08-24 18:40 — measured 2026-08-25 from `data/orchestrator/runs.db` (`select run_id,started_at,completed_at,total_tasks from runs`).

The documented ~8h fleet-deploy clock had been holding very tightly. Per-run uptimes since 2026-08-21, in order: 19.64h, 8.05, 8.86, 8.18, 8.15, 8.96, 8.69, 11.81, 8.08, **1.26**, 8.40, **0.92**, 9.36, **1.33**. Median 8.40h, min 0.92h. The three sub-1.5h runs are all at the end of the series and are the anomaly:

    run-b0f8f5e8f80d  2026-08-24T18:40:29 -> 19:56:03           1.26h
    run-80237b3330da  2026-08-25T04:20:29 -> 05:15:58           0.92h
    run-00016b4099aa  2026-08-25T14:37:45 -> 15:57:29           1.33h

NOTHING under 8h appears before 2026-08-24 18:40 in the whole window, so this is a DATED REGRESSION, not chronic noise — that timestamp is the sharpest available lead for whatever changed. Possibly-correlated, not established as causal: `total_tasks` jumps 913 -> 947 at the first short run and 949 -> 963 at the third.

WHY IT MATTERS: every restart soft-cancels the in-flight workflow of every running task, returning it to `pending`. CLAUDE.md documents three deliberately orthogonal restart mechanisms — watchdog LIVENESS probes (no clock), the watchdog STALENESS backstop, and the merge-landed COORDINATOR (the last two share the one 8h clock). A sub-hour restart therefore points first at a spurious liveness probe, but that is a hypothesis and was NOT confirmed. `scripts/orchestrator-watchdog.py --report` is strictly read-only and is the safe way to look.

An investigation of the root cause was spawned as a separate session on 2026-08-25 (slug `investigate-df-279403`, brief at ~/.claude/spawn-briefs/orchestrator-restart-cycling-brief.md).

GOTCHA (dark-factory, measured 2026-09-13, task 5440): when checking whether a RESTART-TIER config leaf has taken effect, count `service_restart` events BY SERVICE — a bare count answers the question wrongly, and two separate traps sit on that query.

TRAP 1 — the service matters and is easy to drop. `service_restart` covers three services: fused-memory (116), dashboard (51), orchestrator (47) store-wide. Only an ORCHESTRATOR restart reloads an orchestrator restart-tier leaf (`usage_cap.*`, `max_concurrent_tasks`, pool sizes, `sandbox.backend`, `project_root`, merge-lane structural `git.*`). Measured instance: all four service_restart events in the 31 h after the D6 Fable apply (2026-09-12T06:43:16Z) were fused-memory x3 and dashboard x1, while the last orchestrator restart was 2026-09-04T17:32:40Z — eight days BEFORE the apply. So `usage_cap.scoped_cap_models` was configured but inert, even though "4 restarts since the apply" reads as reassuring.

TRAP 2 — these rows carry a task_id. All 214 `service_restart` rows have a non-NULL `task_id` (the merge that triggered the restart). Code that groups events by task_id and then reads the untagged/None bucket silently reports ZERO restarts against the live store — and passes against any test fixture that leaves task_id NULL. Read them flat.

THE DIAGNOSTIC THIS ENABLES. A green-tier leaf and a red-tier leaf applied in the SAME commit will diverge: `models.*` and `routing.*` hot-reload and start working immediately, while `usage_cap.*` waits for a restart that may never have come. "Dispatch works, so the config landed" is therefore not evidence that every leaf in that commit is live. Check the tiers separately.

`scripts/audit_model_admission.py` (task 5440) renders this as a named-service restart table for exactly this reason.

Diagnostic facts for orchestrator restart triage (established 2026-07-08): (a) The escalation MCP binds its port ~2s after process start on a clean tree, so a watchdog "escalation port not listening" during a churn period is a crash-loop SYMPTOM, not slow startup — the watchdog's 120s startup grace is adequate and should not be widened in response. (b) Attribute unit stops via `journalctl --user -u <unit> _PID=<user-manager-pid>` (isolates systemd lifecycle lines from app noise); exit 130 + immediate re-start = external `systemctl restart`; exit 1 within ~2-3s repeatedly = a startup guard refusing deterministically. (c) The watchdog staleness WARNING quotes both the unit start epoch and the triggering commit epoch — `date -d @<epoch>` converts them, and the triggering commit is findable via `git log --format='%h %ct' -- <watched paths>`. (d) A `systemctl daemon-reload` from ANY process prints per-unit config-parse lines into every unit's journal; verify a suspected restart via ExecMainStartTimestamp/NRestarts before RCA-ing it as one.

ORCHESTRATOR DEPLOY/RESTART facts (verified 2026-06-30). Both the reify and dark-factory orchestrators run the SAME shared orchestrator code from /home/leo/src/dark-factory (`uv run --project orchestrator`, WorkingDirectory=/home/leo/src/dark-factory), but each targets a different project_root (reify=/home/leo/src/reify, dark-factory=/home/leo/src/dark-factory). A running orchestrator loads its Python at process start, so a working-tree code change (e.g. a merge_queue.py fix landing on main) is NOT live until the process is RESTARTED — deploying a shared-code fix requires restarting BOTH orchestrators. The orchestrator's dirty-tree START-guard is keyed on PROJECT_ROOT (the target repo), NOT the code tree: an uncommitted TRACKED file under /home/leo/src/dark-factory crash-loops a dark-factory-orch restart but does NOT affect a reify-orch restart (its project_root is clean). cli.py `--force-dirty-start` overrides. `systemctl --user restart orchestrator-<project>.service` does a graceful stop (KillMode=control-group, TimeoutStopUSec=90s: cancels in-flight tasks, reaps agents) then start; a benign "Job ... canceled" message can appear while the slow graceful-stop supersedes the restart job — verify recovery via a fresh MainPID + ActiveEnterTimestamp + clean startup log ("Speculative merge worker started", background loops up, no dirty-tree abort). Restarting cancels in-flight tasks (they requeue; warm lanes retained) — pick a near-quiescent moment (empty merge_queue.json).

MEASURING ORCHESTRATOR ACTIVITY: three traps that produce confidently wrong answers, all hit in one session 2026-08-21/22. (1) data/runs.db at the repo root is a 0-BYTE DECOY. The real event store is data/orchestrator/runs.db (~154MB). (2) The events table's time column is `timestamp` (TEXT, ISO-8601 with +00:00 offset), NOT `ts` — a query using `ts` errors outright, which is the safe failure, but comparing `timestamp` against sqlite's `datetime('now','-N hours')` mixes a space-separated format with a T-separated one and can silently produce wrong row sets. Prefer listing raw rows with ORDER BY timestamp DESC LIMIT N to confirm any aggregate before trusting it; a GROUP BY over a bad window once reported 14 merges in 2 hours when the raw listing showed ONE in eleven. (3) data/orchestrator/scheduler_state.json is written only after an acquire_next tick, so a PAUSED or idle scheduler stops updating it and the file goes stale — it has been observed reading `is_paused: false` fifteen hours after a pause, and `is_paused: true` long after a resume. It lies in BOTH directions and must never be used to confirm pause state. The authoritative reads are: the scheduler_state TABLE in runs.db (an empty result means not paused), and the idempotent `resume_scheduler` MCP call, whose `was_paused` field reports the truth without needing a mutation to have been intended.

Fact (2026-07-09): the orchestrator self-redeploy rate-cap state file is data/orchestrator/last_redeploy_orchestrator.json ({"ts":epoch,"iso":...}), git-ignored, persisted across restarts, and written ONLY by a successful StaleServiceRestartCoordinator fire (service_restart.py _persist_last_fire_wall). Caveat discovered: a timestamp can appear there WITHOUT a real run-loop fire — on 2026-07-09 it held ts=09:02:59 BST with no corresponding orch-selfrestart transient unit and zero idle-branch entries that day, and the then-current daemon had started 4h later; the coordinator's own tests all use tmp_path, so the write was almost certainly a live smoke-test exercising the real path during task 2371's landing. Lesson: a value in this file does not by itself prove the coordinator fired via the run loop — cross-check for an orch-selfrestart-on-merge-N transient unit in the journal.

DIAGNOSTIC TECHNIQUE (dark-factory, 2026-08-06): when a service is suspected of being restart-thrashed but journald retention is too short to see the onset, derive restart history from the application's own data. `data/reconciliation/reconciliation.db`'s `runs` table carries `instance_id`, so:

- distinct `instance_id` per day ≈ restarts per day;
- grouping by `(instance_id, completed_at)` collapses simultaneously-killed runs into KILL EVENTS (one restart killing N in-flight runs appears as N rows sharing an identical `completed_at` to the millisecond);
- per-instance `min(started_at)` → `max(completed_at)` gives INSTANCE LIFETIME.

Instance lifetime was the metric that cracked the case. It fell monotonically: ~20-35h (07-15..07-17) → 155min (07-28) → 106 → 81 → 90 → 53 (08-02) → 45min (08-05). Since a recon cycle needs 10-20 min, a ~45min lifetime makes long cycles structurally unable to finish — which is why the interrupted-run rate and the ~4x DAILY VOLUME COLLAPSE are the SAME cause, not two symptoms.

The key discriminator that ruled out "more restarts" as a sufficient explanation: restart COUNT barely changed (07-23 had 13 instances → only 2 kill events; 07-30 had 12 instances → 13 kill events). What changed is that restarts became LOAD-CORRELATED — the load-sensitive `/health` probe fires precisely when a cycle is in flight, so nearly every restart started killing work. A load-correlated killer is far worse than a more frequent uncorrelated one.

journald on this host retained only ~3.5 days (Aug 02 onward) when investigated on Aug 05-06, so the `runs` table was the only route to the 07-28 onset.

Operational facts for restarting the reify orchestrator (orchestrator-reify.service, systemd --user), learned 2026-06-10: (1) A manual `systemctl --user restart` can be CANCELED ("Job for orchestrator-reify.service canceled") by the orchestrator-watchdog.timer, which fires every 60s and revives/restarts wedged-or-dead services — it races the manual restart. (2) After a crash-loop, use `systemctl --user reset-failed orchestrator-reify.service` then restart, to clear the StartLimit/failed state and force a clean attempt with the fixed config. (3) Editing a TRACKED config file (orchestrator.yaml) in the running orchestrator's project_root opens a dirty-tree crash window: harness.py:613 refuses to start on "uncommitted tracked changes", and the 60s watchdog will crash-loop it until you COMMIT — so edit→commit must be tight, never leave the config dirty. (4) The dirty-tree guard checks TRACKED changes only; untracked files (e.g. *.bak.bench cruft) don't block startup.

Fleet redeploy timing as installed on 2026-10-13: the watchdog staleness backstop runs with ORCH_RESTART_MIN_INTERVAL_SECS=86400 (24h; set in ~/.config/systemd/user/orchestrator-watchdog.service per Leo ruling R9 / task 5020), NOT the script's 8h default. So `orchestrator-watchdog.py --report` printing VERDICT=stale at 8h does not mean the backstop will fire. The merge-landed coordinator inside orchestrator-dark-factory.service uses orchestrator_restart_min_interval_secs (default 8h, not overridden in dark-factory-orchestrator.yaml), and on a merge touching orchestrator/src/ it logs "orchestrator restart pending: merge <sha> for task <id> touched N watched file(s)". It then fires on the polite path or by force-fire about 75 minutes later, never inside the 8h clock. To predict when a landed orchestrator change goes live, grep the dark-factory unit's journal for that line rather than reading the report's verdict.

ROOT CAUSE (investigated 2026-08-25) of dark_factory orchestrator runs collapsing from a tight ~8-9h baseline to three sub-1.5h runs (1.26h / 0.92h / 1.33h) starting 2026-08-24T18:40Z: TWO fleet-redeploy drivers colliding inside an ~81-minute window in which the shared fleet-deploy clock is not yet stamped.

Nothing crashed. Every boundary is a clean SIGTERM drain; systemd's Restart=on-failure never fired (NRestarts=0, Result=success).

The chain:
1. TRIGGER 2026-08-24T14:39:05Z: `orchestrator-watchdog.timer` became active for the first time this boot (InactiveExitTimestamp == ActiveEnterTimestamp == Mon 2026-08-24 15:39:05 BST; its timers.target.wants symlink was recreated 15:39:04 local). It had ZERO service starts on 08-22 and 08-23. So the fleet ran from the 08-22 13:11 boot until 08-24 14:39Z with NO staleness backstop and NO liveness probe — the merge-landed coordinator alone produced the clean 8-9h cadence.
2. FIRST FIRE 18:36:19Z, four hours later, at the first 8h clock-open after the watchdog came online. The backstop ticks every 60s and fires within <=60s of clock-open; the merge-landed coordinator fires only when its run loop next evaluates. The backstop has won 4 of 4 races since.
3. AMPLIFIER: every `restart-all-orchestrators.sh --drain` sweep takes ~81 minutes because orchestrator-my-solar-challenge.service reports merge_idle:false forever, burning the full 75-min busy grace. dark_factory is restarted LAST by design (SELF_UNIT ordering), so it takes the hit at the far end of every sweep.
4. DEFECT: the shared clock data/orchestrator/last_redeploy_orchestrator.json is stamped ONLY on the script's verified-fresh exit-0 path — the END of that 81-min sweep. There is no "redeploy in flight" state anywhere, so for 81 minutes the clock still reads the previous deploy and every other driver's min-interval check legitimately passes.
   - MODE A (the 1.26h and 0.92h runs): the merge-landed coordinator — permanently FORCE-FIRING ("pending restart owed 17300s") and held back only by the clock — fires 2-22 min into the sweep, restarts the whole fleet in ~2 min WITHOUT --drain, and restarts dark_factory. The still-running sweep then reaches dark_factory ~75 min later and restarts it AGAIN.
   - MODE B (the 1.33h run): the backstop's own next tick. TOCTOU — its clock check runs at the top of a multi-second pass, and the sweep stamped the clock and freed the transient unit name one second earlier. Journal: "All 7 orchestrator unit(s) restarted and verified fresh" 15:37:43 -> "delegating fleet-wide staleness redeploy" 15:37:44 -> a whole new 81-min sweep.

Corroboration: a Graphiti fact recorded 2026-08-23T08:46:35Z already stated "The in-orchestrator merge-landed redeploy coordinator is active, but the staleness-backstop is not running" (and likewise the liveness probe) — an independent observation of the same watchdog outage a day before it was re-enabled.

Discovery (2026-07-09): the real operational pain behind the orchestrator restart churn was REIFY VERIFY-THRASH, not stale code. All six orchestrator-*.service units run the SAME dark-factory checkout, so any df orchestrator/src or escalation/src merge staleness-invalidates the whole fleet — including orchestrator-reify.service. The watchdog backstop then SIGTERM-restarts every unit ~every 2.5h. scripts/restart-all-orchestrators.sh does NOT drain (its --drain flag is accepted-and-ignored; drain is "delegated to SIGTERM via systemctl restart bounded by TimeoutStopSec"), so it kills Reify's in-flight verifies (which take >30 min). recover_pending_merges then re-enqueues and re-verifies from scratch → livelock (a merge started right after a restart may never finish before the next restart) + wasted verify CPU that oversubscribes the box and slows all verifies further. This is the same "restart-thrash = anti-throughput" shape as the verify-oversubscription work.

Discovery (2026-07-02, /prd session for task 2003): the orchestrator self-restart-on-merge machinery (U2) was NOT missing — it was fully implemented and wired on main but dormant. Harness._build_orchestrator_restart_coordinator (harness.py ~5289-5350) constructs a third StaleServiceRestartCoordinator with the cgroup-escaping systemd-run executor and the _merge_pipeline_idle restart_precondition, fanned in via _note_merge_all (harness.py:5047) and fired from _maybe_restart_stale_service (harness.py:5352). The knobs exist at config.py:1741-1756 (orchestrator_restart_on_merge_enabled default False; debounce 300s; watch_prefixes default ['orchestrator/src/']; script default scripts/restart-orchestrator.sh; on_active 10s clamped min 5) and dark-factory's own config (orchestrator/config.yaml — NOT at repo root) sets none of them, so defaults applied. The real gap was (a) activation and (b) scope: the default script restarts only the df unit while all six per-project daemons run the SAME /home/leo/src/dark-factory checkout (verified in every unit file: WorkingDirectory=df + uv run --frozen --project orchestrator), so one orchestrator-core merge stales the whole fleet at once. Escalation/brief prose describing U2 as 'deferred/absent' was stale relative to task 1973's landed work — verify wiring in code before designing 'missing' machinery.

DEBUGGING METHOD for a dark-factory/reify task stuck in-progress with no live agent ('stranded zombie'): (1) In data/orchestrator/runs.db, run_id is the ORCHESTRATOR PROCESS instance, NOT per-task — many tasks share one run_id; group a task's events by run_id to find its dispatch→teardown window. (2) A batch of `lock_released` events for MANY different tasks within the same ~0.5s, with NO accompanying task_completed/task_failed, is the signature of an orchestrator SHUTDOWN teardown (SIGTERM/restart), not normal completion — the run's final events. (3) Correlate with `journalctl --user -u orchestrator-<proj>` for the 'SIGTERM received' + systemd Stopping/Started + 'Started run run-...' restart pair. (4) A task whose last events are task_started (no task_completed) then a shutdown lock_released was stranded by that restart. (5) The reconcile sweep's own INFO logs name the recovery branch that fired: 'reverted task N to pending (reason=no-lock|stale-lock)' = recovered; 'branch is degenerate ... reverting stranded in-progress' = recovered by the post-2026-06-19 fix; 'branch is degenerate ... skipping citation-missing escalation' = the OLD pre-fix silent-strand bug.

BLAST RADIUS of an orchestrator restart, measured 2026-08-25 from data/orchestrator/runs.db (dark_factory). Useful as the cost baseline for arguing any fleet-restart-frequency fix.

100% of task cancellations are restart-caused. For every completed run since 2026-08-23, the count of `task_completed` events with outcome='cancelled' occurring within 120s of the run's completed_at equals the run's TOTAL cancelled count exactly (35/35, 31/31, 35/35, 22/22, 5/5, 27/27, 4/4, 34/34, 5/5). Restarts soft-cancel every in-flight workflow; nothing else cancels tasks.

Outcome vocabulary and ratio since 2026-08-21: cancelled 398, done 35, requeued 33, blocked 7, soft-cancelled 1. So ~11 workflows are destroyed for every one that lands, in the healthy regime as well as the broken one — this is a pre-existing condition, not something the 08-24/25 cycling created.

Marginal cost of the three anomalous short runs specifically:
  run-b0f8f5e8f80d  1.26h  $70.27  0 done  5 cancelled
  run-80237b3330da  0.92h  $16.73  0 done  4 cancelled
  run-00016b4099aa  1.33h  $59.39  0 done  5 cancelled
$146.39 of agent spend across the three, ZERO tasks landed in any of them, 14 in-flight workflows destroyed. A run shorter than ~1.5h cannot complete a workflow at all, so the whole run is waste.

Worked example: task 3112 carried 21 commits on task/3112 and 19/19 plan steps done, and was cancelled four times on 2026-08-25 alone, each cancellation landing exactly on a run boundary.

Two red herrings ruled out: the `total_tasks` column jumps (913->947, 949->963) are just task-tree growth between run starts, not causal. And `success` reads 0 for every run because the outcome value is 'done', not 'success' — do not conclude the fleet landed nothing from a query filtering on 'success'.

RCA (2026-07-08): "orchestrator restarting frequently but irregularly" decomposed into FOUR distinct signals, only one pathological. (1) Dirty-tree crash-loop outage 13:26-16:45 BST: uncommitted tracked hotfix edits in the main checkout tripped the harness dirty-tree start-guard on a watchdog staleness restart → exit-1 every ~12s → StartLimitBurst rate-limit → watchdog revive every ~4 min → 459 aborted runs, completely silent (no escalation), until operator commit 0b86841abe cleared it. (2) Watchdog staleness-pass restarts at 17:42 and 20:36 = INTENDED deploy-on-commit behavior (scripts/orchestrator-watchdog.py restarts any running orchestrator unit older than the newest commit touching orchestrator/src/, escalation/src/, or pyproject/uv.lock, after STALENESS_GRACE_SECS=1800) — irregular cadence is just merge cadence. (3) The 19:39 "restart" was NOT a restart: a systemctl daemon-reload issued from inside the orchestrator's own cgroup prints per-unit "RestartMaxDelaySec... Ignoring" lines into the unit's journal, which read like restart activity. (4) orchestrator-solar-challenge-platform.service was simultaneously crash-looping on the SAME dirty-tree guard in its own repo (~19h, resolved 2026-07-09 by committing the WIP as scp 0025a9f — a benign docs repoint of the my-solar-challenge→solar-challenge sibling-repo rename). Lesson: decompose "the orchestrator keeps restarting" into per-event attribution before proposing a fix — the events had four different causes.

Fleet-restart facts (2026-07-14): the orchestrator fleet is 6 supervised systemd --user units — orchestrator-{autopilot-video,dark-factory,know-live,my-solar-challenge,reify,solar-challenge-platform}.service. Each orchestrator EMBEDS its project's escalation MCP server (dark-factory on :8102), so restarting an orchestrator restarts its escalation server. `systemctl --user restart` of an orchestrator can report 'Job canceled' yet still restart cleanly — verify with fresh ActiveEnterTimestamp/MainPID rather than trusting the exit code. Restarting fused-memory.service also caused the dark-factory orchestrator to crash + supervisor-restart (it lost its fused-memory MCP), which (a) interrupted in-flight tasks and (b) left task 2604's uncommitted test_server.py merge as a dirty-tree leftover in project_root — that leftover was a superseded partial of task/2604's branch (authoritative superset) and was safely discarded with `git checkout --`.

A claim that "commit X landed on main, so behaviour Y no longer happens" must be tested against the ORCHESTRATOR PROCESS START TIME, not the merge time — and the gap between the two is itself the experiment. On dark-factory 2026-08-10, task 3429 (e6a7e971ed) merged to main at 2026-08-08T00:07Z, but the dark-factory orchestrator process actually carrying it first started 2026-08-09T08:14:09Z (~26h of stale-code drift). Three plan.files/metadata.files divergence escalations (esc-3743-1, esc-3615-2, esc-3747-1) were filed inside that window; read off the merge date alone they look like counter-evidence that 3429 worked, but they were produced by pre-3429 processes. Splitting the timeline at the process start turned them into a clean natural experiment: 4 narrowings / 3 escalations before, 6 narrowings / 0 escalations after. Method: get the process start with `ps -eo pid,lstart,cmd | grep "orchestrator run --config"` (or ExecMainStartTimestamp for a systemd unit), then bucket the runs.db event-store rows on that boundary. This is the behavioural-claim counterpart of the "editable install != running code" rule.

Restart cost under the D3a deploy pause, re-measured 2026-10-02 across all 7 projects' runs.db plus the journal, window 09-10..10-02:
- Fleet-wide restarts: 0 clock-driven, but 6 happened anyway in 21.6 days. Three were operator-filed deterministic deploy tasks (5439, 5704, 5054), two were hand shell sweeps (09-15, 09-30) and one was a host reboot (09-12). There were also 4 single-unit restarts and 3 reify-own redeploys.
- Rate: DF's run-boundary rate was 0.37/day, against 0.40/day under the 72h throttle and 2.54/day under the 8h cadence.
- Cost per restart: about the full max_concurrent_tasks slot set is cancelled, a median of 23 per busy project and ~67 fleet-wide. About 90% were parked in verify or merge waits, and 0–14 per restart were in an agent phase.
- Redispatch: median 4.7 h after a restart; 102 of 451 cancelled tasks had not restarted yet.
- Hand --drain restarts cost no less per event than the clock restart of 09-10. The halving since 09-11 is entirely the max_concurrent_tasks cut from 48 to 24.
- The 08-28→09-03 claim that runs of 10h or more give more done per hour does not reproduce: DF's done/h follows calendar time, and the shortest recent runs were the most productive (confounded by other changes).
- Fleet now runs 0.49 cancellations per done, against 14.7 in the baseline.
- Orchestrator code landed on all 22 days; the longest undeployed stretch was 8.8 days (09-21..09-30, including 4755 itself).
- Method: R5's scripts (boundaries.py, phases.py, gaps.py, regime.py) were in that session's scratchpad. The rule is cancellations = task_completed outcome cancelled within 600 s before a run end.

content: To answer "has the orchestrator started since time X?" (e.g. has a restart-tier leaf flagged restart_required by a config_reload been loaded yet), read the `runs` table of data/orchestrator/runs.db: `SELECT started_at, run_id FROM runs WHERE started_at > X ORDER BY started_at`. Each row is written by orchestrator/src/orchestrator/run_store.py::RunStore.start_run from harness.py::Harness.run at process start, before any event. Do not use the first-seen timestamp of events.run_id. Windowed, that mislabels a run already live at the window's start as a startup inside it. Unwindowed, it needs a GROUP BY over every events row, while `runs` holds about 1k rows. service_restart is no witness either: its only emitter is orchestrator/src/orchestrator/service_restart.py (the post-merge staleness coordinator), which records a restart REQUEST stamped before the startup. Since task 5930, scripts/audit_model_admission.py section 4 renders both the startups and each restart-required reload paired with the first startup after it.

cb1c6abd-0a1c-4380-9df6-169a54f58300.content:
CORRECTION, 2026-10-02: automatic orchestrator fleet redeploys are PAUSED. They have been since Leo's ruling D3a on 2026-09-10 (plans/agent-capacity-study-2026-09-09.md §10). A landed orchestrator or merge-lane change does NOT reach the running fleet until someone runs an explicit restart.

How the pause is wired:
- `~/.config/systemd/user/orchestrator-watchdog.service` sets `Environment=ORCH_RESTART_MIN_INTERVAL_SECS=2592000`, i.e. 30 days. The watchdog logs "skip: within fleet-deploy min-interval (2592000s) since last deploy".
- `dark-factory-orchestrator.yaml` sets `orchestrator_restart_on_merge_enabled: false`, which disables the merge-landed coordinator.
- Reason: each fleet redeploy soft-cancelled every in-flight task. 09-10's restart cancelled 44 workflows.

Unpause path: task 5020 (pending; restores the 8h staleness interval and the coordinator) waits on task 5371 (pending; agent-aware 45-min drain).

Explicit restarts: `scripts/restart-all-orchestrators.sh --drain`, or a deterministic restart task like 5054 (2026-10-01T05:01:29Z). Only these stamp `data/orchestrator/last_redeploy_orchestrator.json`.

Do NOT predict "the next redeploy at stamp + 8h" from CLAUDE.md or OPERATIONS.md, which describe the unpaused design. Check the unit's Environment line and the yaml flag first.

Consequence observed: tasks 5303 (merged 10-01 17:36Z) and 5034 (merged 10-02 00:03Z) were still not running as of 10-02 06:50Z, because the units had started at 10-01 ~05:00Z.

candidates.content: Targeted rustfmt check gotcha in reify: `rustfmt --edition 2024 --check <file>` follows `mod` declarations. Passing a crate root (lib.rs/main.rs) or a `tests/mod.rs` therefore checks the WHOLE module tree, producing hundreds of KB of pre-existing hunks from the never-formatted workspace. When checking only touched files, pass leaf module files only, and attribute any hunk to yourself only if it lies inside lines you added. Measured 2026-10-02 on gui/src-tauri (task 7274): passing src/lib.rs produced ~455KB of diff output for the reify-gui crate.

Reify rustfmt gotcha (no fmt gate): `rustfmt --edition 2024 --check <crate>/src/lib.rs` follows `mod` declarations into EVERY child module file, so on a lib.rs it reports hundreds of pre-existing hunks in files you never touched. Filter its output by the touched file paths (`grep 'Diff in' | grep -E '<your files>'`). To apply only the hunks lying wholly inside your own code in a file that also carries main's code, intersect `rustfmt --emit stdout` hunks with the added-line set from `git diff -U0 main HEAD -- <file>` (difflib opcodes; apply a hunk only if every source line is branch-added). Used in task 7543.

reify has no rustfmt gate and most test files already carry pre-existing rustfmt hunks, so a bare `rustfmt --edition 2024 --check <file>` cannot tell you whether YOUR edit introduced a hunk. Discriminator that works for a targeted edit: `git show main:<path> > /tmp/<task>-main-<name>.rs`, run `rustfmt --edition 2024 --check` on both that copy and the working file, and compare the `^Diff in` hunk counts. Equal or lower means your new code is clean. Then read only the hunks whose line range overlaps your edit. Measured on task 7482: fdm_bracket_e2e.rs went from 13 hunks at main to 12, and appearance_resolve_e2e.rs stayed at 9 and 9.

Reify gotcha: `rustfmt --edition 2024 --check <crate>/src/lib.rs` follows `mod` declarations and also reports `Diff in` hunks from every submodule file, so the bare line numbers interleave across files (e.g. reify-expr lib.rs reports ~150 hunks from a dozen files). When checking only your own hunks, filter on the full `Diff in <path>/lib.rs:<line>:` prefix rather than reading line numbers alone.

In reify, `rustfmt --edition 2024 --check crates/<crate>/src/lib.rs` (or any file that declares `mod foo;`) follows those module declarations and reports hunks for every child file, flooding the output. To check only the files you touched, filter the `Diff in <path>:<line>:` headers to those paths and compare the line numbers against `command git diff -U0` hunk ranges.

Gotcha for reify's targeted-rustfmt rule: `rustfmt --edition 2024 --check <file>` also follows that file's out-of-line `mod foo;` declarations and reports hunks in THOSE files. For example, checking crates/reify-expr/src/lib.rs prints `Diff in .../calculus.rs:NNNN` and `dual_eval.rs`. When you map hunks to your own edit lines, keep only the `Diff in` lines whose path is the file you passed, or you will misattribute other files' line numbers to your diff.

reify gotcha: `rustfmt --edition 2024 --check <file>` on a crate ROOT (e.g. crates/<c>/src/lib.rs) follows its `mod` declarations and checks the whole crate. reify is not rustfmt-clean, so this prints hundreds of pre-existing hunks in files you never touched. Write the output to a log and keep only the `Diff in <path>` lines for files you edited, then apply only the hunks that fall in your own new code.

In reify, "rustfmt --check is clean on my touched files" is almost never true and must not be claimed without a baseline diff: the workspace was never rustfmt-formatted (~5913 pre-existing hunks across 685 of 1755 tracked .rs files), so a bare `rustfmt --edition 2024 --check <file>` on a large file returns dozens of hunks unrelated to your change. To tell whether YOUR edit added formatting deviation, compare hunk COUNTS against the merge base: `git show <base>:<path> > /tmp/base.rs; rustfmt --edition 2024 --check /tmp/base.rs | grep -c '^Diff in'` versus the same count on the working file. Worked example: crates/reify-eval/src/engine_eval.rs had 34 hunks on main and 41 on a task branch — exactly 7 added by the branch's own new code. To locate which hunks are yours, intersect the rustfmt hunk start lines with the branch's added line ranges from `git diff -U0 <base>..HEAD`. This matters because reify has NO rustfmt gate, so the count is advisory only, and a crate-wide `cargo fmt` "fix" is an unbounded rewrite that becomes a silent cross-module scope breach.

Further worked examples of the same technique (folded in 2026-09-27 from near-duplicate entries 4d9f3f01, a6f5a819 — search this entry before writing a new one on this topic): engine_eval.rs alone reported 43 pre-existing hunks at an untouched HEAD (measured 2026-08-24; use `git show HEAD:$f > /tmp/base_$f` then diff `rustfmt --edition 2024 --check | grep -c '^Diff in'` counts for HEAD vs working tree — equal counts means no new deviation; use `git show HEAD:<path>` for the baseline copy, never `git stash`, which is banned repo-wide since every warm lane shares one `refs/stash`). crates/reify-constraints/src/solver.rs carried 18 pre-existing diffs by the same method (measured 2026-09-27).

In reify, `rustfmt --edition 2024 --check <file>` follows that file's `mod` declarations. Checking a `mod.rs` (e.g. crates/reify-solver-elastic/src/boundary/mod.rs) therefore also reports diffs in its unformatted child modules (neumann.rs). Filter the output with `grep '^Diff in'` to the files you actually touched before deciding that your edit broke formatting.

Reify fmt-drift check for a targeted edit: `rustfmt --edition 2024 --check <file>` on a file with pre-existing drift (e.g. crates/reify-eval/src/engine_build.rs, ~58 hunks) also prints hunks from its child modules (engine_build/tests.rs etc.), so filter the "Diff in <path>:<line>:" headers by path. To prove you added no hunks, extract the HEAD tree with `git archive HEAD crates/<crate>/src | tar -x -C /tmp/x`, run the same check there, and compare per-file hunk counts. Rustfmt cannot check a lone `git show HEAD:file` copy, because it cannot resolve its `mod` children.

In reify, verifying "did my edit introduce a rustfmt hunk?" by copying the HEAD version of a file to /tmp and running `rustfmt --edition 2024 --check` on the copy is INVALID for any file with `mod` declarations (e.g. crates/reify-compiler/src/conformance/mod.rs): rustfmt aborts with "Error writing files: failed to resolve mod `x`: /tmp/x.rs does not exist" and the `grep -c 'Diff in'` baseline reads 0, making every pre-existing hunk look like yours. Compare line numbers of the in-tree `--check` output against `git show HEAD:<path> | grep -n` for the specific construct instead.

reify targeted-formatting gotcha: `rustfmt --edition 2024 --check <file.rs>` RECURSES into that file's child modules, so running it on a crate root (lib.rs) formats the whole crate and reports every pre-existing hunk in every sibling file as if it were yours — measured on crates/reify-audit/src/lib.rs, which reported 200 hunks for a 20-line addition, and errors outright (`failed to resolve mod ...`) when run on a lib.rs copied to /tmp without its siblings. Add `--skip-children` for a genuinely per-file check (same lib.rs: 0 hunks before and after). This matters because CLAUDE.md's Formatting rule mandates checking only the touched files and rewriting a hunk only when it falls entirely inside your own new code — without --skip-children you cannot tell which hunks are yours. Note --skip-children also skips INLINE modules, so a `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` block in your own new file is invisible to it; check that file both ways (plain to see your test module, --skip-children to isolate the file). Reliable attribution method regardless: `git show <base>:<path> > /tmp/b.rs` and diff the hunk COUNT before vs after your edit — equal counts mean you introduced none.

In reify, `rustfmt --edition 2024 --check <file.rs>` follows `mod` declarations into every child module, so checking a parent like crates/reify-eval/src/compute_targets/mod.rs also reports hundreds of pre-existing diffs from sibling files. To check only the touched file, filter the output by filename, e.g. `rustfmt --edition 2024 --check F 2>&1 | awk '/^Diff in /{p=($0 ~ /compute_targets\/mod.rs/)} p'`. Then compare the Diff count against a baseline taken before editing.

When following reify's targeted-rustfmt rule (`rustfmt --edition 2024 --check <touched files>`, never `cargo fmt`), you MUST filter the output by the file path in each `Diff in <path>:<line>:` header. Running the check on `crates/reify-eval/src/geometry_ops.rs` also reports hundreds of hunks for `crates/reify-eval/src/geometry_ops/tests.rs`, because that 32k-line file is the whole `mod tests` body pulled in via `#[cfg(test)] mod tests;` — rustfmt follows the module declaration. geometry_ops.rs itself carries 79 pre-existing hunks, so the only usable signal is: collect the `Diff in .../<your file>.rs:<line>:` line numbers and check whether any fall inside the line ranges of your own `git diff -U0` hunks.

Reify has no rustfmt gate, so the standing rule is "only rewrite a rustfmt hunk that falls entirely inside your own new code". To make that mechanically checkable rather than eyeballed, use a BASELINE-SHIFT diff: `git show HEAD:<path> > /tmp/base/<file>`, run `rustfmt --edition 2024 --check` on BOTH the HEAD copy and the working copy, and compare the two sets of reported line numbers. Pre-existing hunks reappear at their old line number minus (lines you deleted above them) / plus (lines you added above them); if every current hunk maps onto a HEAD hunk under that constant shift, your edit introduced ZERO new fmt divergence and you must leave all of them alone. Measured 2026-09-14 in warm lane _lane-29 (task 6535, hoisting crack_loads out of membrane_load.rs): HEAD baseline reported hunks at lines {154, 427}, the working copy at {154, 374}, and 427−53=374 exactly matched the 53-line function deletion — proving both hunks were pre-existing. Note `rustfmt --check` exits 0 even when it reports diffs here, so the exit code is NOT the signal; parse the `^Diff in` lines. Pair with the `env` prefix bypass (`env grep`, `env cargo`) since the Bash-tool skim wrapper condenses plain `cargo`/`git diff` output.

In reify, a standalone `rustfmt --edition 2024 --check` on a reify-eval test file reports huge phantom drift for two structural reasons, so read the hunks before believing them: (1) `crates/reify-eval/src/geometry_ops/tests.rs` is a `mod tests;` file whose entire body is indented 4 spaces (as if pasted from inside a `mod` block), so standalone rustfmt de-indents the whole file — ~188 hunks that belong to no particular change; (2) rustfmt follows `mod`/`#[path]` declarations, so checking `tests/harness_geometry.rs` also reports hunks in sibling `harness_geometry/*.rs` modules your diff never touched. To decide whether YOUR change introduced drift, map each `Diff in <file>:<line>:` header against the branch's added-line set (`git diff -U0 <base> HEAD` hunk headers) and only act on hunks lying entirely inside added lines. Never run `cargo fmt` at crate or file scope — the workspace has no rustfmt gate and was never formatted.

Reify local-toolchain gotcha (2026-06-23): the locally-installed rustfmt version differs from the repo's pinned/gate rustfmt, so `cargo fmt --check` run locally produces false-positive diffs across the WHOLE workspace — including files already on main (e.g. crates/reify-audit/src/bin/reify-audit.rs and pre-existing multi-line match arms in loop_closure_value.rs/loop_closure_solver.rs). It wants to collapse multi-line match arms / struct bodies onto single lines that the gate's rustfmt keeps multi-line. To verify your OWN edits won't break the gate's fmt step: run `rustfmt --edition 2021 --check <only-your-changed-files>` and confirm every reported diff is in a region you did NOT touch (i.e. your added/changed lines are disjoint from the drift). Do not trust a whole-crate `cargo fmt --check` locally.

rustfmt RECURSES into `mod` declarations, which silently poisons the standard reify "compare rustfmt hunk counts against the merge base" check (canonical recipe: memory 3ff5c531-8807-403c-b86e-47015ade6689) whenever the file you touched is a module ROOT — lib.rs, main.rs, mod.rs, or any file containing `mod foo;`. rustfmt resolves those submodules relative to the checked file's own directory and reports each hunk under the SUBMODULE's path, not the root's. So `git show <base>:crates/X/src/lib.rs > /tmp/base.rs; rustfmt --edition 2024 --check /tmp/base.rs` gives a FALSE-CLEAN baseline: the submodules do not exist in /tmp, their hunks silently vanish, and the count is not comparable to the working-tree run, which does descend. Observed on task 5094: the /tmp baseline copy of crates/reify-ast/src/lib.rs reported 0 hunks while the in-tree run of the same file reported hunks in lib.rs, ast.rs AND decl.rs. `--skip-children` is NOT a way out — rustfmt 1.9.0-stable rejects it with "Unrecognized option: 'skip-children'" (and note it exits non-zero, so a `| grep -c` pipeline reports a meaningless 0 rather than failing loudly). Two working fixes: (a) materialise the whole sibling module set into the scratch dir before checking — `for f in $(git ls-tree --name-only <base> crates/X/src/); do git show "<base>:$f" > /tmp/base/$(basename $f); done` — then run rustfmt on /tmp/base/lib.rs; or (b) skip counting entirely and filter hunk path+line, keeping only hunks whose path is the file you edited AND whose line falls inside your added range: `rustfmt --edition 2024 --check <file> 2>&1 | grep -oE '<file>\.rs:[0-9]+' | awk -F: '$2>START && $2<END'`. This is the same transitive-descent behaviour already noted for `#[path]`-declared C1 harness roots (memory f8b9de2e); the new part is that it also invalidates the /tmp baseline comparison, which is what CLAUDE.md's "rewrite a hunk only when it falls entirely inside your own new code" rule depends on.

Measuring rustfmt cleanliness by copying a Rust file out of its crate (e.g. `git show main:crates/x/tests/cli.rs > /tmp/cli.rs && rustfmt --check /tmp/cli.rs`) gives a FALSE CLEAN: rustfmt aborts with "Error writing files: failed to resolve mod `common`" on any unresolvable `mod` declaration, prints zero "Diff in" lines, and still exits 0. To compare a file's formatting debt across revisions, check it out IN PLACE in the crate directory (back up the working copy first, then restore). Measured 2026-09-01 on crates/reify-audit/tests/cli.rs: 0 hunks reported from /tmp vs 59 in place.

Reify: `rustfmt --edition 2024 --check crates/reify-eval/src/geometry_ops/tests.rs` is useless for a targeted fmt check. That file is an out-of-line `mod tests;` body written with a 4-space indent, so standalone rustfmt reports a whole-file dedent (125+ hunks). To check only your new block, wrap the extracted lines in `mod m { ... }` in a scratch file and rustfmt that; ignore the trailing-blank-line hunk the wrapper itself causes.

content: Reify rustfmt gotcha (measured 2026-10-12, task 7248): `rustfmt --edition 2024 --check crates/<crate>/src/lib.rs` does NOT check only lib.rs — it follows every `mod` declaration and reports hunks in sibling module files too (e.g. ffi.rs, handle.rs for reify-kernel-occt; 125 hunks total, 109 of them in lib.rs, all pre-existing). To verify a targeted edit, filter the output to `^Diff in .*/<file>:<line>:` and check that no hunk falls inside your edited line range; never treat a non-zero exit as caused by your edit.

Completed: serve: Host allow-list entries that still differ from the Host a browser sends (non-canonical INTAKE_PUBLIC_URL hosts; loopback entries on port 80)
Description: Found while planning task 35 (follow-up id agent-followup-35). Task 35 makes src/scoping_intake/cli.py derive the prospect site's Host allow-list entry from INTAKE_PUBLIC_URL the way a browser writes Host: the host in lower case, no port when it is the scheme's default (80 for http, 443 for https) or empty, any other port kept, and an IPv6 address in brackets. The derivation lives in a helper, cli._host_header(scheme, hostname, port), which _public_url calls. web.py RequestHandler._admission_refusal answers only a Host header that is in site.hosts by string equality, and otherwise replies 421 'Not found'. Two cases are left. Both are outside task 35's scope and unlikely in the deployed setup: deploy/README.md sets INTAKE_PUBLIC_URL=https://<machine>.<tailnet>.ts.net, and the units use ports 8471 and 8472.

(1) Host spellings a browser rewrites beyond case and port. Measured on 2026-10-08 with headless Chrome 151 and a capture server: http://[0:0:0:0:0:0:0:1]:P/ is sent as Host [::1]:P. Per the WHATWG URL standard but NOT measured: a non-ASCII name such as https://bücher.example is sent in punycode (xn--bcher-kva.example), and IPv4 shorthand such as http://127.1:P/ is sent as 127.0.0.1:P. urllib.parse.urlsplit keeps all three as typed (CPython 3.14.4, the project venv). The allow-list entry therefore never matches, and every prospect request gets 421. The fix is either to derive the entry the way the browser does (IPv6 compression via ipaddress, IDNA/UTS-46, IPv4 parsing) or to refuse such values at start with UnusablePublicUrl, naming the variable.

(2) cli._loopback_hosts(port) always writes the port: {127.0.0.1:P, localhost:P}. A browser leaves out port 80 for http; measured in Chrome 151, http://intake.example:80/ is sent as Host intake.example. So with --prospect-port 80 or --operator-port 80, a browser at http://localhost/ sends Host 'localhost' and gets 421. The operator site would also refuse http://127.0.0.1/. cli._host_header from task 35 could build these entries too.

Every StrEnum value in record.py is markup-free, and the strings with apostrophes (Exit.headline for advise_elsewhere, three Dimension.in_region_condition values) are already escaped where rendered.

candidates.content: solar_challenge e2e procedure, measured 2026-10-12 by task 649's architect on main 5da62aa (playwright 1.61, chromium-headless-shell 1228). Some effects need requests that really hold a browser connection, such as Chromium's 6-connections-per-host HTTP/1.1 limit for SSE streams. Show those with server-held jobs, not page.route. A progress request held unanswered by page.route takes no connection: 8 held sweep streams left another tab loading in 0.31 s. To hold real streams, install JobManager(simulate_home=<function that waits on a threading.Event>) as _e2e_app.extensions['job_manager'] for the test. At teardown, set the event, wait_until_idle, and put the session manager back. Task 649's plan adds this as the tests/e2e/conftest.py fixture release_held_simulations. Gotcha: on this host a request still waiting for a socket is often failed by a Docker veth event with net::ERR_NETWORK_CHANGED before any timeout. That triggers the conftest's one rerun, so a connection stall shows as 'Page.goto: net::ERR_NETWORK_CHANGED' plus '1 rerun', not a 30 s timeout. The captured werkzeug log shows which requests reached the server, e.g. 6 of 8 progress GETs.

solar_challenge e2e technique, measured 2026-10-12 by task 649's implementer (playwright 1.61, headless Chromium, task/649 at 10d04c1). (1) An unhandled promise rejection on the page arrives as a Playwright 'pageerror' whose text is the bare Error message, e.g. 'this browser opens no event streams', with no 'Uncaught (in promise)' prefix. So tests/e2e/conftest.py's page_errors fixture catches an unawaited async call whose rejection nothing catches. (2) To reach a page's handling of a throwing EventSource constructor without editing src/, call page.add_init_script("window.EventSource = class { constructor() { throw new Error('...'); } };") before page.goto. progress-tracker.js, which base.html loads on every page, constructs its EventSource only on demand, so pages still load. Route the submit POST too, e.g. test_parameter_sweep.py's sweep_jobs fixture, so no job reaches the live server. test_the_page_says_why_it_lost_track_of_a_sweep_it_cannot_follow uses both.

solar_challenge e2e technique (measured 2026-10-09 by task 533's architect, playwright 1.61.0, pytest-playwright 0.8.0, base 39635d0), for tests that hold an SSE progress stream and end it later. (1) After `with page.expect_request(url): button.click()` returns, the page.route handler for that request may not have run yet: the 'request' event precedes 'route', so a list of held routes can still be empty (seen on /simulate/fleet). Make the route fixture register each job's ending, answer an already-held route at once, and answer a route that arrives later on arrival. (2) Response.finished() leaves a watcher task that logs 'Task exception was never retrieved ... Target closed' at page teardown. Instead, `response = route.request.response()` (None if the page dropped the request) then `response.body()`: it waits for the request to finish without that noise. After it returns, the page's EventSource handlers have run, so a negative expect is meaningful. (3) route.fulfill() on a request the page already cancelled (EventSource.close()) is silently ignored.

solar_challenge e2e, Playwright 1.61.0, measured by task 298 on 2026-10-07: how to test a debounced Alpine action without sleeping. The example is tests/e2e/test_scenario_builder.py::test_a_refusal_stays_in_the_preview_over_the_preview_an_earlier_edit_queued.
1. Call page.clock.install() before page.goto. The fake time still advances with real time, so the page behaves normally.
2. Do the user actions.
3. Call page.clock.run_for(5_000). It fires the pending setTimeout, here the builder's 500 ms preview, at once.
4. To show that no request was made, record page.on('request'), do one round trip such as Validate, and only then assert.

Separately, avoid Response.finished() in the sync API: it leaves an asyncio task that logs 'Task exception was never retrieved ... Target closed' at teardown. Reading the body with response.json() or .text() also waits for it, without that noise.

solar_challenge e2e technique (task 637 implementer, measured 2026-10-13, playwright 1.61, headless Chromium): to see how a page's own JS handles a modified page without editing src/, fetch the live page with page.request.get(url), edit its HTML text (assert the anchor you replace occurs exactly once), then serve it with page.route(url, lambda route: route.fulfill(status=200, content_type="text/html; charset=utf-8", body=html)) before page.goto(url). Build the modified HTML in the test body, not inside the route handler: an exception raised in a handler surfaces only as a hung navigation. tests/e2e/test_results_page.py's undrawable-chart test injects a chart container whose data-chart-figure is not JSON this way.

solar_challenge e2e: how headless Chromium 149 (playwright 1.61) EventSource reacts to Playwright route answers, measured 2026-10-11 by task 648's architect at d11d61e. solar_challenge web-test technique (measured 2026-09-29 on task/156, base efe3145): to hold a submitted web job deterministically in 'running', install JobManager(simulate_home=<gated fake>) via app.extensions["job_manager"]. The fake sets a 'started' threading.Event, then waits on a 'released' Event. After 'started', GET /api/jobs/<id>/results is always 409 with status 'running', because _run_job sets the status to running before it calls the simulation. Release the gate in a yield-fixture's TEARDOWN, not in the test body. pytest tears down the root autouse drain (tests/conftest.py::_shutdown_job_managers, shutdown(wait=True)) last, so the release runs before the drain waits, and a failing test cannot hang the suite. A planning prototype passed 40 of 40 runs, with every teardown at or under 0.21 s. solar_challenge convention (task 533, task/533 de593ff plus amendments c6fb3f0..74dce9c, 2026-10-09; on main once task/533 merges): the progress tracker on /simulate/home and /simulate/fleet is a per-job Alpine component, progressTracker(jobId) in static/js/progress-tracker.js, which templates/simulate/partials/progress-tracker.html opens under a keyed x-for over the calling page's jobId; the pages hold only jobId. The tracker's fields (status, step, message, progress, elapsed, error, completedRunId) live in the tracker element's own x-data scope, not on Alpine.$data of the page's homeSimulator()/fleetSimulator() element. base.html loads static/js/progress-tracker.js on every page, deferred and before Alpine core, so a page that calls the macro needs no script tag of its own (this replaces the earlier rule that each calling page loads it in its head block). A new jobId replaces the tracker and the old tracker's destroy() closes its stream: a second Run aborts job-1's /api/jobs/job-1/progress request with net::ERR_ABORTED on both pages, and Playwright reports that as a requestfailed event even while the test holds the route, so a test waits for it with page.expect_event('requestfailed', predicate=...) around the click. For an e2e test whose jobs run until the test ends them, reuse the running_jobs fixture and _RunningJobs in tests/e2e/test_progress_tracker.py. progressTracker._onComplete and _onError close the stream before parsing the event's data.
