The test mocked both endpoints with page.route: POST **/api/simulate/fleet-from-distribution answered 201 with {job_id: 'job-N', run_id: 'run-N'}, and every GET **/api/jobs/*/progress was held unanswered, so the page saw a job that is still running.
1. Click 'Run Fleet Simulation' (job-1). The progress tracker shows 'Waiting to start...'. The Run button is enabled again at once: its :disabled="submitting" (src/solar_challenge/web/templates/simulate/fleet.html:385) is true only while the POST is in flight.
2. Click Run again with the valid form (job-2). Both progress streams were open, and no request had failed.
3. Fulfill job-1's held stream with `event: complete` and data {"status": "completed", "run_id": "run-1"}, so the older job finishes after the newer one started.
RESULT: the page showed 'Simulation completed successfully!' with a View Results link to /results/fleet/run-1, although job-2 (run-2) had not completed. The request GET /api/jobs/job-2/progress was aborted by the page, the only request failure of the run. So the page showed the wrong run's results link for the new run, and stopped following the new run, whose own completion could never reach the tracker.

CAUSE, read from the code (it matches the measurement):
- fleet-simulator.js startProgressTracking() (:241-291) assigns this.evtSource and this.timer without closing the previous ones. submitFleet() (:205-238) never calls stopProgressTracking() before it.
- The older stream's listeners are arrow functions over the same `this`, so they keep writing this.status, this.progress and this.completedRunId. Their 'complete' and 'error' handlers call stopProgressTracking(), which closes whatever this.evtSource is at that moment, which is the newer job's stream. The older stream itself is never closed, and the replaced setInterval timer is never cleared.

Its submitSimulation() calls startProgressTracking(), which assigns this.evtSource and this.timer without closing earlier ones, and its handlers call this.evtSource.close() on the current one (and set it to null).

POSSIBLE FIX DIRECTIONS, for the architect to choose among: call stopProgressTracking() when a submission is accepted, before startProgressTracking() assigns the new stream; and/or make each stream's handlers act only while that stream is still the current one; and/or keep Run disabled while a job runs. content: solar_challenge e2e technique, measured 2026-10-13 by task 648's amendment pass (playwright 1.61, headless Chromium 1228). (1) A page.route answer cannot keep an SSE stream open: route.fulfill delivers the whole body, so right after its events the EventSource sees the stream end (dataless error, readyState CONNECTING). To test a REOPENED stream that stays open while its job runs, use a real job: request release_held_simulations, register page.route('**/api/jobs/*/progress', disconnect_request, times=1) (tests/e2e/_job_requests.py) before goto, and Run on /simulate/home. The first stream is reset, and the browser's reopen ~3 s later reaches the live server. The server drains the held job's progress ('Running home simulation...') and keeps the stream open with heartbeats until the test releases the job. test_progress_tracker.py's test_a_run_whose_reopened_progress_stream_reaches_the_server_no_longer_shows_it_reconnecting does this (6.5 s). (2) With page.clock.install() before goto, page.clock.fast_forward(ms) fires a page setTimeout, such as job-progress-stream.js's reconnect give-up, at once. Chromium's native EventSource reconnection still runs in real time. A classic script's top-level const is readable with page.evaluate('NAME'), as fast_forward_by_the_reconnect_limit reads JOB_PROGRESS_RECONNECT_LIMIT_MS.

solar_challenge e2e gotcha, measured 2026-10-03 by task 409's architect on main bdb831a (Playwright Python, headless Chromium).
- An uncaught page exception reaches page.on('pageerror') ONLY, never page.on('console').
- An Alpine expression error, e.g. an x-data component function that is not defined, arrives as a console message of type 'warning' ('Alpine Expression Error: ...') plus a pageerror. It never arrives as console type 'error'.
- Only an explicit console.error(...) arrives as console type 'error'.
So a 'no JS errors' e2e test must also collect pageerror events, and Alpine warnings if wanted; collecting console messages of type 'error' is not enough. The existing console-only tests cannot see the Alpine race (Bug B1) they target: test_fleet_simulation.py::test_fleet_page_no_js_errors, the no-console-error tests in test_parameter_sweep.py and test_scenario_builder.py, and test_smoke_all_pages.py. Follow-up ticket: tkt_0RVBXTR79DH8MBJGED6H9W1MQV.

Completed: Sweep page: an earlier sweep's in-flight result fetch can write its summary into the row of a sweep submitted after it
Description: Agent follow-up found during task 533 (follow-up escalation id agent-followup-533). OUT OF SCOPE for task 533, which gives each job on /simulate/home and /simulate/fleet its own progress tracker (static/js/progress-tracker.js) so an earlier job's late SSE event cannot reach a newer run's tracker. Task 533 does not touch the parameter sweep page.

READ FROM THE CODE, NOT MEASURED (on task/533, base main 39635d0, 2026-10-09). In src/solar_challenge/web/static/js/parameter-sweep.js:
- submitSweep() calls this.destroy() at submission start, which closes every earlier EventSource, and replaces this.sweepResults with the new sweep's rows. So the stale-SSE race task 533 fixed does not apply to this page's streams.
- But a 'complete' handler calls this._fetchResult(data.run_id, idx), an async method. It builds its URL from this.sweepResults[idx].job_id synchronously (the old sweep's job), then, after `await fetch(...)` and `await resp.json()`, writes generation, self_consumption and grid_import into this.sweepResults[idx], whatever array this.sweepResults is by then.
- Run is enabled again as soon as the sweep's POST returns (submitting is true only during the POST). So if the user submits a new sweep while an old sweep's results fetch is in flight, the old sweep's summary lands in row idx of the new sweep, whose row still says pending. The window is one /api/jobs/<id>/results round trip after a job completes, so the race is narrow.

Hypothesis: the fix is to have each sweep's async writes target that sweep's own rows, e.g. capture the row object (const row = this.sweepResults[idx]) before the awaits and write to it, or give each sweep its own component scope the way task 533 gave each job its own progressTracker. candidates.content: The `scripts/` tree (incl. scripts/legibility/) is NOT in the project's `[tool.pyright]` include/extraPaths in pyproject.toml — pyright only covers `conftest.py` plus the package `src/` dirs. So running `uv run pyright scripts/legibility/foo.py` in isolation surfaces spurious import-resolution errors (e.g. `Import "httpx" could not be resolved`, `"load_config" is not a known attribute of module "config"` from the flat `import config`) that the real per-package pre-commit gate (hooks/project-checks) never checks. When verifying a scripts/ change, rely on the pytest suite + `ruff check`; treat isolated-pyright import errors as environment artifacts, not real defects (confirm they pre-exist at the base commit before chasing them).

tests/scripts/ modules import from the flat repo-root scripts/ directory. Historically pyright could not resolve those imports, so the convention was to add `# pyright: ignore[reportMissingImports]` on the import line, because repo-root scripts/ was deliberately absent from [tool.pyright] extraPaths.

THAT PREMISE IS RETIRED. VERIFIED 2026-08-20 against main: task 3456 added BOTH `"scripts"` and `"scripts/legibility"` (and scripts/local-model-serving) to root pyproject.toml's [tool.pyright] extraPaths, with a comment recording that scripts/tests/conftest.py performs the same sys.path insertions at runtime, pinned by tests/scripts/test_scripts_module_config.py::test_root_pyright_extrapaths_resolves_scripts_imports. The scripts module also now declares a real type gate (`uv run --project shared pyright scripts/`).

CONSEQUENCE, and the actionable part: the `# pyright: ignore[reportMissingImports]` comments are now VESTIGIAL. 9 files under tests/scripts/ still carry one as of 2026-08-20. Do not add new ones. Do not cite "scripts/ is absent from extraPaths" as a live reason -- it is not.
CAUTION before mass-removing them: root [tool.pyright] `include` is only ["conftest.py", "df_pytest_isolation.py"], so which table applies depends on the invocation's working directory and --project. Remove an ignore only with the module's own declared type_check_command re-run green, not on the strength of this note.

DISTINCT NEIGHBOURING TOPICS, do not merge into this one: `pyright-extrapaths-completeness` (gate 3399 -- extraPaths completeness / invocation context for correctly-configured venvs) and the npx-pyright EACCES/npm-cache workaround (gate 3417). Member 03b783d5 belongs to the EACCES cluster and is stamped there; it appears in this cluster's history only for its ignore-comment sentence.

ACCRETION: append here or add a stamped peer under topic `tests-scripts-pyright-ignore-extrapaths-absence` -- do not write a new unstamped entry.

In scripts/legibility/, a bare sibling `import config` (e.g. in census.py) resolves correctly at real runtime (pytest via conftest.py's sys.path insert, and `python scripts/legibility/census.py` via Python's own script-dir-as-sys.path[0]) but is a FALSE POSITIVE under `pyright scripts/legibility/<file>.py` run from the repo root: pyright picks up the unrelated top-level `<repo-root>/config/` directory (an implicit PEP 420 namespace package holding usage-accounts.yaml) instead of scripts/legibility/config.py, producing a spurious "X is not a known attribute of module config" error. Harmless — the root pyproject.toml's `[tool.pyright] include = ["conftest.py"]` doesn't cover scripts/ at all, so this never gates a real merge; verify actual behavior via `python scripts/legibility/<file>.py` directly rather than trusting a standalone pyright run.

To type-check scripts/local-model-serving/*.py (lms_vram, lms_ctl, lms_healthcheck, lms_manifest) run pyright with a config supplying extraPaths, e.g. `uv run pyright -p <tmpdir>/pyrightconfig.json <files>` where the config sets extraPaths to the absolute scripts/local-model-serving and scripts dirs. Those modules import each other by BARE name (`import lms_vram`), so invoking pyright without that path yields a wall of phantom reportMissingImports that looks like a real failure. Note pyright's `include` array silently ignores absolute paths ("Ignoring path ... because it is not relative") — pass the files as CLI args instead — and a config placed directly in /tmp makes pyright sweep all of /tmp, so put it in its own temp subdirectory. scripts/ is NOT in hooks/project-checks' PYRIGHT_PACKAGES (fused-memory, orchestrator, dashboard), so pre-commit never type-checks it.

Measured 2026-08-01 at main 434ca89025 while planning task 3445: `npx pyright scripts/` in dark-factory returns 206 errors across 14 files (162 in scripts/tests/test_legibility_census.py; 20 in non-test production scripts — genuine Optional/`str | None` narrowing defects in consume_redispatch_requests.py, legibility/digest.py, legibility/sampling.py, legibility/census_trigger.py). DO NOT repeat the disproved fix: 9 of the errors are reportMissingImports for the flat scripts/legibility/ modules (census, codebook, coder, digest, inventory) that scripts/tests/conftest.py puts on sys.path at runtime, but adding "scripts" and "scripts/legibility" to the root pyproject.toml `[tool.pyright] extraPaths` makes it WORSE — 206 -> 395 errors (test_legibility_census.py alone 162 -> 350) — because resolving the imports lets pyright check call sites against real signatures instead of Unknown. Any task declaring a `type_check_command` for scripts/ must plan against the 395 figure. By contrast `ruff check scripts/` was only 3 mechanical findings.

scripts/ IS pyright-gated (since task 3456) even though pre-commit never runs pyright for it — measured 2026-08-21 on task 4511. scripts/orchestrator.yaml declares `type_check_command: "uv run --project shared pyright scripts/"` (uv-resolved since task 4358), the root pyproject.toml [tool.pyright] extraPaths includes "scripts" and "scripts/legibility", and the tree is clean: 0 errors / 0 warnings / 0 informations at HEAD. But hooks/project-checks' PYRIGHT_PACKAGES is only (fused-memory, orchestrator, dashboard), so a scripts/ type error commits with NO output line at all and first surfaces at module verify — I committed one and only caught it by running the gate by hand. PRACTICAL RULE: after any scripts/ edit run `uv run --project shared pyright scripts/` AND `uv run --project shared ruff check scripts/` yourself; the test suite passing means nothing about either. THIS CORRECTS TWO STALE ENTRIES that still assert the opposite and would walk you straight into it: 2f1d01db-a9fc-4bba-82b7-dde37e293145 ("scripts/ ... lint-gated but NOT type-gated", plus 5 long-since-fixed digest.py errors) and 613208c1-e873-4c5b-886f-cd302f40588f ("scripts/ is knowingly not yet pyright-clean, which is why scripts/orchestrator.yaml declines to declare a type_check_command ... do NOT add scripts/ to extraPaths" — both halves now false; the extraPaths entries are load-bearing and pinned by tests/scripts/test_scripts_module_config.py::test_root_pyright_extrapaths_resolves_scripts_imports). In-place correction was refused (update_memory's content_amend arm allows only recon-stage-/curator- agents), hence this separate entry.

THE SPECIFIC TRAP in scripts/tests/: an UNANNOTATED parameter defaulting to None infers as type `None`, so a shared test helper written `def _h(..., monkeypatch=None)` reds the gate with `"setattr" is not a known attribute of "None" (reportOptionalMemberAccess)` at every use. A guard placed up front does not fix it if it narrows a DIFFERENT condition than the one reaching the use (e.g. `if branch in ('a','b') and monkeypatch is None: raise` cannot narrow inside a later `if branch == 'a':` arm). House fix, matching scripts/'s fix-don't-suppress precedent (task 3456 cleared 395 errors with zero `# type: ignore`): annotate `monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch | None = None` and `assert monkeypatch is not None, <msg>` inside each arm that uses it.

MEASUREMENT (task 4516, 2026-09-04, tip 65a3b6320a, pinned pyright 1.1.408): pyright's native `reportUnnecessaryTypeIgnoreComment` — the checker-native detector for a suppression that has outlived its condition — WORKS in dark-factory but is not the one-line win it looks like. Probed by temporarily adding `reportUnnecessaryTypeIgnoreComment = "error"` to the ROOT [tool.pyright] table, then restoring the tree byte-clean.

1. It DOES fire under `typeCheckingMode = "basic"` (off by default there, but a one-line opt-in). A probe with a stale suppression on a resolvable `import systemd_unit_parity` drew: error: Unnecessary "# pyright: ignore" rule: "reportMissingImports".
2. Enabling it TODAY turns both root-table gates RED on pre-existing, unrelated suppressions: `uv run --project shared pyright tests/scripts/` -> 8 errors in 6 files (four of them `# type: ignore` comments, three `# pyright: ignore` on reportArgumentType/reportAttributeAccessIssue), and `uv run --project shared pyright scripts/` -> 1 error (scripts/run_vllm_eval.py:910). The rule reports unnecessary `# type: ignore` comments too, and this repo runs no mypy, so pyright is their only consumer.
3. THE ROOT TABLE'S REACH IS THREE TARGETS: tests/scripts/, scripts/, and the root `include` (conftest.py, df_pytest_isolation.py). Every other workspace member (cockpit, dashboard, escalation, fused-memory, orchestrator, sampler, shared) carries its OWN [tool.pyright] table and its declared gate runs `uv run --directory <member> pyright src/ tests/` against that table. So a root-table setting reaches none of them: repo-wide means editing eight tables and clearing eight independent fallout sets. Filed as a follow-up task.

CORRECTION to an older memory (2f1d01db, 2026-08-01, "scripts/ and shared/ are lint-gated but NOT type-gated; root include is just [conftest.py]"): stale. scripts/orchestrator.yaml declares `uv run --project shared pyright scripts/` (task 4358) and tests/scripts/orchestrator.yaml declares `uv run --project shared pyright tests/scripts/`; both measured 0 errors, 0 warnings on this tip. Root `include` is now ["conftest.py", "df_pytest_isolation.py"].

SIGHTING of the already-recorded git-grep norm (5d84ead7 / abf5f757), in a new place — a code REVIEW's factual claims rather than a guard test. A review of this task cited "~800 `# pyright: ignore` sites repo-wide, 382 bare vs 15 single-rule" and called a comma-list spelling "an established repo spelling (13 occurrences)". Re-measured with `git grep -- '*.py'` over TRACKED source: 40 directives total, 4 bare (all four prose inside docstrings/assertion strings), 0 comma lists. The cited numbers are counts of .venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages (902 directives; the cited comma-list spelling is in site-packages/key_value/). When a review hands you a repo-wide count as evidence, re-measure it with git grep before building on it — a plain `grep -r .` from a worktree root sweeps the cold-verified worktree's own .venv.

Task 5086's measurement (2026-09-28, pyright 1.1.408) of pyright reportUnnecessaryTypeIgnoreComment across dark-factory. The root [tool.pyright] table governs only the scripts/ and tests/scripts/ gates plus the root include; every workspace member's gate (`uv run --directory <member> pyright`) reads that member's own table, so enabling the rule is a per-table decision.

Unnecessary-suppression sites per declared module gate:
- cockpit 0, sampler 1, dashboard 12
- scripts 6, tests/scripts 9
- shared 39, escalation 184, fused-memory 307, orchestrator 1547
- total 2105 in 301 files

Some import pragmas are vestigial only because verify runs `uv sync --all-packages` and are load-bearing in a narrower env:
- escalation: about 115 `orchestrator.*` imports
- shared: 3, in tests/test_task_statuses.py
- scripts: 2, the lazy radon/complexipy imports in merge_lane_metrics.py

Outcome: the rule is enabled only in cockpit, dashboard and sampler. The census, criterion and re-measure method live in tests/scripts/test_pyright_unnecessary_ignore_opt_in.py.

Re-measure method: in a worktree with its own .venv (`env -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv sync --all-packages`), temporarily add the key to every table, run all nine module type_check_commands with --outputjson (about 7 min wall clock in parallel), count that rule, and restore the tree with git checkout.

Workspace-member pyright gotcha (task 5267, measured 2026-10-03): a member's module type_check_command `uv run --directory <m> pyright src/ tests/` passes EXPLICIT CLI targets, which override [tool.pyright] include. So widening include alone (e.g. adding "scripts") reaches only BARE `pyright` runs (hooks/project-checks, the fleet chain, editors), never the merge-verify type leg that runs that command verbatim under merge_verify_breadth "full". That is how fused-memory/scripts quietly accumulated 19 pyright errors. Both homes now name scripts/ for fused-memory and orchestrator. tests/scripts/test_member_scripts_type_gate.py discovers every member that has [tool.pyright] and scripts/*.py, and fails if either gate misses a script or an exclude/ignore carves one out. When adding a new checked directory to a member, edit BOTH include and the module type_check_command.

dark-factory has THREE distinct pyright invocation scopes that can disagree on the same file, which is what generated esc-3805-1/esc-3805-6 (task 3931, measured on base ca66f64fdc): (1) pre-commit, hooks/project-checks:106, `cd "$dir" && uv run pyright` — PACKAGE-scoped, venv pyright-python, version pinned by uv.lock (1.1.408); (2) verify's fallback fleet chain, dark-factory-orchestrator.yaml type_check_command — PACKAGE-scoped, unpinned `npx pyright` (resolved 1.1.413); (3) verify's FILE_SCOPED path, taken whenever the diff touches .py files — verify._scope_to_keyword folds away the leading `cd`, so it runs `npx pyright <repo-root-relative-file>` from the WORKTREE ROOT against the ROOT pyproject's [tool.pyright]. Root extraPaths lists `scripts`, per-package extraPaths generally do not — so a test importing a scripts/-only module (e.g. orchestrator/tests/test_run_vllm_eval.py's `import run_vllm_eval`) resolves to real types under (3) and to Unknown under (1) and (2). Measured 14 reportArgumentType errors root-scoped vs 0 package-scoped on the same file, same pyright. Fix direction: add the missing entry to the PACKAGE extraPaths (widen package to match root) — never remove `scripts` from root, which would convert a false-red into a permanent false-green.

Pyright baseline-comparison technique for verifying "no NEW errors": git checkout main -- <files> ; PYTHONPATH=... pyright <files> 2>&1 | grep "errors," ; git checkout HEAD -- <files>. Captures the count on main against the same set of files, then restores. Use this when CI doesn't run pyright on PRs but the plan requires zero net new pyright errors. Pre-existing errors in dark-factory: 16 (aiosqlite/dotenv/uvicorn/starlette import resolution + a few _UnavailableAllAccountsCapped attribute access errors from the import-fallback code path); these are unfixable without refactoring the import-fallback pattern.

EXTENDS the "hooks/project-checks does NOT run ruff over scripts/ or tests/scripts/" paragraph in the ruff-sim300 canonical entry (735a4af5) — the same gate gap applies to PYRIGHT, and the second half is easier to miss because it looks like those trees are simply untyped. Measured on task 4793 (2026-08-27): hooks/project-checks runs pyright only for PYRIGHT_PACKAGES=(fused-memory orchestrator dashboard) and only when a staged .py matches one of those prefixes, so a commit touching only scripts/ and tests/scripts/ prints nothing and skips pyright entirely. But BOTH trees register a real type gate in their module configs — scripts/orchestrator.yaml has `type_check_command: uv run --project shared pyright scripts/` and tests/scripts/orchestrator.yaml has the tests/scripts/ equivalent — so a type error there rides into the commit unnoticed and only fails much later in the verify lane, exactly as the ruff half does. Before committing anything under scripts/ or tests/scripts/, run BOTH yourself: `uv run --project shared ruff check <dir>` and `uv run --project shared pyright <dir>`. Note the first pyright invocation in a fresh worktree builds a .venv (~30-60s) and gets backgrounded by a 120s-default Bash timeout — size the timeout or poll it.

The verify system's fallback type-check path (orchestrator/src/orchestrator/verify.py: _build_fallback_config + _strip_leading_cd) scopes pyright to a single touched file and strips the leading `cd <module> &&`, which fixes path resolution but also discards pyright's CWD-based venv discovery. Any root-level "loose" Python file outside every uv workspace member (e.g. tests/scripts/*.py) that imports a third-party package (like pytest) will fail pyright with reportMissingImports whenever it's the sole file in a diff, because the repo root has no pyrightconfig.json/[tool.pyright]. The established workaround in this codebase is an inline `# pyright: ignore[reportMissingImports]` comment on the import line (see tests/scripts/test_spawn_claude.py and, as of task 2034, tests/scripts/test_orchestrator_watchdog.py). Reproduce/confirm with: `env -u VIRTUAL_ENV PATH=<minimal> npx pyright <file>`.

reify main is a genuinely HOT shared checkout and a /prd session must expect it to move underneath itself. During one ~2-hour authoring session on 2026-08-26/27 the following landed from concurrent sessions: the spec-conformance-suite PRD (#6758–#6791), the gui-purpose-surface PRD (#6803, #6831–#6839), an F2 solver ruling, and several merged task branches — and `git status` showed ~8 other PRD files modified plus ~30 untracked fixtures belonging to other sessions. Practical consequences: (1) task-id ranges INTERLEAVE across concurrently-filing sessions, so a commit message saying "decomposed into #6758-#6791" can span ids that belong to a different PRD — never infer ownership from a range, check metadata.prd_path; (2) `git add -A` or adding a directory would sweep other sessions' untracked work, which is why the overlay mandates listing every path explicitly and using `git commit --only`; (3) a PRD's cross-PRD table can be accurate when written and stale hours later — two sibling PRDs recorded this one as "does not exist on any branch" and "untracked in project_root" respectively, both true at authoring; (4) code anchors verified at one SHA are a DATED SNAPSHOT and should be headed as such rather than re-anchored later.

Reify's project_root is worked by many concurrent sessions and a sibling batch can go from "authored, no tasks filed" to "nine pending tasks" inside one authoring session.

Worked case, gui-purpose-surface: a research agent correctly found gui-on-demand-measurement had no filed tasks at ~20:10. By ~21:15 that PRD had decomposed into #6740-#6748 (commit 901f8f5b25). The PRD text and capability manifest both carried a binding asserting "not decomposed, so no wirable edge" — which would have been a FALSE manifest binding and would have filed four duplicate leaves. It was caught only because an unrelated `get_task` on #6722 happened to quote "#6741 (gui-on-demand-measurement β)" in its coordination note.

Cheap guards that would have caught it directly: `search_tasks` on the sibling PRD's slug right before submit_task, and `git log --oneline -10` right before committing. Both were run at authoring time and neither was re-run at filing time.

Corollary: `submit_task(planning_mode=True)` lands tasks as `deferred`, which is REVERSIBLE — nothing dispatches until `commit_planning` flips the batch. When a late-breaking finding is still being adjudicated, filing deferred and holding the flip is the right sequencing, not blocking the whole batch.

PRD subtask numbering can leak into Taskmaster global task-IDs as bogus deps. The skeptic earned its seat: it overturned two claims the lead and the proposer had both made (that OutsideSystem.failure_behaviour and the per-capability failure criterion are the same fact; that a nested-on-system design was "by construction" the best answer) and surfaced four side findings (validator messages reveal the exit to the prospect; refused write-ups are uncapped; stored drafts have no version; the T3 placement has no validator) that became tasks 14, 28 and 29. Fact (2026-10-07): the failure question is asked twice on purpose across the scoping session's instruments. Fact about scoping-intake session rules: the operator's first (independent) blind placement is not always against draft sequence 1. A prospect can request a write-up, converse more, and request again before Leo places; the second request discards a placement that does not exist, the draft becomes sequence 2, and Leo's first placement is against it. Draft sequence also counts guided rewrites. So 'which draft was this placed against' and 'which placement is this for the prospect' are distinct facts and the calibration row needs both. Also: Intake.place already holds the draft, so draft.sequence and draft.guided are available to the row without waiting on task 3 (R1, hidden sequence field in the placement form).

content: The interviewer prompt rule "a criterion you worded yourself is settled only when the prospect answers about it on its own" exists because of trial P-0001 turns 47-51 (2026-10-09 to 10-12): the prospect said "I'm not sure how to handle the duplicate upload", the interviewer invented a rule, put it seventh in a read-back list, the prospect said "that all seems right", and the analyst pinned it as a requirement the prospect never decided. The mechanism (prospect-UX PRD Appendix B §B5): ask about that criterion by itself in the same or next turn; the analyst prompt (§B6) marks an interviewer-worded criterion accepted only in a list as open, naming it as the interviewer's reading. A 16-turn opus self-play of the rewritten prompt (pottery owner, 2026-10-14) also found the old short-of-time rule would ask six more questions of someone leaving (now: one decisive part-2 question, then close) and that "offer to record it" for developer questions became another question (now: record without asking).

content: A held leaf in a review-all /prd batch can sit upstream of committed siblings: S12 β (894, deferred, x_seam_wait S13) is a dependency of γ/δ/ε (895/897/899), which were committed pending anyway. commit_planning accepted a pending task depending on a deferred one without complaint, and the dependents stay blocked until the held leaf is released and done. A held leaf whose blocking binding stays OPEN in the sidecar (β's S13 simulator) is legitimate under the schema's OPEN semantics, since the leaf itself follows the upstream's shape. Also: metadata.files rejects directories, so a PRD file list naming a fixture directory (e.g. tests/fixtures/stored_runs/) must be replaced by file paths or described in the text.

solar_challenge PV ageing gotcha (task 284 architect; measured 2026-10-09 on main 9ef24ad with pvlib 0.15.1; holds on main once task/284 merges):
- The model chain's DC losses step multiplies each array's p_mp and i_mp by (1 - system_losses) x calculate_degradation_factor(age, rate). So simulate_pv_output's AC for an aged PVConfig is NOT the degradation factor times its new AC.
- Through the CEC Sandia or PVWatts inverters, a 0.90 factor keeps 0.8975-0.8991 of annual Bristol AC for unclipped default sizes. Inverter-limited arrays keep more: 6 kW on 3.68 kW 0.9151, 8 kW on 3.68 kW 0.9332.
- A test that needs an exact aged/new AC ratio uses create_simple_inverter_params, which is exactly linear below its rating (Pso and C0-C3 zero), as tests/unit/test_pv.py's LINEAR_INVERTER_CONFIG does.

candidates.content:
Billing push architecture (review 20260928T062907):
- No flow re-prices an already-billed statement. DirectDebit.recalculate (billing/dd.py) has no production caller; status.py only calls schedule().
- scp-bill's idempotency pre-check returns the existing BillingRun without a re-push.
- status.run pushes the Stripe invoice BEFORE it schedules the GoCardless DD, and persists only after both. A DD refusal therefore strands a Stripe invoice.
- ProviderRefusal is caught nowhere except the fleet close's per-account Exception guard.
- Stripe idempotency keys are reference_key(account, period) with no revision component.
Treat any future "revise a bill" feature as needing a revision-namespaced key and a persisted payment ledger.

Completed: Billing push: a provider refusal leaves a dangling Stripe invoice and crashes scp-bill --account; the collected-payment cancel differs between fake and real
Description: FINDING (review 20260928T062907). Traced by a review sub-agent at HEAD 3d74313, with file:line evidence. Re-verify the line numbers before editing.

1. NOTHING CATCHES ProviderRefusal. A repo-wide grep finds no `except ProviderRefusal`. runtime/roles/bill.py::_bill_single_account (≈:327-374) turns ConsentDenied, BillingOrderError and PropertyOfRecordMismatch into tagged `[TAG] … nothing persisted` lines. A refusal from dd.schedule() instead escapes as a raw traceback. The fleet close is fine: fleet_run.py:203-215 catches Exception per account.

2. PUSH ORDER BREAKS "pushes NOTHING". billing/status.py (≈:386-391) creates the Stripe invoice before it schedules the GoCardless DD, and store.put (≈:301-303) comes after both. When the DD is refused, the Stripe invoice already exists but no BillingRun is persisted. One reachable trigger: dd._require_collectable (billing/dd.py:33-40) checks only amount > 0, and the real GoCardless £1.00 minimum is "not modelled" (billing/cassettes/README.md:27-31). A 1-99p amount due therefore passes locally and is refused by the real rail. Suggested fix: check collectability, including a governed or constant rail minimum, before any provider call, and hold or skip with a typed reason. Alternatively, void the Stripe invoice when the DD is refused. Add a fake-lane test showing that a refused DD leaves no Stripe invoice.

3. cancel_payment IGNORES COLLECTED STATUS, AND FAKE AND REAL DIFFER. DirectDebit.recalculate (dd.py:70-96) cancels `current` with no status check. FakeGoCardless.cancel_payment (billing/providers/fakes.py:293-302) quietly turns a CONFIRMED (collected) payment into CANCELLED. The real GoCardlessDirectDebit.cancel_payment (billing/providers/gocardless.py:185-187) lets gocardless_pro InvalidStateError through untranslated, unlike create_payment, which maps errors to ProviderRefusal. pyright WARNING COUNT IS NOT A STABLE READING UNDER CONCURRENT LOAD. Running `cd fused-memory && npx pyright` while a full `uv run pytest tests/` was in flight returned "0 errors, 2 warnings"; an earlier run with no load returned "0 errors, 0 warnings"; a later quiet run returned "0 errors, 2 warnings, RC=0" again. The same concurrent block also made `uv run ruff check <all 7 members>` report 10 spurious E902 "No such file or directory" errors against directories that demonstrably existed — a clean re-run said "All checks passed!", RC=0. Do not read a lint/type-check failure taken while a big suite is running as a real finding; re-run it quiet before acting. The gates are exit-code-based (both RC=0 here), which is what saved this from being misdiagnosed.

candidates.content: Reify geometry queries split into three eval tiers, and documenting them as uniformly working is a trap. (1) The 4 WHOLE_HANDLE_GEOMETRY_QUERY_NAMES — volume/area/centroid/bounding_box — dispatch via try_eval_geometry_query but need a realized kernel: under `reify check` or with no OCCT they are Value::Undef. (2) 14 top-level helpers eval non-Undef under OCCT (pinned by all_queries_walk_evals_top_level_helpers_to_non_undef). (3) SEVEN sub-handle-arg helpers — normal, curvature (surface AND curve forms), length, perimeter, adjacent_faces, shared_edges — are compile-time typed but STILL evaluate to Value::Undef at DSL eval, because post_process_topology_selectors is single-pass and never hydrates the intermediate `single(faces(s))` cell; their runtime semantics are pinned only by DIRECT OcctKernelHandle queries in multi_feature_part_sub_handle_queries_return_non_undef. The authoritative split is the header table of examples/kernel_queries/all_queries_walk.ri. Separately, topology selectors no longer return List<Geometry>: units.rs::topology_selector_result_type returns Type::Selector(SelectorKind::Face/Edge/...) for faces/edges/edges_by_length/faces_by_area/faces_by_normal, so docs/reify-stdlib-reference.md §3.9's List<Curve>/List<Surface> signatures are STALE — treat the compiler as source of truth for result types.

Reify compiler: sibling-let geometry references are NOT uniformly recoverable from RealizationDecl.operations. The #4668 sibling pre-check (crates/reify-compiler/src/geometry.rs:1374-1385) emits GeomRef::Sub(name) ONLY on the Modify/Transform/Pattern/Sweep/Isosurface argument path. Boolean ops early-return before it (geometry.rs:1290-1308) into resolve_boolean_arg (crates/reify-compiler/src/geometry_boolean.rs:28-107), which only pre-checks the cross-sub `self.<sub>.<member>` shape and otherwise INLINES the operand's initializer, referring to it as GeomRef::Step(n). So for `param geometry : Solid = difference(body, holes)` the names "body"/"holes" appear nowhere in the template's operations. This inlining is deliberate and PINNED by crates/reify-compiler/tests/harness_langcore/let_scope_tests.rs:552-603, so "make Booleans emit GeomRef::Sub" is a cross-crate behaviour change, not a local fix. Consequence: reify_eval::deps::extract_realization_edges (crates/reify-eval/src/deps.rs:691-744) gates every arm on GeomRef::Sub and therefore registers NO edge for sibling Boolean operands — it is NOT a valid oracle for "is this realization consumed downstream".

Correct data source for geometry consumption edges: the value-cell layer. Since #4954 every geometry binding emits a ValueCellDecl alongside its realization, and its `default_expr` holds the un-inlined ValueRef(ValueCellId) operands. Walk it with the existing exhaustive reify_ir::CompiledExpr::collect_value_refs (crates/reify-ir/src/expr.rs:1008) — the repo's dependency-tracking walk; it covers every nesting variant and treats CrossSubGeometryRef as a ValueRef leaf, so no hand-rolled partial walk is needed. CRITICAL filter: only cells whose cell_type == Type::Geometry count as consumers. A `: Rigid` structure auto-derives mass/centroid/moment_of_inertia lets that all reference `geometry` but are Scalar/Point3/Tensor-typed; counting them marks the TERMINAL realization as consumed and hides the finished part. Established while resolving esc-5195-1 (task #5195, default-visibility of intermediate geometry).

Reify language-substrate probe findings (2026-07-24, debug binary @ main 366c63a679; fixtures committed at docs/prds/v0_6/fixtures/ with thread_/hole_/fit_ prefixes): (1) The comment at crates/reify-compiler/stdlib/ports_mechanical.ri:58-62 claiming "if/match don't parse in a let RHS" is STALE — both `match` (bare-variant arms, NO trailing comma) and `if…then…else` (then/else keyword form, NOT braces) parse and evaluate in let RHS today; task 5453 updates the comment. (2) Instance geometry members cannot be consumed in geometry ops — difference(plate, h.cutter) on a let-constructed StructureInstance fails compile with "difference() argument 2 must be a geometry expression", including through a let-alias; scalar member reads and derived-let readback work fine (ThreadSpec(...).tap_drill evals correctly with no stdlib re-declaration on the let path). Delivered by uniform-member-access task 5426. (3) .ri functions returning Geometry parse but the geometry-expression lowering rejects unknown fn names ("unsupported geometry function") — delivered by task 5428. (4) Enum-typed ctor param binding works for stdlib-defined structures/enums (ThreadSpec with ThreadSystem.ISO_Metric binds fine) but FAILS for user-module enums with "argument 'fit' has type 'Enum(Fit)' but param 'fit' requires structure type 'Fit'" — fix is uniform-member-access task 5429. (5) some(geometry) passes check but Option<Geometry> payload is untested end-to-end anywhere in-tree (every in-tree Option<Geometry> is = none); thread-hole task 5453's row-10 test closes this. (6) Calling an op with contract-violating args yields silent undef + OpContractViolation note + exit 0 on reify eval — the INV-SF-1/-2 pre-state.

Reify: cross-sub `distance(a, b)` does NOT resolve on the build path — it is fully indeterminate, not merely "verdict-only". Measured 2026-08-26 at main 2ea72cc5e8 by the P2 decompose D3 run.
- INLINE form: `reify check` exits 0 with `INDETERMINATE`, stderr `warning: constraint ... indeterminate: operator undefined for these operand kinds: StructureInstance` — the operand arrives as a StructureInstance, not a GeometryHandle.
- LET-BOUND form under `reify build -o out.step`: exit 0, INDETERMINATE, `undefined inputs: <cell>`; the STEP is still written.
- A/B/C triple (no constraint | `>= 5mm` | `>= 500mm`): `__auto_pose = frame(point(0 m, 0 m, 0 m), [1,0,0,0]q)` in ALL THREE. The pose does not move, and there is no verdict to move it.
This is task #6583 (cross-sub geometry reads drop the sub's `at` placement) manifesting on the query side. Consequence for any design that drives a pose from a kernel query: it needs POSED operands, so #6583 is a hard prerequisite, not a coordination note. A query over unposed operands measures the wrong assembly.

Separately measured in the same run: the arity-2 `min_clearance(a, b)` overload (belt PRD §7.2, task #5441, pending) does not exist AND is SILENTLY ACCEPTED — `reify check` on a fixture using it exits 0 with INDETERMINATE, never a rejection. Only the arity-3 kinematic `min_clearance(snapshot, a, b)` in KINEMATIC_QUERY_NAMES exists. `distance` IS registered in GEOMETRY_QUERY_NAMES and does resolve on the build path for SAME-SCOPE operands (probe p_a_mixed.ri gave 0.009999999999999997 m), which is why it is the safe capability to write signals against today.

Reify gotcha (examples/kernel_queries/all_queries_walk.ri:135-185): the 7 sub-handle geometry consumers — normal, curvature, length, perimeter, adjacent_faces, shared_edges (args derived from single(faces(b))/single(edges(b))) — evaluate to Value::Undef EVEN on the build path with an OCCT kernel, due to the single-pass post_process_topology_selectors limitation (engine_build.rs:3942). Only top-level-arg geometry ops (e.g. closest_point(pt, b), volume(b), distance(b, p)) genuinely resolve to non-Undef on build. So a 'consumer resolves with a kernel' fixture must use a top-level-solid-arg consumer, not the chained single(faces(b)) idiom. Builtin name families are three distinct sets in reify-compiler/src/units.rs: GEOMETRY_FUNCTION_NAMES (constructors, :21), GEOMETRY_QUERY_NAMES (:629), GEOMETRY_TOPOLOGY_SELECTOR_NAMES (:198).

Reify R1a (task 4651) implementation direction baked into the task description on 2026-06-18: extend the EXISTING honest-decline precedent `detect_unresolved_ad_hoc_selectors` @ crates/reify-eval/src/engine_eval.rs:863 (which runs on the value-eval path at :3088 eval() and :3723 eval_cached(), and currently emits a WARNING for @face/@edge AdHocSelector cells that resolve to Value::Undef) to cover geometry-query consumption. Classify geometry-query calls via the existing `is_geometry_query_call` @ geometry_ops.rs:2464 (NOTE: currently only matches volume/area/centroid/bounding_box single-arg — must be widened, or key on the consumed arg being a geometry-query result that resolved to Undef) plus `GEOMETRY_FUNCTION_NAMES` @ reify-compiler/src/units.rs:21. Q1 says no new IR field is needed if call-shape classification suffices.

KEY INSIGHT (Reify value-eval, 2026-06-18) that overturned the architect's pessimistic options B and C on task 4651: an honest-decline E_EVAL_UNRESOLVED diagnostic does NOT require a Selector-typed stdlib parameter. The architect's premise "no stdlib fn accepts a `: Selector` param, so there's no type-checking consumption site" was a red herring — the consumer needs a GEOMETRY-typed param (not a Selector param), and Selector→List<Geometry>/Geometry coercion is ALREADY wired in type_compat.rs (one-directional, ~:237). Therefore a type-checking, eval-reaching, silently-Undef fixture exists TODAY via the geometry-query-result → geometry-typed-builtin idiom: e.g. `let top_face = single(faces_by_normal(b, zdir, tol)); let neighbors = adjacent_faces(b, top_face)` (examples/kernel_queries/all_queries_walk.ri:~135-186). In pure value-eval (no kernel) the geometry query resolves to Value::Undef and the geometry-typed consumer (adjacent_faces, normal, closest_point, centroid) silently collapses it — exactly the 4577 silent-Undef class. Consequently: option B (add R1a→R2b dependency) was unnecessary (R1a stays independent/lands-first); option C (synthetic Rust test) was an unneeded downgrade that loses the user-observable `reify eval` signal (G2 gate).

Engine/language substrate facts probed 2026-10-08 (main ~09dc41ec1e..a8d99a691b, target/debug/reify) that any field-to-geometry or multi-kernel PRD must respect: (a) a .ri lambda cannot read Point3 coordinates (`p.x` -> "member access not yet supported"; Point3<Length> has no projection .x; distance/norm unavailable on the value-eval surface) — tracked by #6871 (pending) and #6892; a closed-form SDF is unauthorable in .ri. (b) No stdlib namespacing: `sdf.box` is "unknown qualifier", `std.x.y` is out of scope by stdlib-namespace.md §9, `import std.fields as sf` does not resolve; field builtins are bare prelude names (FIELD_OP_NAMES); qualified resolution is stdlib-namespace ν #5505. (c) Named args parse as `name: expr` (never `=`) but BUILTINS BIND BY POSITION and drop labels (lookup_named_arg_value; #6313) — put optional params last. (d) fn_field types its result Field<Real,..> regardless of the lambda, compose requires codomain==domain, no domain remap/transform on fields, no list reduction (min(list) evaluates to Undef; fold/reduce unresolved). (e) `reify check` and `reify eval` never load OpenVDB (only cmd_build under module_has_isosurface, cmd_check under thickness-DFM), so `reify check examples/multi_kernel/voxel_to_mesh.ri` errors today. (f) A user fn whose body calls pointwise_min evaluates to Undef (OpContractViolation) while the direct call works. (g) The VolumeMesh (FEA) edge in engine_build.rs is entered only when the realization's demanded_repr == VolumeMesh && is_terminal_realization; it tessellates the terminal via the OWNING kernel. realize_for_check builds with ExportFormat::Step and exports nothing, so every `reify check` carries a BRep terminal demand — never key a refusal on demand values. (h) Pass order: post_process_kinematic_queries runs after named_steps and BEFORE run_post_processes (an associated fn, no self, default kernel only); derived lets run inside it as a fixpoint; a constraint can consume a post-processed let. (i) realize_solid_sdf_at degrades silently: five None paths with no Diagnostic/UndefCause. (j) Geometry queries (try_eval_geometry_query), kinematic queries, distance_between_placed, resolve_export_body_color and realize_solid_sdf_at all run on the DEFAULT kernel by bare handle id — a body owned by OpenVDB/Manifold (e.g. an isosurface body) silently gets a foreign-id answer; no owning task existed until implicit-solids leaf γ. (k) Transform constructor is transform3(orient_identity(), vec3(..)); density literal is 7850kg/m^3 (m3 is not a unit; no space); planes are plane_xy/xz/yz(offset); constraints are the unnamed `constraint <expr> <= 0mm` form. (l) FEA body-overload BCs are placed by AABB-face coordinate selection (x_min/x_max node sets), which works on any mesh; gmsh is not linked in any shipping binary (#6660, depends on #7052).

Reify geometry/DSL behaviours measured at the M-WASTE decompose (main df968c3c82, 2026-10-11):

Geometry evaluation:
- An emptying boolean is NOT a realisation failure. difference(box(10mm,10mm,10mm), box(20mm,20mm,20mm)) realises with volume 0 m^3 and rc 0.
- A zero or negative box dimension IS a realisation failure: "box dimensions must be finite positive values", the volume is undef, rc 1.
- shell(box 10mm, 6mm) gives a negative kernel volume, which becomes undef with a warning and rc 0.
- OCCT GProp volume of difference(box 40x30x10 mm, cylinder r5 h4 mm) matches the analytic 12000−100π mm³ to about 1e-16 relative.

Language and parsing:
- The one-line form `structure def X { param a : T; param b : U }` is a parse error ("syntax error in structure body"); one member per line is required.
- A trait `let` without a body is a parse error.
- Enums with named-field payload variants, and structures with a List<record> param, both compile and evaluate.
- filter(self.descendants, Trait) compiles and evaluates to entity-path strings.
- An unregistered builtin call gives only a Warning ("unresolved function"), an undef let, and rc 0.

reify: the generic GUI error "geometry error: geometry operation failed: expected numeric value" originates from `extract_f64` in crates/reify-kernel-occt/src/lib.rs:155 (mirrored in the fidget kernel, crates/reify-kernel-fidget/src/kernel.rs:351) when a non-numeric `Value` (almost always `Undef`, since as_f64 returns Some only for Int/Real/Scalar) reaches a geometry-op argument (cylinder radius/height, translate components, etc.). It is HARD to trace because (a) the message says nothing about which op/arg or what the value actually was, and (b) the diagnostic is attached to the whole realization span (crates/reify-eval/src/engine_build.rs:4483-4486, label "in this realization") — so the reported line/column is the enclosing `body = ...` expression, not the failing sub-expression. This is the motivating case for the spawned "make undef self-describing" PRD: make Undef carry provenance (reason + source span) so consumers report the cause, and distinguish genuine partial-determinacy (correctly silent) from masked scoping/ordering bugs (should be loud).

Reify compiles geometry and values in two disjoint worlds, and this is why geometry constructors silently yield Undef in any value-position expression (lambda bodies, list literals). Geometry world: `is_geometry_let` (reify-compiler/src/geometry.rs:202) gates `compile_geometry_call` (geometry.rs:1096), producing `Vec<CompiledGeometryOp>` in a `RealizationDecl` referenced by `GeomRef::Step/Sub`, executed by the kernel; `Value::GeometryHandle` is minted only AFTER the build by `post_process_geometry_handle_cells` (reify-eval/src/engine_build.rs:9479) or symbolically by `mint_symbolic_geometry_handles_into_values` (engine_eval.rs). Value world: `compile_expr` -> `CompiledExpr` -> `reify_expr::eval_expr`, a pure evaluator with no kernel and no realization context. In value position a geometry call hits the ladder arm `is_geometry_function(name) => Type::dimensionless_scalar()` (expr.rs:3346) and at eval time falls through `reify_stdlib::eval_builtin` to its terminal `Value::Undef` (reify-stdlib/src/lib.rs:301) with no diagnostic. Corollary: geometry can never be constructed at expression-eval time; bridging requires compile-time lowering into a RealizationDecl. Sibling geometry lets are resolved by AST RE-INLINING via `geometry_lets: HashMap<&str, &reify_ast::Expr>` (entity.rs:3769) with a `visiting` cycle guard, not by value references.

Why task #4954 (eval-uniform-dependency γ — geometry lets emit first-class value cells) is hard and was repeatedly blocked (as of 2026-07-06, 4 failed verify attempts): giving a geometry let a value cell makes its kernel-less placeholder GeometryHandle{kernel_handle:None} visible in the shared eval `values` map at its topo slot. A DIRECT non-selector geometry-let consumer (canonical witness: restrict()/ContainmentQuery in restrict_field_b5_integration, crates/reify-eval/tests/fields_restrict_e2e.rs — `v_in = sample(restrict(field, region), pt)` where region is a bare geometry let) then evaluates against that placeholder and caches a non-Undef symbolic-only result, which build()'s real-kernel post-pass SKIPS (it only revisits still-Undef cells) → the consumer is permanently pinned to the symbolic result (v_in stuck at Undef instead of Real(42.0)). This is exactly why mint_symbolic_geometry_handles_into_values never feeds its flips into re-eval and why R3f feeds only the selector-mint's flips. γ additionally surfaces a stale-Undef gate clause-8 (is_build_only_dispatch_call) enumeration gap: build-only calls behind a geometry let (union/difference/intersect, max_deviation, 2-arg faces_by_normal) trip no_stale_undef_invariant_gate once the dependency becomes genuinely resolved. A clean fix needs the placeholder kept from leaking to direct non-selector consumers (e.g. scratch-scope resolution), not published wholesale into shared values.

Sub-instance geometry members are undef on the EVAL-VALUE surface even for posed, hand-placed subs: `reify eval` prints `Rig.<sub>.body = undef` (and `distance(a.body, b.body)` is unresolvable at check/eval) while the BUILD pipeline is fully real — the same file exports 2 disjoint solids at correct AABBs in STL and STEP. Realization/posing surfaces only via the `reify build` kernel walk. Discovered by the D3 adversary during the indexed-sub-instantiation decompose (2026-07-25, main 94e1631111; fixtures tests/prd-gate/fixtures/hand_placed_twin_two_subs_eval.ri, posed_subs_distance_query_unresolvable.ri, committed ba7bbcfb53). Consequence: any PRD/probe asserting "eval shows a real body handle" for sub members is claiming NEW capability, not existing behavior — indexed-sub γ (task 5483) delivers it for indexed collection members. Probe sessions must test geometry claims on the build channel, not eval stdout.

Gotcha (measured 2026-10-01, task 5312): in sub-instance elaboration (crates/reify-eval/src/unfold.rs), geometry cells (`let body = box(...)` AND `param body : Solid = box(...)`) evaluate to Undef at instance scope, so any typed selector over them (`face(body, "root")`, hoisted `__sel_N`) is Undef there too. The #6662 @optimized instance-reuse gate (unfold/optimized_instance_reuse.rs) then sees the support/load struct differ from the template's and declines with an InputsDiffer warning, so an FEA solve inside a `sub` falls back to the unsolved `ElasticResult()` shell whenever its supports or loads carry typed selectors.

content: reify engine gaps that leave a geometry query Undef on a correct design, catalogued 2026-10-11 with probes on the OCCT debug binary (they matter because task 5973 will make such cells an Error on capable engines). (1) Instance-qualified geometry cells are Undef on the value surface (`Asm.b.geometry = undef`, `Rig.a.body = undef`) even though the template-level cell is realized; 1-argument queries still fold at the scoped id (`Asm.b.mass`, `Asm.b.centroid` resolve) but the 2-argument `moment_of_inertia(geometry, body_density)` injected by stdlib Rigid does not, so `Asm.b.moment_of_inertia` and `Asm.b.moi_principal` are undef — task 8517; real designs hit: designs/litter_tray/fit_coupon.ri and bottom_deck_split.ri. (2) A geometry query inside a `where` guard branch stays Undef in the ACTIVE branch, both for a geometry declared in the branch (which is not realized at all) and for a top-level geometry queried from inside the branch — task 8518. (3) Cross-sub queries over posed subs: the bare form `distance(a.body, b.body)` is Undef and silent, while the `self.` form `distance(self.a.body, self.b.body)` returns a WRONG value — 0 m, and intersects true, for two cylinders placed 50 mm apart, because the `at` placement is dropped — both owned by task 5436's carried-frame work. (4) An inline geometry argument to the non-volume query family (`intersects(box(10mm,10mm,10mm), b)`) is silently Undef because resolve_geometry_handle_arg only matches ValueRef / cross-sub ref / index access; `volume(box(...))` is hoisted and works — task 5197. (5) Geometry query builtins take any argument types at compile time (`length(vec3)`, `contains(list, x)`, `volume(2.5)` compile clean and evaluate to Undef) — task 8520.

2bd44630-e994-4e97-b522-12ac824b02a8.content: The reify-eval no-stale-Undef invariant checker (task 4952 α, crates/reify-eval/src/invariants.rs) cannot use PRD §6.1's literal predicate alone: `param u = undef` cells (UndefCause::UserUndef, zero deps → the "all deps resolved" clause is vacuously true) and op-domain-failures (UndefCause::OpContractFailed) are legitimately Undef yet would be false-flagged, breaking the green-corpus signal on fixtures undef_causes_layer1.ri / undef_trace.ri. The checker must ALSO exclude cells whose Engine::undef_causes() entry is UserUndef or OpContractFailed, and its debug-gate harness must call engine.set_capture_undef_causes(true) before eval so that map is populated. This exclusion-set extension is sanctioned by PRD §11 Q2/Q4. Unbound/propagated undefs are already exempt via the deps-resolved clause; AwaitingSolve/SolveFailed via the auto-cell clause.

Completed: Version the stored draft and release records so a schema change does not break existing sessions (store.py::Stored)
Description: Draft and Released embed Analysis with extra="forbid" (record.py:11, store.py) and are re-validated on every read (store.py::_read), with no version field and no migration. Intake.prospect_view reads both on every prospect page load, and a ValidationError matches no case in error_pages.session_error_page, so after any schema change or tightened validator an existing session's whole page, chat included, becomes a 500 (web.py:95-100), and the operator page likewise. Tasks 10, 14, the criterion-to-system link and the T3 validator all change the schema or tighten validation. Found in the R13 discussion on 2026-10-07; agreed with Leo.
Analysis: PREMISES, checked on base 0a7cf7c (main = branch tip).
- The task title names store.py::Stored. That class no longer exists: an earlier task folded it into record.Frozen (record.py:12-13, ConfigDict(frozen=True, extra="forbid")). Draft (store.py:35-46) and Released (store.py:49-53) now derive from Frozen directly and embed Analysis, so the defect stands as described.
- SessionStore._read (store.py:177-179) runs kind.model_validate_json on every read. No version field exists and nothing migrates.
- Intake.prospect_view (intake.py:64-72) reads the draft and the release on every prospect page load. The /criteria and /report routes go through it too (prospect_pages.py:80-84, 102-109).
- Intake.operator_view (intake.py:125-137) reads the draft, the operator placement and the release. request_write_up, place, rewrite and release read the draft (intake.py:101-158, 204-212).
- error_pages.session_error_page (error_pages.py:11-30) has no case for ValidationError, so web._dispatch (web.py:92-104) answers 500 "Something went wrong". Any Analysis change or tightened validator therefore turns an existing session's chat page into a 500, and its operator page likewise.
- purge_unused/_last_used (intake.py:228-248) read the release for its time and leave a session whose release cannot be read in place, reporting it. tests/test_session_flow.py:347-363 pins that. A naive versioning would make every session released before a schema change "unreadable" to the purge, so no such session would ever be deleted: the 90-day promise would break.
- Deletion never reads the draft. The prospect route goes intake.delete -> _locked -> store.get (session.json only) -> shutil.rmtree. The operator route goes through by_prospect_id/readable(), which reads session.json only. So deletion already survives an unreadable draft; this task pins that with a test.

POLICY CHOSEN: an operator-facing state, not a migration table (see design decisions).
- store.RECORD_FORMAT = 1 is the record format this version writes drafts and releases in, and the only one it reads.
- Draft and Released derive from a small base, StoredWriteUp(Frozen), holding record_format: int = RECORD_FORMAT and analysis: Analysis. The format is therefore written on save by the record's own serialisation.
- On read, the store first reads only the declared format: a Frozen model _DeclaredFormat(record_format: int = 1), validated with pydantic 2.13.5's per-call model_validate_json(..., extra="ignore"). A record from before formats were numbered declares none and is format 1, so Leo's existing trial sessions keep working.
- Only a record declaring RECORD_FORMAT is validated in full. Every other outcome is returned, never raised, as UnreadableWriteUp(record_format=<declared> | None): another format, unparseable bytes, or a current-format record that fails the record's rules.
- draft() and released() return Draft/Released | UnreadableWriteUp | None.
- A new SessionStore.released_at(token) reads only released_at (a Frozen _ReleaseTime, again extra="ignore" per call) from a release in any format. A damaged release still raises there, so the purge keeps counting a release made in an older format and keeps leaving a damaged one in place.

candidates.content: solar_challenge finance gotcha (measured on main 270864e, 2026-10-01, task 271 architect). Since CR2 (commit 240666d), project_multi_year sums basis-C own-use, export, import and battery discharge over the raw simulated window and does NOT annualise them. Only SEG is annualised (×365/days below 360 days). On a short window, solve_cost_recovery_rate and project_economics therefore set N days of own-use against a year of opex, debt and floor. The older advice "use --start/--end for exploratory optimize/finance runs" (also printed by `optimize configs`) gives every config infeasible_above_retail at the retail clamp today. Measured: a 3-day copy of a fleet that solves at 18.96p on a full year returns 30p infeasible_above_retail. Task 271 plans to annualise all four aggregates through one shared `_annualisation_scale` rule. Until it merges, use full-year windows for any solve or projection.

solar_challenge gotcha (task 488 architect, measured 2026-10-06 on 959baf6): a fleet simulator injected into finance.project_multi_year, directly or through `finance run --project`, must return as many per-home results as the scenario has homes. finance._throughput_at (finance.py:1425) zips the scenario-sized per-home throughput list against the per-home discharge list built from the simulated results with strict=True, so a mismatched constant fleet raises ValueError once a non-seed age is projected. CODE FACT (main 18a3394), src/solar_challenge/finance.py::householder_bill, override branch (when finance.self_consumption_override is set):
- sc_kwh = override * gen_kwh, with no cap at demand_kwh;
- override_import_kwh = max(demand_kwh - sc_kwh, 0.0).
So when override × generation exceeds demand, the householder is billed own-use for solar they never consumed, and import is clamped to 0. _seg_export_income_gbp's override path recomputes export as (1 − override) × generation, which is consistent with the uncapped own-use. So the CBS is also credited with own-use revenue on energy no household consumed.

MEASURED on 2026-10-01 at base 18a3394, CPython 3.12.3, pvlib 0.15.1. The setup: scenarios/bristol-fin-calibration.yaml (5.5 kWp + 5 kWh, demand 3400 kWh, self_consumption_override 0.70), a year-long 2024 Bristol home, and task 252's prototype loss model.
- Generation is 6007.8 kWh lossless, so the override path gives own-use of 4205 kWh.
- With PVWatts losses, generation is 5149.0 kWh, so own-use is 3604 kWh.
- Both exceed the 3400 kWh demand.
- solve_cost_recovery_rate on a 5-home slice (grant × 5/100), lossless → with losses:
  - solved rate 11.440 → 11.819 p/kWh;
  - reported saving vs baseline £300.53 → £358.40;
  - representative outlay £735.11 → £677.24.
  The saving RISES when generation falls, because the uncapped override bills less phantom own-use.

TO DECIDE: cap the override's own-use at demand, i.e. min(override × gen, demand), and carry the remainder to export, or refuse an override that exceeds demand. solar_challenge task 352 premise check (architect, measured 2026-10-02 on main 2bb0402 with a scratch script outside the tree, CPython 3.12.3, scipy 1.17.1). (1) project_multi_year's per-year curve is scipy PCHIP of its node values, and a curve-level test can see it. Setup: an injected simulate with self-consumption 12000*exp(-0.1*age), asset_life 25, and error_target_pct=1e6, which keeps only the seeds, so sampled_ages is (0,12,24). curve.points[y].fleet_self_consumption_kwh then matches PchipInterpolator over the injected node values to 9e-13. Between nodes PCHIP differs from np.interp by up to 935 kWh and from finance._monotone_hermite_interpolate by up to 575 kWh. With sys.modules['scipy.interpolate']=None the curve equals the fallback to 2e-12. So a test against a scipy oracle kills both the fallback and the linear mutant by a wide margin. (2) asset_life_years=1 gives sampled_ages (0,) and one point, so _interpolate_per_year's single-node branch is reachable through project_multi_year. (3) Retiring the fallback is feasible. Locked pvlib 0.15.1 requires scipy>=1.7.2 unconditionally, and uv.lock holds one scipy (1.17.1) for every Python minor. Adding a scipy floor to [project].dependencies then running `uv lock --offline` changes exactly two lines of uv.lock: solar-challenge's dependencies and its requires-dist. scipy ships no py.typed, so its import still needs `# type: ignore[import-untyped]` or a scipy.* mypy override. The PRD's decompose record (review/gap-register.md:91) already said "no fallback needed". (4) No SimulationResults builder exists on main outside tests/unit/test_finance_projection.py, so a curve-level test needs task 349's tests/_finance_builders.py.

In my_solar_challenge, the grid-services seam is fully exogenous: finance.py:1139 (inside project_multi_year._simulate_age) computes grid_services = finance.grid_services_income_per_kw_per_year_gbp × Σ(home.battery_config.max_discharge_kw for battery homes), added linearly to every YearPoint.fleet_revenue_gbp. project_economics then yields mean_fleet_surplus_per_year_gbp = mean(revenue − opex − debt). So changing the band rate shifts the FLEET project surplus by EXACTLY rate × Σ max_discharge_kw, independent of simulated energy. For the board scenario bristol-phase1-flex.yaml: 100 homes × 2.5 kW = Σ 250 kW; resolve_grid_services_band low/central/high = 1.5/12/48 → fleet-surplus increments £375/£3000/£12000/yr. To assert this exactly in a test, inject an age-independent constant simulate into project_multi_year (lambda fc,s,e: fixed FleetResults) so the adaptive-bisection node set is fixed and PCHIP (translation-equivariant) preserves the additive constant.
