candidates.content: GOTCHA (task 204): the embedded amqtt 0.11.3 test broker (tests/mqtt_broker.py::embedded_broker, mqtt pytest lane) races under concurrent QoS-1 fan-out. amqtt/mqtt/protocol/handler.py::_handle_qos1_message_flow registers the PUBACK waiter only AFTER 'await self._send_packet(...)'. A fast subscriber PUBACK is therefore logged as 'Received PUBACK for unknown pending message Id', and the orphaned waiter is cancelled at broker.shutdown(). embedded_broker teardown then raises asyncio.CancelledError even though every message was delivered. Serial publishing is unaffected; production/harness mosquitto 2 is unaffected. Real-broker hermetic tests that drive SimService (tests/integration/test_s1_fleet_to_store.py) must set Settings(sim_publish_concurrency=1).

GOTCHA (task 204, corrected 2026-10-07 by task 264's architect): the embedded amqtt test broker (tests/mqtt_broker.py::embedded_broker, mqtt pytest lane) races under concurrent QoS-1 fan-out. amqtt/mqtt/protocol/handler.py::_handle_qos1_message_flow registers the PUBACK waiter only AFTER 'await self._send_packet(...)'. This holds in 0.11.3 and is unchanged in 0.12.1. A fast subscriber PUBACK is therefore logged as 'Received PUBACK for unknown pending message Id'; a 3.11 run at concurrency 64 on 0.12.1 still logs one. The orphaned waiter then times out after 5 s, or is cancelled at broker.shutdown(). On 0.11.3, embedded_broker teardown then raised asyncio.CancelledError even though every message had been delivered. amqtt 0.12.1 (task 264) stops only that shutdown re-raise; it does not remove the race. Serial publishing is unaffected, and so is mosquitto 2 in production and the validation harness. Until task 264 lands, tests/integration/test_s1_fleet_to_store.py pins Settings(sim_publish_concurrency=1). Task 264 removes the pin. It must also keep the harness's publisher connected until the subscriber has drained, because on Python 3.12+ amqtt 0.12.1 drops already-PUBACKed messages it has not yet routed when their publisher disconnects (memory fe72e290-d3aa-4403-a88b-40ee204a3d48).

Hazard noted 2026-09-28: scp-ingest's durability rests on a stable MQTT client id (Settings.mqtt_ingest_client_id = "scp-ingest") with clean_session=False, so the broker queues a QoS-1 backlog during an outage. Any other client that CONNECTs with the same client id and a clean session (a health probe, a deploy verify, a drill) kicks ingest off and discards its queued backlog — silent telemetry loss. Probes must use an ephemeral per-connection id (P-Ops·γ1 adds a typed ClientId with ClientId.ephemeral(...), and BrokerConfig.from_settings requires an explicit client_id and refuses an ephemeral id equal to the ingest id). validation/drills/broker_probe.py uses a fixed id "scp-drill-probe", so concurrent probes can also take over each other.

GOTCHA (measured by task 274's architect, 2026-09-25, amqtt 0.11.3 via tests/mqtt_broker.py::embedded_broker, aiomqtt 2.5.1): the embedded amqtt broker keeps a clean_session=False session's SUBSCRIPTION across a reconnect (a client reconnecting with the same identifier receives LIVE publishes without re-subscribing; an identifier that never subscribed receives nothing), but it does NOT queue QoS-1 messages published while that session is offline (resumed-without-subscribe and resumed-with-resubscribe both received 0 of 5 offline publishes). So a hermetic mqtt-lane test can prove a durable subscription is held under an identity, but offline-backlog queueing can only be proven against real mosquitto (validation/mosquitto.conf sets max_queued_messages 0), e.g. via validation.run's testcontainers topology or the PLATFORM_TEST_MQTT_HOST lane.

metadata.superseded_reason: Root cause corrected: the loss of persistent-session state is caused by AnonymousAuthPlugin (allow_anonymous flags every session anonymous), not by amqtt itself. See correction 86e8e483.

candidates.content: MEASURED by task 865's architect on 2026-10-13 (aiomqtt 2.5.1, paho 2.1.0, CPython 3.11.15), probing a persistent session (clean_session=False) that resumes a 20-message QoS-1 backlog, against both the embedded amqtt 0.11.3 broker (durable_sessions=True) and eclipse-mosquitto:2.0.22 in docker. (1) Cancelling Client.__aenter__ mid-connect leaves the connection reading: len(client.messages) went from 0-2 right after the cancel to 20 one second later, all PUBACKed, and none were redelivered on the next resume. (2) Letting __aenter__ finish and then calling __aexit__ stopped acknowledgement at once: the queue stayed flat after the close. On mosquitto, the messages still in flight at the close were redelivered on the next resume (19 redelivered, 5 duplicates, 0 missing). On amqtt 0.11.3 they were LOST (17 missing), because amqtt's handler._handle_qos1_message_flow pops an outgoing in-flight QoS-1 message from session.inflight_out in its finally clause when the disconnect cancels the PUBACK waiter. So an mqtt-lane amqtt test can pin aiomqtt's own acknowledge-or-not behaviour, but never in-flight redelivery.

DISCOVERY (M1 validation 2026-07-03, findings F2+F3, fixed by tasks 133/134/141): three unattended-failure modes witnessed on real infra. (1) scp-ingest crashed on broker disconnect (aiomqtt MqttError propagated out of the subscriber's async-for; no reconnect loop) — root disconnect cause was keepalive starvation: blocking synchronous DB writes inside the asyncio event loop starved PINGREQ during a sustained drain, mosquitto k60 dropped the client. (2) The clean-session subscription (auto client-id, c1) meant mosquitto discarded the queued QoS-1 backlog on disconnect — recovery in validation was only possible because the simulator replay is deterministic and store writes are ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING idempotent; real edge data would have been lost. Unbatched per-message commits drained at only ~90-170 msg/s (fine at production's ~1.7 msg/s, ~50x too slow for backfill). (3) A dispatch process wedged silently mid-tick on a half-dead Postgres socket — main thread epoll-parked, DB sessions idle 15+ min, process alive so systemd Restart=on-failure could never fire; only the device-side 60s watchdog protected the fleet (bare create_engine had no connect_timeout/keepalives/statement_timeout/pre-ping).

Convention (solar_challenge_platform tests, since task 691): to model aiomqtt 2.5.1's stop-time transport edge cases, reuse the existing doubles rather than inventing new ones. tests/ingestion/subscriber_harness.py's IdleStream.wait_closed() lets a test cut the close short, as a second SIGTERM cuts aiomqtt's disconnect wait short: cancel a task awaiting it, and a receive still waiting fails with CancelledError. In tests/ingestion/test_ingest_shutdown_drain.py, _SlowToDisconnectClient(stream, disconnect_timeout=None|seconds) models a broker that never acknowledges the disconnect: with a timeout, its exit raises MqttError('Operation timed out') and every later connect raises MqttReentrantError. _ReconnectStuckBeforeConnackClient models a stop that lands in a reconnect's __aenter__, which leaves the connection open and acknowledging. A real-broker mqtt-lane test in tests/ingestion/test_inbox.py pins the cut-short behaviour these doubles mirror.

Ingest F2 backlog-resume THROUGHPUT throttle (task 157): the resume drain is slow (~66 msg/s vs ~634 online) purely because validation/mosquitto.conf omits max_inflight_messages, so the harness broker uses mosquitto's default 20 (broker holds ≤20 unacked QoS-1 msgs in flight to a resuming subscriber). It is NOT a 'batch-write-before-ack' coupling: ingestion/subscriber.py uses aiomqtt's DEFAULT auto-ack (no manual_ack, no client.ack), so PUBACKs fire per-message on receipt, independent of the buffer's N-or-T batch flush. paho's client-side max_inflight governs OUTBOUND publishes only, not subscriber inbound delivery — so the fix is broker-config-side (raise max_inflight_messages in mosquitto.conf + docs/examples/README.md), and subscriber.py/buffer.py need no change. Zero-loss/dupes was never the issue.

FACTS (operational gotchas from the M1 validation session, 2026-07-03): (1) mosquitto's max_queued_messages default of 1000 silently DROPS queued QoS-1 backlog for slow/offline consumers — validation and deployment brokers must set 0 (now in docs/examples/README.md + validation/mosquitto.conf). (2) pgrep/pkill -f self-match trap: the Claude-Code Bash wrapper's own command line contains your pattern string, so `pkill -f "bin/scp-dispatch"` kills the wrapper itself and `pgrep -f` matches a phantom new pid every call — always use [b]racket patterns. (3) /tmp scratchpads are wiped on host reboot — validation evidence and scripts must be copied to durable dirs (mission-control outputs) as they are produced, not at session end. (4) Playwright `wait_until="networkidle"` NEVER fires on pages holding an open SSE stream (the ops dashboard's /api/ops/stream) — use "load". (5) The ops SPA reads its JWT from localStorage['scp_auth_token'] (browser smokes seed it via add_init_script); a real login form was added later by task 145. (6) Postgres RLS: the tenant_isolation policies deliberately evaluate TRUE when the app.current_customer_id GUC is unset (worker/fleet path) — RLS narrows only when the GUC is set; app-layer ScopedRepository is the primary isolation.

GOTCHA (task 264, measured 2026-10-07; amqtt 0.12.1 is the latest PyPI release and upstream main at 2026-10-06 has the same code): the embedded amqtt test broker loses QoS-1 messages it has already PUBACKed. It PUBACKs an inbound PUBLISH once it is queued on the publisher's session (session.delivered_message_queue). Broker._client_message_loop then routes that queue one message at a time and abandons the rest when the publisher DISCONNECTs. On CPython 3.12+, asyncio.wait_for no longer wraps its awaitable in a task, so amqtt's reader loop consumes a buffered burst, DISCONNECT included, before routing catches up. SimService at concurrency 64 then delivers 50/300 to a subscriber; 3.11 delivers 300/300, and swapping amqtt's wait_for shape flips both results. Workaround: keep the publisher connected until the subscriber has received every message. A BaseTopicPlugin whose topic_filtering sleeps on Action.PUBLISH reproduces the loss on any interpreter. mosquitto 2 is unaffected.

GOTCHA (task 274, measured 2026-09-27 with amqtt 0.11.3 DEBUG logs): the embedded amqtt test broker can raise asyncio.CancelledError out of broker.shutdown() even with SERIAL publishing. A companion to d8d5fac9's concurrent-publish race, with a different trigger. The trigger: a client receives a QoS-1 delivery, disconnects at once, and the test then shuts the broker down (e.g. beside_embedded_broker returning). The broker may start shutdown before reading the client's PUBACK. _stop_waiters() then cancels the delivery's PUBACK waiter, the late handle_puback hits InvalidStateError, and _broadcast_loop's final gather re-raises the cancellation. Observed about 1 in 4 runs in one test. Fix used in tests/mqtt_broker.py::delivered_to_resumed_session: before disconnecting, publish one QoS-1 message to a topic nothing subscribes to and await its PUBACK. The broker reads a client's packets in order and runs their handler tasks FIFO, so that PUBACK proves the earlier PUBACKs were handled. It needs no amqtt internals and no CancelledError suppression.

aiomqtt 2.5.1 / paho-mqtt 2.1.0 ack-and-queue facts, verified 2026-09-23 by task 252's architect, for re-planning task 252 (ack-after-persist) once task 240 lands.
(1) aiomqtt's incoming queue, Client._queue, is created once in Client.__init__. __aenter__/__aexit__ never clear it. So messages that are already PUBACKed but not yet consumed survive a disconnect inside the same Client and are consumed after a reconnect; they are lost only at process exit.
(2) MEASURED on CPython 3.11.15, default loop, scratch script: after a clean disconnect (_disconnected done), MessagesIterator.__anext__ still returns queued messages in FIFO order, exactly len(client.messages) of them, then raises MqttError('Disconnected during message iteration') once the queue is empty. So a drain after DISCONNECT through the public iterator, bounded by the public len(), works.
Hypothesis: this relies on asyncio callback ordering (the queue.get() task's first step runs before the done-callback of the already-done _disconnected future), not on any documented aiomqtt contract.
(3) paho 2.1.0: Client.manual_ack_set(True) makes the QoS-1 PUBACK and the QoS-2 PUBCOMP manual. Client.ack(mid, qos) sends them, and is a no-op for qos 0 or when manual_ack is off. aiomqtt's Message carries .mid and .qos. aiomqtt never passes manual_ack, so the only way to enable it is the private client._client.
(4) aiomqtt registers socket writes via loop.call_soon_threadsafe(loop.add_writer, ...).
(5) Broker window: validation/mosquitto.conf pins max_inflight_messages 1000 and max_queued_messages 0, and docs/examples/README.md marks both REQUIRED.

Task 157 (Ingest persistent-session backlog-resume throughput throttled ~66 msg/s vs 634 msg/s online) is done, merged via commit 804c0130500fbfb447e20cd7a36f4087fd93c417. Root cause: validation/mosquitto.conf omitted max_inflight_messages, so the harness broker used mosquitto's default of 20 unacked QoS-1 messages in flight to a resuming subscriber, throttling the backlog-resume drain; zero-loss/zero-dupe delivery held. It was not a batched-write-before-ack coupling: the subscriber uses aiomqtt's default auto-ack, which PUBACKs each message on receipt (see 2245a430 and fb94f85e). Fix scope: raised max_inflight_messages via docs/examples/README.md broker guidance plus a tests/ingestion/test_persistent_session.py resume-throughput assertion.

paho-mqtt 2.1.0 gotcha, verified in the installed source by task 1008's architect on 2026-10-13. A persistent-session client keeps per-object session state that a fresh client lacks. An inbound QoS-2 message is held in `_in_messages` after PUBREC and delivered only on PUBREL. `_messages_reconnect_reset_in` keeps that state across reconnects of the SAME client when clean_session is False. A fresh client receiving the broker's PUBREL for an unknown mid sends PUBCOMP without delivering, so the message is lost. QoS 1 is delivered and PUBACKed at once, so it carries no such state. Consequence for solar_challenge_platform: building a fresh aiomqtt.Client on every scp-ingest reconnect would lose a QoS-2 message (Settings accepts ingestion_subscribe_qos=2) whenever its handshake straddles the drop. It would also strand messages already in the old client's local queue, which paho acknowledged on receipt.

VERIFIED (task 240 architect, 2026-09-23, aiomqtt 2.5.1 + paho-mqtt 2.1.0): an incoming QoS-1 message is PUBACKed to the broker the moment it enters aiomqtt's internal asyncio queue — before the ingest Subscriber decodes, buffers or persists it. paho's Client._handle_publish calls _handle_on_message(message) then _send_puback(mid) unless manual_ack is set, aiomqtt's _on_message only does self._queue.put_nowait(m), and aiomqtt 2.5.1 never enables manual_ack. Consequence: rows sitting in aiomqtt's queue or in the StoreForwardBuffer are NOT redelivered after a restart despite clean_session=False; the persistent session only preserves messages the broker has not yet delivered. The only chance to persist already-received rows is an in-process flush before exit.

amqtt 0.11.3 uses a strict dacite-typed BrokerConfig: legacy hbmqtt/amqtt config keys like `max-connections` are REJECTED (UnexpectedDataError). A working embedded-broker config is {listeners:{default:{type:"tcp", bind:"127.0.0.1:{port}"}}, sys_interval:0, auth:{allow-anonymous:true}, topic_check:{enabled:false}} — auth/topic_check still work but emit DeprecationWarnings (the modern form is the `plugins` section). amqtt.broker.Broker.start()/shutdown() are async. The solar-challenge-platform repo has NO pytest-asyncio (and pyproject/uv.lock are α/task-31-owned + locked), so MQTT/async tests must run via asyncio.run() inside a sync `def test_*` (mirroring the control suite's threaded async server). aiomqtt 2.5 ships py.typed (mypy --strict clean); amqtt does not but is test-only. Bind 127.0.0.1:0 to grab a free ephemeral port to avoid collisions. Validated end-to-end (SimHome.step → wire.encode → aiomqtt publish → subscribe → wire.decode of all 8 metrics).

[SUPERSEDED 2026-09-24: this is a historical defect list for main 43f9141 and does NOT describe current main. The F1 fixes landed via task 133: reconnect-with-backoff, asyncio.to_thread off-load, and N-or-T batching (done, merged b51e767; completion note ca85f01a). The F2 fix landed via task 134: stable client_id and clean_session=False. See 69b2e220. The QoS-1 ack-on-receipt residual loss is still open, as task 252.] Ingest resilience defects confirmed at main 43f9141 (2026-07-03), scoped for the max-scale PRD F1/F2: (1) ingestion/subscriber.py:110 `async for message in client.messages` has NO try/except and NO reconnect — a broker drop kills the process; (2) the sync handle_message runs inside that async loop (:120) and TimescaleStore.write commits one transaction per message (timeseries/timescale_store.py:146), so blocking DB writes starve the event loop → MQTT keepalive starvation → the broker drops the client (the observed root cause); (3) flush happens every message (:93-100) → ~86-170 msg/s, ~50× too slow for a backfill drain; (4) the aiomqtt client (ingestion/service.py:191) sets no client_id and no clean_session (paho defaults → random id + clean session), so a disconnect loses the queued QoS-1 backlog. Fixes: reconnect wrapper + asyncio.to_thread off-load + N-or-T batching (F1); stable client_id + clean_session=False + mosquitto max_queued_messages 0 (F2). Idempotent ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING (:140) makes replay safe.

CORRECTION to memory c64ebbb9 (amqtt embedded broker, measured by task 274's implementer 2026-09-27, amqtt 0.11.3): the loss of persistent-session state is caused by AnonymousAuthPlugin, not by amqtt itself. With allow_anonymous it sets session.is_anonymous=True for EVERY client, and amqtt treats an anonymous session as clean whatever the client asked for. Broker._session_monitor deletes it, subscriptions included, at its next one-second sweep after the disconnect, and broadcasts never queue offline QoS-1 for it. So a clean_session=False hold survives only if the resume beats that sweep: a resume 1-3 s later received nothing, which makes such tests timing-flaky. Fix: tests/mqtt_broker.py's embedded_broker/beside_embedded_broker(..., durable_sessions=True) admits clients through tests.mqtt_broker.DurableSessionAuthPlugin, which authenticates without flagging the session anonymous. Measured with it: the subscription survives a 3 s gap, and 5 of 5 QoS-1 published while the session was offline are delivered on resume, as on mosquitto. The default stays anonymous.

How to apply: when designing leases, holds or watchdogs keyed to interactive sessions, never alarm, escalate or release on a LIVE session's silence or idle age, even after days. RATIONALE for Leo's 2026-09-10 rulings on the agent-capacity study (the WHY, kept alongside the decisions record because the decisions category distils rationale away). The study found the factory queue-bound (task duty cycle 2.4%; 82% of a task's dispatch→done life unphased, mostly restart-redispatch gaps and requeue waits; one verify admission slot per project with p50 2.2 h wait), information-bound (the sole blocking reviewer sees no task, no plan, a truncated diff 46% of the time, and a rubric forbidding structural blocks) and only then capability-bound (Fable never dispatched; 73% of implementer runs already opus). candidates.content: tests/infra/adoption-ratchet.manifest (S19 α, task #8678; the repo's INV candidate 5 adoption-ratchet engine) has these quirks. Rows are `pattern-id | ERE | path glob | ceiling | owner leaf`. The engine (tests/infra/adoption_ratchet.py) expands globs with pathlib root.glob, so `*` does NOT cross `/`: use `crates/<crate>/src/**/*.rs` for any ratchet that must survive a later file split into subdirectories. A glob that matches no file reds the gate. Lines whose first non-blank char is '#' never count, so Rust `#[…]` attribute lines are invisible to it, and such ratchets must be Rust tests. The ERE must be POSIX-compatible: no \b, \d, (?…) or lazy quantifiers.

reify tests/infra/adoption-ratchet.manifest gotchas (adoption_ratchet.py, task 8716 planning).

1. Escape a literal `$` (and `(`) in a row's ERE, e.g. write `_PARENT="\$\(mktemp` and not `_PARENT="$(mktemp`. An unescaped `$` is an end anchor in both POSIX ERE and Python re, so the row silently matches nothing and its ceiling is vacuous.
2. The path column is ONE Python Path.glob, with no {a,b} brace expansion. To cover several files, widen the glob (e.g. tests/infra/test_*.sh) and shape the ERE to exclude false hits, or add separate rows. Remember that test_*.sh also matches test_helpers.sh.
3. Pin each new row with a shape test in test_infra_adoption_ratchet.py: a historical line must match, and the replacement must not.

reify tests/infra/adoption-ratchet.manifest engine facts (tests/infra/adoption_ratchet.py, gated by test_infra_adoption_ratchet.sh): pattern-ids must be kebab-case `[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*` (an underscore or `.rs` in the id is a ManifestError); paths resolve with Path.glob, so `crates/reify-eval/src/engine_*.rs` matches direct children only (unlike a git pathspec, whose `*` spans `/`); the engine skips only lines whose first non-blank char is `#`, so Rust `//` comments DO count unless the ERE starts `^[^/]*`; it scans #[cfg(test)] modules too, so a row targeting 0 must also clean in-crate tests; the ERE must be POSIX-portable (no \b, no backslash-letter escapes, no backslash inside [...], no (?...)). A ratchet row can be vacuous: S1's first per-build-reset row (`[.](field)[.]clear[(]`) counted 0 at main because reset_per_build_state clears destructured locals; verify every row is red/at-ceiling before landing.

tests/infra/adoption-ratchet.manifest ERE pitfall: write a bracket class unescaped. `RUN_RUST=\[01\] RUN_GUI=\[01\]` matches a literal '[01]' (0 hits), while `RUN_RUST=[01] RUN_GUI=[01]` matches the 92 ordered scope greps intended (2026-10-15). The engine rejects a backslash INSIDE [...], not a bracket class. Always evaluate a new ratchet row's ERE with `git grep -c -E` over its path glob before writing the ceiling into a task. Scope its path glob to the files the owning leaf edits: a `grammar_hash\.stamp` row over tests/infra/test_*.sh had 21 hits, 15 of them in files that leaf never touches.

Reify gotcha for repo-wide text scans: reading every tracked *.rs + *.ri file in Python is ~70 MB and took 87 s per pass (measured 2026-10-12, task 7516). The same scan pre-filtered with `git grep -z -n -I -E '<ERE>' -- '*.rs' '*.ri'` took 2.2 s and produced ~9k candidate lines. For an infra gate that must run in run_all.sh's pool or a hook-gated staged leaf, pre-filter with git grep and parse the `file\0line\0content` records. Build the prefilter ERE and the in-Python token regex from the same constants so their boundaries cannot disagree.

Adding a NEW top-level `crates/<c>/tests/<file>.rs` to any of the five harness-ratchet-guarded crates (reify-cli, reify-syntax, reify-kernel-occt, reify-eval, reify-compiler — the list lives at tests/infra/harness-layout-lib.sh:106) requires adding its canonical path as a row in `tests/infra/harness-layout-baseline.manifest` IN THE SAME DIFF, in ASCII sort order. Neither guard fires under a branch-scoped verify — they only surface at the `--scope all` merge gate, so the branch looks green until the merge attempt. This is the same invisible-until-merge shape as verify.sh's `_RUST_COUPLED_RI_FIXTURES`/PG-DRIFT allowlist for tests/prd-gate/fixtures/*.ri, which blocked task #5481 across five separate merge attempts.

(1) HARNESS-LAYOUT RATCHET: a new standalone `crates/*/tests/*.rs` in one of the 5 consolidatable crates (reify-cli, reify-syntax, reify-kernel-occt, reify-eval, reify-compiler) must be `#[path]`-declared from a `harness_<subsystem>` root; adding a `tests/infra/harness-layout-baseline.manifest` row is SUPERSEDED as a remedy (Leo 2026-07-22, esc-5056-11 — the manifest is a shrinking ratchet). reify-solver-elastic and reify-eval-fea-tests are deliberately OUT of that contract. (3) `clippy::neg_cmp_op_on_partial_ord`: `!(x > 0.0)` guards fail the gate's `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`; the in-tree idiom is to bind a bool first (`crates/reify-eval/src/engine_build.rs:12718` names the lint in its comment). (4) PTODO fingerprint ratchet: a literal `TODO(`/`FIXME:`/`HACK(` in a comment with no `#NNNN` cite and no `// ptodo:allow` escape is a NEW untracked fingerprint and reds the severity-blind subset check — note `TODO)` does NOT match the regex, only `TODO(` or `TODO:`. content: To measure a candidate adoption-ratchet row before adding it to tests/infra/adoption-ratchet.manifest, import the engine directly: `sys.path.insert(0, "tests/infra"); import adoption_ratchet as ar` then `ar._non_portable_construct(ere)` (must be None, or the manifest parse rejects the row) and `ar.code_line_hits(text, re.compile(ere))` (comment lines excluded, same counting the gate uses). The ERE column may contain '|' but never ' | ' (space-pipe-space is the column separator); use bracket classes like [$] [}] instead of backslash escapes before letters.

1b0e5c7f-8f45-4d33-8b46-a8a46bcfb5fb.content: Reify's grep-based source gates (scripts/check-nan-safe-ordering.sh, scripts/check-compute-trampoline-registration.sh) share a hand-ported awk Rust lexer, `_AWK_PRODUCTION_PROLOGUE`, that reduces each line to production code (comments dropped; string/char/raw-string contents blanked, delimiters kept; `/* */`, `"…"` and `r#"…"#` state carried across lines; char literal distinguished from lifetime) and — critically — counts the braces driving `depth` from that LEXED view, never from the raw line. A two-regex strip-comments/blank-strings chain is wrong in EITHER order and was replaced, not reordered. When writing a new gate of this shape, port the prologue from check-nan-safe-ordering.sh's copy on main verbatim (change only the escape token and the matched patterns) rather than re-deriving it.

candidates.content: Verified facts about the model adapters at 592b1d9 (2026-10-07): the installed claude CLI accepts every flag ClaudeCodeScopingModel passes (-p, --system-prompt, --tools, --restricted, --model, --output-format, --json-schema; checked with claude --help, which spends nothing). The anthropic SDK is 1.11.0; its structured-output parsing (lib/_parse/_response.py::parse_text) uses pydantic TypeAdapter.validate_json, so a response truncated at max_tokens raises a ValidationError (json_invalid, no input echoed) that AnthropicScopingModel.analyse already catches and turns into ModelOutputUnusable. A candidate finding that truncation could bypass the designed error page was therefore refuted (R15, fk-c286c4c8db9d).

Facts about the two model backends' structured-output paths, verified from the installed anthropic SDK source on 2026-10-07: (1) With output_format=Analysis, the SDK parses via TypeAdapter.validate_json in anthropic/lib/_parse/_response.py, so pydantic model_validators run, and a ValidationError propagates out of stream.get_final_message() inside the with block as model.py assumes. (2) The SDK transforms the pydantic schema before sending (anthropic/lib/_parse/_transform.py): $defs/$ref kept; anyOf with null kept; enum kept; additionalProperties forced false; `default` is STRIPPED and appended to the description as text; minItems kept only if 0 or 1, larger values moved to the description; minLength/maxLength/minimum/maximum moved to the description and enforced client-side only. (3) The record's convention is required-nullable fields (`str | None` with no default), which survive the transform; a field with `= None` becomes non-required. (4) A required nested object adds one $def and survives unchanged. (5) The claude_code.py backend passes Analysis.model_json_schema() raw to `claude --json-schema` and always runs Analysis.model_validate client-side; whether the CLI enforces the same schema subset server-side is undocumented locally and cannot be checked without a live `claude -p` call, which the project forbids. (6) The schema has 22 $defs; StrEnums emit as enum arrays. (7) output_format is deprecated in favour of output_config.format in the SDK docs; the installed SDK still accepts it.

Completed: Pass the claude-code backend's prompt on stdin: a transcript over 128 KiB exceeds Linux's per-argument limit (claude_code.py::ClaudeCodeScopingModel._run)
Description: Found while planning task 8 (translate backend failures at the ScopingModel seam). src/scoping_intake/claude_code.py::ClaudeCodeScopingModel._run passes the whole prompt (NEXT_MESSAGE_INSTRUCTION plus transcript_document(transcript) for a reply, or transcript_document(transcript) for an analysis) as ONE argv element after `-p`. Linux caps a single argument at MAX_ARG_STRLEN = 32 pages = 131,072 bytes on this host (PAGE_SIZE 4096), while intake.py allows a transcript of up to MAX_TRANSCRIPT_CHARS = 300,000 characters. Measured 2026-10-08 with the worktree's Python: subprocess.run(['/bin/true', '-p', 'x' * 140_000]) raises OSError errno 7 'Argument list too long'; 100,000 characters succeed. So once a claude-code trial session's transcript document passes roughly 131 KB, every reply, retry and write-up fails with OSError(E2BIG). That error escapes the seam untranslated and the prospect page shows the generic 500 'Something went wrong on our side'. The session cannot recover, because retrying resends the same transcript. The other long arguments are small: analyst prompt 16,828 bytes, interviewer prompt 12,364 bytes, record schema JSON 8,556 bytes.
Analysis: ## Current state (base 57ecf41, task 8 merged; 59 tests green, measured in this worktree)

- `src/scoping_intake/claude_code.py::ClaudeCodeScopingModel._run` builds the command `[executable, "-p", prompt, "--system-prompt", system_prompt, "--tools", "", "--restricted", "--model", model, "--output-format", "json"]`, adding `"--json-schema", schema` for an analysis.
- It then calls `subprocess.run(command, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=..., cwd=..., env=..., check=False)` with no stdin, so claude inherits the server's stdin.
- `reply` passes `f"{NEXT_MESSAGE_INSTRUCTION}\n\n{transcript_document(transcript)}"` and `analyse` passes `transcript_document(transcript)`.
- `intake.py` lets a conversation grow to MAX_TRANSCRIPT_CHARS = 300,000 characters, in messages of at most MAX_MESSAGE_CHARS = 20,000.

## Facts measured for this plan

1. **The argument limit.** With 4096-byte pages, an argument of 131,071 bytes runs and one of 131,072 bytes raises OSError errno 7 (E2BIG) in the parent, before the child starts. A 300,000-character transcript gives a 300,056-character document and a 300,179-byte reply prompt.
2. **`claude -p` reads its prompt from stdin.**
   - `claude --help` (2.1.294) gives the usage as `claude [options] [command] [prompt]`.
   - `-p, --print` is a flag ("Print response and exit (useful for pipes)"), so the prompt is the positional argument, not the value of -p.
   - `--input-format` is "(only works with --print): text (default), or stream-json".
   - The installed binary was also read statically with grep -a and dd. Nothing was executed and nothing was spent.
   - Its getInputPrompt reads stdin when stdin is not a TTY. It decodes it as UTF-8 (`process.stdin.setEncoding("utf8")`) up to 10 MiB. Once data arrives it waits for EOF; its 3-second timer fires only when no data arrives at all.
   - It returns `[promptArgument, stdin].filter(Boolean).join("\n")`. The no-input error reads "Input must be provided either through stdin or as a prompt argument when using --print".
   - So with no positional prompt, claude's prompt is exactly what we write to stdin.
3. **No hang in the RED run.** Under pytest's default fd capture, which verify uses through plain `uv run pytest`, a child's fd 0 is /dev/null (measured). A stand-in that reads stdin therefore gets '' at once against today's code.
4. **Throwaway-copy trial.** The setup: `git archive HEAD` into /tmp, run with PYTHONPATH=<copy>/src.
   - With the planned test file, today's code fails exactly two tests, in 2.6 s: the reply test, because stdin is '', and the new long-conversation test, with OSError [Errno 7] Argument list too long.

The derivation lives in a helper, cli._host_header(scheme, hostname, port), which _public_url calls. web.py RequestHandler._admission_refusal answers only a Host header that is in site.hosts by string equality, and otherwise replies 421 'Not found'. Two cases are left. Both are outside task 35's scope and unlikely in the deployed setup: deploy/README.md sets INTAKE_PUBLIC_URL=https://<machine>.<tailnet>.ts.net, and the units use ports 8471 and 8472.

Then flip the whole batch deferred→pending in ONE bulk set_task_status(id="35,36,37,38,39", status="pending") call (comma-separated ids supported). Cancel a superseded placeholder via set_task_status(id, "cancelled"). Task ids are global and sequential — P1 got #35-#39 (the prior P2-P5 batch ran #16-#34). PRD files must be committed to main BEFORE/at decompose time because task agents run in worktrees branched from main. get_tasks output is large (~87k chars, exceeds tool limit) — query it with jq on the saved tool-results file instead.

solar_challenge_platform gotchas for injecting a consent-store fault in tests. Measured by the task 1192 architect on 2026-10-14 (SQLAlchemy 2.0.51, SQLite/pysqlite, Python 3.11).
- An exception raised inside an engine before_cursor_execute listener reaches the caller unwrapped. To simulate a store fault, the listener must raise a SQLAlchemyError itself, e.g. sqlalchemy.exc.OperationalError(statement, None, Exception('...')).
- Session.get answers from the identity map without emitting SQL. A fault on consent_current statements fires only when the ConsentCurrent row is not already loaded in that session, so seed grants in a separate committed Session first.
- Session.begin_nested() emits its SAVEPOINT lazily, on the first SQL inside the with.
- `try: with session.begin_nested(): ...` / `except SQLAlchemyError` turns a fault on SAVEPOINT, on the read, on RELEASE or on ROLLBACK TO into a handled failure, and the caller's earlier flushed row still commits.
- With the try inside the with instead, a RELEASE fault raises.

solar_challenge_platform gotcha (read 2026-10-10 at main 1b4b448): SQLite enforces no foreign keys unless `PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON` runs on the connection, and the suite's StaticPool in-memory SQLite engine may be built only in tests/_sqlite_engine.py (tests/test_sqlite_engine_home.py fails any other create_engine of that shape). So a test that needs a real FK violation (the IntegrityError Postgres raises) must take its engine from that helper with the PRAGMA registered as a "connect" listener before create_all, not build its own. With FKs on, an FK violation surfaces at the first flush, not at commit: consent/store.py record_event and the config stores (set_finance/set_battery/set_coverage) flush inside the route handler, before commit_or_409 runs.

solar_challenge_platform test convention (task 453, branch task/453; holds once merged): two shared non-test modules serve SQL store and migration tests. tests/_sql_executions.py::executions_naming(engine, table) records every execution naming a table, each an Execution(statement, executemany); attach it before the call to pin "one statement, not executemany". tests/_schema_state.py::table_shape(engine, table) returns a TableShape (column nullability, PK columns in order, index names, foreign keys); compare the migrated SQLite head with make_in_memory_engine()'s ORM schema. Import these rather than writing private copies: tests/test_private_names.py forbids importing another test module's private helpers. SQL-portable upserts use db/dialects.py::dialect_insert(session, Model), and reads of stored timestamps use db/dialects.py::stored_utc.

solar_challenge_platform test gotcha (verified 2026-10-09, task 209): tests/test_sqlite_engine_home.py only flags create_engine calls that build the shared StaticPool in-memory SQLite engine (in-memory URL + poolclass=StaticPool + a connect_args that may disable check_same_thread); those must come from tests/_sqlite_engine.make_in_memory_engine. A plain sa.create_engine("sqlite://") is allowed, and is the house way to give a SQL store a database with NO tables, so its write raises sqlalchemy OperationalError ("no such table"). Use it for a "store raises the DB error and logs nothing" test. make_in_memory_engine always runs create_all, so it cannot serve there.

solar_challenge_platform test gotcha, measured on task 516's probes at main 40a6556, 2026-10-13. To make the database reject ONE statement for one home, attach a before_cursor_execute(retval=True) listener to the test's engine. It replaces the first statement whose bound values equal the home's UUID with "SELECT * FROM no_such_table" and returns type(parameters)().
- Match the UUID against a tuple of (uuid, str(uuid), uuid.hex) using ==. Do not use a set: some bound values are unhashable. psycopg binds uuid.UUID values in dicts, while SQLite binds 32-char hex strings in tuples.
- SQLite raises OperationalError; Postgres raises ProgrammingError (UndefinedTable) and aborts the transaction.
- On Postgres, without a savepoint (session.begin_nested()) the next home's read in the same Session fails with InFailedSqlTransaction. SQLite never aborts the transaction, so only a timescale-lane test can prove a per-home savepoint.

solar_challenge_platform (measured 2026-10-04, task 357 architect, base 2838c8a): to observe from a hermetic test that code under test disposed a SQLAlchemy engine it created internally, listen at class level with sa.event.listen(sa.Engine, "engine_disposed", fn) and sa.event.remove it in a yield fixture (works on SQLAlchemy 2.0.51; str(engine.url) of an in-memory engine is "sqlite://"). To observe that a ProcessSupervisor's teardown ran, supervise a real sleeper child (signals.SLEEP_FOREVER_SCRIPT) and assert its SupervisedProcess.status == supervisor.STATUS_TERMINATED. Both use public seams only, so tests/test_private_names.py stays green. Docker is available on this host, and the dropped-readings slow capstone passes in about 85 s.

solar_challenge_platform test gotcha, measured 2026-10-14 by the task 1026 architect: the project env runs Python 3.11.15 (so itertools.batched, 3.12+, is unavailable) with Ubuntu's SQLite 3.45.1, whose SQLITE_LIMIT_VARIABLE_NUMBER is 250,000, not upstream's default 32,766. So an oversized multi-row VALUES statement that a default SQLite build or PostgreSQL (65,535) refuses still runs here. A test that needs SQLite to refuse it must lower the limit on the connection: with tests/_sqlite_engine.make_in_memory_engine() (StaticPool, one shared connection), call conn.connection.dbapi_connection.setlimit(sqlite3.SQLITE_LIMIT_VARIABLE_NUMBER, 32_766) inside `with engine.connect() as conn`. The limit persists for every later session, and an oversized statement then raises sqlalchemy.exc.OperationalError "too many SQL variables".

solar_challenge_platform hermetic test pattern, measured 2026-10-10 by the task 778 architect. To prove a TimescaleStore method refuses its input before any I/O, with no database, build TimescaleStore(engine=sqlalchemy.create_engine("postgresql+psycopg://", creator=f)) where f raises. A postgres engine opens nothing until first use. SQLAlchemy lets a non-DBAPI exception raised by the creator propagate unwrapped: an AssertionError arrived as AssertionError. So the test sees either the method's own ValueError or the creator's sentinel, and a sentinel can also pin that an accepted input goes on to the database. Precedent: tests/timeseries/test_timescale_store_write.py.

solar_challenge_platform test pattern (task 790; tests/timeseries/test_timescale_store_write.py): to prove a TimescaleStore method refuses its input before any I/O, with no Docker, build the store through its public constructor over create_engine("postgresql+psycopg://", creator=_refuse_to_connect), where the creator raises AssertionError. SQLAlchemy 2.0.51 re-raises a non-DBAPI exception from the creator unwrapped. So a write that connects first fails the test with the creator's own message, and pytest.raises(ValueError) passes only on a refusal made before I/O. No private name is patched.

In solar_challenge_platform, the `db_session` pytest fixture lives in tests/models/conftest.py and is scoped to tests/models/ only — pytest conftest fixtures do NOT propagate sideways to sibling test packages (tests/consent/, tests/api/). Each new test package under tests/ needs its own conftest.py replicating the in-memory SQLite fixture (create_engine("sqlite:///:memory:") + import solar_challenge_platform.models + Base.metadata.create_all). Task 12 (P5·b) creates tests/consent/conftest.py for this; task 13's gate tests reuse it.

solar_challenge_platform test gotcha: the suite's default Settings.database_url is a table-less sqlite:///:memory:, which uses SingletonThreadPool, so every thread gets its own empty in-memory DB. A test that calls ControlPlaneService.from_settings() and run() therefore sends its dispatch/refresh ticks and feedback rows through the AuditWriter thread into a DB with no tables. Each write raises OperationalError "no such table" (e.g. tests/test_entrypoints.py::test_control_plane_service_from_settings_and_bounded_run). To make audit writes land, use a StaticPool engine with the schema (tests/_sqlite_engine.py::make_in_memory_engine) or a file-backed SQLite plus create_all.

solar_challenge_platform testing technique (verified 2026-10-14 by the task 1036 architect, SQLAlchemy 2.0.51, main 295b6cb). Use it to reach an unsupported-dialect refusal, such as db/dialects.py::dialect_insert's ValueError, through a public seam that runs real queries first. A stand-in session cannot do that.
1. Subclass sqlalchemy.dialects.sqlite.pysqlite.SQLiteDialect_pysqlite. In the subclass's own body, set a fictional `name` such as 'elsewhere' and `supports_statement_cache = True`; without the latter SQLAlchemy warns with code cprf.
2. Register it with sqlalchemy.dialects.registry.register(name, __name__, cls.__name__).
3. Build it with create_engine(f'{name}://', poolclass=StaticPool), then Base.metadata.create_all. The full schema builds: the property after_create listener just skips its SQLite trigger, and RLS does nothing.
Never register a real dialect name such as 'mysql': the registry is process-wide and would shadow SQLAlchemy's own dialect.

solar_challenge_platform gotcha for grep delivered_checks on SQL upserts (verified 2026-10-10 by the task 453 architect at main 5be9312): the platform's SQL stores build upserts with SQLAlchemy dialect constructs (postgresql.insert / sqlite.insert(...).on_conflict_do_update or on_conflict_do_nothing), so the literal text "ON CONFLICT" never appears in executable code. A delivered_check grepping 'ON CONFLICT' in a store module (e.g. task 453's signal-last-upsert-statement-built on ingestion/signal_last.py) can only match the store's docstring that states the statement it executes, as ingestion/health.py::SqlLastSeenStore's docstring does. When authoring such a check, grep a new code symbol instead (the store class name, or on_conflict_do_update scoped to the new file).

Gotcha in solar_challenge_platform tests: with SQLAlchemy 2.x, an engine for 'sqlite:///:memory:' that has no StaticPool (for example db.session.init_db(url='sqlite:///:memory:')) uses one connection per thread. Each thread therefore sees its own empty database. Since task 309, Subscriber.run() runs consent checks on an 'ingest-consent-check' daemon thread, so a database seeded on the test's thread is invisible to them. Use tests/_sqlite_engine.make_in_memory_engine() (StaticPool, check_same_thread=False) with GateConsentChecker(session_factory=lambda: Session(engine)), or a file-backed SQLite under tmp_path. handle_message runs its checks on the calling thread and is not affected.

solar_challenge_platform gotcha (measured 2026-10-07, SQLAlchemy 2.0.51 + psycopg 3): a refused Postgres connection surfaces as sqlalchemy.exc.OperationalError with connection_invalidated=False and statement=None. The psycopg dialect's is_disconnect returns False when there is no connection yet. So a retry predicate keyed only on connection_invalidated misses a DB restart; it must also check the OperationalError/InterfaceError type. On SQLite, a missing table ("no such table: ...") is ALSO an OperationalError, so a type-based transient check retries schema errors there.

solar-challenge-platform test gotcha: pytest rewrites asserts only in test_*.py modules and conftest.py. The repo has no register_assert_rewrite, so the bare `assert`s in shared helper modules under tests/ fail with no values shown. This applies to tests/_statement_round_trip.py, tests/_amount_due_backfill.py, tests/register_seed.py and similar. When moving an assert out of a test module into such a helper, give it an explicit f-string message carrying the compared values. Both helpers named above do this.

Gotcha + technique (probed 2026-09-28, task 516):
- On Postgres, one failed statement aborts the Session's transaction, and every later statement on that Session raises psycopg InFailedSqlTransaction until ROLLBACK or ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT. SQLite never aborts, so a test proving per-item savepoint isolation must run on the timescale lane (tests._timescale_container.timescale_url + tests._migrated_engine.migrated_engine, about 11 s; Docker is present, so the lane runs in verify).
- To inject a genuine DB error hermetically, listen for before_cursor_execute with retval=True on the test's own engine. Swap the first statement whose bound params name a value for ("SELECT * FROM no_such_table", type(parameters)()).
- Match the value against the tuple (uuid, str(uuid), uuid.hex) using ==, never a set, because params can be unhashable. psycopg binds uuid.UUID in dicts; SQLite binds 32-char hex in qmark tuples.
- session.get() calls answered from the identity map emit no SQL, so they cannot be targeted this way.

solar_challenge_platform gotcha (measured 2026-10-06, base 7fcfeac): the dropped-readings drill's raw-row helpers (validation/drills/dropped_readings.py _read_raw_rows / _delete_rows) bind raw uuid.UUID values through sqlalchemy text(). SQLite rejects that bind with "sqlite3.ProgrammingError: Error binding parameter 1: type 'UUID' is not supported", so those helpers only run on Postgres. Hermetic SQLite tests cannot reach them. The one real check is the slow Docker capstone test_dropped_readings_drill_recovers_against_real_docker_and_flows_into_bundle (about 93 s). It cannot tell a home-keyed DELETE from a device-keyed one, because seed_golden_fleet seeds one device per home.

Review pattern (20260928T154500): the highest-severity defects in solar_challenge_platform now sit at seams the tests deliberately stub, not in the engines. Examples: fast lane disables ingest consent and every fixture seeds platform_operation directly, so no test notices the portal cannot grant what consumers check; fakes AND the real Stripe adapter both return total_minor=view.total_minor, so reconcile R1 is tautological; the outage keystone wires a Subscriber over MemoryStore, so the real TimescaleStore's 65,535-parameter limit was never hit; the container smoke only runs --help and /health, so missing package data went unseen; core validation drills fault the harness's own sleep process and a throwaway broker, never scp-ingest/scp-dispatch. When reviewing or writing tests here, check the test drives the PRODUCTION composition across the seam (real store, real adapter response, real portal request body, installed wheel), not a stand-in that shares the code under test's assumptions.

solar_challenge_platform test gotcha (task 209): tests/_sqlite_engine.make_in_memory_engine() uses StaticPool, so every Session shares ONE sqlite3 connection. If a test polls a SQL store (e.g. SqlLastSeenStore.snapshot()) on the event loop while Subscriber's "ingest-store-write" daemon thread is upserting, the reader's Session close does a pool reset-on-return rollback() on that shared connection and can silently undo the writer's uncommitted upsert. So tests driving Subscriber.run() must wait on a completion signal first (tests/ingestion/test_last_seen_hook.py counts returned upserts in a wrapper; test_ingest_tick.py counts returned buffer.flush calls), and read the store only when no write is in flight.

content: solar_challenge_platform test gotcha (task 1192, 2026-10-15): tests/_failing_statements.py::failing_statements(engine, pattern, *, error=...) is the shared store-fault helper. It is an engine before_cursor_execute listener that raises a real OperationalError for every statement whose SQL re.search-es the regex; patterns like r'^SAVEPOINT ', r'^RELEASE SAVEPOINT ' and r'^ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT ' target savepoint statements. A fault on a consent read fires only on an identity-map miss: Session.get answers from the identity map with no SQL, and begin_nested emits SAVEPOINT lazily on the first SQL inside it. So seed the grant in its own Session(engine) and commit it, then decide in a fresh session; otherwise the fault never fires and the test passes vacuously. On SQLite, flush a caller row first so pysqlite's outer BEGIN is open and RELEASE is nested, not a commit.

0cee50f5-1131-45f4-b72f-9105083c92d1.content: solar_challenge_platform test convention (task 426, branch task/426; holds once merged): tests/_schema_state.py is the shared reader of what migrations leave in a database. alembic_revision(engine) returns the alembic_version row's revision. chunk_time_intervals(engine) returns a dict mapping relation name to its new-chunk interval (a timedelta). It covers every hypertable and continuous aggregate; an aggregate is keyed by its VIEW name through the timescaledb_information.dimensions-to-continuous_aggregates join, so never hardcode _materialized_hypertable_N. Migration tests (e.g. task 728's telemetry_hh chunk/compression test) should import these rather than write a private _revision or chunk-interval query. tests/integration/test_timeseries_compression.py still has private copies until follow-up ticket tkt_0RVJRF69WPRETSY4DCVFGRDSYX switches it.

candidates.content: Reify merge-queue ops learnings from landing task 5125 via /unblock: (a) release_workflow(task_id) cancels the WORKFLOW and parks the task 'blocked', but does NOT kill the detached OS process tree — a fork-bombing verify (its own setsid session) kept running and forking after release; had to kill it by session id (ps -o sess=, kill -9 the whole session). (b) When a branch's verify base drifts from main during a long verify, the queue shows persistent "frozen-prefix base-chain broken / verify-base⊄frozen-tip (ε=1890 §5.3)" two_layer_invariants warnings and the verify result is liable to be rejected+re-verified; REBASING the branch onto current origin/main and force-pushing BEFORE (re)submitting eliminated the base-chain churn AND got it dispatched to the fast 'local' host instead of the slow 'laptop' host. (c) The first submit ran ~57 min on the slow laptop host then BLOCKED (on my bug); the rebased resubmit landed cleanly in ~30 min on 'local'. (d) A merge-verify can run over SSH on a remote host (`ssh leo-laptop orchestrator verify-merge --sha ...`), so the local _merge-<hash> lane looks idle (2 bash, 0% CPU) while it's actually working remotely — don't mistake that for a stall. (1) BRANCH ARG — CURRENT BEHAVIOR (verified 2026-07-23 task 5364, re-verified 2026-07-25 ad-hoc landing). `mcp__escalation__merge_request` canonicalizes the `branch` arg via `canonical_queued_branch_name`, which prepends the configured git branch_prefix (`task/`) ONLY IF the value does not already start with it. So BOTH forms work today: passing the real branch name from `git branch --show-current` (e.g. branch="task/5364") is safe and unambiguous, and passing the BARE id (branch="4481") or a bare slug (branch="cost-ceiling") also works. Non-numeric ids are accepted. For an AD-HOC (non-task) branch, the prefix is still mandatory in the ref itself: push under refs/heads/task/<slug> (e.g. `git push origin mybranch:refs/heads/task/docs-truth-gates`) and submit branch="task/<slug>" — a branch named `docs/foo` is looked up as `task/docs/foo` and returns unknown_branch. Use an arbitrary descriptive non-numeric task_id for ad-hoc landings; never borrow a real task's id (merge results are sticky per task_id).

The merge worker resolves the branch HEAD via `git rev-parse HEAD` with cwd = the passed worktree (merge_queue.py:2862/1793), so the directory MUST exist and sit at the branch tip. Passing the main checkout while it is on `main` yields a false `already_merged`.

Task worktrees are at the RELOCATED warm-lane path /media/leo/data_lv_1/leo/reify-build/worktrees/<id>; the merge worker's own are at /home/leo/src/warm-lanes/worktrees/_merge-*. (5) SUBMIT→POLL PROTOCOL. Use the bounded form: merge_request(wait_secs=100), then merge_status(request_id=...) until terminal (done/conflict/blocked/already_merged).

(6) merge_status PITFALLS. After an orchestrator restart the retention ring is lost and merge_status returns state="unknown" — confirm landing deterministically with `git merge-base --is-ancestor task/<id> main`, and NEVER fall back to a direct merge on unknown. Merge-queue landing verification canonical (consolidates 8 incident entries, human-curated via gate task 5324). The reify orchestrator merge worker usually lands a submitted task branch by REBASING it onto latest main (landed commits get NEW SHAs; sometimes it instead creates a --no-ff 'Merge task/<id> into main' commit — landing style varies) and often DELETES the task/<id> branch afterwards. Consequence: `git merge-base --is-ancestor task/<id> main` is NOT a reliable landed-check — it false-negatives (exit 1, or 'Not a valid object name' once the ref is gone) after a rebase-land or branch deletion even though the content IS on main. merge_status is also unreliable post-hoc: it can return done with NO merge SHA, a stale 'verifying', or 'unknown' (retention-ring expired / record lost in queue churn). AUTHORITATIVE landed check = deliverable CONTENT on main: `git grep <deliverable-symbol> main` (=0 for deletions), `git ls-tree main -- <file>` / `git cat-file -e main:<file>` plus `diff <(git show main:<file>) <(git show task/<id>:<file>)`, and `git log main --grep '<id>'` (landed commits under new SHAs). If a --no-ff merge commit exists, corroborate via `git rev-parse main^2` == your branch tip and your fix commit being an ancestor of it; get_merge_queue landings_total incrementing corroborates too. ALWAYS run the content check BEFORE resubmitting a merge_request — resubmitting an already-landed branch creates a duplicate. CONVERSE GUARD (do not over-apply the gotcha): main's HEAD moving is NOT evidence YOUR merge landed. If the task/<id> ref still EXISTS, its tip is NOT an ancestor of main, AND the deliverable content is absent from main, the merge was dropped/conflicted-out, not landed (merge_status 'unknown' + the get_merge_queue entry gone + branch-not-in-main confirms) — verify the SPECIFIC commit you care about, never queue motion alone. AFTERMATH: after a landing the task may be left phantom-in-progress (or the worker may auto-flip blocked→done and auto-resolve its escalations, in which case a manual set_task_status(done) returns no_op and no manual resolve_issue is needed; worktrees are auto-removed). When stamping manually: done_provenance kind='merged' with commit=<the merge commit> for merge-commit landings, or commit=`git rev-parse main` for rebase-lands (passes the pre-done hook's is-ancestor check since a commit is its own ancestor); kind='found_on_main' with an on-main commit + explanatory note is the alternative for rebase-lands. Clean up the local branch with `git branch -D` (plain -d refuses — rebased SHAs make it look unmerged). Incident anchors (provenance of the consolidated entries): tasks 4070/4072 rebase-vs-merge-commit landings + phantom-in-progress (2026-05-31); warm-lane converse case — commit 969be28e8b never landed despite main advancing (2026-06-18); task 4821 rebase-land, branch -D, done_provenance hook-pass (2026-06-26); general merge-queue mechanics incl. done-with-no-SHA + auto-flip/auto-resolve (2026-06-26); task 4827 grep-ground-truth, merge_status unknown, landing 31f82ed6c8 (2026-07-09); task 5033 found_on_main stamp pattern, main tip 3bbcf9185d (2026-07-10); task 5172 verifying→unknown retention-ring + content-diff check (2026-07-12); task 5053 branch-deleted false-negative + main^2 corroboration (2026-07-21).

Intake.prospect_view reads both on every prospect page load, and a ValidationError matches no case in error_pages.session_error_page, so after any schema change or tightened validator an existing session's whole page, chat included, becomes a 500 (web.py:95-100), and the operator page likewise. Tasks 10, 14, the criterion-to-system link and the T3 validator all change the schema or tighten validation. Found in the R13 discussion on 2026-10-07; agreed with Leo.
Analysis: PREMISES, checked on base 0a7cf7c (main = branch tip).
- The task title names store.py::Stored. That class no longer exists: an earlier task folded it into record.Frozen (record.py:12-13, ConfigDict(frozen=True, extra="forbid")). Draft (store.py:35-46) and Released (store.py:49-53) now derive from Frozen directly and embed Analysis, so the defect stands as described.
- SessionStore._read (store.py:177-179) runs kind.model_validate_json on every read. No version field exists and nothing migrates.
- Intake.prospect_view (intake.py:64-72) reads the draft and the release on every prospect page load. The /criteria and /report routes go through it too (prospect_pages.py:80-84, 102-109).
- Intake.operator_view (intake.py:125-137) reads the draft, the operator placement and the release. request_write_up, place, rewrite and release read the draft (intake.py:101-158, 204-212).
- error_pages.session_error_page (error_pages.py:11-30) has no case for ValidationError, so web._dispatch (web.py:92-104) answers 500 "Something went wrong". Any Analysis change or tightened validator therefore turns an existing session's chat page into a 500, and its operator page likewise.
- purge_unused/_last_used (intake.py:228-248) read the release for its time and leave a session whose release cannot be read in place, reporting it. tests/test_session_flow.py:347-363 pins that. A naive versioning would make every session released before a schema change "unreadable" to the purge, so no such session would ever be deleted: the 90-day promise would break.
- Deletion never reads the draft. The prospect route goes intake.delete -> _locked -> store.get (session.json only) -> shutil.rmtree. The operator route goes through by_prospect_id/readable(), which reads session.json only. So deletion already survives an unreadable draft; this task pins that with a test.

POLICY CHOSEN: an operator-facing state, not a migration table (see design decisions).
- store.RECORD_FORMAT = 1 is the record format this version writes drafts and releases in, and the only one it reads.
- Draft and Released derive from a small base, StoredWriteUp(Frozen), holding record_format: int = RECORD_FORMAT and analysis: Analysis. The format is therefore written on save by the record's own serialisation.
- On read, the store first reads only the declared format: a Frozen model _DeclaredFormat(record_format: int = 1), validated with pydantic 2.13.5's per-call model_validate_json(..., extra="ignore"). A record from before formats were numbered declares none and is format 1, so Leo's existing trial sessions keep working.
- Only a record declaring RECORD_FORMAT is validated in full. Every other outcome is returned, never raised, as UnreadableWriteUp(record_format=<declared> | None): another format, unparseable bytes, or a current-format record that fails the record's rules.
- draft() and released() return Draft/Released | UnreadableWriteUp | None.
- A new SessionStore.released_at(token) reads only released_at (a Frozen _ReleaseTime, again extra="ignore" per call) from a release in any format. A damaged release still raises there, so the purge keeps counting a release made in an older format and keeps leaving a damaged one in place.

content: On this machine, `journalctl --user` scanned over a multi-day window (e.g. --since '5 days ago' piped to grep) does not finish within the Bash tool's 180 s timeout, because the user journal is dominated by MCP request chatter. Query narrow windows (seconds to a few minutes, with explicit --since/--until), wrap the call in `timeout`, and filter the noise with grep -v on 'CallToolRequest|Terminating session|HTTP Request: POST|loop_lag|jcodemunch|sampler INFO'. To correlate a file touch with a process, take the file's mtime with find -printf or ls --time-style=full-iso (local BST) and query that exact minute.

Fixed in 47bdd53f0d by typing the resolution module's own output — `validate_requested_lane` already tested membership against `MERGE_LANES` but could not SAY so in the type system, because `MERGE_LANES` is `tuple[str, ...]` and a membership test over it narrows nothing. WHAT CHANGED. `OfflineLaneWorker._run_once` had three red-run seams that captured an output tail and bound it to `_tail`, discarding it: the numeric, infra and generic-command legs. All three default seams DO capture it (each `[-2000:]` the merged stdout+stderr), so the evidence existed and was thrown away at the call site. The three unpack targets are now DISTINCT names (`numeric_tail` / `infra_tail` / `cmd_tail`) so one leg's tail can never leak into another's red path, and each forwards its own via a new keyword-only `output_tail` on `_handle_red_run` -> trailing param on `_file_new_fix_task` -> trailing `output_tail`/`scope_note` on `workflow.build_offline_lane_fix_task_arguments`.

MOTIVATING MEASUREMENT (task 4289). The lane filed 15 failing test IDs plus range b0c480a7f382..ee482c40e6e0, whose only substantive change was a docstring rewrite in escalation/src/escalation/server.py — which cannot affect fused-memory Qdrant tests. The failing set was exactly the 15 Qdrant-dependent integration tests while all 39 FalkorDB ones passed: a host-level Qdrant disturbance. With nothing attached, the fix-task agent burned an entire architect session re-deriving that from journalctl and repeated suite re-runs.

THREE DESIGN POINTS WORTH REMEMBERING, each with its reason:
* The tail goes in the DESCRIPTION, never `metadata`. `metadata` is a governed vocabulary echoed into task listings, reconciliation payloads and dashboards; a 2000-char pytest blob there bloats every read path for zero added reach, since the consumer is the fix agent reading its briefing.
* An EMPTY changed-file list yields NO hint. `GitOps.get_changed_files` does not check rc, so a git failure and a genuinely empty diff both surface as `[]`; emitting "nothing in scope changed" on `[]` would assert an environmental cause from a git error — a confident wrong hint is worse than none.
* `_scope_note` swallows every exception, because a raise there propagates out of `_run_once` AHEAD of the `_last_run_head = head` advance, so `run()`'s poll backstop re-flags the head and the ENTIRE heavy offline-deep suite runs again. A missing diagnostic nicety must never cost a suite re-run.

Deliberately out of scope: the confirm re-run's tail. `ConfirmationRunner`/`CommandConfirmationRunner` are public seam aliases returning `list[str]`; widening them breaks ~6 injection points across four test files, and the RED run's tail is where the traceback lives — the confirm re-run by contract reports only which IDs still fail.

Completed: ts_parser.rs import_declaration dispatch bypasses check_and_lower!, silently swallowing nested parse errors
Description: Discovered while planning task 5931 (canonical destructured-import syntax). OUT OF SCOPE for 5931, which deliberately declined to widen into a shared lowering path.

DEFECT. In crates/reify-syntax/src/ts_parser.rs, the source_file dispatch loop's "import_declaration" arm (lines 337-345) calls `self.lower_import(child)` DIRECTLY, bypassing the `check_and_lower!` macro (lines 13-25) that essentially every other declaration arm routes through. That macro is what turns `child.is_error() || child.has_error()` into a pushed parse error. Because imports skip it, a tree-sitter ERROR node nested INSIDE an import_declaration subtree never becomes a diagnostic: the import lowers silently and `parsed.errors` stays empty.

MEASURED IMPACT (this is not theoretical — it masked a real bug for ~5 months). Before 5931, `import a.b.{C, D}` did not match the tree-sitter rule (which lacked the '.' separator). tree-sitter error-recovered the stray '.' into a sibling ERROR node inside the import_declaration, leaving the `path` and `items` fields intact:

    (import_declaration
      path: (import_path (identifier) (identifier))
      (ERROR [0, 15] - [0, 16])
      items: (import_items (identifier) (identifier)))

`lower_import` collects only `identifier` children of the path node plus the `items` field, so it produced a clean, CORRECT AST from an erroring CST. Four tests across reify-syntax, reify-compiler and reify-lsp therefore passed green on main while the grammar officially rejected the very form they exercised. Task 5931 fixes the grammar; it does NOT fix this bypass.

WORK TO DO.
1. Determine whether the bypass is deliberate (e.g. imports intentionally tolerate partial parses for LSP/incremental-edit reasons) or an oversight. Check git history for the dispatch arm and for any test that depends on a malformed import lowering silently.
2. If an oversight, route the arm through `check_and_lower!` like its siblings.
3. Expect fallout in tests that feed malformed or partially-typed imports — crates/reify-syntax/tests/harness_syntax/cfg_import_attachment_tests.rs is the most likely, and reify-lsp paths that parse incomplete buffers mid-keystroke are the main risk area. Each fallout site needs a judgement call, which is why 5931 did not absorb this.
4. Audit the other dispatch arms in the same loop for the same bypass — imports may not be the only one.

RATIONALE FOR SPLITTING. 5931's mandate was to settle which destructured-import spelling is canonical. Fixing this bypass changes error reporting for unrelated malformed-import inputs across three crates, which is scope 5931 neither asked for nor bounded. After 5931 lands, the canonical form parses cleanly, so this bypass no longer masks anything for that spelling — but it remains latent for every other malformed import.

FILES: crates/reify-syntax/src/ts_parser.rs, crates/reify-syntax/tests/harness_syntax/cfg_import_attachment_tests.rs, crates/reify-syntax/tests/harness_syntax/import_tests.rs

GOTCHA — delivered_check path pins (learned 2026-09-21 from task 173): a capability-manifest sidecar delivered_check that pins a specific FILE (e.g. `def allocate_to_bands` in src/.../billing/reducer.py) fails when the implementer legitimately factors the symbol into a sibling module (task 172/181 moved it to billing/shape.py). The scheduler then holds every dependent with a DEP_CAPABILITY_NOT_DELIVERED L2 (esc-173-1) and does NOT auto-re-pend them; the reconciliation harness reads the resulting blocked-with-worktree state as a "liveness contradiction" and files a human-decision gate (task 184) — task 173 lost 4 days this way. Rule: pin `kind: grep` checks to the package directory (src/solar_challenge_platform/billing/) unless the file itself is the capability. Fix procedure when it happens: update the producer task's metadata.delivered_checks via update_task (merge mode; supply the full corrected list), amend the committed .yaml sidecar + .md manifest, then resolve_issue(action="resume") on the DEP_CAPABILITY escalation — that DID flip the blocked dependent back to pending here. resolve_issue's resolution_class must be one of actionable | benign | moot-terminal-subject | stale-strand. To close a human-decision gate task use set_task_status(status="done", done_provenance={kind:"found_on_main", commit, note}) — update_task cannot change status.

Decompose/filing gotchas learned on the 2026-09-29 five-PRD batch (tasks 595-662): (a) commit_planning stamps ONE capability-manifest sidecar per call — when a batch spans several PRDs, flip everything once, then re-call commit_planning per PRD with that PRD's ids (statuses are a no-op, the sidecar gets stamped and its mechanical delivered_checks copied); (b) its lint REFUSES to copy a check whose pattern is the NAME of a file the leaf creates ("filename_shaped" — declare it kind: path, expect: present, paths: [the file]) and a presence check whose pattern already matches main ("vacuous_present" — assert something the leaf introduces, or make it kind: manual); (c) it warns "absent_overbroad" when an expect:absent pattern still matches a file outside the leaf's declared files (harmless if an upstream leaf deletes that file); (d) `kind: path` validates against CapabilityManifestDoc; (e) the path-scope lint flags prose too: "scenarios/known_gap/conventions" in a description produced metadata.possible_scope_mismatch (suggested_project solar_challenge) on task 652 — write "the scenario, known_gap and convention entries" instead, and treat any recon gate on that flag as a false positive; (f) update_task title/description/priority are replace-only — append coordination notes to `details` with append=true; (g) a decompose seat can and did find G6 dependency-direction defects the drafters' own DAG missed (12 across five PRDs) — keep the decompose walk even for well-critiqued PRDs.

When authoring capability-manifest delivered_checks, every grep pattern must anchor to a symbol the PRD actually NAMES (a contract dataclass field, a constant, a CLI flag, a table name) rather than to guessed phrasing of code nobody has written yet. delivered_checks are copied into producer tasks' metadata.delivered_checks by commit_planning and become a live dispatch-time gate, so a pattern that guesses at wording fails a task agent that did its job correctly. Corollary established 2026-09-22 on the scaling-defects batch: prefer kind:manual over a weak or ambiguous grep (manual checks are recorded but excluded from the dispatch gate); and every expect:absent check must be re-run against HEAD at authoring time to confirm it has NON-ZERO hits today — an absent-check that is already zero-hit proves nothing about the leaf and should be re-anchored or downgraded. Final batch stats under this rule: 130 grep + 24 manual, of which 11 matched HEAD, 111 were zero-hit 'the leaf builds it' gates, and all 8 expect:absent checks had real hits today.

GOTCHA (delivered_check multi-path greps, found by task 344 on 2026-09-26): a kind:grep delivered_check with several `paths` runs as one `git grep -E -e <pattern> <ref> -- <paths...>`. It passes when ANY path matches. A pathspec for a deleted file matches nothing and raises no error. So when a later refactor retires one listed file, the check does not fail: it silently narrows to the surviving paths, and it only starts failing (holding dependents with dep_capability_not_delivered) when the last surviving match moves too. Example: task 173's "billing-service-takes-register-source" lists the retired runtime/cli.py, and it now passes only via api/routers/billing.py. When you retire or move a file, grep the *.capability-manifest.yaml sidecars and any pending dependents' producers' metadata.delivered_checks for its path. Capability-manifest amendment convention in docs/prds/*.capability-manifest.md and its .yaml twin: amendments are insert-only. A row keeps its decompose-time words, and a dated note of the form " · **AMENDED YYYY-MM-DD — <what changed and where the capability lives now> (<task or escalation id>).**" is appended inside the row's Binding cell in the markdown and to the same row's `binding:` string in the YAML, so the two twins stay byte-equal for that field. The YAML row's delivered_check block is left at its decompose-time values even when the live check in task metadata has been repathed (precedent: the dispatch-tick-shard-columns row). In a YAML plain scalar the note must not contain a colon followed by a space or a space followed by a hash. tests/docs/test_capability_manifest_pointers.py resolves only backticked spans that start with `grep:`, so plain backticked paths in a note are not checked. Description: Restore a behavioural test claim that the merge-lane test-seam migration (PRD plans/merge-lane-quality-prd.md, task γ6 = 5029) had to drop because no public seam exists for it.

WHAT IS UNPINNED (measured in esc-5029-2, re-verified by the steward 2026-09-12). The old test_merge_queue_disposition_wiring.py::TestRunInflightVerifyBaseFactsWiring::test_base_facts_forwarded_from_item_not_fresh_main_read asserted `git_ops.get_main_sha.assert_not_called()` while driving `worker._run_inflight_verify(item, lease)` with `orchestrator.merge_queue._run_post_merge_verify` patched to capture kwargs. That is the task-2357 NEGATIVE claim: _run_inflight_verify passes item.base_sha (the FROZEN dispatch-time main SHA) as main_sha and never issues a fresh get_main_sha() re-read. Description: orchestrator/src/orchestrator/verify.py::_serial_pytest_str rewrites every pytest invocation to run serially by appending `-p no:xdist -o addopts=`. Its own docstring states the INTENT of `-o addopts=` narrowly: clear the pyproject-level `-n auto` per task 2045's shared-venv-mutation recovery. But `-o addopts=` is a WHOLESALE BLANK, not a targeted removal, so it also drops every other token the root addopts carries. Root pyproject.toml:66 carries two more, both load-bearing:

    addopts = "--import-mode=importlib -m 'not smoke and not integration and not warm_lane_bash'"

TWO DISTINCT CONSEQUENCES, the second worse than the first.

(1) COLLECTION MODE. Dropping --import-mode=importlib reverts pytest to prepend mode, which breaks any command whose collection depends on importlib. Measured on the task/4377 worktree, single variable, HEAD=40204bf476:
    `uv run --project shared pytest --tb=short -q --timeout=300 -p no:xdist -o addopts= tests/scripts/ scripts/tests/`
      -> 4197 collected + 2 collection errors ("import file mismatch"), rc=2
    same command + `--import-mode=importlib`
      -> 4218 collected, 4216 passed / 2 skipped, rc=0
The scripts module test_command is a deliberate UNION of tests/scripts/ and scripts/tests/ (task 3384/3460); the two dirs share three basenames (conftest.py, test_restart_all_orchestrators.py, test_reviewer_redundancy_diagnostic.py) and neither has an __init__.py. dark-factory-orchestrator.yaml:105-110 states the safety argument in as many words and rests it explicitly on root addopts setting importlib. This surfaced as esc-4377-3, which red-legged task 4377's verify for a defect entirely outside that task.

(2) MARKER SELECTION -- the wider hazard, and NOT fixed by the narrow unblock. Blanking addopts also drops `-m 'not smoke and not integration and not warm_lane_bash'`, so a serial re-run COLLECTS AND RUNS the smoke, integration and warm_lane_bash buckets that every normal run deselects. A serial recovery re-run therefore does not execute the same test set as the run it is recovering, and can go red on tests the primary path never intended to run. cockpit/tests/test_root_config_smoke_deselection.py:365-367 already records this in-repo: "A bare `-o addopts=` with nothing carried over also works today but would silently run collection under different semantics than every real root-bound run."

PROPOSED FIX. Stop blanking. Emit `-o addopts=<root addopts minus the xdist tokens>` -- derive the override from root pyproject.toml and strip only the token(s) actually targeted. The in-repo precedent for exactly this shape already exists: cockpit/tests/test_root_config_smoke_deselection.py::_addopts_without_marker_filter (:202). Note `-p no:xdist` is already appended independently and disables the plugin outright, so the `-n auto` removal is belt-and-suspenders -- task 2045's intent is preserved.

REGRESSION COVERAGE. Assert a serial-rewritten command still carries the root import mode AND the root marker deselection. Both directions matter: importlib is what keeps the two-directory scripts union collectable, and the marker filter is what keeps the recovery run's test SET equal to the primary run's.

RELATED, ALREADY LANDED: scripts/orchestrator.yaml now pins --import-mode=importlib explicitly on its test_command (steward fix for esc-4377-3, commit 9c657d48ca on task/4377). That is a narrow per-module unblock only -- it does nothing for consequence (2), and nothing for any other module whose collection or selection depends on a root addopts token. This task supersedes it as the general fix; the explicit flag becomes redundant but stays correct.

BLAST RADIUS: every module whose verify leg reaches the serial confirm/recovery re-run, which is the ENV_TRANSIENT retry path for the whole fleet.

  "category": "unknown_test_failure",
  "cause_hint": "18619 passed, 1 skipped, 246 warnings in 418.65s",
  "rc": 143, "timed_out": false
The log ends at the pytest summary with no traceback and no failing test id. rc=143 is 128+15, i.e. the SHELL reporting that its child was SIGTERM'd; the shell itself survived, which is why the status is POSITIVE.

A SIGTERM landing on the pytest GRANDCHILD is reported by the shell wrapper as positive 143, the predicate rejects it, and it falls through to unknown_test_failure — which is is_infra_transient=False, so it gets NO infra retry and instead dispatches a DEBUGGER against a suite that fully passed. verify_categories.py already documents the mirror-image residual for positive 137/OOM; 143 is the same mechanism on a signal no branch can deliver to itself.

GUI event channel convention (established 2026-05-12 in docs/prds/v0_3/gui-event-channel-inventory.md §3-§7): (1) kebab-case event names, same string in Rust `app.emit("name", ...)` and TS `listen<T>("name", cb)`; (2) Rust payload `#[derive(Serialize, Deserialize, Debug, Clone)]` struct in `reify-gui::types`; TS interface in `gui/src/types.ts` with field-for-field exact-name match (no `serde(rename_all)` disguise); (3) **no version field by default** — lockstep Rust+TS schema commits; per-channel `version: u32` opt-in only on real migration need; (4) **error semantics: hard-fail on malformed in `cfg(debug_assertions)` (panic/throw); console.warn drop in release** (preserves dev tight loop without crashing users); (5) `reify-gui::event_bus::emit_typed` thin wrapper as single grep-target for emit call sites; (6) bridge.ts `on<Name>(callback): Promise<UnlistenFn>` wrapper per channel; mock-emitter test utility at `gui/src/__tests__/test_utils/mockEvents.ts`; (7) every new channel ships with Rust roundtrip test + TS shape test in CI. Convention applies to NEW channels; retroactive conformance for the 25 existing wired channels is explicitly out of scope.
