- `session_error_page` is the error page of BOTH listeners (cli.py:103 and :108; the test Browser at test_session_flow.py:53). So a refused rewrite on the operator site also gets whatever the page shows.

## Approach

1. **Prospect page.** error_pages shows one fixed message for every ModelOutputUnusable: heading "The assistant could not finish", text "The assistant could not finish just now. What was written is saved. Go back to your session page, reload it, and try again.", status 502 kept.

2. **Structured rules at the seam.** A new `AnalysisBrokeRules(ModelOutputUnusable)` in model.py carries `broken_rules: tuple[str, ...]`, and its message is derived from that tuple byte-identically to today's. `unusable_analysis` returns it, so both adapters raise it unchanged. Callers that catch ModelOutputUnusable keep working.

3. **The record.** `RefusedWriteUp(Frozen)` in store.py holds `at`, `sequence` (the write-up it would have been) and `broken_rules`. It is appended to `refused-write-ups.jsonl` in the session directory. The store's JSONL append/read is factored into private `_append`/`_read_lines`, which the transcript shares.
   - `Intake._analyse` wraps `model.analyse` for both `request_write_up` and `rewrite`. On AnalysisBrokeRules it appends the record and re-raises.
   - The sequence comes from one `_next_sequence(previous)`, shared with `_next_draft`.
   - Nothing is printed or logged.

4. **Operator page.** `OperatorView.refused_write_ups` feeds a section after the review section. It shows the heading "Refused write-ups: N" (the count, derived from the log) and the last refusal's sequence and time. The last refusal's rules sit in a closed `<details>`, because they can name the instrument's…[truncated, 8617 chars total]

Facts about scoping-intake's record and pages that a test author needs (checked 2026-10-08 on main e8c51e5): Report.headline is a computed property over _EXIT_HEADLINES and FIREWALL_HEADLINE, not a model-written field, so a test cannot plant text in it; DimensionPlacement.reason is rendered only by operator_pages._comparison_html on the operator session page after the blind placement, never in either document; the record validators (Criterion._vagueness_is_recorded, Report._ranking_matches_the_exit, the Analysis validators) check structure only, so Criterion.statement, Criterion.capability, DimensionPlacement.reason, Report.needs_summary and Report.first_step accept an `` payload (verified by building an Analysis via SYNTHETIC_ANALYSIS.model_copy); Intake.say checks only length and SessionStore.create stores the operator label as given, so prospect text and the label reach pages unfiltered. Every StrEnum value in record.py is markup-free, and the strings with apostrophes (Exit.headline for advise_elsewhere, three Dimension.in_region_condition values) are already escaped where rendered.

Working method that paid off for the R5 design deliberation in scoping-intake (2026-10-07/08): a scratch copy of the tree made with `git archive HEAD | tar -x -C <dir>` runs `uv sync` in under a second, pytest in about 40 to 50 seconds and pyright in about 11 seconds, so parallel seats could each prototype one candidate design in its own copy, run the real checks, and mutation-test it (deliberately bypass the escaping and record what catches it). Four spike seats (sonnet/high for the two Markup variants and the AST guard, opus/high for the DSL) cost about 80 to 100k tokens and 8 to 12 minutes each and turned a design argument into measured evidence. A separate opus/high critic seat on the PRD draft cost 171k tokens and 30 minutes and found five blocking defects the author had missed (a false signal premise, an overclaimed guarantee, a stale seam table, the orchestrator's scoped pyright gate, the deploy interpreter location). Both were worth their cost for a design that changes every page module and the Python floor.

content: Convention (scoping_intake, 2026-10-14): prospect-facing legal or safety wording is drafted by the lead, then passed to two seats before Leo sees it: an opus/high critic briefed to refute every promise against the notice, the design note §3.1 and the code (deletion, retention, calibration), and a sonnet/medium reader playing a small-business owner who has never read a legal document, asked to quote every sentence they would misread and give a plainer alternative. The critic's findings changed the text materially (seven refutations); the reader's reorder (summary first, exceptions after the promises, legal last) was adopted. Leo's own candidate statements are kept where true and replaced with the mechanism where not (the "deleted if you don't work with us" line became "deleted on request or about 90 days after your last message, whether or not you work with us").

solar_challenge PV ageing gotcha (task 284 architect; measured 2026-10-09 on main 9ef24ad with pvlib 0.15.1; holds on main once task/284 merges):
- The model chain's DC losses step multiplies each array's p_mp and i_mp by (1 - system_losses) x calculate_degradation_factor(age, rate). So simulate_pv_output's AC for an aged PVConfig is NOT the degradation factor times its new AC.
- Through the CEC Sandia or PVWatts inverters, a 0.90 factor keeps 0.8975-0.8991 of annual Bristol AC for unclipped default sizes. Inverter-limited arrays keep more: 6 kW on 3.68 kW 0.9151, 8 kW on 3.68 kW 0.9332.
- A test that needs an exact aged/new AC ratio uses create_simple_inverter_params, which is exactly linear below its rating (Pso and C0-C3 zero), as tests/unit/test_pv.py's LINEAR_INVERTER_CONFIG does.

9e0097a9-9060-4839-a7c0-78743ecefcaa.content: solar_challenge test gotcha, measured 2026-10-14 by task 674's architect at ad42de8. tests/unit/test_web_template_macros.py::test_every_library_macro_is_called_by_some_template counts a components/macros.html macro as used only if some template imports it by name with {% from %} and calls it. A call from another macro inside macros.html does not count (e.g. chart_panel calling chart_container). So a change that removes a macro's last template caller must also delete that macro, or fold it into its in-file caller, in the same commit; otherwise the test fails, naming the macro. That is what happened when compare.html moved from chart_container to chart_panel.

Discovery (S6 PRD, 2026-10-14): moving settlement from first-write-wins to append-a-revision-when-changed creates a degradation hazard first-write-wins never had. Re-settling a window whose raw telemetry retention has partly dropped (drop_chunks works per chunk, and a half-hour's sample window reaches ±90 s past its edges) would derive lower coverage and append a WORSE revision as current.

Guard chosen: TimescaleStore.materialise raises SettlementWindowAgedOut when settlement_sample_window(window) starts before DB now() minus the active raw retention policy's drop_after (read from timescaledb_information.jobs; no policy, no guard). The DB clock is used because retention jobs run on it. The validation harness drops retention policies, so its fixed 2026-06 month is never refused.

A second consequence: a half-hour whose raw rows ALL vanish gets no new revision, so its stale current row would stay. The dropped-readings drill therefore has to inject day-2 loss BEFORE day 2's first scp-settle (settle day 1, bill the baseline, drop rows, then settle day 2) instead of deleting settlement rows (_clear_settlement_hh).

b7536055-9248-4fff-9d9d-fe5e786f8b9e.content: TimescaleStore.materialise_settlement_hh INSERTs with ON CONFLICT (home_id, metric, hh_start, method_version) DO NOTHING -- append/version-only by design. Consequence: if you mutate raw telemetry rows (e.g. deleting some to simulate drops) within a window that scp-settle has already materialised, re-running scp-settle over that same window is a complete no-op -- the stale pre-mutation settlement_hh rows survive untouched and the coverage signal never moves. To force recomputation you must first DELETE the affected telemetry_settlement_hh rows for that home/window before re-running scp-settle (see validation/drills/dropped_readings.py::_clear_settlement_hh). This bit task 154's dropped-readings drill: a post-drop re-settle silently left every drilled HH's coverage at its pre-drop value (1.0).

Completed: rollups.settlement_hh sorts and integrates rows written in a DST zone on their wall clock, so a half-hour whose sample window spans the autumn clock change settles wrong
Description: Follow-up from task 776 ("rollups.settle_half_hours keys half-hours on each sample's own clock (hh_floor), so samples written off UTC settle off-grid half-hours"), found by its architect on 2026-10-03 at main 5ceee69. Idempotency key: agent-followup-776. There is no escalation record. Start this only after task 776 lands: both edit src/solar_challenge_platform/timeseries/rollups.py.

OBSERVED (scratch probe, not committed, at main 5ceee69):
- src/solar_challenge_platform/timeseries/rollups.py::settlement_hh builds `sorted(Sample(r.ts, r.value) ...)` from its rows exactly as they are written. Python compares and subtracts two aware datetimes that share a tzinfo on their wall clock, ignoring fold. On 2026-10-25 at 01:00Z London's clocks go back, so its wall clock reads 01:00-01:59 twice. Rows written in Europe/London (one ZoneInfo) across that change are therefore mis-ordered, and rollups._settle_flow subtracts them on the wall clock.
- Input: 121 pv_power rows, 1000 + 10*m W at minute m from 2026-10-25T00:00Z, each written with .astimezone(ZoneInfo('Europe/London')). Compared with the same instants written in UTC, settlement_hh at the UTC hh_starts 00:00Z, 00:30Z, 01:00Z and 01:30Z gave [equal, NOT equal, equal, equal]. The 00:30Z half-hour differs; its settlement_sample_window reaches 01:01:30Z, past the change.
- Task 776 fixes the same defect in rollups.settle_half_hours by reading every sample as its UTC instant on entry. Before that fix, settle_half_hours on this input returned two London-keyed half-hours with sample_count 62 and 61 instead of four UTC half-hours of 31. A fix that only keyed on utc_hh_floor raised ZeroDivisionError in rollups._power_at.

WHY IT MATTERS: settlement_hh is MemoryStore's SETTLEMENT_HH path (the hermetic default backend). It is also the audit reference that TimescaleStore's materialiser is checked against. MemoryStore.write does not normalise timestamps to UTC (see task 749's description). So a caller writing Europe/London readings silently gets a wrong settlement around the October change. Heuristic 10 (clear invariants, uniformly enforced) in /home/leo/src/dark-factory/docs/code-quality.md applies. After task 776, settle_half_hours and settlement_hh disagree on such input, although settle_half_hours' docstring calls it "the same arithmetic as settlement_hh".

SUGGESTED FIX: settlement_hh writes each in-window row's ts in UTC as it builds the Sample, through the same naive-refusing conversion task 776 adds to rollups (planned as the private rollups._as_utc). Convert AFTER the home/metric/window filter, so rows outside the window get no new per-row work. This matters because of the task 273 gotcha: MemoryStore calls settlement_hh once per half-hour with every row of the home. Test in tests/timeseries/test_settlement_reference.py: using the London ramp above, settlement_hh at each UTC hh_start equals its value for the same instants written in UTC, and equals settle_half_hours' value for that half-hour. Use public names only (tests/test_private_names.py).
Analysis: PREMISES, verified at main 2838c8a, this branch's base. Task 776 merged at d6fe346.
- src/solar_challenge_platform/timeseries/rollups.py::settlement_hh (L303-344) builds `sorted(Sample(r.ts, r.value) for r in rows if <home/metric match> and first <= r.ts <= last)` from the rows as written. It checks only that hh_start is tz-aware (_require_tz_aware).
- Task 776 added the private rollups._as_utc(name, dt) (L164-172). It refuses a naive dt and returns dt.astimezone(timezone.utc). settle_half_hours (L457-504) writes each sample through it and reads t0/t1 through as_utc_hh_aligned.

Leo's hand-carry procedure (stated 2026-10-01), the contract for hand-carrying any dark_factory task outside the orchestrator: "Check task is pending and only proceed if it is. Set task to deferred. Investigate, plan, implement, review in a fresh dedicated reviewer agent, address any issues, /merge-queue, set task done."
How to apply it:
- The pending check is a hard gate. If the task is anything else, stop and report; don't continue a chain.
- Set deferred BEFORE any other write to the task, such as removing a dependency. Removing the last unmet dependency makes the task dispatchable, so the scheduler could grab it mid-carry.
- The reviewer must not have written or rebased the code, and must review the final rebased diff.

reify tests/infra gotcha: making a test_*.sh sourceable exposes its fixture helpers to callers that never built a fixture, and `git -C ""` resolves to the CURRENT directory. A sourced helper like test_verify_scope.sh's plan_for (`git -C "$FIX" add ...; git -C "$FIX" reset -q -- .`) with an empty FIX would silently unstage the caller's own index, and plan_for_branch would checkout -b/commit/branch -D in the caller's real worktree. `set -u` catches only an UNSET var, not an empty or wrong one. Guard each helper by checking that the fixture path is one the suite's constructors registered (e.g. membership in _TMPDIRS) before any git call (task 8476 plan).

Flaky infra test fix (esc-3985-18): tests/infra/test_sync_comments_grep.sh Section 3 subshells `source tests/sync_comments_test.sh` just to obtain its `extract_fn` helper. That file runs `set -euo pipefail`, so sourcing re-enables strict mode in the subshell; its heavy top-level awk/grep/sed side effects over real source files can trip `set -e`/pipefail transiently under the parallel load of run_all.sh, aborting the subshell BEFORE the actual extract_fn assertion runs — a spurious empty-output FAIL that reproduces 0/N standalone. Fix: source each helper in a `|| true` list (suppresses set -e for the source body) plus `set +eo pipefail` afterward; the final accept/reject command is unaffected so no real signal is masked. Pattern to watch: any test that `source`s a strict-mode script for a helper inherits its set -e and is load-flaky.

In reify's tests/infra shell suites, a "(wiring)" assert that greps a script for a bare filename mention (e.g. `grep -Ev '^[[:space:]]*#' script.sh | grep -q 'git-rerere-guard.sh'`) is a reliable FALSE NEGATIVE: the same script's own `_usage` heredoc lines and `warn`/`err` diagnostic strings mention the helper by name, are not comment lines, so the `^#` prefilter does not strip them, and the assert passes even when the entire invocation block is commented out. Measured on scripts/seed-warm-lane.sh and scripts/setup-dev.sh (both had this flaw). Anchor on the executed COMMAND SHAPE instead: `^[[:space:]]*"?\$.*/<helper>\.sh"[[:space:]]+<subcommand>([[:space:]]|$)` — validated to match exactly the one real invocation line in each script and to exit 1 against a copy with that line commented out. Always pair such an assert with the suite's existing negative-control idiom (plant the defect in a temp fixture copy, assert the detector fires).

On Linux loopback, refusing a POST without reading its body did not disturb urllib clients in scoping-intake's tests. CPython 3.12's http.client sends the headers and the body in separate send() calls, and closing a socket with unread request bytes makes the kernel send RST. Even so, in 2,240 POSTs refused for origin or password by a web.py patched to refuse before reading, every client received its refusal status (403 or 401) and none saw a reset. Bodies ranged from 7 B to 255 KB. Measured 2026-10-08 in task 20's architect trial. A remote browser behind Tailscale Funnel was not measured; the risk concerns only refused requests.

Smoke-testing gotcha for scoping-intake (current as of task 20, replaces the task-7 text that named do_POST as the length refuser): web.py's RequestHandler._refusal() decides every refusal before any body is read. It checks Host (refused.host, 421), then a POST's origin (refused.origin, 403), then the password (refused.password, 401), then a POST's Content-Length; only when none refuses does _respond() read the form, so a refused POST's body is never read. A Content-Length that is missing or not a decimal is refused under the route name refused.malformed with the page 'Malformed request'. A decimal length over MAX_FORM_BYTES, or with more digits than MAX_FORM_BYTES has, is refused under refused.too-long with the page 'Too long'. Both are HTTP 400, and the log line records only method, route name and status. Because the length is judged last, a POST that also breaks an earlier rule gets that rule's status instead: an operator-listener POST without credentials and without Content-Length is 401, not 400, and a foreign-Host POST with a bad length is 421. Before task 7 every length case was one refused.length / 'Too long' refusal, which misled the first smoke pass of review-scoping_intake-20261007 (finding R8, fk-d79ef903b73e). curl -X POST with no --data sends no Content-Length, so a curl-driven walk of the flow is still refused (as malformed, once Host, origin and password pass) on consent, write-up and delete: pass --data '' (or use urllib, which sends Content-Length: 0). A working smoke script follows the review session's scratchpad pattern: synthetic backend, mktemp INTAKE_DATA_DIR, free loopback ports, curl with Host matching 127.0.0.1:<port>.

Completed: Lift the request handler out of make_server's closure and refuse a missing Content-Length by name (web.py::make_server)
Description: Two findings at one function. (1) make_server is a 60-line factory whose body is a seven-method RequestHandler class closing over `site`; it is the highest cognitive-complexity unit in the tree (complexipy 16, next highest 9) and the handler cannot be named, imported or tested outside the closure (docs/code-quality.md heuristic 4, small function scopes). (2) do_POST treats an absent Content-Length header the same as an oversize one and answers 'Too long: that message is too long to accept'; a bodyless POST with no Content-Length is legal HTTP and the refusal names the wrong rule (lens kind:defect; heuristic 10, informatively). Browsers always send the header, so (2) is low.
Analysis: Two findings at one function (R7 fk-da190964bd10, heuristic 4; R8 fk-d79ef903b73e, kind:defect, heuristic 10). Both touch only src/scoping_intake/web.py. The new test goes in a new file, tests/test_web.py.

PREMISES VERIFIED. Context: worktree task/7 at 368e171 (main == 368e171), the worktree's own uv .venv from uv.lock, CPython 3.12.3.
- web.py:104-173: make_server's body is a seven-method RequestHandler class closing over `site`. complexipy at base: make_server 16, _dispatch 9, module total 25.
- web.py:111-117: do_POST runs `if not length.isdecimal() or int(length) > MAX_FORM_BYTES` and answers every failure with one refusal, route "refused.length", page "Too long". Probed with a scratch one-route Site on port 0: a missing header gives 400 'Too long'; "-1" and "abc" give 400 'Too long'; 256001 gives 400 'Too long'; "0" gives 200 and the request is routed.
- A further defect the review did not report, on the same line: a Content-Length of 5000 digits makes int() raise ValueError (sys.get_int_max_str_digits() == 4300) at web.py:113. socketserver then prints a traceback to stderr and the client gets RemoteDisconnected with no response at all. The task says to keep 'Too long' for the size limit, so this decimal value over the limit must also be answered as 'Too long'. RFC 9110 §8.6 also requires a recipient to expect very large numerals.
- Callers: make_server(site, host, port) is called from cli.py:71 and :75 and from tests/test_session_flow.py:42. The signature stays, so task 9 (in progress, cli.py) is unaffected. No file other than web.py contains "refused.length", and nothing is deployed.
- Base checks: 31 passed, ruff check clean, pyright clean, and `ruff format --check .` clean (28 files). The project keeps its code formatted, so format any changed file.

APPROACH
1. Lift (behaviour-preserving). Make RequestHandler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler) a module-level class. Its typed constructor takes `site` as a keyword-only argument and assigns self.site before calling super().__init__(). make_server becomes `return ThreadingHTTPServer((host, port), partial(RequestHandler, site=site))`. Method bodies are unchanged apart from `site` becoming `self.site`. Measured on a prototype: complexipy max per function falls from 16 to 9 and the module total stays at 25, so complexity is moved, not added.
2. Refuse by name. do_POST gets three branches:
   - The header is not decimal (a missing header reads as ""): route "refused.malformed", status 400, heading "Malformed request", message "That request was malformed: its length was missing or unreadable."
   - The value has more digits than MAX_FORM_BYTES or exceeds it: route "refused.too-long", status 400, the same "Too long" page as today.
   - Otherwise: read and route the form as today.
   Measured: do_POST goes from 3 to 6 and the total to 28. The +3 is the new behaviour.
3. Test. tests/test_web.py builds a one-route Site on port 0 and sends requests from a bare socket client, which can send a POST with no Content-Length as curl does. Completed: Check Host, Origin and password before reading a POST body: one ordered refusal chain (web.py RequestHandler)
Description: In src/scoping_intake/web.py, a POST's refusals are applied in two places, in an order that reads the body before deciding whether the request may be answered at all.

do_POST (web.py:111-117 at main 368e171; after task 7 lands, RequestHandler.do_POST at module level) does these steps in order:
1. Checks the Content-Length header.
2. Reads the body: self.rfile.read(...), up to MAX_FORM_BYTES = 256,000 bytes.
3. Calls _respond, which only then runs _refusal(): Host allow-list (refused.host), same-origin via Sec-Fetch-Site/Origin (refused.origin), then the operator password (refused.password).

Consequences:
(a) A POST with a foreign Host, from another website, or without the operator password still makes the server read up to 256 KB before refusing it.
(b) A foreign-Host POST with a bad Content-Length is answered with the length refusal instead of the Host refusal.
(c) The refusal policy has two homes: the inline length checks in do_POST and the _refusal() chain. This is docs/code-quality.md heuristic 10, 'uniformly enforced': one mechanism everywhere, and the invariant's definition has one home.

Proposal: one ordered refusal chain run before any body is read. The order is Host, then origin, then password, then length (missing or unreadable as malformed, over the limit as too long), then read the form. Keep every refusal's route name, status and page.

Tests: through make_server with a bare socket client, as tests/test_web.py does after task 7. A foreign-Host POST with a bad length is refused as refused.host (421), and a refused request's body is never read. One way to show the second: declare a Content-Length larger than the body sent and confirm the refusal still arrives at once, before the 30-second socket timeout.

Completed: serve: Host allow-list entries that still differ from the Host a browser sends (non-canonical INTAKE_PUBLIC_URL hosts; loopback entries on port 80)
Description: Found while planning task 35 (follow-up id agent-followup-35). Task 35 makes src/scoping_intake/cli.py derive the prospect site's Host allow-list entry from INTAKE_PUBLIC_URL the way a browser writes Host: the host in lower case, no port when it is the scheme's default (80 for http, 443 for https) or empty, any other port kept, and an IPv6 address in brackets. The derivation lives in a helper, cli._host_header(scheme, hostname, port), which _public_url calls. web.py RequestHandler._admission_refusal answers only a Host header that is in site.hosts by string equality, and otherwise replies 421 'Not found'. Two cases are left. Both are outside task 35's scope and unlikely in the deployed setup: deploy/README.md sets INTAKE_PUBLIC_URL=https://<machine>.<tailnet>.ts.net, and the units use ports 8471 and 8472.

(1) Host spellings a browser rewrites beyond case and port. Measured on 2026-10-08 with headless Chrome 151 and a capture server: http://[0:0:0:0:0:0:0:1]:P/ is sent as Host [::1]:P. Per the WHATWG URL standard but NOT measured: a non-ASCII name such as https://bücher.example is sent in punycode (xn--bcher-kva.example), and IPv4 shorthand such as http://127.1:P/ is sent as 127.0.0.1:P. urllib.parse.urlsplit keeps all three as typed (CPython 3.14.4, the project venv). The allow-list entry therefore never matches, and every prospect request gets 421. The fix is either to derive the entry the way the browser does (IPv6 compression via ipaddress, IDNA/UTS-46, IPv4 parsing) or to refuse such values at start with UnusablePublicUrl, naming the variable.

(2) cli._loopback_hosts(port) always writes the port: {127.0.0.1:P, localhost:P}. A browser leaves out port 80 for http; measured in Chrome 151, http://intake.example:80/ is sent as Host intake.example. So with --prospect-port 80 or --operator-port 80, a browser at http://localhost/ sends Host 'localhost' and gets 421. The operator site would also refuse http://127.0.0.1/. cli._host_header from task 35 could build these entries too.

Files: src/scoping_intake/cli.py and tests/test_serve.py. Test through tests/test_serve.py's composed() / cli.sites_for, asserting sites.prospect.hosts and sites.operator.hosts.
Analysis: STATE ON MAIN (8541f87, task 35 merged; this worktree's baseline `uv run pytest` = 184 passed).
- cli._public_url checks INTAKE_PUBLIC_URL with urlsplit, then derives PublicUrl.host with cli._host_header(scheme, hostname, port). That helper puts an IPv6 address in brackets and leaves the port out when it is DEFAULT_PORTS[scheme]; urlsplit has already lower-cased the host.
- Commit 99258fd already refuses a non-ASCII host and port 0. So the IDNA half of case (1) is done, and the remaining work is IPv6, IPv4 and other host spellings.
- cli._loopback_hosts(port) always writes f"{LOOPBACK}:{port}" and f"localhost:{port}".
- web.RequestHandler._admission_refusal answers only a Host that is in Site.hosts, by string equality, and otherwise replies 421.

MEASURED WHILE PLANNING. Headless Chrome 151.0.7922.169, 2026-10-08, through a capture proxy on an ephemeral loopback port. No service port was touched. The recipe is in memory topic browser-host-header.
- http://localhost:80/ is sent as Host localhost, and http://127.0.0.1:80/ as Host 127.0.0.1. This confirms case 2.
- IPv6 is written compressed in lower-case hex:
  - [0:0:0:0:0:0:0:1]:P is sent as [::1]:P.
  - [::FFFF:127.0.0.1]:P is sent as [::ffff:7f00:1]:P.
  - [::127.0.0.1]:P is sent as [::7f00:1]:P.
- 127.1, 0x7f.0.0.1, 2130706433, 0177.0.0.1 and 127.0.0.1. (trailing dot) are all sent as 127.0.0.1. This confirms the IPv4 half of case 1.
- intake%2eexample and intake%2Eexample are sent as intake.example. intake.example\evil:P is sent as Host intake.example: the backslash starts the path, and the port is lost.

content: Discovery (2026-10-15, uploads PRD design spike): under the scoping-intake unit's MemoryMax=1G, concurrent multipart uploads are unbounded by ThreadingHTTPServer (TasksMax=128); one upload holds its body plus one copy of the file (~2x max_file_bytes, measured 10 MB peak for a 10 MB part), so ~50 concurrent 10 MB uploads would exhaust memory and systemd would kill both listeners. The PRD therefore adds UploadBudget(UPLOADS_IN_FLIGHT=8) held on the Site (not the module, so each listener and test Site has its own), a slot taken after the Content-Length check and before the read, 503 with Retry-After when full, released in finally: at most 8 x 2 x 8 MB = 128 MB. Pre-existing and named, not fixed: SOCKET_TIMEOUT_SECONDS bounds each recv, not a whole body, so a trickling client holds a thread and a slot until it stops. Also noted: the refusal page for an oversized upload was verified only on loopback; through Tailscale Funnel an early close may surface as a connection reset (Leo to check on a trial).

22ec50d2-a112-4552-9bc2-ac9498898cbe.content: Facts about scoping-intake's record and pages that a test author needs (checked 2026-10-08 on main e8c51e5): Report.headline is a computed property over _EXIT_HEADLINES and FIREWALL_HEADLINE, not a model-written field, so a test cannot plant text in it; DimensionPlacement.reason is rendered only by operator_pages._comparison_html on the operator session page after the blind placement, never in either document; the record validators (Criterion._vagueness_is_recorded, Report._ranking_matches_the_exit, the Analysis validators) check structure only, so Criterion.statement, Criterion.capability, DimensionPlacement.reason, Report.needs_summary and Report.first_step accept an `` payload (verified by building an Analysis via SYNTHETIC_ANALYSIS.model_copy); Intake.say checks only length and SessionStore.create stores the operator label as given, so prospect text and the label reach pages unfiltered. Every StrEnum value in record.py is markup-free, and the strings with apostrophes (Exit.headline for advise_elsewhere, three Dimension.in_region_condition values) are already escaped where rendered.

solar_challenge PV ageing gotcha (task 284 architect; measured 2026-10-09 on main 9ef24ad with pvlib 0.15.1; holds on main once task/284 merges):
- The model chain's DC losses step multiplies each array's p_mp and i_mp by (1 - system_losses) x calculate_degradation_factor(age, rate). So simulate_pv_output's AC for an aged PVConfig is NOT the degradation factor times its new AC.
- Through the CEC Sandia or PVWatts inverters, a 0.90 factor keeps 0.8975-0.8991 of annual Bristol AC for unclipped default sizes. Inverter-limited arrays keep more: 6 kW on 3.68 kW 0.9151, 8 kW on 3.68 kW 0.9332.
- A test that needs an exact aged/new AC ratio uses create_simple_inverter_params, which is exactly linear below its rating (Pso and C0-C3 zero), as tests/unit/test_pv.py's LINEAR_INVERTER_CONFIG does.

solar_challenge web storage seam after task 446 (planned on task/446 at base 51edc0f, 2026-10-04; it holds once task 446 merges).

RunStorage in src/solar_challenge/web/storage.py is the one reader of a runs row by id:
- run_record(run_id) -> RunRecord | None. RunRecord is a frozen dataclass with one field per runs column, under the column's name. config_json and summary_json stay raw JSON text. dataclasses.asdict(record) reproduces the old dict(row).
- latest_run_named(name) -> RunRecord | None.
- update_run_labels(run_id, labels: Mapping[RunLabel, str | None]) -> RunRecord | None. RUN_LABELS = ('name', 'notes'). An absent key is left unchanged, None is written as NULL, and a non-label key raises ValueError before any write.

api.py, history.compare_page and assistant.get_run_results call these instead of SQL. assistant.get_run_results now takes a RunStorage, not a db_path.

1. request_json_object;

3. labels = {label: data[label] for label in RUN_LABELS if label in data};
4. 400 'No fields to update';
5. update_run_labels.

Task 331's 'name/notes must be a JSON string' 400 belongs on the label values between steps 4 and 5.

candidates.content: solar_challenge_platform gotcha (measured 2026-10-14 on main 2db33ae, task 1080): ReferenceDeviceDouble._merge_settings persists EVERY PERSISTED_SETTINGS register (2901, 2700, 2704, 2705) from a write in EITHER mode. So a hand-built Mode-3 map such as {37: 500.0, 2901: 95.0} persists the 95 % floor even though the Mode-3 delivery omits min_soc. Every later Mode-2 delivery then echoes it, through _mode2_delivery. In PhysicsDeviceEnd, any 2901 check must therefore apply whenever 2901 is present in the map, not only to Mode-2 maps. The transports' require_min_soc_in_domain checks are also mode-blind (`if REG_MODE2_MIN_SOC in registers`).

solar_challenge_platform gotcha (measured 2026-10-11, main ab544aa, pymodbus 3.13.1, task 826): an exception a device end raises inside write_setpoint does NOT surface at FrontingDeviceContext.async_setValues. Example: SimService.build_battery_factory(n)'s LookupError for a home outside the n-home fleet. It surfaces at the WRITE_TRIGGER read, in async_getValues -> _do_write, which resets the pending selector, registers and charge before calling the device end. pymodbus's server/requesthandler.py::handle_request catches it, logs it at ERROR on logger pymodbus.logging ("Datastore unable to fulfill request: <reason>"), keeps serving, and answers ExceptionResponse(fc, DEVICE_FAILURE). ModbusTcpTransport.write_setpoint then raises a plain OSError whose message names the home and ends with 'ExceptionResponse(dev_id=1, function_code=131, exception_code=4)'. The device end's reason never reaches the client. To assert the response without hand-typing pymodbus's format, compare against str(ExceptionResponse(ReadHoldingRegistersRequest.function_code, ExcCodes.DEVICE_FAILURE)); both classes are exported by pymodbus.pdu. A scratch script under /tmp that imports tests.* needs PYTHONPATH set to the worktree root.

solar_challenge_platform test convention (task 542, 2026-10-05): to deliver a valid Mode-2 command to a PhysicsDeviceEnd in a test, call tests/simulator/device_end_harness.py::write_valid_mode2(device, home_id). It runs the real SetpointCommand(mode=MODE_2, min_soc_pct=20.0, far-future expiry) -> contract.to_registers -> write_setpoint path. Do not inline another copy of that recipe. tests/simulator/test_service.py and tests/validation/test_run.py share it, and new device-end helpers belong in that module.

solar_challenge_platform typing gotcha (task 598, verified with strict mypy on 2026-10-02):
- To make a SetpointTransport implementer's register-map parameter admit None ("no limit" on 2704/2705), type it Mapping[Any, float | None], not dict[Any, float | None]. dict is invariant, so the dict form breaks structural conformance to SetpointTransport.write_setpoint's dict[Any, float] and rejects every caller that passes to_registers' dict[Any, float]. ModbusTcpTransport.write_setpoint uses the Mapping form.
- Widening SetpointTransport itself breaks mypy conformance of ReferenceDeviceDouble (dict[Any, float]) and PhysicsDeviceEnd (dict[object, float]) unless both widen in the same change.

solar_challenge_platform gotcha (checked 2026-10-03 at main 9d73876): docs/victron-register-contract.md and control/contract.py::WATCHDOG_COVERED_MODES exist ONLY on branch task/585, which is pending. On main, ReferenceDeviceDouble still reverts Mode-2 writes to PASSTHRU after WATCHDOG_WINDOW, and each write replaces the home's whole state. Task 585 makes Mode-2 2700/2901 persist and merge per home, and never revert. solar_challenge_platform gotcha (measured 2026-10-08, pydantic 2.13.4, task 802):
- SetpointCommand's float fields accept NaN and +inf by default, because pydantic's allow_inf_nan is True.
- A range check written in negative form (`if v < lo: raise`) therefore admits NaN. Write it in positive form, `if not (lo <= v <= hi): raise`, or reuse contract._is_finite_real.
- When such a value reaches a wire encoder, round(nan * k) raises ValueError, but round(inf * k) raises OverflowError, which is not a ValueError.
- So a ValueError-only refusal path misses inf unless finiteness is checked first.

solar_challenge_platform gotcha (measured 2026-10-04, pymodbus 3.13.1, task 739): the sync ModbusTcpClient never raises for a Modbus exception reply. write_register / write_registers / read_holding_registers return ExceptionResponse(function_code=fc|0x80, exception_code=N), whose isError() is True, so every call site must check isError() itself. On the server side, a ModbusServerContext refuses a transaction by RETURNING a pymodbus.constants.ExcCodes value from async_setValues / async_getValues; the client then gets that exception code. An exception RAISED inside them becomes DEVICE_FAILURE (0x04) plus an ERROR log with traceback from pymodbus's request handler.

solar_challenge_platform gotcha (measured 2026-10-08, task 600): never round a commanded min_soc_pct derived from a governed fraction. optimiser/planner.py::require_reserve_floor_inside_governed_band compares against governed_min_soc_fraction * 100.0, and that product is not always an integer: 0.07*100 = 7.000000000000001 and 0.29*100 = 28.999999999999996. Rounding 7.000000000000001 down to 7.0 lands below the guard's floor and gets refused as ReserveFloorOutsideGovernedBand. Derive the floor with the guard's own expression (fraction * 100.0); the 2901 wire encoder rounds to 0.1 % on its own.

Description: Split out of task 3697 (esc-3697-4) by the steward on 2026-08-06. 3697 is rescoped to ship its documentation + tested migration script; THIS task provides the write path 3697 needs, then executes the live migration 3697 could not.

   for ANY metadata payload that parses to a dict containing 'done_provenance'. The check
   is PRESENCE-ONLY: no value-unchanged carve-out, no metadata_mode carve-out. It fires
   before _resolve_metadata_mode, before ensure_connected(), before the row SELECT.

2. _merge_metadata has no deletion sentinel (merge is shallow {**old, **new}), and there is
   no task-level metadata_delete_keys — that API exists only for MEMORIES

   (sqlite_task_backend.py:1938-1947) accepts no metadata argument.

3. The privileged non-protocol seam stamp_audit_metadata (sqlite_task_backend.py:2835,
   added by task 2201) also hardcodes _merge_metadata(mode='merge'), so it cannot retire a
   key either, and it is not reachable over MCP.

done_provenance, so metadata_mode='replace' is structurally unusable on ALL of them — while
task_backend_protocol.py:209 and server/tools.py:5956 both document replace mode as
"the sanctioned repair path". That doc claim and this floor are in direct tension. Any
task needing a key RETIRED (not just added) from a done task's metadata is currently
unfixable through public API.

  (C) Widen the privileged stamp_audit_metadata seam to accept a mode/deletion argument and

server/tools.py:5956 so "the sanctioned repair path" is either true or qualified.

Description: Filed from the /unblock of task 4926 (esc-4926-5). An independent pre-merge review of 4926's re-cut diff returned MERGE WITH NITS. These are its should-fix and nit findings. They were deliberately NOT folded into 4926, because the unblock brief limited the re-cut to 4926's own seven commits. None is a regression against pre-4926 main: every failure mode below falls through to the citation gate and never produces a wrong stamp.

(1) SHOULD-FIX: skills/_shared/deriving-landed-sha.md, rc=0 arm, the paragraph "`$c^1` is main-just-before-the-merge only when `$c` was created ON main". Its confirmation step cannot detect the hazard it names. The step reads: "`git rev-list --parents -n 1 "$c"` — the first parent listed must itself be on main before `$c`; if it is the branch side, read `$c^2`".
- Take a merge built on the branch side (an integration branch cut from task/T merges main, then main is fast-forwarded to it). `$c^1` is the task tip, yet `git merge-base --is-ancestor $c^1 main` exits 0 and `--is-ancestor $c^1 $c` exits 0.
- `$c^1` even sits on `git rev-list --first-parent main`, because the fast-forward makes the branch side main's first-parent chain. After a fast-forward, git keeps no record of which side was main.
- Separately, `rev-list --parents -n 1` prints `$c` itself first, so "the first parent listed" is ambiguous.
Failure: an agent on a target project that merges branch-side runs the check and sees it pass. It then trusts `contained-before rc=0` and skips a merge sha it could have stamped, degrading to the citation gate. Fix direction (the architect decides, after validating against real git):

- OR say plainly that parent order is not recoverable, and treat rc=0 on a project with unknown merge direction as undecided, deferring to the citation gate.

The realistic single-machine cause is several commits sharing one committer-date second. The reviewer reproduced this: with every commit in one second and no skew, the default order picked an unrelated side-branch merge (contained-before rc=0) and --topo-order picked the right one. Completed: Repair path books a degraded uuid lookup as minted=True telemetry; consume ReferentFinding.uuid_lookup_degraded once task 4506 lands it
Description: Filed by task 4506's architect as out-of-scope follow-up work. DEPENDS ON task 4506 landing first -- the discriminator this task consumes does not exist until then.

THE DEFECT (verified by reading main at 2026-09-08, not inferred). fused-memory/src/fused_memory/services/memory_service.py::_intended_endpoint_uuid (currently :3921-3959) collapses THREE outcomes into a bare `None` return: node absent, duplicate-name group, and BACKEND LOOKUP FAILED. The first two are deliberate and documented in its docstring; the third is not distinguishable by any consumer.

Task 3672's landed repair path reads `new_endpoint_uuid` at exactly ONE site -- memory_service.py:4713, `minted=finding.new_endpoint_uuid is None`. So a transient FalkorDB error during verification currently books as `minted=True` on the repair record: eta proceeds to resolve-or-MINT off degraded information rather than deferring, and the mint telemetry leaf iota reads is inflated by infrastructure failures. Given the repo's loud-over-silent-degradation norm and that eta performs DESTRUCTIVE edge surgery, an infrastructure signal should not read as a scanner outcome -- the same argument REFERENT_REPAIR_OUTCOMES already makes in its own comment for keeping 'failed' out of the refusal bucket ("conflating them would let a FalkorDB outage read as a scanner regression in leaf iota's rate").

ORIGIN: this is the downstream half of reviewer_comprehensive suggestion S2 (robustness) filed against task 3671, escalation esc-3671-3. Task 4506 actions the UPSTREAM half only -- it adds `uuid_lookup_degraded: bool = False` to ReferentFinding and sets it on the `except Exception` path of _intended_endpoint_uuid, deliberately scoped to RECORDING the fact. The reviewer's own wording is "so eta CAN tell 'not found' from 'could not look'": producing the discriminator is zeta's job, acting on it is eta's, and eta has nothing to branch on until 4506 lands.

THE WORK: once ReferentFinding.uuid_lookup_degraded exists, decide and implement eta's disposition for a degraded finding. Candidate: do not mint on a degraded lookup -- defer the repair and record it under the existing 'failed' outcome (the INFRASTRUCTURE bucket in REFERENT_REPAIR_OUTCOMES, which exists precisely for "we tried and the backend did not cooperate"), rather than minting a node off information known to be incomplete. At minimum, stop reporting `minted=True` for it. Confirm the choice against the repair-storm streak: a backend outage must not feed a false repair-storm alarm.

FILES: fused-memory/src/fused_memory/services/memory_service.py (the repair path, ~:3961-4720, especially the minted computation at :4713), fused-memory/tests/test_referent_repair.py.
Analysis: PREMISES VERIFIED on branch task/5191 (== main c4cfd6691d; no prior task commits).

* Task 4506 HAS LANDED (ef8104f872 "feat(4506): GREEN — report a degraded uuid lookup on the finding", plus amends bf23ca33dd etc., all on main). `ReferentFinding.uuid_lookup_degraded: bool = False` exists at fused-memory/src/fused_memory/utils/referent_verification.py (the dataclass moved there in task 5262) and is in `to_dict()`. `MemoryService._intended_endpoint_uuid` now returns `(uuid_or_None, degraded)` and `_verify_episode_referents`' second pass stamps both via `dataclasses.replace`, sharing one cached verdict per distinct intended referent. So the discriminator exists and no blocking dependency remains.
* The defect the task names is still live: `_repair_edge_findings` (memory_service.py, ~:5125-5476) computes `minted=finding.new_endpoint_uuid is None` (~:5419) and never reads `uuid_lookup_degraded`. A degraded finding today proceeds to `ensure_entity_node` -> `reassign_edge` and books `minted=True`, inflating `ReferentRepairStats.nodes_minted` and `_referent_repair_counts['nodes_minted']` (leaf iota's mint telemetry).
* SECOND, UNNAMED CONSEQUENCE found while reading: the target-plausibility guard reads `target_node_exists=finding.new_endpoint_uuid is not None` (~:5241) off the same lookup. On the whole-set-fallback arm a degraded lookup therefore produces an 'unrepairable' refusal whose reason text (`_implausible_target_reason`) asserts "no node of that name exists in this group" — a claim nobody could check (heuristic 1, a name/message that lies). The comment at ~:5229-5232 explicitly lists "a degraded lookup" among the fail-closed None cases.
* Streak (`_record_referent_repair_pass`, ~:4690-4763): +1 only on `repaired` (outcome 'repaired' AND moved); reset to 0 when zero repairs and `endpoints_checked > 0`; else unchanged. 'failed' never increments — so no false ALARM is possible — but a failed-only pass RESETS the streak (pinned today by tests/test_referent_repair.py::TestReferentRepairStreakSemantics::test_a_failed_only_pass_does_not_increment asserting 0). Routing degraded findings to 'failed' would convert a mid-storm FalkorDB blip (which today usually still repairs, since `ensure_entity_node` re-reads under the lock) into a reset that disarms an in-progress storm alarm. That is the "infrastructure signal read as a scanner outcome" defect in the other direction, and it is caused by this task's own choice, so it is in scope.

DISPOSITION CHOSEN: a finding with `uuid_lookup_degraded=True` is DEFERRED — no `ensure_entity_node`, no `reassign_edge` — and recorded as `outcome='failed'` (the registered INFRASTRUCTURE bucket of REFERENT_REPAIR_OUTCOMES) with `intended_referent` set, `minted=False`, and an eta-authored reason naming the degraded lookup. The new arm sits AFTER the NEVER-GUESS arm and BEFORE the target-plausibility arm in `_repair_edge_findings`, so the plausibility guard never reads a degraded existence answer. Every finding that reaches the write block then has `uuid_lookup_degraded=False`, which makes the existing `minted=` expression truthful without editing it. The finding is deferred, not lost: zeta already journals every resolvable finding (degraded ones included, flag on the payload) to write_journal's `referent_findings` table for the phase-5 replay pass, and the 'failed' record + WARNING carry it to the operator.

STREAK CONFIRMATION: add one arm to `_record_referent_repair_pass` — zero repairs and at least one 'failed' record leaves the streak UNCHANGED (key not created, returns None so the gate cannot page). `repaired >= 1` still wins first, so a pass that repaired and also failed still increments. Result: a backend outage neither feeds a false alarm (unchanged: 'failed' never increments) nor disarms a true one (new: it no longer resets).

FILES: memory_service.py (new arm in `_repair_edge_findings`; one arm in `_record_referent_repair_pass`; docstring/comment updates at REFERENT_REPAIR_OUTCOMES' 'failed' bullet, ReferentRepair.reason, `_intended_endpoint_uuid`, `_repair_episode_referents`' pre-write-guard list, `_repair_edge_findings`' disposition list, the `target_node_exists` comment and the `minted=` comment, and the streak docstring); referent_verification.py (the `uuid_lookup_degraded` field comment's "THE CONCRETE STAKE ... filed as its own follow-up" paragraph becomes a pointer to eta's disposition); tests/test_referent_repair.py (new tests + one changed streak assertion); tests/test_referent_verification.py (class docstring of TestADegradedLookupIsDistinguishableFromAnAbsentNode states the now-fixed defect in the present tense and says eta's half "is filed separately" — prose this change makes false); CHANGELOG.md (operator-visible telemetry and streak semantics change).

Baseline: `cd fused-memory && uv run pytest tests/test_referent_repair.py -q` -> 164 passed (measured in this worktree's own .venv).
Key decisions: A degraded-lookup finding is DEFERRED and booked outcome='failed'. It is not sent through ensure->reassign with a corrected `minted` flag.; The deferral arm runs AFTER the NEVER-GUESS arm and BEFORE the target-plausibility arm. It is an inline check of the recorded `finding.uuid_lookup_degraded` field, not a new module-level rule function, and the existing `minted=` expression is left unedited.; Repair-storm check: 'failed' still never increments the streak (no false alarm, unchanged). New: a pass with zero repairs and at least one 'failed' record leaves the streak UNCHANGED instead of resetting it. This deliberately changes the assertion of the 3672-pinned test `test_a_failed_only_pass_does_not_increment` from 0 to "unchanged".
Steps completed: 5/5
Modules: CHANGELOG.md, fused-memory/src/fused_memory/services/memory_service.py, fused-memory/src/fused_memory/utils/referent_verification.py, fused-memory/tests/test_referent_repair.py, fused-memory/tests/test_referent_verification.py

Three correctness findings from the first /review of scoping-intake worth knowing before touching intake.py or calibration.py: (1) Intake.place binds nothing to the draft it was made against while Intake.request_write_up holds the per-session lock for the whole model call, so a placement posted from a stale operator page lands on the newer draft (task 3); (2) CalibrationLog.save keeps one file per prospect and overwrites it at each blind placement, so a later, non-independent placement (made after seeing the instrument's earlier draft) replaces the only independent row, and the write is not atomic (finding R2, structural, open for Leo); (3) purge_unused still deletes a session whose transcript or released file is unreadable when created_at is past the retention period, while the CLI says it was left in place (task 4). Also: retry_reply, rewrite, the Try-again form and all four session caps have no tests (task 5).

Convention (scoping_intake, 2026-10-14): prospect-facing legal or safety wording is drafted by the lead, then passed to two seats before Leo sees it: an opus/high critic briefed to refute every promise against the notice, the design note §3.1 and the code (deletion, retention, calibration), and a sonnet/medium reader playing a small-business owner who has never read a legal document, asked to quote every sentence they would misread and give a plainer alternative. The critic's findings changed the text materially (seven refutations); the reader's reorder (summary first, exceptions after the promises, legal last) was adopted. Leo's own candidate statements are kept where true and replaced with the mechanism where not (the "deleted if you don't work with us" line became "deleted on request or about 90 days after your last message, whether or not you work with us").

Facts about scoping-intake's record and pages that a test author needs (checked 2026-10-08 on main e8c51e5): Report.headline is a computed property over _EXIT_HEADLINES and FIREWALL_HEADLINE, not a model-written field, so a test cannot plant text in it; DimensionPlacement.reason is rendered only by operator_pages._comparison_html on the operator session page after the blind placement, never in either document; the record validators (Criterion._vagueness_is_recorded, Report._ranking_matches_the_exit, the Analysis validators) check structure only, so Criterion.statement, Criterion.capability, DimensionPlacement.reason, Report.needs_summary and Report.first_step accept an `` payload (verified by building an Analysis via SYNTHETIC_ANALYSIS.model_copy); Intake.say checks only length and SessionStore.create stores the operator label as given, so prospect text and the label reach pages unfiltered. Every StrEnum value in record.py is markup-free, and the strings with apostrophes (Exit.headline for advise_elsewhere, three Dimension.in_region_condition values) are already escaped where rendered.

Routing lesson from the /team run on review finding R13 (2026-10-07, fable lead): roster was one opus/high proposer (111k tokens, 8.7 min), one sonnet/medium fact-checker of SDK and schema behaviour (102k, 3.5 min), and one opus/high skeptic handed the merged drafts (134k, 11.1 min). The skeptic earned its seat: it overturned two claims the lead and the proposer had both made (that OutsideSystem.failure_behaviour and the per-capability failure criterion are the same fact; that a nested-on-system design was "by construction" the best answer) and surfaced four side findings (validator messages reveal the exit to the prospect; refused write-ups are uncapped; stored drafts have no version; the T3 placement has no validator) that became tasks 14, 28 and 29. Lesson: for a design discussion over a small codebase, the lead can draft inline, but a skeptic on the MERGED draft is where the value is; two independent proposers converging on the same wrong framing is exactly what it catches.

candidates.content: dark_factory GOTCHA (verified 2026-07-31, task 3031): any TERMINAL workflow exit that deliberately files NO escalation must still durably write status='blocked' via scheduler.set_task_status — an in-memory self._enter_phase(WorkflowState.BLOCKED) is NOT enough. The recovery table's rows (c)/(d) in orchestrator/src/orchestrator/task_ground_truth.py match on (IN_PROGRESS, no live claimant, branch off main / gone-no-marker, NO open escalation) → RecoveryAction.REVERT_TO_PENDING, so the sweep sets the task back to 'pending' (harness.py `_reconcile_stranded_in_progress`) and replans it. 'blocked' + no escalation is LEAVE-shaped instead. The no-escalation exits are exactly the ones exposed to this, because an open escalation is what normally vetoes the sweep. Caveat: you often cannot just route through _mark_blocked to get the write — its `if not merge_phase:` block calls _spawn_dry_run_unblock regardless of skip_escalation, which would launch a "why is this stuck?" LLM investigation against a task that is merely awaiting a queued merge; write the status directly and treat TerminalExitRejection as the benign already-terminal race (leave the row terminal, never reopen or retry).

In orchestrator/src/orchestrator/workflow.py, TaskWorkflow._mark_blocked's non-escalate_to_human path files escalations via two BARE has_open_l1(task_id) gates: the pre-steward L0 gate (~:9704) and the fall-through L1 gate inside _ensure_l1_escalation_for_blocked (~:10010), which is reached UNCONDITIONALLY from _mark_blocked's terminal fall-through (~:9873). Because has_open_l1 historically checked only task-id (any open level-1), ANY unrelated open L1 for the task silently suppresses a NEW root cause at both gates. Combined with merge_phase=True (which suppresses the status write/requeue/dry-run at ~:9586-9626), the generic merge-blocked fall-through in _submit_to_merge_queue (~:6856) could produce merge_finalized state=blocked followed by total silence (Reify 5120 07-13 RCA RC-2). Task 2757 fixes this by making has_open_l1 category-aware and emitting an unconditional EventType.merge_blocked at the fall-through.

GOTCHA (dark-factory, verified in code while planning task 4377): closing an escalation is a STATE-CHANGING ACT ON ITS SUBJECT TASK, even under `action='close_only'` whose documented task-status effect is "unchanged".

MECHANISM. `orchestrator/src/orchestrator/task_ground_truth.py::_RECOVERY` is a dict keyed on (status, live_claimant, branch_state, has_open_escalation, deploy_phase), read through `.get(_shape(report), RecoveryAction.LEAVE)`. The shape (IN_PROGRESS, live_claimant=None, EXISTS_OFF_MAIN, has_open_escalation=True, deploy_phase=None) is ABSENT from the table, so it falls through to the default and the row is PRESERVED. Close the record and the boolean flips: the shape becomes the (…, has_open_escalation=False, …) row that IS in the table, mapping to REVERT_TO_PENDING. The veto sites read `report.open_escalations` directly (harness.py ~:6185 and ~:6274).

WHY THIS IS EASY TO GET WRONG. The preservation is an EMERGENT PROPERTY OF A MISSING TABLE ROW, not a declared rule — nothing anywhere says "this record is holding this task". `resolve_issue`'s own docstring table lists `close_only` -> "task-status effect: unchanged", which is true of the call mechanically and false of its consequence. `escalation/src/escalation/pins.py::classify_pins` answers only "does this OPEN record veto recovery?" (classification at recovery time) and protects nothing from being CLOSED.

WHAT IT COST. On 2026-08-08 an L2 cascade close of the 11-member cluster esc-3237-5 dismissed esc-3371-2, the only pin preserving mu-gate validation specimen task 3371; the task reverted to pending 879.6s later and the specimen is permanently gone. The closing watcher checked for harm and reasoned correctly within what it could see — none of the eleven was `blocked`, so no stranded-blocked shield was stripped. An orphan-reaper false-positive record and a deliberate pin are indistinguishable by id, level, category, severity, agent_role or content. The sibling pin esc-3105-3 (a 15-member L2 cluster head) is still the last hold on task 3105.

PRACTICE. Before closing any pending escalation on a non-terminal task — and before designating a homogeneous cluster for a bulk/cascade close — check the subject task's status and branch state, not just whether the record looks moot. Note `escalation/src/escalation/sweep.py` is a file-RELOCATOR (moves already-terminal records to the archive), not a closer, despite the name.

candidates.content: Bash gotcha in reify shell scripts: `IFS=$'\t' read -r a b c` silently COLLAPSES empty fields, because tab (like space and newline) is IFS *whitespace* — runs of it count as one delimiter and leading/trailing ones are stripped, so an empty field shifts every later field left. Any tab-separated record with an optional/nullable middle column is therefore mis-parsed (observed in scripts/deterministic-gate-closure-staleness-sweep.sh: an absent JSON `block_class` shifted `head_sha` into `main_sha`, and a `tasks` row with NULL `heartbeat_at` plus a populated `claimant_run_id` read the claimant as the heartbeat). Use a non-IFS-whitespace separator — ASCII US, `_FS=$'\x1f'` — for both the producer (`sqlite3 -separator "$_FS"`, python `"\x1f".join(...)`) and the consumer (`IFS="$_FS" read -r ...`), and neutralize US/newline inside any prose field so it cannot forge a field or row boundary.

GOTCHA when writing a live-corpus sweep over `git ls-files -s` in reify (verified task 6068, 2026-08-21): always parse with `-z` + `awk 'BEGIN { RS = "\0"; FS = "\t" }'` and take `$2`, NEVER a whitespace-splitting `awk '{print $4}'`. `git ls-files -s` emits "<mode> SP <sha> SP <stage> TAB <path>", so a whitespace split truncates any tracked path containing a space. Two distinct failure modes, and the second is EXTENSION-SPECIFIC and worse. Measured in a scratch repo tracking `docs/notes.md`, `data/report v2.csv`, `docs/foo.bar baz.qux`: the tab-split form emits {csv, md, qux} (correct) while the whitespace form emits {bar, md}. (1) PHANTOM: `docs/foo.bar baz.qux` truncates to `docs/foo.bar`, whose post-dot token `bar` names an extension existing nowhere — a loud RED sending the reader hunting a nonexistent file. (2) SILENT MISS: `data/report v2.csv` truncates to the now-DOTLESS `data/report`, so a dotted-segment branch DROPS it and the real `csv` is never checked — the alarm quietly weakens instead of failing. Mode (2) cannot arise on an extensionLESS sweep (a truncated path stays dotless and is still swept), so an extension-side sweep depends on the parse shape MORE, not less. reify tracks zero paths containing a space today (`git ls-files | grep -c ' '` -> 0), so both are latent — but a standing alarm exists precisely to outlive today's corpus. Also pass `--` to grep (`grep -cxF -- "$tok"`) when the swept token could begin with a dash, else grep parses it as an option bundle and the assertion errors instead of answering. Live instances: Cycles 9 and 10 of tests/infra/test_lock_charter_guard.sh.

Bash path-shape gotcha (found in review of task #5990, tests/infra/harness-layout-lib.sh): a `case` glob like `crates/*/*` does NOT establish "two non-empty segments" — bash lets each `*` match the EMPTY string, so a doubled-slash path `crates//foo.rs` MATCHES the pattern with an empty first segment. Any `${rest%%/*}`-style extraction after that arm then yields an empty string, not the intended value. Consequence for structured verdict lines: a guard that documents its field as `crate=<c>` silently emits `crate=` (blank) instead of its `-` sentinel — the shape passes the pattern guard but fails the contract the guard was written to enforce. Verified: `crates//foo.rs` and `crates///a/b` both matched and produced ''; `crates/loneseg`, `crates/`, '' and non-crates/-rooted paths correctly fell through to the sentinel. FIX: re-check the DERIVED value, not just the pattern — `case "${rest%%/*}" in '') ;; *) out="${rest%%/*}" ;; esac`. Prefer that empty `case` arm over the terser `[ -n "${rest%%/*}" ] && out=...`: as a function's LAST command the `&&` form returns non-zero on the empty branch and aborts a caller running under `set -e`. Reachability is the thing to check before dismissing this as theoretical — here the row came from a hand-written manifest fed through `harness_layout_baseline_rows`, which passes doubled-slash rows through unfiltered.

Bash gotcha in reify's tests/infra/*.sh hermetic test harnesses: capturing a script's stdout via command substitution (`OUT="$(bash "$SCRIPT" ... )"`) blocks until EVERY process holding the pipe's write end closes it — including any backgrounded grandchild (`{ cmd; } &`) that inherited stdout and hasn't exited yet, not just the direct child. This masks bugs where a script is supposed to return control before a background job finishes (e.g. an FD-hygiene/lock-leak test). Fix: capture stdout via a real file redirect (`bash "$SCRIPT" ... >"$OUT_FILE" 2>"$ERR_FILE"; OUT="$(cat "$OUT_FILE")"`) instead of `$(...)`, matching how stderr is typically already captured via a real ERR_FILE in these harnesses. File redirects have no EOF-on-all-writers semantics, so the capture returns as soon as the direct child exits (like a plain `wait`), independent of detached grandchildren. Fixed in tests/infra/test_seed_warm_lane.sh's run_helper_real (task #5223 step-3, commit f22f51b770).

Test-assert convention (from the 2026-07-03 T1/T3 quoting-bug incident): in bash infra tests, NEVER interpolate captured command output unescaped into a bash -c string — `bash -c "printf '%s\n' \"${CAPTURED}\" | grep ..."` re-enters the parser and explodes the moment the captured text contains double quotes/parens/& (verify.sh plan lines contain `-E "not ((package(x) & binary(y)))"` whenever REIFY_GATE_EXCLUDE_HEAVY=1). The safe idiom, already used by test_occt_flock_gate.sh T2/Test 17: export the variable and reference it ESCAPED inside bash -c (`bash -c "printf '%s\n' \"\$CAPTURED\" | grep ..."`) so expansion happens inside bash -c's own parse. Task 4965 converts the 8 unsafe sites (T1/T3 firing today; T4–T7 latent only because lint/check plan lines happen to contain no quotes yet). When reviewing new infra tests, grep for `\"\${_` inside bash -c strings.

Reify shell-output condensation hook: the source-mangling behaviour documented for Rust files (memory c9b73a7f, which says ".rs") ALSO applies to TypeScript and TSX. Confirmed 2026-08-24 in warm lane _lane-22 (task 6185): `cat gui/src/viewport/scalarRange.ts` displayed `export function computeScalarRange(meshes: Record<string, MeshData>, channel: string): {min: number; max: number} | null` as `function computeScalarRange(meshes, channel) {` — `export` and every type annotation gone — and displayed the loop header `for (let i = 0; i < data.length; i++)` with its FIRST semicolon missing. `cat -A` confirmed the semicolon was absent from the displayed bytes while the Read tool showed it present, so it is a display-layer rewrite and the file on disk is intact. The under-appreciated risk is not a failed Edit match (that fails loudly) but an agent "repairing" the phantom syntax error or re-adding stripped annotations, silently degrading correct code. Corollary that worked well: drive edits from a Python script doing exact-string replacement with `assert src.count(old) == 1`, which reads the true bytes and fails loudly, and reserve the Read tool for inspection.

In reify agent sessions, Bash output is passed through a display condenser that SILENTLY REWRITES file contents: `cat`/`tail`/`head` of a Rust source file drops attribute lines (`#[test]`, `#[derive(..)]`) entirely and strips trailing semicolons, so valid code renders as syntactically invalid. It also condenses `ls` (to "LS: ls | N entries") and `git log` (to "[log] N commits"). Measured 2026-09-14 on crates/reify-cli/tests/harness_cli/cli_affine_eval.rs: `cat` showed zero `#[test]` and no semicolons while `grep -c '#\[test\]'` returned 6 and `grep -c ';$'` returned 41. Never conclude a file is malformed or missing test attributes from `cat` output — confirm with `grep -n`/`grep -c` (which report raw bytes) or the Read tool. Writes are unaffected.

Reify shell-instrument gotcha (measured 2026-08-20, task 6018, lane _lane-5): a shell variable whose VALUE is a glob pattern must never be word-split with a bare unquoted `for x in $VAR` — that expansion gets pathname expansion as well as the intended splitting, so when the process's cwd happens to contain a matching tree the loop variable binds to real RELATIVE paths instead of the pattern. In scripts/sample-test-binary-concurrency.sh this made the reading CWD-DEPENDENT and SILENT: the identical one-pid fixture reported peak=1 from a lane root but peak=0 from /home/leo/src/warm-lanes/worktrees, with no error. The fix is to split ONCE at parse time under `set -f` (which kills globbing but leaves word-splitting intact — verified) into an array, then `set +f` immediately: the restore is load-bearing whenever the script later `eval`s a caller-supplied command that may itself rely on globbing. Keep the `case "$x" in ($pat)` pattern UNQUOTED — case patterns undergo neither pathname expansion nor field splitting, so quoting there would turn pattern matching into literal comparison. Also reject a whitespace-only pattern string explicitly: `[ -n "$VAR" ]` passes on whitespace but the split yields ZERO patterns, after which every check silently matches nothing. Applies to any host-inspection instrument in scripts/ that carries a glob-valued pattern list (cf. scripts/lib_proc_reaper.sh's /proc/<pid>/exe confirmation idiom).

Reify tests/infra quoting nuance (verified task 6374, test_occt_gated_scope.sh): a `"` inside a SHELL VARIABLE's value does NOT terminate the enclosing `bash -c "..."` double-quoted string — the outer shell finishes parsing quotes before expansion, and expansion results are never re-scanned for quoting. So an awk/sed/grep program held in a single-quoted assignment (e.g. `_PAT='^test-threads = \("num-cpus"\|[0-9][0-9]*\)$'`) can be interpolated as `grep -c '${_PAT}' "$FILE"` inside the outer `bash -c "..."` and its `"`, `$`, `\(` and `\|` all survive intact. This CONTRADICTS the caveat comment at test_occt_gated_scope.sh:949-952 ("a double quote cannot appear in this file's bash -c \"...\" assert form"), which is true only of a `"` typed LITERALLY into the assert body — there it must be written `\"`. Distinct from the task-4965 lesson (memory 2a55fbdd): that one is about the INNER bash re-parsing interpolated CAPTURED content as shell syntax, and still applies — prefer the positional-arg form for untrusted/captured data. This nuance is safe specifically for a fixed, author-controlled pattern constant.

GOTCHA when hand-building a synthetic NUL-separated stream to unit-check an `awk 'BEGIN{RS="\0"}'` parser (hit first-hand in reify task 6068, 2026-08-21): bash's printf parses `\0nnn` as an OCTAL escape, not as "NUL then digits". So `printf '160000 a 0\tgraphiti\0100644 b 0\tsrc/a.rs'` does NOT emit two records — `\0100` becomes '@' and the second record is silently glued onto the first, so the awk filter appears to emit nothing and you misread a WORKING filter as broken. Use the separator form instead: `printf '%s\0' 'rec1' 'rec2'`, which emits a real NUL after each argument. Verified: the `$1 !~ /^160000 /` gitlink filter over `git ls-files -s -z` correctly keeps `src/a.rs` and drops both `160000` mount points once the fixture is built with `printf '%s\0'`. Same trap applies to any `printf` fixture where a `\0` is immediately followed by a digit (mode bits, shas, stage numbers all start with digits, so `ls-files -s` fixtures hit it every time).

Bash-tool output condensation in reify extends to `cat` of a SOURCE FILE, and this instance is more dangerous than the cargo/git ones because the result still reads as valid code. `cat crates/.../foo.rs` came back with `pub` qualifiers stripped, statement-terminating semicolons removed, and return types dropped — e.g. the real `pub fn seed_tasks_db() -> Connection {` displayed as `fn seed_tasks_db() {`, and `use rusqlite::Connection;` as `use rusqlite::Connection`. Unlike the cargo-skim `PASS/FAIL/SKIP` summary or the git-diff pretty-printer (canonical entries: cargo 80932c8e, git diff 408a5249), nothing about the output announces itself as condensed, so an agent can silently misread a symbol's visibility or signature and then "fix" code that was never broken.

WHAT WORKS: `sed -n '<a>,<b>p' <file>` and `grep -n <pat> <file>` both return verbatim bytes, including `pub`, `;` and return types — use those to read Rust (or any language where a dropped token changes meaning), not a bare whole-file `cat`. To be certain of exact bytes, append `| cat -A` and read the `$` line terminators. The `env <cmd>` prefix that bypasses the cargo and git wrappers was not tested for `cat`.

Measured 2026-09-18 in warm lane _lane-12 (task 7550), reading crates/reify-audit/tests/common/schema.rs: the bare `cat` showed `fn seed_tasks_db() {` at the same place `grep -n 'fn seed_tasks_db' | cat -A` showed `71:pub fn seed_tasks_db() -> Connection {$`.

In reify, a bash helper that allocates a temp file/dir and registers it in a caller-scoped cleanup array (`_TMPFILES+=("$f")`) silently leaks when the helper is invoked through command substitution (`f="$(_scan_file ...)"`), because the substitution runs in a subshell and the array append mutates a copy that dies with it — the EXIT trap then always sees an empty array. Measured 32 leaked entries per run of tests/infra/test_cited_test_paths_resolve.sh before the fix. Allocate everything under ONE run-private `mktemp -d` and `rm -rf` just that directory in the trap; this removes the failure mode by construction instead of requiring every helper to register correctly. Same subshell hazard test_helpers.sh documents for assert() (esc-4959-57).

Bash gotcha in reify's tests/infra/*.sh hermetic test harnesses (task 5590, verified empirically): a bash ARRAY append (`ARR+=("$x")`) made inside a backgrounded `( ... ) &` subshell is silently discarded when the subshell exits — the parent shell's array is unaffected. Probe: `HITS=(); note main; ( note bg1; note bg2 ) & wait` yields `count=1 elems=main`. This blinds any runtime detector/recorder fed from inside a backgrounded fixture (e.g. tests/infra/test_seed_warm_lane.sh's H5d/H9, which run `run_helper_real` inside `( ... ) &` to test blocking-lock behaviour) — the detector silently reports all-clear even when the backgrounded invocation truly hit the condition being watched for. Fix: back the detector's state with an append-only FILE instead of an array (e.g. `printf '%s\n' "$x" >> "$STATE_FILE"`) — a `>>` append performed inside a subshell IS visible to the parent, because it's a kernel-level write to a shared inode, not a shell-variable mutation. Anchor the file under the suite's existing per-run tmpdir-root (reclaimed by the EXIT trap) so no new cleanup registration is needed. Single-line `printf` appends to an O_APPEND file are atomic well below PIPE_BUF (4096), so concurrent appends from a background job and the main shell's own use cannot corrupt a record. Non-vacuity discipline: pair the fix with a mechanism-guard test that constructs its own `( ... ) &` around the real recorder function and asserts the append survives — an end-to-end assert against real backgrounded call sites alone can go vacuous if those call sites are ever un-backgrounded.

Two environment/tooling gotchas hit during the 2026-06-24 reify session: (1) The repo's `target/` is a symlink to /media/leo/data_lv_1/leo/reify-build/target (off-main-disk build dir, intentional per CLAUDE.md symlink design). That dir had been removed (the data volume /media/leo/data_lv_1 was still mounted, 17T, but reify-build/ was gone), so `cargo build` failed with "failed to create directory `target` … Not a directory (os error 20)". Fix: `mkdir -p /media/leo/data_lv_1/leo/reify-build/target` to make the symlink resolve again (preserves the off-main-disk design). (2) The Claude Code Bash tool (this environment) FLATTENS newlines in a multi-line command into spaces when it evals via the shell snapshot, so statements separated only by bare newlines get concatenated — e.g. `cd /home/leo/src/reify` followed by a newline then another statement becomes `cd /home/leo/src/reify <next> …` → "cd: too many arguments" and nothing runs. Workaround: separate statements with `;`/`&&`, or (for anything multi-line/non-trivial) write the script to a file and run `bash <file>` — heredocs and single-`;`-joined commands are unaffected.

bash 5.2 gotcha in Reify shell scripts: a NUL byte can never be used as a sentinel across command substitution. Both `st="$(python3 -c '...writes \x00...')"` and a case pattern written as `"$(printf '\000')"` strip the NUL and emit `warning: command substitution: ignored null byte in input` to the SCRIPT'S OWN stderr — the same channel the project's `warn()`/`info()` helpers write to, so the noise interleaves with real `[warn]` lines. Both sides collapsing to the empty string makes such code look correct while leaking one warning per loop iteration (measured: 2 warnings for a 2-file loop in scripts/deterministic-gate-closure-staleness-sweep.sh `_esc_state`). Use a literal token like `__PARSE_ERROR__` instead. Assertable in shell test suites via the `_err_has`-style stderr capture with `_not _err_has 'ignored null byte'`.

Reify shell COUNTING guards over a script's own source (e.g. tests/infra/test_infra_git_env_isolation.sh arm F, which asserts every member-spawn / `git -C` site in tests/infra/run_all.sh is wrapped in reify_git_env_scrub): normalize in this ORDER — fold line continuations FIRST (`sed -e :a -e '/\\$/N; s/\\\n//; ta'`), THEN drop comment lines (`grep -v '^[[:blank:]]*#'`). Folding first is needed so a wrapper sitting on the preceding physical line counts as one logical statement; stripping comments is needed because run_all.sh is heavily commented and a comment that quotes the invocation shape verbatim otherwise scores as a real, unscrubbed call site. MEASURED and self-inflicted on task #7106: the explanatory block comment added alongside the fix contained `git -C "$FIX"`, which took the guard from 7-of-7 to 7-of-8 and would have redded the merge gate on pure prose. Prefer the comment strip over anchoring the pattern to a leading `bash `/`reify_git_env_scrub` token — narrowing the pattern also stops it matching a legitimately reshaped call site (e.g. inside a command substitution), turning a real coverage hole into a silent pass, and a `>= N` floor only catches sites DISAPPEARING, never ones the pattern was narrowed past. Same family as memories 07b67efe (self-matching static source-scan guard) and fb0ff32e (header comment over-counting a manifest grep).

In reify, a fixture helper that registers cleanup by appending to an array (e.g. `CLEANUP_ACTIONS+=(...)`) silently leaks when it is called as `x=$(helper)`: the command substitution is a subshell, so the append is discarded. Measured in tests/infra/test_tree_sitter_pipeline.sh, where mk_ts_generate_fixture, mk_ts_build_fixture, ts_masked_path_dir and mk_verify_fixture leaked every run (task 8725). reify Bash-tool commit-message gotcha, the SILENT variant (complements the loud heredoc-collapse entries 38e5a221 / 38db8181 / 6e5431ea, which all describe a bash syntax error): a PLAIN multi-line `git commit -m "line1\n\nline2..."` — no heredoc, no command substitution — does NOT error. It succeeds, with every newline collapsed, producing a single ~1000-char subject line and an empty body. Nothing in the tool output flags it; `git log --oneline` on main is where it shows up, permanently. Detect with `git log -1 --format=%B <sha> | wc -l` (2 lines == collapsed) or `git log -1 --format=%s <sha> | wc -c`. Measured 2026-08-20 on task 6391: 3 of 8 commits were mangled this way and only the `-F`-file commits survived intact. ALWAYS use `cat > /tmp/<task>-<step>-msg.txt <<'EOF' ... EOF` followed by a separate `git commit -F /tmp/...txt` for any multi-paragraph message — that form is verified to preserve structure AND to stop unescaped backticks from being command-substituted out of the message (entry 45c8d965). Amending afterwards is possible but rewrites SHAs already recorded via mark_step_done, so get it right on the first commit.

content: Bash gotcha for TSV produced by a helper and read in reify scripts: `IFS=$'\t' read -r a b c` COLLAPSES consecutive tabs, because tab is an IFS-whitespace character, so an empty middle field silently shifts every later column. Emit a non-empty placeholder (e.g. `-`) for empty fields and put the free-text field (the path) LAST so `read` hands it the remainder of the line. Task 8662's plan specifies this shape for reify_path_attribution.py's `attribute --format tsv`; it is not implemented as of 2026-10-15.
