candidates.content: Web home parsing fact (solar_challenge): the web home-config parser, solar_challenge.web.simulation_params.parse_home_config, is hand-rolled and does NOT call the canonical config._parse_home_config. Task 144 moved it verbatim from web/api.py:_parse_home_config. It builds PVConfig/BatteryConfig/LoadConfig/HomeConfig directly from the JSON body. Consequences: (1) new engine fields must be added to the web parser explicitly; they are NOT inherited from the YAML parser. (2) Because the web parser builds PVConfig() directly, exposing the P3 PV-age fields in the web form depends on task #16 (which adds the fields to PVConfig), NOT #17 (which only updates config._parse_pv_config + the fleet sampler). The canonical parsers config._parse_tariff_config and config._parse_dispatch_strategy_config ARE module-level and reusable consume-only from the web parser. There is NO singular YAML heat-pump parser (only _parse_heat_pump_distribution_config), so the web must construct HeatPumpConfig directly.

solar_challenge config.py convention, once task 373 merges (branch task/373, final code commit 3e98a9f, 2026-10-09); it amends memory 51b58a15's three-edit recipe for the blocks it converts. parse_home_block and the pv, battery, load and grid_charging block parsers now pass their dataclass only the keys a block sets: an omitted key takes the dataclass's declared default, a null is handed on as None (never read as the default), and no value is coerced. They hold no data.get(key, default) line, so adding a field to one of those blocks takes two edits, not three:
- the key in the block's recognised-key constant (_PV_BLOCK_KEYS, _BATTERY_BLOCK_KEYS, _LOAD_BLOCK_KEYS, _GRID_CHARGING_BLOCK_KEYS; _HOME_SCALAR_KEYS for a home scalar such as name, which _HOME_BLOCK_KEYS derives from);
- the key in that block's "every recognised key is accepted" test in tests/unit/config/test_unrecognised_keys.py.
The only parser-owned values are the capacity fallbacks for an omitted key, _PV_CAPACITY_KW_WHEN_OMITTED (4.0) and _BATTERY_CAPACITY_KWH_WHEN_OMITTED (5.0), because PVConfig and BatteryConfig declare no capacity. Omitted-key and null handling is pinned through parse_home_block by TestOmittedAndNullKeys in tests/unit/config/test_home_block.py. The heat_pump and ev parsers and the fleet-distribution layer still restate their defaults, so memory 9540324f (explicit data.get lines, no splat) still holds for them.

Solar-challenge sim facts useful for the financial layer: (1) all scenarios run a FULL YEAR (period 2024-01-01→2024-12-31, simulation_days==365), so the sim produces an annual energy figure directly — no annualization hack needed for the householder bill. (2) PVGIS weather is location-MD5-cached, so re-running the sim at different system ages re-costs only the flow/dispatch loop, not the PVGIS fetch — making the multi-age 25-yr projection much cheaper than it looks (aged generation is a pure multiplicative degradation factor; only battery behavior is non-linear in capacity and needs the dispatch re-run). solar_challenge gotcha, measured 2026-10-10 on main 94281d4 (task 610 architect). A HomeConfig field reaches a web or CLI run through two paths that both go via config.py's YAML grammar. (1) Web run-history YAML export: GET /api/history/runs/<id>/export/yaml writes stored runs with scenario_writer.home_scenario/_pv_block, and `home run` reads that YAML back. A field the web form sets but _pv_block does not write is silently reset to its default on export, and the round trip is unequal: PVConfig(system_losses=0.10) came back as 0.14075660688264469. (2) CLI `home run` overrides (--pv-kw etc.) are written into the config dict by cli/utils.load_config_with_overrides and parsed by config.parse_home_block. A new override key is therefore refused unless config's block key set (e.g. _PV_BLOCK_KEYS) lists it: "Unrecognised keys in home.pv: 'system_losses'". So expose a field on the web form or CLI only after config.py reads it and scenario_writer writes it.

Measurement technique for solar_challenge finance: to compare the projection's own-use rate base on and off the override WITHOUT a code change, monkeypatch solar_challenge.finance._billed_energy. Have the wrapper pass the real FinanceConfig only when sys._getframe(1).f_code.co_name == 'householder_bill'. Otherwise pass dataclasses.replace(finance, self_consumption_override=None). Bills then keep the override, and project_multi_year falls back to basis C. That emulates task 308's rejected option (b) and reproduces the pre-308 figures exactly (CR6 anchor: 12.2232 p, outlay £666.32). To keep real-weather runs cheap, memoize the injected simulate by repr(FleetConfig): solve_cost_recovery_rate calls simulate for several ages, and the three variants share every simulation. A 5-home slice with max_workers=5 completes in a few minutes. Two parallel full 100-home `finance run --cost-recovery --project` runs through typer's CliRunner died silently with empty output while the offline lane's pytest shared the machine.

Solar Challenge sim CLI/usage facts (as of 2026-06-19, after the W2/W3 finance build). Invoke via `uv run --extra dev solar-challenge ...` (no global entry point; .venv is present in the repo root). Two finance surfaces: (1) `solar-challenge finance run <scenario> [--assumptions physics|spreadsheet|both] [--project] [--start --end]` prints a householder bill (standing charge + import@tariff + VAT − self-consumption saving − SEG export) for a representative home + fleet distribution, optionally project economics (DSCR/IRR/payback), and a flexibility-value block. (2) `solar-challenge optimize configs <scenario> --pv 3,4,5,6 --battery 0,5,10 --inverter 3.68 --sensitivity retained_floor,grid_services` sweeps the PV×battery×inverter product, solves the cost-recovery rate per config, ranks by householder outlay, and renders a two-table markdown report + OAT sensitivity panel. The board scenario is scenarios/bristol-phase1-flex.yaml (100 homes, Economy-7 grid-charging arbitrage, fixed 5 kWh battery, capacity_at_events grid-services at the Central band). PERFORMANCE: a full-year (366-day) 12-config sweep is heavy (~12 sequential 100-home fleet-years; the CLI itself warns above ~100k home-days); the sensitivity panel re-runs the whole sweep across each axis × 3 values (~10× the base sweep). For exploratory runs use --start/--end to shrink the window, but note a short window biases the install-config ranking seasonally (winter over-rewards arbitrage, summer over-rewards export).

In solar_challenge, config.py's YAML parsers (_parse_pv_config, _parse_battery_config, _parse_load_config, etc.) build each config dataclass from an EXPLICIT field-by-field data.get(key, default) list — they do NOT use a **data splat. Consequence/gotcha: when you add a new field to a config dataclass (e.g. PVConfig.system_age_years), you MUST also add a matching data.get(...) line in the corresponding _parse_* function, or any value set in a scenario YAML is silently dropped (no error) and the simulation runs with the dataclass default. Always pair a new config field with a parser-level test that a dict carrying the key produces a config object holding it.

Description: FINDING (review 20261007T025143, at HEAD a2c8076). A review sub-agent confirmed it by constructing Settings. Convention: production secrets fail fast at boot. Heuristic 10: the invariant has to fail closed.

WHERE: src/solar_challenge_platform/settings.py. `environment` (~L66) is a free-form str. is_production (~L285) exact-matches it against the production spellings. Every production guard keys on that predicate: the placeholder-jwt_secret refusal (~L24/L59) and, since task 512, the refusal of the in-memory telemetry store.

SCENARIO: an operator sets ENVIRONMENT=production through a Docker --env-file written as ENVIRONMENT="production". --env-file keeps the quotes, so the value is '"production"'. A trailing space or a typo ('prodution') does the same. is_production is then False. The container boots with the public placeholder JWT secret (anyone can mint an ADMIN token) and may run the in-memory telemetry store, all without a warning. Neither compose.yaml nor the Dockerfile sets ENVIRONMENT, so this value comes entirely from operator input.

SUGGESTED APPROACH: make the environment a closed set, the same way task 512 closed the telemetry backend. Use a Literal or Enum of the accepted values (e.g. development / test / production, plus the existing 'prod' alias if it is kept). Settings must refuse any other value at construction, naming the value and the accepted set. Do not strip or normalise silently. Tests: '"production"', 'production ' and 'prodution' are each refused with a message naming them; 'production' with the placeholder secret is still refused, as today; the default (development) still builds. Re-verify line numbers first.

99ca39d1-415b-435e-8196-75badda2918b.content: CONVENTION (task 346, 2026-09-26): tests/test_private_names.py is a repo-wide AST guard — no module under src/, tests/ or migrations/ may reach a leading-underscore name of a src module from outside that module (or, for a package's private names/submodules like runtime.roles._common, outside that package); it sees imports (every private path segment), attribute lookups through import bindings, setattr/getattr/monkeypatch.setattr/patch.object with a private string, and code inside any string constant mentioning `solar_challenge_platform` (subprocess scripts, dotted patch targets). Remedy is to promote the name by a rename with no alias/re-export, or re-seam the test onto public behaviour; a temporary exception goes in `_AWAITING_PROMOTION: dict[PrivateName(module, name), int task_id]` against a real owning task (never the current one), and self-expires — the guard fails, telling you to delete the entry, once the name is no longer reached. GOTCHA: because string constants are read as code, an AST-reader test's case table must spell a stand-in package (e.g. "pkg", as tests/test_entrypoints.py's roles guard does with "pkg.runtime.roles"), never a real `solar_challenge_platform.x._y` path as one string.

candidates.content: Merge lane: an injected VerifyPort does not reach a merge's post-advance gates (task 6160 architect, main 27fb2a0bee, 2026-10-13). `merge_lane/gates.py::_finalize_advanced_merge` has NO verifier parameter, on the single-branch path and the train path alike. Its post-advance gates `gates.py::_run_equivalence_gate` and `::_run_pyright_gate` call gates.py's OWN `_check_post_merge_equivalence` / `_check_post_merge_pyright` directly; there is no longer a function-local import from merge_queue. The single-branch gate re-verify (`_finalize_inflight` -> `_reverify_rebased_tree(run_post_merge_verify=_run_post_merge_verify)`) also drops the verifier; that is task 6344.

Production seam gap found during task 5034: in orchestrator/src/orchestrator/merge_queue.py::_do_train_merge, the calls to _run_post_merge_verify(...) and _finalize_advanced_merge(...) pass no verifier=, so trains always use PRODUCTION_VERIFIER and ignore the worker's injected VerifyPort. A train driven through make_lane(verifier=FakeVerifier(fails(...))) or FakeVerifier(disk_reason=...) still runs the production verifier, which in tests is the conftest autouse run_scoped_verification stub. That makes a vacuously-green train test easy to write. Train tests that need a verify, disk-guard or equivalence outcome must therefore use MergeLane(git_ops, queue) with no verifier= plus module patches, until the gap is fixed. The fix is owned by task 6160 (pending, medium, depends on 5036): thread worker._verifier through both calls and add _verifier to the _TrainMergeHost Protocol.

- gates.py imports run_verification at module level.

In orchestrator/merge_queue.py the disjoint-delta re-verify gate (task 1595: advance_main(reverify_on_rebase=True) + _reverify_rebased_tree) lives ONLY in SpeculativeMergeWorker._verify_and_advance's CAS loop — it was NOT folded into the shared _finalize_advanced_merge. Therefore "route the train through the shared post-merge core for parity" means parity with the MergeWorker reference (equivalence/pyright/push/disk-guard/wip-halt/loop-breaker), NOT the spec-worker disjoint-delta gate.

dark-factory production merge path architecture (as of 2026-06-07): the live worker is SpeculativeMergeWorker (built at harness.py:3238), NOT the deprecated serial MergeWorker. Flow: `_merger_loop` (merge_queue.py:3927) builds the merge worktree via `merge_to_main`→`_create_merge_worktree` (git worktree add --detach at base; git merge --no-ff; scrub .task/) and enqueues a SpeculativeItem; `_verifier_loop` (merge_queue.py:4369) picks it up, applies Mechanism 2 freshness re-base (4440-4489) for real items, then `_verify_and_advance` runs `_run_post_merge_verify` (Step 4, unless skip_verify) and `advance_main(..., reverify_on_rebase=True)` (Step 5). Key sub-pieces: `_remerge` (4580) re-merges branch against freshly-read main; skip_verify is computed as `pre_rebased AND pre_merge_sha == actual_main` (build time 4232; recomputed in _remerge ~4741-4751). #1595 disjoint-delta reverify-on-rebase gate (git_ops.py:1737-1756, _reverify_rebased_tree/_rebase_delta_touched_overlap at merge_queue.py:1273-1475) fires only when advance_main had to rebase because main moved DURING verify. #1602 fail-closed pre-advance unscoped type-check gate is _run_unscoped_typechecks inside _run_post_merge_verify (447-477). The TRAIN path (_do_train_merge, 2742) is EXEMPT from Mechanisms 1&2 but is rebase-before-verify by construction (rebase_onto_main, read main HEAD after rebase, merge, then verify); exemption enforced by `immediate_outcome is None and not GroupMergeRequest` guards at 4441-4443.

Merge-lane functional landscape measured 2026-09-03. Remote verify hosts: the whole mechanism is LANDED in orchestrator/src/orchestrator/verify_runner.py (VerifyRunnerPool, LocalRunner, RemoteRunner with git-push + ssh verify-merge, HostAllocator/HostLease giving at most one in-flight verify per host, runner quarantine plus _reprobe_quarantined_hosts in merge_queue.py from task 3043, DriftDetector for verdict parity, and the INV-1..5 verdict-integrity checks from tasks 2883/2884), but dark-factory's own dark-factory-orchestrator.yaml has ZERO verify_runners entries — only reify's configs (and its fix/recovery clones) enable remote runners, so "better use of remote verify hosts" is mostly policy inside the dispatch decision in _run_post_merge_verify, and it can only be exercised on reify. Speculative merge: deep merge-ahead (plans/deep-merge-ahead-prd.md) is PARTIAL — build_chain, select_chain_depth, _deep_chain_placement, _land_chain_prefix exist, but the chain cap (config merge_deep.chain_cap, default 0 = kill switch) is set in NO project's config, so the mechanism has never run in production, and its Phase 3 telemetry (chain_items digest reader, analyze_speculation_depth script) is not landed; 7 of its 13 tasks are done. GOTCHA (dark-factory merge lane, planning task 6647, read 2026-10-10): to make a rebased merge candidate keep its exact git tree in a test, commit onto main a patch IDENTICAL to one of the branch's commits. git_ops.py::GitOps::advance_main rebases with a plain `git rebase main` on top of the --no-ff merge commit. That linearises, drops the merge commit, and skips any branch commit whose patch-id is already upstream, so `<rebased>^{tree} == <merge_commit>^{tree}`. This is the follower-stacked-on-a-landed-head case. Separately, the single-branch gate re-verify (_finalize_inflight → gates.py::_reverify_rebased_tree → _run_post_merge_verify) runs PRODUCTION_VERIFIER rather than the lane's injected FakeVerifier (task 6344). Lane tests must therefore patch orchestrator.merge_lane.worker.run_scoped_verification to observe or answer that re-verify, and a held FakeVerifier verify needs make_lane(clock=healthy_verify_clock()).

In orchestrator/src/orchestrator/merge_queue.py, the single post-merge "merge gate" verify is _run_post_merge_verify (~line 683, builds build_merge_verify_spec + run_scoped_verification + unscoped type-check). There is exactly ONE post-merge verify path; both MergeWorker._do_merge and SpeculativeMergeWorker._verify_and_advance funnel through it. GroupMergeRequest/train items always set immediate_outcome and return in the verifier loop (~6335) BEFORE reaching _verify_and_advance (they verify inside _do_train_merge), so changes to _verify_and_advance's verify gating never affect trains.

In the dark-factory orchestrator merge queue, the single post-merge verify (build) chokepoint is `_run_post_merge_verify` in merge_queue.py, called from MergeWorker._process (deprecated serial worker), SpeculativeMergeWorker._verify_and_advance (the DEFAULT production worker, line ~5796), the train path `_do_train_merge`, and the reverify-after-rebase helper. `advance_main` only touches the merge worktree for the CAS-rebase fallback (when main moved mid-verify); the common path breaks immediately on the merge SHA without using the worktree.

RECIPE (task 5030, PRD merge-lane-quality γ7): how to drive the merge lane from a test through PUBLIC surfaces only — the technique every γ file migration needs, validated on four files.

SETUP. `MergeLane(git_ops, queue, verifier=FakeVerifier(...), clock=FakeClock(), escalation_queue=...)` + `asyncio.ensure_future(lane.run())`, torn down with `await asyncio.wait_for(lane.stop(), timeout=30)`. GOTCHA THAT SILENTLY BREAKS THE CONFLICT GRAPH: `git_ops.create_worktree(x)` PREFIXES x with `git.branch_prefix` itself. Pass the BARE task id (`create_worktree('t1')` → branch `task/t1`). Passing `'task/t1'` creates `task/task/t1`, the merge still works (it uses the worktree), but `SuffixConflictTracker.recompute()` resolves `req.branch.full_name` via `resolve_branch_sha` → None → the item is silently SKIPPED from `conflicts_with_main`, so any bounce/conflict-graph test quietly tests nothing. Measured: a bounce e2e that looked correct never bounced until the branch name was fixed.

FAULT INJECTION, all public: verify FAIL/RAISE/PARK via `FakeVerifier(scripts={task_id: VerifyScript(result=..., release=asyncio.Event())})` (`_merge_lane_fakes`; `hangs_until` parks, and a subclass overriding `run_scoped` can raise `RunnerUnavailable` once); a FROZEN PREFIX by parking the head's verify (its merge commit becomes `snapshot()['frozen_prefix']['tip_merge_commit']` while main stays behind); a second host via `_inject_two_host_allocator(lane, _gated_runner(...))` from test_merge_queue_concurrent_verify.py; operator faults via the public `operator_halt`/`unhalt_all_lanes`; abandonment via `req.result.cancel()`; a STALE VERIFY BASE by committing on main out of band while a verify is parked (yields real `two_layer_invariants()` violations); CAS-retry paths via `patch.object(git_ops, 'advance_main', ...)` (a git_ops method, not a lane internal, so the ratchet does not count it); heartbeat-timed behaviour (request-liveness escalation) by injecting `FakeClock` — its `sleep` advances time, so `_HEARTBEAT_POLL_S` carries wall-clock past the stuck threshold in a few event-loop turns.

OBSERVATION MAP: `snapshot()` keys `entries` (live-item census — empty == quiesced), `occupancy.inflight_*`, `hosts[*].{slot_state,quarantined}`, `frozen_prefix.{verify_depth,tip_merge_commit}`, `suffix_conflict_graph.conflicts_with_main`, `resource_audit`, `two_layer_invariants`, `owned_merge_worktrees`, `metrics`, `speculation`, plus the public methods `speculation_accounting_violations()` / `worktree_ledger_violations()` / `two_layer_invariants(main_sha)` (all short-circuit to [] once STOPPED — sample while running or the assertion is vacuous).

NO PUBLIC COUNTERPART (delete the assertion or keep it at its own seam): the request-liveness ledger (`_request_ledger.sweep_resolved()/is_empty()`), the ItemLifecycle registry identity, forcing an I4 permit leak, the `_remerge` path, and the post-merge equivalence gate's kwargs (`_run_equivalence_gate` reaches back to `orchestrator.merge_queue._check_post_merge_equivalence` deliberately, so the verify port's `check_post_merge_equivalence` is NEVER called on the finalize path — a FakeVerifier subclass recording it sees nothing).

Gotcha for merge-lane mutation-survivor tests (measured 2026-10-06, task 6414): gates.py::_run_unscoped_typechecks passes run_verification the kwargs role, is_merge_verify and max_retries. Each is observable through the PUBLIC orchestrator.merge_lane.worker.PRODUCTION_VERIFIER.run_unscoped_typechecks, using real commands with no seam:
- role: the type command writes "$DF_VERIFY_ROLE" to a marker file.
- is_merge_verify: set warm=cold=1.0s, merge_verify_cold_command_timeout_secs=60, and use a `sleep 3` command. True passes; False or None times out.
- max_retries: set verify_timeout_retries=2 explicitly and use a hanging command that appends to a counter file. Expect 1 run vs 3.
Separately, the autouse conftest loads dark-factory-orchestrator.yaml, whose verify_cold_preprovision_command (`uv sync … && npm ci`) runs on every merge (cold) verify. Pin verify_cold_preprovision_command='' in such tests' config.

OBSERVATION (2026-06-09): The dark-factory orchestrator's merge-verify pipeline integration points, confirmed by grep while designing multi-host verify. `_run_post_merge_verify` (merge_queue.py ~:364) is the dispatch seam — it calls run_scoped_verification + _run_unscoped_typechecks (~:473/def ~:1555) on the materialized merge tree; this is what a VerifyRunnerPool.dispatch would replace. Speculation depth is capped at 1 by `_speculation_slot` (asyncio.Event, ~:3788) + `_merge_ahead_cap = Semaphore(_MERGE_AHEAD_BOUND)` (~:3795, _MERGE_AHEAD_BOUND=1 ~:103) — the cap exists because there is one CPU, NOT for correctness; raising K means generalizing the Event to a K-permit semaphore. The speculative pipeline already handles build-ahead + chain-invalidation: `_verifier_loop` (~:4613), `_remerge` (~:4855), chain_invalidated/previous_failed re-merge. `check_merge_liveness_margin` (~:5477) + INFLIGHT_MERGE_WORKTREE_LIVENESS_SECS=10800 (~:1847) govern stale-worktree reaping. The `orchestrator` CLI (pyproject [project.scripts] orchestrator = orchestrator.cli:main) is the host for a new `verify-merge` subcommand. There is NO existing VerifyRunner/RemoteRunner/orchestrator-verify — all net-new. The train path also exists: GroupMergeRequest + _maybe_enqueue_group_merge δ₂ (workflow.py ~:547/579/648), _do_train_merge, _train_predecessor stacking (git_ops.py ~:500); the under-verify bug is GroupMergeRequest taking tip-only task_files (workflow.py ~:653-654).

MERGE-LANE TESTS — GATING an injected collaborator subclass, the deterministic way to observe a lane timing window. Extends the task-5031 amendment (7691ba5e, under 66fb4013), which established that a FakeVerifier SUBCLASS overriding a port method beats a monkeypatch and costs the ratchet nothing. Two increments, both measured on task 5461.

INCREMENT 1 — the technique is not limited to Protocol PORTS. `git_ops` is a CONCRETE class (`orchestrator.git_ops.GitOps`) passed as a constructor parameter of `MergeLane`, so a plain subclass overriding a PUBLIC method is the same seam: no `patch`, no `setattr`, no private read. test_merge_queue_metrics.py stayed at its baseline `{"patch_targets": [], "private_reads": 0}` with the subclass in the file (confirmed by `scripts/merge_lane_metrics.py --check` exiting 0). `self._gated_branch` on the subclass is free — the instrument exempts the bare `self` receiver.

INCREMENT 2 — the subclass can GATE, not just observe, and that is what buys DETERMINISM. Override the public method to `self.at_gate.set()` then `await self.release_merge.wait()` for ONE branch, and fall through to `super()` otherwise. This converts a few-awaits-wide internal window into a state the test holds open indefinitely. Concretely: the lane calls `_note_merge_started(req)` (stashing the drift base at the current main_position) immediately before `merge_to_main`, so parking INSIDE `merge_to_main` makes `at_gate` being set PROOF the base was already stashed — the test can then drive an unrelated request all the way to a landing, confirm it on the public counter, and only then release.

WHY IT MATTERS: the obvious alternative (submit both, poll `snapshot()['entries']` for the follower's state, release) was measured at 3 passes in 8 runs, with BOTH failure modes seen — drift 0 when the follower's speculative merge beat the landing, and the follower still `queued` at release time. The gated-merge drive measured 11/11 in probes and 5/5 as committed. Nothing in the public snapshot marks that window stably, so no amount of polling fixes the naive shape.

MANDATORY COMPANION: whatever helper starts the lane must release EVERY gate BEFORE `stop()` (see test_merge_queue_dispatch_fill_redispatch.py::_running_lane), or a failing assertion leaves a verify or a merge parked and hangs teardown instead of reporting. Extend the file's existing lane helper in place with keyword-only params defaulting to today's behaviour rather than adding a second lane-lifecycle helper.

Also note `speculation_depth` must be raised above the default `_MERGE_AHEAD_BOUND` (= 1) for any two-requests-in-flight drive: at depth 1 the lane never dequeues the second request while the first verifies, so its drift base is stashed AFTER the landing and the drift is 0 by construction.

To drive the REAL merge-gate/workflow verify seams in orchestrator tests with NO subprocess/ssh (the 1737/2260/2309 boundary-suite shape): (1) Merge-gate consumer side — call `merge_queue._run_post_merge_verify(..., runner=<MagicMock with .is_local + .run_merge_verify=AsyncMock(return_value=VerifyResult(...))>, escalation_queue=EscalationQueue(tmp))`; vary the canned VerifyResult's category/failing_test_ids/passed to hit μ NEW-ids blame, MAIN_HEALTH_RED, or ν infra-transient. The NEW-ids path is cache-ONLY, so seed `verify.seed_main_baseline(main_sha, {ids})` first. (2) Producer/plan side — call `verify.run_scoped_verification(..., role=, is_merge_verify=)` under `patch.object(verify,'run_verification', _run_verification_spy())` (reuse from test_verify_scope_kappa.py) and inspect `_executed_module_configs()` + `result.plan`. (3) Train — `build_group_merge_request` + `MergeWorker._do_merge` with a counting spy over `orchestrator.merge_queue.run_scoped_verification`; assert exactly one `is_merge_verify=True, role='merge'` call (precedent: test_atomic_train_merge.py::test_group_merge_workspace_verify_green, 3 stacked members). (4) Infra ν — patch `orchestrator.workflow.run_scoped_verification` to return `VerifyResult(passed=False, category='semaphore_timeout')` (∈ INFRA_TRANSIENT_CATEGORIES); assert verify_attempt unchanged + no debugger + `_infra_hold_info` set. Autouse conftest fixtures apply for free: `_clear_probe_cache` resets `verify._PROBE_CACHE`+`_BASELINE_FAILING_IDS_CACHE` per test; `_mock_merge_queue_verification` stubs merge verify to passed=True by default — opt out with the registered `@pytest.mark.exercise_merge_verify` marker to run the real gate.

Since dark-factory commit fa95988c8e (2026-09-23 14:53, 'stop laundering unverified main drift'), merge_gates.py::_reverify_rebased_tree (now orchestrator/merge_lane/gates.py) skips the post-rebase re-verify on disjoint footprints ONLY if _disjoint_skip_blockers is empty: P1 blocks when merge_verify_breadth=='full' (dark_factory sets 'full', so EVERY moved main re-verifies there); P2 blocks when the new main tip is not in the in-process registry of tips the queue itself landed green (note_queue_verified_main_tip has one caller, _finalize_advanced_merge) — so ANY direct commit, timer commit or push to main forces the in-flight solo merge to re-verify in full regardless of file overlap. Kill switch merge_disjoint_skip_requires_verified_drift (green-tier, default True) is unset in both dark_factory and reify. Consequence: task 5293 Workstream C's docs-path exclusion (absorbed from 5064) now only helps scoped-breadth projects when the drift is another queue landing; it was re-scoped 2026-09-29 to re-measure before implementing.

Fact, dark-factory merge lane, measured 2026-08-27/28: post-merge verify duration is dominated by box load, not by change size, and varies by two orders of magnitude. Observed durations for full post-merge verifies: 25s and 164s at low load, then 1580s, 2440s, 2900s, 3208s, 4134s and 4562s while the machine sat at load average 130-430 (the load being driven almost entirely by reify's warm-lanes cargo test fleet under /home/leo/src/warm-lanes, not by dark-factory). Practical consequences: the lane, not review and not the operator's own pre-verification, is the throughput ceiling for any recovery sweep; a task whose verify scope is a single package (e.g. cockpit or scripts only) completes far faster than one that touches shared/ or triggers the __fallback__ whole-tree scope; and a 40-minute verify on an 8-hour fleet-redeploy cadence has a materially non-zero chance of straddling a redeploy, which is how the deploy-clock guard defect (task 4823) gets triggered. Also measured: the merge queue survives an orchestrator restart intact — across two restarts (02:22 and 10:38 UTC, which soft-cancelled 16 and 24 in-flight tasks respectively) every queued entry rehydrated from the durable journal, so a 'Merge worker shutting down' finalization is bookkeeping and not a reason to resubmit.

Merge-gate hole map for dark-factory as of 2026-09-03 (code-read across verify.py, verify_plan.py, merge_queue.py, merge_gates.py, verify_runner.py, git_ops.py, hooks/). Under merge_verify_breadth=full the merge role runs every registered module's full lint, pyright and pytest before landing (9 modules; all 1,188 real test files are covered; nothing is covered by nobody). Ways a broken test still reaches main without any gate executing it: (1) direct commits to main, where hooks/project-checks runs ruff on five packages and conditional pyright but NO pytest; (2) restart-rehydrated merge requests, verified file-scoped (task 5063); (3) genuinely zero-module tasks (plan files only under conftest.py, skills/, hooks/, root config/), which the boundary deliberately does not widen; (4) the disjoint-delta skip on a single-branch rebase (won't-fix, measured harmless); (5) the train path, which re-merges onto a moved main with no overlap check at all (task 5070, latent); (6) chain-prefix landings, where intermediate links land on the tip's verdict only; (7) verify.py::apply_merge_flake_suppression, which converts a red merge verify to PASS when the failing ids pass in isolation; (8) the pytest markers 'integration' and 'warm_lane_bash', deselected from every gating verify and run only on the post-landing offline lane, which files a fix task rather than blocking. Also: the post-advance pyright gate (merge_gates.py::_check_post_merge_pyright) uses the task's OWN module set, not the widened set, and is fail-open on timeout; task-role scope is derived from the architect plan's file list, not the git diff, so a touched-but-undeclared file never enters task-role scope (merge-role full breadth covers it anyway); the main-tip sweep every 1800 s and the review checkpoint are detective, post-landing, not gates.

Task 5777 architect measurement (2026-10-12, main fddcdd083f), for whoever converts conftest's autouse `_mock_merge_queue_verification` (a string patch of orchestrator.merge_queue.run_scoped_verification) into FakeVerifier injection. PROTOTYPE: swapping every def-time `verifier=PRODUCTION_VERIFIER` default (SpeculativeMergeWorker.__init__, _run_post_merge_verify, reverify_member_solo, _spawn_merge_verify_dry_run in merge_lane/worker.py) for one FakeVerifier, unless the test carries exercise_merge_verify, failed 69 of 8960 tests across the 242 lane-importing orchestrator test files (baseline: all 8960 passed). By file: test_merge_queue.py 44, test_train_moved_main.py 10, test_merge_lane_restart_drain.py 4, test_atomic_train_merge.py 3, test_merge_queue_multihost_wiring.py 2, test_coalesce_integration_gate.py 2, plus 1 each in test_verify_scope_inversion_boundary, test_train_integration, test_merge_queue_coalesce and test_merge_verify_mock_autouse. About 26 failures are on the train path. CAUSES: (1) in-body patches of the module's run_scoped_verification stop intercepting once a lane runs on an injected port, and that includes the `_VERIFY_TARGET = 'orchestrator.merge_lane.worker.run_scoped_verification'` constants, which the ratchet's patch_targets measure does not count. Tests whose patch stops intercepting but which still PASS are silently vacuous, so a guard is needed, not just a green run. (2) worker.py::_do_train_merge builds its verify partial without verifier=, so a train always uses PRODUCTION_VERIFIER. That is task 6160's gap, and the injection cannot reach a train until 6160 threads worker._verifier. (3) Real disk-guard/unscoped tests: TestGate01TrainDiskGuard patches shutil.disk_usage, and TestUnscopedTypecheckGate needs the real port legs. DESIGN CONSTRAINT: never rebind PRODUCTION_VERIFIER itself as the autouse seam. Tests read merge_queue.PRODUCTION_VERIFIER at call time as the true production adapter: test_merge_queue_deep_integration_gate.py::_verifier_with_scoped and _make_worker, and test_merge_queue.py::_production_verifier_with. Those two helpers (dataclasses.replace of the production port with only the named leg replaced) are the exact-semantics way to migrate an in-body scoped patch.

dark_factory merge lane, measured 2026-10-03 by the task-5302 architect (read-only: runs.db, git, journal). The 2026-08-12 (mr-763d254b/task 3956) and 2026-08-28 (mr-4ee12a75/task 3122, mr-627b607f) non-empty reads of snapshot()['two_layer_invariants'] were NOT detector false positives. They are a genuine INV-3 gap. Main moves under an in-flight head (e.g. a human direct commit). The head then lands REBASED (rebased_pending_reverify / gate_retry), and that landing branch in merge_lane/worker.py never calls _record_dead_base for the head's pre-rebase merge commit. The successor, built on that orphaned commit at depth 0, passes INV-3's dead-base checks and verifies on a base that never reaches main. Only the post-rebase re-verify gate keeps this sound. 121 such successor merges since July. The 2026-07-08 incident was the different stale-_last_known_main_sha class that task 2357 fixed. Follow-up ticket tkt_0RVCCP8KXSASX0M2M5RSBSCVWW; related open tasks 5923 and 6232.

dark_factory merge lane, measured 2026-10-13 at main 66cd6cf7fc by the task-5064 architect. The two callers of gates.py::_reverify_rebased_tree thread verify handles differently.
- worker.py::_advance_train (train) injects train_verify, a wrapper over a functools.partial(_run_post_merge_verify, event_store, escalation_queue, task_client) built in _do_train_merge. Train gate re-verifies therefore already emit merge_verify rows.
- SpeculativeMergeWorker._finalize_inflight (single-branch) injects bare _run_post_merge_verify. Its gate re-verify runs with no event_store (no merge_verify row), no task_client (no flake_debt row), no escalation_queue, and the PRODUCTION verifier even on a lane built with an injected FakeVerifier.
So a lane test reaching the single-branch gate is served by conftest's autouse stub of orchestrator.merge_queue.run_scoped_verification, not by the lane's fake.

6acf83a2-faaa-4c5d-9b58-912e3db32a36.content:
MERGE-LANE VERIFYPORT: WHICH CALLS AN INJECTED VERIFIER ACTUALLY INTERCEPTS (measured on task 5032, branch task/5032, 2026-09-12).

`VerifyPort` (orchestrator/src/orchestrator/merge_lane/ports.py) declares SEVEN methods, but injecting a fake verifier into `MergeLane`/`SpeculativeMergeWorker` does NOT intercept all seven on the post-merge path. Measured truth:

INTERCEPTED. `run_scoped` and `run_unscoped_typechecks`. The lane threads `verifier=self._verifier` into `_run_post_merge_verify` (merge_queue.py, the `verify_task = asyncio.ensure_future(_run_post_merge_verify(...))` call site), which builds `LocalRunner(run_scoped=verifier.run_scoped, run_unscoped=verifier.run_unscoped_typechecks)`. So an injected `FakeVerifier` supplies the scoped verify AND the PRE-advance fail-closed unscoped type-check gate.

NOT INTERCEPTED. `check_post_merge_pyright`, despite the port method existing. The post-ADVANCE gate is `merge_gates._run_pyright_gate`, which does a function-local `from orchestrator.merge_queue import _check_post_merge_pyright` and calls the MODULE function; its `_PostAdvanceContext` dataclass carries no verifier field at all. Grepping confirms nothing in orchestrator/src calls `verifier.check_post_merge_pyright` — the port method is declared and wired into PRODUCTION_VERIFIER but has no consumer. Same shape for `check_post_merge_equivalence` via `_run_equivalence_gate`.

CONSEQUENCE FOR TESTS. A test that needs the post-advance pyright gate to report broken cannot script it through the port; it must either patch the dotted path (what the γ ratchet is retiring) or produce the real condition — give the module a real `type_check_command` that exits non-zero on the landed tree.

ALSO NOT INTERCEPTED, and a distinct trap: `orchestrator/tests/_serial_merge_worker.py::MergeWorker` (the serial test-helper worker) has no `verifier` constructor parameter and calls `_run_post_merge_verify` without one, so it always gets `PRODUCTION_VERIFIER`. Both of ITS gates run the real command. `_serial_merge_worker.py` is in the merge-lane ratchet's CLUSTER_PATHS, so adding a parameter to it trips the `files` line check.

candidates.content: PTODO FINGERPRINT RATCHET — A WELL-FORMED LIVE CITE NEEDS NO BASELINE LINE. Measured 2026-09-01, correcting a natural misreading of CLAUDE.md's "reds on any live fingerprint absent from crates/reify-audit/ptodo-baseline.txt". The baseline holds only VIOLATIONS: all 5 entries at the time were `#[allow(dead_code)]` patterns classified untracked / orphaned / malformed-cite. A properly-formed `TODO(#NNNN)` citing a PENDING (live, non-terminal) task produces NO finding at all, hence no fingerprint and no baseline entry. Verified three ways: (1) tests/infra/test_reify_audit_ptodo.sh passed 22/0 both before and after adding such a TODO to crates/reify-core/src/units.rs; (2) `reify-audit --pattern PTODO` reported nothing on that file afterwards; (3) the suite's own scenario `(d-control) pending-task cite -> live cite -> reify-audit exits 0` pins exactly this, alongside `(d-orphan) orphaned cite (#4444) -> done-task -> exits 1`. So adding a compliant TODO is a one-line source change, NOT a source+baseline change. A baseline line is needed only when the marker is itself a violation (untracked, orphaned, or malformed-cite). Retiring an existing baselined site DOES require removing its baseline line in the same commit. Also useful: `reify-audit --pattern PTODO` emits many Medium `task-cites-renamed-path` / `task-cites-deleted-path` findings that are about TASK METADATA citing moved files, not about source markers — do not confuse them with the source-side fingerprints the ratchet compares.

The reify PTODO fingerprint ratchet (tests/infra/test_reify_audit_ptodo.sh vs crates/reify-audit/ptodo-baseline.txt) is a FINDINGS baseline, not an all-markers baseline: adding a compliant `// TODO(#NNNN): ...` that cites a LIVE non-terminal task produces no fingerprint and needs no baseline edit. Evidence (2026-09-03): the baseline holds 5 entries, all violation kinds (untracked/orphaned/malformed-cite), while main's crates/reify-eval/tests/joint_drive_expansion_boundary.rs:1680 carries a compliant `tracked separately (#5835)` cite that is absent from the baseline on a green main. The converse trap is real and has bitten twice: task #5017 took two merge-verify REDs on this exact file for phantom-tracking PROSE ("tracked separately", "tracked as a follow-up (ticket tkt_...)") with no `#NNNN` — a `tkt_...` ticket id does NOT satisfy the grammar. Always verify the cited task's status is non-terminal via get_task before writing the cite; a done/cancelled cite classifies as orphaned and reds the gate.

Reify PTODO §6.6 ratchet: scenario (a) of tests/infra/test_reify_audit_ptodo.sh runs ptodo-baseline-gen under `env -u REIFY_PTODO_TASKS_DB` (DB-ABSENT), so the β liveness lane is OFF and `orphaned` findings never enter the live set — the oracle is only `comm -23 <live> <baseline>` (subset-of), with no byte-identity or entry-count assertion anywhere (crates/reify-audit/tests/ptodo_baseline.rs asserts existence + grammar only). Consequence: the committed ptodo-baseline.txt's `orphaned` entries are INERT for the merge gate, and a DB-PRESENT regeneration drifts upward over time as cited tasks close. Blindly running `ptodo-baseline-gen` WITH the tasks DB and committing its stdout therefore silently GROWS the baseline with unrelated liveness-drift entries, weakening the ratchet — measured 2026-09-11: main @7259a3b453 committed 10 entries while a DB-present regeneration emitted 11, of which 5 (builtin_signatures #5662, detectors #5062, node_traits_boundary #5065, ri_literal #6466, temp_dirs #5639) were pure liveness drift absent from the committed file. Burn down the baseline by DELETING the specific fingerprints your source fix resolved (the shrink-only flow the ptodo_baseline.rs NOTE at ~:213 endorses), and use a DB-present run only as a PREVIEW/diff.

The PTODO ratchet baseline `crates/reify-audit/ptodo-baseline.txt` is intentionally ≈EMPTY and only ever holds STRUCTURAL findings (untracked / malformed-cite / phantom-tracking / bare-ignore). A canonical `TODO(#NNNN)` marker classifies as `Cited` and routes to the liveness lane — it produces NO structural fingerprint and therefore can NEVER belong in the baseline. This refutes a recurring misdiagnosis seen twice in reify task 5566's `dry_run_proposals` (2026-07-28), which claimed a ratchet regression was caused by task #5652 adding `TODO(#5662)` and `TODO(#4727)` markers "without regenerating the baseline", and recommended regenerating it. That remediation would have been wrong — those cited markers were never baseline candidates. The actual regression was an UNCITED prose phrase in the failing branch's own diff. RULE OF THUMB when triaging a PTODO ratchet regression: the offending fingerprint is printed verbatim in the failure output as `<path> :: <kind> :: <line text>` — read that line, and if the kind is phantom-tracking/untracked/malformed-cite, the fix belongs in that file, not in the baseline. Never add a fingerprint to the baseline to silence the gate; that defeats the ratchet.

crates/reify-audit/ptodo-baseline.txt (the PTODO fingerprint-ratchet baseline) only ever contains VIOLATION fingerprints — kind ∈ {untracked, orphaned, malformed-cite, bare-ignore} etc. A well-formed marker like `TODO(#NNNN): ...` that cites a genuinely live, non-terminal task produces NO finding at all (per docs/prds/reify-audit-ptodo-detector.md §8.1-8.3), so adding one to tracked source needs no baseline edit. Only a malformed or orphaned citation would need (and should get) a baseline entry, and that file lives in crates/reify-audit/ — outside most tasks' scope, so don't touch it just because you added a correctly-cited TODO.

A reify task worktree (warm lane) has NO .taskmaster/tasks/tasks.db, so reify-audit's PTODO beta liveness lane silently DEGRADES there and emits none of the cite-anchored `orphaned` fingerprints. To re-measure the §6.6 ratchet with liveness ON from a lane, run `REIFY_PTODO_TASKS_DB=/home/leo/src/reify/.taskmaster/tasks/tasks.db ./target/release/ptodo-baseline-gen --project-root .` and diff against crates/reify-audit/ptodo-baseline.txt with `comm -23`. Regenerating that shrink-only baseline DB-ABSENT silently under-seeds it, which matters because §6.6 makes baseline contents permanent by design.

PTODO gotcha for any task whose own id is cited in tracked source: a `#NNNN` cite to a LIVE (non-terminal) task produces no finding, so it has no entry in `crates/reify-audit/ptodo-baseline.txt`. The moment that task goes `done`, every surviving cite to it reclassifies to `orphaned` — a live fingerprint absent from the baseline — and `tests/infra/test_reify_audit_ptodo.sh`'s severity-blind ratchet reds. Scenario (g) (lane δ-B, #6103) also hard-gates ORDINARY comments that defer work and cite a terminal task, not just `TODO(...)` / `todo!()` forms. So a task that lands a `TODO(#self)` breadcrumb must delete EVERY cite to itself (including plain prose mentions) before merging; adding baseline entries instead papers over a violation. Check with `grep -rn '<task-id>' crates/ scripts/ tests/` returning nothing.

reify: in a warm lane, `REIFY_AUDIT_NO_COLD_BUILD=1 bash tests/infra/test_reify_audit_ptodo.sh` SKIPs its fingerprint-ratchet scenarios (the seeded target/release/ptodo-baseline-gen has stamped mtimes, so the freshness guard calls it stale) while still exiting 0. To actually check that a new TODO adds no fingerprint without a release rebuild, run `REIFY_PTODO_TASKS_DB=/dev/null/tasks.db ./target/release/ptodo-baseline-gen --project-root "$PWD"` and diff its sorted output against the data rows of crates/reify-audit/ptodo-baseline.txt (the baseline had 0 rows on 2026-10-02). A canonical `TODO(#NNNN)` emits no fingerprint.

Reify fact (jun22/23): the PTODO ratchet baseline crates/reify-audit/ptodo-baseline.txt is EMPTY (zero accepted violations), so ANY orphaned/untracked/bare-ignore cite makes live ⊄ baseline → test_reify_audit_ptodo.sh RED. Only PTODO-grammar forms are flagged as cites: #[ignore="...#NNNN"], TODO(#NNNN), FIXME(#NNNN), HACK(#NNNN), todo!(...#NNNN), unimplemented!(). Prose mentions like `// Task 4628:` or `(task 4628, done)` in doc comments are NOT flagged (verified: reify-audit reported exactly the 2 marker-cites, ignoring ~8 prose `#4628` mentions in the same/other files). To confirm a PTODO fix locally: apply the edit to the MAIN checkout working tree (reify-audit needs data/orchestrator/runs.db + correct fused-memory project key, both only present in the main checkout — not in a linked worktree), run ./target/release/reify-audit --pattern PTODO (expect `0 findings`, exit 0), then `git checkout` to revert. reify-audit reads working-tree file contents (uncommitted edits ARE seen).

PTODO fingerprint-ratchet trap when retiring a TODO: the enforced merge gate (tests/infra/test_reify_audit_ptodo.sh) is severity-blind and reds on any live fingerprint (`path :: kind :: text`) ABSENT from crates/reify-audit/ptodo-baseline.txt. So REMOVING a TODO cite is always safe (it only drops a fingerprint), but REWRITING one — e.g. retargeting `TODO(#5385)` to `TODO(#6460)` when the first task lands — mints a NEW unbaselined fingerprint and reds the gate. When a landing task must retire a cite, delete the cite outright and keep any follow-up task reference as plain prose. Note the baseline currently contains only crates/**/*.rs entries (zero `examples/` entries).

CORRECTION to the canonical PTODO phantom-tracking entry (Mem0 35e0187a, topic `ptodo-phantom-tracking-phrases`): `crates/reify-audit/ptodo-baseline.txt` is NO LONGER committed empty. As of 2026-08-26 it carries 5 accepted-violation fingerprints (3 in crates/reify-eval/src/engine_build.rs — one `malformed-cite` for "task 4050", one `orphaned` for a done #4744, one `untracked` T12-layer-B; one `untracked` in crates/reify-eval/src/significance_filter.rs; one `untracked` in crates/reify-stdlib/src/joints.rs). So 35e0187a's debugging advice that "main emits 0 — any single live fingerprint is the whole 1-vs-0 delta against the ratchet" is STALE and will mislead: a clean main now emits 5, and the ratchet asserts live-fingerprints-are-a-SUBSET-of-baseline, not zero. Diff your live fingerprints against the committed baseline rather than expecting 0. The baseline holds VIOLATIONS ONLY, so a well-formed `TODO(#NNNN)` citing a live task adds no baseline entry and needs no baseline edit — do not "register" a correct marker there. Verified 2026-08-26 on task 5843's branch: `bash tests/infra/test_reify_audit_ptodo.sh` → 22 passed / 0 failed, incl. "live fingerprints are a subset of committed baseline". Also note `cargo run -p reify-audit -- --pattern PTODO` fails in a warm lane with "error opening runs-db 'data/orchestrator/runs.db'" (relative path absent in a lane) and needs `--bin reify-audit` (the crate ships two binaries); running the infra script is the simpler path.

PTODO ratchet gotcha: `target/release/ptodo-baseline-gen` run WITHOUT `REIFY_PTODO_TASKS_DB` degrades its liveness lane to structural-only, so it emits a strict SUBSET of the real fingerprint set — `orphaned` / `unknown-id` kinds are simply not classified and silently vanish from the output. Never regenerate `crates/reify-audit/ptodo-baseline.txt` wholesale from a DB-less run: that drops live orphaned grandfather entries and hands future findings free immunity. For a targeted burndown, delete only the one line you resolved, and only if its kind is structural (`untracked` / `malformed-cite` / `bare-ignore` / `phantom-tracking`), whose absence from a DB-less live set IS conclusive. Point it at the real DB with `REIFY_PTODO_TASKS_DB=/home/leo/src/reify/.taskmaster/tasks/tasks.db` when you need the liveness lane.

Reify's crates/reify-audit/ptodo-baseline.txt is structural-only by construction since task #7001 (commit 3910accacf): its validator accepts only ptodo.rs STRUCTURAL_KINDS, and the committed file was emptied (0 lines as of 2026-10-11). So no DB-dependent finding (orphaned, or a stale prose promise citing a done/cancelled task) can ever be seeded there. A task brief saying "drop the site's fingerprint line from ptodo-baseline.txt in the same commit" for such a finding is moot: check `wc -l` first and leave the baseline untouched.

The PTODO fingerprint ratchet (tests/infra/test_reify_audit_ptodo.sh) blocks a merge on ORDINARY PROSE, not just TODO markers. reify task 7244's first merge attempt (mr-63d1c582) was blocked in post-merge verify by one live fingerprint absent from crates/reify-audit/ptodo-baseline.txt:

  scripts/task-branch-contamination-sweep.sh :: phantom-tracking :: # TASK_MODE is tracked separately from TASK_ID because ...

Cause: `PHANTOM_PHRASES` in crates/reify-audit/src/ptodo.rs is a case-insensitive SUBSTRING list — "tracked separately", "tracked as a follow-up", "tracked in project memory", "follow-up task will". The comment was explaining why a mode flag is a separate shell variable; it mentioned no TODO at all. The line carried no TODO/FIXME/HACK token.

Fix applied: reword the comment. The `# ptodo:allow — reason` escape exists but was the wrong tool here, because the line was never making a tracked-elsewhere claim.

PTODO ratchet drift RULING 2026-09-26 (Leo, esc-5714-9; normative home PRD docs/prds/reify-audit-ptodo-detector.md §19, landed via task 7952): (1) the §6.6 per-merge ratchet is structural-only, EXPLICITLY DB-absent (unsetting REIFY_PTODO_TASKS_DB is NOT DB-absent on the main checkout — the default path resolves there, which had the hook-gated commit ratchet running DB-present and red on orphaned-cite drift), mode-invariant and TWO-directional (comm -13 added) over a structural-only baseline; §18 re-opened and adopted on new grounds; owner reify #7001 (revived). reify PTODO ratchet: `tests/infra/test_reify_audit_ptodo.sh`'s scenario (a) runs `env -u REIFY_PTODO_TASKS_DB ptodo-baseline-gen --project-root "$REPO_ROOT"`, whose comment claims "degraded-structural mode (no task DB)". That is only true in a TASK WORKTREE — `env -u` unsets solely the env override, and the `<project_root>/.taskmaster/tasks/tasks.db` fallback still resolves in the MAIN checkout. So a cite-anchored PTODO lane (one emitting only `LineClass::Cited`, e.g. δ-B) contributes ZERO fingerprints during worktree verify and the ratchet passes while asserting nothing about it, then goes RED under `scripts/land.sh`'s `pre-merge-commit` gate on main. Always regenerate `ptodo-baseline.txt` with the DB present (PRD §6.6) and diff `comm -23` in BOTH modes before landing such a lane.

PTODO ratchet failure mode (root-caused jun18 on task 4577): `crates/reify-audit/ptodo-baseline.txt` is intentionally EMPTY (0 bytes, git-tracked), so the degraded-structural ratchet in tests/infra/test_reify_audit_ptodo.sh part (a) requires the live structural finding set to ALSO be empty — every TODO/FIXME/HACK marker in tracked source must be either canonically `#NNNN`-cited on the same line or escaped with a trailing `// ptodo:allow`. The line-based detector (ptodo.rs scan_file, regex `\b(TODO|FIXME|HACK)\b\s*[(:]`) classifies a marker line with no canonical cite as MalformedCite (if it has a legacy "task NNNN"/Greek/PRD-relative form) or Untracked, and the ratchet checks fingerprint-subset against the empty baseline REGARDLESS of severity (so even a Medium MalformedCite breaks the merge gate). Common trap: prose comments that REPRODUCE a literal `TODO(...)` token — a "See TODO(...) below" cross-reference or a "Resolved: TODO(...)" note — that line-wrap so the `#NNNN` falls onto the next line. FIX: reword the prose to drop the swept `TODO(` token (cleaner than `// ptodo:allow`, which is meant for lines that genuinely need the literal token). Verify locally by building the ptodo-baseline-gen binary (debug is fine) and running it in degraded-structural mode (`env -u REIFY_PTODO_TASKS_DB ptodo-baseline-gen --project-root <root>`) — output must be empty. Do NOT regenerate the baseline; it stays empty by design.

Reify PTODO ratchet scope: adding a `// TODO(#NNNN)` comment to a file under `crates/*/tests/` does NOT require a `crates/reify-audit/ptodo-baseline.txt` entry — verified 2026-08-31 by adding `// TODO(#5835)` to `crates/reify-eval/tests/joint_drive_expansion_boundary.rs` with no baseline change and seeing `tests/infra/test_reify_audit_ptodo.sh` pass 22/22, with arm "(a) Ratchet: live fingerprints subset of committed baseline" explicitly PASSing (not skipped). The committed baseline holds only 5 entries, all `#[allow(dead_code)]`-kind deferral rationales under `crates/*/src/`, and zero `crates/*/tests/` entries. CLAUDE.md's phrasing ("reds on any live fingerprint, *any* kind") reads as broader than the ratchet's actual live-fingerprint set, so do not assume a plain TODO comment needs a baseline bump. IMPORTANT when checking this: that ratchet arm SKIPS silently when `target/release/ptodo-baseline-gen` is stale (see the `RATCHET_SKIP=1` / freshness-guard path around line 421 of the infra test), and the suite still reports overall PASS — so grep the output for the "(a) Ratchet" PASS line rather than trusting the summary count.

REIFY PTODO BASELINE IS "SHRINK-ONLY" BY CONVENTION ONLY — the implemented oracle is SUBSET-OF, so every grandfathered fingerprint is a PERMANENT RE-ENTRY PERMIT. (Found 2026-08-27; filed as task #6859.)

PRD docs/prds/reify-audit-ptodo-detector.md §6.6 calls the baseline "shrink-only (ratchet-above-baseline oracle pattern, Leo-ratified jun11 on 4521)" and says "After δ the baseline should be ≈ empty". The actual assertion is `comm -23 <live> <baseline>` (tests/infra/test_reify_audit_ptodo.sh:595) — it asserts live ⊆ baseline and NOTHING ELSE. Nothing asserts the baseline shrinks; nothing asserts a baseline entry is still live.

Two consequences:
1. NO DRAIN FORCING FUNCTION. The 5 fingerprints seeded by #6087 can persist indefinitely. "≈ empty" is aspiration enforced by nothing.
2. RE-ENTRY IS FREE. Because fingerprints are line-number-erased (`{path}::{kind}::{text}`), you can delete an offending line and someone can re-add that EXACT comment text later, ANYWHERE in the same file, and the ratchet stays green. Therefore any burn-down MUST shrink ptodo-baseline.txt in the same diff, or it leaves the permit behind.

CONSTRAINTS ON ANY FIX (these are why it is a design task, not a one-liner):
(a) §6.7 DB-DEGRADATION ASYMMETRY — load-bearing. The committed baseline is generated WITH the task DB and is DELIBERATELY a superset of the degraded (no-DB) live set, because a Cited line yields an `orphaned` fingerprint when the DB is reachable and none when it degrades. Ratchet scenario (a) runs under `env -u REIFY_PTODO_TASKS_DB` (degraded) precisely so the subset oracle stays empty in both the main checkout and a task worktree. A naive set-equality assertion would RED in every no-DB context.
(b) MUST NOT REINTRODUCE THE #6127 FALSE-RED. §6.6 records that a burn-down commit leaving a non-empty baseline against a legitimately empty live set "would hard-RED". The self-disarm that existed for this was RETIRED by #6241, which also removed ALL detector-kind knowledge from bash ("derivation lives only in the generator"). A fix must not drag a kind list back into the shell.
(c) A weaker form may be right: assert liveness only for DB-INDEPENDENT structural kinds (untracked / malformed-cite / bare-ignore), leaving DB-dependent kinds subset-only — but note that reintroduces a kind list, weigh against (b).

A task that cites its OWN id in tracked source (`// TODO(#NNNN): …`) must DELETE that cite as its final step, because the cite is valid only while the task is non-terminal — the moment the task flips to done it becomes an `orphaned` finding, and since the enforced gate is the severity-blind fingerprint ratchet in `tests/infra/test_reify_audit_ptodo.sh` (fingerprint = `path :: kind :: text`, checked against `crates/reify-audit/ptodo-baseline.txt`), it reds ON MAIN *after* the merge, where nothing in the task's own verify run would have caught it. Delete rather than retarget at a successor task: a rewritten cite mints a new fingerprint equally absent from the baseline and reds identically. Scope check before assuming safety: `.ri`/`.sh`/`.py`/`.ts`/`.tsx`/`.js` are swept alongside `.rs` (`is_swept_ext`, crates/reify-audit/src/ptodo.rs), `.md`/`.toml`/`.yaml` are not, and ALLOWLIST_PREFIXES holds only three entries, all under `crates/` — so `examples/*.ri` is swept and unexempt. Prose mentions like `// (task #NNNN)` are NOT markers and never mint a fingerprint; only TODO/FIXME/HACK comments, `todo!()`/`unimplemented!()` stubs and `#[ignore]` reasons are scanned.

A well-formed `TODO(#NNNN)` cite therefore produces NO fingerprint. Adding, repointing or deleting a cite needs NO baseline row, and adding one would red the converse stale-baseline oracle. 35e0187a-2a81-436f-892f-0fa980fc70eb.content:
GOTCHA — reify-audit's PTODO ratchet (test_reify_audit_ptodo.sh) has a "phantom-tracking" heuristic (crates/reify-audit/src/ptodo.rs §8.3, PHANTOM_PHRASES ~line 1719) that flags ANY source line — including plain `///` doc comments, not just TODO/FIXME/HACK markers — containing one of four phantom phrases ("tracked separately", "tracked as a follow-up", "tracked in project memory", "follow-up task will") with no canonical `#NNNN` cite on that SAME line, as a Medium-severity structural finding. The check fires per-LINE, independent of the TODO/FIXME/HACK marker regex and with NO above-line lookback: in a multi-line `//` comment block, a properly-cited `TODO(#NNNN)` on one line does NOT protect a later line in the same block that happens to contain a phantom phrase without its own same-line cite. Because crates/reify-audit/ptodo-baseline.txt is committed empty (zero-residual-state policy), ANY new PTODO-pattern fingerprint fails the ratchet and blocks merge.

Confirmed trigger in the wild: a doc comment using "Tracked separately from `other_field`" (added by task 4636 in engine_build.rs) tripped this heuristic on an otherwise unrelated code comment.

FIX POLICY — RATIFIED 2026-08-20 (curator gate 5821). Choose by whether a real follow-up actually exists:
1. A REAL, live, non-terminal follow-up exists → CITE IT: `#NNNN` on the same line. This is the primary fix. It is also what the project's hard convention requires for every TODO/FIXME/HACK marker, todo!()/unimplemented!() stub, and blocker #[ignore] (CLAUDE.md "TODO citation convention"; grammar in docs/prds/reify-audit-ptodo-detector.md §8). Rewording away a genuine pointer destroys information and is the wrong fix here.
2. NO real follow-up exists — the phrase is incidental prose and no citation would be meaningful → REWORD (comment-only, no logic change): "Distinct from X" / "Not the same set as X" instead of "Tracked separately from X".
3. A cite you added later goes terminal (done/cancelled) → it becomes an `orphaned` High-severity finding. Re-point it at a live task, or, if no follow-up remains, reword per (2). Cited != tracked.
Escape hatch for a legitimate pattern string that is neither: append `// ptodo:allow — reason`.

To debug/find the exact offending fingerprint: run `env -u REIFY_PTODO_TASKS_DB target/release/ptodo-baseline-gen --project-root $PWD` and inspect the `path :: kind :: text` output.

[CURATOR CORRECTION 2026-08-20, gate 5821.] This entry previously carried a BLANKET "Do NOT fix by adding a `#NNNN` cite ... that opts the line into the β liveness resolution lane and can itself become an `orphaned` High-severity finding instead." That was read fleet-wide as "never cite", which conflicts with the project's own hard gate and with the lesson drawn from /unblock of task 5566 (Graphiti decisions_and_rationale episode 16e38e28-819d-4293-8656-ba5c1f5e81bd, 2026-07-29: cite a real live task instead of rewording, because "rewording destroys a real pointer"). The two were never truly contradictory — this entry's clause was about a NON-MARKER doc comment where no citation would apply, while 16e38e28 is about a line with a genuine follow-up — but the unscoped wording made them read as opposed. The orphaning risk is real and is now handled as case (3) above rather than as a reason to avoid citing. Mem0 0431790f-4e4e-4a8a-b0dd-f78656819384 (with 85c1120b-6e81-4bc9-890c-521d07ed25cf), which already listed citing a live non-terminal task among three legitimate fixes, is consistent with this ratified policy.

(Consolidation, 2026-07-17, Stage 1 run a0318deb-afac-4667-86fb-f33427061f84: merges 3 rediscoveries of the same PHANTOM_PHRASES/phantom-tracking gotcha: b68c69b4, c734b74b, 0daf5014. This is the SOLE canonical entry for this topic — if about to write a new memory documenting the PTODO "tracked separately"/phantom-tracking phrase gotcha, append to this entry or write a stamped peer under topic `ptodo-phantom-tracking-phrases`; do not write a new unstamped entry.)

Draft (store.py:35-46) and Released (store.py:49-53) now derive from Frozen directly and embed Analysis, so the defect stands as described.

- Intake.prospect_view (intake.py:64-72) reads the draft and the release on every prospect page load. The /criteria and /report routes go through it too (prospect_pages.py:80-84, 102-109).

- error_pages.session_error_page (error_pages.py:11-30) has no case for ValidationError, so web._dispatch (web.py:92-104) answers 500 "Something went wrong". Any Analysis change or tightened validator therefore turns an existing session's chat page into a 500, and its operator page likewise.
- purge_unused/_last_used (intake.py:228-248) read the release for its time and leave a session whose release cannot be read in place, reporting it. tests/test_session_flow.py:347-363 pins that. A naive versioning would make every session released before a schema change "unreadable" to the purge, so no such session would ever be deleted: the 90-day promise would break.
- Deletion never reads the draft. The prospect route goes intake.delete -> _locked -> store.get (session.json only) -> shutil.rmtree. POLICY CHOSEN: an operator-facing state, not a migration table (see design decisions).
- store.RECORD_FORMAT = 1 is the record format this version writes drafts and releases in, and the only one it reads.
- Draft and Released derive from a small base, StoredWriteUp(Frozen), holding record_format: int = RECORD_FORMAT and analysis: Analysis. The format is therefore written on save by the record's own serialisation.
- On read, the store first reads only the declared format: a Frozen model _DeclaredFormat(record_format: int = 1), validated with pydantic 2.13.5's per-call model_validate_json(..., extra="ignore"). A record from before formats were numbered declares none and is format 1, so Leo's existing trial sessions keep working.
- Only a record declaring RECORD_FORMAT is validated in full. Every other outcome is returned, never raised, as UnreadableWriteUp(record_format=<declared> | None): another format, unparseable bytes, or a current-format record that fails the record's rules.
- draft() and released() return Draft/Released | UnreadableWriteUp | None.
- A new SessionStore.released_at(token) reads only released_at (a Frozen _ReleaseTime, again extra="ignore" per call) from a release in any format. A damaged release still raises there, so the purge keeps counting a release made in an older format and keeps leaving a damaged one in place.

(1) build_reviewer_prompt cuts the task diff at 50,000 characters. workflow._review diffs `git diff <base_commit>...HEAD`, so if a merge of main leaves base_commit at an old fork point, the cut keeps main's alphabetically first files (.gitignore, CLAUDE.md, README.md, docs/...) and none of the task's own. That makes a rebase-style integration step mandatory, not just tidier.
(2) Rebasing a branch that earlier integrated main by merge drops its merge commits. Map the plan steps that recorded them to the replayed commit carrying their effect.
(3) If the branch holds a doc-only commit that a later commit reverts, and the doc has since been rewritten on main, `git rebase --skip` the doc commit and resolve its revert's doc hunk to main's copy.
(4) `git rebase --continue` opens an editor unless GIT_EDITOR=true. Pass `-c rerere.enabled=false` so no recorded resolution applies.

candidates.content: In fused-memory/src/fused_memory/reconciliation/harness.py, structured observability events use a message-is-token convention: the log MESSAGE is a dotted token like `reconciliation.iteration_timed_out` / `reconciliation.full_cycle_timed_out` / `reconciliation.drain_ack`, and identifying fields (e.g. project_id) go in `extra={...}` so consumers read `record.project_id` rather than scraping prose (harness.py ~1727-1736). Follow this shape when adding any new recon-loop event token.

pytest caplog gotcha (hit on task 3515, fused-memory tests): `caplog.records[i].message` is ALREADY the interpolated message — caplog's handler calls `record.getMessage()` and assigns the result to `.message` before the record is stored. So the natural-looking `rec.message % rec.args` double-formats and raises `TypeError: not all arguments converted during string formatting` whenever the logger was called with lazy `%s` args. When a test needs the interpolated text (e.g. to regex out the `--flag` tokens a WARNING actually emits), use `rec.getMessage()`; plain `rec.message` also works and is what the rest of fused-memory's tests use. `rec.msg` is the raw un-interpolated format string, which is what you want only if you are asserting on the template itself.

Convention in fused-memory/tests/test_memory_service.py: when a test asserts on a logging.WARNING record's `extra` fields, prefer structural assertions (e.g. record.missing_cycle_summary_keys, record.run_id, record.stage) over asserting substrings of the free-text record.message — message prose is cosmetic and can churn independently of behavior, while the extra fields are the real, stable contract.

Reconciliation helper functions that perform Mem0 search/write should accept an optional `log: logging.Logger | None = None` parameter and use the caller's logger (passed by name) when logging WARNINGs. This preserves test caplog scopes that filter by caller logger (e.g., `caplog.at_level(level, logger='fused_memory.reconciliation.flag_dedup')`) and keeps log aggregation aligned with the caller's namespace rather than the helper module.

Log forensics for fused-memory incidents (2026-09-16).
- **Retention.** /var/log/syslog keeps fused-memory lines back to ~08-16 across syslog, syslog.1 (plain, ~4 GB) and syslog.2–4.gz. The line prefix is ISO local time +01:00 (BST); app lines carry `uv[<pid>]:`.
- **Minute windows.** `LC_ALL=C grep -a '^2026-09-14T16:07:'` on the current file returns in ~0.5 s.
- **Full census.** `zcat f | LC_ALL=C grep -a -B80 -A3 'database is locked'` across all rotations ran in ~2 minutes as a setsid nohup job.
- **journalctl.** `journalctl --user -u fused-memory` must be bounded with `--since/--until` a few minutes apart, or it hangs.
- **Timing.** Microsecond prefixes bound lock-error latency. Measure from the preceding event (agent exit, stage_completed) to the ERROR line: under 5 s means an immediate SQLITE_BUSY from a pinned read, not busy_timeout expiry.
- **Noise.** Heavy noise to filter: event_buffered, schema_warning, HTTP Request, POST /mcp, Terminating session, Processing request, GET /alive.

Syslog forensics recipe that worked 2026-09-16: `journalctl --user -u fused-memory` times out, but a single `grep -a -F -f patterns.txt` pass over /var/log/syslog (1.7 GB) + syslog.1 (4 GB) plus `zcat syslog.{2,3}.gz | grep -a -F -f` (~330-380 MB compressed each) finished in ~3 minutes when run detached as `setsid nohup script.sh > log 2>&1 &` with a progress file to poll — no need to bound with --since. Syslog rotates weekly at 00:00 (syslog.1 covers the previous week; .2.gz/.3.gz the two before), so a 3-week window needs all four files. Syslog timestamps are +01:00; the reconciliation journal is UTC. Run ids appear in syslog only in the cli_invoke "Command:" line (as claude-config-<run_id>), in "Recovering stale run <id>" and in "Reconciliation run <id> INTERRUPTED (resumable)" lines; structured `extra=` fields (run_id on reconciliation.remediation_started etc.) are NOT rendered by the log formatter, so those events cannot be keyed by run id from syslog. The uv[<pid>] prefix identifies the fused-memory process incarnation; "EventBuffer initialized (instance=<uuid>)" marks a new instance id.

CORRECTION (2026-08-27) to the 2026-08-20 memory 96e2e42a-bebc-474c-a4e9-7bd1278b5cf3, section 3 "NO OTHER SINK EXISTS". Its narrow claim is still true — fused-memory has no FileHandler and no logfile config, so the application writes no log file of its own. But its CONCLUSION, "the only place a leaked payload survives verbatim is the caller's own agent transcript", is FALSE, and acting on it costs real evidence.

journald's ForwardToSyslog is ENABLED on this host, and rsyslog's /etc/rsyslog.conf rule writes everything to /var/log/syslog, which rotates WEEKLY x4 — so roughly two to four weeks of coverage against journald's ~3 days. Every fused-memory ERROR line, including markup-guard residue lines carrying a caller's whole payload inline, is in /var/log/syslog too.

Measured consequence on 2026-08-27: a markup-residue investigation believed journald held the complete population of destroyed payloads and found 5. /var/log/syslog held ELEVEN — six had already aged out of journald and would have been lost. Those six were recovered and committed to the repo only because syslog was checked. Line lengths make the stakes visible: destroyed-payload lines run 2216-3928 chars because they carry the payload inline, while preserved-path lines are 383-388 chars (just an escalation pointer).

PRACTICE: when a journald window comes up short, or before concluding a log-borne payload is unrecoverable, check /var/log/syslog and its rotations (syslog.1, syslog.2.gz ...) with `grep -a` before declaring anything gone. Run a positive control on a string you know is present, because a rotated-file sweep can false-negative. Specifically: a `grep -r` over /var/log with a `|| echo "not found"` idiom returned a FALSE NEGATIVE in this session — unreadable files made grep exit rc=2, firing the fallback branch even though genuine matches had already printed.

In fused-memory, migrating a hand-rolled gather-Pass-2 site onto async_utils.gather_or_raise MUST pass logger=<caller module logger> (not the default async_utils logger). Several get_entity tests do patch('fused_memory.services.memory_service.logger') and assert mock_logger.warning.call_count (0 for CancelledError, 1-2 for Exceptions); using the default logger would leave call_count at 0 and break them.
