Two journald facts that determine what markup-tripwire (and any fused-memory) forensics is possible, established 2026-08-20.

1. RETENTION HISTORY. Until 2026-08-17 the host ran journald's default cap (10% of the filesystem, capped at 4G), and the user-1000 journals rotate roughly every two hours while sharing that budget with the system journal — so oldest-first vacuuming kept only about four days. /etc/systemd/journald.conf.d/99-reify-retention.conf raising SystemMaxUse to 32G was written 2026-08-17 18:04 and journald picked it up on its 2026-08-18 08:58 restart. CONSEQUENCE: the 2026-07-30, 08-05 and 08-10 markup burst windows are UNRECOVERABLE (oldest retained entry for fused-memory.service is 2026-08-15T08:12:41+01:00); at ~1.1 GiB/day every window from 2026-08-15 onward is durable for roughly four weeks. Repeated requests in old escalation records to "pull the journalctl evidence for this burst" for those dates cannot be satisfied.

2. PRIORITY-FILTERING THE FUSED-MEMORY JOURNAL DOES NOT WORK. fused-memory logs to stderr via logging.basicConfig (server/main.py:50) with StandardOutput/StandardError=journal, so journald assigns every application line PRIORITY=6 (info) regardless of the Python level. A line whose TEXT reads "WARNING - markup_tripwire: rejected write..." or "ERROR - markup_tripwire_storm:..." is still priority INFO to journalctl. `journalctl --user -u fused-memory.service -p warning` returns essentially nothing but systemd's own RestartMaxDelaySec noise and will make an active leak look absent. Grep the full INFO stream instead; it is slow (minutes for a multi-day window) so run it backgrounded.

3. NO OTHER SINK EXISTS. There is no FileHandler/RotatingFileHandler/dictConfig anywhere in fused-memory/src outside one-shot maintenance CLIs, and no logfile key in fused-memory/config/config.yaml. The tripwire's rejection path does exactly three things — logger.warning, feed the process-local MarkupStormCounter (explicitly "not durable statistics", resets on restart), and on a trip file an escalation. There is no dead-letter table, no sqlite, no JSONL audit and no metrics store. The rejection dict's agent_id/field/matched_pattern/content_excerpt go ONLY to the calling agent, never to disk. And content_excerpt is text[:200] — the HEAD of the field, while the leak lands at the TAIL — so even the rejection response never captures the leaked bytes. The only place a leaked payload survives verbatim is the caller's own agent transcript, and dispatched-agent transcripts are reaped.

Gotcha when moving a logging helper out of fused-memory's task_interceptor.py to another module: many tests in fused-memory/tests/test_task_interceptor.py capture with caplog.at_level(logging.WARNING, logger=_TI_LOGGER) and filter records by `r.name == _TI_LOGGER`. After such a move, those filters still pass on every 'assert not warns' test, because they now match nothing, so the no-warning tests become vacuous instead of failing. Retarget them to root caplog with message-content filters (e.g. 'task_metadata.schema_warning' in getMessage()), not to the new logger name.

Offline/CLI callers of fused-memory internals: FusedMemoryConfig is a pydantic BaseSettings, so the BARE CONSTRUCTOR is the loader (server/main.py:521, maintenance/_utils.py:79) — there is no .load() or .from_yaml() classmethod, and a config path is supplied via the CONFIG_PATH env var that settings_customise_sources reads (config/schema.py:2047). Two adjacent signature traps: SqliteTaskBackend takes NO project_root constructor kwarg — project_root is an argument to get_statuses, which is a COROUTINE (backends/sqlite_task_backend.py:1662) — and TicketStore.get/.initialize are likewise coroutines (middleware/ticket_store.py:90,236). Also note RECONCILIATION_DATA_DIR defaults to './data/reconciliation' RELATIVE TO THE PROJECT ROOT, so a script run from fused-memory/ will not find tickets.db unless it is set absolute. Task 3381 hit all of these: each sat inside an `except Exception: continue` fallback, so the sweep did not crash — it silently resolved every authority to 'unverifiable' and would have reported a clean corpus. pyright caught them; the tests could not, because they inject the probe facade and never exercise the default path.

Gotcha (Python logging, dark-factory tests): when a log call passes a SINGLE non-empty dict as its only argument — `logger.info('Referent repair executed: %s', {...})` — `LogRecord.__init__` UNWRAPS it, so `record.args` IS that dict, not a 1-tuple containing it. `record.args[0]` therefore raises `KeyError` rather than returning the payload. (CPython special-cases `len(args) == 1 and isinstance(args[0], Mapping) and args[0]` to support `%(name)s`-style formatting; a dict that is EMPTY is not unwrapped, so the shape is not uniform.) `'%s' % {...}` still renders the whole mapping correctly, so nothing about the emitted line looks unusual.

Practical consequence for a caplog assertion: read the structured payload as `record.args` directly (assert `isinstance(record.args, dict)` first), never as `record.args[0]`.

Complements the existing norm "prefer asserting against `LogRecord.args` rather than substring-matching the rendered message" (memory 29fe5a45) — that entry says WHERE to read the payload; this one says what SHAPE it arrives in for the single-dict case, which is the spelling structured-payload log lines in this repo actually use.

Related pairing when counting such lines in a test: filter on `record.msg` (the FORMAT STRING) rather than on `record.getMessage()`, so a sibling line that happens to render a matching substring cannot be miscounted.

GOTCHA (dark-factory, measured 2026-09-14, task 4194): every orchestrator log line is bounded at 48K by journald, so a WARNING that interpolates an unbounded captured stream silently loses its TAIL — usually the part that carried the signal.

MECHANISM, all three links verified on this tree: `cli.py` `main()` calls `logging.basicConfig(..., stream=sys.stderr)`; every unit in `scripts/orchestrator-*.service` sets `StandardError=journal`; journald's `LineMax` default is 48K (confirmed as the commented-out default in `/etc/systemd/journald.conf`). Stream input longer than LineMax is truncated by journald itself, not by Python — so nothing in the code or the test suite reveals the loss, and `caplog` assertions pass happily on a line that will never reach an operator intact.

WHERE THIS BITES. Any log call that formats a subprocess's captured stderr/stdout into the message. Concretely `verify_runner.py` builds `RunnerUnavailable(f'ssh {host} exited {rc}: {ssh_stderr}')` with the FULL remote stderr, and a remote verify's stderr carries that whole run's INFO logging (a measured healthy dispatch ran 1370s). Log that whole string and journald keeps the head and drops the rest.

THE NON-OBVIOUS PART: which end to keep. When BOTH ends carry signal — here the ssh rc is at the head and a `watchdog_fire_trigger=` token at the tail — a head slice and a tail slice are each wrong, and `[:N]` (the existing convention at `merge_queue.py:1580 outcome.reason[:200]`) is the head slice. Elide the MIDDLE instead, keeping a head and a tail with a visible marker naming the dropped character count, so a reader cannot mistake a truncated reason for a complete one.

Bound the LOG LINE only. The same string usually also feeds an escalation body (e.g. `merge_liveness.py::_alarm_verify_host_unreachable`), which is not a journald-shaped channel and must keep complete evidence. Different channel, different bound — do not push the truncation upstream into the stored `reason`.

fused-memory ReconciliationConfig (fused-memory/src/fused_memory/config/schema.py) declares no model_config, so it runs under pydantic's default extra='ignore'. Deleting one of its fields therefore cannot break an operator yaml that still sets the key; the key is just dropped silently. If a removed or renamed key is safety-relevant, add an explicit mode='before' rejecting validator, as _reject_legacy_bulk_reset_threshold does. Measured 2026-09-25 while planning task 5890.

In fused-memory, the sanctioned pattern for making a reconciliation-stage write discipline CODE-ENFORCED rather than LLM-prompt convention is a five-part shape established by task 2624: (1) a leaf `middleware/` module holding frozen dataclasses + pure detectors + one async guard, importing nothing from `reconciliation/` or `server/`; (2) an injected async filer callback so the module stays channel-agnostic; (3) a `TaskInterceptor.set_*_filer` post-construction setter defaulting to None so the path is off in unit-test fixtures; (4) a `server/recon_*_filer.py` adapter mapping the finding onto `ReconReportState.add_finding`, a logged no-op when `active_run_for_stage` finds no live Stage-2 run; (5) bootstrap wiring in `server/main.py` right after ReconReportState is constructed. Reference implementation: `middleware/live_task_write_guard.py` + `server/recon_lifecycle_filer.py` + `server/main.py:904-909`. Filing is always best-effort — an exception in the after-read/detect/file sequence is logged and swallowed, never converting an already-succeeded write into a failure.

WriteJournal API (fused-memory/src/fused_memory/services/write_journal.py): `log_write_op(*, write_op_id, causation_id, source='mcp_tool', provenance='original', operation, project_id, agent_id, session_id, kind='write', params, result_summary, success=True, error=None)` records intent at line 130; `log_backend_op(*, write_op_id, causation_id, backend, operation, payload, result_summary, success, error)` records per-backend outcome at line 176. Both fire-and-forget — wrapped in try/except, never raise (only log warnings on failure). Bootstrap wiring: server/main.py:315-320 constructs WriteJournal and calls memory_service.set_write_journal(). Mirror this for task_interceptor.

Write-journal attribution for scripted fused-memory clients (measured 2026-09-26). merge_entities calls made through the scripted FusedMemoryClient (scripts/migrate_metadata_modules_to_files.py) landed in data/reconciliation/write_journal.db write_ops with agent_id BLANK. The clientInfo name was not recorded as agent_id, and session_id held the client's MCP session id. The call's metadata dict is not stored in params either. To make scripted writes attributable, pass agent_id explicitly in every tool call and keep your own run log with the uuid pairs.

Avoid asserting on field-qualified substrings of log messages (e.g. `'signal=recon_reset_count'`); they couple tests to the exact format string and break on cosmetic refactors. Prefer asserting on the bare value (`'recon_reset_count'`) or capturing structured log kwargs via a fixture.

GOTCHA (dark-factory, measured 2026-09-22, task 4854): when consolidating N duplicated implementations into one shared helper, the emitted LOG LEVEL is a behaviour dimension that is silently lost if the copies disagreed — and the standard caplog assertion cannot catch it.

THE SHAPE. Seven fused-memory filers each carried the same pending-anchor-fold escalation skeleton. Six logged "escalation package unavailable" at logger.debug and the fold at logger.info; referent_repair_storm_escalator alone used logger.warning for BOTH. The consolidation into middleware/_folded_escalation.py hardcoded the majority levels, silently downgrading that one caller WARNING->DEBUG and WARNING->INFO. The suite stayed 417/417 green.

WHY NO TEST CAUGHT IT: every assertion was `assert caplog.records` (truthy) under `caplog.at_level('DEBUG')`. That passes at ANY level. A bare `assert caplog.records` pins existence, never severity, so it is blind to precisely the regression a consolidation introduces. On a never-raise ALARM path this is maximally costly: the only symptom of a downgrade is absence of output at the default level, which is indistinguishable from health.

THE CHECK, cheap and mechanical: before consolidating, diff each copy's level per arm against the merge base — `for f in <copies>; do git show <merge-base>:$f | grep -n 'logger\.\(debug\|info\|warning\)'; done`. A minority level is usually deliberate, not sloppy; find out which before flattening it.

THE FIX SHAPE: make the level a caller parameter (`no_escalation_level: int = logging.DEBUG`) defaulting to the MAJORITY value, so the majority stays behaviour-preserving and the outlier opts up explicitly. Do NOT raise the default for everyone to "fix the house level" inside a refactor — that converts a reviewable one-caller fix into an unreviewed N-caller behaviour change and destroys the diff's verifiability against the merge base. File the house-level question separately.

AND DO NOT ADD A SECOND KNOB FOR AN ARM THAT ALREADY HAS ONE: this helper already had an `on_fold` hook whose docstring promised callers "ITS OWN logger and at its own level", so the fold arm was restored via that hook (recovering level, message wording AND logger attribution together), not via a parallel `fold_level` int. Two knobs for one arm is an SPOT violation (heuristic 11) where passing both silently ignores one.

Assert on `r.levelno` against `logging.*` constants, never on `levelname` strings (heuristic 12). Companion entry: the task-4310 memory on hoisting a guard's log message into the guard function and what it does to tests that monkeypatch that function away.

content: fused-memory logging gotcha (verified 2026-10-12, task 5478): server/main.py configures logging.basicConfig with LOG_FORMAT '%(asctime)s - %(name)s - %(levelname)s - %(message)s' and adds no other handler. So `extra={...}` fields on logger calls (the convention throughout reconciliation/harness.py, e.g. 'reconciliation.graphiti_queue_unhealthy') are NEVER rendered in the journald or /var/log/syslog line. Only caplog and record attributes see them. If an operator must read a value in the log, put it in the message text with lazy %-args as well as in extra.

candidates.content: reify-eval's `Engine::eval` elaborates sub-components in two SEPARATE module-wide loops: Phase A (engine_eval.rs:4943-5126, `evaluate_params_and_lets_unified`) evaluates every template's params/lets, then Phase B (engine_eval.rs:5130-5410) elaborates subs in PLAIN DECLARATION ORDER with no topological sort, forwarding `sub.args` RAW to `unfold.rs::elaborate_child_params_only`. Phase A's dependency graph (`build_combined_param_let_graph`, :517-624) is built only from `template.value_cells`, so a read of `ValueCellId("Top.mid","p")` creates no ordering edge — a parent `let` sourced from `self.<sub>.<member>` is therefore still Undef when Phase B evaluates a sibling sub's constructor args. The post-sub `evaluate_let_bindings` at :5396 fixes the parent let but nothing re-elaborates the child, and there is no fixpoint. Discriminator measured on task #6586: a DIRECT `Bar(length: self.leaf.doubled)` arg WORKS; only an intervening parent `let` is stale.

reify-eval has TWO evaluation scopes with DIFFERENT cell-ordering behaviour, and this asymmetry is a recurring silent-divergence source. TEMPLATE scope (crates/reify-eval/src/engine_eval.rs) evaluates all non-Auto body cells in ONE dependency-ordered pass since task #4317. INSTANCE scope (crates/reify-eval/src/unfold.rs) still runs a kind-partitioned multi-pass: elaborate_child_params_only (phase 1, params in DECLARATION order), then elaborate_child_instance (phase 1.5, nested subs), then elaborate_child_lets_only (phase 2, lets topologically sorted). Consequence measured 2026-09-13 on main @5efc4c04ce: a param default reading a later-declared sibling param, or any sibling let, evaluates correctly at template scope but degrades silently to Value::Undef at instance scope with NO diagnostic. When investigating an Undef that "should" have a value, always check whether the cell is at instance scope (entity name contains a dot, e.g. "Outer.a") before suspecting the expression or the solver.

Reify eval elaborates sub-components ONE level only: engine_eval.rs's sub-elaboration loop iterates module.templates x sub_components and calls elaborate_child_instance at scope "{template}.{sub}" (e.g. Parent.m, Mid.k) but never at instance-nested scope (Parent.m.k). unfold.rs::elaborate_child_instance also does NOT recurse into the child template's own subs. So instance-scoped grandchild cells (Parent.m.k.*) simply don't exist. Template-scoped cells resolve cross-sub reads via evaluate_let_bindings reading the GLOBAL values map; instance-scoped child lets resolve against a template-keyed child_values map that (pre-#5360) was only enriched with sub cells for RECURSIVE subs (elaborate_child_lets_only projection gated on non-empty recursive_sub_names). That asymmetry is why a sub's `let relay = self.k.off` works at template scope but is silently Undef on an instance.

reify-eval: `Engine::evaluate_let_bindings` (engine_eval.rs) is no longer part of eval()'s initial pass. The initial pass is `evaluate_params_and_lets_unified` → `build_combined_param_let_graph`. evaluate_let_bindings is only called by three RE-eval passes over already-diagnosed templates: after sub-elaboration (when the template has subs), the per-scope solver Solved arm, and the merged-cluster per-member loop. Any diagnostic emitted inside it is therefore duplicated per re-eval pass. This is how task #5819's twice-emitted "circular let-binding dependency in template T" arose.

reify-eval instance-nested sub elaboration (unfold.rs `elaborate_child_instance_nested`, phase 1.5): nested-sub constructor args are evaluated against `values.clone()` overlaid with `child_values`, but `child_values` holds PARAMS ONLY at that point (`elaborate_child_params_only` filters on ValueCellKind::Param; `elaborate_child_lets_only` runs after). Any arg read that is not a param of the child template — a `let` of the child, or a sibling sub's member via `self.<sub>.<member>` — misses the overlay and falls through to the TEMPLATE-scope entry in the global map, silently substituting the template default for the instance value with ZERO diagnostics. Confirmed on four shapes (arg reads a let; reads a sibling sub; reads a let derived from an earlier sub; reads a forward-declared sibling), so declaration order is not the issue — a fix must be dependency-ordered over {child lets} U {plain nested subs}, not source-ordered.

reify-eval `unfold.rs`: a child param supplied by an explicit ctor arg (`sub a = Inner(q: 5)`) NEVER evaluates its `default_expr` — the arg expression is evaluated against the PARENT's `values`, not the child's. So any dependency analysis over a child template's params must build each param's trace from the expression that will ACTUALLY run (empty trace for arg-supplied params), not unconditionally from `default_expr`. Doing the latter invents edges: measured on task #7418, `structure Pair { param p = q  param q = p }` built as `Pair(q: 5)` fabricates a false p<->q 2-cycle, and since `topological_sort` reports cycles by OMISSION both cells fall into the declaration-order residue and `p` degrades to Undef. The same asymmetry is why `resolve_optimized_instance_cell` is deliberately not applied to the args arm.

reify-eval engine_eval.rs has TWO independent kind-partitioned two-pass body evaluators that both evaluate Param defaults BEFORE Let bindings, violating spec §8.2 order-independence for `param x = <expr referencing a sibling let>` (yields silent Value::Undef): (1) cold `Engine::eval` (pass-1 param/auto arm ~L1822-1988, then `evaluate_let_bindings` call), (2) `Engine::eval_cached` (param pass ~L2944-3116, then a `detect_let_cycle`-ordered let pass). `evaluate_let_bindings` is shared by 3 callers — the cold initial call (needs params interleaved) plus post-sub-elaboration and post-solver re-eval calls which are DELIBERATELY lets-only (params must NOT re-evaluate post-solve). The incremental `edit_param`/`edit_source` path is NOT affected — it already uses compute_eval_set→topological_sort over the kind-agnostic graph. Fix = unified topological eval over params∪lets dispatched by kind. Gotcha: `detect_let_cycle` returns HashMap<NodeId,&CompiledExpr> (the expr, not ValueCellDecl) and is shared byte-identically by eval_cached + the two re-eval passes — add a separate detect_body_cycle returning &ValueCellDecl rather than mutating it.

In crates/reify-eval/src/engine_eval.rs, both `Engine::eval` (~L1617) and `Engine::eval_cached` (~L2822) evaluate structure-body cells in a KIND-partitioned two-pass: pass 1 evaluates Param defaults + Auto cells (Auto->Undef), pass 2 (`evaluate_let_bindings`, ~L3541) evaluates Let bindings in topological order. Gotcha (task 4317): because params are evaluated before any let exists in the `values` map, a structure `param p = <expr referencing a sibling let>` silently resolves the let to Value::Undef (via ValueCells::get_or_undef) with NO diagnostic — violating language-spec §8.2 order-independence (docs/reify-language-spec.md:1554). The reverse (let referencing a param) works. The fix is to collapse the two passes into one dependency-ordered evaluation over all Param+Let cells (autos pre-seeded as Undef leaves) and generalize the let-only cycle detector (`detect_let_cycle`, ~L312) to the combined node set. Any future change to eval ordering must keep eval and eval_cached in parity.

reify eval-order bug (task 4317, high): a structure `param` whose default expression references a sibling `let` binding silently evaluates to `Value::Undef` (no diagnostic), violating language-spec §8.2 order-independence ("all declarations within a body are mutually visible regardless of textual order"). Referencing other `param`s works; the identical expression as a `let` works. Root cause = two-pass evaluation in crates/reify-eval/src/engine_eval.rs (pass 1 ~:1531-1668 evaluates Param defaults+Auto with a values map lacking lets; pass 2 ~:1739-1754 evaluate_let_bindings runs later), so a let-reference resolves via ValueCells::get_or_undef (crates/reify-ir/src/value.rs:3319) → Undef. NOTE the related but INTENTIONAL restriction (done task 3703): FUNCTION params have a "neutral scope" and may NOT reference siblings — that does not apply to structure-body params (§8.2 governs those).

reify-eval testing gotcha: a plain `engine.eval()` on a fixture with NO sub-components and NO solver resolution never reaches `Engine::evaluate_let_bindings` — that evaluator is called only from the sub-component elaboration pass and the two post-solver resolution passes; a flat single-structure module's lets go through `evaluate_params_and_lets_unified` instead. So an integration test written against a flat `.ri` fixture cannot pin anything inside `evaluate_let_bindings`. Cover it with an in-crate `#[cfg(test)]` module that calls `engine.evaluate_let_bindings(..)` DIRECTLY on a pre-seeded two-cell module (param + let reading it), as `evaluate_let_bindings_provenance_and_freshness_tests` at the tail of crates/reify-eval/src/engine_eval.rs does.

In reify-eval engine_eval.rs the eval() Param branch (lines ~592-642) and eval_cached() Param branch (lines ~1396-1547) deliberately mirror each other's structure (re-borrow `self.param_overrides.get(&cell.id)` and clone only inside the validation `Ok(())` arm). When refactoring one path, audit the other to keep them aligned — diverging shapes increase the maintenance burden when validate_param_override gets new rejection variants.

Task 'Fix eval-order bug: structure `param` default referencing a sibling `let` yields silent Undef (violates spec §8.2 order-independence)' completed. A structure `param` whose default expression references a sibling `let` binding silently evaluates to `Value::Undef`, with NO diagnostic. References to sibling `param`s work; the IDENTICAL expression written as a `let` works. This violates language-spec §8.2 ("All declarations within a body are mutually visible regardless of textual order"). Reify eval architecture fact (verified 2026-06-11, /unblock 4287): stdlib prelude templates live in Engine::prelude (&'static [CompiledModule], reify-eval/src/lib.rs) and are deliberately NOT merged into the user CompiledModule — module.templates contains only user templates and module.trait_defs is EMPTY for user modules (stdlib trait defs like `trait Output : Sink` live in the prelude's std.io module). Until the esc-4287-15 fix, eval's sub-component resolver searched module.templates only, so `sub o = STLOutput(...)` emitted "references unknown structure" and never elaborated — a LATENT GAP, not a regression: user-defined occurrences elaborated fine (m5_integration), prelude STRUCTURES instantiated fine (stdlib_prelude_tests), but prelude-template-as-sub was never exercised before io-export δ. Corollary for any code consuming occurrence instances: pass module ⊕ prelude trait_defs to trait-closure predicates like conforms_to_output, and search prelude when resolving occurrence templates by structure_name. Also: the compiler does NOT validate sub.structure_name at all (lenient by design, cli_check_cfg.rs) — `reify check` passes for unknown sub types; follow-up task 4528 owns compile-time validation against module⊕prelude.

Measured on reify main 2151ed59c5 (task/5867 lane, zero src changes): the two-level instance-scope chain `Parent { sub m = Mid(); let echo = self.m.relay }` where `Mid { sub k = Kid(); let relay = self.k.off }` yields Parent.echo = Undef, Parent.m.relay = Undef, and Parent.m = StructureInstance{fields:{"relay": Undef}} with ZERO diagnostics — for a plain USER-MODULE sub, not just a prelude-typed one. Template scope is fine (Mid.relay = Scalar). So on main the instance-scope half of any nested-sub member-read acceptance criterion is unreachable regardless of whether the sub's target is prelude- or module-typed; that half is task #5360's territory (eval-side unfold.rs/engine_eval.rs), not a compiler-side typing fix.

Task 'Engine: project derived `let` cells off Value::StructureInstance (fn-returned/param-held) — not only the `sub` elaborate_child_instance path' completed. ROOT CAUSE (architect capability trace): derived `let` cells of a structure (e.g. upper_limit/lower_limit/tolerance_band, max_clearance/min_clearance) are materialized ONLY when the structure is instantiated as a `sub`-component. The engine's `elaborate_child_instance` computes child-scope lets — that is why `Flange.dim_tol.upper_limit` resolves correctly when reached via a `sub` (see m8_3_stdlib_integration.rs:557-615, the REFERENCE semantics that already work). A structure produced as a `Value::StructureInstance` — returned from a `.ri` free fn (`symmetric_tolerance`/`limit_tolerance`) or held in a `param` (`Fit.hole_tolerance`/`shaft_tolerance`) — carries ONLY constructor args+defaults: `eval_structure_instance_ctor` inserts only ordered_args+defaults into `fields`, never the template's let bindings (reify-expr/src/lib.rs:893-916); `eval_index_access` then projects members as fields.get(k).unwrap_or(Undef) (reify-expr/src/lib.rs:946-948). So any derived `let` member of a fn-returned or param-held struct reads as undef.

EMPIRICAL (prebuilt `reify eval`):
(1) DimensionalTolerance(...).upper_limit → undef, while .nominal (a stored param) → 0.01 m.
(2) `sub f` with derived `let max_clearance = hole_tolerance.upper_limit - ...` → f.max_clearance = undef AND f.hole_tolerance.upper_limit = undef (the param-held struct member is itself a fn/ctor-produced StructureInstance, so its lets are undef even from within an elaborated sub).
(3) `sub st = symmetric_tolerance(...)` is a PARSE ERROR (a `sub` cannot bind a function call), so the `sub` elaborate_child_instance path cannot rescue the fn-returned-struct case at all.

USER-OBSERVABLE SIGNAL (acceptance): via `reify eval`, DimensionalTolerance(5mm, +0.02, -0.01).upper_limit must evaluate to a concrete value (not undef); and the param-held case Fit.hole_tolerance.upper_limit must likewise resolve, so derived `let` members of fn-returned and param-held struct values behave consistently with the working `sub`-child case.

DESIGN NOTE (do NOT pre-decide — weigh both in the plan): the implementer must choose between (a) EAGER evaluation of template `let` bindings inside `eval_structure_instance_ctor` (populate `fields` with the derived cells at construction), versus (b) LAZY projection at member-access time in `eval_index_access` (evaluate a requested `let` member against the template + stored fields on demand). The acceptance bar is CONSISTENCY with the existing `sub` semantics: mirror `elaborate_child_instance`'s child-scope scoping so a derived member resolves to the same value regardless of whether the struct arrived via a `sub`, a free-fn return, or a `param`. Consider cost/cycles if template lets are expensive (eager pays at every construction even when members are never read; lazy must guard against recomputation and cycles) — but keep sub-consistency as the bar, not a particular evaluation strategy.

CONSUMER (G1): task 4267 (tolerancing γ) depends on this — its RED tests (upper_limit/max_clearance read off fn-returned and param-held struct values) are the immediate consumers. More broadly, every stdlib structure with derived `let` members benefits; this is a language-semantics trap for all such structures, currently masked because most are reached via `sub`.

REFERENCES: reify-expr/src/lib.rs:893-916 (eval_structure_instance_ctor — inserts only ordered_args+defaults); reify-expr/src/lib.rs:946-948 (eval_index_access — fields.get(k).unwrap_or(Undef)); engine `elaborate_child_instance` + m8_3_stdlib_integration.rs:557-615 (the working `sub`-child reference semantics to mirror).

reify-eval engine_eval.rs has TWO solve entry points: `pub fn eval` (~L2226, with a post-pass diagnostics block running detect_underdetermined/detect_mechanism_errors/etc.) and `pub fn eval_cached` (~L3731, the incremental path with a DIFFERENT, smaller post-pass set that does NOT include detect_underdetermined). For a per-template diagnostic that mirrors detect_underdetermined (e.g. task-4789 RobustnessFloorApplied Info), add a `detect_*` post-pass and wire it via diagnostics.extend(...) in `pub fn eval` only — this decouples it from both `.solve()` sites and matches the eval-only placement convention. AutoParam (reify-constraints) gained a `free: bool` field (task 4019) — solver tests must construct AutoParam { id, param_type, bounds, free }; strict autos use free:false. DiagnosticCode is #[non_exhaustive] with DERIVED serde (rename_all=PascalCase), so new variants are purely additive with no match/serde arm to extend.

reify-eval instance-scope gotchas (measured 2026-10-07, HEAD 3bae3c7bda): (1) `where`-guard cells (`T.__guard_N`) exist only at template scope; sub-instance elaboration never materializes `Root.t.__guard_N`, so instance-scoped code must evaluate the rescoped `CompiledGuardedGroup::guard_expr` itself. (2) reify-expr's DeterminacyPredicate (`determined(x)` etc.) hits `debug_assert!(false)`, a debug-build PANIC, when its cell is absent from the determinacy snapshot, while a plain ValueRef to an absent cell safely yields Undef. Any rescoped expr containing determined() needs its cell present in the determinacy map. (3) The collapsed `Value::StructureInstance` at a sub cell (`Root.u = Cube { body: undef, vol: undef, w }`) keeps stale `undef` for geometry-derived lets, even after the per-member cell `Root.u.vol` is folded post-geometry. Compare PARAM fields, never collapsed let fields, when deciding whether an instance matches template defaults.

Reify eval: a stdlib/prelude free function that constructs and returns a prelude STRUCTURE (e.g. symmetric_tolerance(...) -> DimensionalTolerance) DOES expose that structure's derived `let` members (.upper_limit, .max_clearance, ...) at eval, using the REAL stdlib with NO local redeclaration. Mechanism: derived lets are captured at COMPILE time into the StructureInstanceCtor (the prelude template registry in reify-compiler/src/entity.rs is available when the stdlib is compiled), then replayed registry-free at eval by materialize_template_lets (reify-expr/src/lib.rs:929/955, landed by task 4342) via eval_user_function_call (lib.rs:1190) -> eval_structure_instance_ctor. The well-known "eval engine resolves templates from the user module only, not stdlib" limitation applies ONLY to `sub` components (runtime find_template on module.templates); it does NOT apply to let/param/fn-returned ctor expressions. So `let f = Fit(...)` then `f.max_clearance`, and `symmetric_tolerance(10mm,0.1mm).upper_limit`, evaluate correctly; only `sub s = StdlibStruct()` needs a local redeclaration. Discovered planning task 4267 (tolerancing gamma §7.1 reshape); relevant to PRD tolerancing-gdt-surface-completion tasks epsilon (end-to-end example) and delta.

To probe an instance-vs-template scope bug in reify-eval without writing a Rust test, run `reify eval <file.ri>` on a scratch .ri: it prints EVERY scoped value cell, so template-scope cells (e.g. `Mid.relay`) and instance-scope cells (e.g. `Parent.m.relay`, `Parent.m.k.off`) appear side by side. A cell that is absent entirely means the instance was never elaborated; a cell printed as `undef` means it elaborated but its expr failed to resolve — two different root causes that a pass/fail Rust assertion cannot distinguish.

reify-eval's warm-Resolution back-prop write set has SEVEN legs across SIX arms, not five. Four entry points resolve Auto params and back-propagate: Engine::eval, Engine::eval_cached, Engine::edit_param, Engine::edit_source; eval and eval_cached each additionally take a merged-cluster branch (dispatch_merged_cluster_solve / _cached, task #5118) selected PER TEMPLATE INDEX inside `for &idx in &ro.order` — not per call — so one eval() over a module with one clustered and one uncoupled scope runs BOTH arms. Uniform legs: values, snapshot-as-Determined, cache entry. Non-uniform: param_overrides (edit_param/edit_source only); journal (all but eval_cached's per-template arm and edit_source); resolved_params (all but BOTH eval_cached arms); objective_provenance (eval's two arms only). eval_cached hard-codes the last two empty at engine_eval.rs:8910-8911 — DELIBERATE, documented at dispatch_merged_cluster_solve_cached's own doc, not drift to be "fixed".

content: reify-eval template scope (Engine::eval in engine_eval.rs) evaluates params and lets once, in one dependency-ordered pass, BEFORE sub-component elaboration. After the subs are elaborated it re-runs only `evaluate_let_bindings`, never the params. So a param default that reads a let which reads `self.<sub>.<member>` stays Undef at template scope (measured 2026-10-12 @ b8e8c32a05: `Mid{sub k=Kid() let relay=self.k.off param p:Int=relay}` gives Mid.relay=7 but Mid.p=Undef). Instance-scope fixes in unfold.rs must mirror that pre-sub view or they create a new template/instance divergence.

candidates.content:
Fact (scoping_intake, verified 2026-10-14 on main f628a00): web.py::route compiles the path as a regex and _dispatch uses fullmatch, so a literal path like "/confidentiality" routes with no token; a Handler may ignore both the match and the form (tests/test_web.py already does). wording.py::wording_html is called only from cli.py::sites_for, substitutes only {{retention_days}}, html-escapes each blank-line chunk into

, and cannot render headings, lists, links or line breaks; markdown markers come out literally. A copy/*.md file therefore cannot carry an anchor, so a link from the notice page must be added in prospect_pages.py::_notice_page. Completed: Check Host, Origin and password before reading a POST body: one ordered refusal chain (web.py RequestHandler)
Description: In src/scoping_intake/web.py, a POST's refusals are applied in two places, in an order that reads the body before deciding whether the request may be answered at all.

do_POST (web.py:111-117 at main 368e171; after task 7 lands, RequestHandler.do_POST at module level) does these steps in order:
1. Checks the Content-Length header.
2. Reads the body: self.rfile.read(...), up to MAX_FORM_BYTES = 256,000 bytes.
3. Calls _respond, which only then runs _refusal(): Host allow-list (refused.host), same-origin via Sec-Fetch-Site/Origin (refused.origin), then the operator password (refused.password).

Consequences:
(a) A POST with a foreign Host, from another website, or without the operator password still makes the server read up to 256 KB before refusing it.
(b) A foreign-Host POST with a bad Content-Length is answered with the length refusal instead of the Host refusal.
(c) The refusal policy has two homes: the inline length checks in do_POST and the _refusal() chain. This is docs/code-quality.md heuristic 10, 'uniformly enforced': one mechanism everywhere, and the invariant's definition has one home.

Proposal: one ordered refusal chain run before any body is read. The order is Host, then origin, then password, then length (missing or unreadable as malformed, over the limit as too long), then read the form. Keep every refusal's route name, status and page.

Tests: through make_server with a bare socket client, as tests/test_web.py does after task 7. A foreign-Host POST with a bad length is refused as refused.host (421), and a refused request's body is never read. One way to show the second: declare a Content-Length larger than the body sent and confirm the refusal still arrives at once, before the 30-second socket timeout.

Smoke-testing gotcha for scoping-intake (current as of task 7): web.py's do_POST refuses a POST whose Content-Length header is missing or not a decimal under the route name refused.malformed with the page 'Malformed request'. A decimal length over MAX_FORM_BYTES, or with more digits than MAX_FORM_BYTES has, is refused under refused.too-long with the page 'Too long'. Both are HTTP 400, and the log line records only method, route name and status. Before task 7 every such case was one refused.length / 'Too long' refusal, which misled the first smoke pass of review-scoping_intake-20261007 (finding R8, fk-d79ef903b73e). curl -X POST with no --data sends no Content-Length, so a curl-driven walk of the flow is still refused (now as malformed) on consent, write-up and delete: pass --data '' (or use urllib, which sends Content-Length: 0). A working smoke script follows the review session's scratchpad pattern: synthetic backend, mktemp INTAKE_DATA_DIR, free loopback ports, curl with Host matching 127.0.0.1:<port>.

solar_challenge gotcha (task 626, measured 2026-10-10 with the locked tailwindcss 3.4.19): when a class is the last word of an Alpine `:class` object key, as in `:class="{'bg-primary-50 dark:text-primary-400': cond}"`, Tailwind's extractor also compiles the bare `.text-primary-400`; a plain `class="... dark:text-primary-400"` compiles only the dark: rule. So rewriting a template's `:class` objects into server-rendered class attributes changes static/dist/style.css even when no class name changes (task 363's nav-sidebar.html did this, and only the css-build lane caught it). The per-task guard tests/unit/test_web_compiled_css.py checks only that applied classes have rules, never leftover rules, so after ANY template or static/js edit run `cd src/solar_challenge/web && npm ci --cache /tmp/<dir> && npm run build:css` and commit static/dist/style.css if it changed.

solar_challenge Tailwind gotcha, measured 2026-10-17 by task 736's architect at main c1859d5. The method was a scratch copy of src/solar_challenge/web, then npm ci --cache /tmp/<dir> and npm run build:css. tailwind.config.js scans static/js/**/*.js as raw text, and its extractor splits on '.'. So a plain JS call such as Plotly.Plots.resize(container) in static/js/chart-renderer.js makes the build emit a .resize{resize:both} utility into static/dist/style.css. Before that edit the fresh build was byte-identical to the committed file; after it, the only difference was the .resize selector. A JS-only edit can therefore require rebuilding and committing static/dist/style.css. The per-task verify does not catch a stale stylesheet; the post-merge css-build lane job does. The npm registry was reachable from the task sandbox that day.

solar_challenge Tailwind gotcha (measured 2026-10-02 while planning task 343, tailwindcss 3.4.19). The compiled static/dist/style.css emits utilities of the same plugin and variant in alphabetical order of class name. So renaming a palette, such as amber-* to primary-*, keeps every rule body but moves its rules past others (black, blue, current, emerald, green and so on), which flips the cascade on any element that applies both kinds at once.

How to check:
1. Split the old and new dist on '}' (`tr '}' '\n'`). Rename the palette in the old file and sort both: the sets must match.
2. Scan each template element's class attribute plus every :class literal for pairs with the same property and the same variant.

In task 343 such pairs occurred only in mutually exclusive branches: the status badges and some ternaries.

solar_challenge convention (task 221, 2026-09-30): tests/unit/test_web_hand_written_css.py, the reverse of test_web_compiled_css.py, runs in every verify.

solar_challenge procedure (task 343, measured 2026-10-07 at task/343 d2b2d1c): to prove a Tailwind palette rename in the dashboard changes no painted pixel, check two things. (1) Rule set: split the old (git show HEAD:...static/dist/style.css) and new dist on '}', map new palette name back to old with re.sub in both, and compare as sets; equal means no declaration changed, only names and rule order. (2) Cascade: Tailwind 3.4 reorders the renamed rules, so scan every template element (static class plus every string literal of :class / x-bind:class, Jinja blanked, via html.parser) for a renamed colour utility sharing the element with another colour utility of the same kind (bg, text, border, ring...) and the same variant chain. For each such pair, compare the two rules' positions (index of the escaped selector, e.g. '.dark\:text-primary-400') in the old dist (old name) and the new dist; no order flip means no cascade change, even where both classes apply at once. In task 343 the amber->primary rename hit 9 such pairs (against slate, white, transparent) and none flipped. Check static/js class strings by hand.

solar_challenge convention (task 235, task/235 commits 44aa38c..3378155, 2026-10-02): tailwind.config.js is the one home of the dashboard's theme colours, and two guards run in every verify.
(1) tests/unit/test_web_theme_colours.py fails when any template (templates/**/*.html) or static/style.css writes a six-digit hex colour that tailwind.config.js defines. Matching is case-insensitive and includes comments; an 8-digit alpha copy counts through its prefix. (2) tests/unit/test_web_range_inputs.py fails when any template other than components/macros.html writes an <input type="range">. Draw every slider with {{ range_input(id=..., model=..., min=..., max=..., step=..., name='', width_class='w-full') }} from components/macros.html, which binds x-model.number and owns the class list, including the four thumb-fill utilities (primary-500, dark primary-400). static/style.css shapes the thumb but gives it no fill, so a slider written out by hand shows a hollow thumb with the track showing through.

candidates.content: GOTCHA (solar_challenge_platform): some src/ docstrings point into tests/ with "mirroring tests/..." provenance notes. Examples: validation/run.py::drop_retention_and_ca_policies pointed at tests/integration/test_timescale_store.py, and timeseries/timescale_store.py's CA refresh docstring points at test_timescale_store.py::_force_refresh_all. solar_challenge_platform gotcha, checked by task 1032's architect on 2026-10-14 at main e4f2a2b. Before you reword or remove text in a src module, look for capability-manifest YAML grep checks on it. Running `git grep -n <module path> -- 'docs/prds/*.capability-manifest.yaml'` is not enough: it misses every delivered_check whose `paths:` lists a PARENT directory of the module, and those checks still match the module's text. Examples: fleet-dispatch-policy-and-config-freshness's 'provenance: CommandProvenance \| None' expect: present over src/solar_challenge_platform/control, and collection-mechanics's expect: absent checks over src/solar_challenge_platform such as 'def handle_event\(' and 'recon_collected'. Instead, yaml.safe_load each docs/prds/*.capability-manifest.yaml, walk it for delivered_check entries with kind: grep, and keep those whose paths name the file or any ancestor directory.

GOTCHA (fused-memory tooling, measured 2026-10-11 by task 958's architect): scan_memory_content is not a general literal-substring search. It was given custom needles ('EXPECTED TO PASS', 'green when written', ...) and returned matches=[] with scanned=6, because every prefilter hit is re-checked by the tool-call-XML-leak detector, which is the authoritative verdict. To find precedent plans by literal text in this project, grep the orchestrator's task-meta instead, e.g. `command grep -l -i 'EXPECTED TO PASS' /home/leo/src/solar-challenge-platform/.worktrees/.task-meta/*/plan.json`. Each task's iterations.jsonl beside its plan shows how its implementer fared.

Gotcha (solar_challenge_platform): since task 773 (2026-10-03), tests/docs/test_capability_manifest_pointers.py fails on any backticked `grep:<path>::<symbol>` in docs/prds/*.capability-manifest.md that no longer resolves. So a task that deletes or renames a src symbol must also `git grep` docs/prds for it, not just src and tests. For a renamed or moved symbol, re-point the token. For a removed symbol, keep the token, append a dated AMENDED note naming the successor to its row, and add a Cited(...): Kept.RETIRED entry to _KEPT_UNRESOLVED. Those files are usually outside a task's plan files, so first file escalate_blocker(category='scope_violation'). Task 207 hit this when the pointer test arrived through a verify-phase rebase.

Counterpoint to the 'force a real RED' planning advice for test-only guard tasks (memory 4e7c1924, task 561's missing-helper trick): a single test step that is green when written also runs cleanly in solar-challenge-platform, provided its description says outright that the test is "EXPECTED TO PASS as soon as it is written ... by design, not a plan error" and names the tmp-copy mutation probe as the run in which it fails. Tasks 377 and 424 each completed such a step in ONE implementer iteration with no escalation (.worktrees/.task-meta/{377,424}/iterations.jsonl, checked 2026-09-30 by task 580's architect). Prefer this shape when the only forceable RED would be irrelevant to the invariant. Example: a TypeScript type-level *.test-d.tsx guard, where omitting a helper just gives TS2304 and commits a tree whose `npm run build` fails.

GOTCHA (task 773, tests/docs/test_capability_manifest_pointers.py, pending merge): in any docs/prds/*.capability-manifest.md, EVERY backticked code span that starts with `grep:` and holds no '<' is read as a pointer and must resolve. So prose such as "resolves every `grep:` pointer" or "every `grep:file:line` pin" in an AMENDED note fails the test as a malformed token. In notes, write the vocabulary forms with angle brackets (`grep:<path>::<symbol>`, `grep:<file>:<line>`), or write plain-text grep: without backticks. Name a retired or external path in a plain code span with no grep: prefix (e.g. `runtime/cli.py`). A deliberately kept unresolvable token needs an entry in that test's _KEPT_UNRESOLVED, keyed by (manifest file name, exact token), with a Kept reason: RETIRED, EXTERNAL or NOT_A_POINTER.

The orchestrator lint_command is `true` and mypy covers only src/solar_challenge_platform, so after deleting a helper you must remove its now-unused imports by hand. solar-challenge-platform gotcha: editing a PRD's *.capability-manifest.yaml after decomposition does NOT change any task's gate. commit_planning copied each check into the producer task's metadata.delivered_checks, and that stored copy is what the mark-done gate runs, so retarget it on the task record (fused-memory) too. For kind=grep, several `paths` are one `git grep -E -e <pattern> <ref> -- <paths...>`, so a match in any listed path passes and a path missing at ref is not an error. kind=path checks are conjunctive, every path must exist. To lint a check before committing it, run dark-factory's shared.delivered_check_polarity.lint_delivered_checks(checks, files=..., repo_root=..., ref='HEAD'). It flags a check that already passes at the authoring tree (vacuous_present).

solar_challenge_platform gotcha, measured 2026-10-18 by task 1194's implementer at main 17d9036: docs/prds/member-onboarding-consent-renewal.capability-manifest.yaml still lists, under δ1b (task 618), grep checks expecting `categories_for` PRESENT under src/solar_challenge_platform/optimiser (optimiser-reads-catalogue), and likewise for ingestion and billing. Task 618's own metadata.delivered_checks dropped all three per Leo's 2026-10-16 ruling, because S13 γ1/γ2/γ3 (tasks 1194/493/1195) route consumers through ConsentGate.decide(purpose) with no category set and forbid a categories_for name. So when `git grep <module> -- 'docs/prds/*.capability-manifest.yaml'` surfaces a check, confirm it against the owning task's metadata.delivered_checks (fused-memory get_task) before acting on it; the YAML can lag a ruling.

When authoring capability-manifest delivered_checks, every grep pattern must anchor to a symbol the PRD actually NAMES (a contract dataclass field, a constant, a CLI flag, a table name) rather than to guessed phrasing of code nobody has written yet. delivered_checks are copied into producer tasks' metadata.delivered_checks by commit_planning and become a live dispatch-time gate, so a pattern that guesses at wording fails a task agent that did its job correctly. Corollary established 2026-09-22 on the scaling-defects batch: prefer kind:manual over a weak or ambiguous grep (manual checks are recorded but excluded from the dispatch gate); and every expect:absent check must be re-run against HEAD at authoring time to confirm it has NON-ZERO hits today — an absent-check that is already zero-hit proves nothing about the leaf and should be re-anchored or downgraded. Final batch stats under this rule: 130 grep + 24 manual, of which 11 matched HEAD, 111 were zero-hit 'the leaf builds it' gates, and all 8 expect:absent checks had real hits today.

solar_challenge_platform gotcha (measured by task 1022 on a branch based at e4f2a2b, 2026-10-14): a task spawned from a /review-all finding cannot satisfy a plan check of the form "`git grep -n <deleted-name>` is empty". The generated reports plans/review-all-solar_challenge_platform-<date>.json and review/reports/review-solar_challenge_platform-<date>.json quote the finding's text, including the identifier it asks to delete, and stay in the tree (4 matches for all_present_hhs_below_floor). Scope the emptiness check as `git grep -n <name> -- . ':!plans' ':!review'` (rc 1 means no match), and leave those reports unedited: they are historical records, not code. Plans for review-derived deletions should word their verify step that way.

GOTCHA (solar_challenge_platform merge gate): this project sets no merge_verify_breadth, so the dark-factory default 'scoped' applies. When a branch's files and the main delta since its verify are disjoint, merge_gates._reverify_rebased_tree can advance main WITHOUT re-running tests. A rename in a shared test helper (e.g. task 397 renaming tests/_migrated_engine.py::migrated_engine's keyword remove_retention_policies -> pause_policy_jobs) therefore does not protect a sibling task's NEW call site in a different file: whichever lands second can redden main with a TypeError. When planning around an in-flight rename, make the new call site follow the branch's helper, re-check before the final verify, and flag the ordering to the steward (see esc-202-9).

solar_challenge_platform gotcha (task 1099 planning, 2026-10-14). The instance-reach rule of tests/test_private_names.py (PRD review-all-declared-package-strata §6.2) counts any call whose second positional argument is a private string literal, hasattr(obj, "_x") included. It also counts lookups inside f-string expressions, because those parse as AST code. A stream retiring an _AWAITING_PUBLIC_READ group must remove every such site, or the gate still sees the group and its entry cannot be deleted. For example, S5's _consent_guard group in tests/ingestion/test_consent_enforcement.py has 7 sites at 6791755, including hasattr at line 589 and an f-string at line 509. A receiver that resolves through the file's imports to a src module stays with the module rule, and bare self/cls is never a reach.

GOTCHA (solar_challenge_platform ops design-spec gate, since task 935): tests/ops/test_design_spec_binding.py resolves §9 identifiers against FOUR sources — ops/contract.py (AST + runtime sweep of imported dataclasses/enums), OpsSnapshot's constructor keywords, the ops router's wire keys (build_wire_vocabulary: string keys of every dict literal in api/routers/ops.py, read by AST, never imported), and PRD §9. The wire source is the only one carrying the flattened tick keys `shard_index`/`shard_count`, so a change that deletes or renames the router's dict-literal serializers (planned by task 1112) turns those §9 rows and the minimal fixture's `shard_index` row into phantoms until the spec and fixture are rebound. Separately: the brief's divergence sample lists devices most-recently-actuated first, because the route passes limit=ops_read_limit and read_fleet_divergence sorts by latest ts descending.

Gotcha for refactors that move code out of a file, observed 2026-10-12 in solar_challenge_platform (task 308's architect). Pending tasks' metadata.delivered_checks grep named files for literal strings. Tasks 213 and 214, for example, grep validation/run.py for drain_stall_seconds, VALIDATION_HOMES, compress_chunk, load_golden(ONE_MIN_GOLDEN), `def _settle_timeout_seconds`, --shard and refresh_tick. A split can silently empty such a check on a task that has not run yet, and its delivered-check gate then fails at merge. Before moving symbols out of a file, read the delivered_checks of every pending task whose files list names it (mcp__fused-memory__get_task, metadata.delivered_checks). Then keep the pinned strings in that file, or append a coordination note to the affected task's details.

Re-pinning capability-manifest grep pointers (tasks 771/772, solar_challenge_platform, 2026-10-03). An in-place pointer conversion cannot pass the insert-only word-diff check (mem 69249565). To prove that no claim, check type or verdict changed, split each `| ... |` table row on '|' into its 4 cells. Then assert that cells 1, 2 and 4 are byte-identical to `git show <base>:FILE`, and that only the cell-3 Evidence differs. Resolve `grep:<path>::<symbol>` tokens with stdlib ast: walk a ClassDef/FunctionDef/Assign/AnnAssign chain down the body lists. This needs no venv. Skip `<placeholder>` vocabulary tokens. A token without '::' must name an existing file. A nested closure (e.g. require_role's inner _dep) is not a dotted name, so point at the enclosing function. A pin into a module docstring has no symbol, so point at the definition the docstring describes (e.g. control/contract.py::SetpointState).

GOTCHA (delivered_check multi-path greps, found by task 344 on 2026-09-26): a kind:grep delivered_check with several `paths` runs as one `git grep -E -e <pattern> <ref> -- <paths...>`. It passes when ANY path matches. A pathspec for a deleted file matches nothing and raises no error. So when a later refactor retires one listed file, the check does not fail: it silently narrows to the surviving paths, and it only starts failing (holding dependents with dep_capability_not_delivered) when the last surviving match moves too. Example: task 173's "billing-service-takes-register-source" lists the retired runtime/cli.py, and it now passes only via api/routers/billing.py. When you retire or move a file, grep the *.capability-manifest.yaml sidecars and any pending dependents' producers' metadata.delivered_checks for its path. Re-point in the task metadata and the sidecar together (85a5397 precedent); a sidecar-only edit is drift that dark-factory scripts/audit_manifest_descriptor_drift.py reports.

GOTCHA (solar-challenge-platform): the dark-factory orchestrator's review checkpoint runs its Phase 1, the project test_command `uv run --extra dev pytest -m 'not slow'`, in the MAIN checkout /home/leo/src/solar-challenge-platform, not a worktree. Source: dark-factory review_checkpoint.py:167, run_full_verification(project_root, ...). It runs every review.interval merges (DF default 40), on idle full reviews and on exit, and writes data/review-checkpoints/review-<id>.json. So gitignored main-checkout state decides what node_modules- or dist-gated tests do there: frontend*/node_modules, frontend*/dist, and playwright in the shared .venv. A stale install or bundle turns the checkpoint red even when every per-task verify was green, because fresh worktrees have none of that state and skip. The fix is environmental (`npm --prefix <pkg> ci`, then a rebuild), not a code task (verified 2026-09-26 by task 321's architect).

CROSS-PROJECT PRECEDENT CORRECTION (verified 2026-09-18 during solar_challenge_platform task 183). The widely-cited "solar_challenge task 107 briefing-drift fix" did NOT land a pytest guard. Verified against /home/leo/src/solar-challenge main: `tests/unit/test_review_briefing.py` is ABSENT (git cat-file -e main:... fails), and the task-107 merge 3f4a1c1002850783480b6d52002fc30e6458639c changed exactly ONE file (review/briefing.yaml, +26/-16). The guard was added mid-branch (2b4c6a0, 61c57c4, eeb741c) then DELETED by b435273 — the task/107 branch tip, on main — to resolve two BLOCKING review issues: it was a prose meta-test that "covered nothing executable", was trivially bypassable (`2 in progress`, `96 total tasks`, `tasks: 96`, `eighty-five done` all slipped its `_TALLY_RE`), false-positived on innocent prose like `2 deferred gaps`, and was load-bearing on the drift text itself.

WHAT ACTUALLY LANDED as the durable mechanism: (1) delete the hand-maintained tally / stored PASS verdict outright; (2) replace with an explicit "NO TALLY IS STORED HERE — re-derive live via get_statuses(project_root=...)" instruction plus the drift history; (3) add a `# human-edited — ... preserve on regeneration` marker comment above each de-tallied block, which is the contract with the /review-briefing regenerator (briefing.yaml line 2 already declares "Human edits preserved on update"). Build/merge-time GENERATION was also explicitly considered and REJECTED in the landed text, because the task tree lives in a private untracked SQLite DB outside every worktree and outside CI — a generator would have to hardcode an absolute host path and parse another tool's private schema, and a merge-time hook belongs to the dark-factory orchestrator, not the repo.

SCOPE NUANCE worth copying: task 107 deleted the TASK-TALLY verdict (external, private-DB-derived) but deliberately KEPT the TODO/FIXME-marker verdict, softened with a "a fresh /review grep should confirm ... before relying on this" hedge — because an in-repo marker set is re-derivable by grepping the tracked tree, unlike a task tally.

Hypothesis: dark_factory design-rationale memory 89939e89-5159-4b9f-bd93-52bcfaece322 (and reconciliation finding b5505a02-f9c7-425d-8b0b-9024c419662d, run ca07417d, which seeded task 183) captured task 107's MID-BRANCH state rather than its merged state. Any future replication of this pattern into a sibling repo should plan the documentation edit + human-edited marker ONLY, and must NOT plan a tally-regex guard — it will be blocked at review for the same reasons it was in solar_challenge.

- 1097 greps `tests/test_package_strata\.py::`
