A `proposed` entry's Enforced by must therefore never contain a planned test's `path::name` node id or its function name. If one is written early, that task's check passes before its test exists. A planned clause names only the stream, a description and at most the planned file path.

99ca39d1-415b-435e-8196-75badda2918b.content: CONVENTION (task 346, 2026-09-26): tests/test_private_names.py is a repo-wide AST guard — no module under src/, tests/ or migrations/ may reach a leading-underscore name of a src module from outside that module (or, for a package's private names/submodules like runtime.roles._common, outside that package); it sees imports (every private path segment), attribute lookups through import bindings, setattr/getattr/monkeypatch.setattr/patch.object with a private string, and code inside any string constant mentioning `solar_challenge_platform` (subprocess scripts, dotted patch targets). Remedy is to promote the name by a rename with no alias/re-export, or re-seam the test onto public behaviour; a temporary exception goes in `_AWAITING_PROMOTION: dict[PrivateName(module, name), int task_id]` against a real owning task (never the current one), and self-expires — the guard fails, telling you to delete the entry, once the name is no longer reached. GOTCHA: because string constants are read as code, an AST-reader test's case table must spell a stand-in package (e.g. "pkg", as tests/test_entrypoints.py's roles guard does with "pkg.runtime.roles"), never a real `solar_challenge_platform.x._y` path as one string.

d1f55e3c-fb5d-40c7-9b66-423dcc8b4857.content: To bind a new ops-dashboard panel in docs/design/ops-dashboard.design-spec.md §9 (e.g. task 210's ingest tile), extend tests/ops/test_design_spec_binding.py in three places: REQUIRED_SURFACES, the _SURFACE_MAP header keywords (headers resolve by the LONGEST contained key via _surface_of, so a "Dispatch-liveness"/"Ingest-health" header never folds into plain "liveness"), and a section in _build_minimal_spec_text (the dropped-surface test is parametrized over REQUIRED_SURFACES and asserts exactly one surface disappears). Since task 435 the gate's vocabulary is ops/contract.py AST names ∪ the name and fields of every dataclass ops.contract exposes (so imported ones like DispatchTick count) ∪ OpsSnapshot's constructor keywords (the SSE snapshot keys, e.g. `dispatch`) ∪ the PRD §9 text. Every backticked simple identifier after the first ### header is checked, so a class that is not an ops.contract dataclass (e.g. OpsSnapshot itself) must stay unbackticked in row-group labels, or it reads as a phantom field.

ea7b90f3-bc37-44e2-90b1-a42606a6f183.content: Decompose/filing gotchas learned on the 2026-09-29 five-PRD batch (tasks 595-662): (a) commit_planning stamps ONE capability-manifest sidecar per call — when a batch spans several PRDs, flip everything once, then re-call commit_planning per PRD with that PRD's ids (statuses are a no-op, the sidecar gets stamped and its mechanical delivered_checks copied); (b) its lint REFUSES to copy a check whose pattern is the NAME of a file the leaf creates ("filename_shaped" — declare it kind: path, expect: present, paths: [the file]) and a presence check whose pattern already matches main ("vacuous_present" — assert something the leaf introduces, or make it kind: manual); (c) it warns "absent_overbroad" when an expect:absent pattern still matches a file outside the leaf's declared files (harmless if an upstream leaf deletes that file); (d) `kind: path` validates against CapabilityManifestDoc; (e) the path-scope lint flags prose too: "scenarios/known_gap/conventions" in a description produced metadata.possible_scope_mismatch (suggested_project solar_challenge) on task 652 — write "the scenario, known_gap and convention entries" instead, and treat any recon gate on that flag as a false positive; (f) update_task title/description/priority are replace-only — append coordination notes to `details` with append=true; (g) a decompose seat can and did find G6 dependency-direction defects the drafters' own DAG missed (12 across five PRDs) — keep the decompose walk even for well-critiqued PRDs.

candidates.content: Gotcha when splitting an L2 escalation cluster: resolve_issue on an L2, close_only included, cascade-resolves EVERY id in its members list (escalation/queue.py::resolve, resolved_by='l2-cascade:<id>'), even members belonging to OTHER tasks. If the L2 watcher mis-clustered another task's L1 into the L2 you are closing, first mint a separate L2 for that task with promote_to_l2 (task_id=<other task>, member_ids=[<its L1>], a distinct root_cause). Then close yours. The new L2 stays pending and keeps pinning the other task after the cascade closes the shared member. The resolve response's related_pending census then lists the surviving L2, which confirms the split worked.

Resolving an L2 escalation CASCADES the same resolution to every record in its `members` list, and those members can belong to OTHER tasks entirely. On 2026-08-17, resolving esc-3543-14 with action='close_only' also dismissed esc-3543-13, esc-4004-3, esc-3537-5 and esc-3980-6 — un-pinning tasks 4004, 3537 and 3980 whose specific failure mechanism had not been individually verified at the time of the call. The members list had also GROWN between first reading the escalation and resolving it (initially just esc-3543-13, later four entries), because the auto-watcher keeps attaching same-root_cause records to an open L2 parent. Practical consequences: (1) re-read `members` immediately before resolving, not from an earlier snapshot; (2) expect the cascade to release other tasks' `already-landed dispatch gate` pins, which means those tasks become re-dispatchable and will re-hit whatever they were failing on; (3) if the ruling is meant to cover them, gather the evidence for the whole member set before resolving, not just for the task you were sent to unblock.

Closing an L2 escalation whose subject task is already done: resolve_issue(action='close_only') maps to TaskEffect(target_status=None, WORKFLOW_NONE) in escalation/src/escalation/action_effects.py::ACTION_EFFECTS, so the task status is untouched; the record becomes 'dismissed' and EscalationQueue.resolve in escalation/src/escalation/queue.py cascades the same resolution text and resolution_class to every id in the record's `members` list with resolved_by='l2-cascade:<parent-id>' (verified 2026-09-08: esc-5050-3 was dismissed this way when esc-5050-4 was closed). resolution_class is validated against escalation/src/escalation/models.py::RESOLUTION_CLASSES = {benign, actionable, moot-terminal-subject, stale-strand}; there is no already_fixed, stale, fixed or wont_fix. 'moot-terminal-subject' is the class for "the subject task went terminal so the human decision no longer matters" and was created because 'benign' destroyed the evidence that a true positive existed; an unstamped human close_only is inferred as 'benign' at read time. The auto-watcher cannot close design_concern or risk_identified records at all (escalation/src/escalation/authority.py::l2_auto_close_class denylist) and the revalidation sweep's default allowlist is {task_failure, stranded_blocked}, so these always need a human ratification. A closed L2 cannot be re-filed by the reaper (it walks level-0 pending only) and reconciliation never files design_concern.

Resolving an L2 escalation CASCADES to its L1 members automatically — no second resolve_issue call is needed. Verified 2026-09-03: resolving esc-3476-2 (which carried members: ["esc-3476-1"]) left esc-3476-1 with status=dismissed, the identical resolution text, and resolved_by="l2-cascade:esc-3476-2". Also useful from the same session: escalation resolve_issue's action vocabulary maps as resume -> task stays in-progress, restart -> task reset to PENDING with disposition restart_from_scratch, park -> kept open at L2 and task blocked, abandon -> task cancelled, close_only -> record dismissed and task status UNCHANGED. Choose close_only when the workflow effect has already been applied by hand and you do not want to touch task status; note it marks the record 'dismissed' rather than 'resolved' even for a properly adjudicated ruling.

ORDERING TRAP when closing an L2 escalation cluster (learned 2026-09-21 on esc-4811-3): escalation/src/escalation/queue.py::EscalationQueue.resolve CASCADES an L2's resolution to every id in its `members` (resolved_by 'l2-cascade:<id>', same text, same dismiss flag) — no separate resolve of the member is needed, and a second explicit resolve on an already-cascaded member lands in `late_resolutions` rather than `resolution`. Consequence: the cascade removes the has_open_l1 shield under which orchestrator/src/orchestrator/harness.py::Harness._reap_orphan_l0_escalations DISMISSES the task's other pending L0 notes ("open L1 already covers this task"). So disposition any remaining pending L0 notes on the task FIRST, then close the cluster; otherwise the surviving L0 orphan-promotes into a fresh L1 and, for design_concern, a fresh L2 (skills/escalation-watcher-auto/SKILL.md routes every design_concern to promote_to_l2 with no info fast path).

Fact (2026-07-19): resolving an L2 escalation that has an L1 member (esc-2773-3 had members=[esc-2773-2]) with resolve_issue(action='restart') cascade-closes the member automatically — after resolving esc-2773-3, get_pending_escalations(task_id=2773) returned empty (both closed) without a separate resolve call on esc-2773-2. Also confirmed the resolve_issue action table in practice: action='restart' both marks the escalation 'resolved' (resolution_action='restart', audit-recorded) AND resets the task from blocked to pending in one call — the clean one-shot for 'resolve the escalation and re-pend the task'. The resolution text is stored for audit but NOT injected into any agent briefing for non-'resume' actions. Verified the returned resolution_action field equals the requested action (guards against the known bug where a trailing action after a long resolution silently defaults to resume).

An L1 escalation can be a MEMBER OF MULTIPLE pending L2 parents at once, and closing one parent silently orphans the others. Verified in dark-factory 2026-08-10 by reading the code: promote_to_l2 dedups on root_cause ALONE (escalation/src/escalation/queue.py:825 find_pending_l2_by_root_cause, called from server.py:1396-1397) and never checks whether the candidate's members already belong to another pending L2 — so two L2s with different root_cause strings can claim the same member L1. Resolution then cascades strictly DOWNWARD, parent -> members (queue.py:621-623, 708-730, stamping resolved_by='l2-cascade:<id>'; consumed at orchestrator/src/orchestrator/harness.py:12661-12668 and 13004-13020). Nothing notifies a SIBLING parent. Net effect: closing one L2 dismisses the shared member and leaves the co-parent pending with 100% of its members dismissed and no live signal — it then re-surfaces to humans indefinitely because the staleness detector re-derives it as "fresh" once its triage stamp ages past 6h. Two pre-existing memories state the ingredients separately ("the L2 parent cascade-closes all member L1s when close_only is applied", "L2 clusters use root-cause dedup"); it is their INTERACTION that is the defect. Concrete instance: esc-3713-9 was a member of both esc-3713-10 and esc-3713-12; closing esc-3713-10 stranded esc-3713-12 for 44h until an /unblock session closed it by hand. Filed into task 3587.

Confirmed (2026-06-04): resolving an L2 escalation with resolve_issue(terminate=False) when its task is ALREADY done does NOT re-pend the task — the running orchestrator's done/cascade-skip guard (commit 96634213e5) holds. For esc-1637-9 (L2, member esc-1637-8): resolving the L2 head cascaded to auto-close the member L1 (esc-1637-8 became resolved_by="l2-cascade:esc-1637-9"), get_pending_escalations(task_id=1637) went empty, and task 1637 stayed done. So for an already-done task, resolve_issue(terminate=False) on the L2 head is the safe one-call path: cascade closes members, no re-pend. (terminate=True is never needed here, consistent with the earlier correction that terminate=true never helps.)

Before closing an L2 escalation, run the CO-PARENT check — it is cheap and it is the known way closing one L2 permanently strands another. promote_to_l2 dedups on root_cause ALONE (escalation/src/escalation/queue.py find_pending_l2_by_root_cause, called from server.py), so one L1 can be a member of SEVERAL pending L2s with different root_cause strings; resolution then cascades strictly DOWNWARD (parent→members) and nothing notifies a sibling parent, leaving it pending with 100% of its members dismissed. Concrete check used successfully on 2026-08-10 before closing esc-3667-3: scan the queue dir for any OTHER pending record listing your target's members — `cd /home/leo/src/dark-factory/data/escalations` then for each *.json test whether `members` intersects your target's member list. esc-3667-3 came back the SOLE parent of esc-3667-2, so close_only was safe and the cascade dismissed the member as intended. Note the orchestrator queue lives at data/escalations/ and the reconciliation queue is a SEPARATE store at data/reconciliation/escalations/ — do not conflate them.

Escalation-queue mechanics observed while closing the task-4008 group, 2026-08-17. (1) SIX pending escalations existed for one task, all reporting the SAME finding: esc-4008-1 (L0, dismissed), -2 (L1), -3 (L2 blocking), and -4/-5/-6/-7 filed 08-16/08-17 — the L2 watcher had triaged the later four in "batch F" and designated esc-4008-7 the primary. Anyone ruling on a single escalation id should call get_task_escalations(task_id) FIRST: resolving only the record you were handed leaves near-identical siblings pending, and the group can have grown substantially since the record you were pointed at was filed. (2) Resolving a record that has a `members` array CASCADES to its members automatically — resolving esc-4008-3 (members: ["esc-4008-2"]) immediately dismissed esc-4008-2 with resolved_by="l2-cascade:esc-4008-3" and copied esc-4008-3's resolution text onto it. A separately-drafted resolution for the member is therefore wasted work: the cascade wins, and a later explicit resolve of the member does not overwrite it. Draft the parent's text to stand alone for every member.

Resolving an L2 escalation with mcp__escalation__resolve_issue CASCADES to its members automatically — do not resolve them individually afterwards.

Observed 2026-08-20 resolving reify's esc-markup-tripwire-7 (members: esc-markup-tripwire-6, esc-6221-2). A single resolve_issue(action='close_only') on the L2 dismissed all three within the same 3-millisecond window. The member records were stamped resolved_by='l2-cascade:esc-markup-tripwire-7' and received a COPY of the L2's resolution text; all three moved to data/escalations/archive/<date>/. A subsequent explicit resolve_issue call on a member is a no-op that returns the already-cascaded record — so any member-specific resolution prose written after the parent resolve is silently discarded. If a member needs its own distinct note, it has to be recorded some other way (or the member resolved BEFORE the parent).

Also worth knowing: resolution_class is a closed three-value enum — 'actionable', 'benign', 'moot-terminal-subject'. Passing anything else (e.g. 'superseded') fails with code=invalid_resolution_class and the whole resolve is rejected. A supersession closure is 'actionable' when it produced follow-up work.

Resolving an L2 escalation via mcp__escalation__resolve_issue CASCADES the resolution text verbatim to its member L1s, and all of them are archived out of data/escalations/ into data/escalations/archive/<date>/ in the same pass. Measured 2026-08-12: resolving esc-3223-5 (whose members were ["esc-3223-3"]) resolved esc-3223-3 at the identical timestamp with a byte-identical resolution body (both res_len 3498); resolving esc-3223-4 separately 17 seconds later did NOT overwrite esc-3223-3's already-set resolution. Practical consequences: (a) you do not need to resolve member L1s individually — resolve the L2 and the members follow; (b) when the SAME L1 has two L2 parents (co-parent orphaning), the FIRST L2 you resolve is the one whose text the shared member inherits, so resolve the more complete/authoritative L2 first; (c) after resolving, escalations disappear from data/escalations/ — a "file not found" there is the archived-success case, not a loss, so check archive/<date>/ before concluding anything went missing. Note also that a task transitioning to `done` did NOT auto-close these pending escalations, despite esc-3223-4 carrying a triage note saying it would be closable via stale_task_scoped once the task reached a terminal status.

POSITIVE DATA POINT on L2→L1 cascade: closing a single-parent L2 with action='close_only' DOES cascade-close its members. Counterweight to the known L2 co-parent orphaning failure mode.

Observed 2026-08-10 (dark-factory). esc-3206-3 was an L2 (agent_role='escalation-watcher-auto') carrying members=['esc-3206-2'], where esc-3206-2 was an L1 filed by harness-orphan-reaper. Resolving ONLY the parent — `resolve_issue(escalation_id='esc-3206-3', action='close_only', resolved_by='interactive', resolution_turns=3)` — left `get_pending_escalations(task_id='3206')` returning `[]`. The L1 member was closed by the cascade; no separate resolve_issue call on esc-3206-2 was needed, and it was NOT stranded.

SCOPE OF THIS EVIDENCE: this was the ONE-PARENT case (esc-3206-2 had exactly one L2 claiming it). It does NOT contradict the known co-parent orphaning defect, where root_cause-only dedup lets TWO L2s claim the same L1 member and closing one leaves the other stranded — the cascade goes DOWN only. Both facts hold: the downward cascade works, and it is the multi-parent case that breaks.

PRACTICAL RULE: after closing an L2 with members, always re-run `get_pending_escalations(task_id=...)` to confirm the member set actually cleared rather than assuming either outcome. That single call distinguishes the working single-parent cascade from a stranded co-parent member, and costs nothing.

GOTCHA — `resolve_issue(action='close_only')` is documented as "task-status effect: unchanged", but that is NOT reliable when the escalation you are closing is the SOLE remaining open escalation holding a task. On 2026-08-05, closing esc-3404-5 with close_only CASCADED its member esc-3404-4 shut (`resolved_by: l2-cascade:esc-3404-5`) and RELEASED task 3404 from `blocked` to `pending`. That was actively dangerous: 3404's plan.json read 13/13 done, so a dispatch would have run straight to VERIFY/REVIEW/merge and landed a branch that was still missing recovered work. ALWAYS re-read the task's status immediately after resolving an escalation, especially when the task's plan reads complete. To hold a task afterwards, prefer `deferred` over `blocked`: `blocked` with no open escalation is the "stranded blocked" state that unblock_auto and the stranded-blocked reconciler try to heal, whereas `deferred` is a quiet park that nothing auto-dispatches.

Observation: the escalation server's L2 cluster cascade is live and working. Resolving an L2 escalation via mcp__escalation__resolve_issue automatically closes its L1 member escalations — observed esc-1573-7 (L1) auto-resolved with resolved_by="l2-cascade:esc-1573-8" and inheriting the L2's resolution text when esc-1573-8 (its parent L2) was resolved. So an L2 watcher should resolve only the L2; members close via cascade.

What resolve_issue does for a BLOCKED task with no live workflow (traced 2026-09-11 for task 2917). action='resume' on an L2: queue.resolve archives the L2 and cascades to its member L1s (resolved_by='l2-cascade:<L2 id>'). Harness._on_escalation_resolved takes the orphan branch and calls _cascade_unblock_member, which checks status in {blocked, in-progress}, no live claimant, the re-block guard (3 repeats of the same failure) and a fresh re-read, then sets the task to pending. Members inherit the parent's action. Log line: 'cascade-unblock: task N flipped blocked→pending'. Neither the re-pend nor scheduler dispatch checks OTHER open escalations, but the reconcile sweep does hold escalation-pinned tasks, so close sibling records in the same sitting. action='close_only' changes no task status at the moment it runs, yet it is NOT a durable hold: scheduler._phase_redispatch_stranded_blocked (on by default) later flips a blocked task with no live claimant and no pending escalation to pending. release_workflow on an already-blocked task returns parked=null, which is expected.

ESCALATION MECHANICS confirmed by observation 2026-08-10 (resolving esc-3989-2). (1) `resolve_issue(resolution_class=...)` accepts EXACTLY three values — `'actionable'`, `'benign'`, `'moot-terminal-subject'`. Anything else is rejected with `{"error": "invalid resolution_class '<x>'; expected one of [...]", "code": "invalid_resolution_class"}` and the whole call fails, so the long resolution text has to be resent. Draft the resolution_class from that enum BEFORE composing a long resolution body. A task being cancelled as part of the resolution is still `'actionable'` — `'moot-terminal-subject'` is for a subject that was ALREADY terminal when the escalation was filed. (2) `action='abandon'` does BOTH halves in one call: the escalation record goes to `status='dismissed'` with `resolution_action='abandon'`, and the task is cancelled outright — verified, task 3989 went `blocked` -> `cancelled` with `updated_at` matching the escalation's `resolved_at` to the millisecond. No separate `set_task_status(cancelled)` is needed and issuing one would be redundant. (3) The L2 down-cascade works: esc-3989-2 carried `members: ["esc-3989-1"]`, and after resolving only the L2, `get_pending_escalations(task_id="3989")` returned `[]` — the member L1 was closed by the cascade. (Consistent with the known "cascade goes DOWN only" behaviour: resolving the L2 closes its members, but resolving a member would not close the L2.)

resolve_issue(action='resume') behavior confirmed 2026-06-30 on a normal task_failure escalation: resolving the L2 (esc-1933-32) with action='resume' cascaded to close its member L1 (esc-1933-31) AND re-dispatched the blocked task immediately (1933: lock_acquired→task_started within ~1s, then plan reused → execute no-op → verify). So for a normal blocked task whose L2 lists the L1 in `members`, resume alone re-dispatches — no separate set_task_status('pending') needed. (This differs from the older caveat that memberless born-at-L2 escalations don't re-pend.) NOTE the fused-memory escalation MCP tools (get_pending_escalations/resolve_issue) in a dark-factory session target the dark_factory escalation queue. Also, a bare resume only works if the branch is actually mergeable — if it was blocked on a fixable branch defect (e.g. uncommitted file), fix the branch FIRST, then resume, or it re-blocks.

NORM (dark_factory, established 2026-08-20): when an L2 cluster carrier has MIS-GROUPED members, close each mis-grouped member on its OWN rationale BEFORE resolving the carrier. Resolving a carrier CASCADES its resolution onto members — evidence: esc-3653-7 carries `resolved_by: "l2-cascade:esc-3653-11"` — so a member closed by cascade is stamped with a resolution about a defect it is not an instance of, and the mis-grouping signal is destroyed. Applied on 2026-08-20: esc-3653-12 listed FIVE members of which TWO (esc-3610-4, esc-4105-3) were `reason=no_citation`, a benign in-flight phenomenon, versus three `effect_absent` detector false positives; esc-4105-3 was closed first with its own predicate, then the carrier. SECOND REASON TO CLOSE PROMPTLY rather than letting a stale member sit: `file_unattributed_landing_escalation` calls `has_open_l1` with a BARE task id (landing_evidence.py:429) and `category=None` means ANY pending L1 suppresses every subsequent filing for that task — so a stale member blindfolds its task's whole escalation channel. It is also a latent pin: if the task ever goes `blocked`, the open record trips the `escalation_pinned` veto at scheduler.py:6355 and stalls recovery.

GOTCHA (dark-factory, verified in code while planning task 4377): closing an escalation is a STATE-CHANGING ACT ON ITS SUBJECT TASK, even under `action='close_only'` whose documented task-status effect is "unchanged".

MECHANISM. `orchestrator/src/orchestrator/task_ground_truth.py::_RECOVERY` is a dict keyed on (status, live_claimant, branch_state, has_open_escalation, deploy_phase), read through `.get(_shape(report), RecoveryAction.LEAVE)`. The shape (IN_PROGRESS, live_claimant=None, EXISTS_OFF_MAIN, has_open_escalation=True, deploy_phase=None) is ABSENT from the table, so it falls through to the default and the row is PRESERVED. Close the record and the boolean flips: the shape becomes the (…, has_open_escalation=False, …) row that IS in the table, mapping to REVERT_TO_PENDING. The veto sites read `report.open_escalations` directly (harness.py ~:6185 and ~:6274).

WHY THIS IS EASY TO GET WRONG. The preservation is an EMERGENT PROPERTY OF A MISSING TABLE ROW, not a declared rule — nothing anywhere says "this record is holding this task". `resolve_issue`'s own docstring table lists `close_only` -> "task-status effect: unchanged", which is true of the call mechanically and false of its consequence. `escalation/src/escalation/pins.py::classify_pins` answers only "does this OPEN record veto recovery?" (classification at recovery time) and protects nothing from being CLOSED.

WHAT IT COST. On 2026-08-08 an L2 cascade close of the 11-member cluster esc-3237-5 dismissed esc-3371-2, the only pin preserving mu-gate validation specimen task 3371; the task reverted to pending 879.6s later and the specimen is permanently gone. The closing watcher checked for harm and reasoned correctly within what it could see — none of the eleven was `blocked`, so no stranded-blocked shield was stripped. An orphan-reaper false-positive record and a deliberate pin are indistinguishable by id, level, category, severity, agent_role or content. The sibling pin esc-3105-3 (a 15-member L2 cluster head) is still the last hold on task 3105.

PRACTICE. Before closing any pending escalation on a non-terminal task — and before designating a homogeneous cluster for a bulk/cascade close — check the subject task's status and branch state, not just whether the record looks moot. Note `escalation/src/escalation/sweep.py` is a file-RELOCATOR (moves already-terminal records to the archive), not a closer, despite the name.

content: Before closing an L2 escalation with resolve_issue(action='close_only'), read its `members` list. The close cascades to every member, including another task's L1 that was misclustered into it. In the 2026-10-13 /unblock of task 6853, esc-6853-2's members were only ["esc-6853-1"], the same task, so the cascade was safe; afterwards related_pending came back [] and get_pending_escalations(task_id=6853) was empty. When a member belongs to a different task, split it out with promote_to_l2 before closing.

candidates.content: In reify, stale `crates/<c>/tests/**/*.rs` prose path citations are machine-gated by task #7095's one-directional ratchet: tests/infra/test_cited_test_paths_resolve.sh (--gate-only, <1s) against tests/infra/cited-test-path-baseline.manifest, with derivation in tests/infra/cited-test-path-lib.sh (`cited_test_path_scan .` lists every stale cite plus its suggested target). For any citation-repoint sweep, drain the relevant baseline rows first; the gate then reds naming every live site (a free RED test), repointing turns it green, and dead rows can be dropped freely. The regex anchors on `crates/`, so partial forms like `reify-compiler/tests/x.rs` are invisible to it.

Reify's cited-test-path ratchet (tests/infra/test_cited_test_paths_resolve.sh, --list prints a suggested target per stale citation) resolves by `<crate>/<basename>` only. Its suggestion is a basename hint, not proof: in task 5703 it pointed macros.rs's `corpus_shard_tests!` cite at harness_cache/snapshot_cache_divergence_gate.rs, but that macro had since been split into harness_corpus_gates/eval_invariant_corpus_sweep.rs. Units moved across crates (reify-eval → reify-eval-fea-tests) are not reported at all. Always grep the cited symbol in the suggested target before repointing.

reify's cited-test-path gate (tests/infra/test_cited_test_paths_resolve.sh) uses a ONE-DIRECTIONAL subset ratchet against tests/infra/cited-test-path-baseline.manifest: current findings must be a SUBSET of the baseline. So FIXING a grandfathered stale citation (repointing prose to the real crates/<crate>/tests/harness_<subsystem>/<file>.rs path) keeps the gate green with no baseline edit — the now-unused baseline row is harmless. That matters for scoped tasks, which usually do not hold a lock on the manifest. Note also its documented scope limit: a citation whose basename resolves NOWHERE (a deleted or renamed-away test) is deliberately NOT reported, so stale cites of vanished test NAMES must be caught by review, not by this gate.

Reify test-path citation resolution (measured 2026-09-16 on main af103dcc53): every test basename is UNIQUE within its crate across the whole tests tree — `git ls-files 'crates/*/tests/**/*.rs' | awk -F/ '{print $2"/"$NF}' | sort | uniq -d` yields zero duplicates — so `(crate, basename) -> path` is a deterministic index for resolving a stale `crates/<c>/tests/<stem>.rs` prose citation to its post-harness-consolidation target. Resolving by that index and emitting NOTHING when the basename matches nowhere is what keeps hermetic fixture paths (`crates/foo/tests/bar.rs`) and genuinely deleted files out of the finding set: of 257 unresolved cited paths tree-wide, only 149 are genuinely stale; the other 108 are fixtures or deletions.

Reify now HAS a gate for stale prose citations of moved test files. Task #7095 landed tests/infra/test_cited_test_paths_resolve.sh, a one-directional ratchet (live ⊆ baseline) over every `crates/<c>/tests/**/*.rs` citation in tracked files. Its scan is tests/infra/cited-test-path-lib.sh (`cited_test_path_scan .` emits file\tcited\tverdict\ttarget) and its grandfather list is tests/infra/cited-test-path-baseline.manifest. The sweep recipe used by task #6468: (1) delete that path's baseline rows with a filter, which gives RED; (2) repoint with an in-place sed, which gives GREEN. The gate's regex anchors on `crates/`, so a partial form like `reify-compiler/tests/x.rs` is invisible to it.

Reify's cited-test-path ratchet (tests/infra/test_cited_test_paths_resolve.sh + cited-test-path-lib.sh) validates PATHS ONLY, never line numbers: cited_test_path_fingerprint deliberately erases the line number ("never captured in the first place") so a citation moving within its file cannot spuriously red the gate. Consequence when repointing a stale `grep:<path>:<start>-<end>` citation after a test-file rename: fixing the path alone turns the gate green even if the line range now brackets a completely different test. Re-derive the range from two independent anchors (the `fn` line and a distinctive fixture line inside the body) and check the span length — the gate will not catch a wrong number for you.

Repointing a stale `crates/*/tests/**.rs` citation in reify prose has a ready-made TDD RED: delete that citation's row from tests/infra/cited-test-path-baseline.manifest, and the landed gate `bash tests/infra/test_cited_test_paths_resolve.sh --gate-only` exits 1 with `RATCHET REGRESSION — N live citation(s)`, naming each file and printing the exact repoint target after `->`. Repointing the citation makes it green. The ratchet is one-directional (live ⊆ baseline), so removing rows never reds it spuriously, and the manifest header sanctions hand-removal — "never by hand" governs deriving/ADDING rows only. No new test file is needed, hence no run-all-classification.manifest row and no nextest partition entry.

Stale crates/<crate>/tests/**/*.rs prose citations ARE gated in reify now. The 2026-08-31 observation that there is "no gate" is outdated. tests/infra/test_cited_test_paths_resolve.sh (task #7095) ratchets live stale citations ⊆ tests/infra/cited-test-path-baseline.manifest, and its `--list` flag prints (file, cited, verdict, suggested target) records. The sanctioned burn-down is two commits: first drain the rows from the baseline (RED), then repoint by running a literal substitution driven by `--list` (GREEN), as #6468 did (b376faca03, 1754c8d7e6) and #7501 does. The gate deliberately ignores citations whose basename resolves nowhere (deleted tests, fixtures, forward refs), so renamed-and-moved targets such as money_force_diag_tests.rs -> harness_units_materials/money_force_diagnostic_tests.rs need a manual check.

In reify, a repo gate that checks "every cited crates/<c>/tests/<stem>.rs path in prose resolves on the tree" is UNUSABLE as stated: of 820 distinct cited test paths, 230 do not resolve, and 108 of those are hermetic fixture strings living inside existing test source (crates/alpha/tests/foo.rs, crates/foo/tests/bar.rs, crates/beta/tests/thing.rs, ...) plus deleted files and illustrative examples. Only the harness-consolidation move class is actionable: cited path unresolved AND exactly one crates/<same crate>/tests/harness_*/<same basename> exists. Phrase the predicate that way rather than "flat path moved under harness_", so it also catches harness-to-harness re-moves from the #5620 over-cap SPLIT (live example: harness_fea_solver_e2e/stress_error_messages.rs is cited but the file now lives in harness_stress_scenarios/). A single `git grep -nIoE` pass over all 4161 tracked files costs ~1.1s, so whole-tree prose scanning is cheap enough for a merge gate.

Reify harness-split tasks (HARNESS_KLOC_CAP rule (a)): before choosing which modules to move, run the cited-test-path gate's own harvester to price each candidate cut — `source tests/infra/cited-test-path-lib.sh; cited_test_path_citations . | grep -F "harness_<sub>/"`. Its resolver keys on <crate>/<basename>, so moving a file inside the same crate's tests/ tree keeps it RESOLVABLE but makes the literal cited path untracked, which is a GATING stale finding unless the citation is repointed or baselined. On task #7466 the two candidate cuts of harness_occt differed by 13 broken citations vs 2 (across 4 crates and 5 PRD docs), which decided the split direction. Citations only count if they carry the `crates/` prefix — CITED_TEST_PATH_REGEX is 'crates/[a-z0-9-]+/tests/[A-Za-z0-9_./-]+\.rs', so a comment saying `reify-kernel-occt/tests/...` is ungated (but still goes stale and should be fixed).

Any reify task that MOVES a test file must run `bash tests/infra/test_cited_test_paths_resolve.sh` before considering the move done — a hand `git grep` sweep for citations is not sufficient. The gate (landed task #7095) is a whole-tree one-directional ratchet over `<citing file> :: <cited full path>` fingerprints, scanning tracked .rs doc comments, .md prose, .yaml manifests and .ri example comments alike; it prints each break with its exact repointing target after a `->` marker. Measured on task #5696: a manual stem-based grep found 4 of the 15 full-path citations a 24-file harness move broke, while the gate found all 15. Because the scan is whole-tree, a stale citation left on main re-fires for every unrelated task that later rebases onto that tip.

Reify citation convention for cross-file references after a test-file relocation into a consolidated harness dir: cite the FULL repo-relative path (e.g. `crates/reify-compiler/tests/harness_compilation_surface/examples_smoke.rs`) plus a symbol name, never a bare directory-relative prefix like `harness_compilation_surface/examples_smoke.rs` and never a `:<line>` number. The half-path form resolves from nowhere when the citing file lives in a different crate — e.g. `crates/reify-eval/tests/harness_corpus_gates/` — so it trades a wrong path for an unresolvable one. The cited-test-path gate (tests/infra/cited-test-path-lib.sh, CITED_TEST_PATH_REGEX = `crates/[a-z0-9-]+/tests/[A-Za-z0-9_./-]+\.rs`) only sees full paths, so half-paths escape the staleness ratchet entirely, and line numbers rot silently. This cost task 7015 two separate review amendments (341903acd2 for the .rs, 1a94998e5e for SKILL.md) after its own task description had literally suggested the half-path prefix. Two companion rules from the same task: replace a hardcoded line number with a symbol-name anchor rather than a refreshed number (one #5693-era relocation drifted three citations by three different magnitudes: 13→15, 636→426, 248→368), and never anchor a citation by quoting the cited comment's prose verbatim — nothing in the tree checks such a quotation, so it is an unchecked second copy that goes silently false on the next rewording.

tests/infra/test_cited_test_paths_resolve.sh only scans citations matching CITED_TEST_PATH_REGEX `crates/[a-z0-9-]+/tests/...\.rs` (tests/infra/cited-test-path-lib.sh). So a doc comment citing a test file WITHOUT the `crates/` prefix (e.g. `reify-compiler/tests/foo.rs`) is never checked and can go stale silently. Observed on task #7357: crates/reify-eval/src/modal_ops.rs cited the pre-#5694 path `reify-compiler/tests/modal_mechanism_compile.rs` long after #5694 moved that file into harness_mechanics/. When writing or repointing a test-file citation, use the full `crates/<crate>/tests/...` form so the gate guards it.

reify's cited-test-path gate (tests/infra/test_cited_test_paths_resolve.sh, task #7095) SUPPLEMENTS memory 0c1a520e-6eac-4ccd-9b3d-cb395148cb5e with its scan GRAMMAR, which decides whether a citation is guarded at all: CITED_TEST_PATH_REGEX='crates/[a-z0-9-]+/tests/[A-Za-z0-9_./-]+\.rs' (tests/infra/cited-test-path-lib.sh:53). Only the FULL repo-relative form is scanned — a bare stem (`examples_smoke.rs`) and, the non-obvious one, a HALF-PATH (`harness_compilation_surface/examples_smoke.rs`) both match nothing and are completely invisible to the gate. So when repairing a stale citation, writing the half-path looks like a fix, reads like a fix, and leaves the citation just as unguarded as the bare stem was; it is also unresolvable for a human reader whenever the citing file lives under a different crate. Measured first-hand on task #7015 (branch tip vs base main 362adf9bd3): the two files it repaired carried 0 guard-visible citations on base and 8 on HEAD (7 in crates/reify-eval/tests/harness_corpus_gates/best_practices_constraint_gate.rs, 1 in .claude/skills/reify-design/SKILL.md) — i.e. the repair's real payoff was moving citations from human-only to machine-enforced, and two review-driven amendment commits were needed precisely because the first drafts used the half-path. Pair this with the standing preference for symbol-name anchors (`foo.rs::some_fn`) over line numbers (`foo.rs:248`): line numbers are what rot, and nothing in the tree gates them (1890 `<file>.rs:<N>` citations across 452 tracked .rs files on that same tree).

Measuring stale prose citations of moved test files in reify: `git grep -ohE 'crates/[a-z0-9-]+/tests/[a-z0-9_]+\.rs' -- ':!*.lock' | sort -u` then diffing against `git ls-files` yields three distinct classes that must NOT be conflated. On main @ e15915432b: 456 resolve fine; 103 are stale AND resolve to exactly one crates/<c>/tests/harness_*/<stem>.rs (the CMP-*/C-eval-* harness-consolidation move class, mechanically fixable, zero ambiguity); 67 are stale with the crate present but no harness match (test deleted/renamed — no mechanical replacement); 25 cite crates that do not exist at all and are hermetic fixture literals inside reify-audit's own detector tests (crates/foo/tests/bar.rs, crates/alpha/tests/foo.rs) which must never be flagged. Only the 103 class is actionable. Those 103 span 170 files across .ri (82), .md (48), .rs (28) and .yaml (9), so any gate for this must be extension-agnostic, and its own fixtures must be built at runtime from shell variables or it flags itself.

Reify has NO gate validating `<path>:<line>` citations into `src/`: tests/infra/test_cited_test_paths_resolve.sh resolves only `crates/<crate>/tests/**/*.rs` PATHS, so a stale source line number in docs or a doc-comment rots silently through the merge gate. Measured case (task 7022): the `frame_to_frame` arm cite rotted 512 → 605 → stale-at-620 as the arm migrated 605→612→613→618→620, and the re-pin to `:605` landed already-stale in the very commit meant to fix the staleness, stamped `as of <date>`. Cite source locations by grep-able symbol anchor (e.g. `grep -n '"frame_to_frame" =>'`) instead of a line number; the capability-manifest yaml already models this with `delivered_check: {kind: grep, pattern: ...}` and `binding: grep:<path> <symbol>` clauses.

reify harness-layout, split checklist gap: a C1 harness split (`git mv` of modules from harness_<sub>/ to a new harness_<sub2>/) leaves cross-file doc-comment path cites dangling, and NOTHING gates them — no cite-resolution guard covers `crates/**/tests/harness_*/` paths, so test_harness_kloc_cap.sh, check-harness-baseline-registration.sh and cargo all stay green over dead pointers. Task #7365's 7-file split left 7 stale cites in 4 files (3 in crates/reify-eval-fea-tests/tests/persistent_cache_cross_session.rs, 2 in gui/src-tauri/tests/rpath_smoke.rs, 1 in tests/infra/test_no_new_wallclock_rust_deadlines.sh, 1 inside a moved file itself), most carrying line numbers into a path the reader cannot open. Sweep in the SAME diff as the move: `grep -rn 'harness_<sub>/\(<stem1>\|<stem2>\|...\)' --include='*.rs' --include='*.sh' --include='*.md' . | grep -v '^./target/'` — and beware stem prefix false positives (cli_cache matches cli_cache_concurrent_writers, which may legitimately stay). Prefer re-anchoring a cite to a bare module NAME over a path when the target is a sibling module in the same harness; that survives the next rename. Note the tension with the layout-only R100 invariant: editing a cite inside a moved file costs it R100 across main...HEAD, so make the move commit pure and put cite fixes in a separate commit, then verify purity with `git show --numstat -M100% <move-sha>` rather than at the branch tip.

Reify C1 test-harness consolidation (PRD docs/prds/merge-gate-compile-cost.md §5 C1, the CMP-*/EVAL-* leaf series): after `git mv`-ing standalone `tests/<stem>.rs` binaries under `tests/harness_<subsystem>/`, the stale-citation sweep must match TWO pointer forms, not one. Task #5694 (CMP-4) scanned only the full `crates/reify-compiler/tests/<stem>.rs` form, landed that fix, and then needed a second commit for SHORT-form `tests/<stem>.rs` citations it had missed (found in harness_constructor_typing.rs and harness_traits/trait_typed_param_tests.rs). Scan with `git grep -In "tests/$s\.rs"` and filter out the already-correct `harness_[a-z_]*/$s\.rs` hits, rather than grepping the full path prefix. Note these citations are prose/doc-comment only — no `#[path]`, `include_str!` or test filterset resolves them, so a miss is documentation debt, never a build break. Also expect most invalidated citations to live OUTSIDE the leaf's within-crate lock set (29 of 34 for #5694, in docs/, examples/, reify-eval, reify-compiler/src, reify-core); repointing those is a separate follow-up, since chasing them would widen the lock set across three crates and inflate the next leaf's rebase surface.

In crates/reify-eval/src/engine_edit.rs (edit_param/edit_source Contract-lock comment blocks), doc-comment citations to pinning tests by file PATH ("in `tests/tolerance_wiring_e2e.rs`") were stale the same way raw line numbers are: the real path is `crates/reify-eval/tests/harness_tolerance/tolerance_wiring_e2e.rs`, reachable only via `#[path = "harness_tolerance/tolerance_wiring_e2e.rs"]` in `tests/harness_tolerance.rs` — the bare `tests/tolerance_wiring_e2e.rs` never existed. A test-file path cite rots whenever tests get reorganized into a `#[path]`-based harness crate root; grep the actual `#[path = ...]` directive rather than trusting a cited path. Task 6479 (commit 5d754e74f0) fixed all four occurrences by dropping the path entirely and citing only the already-unique test function name, matching a no-path style the same paragraphs already used in one spot ("... plus `edit_source_clears_realization_cache_..._build` (step-19)." with no path) — i.e. prefer symbol/name anchors over any location pin, including file paths, not just line numbers. See sibling entry on task 6230/6479 line-number cite rot in the same file (mem0 id 671e9f88-2cfd-4f15-9903-dd55b0000312) for the line-number half of this pattern.

Reify has NO gate for stale prose path references to moved integration tests: the CMP-*/C-eval-* harness-consolidation series git-mv'd crates/<c>/tests/<stem>.rs into crates/<c>/tests/harness_<subsystem>/<stem>.rs, silently orphaning every doc-comment/PRD/manifest citation of the old flat path, and crates/reify-audit/src/ (p1/p2/p5/pdead/pdoccover/pdssentinel/player/ptodo/puntested) plus tests/infra/ contain no path-resolution check. Correction has been by manual sweep only — task #6214 (commit 276d32f025, 123 files) then task #6468 (60 files / 69 occurrences for the basename examples_smoke.rs alone) — and manual sweeps demonstrably do not converge: #6214 fixed tree-sitter-reify/test/corpus/io-formats.txt line 5 while leaving the same defect on line 7 of that header block, and fixed a capability-manifest .md without its .yaml twin. The sweep convention both tasks used is a pure path-segment insertion that preserves trailing :LINE numbers and ::selector suffixes verbatim, with a never-edit exclusion set of docs/architecture-audit/findings/*.md, docs/notes/*-2026-*.md and docs/legibility/confusion-codebook.yaml. The citation surface is wider than .rs/.md/.sh — live references also sit in .ri example header comments, .yaml capability manifests and tree-sitter .txt corpus headers — so any future scanner must be extension-agnostic over tracked files.

content: Reify's cited-test-path ratchet (tests/infra/test_cited_test_paths_resolve.sh via tests/infra/cited-test-path-lib.sh::cited_test_path_scan) flags a citation of crates/<crate>/tests/<x>.rs only when the cited path no longer resolves BUT a file with the same basename still exists under the SAME crate's tests tree (index key `<crate>/<basename>`). So moving a test file into a different crate's tests/ never reds that gate. Stale cross-crate citations go undetected and have to be fixed by hand. Moving a file within a crate (e.g. flat -> harness_*/) does red it unless the citation is repointed.

candidates.content: fused-memory update_task behaviour (seen 2026-10-17): a call that sets details with append=True and also sets metadata with metadata_mode='merge' is rejected as contradictory. append=True means an additive union, merge means a shallow overwrite, and the backend refuses to guess. To append details and replace one metadata key such as files in a single change, make two calls: (1) details with append=True and no metadata; (2) metadata with metadata_mode='merge' and no append. Also: calling get_tasks on solar_challenge returns about 4.8 MB and overflows the tool result. Use get_statuses with ids, find_tasks_by_metadata or get_task instead, or jq the saved file. Its task ids are integers in some fields and strings in others, so select with (.id|tostring)=="N".

fused-memory MCP task-tool quirks (observed 2026-06-16): get_task takes the parameter `id` (NOT `task_id`); search_tasks requires `project_root`; submit_task with planning_mode=True creates a task directly in `deferred` status synchronously and returns {task_id, status:"deferred"} (no ticket/resolve_ticket round-trip) — used for human decomposition so the scheduler can't claim tasks before sibling deps are wired; activate by set_task_status to `pending` (id accepts comma-separated for bulk). add_dependency depends_on accepts a bare integer (intra-project) or "project_id:task_id" (cross-project, lenient/unverified). update_task with append=True appends to details+metadata only (description/title always overwrite).

A decompose session that finds a step-1 target in progress with a live heartbeat should take a dependency edge on it instead of cancelling (ruled L36). /prd decompose mechanics that worked this session (my_solar_challenge / fused-memory): file each subtask via submit_task with planning_mode=true (lands directly as `deferred`, returns {task_id} synchronously — no resolve_ticket needed, curator bypassed so siblings aren't recombined). Then wire deps via add_dependency(id, depends_on) while still deferred. Then flip the whole batch deferred→pending in ONE bulk set_task_status(id="35,36,37,38,39", status="pending") call (comma-separated ids supported). Cancel a superseded placeholder via set_task_status(id, "cancelled"). Task ids are global and sequential — P1 got #35-#39 (the prior P2-P5 batch ran #16-#34). PRD files must be committed to main BEFORE/at decompose time because task agents run in worktrees branched from main. get_tasks output is large (~87k chars, exceeds tool limit) — query it with jq on the saved tool-results file instead.

A retry carrying the same metadata escalation_id + suggestion_hash was folded harmlessly: its ticket resolved status=combined, reason=idempotency_hit, onto the same task.

The safe recovery that worked: do not retry immediately; poll the store read-only by title, check get_status's started_at/uptime_seconds to detect a restart, and resubmit exactly once only after confirming no row exists, then re-query to confirm a single task. planning_mode submits bypass curator dedupe, so a blind retry risks a double-filing.

fused-memory tool quirks seen at the S8 decompose (2026-10-17):

candidates.content:
GOTCHA (design-spec §9 binding gates, e.g. tests/portal/test_design_spec_binding.py). Inside '## §9 data-binding', parse_binding_block treats every backticked token matching [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]* as a contract field, which must exist in the contract ∪ PRD-§9 vocabulary. Consequences:
- Backticking a rule or decision id such as `E8` or `D16` there turns the gate red as a phantom.
- Dotted or compound spans such as `EnergyTotals.self_consumption_fraction` are silently skipped, so they escape the check entirely.
- A row placed outside a '### <Surface>' header is never checked either.
Rule: reference fields in §9 by simple name, keep rule ids un-backticked, and assert that new identifiers appear in parse_binding_block(...)[surface].

GOTCHA (solar_challenge_platform docs, found planning task 827): the claude-design specs and their briefs nest the same material at different heading levels (spec panels/areas are `##` with `###` sub-sections; brief panels/areas are `###`), so a docsgen `quoted:` passage must hold no heading line. A spec section with numbered sub-headings is quoted one passage per sub-section, and those headings stay: code cites them (ops spec §4a in frontend RunsPanel.tsx, RunsPanel.test.tsx and tests/ops/test_design_spec_binding.py's failure message; admin spec §3.1 in tests/e2e/test_admin_portal_smoke.py; ops §2/§6/§7 in tones.ts, LivenessPanel.tsx, opsClient.ts and FleetHealthView.tsx).

GOTCHA (solar_challenge_platform docsgen, since task 821's amendment): a passage that docs/design/customer-portal.design-spec.md marks for quoting may hold no marker line of either kind (a whole line `<!-- quoted:NAME:begin|end -->` or `<!-- generated:NAME:begin|end -->`), and a passage name must be one character or more with no colon or whitespace. Otherwise `docsgen --check`/`--write` exits 2, naming the spec line, and QuotedPassages refuses such a name at construction. In tests, build marker lines with the public builders in src/solar_challenge_platform/docsgen/regions.py (begin_marker, end_marker, quoted_begin_marker, quoted_end_marker) instead of typing the format by hand.

Doc<->code congruence gates (test modules that scrape a code/PRD vocabulary and assert a markdown's backtick identifiers all appear in it) are only justified for HIGH-STAKES production surfaces — the sanctioned precedent is the billing-methodology money-correctness gate. Do NOT build such a gate for a `docs/design/*.design-spec.md` Claude-Design functional spec: those markdowns only feed Claude Design, so field-name drift merely mislabels a design mock (cannot corrupt data or break an API), making the ROI/risk profile inverted. Review rejected task 122's 862-line tests/admin/test_design_spec_binding.py as a `prose_meta_test`. Correct approach for a design spec: keep the spec's data-binding block as a hand-maintained reference, verify its field names ONCE against the landed §10 schemas at authoring time, and rely on the real schema tests + code review thereafter — no standing prose-pinning gate. Note the sibling tests/portal & tests/ops design-spec gates predate this ruling; treat new ones as rejected.

Design-spec tasks in solar_challenge_platform commit a FUNCTIONAL spec (docs/design/<area>.design-spec.md) PLUS a machine-checkable "## §9 data-binding" block, guarded by an executable congruence gate tests/<area>/test_design_spec_binding.py. The gate builds an authoritative vocabulary from landed contract files (AST-walk of dataclass/Pydantic field names + runtime enum .value members) UNION the PRD §9 envelope text, parses the spec's per-surface backtick identifiers, and asserts: (1) no phantom fields (every spec identifier resolves in the vocabulary — "no backend-absent field"), (2) all required surfaces present, (3) cardinal design-constraint vocab present, (4) anti-vacuity, (5) seeded-divergence ACTIVENESS (inject a phantom token / drop a surface → gate MUST fire) so it is never a no-op. This is the project's "adversarial doc↔code congruence gate" applied to design specs. P11 ops-dashboard set it (tests/ops/test_design_spec_binding.py, 9 passing); P10 customer/admin portals adopt it. It is a referential-integrity contract gate, NOT a docstring/prose meta-test.

GOTCHA (solar-challenge-platform portal wire, found planning task 521): tests/portal/test_design_spec_binding.py builds the vocabulary for docs/design/customer-portal.design-spec.md's §9 block ONLY by AST-reading seven files: portal/contract.py, schemas/{billing,consent,account,property,device}.py, api/routers/auth.py (plus the PRD §9 text). So a model nested in StatementOut but declared elsewhere (e.g. reusing schemas/config.py::FleetFinanceValuesOut) makes its field names fail the gate once the spec names them. Declare the nested wire type in schemas/billing.py (task 521 does this with StatementRatesOut) rather than widening the gate's CONTRACT_PATHS.

GOTCHA (solar_challenge_platform docsgen, found planning task 438): ADDING a new quoted passage to a design spec takes four edits in ONE commit, more than editing an existing one. (1) Put whole-line `<!-- quoted:NAME:begin/end -->` markers in the spec. (2) Add NAME to that pair's QuotedPassages names tuple in document order, e.g. src/solar_challenge_platform/docsgen/ops_passages.py. (3) Add an empty `<!-- generated:NAME:begin -->`/`<!-- generated:NAME:end -->` region to the brief under a hand-written heading. (4) Run `uv run --extra dev python -m solar_challenge_platform.docsgen --write`. If you skip (2), QuotedPassages.bodies raises "the source must mark a passage for each region named and no other, but marks passage 'NAME'", and tests/docs/test_brief_passages.py goes red. fused-memory harness test gotcha (task 2708): when a fire-and-forget asyncio task is tracked in a set via `s.add(task); task.add_done_callback(s.discard)` (the `_judge_tasks`/`_spawn_judge` pattern in reconciliation/harness.py), a test asserting the set is non-empty AFTER the spawning coroutine returns will FLAKE/FAIL if the task body is a no-op `AsyncMock()`: the task completes during a later `await` inside the caller and its done-callback discards it from the set before the assertion runs. Fix: patch the task body with a blocking Event-gated coroutine (`async def _blocking(run_id): await never_set.wait()`) so the task stays observably in the set; assert, then `task.cancel()` + `await asyncio.gather(*s, return_exceptions=True)` to clean up. Also: assigning such a stand-in to a typed method attribute (`harness._run_judge = _blocking`) requires the stand-in's parameter name to MATCH the real signature (`run_id`, not `_run_id`) or pyright flags reportAttributeAccessIssue (parameter name mismatch); ruff here does not lint unused args (select=E,F,UP,B,SIM,I — no ARG), so a matching-but-unused param is fine.

GOTCHA (dark-factory, measured 2026-09-06, task 4592): PRODUCTION code that calls a method on a value which may be a mock ATTRIBUTE takes a silently-wrong branch AND leaks a coroutine. Distinct from the existing AsyncMock memories, which are all about test-side mock CONFIGURATION (side_effect shapes, pyright narrowing of .await_args); this one is about defensive shape checks in production code.

THE SHAPE. `recon_config_base_dir(data_dir)` guarded with `if not base.is_absolute(): base = Path.cwd() / base`. The recon stage suite drives BaseStage with an `AsyncMock` journal, so `journal.data_dir` is an AsyncMock, and `AsyncMock().data_dir.is_absolute()` returns a COROUTINE — not a bool. Measured: truthy, so `not <coroutine>` is False and the branch is skipped. Two consequences, only one visible:
- The branch decision was made by the truthiness of a coroutine object, not by any property of the path. It happened to select the safe branch here; nothing guarantees that in general, and an inverted guard would silently do the wrong thing.
- The coroutine is never awaited, so CPython emits `RuntimeWarning: coroutine 'AsyncMockMixin._execute_mock_call' was never awaited`, pointing at the PRODUCTION line, not the test.

Note MagicMock does NOT reproduce it (`MagicMock().data_dir.is_absolute()` returns a MagicMock, no coroutine), so a test parametrized only over MagicMock — the convenient default — cannot see this at all. Parametrize over `(MagicMock, AsyncMock)` when the suite actually uses AsyncMock.

THE FIX SHAPE: type-guard before calling, `if isinstance(base, PurePath) and not base.is_absolute():`. Verified `isinstance(AsyncMock(), PurePath)` is False, so a duck type is left uncoerced AND uncalled. This is strictly better than `Path(base)` coercion, which is worse than useless here: MagicMock and AsyncMock both implement `__fspath__`, so `Path(mock)` silently yields the RELATIVE path `AsyncMock/mock.data_dir/<id>` which downstream `mkdir(parents=True)` then really creates, littering the repo on every suite run.

candidates.content: fused-memory commit_planning REWRITES the /prd YAML capability-manifest sidecar with yaml.dump when it stamps task ids — reflowing quoting and line wrapping. Consequence observed in reify 2026-08-27: any later edit to that sidecar by exact-string matching against the text you originally wrote will FAIL to match. Edit a stamped sidecar STRUCTURALLY instead — yaml.safe_load, mutate the dicts, yaml.dump(..., allow_unicode=True, sort_keys=False, width=88) — which is consistent with how commit_planning itself maintains the file. Two related mechanics from the same session: commit_planning stamps only the labels whose task ids are in the batch you flip, and calling it again on an already-deferred task with target_status=deferred returns {"success": true, "no_op": true} and stamps NOTHING (hand-stamp that label instead); and it copies only MECHANICAL delivered_checks (kind grep/script) into producer metadata.delivered_checks — kind: manual checks stay sidecar-only and are excluded from the dispatch gate, so a binding added to the sidecar AFTER commit_planning has run will never reach task metadata.

TWO /prd DECOMPOSE-TIME TOOLING GOTCHAS hit in the reify P1 driver-parity session, 2026-08-26.

1. `commit_planning` DID NOT AUTO-STAMP the capability-manifest YAML sidecar. All 15 `task_id:` entries stayed `null`, and the tool result carried NO manifest disposition at all (no `missing_labels`, no stamper line — just the 16 per-task status flips). The reify /prd overlay documents commit_planning as stamping the on-disk sidecar in place and warns "Never land an unstamped sidecar and stamp afterwards", so a session that trusted the automation would have landed an unstamped sidecar silently. Likely cause: the stamper keys on a `metadata.label` field that the filed leaves did not carry (the leaves DID carry `metadata.prd_path`, which was evidently not sufficient). WORKAROUND USED: verify with `grep -n "task_id:" <sidecar>` immediately after commit_planning and hand-stamp the label->id map before committing. ALWAYS CHECK — do not assume it fired.

2. YAML capability-manifest sidecars MUST QUOTE their `binding:` scalars, because a task reference of the form ` #6665` is parsed as the START OF A YAML COMMENT and silently truncates the line, producing a parser error further down (or, worse, a quietly truncated binding). This is why the committed exemplar sidecars carry single-quoted binding strings — that is yaml.dump's output, not a style choice. When hand-authoring a sidecar, either quote every binding or round-trip it through yaml.safe_dump before committing, then validate by loading it and asserting no binding ends mid-sentence.

PLANNING-MODE FILING GOTCHA (reify/dark-factory, verified across four batches 2026-08-26): commit_planning's capability-manifest stamper auto-stamps sidecar task_ids ONLY when each leaf's metadata carries the key `prd_task_label` whose value matches the sidecar yaml `label:` BYTE-FOR-BYTE (Greek `γ`, not Latin "gamma"; not the near-miss key `prd_label`). When zero leaves carry the key, the stamper SILENTLY skips — no manifest_stamping block in the result at all — so a session trusting the automation lands an unstamped sidecar. Three of four independent planning sessions missed the contract in one evening (P1: no key; P3: wrong key + Latin form; only P2 and the IVF-κ filing got it right). Until DF #4628 lands the loud disposition: always include metadata.prd_task_label on every planning-mode leaf AND verify the commit_planning result's manifest_stamping block reports stamped==N — silence is not success.

Build the doc as a Python dict (prd, schema_version, tasks[{label, task_id, title, capabilities[{name, binding, verdict, delivered_check}]}]), dump, and verify round-trip stability (safe_load→safe_dump byte-identical). Validate against the schema with dark-factory's venv: cd /home/leo/src/dark-factory && uv run python -c "from shared.capability_manifest import load_capability_manifest; ..." (system python fails: shared/__init__ imports aiosqlite). Worked for the indexed-sub batch: commit_planning stamped all 11 labels and git cmp confirmed the on-disk sidecar byte-identical to the pre-stamped landed copy.

PRD decompose sidecar-stamping gotchas (learned the hard way 2026-08-27, damped-modal batch): (1) commit_planning's YAML sidecar stamping fails on TWO silent YAML traps in hand-written .capability-manifest.yaml files: an unquoted `: ` (colon-space) inside a plain binding/reason scalar aborts the whole stamping pass with "mapping values are not allowed here" (the flip itself still succeeds — tasks go pending with NO stamped ids and NO delivered_checks copied); and a bare ` #NNNN` (space-then-hash) inside a plain scalar is parsed as a YAML COMMENT — the tail is silently dropped and the stamper's re-dump bakes the loss into the file. Quote any scalar containing `: ` or ` #` with single quotes ('' to escape internal quotes); parenthesized `(#NNNN)` is safe (no space before #). Validate with python3 yaml.safe_load before the flip. (2) RECOVERY: re-running commit_planning on already-pending ids is SAFE — each task returns {success, no_op:true} and the manifest_stamping pass re-runs fully, stamping all labels; no hand-stamping needed. (3) Read the response's manifest_stamping block ({stamped, missing_labels, errors}) every time — a green flip with an errors entry means an unstamped sidecar. (4) After stamping, diff-check plain scalars for comment-eaten tails before committing.

PROCEDURAL facts about commit_planning's sidecar stamping learned 2026-07-25 (stdlib-namespace decompose): (1) if manifest_stamping errors (e.g. YAML parse failure from an unquoted ` #` starting a comment mid-scalar — 'boundary #12/#14' truncated the value and orphaned its continuation line), the batch status flip still succeeds; fix the YAML and simply RE-CALL commit_planning with the same already-pending ids — each returns no_op:true for status but the stamper runs and stamps successfully; (2) stamping is idempotent — a later commit_planning on a subset (e.g. re-pending parked tasks) harmlessly re-stamps the same ids; (3) the stamper rewrites the sidecar on disk in canonical yaml.dump form, so quote EVERY plain scalar containing '#' before first submission. Delivered_checks copy to producer metadata was verified working (grep checks appeared on task 5494's metadata.delivered_checks).

PRD CAPABILITY-MANIFEST SIDECARS CAN SILENTLY FAIL SCHEMA VALIDATION, AND THE TASK-STAMPING STEP THEN SKIPS THAT PRD WITHOUT ANYTHING ENFORCING IT.

Discovered 2026-07-28. `commit_planning` returns a `manifest_stamping` block; for docs/prds/merge-gate-compile-cost.capability-manifest.yaml it came back with `stamped: []` and 8 pydantic errors against `CapabilityManifestDoc`: `schema_version` and `tasks` required-but-missing, plus `program_milestone`, `batches`, `revived_re_premised`, `cross_prd_deps`, `manual_checks`, `bindings` all rejected as "Extra inputs are not permitted".

ROOT CAUSE: the file is an OLD hand-stamped interim format (its own header says "hand-stamped, interim per overlay", dated 2026-07-19) that predates the schema now enforced. 19 sidecars exist under docs/prds/ and docs/prds/v0_6/; several already carry `schema_version`, so this is per-file drift, not a global format change awaiting migration.

CONSEQUENCES: no task filed against that PRD gets a manifest binding, and the sidecar's own `batches.reify` task list silently goes stale (it was missing the four CMP-3..6 leaves filed the same day). Combined with the known heuristic that a manifest leaf with NO producer:task binding reads as a false-premise tell, a whole PRD's worth of unstamped leaves can be mis-diagnosed downstream.

HOW TO CATCH IT: the errors appear ONLY in the `manifest_stamping.errors` array of the commit_planning response. Nothing gates on them, no escalation is filed, and the tasks are created successfully regardless — so the failure is invisible unless you read that field. Read it after any planning_mode batch commit.

A PRD capability-manifest sidecar is stamped into task metadata by commit_planning only if the leaf task's metadata carries BOTH `prd_path` and `prd_task_label` (that exact key). A leaf that instead carries `prd_label` is silently skipped by the stamper, so its sidecar delivered_checks are never copied and the dispatch gate evaluates nothing — with the sidecar's `task_id` fields still looking populated if they were filled in by hand. Measured on docs/prds/v0_6/solution-set-completeness.capability-manifest.yaml (2026-09-03): all ~14 leaves #6706-#6719 use `prd_label` and none has a `delivered_checks` key in metadata.

commit_planning sidecar stamping gotchas (observed 2026-07-24): (1) the stamper RE-SERIALIZES the capability-manifest YAML on write-back — comments dropped, quotes removed, long lines re-wrapped — so a pre-stamped landed sidecar will textually differ from the post-stamp working copy while being semantically identical; no re-landing is needed, discard the rewritten copy. (2) YAML comment hazard: an UNQUOTED scalar containing " #NNNN" (task cite) is truncated at the "#" by any YAML parser — e.g. a manual delivered_check reason "asserted by e2e on the #5386 repro shape" parses as "asserted by e2e on the". Always single-quote binding/reason strings containing #task cites in capability-manifest YAML sidecars.

`commit_planning`'s capability-manifest sidecar stamping VALIDATES the YAML against a strict pydantic schema and silently declines to stamp on any extra key — the flip still succeeds, so it is easy to miss.

MEASURED 2026-09-01 (reify, assembly-modal decompose): the first `commit_planning` call flipped all 14 tasks deferred->pending with `success: true`, but `manifest_stamping` carried `stamped: []` and an error listing 8 pydantic `extra_forbidden` violations — I had added a `note:` key to several capability entries. `CapabilityManifestDoc` (shared/src/shared/capability_manifest.py) forbids extra inputs.

PERMITTED KEYS, confirmed by a clean stamp afterwards:

Capability-manifest YAML sidecar trap (hit 2026-08-31, result-field-vacuity decompose): a bare task cite like " #7079" inside a PLAIN (unquoted) YAML scalar starts a YAML COMMENT — space-hash is a comment introducer in plain scalars — truncating the value and usually breaking the parse on the continuation line. commit_planning's manifest stamper then reports the parse failure only inside manifest_stamping.errors while the deferred→pending FLIP still SUCCEEDS, so the batch goes live with an unstamped sidecar and, critically, NO delivered_checks copied into producer task metadata (the dispatch gate reads metadata.delivered_checks, not the file). commit_planning gotcha (2026-09-30, task 8012): when a PRD's evidence files (probe sets, README rows) are landed AHEAD of decompose — e.g. by a docs vehicle — any delivered_check in the manifest that asserts their presence becomes VACUOUS ("ALREADY matches the authoring tree at main ... gates nothing") and commit_planning REFUSES to copy it into the producer task's metadata while still flipping the batch to pending and stamping the other checks. The task is then gated only by its remaining checks, but the manifest .yaml/.md twins still list the refused check — the three surfaces (yaml, md twin, task metadata) drift. Fix: delete the vacuous check from both twins in the producer leaf's own diff and rewrite the leaf's description so it does not re-do the pre-landed deliverable (leaf 8012's text originally told the agent to create six probe-set files that were already on main). General rule: a sound delivered_check FAILS at the authoring tree and PASSES once its producer lands; assert a symbol the leaf INTRODUCES.

Bulk-filing a /prd decompose batch exactly (worked 2026-10-11, M-WASTE, 18 long task texts):

Behaviour observed on readback:
- metadata.execution_class='decision' leaves are converted at submit to task_kind='deterministic' plus always_escalates=true.
- An add_dependency client_op_id makes the edge writes idempotent.

For delivered_checks:
- Use kind='path' to assert that a new file exists. A grep for a filename never goes green.

Completed: Pass the claude-code backend's prompt on stdin: a transcript over 128 KiB exceeds Linux's per-argument limit (claude_code.py::ClaudeCodeScopingModel._run)
Description: Found while planning task 8 (translate backend failures at the ScopingModel seam). src/scoping_intake/claude_code.py::ClaudeCodeScopingModel._run passes the whole prompt (NEXT_MESSAGE_INSTRUCTION plus transcript_document(transcript) for a reply, or transcript_document(transcript) for an analysis) as ONE argv element after `-p`. Linux caps a single argument at MAX_ARG_STRLEN = 32 pages = 131,072 bytes on this host (PAGE_SIZE 4096), while intake.py allows a transcript of up to MAX_TRANSCRIPT_CHARS = 300,000 characters. Measured 2026-10-08 with the worktree's Python: subprocess.run(['/bin/true', '-p', 'x' * 140_000]) raises OSError errno 7 'Argument list too long'; 100,000 characters succeed. So once a claude-code trial session's transcript document passes roughly 131 KB, every reply, retry and write-up fails with OSError(E2BIG). That error escapes the seam untranslated and the prospect page shows the generic 500 'Something went wrong on our side'. The session cannot recover, because retrying resends the same transcript. The other long arguments are small: analyst prompt 16,828 bytes, interviewer prompt 12,364 bytes, record schema JSON 8,556 bytes.
Analysis: ## Current state (base 57ecf41, task 8 merged; 59 tests green, measured in this worktree)

- `src/scoping_intake/claude_code.py::ClaudeCodeScopingModel._run` builds the command `[executable, "-p", prompt, "--system-prompt", system_prompt, "--tools", "", "--restricted", "--model", model, "--output-format", "json"]`, adding `"--json-schema", schema` for an analysis.
- It then calls `subprocess.run(command, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=..., cwd=..., env=..., check=False)` with no stdin, so claude inherits the server's stdin.
- `reply` passes `f"{NEXT_MESSAGE_INSTRUCTION}\n\n{transcript_document(transcript)}"` and `analyse` passes `transcript_document(transcript)`.
- `intake.py` lets a conversation grow to MAX_TRANSCRIPT_CHARS = 300,000 characters, in messages of at most MAX_MESSAGE_CHARS = 20,000.

## Facts measured for this plan

1. **The argument limit.** With 4096-byte pages, an argument of 131,071 bytes runs and one of 131,072 bytes raises OSError errno 7 (E2BIG) in the parent, before the child starts. A 300,000-character transcript gives a 300,056-character document and a 300,179-byte reply prompt.
2. **`claude -p` reads its prompt from stdin.**
   - `claude --help` (2.1.294) gives the usage as `claude [options] [command] [prompt]`.
   - `-p, --print` is a flag ("Print response and exit (useful for pipes)"), so the prompt is the positional argument, not the value of -p.
   - `--input-format` is "(only works with --print): text (default), or stream-json".
   - The installed binary was also read statically with grep -a and dd. Nothing was executed and nothing was spent.
   - Its getInputPrompt reads stdin when stdin is not a TTY. It decodes it as UTF-8 (`process.stdin.setEncoding("utf8")`) up to 10 MiB. Once data arrives it waits for EOF; its 3-second timer fires only when no data arrives at all.
   - It returns `[promptArgument, stdin].filter(Boolean).join("\n")`. The no-input error reads "Input must be provided either through stdin or as a prompt argument when using --print".
   - So with no positional prompt, claude's prompt is exactly what we write to stdin.
3. **No hang in the RED run.** Under pytest's default fd capture, which verify uses through plain `uv run pytest`, a child's fd 0 is /dev/null (measured). A stand-in that reads stdin therefore gets '' at once against today's code.
4. **Throwaway-copy trial.** The setup: `git archive HEAD` into /tmp, run with PYTHONPATH=<copy>/src.
   - With the planned test file, today's code fails exactly two tests, in 2.6 s: the reply test, because stdin is '', and the new long-conversation test, with OSError [Errno 7] Argument list too long.

Completed: Frozen-surface lock: flipping a pinned dataclass's frozen flag (or order/eq) is caught by no guard (fails open)
Description: Agent follow-up found while planning task 550 (escalation id agent-followup-550). OUT OF SCOPE for task 550. That task makes tests/_surface_forms.py's member_forms spell a dataclass field its constructor does not take, e.g. field(init=False), as 'attribute <annotation>', so FROZEN_MEMBERS can pin it.

FINDING. Observed 2026-10-07 on main 460f9a1 by reading the code and grepping:
- tests/unit/test_public_api_surface.py pins each exported or FROZEN_CLOSURE class two ways. FROZEN_SURFACE and FROZEN_CLOSURE pin its constructor signature (tests/_surface_forms.py::surface_form). FROZEN_MEMBERS pins its public members (member_forms).
- member_forms spells whether a property can be set or deleted, e.g. 'property[settable, deletable]'. Nothing spells whether a dataclass's fields can be assigned: @dataclass(frozen=True) versus frozen=False appears in no form.
- grep finds no __dataclass_params__ or FrozenInstanceError in tests/_surface_forms.py, tests/unit/test_public_api_surface.py or tests/unit/test_init_lazy_surface.py.
- Precedent: task 436 made home.SimulationResults frozen. docs/domain-library-consumption.md records this by hand as a break: 'Assigning to one of its fields, such as results.demand = series, raises dataclasses.FrozenInstanceError; the 0.5.0 tag accepts the assignment.' No guard asked for that note.

CONSEQUENCE. Any of the 34 pinned dataclasses (26 in solar_challenge.__all__ plus the 8 FROZEN_CLOSURE classes) could flip frozen, and every guard would stay green. Turning frozen on breaks consumers that assign fields. Turning it off drops the immutability and hashability consumers rely on. Yet review/briefing.yaml's frozen-API rule treats a change to a public member as a breaking change that needs an 'Unreleased on main' line. The same holds for the other dataclass parameters that change public behaviour: order=True adds <, <=, > and >=, and eq and unsafe_hash change equality and hashing.

DECISION NEEDED FIRST. Task 404's rule, pinned by tests/unit/test_surface_forms_helper.py::test_private_and_dunder_names_are_not_members, deliberately keeps dunders out of member forms. frozen, order and eq appear only as generated dunders (__setattr__, __delattr__, __lt__, __eq__, __hash__). So first decide whether a dataclass's parameters belong to the frozen surface. If they do, decide where to spell them. One option is to prefix a dataclass's class form with its non-default parameters, which changes every FROZEN_SURFACE/FROZEN_CLOSURE value of a frozen dataclass. Another is a separate pin. Then add a rule test in tests/unit/test_surface_forms_helper.py and edit the tables in tests/unit/test_public_api_surface.py. Follow the 'Tag / release convention' section of docs/domain-library-consumption.md on whether a release note is due when the contract widens; tasks 426 and 505 each added one.

How to witness the validation-cadence alert path on demand, when no lane is naturally red: add a temporary systemd drop-in to one pytest lane that makes pytest fail with a usage error, e.g. ~/.config/systemd/user/scp-validation@dropped-readings-drill-weekly.service.d/force-red.conf containing "[Service]\nEnvironment=PYTEST_ADDOPTS=--scp-forced-red-alert-witness".
Then run daemon-reload and `systemctl --user start scp-validation@dropped-readings-drill-weekly.service`. The lane goes red (exit 4), and OnFailure runs scp-validation-alert@<lane>, which files the born-at-L2 urgent escalation esc-validation-cadence-<lane>-N within about 1 s.
Clean up afterwards: delete the drop-in, run daemon-reload and reset-failed, re-run the lane green, and close the test L2 with close_only.

Single-instance-at-a-time for the slow-lane cadence is enforced at the PROCESS level via a non-blocking fcntl.flock lockfile (single_instance_lock + AlreadyRunning + a --lock-file CLI arg on ci/slow_lane.py main()), so overlapping merge/cron trigger invocations cannot run the heavy pvlib/backtest/timescale/modbus/mqtt_tls lanes concurrently. run_slow_lane only serializes lanes WITHIN one process — it does not guard against two processes.
