ROOT CAUSE (measured, task 7630) of the recurring GUI-vitest merge-gate flake `[vitest-worker]: Timeout calling "fetch"` — supersedes the "suspected/unverified" note in the esc-7431-3 triage memory. The bound is birpc's DEFAULT_TIMEOUT = 6e4 (60s) on the WORKER->HOST channel (vitest/dist/chunks/index.*.js:3, armed only when `timeout >= 0`), NOT testTimeout — which is why 3185's and 4856's per-test-site bumps could never fix it. It is UNREACHABLE by config in vitest 3.2.4: createForksRpcOptions returns only {serialize,deserialize,post,on}, and the public type excludes it deliberately — `WorkerRpcOptions = Pick<BirpcOptions,"on"|"post"|"serialize"|"deserialize">` (dist/workers.d.ts:23). No VITEST_* env var covers it; the worker module path is hardcoded (`resolve(vitest.distPath,"workers/forks.js")`), so the only injection point (createRuntimeRpc spreads `...options` LAST, so `timeout: -1` would win) needs a custom pool — and createForksPool is NOT exported from vitest/node. Chunk filenames are content-hashed, so always glob them, never hardcode a hash. KEY NEW FACT: in all 5 occurrences (5982, 5757, 6478, 6094, 7431) the timed-out `fetch` is the SAME module, gui/vitest.setup.ts — which is 65 lines with ZERO imports, so it is the victim by FREQUENCY, not cost: `isolate ?? true` gives every test file a fresh fork with a cold vite-node module cache, so the single setupFiles entry is fetched once per test file (173x), always first, before any test runs. That explains the "random subset of failing suites". Transform time across the five ranges 37.16s-166.57s with NO correlation to failure, ruling out transform cost; the real invariant is wall-clock dilation 186-474s vs a 51s idle baseline. `onQueued`/`snapshotSaved`/`onUnhandledError`/`resolveSnapshotPath` time out in the same runs — all share the one 60s bound — so the common cause is host unresponsiveness, not any one method or suite.

Completed: purge_unused must leave a damaged session in place instead of deleting it on created_at (intake.py::purge_unused)

Draft (store.py:35-46) and Released (store.py:49-53) now derive from Frozen directly and embed Analysis, so the defect stands as described.
- SessionStore._read (store.py:177-179) runs kind.model_validate_json on every read. No version field exists and nothing migrates.

- purge_unused/_last_used (intake.py:228-248) read the release for its time and leave a session whose release cannot be read in place, reporting it. tests/test_session_flow.py:347-363 pins that. A naive versioning would make every session released before a schema change "unreadable" to the purge, so no such session would ever be deleted: the 90-day promise would break.
- Deletion never reads the draft. The prospect route goes intake.delete -> _locked -> store.get (session.json only) -> shutil.rmtree. The operator route goes through by_prospect_id/readable(), which reads session.json only. So deletion already survives an unreadable draft; this task pins that with a test.

POLICY CHOSEN: an operator-facing state, not a migration table (see design decisions).
- store.RECORD_FORMAT = 1 is the record format this version writes drafts and releases in, and the only one it reads.
- Draft and Released derive from a small base, StoredWriteUp(Frozen), holding record_format: int = RECORD_FORMAT and analysis: Analysis. The format is therefore written on save by the record's own serialisation.
- On read, the store first reads only the declared format: a Frozen model _DeclaredFormat(record_format: int = 1), validated with pydantic 2.13.5's per-call model_validate_json(..., extra="ignore"). A record from before formats were numbered declares none and is format 1, so Leo's existing trial sessions keep working.
- Only a record declaring RECORD_FORMAT is validated in full. Every other outcome is returned, never raised, as UnreadableWriteUp(record_format=<declared> | None): another format, unparseable bytes, or a current-format record that fails the record's rules.
- draft() and released() return Draft/Released | UnreadableWriteUp | None.
- A new SessionStore.released_at(token) reads only released_at (a Frozen _ReleaseTime, again extra="ignore" per call) from a release in any format. A damaged release still raises there, so the purge keeps counting a release made in an older format and keeps leaving a damaged one in place.

So the prospect sees the full message, which for an analysis is `analysis: the write-up broke N rules of the record: ['Value error, a block_offer exit must rank lde_block first; it ranks A2 first', ...]`.

- `intake.py:194-196::_require_write_ups_left` caps on the saved draft's `sequence`, so a refused write-up saves no draft and consumes no cap.
- The rule texts are in record.py: :394 (`a {exit} exit must rank {alt} first`) and :423 (the block_offer gating dimensions).
- The no-echo tests are test_anthropic_model.py:137-146 and test_claude_code_model.py:129-134.

## Approach

1. **Prospect page.** error_pages shows one fixed message for every ModelOutputUnusable: heading "The assistant could not finish", text "The assistant could not finish just now. What was written is saved. Go back to your session page, reload it, and try again.", status 502 kept.

2. **Structured rules at the seam.** A new `AnalysisBrokeRules(ModelOutputUnusable)` in model.py carries `broken_rules: tuple[str, ...]`, and its message is derived from that tuple byte-identically to today's. `unusable_analysis` returns it, so both adapters raise it unchanged. Callers that catch ModelOutputUnusable keep working.

3. **The record.** `RefusedWriteUp(Frozen)` in store.py holds `at`, `sequence` (the write-up it would have been) and `broken_rules`. 4. **Operator page.** `OperatorView.refused_write_ups` feeds a section after the review section. It shows the heading "Refused write-ups: N" (the count, derived from the log) and the last refusal's sequence and time. Completed: Treat an empty INTAKE_PUBLIC_URL or INTAKE_DATA_DIR as unset, and refuse a public URL without a scheme and host (cli.py)
Description: Found while planning task 9 (follow-up id agent-followup-9); read in the code, not reproduced. src/scoping_intake/cli.py reads two settings with os.environ.get(name, default). After task 9 these reads are environment.get inside sites_for and _data_dir. A variable that is set but empty, such as a blank `INTAKE_PUBLIC_URL=` line in an env file, is used as a value, not as unset:

(1) INTAKE_PUBLIC_URL="" makes the public URL "", and urlsplit("").netloc is "", so "" joins the prospect site's Host allow-list. web.py's check, `self.headers.get("Host", "") in site.hosts`, then answers a request that sends no Host header, and the operator page offers a relative private link ("/s/<token>"). A value with no scheme, such as "intake.example", has the same effect, because urlsplit puts it in the path and leaves the netloc empty.
(2) INTAKE_DATA_DIR="" gives Path(""), which is the current working directory, so session data would be written under ./sessions wherever serve, calibration or purge is run. That breaks the briefing's rule that session data lives outside every git repository. The deploy unit sets the variable explicitly, so the installed service is not affected.

Task 9 makes an empty INTAKE_OPERATOR_PASSWORD count as unset (`or None`). This task applies the same rule to these two settings, and refuses at start, with a message naming the variable, an INTAKE_PUBLIC_URL that has no http or https scheme or no host.

Tests go in tests/test_serve.py through cli.argument_parser() and cli.sites_for(), with real models kept out of reach by that module's fixture:
- an empty public URL gives loopback-only hosts and a loopback link;
- a schemeless one is refused;
- an empty data dir falls back to the default. Test this with HOME monkeypatched into tmp_path so the default lands in a temp directory: never touch the real ~/.local/share/scoping-intake (CLAUDE.md).

Depends on task 9 having landed.

Completed: serve: Host allow-list entries that still differ from the Host a browser sends (non-canonical INTAKE_PUBLIC_URL hosts; loopback entries on port 80)
Description: Found while planning task 35 (follow-up id agent-followup-35). Task 35 makes src/scoping_intake/cli.py derive the prospect site's Host allow-list entry from INTAKE_PUBLIC_URL the way a browser writes Host: the host in lower case, no port when it is the scheme's default (80 for http, 443 for https) or empty, any other port kept, and an IPv6 address in brackets. The derivation lives in a helper, cli._host_header(scheme, hostname, port), which _public_url calls. web.py RequestHandler._admission_refusal answers only a Host header that is in site.hosts by string equality, and otherwise replies 421 'Not found'. Two cases are left. Both are outside task 35's scope and unlikely in the deployed setup: deploy/README.md sets INTAKE_PUBLIC_URL=https://<machine>.<tailnet>.ts.net, and the units use ports 8471 and 8472.

(1) Host spellings a browser rewrites beyond case and port. Measured on 2026-10-08 with headless Chrome 151 and a capture server: http://[0:0:0:0:0:0:0:1]:P/ is sent as Host [::1]:P. Per the WHATWG URL standard but NOT measured: a non-ASCII name such as https://bücher.example is sent in punycode (xn--bcher-kva.example), and IPv4 shorthand such as http://127.1:P/ is sent as 127.0.0.1:P. urllib.parse.urlsplit keeps all three as typed (CPython 3.14.4, the project venv). The allow-list entry therefore never matches, and every prospect request gets 421. The fix is either to derive the entry the way the browser does (IPv6 compression via ipaddress, IDNA/UTS-46, IPv4 parsing) or to refuse such values at start with UnusablePublicUrl, naming the variable.

(2) cli._loopback_hosts(port) always writes the port: {127.0.0.1:P, localhost:P}. A browser leaves out port 80 for http; measured in Chrome 151, http://intake.example:80/ is sent as Host intake.example. So with --prospect-port 80 or --operator-port 80, a browser at http://localhost/ sends Host 'localhost' and gets 421. The operator site would also refuse http://127.0.0.1/. cli._host_header from task 35 could build these entries too.

Completed: Refuse a relative INTAKE_DATA_DIR at start (cli.py _data_dir)
Description: Found while planning task 22 (follow-up id agent-followup-22). Read in the code, not reproduced.

Task 22 makes src/scoping_intake/cli.py's _data_dir treat an empty INTAKE_DATA_DIR as unset. Any other relative value, such as `INTAKE_DATA_DIR=data`, is still used as given and resolves against the working directory of whichever command runs it. serve (through sites_for), calibration and purge each call _data_dir(os.environ). That has two consequences:

(1) Run from the repository root, `data` puts the session directories under ./data/sessions, inside the git repository. .gitignore ignores only data/escalations/, data/orchestrator/, data/queue/ and data/reconciliation/, so session data could be committed. This breaks review/briefing.yaml's rule that session data lives outside every git repository.

(2) A purge run from a different working directory than serve builds a SessionStore on a different, empty directory (SessionStore mkdirs it at construction) and prints 'purged 0 sessions: none'. The retention promise can therefore fail without any sign.

The deploy units (deploy/scoping-intake.service, deploy/scoping-intake-purge.service) and every README example use absolute paths, so the installed service is not affected. The exposure is a hand-typed relative path.

Proposal, for Leo's judgement: refuse a relative INTAKE_DATA_DIR at start, with a message naming the variable and quoting the value. Do it in serve, calibration and purge alike, reusing the UnusableIntakeVariable refusal type that task 22 introduces in cli.py. calibration and purge would need the same refusal-to-exit translation that _serve has. Test through cli.sites_for and through cli.main() in tests/test_serve.py or a sibling test module. Never let a test resolve the real ~/.local/share/scoping-intake: patch HOME into tmp_path and chdir into a tmp directory, as task 22's data-directory test does.

Rationale: docs/code-quality.md heuristic 10 (an invariant enforced where the value enters, and named when violated), and the briefing convention on where session data lives. Depends on task 22 having landed.
Analysis: PREMISES (checked on the worktree, HEAD = main = 4c39050, "Merge task/22 into main"): task 22 has landed, so the dependency is met. src/scoping_intake/cli.py now has UnusableIntakeVariable(ValueError) with the subclasses MissingOperatorPassword and UnusablePublicUrl. UnusablePublicUrl owns its message and takes the offending value. _data_dir(intake_variables) (cli.py:69-71) treats an empty value as unset: `Path(intake_variables.get("INTAKE_DATA_DIR") or default)`. Every other relative value is still used as given. All three commands read the directory through _data_dir: sites_for (cli.py:136, used by _serve), _calibration (cli.py:166) and _purge (cli.py:171). Only _serve turns an UnusableIntakeVariable into an exit (cli.py:153-157). _calibration and _purge have no such translation, so a refusal raised there would surface as a traceback. SessionStore (store.py:64-68) and CalibrationLog (calibration.py:93-95) mkdir their subdirectories with parents=True when they are constructed. The refusal must therefore be raised before either object exists. Baseline: `uv run pytest` gives 147 passed.

candidates.content: solar_challenge web-template gotcha, measured 2026-10-10 by the task 595 architect in worktree 595's .venv (CPython 3.12.3, Flask render_template_string in an app context). A Jinja lookup such as charts.heat_pump.load_share_chart reads a frozen dataclass exactly as it reads a dict, because Jinja tries getattr before getitem. {% if value %} is true for any dataclass instance without __bool__ or __len__, and false for None. A name the object lacks renders Undefined, and Flask's tojson then raises TypeError: Object of type Undefined is not JSON serializable, so a page test catches a misspelt lookup either way. Flask's tojson serialises a whole dataclass through dataclasses.asdict.

candidates.content: Fused-memory MCP tool's update_task expects metadata as a JSON string

fused-memory's `submit_task` MCP tool is two-phase: it returns a ticket (`{"ticket": "tkt_<id>"}`), not a task_id — the curator worker asynchronously decides create/drop/combine, and callers resolve the real id via `resolve_ticket`. Orchestrator code that files tasks via `scheduler.dispatch_tool('submit_task', args)` therefore cannot rely on getting a task_id back synchronously (harness._OfflineLaneTaskClient treats it best-effort via Harness._extract_task_id). Dedup should key on content/title (search_tasks) or persistent local state, not on a returned id.

GOTCHA confirmed 2026-08-27 for scripted (non-MCP-tool) writes against the fused-memory server: the tool parameters are `id`, NOT `task_id`, for BOTH get_task and update_task — passing task_id fails every call with a pydantic "Field required" ToolError. This is actively misleading because the write journal records the parameter as task_id. Second gotcha: get_task returns the task record UNWRAPPED (top-level id/title/status/metadata/...), with no {'task': ...} envelope — a gate written against an envelope rejects 100% of candidates and looks exactly like a server outage. Both were hit during the 164-task tagger-scope restore; the first two apply passes wrote nothing because of them. The client to subclass is scripts/migrate_metadata_modules_to_files.py::FusedMemoryClient (default server http://127.0.0.1:8002); set _client_name on the subclass because that string becomes the write's agent_id via _resolve_identity. Run such a script as `uv run --frozen python <abs-path>` FROM THE REPO ROOT — cd-ing to the script's own directory makes uv resolve a different project and httpx goes missing. Always classify replies with write_failure_reason from the same module: an empty {} reply carries no positive write signal and is a FAILURE, not a success.

Task 'fused-memory update_task: make non-destructive shallow-merge the DEFAULT metadata mode (fix _causation_id/memory_hints clobber) + correct docstrings + tests' completed. mcp__fused-memory__update_task defaults to whole-blob REPLACE (append=False → _merge_metadata returns `incoming` verbatim, sqlite_task_backend.py:1350), yet the MCP tool docstring (server/tools.py:2734) says metadata is "JSON metadata to merge". A partial write therefore SILENTLY destroys sibling keys. Confirmed on reify task #4271: a files-only {"files":[...]} write (orchestrator module-tagger, harness.py:1347) clobbered _causation_id + memory_hints on 2026-06-04 AND again 2026-06-18 (write_journal evidence; restored by hand each time). Make non-destructive merge the DEFAULT and correct the contract at every fused-memory layer.
Details: ROOT CAUSE: API default is replace-whole-blob but the MCP docstring claims "merge"; every partial-write caller that trusts the docstring clobbers siblings. The bug class was already known (task 1511) and patched at ONE call site (scheduler.py:3396 read-modify-write "so memory_hints / _causation_id … survive the blast-radius-failure files write") instead of at the API — so it keeps recurring.

CRITICAL DESIGN — do NOT naively flip append default to True. The current append=True path (_merge_value

update_task metadata-clobber root cause (investigated 2026-06-18 via /deb on reify task #4271): mcp__fused-memory__update_task defaults to append=False, and the backend _merge_metadata (fused-memory/src/fused_memory/backends/sqlite_task_backend.py:1350) returns the incoming JSON VERBATIM when not append — i.e. the default REPLACES the whole metadata blob. But the MCP tool docstring (server/fused_memory/server/tools.py:2734) says metadata is "JSON metadata to merge" — that is the lie. So any partial write (e.g. files-only {"files":[...]}) with the default silently destroys sibling keys like _causation_id and memory_hints. The orchestrator scheduler docstring (orchestrator/src/orchestrator/scheduler.py:1844) is, by contrast, HONEST that append=False replaces the whole blob.

Retiring a task metadata key requires update_task metadata_mode='replace', NOT 'merge'. _merge_metadata (fused-memory/src/fused_memory/backends/sqlite_task_backend.py:3301-3376) implements merge as a shallow {**old, **new} with no deletion sentinel, so a merge-mode write can ADD a renamed key but can never REMOVE the old spelling — both coexist and the code=unknown_key census line persists. The safe recipe (precedent: fused-memory/scripts/strip_leaked_control_keys.py) is read the full blob, transform it purely, write it back with metadata_mode='replace' carrying ONLY {id, project_root, metadata, metadata_mode}, then read back and diff every key plus the sha256 of description/details. That payload restriction is what keeps a replace from repeating the task-2180 hazard of wiping live data.

fused-memory update_task(append=True) metadata merge is ADD-ONLY for existing scalar keys: it added a new key (reify_activation_authorized) and replaced a list value (modules) but silently KEPT the old value of an existing scalar key (user_observable_signal) across two attempts (observed 2026-06-10 on task 1722). To overwrite an existing scalar metadata key, read the current full metadata blob (it comes back in the update_task/get_task response) and re-send the corrected complete blob with append=False. This is the inverse hazard of the known set_task_status append=False metadata-nuke: append=True can't fix a stale scalar, append=False replaces everything — so full-blob replace with all keys present is the safe overwrite pattern.

update_task on the fused-memory MCP now supports structured field updates (title/description/details/priority/status/dependencies overwrite their columns; metadata has metadata_mode merge/additive/replace, with bare append=False rejected since the task-2180 metadata-wipe incident). Verified empirically 2026-07-29 by amending task 3211's description + metadata and reading the change back in the response. This supersedes the 2026-07-23 observation that update_task description/priority updates silently no-op — that behavior is FIXED; still verify by readback after any amendment, since amendments never reach an already-claimed/running workflow.

Task 'Extend fused-memory update_task to support dotted subtask IDs' completed. The fused-memory `update_task` MCP tool currently rejects dotted subtask IDs (e.g. "2696.1") with "taskId must be a positive integer". No `update_subtask` MCP tool exists. This prevents reconciliation from attaching `memory_hints` to expanded subtasks, silently degrading knowledge continuity each cycle.

**Root cause**: The tool validates task IDs as positive integers at the MCP boundary, so dotted IDs (Taskmaster's subtask notation) are rejected before reaching the backend.

**Required fix**: Either:

Gotcha (fused-memory task writes, caught during task 3329's review of scripts/repair_wiped_metadata_files.py): `get_task`/`update_task` MCP tools take `tag: str | None = None` (server/tools.py:4182-4186; update_task signature at :2612), and when omitted the backend does NOT error — it substitutes `DEFAULT_TAG = 'master'` (backends/sqlite_task_backend.py:127; `tag = tag or DEFAULT_TAG` appears at ~19 call sites including the update_task path). Tasks are keyed by PRIMARY KEY `(tag, id)`, so the same numeric id can exist under two tags as two DISTINCT tasks. A script that reads task rows straight from tasks.db (or reads their own `tag` column) but drops the tag when writing back through MCP SILENTLY RETARGETS onto whichever master-tag row shares that numeric id — a wrong-task write, not a visible failure. Always thread the row's own `tag` verbatim through every get_task/update_task call; never coalesce it to 'master' "because it always is". The live dark-factory tasks.db being single-tag today (`SELECT DISTINCT tag FROM tasks` -> [('master',)], measured 2026-08-01 over 3379 rows) is a property of the DATA, not the code, and does not hold for an arbitrary `--project-root`. b2cc5bec-0309-46a2-bc37-825983263e35.content: GOTCHA measured 2026-08-20 on fused-memory's bundled FastMCP: the tool dispatcher ACCEPTS a JSON-encoded STRING for a parameter declared list[str] and coerces it to the list. Probed live: scan_memory_content(project_id=..., needles=json.dumps(['</content>'])) ran and returned normally, despite needles being declared `list[str] | None`. This matters for any boundary middleware that scans tool arguments, because such scanners typically inspect only isinstance(value, str) arguments — so a list-typed parameter is normally skipped, but its JSON-string wire form IS scanned. Concretely it makes the scan_memory_content exemption in fused_memory/server/markup_guard.EXEMPT_TOOLS load-bearing rather than a precaution: without the exemption, a corpus sweep whose needles arrive as a JSON string is refused with error_type=mcp_markup_unrepairable, i.e. the retroactive-sweep tool cannot look for the very literals it exists to find. When reasoning about which arguments a boundary guard will or will not see, check the coerced wire shapes, not just the declared annotation.

candidates.content: DimensionalSolver (crates/reify-constraints/src/solver.rs) feasibility-residual floor: the Nelder-Mead cost is the SQUARED constraint violation (comparison_violation → d.powi(2)) but the feasibility check uses the LINEAR residual (comparison_residual → |d|) compared against FEASIBILITY_THRESHOLD=1e-12. With with_sd_tolerance(1e-15) on the squared cost, the linear-residual floor is ≈ sqrt(1e-15) ≈ 3e-8, so any auto param that must MOVE from an off-target seed (e.g. seed 20mm, constraint x==10mm) converges only to residual ~1e-8 >> 1e-12 and the solver returns Infeasible. Empirically confirmed (seed 0.02→target 0.01 → Infeasible residual 1.05e-8). Tightening sd_tolerance to 1e-30 (≲ FEASIBILITY_THRESHOLD²) drives the residual to ~1e-16 (Solved); full reify-constraints suite (108 lib + integration tests) still passes. extract_initial_point seeds auto params with bounds:None at a HARDCODED 0.01 — which coincidentally equals 10mm, so existing warm back-prop tests pass only because the seed already equals the solution (no movement needed).

DimensionalSolver (crates/reify-constraints/src/solver.rs) has a convergence-floor gotcha: solve_core's Nelder-Mead minimizes the SQUARED constraint violation (comparison_violation uses d.powi(2)) and terminates at sd_tolerance(1e-15), so its achievable L1 residual floor is ≈sqrt(1e-15)≈3e-8 — but the feasibility gate (final_max_residual > FEASIBILITY_THRESHOLD=1e-12) checks the LINEAR residual (comparison_residual). Any auto that must MOVE from its seed to satisfy an equality constraint stalls ~2.6e-8 >> 1e-12 → Infeasible. Cold solves of `param x:Length=auto` only pass when the target happens to equal extract_initial_point's 0.01 default seed (no bounds → 0.01), triggering the initially_feasible early-exit (no NM run). Task 4700 fixes this with a near-feasible polish/restart at tighter sd_tolerance.

MEASURED 2026-08-26 (main 2128c3692c, reproduced independently twice): mixing an EQUALITY and an INEQUALITY on the same reify `auto` param is UNCONDITIONALLY reported infeasible, even when trivially satisfiable. `constraint L >= 8mm` + `constraint L == 10mm` (10mm satisfies both) yields "constraints could not be satisfied (max absolute residual: 5.00e-7)" and leaves L undef. The equality ALONE resolves to exactly 0.01 m.

The residual is ALWAYS exactly 5.00e-7 — verified scale-invariant, direction-invariant, order-invariant and strictness-invariant across six controls (including a x10-scaled twin). MECHANISM: the synthetic max-min-slack objective is added ALONGSIDE the equality's penalty, and minimising PENALTY_WEIGHT*d^2 - x with PENALTY_WEIGHT = 1e6 is stationary at 2*1e6*d = 1, i.e. d = 5.0e-7 exactly. That is five orders above FEASIBILITY_THRESHOLD = 1e-12.

DISPOSITION (important — do not re-file this as a new defect): the VERDICT half is ALREADY OWNED by task #6653, whose evidence names this exact probe (expr_ineq_eq.ri) and this exact residual, and whose acceptance criterion requires all four of its evidence probes to flip. Its work item (2) — replacing the flat dimension-blind FEASIBILITY_THRESHOLD with a relative + dimension-aware-absolute-floor policy — is the mechanism (0.5 um on a metre-scale length falls below any sensible engineering floor). A P1 authoring session was about to file a duplicate and caught it only by reading #6653's full description.

What #6653 does NOT fix, filed separately as #6688: the underlying BIAS. #6653 makes the verdict correct by TOLERATING the residual, leaving the solver returning 9.9995mm where the design says 10mm. The offset is ABSOLUTE and scale-invariant, so the relative error grows without bound as designs shrink — 5e-5 at 10mm, but 25% on a 2 micron feature.

Reify solver tolerance inventory, measured 2026-08-26 at main 2ea72cc5e8 — useful for anyone touching #6653 (toleranced Scalar verdicts) or solver conditioning.

The dimensional path's constants are DIMENSION-BLIND ABSOLUTES applied to raw SI magnitudes: FEASIBILITY_THRESHOLD = 1e-12 (the acceptance gate, L-infinity, so 1 picometre on a metre-scale length), NM_SD_TOLERANCE = 1e-30 (argmin simplex termination on the squared-residual cost SD; deliberately <= FEASIBILITY_THRESHOLD^2 per task #4700), PENALTY_WEIGHT = 1e6, UNDEF_OBJECTIVE_PENALTY = f64::MAX/2, MAX_ITERS = 5000, FEASIBLE_OPT_ITERS_PER_DIM = 500. Inline deadbands: 1e-15 for Eq/Ne, a +1e-12 offset in comparison_violation. So a Money objective (~1e2) and a Length constraint (~1e-2) sit in the same unnormalised sum with a fixed 1e6 objective/penalty ratio regardless of physical scale.

The ONLY relative-plus-floor tolerance in the solver today is the uniqueness check's UNIQUENESS_REL_TOL = 1e-6 / UNIQUENESS_ABS_TOL = 1e-10 pair in solutions_agree. The ONLY normalisation anywhere is cost_robustness_tradeoff's normalised_blend_term. The robustness floor uses REL_MARGIN = 0.02 with ABS_FLOOR_SI = 1e-9.

The ONLY coherent tolerance HIERARCHY in the codebase is RelateTolerance::kernel_default() in crates/reify-constraints/src/relate_solve.rs — kernel_local 1e-7 m <= solver_convergence 1e-6 m <= assertion 1e-5 m, all metres, seeded from one base length. It has PRIVATE fields, exactly one constructor, no setters and no DSL knob. That ladder is the shape #6653 should generalise, and note solver_convergence (1e-6) happens to EQUAL FD_STEP, i.e. the differencing step is the same size as the convergence target.

The engine verdict fold meanwhile uses EXACT f64 equality (reify-expr eval_eq), which is why correctly-solved models report false VIOLATED at ~1e-15 residuals (probe-measured on multi_auto2/multi_auto6/auto_probe). crates/reify-core/src/scalar_tolerance.rs does not exist yet — #6653 creates it.

Reify's DimensionalSolver keeps TWO parallel per-comparison functions in crates/reify-constraints/src/solver.rs that are easy to conflate: comparison_violation (:521-584) returns SQUARED magnitudes and is the Nelder-Mead COST that drives convergence, while comparison_residual (:464-519) returns ABSOLUTE distances and is the accept/reject VERDICT checked against FEASIBILITY_THRESHOLD (:20). Only comparison_residual is a verdict. Widening the cost function's deadband flattens the objective inside the band and degrades solutions from ~1e-16 to ~deadband, and also invalidates the NM_SD_TOLERANCE <= FEASIBILITY_THRESHOLD^2 derivation documented at solver.rs:38-82. Both functions drop dimension via Value::as_f64() (reify-ir/src/value.rs:1635-1642) at :477-478 / :535-536, so FEASIBILITY_THRESHOLD is a dimension-blind, scale-blind absolute gate; Value::dimension() (value.rs:1655) recovers it without any signature change to max_constraint_residual/constraint_residual.

In reify-constraints `solve_core_with_sd_tolerance`, the value returned by `DimensionalSolver::solve` is `best_param` after a `val.clamp(lo, hi)` into the effective box (`build_solved_values(&problem.auto_params, &clamped)`), so a test pinning an answer to a `default_bounds_for` corner (Length = 1e-6..10.0 m) is bit-exact because of that clamp, NOT because Nelder-Mead converged there. Pin such corner expectations with a RELATIVE tolerance (`tol * max(|expected|, 1.0)`); an absolute 1e-9 against the 10 m corner is a 1e-10 relative tolerance and goes RED on any future NM change that terminates marginally inside the bound, even though the characterised behaviour is unchanged.

When asserting reify-eval solver-resolved auto-param values, the tolerance depends on which DimensionalSolver path the fixture drives, and copying the wrong one gives a guessed threshold with no achievability basis. Seeding the edit AT the constraint's solution takes the initially-feasible early-exit (no Nelder-Mead search) and supports 1e-9, as `edit_param_back_props_solved_auto` does. Seeding OFF-target forces a real Nelder-Mead search and needs 1e-6 — its sibling `edit_param_back_props_moved_auto` declares `const MOVED_AUTO_TOL: f64 = 1e-6` (crates/reify-eval/src/engine_edit.rs:6202) and applies it to all four of its assertions. `crates/reify-eval/tests/common/differential.rs:1793` gives the underlying reason: warm-started and cold-seeded Nelder-Mead runs are not bit-identical, so solver-resolved cells must be compared to tolerance, never by content_hash.

DimensionalSolver feasibility-fallback gotcha: when a minimize objective pushes an auto param toward a strict lower-bound constraint (e.g. `constraint thickness > 1mm`), Nelder-Mead may converge just below the boundary (floating-point), triggering the `final_max_residual > FEASIBILITY_THRESHOLD` check in solver.rs and falling back to the 10mm initial feasible point. Solution: use only an upper-bound constraint for minimize fixtures (single upper bound avoids this), matching the design of `e2e_minimize_through_real_solver` in crates/reify-eval/tests/resolution.rs:889 which explicitly notes "Single upper-bound constraint avoids floating-point boundary issues at the lower bound."

When reproducing reify-constraints' real solver path in a scratch unit test in `crates/reify-constraints/src/solver.rs`, always pass `NM_SD_TOLERANCE` to `solve_core_with_sd_tolerance` — never an ad-hoc value like 3.0. `DimensionalSolver::solve` reaches `solve_core` which hardcodes `NM_SD_TOLERANCE`, so a looser tolerance makes the same sub-solve return `Infeasible` where the production path returns `Solved`, which reads as a contradiction between the emitted diagnostic and your probe and sends you hunting a nonexistent bug. Measured on task #5714: probing `original_constraints_witness` at sd_tolerance=3.0 declined on two brackets (`2*x > 60mm AND 2*x < 62.5mm`, `< 65mm`) that the real path witnesses fine.

In reify-solver-elastic's form-finding code, any convergence or degeneracy threshold compared against a quantity built from the force-density matrix D (= C^T Q C plus the sum over triangles of sigma_T * L_T) must be RELATIVE, never absolute: D is exactly linear in the gauge pair (q, sigma), so an absolute bound makes convergence gauge-DEPENDENT. A large lambda inflates the residual so the solve never converges (loud failure); a small lambda shrinks it below tolerance so the solve stops prematurely on unconverged geometry (silent wrong answer) — a suite testing only one direction is blind to the other. The house pattern is to divide by d_scale = the infinity-norm of D restricted to the free rows, which cancels lambda exactly since numerator and denominator each pick up one factor. DEGENERATE_AREA_EPS in the same file is the older instance of the same principle ("relative so the test is scale-free"). Task 6119 applied this to the ANCHORED surfaces path (SURFACE_EQUILIBRIUM_REL_TOL, calibrated so the relative 1e-11 reproduces the previous absolute 1e-10 stop point against a measured d_scale of about 9 on the catenoid goldens). The identical absolute-threshold shape still exists on the FREE-STANDING path in form_find_free.rs (FREE_SURFACE_EQUILIBRIUM_TOL, all_node_equilibrium_residual), tracked as tasks 6413 and 6983.

Reify's solver and its constraint CHECKER disagree about equality by construction. The DimensionalSolver treats `==` as satisfied within a bare `1e-15` slop, inlined (no shared constant) at four sites in crates/reify-constraints/src/solver.rs: `comparison_residual` Eq/Ne (:511, :514) and `comparison_violation` Eq/Ne (:575, :577). The checker path is EXACT: `eval_eq` in crates/reify-expr/src/lib.rs:5359-5380 bit-compares `Value::Scalar` after a dimension check, and that is what SimpleConstraintChecker (crates/reify-constraints/src/lib.rs:169-183) folds into Satisfied/Violated. So a solve that lands within 1e-15 is "feasible" to the solver and "violated" to the checker — the false-VIOLATED class task #6653 was filed to fix. Separately, the four inequality nudges at solver.rs:545/553/561/569 are a DIFFERENT `1e-12` constant with a different job; do not fold them together.

In reify's tensegrity solver, changing a convergence criterion's DENOMINATOR requires recalibrating its constant in the same change, or the fix silently loosens accuracy. Task 6119 divided the surfaces-path equilibrium residual by `d_scale = ||D||_inf` (over free rows) to make it gauge-invariant; since measured d_scale is ~8.5-9.7 at sigma~1 on the catenoid meshes, keeping the old absolute 1e-10 would have moved the stop point ~9x looser. The landed SURFACE_EQUILIBRIUM_REL_TOL = 1e-11 was chosen so the new relative bound reproduces the OLD absolute stop point to within ~10%, staying ~11.5x below the gamma catenoid golden's independent EQUIL_TOL = 1e-9. The house convention is to justify such constants against a measured quantity on the real fixtures plus an independent golden's bound, not to guess.

Reify solver gotcha (measured 2026-08-27, task #6756): for any NON-Money objective, `DimensionalSolver` silently returns the SEED instead of the optimum whenever the objective is active against an inequality bound. Chain in crates/reify-constraints/src/solver.rs: the exact-penalty cost (:1544, PENALTY_WEIGHT=1e6 at :25) has its stationary point w/(2*PENALTY_WEIGHT) OUTSIDE the bound (5e-7 m for a unit-gradient Length objective); that residual fails the FEASIBILITY_THRESHOLD=1e-12 re-check (:20, :1997); and the `initially_feasible` drift-fallback (:1998-2032) then returns the seed with `unique: true` and only a tracing::debug!. The #5618 derived clamp box that would snap the undershoot onto the bound is gated on `floor_applied` (:1809), which requires `objective_is_money` — so Money objectives are the ONLY ones that reach their optimum, and they do so via the clamp at :1970-1979, not via the optimiser. Symptom: `minimize length` under `length >= 8mm` returns 8.8mm (the one-sided seed nudge); under `[8mm,40mm]` both minimize AND maximize return 24mm (the box midpoint). Do NOT diagnose this as Nelder-Mead stalling — the budget is never exhausted and `iter_limited` is false.

Reify cost-min (PRD v0_6 continuous-cost-minimisation) eval-layer gotcha: at the .ri/eval layer the DimensionalSolver derives auto-param bounds INTERNALLY (default_bounds_for: Length=[1µm,10m], dimensionless/Real=[-1e6,1e6]) — .ri cannot inject numeric bounds. So a Money-dimensioned `minimize` driving an auto param TOWARD a lower-bound inequality (e.g. `thickness > t_min`, cost ∝ thickness) does NOT converge to t_min+margin; Nelder-Mead drifts sub-boundary (money savings dominate the small floor penalty) and the solver returns the initially-feasible SEED (~10mm) via the initially_feasible fallback — strictly OFF the boundary but NOT at bound+margin. Therefore eval/example tests must assert the off-boundary STRUCTURAL property (value > boundary) + the RobustnessFloorApplied Info diagnostic, never precise convergence (the precise bound+margin value is only reachable in solver-level tests that inject explicit bounds, e.g. crates/reify-constraints/tests/robustness_floor.rs uses [1mm,1.5mm]). Also: such an auto param must be `auto(free)` (strict `auto` trips ConstraintNonUnique via the perturbed uniqueness re-solve since the seed-fallback value isn't a unique convergent point), and must be `Length` not bare `Real` (Real default bounds [-1e6,1e6] let cost-min drive toward -1e6, unphysical/infeasible). Canonical landed reference: crates/reify-eval/tests/robustness_floor_signal.rs::money_floor_resolves_off_boundary_and_emits_info (task #4789 α).

Solver-intake silent-failure seam map (verified 2026-07-24 on main 0d70ef1d5b, DIC PRD evidence): (1) a declared objective is silently dropped at THREE SolverRegistry::solve_inner sites — registry.rs:152-162 (no auto params, early Solved return), :182-192 (components.is_empty — the unconstrained-minimize shape), :208-210 (objective refs match no component → silently attached to component 0, an arbitrary fallback); (2) NO representability check exists anywhere in the intake — classifier.rs:115 explicitly no-ops String refs (Enum/geometry also flagless) → Dimensional default → DimensionalSolver, whose build_trial_values/build_solved_values (solver.rs:138-150/:110-129) construct Value::Scalar unconditionally with dimension_of mapping any non-Scalar type to DIMENSIONLESS — so a Bool/String/Enum auto is coerced to f64, optimized by Nelder-Mead, and would be written back KIND-CLOBBERED as Value::Scalar; (3) objective_term_contributions (engine_eval.rs:3526-3561) maps a failed/non-Scalar term eval to f64::NAN with no diagnostic. A String auto with an equality constraint yields 'constraints could not be satisfied (max absolute residual: 1.00e0)' (eval exits 1 — the misleading TEXT is the bug, not the exit code).

Task 4700 (esc-4700-33) root cause: the committed step-2 fix tightening DimensionalSolver NM_SD_TOLERANCE from 1e-15 to 1e-30 (crates/reify-constraints/src/solver.rs) REGRESSES crates/reify-eval/tests/auto_binding_sites_remaining_resolution.rs::example_auto_binding_sites_ri_all_four_resolve, which fails with a spurious ConstraintNonUnique error. Verified by toggling the constant: 1e-15 PASSES, 1e-30 FAILS. The escalation was mislabeled transient ENOSPC; a verify retry surfaces this real code regression. Mechanism: in the AllFourSites resolution problem there are 3 strict autos (bolt.length, m, __connector_0.gain) with current_values all None. bolt.length and m have determining constraints (==10mm) in that problem; __connector_0.gain does NOT — its determining constraint self.gain==10mm lives in EpsilonConnector's OWN scope (design D5: parent cannot name the synthesized __connector_N), so gain is genuinely underdetermined within the parent problem. verify_uniqueness perturbs all 3 to ~9m and re-solves: with the old 1e-15 tolerance the perturbed re-solve failed feasibility on bolt/m (residual ~3e-8 > 1e-12) and hit the 'perturbed solve did not converge -> assume unique' fallback, ACCIDENTALLY masking gain's non-uniqueness. With 1e-30 the perturbed re-solve now converges bolt/m to 1e-12 feasibility and lands gain at 0.158 vs the original 0.01 (diff 0.148 >> uniqueness tol) -> solutions_agree=false -> ConstraintNonUnique. So tightening the tolerance removed the accidental masking and exposed a latent problem-construction issue: connector-internal autos appear as unconstrained auto_params in the parent resolution problem. Fix is design-laden (solver uniqueness machinery or eval problem-construction); re-escalated to L1.

Solver-integration landscape audit (2026-08-26, main @ 181d1ec24c, probe-verified): The production solver surface map is — reify eval/run, report, explain, GUI edit/load paths: full SolverRegistry::production() (DimensionalSolver + SolveSpaceSolver; CpSat NOT registered until PRD2 gamma #5469; Logical/CrossDomain slots fall back to Dimensional). reify build/check/test, LSP, CLI mcp-server: NO dimensional solver. relate_solve (at-auto 6-DOF pose, damped Gauss-Newton, NOT SolveSpace) is the exception on the geometry path: its single call site is Engine::build_with_geometry_output (engine_build.rs:3979, kernel-gated not solver-gated), so solved POSES reach STEP via reify build and GUI export — but never the GUI live viewport (tessellate_snapshot has no solve; eval_auto_sub_pose identity fallback) and never check. Solved VALUE autos (ctor-arg/let/param) reach no realization surface at all (#6631/#5617). Two probe-proven verdict defects: (1) engine post-solve equality verdicts compare exact f64 while the solver accepts at 1e-12 L-inf, so numerically-solved (non-exactly-representable) solutions report "constraint violated"/exit 1 from eval, and a feasible ineq+eq mix is declared infeasible at 5e-7 residual; (2) inequality-only strict autos silently resolve to a bound corner (10 m default) with no warning (Chebyshev centrality on an unbounded-above region). Constraint expressiveness is NOT a gap: min/max/clamp, if-then-else, abs, sqrt, trig, dot/cross/magnitude all work inside comparison operands (continuous residuals). The traps are: any std::distance/std::tangent/std::geo::* call classifies the constraint Geometric -> SolveSpaceSolver pattern-matcher -> inequalities/arithmetic unrecognized -> NoProgress kills the WHOLE resolve; tangent() typechecks but contributes zero residual rows anywhere (#5540 low); seed/bound derivation only understands linear-in-one-auto shapes so sqrt-algebra clearance constraints contribute no seed box.
DimensionalSolver returns exactly the boundary value for lower-bound constraints, so assertions use >= not > for real-solver boundary tests

Task 'DimensionalSolver warm re-solve convergence gap blocks concurrent/eval_cached back-prop of MOVED autos (residual ~2.6e-8 >> 1e-12 threshold)' completed. Found while resolving esc-4361-11 (task 4361, unified-dag θ). The warm Resolution back-prop arms (concurrent.rs resolve_concurrent_edit:413, engine_eval.rs eval_cached Solved arm) are correctly wired and land solved autos as Determined. BUT they only fire when the solver returns SolveResult::Solved. The DimensionalSolver (crates/reify-constraints/src/solver.rs) seeds Nelder-Mead from current_values (extract_initial_point:98) and uses FEASIBILITY_THRESHOLD=1e-12. When a warm edit forces an auto param to MOVE (e.g. cold x=10mm, then edit seeds x=20mm with constraint x==10mm), Nelder-Mead converges only to residual ~2.6e-8 from the off-target start — exceeding 1e-12 — so the solver returns Infeasible and the constraint silently fails to re-derive the auto on the warm path. The eval_cached step-4 test passes ONLY because x starts AT its solution (no movement). Net: warm re-solve of constrained autos after an edit is not demonstrably correct to tolerance. Decide: (a) relax/scale the feasibility threshold or add a polishing/restart step in DimensionalSolver, or (b) re-seed from default rather than the edited value, then add a concurrent back-prop regression test (the step-7 part-A guard in 4361 was removed because it asserts this unachievable-today behaviour). Also re-add the run_unified_pass linear-schedule regression guard (step-7 part-B, passing, was reverted alongside part-A). Spawned from task 4361 esc-4361-11.

geometric-relations numeric premises are NOT error-floor bounds (capability manifest numeric-floor = N/A): DOF figures (concentric removes 4, flush 3 with 2 redundant, spent 5 / free 1) are exact integer codimensions from the `coincident(X,X) removes codim(X)` law in relation_signatures.rs (relation_delta_dof). The relate-solve tolerance is one kernel-defaulted Length knob with hierarchy kernel_local ≤ solver_convergence ≤ assertion/dedup. Tests asserting "coaxial/flush within tol" must assert against the solver's own convergence tolerance (a method guarantee when SolveSpaceSolver returns Solved), never a hand-picked epsilon — a tuned epsilon would be a false numeric premise.

content: Measured 2026-10-14 (main 5b8a33011d): the DimensionalSolver's Nelder-Mead stops on cost-SD NM_SD_TOLERANCE=1e-30 over SQUARED residuals, so equality residuals land around 1e-15 in raw SI units regardless of dimension — e.g. `param v : Volume = auto; constraint v == 1000mm^3` solves to 1.0000000011823468e-6 m^3 (residual 1.18e-15, RELATIVE 1.2e-9). Consequence for any acceptance/verdict tolerance (task #6653): an absolute floor below ~1e-12 SI (e.g. (1um)^3 = 1e-18 m^3 for Volume) or a pure-relative 1e-9 policy turns ordinary mm^3-scale volume equalities into false Infeasible/Violated. Keep every per-dimension floor >= 1e-12 (today's FEASIBILITY_THRESHOLD), so a toleranced acceptance is never stricter than the old flat gate.

   - Nothing is printed or logged.

4. **Operator page.** `OperatorView.refused_write_ups` feeds a section after the review section. - Intake.operator_view (intake.py:125-137) reads the draft, the operator placement and the release. request_write_up, place, rewrite and release read the draft (intake.py:101-158, 204-212).

A naive versioning would make every session released before a schema change "unreadable" to the purge, so no such session would ever be deleted: the 90-day promise would break.

The operator route goes through by_prospect_id/readable(), which reads session.json only. So deletion already survives an unreadable draft; this task pins that with a test.

POLICY CHOSEN: an operator-facing state, not a migration table (see design decisions).

candidates.content: GOTCHA (fused-memory, task 4513): after task 4513 the ticket worker no longer converts a curator exception into a create. Any curator failure that is not a zero-output hang now parks the ticket as status 'awaiting_curation'. A test that stubs TaskCurator.curate must therefore accept the `prepared=` kwarg (e.g. `async def stub(self, candidate, project_id, project_root, **_kw)`), because curate_batch_prepared's size-1 path calls `self.curate(..., prepared=...)`. Before 4513, a TypeError from a too-narrow stub was silently turned into a create by the batch `except Exception`, so such tests passed by accident. Now the ticket resolves `awaiting_curation` with reason 'batch-curation-raised: TypeError'. Precedent: tests/test_operational_routing_boundary_matrix.py::_submit_normal_and_get.

fused-memory curator gotcha (task 5491): to tell whether a TaskCurator create was degraded by a zero-output hang (ZOT), read CuratorDecision.degraded_by_zot (and zot_escalation_id), never the justification string — 'llm-error-escalated' is shared by EVERY CuratorFailureError, and 'zero-output-breaker-open' covers only the breaker short-circuits. CuratorEscalator.report_failure now returns the live curator_zero_output_hang record id (the PARENT id when the report folded via submit_or_dedupe, the remembered id for a batch sibling inside the 60s in-process window, None on every non-ZOT branch or failed submit). To simulate a ZOT in tests, patch fused_memory.middleware.task_curator.invoke_with_cap_retry to return AgentResult(success=False, output='', subtype='error_empty_output', timed_out=True, turns=0, cost_usd=0.0) and pass curate(..., prepared=PreparedCandidate(candidate=c, pool=[], pool_sizes={...zeros...}, prompt_tokens=0)) instead of patching the private _build_corpus.

In fused-memory/tests/test_ticket_worker.py, any curator MagicMock that drives the actual worker (submit_task + drain, or _process_add_tickets_batch) MUST cover `prepare_candidate`, because TaskInterceptor._prepare_ticket (task_interceptor.py:2797) unconditionally awaits `curator.prepare_candidate(...)`. A plain MagicMock child raises a swallowed `TypeError: object MagicMock can't be used in 'await' expression` (logged at task_interceptor.py:2808, logger fused_memory.middleware.task_interceptor); the ticket still succeeds via the backfill curate() path (3531-3545), so it PASSES in isolation but flakes under xdist ordering/load. For create-path tests that keep `curate` as the decision source, add `mock_curator.prepare_candidate = AsyncMock(return_value=None)` (returns None → routes to backfill curate, behaviour-preserving). Use the `_stub_prepare_candidate` helper only for batch-path tests, since it returns a real PreparedCandidate and reroutes decisions to curate_batch_prepared/curate_batch (requiring a curate_batch stub too). Task 2720.

On fused-memory main as of 2026-10-01 (f3aa08d619), TaskCurator degrades to action='create' on a zero-output hang (ZOT) at THREE sites, not two: (1) curate()'s breaker short-circuit, (2) curate()'s `except CuratorFailureError` branch, and (3) curate_batch_prepared's OWN breaker gate, which never calls curate(). The justification 'llm-error-escalated' covers EVERY CuratorFailureError, so it cannot tell a ZOT apart from other failures; use exc.zero_output_timeout or a structured flag. Also, no `curator.*` config leaf is in fused_memory/config/reload.py::RELOADABLE_FIELDS, so curator knobs take effect only after a fused-memory restart, not via reload_config.

The curator's all-accounts-capped DEFER machinery already exists, but only on the batch path: curate_batch/curate_batch_prepared re-raise AllAccountsCappedException (task_curator.py:1788, :2681) and _curator_worker catches it, re-enqueues the batch's ticket ids and parks on usage_gate.wait_for_open (task_interceptor.py:3325-3349), leaving rows 'pending' and unsignalled. Only the single-item curate() (task_curator.py:1388-1406) swallows the cap and fabricates action='create'. That asymmetry leaks into the batch path too: _call_llm_batch_with_fallback bisects to size 1 and then calls self.curate() (task_curator.py:2668-2674), and the two single-item curate() calls inside _process_add_tickets_batch_prepared (task_interceptor.py:4203, :4231) catch only CuratorFailureError — so a cap on any of those three paths is silently swallowed despite the batch path being documented as re-raising. Fixing this is task 4503; the right shape is to make curate() re-raise like its sibling rather than add a parallel defer mechanism.

In fused-memory's TaskInterceptor, the ticket/curator drain has a decoy: `_process_add_ticket` (task_interceptor.py:3769) and its single `curator.curate()` call have NO production caller — only tests reach them. The live path is `_curator_worker` -> `_prepare_ticket` (-> `curator.prepare_candidate`) -> `_process_add_tickets_batch_prepared` -> `curator.curate_batch_prepared`, with `curate()` reached only as a per-item fallback after a CuratorFailureError or for records whose prepare step failed. `curate_batch()` itself is never called from the interceptor at all. Any change to curator failure/degrade handling must be made on the batch path (and in the shared `_dispatch_ticket_decision` chokepoint at :3470) or it will pass its unit tests and do nothing in production.

FACTS/quirks discovered while filing tasks via fused-memory (2026-07-13): (1) submit_task metadata.files rejects extensionless file paths as "directory declarations" (LockCharterViolation) — hooks/project-checks was refused; use files=[] to defer scope to the architect for extensionless scripts (extension matching is case-sensitive lowercase). (2) The curator's dedup is genuinely good when descriptions carry precise context: it combined our claimant-dispatch-gate candidate into existing task 2408 with correct reasoning (complementary halves of one feature, same module locks), and dropped our /unblock-guardrail candidate because in-progress task 2509 already targets the same incident — write rich descriptions and let it route. (3) resolve_ticket can time out (~115s MCP cap) while the curator still creates the task — retrying resolve_ticket on the same ticket returns the terminal result (created id 2555 recovered this way); don't re-submit on timeout. (4) search_tasks is permanently blind to planning_mode-created tasks (curator corpus never indexes them at submit or commit_planning — verified in task_interceptor.py:2029 + tools.py:3287) — this is the root cause behind the "verify a batch with get_task, not search" rule; fix filed as task 2562.

fused-memory's TaskCurator has THREE failure arms in curate(), and the third is a SILENT SINK. AllAccountsCappedException (task_curator.py:1387) and CuratorFailureError (:1406) both call escalator.report_failure(); the bare `except Exception` at task_curator.py:1442 does NOT — it only logs a WARNING ("task_curator: LLM call failed, falling through to create: %s") and returns CuratorDecision(action='create'). It also does not advance the ZOT circuit breaker. So any exception class outside the two named ones degrades dedupe to create with zero escalation at any level and no durable trace beyond a journal that rolls in ~5 days. Discovered 2026-08-19 while investigating reify escalations esc-task-curator-7/-8. Filed as dark-factory task 4448 (high). Disambiguation tip: three log sites contain "falling through to create" — :1362 is corpus-assembly ("corpus assembly failed, ..."), :1428 is the no-escalator-wired path ("LLM failure with no escalator wired — ..."), and :1444 is this bare-except arm ("LLM call failed, ..."). The exact string identifies which arm fired.

FACTS about the fused-memory task tooling, learned 2026-07-27 while filing DF 3081/3082.

1. THE CURATOR COMBINES CONCURRENT NEAR-DUPLICATE TICKETS AND REWRITES RATHER THAN DROPS. Two agents independently filed the same merge_queue stranding defect ~2 minutes apart (tkt_0RRRB06C… at 07:48 from an /unblock triage, tkt_0RRRB1TE… at 07:50 from a /deb root-cause). The curator resolved the second as status='combined' onto task_id 3082 and REWROTE 3082 to fold in the candidate's more precise root cause, explicitly reasoning that "rewriting rather than dropping preserves the more precise root-cause detail the candidate contributes; rewriting rather than creating avoids a duplicate architect cycle on the same defect." The merged result was materially better than either input. PRACTICAL UPSHOT: do not pre-emptively suppress a filing because another agent might be working the same defect — file it with your distinct evidence and let the curator merge. But DO check `list_tickets` afterwards to see whether yours was combined, and verify the rewrite kept your evidence.

2. `update_task(append=True, details=...)` APPENDS TO `details` WITHOUT TOUCHING `description`. This is the safe way to add field corroboration to a long, well-formed task: it avoids retyping (and risking mangling) a multi-thousand-character description. Verified: after the append, `description` was byte-unchanged and `candidate_key` stayed b691b7821100d5b1 — so it does NOT trip the candidate_key recomputation that a description rewrite causes. `append` is documented as "the only knob that governs details/prompt append".

3. `add_dependency` takes `depends_on` (snake_case), not `dependsOn` — the camelCase form fails pydantic validation.

4. `get_statuses` requires `ids` as a real JSON LIST, not a comma-separated string.

5. `resolve_ticket` can time out at the MCP layer while the curator STILL creates the task. Two consecutive timeouts on tkt_0RRRB06C… masked a successful creation (task 3082). Do not re-submit on timeout — poll `list_tickets` instead and read the ticket's status/task_id.

In fused-memory's task_interceptor.py, the curator (TaskCurator.curate) runs ONLY at task creation, never on status transitions. set_task_status / _apply_status_transition emits task_status_changed events and may trigger targeted reconciliation, but does NOT invoke the curator. This means a "human_decomposed=true" or "skip_curator=true" metadata flag persisted at creation does NOT need to be read again on later deferred→pending transitions to defend against curator recombination. Verified via exploration of task_interceptor.py and task_curator.py on 2026-04-28.

In fused-memory/tests/test_ticket_worker.py, test_worker_created_path_emits_journal_event and test_worker_record_task_failure_still_resolves_as_created can fail from two independent, unrelated causes that share the same test names — don't conflate them when diagnosing a failure there. (1) Leaked TaskInterceptor._curator_worker async-pollution (task 2737, fixed): shows as task-destroyed/loop-closed noise; fixed via the autouse reap_leaked_ticket_workers() fixture in conftest.py. (2) Incomplete curator mock (task 2720, still open as of 2026-07-18): these two tests never call _stub_prepare_candidate() on their curator MagicMock, so under CPU contention (e.g. pytest -n auto) _prepare_ticket's `await curator.prepare_candidate(...)` can hit the unconfigured MagicMock attribute and raise `TypeError: object MagicMock can't be used in 'await' expression`, silently dropping the ticket's task_created event. Diagnostic: check the traceback — task-destroyed/loop-closed noise implicates the 2737 class (now fixed); a curator.prepare_candidate TypeError implicates 2720 (unfixed).

When the fused-memory curator's UsageGate is PAUSED, submit_task tickets accumulate as 'pending' and resolve_ticket BLOCKS until its timeout rather than returning a status — so a caller that treats a resolve_ticket timeout as a transport hiccup will believe a task was filed when none exists. Observed 2026-08-12 ~11:58Z: get_curator_state returned {paused: True, paused_reason: 'HTTP 403', soonest_open_at: '2026-08-12T13:00:00Z', account_count: 6}, and four submitted tickets sat pending with task_id null — three filed at 11:41-11:42 by another session plus one at 11:57 — so task filing was stalled project-wide, not per-caller. The diagnostic sequence when resolve_ticket times out: list_tickets(status='pending') to see whether a task_id was ever assigned, then get_curator_state to learn WHY. Nothing is lost while paused (candidate_title is preserved on the ticket and the worker drains when the gate reopens), but the tickets must be re-polled afterwards to confirm they became tasks. Note six accounts returning HTTP 403 together reads more like an auth failure than a quota exhaustion.

Root-cause mechanism for the fused-memory task-curator's misclassified timeouts (found 2026-08-10, owned by task 3995): task_curator._call_llm / _call_llm_batch call shared.cli_invoke.invoke_with_cap_retry WITHOUT config_dir or session_id. Two consequences follow from that single omission. (1) In cli_invoke._run_subprocess the two-regime liveness watchdog computes `_grace_spent = seen_turn or elapsed >= startup_grace_secs or not (config_dir and session_id)`; with both None the third disjunct is permanently True, so the 120s startup-grace fast kill CAN NEVER FIRE for the curator and every failure necessarily runs to the full 180s ceiling. This means "it burned the full 180s budget", cited as evidence of a backend hang in every curator escalation, is actually an artifact of the watchdog being disabled. (2) transcript_turns stays None, so _parse_claude_output's `error_timeout_killed_with_progress` arm (which requires transcript_turns > 0) is unreachable and the subtype is always error_empty_output, while is_zero_output_timeout falls back to the legacy `turns==0 and cost_usd==0.0` heuristic and returns True on every timeout. Task 1778 (status done) fixed exactly this class of misdiagnosis in the orchestrator by threading config_dir/session_id and reading the transcript; the curator never opted in.

Fact (fused-memory task curator internals, observed 2026-07-13): the curator builds its drop/combine/create dedup pool from four streams in TaskCurator._build_corpus (task_curator.py) — review-chain anchor, module-lock pool, embedding neighbors (Qdrant semantic search over the curator corpus), and dependency neighbors of the anchor. Each PoolTask carries status and combine_eligible (combine_eligible = status=='pending'). The LLM decides drop (covered by an existing non-cancelled task, any of pending/in-progress/blocked/done) / combine (fold into a PENDING target, rewrite it) / create. submit_task(planning_mode=True) is the curator-bypass path: it writes the task directly in 'deferred' status with no dedup and no LLM call; commit_planning then flips the deferred batch to 'pending'. This is the reliable escape hatch when curator dedup misfires (e.g. against an orphaned corpus vector) or when filing a batch of intentionally-related tasks that must not be merged.

Completed: Post-ZOT duplicate sweep: after a curator zero-output hang degrades dedupe to create, diff the tasks created in that window against the corpus and flag near-duplicates — the class has no live owner
Description: RULING (Leo, 2026-09-14, decision docket D5 option A; from reify esc-7459-1). Give the curator-ZOT duplicate class a live owner and a structural safeguard.

THE MECHANISM. When the task-curator's LLM call hangs with zero output until the 180s timeout (subtype=error_empty_output, turns=0, sonnet + json-schema call shape), dedupe silently DEGRADES TO CREATE: the caller sees a normal {status:"created"} with no signal that the dedupe check never ran. dark_factory 1743 (done, merged f8a612d8) shipped the defensive patch that stops one hung call wedging subsequent calls, and its predecessor 1550 is cancelled — so the class currently has NO live owner, and duplicates keep landing. NOTE: an earlier reify record claimed "task 1743 is unrelated GUI work"; that was a project-attribution error (reify 1743 is GUI; dark_factory 1743 is this) — cite "dark_factory 1743".

BASE RATE, five confirmed degrade windows: 2026-08-25 DUPLICATE (reify 6583 filed as a strict subset of pending 5436); 2026-09-11 DUPLICATE (reify 7416 vs 7383 at cosine 0.68, retitled SUPERSEDED and cancelled); 2026-09-12 21:07 clean (candidate resolved to exactly one task, 7480); 2026-09-13 00:56 clean (7490); 2026-09-14 01:42 clean (7517). Two of five produce duplicates; the three clean windows were each verified by search_tasks during the reify L2 watch, not assumed. Manual discipline ("search_tasks before AND after filing", procedural memory 377a4ad6) has already failed twice.

WORK. On each curator ZOT event (the circuit-breaker/escalator already files a curator_zero_output_hang escalation with the candidate title and timestamp), run a sweep: for every task created in the project within +/- N minutes of the hang, run the curator's own dedupe query against the corpus EXCLUDING the task itself, and if a near-duplicate scores above the curator's combine threshold, either (a) auto-file a curator ticket proposing the combine, or (b) at minimum stamp the escalation and the new task's metadata with the candidate duplicate id and score so a human sees it in the L2 record rather than discovering it later. Prefer (a) if the combine path is already idempotent. Do not delete or cancel automatically.

VERIFY. A test that simulates a ZOT (mock the LLM call to return empty output), files a candidate whose near-duplicate exists, and asserts the sweep flags the pair. Plus a control where no near-duplicate exists and nothing is flagged.
Analysis: GOAL (Leo ruling, docket D5 option A). When the task-curator's LLM call hangs with zero output until the 180s timeout, dedupe silently DEGRADES TO CREATE and the caller sees a normal {status:"created"}. Two of five confirmed degrade windows produced a real duplicate. Give the class a live owner: on each ZOT degrade, run the curator's own dedupe query against the corpus EXCLUDING the new task, and if a near-duplicate scores above a flagging threshold, stamp the new task's metadata AND file an operator-visible escalation. Never delete, cancel, or auto-combine.
