FACT, verified 2026-08-24: there is NO code path anywhere that dispatches, schedules or launches a memory-consolidation curation sitting. The sitting is 100% human-initiated via the /curate-fused-memories slash command. Evidence: skills/curate-fused-memories/ contains SKILL.md and nothing else (no scripts, no references/, no hooks/); ~/.claude/commands/curate-fused-memories.md is a SYMLINK to it and is the sole registration, registering it as a human-typed slash command rather than an agent-invocable skill; it is NOT installed under ~/.claude/skills/. `git grep -n 'curate-fused-memories'` over tracked files gives 10 hits, all prose or comments (CHANGELOG.md:211, OPERATIONS.md:676, fused-memory/config/config.yaml:359 in a commented-out block, config/schema.py:2329 in a field description, server/mem0_update_authz.py:51 in a comment, a test docstring, plans/mem0-in-place-update-decision.md, plans/memory-consolidation-cluster-ledger.md, and SKILL.md twice) — ZERO call sites. `git grep 'curator_sitting'` over *.py gives zero. crontab -l has one unrelated entry (cleanup_test_collections.py). No systemd user unit matches curat*/consolid*. No watcher skill (escalation-watcher, recon-escalation-watcher, spawn) mentions curation at all. HOMONYM TRAP worth knowing: fused-memory/src/fused_memory/middleware/task_curator.py and middleware/curator_escalator.py are the TASK-creation curator (the LLM drop/combine/create gate at add_task time) and have nothing to do with memory curation — likewise dashboard tab_curator.jsx and the esc-task-curator-* escalation ids. RELATED: recon Stage 1's memory_consolidator DOES hold memory-write tools under agent_id='recon-stage-memory_consolidator' and does consolidate — but only inline and finding-scoped, fenced at reconciliation/prompts/stage1.py:417 ("ONLY address the specific findings listed in the payload. Do NOT perform general consolidation."). Recon's only relationship to the sitting is FILING gate tasks and escalations; nothing reads the gate backlog and launches an adjudication pass.

Flaky test finding (2026-07-17): fused-memory tests/test_ticket_worker.py has async-worker test pollution — background ticket-worker tasks leak between tests under xdist/ordering, intermittently causing test_worker_created_path_emits_journal_event (0 task_created events) or test_worker_record_task_failure_still_resolves_as_created ("record broke" leak) to fail. The 'curator.prepare_candidate failed: MagicMock can't be used in await' ERROR in the log is a red herring — it is swallowed (fallback to per-ticket curate) and appears in passing runs too. Confirmed NOT attributable to task 2711 (stale-run recovery): 2711 touches only reconciliation harness/journal/event_buffer, never task_interceptor.py or test_ticket_worker.py (byte-identical to main), and the ticket_worker file passes 39/39 both with and without 2711's src changes applied. Root cause and fix belong in test_ticket_worker.py isolation (worker draining/cancellation), out of 2711's scope. Related: task 2564 main-health probe.

Curator empty-output/full-timeout hang (subtype=error_empty_output, turns=0, cost_usd=0.0, latency≈180s): the existing shared.cli_invoke._run_subprocess timeout+SIGTERM/SIGKILL process-group reaping already kills the hung child (confirmed 2026-06-12: no lingering process after reap), and usage_gate.invoke_slot releases the slot, so a single hung curator call does NOT wedge subsequent calls at the OS/gate level. The real defects are (1) curator_escalator's 1h rolling burst window masks a sustained outage as 'failure 1 of 3' when hangs are hours apart, and (2) no watchdog stops every curate() call from burning the full 180s timeout during a hang window. Root cause is external (transient Anthropic backend degradation on the curator's sonnet+json-schema call shape, account-correlated) per cancelled task 1550 — not reproducible, so the deliverable is a defensive watchdog + distinct un-suppressed escalation + forensic evidence capture, contained to the curator middleware (NOT shared cli_invoke, which recon uses healthily on the same accounts).

=== CORRECTED 2026-08-20 — THE "ROOT CAUSE IS EXTERNAL ... PER CANCELLED TASK 1550" CLAIM ABOVE IS UNSUPPORTED. READ THIS FIRST. ===
The "transient Anthropic-backend degradation" root cause was never established by task 1550 (a cancelled, open-ended investigation that named it only candidate #2 of 4 and was cancelled without ever producing the "concrete evidence" its own acceptance criteria demanded) — it is doc drift from a code comment landed by task 1743 (fused-memory/src/fused_memory/config/schema.py:1959-1964), restated here as if settled. Direct transcript audit (task 3995, escalation esc-task-curator-14) of the three ever-filed curator zero-output cases found only 1 of 3 was a genuine pre-turn stall (transcript 42efe70b); d9b60a7a had a COMPLETED StructuredOutput verdict computed 57s before SIGTERM and thrown away, and 91c4bcfd wandered into tool calls before being killed at the wall. See memory da752628-9dec-4b06-be4e-cc03aeefd6e2 for the full correction. The rest of this entry — cli_invoke reaping behavior, the curator_escalator burst-window masking defect, and the no-watchdog gap — is unaffected and still correct.

In fused-memory, planning_mode tasks (submit_task planning_mode=True → TaskInterceptor._submit_task_planning_mode) bypass the ticket/curator path and NEVER call curator.record_task, and commit_planning (server/tools.py) does not index either — so PRD-decomposed tasks stay invisible to search_tasks/curator dup-detection. No cron or reconciliation stage runs maintenance/backfill_curator_corpus.py; the only automatic path is TaskInterceptor._maybe_backfill_corpus, a one-shot that runs ONLY when the curator corpus is empty (corpus_count==0). Root fix (task 2562) is write-time indexing at commit_planning's deferred→pending flip.

OBSERVATION (dark_factory, 2026-08-04): the TaskCurator can be cap-hit on ALL accounts simultaneously, which silently stalls every two-phase task filing fleet-wide. Observed in fused-memory.service logs: "task-curator[dark_factory]: cap hit (4 consecutive), sleeping 5s then resuming ... on account max-b", escalating through max-b / max-d to "cap hit on all accounts (6 consecutive), sleeping 5s then waiting for reset".

SYMPTOM AT THE CALL SITE: `submit_task` returns a ticket normally, then `resolve_ticket` TIMES OUT — twice in a row here, at 115s and 110s. That reads like a curator failure but is not: querying data/reconciliation/tickets.db directly showed the ticket row present with status='pending', task_id=NULL, reason=NULL. The ticket is DURABLE and will be curated when caps reset; nothing was lost and re-filing would duplicate.

WHAT TO DO: on a resolve_ticket timeout, check the ticket's row in tickets.db and the curator's account state in the fused-memory journal BEFORE retrying or re-filing. Three tickets were left legitimately pending this way at session end.

NOTE the contrast with the usual multi-account guidance ("≥1 uncapped account = full capacity"): that holds only while some account is uncapped. Here all accounts were capped at once, so the pool offered no headroom at all — the failure mode is total, not degraded.

A separate, earlier curator failure the same day (escalation esc-task-curator-8) was an isolated LLM error: empty output, subtype=error_during_execution, turns=3, duration_ms=158411 against a 180s configured timeout, cost_usd=0.4415, failures_in_window=1 of 3. Different cause; do not conflate a single empty-output failure with account exhaustion.

content: fused-memory curator gotcha (task 4513, 2026-10-13): since 4513, TaskCurator.curate returns action='defer' (never 'create') when the curator cannot judge — non-ZOT CuratorFailureError, corpus failure, all-accounts-capped, generic exception, ZOT breaker open (justification 'curation-deferred: <reason>'); the batch path defers an escaped exception too, so the ticket parks as 'awaiting_curation'. Consequence for tests: a class-level monkeypatch stub of TaskCurator.curate MUST accept the keyword-only `prepared=` argument (curate_batch_prepared calls curate(..., prepared=...)); a stub without it used to pass silently because the TypeError fell through to create, and now parks the ticket instead. Tests pinning create-on-outage also live outside test_task_curator.py (e.g. test_task_curator_timeout_evidence.py, test_operational_routing_boundary_matrix.py), so run the FULL fused-memory suite (`uv run pytest -n 8`, ~5 min) rather than only a curator-targeted list.

candidates.content: Reify doc-chunk harness gotcha: geometry.md, units.md and examples/tolerancing/gdt_zones.ri cite harness tests as `geometry_chunk_smoke.rs::<fn>` / `units_chunk_smoke.rs::<fn>` (about 17 distinct cites), and the cite gate resolves each to a declared fn. Renaming or deleting a cited #[test] in crates/reify-compiler/tests/harness_doc_chunks/ reds the cite gate unless the chunk is edited in the same commit. List them before any refactor: `git grep -h -o -E '(units|geometry)_chunk_smoke\.rs::[a-z_]+' -- crates/reify-mcp/src/tools/chunks/ examples/ docs/ | sort -u`.

Reify's cited-test-path ratchet (tests/infra/test_cited_test_paths_resolve.sh via tests/infra/cited-test-path-lib.sh::cited_test_path_scan) flags a citation of crates/<crate>/tests/<x>.rs only when the cited path no longer resolves BUT a file with the same basename still exists under the SAME crate's tests tree (index key `<crate>/<basename>`). So moving a test file into a different crate's tests/ never reds that gate. Stale cross-crate citations go undetected and have to be fixed by hand. Moving a file within a crate (e.g. flat -> harness_*/) does red it unless the citation is repointed.

Reify's cited-test-path ratchet (tests/infra/test_cited_test_paths_resolve.sh, --list prints a suggested target per stale citation) resolves by `<crate>/<basename>` only. Its suggestion is a basename hint, not proof: in task 5703 it pointed macros.rs's `corpus_shard_tests!` cite at harness_cache/snapshot_cache_divergence_gate.rs, but that macro had since been split into harness_corpus_gates/eval_invariant_corpus_sweep.rs. Units moved across crates (reify-eval → reify-eval-fea-tests) are not reported at all. Always grep the cited symbol in the suggested target before repointing.

tests/infra/test_cited_test_paths_resolve.sh only scans citations matching CITED_TEST_PATH_REGEX `crates/[a-z0-9-]+/tests/...\.rs` (tests/infra/cited-test-path-lib.sh). So a doc comment citing a test file WITHOUT the `crates/` prefix (e.g. `reify-compiler/tests/foo.rs`) is never checked and can go stale silently. Observed on task #7357: crates/reify-eval/src/modal_ops.rs cited the pre-#5694 path `reify-compiler/tests/modal_mechanism_compile.rs` long after #5694 moved that file into harness_mechanics/. When writing or repointing a test-file citation, use the full `crates/<crate>/tests/...` form so the gate guards it.

Reify doc-chunk gotcha (crates/reify-mcp/src/tools/chunks/*.md): chunk_cite_gate.rs scans the WHOLE markdown, fenced blocks included, and treats any `/`-bearing token whose last segment has a letter-led extension (e.g. `parts/bolt.ri`, `sub/dep.ri`) as a repo cite that must resolve to a real file. A hypothetical illustrative path therefore reds `cargo test -p reify-compiler --test harness_doc_chunks`. Bare basenames (`bracket.ri`, `mod.ri`) are safe unless followed by `::fn`. Describe hypothetical nested locations in words ("`bolt.ri` in a `parts` directory") instead.

In reify, stale `crates/<c>/tests/**/*.rs` prose path citations are machine-gated by task #7095's one-directional ratchet: tests/infra/test_cited_test_paths_resolve.sh (--gate-only, <1s) against tests/infra/cited-test-path-baseline.manifest, with derivation in tests/infra/cited-test-path-lib.sh (`cited_test_path_scan .` lists every stale cite plus its suggested target). For any citation-repoint sweep, drain the relevant baseline rows first; the gate then reds naming every live site (a free RED test), repointing turns it green, and dead rows can be dropped freely. The regex anchors on `crates/`, so partial forms like `reify-compiler/tests/x.rs` are invisible to it.

reify's cited-test-path gate (tests/infra/test_cited_test_paths_resolve.sh, task #7095) SUPPLEMENTS memory 0c1a520e-6eac-4ccd-9b3d-cb395148cb5e with its scan GRAMMAR, which decides whether a citation is guarded at all: CITED_TEST_PATH_REGEX='crates/[a-z0-9-]+/tests/[A-Za-z0-9_./-]+\.rs' (tests/infra/cited-test-path-lib.sh:53). Only the FULL repo-relative form is scanned — a bare stem (`examples_smoke.rs`) and, the non-obvious one, a HALF-PATH (`harness_compilation_surface/examples_smoke.rs`) both match nothing and are completely invisible to the gate. So when repairing a stale citation, writing the half-path looks like a fix, reads like a fix, and leaves the citation just as unguarded as the bare stem was; it is also unresolvable for a human reader whenever the citing file lives under a different crate. Measured first-hand on task #7015 (branch tip vs base main 362adf9bd3): the two files it repaired carried 0 guard-visible citations on base and 8 on HEAD (7 in crates/reify-eval/tests/harness_corpus_gates/best_practices_constraint_gate.rs, 1 in .claude/skills/reify-design/SKILL.md) — i.e. the repair's real payoff was moving citations from human-only to machine-enforced, and two review-driven amendment commits were needed precisely because the first drafts used the half-path. Pair this with the standing preference for symbol-name anchors (`foo.rs::some_fn`) over line numbers (`foo.rs:248`): line numbers are what rot, and nothing in the tree gates them (1890 `<file>.rs:<N>` citations across 452 tracked .rs files on that same tree).

Reify has NO gate validating `<path>:<line>` citations into `src/`: tests/infra/test_cited_test_paths_resolve.sh resolves only `crates/<crate>/tests/**/*.rs` PATHS, so a stale source line number in docs or a doc-comment rots silently through the merge gate. Measured case (task 7022): the `frame_to_frame` arm cite rotted 512 → 605 → stale-at-620 as the arm migrated 605→612→613→618→620, and the re-pin to `:605` landed already-stale in the very commit meant to fix the staleness, stamped `as of <date>`. Cite source locations by grep-able symbol anchor (e.g. `grep -n '"frame_to_frame" =>'`) instead of a line number; the capability-manifest yaml already models this with `delivered_check: {kind: grep, pattern: ...}` and `binding: grep:<path> <symbol>` clauses.

Reify's cited-test-path ratchet (tests/infra/test_cited_test_paths_resolve.sh + cited-test-path-lib.sh) validates PATHS ONLY, never line numbers: cited_test_path_fingerprint deliberately erases the line number ("never captured in the first place") so a citation moving within its file cannot spuriously red the gate. Consequence when repointing a stale `grep:<path>:<start>-<end>` citation after a test-file rename: fixing the path alone turns the gate green even if the line range now brackets a completely different test. Re-derive the range from two independent anchors (the `fn` line and a distinctive fixture line inside the body) and check the span length — the gate will not catch a wrong number for you.

Backticked file-path citations in reify Rust doc comments are written BOTH repo-relative and CRATE-relative, and any tool that resolves them must try both. Measured 2026-09-03 over tracked .rs comment lines: 3156 cites total — 2655 resolve at repo root, 235 resolve ONLY against the citing file's crate root (e.g. `tests/common/mod.rs` cited from inside crates/reify-eval means crates/reify-eval/tests/common/mod.rs), 2 only against the citing file's directory, 73 are glob PATTERNS not paths (`tests/*.rs`, `examples/**/*.ri`), and 166 resolve under none of the three (= genuinely stale). A naive repo-root-only existence check therefore has a ~59% false-positive rate. Related rot on main: crates/reify-types was folded into crates/reify-core by commit 19a312f6ef, and ~20 doc comments still cite the dead crates/reify-types/src/{diagnostics,value,hash,stubs}.rs; 5 files still cite crates/reify-compiler/tests/examples_smoke.rs, whose live path is crates/reify-compiler/tests/harness_compilation_surface/examples_smoke.rs.

In reify's `crates/reify-eval/` doc comments, cross-references must be SYMBOL ANCHORS (a greppable fn/type name, or a twin's block-header comment text), never raw line numbers or file paths — line-number cites rot within weeks in these large files. Measured drift: task 6230's cite of the `TopologyAttributeTable::default()` reset moved :3239→:3348 in under three weeks; the two intra-file "around line NNNN" pins in engine_edit.rs were ~330 and ~1280 lines off. Landed convention: task 6230 (lib.rs, 001eb7f206), task 6423 D8 (engine_edit.rs, e1bc303e2c), task 6479. Extend it to file paths too — cite a unique test-FUNCTION name with no path, since a corrected path re-rots when the test moves (engine_edit.rs cited `tests/tolerance_wiring_e2e.rs`, which never existed; the file is at `crates/reify-eval/tests/harness_tolerance/tolerance_wiring_e2e.rs`). When repairing such a cite, reuse the exact phrasing already landed at the sibling site rather than composing new wording, so all copies stay grep-identical (SPOT).

In reify, a repo gate that checks "every cited crates/<c>/tests/<stem>.rs path in prose resolves on the tree" is UNUSABLE as stated: of 820 distinct cited test paths, 230 do not resolve, and 108 of those are hermetic fixture strings living inside existing test source (crates/alpha/tests/foo.rs, crates/foo/tests/bar.rs, crates/beta/tests/thing.rs, ...) plus deleted files and illustrative examples. Only the harness-consolidation move class is actionable: cited path unresolved AND exactly one crates/<same crate>/tests/harness_*/<same basename> exists. Phrase the predicate that way rather than "flat path moved under harness_", so it also catches harness-to-harness re-moves from the #5620 over-cap SPLIT (live example: harness_fea_solver_e2e/stress_error_messages.rs is cited but the file now lives in harness_stress_scenarios/). A single `git grep -nIoE` pass over all 4161 tracked files costs ~1.1s, so whole-tree prose scanning is cheap enough for a merge gate.

reify's cited-test-path gate (tests/infra/test_cited_test_paths_resolve.sh) uses a ONE-DIRECTIONAL subset ratchet against tests/infra/cited-test-path-baseline.manifest: current findings must be a SUBSET of the baseline. So FIXING a grandfathered stale citation (repointing prose to the real crates/<crate>/tests/harness_<subsystem>/<file>.rs path) keeps the gate green with no baseline edit — the now-unused baseline row is harmless. That matters for scoped tasks, which usually do not hold a lock on the manifest. Note also its documented scope limit: a citation whose basename resolves NOWHERE (a deleted or renamed-away test) is deliberately NOT reported, so stale cites of vanished test NAMES must be caught by review, not by this gate.

Any reify task that MOVES a test file must run `bash tests/infra/test_cited_test_paths_resolve.sh` before considering the move done — a hand `git grep` sweep for citations is not sufficient. The gate (landed task #7095) is a whole-tree one-directional ratchet over `<citing file> :: <cited full path>` fingerprints, scanning tracked .rs doc comments, .md prose, .yaml manifests and .ri example comments alike; it prints each break with its exact repointing target after a `->` marker. Measured on task #5696: a manual stem-based grep found 4 of the 15 full-path citations a 24-file harness move broke, while the gate found all 15. Because the scan is whole-tree, a stale citation left on main re-fires for every unrelated task that later rebases onto that tip.

Reify now HAS a gate for stale prose citations of moved test files. Task #7095 landed tests/infra/test_cited_test_paths_resolve.sh, a one-directional ratchet (live ⊆ baseline) over every `crates/<c>/tests/**/*.rs` citation in tracked files. Its scan is tests/infra/cited-test-path-lib.sh (`cited_test_path_scan .` emits file\tcited\tverdict\ttarget) and its grandfather list is tests/infra/cited-test-path-baseline.manifest. The sweep recipe used by task #6468: (1) delete that path's baseline rows with a filter, which gives RED; (2) repoint with an in-place sed, which gives GREEN. The gate's regex anchors on `crates/`, so a partial form like `reify-compiler/tests/x.rs` is invisible to it.

Reify citation convention for cross-file references after a test-file relocation into a consolidated harness dir: cite the FULL repo-relative path (e.g. `crates/reify-compiler/tests/harness_compilation_surface/examples_smoke.rs`) plus a symbol name, never a bare directory-relative prefix like `harness_compilation_surface/examples_smoke.rs` and never a `:<line>` number. The half-path form resolves from nowhere when the citing file lives in a different crate — e.g. `crates/reify-eval/tests/harness_corpus_gates/` — so it trades a wrong path for an unresolvable one. The cited-test-path gate (tests/infra/cited-test-path-lib.sh, CITED_TEST_PATH_REGEX = `crates/[a-z0-9-]+/tests/[A-Za-z0-9_./-]+\.rs`) only sees full paths, so half-paths escape the staleness ratchet entirely, and line numbers rot silently. This cost task 7015 two separate review amendments (341903acd2 for the .rs, 1a94998e5e for SKILL.md) after its own task description had literally suggested the half-path prefix. Two companion rules from the same task: replace a hardcoded line number with a symbol-name anchor rather than a refreshed number (one #5693-era relocation drifted three citations by three different magnitudes: 13→15, 636→426, 248→368), and never anchor a citation by quoting the cited comment's prose verbatim — nothing in the tree checks such a quotation, so it is an unchecked second copy that goes silently false on the next rewording.

Stale crates/<crate>/tests/**/*.rs prose citations ARE gated in reify now. The 2026-08-31 observation that there is "no gate" is outdated. tests/infra/test_cited_test_paths_resolve.sh (task #7095) ratchets live stale citations ⊆ tests/infra/cited-test-path-baseline.manifest, and its `--list` flag prints (file, cited, verdict, suggested target) records. The sanctioned burn-down is two commits: first drain the rows from the baseline (RED), then repoint by running a literal substitution driven by `--list` (GREEN), as #6468 did (b376faca03, 1754c8d7e6) and #7501 does. The gate deliberately ignores citations whose basename resolves nowhere (deleted tests, fixtures, forward refs), so renamed-and-moved targets such as money_force_diag_tests.rs -> harness_units_materials/money_force_diagnostic_tests.rs need a manual check.

In crates/reify-eval/src/engine_edit.rs (edit_param/edit_source Contract-lock comment blocks), doc-comment citations to pinning tests by file PATH ("in `tests/tolerance_wiring_e2e.rs`") were stale the same way raw line numbers are: the real path is `crates/reify-eval/tests/harness_tolerance/tolerance_wiring_e2e.rs`, reachable only via `#[path = "harness_tolerance/tolerance_wiring_e2e.rs"]` in `tests/harness_tolerance.rs` — the bare `tests/tolerance_wiring_e2e.rs` never existed. A test-file path cite rots whenever tests get reorganized into a `#[path]`-based harness crate root; grep the actual `#[path = ...]` directive rather than trusting a cited path. Task 6479 (commit 5d754e74f0) fixed all four occurrences by dropping the path entirely and citing only the already-unique test function name, matching a no-path style the same paragraphs already used in one spot ("... plus `edit_source_clears_realization_cache_..._build` (step-19)." with no path) — i.e. prefer symbol/name anchors over any location pin, including file paths, not just line numbers. See sibling entry on task 6230/6479 line-number cite rot in the same file (mem0 id 671e9f88-2cfd-4f15-9903-dd55b0000312) for the line-number half of this pattern.

Reify has NO gate for stale prose path references to moved integration tests: the CMP-*/C-eval-* harness-consolidation series git-mv'd crates/<c>/tests/<stem>.rs into crates/<c>/tests/harness_<subsystem>/<stem>.rs, silently orphaning every doc-comment/PRD/manifest citation of the old flat path, and crates/reify-audit/src/ (p1/p2/p5/pdead/pdoccover/pdssentinel/player/ptodo/puntested) plus tests/infra/ contain no path-resolution check. Correction has been by manual sweep only — task #6214 (commit 276d32f025, 123 files) then task #6468 (60 files / 69 occurrences for the basename examples_smoke.rs alone) — and manual sweeps demonstrably do not converge: #6214 fixed tree-sitter-reify/test/corpus/io-formats.txt line 5 while leaving the same defect on line 7 of that header block, and fixed a capability-manifest .md without its .yaml twin. The sweep convention both tasks used is a pure path-segment insertion that preserves trailing :LINE numbers and ::selector suffixes verbatim, with a never-edit exclusion set of docs/architecture-audit/findings/*.md, docs/notes/*-2026-*.md and docs/legibility/confusion-codebook.yaml. The citation surface is wider than .rs/.md/.sh — live references also sit in .ri example header comments, .yaml capability manifests and tree-sitter .txt corpus headers — so any future scanner must be extension-agnostic over tracked files.

Reify harness-split tasks (HARNESS_KLOC_CAP rule (a)): before choosing which modules to move, run the cited-test-path gate's own harvester to price each candidate cut — `source tests/infra/cited-test-path-lib.sh; cited_test_path_citations . | grep -F "harness_<sub>/"`. Its resolver keys on <crate>/<basename>, so moving a file inside the same crate's tests/ tree keeps it RESOLVABLE but makes the literal cited path untracked, which is a GATING stale finding unless the citation is repointed or baselined. On task #7466 the two candidate cuts of harness_occt differed by 13 broken citations vs 2 (across 4 crates and 5 PRD docs), which decided the split direction. Citations only count if they carry the `crates/` prefix — CITED_TEST_PATH_REGEX is 'crates/[a-z0-9-]+/tests/[A-Za-z0-9_./-]+\.rs', so a comment saying `reify-kernel-occt/tests/...` is ungated (but still goes stale and should be fixed).

content: Reify gotcha: a `path::fn` cite inside a Rust doc comment under crates/*/tests/ is NOT checked by any gate. `chunk_cite_gate.rs::assert_cited_paths_resolve` (harness_doc_chunks) scans only the MCP chunk markdown (crates/reify-mcp/src/tools/chunks/*.md). PLINECITE (#6935) excludes crates/*/tests/ by design. tests/infra/test_cited_test_paths_resolve.sh (#7095) catches only a cited crates/<c>/tests/*.rs PATH whose basename moved, never a renamed or retired fn. Before writing such a cite, `git grep 'fn <name>('` to confirm the target exists. Example: geometry_chunk_smoke.rs::polygon_compiles was retired by #6956, so a task-suggested cite to it would have dangled silently (task 7056).

The undertaking sentence was sent back with direction: say plainly that the download exists only until the session is deleted, by the prospect's button, by request, or by the automatic purge, because people delete first and then are annoyed; redrafted in the PRD §Wording under "Deleting it, and what is left", awaiting approval. Still unreviewed in that section: the control's note, the archive and entry names, the conversation document's heading and the "Times are UTC" note.

candidates.content: solar_challenge e2e: to simulate the CDN-Alpine flake on demand (memory 3cd4261b), add `page.route(lambda url: "alpinejs@" in url, lambda route: route.abort())` as a test's first statement. Measured 2026-09-30 while planning task 161: with Alpine absent, any Playwright click on the main content times out after 30 s with "<aside> ... subtree intercepts pointer events", because the Alpine-bound `lg:ml-64` margin never applies and the fixed desktop sidebar covers the page. fill() does no hit-test and still works. So in an Alpine-dependent test, put the first user-visible expect() before any click, so a lost Alpine fails in 5 s naming the element instead of 30 s naming the sidebar.

solar_challenge e2e Alpine flake: the first sighting after Alpine was vendored (2026-10-03, task 409 implementer, task/409 on base main bdb831a, which includes task 194's merge 8cc1a19). Full non-slow lane run 1 gave 1 failed, 171 passed. The failure was tests/e2e/test_home_simulation.py::test_optional_block_form_submission_is_accepted[chromium-seg-EDF]: the 30 s Locator.click timeout on its first tab click after goto ('Tariff'). Its captured server log had GET /simulate/home, both stylesheets and GET /static/vendor/alpinejs/collapse-3.14.8.min.js. It had no GET of /static/vendor/alpinejs/alpinejs-3.14.8.min.js and no GET /api/presets. The node passed alone on rerun (4.34 s), and run 2 was 172/172 green. loadavg was 90-185 on 32 cores. /simulate/home loads only local resources. This contradicts amendment c3369176's inference that a page loading only base.html's now-local scripts can no longer show this shape: the shape does not need a CDN fetch. Its cause is unmeasured; follow-up ticket tkt_0RVBZFZGJXR2F9WHADTJSSR5HW (agent-followup-409) asks for browser-side evidence. Until then, when this shape is the only red after a change that does not touch the page, rerun the node once before debugging the change, and add a sighting here.

solar_challenge e2e technique, measured 2026-10-08 by task 512's architect (playwright 1.61, pytest-playwright 0.8.0). To see a page as it renders before Alpine starts, open it in a context from pytest-playwright's new_context fixture with java_script_enabled=False. The fixture is typed pytest_playwright.CreateContextCallback and closes the context at teardown. Locators still work with JavaScript off. After page.goto's load event, static/style.css's [x-cloak] rule has hidden every cloaked element, so get_by_role(...).is_visible() reads what the page shows until Alpine starts. tests/e2e/conftest.py's network-change rerun hook watches only the default `context`, so keep a test's request-heavy JS-on half on the default `page`.

solar_challenge e2e flake, 2nd sighting (task 173, 2026-09-30; the first is memory f279df6a): a page load can lose its CDN-hosted Alpine (both cdn.jsdelivr.net scripts fail with net::ERR_NETWORK_CHANGED and `typeof window.Alpine` is 'undefined'), so the Alpine-rendered tabs never appear. The test then dies with a 30 s Locator.click timeout on its first interaction after page.goto (the server log lacks the GET /api/presets that Alpine's init makes on healthy loads), or a guard such as test_toast_and_dialogs.py::test_confirm_dialog_appears_on_delete silently skips. Measured with a 500-load loop and no test code: 1 total loss plus 1 collapse-plugin-only loss; 2 of 4 full non-slow runs were affected. If an e2e-lane fix task names a test that timed out on its first tab or element after goto, rerun once before debugging code (follow-up ticket tkt_0RV80928W194R3727KH2RPX9X1, escalation esc-173-1).

Amendment to 8d98ecaa (task 288's e2e layout gotcha), measured 2026-10-09 on main 7b6d1ae by task 288's architect with Playwright headless Chromium on /simulate/fleet at 1100 px: right after page.goto returns, the main column's margin-left CSSTransition was still running with the margin at 0px in 5 of 5 loads, so the cards are about 256 px wider than when settled and a width check made then passes falsely; the wait before measuring is required, not insurance. Prefer page.wait_for_function("() => !document.getAnimations().some(animation => animation instanceof CSSTransition)") over getAnimations().length === 0: transitions are always finite, so an infinite CSS animation added to the page later (e.g. an animate-spin spinner) cannot hang the wait, and it gave the same RED on base and GREEN on the fix as the all-animations wait.

solar_challenge e2e CDN-Alpine flake, sightings 6-8 (2026-10-01, task 234 implementer, task/234 at 07fddd7 on base main 545fcc4; host load average 200-330 on 32 cores). Two 130-node --keep-duplicates stability loops over tests/e2e/test_home_simulation.py + test_enable_switches.py failed 2 nodes and then 1 node. Each failure's captured log had GET /simulate/home and both stylesheets but no GET /api/presets, and each node passed when rerun once. Two were the known 30 s Locator.click timeout on the first tab click after goto. The third is a NEW shape: `Page.goto: Timeout 30000ms exceeded ... waiting until "load"` (test_enable_switches.py::test_home_switch_shows_and_hides_its_settings[chromium-tariff]). base.html's only external fetches are the two deferred cdn.jsdelivr.net Alpine scripts; the cdn.tailwindcss.com tag sits inside an HTML comment. Hypothesis: a stalled, rather than dropped, jsdelivr fetch held back the load event. So treat a goto that times out at "load" with no presets fetch as this flake, and rerun once before debugging. The ticket VERIFY (37 passed) and the full non-slow suite (122 passed, 1 skipped) were clean in the same session.

solar_challenge e2e, Playwright 1.61.0, measured by task 298 on 2026-10-07: how to test a debounced Alpine action without sleeping. The example is tests/e2e/test_scenario_builder.py::test_a_refusal_stays_in_the_preview_over_the_preview_an_earlier_edit_queued.
1. Call page.clock.install() before page.goto. The fake time still advances with real time, so the page behaves normally.
2. Do the user actions.
3. Call page.clock.run_for(5_000). It fires the pending setTimeout, here the builder's 500 ms preview, at once.
4. To show that no request was made, record page.on('request'), do one round trip such as Validate, and only then assert.

Separately, avoid Response.finished() in the sync API: it leaves an asyncio task that logs 'Task exception was never retrieved ... Target closed' at teardown. Reading the body with response.json() or .text() also waits for it, without that noise.

- (3) The desktop sidebar is open by default in a fresh context. Its toggle has no aria-expanded; its title reads "Collapse sidebar" when open, so get_by_title("Collapse sidebar", exact=True) is the open-state check.

solar_challenge e2e gotcha: chart widths on page load. Measured 2026-10-14 by task 674's architect at ad42de8, headless Chromium, 1280x720.

solar_challenge e2e technique: proving deterministically whether Alpine's start fires CSS transitions on page load. Measured 2026-10-17 by task 857's architect on main b3d45a3, playwright 1.61, headless Chromium.
- Add an init script with page.add_init_script. It reads the layout in a document 'readystatechange' listener when document.readyState === 'interactive'. That fires after parsing and before any deferred script, so before Alpine, and the read forces a style computation.
- In a document 'alpine:initialized' listener (Alpine 3 fires it once start() has applied every binding), take document.getAnimations().filter(a => a instanceof CSSTransition). getAnimations() flushes style, so a transition Alpine just caused is there, at 0 ms elapsed.
- Do not rely on transitionrun events or waiting frames. In one session's first test, no animation frame advanced for over 600 ms, so no transitionrun fired.
- A width going from auto to a length (e.g. an aside gaining w-64) snaps; it never makes a CSSTransition. Catch it in the pre-Alpine layout instead.
- To check that a click starts a transition, click in the page (locator.evaluate: el.click(); await setTimeout 0; getAnimations()), once per page load. A second click a few ms later reverses transitions that have not advanced a frame and creates no new one.

candidates.content: Open design conflict, escalated as esc-review-cycle-20261010T005928-1 at HEAD c46ea94: ingestion's fail-closed consent check (DecisionReason.CHECK_FAILED, task 440) drops rows that the subscriber has already acked. The telemetry store and the consent session share the db.session engine. So in a Postgres outage longer than consent_recheck_ttl_seconds (300 s), every device's re-check fails and arriving telemetry is dropped and never replayed. This contradicts the briefing's "a DB outage must buffer and replay, no data loss" convention. The options put to the owner: hold the rows unprocessed, honour the last GRANTED standing for a bounded grace, or accept and document the loss. Until it is ruled, do not re-file it as a new defect; cite the escalation.

Ingestion ACK semantics (traced in review 20260928T062907, HEAD 3d74313):
- aiomqtt/paho ACK every QoS-1 message when it arrives, because manual_ack is never set.
- clean_session=False therefore protects only messages the broker has not delivered yet.
- Rows in the in-memory StoreForwardBuffer (up to 2M) are already ACKed, so a restart during a DB outage loses them. The only record is the ERROR "N rows unconfirmed" at subscriber.py:392-396.
- Since task 270, a write still running at shutdown is abandoned on a daemon thread.
This is escalated as a design question (manual ACK after the write, a disk spill, or an accepted carve-out). Do not assume the persistent session makes ingestion restart-lossless.

DISCOVERY (M1 validation 2026-07-03, findings F2+F3, fixed by tasks 133/134/141): three unattended-failure modes witnessed on real infra. (1) scp-ingest crashed on broker disconnect (aiomqtt MqttError propagated out of the subscriber's async-for; no reconnect loop) — root disconnect cause was keepalive starvation: blocking synchronous DB writes inside the asyncio event loop starved PINGREQ during a sustained drain, mosquitto k60 dropped the client. (2) The clean-session subscription (auto client-id, c1) meant mosquitto discarded the queued QoS-1 backlog on disconnect — recovery in validation was only possible because the simulator replay is deterministic and store writes are ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING idempotent; real edge data would have been lost. Unbatched per-message commits drained at only ~90-170 msg/s (fine at production's ~1.7 msg/s, ~50x too slow for backfill). (3) A dispatch process wedged silently mid-tick on a half-dead Postgres socket — main thread epoll-parked, DB sessions idle 15+ min, process alive so systemd Restart=on-failure could never fire; only the device-side 60s watchdog protected the fleet (bare create_engine had no connect_timeout/keepalives/statement_timeout/pre-ping).

Task 583 architect pre-analysis, 2026-10-01, main e1ac08e. Task 583 buffers consent-PENDING rows through a DB outage and re-judges them at flush. It was reported blocked on task 440. Main has no DecisionReason.CHECK_FAILED: task 440's plan exists, but its branch has no commits. Task 309's unmerged branch (task/309, tip 6cae37d) rewrites the same failure path:
- GateConsentChecker raises a failed read.
- ConsentGuard._fail_closed becomes the single fail-closed path.
- Consent checks run through afilter_rows and a CheckRunner on an 'ingest-consent-check' daemon thread.
- Subscriber._admit becomes async, beside a new _admit_blocking.
So plan 583 after both: CHECK_FAILED from _fail_closed becomes a PEND disposition instead of a drop.

Design constraints found:
(1) In Subscriber.run, every flush runs _write_pending on an abandonable 'ingest-store-write' daemon thread under _flush_lock. The guard's cache, counters and logging must stay on the event loop (the 270/309 invariant). So re-judge pending rows on the loop, before rows go to the write thread, never inside _write_pending or StoreForwardBuffer.flush.
(2) Pending rows must share StoreForwardBuffer's one drop-oldest max_depth cap: Settings.ingestion_buffer_max_depth = 2_000_000, with evictions counted in .dropped.
(3) Task 617 makes PLATFORM_OPERATION contract-basis: ConsentGate.check then returns OTHER_LAWFUL_BASIS without reading a row. After that, withdrawing platform_operation consent no longer refuses ingest. A keystone 'withdrawn device' must then be modelled differently, e.g. as a device whose Account is no longer ACTIVE, which GateConsentChecker denies as NO_CONSENT.

Discovery (2026-09-28): consent/enforcement.py::GateConsentChecker.check_device catches every exception and RETURNS a normal NO_CONSENT standing, so ConsentGuard._get_standing caches it for consent_recheck_ttl_seconds (300 s); the guard's own "exception-derived decisions are not cached" branch is unreachable for GateConsentChecker. One DB blip therefore makes scp-ingest drop a consented home's telemetry for up to 5 minutes, violating the briefing's "deny but do not cache" convention. Filed as task 440: DecisionReason.CHECK_FAILED cached only for a short consent_check_failure_ttl_seconds (15 s). Never-cached was rejected because the checker call is synchronous on ingest's event loop (up to the connect timeout per message during a DB fault).

Task 309 (scp-ingest consent re-check blocks the event loop) architect pre-analysis, 2026-09-25, main 4597c4c. MEASURED: a Subscriber under serve() with a ConsentGuard whose checker never returns runs check_device on MainThread and is still alive 8 s after SIGTERM (SIGKILLed); probe at /tmp/scp309/hung_consent_probe.py. Only option (a), moving the read off the loop, can meet the task's required 5 s stop test. Option (b) fails because statement_timeout is server-side, so it cannot bound a network black hole or a hang at the Python level, and pool_timeout 30 s, connect_timeout 10 s and keepalive ~60 s all exceed the grace. Option (c) contradicts that test. asyncio.to_thread is not enough, because asyncio.run and concurrent.futures join default-executor workers at exit, so the read needs task 270's daemon-thread _to_daemon_thread; that helper's thread name 'ingest-store-write' is write-specific. Design points for the re-run: (1) run only checker.check_device on the thread and keep ConsentGuard's cache writes, counters and per-row WARNINGs on the loop, so nothing mutates guard state across threads; (2) GateConsentChecker.check_device logs its own fail-closed WARNING on whatever thread runs it, which brings back task 270's interpreter-finalization logging hazard, and it catches DB faults, so its denial IS cached for the TTL, while the guard backstop's exception denial is NOT cached; preserve that; (3) awaiting the read mid-message adds a new cancellation point: a message already PUBACKed on receipt, with its rows not yet buffered, must be handed to task 252's stop write (Inbox drain / _buffer_and_flush) or reported as unconfirmed; (4) with 252, _drain_and_flush runs _accept, consent included, on an asyncio.to_thread worker at stop, so the 252+270 merge must route it through _to_daemon_thread. Model the stop test on task 270's tests/ingestion/hung_write_process.py plus its subprocess SIGTERM test (_STOP_GRACE_S = 5.0, exit code 0).

[SUPERSEDED 2026-09-24: this is a historical defect list for main 43f9141 and does NOT describe current main. The F1 fixes landed via task 133: reconnect-with-backoff, asyncio.to_thread off-load, and N-or-T batching (done, merged b51e767; completion note ca85f01a). The F2 fix landed via task 134: stable client_id and clean_session=False. See 69b2e220. The QoS-1 ack-on-receipt residual loss is still open, as task 252.] Ingest resilience defects confirmed at main 43f9141 (2026-07-03), scoped for the max-scale PRD F1/F2: (1) ingestion/subscriber.py:110 `async for message in client.messages` has NO try/except and NO reconnect — a broker drop kills the process; (2) the sync handle_message runs inside that async loop (:120) and TimescaleStore.write commits one transaction per message (timeseries/timescale_store.py:146), so blocking DB writes starve the event loop → MQTT keepalive starvation → the broker drops the client (the observed root cause); (3) flush happens every message (:93-100) → ~86-170 msg/s, ~50× too slow for a backfill drain; (4) the aiomqtt client (ingestion/service.py:191) sets no client_id and no clean_session (paho defaults → random id + clean session), so a disconnect loses the queued QoS-1 backlog. Fixes: reconnect wrapper + asyncio.to_thread off-load + N-or-T batching (F1); stable client_id + clean_session=False + mosquitto max_queued_messages 0 (F2). Idempotent ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING (:140) makes replay safe.

[SUPERSEDED 2026-09-24: the idle-flush fix this note waits on HAS LANDED. Task 197 is done (merge 7a604e25589a11b067a754d9bc54f24652508bc3, done_provenance found_on_main), and it carries the scp-ingest idle T-bound flush fix plus drill drain convergence. Task 240 (done, commit 400d6ea1cb0a9a337c466575c8d421ea3a12e9b0) added the Subscriber.run drain on SIGTERM. The stranded-tail behaviour below describes main at ad9557e, not current main. Keep it as a history and diagnosis recipe only. The QoS-1 ack-on-receipt loss, which is a separate issue, is still open as task 252.] GOTCHA (measured by task 197's architect, 2026-09-23, HEAD ad9557e, real Timescale+mosquitto): scp-ingest's Subscriber.run evaluates the buffer's T-bound (ingestion_batch_max_seconds) only when a message ARRIVES (subscriber.py amend-1). When the publisher goes idle, the final partial batch (fewer than ingestion_batch_max_rows=500 rows) sits unflushed in memory indefinitely, and a SIGTERM loses it. One message = one home-tick = len(TICK_METRICS) rows (11 since task 170), so the N-bound flushes every 46 messages. In the dropped-readings drill (2 homes, 1922 ticks), 3844 = 83x46 + 26: the last 13 ticks per home never reached the store. The raw table held 41,998 of 42,284 rows, max(ts) was 23:42, and hh_period 47 read coverage 0.4 on both homes with no drop injected. ONE further message on sc/v1/tel/# (even a junk one the decoder rejects) flushes the whole stranded tail. Consequence for any real-topology harness: a count(*)-quiescence drain cannot tell 'drained' from 'stranded', and a count-convergence drain (_estimate_telemetry_rows) never converges, until the idle-flush fix planned in task 197 lands. How to diagnose: compare SELECT count(*) FROM telemetry against validation.run._estimate_telemetry_rows(...), and check per-home max(ts) against horizon_end.

Task 'P-MaxVal·F1: ingest reconnect + off-loop (asyncio.to_thread) batched writes' completed. Fix the ingest resilience defects the M1 drain hit: the subscriber dies on a broker disconnect with no reconnect, and blocking synchronous per-message DB commits starve the event loop (keepalive starvation -> the broker drops the client). Witnessed live at 43f9141.

Work:
- src/solar_challenge_platform/ingestion/subscriber.py: wrap the `async for message in client.messages` loop (subscriber.py:110, currently NO try/except) in a reconnect-with-backoff loop that resumes cleanly. Off-load the blocking store write via asyncio.to_thread so the event loop keeps servicing MQTT keepalive under sustained write load (root cause of the disconnect: subscriber.py:120 calls the sync handle_message in the async loop; timeseries/timescale_store.py:146 commits one txn per write).
- src/solar_challenge_platform/ingestion/buffer.py: batch — flush at N rows OR T seconds (whichever first), not every message (currently subscriber.py:93-100 flushes per message). Preserves production low-latency (T bound) while making a backfill drain fast (N bound). Thresholds are settings constants.
- tests/ingestion/test_ingest_reconnect.py (hermetic fake broker).

PRD: docs/prds/max-scale-validation-and-endpoint-registry.md task F1 (§3.2/3.4, §4 D11, §9·E, §10·K1, §11·F1)
Capability manifest: docs/prds/max-scale-validation-and-endpoint-registry.capability-manifest.md (Leaf F1)

User-observable signal: a mid-stream broker drop is transparently recovered (reconnect); the event loop keeps servicing keepalive under load (no self-inflicted disconnect); batched throughput >> 170 msg/s; no processed-but-unpersisted message (idempotent ON CONFLICT, timescale_store.py:140); suite + mypy --strict green.
Consumer: production ingest; proven by the drill framework (task G) + GREEN capstone (task H).
Modules touched: src/solar_challenge_platform/ingestion/subscriber.py, src/solar_challenge_platform/ingestion/buffer.py, tests/ingestion/test_ingest_reconnect.py
Prereqs: none (hermetic). NOTE: edits shared ingestion/* — sequence BEFORE F2 (both touch subscriber.py); single-writer within this PRD.

Discovery (review 2026-09-28, demonstrated with TestClient): the consent purpose→data-category pairs are restated in four places and disagree. ingestion/service.py gates every row on platform_operation × {realtime_telemetry, soc_state}, which NO UI can grant (only runtime/seed.py writes it); the portal's ConsentScreen grants cbs_optimisation with scope ['settlement_hh'] while the optimiser checks {soc_state, realtime_telemetry}, so every portal-consented member is SCOPE_INSUFFICIENT and skipped while the portal shows 'Active'. A member onboarded the real way therefore has all telemetry dropped and is never optimised. Hidden because the fast lane disables ingest consent enforcement and every fixture seeds platform_operation directly. Task 582 builds the single server-side catalogue.

Review 20261007T025143 pattern: the no-data-loss convention is applied unevenly across write paths. Ingestion buffers and replays a DB outage idempotently. The dispatch loop's audit trail (control/audit_writer.py, task 528: control_command_log rows and dispatch ticks) is write-behind but runs each write once, so a fast-failing outage such as a DB restart (connection refused) discards every row for its duration, and only a stalled socket actually buffers. A second instance: the wire boundary (ingestion/wire.py decode_batch) catches only json.JSONDecodeError, so a non-UTF-8 payload's UnicodeDecodeError escapes and crashes scp-ingest. When hunting fail-safe defects here, check each boundary's except clause for the full set of exception types its input can raise, and check whether a write-behind queue retries transient errors.

Coordination for task 617 (PLATFORM_OPERATION becomes contract-basis). Task 583's plan (2026-10-09) changes how ingest handles a failed consent check: a CHECK_FAILED row is deferred in StoreForwardBuffer's deferred lane and re-judged on a later flush, instead of being dropped. Its keystone, tests/integration/test_s1_fleet_to_store.py::test_keystone_consent_outage_defers_telemetry_and_rejudges_it_on_recovery, models the 'withdrawn' household as a PLATFORM_OPERATION WITHDRAW recorded during the outage. Once 617 lands, that withdrawal no longer refuses ingest. Observation (checked against the tree at commit 56f042b): the last bullet of "## Delivery guarantee" in docs/examples/README.md says an OOM kill, SIGKILL or interpreter abort "loses what was delivered but not yet written" and bounds the loss: "The loss is up to one batch (`INGESTION_BATCH_MAX_ROWS` rows or `INGESTION_BATCH_MAX_SECONDS`) plus the client's queue, and during a backlog resume that queue can hold much of the backlog." Those rows were acknowledged to the broker on receipt, so an OOM kill, SIGKILL or interpreter abort while the store is down, or while the backlog is still draining (about 2 minutes for a full buffer, per D11), loses up to that whole backlog, not "one batch plus the client's queue".

Completed: Consent check failure denies without caching the denial for the 300 s standing TTL (DecisionReason.CHECK_FAILED)
Description: DEFECT (verified on main 2085985 by the /prd lead session of 2026-09-28, while adversarially reviewing docs/prds/push-alerting-deep-health.md). consent/enforcement.py::GateConsentChecker.check_device catches every exception (e.g. a transient DB failure) and RETURNS an ordinary DeviceStanding whose decision is NO_CONSENT (property_id None). Because it returns normally, consent/enforcement.py::ConsentGuard._get_standing caches that standing like any other for consent_recheck_ttl_seconds (Settings, default 300 s). The guard's own branch 'exception-derived decisions are NOT cached' is unreachable for GateConsentChecker, since the checker already swallowed the exception. Consequence: one DB blip makes scp-ingest drop a CONSENTED home's telemetry for up to 5 minutes. This violates the review/briefing.yaml fail-safe convention: 'a transient DB failure in the consent path must deny (fail-closed) but NOT cache the denial, so the next tick retries'.

WORK
- models/consent_enums.py::DecisionReason gains CHECK_FAILED (a denial reason distinct from NO_CONSENT).
- consent/enforcement.py::GateConsentChecker.check_device returns CHECK_FAILED (not NO_CONSENT) when it catches an exception. The guard's own exception backstop in ConsentGuard._get_standing also yields CHECK_FAILED.
- ConsentGuard._get_standing caches a CHECK_FAILED standing only for a new Settings.consent_check_failure_ttl_seconds (default 15.0; validated 0 < value < consent_recheck_ttl_seconds). It is a SHORT negative cache: never-cached would put a synchronous DB checker call (up to the connect timeout) on every MQTT message on ingest's event loop during a DB fault; 15 s bounds that while recovery is seen within 15 s. Genuine NO_CONSENT / WITHDRAWN / EXPIRED standings keep the full TTL.
- The guard's dropped-row counters distinguish check_failed from no_consent, so the cause is visible.
- Every consumer of DecisionReason treats CHECK_FAILED as denied (fail-closed): grep DecisionReason usages in src (NO_CONSENT is used in ~6 places) and keep behaviour identical for them except the cache lifetime.
- Wire the new Setting through ingestion/service.py::IngestionService.from_settings (where ConsentGuard gets ttl_seconds).

CONSUMERS: scp-ingest (ConsentGuard via IngestionService.from_settings); P-Alert·η2 of docs/prds/push-alerting-deep-health.md, whose three-valued consent standing reads CHECK_FAILED as UNKNOWN.

USER-OBSERVABLE SIGNAL: with a GateConsentChecker whose session factory raises once and then recovers, a consented device's rows are dropped (counted as check_failed) for at most consent_check_failure_ttl_seconds and are accepted again after it, not after 300 s; a genuinely withdrawn consent still caches for the full TTL; tests/integration/test_consent_cross_consumer.py (the cross-consumer keystone) stays green; pytest -m 'not slow' and mypy src/solar_challenge_platform are green.

MODULES: src/solar_challenge_platform/models/consent_enums.py, src/solar_challenge_platform/consent/enforcement.py, src/solar_challenge_platform/settings.py, src/solar_challenge_platform/ingestion/service.py, tests/ingestion/test_consent_enforcement.py, tests/integration/test_consent_cross_consumer.py.

OPERATING PATTERN that made a 26-hour interactive L2 watch survivable, 2026-09-14/16 — worth reusing verbatim. (2) Keep the tick OFF the compact MCP drain — a read-only python scan over `data/escalations/esc-*.json` filtering level==2/status=='pending', diffed against a known-holds set, is what keeps a multi-day session's context alive; the MCP drain is the dominant context sink. (4) Give each spawned session a written brief at `~/.claude/spawn-briefs/<date>-<task>-<slug>.md` containing the already-verified facts, the exact remedy, the declined options with reasons, and the known traps — the fresh session then spends its context on the work rather than re-deriving the diagnosis. candidates.content: Reify's solver and its constraint CHECKER disagree about equality by construction. The DimensionalSolver treats `==` as satisfied within a bare `1e-15` slop, inlined (no shared constant) at four sites in crates/reify-constraints/src/solver.rs: `comparison_residual` Eq/Ne (:511, :514) and `comparison_violation` Eq/Ne (:575, :577). The checker path is EXACT: `eval_eq` in crates/reify-expr/src/lib.rs:5359-5380 bit-compares `Value::Scalar` after a dimension check, and that is what SimpleConstraintChecker (crates/reify-constraints/src/lib.rs:169-183) folds into Satisfied/Violated. So a solve that lands within 1e-15 is "feasible" to the solver and "violated" to the checker — the false-VIOLATED class task #6653 was filed to fix. Separately, the four inequality nudges at solver.rs:545/553/561/569 are a DIFFERENT `1e-12` constant with a different job; do not fold them together.

`reify check` evaluates a `==` constraint with EXACT f64 equality; there is no tolerance on the check path (SimpleConstraintChecker → reify_expr::eval_eq compares si_value with `a == b` after a dimension check). Measured 2026-10-07 on main: with a = 0.1m and b = 0.2m, `constraint a + b == 0.3m` is VIOLATED, exit 1. A probe like 6mm + 8mm + 6.5mm + 4.5mm == 25mm passes only because that sum rounds to the same double as the literal; a single passing sum proves nothing. The only tolerances are private to the solver: solver.rs comparison_residual uses |l-r| < 1e-15 absolute, FEASIBILITY_THRESHOLD is 1e-12, and within_uniqueness_tol is relative 1e-6 / absolute 1e-10. Task #6653, ruled 2026-08-26, will introduce one single-sourced toleranced policy for all Scalar equality verdicts.

When reproducing reify-constraints' real solver path in a scratch unit test in `crates/reify-constraints/src/solver.rs`, always pass `NM_SD_TOLERANCE` to `solve_core_with_sd_tolerance` — never an ad-hoc value like 3.0. `DimensionalSolver::solve` reaches `solve_core` which hardcodes `NM_SD_TOLERANCE`, so a looser tolerance makes the same sub-solve return `Infeasible` where the production path returns `Solved`, which reads as a contradiction between the emitted diagnostic and your probe and sends you hunting a nonexistent bug. Measured on task #5714: probing `original_constraints_witness` at sd_tolerance=3.0 declined on two brackets (`2*x > 60mm AND 2*x < 62.5mm`, `< 65mm`) that the real path witnesses fine.

Reify solver tolerance inventory, measured 2026-08-26 at main 2ea72cc5e8 — useful for anyone touching #6653 (toleranced Scalar verdicts) or solver conditioning.

The dimensional path's constants are DIMENSION-BLIND ABSOLUTES applied to raw SI magnitudes: FEASIBILITY_THRESHOLD = 1e-12 (the acceptance gate, L-infinity, so 1 picometre on a metre-scale length), NM_SD_TOLERANCE = 1e-30 (argmin simplex termination on the squared-residual cost SD; deliberately <= FEASIBILITY_THRESHOLD^2 per task #4700), PENALTY_WEIGHT = 1e6, UNDEF_OBJECTIVE_PENALTY = f64::MAX/2, MAX_ITERS = 5000, FEASIBLE_OPT_ITERS_PER_DIM = 500. Inline deadbands: 1e-15 for Eq/Ne, a +1e-12 offset in comparison_violation. So a Money objective (~1e2) and a Length constraint (~1e-2) sit in the same unnormalised sum with a fixed 1e6 objective/penalty ratio regardless of physical scale.

The ONLY relative-plus-floor tolerance in the solver today is the uniqueness check's UNIQUENESS_REL_TOL = 1e-6 / UNIQUENESS_ABS_TOL = 1e-10 pair in solutions_agree. The ONLY normalisation anywhere is cost_robustness_tradeoff's normalised_blend_term. The robustness floor uses REL_MARGIN = 0.02 with ABS_FLOOR_SI = 1e-9.

The ONLY coherent tolerance HIERARCHY in the codebase is RelateTolerance::kernel_default() in crates/reify-constraints/src/relate_solve.rs — kernel_local 1e-7 m <= solver_convergence 1e-6 m <= assertion 1e-5 m, all metres, seeded from one base length. It has PRIVATE fields, exactly one constructor, no setters and no DSL knob. That ladder is the shape #6653 should generalise, and note solver_convergence (1e-6) happens to EQUAL FD_STEP, i.e. the differencing step is the same size as the convergence target.

The engine verdict fold meanwhile uses EXACT f64 equality (reify-expr eval_eq), which is why correctly-solved models report false VIOLATED at ~1e-15 residuals (probe-measured on multi_auto2/multi_auto6/auto_probe). crates/reify-core/src/scalar_tolerance.rs does not exist yet — #6653 creates it.

Reify gotcha: when tightening a stdlib trait param from Real to a dimensioned scalar alias, any pre-existing trait-level comparison constraint with a bare numeric RHS (e.g. `constraint stiffness > 0`) compiles fine (compile-time dim-check at expr.rs:738 is gated to Add/Sub only) but evaluates to Value::Undef at runtime in reify-expr's `eval_cmp` (crates/reify-expr/src/lib.rs:2477) because Scalar-vs-non-Scalar with non-dimensionless LHS is mapped to Undef. Constraint evaluator then yields Satisfaction::Indeterminate (crates/reify-constraints/src/lib.rs:70). Fix: rewrite the trait constraint to use a dimensioned RHS literal, e.g. `constraint stiffness > 0 * 1N / 1m`. Discovered while implementing task #3115 step-15; the drivebelt_trait_bounds eval test caught it.

MEASURED 2026-08-26 (main 2128c3692c, reproduced independently twice): mixing an EQUALITY and an INEQUALITY on the same reify `auto` param is UNCONDITIONALLY reported infeasible, even when trivially satisfiable. `constraint L >= 8mm` + `constraint L == 10mm` (10mm satisfies both) yields "constraints could not be satisfied (max absolute residual: 5.00e-7)" and leaves L undef. The equality ALONE resolves to exactly 0.01 m.

The residual is ALWAYS exactly 5.00e-7 — verified scale-invariant, direction-invariant, order-invariant and strictness-invariant across six controls (including a x10-scaled twin). MECHANISM: the synthetic max-min-slack objective is added ALONGSIDE the equality's penalty, and minimising PENALTY_WEIGHT*d^2 - x with PENALTY_WEIGHT = 1e6 is stationary at 2*1e6*d = 1, i.e. d = 5.0e-7 exactly. That is five orders above FEASIBILITY_THRESHOLD = 1e-12.

DISPOSITION (important — do not re-file this as a new defect): the VERDICT half is ALREADY OWNED by task #6653, whose evidence names this exact probe (expr_ineq_eq.ri) and this exact residual, and whose acceptance criterion requires all four of its evidence probes to flip. Its work item (2) — replacing the flat dimension-blind FEASIBILITY_THRESHOLD with a relative + dimension-aware-absolute-floor policy — is the mechanism (0.5 um on a metre-scale length falls below any sensible engineering floor). A P1 authoring session was about to file a duplicate and caught it only by reading #6653's full description.

What #6653 does NOT fix, filed separately as #6688: the underlying BIAS. #6653 makes the verdict correct by TOLERATING the residual, leaving the solver returning 9.9995mm where the design says 10mm. The offset is ABSOLUTE and scale-invariant, so the relative error grows without bound as designs shrink — 5e-5 at 10mm, but 25% on a 2 micron feature.

Gotcha for DimensionalSolver (crates/reify-constraints/src/solver.rs) seam tests that must red under a mutation of ONE row's acceptance (e.g. RowResidual::any): if every row depends on the same auto, the penalty minimiser lands at a compromise point. For example, `w == 10mm; w == 10.1mm or w == 9.9mm` lands at about 10.05mm, where the OTHER rows also fail acceptance. The result is Infeasible whatever the mutated row decides, so the test is vacuous against that mutation. Isolate the row under test by putting it on a fixed non-auto cell seeded in current_values (e.g. p = 10mm with `p == 10.1mm or p == 9.9mm`), so that every other row is satisfiable. Measured in task 6653, commit 28d5bd7207.

In reify-constraints `solve_core_with_sd_tolerance`, the value returned by `DimensionalSolver::solve` is `best_param` after a `val.clamp(lo, hi)` into the effective box (`build_solved_values(&problem.auto_params, &clamped)`), so a test pinning an answer to a `default_bounds_for` corner (Length = 1e-6..10.0 m) is bit-exact because of that clamp, NOT because Nelder-Mead converged there. Pin such corner expectations with a RELATIVE tolerance (`tol * max(|expected|, 1.0)`); an absolute 1e-9 against the 10 m corner is a 1e-10 relative tolerance and goes RED on any future NM change that terminates marginally inside the bound, even though the characterised behaviour is unchanged.

Measured 2026-10-14 (main 5b8a33011d): the DimensionalSolver's Nelder-Mead stops on cost-SD NM_SD_TOLERANCE=1e-30 over SQUARED residuals, so equality residuals land around 1e-15 in raw SI units regardless of dimension — e.g. `param v : Volume = auto; constraint v == 1000mm^3` solves to 1.0000000011823468e-6 m^3 (residual 1.18e-15, RELATIVE 1.2e-9). Consequence for any acceptance/verdict tolerance (task #6653): an absolute floor below ~1e-12 SI (e.g. (1um)^3 = 1e-18 m^3 for Volume) or a pure-relative 1e-9 policy turns ordinary mm^3-scale volume equalities into false Infeasible/Violated. Keep every per-dimension floor >= 1e-12 (today's FEASIBILITY_THRESHOLD), so a toleranced acceptance is never stricter than the old flat gate.

When writing a reify-constraints test fixture whose optimum sits ON an active constraint, put that active bound on the auto's BOX (`AutoParam.bounds`), not on an inequality against a non-constant operand. Measured on task 5954: minimising `a` against a floor visible only as a penalty term (`a >= side`, `side` a derived cell) parks `a` ~5e-7 BELOW the floor — the `PENALTY_WEIGHT = 1e6` trade-off at `derive_param_intervals` in crates/reify-constraints/src/solver.rs — which is six orders above `FEASIBILITY_THRESHOLD = 1e-12`, so the whole solve returns `Infeasible (max absolute residual: 5.00e-7)`. A penalty method converges onto an active constraint FROM THE OUTSIDE; only `derive_param_intervals`' clamp snaps the undershoot back, and it mines CONSTANT operands only, so a derived-cell or param operand yields no clamp. Corollary for test design: assert the bare `DimensionalSolver` on the undecomposed problem FIRST as a measured precondition, so an unattainable fixture fails as a precondition rather than being misread as a registry/decomposition defect.

Reify eval-test gotcha: mm-lowered decimal lengths are NOT exactly representable in f64. mm→SI factor is 1000 (reify-core/src/dimension.rs), so 2mm → 0.002_f64, and 0.002 = 1/(2^2·5^3) is not a dyadic rational. Consequently 2mm*4.5 evaluates to 0.009000000000000001, which is 1 ULP (~1.7e-18) off the f64 literal 0.009 — so a bit-exact assert_eq!(si_value, 0.009) is doomed. Eval tests over pure DSL arithmetic on decimal-mm quantities must assert with a tolerance (sibling convention dimensionless_real_arithmetic_e2e.rs uses EPSILON=1e-9; 1e-12 is safe), never bit-exact ==.

DimensionalSolver (crates/reify-constraints/src/solver.rs) has a convergence-floor gotcha: solve_core's Nelder-Mead minimizes the SQUARED constraint violation (comparison_violation uses d.powi(2)) and terminates at sd_tolerance(1e-15), so its achievable L1 residual floor is ≈sqrt(1e-15)≈3e-8 — but the feasibility gate (final_max_residual > FEASIBILITY_THRESHOLD=1e-12) checks the LINEAR residual (comparison_residual). Any auto that must MOVE from its seed to satisfy an equality constraint stalls ~2.6e-8 >> 1e-12 → Infeasible. Cold solves of `param x:Length=auto` only pass when the target happens to equal extract_initial_point's 0.01 default seed (no bounds → 0.01), triggering the initially_feasible early-exit (no NM run). Task 4700 fixes this with a near-feasible polish/restart at tighter sd_tolerance.

DimensionalSolver feasibility-fallback gotcha: when a minimize objective pushes an auto param toward a strict lower-bound constraint (e.g. `constraint thickness > 1mm`), Nelder-Mead may converge just below the boundary (floating-point), triggering the `final_max_residual > FEASIBILITY_THRESHOLD` check in solver.rs and falling back to the 10mm initial feasible point. Solution: use only an upper-bound constraint for minimize fixtures (single upper bound avoids this), matching the design of `e2e_minimize_through_real_solver` in crates/reify-eval/tests/resolution.rs:889 which explicitly notes "Single upper-bound constraint avoids floating-point boundary issues at the lower bound."

Reify: interval/bound work on the DimensionalSolver must not change RankedSolveResult — reify-ir already defines `Completeness::Refuted { narrowing: ConstraintNodeId }` with a `describe()` rendering, but ranked.rs documents an OPEN SEAM: no RankedSolveResult arm can carry Refuted yet (Ranked requires non-empty candidates, I2), and the choice of how is reserved for solution-set-completeness ε #6710→#6900. A pre-solve refutation therefore flows through `SolveResult::Infeasible { diagnostics }` with a typed DiagnosticCode, reusing `Completeness::Refuted{..}.describe()` as the message. Also: ~4 existing tests (robustness_floor.rs non_money_infeasible..., solver_integration.rs infeasible_residual..., reify-eval objective_consumption_e2e.rs `w >= 50mm ∧ w <= 10mm` fixtures) use interval-provable contradictions to exercise the residual 'could not be satisfied' path, so any pre-solve infeasibility proof flips them.

When asserting reify-eval solver-resolved auto-param values, the tolerance depends on which DimensionalSolver path the fixture drives, and copying the wrong one gives a guessed threshold with no achievability basis. Seeding the edit AT the constraint's solution takes the initially-feasible early-exit (no Nelder-Mead search) and supports 1e-9, as `edit_param_back_props_solved_auto` does. Seeding OFF-target forces a real Nelder-Mead search and needs 1e-6 — its sibling `edit_param_back_props_moved_auto` declares `const MOVED_AUTO_TOL: f64 = 1e-6` (crates/reify-eval/src/engine_edit.rs:6202) and applies it to all four of its assertions. `crates/reify-eval/tests/common/differential.rs:1793` gives the underlying reason: warm-started and cold-seeded Nelder-Mead runs are not bit-identical, so solver-resolved cells must be compared to tolerance, never by content_hash.

2026-06-10 DISCOVERY (general Reify language gap, currently UNOWNED — flagged in gdt-geometric-zones-and-containment.md §11 Q5 for separate triage): template-declared .ri constraints are NOT enforced per ctor instance. Empirically verified: `DimensionalTolerance(nominal: 10mm, upper_deviation: -1mm, lower_deviation: 1mm)` flagrantly violates the template's own `constraint upper_deviation >= lower_deviation` guard yet `reify check` reports "All constraints satisfied" — template constraints evaluate ONCE at template scope with default param values (a template whose DEFAULTS violate its constraint does flag VIOLATED), never against ctor-let or sub instances with overridden values. Consequence 1: every guard constraint inside shipped stdlib templates (DimensionalTolerance's band guard, etc.) is toothless for real instances. Consequence 2: .ri constraint guards CANNOT implement per-instance legality rules — the GD&T legality lint (task 4475 β) had to be Rust-side check-time diagnostics over enumerated callout instances instead. Also verified in the same probes: enum equality (e.g. `material_condition == MC.RFS`) DOES work in constraint bodies; sub bodies require newline-separated members (comma-separated `sub x : T { a = 1, b = 2 }` is a parse error).

Reify testing norm: a new regression fixture MUST be measured RED against the pre-fix tree before it is accepted as coverage — never infer discrimination from an architect's/plan's prose prediction that "this fails today". A fixture specified in good faith can be VACUOUS: it passes both before and after the fix and proves nothing, while looking like real coverage forever.

Measured instance (task #7186 defect B, esc-7186-1): the plan specified a rigid-platform loop-closure fixture (two +Z prismatic posts 200mm apart, closing pose = translate(200mm,0,0), bind j2=300mm) and predicted it would fail pre-fix because "the closure reduces to d2 == d1 with a 200mm x-offset that nothing can absorb". Implemented verbatim it PASSED on the pre-fix tree. Root cause: the sole free variable d1 translates only along +Z, so the unabsorbable 200mm x-residual was ORTHOGONAL to the free direction; Gauss-Newton's least-squares point was still d1 = 0.300, numerically identical to the correct post-fix answer. The defect was real but invisible in the converged value — it showed up only in the residual NORM, which snapshot() does not surface in the Snapshot Map (only is_singular is).

Generalizable rule for least-squares / Gauss-Newton solver fixtures: an error component orthogonal to the free-variable subspace is INVISIBLE in the converged value. To make a solver defect observable through the converged value, give the injected offset a component ALONG a free direction. Fix applied here: pose translate(200mm,0,0) -> translate(200mm,0,50mm), making the exact solution d1 = d2 - 0.050 = 0.250m post-fix versus the 0.300m least-squares point pre-fix — genuinely RED before, GREEN after, with an exact algebraic solution so the 1e-6 tolerance stays the solver's own NewtonConfig::default() tol_pos_m rather than a fitted threshold.

Corollary: when a fixture's discriminating power depends on a specific constant, say so IN the test's doc comment ("the 50mm z-component is load-bearing"), or a later reader will "simplify" it back to the vacuous form.

Reify's DimensionalSolver keeps TWO parallel per-comparison functions in crates/reify-constraints/src/solver.rs that are easy to conflate: comparison_violation (:521-584) returns SQUARED magnitudes and is the Nelder-Mead COST that drives convergence, while comparison_residual (:464-519) returns ABSOLUTE distances and is the accept/reject VERDICT checked against FEASIBILITY_THRESHOLD (:20). Only comparison_residual is a verdict. Widening the cost function's deadband flattens the objective inside the band and degrades solutions from ~1e-16 to ~deadband, and also invalidates the NM_SD_TOLERANCE <= FEASIBILITY_THRESHOLD^2 derivation documented at solver.rs:38-82. Both functions drop dimension via Value::as_f64() (reify-ir/src/value.rs:1635-1642) at :477-478 / :535-536, so FEASIBILITY_THRESHOLD is a dimension-blind, scale-blind absolute gate; Value::dimension() (value.rs:1655) recovers it without any signature change to max_constraint_residual/constraint_residual.

Reify gotcha: a deliberately COMPARATIVE integration assertion (strict inequality against a baseline derived in-test) cannot catch drift between two values that both sit on the same side of that baseline, so published example-header figures can rot silently for months while the suite stays green. Seen in `crates/reify-eval/tests/joint_drive_expansion_boundary.rs` BT-5, where the merged auto drifted 0.01 -> 1e-9 with the frozen-cascade baseline at 50.0 and nothing failed (task #5939). The fix pattern is to add a sibling anti-rot pin that asserts the RULE across two configurations rather than tightening the comparative test (which would trade away the property that makes it robust): BT-5b pins an order-of-magnitude band in one regime, the closed-form value in a second, and the monotone tie between them. Such a pin is GREEN on arrival by design — its value is prospective, so say so in its docstring or a reader will mistake it for vacuous.

reify DimensionalSolver budget gotcha (verified 2026-08-26, task #6654 planning): the iteration budget in crates/reify-constraints/src/solver.rs has TWO paths, and the repo's only end-to-end W_SOLVER_OPTIMALITY_UNPROVEN fixture rides the one people don't expect. `examples/solver_optimality_unproven.ri` and crates/reify-eval/tests/solver_optimality_unproven.rs seed 12 Length params at 10mm INSIDE their (9mm, 11mm) windows — the seed is FEASIBLE, so the solve takes the WARM branch `min(FEASIBLE_OPT_ITERS_PER_DIM * (n+1), MAX_ITERS) = min(500*13, 5000) = 5000` (solver.rs:1881-1890), NOT the cold `MAX_ITERS` branch. Anyone raising the warm cap silently dissolves that fixture's exhaustion premise and the warning stops firing while the test still "passes" its feasibility assertion. Second gotcha in the same file: `iter_limited` (solver.rs:1931-1932) is gated on the EFFECTIVE objective, which includes the SYNTHESISED centrality (Chebyshev-centre) objective built at solver.rs:1861-1866 for any scope with inequality constraints and no explicit objective. That leaks nowhere today only because the engine reaches the optimality channel via `solve_ranked`, which engine_eval.rs:5874 calls solely when `problem.objective.is_some()`. Any new narration on the plain `solve()` path must gate on the USER objective or it fires on essentially every inequality-bearing scope.

content: Gotcha when testing toleranced equality in the reify DimensionalSolver (task #6653): `==` is toleranced through reify_core::scalar_tolerance (Length floor 1e-6 m) and is NOT transitive. So a fixture like `w == 10mm; w != 10.0000005mm` is still satisfiable, in a thin sliver about 1 µm below 10mm, and asserting "not Solved" on it only pins which side Nelder-Mead happens to land on. To build a truly unsatisfiable `!=` fixture, pin the auto with exact inequalities instead (`w >= 10mm; w <= 10mm; w != 10.0000005mm`), because inequalities are never toleranced.

candidates.content: solar_challenge full-verify wait recipe that works in a headless implementer session (task 391, measured 2026-10-10 on task/391 over main aca7236). Launch the verify with Bash run_in_background, under a lock held for exactly its lifetime: `flock -o /tmp/<task>-verify.lock bash -c "uv run --locked --extra dev --extra web pytest -m 'not slow and not e2e' --ignore=tests/e2e -p no:cacheprovider -q > /tmp/<task>-verify.log 2>&1; echo rc=\$? >> /tmp/<task>-verify.log"`. The -o flag closes the lock fd in the child, so no leaked grandchild keeps the lock. Check the lock is taken with `flock -n /tmp/<task>-verify.lock true` (exit 1 means held). Then wait in bounded foreground blocks with `timeout 1380 flock /tmp/<task>-verify.lock true` and a Bash timeout of 1440000 ms: exit 0 means the run ended, 124 means wait again. It needs no sleep, so the anti-polling guard does not block it. This run took 1028 s (17m08s) for 4624 passed, 107 deselected.

New verify measurement, 2026-10-02 (task 220 implementer; task/220 at e9d3823 on base c83b5a3, CPython 3.12.3): `uv run --extra dev --extra web pytest -m 'not slow and not e2e' --ignore=tests/e2e` ran 2789 passed / 105 deselected in 790 s (13m10s) with host load average ~107 on 32 cores (sampled once at launch), so it fit inside a 20-minute window under heavy load; compare memory e8c80404's 13% in ~10 min at load ~130. `mypy src/solar_challenge` now checks 47 source files. A way to wait for it without sleep-polling or guessing a pid: launch via Bash run_in_background as `flock /tmp/<task>-verify.lock bash -c '<verify> > <log> 2>&1; echo rc=$?'`, confirm the job holds the lock (`flock -n <lock> true` returns 1), then block in the foreground on `flock -w 1200 <lock> true` with a ~1320000 ms Bash timeout: rc 0 means the run finished, rc 1 means the 20-minute window elapsed, so repeat. No turn gap exceeds ~20 min.

content: Capability-manifest sidecar authoring tip: validate the YAML before handing back by running `cd /home/leo/src/dark-factory/shared && uv run python -c "from shared.capability_manifest import load_capability_manifest; load_capability_manifest('<abs path>')"`. Unquoted YAML plain scalars containing ': ' (e.g. 'graph: ApiGraph') or ' #' (e.g. '"Any"  # type') break parsing ('mapping values are not allowed here' or silent truncation as a comment). Single-quote every binding/reason value, double any inner single quotes, and remember that backslashes are literal inside YAML single quotes, which suits ERE patterns like 'plan\.json'. The sidecar schema forbids extra keys; task fields are label, task_id, external_task_id, title, note, capabilities.
