GOTCHA (measured 2026-09-02, task 4319): BOTH of dark-factory's non-memory shared stores SILENTLY MANUFACTURE THEMSELVES when a script is pointed at the wrong path, turning a mis-targeted run into a clean-looking zero-work success. Verified first-hand by running each:

(1) `EscalationQueue(Path(dir))` calls `self.queue_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)` in `__init__` (escalation/src/escalation/queue.py:390). Point it at a missing path and it CREATES the tree; `get_pending()` then returns `[]`.
(2) `SqliteTaskBackend.get_tasks(project_root)` auto-creates `<project_root>/.taskmaster/tasks/tasks.db` and returns `{"tasks": []}` for ANY path, never raising.

WHY THIS BITES AGENTS SPECIFICALLY. `fused-memory/scripts/backfill_recon_escalations.py` and `dismiss_recon_integrity_noise.py` both default `--queue-dir` to the RELATIVE `./data/reconciliation/escalations`, resolved against CWD, passed through with no `.resolve()` and no existence check. A task worktree has no `data/reconciliation/` and no `.taskmaster/` (neither is tracked in git), so running either script — or any of the three tasks.db scripts with `--project-root <worktree>` — from a worktree yields `"pending_before": 0, "to_dismiss": 0` / an empty task plan. Both escalation `main()`s then `return 0` UNCONDITIONALLY (backfill:355, dismiss:141). The harness, unlike the scripts, DOES absolutize the same config default (orchestrator harness.py:11658-11660) — so the scripts are the odd ones out, not the config.

CONSEQUENCE FOR YOU: a zero-count report from any of these five scripts is NOT evidence the queue or task tree is clean. Check the target exists BEFORE believing the number: `ls data/reconciliation/escalations` / `ls .taskmaster/tasks/tasks.db`, and run from the project root or pass an absolute path. Completed: Unblock whole-blob metadata repair on done tasks: update_task's done_provenance floor makes metadata_mode='replace' structurally unusable
Description: Split out of task 3697 (esc-3697-4) by the steward on 2026-08-06. 3697 is rescoped to ship its documentation + tested migration script; THIS task provides the write path 3697 needs, then executes the live migration 3697 could not.

OBSERVED, first-hand code reads (not inferred):

1. sqlite_task_backend.py:2575-2591 — update_task raises DoneProvenanceWriteAuthorityError
   for ANY metadata payload that parses to a dict containing 'done_provenance'. The check
   is PRESENCE-ONLY: no value-unchanged carve-out, no metadata_mode carve-out. It fires
   before _resolve_metadata_mode, before ensure_connected(), before the row SELECT.

2. _merge_metadata has no deletion sentinel (merge is shallow {**old, **new}), and there is
   no task-level metadata_delete_keys — that API exists only for MEMORIES
   (memory_service.py / update_memory). backend.set_task_status
   (sqlite_task_backend.py:1938-1947) accepts no metadata argument.

3. The privileged non-protocol seam stamp_audit_metadata (sqlite_task_backend.py:2835,
   added by task 2201) also hardcodes _merge_metadata(mode='merge'), so it cannot retire a
   key either, and it is not reachable over MCP.

4. Single enforcement point: the interceptor does NOT pre-check independently — it catches
   the backend exception at task_interceptor.py:4366 and converts via .to_error_dict().
   Task 2203 deliberately deleted the duplicate guard copies. So a fix has ONE code site,
   not several.

CONSEQUENCE (the generalization worth fixing): every done/merged task carries
done_provenance, so metadata_mode='replace' is structurally unusable on ALL of them — while
task_backend_protocol.py:209 and server/tools.py:5956 both document replace mode as
"the sanctioned repair path". That doc claim and this floor are in direct tension. Any
task needing a key RETIRED (not just added) from a done task's metadata is currently
unfixable through public API.

CANDIDATE DESIGNS (architect decides; do not assume):
  (A) Identical-passthrough carve-out — permit a payload whose done_provenance is
      byte-identical to the stored value, on the reasoning that an unchanged passthrough is
      not a write of that key. Smallest change, preserves the floor's actual intent
      (set_task_status remains the only thing that can CHANGE done_provenance), and unblocks
      whole-blob repair on every done task. Must compare against the STORED value read under
      the same txn, not trust the caller.
  (B) Task-level metadata_delete_keys on update_task, mirroring the memories API. Most
      general, largest blast radius, and needs its own write-authority thinking (deleting
      done_provenance must stay forbidden).
  (C) Widen the privileged stamp_audit_metadata seam to accept a mode/deletion argument and
      expose a narrow operator-only path. Follows the existing 2201 precedent.

WHATEVER IS CHOSEN, also reconcile the docstrings at task_backend_protocol.py:209 and
server/tools.py:5956 so "the sanctioned repair path" is either true or qualified.

Gotcha for any reify tests/infra gate that greps the tree for a string pattern the gate itself must quote: exclude the gate's OWN artifacts via git pathspec magic (`git grep ... -- . ':(exclude)<own path>'`). This bites hardest when the gate ships a baseline manifest whose every row ENDS in an instance of the scanned pattern — an unexcluded scan harvests its own baseline as fresh findings and regeneration folds the baseline into itself. Canonical in-repo instance of the idiom: `tests/infra/test_orchestrator_config_canonical_path.sh` (`assert_no_legacy_config_refs`).

CORRECTED 2026-09-22 (task 7788, see peer memory 29ba91db-b6c8-48a9-84bc-66bfb85d9a1d): do NOT append `|| true` to the scan. A no-match `git grep` exits 1 (which is meant to abort under `set -euo pipefail`), but git grep ALSO exits 128 on a bad pathspec magic, an unenterable root, or a `-P` search on a git built without PCRE — and `|| true` launders all of those into a vacuous "no matches" PASS. Measured in task 7788 (git 2.43.0): with `|| true`, the canonical-path absence check passed on a root git could not even enter. Instead capture the status (`... || rc=$?`), accept only 0/1 as a real result, and let any other status fail the assert loudly.

Committing a change to reify's dark-factory-orchestrator.yaml alone is CHEAP, not a full-suite gate — useful to know before hesitating over an operator config commit on main. The pre-commit hook delegates to `scripts/verify.sh all --profile debug --scope staged --include-infra` (hooks/project-checks), and verify.sh's decide_scope classifier has an explicit `docs/*|*.md|*.yaml|*.yml)` no-heavy arm, so a stage containing only that yaml yields RUN_RUST=0 RUN_GUI=0 RUN_OCCT_GATE=0 and a plan of exactly ONE command: `tests/infra/test_verify_admission_knob_parity.sh`. Measured 2026-08-21: that test runs in seconds, 17 passed / 0 failed, and the real commit's hook run agreed ("verify.sh: all checks passed (action=all profile=debug scope=staged)"). Two related facts. (1) verify.sh has `--print-plan`, a dry run that prints the exact ordered command list — the right way to price any commit before making it. (2) The classifier's catch-all arm is conservative (`*)` -> rust=1 gui=1 gate=1), and there is a contract-C5 "fail WIDE" path that escalates to the full workspace when its rename-source diff errors, printing a WARNING to stderr first — so an unexpectedly heavy plan should be re-run and its leading stderr read before being believed. Also note reify's main-branch commits are gated only for main (worktree branches used by orchestrator agents are not gated) and a reference-transaction hook logs "main-gate <ts>: sanctioned main move <old> -> <new>" on success.

Two — and only two — mechanisms make a `docs/` file gate-relevant on the DOCS-ONLY DIRECT-COMMIT-ON-MAIN path (hooks/pre-commit -> hooks/project-checks -> `verify.sh all --profile debug --scope staged --include-infra`). Choosing the wrong one produces a manifest row that reads as "hole closed" while gating nothing.

(1) NOT scripts/verify-pipeline-paths.txt / verify-pipeline-guard.sh. verify.sh has ZERO references to either. The guard's only live consumer is dark-factory's orchestrator/verify.py:6584 and :6760, both reached only when role=='merge' AND the diff has no source files (merge-worker trivial-pass); merge_skew_tripwire.py's load_bearing_oracle_cmd is the second consumer and defaults to None, unconfigured in both repos. Its manifest also matches by `grep -xF` — exact whole-line fixed strings, so prefixes/globs are NOT expressible in it (the only glob, `^tests/infra/[^/]*\.sh$`, is hardcoded in the guard).

(2) scripts/verify-pipeline-infra-tests.txt DOES reach it. verify.sh's select_infra_tests() (:1199-1226) builds SELECTED_INFRA_GLOBS, and the plan-emission block at verify.sh:2727 is gated on DO_TEST, **NOT** on RUN_RUST. Measured with a hermetic fixture built from tests/infra/test_verify_scope.sh's own make_fixture: staging only `docs/prds/v0_6/fixtures/discrete_let_cont.ri` gives RUN_RUST=0 and 0 plan commands; adding ONE row gives RUN_RUST=0 and 1 emitted plan command. Contrast `--include-infra`'s own block at verify.sh:2493, which IS gated on RUN_RUST=1 and is therefore a no-op on any docs-only stage.

(3) scripts/verify.sh decide_scope, via a case arm placed AHEAD of `docs/*|*.md|*.yaml|*.yml)` (:1161) — the task-#5536 `_RUST_COUPLED_RI_FIXTURES` shape. Note RUN_RUST=1 on a docs path means the FULL workspace nextest, never a narrowed one: affected-crates-lib.sh:66 maps `docs/*` to no crate, so the closure is empty and narrowing never engages.

CAVEAT — mechanism (2) IS RENAME-BLIND TODAY (live defect in task #4955's landed work, not hypothetical). `git diff --cached --name-only` reports only a rename's DESTINATION (`--name-status -M` shows `R100 old new`), and select_infra_tests() matches rows exact-string against CHANGED_FILES_RAW, which decide_scope deliberately builds from `_files` alone (:1173) — rename sources are recovered only into `_classify`, and only for `^tests/prd-gate/fixtures/.*\.ri$` (:1089). Measured against the LANDED row docs/notes/verify-pipeline-knobs.md -> test_verify_compile_gate.sh: edit -> pole emitted; delete -> pole emitted; `git mv` -> "# (no commands — nothing to verify for this action/scope)". All SEVEN doc-sync rows (verify-pipeline-infra-tests.txt:167-173) are affected. Repair is scoped into task #6077.

For a change touching only config/shell files (no Rust), the PROPORTIONATE local verification in reify is the infra suite, not the full Rust gate. Established landing task 5909 (2026-08-19, changed files = dark-factory-orchestrator.yaml + tests/infra/test_sandbox_cache_writability_seam.sh). `bash scripts/verify-pipeline-guard.sh requires-full-gate <files>` returned 0 (the seam test is a pipeline artifact, so no config-only trivial pass applies), but a full `--scope all --profile both` cannot be affected by a yaml/sh edit when `git diff main...HEAD --name-only | grep -c '\.rs$'` is 0. The real risk surface is the ~30 tests that READ the yaml — find them with `grep -rln 'dark-factory-orchestrator\.yaml' tests/ scripts/ hooks/`, then run `bash tests/infra/run_all.sh` (153 discovered, ~152 expected green). Watch out: run_all.sh's own meta-test (test_run_all.sh) emits literal "=== FAILED:" and "FAILED-DETAIL" strings as PASSING assertions about its reporting format, so grep the authoritative `^=== Summary: N discovered, M failed ===` line rather than counting FAILED matches.

Adding a path to scripts/verify-pipeline-paths.txt does NOT gate a docs/→compiled-test coupling, and is a repeatedly-proposed dead repair. Measured on main 2026-09-07: scripts/verify.sh contains ZERO references to that manifest; it is matched with `grep -xF` (exact whole-line fixed strings — scripts/verify-pipeline-guard.sh:708,743,809,822) so a `dir/**` glob entry is not expressible (0 of 204 lines contain `**`); and it is consumed only by dark-factory's merge-worker trivial-pass at role=='merge'. It therefore cannot affect the hook-gated docs commit on `main`, which is the only ungated route for a docs/ edit. The real mechanism is `_RUST_COUPLED_RI_FIXTURES` in scripts/verify.sh — but that is consulted ONLY inside decide_scope's `tests/prd-gate/fixtures/*.ri)` case arm (:1275), so registering a basename whose file still lives under docs/prds/**/fixtures/ is inert: that path does not match the arm and falls through to `docs/*|*.md|*.yaml|*.yml)` (:1376, no heavy checks). Registration only becomes load-bearing once the fixture is physically moved under tests/prd-gate/fixtures/.

verify.sh --scope staged picker contract (the hook fast path; encoded in tests/infra/test_verify_scope.sh): docs/*,*.md,*.yaml → nothing heavy; gui/src/** frontend TS → GUI only (Rust ⊥ GUI); crates/**, gui/src-tauri/**, Cargo.*, .cargo/*, tree-sitter-reify/* → Rust+GUI; unknown path → conservative Rust+GUI+gate. The OCCT gated pass runs iff a changed crate is in the OCCT-touching set (scripts/occt-scope-lib.sh occt_declared_set) OR a workspace-global/unknown change (Cargo.lock/.cargo/tree-sitter-reify all force the gate). gui/src-tauri is Rust but OCCT-clean → no gate. A `.git/MERGE_HEAD` (or --scope staged during a merge) forces --scope all, since a merge index isn't a curated stage. occt-scope-lib.sh is the SINGLE impl of occt_declared_set (reads occt-touching-crates.txt) + occt_touching_set (cargo-metadata closure), sourced by BOTH verify.sh and the drift test test_occt_gated_scope.sh, so they can't diverge.

verify.sh's OCCT gated/ungated test-plan structure is asserted by EIGHT tests/infra files (test_occt_flock_gate.sh, test_occt_gated_scope.sh, test_release_scoped_scope.sh, test_release_mode_in_test_command.sh, test_verify_scope.sh, test_verify_throughput.sh, test_verify_role_prio.sh, test_scope_boundary.sh), all driven by `verify.sh --print-plan | grep -v '^#'`. Any change to the gated-pass / --exclude structure breaks all eight. These infra tests run on a task's own branch verify whenever RUN_RUST=1 (orchestrator `--scope branch --include-infra` + local project-checks hook), and `.config/*` changes set RUN_RUST=1 — but the merge gate (hooks/pre-merge-commit) runs WITHOUT --include-infra, so it does NOT run run_all.sh.

To prove what reify's pre-commit gate actually plans for a given staged changeset WITHOUT touching the shared main checkout's index, reuse tests/infra/test_verify_scope.sh's OWN hermetic harness rather than writing a fixture by hand. verify.sh's scope picker needs only a git repo plus a handful of sibling scripts — no cargo workspace — so a throwaway repo answers the question exactly.

Recipe (used 2026-08-19 to settle esc-6077-3):
  source tests/infra/{test_helpers,plan_capture_lib,copy_list_preflight_lib}.sh
  eval "$(sed -n '/^make_fixture() {/,/^}/p' tests/infra/test_verify_scope.sh)"
  eval "$(sed -n '/^plan_for() {/,/^}/p'    tests/infra/test_verify_scope.sh)"
  FIX=""; make_fixture FIX; plan_for staged <paths...>; echo "$PLAN_OUT"

EXTRACTING the two functions with `sed` (rather than retyping them) is the load-bearing part: make_fixture's copy list is long and drifts, and it runs assert_source_closure_copied, so a hand-rolled clone silently rots the moment verify.sh gains a new sourced lib. Note make_fixture also copies scripts/verify-pipeline-infra-tests.txt into the fixture, so manifest-row experiments work by appending to "$FIX/scripts/verify-pipeline-infra-tests.txt".

For rename/delete scenarios plan_for is not enough — it only stages NEW files. Seed and commit the file in the fixture first (`git -C "$FIX" -c commit.gpgsign=false commit`), then `git mv` / `git rm` and capture the plan, so the diff carries a real R/D entry.

Read the result from two places: the `# scope decision — RUN_RUST=… RUN_GUI=… RUN_OCCT_GATE=…` line, and plan_count_noncomment_lines "$PLAN_OUT" for the emitted command count (a docs-only stage legitimately yields 0 and `# (no commands — nothing to verify for this action/scope)`).

This is strictly better than reasoning from verify.sh's source or from a script header: hooks/project-checks' own header claims a docs-only stage "produces an empty plan and exits 0", which is true today but says nothing about which manifests can still inject a pole — the measured plan does.

Landing path for reify's `dark-factory-orchestrator.yaml` (determined 2026-09-04): it goes through the MERGE QUEUE, not direct-to-main. CLAUDE.md's direct-commit exemption covers DOCS artifacts (docs/, PRDs, capability manifests, *.md/*.yaml); the orchestrator config is live operational config that merely happens to be a .yaml, so the exemption does not apply — and direct-committing main while the queue is live jams it on the git index lock, builds cold, and forces gate_reverify. The oracle clears it as cheap: `bash scripts/verify-pipeline-guard.sh requires-full-gate dark-factory-orchestrator.yaml` exits 1 (exit 0 would mean the full --scope all gate is required), so the file is NOT a verify-pipeline artifact and is eligible for the merge worker's trivial config-only pass. Sequencing when the change is red-tier: LAND FIRST, then restart via scripts/orchestrator-redeploy-restart.sh — the dirty-start guard refuses uncommitted tracked changes in project_root and a dirty restart is a crash-loop outage.

In reify, `scripts/verify.sh --scope staged` has exactly ONE production caller: hooks/project-checks (invoked by hooks/pre-commit, main branch only). Every per-task lane uses `--scope branch`, and DF_VERIFY_ROLE=merge|background force `--scope all`. So a verify.sh change gated on `[ "$SCOPE" = "staged" ]` affects only the hook-gated main-commit landing path and cannot perturb task lanes, the merge gate, or the branch-scope VS-*/PG-1b infra scenarios.

The reify orchestrator merge path lands via advance_main git plumbing + main_gate_mark_command, which does NOT fire hooks/pre-merge-commit (that hook runs only on `git merge`, i.e. the land.sh/manual path). Consequence: a reify-side git hook CANNOT guard the orchestrator merge-worker fast-path — closing fast-path gaps requires either a consultable oracle script that dark-factory's merge worker shells out to, or a dark-factory-side change. Task 4626 ships such an oracle: scripts/verify-pipeline-guard.sh `requires-full-gate <files>` (exit 0 = full --scope all gate required, 1 = fast-path safe, 2 = usage), classifying scripts/verify.sh + its live `source`d libs + the verify-pipeline data files (.config/nextest.toml, *-crates.txt, verify-pipeline-infra-tests.txt, gen-nextest-config.sh) as load-bearing.

In reify, scripts/verify-pipeline-guard.sh + scripts/verify-pipeline-paths.txt gate ONLY the dark-factory merge-worker trivial-pass fast-path — they are not consulted anywhere on the docs-only direct-commit-on-main path. hooks/pre-commit calls hooks/project-checks, whose entire body is `exec scripts/verify.sh all --profile debug --scope staged --include-infra`, and scripts/verify.sh contains zero references to the guard or its manifest (verified 2026-08-09 at main d5b3c23a78). So adding a docs/ path to verify-pipeline-paths.txt does NOT force a gate on a direct `git commit` on main; only relocating the artifact under a source tree that --scope staged actually covers does.

CORRECTION, measured 2026-08-03 on task/5687 HEAD=20d029a5b2: `scripts/verify-pipeline-guard.sh requires-full-gate` does NOT treat "any tests/infra/* path" as full-gate. Only `tests/infra/*.sh` (the glob special-case `^tests/infra/[^/]*\.sh$`) plus paths with a LITERAL row in scripts/verify-pipeline-paths.txt qualify. Per-path exit codes (0 = full `--scope all --profile both` required): test_new_guard.sh 0, harness-layout-lib.sh 0, run-all-ambient-vars.manifest 0 (literal row, line 95) — but run-all-classification.manifest 1, run-all-skip-closures.manifest 1, harness-layout-baseline.manifest 1 (all three absent from verify-pipeline-paths.txt; `grep -xF -c` returns 0). Consequence for planners: adding a new tests/infra/test_*.sh DOES force the full gate (the script file itself is the trigger), but the classification-manifest ROW is not the trigger — so a manifest-only reclassification takes the config fast-path. reify: how to make an infra guard actually SEE a dark-factory-orchestrator.yaml-only edit (measured 2026-08-20, task 6393). A yaml-only change does NOT force the full gate — `bash scripts/verify-pipeline-guard.sh requires-full-gate dark-factory-orchestrator.yaml` returns exit 1, and per CLAUDE.md a *.yaml change commits DIRECTLY on main through hooks/pre-commit -> hooks/project-checks -> `verify.sh all --profile debug --scope staged --include-infra`, whose staged scope normally yields an EMPTY plan for a docs/config-only stage. So a guard registered only in run-all-classification.manifest would never run on the edit direction that matters. The lever is a row in scripts/verify-pipeline-infra-tests.txt mapping the artifact to the guard: `dark-factory-orchestrator.yaml    tests/infra/test_verify_admission_knob_parity.sh`. verify.sh's select_infra_tests() reads that map against CHANGED_FILES_RAW and the selective-infra emission is gated on DO_TEST=1 only (NOT RUN_RUST), so a yaml-only staged commit then produces a one-command plan running just that guard — verified empirically by staging only the yaml and diffing --print-plan. Note the existing `scripts/verify.sh -> tests/infra/test_verify_*.sh` glob row is self-maintaining for additions, so naming a new guard test_verify_*.sh auto-covers the verify.sh direction with no map edit. Registration surface for a NEW tests/infra/test_*.sh is smaller than it looks: only run-all-classification.manifest is mandatory (run_all.sh auto-discovers by glob); run-all-skip-closures.manifest rows are OPTIONAL ("every member unmapped" = full pool runs), and harness-layout-baseline.manifest applies only to crates/<c>/tests/*.rs, not shell tests.

CORRECTION to the reify tests/infra self-excluding git-grep gate idiom: do NOT end the scan with `|| true`. A no-match `git grep` exits 1, which does abort under `set -euo pipefail`, but git grep also exits 128 on a bad pathspec magic (e.g. `:(exclud)`), an unenterable root, or a `-P` search on a git built without PCRE. `|| true` turns all of those into a vacuous "no matches" PASS. Measured in task 7788 (git 2.43.0): with `|| true`, the canonical-path absence check passed on a root git could not enter. Capture the status (`|| rc=$?`), accept only 0/1 as a result, and return any other status so the assert fails loudly. Canonical instance once task 7788 lands: `tests/infra/test_orchestrator_config_canonical_path.sh::legacy_config_refs`, whose Section (D) pins that a scan which cannot run fails the check. Before that, main's `assert_no_legacy_config_refs` still shows the old `|| true` form.

Facet of the tests-infra full-gate topic, observed on task 7257 (2026-09-09): validate a task's "no full-gate escalation" premise against the COMPLETE changed set, not the subset the description names. #7257's description asserted "Not a verify-pipeline artifact — requires-full-gate returns 1 for these paths", and the architect's plan analysis confirmed it by running the oracle on the three scripts/prd-decompose-verify.* files plus .claude/skills/prd/project.md — exit 1, correct for those four. But the delivered diff also modified tests/infra/test_prd_decompose_verify.sh (an already-registered driver it was extending, not adding), and that file ALONE returns exit 0 via the tests/infra/*.sh glob, so the real merge took the full --scope all --profile both gate. The oracle was never wrong; it was consulted on an incomplete file list, because the .sh edit was implied by "add regression tests" rather than named in the premise. Cheap habit: at merge-request time run `bash scripts/verify-pipeline-guard.sh requires-full-gate $(git diff --name-only main...HEAD)` and report the answer to the merge worker, rather than inheriting the description's claim. Note the trap generalizes past NEW infra tests — extending an existing registered driver is the easier case to miss, since no manifest row changes and nothing feels "added".

Completed: Enforce the record tables' completeness without module-level assert (record.py)
Description: record.py checks that _IN_REGION_CONDITIONS, _ALTERNATIVE_NAMES and _EXIT_HEADLINES cover their enums with three module-level assert statements. `python -O` strips asserts, after which a missing table entry surfaces as a KeyError at the first prompt build or page render instead of at import. These tables are what the analyst prompt and the operator page are generated from, so the invariant is load-bearing and its enforcement is conditional (docs/code-quality.md heuristic 10, uniformly enforced).
Analysis: PREMISES VERIFIED (worktree task/11 at base 368e171):
- record.py checks _IN_REGION_CONDITIONS (line 157, 24 Dimension entries), _ALTERNATIVE_NAMES (line 232, 12 Alternative entries) and _EXIT_HEADLINES (line 265, 4 Exit entries) with three module-level asserts (lines 183, 246, 271). They are the only `assert` statements in src/ (`grep -rnw assert src/`). The task is not done on main and no sibling has done it.
- The tables are read only through three properties: Dimension.in_region_condition (used by model.analyst_prompt and operator_pages._placement_form), Alternative.plain_name (used by model.analyst_prompt and documents._alternatives) and Exit.headline (used by operator_pages and Report.headline). Nothing else touches the private dicts.
- Baseline on this worktree: `uv run pytest` gives 31 passed (~18 s), `uv run ruff check .` is clean, `uv run pyright` reports 0 errors, and `uv run ruff format --check` reports all 24 files already formatted. The checks run sequentially (concurrent_verify false).

APPROACH. Use one public checked-table helper in a new stdlib-only module, src/scoping_intake/enum_tables.py:
  exhaustive_table[K: Enum, V](enum: type[K], entries: Mapping[K, V]) -> Mapping[K, V]
It raises ValueError naming the invariant, the missing members and the extra keys. Otherwise it returns a read-only copy (MappingProxyType(dict(entries))). record.py builds each of its three tables through it and the three asserts go. No string, key or entry order changes: the strings are Leo's prospect-facing wording (review/briefing.yaml).

PROBES. Run in /tmp scratch with the worktree's venv; no repo file was touched.
- The message renders as "...; missing [<Colour.GREEN: 'green'>], extra []".
- A key from another enum is reported as extra [<Size.LARGE: 'large'>].
- A plain-string key 'red' hashes equal to the StrEnum member, so the member does not count as missing. The string itself is reported as extra by the isinstance test.
- Pyright accepts the PEP 695 signature and infers Mapping[Colour, str] at a call site. For a dict mixing two enums it infers K = Colour | Size with 0 errors, so the runtime extra check is the only guard against a wrong-enum key.
- `sys.executable -O -c ...` from the worktree's .venv imports scoping_intake (editable install).
- Ruff 0.16.10 does not flag a repeated attribute key (Colour.RED twice) in a dict literal.

TESTS.
- The helper gets tests/test_enum_tables.py through its public seam, with toy StrEnums.
- One of those tests runs a `python -O` child, because pytest itself runs without -O. That test pins the actual finding: an in-process test would still pass if the check were rewritten as assert.
- record.py's change is a behaviour-preserving refactor. It gets no new test: a record table can only be made incomplete by editing the source. The existing suite already resolves every member of all three tables. analyst_prompt iterates every Dimension and Alternative (tests/test_anthropic_model.py). The operator placement form renders every Dimension condition and every Exit headline (the tests/test_session_flow.py placement tests). A key or entry lost in the rewrap therefore fails either at import or in the suite. A `python -O` smoke command was pre-verified on the base: it prints `24 12 4`.

SCOPE AND COORDINATION.
- Files: the new module, record.py and the new test file.

Completed: One frozen record base class instead of five copies of the same ConfigDict (store.py::Stored)
Description: The configuration 'frozen, extra forbidden' is declared five times: record.Frozen, store.Stored, transcript.Turn, calibration.DimensionRow and calibration.CalibrationRecord, and 'frozen' alone three more times in intake (ProspectView, OperatorView, PurgeResult). The cost shows at SessionStore._read, whose type bound is 'Stored | OperatorPlacement' because OperatorPlacement descends from record.Frozen rather than store.Stored. One policy, several homes (docs/code-quality.md heuristic 11, SPOT). The briefing records that the near-duplicate frozen base classes are not grandfathered.
Analysis: Premises checked on base c749e94, which is the branch tip and main.

Every `ConfigDict` in the package was confirmed by grep:
- `record.Frozen` at record.py:12-13 is `ConfigDict(frozen=True, extra="forbid")`. It is the base of every record.py class, OperatorPlacement included.
- `store.Stored` at store.py:27-28 repeats it. Session, Draft and Released derive from Stored.
- `transcript.Turn` at transcript.py:16-17 repeats it inline.
- `calibration.DimensionRow` and `CalibrationRecord` at calibration.py:24-35 repeat it inline.
- `intake.ProspectView`, `OperatorView` and `PurgeResult` at intake.py:27-28, 40-41 and 205-206 declare `frozen=True` alone, so they silently ignore unknown fields.
- `SessionStore._read` at store.py:157 is bound to `Stored | OperatorPlacement`. `SessionStore._write` at store.py:161 takes `record: BaseModel`.

Nothing else mentions `Stored`: no other source module, test, README or deploy file. web.py's `@dataclass(frozen=True)` types are stdlib HTTP plumbing, not pydantic records, so they are out of scope.

Import graph:
- record.py imports only enum_tables, which imports nothing first-party.
- store, calibration and intake already import record.
- transcript imports no first-party module today. Deriving Turn from `record.Frozen` adds one import, transcript -> record. It points downward (record never imports transcript), so it creates no cycle.

Approach, as the task specifies:
- Keep `record.Frozen` as the single base.
- Derive Turn, Session/Draft/Released, DimensionRow, CalibrationRecord and the three intake views from it, deleting each inline `model_config`.
- Delete `Stored`.
- Narrow `_read`'s bound to `Frozen`, and `_write`'s `record` parameter to match.
- Remove the pydantic imports this leaves unused: store keeps only `ValidationError`; calibration and intake keep none.

record.py itself is not edited.

The only runtime difference is that the three intake views now refuse unknown fields. Intake builds them with keyword arguments naming exactly their fields, and nothing validates them from input, so nothing the app does changes. That one difference is what the RED test pins.

- Baseline: 45 passed; ruff and pyright clean.
- New test against unchanged code: 3 failed, 19 passed. The three failures are exactly the unknown-field case for ProspectView, OperatorView and PurgeResult.

Facts about scoping-intake's record and pages that a test author needs (checked 2026-10-08 on main e8c51e5): Report.headline is a computed property over _EXIT_HEADLINES and FIREWALL_HEADLINE, not a model-written field, so a test cannot plant text in it; DimensionPlacement.reason is rendered only by operator_pages._comparison_html on the operator session page after the blind placement, never in either document; the record validators (Criterion._vagueness_is_recorded, Report._ranking_matches_the_exit, the Analysis validators) check structure only, so Criterion.statement, Criterion.capability, DimensionPlacement.reason, Report.needs_summary and Report.first_step accept an `` payload (verified by building an Analysis via SYNTHETIC_ANALYSIS.model_copy); Intake.say checks only length and SessionStore.create stores the operator label as given, so prospect text and the label reach pages unfiltered. Every StrEnum value in record.py is markup-free, and the strings with apostrophes (Exit.headline for advise_elsewhere, three Dimension.in_region_condition values) are already escaped where rendered.

Fact about scoping-intake's calibration record: a later (ordinal 2+) placement by Leo is anchored evidence, since Leo has read the instrument's placement, confidence, source and per-dimension reason text for the same prospect, and places again against a superset transcript, possibly after a guided rewrite. The instrument's columns in such a row are still clean (an unguided analysis never sees Leo's placement). Narrow edge: if save_draft fails after discard_operator_placement in request_write_up, the previous, possibly guided and already-read draft returns to the blind form, so a row could be placed against a guided draft; carrying the guided flag in the row makes this visible. CalibrationRecord forbids extra fields and had no defaults, so adding fields breaks loading of old-shape rows unless the new fields default; trial data directories (off limits to agents) may hold old-shape rows.

In scoping-intake, tests/test_frozen_records.py builds one instance of every record the package hands between modules at import time, in its module-level RECORDS list. That list includes the intake views OperatorView, ProspectView and PurgeResult, and the store and calibration records. Any field added, renamed or removed on one of those models must be reflected in RECORDS in the same commit. Otherwise the whole module errors at collection, with extra_forbidden or a missing field. Verified at f11e599, 2026-10-08: OperatorView is built there with draft_exists=True.

Gotcha: docs/briefing.yaml (review/briefing.yaml) carries several independent sections that each go stale when a fix lands elsewhere in the codebase — the POSTURE header task-tally, the known_gaps list, the NEWCOMER/CONSUMER FOOTGUNS bullets, and rule-N "latent bug" warnings. A separate POSTURE-header tally gap was tracked as task 92, cancelled as redundant: task 91's own commit had already atomically fixed both the POSTURE header (~line 9) and the Deferred-task-invariant tally (~line 155) in the same edit. A rule-43 warning gap (task 90) was likewise cancelled as redundant — its target staleness was independently fixed before dispatch. The POSTURE header + Deferred-task-invariant CURRENT STATE tally recurred a THIRD time as task 96 (filed 2026-07-22, "third recurrence (92 doesn't cover)"). Guidance: when a code fix invalidates a briefing.yaml claim, sweep ALL of POSTURE header / known_gaps / FOOTGUNS bullets / rule-N warnings / doc naming hygiene in one pass rather than filing single-section patches serially — serial patching has repeatedly produced follow-up "residue" tasks.

candidates.content: Gotcha (solar-challenge-platform frontends, observed 2026-09-28 by task 429's architect): inside an orchestrator or Claude Code agent shell, where AI_AGENT, CLAUDECODE and CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION are set, `npx vitest run <file>` printed only the pass/fail summary and none of the tests' console.log output. Adding `--silent=false` gave empty output with exit 1. To see console logs from a probe test, run `env -u AI_AGENT -u CLAUDECODE -u CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION npx vitest run <file> --reporter=default` from the frontend directory.

GOTCHA (solar-challenge-platform frontends, measured 2026-09-28 by task 499's architect): to run ONE vitest file, use `npm --prefix frontend-portal test -- src/path/X.test.tsx` (npm run-script sets cwd to the package dir, so vite.config.ts's jsdom environment + setupFiles load). `npm --prefix frontend-portal exec -- vitest run src/X.test.tsx` from the repo root runs vitest with cwd = repo root: it skips the package's vite.config.ts (every DOM test fails "ReferenceError: window is not defined") and leaves a stray untracked `node_modules/.vite` cache at the worktree root that must be deleted.

PROCEDURAL (solar-challenge-platform frontends, used 2026-09-30 by task 704's architect for a 20-run mutant matrix): to compare WHICH tests a mutant kills across runs, have vitest write a JSON report instead of reading console output: `npm --prefix "$M" test -- src/A.test.tsx src/B.test.ts --reporter=json --outputFile="$M/result.json"`. Then parse testResults[].assertionResults[], whose entries carry status ('passed'/'failed') and fullName (the describe name plus the test name, with it.each cases expanded). numTotalTests, numPassedTests and numFailedTests give the counts. This extends the throwaway-copy mutation probe (memory e92ef1fd): exit codes and the summary line alone cannot show a vacuous pass moving from one test to another.

GOTCHA (solar_challenge_platform frontends, measured 2026-09-30 by task 668's architect): if <frontend>/node_modules is absent, `npx vitest ...` or `npx tsc ...` does not fail. npx silently downloads the registry's latest package instead; measured: vitest@5.0.2, which then fails with "Cannot find package 'vitest'" while loading vite.config.ts. Install first with `npm --prefix frontend-portal ci`, then call the pinned binaries explicitly: `npm --prefix frontend-portal test` for vitest, and `frontend-portal/node_modules/.bin/tsc -p frontend-portal` for a noEmit type-check from the worktree root. That type-check leaves no dist/ behind, unlike `npm run build`.

frontend-portal vitest under host load (measured 2026-10-10 by task 926's amendment pass): with load average ~156 on 32 cores, one full `npm --prefix frontend-portal test` run took 26 s (baseline 12.6 s) and failed only BillExplainerScreen.test.tsx "names each line's CBS slice ..." with "Test timed out in 5000ms" (vitest's default testTimeout), in a file the task never touched. The file alone then passed (16 tests, 3.9 s) and the full suite passed on rerun (8.8 s). Treat a lone 5000 ms timeout in an untouched file as load: rerun it alone and in full before diagnosing a regression.

GOTCHA (solar_challenge_platform, observed 2026-10-11 by task 582's architect): a fresh task worktree has no frontend-portal/node_modules. Without them, pytest's frontend lane (tests/e2e/test_frontend_unit_suites.py::test_the_vitest_suite_passes) SKIPS instead of running vitest, so a green `uv run --extra dev pytest` proves nothing about portal changes. Run `cd frontend-portal && npm ci`, then `npx vitest run` and `npx tsc --noEmit`, before claiming a portal step is green.

Operator-console (frontend/) vitest facts, verified 2026-09-26 by task 319's architect:
(1) In vitest 4's jsdom environment, vi.useFakeTimers() also intercepts `window.setTimeout`. So a debounced component such as SearchBox is testable with fireEvent.change followed by `act(() => { vi.advanceTimersByTime(ms) })`, with no act() warnings.
(2) Importing a name that a local module does not export does NOT fail in vitest: the binding is just `undefined`. Cases that use it can then pass vacuously; for example, advanceTimersByTime(NaN) advances nothing, so a "never called" assertion passes. Only tsc (`npm --prefix frontend run build`) catches it, as TS2459. So confirm a RED test's import with the build, not only with vitest.

GOTCHA (solar_challenge_platform frontends): the orchestrator verify lane (`uv run --extra dev pytest -m 'not slow'`) only runs a frontend's vitest suite via tests/e2e/test_frontend_unit_suites.py when that frontend's node_modules exists. node_modules is gitignored, so in a fresh task worktree that test SKIPS and new or changed vitest cases go unexercised by verify. To actually run them in a worktree: `npm --prefix frontend-portal ci --no-audit --no-fund` (about 3s; same for `frontend`), then `npm --prefix frontend-portal test`. Vitest does not type-check, so also run `npx tsc -p .` from the frontend directory (strict, noUnusedLocals).

PROCEDURAL (solar-challenge-platform frontends: test harness).
- node_modules is gitignored for frontend/ and frontend-portal/, so a fresh git worktree has none. Run `npm --prefix <f> ci` (or install) before `npm --prefix <f> test`. Per-task orchestrator verify does not install node_modules (task 382 is open on whether it should), so run npm test and npm run build by hand in a worktree.
- Both frontends have a component-test harness:
  - frontend-portal (task 174): @testing-library/react 16.x, @testing-library/dom 10.x and jsdom, plus a vite.config.ts test block (environment 'jsdom', setupFiles ['./src/testSetup.ts']). testSetup.ts registers afterEach(cleanup), because vitest globals are off. Component tests vi.mock('../api/portalClient').
  - frontend/ (task 292): setupFiles './src/test/setup.ts', with a fetch stub instead of a client mock (see memory e99a21ee).
- Versions since task 742: jsdom ^30 and vitest 5 on vite 8 (see topic frontend-npm-vitest-jsdom-pins).

candidates.content: GOTCHA (dark-factory merge lane, planning task 6647, read 2026-10-10): to make a rebased merge candidate keep its exact git tree in a test, commit onto main a patch IDENTICAL to one of the branch's commits. git_ops.py::GitOps::advance_main rebases with a plain `git rebase main` on top of the --no-ff merge commit. That linearises, drops the merge commit, and skips any branch commit whose patch-id is already upstream, so `<rebased>^{tree} == <merge_commit>^{tree}`. This is the follower-stacked-on-a-landed-head case. Separately, the single-branch gate re-verify (_finalize_inflight → gates.py::_reverify_rebased_tree → _run_post_merge_verify) runs PRODUCTION_VERIFIER rather than the lane's injected FakeVerifier (task 6344). Lane tests must therefore patch orchestrator.merge_lane.worker.run_scoped_verification to observe or answer that re-verify, and a held FakeVerifier verify needs make_lane(clock=healthy_verify_clock()).

RESIDUAL verify-integrity hole found 2026-06-07, filed as task 1672 (follow-up to 1646). Mechanism 2's _remerge normal success return recomputes skip_verify = req.pre_rebased AND pre_merge_sha == actual_main (merge_queue.py:4741-4751), which is TRUE for a pre_rebased request because the re-merge was just built against fresh main. So a pre_rebased item whose main advanced ONLY while it waited in the verifier queue (M0→M1) is re-merged onto current main but then SKIPS both _run_post_merge_verify and the #1602 typecheck gate (skip_verify honored at merge_queue.py:4768). And because the pickup re-merge already rebuilt the tree on current main, the subsequent advance_main fast-forwards with no rebase, so the #1595 reverify_on_rebase gate also does NOT fire. Net: the M0→M1 delta can land UNVERIFIED. It is the inverse of the StatusBar false-failure (a genuine new break landing silently, not a false failure) but the same stale-base verify-integrity class. Narrow (needs pre_rebased=True AND main advancing only while queued). Fix: force skip_verify=False on the 'main_advanced' re-merge, mirroring the speculation-race-retry path.

dark-factory merge-queue lesson (task 1672, found+fixed 2026-06-07, merged 7c582b8263): moving stale-base freshening from advance-time to PICKUP-time (task 1646 Mechanism 2) created an inverse integrity hole — Mechanism 2 re-merged a `pre_rebased` item onto fresh main at verify-pickup but `_remerge`'s success return recomputed skip_verify=True (because pre_merge_sha==actual_main after the re-merge), so `_verify_and_advance` SKIPPED both `_run_post_merge_verify` and the #1602 typecheck gate; and because the pickup re-merge already put the tree on current main, advance_main fast-forwarded with NO rebase, so the #1595 reverify-on-rebase gate also did not fire. Net: for a pre_rebased item whose main advanced only while it waited in the verifier queue, the new main delta could land UNVERIFIED (the inverse of the StatusBar false-failure). Fix (1672): a re-merge triggered by remerge_reason=='main_advanced' MUST force skip_verify=False — mirroring the speculation-race-retry sub-path which already did this unconditionally with the comment "Always verify … skipping verification would let semantically-unverified main commits land". GENERAL LESSON: when you move a freshness/rebase step to a different point in the pipeline, re-check that every verify/re-verify gate keyed off the OLD step's trigger still fires; a gate that keyed off "advance_main had to rebase" silently stops firing once an earlier step removes that rebase.

Since dark-factory commit fa95988c8e (2026-09-23 14:53, 'stop laundering unverified main drift'), merge_gates.py::_reverify_rebased_tree (now orchestrator/merge_lane/gates.py) skips the post-rebase re-verify on disjoint footprints ONLY if _disjoint_skip_blockers is empty: P1 blocks when merge_verify_breadth=='full' (dark_factory sets 'full', so EVERY moved main re-verifies there); P2 blocks when the new main tip is not in the in-process registry of tips the queue itself landed green (note_queue_verified_main_tip has one caller, _finalize_advanced_merge) — so ANY direct commit, timer commit or push to main forces the in-flight solo merge to re-verify in full regardless of file overlap. Kill switch merge_disjoint_skip_requires_verified_drift (green-tier, default True) is unset in both dark_factory and reify. Consequence: task 5293 Workstream C's docs-path exclusion (absorbed from 5064) now only helps scoped-breadth projects when the drift is another queue landing; it was re-scoped 2026-09-29 to re-measure before implementing.

Merge-lane test GOTCHA (task 5447 planning, 2026-10-05): on a single-host public lane drive (MergeLane.run, no _host_allocator write), production keeps item.base_sha == real main at dispatch — Mechanism 2 re-merges a stale non-speculative item and a speculative item dispatches only after its predecessor lands — so a test of 'the verify uses the FROZEN base, not a fresh get_main_sha()' is vacuous unless main moves INSIDE the verify before its facts resolve. The ratchet-clean way: persistent_merge_worktree=True plus a GitOps subclass overriding the public reset_persistent_merge_worktree to land an outside commit on main first (the warm swap runs before _run_inflight_verify resolves main_sha), and assert main actually moved.

The dark-factory merge-queue "rebase-before-verify gap" (merge worktree built on a STALE base, re-surfacing already-landed fixes as false verify failures — bit reify tasks 4178 & 4293 with StatusBar.tsx in early June 2026) is now CLOSED, fixed by task 1646 "Bound stale-merge accumulation: cap merger-ahead + freshness re-base at verify-pickup" (merged 9351e6e348, 2026-06-04). Its Mechanism 2: in SpeculativeMergeWorker's verifier loop, when a real merge item is dequeued whose base_sha != current main, the stale merge worktree is discarded and the branch is RE-MERGED against actual main BEFORE `_run_post_merge_verify` runs (orchestrator/src/orchestrator/merge_queue.py:4440-4489). Mechanism 1 (_MERGE_AHEAD_BOUND=1 semaphore) caps non-speculative/non-train build-ahead so the merger re-reads fresh main on resume. Supporting batch tasks: #1658 (pin verify to merge-result SHA = merge_sha^2 so post-verify branch commits can't ride onto main unverified, git_ops.py advance_main), #1645 (verify-phase broken-main contagion guard — detect a failure inherited from main and escalate ONCE instead of N tasks self-patching the same file; this killed the 4293 StatusBar conflict-STORM at its source), #1644 (deliver immediate merge outcomes out-of-band of the verifier FIFO — latency). Verified: the StatusBar-class stale-base FALSE-failure can no longer occur on the production path.

Task 'merge_queue: close the rebase-FF-without-reverify main-safety hole (disjoint-delta re-verify gate)' completed. GitOps.advance_main rebases an already-verified merge commit onto a moved main and fast-forwards it WITHOUT re-verifying the rebased tree (the `for attempt in range(max_attempts)` loop in git_ops.py advance_main; reached on ~28% of reify merges via cas_retry). The post-merge equivalence and drop-guard checks compare file CONTENT, not test-green, so a rebase that applies cleanly but breaks SEMANTICALLY (a sibling that touched interacting files) lands on main unverified. A broken main is catastrophic here: the 20–48 in-flight tasks rebase onto main before verify and inherit the breakage, and new merges verify against broken main and block — a single bad landing cascades to the whole fan-out.

Add a disjoint-delta re-verify gate: when advance_main had to rebase (main moved off expected_main), compute the intervening delta `expected_main..new_main` ∩ (this merge's touched files), reusing the touched-set diff machinery already in _check_post_merge_equivalence. If DISJOINT → land as today (behaviour-preserving, cheap — must preserve the current ~100ms cas-retry fast path). If OVERLAPPING → re-verify the rebased tree before it becomes the source of truth on main.
Details: DESIGN-FIRST / HIGH-STAKES: this is the single critical path through which all code reaches main; design the approach before implementing.

WHERE: the live worker is SpeculativeMergeWorker (harness.py builds only it). The rebase-without-reverify originates INSIDE GitOps.advance_main and is currently invisible to the caller. The shared post-advance block is merge_queue.py `_finalize_advanced_merge` (extracted by task 1593), which both non-train workers call and which already houses the equiv/pyri

dark-factory merge worker skip-verify residual (filed as #1687, found via reify red-main livelock 2026-06-09): merge_queue.py's re-merge dispatch (~line 4709) calls `_remerge(..., force_verify=(remerge_reason == 'main_advanced'))`. #1672 closed the `main_advanced` item path, but the `chain_invalidated` and `previous_failed` paths still pass force_verify=False on the assumption "chain_invalidated ⟹ a prior item FAILED ⟹ main hasn't advanced ⟹ pre_rebased skip is safe". That assumption is FALSE when chain-invalidation PROPAGATED from a `main_advanced` re-merge (a sibling actually LANDED, so main DID advance): the downstream speculative item is re-merged against a moved main → a NEW unverified merge-commit, yet `skip_verify = pre_rebased AND pre_merge_sha == actual_main` re-evaluates True and _verify_and_advance skips both _run_post_merge_verify and the #1602 type-check gate. Empirically: reify task 4401 (commit 2a9df1fe11) landed a gui-tsc-RED tree via "discarding stale merge (chain_invalidated) → skipping re-verification (pre-rebased, main unchanged) → merged". Robust fix (#1687): key the skip on the actual verified merge-commit SHA (extend #1658's "pin verify to the merge-result SHA"), force_verify on ANY re-merge that changes the tree.

In orchestrator merge_queue.py, SpeculativeMergeWorker._remerge re-reads main itself (get_main_sha() then merge_to_main(base_sha=None), which pins pre_merge_sha to the freshly-read main). Consequently the normal-success skip_verify computation `req.pre_rebased and pre_merge_sha == actual_main` is effectively a tautology on pre_merge_sha==actual_main, so it degenerates to skip_verify=req.pre_rebased. This is why a pre_rebased=True request that gets re-merged (e.g. Mechanism 2 'main_advanced' freshness re-base at verify pickup) wrongly inherits skip_verify=True and advances to main UNVERIFIED — the same stale-base hazard the speculation-race retry path already guards by forcing skip_verify=False. Fix (task 1672): _remerge gains keyword-only force_verify=False; the verifier passes force_verify=(remerge_reason=='main_advanced').

GOTCHA (merge-lane tests that pin a _disjoint_skip_blockers SKIP, measured task 5070 2026-10-03): a lane-scene OrchestratorConfig resolves merge_verify_breadth='full' (the live dark-factory-orchestrator.yaml is layered in; the Field default 'scoped' is not what the test sees), so P1 forces a re-verify and any mutation that empties the overlap delta SURVIVES. Pass merge_verify_breadth='scoped' explicitly and register the drift with note_queue_verified_main_tip. Also: GitOps.advance_main checks `merge-base --is-ancestor main <merge>` before update-ref, so a drift committed just BEFORE advance_main yields rebased_pending_reverify, never cas_failed. For a REAL cas_failed, commit the drift inside a wrapped merge_to_main (the merge is built on the drift while expected_main is stale); to land a second drift before the loop re-reads main, wrap advance_main and commit after the first real call returns. Worked example: orchestrator/tests/test_train_moved_main.py test J (test_rebase_after_a_lost_cas_is_gated_against_the_verified_base_not_the_reread_main).

GOTCHA (dark-factory merge lane, measured 2026-10-04 for task 4976): a census of `_run_post_merge_verify` callers done by grepping `_run_post_merge_verify(` MISSES SpeculativeMergeWorker._finalize_inflight's rebased_pending_reverify gate. That site passes the function as an injected callable (`run_post_merge_verify=...`) into merge_lane/gates.py::_reverify_rebased_tree, which forwards only timeouts/enospc/merge_sha/keep_worktrees. So any handle the worker must thread (event_store, escalation_queue, task_client, verifier, probe handles) is silently dropped there unless it is bound into a functools.partial, as _do_train_merge's train_verify does. Also grep `run_post_merge_verify=` when auditing what reaches the recorder.

dark-factory production merge path architecture (as of 2026-06-07): the live worker is SpeculativeMergeWorker (built at harness.py:3238), NOT the deprecated serial MergeWorker. Flow: `_merger_loop` (merge_queue.py:3927) builds the merge worktree via `merge_to_main`→`_create_merge_worktree` (git worktree add --detach at base; git merge --no-ff; scrub .task/) and enqueues a SpeculativeItem; `_verifier_loop` (merge_queue.py:4369) picks it up, applies Mechanism 2 freshness re-base (4440-4489) for real items, then `_verify_and_advance` runs `_run_post_merge_verify` (Step 4, unless skip_verify) and `advance_main(..., reverify_on_rebase=True)` (Step 5). Key sub-pieces: `_remerge` (4580) re-merges branch against freshly-read main; skip_verify is computed as `pre_rebased AND pre_merge_sha == actual_main` (build time 4232; recomputed in _remerge ~4741-4751). #1595 disjoint-delta reverify-on-rebase gate (git_ops.py:1737-1756, _reverify_rebased_tree/_rebase_delta_touched_overlap at merge_queue.py:1273-1475) fires only when advance_main had to rebase because main moved DURING verify. #1602 fail-closed pre-advance unscoped type-check gate is _run_unscoped_typechecks inside _run_post_merge_verify (447-477). The TRAIN path (_do_train_merge, 2742) is EXEMPT from Mechanisms 1&2 but is rebase-before-verify by construction (rebase_onto_main, read main HEAD after rebase, merge, then verify); exemption enforced by `immediate_outcome is None and not GroupMergeRequest` guards at 4441-4443.

GOTCHA (dark_factory, hit 2026-08-03): the merge worker REBASES the branch, so a `git merge-base --is-ancestor <pre-merge-tip> main` check returns FALSE for work that has already landed, and reads as "never merged". Task 3042's branch tip was 77ae9f35a9 before submission; the work landed under new SHAs topped by f4b03f36a6, and a background poller watching the pre-rebase SHA reported "not landed" for 30 minutes after `merge_status` had already returned `state: done, finished_at 11:01:55Z`.

VERIFY BY CONTENT, NOT BY SHA. For task 3042 the decisive check was `git show main:<file> | grep <symbol>`; for task 3214 it was `git ls-tree -r --name-only main -- <fixture dir> | grep '\.gz$'` returning nothing plus the new call site being present. Alternatively poll `mcp__escalation__merge_status(request_id=...)`, which is authoritative and unaffected by rebasing.

Not every merge rebases: task 3214's second attempt (mr-2b826e02) landed with its original SHAs 21a87902df / a6a54244da intact because the branch was already current. So SHA-based checks fail INTERMITTENTLY, which is worse than failing always — do not rely on them.

In orchestrator/src/orchestrator/merge_queue.py, SpeculativeMergeWorker._remerge re-reads main (get_main_sha) and merges against it, so its non-force skip_verify guard `merge_result.pre_merge_sha == actual_main` is structurally a TAUTOLOGY — it degenerates to `skip_verify == req.pre_rebased`. A pre_rebased speculative follower also gets skip_verify=True at build time (merger loop, `req.pre_rebased and pre_merge_sha == base_for_merge`). Therefore a pre_rebased item re-merged on the chain_invalidated/previous_failed path (force_verify=False) skips post-merge verify even when main actually advanced (sibling landed) and the re-merge produced a NEW, never-verified tree. The sound gate is tree-SHA identity (`git rev-parse <commit>^{tree}`), not the pre_rebased proxy flag; merge_to_main uses --no-ff so commit SHAs differ on identical content but tree SHAs are deterministic.

In orchestrator/src/orchestrator/merge_queue.py, _do_train_merge's advance_main call does NOT pass reverify_on_rebase=True (unlike the single-branch _finalize_inflight site, which does). This means when advance_main's own internal CAS-retry loop rebases merge_commit onto a moved main during a train merge, it silently lands the rebased SHA and returns 'advanced' with AdvanceOutcome.advanced_sha != the pre-advance merge_commit the caller expected — there is no rebased_pending_reverify branch/reverify loop at the train site to catch this (that mechanism only exists in _finalize_inflight's while-loop). Task 2154's write-ahead LandedRow journaling (_journal_landed_then_advance) was amended to re-record the row with the true post-rebase advanced_sha whenever it diverges from the journaled merge_commit, so the row stays accurate; any other code that assumes the train's merge_commit variable equals what's actually on main after advance_main returns should double-check adv_outcome.advanced_sha instead.

Task 'merge_queue: chain_invalidated re-merge skips post-merge verify (residual of #1672) — pin skip-verify to the verified merge-commit SHA' completed. INCIDENT (reify, 2026-06-09): a GUI-tsc-RED StatusBar.tsx landed UNVERIFIED on reify main via the chain_invalidated re-merge skip path, then jammed the reify merge queue ~8h — every subsequent full-scope merge verify failed on the inherited red, and the serial queue carouselled cold ~85min verifies, landing nothing. Journal: "Task 4401: discarding stale merge (chain_invalidated), re-merging against actual main" -> "Task 4401: skipping re-verification (pre-rebased, main unchanged)" -> "merged to main successfully". The merged tree was never post-merge-verified.

ROOT CAUSE (residual of #1672): SpeculativeMergeWorker re-merge dispatch (orchestrator/src/orchestrator/merge_queue.py ~4648-4711) computes remerge_reason in {previous_failed, chain_invalidated, main_advanced} and calls _remerge(req, ..., force_verify=(remerge_reason == 'main_advanced')). #1672 closed the main_advanced hole (force verify) but chain_invalidated and previous_failed still pass force_verify=False, on the comment's assumption (lines ~4700-4708) that "chain_invalidated => a PRIOR item failed => main has NOT advanced => the pre_rebased skip invariant holds." That assumption is FALSE when the chain invalidation PROPAGATED from a main_advanced re-merge (a sibling actually LANDED, so main DID advance): the downstream speculative item is re-merged against a moved main, producing a NEW merge-commit/tree that was never verified, yet skip_verify = pre_rebased AND pre_merge_sha == actual_main re-evaluates True and _verify_and_advance skips both _run_post_merge_verify and the #1602 pre-advance unscoped-type-check gate.

FIX (extend #1658's "pin verify to the merge-result SHA" principle to the skip decision): make skip-verify provably sound by keying it on the ACTUAL verified tree, not proxy flags. Record the merge-commit (or tree) SHA that last passed _run_post_merge_verify for the request; skip re-verify ONLY if the about-to-advance merge-commit SHA == that verified SHA. Any re-merge yielding a different SHA (chain_invalidated, previous_failed, main_advanced) must force_verify=True. Re-derive/confirm the exact chain_invalidated unsoundness from the code path first — 4401's verify logs were GC'd with its worktree, so reproduce from the merge_queue path rather than the logs.

Latent main-safety hole in the merge queue (the basis for task 1595, found 2026-06-01): GitOps.advance_main's internal rebase loop (and the SpeculativeMergeWorker CAS-retry loop) lands a REBASED merge tree WITHOUT re-verifying it. The post-merge equivalence and drop-guard checks compare file CONTENT, not test-green, so a rebase that applies cleanly but breaks SEMANTICALLY (a sibling that touched interacting files) lands on main unverified. Exercised on the cas_retry population (~28% of merge_attempts historically). Measured exposure on reify (last 40d, 678 task-merges): only ~6% of adjacent merge pairs share ANY file (confirms max_per_module:1 + module locking → ~94% disjoint concurrent work); of the rebased (cas_retry) subset ~8% overlap the immediate predecessor (up to ~22% vs two predecessors). So a disjoint-delta gate would re-verify only ~1-3% of all merges; overlap when it happens is tiny (median 1 file, max 3) so the re-verify can be crate-scoped; the Cargo.lock over-fire concern is negligible in reify data.

Fifth measured instance of the rebase-landing class (2026-09-14, task 5379, mr-b3d8eb30), and a distinct mechanism from the coalesce-derail one: a SOLO, non-train merge request whose worker verify passed was landed via git_ops advance_main's reverify_on_rebase path ("rebased tree parked at <sha>; returning rebased_pending_reverify (no update-ref)" followed by merge_queue "gate cleared (disjoint or green re-verify); advancing with rebased SHA"). Consequences for anyone polling: merge_status(request_id) returns state=done with outcome=done and NO merge_sha; the branch ref survives at its pre-landing tip; `git merge-base --is-ancestor task/<id> main` is rc=1; the marker grep is empty; and `git branch -d` refuses (needs -D after content verification). The unblock skill's polled-done procedure ("re-derive via the marker search") therefore comes back empty on this path and must fall through to content verification. Context: the §5.3 advisory ("dispatched for real-verify against a base that is NOT the frozen-prefix tip") also fired for this request and, as documented, changed nothing — the request verified and landed.

CORRECTION (measured by code reading on main ac4c66ce80, task 4585): the merge gate's per-main-SHA failing-test baseline is seeded on the PASS path ALWAYS as the EMPTY set (orchestrator/src/orchestrator/merge_lane/worker.py::_run_post_merge_verify calls seed_main_baseline(merge_sha, frozenset())), and verify.py::verify_failure_is_preexisting_on_main's merge+full (μ) fork treats a warm baseline as decisive without re-running main. Later merges can NOT make such a failure 'recognised as pre-existing' (they only ever seed empty), contrary to the 2026-08-22 outcome note about merge request mr-42afb0b5; that attempt's landing is consistent with its full run scheduling the test favourably. candidates.content: scripts/prd-capability-check.py has TWO subprocess launch arms, and the load-bearing one is easy to miss: run_probe() uses subprocess.run for the unbounded case, but grammar_substrate_usable() calls run_probe(probe, timeout=_SUBSTRATE_PROBE_TIMEOUT_S), which routes through _run_bounded()'s subprocess.Popen instead. Any change to how probes are launched (env, cwd, limits) must be applied to BOTH arms or the first real tree-sitter probe any PRD gate runs will silently bypass it. Measured during task 5925: after fixing only subprocess.run, --grammar-substrate-status still ran unisolated in 0.11s off the shared cache.

GOTCHA when writing a structural shell guard that asserts a Python call site passes a given kwarg (e.g. "subprocess.run must pass env="): keying on the bare string "subprocess.run(" and walking forward to the next /^[[:space:]]*)/ produces a FALSE NEGATIVE, because docstrings and comments mention the call in prose. A prose mention opens a block that runs on until it finds a DIFFERENT call site's kwarg, so the guard reports PASS even with the kwarg stripped from the arm under test (reproduced on scripts/prd-capability-check.py, task 5925, where "subprocess.run()" appears in prose at two docstring lines). The discriminator that works: prose is always the EMPTY-paren form, a real call never is — so filter opener lines with `grep -nE 'subprocess\.run\(' | grep -vE 'subprocess\.run\(\)'`, require EVERY surviving site to carry the kwarg, and fail when zero sites are found so the check cannot go vacuously green under a rename. Always negative-control each arm independently (strip the kwarg, confirm only that arm reds, restore) — a structural guard that has silently stopped firing is the exact failure mode it exists to prevent.

Gotcha in scripts/prd-capability-check.py (prd-gate-exec harness, task 4607): a subprocess probe runner that changes CWD must resolve fixture paths to absolute against repo_root BEFORE invoking the subprocess. Grammar probes run with CWD=<repo_root>/tree-sitter-reify/, so a repo-relative fixture (e.g. tests/prd-gate/fixtures/arrow_type.ri) silently resolves under tree-sitter-reify/ and is not found; tree-sitter then exits 1, which observe() misclassifies as a real ABSENT observation rather than a harness file-not-found — producing wrong PASS/FAIL verdicts. Fix: build_command(probe, repo_root) joins os.path.join(repo_root, probe.fixture) for ALL kinds so the executed argv and the recorded evidence command both carry the absolute path and never depend on the caller's CWD.

The scripts/prd-capability-check.py unittest suite is split, as of task 8633, into scripts/test_pcc_*.py partitions (probe_set, verdict, run_probe, grammar_cache, grammar_substrate, main) plus a downward, stdlib-only support module, scripts/_pcc_test_support.py. That module holds the `pcc` loader, the shared constants and the TREE_SITTER_BIN stubs. tests/infra/test_prd_capability_check.sh runs every partition in ONE `python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts -t scripts -p 'test_pcc_*.py'`, so a new partition is picked up without a wrapper edit. In the reify repo, `run_probe()` in scripts/prd-capability-check.py (the grammar-probe branch, `[tree-sitter, parse, --quiet, <fixture>]`) is the ONLY real `tree-sitter parse` CLI invocation in the entire tracked tree — every other `tree-sitter parse` hit is prose, a comment, a grep-on-script-text assertion, or the in-process Rust `tree_sitter` crate API. That call site does `subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True, cwd=cwd)` with NO `env=` kwarg, so it inherits ambient env and shares the host-global, language-name-keyed `~/.cache/tree-sitter/lib/reify.so` across every concurrent warm lane. EDITING GOTCHA (reify tests/infra/test_test_helpers.sh, ~1651 lines): this suite self-greps `${BASH_SOURCE[0]}` in a block of self-checks (~lines 900-980), so several ordinary-looking edits fail the suite in ways that read as unrelated. Before adding checks or comments there: (1) every new `check "<desc>" ...` description must be UNIQUE up to its first quote — a self-check greps `check "[^"]+"` and fails on any duplicate, and that includes the literal text `check "` appearing inside a heredoc or string; (2) comments must not match `lines [~][34][0-9]{2}` — cite `#NNNN` task ids and function names, never "lines ~NNN" (a self-check bans drifting line references); (3) do not use the phrasing `absent until step-[23] adds it` (banned by another self-check); (4) exactly 3 lines may match `_src_beh.*_out=$(bash -eu -c` — do not add a 4th; (5) `trap cleanup_robust EXIT` (line ~633) is the ONLY main-shell EXIT trap and the file self-checks for it, so add no second one — write scratch state under `$_WL_DIR` (line ~1059, itself under `$_robust_tmpdir`), which that trap already reclaims. The suite runs in ~1s, so re-running it after every edit is cheap; a self-exec regression guard that re-enters the file is idiomatic here given (1)-(5) and the existing `${BASH_SOURCE[0]}` precedent.

Reify prd_gate wrappers (tests/infra/test_prd_gate_*.sh) must preflight the tree-sitter grammar substrate via `scripts/prd-gate-substrate-guard.sh` (sourced; task 5897), not via hand-rolled `command -v tree-sitter` + parser.c isfile() guards — neither of those can see a present CLI + present grammar that tree-sitter still cannot LOAD, which is what a sandboxed role's unwritable ~/.cache/tree-sitter/lock/ causes (HARNESS_ERROR -> checker exit 70 -> spurious gate FAIL). The guard's contract is PER-ROW, not whole-script: on an unusable substrate it drops only probe_kind=="grammar" rows and the check rows still run and are still asserted, behind a loud stdout+stderr banner. Whole-script `exit 0` is wrong here because these probe-sets are mostly check probes (corpus 1 grammar + 2 check; compiler-type-hygiene 1 grammar + 6 check) and check probes never touch the substrate. Feed the filtered probe-set to BOTH the checker argument and the CORPUS_PATH env var so the gates' existing completeness assertions self-calibrate with no python change.

Guarding a tree-sitter grammar probe on PRESENCE (`command -v tree-sitter` + `[ -f tree-sitter-reify/src/parser.c ]`) is insufficient in reify — in a sandboxed agent role both hold yet the grammar cannot LOAD, because ~/.cache/tree-sitter/lock/ is outside the landlock write set (see memory 223af5ac). Shell gates should print a visible `SKIP:` line carrying that reason and keep exiting 0, since tests/infra/run_all.sh classifies on exit code only. Pending follow-ups 5904/5897 adopt this in test_prd_gate_corpus.sh and test_prd_gate_compiler_type_hygiene.sh.

So a naive "grep docs/ for path:line" regression guard is actively WRONG — it fails on correct output.

THE CHECK THAT DOES WORK: diff the sorted path:line TOKEN MULTISET between branch base and HEAD — `git grep -hoE '\b[A-Za-z0-9_/.-]+\.py:[0-9]+(-[0-9]+)?' <rev> -- docs/ | sort`. A correct sweep yields DELETIONS ONLY, ZERO ADDITIONS; any added token is a digit that was rewritten, i.e. a "Never re-anchor a dated snapshot" violation (Leo's ratified ruling 2026-08-19, which explicitly extends to dated docs/notes/ survey files). Task 6337 landed 87 deletions / 0 additions. Re-run the same diff restricted to NON-.py extensions to prove scope containment: that multiset must be IDENTICAL. reify: when writing a tests/infra structural guard that greps for a bare CLI invocation, discriminate by COMMAND POSITION, not by mere mention. Measured for `tree-sitter parse` at main 2227f36c4d: a whole-repo literal grep hits 170+ tracked files (PRD prose, .ri fixture header comments, Rust doc comments), but the ERE `^[[:space:]]*(\$ )?([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*=[^[:space:]]+[[:space:]]+)*<cmd>` hits only 7 lines in 4 files. Also exclude docs/prds/**/*.capability-manifest.{md,yaml} by SCOPE: their command lines are archival evidence of probes executed on a stated date, so "fixing" them falsifies a measurement record. House conventions for such guards: POSIX ERE only (grep -P is silently broken on BSD grep and makes negated assertions false-positive), bracketed char-class self-avoidance (`tree-[s]itter`), plus a not-vacuously-green enumeration check and a synthetic positive control — skeleton at tests/infra/test_no_prebuilt_reify_bin_spawn.sh, assertion shape at scripts/test_tree_sitter_generate.sh:166.

Reify shell COUNTING guards over a script's own source (e.g. tests/infra/test_infra_git_env_isolation.sh arm F, which asserts every member-spawn / `git -C` site in tests/infra/run_all.sh is wrapped in reify_git_env_scrub): normalize in this ORDER — fold line continuations FIRST (`sed -e :a -e '/\\$/N; s/\\\n//; ta'`), THEN drop comment lines (`grep -v '^[[:blank:]]*#'`). Folding first is needed so a wrapper sitting on the preceding physical line counts as one logical statement; stripping comments is needed because run_all.sh is heavily commented and a comment that quotes the invocation shape verbatim otherwise scores as a real, unscrubbed call site. MEASURED and self-inflicted on task #7106: the explanatory block comment added alongside the fix contained `git -C "$FIX"`, which took the guard from 7-of-7 to 7-of-8 and would have redded the merge gate on pure prose. Prefer the comment strip over anchoring the pattern to a leading `bash `/`reify_git_env_scrub` token — narrowing the pattern also stops it matching a legitimately reshaped call site (e.g. inside a command substitution), turning a real coverage hole into a silent pass, and a `>= N` floor only catches sites DISAPPEARING, never ones the pattern was narrowed past.
