solar_challenge community-billing test pattern, measured by the task 510 architect on main 291cf22 (2026-10-06). CommunityResults exposes billing only as net figures (baseline_net_cost_gbp, community_net_cost_gbp, community_savings_gbp), so a test that drives simulate_community isolates one pricing leg with a one-sided fleet. An import-only _make_fleet fleet's baseline net cost is its import bill alone, so it is also the guard that a zero export earns nothing. A fleet whose netting leaves zero community import isolates the export leg, as TestCommunityBillingSavings::test_community_net_cost does. On 291cf22 every billing test through simulate_community, in tests/unit and tests/integration, used FlatRateTariff, so a transient mutation pricing the import at tariff.mean_period_rate was caught only by the private TestPriceGridFlows TOU test. Task 510's plan replaces it with tests/unit/test_community.py::TestCommunityBillingTimeOfUse: Economy 7 on a 2-hour index, 2 kW then 3 kW import = 4×0.09 + 6×0.25 = £1.86. It takes effect once task 510 merges.

Architecture fact (TOU dispatch): the two TOU paths are mutually exclusive, selected at home.py:257. The rate-aware FUNCTION path (flow.simulate_timestep_tou, uses actual £/kWh from TariffConfig) runs when HomeConfig.dispatch_strategy=="tou_optimized" AND tariff set AND BatteryConfig.dispatch_strategy is None. The STRATEGY-pattern path (flow.simulate_timestep + a DispatchStrategy subclass, hour-window based) runs when BatteryConfig.dispatch_strategy is set. Consequence for P4: the function path gets battery.config (hence GridChargeConfig) for free with no signature change; the strategy path's simulate_timestep had NO tariff param, so ε (#28) must thread tariff=config.tariff_config into the simulate_timestep call at home.py:290 for grid-charging to engage there.

Solar Challenge finance/physics facts verified 2026-06-17 (load-bearing for the flex work): (1) home.py:322 prices grid import PER-TIMESTEP at the TOU rate (`r.grid_import * rate`), so cheap-rate grid charging genuinely lowers total_import_cost_gbp — the arbitrage time-shift reaches the householder bill correctly today. (2) project_multi_year computes fleet_revenue = Σ(self_consumption_saving + seg_export) ONLY (finance.py:864-877) — it does NOT include the arbitrage import-cost reduction; the time-shift only leaks into project surplus via self_consumption counting grid-charged battery DISCHARGE as self-consumption (flow.py:276) valued at full retail, which OVERSTATES it (the 'self-consumption-inflation'; the W2 cost-recovery CR2 task now owns a cbs_grid_charge_cost correction that reassigns the off-peak grid-charge cost from householder import to a CBS outgoing). (3) Fleet-distribution homes are hardcoded tariff_config=None (config.py:1579 in generate_homes_from_distribution), so the canonical fleet sees ZERO arbitrage value until a fleet-wide TOU tariff is threaded (W1 task β). (4) max_discharge_kw is a real BatteryConfig field (config.py:264, default 2.5 kW), exposed on home.battery_config like capacity_kwh — used as the per-kW grid-services multiplier.

solar_challenge finance test gotcha (verified 2026-10-02, task 307): since task 307, householder_bill resolves the missing-tariff retail fallback (finance._physics_import_cost_gbp) BEFORE the physics/override switch. So a home whose physics import cost is £0 with import > 0 (e.g. test_finance_bill's _make_summary(total_import_cost_gbp=0.0, total_export_revenue_gbp=0.0, net_cost_gbp=0.0, seg_revenue_gbp=None)) emits the "no tariff configured" UserWarning on EVERY path. That includes an override home whose cap binds and so bills 0 kWh of import. A test on such a home that uses warnings.simplefilter("error"), or asserts no warnings, will now fail; pytest.warns(match=<other text>) still passes, because pytest re-emits the extra warning.

solar_challenge test gotcha (task 660, tests/unit/test_home.py, 2026-10-12): _results_with_every_series_set() gives each series arange(60) + 100 × its field position, so grid_charge (the last field, 1300-1359 kW) carries more energy than battery_charge (300-359 kW) and grid_import (600-659 kW). calculate_summary therefore always raises SummaryStatistics' "total_grid_charge_kwh is a part of both total_battery_charge_kwh and total_grid_import_kwh" ValueError on it. A test that runs calculate_summary on it should first build dataclasses.replace(_results_with_every_series_set(), grid_charge=None). Otherwise a pytest.raises(ValueError) around calculate_summary passes or fails for the wrong reason.

content: solar_challenge test gotcha, measured 2026-10-14 by the task 710 implementer (CPython 3.12, synthetic_june_weather for 2024-06-21). To tell simulate_home's tariff-rate TOU path (simulate_timestep_tou) from self-consumption by behaviour, do not use grid_charge > 0: both paths grid-charge only when BatteryConfig.grid_charging is set, so with a plain BatteryConfig(capacity_kwh=5.0) both show 0 kWh. Compare battery discharge in the cheap minutes (tariff_rate < tariff_rate.max()) instead. Measured on an Economy 7 home with 4 kW PV, a 3000 kWh/yr load and a 5 kWh battery: the TOU path discharged exactly 0 kWh in the 420 cheap minutes and 1.57 kWh at the dear rate, while self-consumption discharged 0.31 kWh in 309 of the 420 cheap minutes. A home with no battery cannot be told apart by behaviour: both paths produce identical results frames, so only strategy_name distinguishes them. This sign is used by tests/unit/test_home_dispatch.py::test_tou_optimized_saves_the_battery_for_the_dear_rate_and_self_consumption_does_not, which was on task/710 and not yet merged when this was written.

44d86660-0e17-4aca-a0e4-a0301e847b97.content: solar_challenge gotcha (task 469 amendment 222ffc6, on task/469, not yet merged when written 2026-10-10): SummaryStatistics.__post_init__ raises ValueError unless 0 <= total_grid_charge_kwh <= total_battery_charge_kwh and total_grid_charge_kwh <= total_grid_import_kwh; a NaN in any of the three also raises. So a test that hand-builds a summary, or dataclasses.replace()s one, giving it a grid charge must keep the battery charge and grid import at least that large. With the default grid charge of 0.0, it now also refuses a negative or NaN battery charge or grid import total. calculate_summary's totals always meet the check, because flow.py adds the same non-negative grid-charged kWh to both. SummaryStatistics is not frozen, so the check runs at construction only.

candidates.content: solar_challenge_platform SQLAlchemy gotcha, measured 2026-10-15 by the task 1192 architect at a26f41e (project venv, in-memory SQLite). Session.begin_nested() flushes the caller's pending objects before it emits SAVEPOINT, whatever autoflush is set to, so a `try: with session.begin_nested(): ... except SQLAlchemyError` also catches the CALLER's failed write. That includes an IntegrityError from a pending duplicate row, or a store fault on the caller's INSERT. The flush failure has already rolled the caller back, and its next statement raises PendingRollbackError. A savepoint-isolated read that maps store faults (e.g. ConsentGate.decide, or a per-home optimiser savepoint) must call session.flush() BEFORE the try, so the caller's own flush errors propagate. Session.no_autoflush does not prevent this flush.

solar_challenge_platform gotchas for injecting a consent-store fault in tests. Measured by the task 1192 architect on 2026-10-14 (SQLAlchemy 2.0.51, SQLite/pysqlite, Python 3.11).
- An exception raised inside an engine before_cursor_execute listener reaches the caller unwrapped. To simulate a store fault, the listener must raise a SQLAlchemyError itself, e.g. sqlalchemy.exc.OperationalError(statement, None, Exception('...')).
- Session.get answers from the identity map without emitting SQL. A fault on consent_current statements fires only when the ConsentCurrent row is not already loaded in that session, so seed grants in a separate committed Session first.
- Session.begin_nested() emits its SAVEPOINT lazily, on the first SQL inside the with.
- `try: with session.begin_nested(): ...` / `except SQLAlchemyError` turns a fault on SAVEPOINT, on the read, on RELEASE or on ROLLBACK TO into a handled failure, and the caller's earlier flushed row still commits.
- With the try inside the with instead, a RELEASE fault raises.

solar_challenge_platform SQLAlchemy gotcha (measured 2026-10-15 on SQLAlchemy 2.0.51, task 1192): Session.begin_nested() flushes the session's pending objects BEFORE it emits SAVEPOINT, whatever autoflush is set to (Session.no_autoflush does not stop it), so `try: with session.begin_nested(): ... except SQLAlchemyError:` also catches the caller's own failed write (e.g. an IntegrityError from an unflushed duplicate row), and by then SQLAlchemy has already rolled the caller back to its innermost transaction or savepoint, so the caller's next statement raises PendingRollbackError. Call session.flush() before the try, so a failure of the caller's pending writes propagates and the except covers only SAVEPOINT, the statements inside the savepoint, and RELEASE or ROLLBACK TO; consent/gate.py::ConsentGate.decide does exactly this, pinned by tests/consent/test_gate.py::test_a_store_fault_on_the_callers_pending_writes_propagates_from_decide.

solar_challenge_platform gotcha, measured by the task 1192 implementer on 2026-10-15 (SQLAlchemy 2.0.51, SQLite). After a failed RELEASE SAVEPOINT, SQLAlchemy marks the nested transaction inactive and never emits ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT. A tests/_failing_statements fault on SAVEPOINT, RELEASE or ROLLBACK TO never reaches the database, so the caller's later commit succeeds through the open savepoint. Only that client-side injection makes it succeed: on Postgres, a real server-side failure of those statements leaves the caller's transaction aborted. Only a fault on the read itself models production: SQLAlchemy's ROLLBACK TO then clears the aborted state. Assert a caller commit after a savepoint-statement fault only as "decide does not end the caller's transaction", never as a production guarantee.

solar_challenge_platform gotcha (measured 2026-10-07, SQLAlchemy 2.0.51 + psycopg 3): a refused Postgres connection surfaces as sqlalchemy.exc.OperationalError with connection_invalidated=False and statement=None. The psycopg dialect's is_disconnect returns False when there is no connection yet. So a retry predicate keyed only on connection_invalidated misses a DB restart; it must also check the OperationalError/InterfaceError type. On SQLite, a missing table ("no such table: ...") is ALSO an OperationalError, so a type-based transient check retries schema errors there.

solar_challenge_platform test gotcha (task 1192, 2026-10-15): tests/_failing_statements.py::failing_statements(engine, pattern, *, error=...) is the shared store-fault helper. It is an engine before_cursor_execute listener that raises a real OperationalError for every statement whose SQL re.search-es the regex; patterns like r'^SAVEPOINT ', r'^RELEASE SAVEPOINT ' and r'^ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT ' target savepoint statements. A fault on a consent read fires only on an identity-map miss: Session.get answers from the identity map with no SQL, and begin_nested emits SAVEPOINT lazily on the first SQL inside it. So seed the grant in its own Session(engine) and commit it, then decide in a fresh session; otherwise the fault never fires and the test passes vacuously. On SQLite, flush a caller row first so pysqlite's outer BEGIN is open and RELEASE is nested, not a commit.

solar_challenge_platform testing technique (verified 2026-10-14 by the task 1036 architect, SQLAlchemy 2.0.51, main 295b6cb). Use it to reach an unsupported-dialect refusal, such as db/dialects.py::dialect_insert's ValueError, through a public seam that runs real queries first. A stand-in session cannot do that.
1. Subclass sqlalchemy.dialects.sqlite.pysqlite.SQLiteDialect_pysqlite. In the subclass's own body, set a fictional `name` such as 'elsewhere' and `supports_statement_cache = True`; without the latter SQLAlchemy warns with code cprf.
2. Register it with sqlalchemy.dialects.registry.register(name, __name__, cls.__name__).
3. Build it with create_engine(f'{name}://', poolclass=StaticPool), then Base.metadata.create_all. The full schema builds: the property after_create listener just skips its SQLite trigger, and RLS does nothing.
Never register a real dialect name such as 'mysql': the registry is process-wide and would shadow SQLAlchemy's own dialect.

solar_challenge_platform gotcha (verified 2026-10-07, task 209 planning): SQLAlchemy's DateTime(timezone=True) on SQLite binds a tz-aware datetime by its wall-clock fields and drops the offset, so a non-UTC instant is stored wrong. Every store converts to UTC before binding (as DispatchLivenessStore.write_refresh_tick does) and re-attaches UTC to the naive values SQLite reads back. The repo had no portable upsert: on_conflict_do_update exists only on the dialect-specific constructs (sqlalchemy.dialects.postgresql.insert / sqlalchemy.dialects.sqlite.insert). A store that must run on both the hermetic SQLite suite and Postgres picks one by session.get_bind().dialect.name.

solar_challenge_platform test gotcha, measured 2026-10-14 by the task 1026 architect: the project env runs Python 3.11.15 (so itertools.batched, 3.12+, is unavailable) with Ubuntu's SQLite 3.45.1, whose SQLITE_LIMIT_VARIABLE_NUMBER is 250,000, not upstream's default 32,766. So an oversized multi-row VALUES statement that a default SQLite build or PostgreSQL (65,535) refuses still runs here. A test that needs SQLite to refuse it must lower the limit on the connection: with tests/_sqlite_engine.make_in_memory_engine() (StaticPool, one shared connection), call conn.connection.dbapi_connection.setlimit(sqlite3.SQLITE_LIMIT_VARIABLE_NUMBER, 32_766) inside `with engine.connect() as conn`. The limit persists for every later session, and an oversized statement then raises sqlalchemy.exc.OperationalError "too many SQL variables".

Gotchas for DB triggers in solar_challenge_platform, verified 2026-09-25 while planning task 325. (1) sqlalchemy.DDL(...) is untyped in SQLAlchemy 2.0.51, so mypy --strict reports no-untyped-call. Use a typed @event.listens_for(Model.__table__, "after_create") listener that calls connection.exec_driver_sql(...) instead. (2) SQLite 3.45's RAISE(ABORT, msg) accepts only a string-literal message; `'...' || OLD.id` is a syntax error. (3) A refused delete surfaces as sqlalchemy.exc.IntegrityError on both dialects: SQLite reports SQLITE_CONSTRAINT_TRIGGER, and Postgres does too when the plpgsql trigger uses RAISE ... USING ERRCODE = 'restrict_violation' (SQLSTATE 23001). (4) A row-level BEFORE DELETE trigger does not fire on Postgres TRUNCATE (not even a cascaded one); that needs a separate BEFORE TRUNCATE FOR EACH STATEMENT trigger.

solar_challenge_platform gotcha (measured 2026-10-06, base 7fcfeac): the dropped-readings drill's raw-row helpers (validation/drills/dropped_readings.py _read_raw_rows / _delete_rows) bind raw uuid.UUID values through sqlalchemy text(). SQLite rejects that bind with "sqlite3.ProgrammingError: Error binding parameter 1: type 'UUID' is not supported", so those helpers only run on Postgres. Hermetic SQLite tests cannot reach them. The one real check is the slow Docker capstone test_dropped_readings_drill_recovers_against_real_docker_and_flows_into_bundle (about 93 s). It cannot tell a home-keyed DELETE from a device-keyed one, because seed_golden_fleet seeds one device per home.

solar_challenge_platform test gotcha, measured on task 516's probes at main 40a6556, 2026-10-13. To make the database reject ONE statement for one home, attach a before_cursor_execute(retval=True) listener to the test's engine. It replaces the first statement whose bound values equal the home's UUID with "SELECT * FROM no_such_table" and returns type(parameters)().
- Match the UUID against a tuple of (uuid, str(uuid), uuid.hex) using ==. Do not use a set: some bound values are unhashable. psycopg binds uuid.UUID values in dicts, while SQLite binds 32-char hex strings in tuples.
- SQLite raises OperationalError; Postgres raises ProgrammingError (UndefinedTable) and aborts the transaction.
- On Postgres, without a savepoint (session.begin_nested()) the next home's read in the same Session fails with InFailedSqlTransaction. SQLite never aborts the transaction, so only a timescale-lane test can prove a per-home savepoint.

solar_challenge_platform gotcha (probed 2026-10-03 at main 9acba73, task 352): TimescaleStore's public write and query cannot run on a hermetic SQLite engine, even after the telemetry table is created from its Core Table. write() raises OperationalError "ON CONFLICT clause does not match any PRIMARY KEY or UNIQUE constraint", because the Core telemetry Table declares no unique key. query(..., RAW) raises ProgrammingError "type 'UUID' is not supported", because text() passes a raw uuid.UUID bind and sqlite3 rejects it. So a hermetic test of a SQL reader of telemetry or telemetry_settlement_hh (ops/reads.py) must create and seed the tables from timescale_store's Core Table objects. Task 352 promotes those as telemetry_table and settlement_table.

solar_challenge_platform hermetic test pattern, measured 2026-10-10 by the task 778 architect. To prove a TimescaleStore method refuses its input before any I/O, with no database, build TimescaleStore(engine=sqlalchemy.create_engine("postgresql+psycopg://", creator=f)) where f raises. A postgres engine opens nothing until first use. SQLAlchemy lets a non-DBAPI exception raised by the creator propagate unwrapped: an AssertionError arrived as AssertionError. So the test sees either the method's own ValueError or the creator's sentinel, and a sentinel can also pin that an accepted input goes on to the database. Precedent: tests/timeseries/test_timescale_store_write.py.

solar_challenge_platform test gotcha (verified 2026-10-09, task 209): tests/test_sqlite_engine_home.py only flags create_engine calls that build the shared StaticPool in-memory SQLite engine (in-memory URL + poolclass=StaticPool + a connect_args that may disable check_same_thread); those must come from tests/_sqlite_engine.make_in_memory_engine. A plain sa.create_engine("sqlite://") is allowed, and is the house way to give a SQL store a database with NO tables, so its write raises sqlalchemy OperationalError ("no such table"). Use it for a "store raises the DB error and logs nothing" test. make_in_memory_engine always runs create_all, so it cannot serve there.

solar_challenge_platform test pattern (task 790; tests/timeseries/test_timescale_store_write.py): to prove a TimescaleStore method refuses its input before any I/O, with no Docker, build the store through its public constructor over create_engine("postgresql+psycopg://", creator=_refuse_to_connect), where the creator raises AssertionError. SQLAlchemy 2.0.51 re-raises a non-DBAPI exception from the creator unwrapped. So a write that connects first fails the test with the creator's own message, and pytest.raises(ValueError) passes only on a refusal made before I/O. No private name is patched.

solar_challenge_platform gotcha (read 2026-10-10 at main 1b4b448): SQLite enforces no foreign keys unless `PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON` runs on the connection, and the suite's StaticPool in-memory SQLite engine may be built only in tests/_sqlite_engine.py (tests/test_sqlite_engine_home.py fails any other create_engine of that shape). So a test that needs a real FK violation (the IntegrityError Postgres raises) must take its engine from that helper with the PRAGMA registered as a "connect" listener before create_all, not build its own. With FKs on, an FK violation surfaces at the first flush, not at commit: consent/store.py record_event and the config stores (set_finance/set_battery/set_coverage) flush inside the route handler, before commit_or_409 runs.

Gotcha in solar_challenge_platform tests: with SQLAlchemy 2.x, an engine for 'sqlite:///:memory:' that has no StaticPool (for example db.session.init_db(url='sqlite:///:memory:')) uses one connection per thread. Each thread therefore sees its own empty database. Since task 309, Subscriber.run() runs consent checks on an 'ingest-consent-check' daemon thread, so a database seeded on the test's thread is invisible to them. Use tests/_sqlite_engine.make_in_memory_engine() (StaticPool, check_same_thread=False) with GateConsentChecker(session_factory=lambda: Session(engine)), or a file-backed SQLite under tmp_path. handle_message runs its checks on the calling thread and is not affected.

solar_challenge_platform conventions confirmed while planning P1·β (S7 models): (1) the orchestrator verify runs `mypy --strict` on src/solar_challenge_platform ONLY — test files under tests/ are NOT type-gated, so test code can be loosely typed but every src/ symbol must be mypy-clean. (2) Cross-module SQLAlchemy 2.0 ORM relationships should use TYPE_CHECKING imports + string forward refs (Mapped[list['Account']]) and declare FKs via 'table.id' strings — SQLAlchemy resolves targets from its class registry, so no runtime imports between mutually-referencing entity modules are needed (avoids import cycles) while staying mypy --strict clean. models/__init__.py must import every entity module so Base.metadata is fully populated for create_all and Alembic autogenerate. UUID PKs use sqlalchemy.Uuid + default=uuid.uuid4 (portable SQLite/Postgres); money uses Numeric/Decimal.

solar_challenge_platform SQLAlchemy gotcha (SQLAlchemy 2.0.51, measured 2026-10-10 by the task 549 architect): sa.JSON's none_as_null defaults to False. An ORM attribute explicitly set to Python None on a nullable JSON column is therefore stored as the JSON text 'null', not SQL NULL. It still reads back as None, but `IS NULL` misses it, unlike the rows a migration's add_column leaves NULL. When NULL in a JSON column means "not reported" (the migration-0022 convention), declare the ORM column sa.JSON(none_as_null=True). An integer column needs nothing special.

solar_challenge_platform SQLAlchemy gotcha, measured by task 1225's architect on 2026-10-18 at main 0fdcf5f (SQLAlchemy 2.0.51, SQLite). Several things that are not database faults are still SQLAlchemyErrors, so a broad `except SQLAlchemyError` reports caller bugs as store faults:
- Passing a str or int where a Uuid primary key is expected (e.g. ConsentGate.decide(session, "not-a-uuid", ...)) raises a plain sqlalchemy.exc.StatementError ("(builtins.AttributeError) 'str' object has no attribute 'hex'") while binding the parameter, before the database is asked.
- After a flush fails and the caller does not roll back, the session is clean, so the next flush() is a no-op and the next begin_nested() raises PendingRollbackError.
To catch only "the store could not answer", use `except (DBAPIError, sqlalchemy.exc.TimeoutError)`:
- SQLAlchemy wraps a failed connect as DBAPIError.
- The pool-exhaustion TimeoutError subclasses SQLAlchemyError, not DBAPIError.
- DisconnectionError is consumed inside the pool's checkout loop and never reaches the caller.

Gotcha + technique (probed 2026-09-28, task 516):
- On Postgres, one failed statement aborts the Session's transaction, and every later statement on that Session raises psycopg InFailedSqlTransaction until ROLLBACK or ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT. SQLite never aborts, so a test proving per-item savepoint isolation must run on the timescale lane (tests._timescale_container.timescale_url + tests._migrated_engine.migrated_engine, about 11 s; Docker is present, so the lane runs in verify).
- To inject a genuine DB error hermetically, listen for before_cursor_execute with retval=True on the test's own engine. Swap the first statement whose bound params name a value for ("SELECT * FROM no_such_table", type(parameters)()).
- Match the value against the tuple (uuid, str(uuid), uuid.hex) using ==, never a set, because params can be unhashable. psycopg binds uuid.UUID in dicts; SQLite binds 32-char hex in qmark tuples.
- session.get() calls answered from the identity map emit no SQL, so they cannot be targeted this way.

CORRECTION to the restart-drain diagnostic rule (the rule recorded with the 3112 specimen, mem0 76fe59fd, says "an outcome=cancelled with an EMPTY reason string is the signature of a restart drain"). The EMPTY-REASON half of that rule is VACUOUS and does no discriminating work. Measured 2026-08-27 across all seven orchestrator-targeted projects: 0 of 3,650 task_completed events with outcome='cancelled' carry a non-empty reason. dark_factory alone: 0 of 1,438. A cancellation NEVER carries a reason — that is precisely the defect task 3172 exists to fix, so the field can only start discriminating once 3172 lands. By contrast the field IS populated for other outcomes: blocked 98 of 427, requeued 329 of 1356 (e.g. 'plan_blast_radius_lock_conflict'); done is also 0 of 2,671. There is also a separate 'soft-cancelled' outcome (dark_factory 40, reify 28), likewise always empty-reason.

USE INSTEAD: outcome='cancelled' alone IS the drain marker. The discriminating power for finding stranded work lives entirely in the other two conjuncts — the task is still NON-TERMINAL, and a task/<id> branch exists with commits not on main. Mechanics: `reason` is a JSON key inside events.data, not a column; two empty forms exist (key MISSING for the pre-2026-07-31 event schema, empty string '' after), so test `coalesce(json_extract(data,'$.reason'),'') <> ''`.

candidates.content: reify-audit gotcha: the binary opens its runs-db (default cwd-relative `data/orchestrator/runs.db`, gitignored) with rusqlite `Connection::open` (read-WRITE, creates), and a warm-lane/task worktree has no such file, so any sweep from a lane exits 125 "error opening runs-db" before any detector runs. To smoke-test a detector against the live corpus from a lane (e.g. `scripts/pprdstatus-escalate.py --dry-run`, which passes no --runs-db), create a throwaway `data/orchestrator/runs.db` in the lane holding just `CREATE TABLE events (task_id TEXT, event_type TEXT)` and delete it afterwards. Never point it at the main checkout's runs.db from a lane, because the open is read-write.

Running `target/debug/reify-audit --pattern <token>` against a real reify task worktree/lane fails with exit 125 ("error opening runs-db 'data/orchestrator/runs.db'"), because a lane has no data/orchestrator/. For a tree-only lane (PTODO-free structural lanes such as PLINECITE, PCITE), pass `--no-jcodemunch --project-root "$PWD" --tasks-file <tmp>/tasks.json --runs-db <tmp>/runs.db`. tasks.json contains `[]`. runs.db is a sqlite file with `CREATE TABLE events (task_id TEXT, event_type TEXT)`. This is the same hermetic shape crates/reify-audit/tests/plinecite.rs uses in its CLI test.

Running `reify-audit --pattern

` by hand in a warm-lane worktree fails with exit 125 ("error opening runs-db 'data/orchestrator/runs.db'") because the lane has no orchestrator DB. The hermetic invocation the infra gates use is: a 0-byte file for `--runs-db` (structural patterns never read ctx.conn), a tasks file whose top level is a JSON **array** (`[]`, not `{"tasks": []}` — a map is rejected with "invalid type: map, expected a sequence"), plus `--no-jcodemunch`. i.e. `reify-audit --pattern PDIAG --runs-db "$AUX/runs.db" --tasks-file "$AUX/tasks.json" --no-jcodemunch`.

Running the `reify-audit` binary from a warm-lane / task worktree fails immediately with "error opening runs-db 'data/orchestrator/runs.db'" and exits 0, because the default runs-db path is relative to cwd and that SQLite file only exists in the main checkout (/home/leo/src/reify). Pass `--runs-db /tmp/scratch.db` to exercise a detector against the real tree from a lane. The CLI's exit code is the count of High-severity findings, so a non-zero exit from `reify-audit --pattern X` is the finding count, not a crash.

Running the `reify-audit` binary manually from a task worktree fails before any detector runs: it opens `data/orchestrator/runs.db` unconditionally at startup, and a warm-lane/task worktree has no such file, so `./target/debug/reify-audit --pattern PDOCCOVER` exits 125 with "error opening runs-db 'data/orchestrator/runs.db'". This bites even for purely structural patterns (PTODO, PDSSENTINEL, PDOCCOVER) that read only the working tree and never touch runs.db. Pass `--runs-db /home/leo/src/reify/data/orchestrator/runs.db` (the main checkout's copy) to get a real run. The exit code is then the High-severity finding count, not 0/1.

Since task #7787 the reify-audit G-allow liveness gates (`g_allow_repo_wide_hard_gate_live` in tests/g_allow_repo_wide_hard_gate.rs and `engine_seam_g_allow_owner_cites_resolve_live_real_db` in tests/engine_seam_g_allow_cites_live.rs) are `#[ignore]`d on-demand checks that FAIL LOUD (not skip) when the task DB can't be read. To run one from any lane, use `REIFY_PTODO_TASKS_DB=/home/leo/src/reify/.taskmaster/tasks/tasks.db cargo test -p reify-audit --test g_allow_repo_wide_hard_gate g_allow_repo_wide_hard_gate_live -- --ignored`. The main WAL-mode tasks.db opened read-only fine from a sandboxed lane (2026-10-04). The DB-present scan takes 600–900 s, so background it to a log; to avoid holding the cargo lock, run the prebuilt target/debug/deps/<test>-<hash> binary directly. The CLI equivalent for sweeps is `reify-audit --pattern PTODO --require-tasks-db`, which exits 255 naming the resolved path if the DB can't be opened.

Running the built `reify-audit` binary — directly, or from any warm-lane/task worktree other than the main checkout — needs fixups the task descriptions and PRD text omit, or it fails before any detector runs:
(1) `LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/opt/reify-deps/lib:/opt/reify-deps/manifold/lib:/opt/reify-deps/tbb-pin` (lib + tbb-pin are the confirmed-minimum working set; manifold/lib appeared in one verified-working invocation and is safe to keep). Without it the binary exits 127 on `libopenvdb.so.13.0: cannot open shared object file` — unlike `reify`/`reify-gui`, `reify-audit` has no baked RUNPATH for the prebuilt native deps.
(2) `--runs-db` must be an ABSOLUTE path, e.g. `/home/leo/src/reify/data/orchestrator/runs.db` — its default `data/orchestrator/runs.db` is CWD-relative, and `--project-root` does NOT rebase it, so a sweep launched from any worktree other than the main checkout exits 125 "error opening runs-db" before any detector runs.
(3) `reify-audit` has no `--format` flag — output is plain text only.
(4) `--tasks-file` must be a JSON **array** (`[]` is accepted; a `{"tasks": []}` map form is rejected).

Full working invocation: `LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/opt/reify-deps/tbb-pin:/opt/reify-deps/lib ./target/debug/reify-audit --pattern <PATTERN> --project-root /home/leo/src/reify --runs-db /home/leo/src/reify/data/orchestrator/runs.db`.

(Distinct from the separate `reify-gui` tbb-pin LD_LIBRARY_PATH-ordering hazard under topic `reify-gui-tbb-pin-ld-library-path` (task #7254) — that one is about LD_LIBRARY_PATH being searched before DT_RUNPATH and breaking the GUI binary specifically; this entry is about `reify-audit` needing the var set at all, plus its runs-db/format/tasks-file flag quirks.)

To run reify-audit (e.g. `--pattern PPRDSTATUS`) offline from a reify warm lane, use the prebuilt target/debug/reify-audit with LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/opt/reify-deps/lib:/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu. Without it the binary exits 127 with "libopenvdb.so.13.0: cannot open shared object file". Pass `--no-jcodemunch --project-root . --tasks-file <json array of TaskMetadata> --runs-db <sqlite file with CREATE TABLE events (task_id TEXT, event_type TEXT)>`. A synthetic --tasks-file that sets `prd` on a PRD's leaves lets you check whether the stale-status-header lane would fire. You need it for legacy leaves that carry no metadata.prd, which the live detector cannot see. Fixture shape: crates/reify-audit/tests/pprdstatus_cli.rs.

Driving scripts/reify-audit-predone-wrapper.sh end-to-end in a test: put a fake `curl` (and a fake reify-audit binary) on PATH in a tmpdir rather than standing up a listener on FUSED_MEMORY_MCP_URL — the house idiom in tests/infra/test_reify_audit_predone_wrapper.sh (Check 6, and Check 5f-i..k). The shim reads its response body / exit code from an env var set on the wrapper invocation (FAKE_RC, FAKE_CURL_BODY), which reaches the shim through the wrapper's inherited environment. GOTCHA: every such invocation MUST also set REIFY_AUDIT_ADVISORY_SENTINEL to a path inside the tmpdir. Its default is a host-wide ${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/reify-audit-predone-advisory.$(id -u), and the wrapper's freshness guard stamps it whenever it has something to say — so a test running against a deliberately-stale shim binary otherwise makes a real operator staleness sweep report a stale fleet.

To exercise a `tests/infra/test_reify_audit_*.sh` gate from a task worktree WITHOUT paying for a full release build: run it as `REIFY_AUDIT_BIN="$PWD/target/debug/reify-audit" REIFY_AUDIT_NO_COLD_BUILD=1 bash tests/infra/test_reify_audit_<pattern>.sh`. The scripts default `REIFY_AUDIT_BIN` to `$REPO_ROOT/target/release/reify-audit` and source `scripts/reify-audit-freshness.sh`, whose `reify_audit_guard ... rebuild-budget-safe` would otherwise fork a `cargo build --release`. `REIFY_AUDIT_NO_COLD_BUILD=1` makes the guard return 75, which the scripts map to `RATCHET_SKIP=1` (not exit 0), so the hermetic hard-gate scenarios still run against whatever binary the env var points at. A warm lane's seeded `target/release/reify-audit` is the BASE build and does not know a branch's new `--pattern` token — check with `./target/release/reify-audit --help | grep -i <pattern>` before trusting it.

To observe reify's tasks.db-dependent audit gates (e.g. crates/reify-audit/tests/g_allow_repo_wide_hard_gate.rs::g_allow_repo_wide_hard_gate_live) from a task worktree, which has no local .taskmaster/tasks/tasks.db and therefore graceful-skips them, run: REIFY_PTODO_TASKS_DB=/home/leo/src/reify/.taskmaster/tasks/tasks.db env cargo test -p reify-audit --test g_allow_repo_wide_hard_gate. The `env cargo` prefix is required to bypass the skim output-condensation wrapper that would otherwise hide the assertion text, and the DB open is SQLITE_OPEN_READ_ONLY so this is the detector's own documented production path rather than a write-side reach-around of fused-memory. Note the sibling hermetic test deliberately SKIPS while that env var is set. Measured 2026-09-22: ~10 min 39 s cold build plus 605 s for the live test itself.

`reify-audit` cannot be run as-documented from a warm lane / task worktree: it defaults to `--runs-db data/orchestrator/runs.db` and `--project-root .`, but a lane is seeded tracked-files-only, so neither `data/orchestrator/runs.db` nor `.taskmaster/tasks/tasks.db` exists there (both live in the main checkout `/home/leo/src/reify`). Bare `reify-audit --pattern PTODO` exits 125 with "error opening runs-db ... unable to open database file". Forcing `--runs-db /home/leo/src/reify/data/orchestrator/runs.db` makes it run but DEGRADED — it prints "tasks.db unreachable at './.taskmaster/tasks/tasks.db' — PTODO liveness (β), inverse (ζ), and G-allow advisory lanes degraded; structural checks still run" and then reports `#[allow(dead_code)] // <prose>` lines as untracked/malformed-cite findings (13 of them on 2026-08-26, RC=10) that are pre-existing on main and are NOT real gate failures. Treat any run carrying that "advisory lanes degraded" banner as non-authoritative for untracked/malformed-cite verdicts. To check whether YOUR branch introduced a PTODO marker, compare marker counts directly instead: `git show main:<file> | grep -cE '#\[allow\(dead_code\)\] *//'` vs the worktree copy, and scan `git diff main...HEAD -U0` added lines for TODO/FIXME/HACK/todo!()/#[ignore]. Note ptodo.rs deliberately SKIPS `///` and `//!` doc-comment prose mentioning `#[ignore = "..."]`, and `#[ignore` scanning is `.rs`-only, so rustdoc history notes and `.md` paragraphs quoting an old ignore reason are never findings. The real PTODO gate runs at merge time via the tests/infra verify step regardless.

Running the PTODO oracles from a task WORKTREE (not the main checkout) needs three env/flag fixups that the PRD's documented commands omit, because a lane is seeded tracked-files-only: (1) `reify-audit` exits 125 with "error opening runs-db 'data/orchestrator/runs.db'" — pass `--runs-db /home/leo/src/reify/data/orchestrator/runs.db`, plus `--no-jcodemunch` when offline; (2) `.taskmaster/` is untracked so the beta liveness lane silently degrades to structural-only — export `REIFY_PTODO_TASKS_DB=/home/leo/src/reify/.taskmaster/tasks/tasks.db` for both `reify-audit` and `ptodo-baseline-gen`; (3) the debug test binary `target/debug/deps/ptodo_baseline-*` fails at exec with "error while loading shared libraries: libopenvdb.so.13.0" unless `LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/opt/reify-deps/lib` is set. Note `cargo test -p reify-audit --test ptodo_baseline -- --ignored` is killed at 300s by the skim wrapper's internal timeout (logs "error: command timed out after 300s", exit 1) — that is a timeout, not a test failure; the debug build of `live_findings_are_within_baseline` walks the whole tree and runs multiple minutes, whereas the release `ptodo-baseline-gen` does the same scan in seconds. `tests/infra/test_reify_audit_ptodo.sh` scenario (a) is the identical `comm -23 <live> <baseline>` subset oracle run on the real tree with the release binary, so it is the cheap substitute.

Running `reify-audit --pattern PDOCCOVER --project-root .` bare in a reify lane exits 125 with "error opening runs-db 'data/orchestrator/runs.db'". Use the same flags as tests/infra/test_reify_audit_pdoccover.sh: `--runs-db <0-byte file> --tasks-file <file containing []> --no-jcodemunch` (PDOCCOVER never reads the runs DB). To see the full live debt without touching the ledger, run `pdoccover-baseline-gen --project-root . --admit-new` and omit --write: it prints to stdout. At 54a0411bc9 that render was byte-identical to crates/reify-audit/pdoccover-baseline.txt (38 omission + 4 fabrication rows), so diffing it before and after a change is a cheap "PDOCCOVER output unchanged" check.

To isolate one PTODO lane's real-tree population in reify, run reify-audit twice under a synthetic all-terminal tasks.db and diff the outputs. Build the DB with `LD_LIBRARY_PATH="" sqlite3` using the tests' `tasks` schema plus a recursive CTE that inserts ids 1..99999 as ('master', i, 'done'). Run the branch binary and the merge-base binary over the same tree with REIFY_PTODO_TASKS_DB=<db> --pattern PTODO --no-jcodemunch --tasks-file <[]> --runs-db <empty>; every Cited line then reports `orphaned`. In a sandboxed warm lane, `git worktree add` for the base FAILS (EACCES on <main>/.git/worktrees). (3) The CLI requires a readable --runs-db sqlite at startup even for `--pattern PTODO` (which never reads ctx.conn) — in a task worktree data/orchestrator/runs.db is absent → exit 125; pass `--runs-db <path>` pointing at any sqlite, and a touch-created 0-byte file is accepted (sqlite treats it as an empty DB). reify warm-lane gotcha: crates/reify-test-support/src/orphan_audit.rs::resolve_script_and_root bakes env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR") into the reify-test-support rlib. seed-warm-lane.sh's env!()-relink (task 4983) touches only tests/ and benches/ sources, so in a CoW-seeded lane every run_orphan_audit G-allow pin test (reify-audit *_g_allow.rs, reify-mesh-morph *_g_allow.rs) audits whatever tree _merge-verify currently holds, not the lane's own. The result is a false RED (or GREEN) that depends on _merge-verify's checkout, e.g. 'expected exactly 1 entry in allowed[]; 0 entries' with the dump naming a file path the lane no longer has. Diagnose: `strings target/debug/deps/libreify_test_support-*.rlib | grep warm-lanes`. In-lane remedy: `touch crates/reify-test-support/src/orphan_audit.rs` (forces a rebuild that bakes the lane's path). Measured task 7491, _lane-12, esc-7491-13.

Verifying reify-audit PTODO findings in a warm lane requires a DB-PRESENT sweep, which the infra test does NOT give you. `tests/infra/test_reify_audit_ptodo.sh` scenario (a) runs `env -u REIFY_PTODO_TASKS_DB ptodo-baseline-gen --project-root "$REPO_ROOT"`, and warm lanes have no `.taskmaster/` (seeded tracked-files-only), so that sweep runs DB-ABSENT: the liveness lane is skipped entirely and the ratchet only proves `live ⊆ baseline` — it cannot confirm an `orphaned`/`unknown-id` finding is actually produced. To verify a liveness finding, snapshot the real DB (`cp /home/leo/src/reify/.taskmaster/tasks/tasks.db{,-wal,-shm} /tmp/snap/`, read-only, avoids racing fused-memory) and run `REIFY_PTODO_TASKS_DB=/tmp/snap/tasks.db ./target/release/ptodo-baseline-gen --project-root "$PWD"`, then diff against `crates/reify-audit/ptodo-baseline.txt` in BOTH directions (`diff <(sort live) <(sort baseline)`) — never the one-way `comm -23` subset oracle, which is blind to a LOST finding. Baseline fingerprints are `path :: kind :: text` and so are line-number independent; a finding's cited line number drifts as the file grows while its fingerprint does not.

To make tests/infra/test_reify_audit_ptodo.sh's precision-sensitive ratchet (scenarios a/b) run DETERMINISTICALLY from a meta-test, copy target/release/reify-audit to a temp path and leave its mtime at NOW, then pass it as REIFY_AUDIT_BIN. reify_audit_is_stale compares mtime against `git log -1 --format=%ct -- crates/reify-audit`, so a now-mtime copy is judged FRESH, the guard returns rc 0, and RATCHET_SKIP stays 0 regardless of ambient warm-lane binary staleness. This is the inverse of test_reify_audit_ptodo_orphan_hardgate.sh's `touch -t 200001010000` trick, which forces STALE to test the opposite partition. Without the inversion a ratchet meta-test passes vacuously in any lane where REIFY_AUDIT_NO_COLD_BUILD=1 (which run_all.sh/verify.sh export) meets a stale binary.

The dashboard (dashboard/src/dashboard/static/redux/*.jsx) has NO JS/DOM test runner (React+babel are CDN-only, no build step). The established way to unit-test JSX logic is to extract a PURE-JS predicate/helper into scheduler_utils.jsx (exported via window.DF_SCHED_UTILS) and execute it in a node-vm sandbox via `_eval_sched_utils_fn` in dashboard/tests/test_chip_label_disambiguation.py. Dashboard classic-script collision — the sub-case the existing memories DON'T name, hit three times in one task (5588). The known gotcha is framed as "two modules both declare a bare `const API`, so give each a module-unique `<MODULE>_API`". That framing is too narrow. The hazard is ANY top-level lexical binding, and it bites hardest in a shape the API-const rule does not cover:

  a classic script that CONSUMES another classic script's exports by name.

`const { formatAge } = window.DF_ENDPOINT_STALENESS;` at the top of a new classic script dies with "SyntaxError: Identifier 'formatAge' has already been declared", because endpoint_staleness.js declares `function formatAge` at top level and a global `function` declaration is var-scoped — a later global-lexical `const` of the same name is a redeclaration. The consumer then never reaches its own trailing `window.DF_X = ...`, so EVERY downstream destructure of DF_X sees undefined and the whole dashboard blanks.

This did not arise before because, until task 5588, no classic script destructured another's functions at module scope: data.js reads `window.DF_ENDPOINT_STALENESS.STALE_FAILURE_THRESHOLD` lazily through a property access inside a function, which is collision-free. Task 5588 added datum.js (consuming endpoint_staleness.js), data.js consuming datum.js, and task_row_cells.js consuming datum.js — three instances, all of which would have shipped dead.

THE FIX, and why it is not "just use a property access". Rename in the destructure: `const { formatAge: formatAgeMs } = window.DF_ENDPOINT_STALENESS;`. That keeps the two properties the convention actually wants — it is still a DESTRUCTURE, so an absent global throws loudly AT LOAD (the DF_SPARK_PATH "no `|| {}` fallback" rule) — while the binding name is module-unique. `const X = window.DF_OTHER;` followed by `X.foo()` is also collision-free but SILENTLY binds undefined when the global is missing, deferring the failure into a render, which is the silent degradation the convention exists to prevent.

DETECTION. dashboard/tests/js/classic_script_scope.test.mjs is the ONLY thing that catches this — it loads every classic script into one shared node:vm context in index.html document order. The per-module `node --test` suites are structurally blind (each require()s its module in isolation, where no shared scope exists), and so is `uv run pytest tests/` unless you notice that wrapper failing. Run it the moment you add a module-scope `const {` to any `/static/redux/*.js`. In 5588 it caught all three, with a message naming the offending file and identifier.

NOT a hazard in the `type="text/babel"` .jsx files — Babel transpiles those bindings before evaluation, which is why tabs.jsx and tab_tasks.jsx can both declare `const { rtCell, rtAge } = window.DF_RUNTIME_FMT` alongside runtime_format.js's `function rtCell`.

content: Console capture in data.js node suites (task 5834 amendment, 2026-10-14): dashboard/tests/js/_data_loader.mjs exports the one console.warn redirect every data.js suite uses. `await warningsFrom(fn)` resolves to the warn calls fn made, each as its argument list, for a test that asserts on the warning. `await quietly(fn)` resolves to fn's own result with the expected warning dropped. Both await fn, so they cover an async refreshOne/requestOnDemand and a sync applyKey alike. Use them; do not hand-roll a save/redirect/restore of console.warn in a data_*.test.mjs suite.

Description: Filed from escalation esc-6232-5. Leo's explicit instruction, 2026-08-19: "Make sure that once the detector is live, the things that are detected deterministically get some attention. Something like detection itself raises to L2, and/or have a capstone task deterministically escalate to L2 to tell me to run a session to resolve the things that have been found by the detector."

This is the RECURRING-ATTENTION half. The one-shot wiring (a non-empty PPRDSTATUS finding set raising to L2) is a hard done-criterion of the detector task itself, deliberately NOT split out, because splitting it is precisely how PDOCCOVER ended up with a landed detector (#5478, done) and a gate that is still pending (#5480) — a detector finding things and gating nothing. This task is the different, additional mechanism: a periodic sweep whose output is a booked human sitting, so findings do not merely accumulate in a log.

WHY A SITTING RATHER THAN AUTO-FILED TASKS. Leo's ruling (2026-08-19): adjudicating doc-drift findings is workflow-shaped, not task-shaped. Each finding needs a per-doc judgement that an autonomous agent should not make unsupervised — genuinely-still-active PRD vs completed plan needing a SHIPPED header vs capability manifest that must not be touched vs dated snapshot that must NOT be retroactively edited (the #6232 principle: "retroactively editing a historical snapshot destroys its value as a record"). An agent mass-stamping SHIPPED across live PRDs would be a worse outcome than the drift it fixes. Note also that the orchestrator contributes nothing here: scripts/verify.sh:1161 routes *.md to `: # no heavy checks`, so a docs-only task produces an empty plan and exits 0 — there is no gate for a docs task to pass.

SCOPE TO DECIDE FIRST (this is part of the deliverable, argue it explicitly):
  1. Cadence. Doc drift accrues on the timescale of leaves landing, not commits. Weekly or fortnightly is likely right; daily will produce an ignored alert. Justify the choice.
  2. Trigger shape. Options: (a) pure timer; (b) event-driven — sweep when a PRD's last non-terminal leaf goes terminal, which is the exact moment a PRD becomes freezable and is cheap to detect from the reconciliation path; (c) both. (b) is the more precise instrument and is worth costing before defaulting to (a).
  3. Silence discipline. The sweep must NOT escalate when the finding set is empty, and must not re-escalate the same unchanged finding set every period — otherwise it trains the L2 queue to ignore it. Some fingerprint/dedupe over the finding set is required (the escalation MCP already supports dedupe_fingerprint).
  4. What the escalation says. It should carry the finding COUNT and the doc list, and name the sitting to run, so the L2 consumer can triage without re-deriving anything.

Two structural facts that make whole CLASSES of work impossible in the reify repo, useful for fast cross-repo scope adjudication (verified 2026-07-27): (1) reify has ZERO systemd/timer install surface — no timer/systemd/cron script anywhere under scripts/. dark-factory owns systemd (systemd_inspect.py, service_restart.py, deploy_state.py) and has precedent installing a timer FOR reify from the DF side (DF task 2585, scripts/legibility/install-trickle-timer.sh reify). (2) reify's ONLY fused-memory client, crates/reify-audit/src/fused_memory_client.rs, exposes get_task/get_tasks ONLY — it is READ-ONLY. There is no reify-side set_task_status write path at all. So any asked work that (a) schedules something recurring or (b) performs a task-state write is structurally dark-factory-side, and can be adjudicated as such in seconds without reading the task's plan. This is the mechanical basis behind CLAUDE.md's "reify ships the primitive, dark-factory wires the invocation".

Two reify-audit facts that PRD prose gets wrong (both measured 2026-08-31). (1) `--format markdown` is NOT a reify-audit binary flag. `parse_args` accepts only --task, --pre-done, --since, --pattern, --tasks-file, --fused-memory-url, --runs-db, --project-root, the --jcodemunch family, --no-jcodemunch, --help, --version, and hard-rejects anything else as "unknown flag". `--format markdown` is an argument of the /audit SKILL, which renders the report itself. The binary emits a JSON Finding array on stderr and a human summary on stdout. (2) PTODO's task-liveness lane does NOT use `crates/reify-audit/src/fused_memory_client.rs`, despite PRDs citing it. It opens the task store directly READ-ONLY via rusqlite — `tasks_db_path` (honoring a REIFY_PTODO_TASKS_DB env override) and `open_tasks_db` with SQLITE_OPEN_READ_ONLY — and queries status+metadata for one id under the master tag. Both mechanisms exist in the crate; a new detector copying "the same mechanism PTODO uses" must copy the rusqlite one, reusing `is_terminal_status` (done or cancelled are terminal; every other present status is live) and its fail-soft contract (missing store degrades the lane with one stderr breadcrumb, exit class untouched, never exit 125).

To run reify-audit (e.g. `--pattern PPRDSTATUS`) offline from a reify warm lane, use the prebuilt target/debug/reify-audit with LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/opt/reify-deps/lib:/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu. Without it the binary exits 127 with "libopenvdb.so.13.0: cannot open shared object file". Pass `--no-jcodemunch --project-root . --tasks-file <json array of TaskMetadata> --runs-db <sqlite file with CREATE TABLE events (task_id TEXT, event_type TEXT)>`. A synthetic --tasks-file that sets `prd` on a PRD's leaves lets you check whether the stale-status-header lane would fire. You need it for legacy leaves that carry no metadata.prd, which the live detector cannot see. Fixture shape: crates/reify-audit/tests/pprdstatus_cli.rs.

Requiring a closer (`)`, `,`, backtick) after the asserted status word would silence 4 true positives (#6663, #6759, #4269, #3114), so asserted_status deliberately accepts prose after the word; pinned by tests/pprdstatus.rs `status_word_followed_by_prose_still_asserts_the_status`.

DISCOVERY (reify, 2026-07-26): the reify orchestrator's own log is the ONLY place many dispatch failures are diagnosable, and two things conspire to hide it.

1. `orchestrator-reify.service` IS a systemd **`--user`** unit (cgroup: `user.slice/user-1000.slice/user@1000.service/app.slice/orchestrator-reify.service`). Running `systemctl status orchestrator-reify.service` WITHOUT `--user` queries the system manager and reports "Unit ... could not be found" — a false negative that reads exactly like "this isn't a systemd service, it's a bare `uv run` process". A prior reify memory asserted precisely that and was WRONG; it was corrected this session. Every project has one: orchestrator-{reify,dark-factory,know-live,pump-web-ui,my-solar-challenge,solar-challenge-platform,autopilot-video}.service.

2. `runs.db` cannot answer "why did this requeue". The `task_completed` event payload is counters-only (`outcome`, `agent_invocations`, `execute_iterations`, `verify_attempts`, `review_cycles`, `steward_cost_usd`, `steward_invocations`) and the `task_results` table has no `block_reason` column either. The reason IS computed and lives on `TerminalReport.reason` -> `TaskReport.block_reason`, but is dropped at BOTH persistence layers. `SELECT DISTINCT json_extract(data,'$.reason'), '$.requeue_reason', '$.error'` returns all-NULL. Filed as reify task 5569.

Correct commands:

395d6a09-665a-419c-b255-40f64e3e0d37.content: Regenerating crates/reify-audit/ptodo-baseline.txt is asymmetrically expensive by DB mode. `ptodo-baseline-gen --project-root <root>` under `env -u REIFY_PTODO_TASKS_DB` (degraded/structural-only, the mode the ratchet gate runs in) finishes in seconds; the same binary with REIFY_PTODO_TASKS_DB pointed at a real tasks.db exceeded 5 minutes without completing, because the ζ inverse lane walks git history per finding (51 task-cites-deleted-path findings on main as of 2026-08). Budget a long foreground timeout or background+poll for a correct (DB-present, superset) regen — and note that a task worktree has no .taskmaster/, so a correct regen is not available there at all: regenerating in a lane silently drops the DB-dependent `orphaned` fingerprints, yielding a baseline that then fails the `comm -23` subset check wherever the DB IS present.

4ec04e82-a134-46ab-91dc-30f6bc960b8f.content: Reify PTODO baseline seeding: regenerate `crates/reify-audit/ptodo-baseline.txt` WITH the task DB set (`REIFY_PTODO_TASKS_DB=/home/leo/src/reify/.taskmaster/tasks/tasks.db target/release/ptodo-baseline-gen --project-root . > ...`), never in degraded mode. A cited line yields an `orphaned` fingerprint only when the DB is reachable, so degraded_live is a strict subset of db_present_live; `tests/infra/test_reify_audit_ptodo.sh` scenario (a) runs the generator under `env -u REIFY_PTODO_TASKS_DB` (task worktrees have no `.taskmaster/`) while `/audit` runs in the main checkout WITH the DB. Seeding from a DB-present run makes the baseline a superset of both so `comm -23 live baseline` stays empty in either context; seeding from a degraded run leaves the main-checkout ratchet red.

6740109b-d486-46c2-bf29-e1123af3d9d1.content: crates/reify-audit/ptodo-baseline.txt fingerprints are line-number-erased and deduped (format "{path} :: {kind} :: {text}", separator is space-colon-colon-space), so ONE baseline entry can stand for MANY source lines — the 5 entries seeded by task #6087 cover 14 lines, and the T12 layer-B seam entry alone covers 8 identical lines that must ALL be fixed or the entry survives. The section 6.6 ratchet is a SUBSET oracle (comm -23 live baseline), so shrinking SOURCE keeps it green while shrinking the BASELINE first turns it red: always land source fixes BEFORE regenerating the baseline. Regenerate only via target/release/ptodo-baseline-gen with REIFY_PTODO_TASKS_DB pointed at the real tasks.db (a DB-present run is a strict superset of the degraded run the ratchet performs); never hand-edit or sed it. An empty 0-byte baseline is the valid PRD section 6.4 zero-residual-debt end state, pinned by tests/ptodo_baseline.rs validate_accepts_empty_baseline, but the file must stay tracked and present because baseline_is_well_formed asserts path.exists().

98924967-4569-401b-82c7-418c045a037c.content: PRD probe verification trap (reify): scripts/prd-capability-check.py (and the prd-decompose-verify.mjs/.py workflow that wraps it) resolves the probe binary via REIFY_BIN → target/release/reify → target/debug/reify → PATH, but does NOT build it — a stale binary (release OR debug) silently wins over a fresh build. Compounding: the stdlib is include_str!-embedded (stdlib_loader.rs), so a binary predating a stdlib migration merge probes OLD language semantics even against a current .ri corpus. Worked case 2026-07-20 (struct-ctor-conformance decompose): probe matrix rows verified against an hours-stale binary missed that task 4370's merge had flipped PressureLoad.face to Option<FaceSelector> — re-probing with a fresh binary found one row already fixed and one still a live hole; PRD baselines were amended (commit 1ab6d71c2b) rather than freezing a false baseline into RED fixtures. SOP before any /prd probe run: `cargo build -p reify-cli --bin reify` at HEAD, remove (or REIFY_BIN-override) any stale target/release/reify, and re-run probes live if any crates/ or embedded-stdlib merge landed since the last verification. Probe-harness mechanics: grammar probes run with CWD=tree-sitter-reify/; check probes are `reify check <fixture>`; the match predicate is stream-specific (stderr_contains/stdout_contains) — reify diagnostics go to STDERR. Note: the Workflow tool resolves scriptPath relative to the shell CWD — pass an ABSOLUTE path (CWD drifts after a `cd` in a Bash call).

c0a5bda3-712e-4373-91ee-83fa4aca402c.content:
Running the built `reify-audit` binary — directly, or from any warm-lane/task worktree other than the main checkout — needs fixups the task descriptions and PRD text omit, or it fails before any detector runs:
(1) `LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/opt/reify-deps/lib:/opt/reify-deps/manifold/lib:/opt/reify-deps/tbb-pin` (lib + tbb-pin are the confirmed-minimum working set; manifold/lib appeared in one verified-working invocation and is safe to keep). Without it the binary exits 127 on `libopenvdb.so.13.0: cannot open shared object file` — unlike `reify`/`reify-gui`, `reify-audit` has no baked RUNPATH for the prebuilt native deps.
(2) `--runs-db` must be an ABSOLUTE path, e.g. `/home/leo/src/reify/data/orchestrator/runs.db` — its default `data/orchestrator/runs.db` is CWD-relative, and `--project-root` does NOT rebase it, so a sweep launched from any worktree other than the main checkout exits 125 "error opening runs-db" before any detector runs.
(3) `reify-audit` has no `--format` flag — output is plain text only.
(4) `--tasks-file` must be a JSON **array** (`[]` is accepted; a `{"tasks": []}` map form is rejected).

Full working invocation: `LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/opt/reify-deps/tbb-pin:/opt/reify-deps/lib ./target/debug/reify-audit --pattern <PATTERN> --project-root /home/leo/src/reify --runs-db /home/leo/src/reify/data/orchestrator/runs.db`.

(Distinct from the separate `reify-gui` tbb-pin LD_LIBRARY_PATH-ordering hazard under topic `reify-gui-tbb-pin-ld-library-path` (task #7254) — that one is about LD_LIBRARY_PATH being searched before DT_RUNPATH and breaking the GUI binary specifically; this entry is about `reify-audit` needing the var set at all, plus its runs-db/format/tasks-file flag quirks.)

d0dcf25a-0d12-4ae6-9355-cadd8e82de49.content: PTODO ratchet gotcha: `target/release/ptodo-baseline-gen` run WITHOUT `REIFY_PTODO_TASKS_DB` degrades its liveness lane to structural-only, so it emits a strict SUBSET of the real fingerprint set — `orphaned` / `unknown-id` kinds are simply not classified and silently vanish from the output. Never regenerate `crates/reify-audit/ptodo-baseline.txt` wholesale from a DB-less run: that drops live orphaned grandfather entries and hands future findings free immunity. For a targeted burndown, delete only the one line you resolved, and only if its kind is structural (`untracked` / `malformed-cite` / `bare-ignore` / `phantom-tracking`), whose absence from a DB-less live set IS conclusive. Point it at the real DB with `REIFY_PTODO_TASKS_DB=/home/leo/src/reify/.taskmaster/tasks/tasks.db` when you need the liveness lane.

Gotcha, observed 2026-10-01 by task 121's architect: fused-memory's completion-claim gate checks every task number in a memory against the writing project's own task tree. So a solar_challenge memory that names a dark-factory task together with a status word cannot be verified. The write is stored, but it is tagged unverified_claim, and an info L0 escalation is filed on solar_challenge's own escalation queue (port 8106) under a made-up task id, unverified-claim-<number>. That escalation is noise, and the orphan reaper can push it up the ladder. To avoid it, refer to a dark-factory task by its title or role without a status word, or record the fact under project_id dark_factory.

Convention for cross-project task dependencies in fused-memory (validated 2026-06-20): to gate a task in project B on tasks in project A, file the task in B (project_root = B's root) and call add_dependency(id=<B_task>, depends_on="<A_project_id>:<A_task_id>", project_root=<B_root>). The qualified form (containing ':') is routed to the dependent task's metadata.external_deps list rather than the integer `dependencies` table; the foreign target is NOT verified at write time. At dispatch the dependent's scheduler resolves each via get_external_statuses and gates until every external dep is `done` (a cancelled upstream escalates immediately; an unresolvable one escalates after a grace period). Worked example: solar_challenge_platform:1 depends_on my_solar_challenge:80/81/82 — landed correctly as metadata.external_deps with the integer dependencies table left empty.

aiomqtt 2.5.1 / paho-mqtt 2.1.0 ack-and-queue facts, verified 2026-09-23 by task 252's architect, for re-planning task 252 (ack-after-persist) once task 240 lands.
(1) aiomqtt's incoming queue, Client._queue, is created once in Client.__init__. __aenter__/__aexit__ never clear it. So messages that are already PUBACKed but not yet consumed survive a disconnect inside the same Client and are consumed after a reconnect; they are lost only at process exit.
(2) MEASURED on CPython 3.11.15, default loop, scratch script: after a clean disconnect (_disconnected done), MessagesIterator.__anext__ still returns queued messages in FIFO order, exactly len(client.messages) of them, then raises MqttError('Disconnected during message iteration') once the queue is empty. So a drain after DISCONNECT through the public iterator, bounded by the public len(), works.
Hypothesis: this relies on asyncio callback ordering (the queue.get() task's first step runs before the done-callback of the already-done _disconnected future), not on any documented aiomqtt contract.
(3) paho 2.1.0: Client.manual_ack_set(True) makes the QoS-1 PUBACK and the QoS-2 PUBCOMP manual. Client.ack(mid, qos) sends them, and is a no-op for qos 0 or when manual_ack is off. aiomqtt's Message carries .mid and .qos. aiomqtt never passes manual_ack, so the only way to enable it is the private client._client.
(4) aiomqtt registers socket writes via loop.call_soon_threadsafe(loop.add_writer, ...).
(5) Broker window: validation/mosquitto.conf pins max_inflight_messages 1000 and max_queued_messages 0, and docs/examples/README.md marks both REQUIRED.

VERIFIED (task 240 architect, 2026-09-23, aiomqtt 2.5.1 + paho-mqtt 2.1.0): an incoming QoS-1 message is PUBACKed to the broker the moment it enters aiomqtt's internal asyncio queue — before the ingest Subscriber decodes, buffers or persists it. paho's Client._handle_publish calls _handle_on_message(message) then _send_puback(mid) unless manual_ack is set, aiomqtt's _on_message only does self._queue.put_nowait(m), and aiomqtt 2.5.1 never enables manual_ack. Consequence: rows sitting in aiomqtt's queue or in the StoreForwardBuffer are NOT redelivered after a restart despite clean_session=False; the persistent session only preserves messages the broker has not yet delivered. The only chance to persist already-received rows is an in-process flush before exit.

aiomqtt 2.5.1 / paho-mqtt 2.1.0 receive-side gotchas, MEASURED against a real embedded amqtt broker (task 252, 2026-09-23 and re-checked 2026-09-25):
(1) paho PUBACKs each QoS-1 message as soon as aiomqtt enqueues it, and aiomqtt exposes no manual ack.
(2) If MessagesIterator.__anext__ is cancelled, it drops a message its inner queue.get task had already dequeued. That message is lost for good, so never cancel a receive: keep it as a task and asyncio.wait on it with a timeout.
(3) Client._queue survives __aexit__. After a clean disconnect, a receive left pending resolves with its message, or else with MqttError('Disconnected during message iteration'). Exactly len(client.messages) queued messages are then still returned in FIFO order, and a receive on an empty, closed queue raises MqttError.

paho-mqtt 2.1.0 gotcha, verified in the installed source by task 1008's architect on 2026-10-13. A persistent-session client keeps per-object session state that a fresh client lacks. An inbound QoS-2 message is held in `_in_messages` after PUBREC and delivered only on PUBREL. `_messages_reconnect_reset_in` keeps that state across reconnects of the SAME client when clean_session is False. A fresh client receiving the broker's PUBREL for an unknown mid sends PUBCOMP without delivering, so the message is lost. QoS 1 is delivered and PUBACKed at once, so it carries no such state. Consequence for solar_challenge_platform: building a fresh aiomqtt.Client on every scp-ingest reconnect would lose a QoS-2 message (Settings accepts ingestion_subscribe_qos=2) whenever its handshake straddles the drop. It would also strand messages already in the old client's local queue, which paho acknowledged on receipt.

MEASURED by task 865's architect on 2026-10-13 (aiomqtt 2.5.1, paho 2.1.0, CPython 3.11.15), probing a persistent session (clean_session=False) that resumes a 20-message QoS-1 backlog, against both the embedded amqtt 0.11.3 broker (durable_sessions=True) and eclipse-mosquitto:2.0.22 in docker. (1) Cancelling Client.__aenter__ mid-connect leaves the connection reading: len(client.messages) went from 0-2 right after the cancel to 20 one second later, all PUBACKed, and none were redelivered on the next resume. (2) Letting __aenter__ finish and then calling __aexit__ stopped acknowledgement at once: the queue stayed flat after the close. On mosquitto, the messages still in flight at the close were redelivered on the next resume (19 redelivered, 5 duplicates, 0 missing). On amqtt 0.11.3 they were LOST (17 missing), because amqtt's handler._handle_qos1_message_flow pops an outgoing in-flight QoS-1 message from session.inflight_out in its finally clause when the disconnect cancels the PUBACK waiter. So an mqtt-lane amqtt test can pin aiomqtt's own acknowledge-or-not behaviour, but never in-flight redelivery.

aiomqtt 2.5.1 gotcha, read in client.py by task 865's architect on 2026-10-07: Client.__aenter__ catches only OSError/WebsocketConnectionError around the executor connect and MqttError around the CONNACK wait (_wait_for(self._connected)). A CancelledError landing in either releases nothing: the reentrancy _lock stays held (a later `async with client` raises MqttReentrantError) and _disconnected is not reset. A cancel during the CONNACK wait also cancels _connected (asyncio.wait_for cancels its inner future), so _on_connect ignores the CONNACK that arrives later, yet paho keeps PUBACKing incoming QoS-1 PUBLISHes into Client._queue. A cancel during the executor connect leaves the connect thread running, and _connected then completes normally on CONNACK.

solar_challenge_platform gotcha (task 866 architect, measured 2026-10-13 on aiomqtt 2.5.1 / paho-mqtt 2.1.0). aiomqtt Client.__aexit__ waits up to Client.timeout (10 s default) for paho to WRITE the queued DISCONNECT; MQTT 3.1.1 has no DISCONNACK. Ingestion ACK semantics (traced in review 20260928T062907, HEAD 3d74313):
- aiomqtt/paho ACK every QoS-1 message when it arrives, because manual_ack is never set.
- clean_session=False therefore protects only messages the broker has not delivered yet.
- Rows in the in-memory StoreForwardBuffer (up to 2M) are already ACKed, so a restart during a DB outage loses them. The only record is the ERROR "N rows unconfirmed" at subscriber.py:392-396.
- Since task 270, a write still running at shutdown is abandoned on a daemon thread.
This is escalated as a design question (manual ACK after the write, a disk spill, or an accepted carve-out). Do not assume the persistent session makes ingestion restart-lossless.

amqtt 0.11.3 uses a strict dacite-typed BrokerConfig: legacy hbmqtt/amqtt config keys like `max-connections` are REJECTED (UnexpectedDataError). A working embedded-broker config is {listeners:{default:{type:"tcp", bind:"127.0.0.1:{port}"}}, sys_interval:0, auth:{allow-anonymous:true}, topic_check:{enabled:false}} — auth/topic_check still work but emit DeprecationWarnings (the modern form is the `plugins` section). amqtt.broker.Broker.start()/shutdown() are async. The solar-challenge-platform repo has NO pytest-asyncio (and pyproject/uv.lock are α/task-31-owned + locked), so MQTT/async tests must run via asyncio.run() inside a sync `def test_*` (mirroring the control suite's threaded async server). aiomqtt 2.5 ships py.typed (mypy --strict clean); amqtt does not but is test-only. Bind 127.0.0.1:0 to grab a free ephemeral port to avoid collisions. Validated end-to-end (SimHome.step → wire.encode → aiomqtt publish → subscribe → wire.decode of all 8 metrics).

aiomqtt 2.x (repo pins aiomqtt==2.5.1): the MQTT client-id constructor kwarg is named `identifier` (NOT `client_id`, which was the paho/aiomqtt-1.x name); the persistent-session flag is `clean_session: bool`. aiomqtt.Client defaults protocol=None -> paho MQTTv3.1.1, so `clean_session=False` IS honored (clean_start is MQTT5-only and ignored under v3.1.1). Gotcha: aiomqtt.Client.__init__ calls asyncio.get_running_loop(), so a Client can only be constructed INSIDE a running event loop (build it in an async path or wrap in asyncio.run() for scripts/tests) — a bare module-level construction raises RuntimeError: no running event loop.

Subscriber._run_reconnecting at main b542c44 caught that MqttError as a broker drop, so a stop whose disconnect timed out turned into an endless reconnect loop. A drain then reading the client queue must never read past len(client.messages): once _disconnected is cancelled, a read on an empty queue raises CancelledError, not MqttError.

In solar_challenge_platform ingestion, a persistent MQTT session (aiomqtt clean_session=False + stable identifier) only resumes an offline backlog if the SUBSCRIBE is at QoS 1. aiomqtt's client.subscribe(topic) defaults to qos=0, and per MQTT 3.1.1 a broker discards (never queues) QoS-0 messages for an offline persistent session. So Subscriber.run() must call client.subscribe(topic_filter, qos=1). Gotcha: changing that call breaks 6 duck-typed FakeClient.subscribe(self, topic_filter) test doubles that are injected into Subscriber.run() (tests/ingestion/test_persistent_session.py, test_ingest_reconnect.py x4, test_ingestion.py) — they TypeError on the qos kwarg. The fake at tests/runtime/test_ingest_entrypoint.py uses `async def subscribe(self, topic_filter, **kwargs)` and is the template to copy.

candidates.content: Ingest F2 backlog-resume THROUGHPUT throttle (task 157): the resume drain is slow (~66 msg/s vs ~634 online) purely because validation/mosquitto.conf omits max_inflight_messages, so the harness broker uses mosquitto's default 20 (broker holds ≤20 unacked QoS-1 msgs in flight to a resuming subscriber). It is NOT a 'batch-write-before-ack' coupling: ingestion/subscriber.py uses aiomqtt's DEFAULT auto-ack (no manual_ack, no client.ack), so PUBACKs fire per-message on receipt, independent of the buffer's N-or-T batch flush. paho's client-side max_inflight governs OUTBOUND publishes only, not subscriber inbound delivery — so the fix is broker-config-side (raise max_inflight_messages in mosquitto.conf + docs/examples/README.md), and subscriber.py/buffer.py need no change. Zero-loss/dupes was never the issue.

GOTCHA (aiomqtt 2.5.1, read from the installed package): MessagesIterator.__anext__ receives through a separate queue.get task, and on CancelledError it cancels that task and re-raises. A message the task had already dequeued is then silently dropped, and paho has already PUBACKed it, so the broker never redelivers it. Never time out an MQTT receive with asyncio.wait_for(anext(client.messages)). Instead keep ONE pending receive task, wait on it with asyncio.wait({task}, timeout=...) (which never cancels it), and cancel it only at shutdown or connection loss. ingestion/subscriber.py::Subscriber._consume is the reference pattern. tests/ingestion/test_idle_flush.py::test_idle_flush_never_cancels_a_pending_receive pins it with a fake stream that counts cancelled receives.

GOTCHA (task 204): aiomqtt 2.5.1 Client logs WARNING 'There are N pending publish calls.' on EVERY publish/subscribe while pending calls exceed Client.pending_calls_threshold (a public attribute, default 10; see aiomqtt/client.py::_pending_call). Measured: about 590 warnings for 600 publishes at Semaphore(64). A publisher that deliberately keeps K calls in flight should set client.pending_calls_threshold = K on a client it owns. Task 204 does this in simulator/service.py::SimService.build_client and leaves injected clients untouched.

content:
Library facts verified 2026-10-14 against uv.lock (aiomqtt 2.5.1, paho-mqtt 2.1.0).
paho:
- paho-mqtt 2.1.0 supports manual acknowledgement through Client.manual_ack_set(True) and Client.ack(mid, qos).
- _handle_publish's QoS-1 branch skips _send_puback when manual ack is on. For QoS 2 it still sends PUBREC immediately, so QoS 2 hands over before the commit.
aiomqtt:
- aiomqtt 2.5.1 has NO public manual-ack switch. The paho client is the private attribute aiomqtt.Client._client, so manual ack needs one adapter module reaching that private attribute, plus an upgrade-guard test.
- aiomqtt.Message exposes .mid and .qos publicly.
- max_queued_incoming_messages and queue_type are public Client parameters. On overflow, Client._on_message catches asyncio.QueueFull and only logs 'Message queue is full. Discarding message.' at WARNING. A queue_type subclass is the public way to count discards.
- With max_queued_incoming_messages unset, the queue is unbounded (maxsize 0).
- Client.__aexit__ waits for the disconnect with timeout=None. Its reuse lock is released only after that wait succeeds.
Ack threading:
- Acks must be sent from the event-loop thread, because aiomqtt drives paho's socket through loop callbacks (add_writer).

DASHBOARD JS TEST SUBSTRATE — stamped peer under topic `dashboard-js-test-substrate`. A parsing gotcha in the shared JSX source-assertion helper, met while writing a wiring test for a React destructure.

`dashboard/tests/_dashboard_helpers.py::destructure_bindings` splits a brace body on ',' and partitions each part on the FIRST ':' — canonical left, local-alias right. It knows about ALIASES and nothing about DEFAULTS. So for a React props/state destructure with defaults, which is the dominant shape in `static/redux/*.jsx`:

    const { offline = false, offline_projects = [], ... } = sched;

the returned canonical names are the literal strings `'offline = false'` and `'offline_projects = []'`, NOT `'offline'` and `'offline_projects'`. A membership test like `assert 'offline_projects' in bound` is therefore UNSATISFIABLE — it fails identically before and after the implementation lands, so it looks like a correct RED but can never go GREEN, and an implementer can burn a cycle "fixing" working code.

MEASURED (task 4889, 2026-09-22): a first-cut test against `SchedulerTab` reported bound names as `['events_by_task = {}', 'modules = []', 'offline = false', ...]`.

THE FIX, which is a projection over the shared parse rather than a second dialect of it: `canonical.split('=')[0].strip()`. The existing callers (`test_charts_axis_labels.py`, `test_charts_consumer_bindings.py`) never hit this because the `window.DF_CHARTS` destructures they parse carry no defaults.

Discriminator for which shape you are looking at: a `window.DF_SHELL`/`DF_CHARTS` component-import destructure has no defaults, a `= D.SOMEKEY || {}` payload destructure almost always does.

Dashboard `?v=` cache-buster tests: assert the two properties separately. UNIFORMITY ("all /static/redux/*?v= share ONE version") belongs ONCE, canonically, in dashboard/tests/test_index_html.py — it had been replicated byte-identically across five test modules, so every bump re-failed several tests with several stale floors in the messages. A per-task monotonic FLOOR is still fine, but spell it `min(versions) >= N` (plus a non-empty guard on the tag set): under mixed versions that is the strictly stronger claim and needs no uniformity precondition, since the OLDEST asset is the one that would still serve stale module code. Established by task 3470 (commit a0bf8fd77a); test_esc_flow_diagram.py, test_tab_escalation_analytics.py and test_scheduler_page.py still carry the old duplicated form.

Dashboard redux gotcha: every `/static/redux/*.js` plain-JS file is loaded as a CLASSIC (non-module) `<script>` in index.html, so all their top-level `const`/`let`/`class` declarations share ONE global lexical scope — a duplicate name makes the second-loading script die with `SyntaxError: Identifier 'X' has already been declared`, silently leaving its `window.DF_*` export undefined. Hence the unique-API-const convention (`PRD_GROUPING_API`, `RUNTIME_FORMAT_API`, `DF_DATA_LOADER_API`), documented at runtime_format.js:44-51. The `dashboard/tests/js/*.test.mjs` suites CANNOT catch this: each `require()`s its module in isolation as CommonJS, where no shared classic-script scope exists. Verified 2026-07-30 that graph_layout.js:368 and esc_flow_layout.js:261 both declare `const API` and collide (filed as a follow-up from task 3305).

Dashboard node tests (dashboard/tests/js/*.test.mjs) MUST default-import then destructure — `import fmt from '../../src/.../mod.js'; const { fn } = fmt;` — never `import { fn } from ...`. There is no package.json in the repo, so redux .js files resolve as CommonJS, and node's cjs-module-lexer cannot statically detect named exports assigned from a variable (the `module.exports = SOME_API_CONST` idiom these modules use), so a named import silently comes back undefined rather than erroring. The companion browser dual-export test must also shim globalThis.window and then createRequire + `delete require.cache[require.resolve(SPEC)]` before re-requiring, because the top-level ESM import has already populated the shared CJS require cache and a plain require() would return the cached exports without re-running the body against the window shim.

Convention (reify, 2026-09-30) for task-record provenance on members retired into a coarser combiner task, mirroring the E3 A/B shape. A deferred member carries: x_backlog_sweep_arm='retired', x_backlog_sweep='<sweep date>', x_replacement='<delivering task id as a string>', and x_flip_condition naming the exact condition that flips it back to pending. A member CANCELLED because its combiner is done also carries superseded_by='<combiner>' and x_cancel_reason, and its x_flip_condition is overwritten to 'None: cancelled … Reopen only if #<combiner>'s landed work is reverted'. Combiners carry x_coalesced_from; x_backlog_sweep alone does NOT identify a combiner, because sweep cancellations carry it too.
