RECIPE: deciding whether a `deferred` task with no flip trigger was retired by a task-COMBINING pass (every known pass concatenates member descriptions into the combiner). (1) Check higher-numbered tasks' metadata for x_coalesced_from / x_e3_replacement / supersedes / curator_action=combine naming the member id, and for dependency edges remapped off the member. (2) Deterministic text check: fraction of the member's 8-word shingles (title+description) found verbatim in each candidate's title+description+details; a true combiner scores ~0.7 on s8 even after amendment, noise is <0.03. Also a sentence-level check (≥1 verbatim 6-word window per member sentence) shows what was dropped or compressed. (3) Judge residue: a combiner may compress dated provenance paragraphs into 're-measure' wording — scope preserved, prose not. Coverage: the full population is reachable — get_tasks paged at page_size=200 via the fused-memory HTTP MCP client fetched all 8008 reify tasks (ids 1–8047) in one sub-agent run (~11 min); search_tasks limit=100 is only a shortlist and must be labelled as such. Amending a task that the E3 granularity experiment coalesced (Leo's rule, 2026-09-01): mirror the amendment into BOTH the live coarse task AND the retired standard constituent(s), and do NOT undefer the retired leaves as a matter of course. The retired leaves are not dead text — E3's abort procedure (docs/prds/v0_6/e3-decomposition-granularity-ab.md §11) flips them back to `pending` BEFORE cancelling the coarse tasks, so a stale retired leaf is a live rollback hazard until its coarse task lands. Retired leaves are discoverable by metadata x_e3_arm: "standard-retired" plus x_e3_replacement and x_e3_flip_condition; coarse tasks carry x_e3_arm: "coarse", x_e3_prd, x_e3_constituents and x_e3_spec. Background: two coalescing passes were done (a backlog walk over small related tasks, and the E3 A/B over a sample of recent PRDs), both by deferring the originals and creating fewer new tasks holding the concatenated specifications — so a batch that looks mysteriously "mostly deferred" days after decompose has probably been coalesced, not abandoned. Integration-gate and PRD-close leaves are preserved as SINGLETONS by protocol, which is why a coalesced batch shows a pending gate/close leaf beside deferred producers.

INFERENCE TRAP when auditing a triage sweep: "no tasks were filed citing origin range X" does NOT imply "range X was never triaged" — in a sweep whose dominant verdict is SKIP, zero filings is the EXPECTED outcome of a completed triage. Check the sweep's per-item ledger, not just its task/ticket output. High-severity findings from review-solar_challenge-20261013 (solar-challenge at 7dfea36e). Task coverage checked against the task store on 2026-10-14 and corrected on 2026-10-16. Every item names its task, so do not re-file any of them.
(1) load.py::generate_load_profile, and ev.py the same way: each day's 1440 one-minute values are laid positionally onto a tz-aware Europe/London index, so demand runs an hour late after any in-window clock change. In a Jan–Dec run every BST minute is shifted while PV is UTC-aligned: PV-direct self-consumption reads -1.87% and Economy 7 cost is off about £6.64/yr for a 4 kWp/3400 kWh home. Tracked by task 728 (filed 2026-10-14 by recon Stage 2).
(2) flow.py::simulate_timestep: grid_export = excess - post-loss stored charge, so the battery charge loss is booked as SEG-earning export (about 25.8 kWh/yr, 1.6%). Grid import adds only post-loss stored energy, so grid-charge losses are free. The energy-balance check has no loss term, so it passes. The P4 PRD calls it 'phantom export' and puts it out of scope (Mem0 f11168db). Whether to lift that scope is a human decision: gate task 729.
(3) config.py::parse_fleet_config: load_fleet_config never reads a scenario's top-level seg: block, so `fleet run`/`fleet sweep` book £0 SEG revenue on SEG-configured scenarios (bristol-phase1 etc.). Tasks 185/325/542 cover parts.
(4) cli/home.py::home_config_for_run: `home run` reads files through cli/utils.load_config_with_overrides, not config.load_home_config. Flat files and typos silently run the default home, and period: is ignored. Tracked by task 422.
(5) config.generate_homes_from_distribution: some spec types silently produce 0 heat pumps or 0 batteries (task 403 covers part).
(6) PVConfig.module_efficiency and temperature_coefficient have no effect on the default CEC module path. Tracked by task 825 (review-all S14 leaf ζ). 825 makes both fields live Optional model inputs, not retired ones. It supersedes task 195, which was cancelled on 2026-10-15 under ruling D14/D35 (do not merge or re-dispatch 195).
(7) web/assistant.py::chat persists an empty assistant row after a pre-first-token API error and replays it on the next turn. Fixed by task 701, done and merged on 2026-10-14 (commit 5e5358cf).
(8) web fleet runs above 100 homes 500 (IndexError) on the default 100-value shuffled pools. Tracked by tasks 297 and 723.
(9) finance.project_multi_year: 318 lines, cognitive complexity 78. Tracked by task 730 (filed 2026-10-14 by recon Stage 2); task 350 (finance.py split) is related.

solar_challenge merge gotcha (task 632 architect, 2026-10-11, base main b686cc0; applies once task/632 merges). Task 632 makes flow.simulate_timestep and flow.simulate_timestep_tou pass battery.effective_capacity_kwh (capacity_kwh × SoH), not battery.config.capacity_kwh, as decide_action's battery_capacity_kwh and compute_grid_charge_power_kw's capacity_kwh. So a grid-charge target becomes target_soc_fraction × effective capacity. Deferred task 183 (branch task/183, tip ca7a86d) converts its kWh ceiling to a fraction in _build_grid_charge_context with min(gc.target_soc_fraction, charge_ceiling_kwh / battery.config.capacity_kwh). Whoever merges 183 after 632 must divide by battery.effective_capacity_kwh there. Otherwise the ceiling comes back as ceiling × SoH, which is too low below SoH 1.

Use these before inventing anything; each one is a pre-existing public API, so the rewrite is a strict improvement rather than a measure dodge.

- Warm-lane pool state: `git_ops.spec_warm_lane_pool._lanes[lane]` -> `pool.state(lane)` (returns LaneState | None, matches through the pool's own _match_lane); `_lanes.values()` -> `pool.state(l) for l in pool.lane_paths()`; `{p for p in _lanes}` -> `pool.lane_paths()`. - Item lifecycle states: `dict(worker._lifecycle._states)` -> `{e['request_id']: e['state'] for e in worker.snapshot()['entries']}`. snapshot() builds entries by iterating `ItemLifecycle.non_terminal_items()` and mapping each state through `_REGISTRY_STATE_TO_WIRE`, so this IS the published projection of that registry. When the file already imports a same-named successor (e.g. verify_plan's `_is_conftest`), alias the legacy one (`_legacy_is_conftest`) so the assertion says which side is which.

THE RESOLUTION SHAPE, under the ratchet's constraints. Three options and only one is legal: (1) keeping the harness in your migrated file restores its private writes and undoes your 0/0; (2) moving it into the CONSUMER raises that path's private_reads above ITS baseline, and the ratchet permits a measure to fall or hold, never rise; (3) extract it verbatim to a new orchestrator/tests/_<name>_harness.py and RE-EXPORT the names from your file, so the consumer's import line is untouched (it belongs to another group — do not edit it).

Without them `--check` fails with "total:private_reads rose N -> N+k for <cluster> -- totals are DERIVED by summing the per-path baseline, so moving code to a new path does not lower them" — that check exists precisely to catch relocation. Add the entry (procedure: `--write-baseline /tmp/fresh.json`, diff against the committed file, confirm the ONLY difference is your three lines, then copy it over) rather than dodging the sweep by importing lane types indirectly. candidates.content:
Gotchas when writing .ri fixtures for reify-eval tests (parse_and_compile):
- A recursive sub's ctor arg must contain a modifying operation. `sub child = R(depth: st) where depth > 0` is a compile error ("recursive sub does not decrement parameter"); use `R(depth: depth - st)`.
- In a param/let dependency cycle, the let's type infers as Real. So `param p : Int = dbl + 1  let dbl = p * 2` fails with ParamDefaultTypeMismatch; spell the cycle with Real (`param p : Real = dbl + 1.0  let dbl = p * 2.0`).

Reify `.ri` structure-CONSTRUCTION arguments are NOT dimension-checked: `Flatness(tolerance_value: 0.45kg)` compiles with zero diagnostics, and so does an entirely undefined `NoSuchThing(a: 1)`. A test that pins a field's declared unit by passing a unit-bearing literal to a constructor therefore passes vacuously in BOTH directions and pins nothing. Binding a field back OUT into a declared param IS checked — `structure P { param w : Length = Bead().width }` yields `DiagnosticCode::ParamDefaultTypeMismatch` while the field is `Real` and compiles clean once it declares `Length` — so param-default binding is the observation point to use. Caveat: that check does not descend into List element types or `Point3` component types (`param c : List<Int> = Bead().centerline` and `param p : Point3<Real> = Bead().centerline[0]` both compile clean regardless); for those, assert on the type the compiler RENDERS in a deliberate wrong-dimension rejection (e.g. `Point3<Scalar[m]>`). Measured on task #6301; the worked example is `stdlib_bead_and_layer_fields_declare_the_si_dimensioned_regime` in crates/reify-eval/tests/fdm_slice_e2e.rs.

Reify compiler gotcha (η/4480): constraint-def `param` defaults are compiled in a NEUTRAL scope (functions.rs:106-130) but are NOT strictly type-checked against the declared param type, and do NOT emit the "cannot infer return type of zero-arg function" warning — unlike a structure `let g = expr` whose cell type IS the RHS's inferred type. Consequence: `param actual : Geometry = nominal()` already "compiled with no error" even BEFORE `nominal` was registered as a Geometry-returning builtin. So to RED-test that a zero-arg builtin resolves to a specific Type, assert the result_type of a structure `let g = builtin()` cell's default_expr (the affine_identity precedent in tests/affine_constructor_typing_tests.rs), NOT the param-default path. The zero-arg builtin registration pattern is: add a name-family + result-type helper in units.rs (mirror `tolerancing_marker_result_type`/`affine_map_constructor_result_type`) and an arm in the expr.rs `NoUserFunctions` result-type ladder before the zero-arg fallback.

reify eval-order bug (task 4317, high): a structure `param` whose default expression references a sibling `let` binding silently evaluates to `Value::Undef` (no diagnostic), violating language-spec §8.2 order-independence ("all declarations within a body are mutually visible regardless of textual order"). Referencing other `param`s works; the identical expression as a `let` works. Root cause = two-pass evaluation in crates/reify-eval/src/engine_eval.rs (pass 1 ~:1531-1668 evaluates Param defaults+Auto with a values map lacking lets; pass 2 ~:1739-1754 evaluate_let_bindings runs later), so a let-reference resolves via ValueCells::get_or_undef (crates/reify-ir/src/value.rs:3319) → Undef. NOTE the related but INTENTIONAL restriction (done task 3703): FUNCTION params have a "neutral scope" and may NOT reference siblings — that does not apply to structure-body params (§8.2 governs those).

Reify compiler gotcha (entity.rs compile_entity): UNTYPED params (no `: Type` annotation) get a `Type::Real` inference fallback in the first pass — top-level at ~entity.rs:882-884 (the "infer from default" comment is stale; it just assigns Real) and port-member at ~entity.rs:1140-1142 (the path never inspects the initializer). The param's `cell_type` therefore does NOT reflect the initializer's real type for untyped params. Consequence: any declared-vs-initializer cross-check (e.g. `check_param_default_type` / ParamDefaultTypeMismatch) MUST be gated on `param.type_expr.is_some()` (the explicit-annotation flag, ParamDecl.type_expr in crates/reify-ast/src/decl.rs:203), otherwise it false-fires on untyped params whose initializer is a non-Real type (e.g. an enum-valued port member `param fluid_type = FluidType.Liquid` compares Real-fallback vs enum and errors). Task 4318 review caught exactly this.

Reify gotcha (measured 2026-10-03, main 7da9051b0e): explicit sub type-args and type-param defaults never reach the compiler as Type::Applied or Type::Error. entity.rs's two sub type-arg arms (~3281, ~5674) and convert_type_params' default arm (type_resolution.rs ~4518) match `Named { name, .. }`, which drops nested args, so `Box<SealA>` becomes StructureRef("Box") and `List<Real>` becomes StructureRef("List"). Any unknown name falls back to StructureRef(name) with no diagnostic unless the type param has a bound. A quick way to probe compile+eval behaviour without building tests is the warm lane's prebuilt `target/debug/reify check|eval <file.ri>`.

Reify grammar/compiler param-default facts (jun2, verified via tree-sitter + shipped .ri): (1) `= undef` is GRAMMAR-FICTION — authoritative comments at io.ri:11-12 and materials_electrical.ri:24 ('The Reify grammar has no undef keyword'); tree-sitter PARSES `= undef` (treats undef as an identifier expr) but the compiler rejects it, so parse-pass ≠ compile-pass. Idiomatic optional param = `Option<T> = none` (fdm_correlations.ri:242) or `some(v)` (materials_fea.ri:136). (2) Param defaults DO work, including ENUM-VARIANT defaults: `param element_order : ElementOrder = ElementOrder.P1` (solver_buckling.ri:101) — so `Port.direction : Directionality = Directionality.Bidi` is achievable. (3) Bodiless `trait X : Y` (no braces) does NOT parse — marker traits need `{}` (shipped convention `trait MechanicalPort : Port {}`). (4) `if`/`match` expressions do NOT parse in a `let` RHS — structure-def derived `let`s must be pure arithmetic over params. (5) multi-supertrait refinement `trait X : A + B { }` parses fine.

Reify let-binding annotation-vs-initializer type checking is split across THREE sites with DIFFERENT mechanisms: (1) trait-DEFAULT-injected lets already get a check in crates/reify-compiler/src/conformance/checker.rs (~line 2019, DiagnosticCode::TypeMismatchForTraitMember, unrestricted type_compatible); (2) structure-body lets (entity.rs ~1898) and (3) port-member lets (entity.rs ~2794) had NO check until task 4705, which added DiagnosticCode::LetAnnotationTypeMismatch via a check_let_annotation_type helper mirroring check_param_default_type (entity.rs:416). The skeleton/ctor-lowering let pass (entity.rs ~5391) writes to throwaway_diags and is intentionally excluded. expected-type-pushdown β (#4702) resolves the let annotation into a throwaway sink at entity.rs:1888 and threads it to compile_expr_with_expected, but only the collection-literal arms (expr.rs) consult it — scalar RHS like `5N` is never coerced, so a let-level annotation-vs-RHS check is needed for non-collection RHS.

Reify compiler GOTCHA: nominal `StructureRef`-typed params (structure-def fields AND function params declared as a `structure def` type) are NOT type-checked against argument types — a wrong-typed arg (e.g. a String literal passed where a struct type is required) is SILENTLY ACCEPTED, no diagnostic. Only `TraitObject` params and `Option/List/Set/Map` wrapper shapes are enforced. Code: `conformance/mod.rs` `walk_param_against_arg_type` fall-through arm ("Non-wrapper non-trait params ... fall through silently; a fully general arg-shape pass is future work"); structure-ctor pass `check_expr_struct_ctor_args` (compile_builder/entities_phase.rs:864-892) gates ONLY on `List<TraitObject>`. Landed pin-down proving it: `solid_param_tests.rs::solid_param_with_non_geometry_default_silently_accepts` (`param g : Solid = 42` → zero Error diagnostics). IMPLICATION: swapping a stdlib placeholder field from `String` to a `structure def` type (e.g. the `part : String` → `part : Part` Part-structdef migration, task 4578) adds ZERO type-safety enforcement — a "string rejected where the struct is required" boundary test is a doomed RED test until that general arg-shape conformance pass is implemented.

In reify-compiler, an UNTYPED `param` (no `: Type` annotation) gets `Type::dimensionless_scalar()` as a language-default inference fallback — entity.rs's top-level param arm and its port-member param arm, both tagged `ds-sentinel:allow`. That fallback is INDISTINGUISHABLE from an explicitly declared `: Real` (real-dimensionless unification resolves `Real` to the same dimensionless `Type::Scalar`), and `ValueCellDecl` carries no "was the annotation written" flag, so any checker consuming `ValueCellDecl` alone cannot tell declared intent from inference. `check_param_default_type` avoids the trap by taking `has_explicit_type = param.type_expr.is_some()` as an argument at its two call sites (task 4318 step-7); `check_param_default_conformance` does not, and consequently false-positives on `param c = SomeEnum.Variant` with "argument 'c' has type 'Enum(...)' but param 'c' requires type 'Real'" (measured on main, top-level surface). Before adding a new param-default check, decide which of these two shapes you need — threading the flag costs 106 `ValueCellDecl` construction sites across reify-compiler, reify-eval and reify-test-support.

Reify eval-engine gotcha (verified task 4474, simple engine): when a `structure def S : SomeTrait` re-declares its trait params AND appends an extra param that NO refined trait declares, the named-argument binder misbinds if that extra param is declared AFTER `material_condition` (or generally after the trait params). Symptom: the extra param's slot receives a sibling's value and the sibling (e.g. material_condition) goes `undef`, which silently collapses any inherited derived `let` that reads it (e.g. `nominal_zone = effective_tolerance_zone(tolerance_value, material_condition, 0mm)`) to `undef`. Structures whose extra param comes from a refined sub-trait (e.g. Position.datum_refs via LocationTolerance) are unaffected. WORKAROUND: declare the beyond-trait extra param immediately BEFORE material_condition (tolerance_value, feature, <extra>, material_condition) — empirically this is the only ordering that materialises the derived let. Applied to CircularRunout/TotalRunout/ProfileOfSurfaceRelated/ProfileOfLineRelated in stdlib/tolerancing.ri (see the PARAM-ORDER NOTE comments). Note the stdlib .ri is embedded via include_str! in crates/reify-compiler/src/stdlib_loader.rs, so editing a stdlib .ri requires rebuilding the reify binary before `reify eval` reflects the change.

Reify `.ri` fixtures: reaching the `TypeNotConformingToTrait` "required by param '<f>'" diagnostic requires a `sub =` binding, not a `let =` binding. `structure def Root { sub h = Holder(part: Bolt()) }` with `trait Fastener {}` / `structure def Holder { param part : Fastener }` emits it; the same ctor call written as `let h = Holder(part: Bolt())` produces NO diagnostic at all, so a fixture using `let` is silently vacuous rather than red. Measured 2026-09-01 via the real parse_with_stdlib -> compile_with_stdlib pipeline. The proven-emitting shape is `crates/reify-compiler/tests/m9_error_cases.rs::type_does_not_conform_to_trait`; copy its `sub`+empty-trait form when writing a new fixture for this code. (The two ε ctor codes have no such constraint: `Widget(nosuchfield: "v")` reaches CtorUnknownField and `Widget("a","b")` against a 1-param def reaches CtorArity, both under a plain `let`.)

Reify compiler: a type-parameter default (`<T = X>` on alias/structure/fn/trait/constraint/enum) is lowered by convert_type_params (crates/reify-compiler/src/type_resolution.rs), NOT by the full type resolver — builtins only, else Type::StructureRef(X). It becomes user-visible through parametric-alias default substitution: `type Picked<T = E> = T` + bare `param a: Picked` gives a's cell type the StructureRef default (probe 2026-10-01: enum default E → 'no matching overload ... candidates: f(Enum(E))'). Fast probe: write a .ri with that shape and run target/debug/reify check.

In task 4564 (divergence channel α), the Reify .ri evaluator does NOT statically type-check struct field names on StructureInstance values — field access (e.g., `result.divergence`) is a runtime lookup. So a .ri accessor test for a new param passes even before the param is declared in the struct def, as long as the Rust trampoline already emits the field in the StructureInstanceData map. This means the "RED until param declared" signal for accessor tests is absent in Reify.

Reify compiler: a builtin-call typing arm in expr.rs's NoUserFunctions ladder can safely set a value-cell's type to Type::StructureRef("Nominal") even when the builtin evaluates to a concrete Value::Map/Int/List (not Value::Undef). Reason: the only value-vs-type check, value_type_kind_matches (reify-eval/src/lib.rs:215), is invoked ONLY on param-override/admin-edit paths (engine_admin.rs:127, engine_edit.rs) — NOT on the Engine::eval cold-start for let-cells; and the debug-only invariant that DOES run during normal eval, assert_value_cell_types_representable (engine_eval.rs:144), explicitly permits Type::StructureRef (engine_eval.rs:122-124). Confirmed empirically: §13 joint builtins (prismatic/couple/bind/…) already carry a first-arg-fallback cell type that mismatches their stored Value::Map today, yet mechanism eval tests pass. This is the load-bearing premise behind the constructor-signature-family pattern (math_signatures.rs, dynamics body_mass_props→StructureRef("MassProperties"), and task 4311's joint_signatures.rs) and the planned B1/B2 follow-ups (tolerancing, geometry Plane/Axis).

Reify compiler gotcha (measured on main 823502024d, task 6477): a PARAMETRIC type alias whose body names an entity (enum / structure def) never resolves at its use site — and this is NOT prelude- or cross-module-specific as task 6477's title claims. A purely module-local `enum Zq` + `type Jq<T> = Option<Zq>` + `param p : Jq<Real>` fails identically with `unresolved type: Jq<Real>`. Root cause: `resolve_parameterized_alias` (type_resolution.rs:2315) hands the body to `resolve_type_alias_expr_with_subst` (:2416), whose terminal `Named` fallback (:3299-3308) hard-codes empty structure/trait sets — while the use-site caller at :2188 does hold the real sets and simply drops them. Separately, `validate_pub_parametric_alias_def_site` (:4469-4481) builds `is_known` from builtins || structure_names || trait_names with NO enum check, so `pub type Gq<T> = Option<Zq>` with `enum Zq` in the same module is FALSELY rejected at its definition site ("references unknown name 'Zq'"); the non-pub spelling is silently accepted because that validator is is_pub-gated. The NON-parametric equivalents are all clean — #6259 fixed those, including non-bare bodies like `Option<Zq>`.

Reify: a trait-typed structure param WITH an instance default compiles and evaluates fine — e.g. `structure def MyDamping : DampingDescriptor { param extra : DampingDescriptor = NoDamping() }` resolves the default AND accepts an override of a different refinement (`MyDamping(extra: RayleighDamping(alpha: 0.5Hz, beta: 0.001s))`). Probed green 2026-09-03 on task/6878. This CONTRADICTS the stale note at crates/reify-compiler/stdlib/modal_analysis.ri:394-399 ("(c) A trait-typed default `damping = NoDamping()` is intentionally DEFERRED … uncharted compiler territory") — that claim was written when no stdlib structure_def exercised the path; it is not a compiler limitation. Do not defer a trait-typed default on the strength of that comment; probe it.

Reify structure constructors do NOT type-check their arguments. Verified live 2026-08-08 against the prebuilt reify binary: passing 5.0mm (Length) to a `Frequency` param and 0.0003kg (Mass) to a `Time` param passes `reify check` and evals verbatim (`Probe { a: 0.005 m, b: 0.0003 kg }`). The same holds for stdlib structures ALREADY tightened to a dimension — `Mode(frequency: 5.0mm, ...)` (task 4548's retype) is equally silent. Dimension checking DOES work in expressions (`1.0mm + 1.0kg` -> "error: dimension mismatch in addition: Scalar[m] vs Scalar[kg]"), so the gap is specific to constructor-argument binding. `is_syntactic_zero_literal` (crates/reify-compiler/src/type_compat.rs:1614) is wired ONLY into expr.rs::compile_binop (:337/:353), so zero-polymorphism is not the explanation. The repo already states this in prose at examples/modal/transient_step_response.ri:44 ("structure ctors do not type-check args").

WHY THIS MATTERS: the "type-decision enshrinement" review family — tasks retyping a stdlib .ri param from `Real` to a named dimension (4548 Mode.frequency, 6093 RayleighDamping.alpha/beta, and the rest of that C2 review batch) — keeps writing an acceptance clause of the form "bare-Real args now produce the standard structure-field dimension diagnostic". There is no such diagnostic, and the retype alone cannot create one. Enforcement in this codebase lives EVAL-SIDE in readers, owned by docs/prds/v0_6/dimension-checked-readers.md; gating a reader is that PRD's scope, not the retyping task's (and those tasks typically scope it out themselves with "NO marshalling blocker; declaration change plus caller migration only").

HOW TO APPLY: when a task in this family asserts a construction-time diagnostic, treat that clause as a false premise, deliver every other clause in full, and substitute the signal the retype genuinely does produce — the declared type propagates into expression type-checking on field READS. So `x.beta + 1.0s` flips from "dimension mismatch in addition: Real vs Scalar[s]" to clean, and bare `x.beta + 1.0` flips from clean to an error. Do not gate the eval-side reader to manufacture the asked-for diagnostic. Note also that such a retype is numerically inert wherever the reader is a tolerant read_scalar_si (e.g. crates/reify-eval/src/modal_ops.rs:2553), which accepts Value::Scalar/Real/Int and returns the raw SI magnitude for all three.

Reify `structure def` canonical syntax requires `param` keyword before each field declaration: `structure def Foo { param x : Int = 10; param y : Real = 0.0 }` parses; `structure def Foo { x: Int = 10 }` does NOT parse (PRD-prose informality that drops `param` keyword is common — PRD §4 of buckling-eigensolver did this — but does not match grammar). Also: stdlib uses `Int` not `Integer` for the type name. Cosmetic gap between PRD prose and canonical stdlib syntax; not blocking — actual stdlib code uses canonical form even when PRD prose drops `param`. Discovered may13 during buckling-eigensolver G3 grammar-gate walk (fixtures /tmp/prd-gate-fixtures/buckling-1*.ri).

In reify, a stdlib `.ri` structure param's declared Field type is NOT enforced at runtime against the emitted `Value::Field`'s codomain: `value_type_kind_matches` (crates/reify-eval/src/lib.rs:324) matches `Value::Field` by KIND only, never comparing domain_type/codomain_type, and ElasticResult is built as a raw `Value::StructureInstance` (compute_targets/elastic_static.rs:1358) that bypasses the structure ctor entirely. So the `.ri` declaration and the Rust producer helper can silently drift apart — only hand-written tests bind them (reify-compiler/tests/solver_elastic_tests.rs pins the declared side; reify-eval-fea-tests/tests/solve_elastic_static_e2e.rs pins the runtime side). Compile-time typing IS real though: a member access like `result.curl` takes its static type from the declared param (reify-compiler/src/expr.rs:3607). When changing a Field param's codomain, change BOTH sides and check both test families.

content: reify compiler gotcha: a typed param initializer is type-checked only against lets declared EARLIER in the structure body. `structure Z { param out : Int = l2 + 1  let l2 = mid * 2 ... }` fails with ParamDefaultTypeMismatch (`l2 + 1` falls back to Real), and it fails the same way with a typed let (`let l2 : Int = ...`) or a bare read (`out = l2`). A let reading a LATER-declared param is fine, because param types are known up front. When writing a .ri fixture where a param reads a let, declare the let above the param. Measured 2026-10-12 on base b8e8c32a05 (task 7511).

candidates.content: solar_challenge gotcha (task 242, 2026-10-04): an `import X as X` / `from m import X as X` re-export marker is runtime-inert. Only mypy strict (pyproject [tool.mypy] strict = true, so no_implicit_reexport) sees it: without the marker, `from solar_challenge.config import FinanceConfig` fails mypy with `Module "solar_challenge.config" does not explicitly export attribute "FinanceConfig"  [attr-defined]`, yet still resolves at runtime. The verify type-check is `mypy src/solar_challenge` only, so tests/ are never type-checked and can keep using a retired path unnoticed. Probe a module's typed exports from the worktree root with `uv run --locked --extra dev --extra web mypy --cache-dir=/dev/null -c '<import line>'` (about 9 s cold).

solar_challenge packaging gotcha (measured 2026-10-01, task 257): `setuptools>=62.3.0` resolves to setuptools 84 in uv's isolated build env, and its build_py ships py.typed implicitly (_IMPLICIT_DATA_FILES = ('*.pyi', 'py.typed')). So removing `solar_challenge = ["py.typed"]` from [tool.setuptools.package-data] still yields a wheel with solar_challenge/py.typed. A mutation check of test_external_install.py::test_built_wheel_is_typed must delete src/solar_challenge/py.typed instead, which makes it fail as intended.

solar_challenge gotcha (task 608 architect, measured 2026-10-10). Two Python behaviours bite any annotation walker that follows a type variable's bound, such as tests/_surface_forms.py.
(1) On 3.12+, a type parameter's bound and default are evaluated lazily. So `def f[T: Node[T]]` gives T.__bound__ == Node[T], which holds T itself, and walking it recurses until RecursionError. The old-style TypeVar('T', bound='Node[T]') stays a ForwardRef and loops only once the string is evaluated.
(2) mypy 2.1.0 --strict rejects that F-bound ('Type variable ... is unbound [valid-type]'), but it accepts a recursive implicit alias, JSON = Union[dict[str, "JSON"], list["JSON"], str, None]. That alias already makes main's named_classes recurse (follow-up tkt_0RVMAV5V6AFWJQ99R5YJKF1BJ1).
Task 608's fix threads an immutable `enclosing` frozenset of the TypeVar and NewType objects being read through _parsed, and keeps it in _Unevaluated. A declaration met inside its own declaration is then read by its name alone and names no class.

solar_challenge gotcha (task 630 architect, base 84befcb, 2026-10-11; measured on CPython 3.11.15, 3.12.3, 3.13.9 and 3.14.4): in tests/_surface_forms.py, text() and surface_form can meet a NewType or type variable inside its own declaration as an OBJECT only through a PEP 695 type parameter. Its bound, constraints or (3.13+) default is evaluated lazily, so `class Tree[T: Tree.Branch]: Branch = NewType('Branch', list[T])` spells `Branch(list[T(bound=Branch)])` only because _parsed_new_type's `if new_type in enclosing` guard is there; without it you get `Branch(list[T(bound=Branch(list[T]))])`. A string self-reference (NewType('Chain', 'list[Chain]'), or TypeVar bound='Chain') does reach that guard, but only inside named_classes, where deleting it is unobservable: the _Evaluation key cuts one level later with the same classes. classes() can never observe a declaration guard, because a larger enclosing set names a subset of the classes. So pin such a guard on the spelling, with a 3.12+ input written through _imported and a skipif. mypy 2.1.0 --strict accepts that Tree/Branch input.

Python typing gotcha for solar_challenge (task 608 architect; measured 2026-10-10 on CPython 3.11.15, 3.12.3, 3.13.9 and 3.14.4 GIL, base 9ce8827). A type variable's declaration attributes differ across admitted minors:
- An unbound ParamSpec's __bound__ is None on 3.11 but type(None) on 3.12+. An unbound TypeVar's is None everywhere.
- A string bound becomes a typing.ForwardRef on every minor, while string constraints are a ForwardRef on 3.11 but a plain str on 3.12+.
- typing.TypeVar/ParamSpec/TypeVarTuple(default=...) raises TypeError before 3.13. From 3.13 an undeclared __default__ is the typing.NoDefault sentinel, so test getattr(v, 'has_default', lambda: False)() rather than __default__. default=None gives has_default() True.
- ParamSpec has no __constraints__; TypeVarTuple has neither __bound__ nor __constraints__.
- NewType keeps a string supertype as a str. Its __qualname__ is the given name, and its repr is '<module>.<name>'.
- __module__ is the declaring module for all four kinds (typing.AnyStr's is 'typing').
- An Optional bound is typing._UnionGenericAlias on 3.11-3.13 and typing.Union on 3.14.
- mypy strict rejects a self-referential bound such as TypeVar('T', bound='Comparable[T]') with 'Type variable ... is unbound [valid-type]'.

solar_challenge gotcha, measured 2026-10-02 on task/339 (ce5fd8d + dfee847, pending merge): web/storage.py's stored-config decoder no longer reloads BatteryConfig.dispatch_strategy / grid_charging as dicts. A new _field_types(cls) resolves field annotations in the defining module's namespace merged over solar_challenge.config's, and the old `except NameError` fallback to raw f.type is gone. Consequence: if you give a RunStorage-stored dataclass a TYPE_CHECKING-only annotation whose type is defined in neither its own module nor solar_challenge.config, every load of that class raises NameError naming the type. It no longer degrades silently to a dict. history_export_yaml's decode guard now also catches ConfigurationError, so a stored sub-config its class refuses answers JSON 500 "Invalid config data: ...". This supersedes the 2026-10-01 memory about the dict reload once task 339 merges.

solar_challenge (task 850 implementer, branch task/850 at fd55163, base main b3d45a3, 2026-10-17; holds once 850 merges): an unhashable dataclass field default such as MappingProxyType({}) is now caught in every per-task verify on the 3.12 pin by tests/unit/test_dataclass_defaults.py, not only by the offline lane's 3.11 interpreter-matrix case. The test imports every solar_challenge module through tests/_package_modules.py::package_modules, the walk test_docstring_examples.py also uses. It hashes every field default of each module-level dataclass and fails naming module.Class.field with the default's repr; the fix is dataclasses.field(default_factory=...). Known gap, measured on CPython 3.11.15 and 3.12.3: a default that hashes on 3.12 but whose class 3.11 judges unhashable, e.g. slice(1, 2), passes the census on the pin but raises ValueError at class definition on 3.11, so only the matrix catches it.

solar_challenge convention (task 775, task/775 at fa57ad6 on base 70f3f00, 2026-10-17; holds once task 775 merges): no solar_challenge module imports another inside a function unless tests/unit/test_import_structure.py's ALLOWED_FUNCTION_LOCAL_IMPORTS lists the (importing module, imported module) pair as Permanent(contract) or Transitional(owner). The test checks both ways, so the commit that removes a pair's last function-local import deletes its entry, and one that adds an import hoists it or adds an entry. Its seeded violation imports load_scenarios, never ConfigurationError: the capability manifest's importers-repointed-to-errors check (docs/prds/errors-leaf.capability-manifest.yaml) greps src/ and tests/ for the text `from solar_challenge.config import ConfigurationError` and expects it absent, so do not write that text anywhere in tests/, even inside a string.

solar_challenge, task 775 (task/775 commit 8895732 on base 70f3f00, CPython 3.12, 2026-10-17; holds once task 775 merges): tests/unit/test_import_structure.py classifies cli/web.py's function-local imports of solar_challenge.web and solar_challenge.web.jobs as Permanent (the optional web extra), although hoisting them is harmless today. With flask, plotly, pyarrow, anthropic, werkzeug and jinja2 blocked in a fresh interpreter, both imports succeed after `import solar_challenge.cli.main`, add 7 modules and 0.007-0.009 s (5 runs), and import none of the blocked packages. solar_challenge, correction to a06c20c9 (task 719's note on what checks a frozen-surface re-point), from task 719's amendment pass (task/719 876d98c on base ad42de8, 2026-10-14; applies once task/719 merges). (1) tests/unit/test_init_lazy_surface.py::test_every_name_resolves_to_its_type_checking_import checks that each __all__ name resolves to the object __init__.py's top-level `if TYPE_CHECKING:` block imports under that name, and stays that object across accesses. It does NOT check a name's first access, as a06c20c9 says. solar_challenge.__getattr__ caches each resolved object into the package's globals(), and the package is imported once per pytest session. So once any earlier test reads a name, every later in-session access is a cache hit, and only a subprocess (as test_import_is_pvlib_free does) sees a true first access. The check still catches a wrong mapping, because the cached value came from the same __getattr__. Measured: with a scratch -p plugin pre-caching all 69 names after setting _SYMBOL_MODULE['TariffPeriod'] = 'dispatch', the test failed with "solar_challenge.TariffPeriod is not solar_challenge.tariff.TariffPeriod". (2) a06c20c9's commit range b028f6e..a90b42f is pre-rebase and not on task/719; the branch's commits are aadd4ad..876d98c.

solar_challenge typing gotcha (task 395 architect, measured 2026-10-12 with mypy 2.1.0 strict): mypy checks dataclasses.replace() keywords against the dataclass's field annotations. So passing a float to a field annotated int that __post_init__ normalizes (LoadConfig.household_occupants, which holds a whole-number float 3.0 as int 3) fails both LoadConfig(household_occupants=x) and replace(cfg, household_occupants=x) with 'incompatible type "float"; expected "int"'. Passing it as replace(cfg, **changes) with changes: dict[str, Any] type-checks clean and leaves the dataclass's own rule to decide. Do not reach for int() or cast(), which truncate or hide the value the rule should see.

solar_challenge procedural gotcha (task 491 architect, measured 2026-10-08 on main 23c019e, CPython 3.12.3). For a task-455-style byte-identity probe, you write `git show HEAD:src/solar_challenge/web/charts.py` to /tmp and load it with importlib.util.spec_from_file_location + module_from_spec. Set sys.modules[spec.name] = module BEFORE spec.loader.exec_module(module). Without it, exec_module raises AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute '__dict__' inside dataclasses: charts.py defines a @dataclass under `from __future__ import annotations`, and dataclasses looks the class's module up in sys.modules. To prototype a whole change without touching a worktree, rsync the tree (minus .venv, .git, .task) to /tmp and run the worktree's .venv/bin/python -m pytest there with PYTHONPATH=<copy>/src. (2) To prove a kept `# type: ignore[<code>]` is needed and names the right code, check a copy with the ignore stripped in place of the real file: `mypy --cache-dir /tmp/<dir> --warn-unused-ignores --no-error-summary --shadow-file <file> /tmp/<copy>.py <file>`. A deliberate frozen-dataclass write gives `Property "x" defined in "C" is read-only [misc]`, and a deliberate extra positional argument gives `Too many positional arguments for "f" [misc]`, not [call-arg]. (3) An ignore on a value annotated `object`, e.g. a fixture parameter, is not the Any case. mypy reports the ignore unused and also the real error, e.g. `"object" has no attribute "x" [attr-defined]`. The fix is to narrow with `assert isinstance(v, Cls)`, as tests/integration/test_community_fleet.py does.

solar_challenge mypy gotcha for tests/ (measured 2026-10-03, task 352 architect, main 9fa9dd5). A `# type: ignore[misc]` on a deliberate frozen-dataclass assignment can be reported as `[unused-ignore]` only because the variable's type is an unresolved string annotation. Example: `yp.year = 99` in a method annotated `-> "YearPoint":  # type: ignore[name-defined]` when the module never imports YearPoint. That annotation is pyflakes F821, and mypy then treats yp as Any.

Resolve the annotation instead of deleting the misc ignore: `if TYPE_CHECKING: from solar_challenge.finance import YearPoint`. The misc ignore becomes needed and the name-defined ignore becomes unused. In tests/unit/test_finance_multi_year_curve.py this applies to L54/L209 (misc) and L22/L161/L174 (name-defined). Deleting the misc ignores would plant errors that resurface once task 300's F821 sweep resolves the names.

f9ed7f9d-5118-4719-b13a-e46a59d927b2.content: solar_challenge Python gotcha (task 850 architect, measured 2026-10-17 on CPython 3.11.15 and 3.12.3, main 7a47ab4): a dataclass field whose default is a MappingProxyType, e.g. `cache_usage: Mapping[str, int] = MappingProxyType({})`, imports on the 3.12 pin but raises ValueError("mutable default <class 'mappingproxy'> for field ... is not allowed: use default_factory") at class definition on 3.11. The reason: 3.11's dataclasses rejects a default whose class has __hash__ None, and 3.12 gave mappingproxy a __hash__ (although hash(MappingProxyType({})) still raises TypeError, because the dict inside it is unhashable). The per-task verify runs only on the pin, so only the offline lane's interpreter matrix catches this. In the 3.11 run, pytest stops at collection, so the whole matrix case fails within about a minute. Fix: `field(default_factory=lambda: MappingProxyType({}))`. To reproduce in a minute: UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT=/tmp/<dir> UV_PYTHON=3.11+gil UV_OFFLINE=1 uv run --locked --extra dev --extra web pytest -m 'not slow and not e2e' --ignore=tests/e2e --ignore=tests/interpreter_matrix --collect-only -q

SQLAlchemy enum-storage gotcha for solar_challenge_platform S7 models: SQLAlchemy's Enum type stores the enum MEMBER NAME by default (e.g. 'ACTIVE'). The P1·β model deliberately uses (str, Enum) subclasses with lowercase values plus Enum(values_callable=lambda e:[m.value for m in e]) so the DB stores '.value' (e.g. 'active'). This is REQUIRED for the at-most-one-active-account-per-property partial unique Index, whose where-clause must read status = 'active' (lowercase). Specify both sqlite_where and postgresql_where on the Index; SQLite has supported partial indexes since 3.8.0, so the rule is DB-enforced (IntegrityError) even in the default in-memory test suite.

DISCOVERY/CORRECTION (2026-06-22): The esc-25-7 escalation prose mis-attributed the "0001→head fails on Postgres" bug. (1) It blamed the MODEL enum at models/consent.py:47 lacking create_type=False — but migrations use their own frozen snapshots and never touch the model enum during a migration run; adding create_type=False to the model was TESTED and does NOT fix the chain. Base.metadata.create_all() on PG is also fine because the model shares one `_purpose_enum` object (it dedups). The model enums need no change. (2) The in-code comments (tests/integration/test_timescale_store.py:98-104, test_settlement_audit.py:57) attribute esc-25-7 to a 0002 RLS predicate bug (properties policy using property_id instead of id) — but that predicate is ALREADY CORRECT in 0002_rls_policies.py:84-89 (`_PROP_ID_HUB` uses `id`); that attribution and the three `stamp 0003` workarounds are stale. The real current chain failure is the 0003 generic-sa.Enum create_type adaptation bug. Lesson: reproduce migration-chain claims on a real container before encoding the prescribed remedy into a PRD.

Adding a member to a consent (str, Enum) vocabulary in models/consent_enums.py (PurposeType, DataCategory, etc.) needs NO Alembic migration and won't break tests/test_consent_migrations.py. The 0003_consent_s8.py migration deliberately INLINES a frozen snapshot of enum value literals ("Do NOT import from consent_enums") and is left immutable; the migration tests assert column NAMES only (plus an ORM column-name cross-check), never enum value sets. SQLAlchemy Enum defaults to create_constraint=False so SQLite columns are bare VARCHAR (no CHECK to violate), and functional consent tests build schema via Base.metadata.create_all (regenerated with the new value). The shared _purpose_enum = Enum(PurposeType, ...) in models/consent.py auto-introspects new members, and ConsentGate.check is purpose-agnostic (O(1) composite-PK lookup), so default-deny + permit-on-grant work for a new purpose with zero edits to consent.py/gate.py/store.py. (A live Postgres ALTER TYPE ... ADD VALUE would still be needed for a real PG deploy, but no default-suite test exercises that path.)

GOTCHA (consent S8 / migrations): PurposeType/ConsentAction/ConsentStatus are (str, Enum)s persisted as NATIVE Postgres ENUM types (consent_purpose, etc.) created by migration 0003_consent_s8.py from a FROZEN hardcoded label list. Adding a member to one of these Python enums REQUIRES a paired Alembic migration issuing `ALTER TYPE <type> ADD VALUE IF NOT EXISTS '<value>'` on the postgresql dialect (no-op on SQLite). The default pytest suite uses in-memory SQLite where SQLAlchemy Enum defaults to create_constraint=False (bare VARCHAR) and Base.metadata.create_all rebuilds the schema each run — so it gives a FALSE GREEN and cannot catch the missing PG enum value; on Postgres any INSERT with the new value fails with "invalid input value for enum". ADD VALUE cannot run inside a transaction block on older PG, so use the raw-DBAPI autocommit pattern (raw=bind.connection.dbapi_connection; raw.commit(); raw.autocommit=True; ... finally raw.autocommit=False) from migrations 0004/0005. PG has no DROP VALUE, so the downgrade must be a documented no-op. Migration chain head as of task 45: ...->0003->0004->0005; tests/test_consent_migrations.py asserts the single linear head and version_num, so adding a migration requires bumping those assertions.

Alembic/SQLAlchemy gotcha (solar_challenge_platform migrations): a generic `sa.Enum(name=..., create_type=False)` SILENTLY DROPS create_type=False when it adapts to the Postgres dialect — `sa.Enum(...,create_type=False).dialect_impl(postgresql.dialect()).create_type` returns True. So if a migration explicitly calls `_enum.create(bind, checkfirst=True)` and then uses that same Enum in `op.create_table`, the adapted column impl RE-EMITS CREATE TYPE during table creation and the upgrade fails with psycopg DuplicateObject: type already exists. Fix in the MIGRATION (frozen snapshot): use dialect-native `postgresql.ENUM(name=..., create_type=False)`, which honors the flag unconditionally — the resulting PG schema is byte-identical, only the DDL-emission path changes. Editing the model enums does NOT help — migrations use frozen snapshots, never the live model object. Fixed in migration 0003_consent_s8.py (task 52, commit 9f986b9).

As of task 169 (P-BasisC·α1), adding a `MetricKind` member to solar_challenge_platform is a compile-time-forced edit in exactly FOUR places, all closed by `typing_extensions.assert_never` so `mypy src/solar_challenge_platform --strict` names each one: timeseries/schema.py::UNIT_FOR (made exhaustive by task 169 — it previously let FLOW_POWER fall through the tail, so a new kind silently inherited "W"), timeseries/rollups.py::settlement_hh, timeseries/memory_store.py::_aggregate, and timeseries/timescale_store.py::_ca_value_expr (extracted from _query_ca by task 169 so the kind→CA-column choice has hermetic fast-lane coverage; the CA read path itself needs Docker/Postgres). `KIND` in schema.py stays the single source of truth for metric→kind. Per PRD D11 the CUMULATIVE_ENERGY arms are deliberate verbatim copies of the STATE_ENERGY ones rather than a widened `kind in (...)` condition — a meter register is not a battery state of charge, and register-specific semantics (rollover, meter swap) get one home each. Claude CLI 2.1.287 permission mechanics (measured 2026-10-02, task 4344 architect, headless --print with --json-schema):
(1) StructuredOutput survives a non-empty registry filter such as `--tools Read,Grep,Glob,Bash`.
(2) Under `--permission-mode dontAsk` with NO allow rules, Read/Grep inside cwd are allowed, while Read/Grep outside cwd (e.g. /etc/hostname) are denied.
(3) Adding a bare `Read` allow rule lets Read reach /etc/hostname.
(4) `Bash(git log:*)` under dontAsk permitted `git log -1 --output=/tmp/x.txt`, which WROTE the file. A git-scoped Bash allow rule is therefore not read-only.

CORRECTION + MECHANISM (dark-factory, reproduced first-hand 2026-09-20, task 5683 architect, 8 probes from .worktrees/5683): Bash multi-line flattening is CONDITIONAL, not unconditional. Existing memories b1002b25 and d899db68 (and graphiti 8a7e4a5d, "the Bash tool's eval flattens all multi-line constructs") say a multi-line `python3 -c "..."` always collapses. It does not, and believing it does leaves you unable to predict which commands break.

WHAT ACTUALLY TRIGGERS IT. A host PreToolUse hook on Bash — `~/.claude/settings.json` matcher "Bash" -> `~/.claude/hooks/skim-rewrite.sh` -> `exec /home/leo/.cargo/bin/skim rewrite --hook` (skim-hook v2.1.0, skim 2.3.1) — parses and re-serialises any command whose TEXT contains one of its rewrite targets (`git status`, `git log`, `head`, `cat`). The re-serialisation joins every physical line into one, so a multi-line `python3 -c "..."` argument in the SAME command reaches the interpreter space-joined on line 1 and raises `IndentationError: unexpected indent`. Nothing reports that the command was altered.

MEASURED (each one Bash call, all from the same worktree):
- `python3 -c "<multi-line>"` alone -> OK, newlines preserved.
- `echo F1 && python3 -c "<multi-line>"` -> OK. So `&&` compounds per se are fine.
- `git status --short && python3 -c "<multi-line>"` -> FLATTENED, IndentationError. Same for `git log --oneline -1 && ...` and `head -1 CLAUDE.md && ...`.
- `echo "git status" && python3 -c "<multi-line>"` -> FLATTENED, even though `git status` is a quoted argument to `echo` and never runs. THE MATCH IS TEXTUAL, and `echo` itself was left un-rewritten — so the flattening is the parse/re-serialise round-trip, independent of whether a substitution is applied.
- `git status --short && python3 - <<'PY' ... PY` -> OK, newlines intact, and `git status` was NOT rewritten. A heredoc makes the hook decline the whole command (cf. the codebook's founding evidence quote for entry-cand-20260722-6, "Contains shell syntax (file_redirect) that cannot be statically analyzed").

THE RULE. Never put a multi-line script and a `git status`/`git log`/`head`/`cat` token in the same Bash call. Issue the script as its own call, or feed it on stdin with a heredoc REDIRECT (`python3 - <<'PY' ... PY`). Scope the heredoc advice to a redirect supplying the script — a heredoc nested inside `$(...)` to build an argument (`git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF' ...)"`) is still destroyed, which is what d899db68 correctly observed; that command contains `cat`, so this model explains it rather than contradicting it.

SCOPE: the cause is third-party (skim) wired in by host-level operator config under ~/.claude/. Nothing in dark-factory can fix it; task 5683 lands the rule as a role-prompt constant instead. This also answers census 2026-09-20 §4's open question ("whether `skim rewrite --hook` joins lines"), which that synthesis could not test because its sandbox refused the live probe.

Two empirically confirmed headless claude CLI gotchas (source: external PR #4, A/B-tested on a fresh droplet) for launching skills via non-interactive `claude -p`: (1) MCP tools are NOT covered by permission-bypass mode in -p sessions — each mcp__server__tool must be named explicitly in --allowedTools (bypass alone: every MCP call denied; explicit allowlist: works with no bypass needed at all); (2) Bash allowlist prefix rules like `Bash(/path/to/script *)` match against the literal invoked command string, so an inline env-var prefix (`VAR=val script ...`) silently breaks the prefix match — export vars in the calling shell instead, and state absolute paths directly in the prompt since the agent cannot discover env vars without a permitted printenv. Relevant to skills/spawn, eval bootstrap, and any headless skill runner. Being recorded into skills/escalation-watcher-auto/SKILL.md by DF task 2937; caveat: version-dependent CLI behavior, and the PR cited the flag as --allow-dangerously-skip-permissions (actual flag: --dangerously-skip-permissions), so re-verify locally before relying on the exact mechanism claim.

GOTCHA (dark-factory, measured 2026-08-27 while planning task 3993): for BUILT-IN Claude Code tools, an orchestrator role's `allowed_tools` list grants nothing and blocks nothing — only `disallowed_tools` enforces. Every orchestrator agent runs under `--permission-mode bypassPermissions`, so the allowlist is a permission PRE-GRANT, not an exposure whitelist: a built-in absent from BOTH lists is fully reachable. `harness.py`'s own comment above `_WATCHER_ALLOWED_TOOLS` says this ("ADVISORY, not the durable enforcement boundary") and the 2026-08-08 incident measured it — 253 Edit/Write attempts by the escalation-watcher-auto rotation all failed (both are in `_WATCHER_DISALLOWED_TOOLS`) while 77 of 78 `Skill` calls launched (`Skill` was in neither list). This is the exact INVERSE of the already-recorded MCP rule (memory bed54d0a: an `mcp__*` tool is inert unless allowlisted, because MCP tools are NOT covered by permission bypass) — the two tool classes have opposite defaults, so reason about them separately: MCP → allowlist is the grant; built-ins → denylist is the only guard.

Second, non-obvious half: the contracts an agent can adopt via the `Skill` tool are NOT in `~/.claude/skills/` — they are `~/.claude/commands/*.md` (on this host: escalation-watcher.md, spawn.md, merge-queue.md, unblock.md, unblock-low-risk.md, review.md, orchestrate.md …), user-level and cwd-independent, surfaced through the `Skill` tool on CLI 2.1.247 and through `SlashCommand` historically. `~/.claude/commands/escalation-watcher.md` is a full copy of `skills/escalation-watcher/SKILL.md`. So denying `Skill` without also denying `SlashCommand` leaves a same-artifact alternate route, and no in-repo grep of `skills/` will reveal what is reachable — check `~/.claude/commands/` instead.

Practice when auditing or tightening any role's tool surface: enumerate the BUILT-INS you intend to be unreachable and put them in the deny list explicitly. Also check `shared/src/shared/cli_invoke.py::_REAL_BUILTIN_TOOLS_DENYLIST` — it is what `disallowed_tools=['*']` expands to when an `output_schema` is present, and it is hand-maintained, so any built-in the CLI has added since it was written (e.g. `Skill`) is silently reachable by every "no tool access" classifier.

GOTCHA (verified 2026-08-21, task 4511 planning): any test under scripts/tests/ that reaches scripts/legibility/coder.py's `_invoke_cli` WITHOUT passing an explicit `claude_bin=` can spawn the REAL claude CLI and incur real LLM spend. Resolution is `claude_bin or os.environ.get('LEGIBILITY_CLAUDE_BIN') or "claude"` (coder.py:315) — that trailing bare-name fallback resolves via PATH, and a real claude IS installed at /home/leo/.local/bin/claude on the test runner. WHAT EXISTS NOW. Task 3959 landed `tests/scripts/test_package_source_lookup_convention.py`, which does assert on CLAUDE.md content — and does it one step past a string mirror: it extracts the command from a `<!-- package-source-lookup:begin -->` / `:end` HTML-comment marker pair wrapping a labelled inline-code bullet, then EXECUTES it, so the recipe is certified to still work rather than merely to still be spelled the same way. SO: a CLAUDE.md recipe CAN be TDD'd, and the marker-plus-execute shape is the house way to do it.

WHAT STILL HOLDS, and is the real constraint. Carry the command, never the data it prints — a data table is bulk billed on every call AND a second copy free to rot.

GOTCHA when moving a bare `claude -p` caller onto shared.cli_invoke.invoke_claude_agent (dark-factory, found while planning task 6041). Three defaults silently change behaviour. (3) _run_subprocess needs a real cwd (it calls str(cwd), so None becomes the literal 'None'), and pre-allocating a session_id with config_dir turns on the 120s startup-wedge kill, which would kill a legitimate single long no-tool turn. A caller wanting account isolation should pass config_dir=TaskConfigDir(...).path with write_credentials(token).
