Completed: dual AD: give residual_jacobian a solve-invariant workspace (reuse Seeds, collapse the 7-arg list)
Description: Follow-up filed by task #6672 (solver-unification ε, forward-mode dual-number AD). Review cycle 2 suggestions #9 and #12-second-half; both want the same new type, so they are one task. Escalation id: agent-followup-6672.

FILES: crates/reify-constraints/src/dual_jacobian.rs (`residual_jacobian` ~:243, `fold_dependent_duals` ~:320), crates/reify-constraints/src/solver.rs (`build_trial_values`), crates/reify-expr/src/dual_eval.rs (`Seeds`, :63-190).

PROBLEM 1 — the memos are discarded every call. `residual_jacobian` builds a fresh `reify_expr::dual_eval::Seeds` on every invocation, throwing away its `depends` and `kinky` memos. Both are pure functions of (subtree content hash, seed set), and the seed set is `auto_params`, which is FIXED for the whole solve — so both memos are valid across every trial point, not just within one. `Seeds::depends_on_seed` runs an allocating `expr.collect_value_refs()` full-subtree walk at essentially every node on first visit, so one cold call costs O(nodes x depth) allocations. The module header calls this the solver's hot path, and task η (#6675) will call it once per Gauss-Newton iteration, so the cold cost is paid every iteration.

PROBLEM 2 — a 7-positional-argument signature three consumers must thread. `residual_jacobian` carries `#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]`; five of its arguments (`auto_params`, `base_values`, `dependent_cells`, `functions`, `dispatch`) are exactly `build_trial_values`' trailing parameter list, and the `x`/`auto_params` positional correspondence is enforced only by a runtime `assert_eq!`. Tasks η (#6675), μ (#6680) and λ (#6679) will each thread all seven.

SUGGESTED SHAPE (from the review): extract the solve-invariant half into a borrowed `TrialModel<'_>` holding `auto_params`, `base_values`, `dependent_cells`, `functions`, `dispatch` — plus the `Seeds` built once — so the call becomes `residual_jacobian(&model, residual_exprs, x)`. Have `build_trial_values` take the same struct, which removes the parallel parameter list rather than hiding it behind the allow-attribute, and gives the Seeds reuse a natural home. Keep the current 7-arg entry point as a one-shot wrapper if any caller still wants it.

ALSO (cheap, same file): the review asks that if the double dependent-cell traversal stays — `fold_dependent_duals` re-traverses every dependent cell that `build_trial_values` just evaluated, discarding `dual.value`, so two traversals per dependent cell per trial point — the comment at dual_jacobian.rs ~:320-323 say it is a deliberate 2x for value/derivative-path consistency rather than an oversight.

RATIONALE FOR DEFERRING: #6672's review verdict was `suggestions_only` and its one blocking finding is fixed. This is the only suggestion that is a genuine API redesign with three unwritten downstream consumers (η, μ, λ), so the shape is better chosen with at least one of them in hand than guessed now. Nothing is wrong today — it is cost and call-site ergonomics, not correctness.
Analysis: Re-plan after the plan file was lost. Branch task/7492 already carries the complete, committed implementation. Its merge-base with main is ecf5ff34fa. Main has since moved 82 commits ahead, but `git log ecf5ff34fa..main -- crates/reify-constraints crates/reify-expr` is empty, so main has nothing that conflicts with these crates and no new callers of the APIs. The branch is not a fast-forward of main, so report_ready_to_merge does not apply. That leaves a full plan with every step pre-satisfied.

Measured on this branch tip (5d8dc113e5), in this lane:
- `RUSTC_WRAPPER=sccache CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 cargo test -p reify-constraints` exits 0. `scripts/cargo-test-tally.py` reports GREEN: 652 passed, 0 failed across 20 binaries. Every named step test appears as `ok` in that log.
- `cargo clippy -p reify-constraints --all-targets -- -D warnings` exits 0 with zero warnings.

What the task asked for, and where it now lives:
- PROBLEM 2 (the parallel parameter list). `solver.rs` now has `pub struct TrialModel<'a>` (Copy). It holds `auto_params`, `base_values`, `dependent_cells`, `functions` and `dispatch`, and `TrialModel::from_problem(&ResolutionProblem, dispatch)` builds it from a problem.
  - `build_trial_values(model: &TrialModel, x)` takes that struct. It hard-asserts `x.len() == auto_params.len()`; the old `zip` silently truncated a short `x`.
  - `ConstraintCostFunction` holds one `trial: TrialModel` in place of its five mirrored fields.
  - `solve_core_with_sd_tolerance` builds `trial_model` once and reads functions and dispatch through it everywhere (heuristic 11, SPOT).
- PROBLEM 1 (Seeds memos discarded on every call). `dual_jacobian.rs` now has `pub struct JacobianModel<'a> { trial: TrialModel, seeds: Seeds }` with private fields.
  - `JacobianModel::new(trial)` builds the `Seeds` once, from `auto_params` in order, so the column contract holds by construction. It runs the repeated-auto-id check once per solve instead of once per trial point.
  - `residual_jacobian(&JacobianModel, residual_exprs, x)` is the single entry point. The 7-arg form, `residual_jacobian_with_seeds`, the seed-mismatch assert and both `too_many_arguments` allows are gone; no caller used them.
  - `fold_dependent_duals(values, &JacobianModel)` reads the model.
  - `lib.rs` re-exports `JacobianModel` and `TrialModel`; `Seeds` no longer crosses the crate root.
- ALSO. The `fold_dependent_duals` comment now states that the 2x dependent-cell traversal is deliberate: the value comes only from the single fold authority (PRD §6.3).

`crates/reify-expr/src/dual_eval.rs` (`Seeds`) is reused unchanged, so it is not in the files list. No module cycle is introduced: `dual_jacobian` imports from `solver`, and `solver` does not import `dual_jacobian`.

Steps are listed in commit order, each pre-satisfied with the commit that carries it. VERIFY remains the semantic gate.
Key decisions: Two types, not one: TrialModel (Copy, in solver.rs) holds the five solve-invariant trial inputs; JacobianModel (in dual_jacobian.rs) owns a TrialModel plus the Seeds, behind private fields.; Drop the 7-arg residual_jacobian and residual_jacobian_with_seeds outright instead of keeping a one-shot wrapper.; Make the x-length check a hard assert in build_trial_values only, and the repeated-auto-id check a panic in JacobianModel::new only.
Steps completed: 7/7
Modules: crates/reify-constraints/src/dual_jacobian.rs, crates/reify-constraints/src/lib.rs, crates/reify-constraints/src/solver.rs, crates/reify-constraints/tests/dual_jacobian_tests.rs

Reify solver tolerance inventory, measured 2026-08-26 at main 2ea72cc5e8 — useful for anyone touching #6653 (toleranced Scalar verdicts) or solver conditioning.

The dimensional path's constants are DIMENSION-BLIND ABSOLUTES applied to raw SI magnitudes: FEASIBILITY_THRESHOLD = 1e-12 (the acceptance gate, L-infinity, so 1 picometre on a metre-scale length), NM_SD_TOLERANCE = 1e-30 (argmin simplex termination on the squared-residual cost SD; deliberately <= FEASIBILITY_THRESHOLD^2 per task #4700), PENALTY_WEIGHT = 1e6, UNDEF_OBJECTIVE_PENALTY = f64::MAX/2, MAX_ITERS = 5000, FEASIBLE_OPT_ITERS_PER_DIM = 500. Inline deadbands: 1e-15 for Eq/Ne, a +1e-12 offset in comparison_violation. So a Money objective (~1e2) and a Length constraint (~1e-2) sit in the same unnormalised sum with a fixed 1e6 objective/penalty ratio regardless of physical scale.

The ONLY relative-plus-floor tolerance in the solver today is the uniqueness check's UNIQUENESS_REL_TOL = 1e-6 / UNIQUENESS_ABS_TOL = 1e-10 pair in solutions_agree. The ONLY normalisation anywhere is cost_robustness_tradeoff's normalised_blend_term. The robustness floor uses REL_MARGIN = 0.02 with ABS_FLOOR_SI = 1e-9.

The ONLY coherent tolerance HIERARCHY in the codebase is RelateTolerance::kernel_default() in crates/reify-constraints/src/relate_solve.rs — kernel_local 1e-7 m <= solver_convergence 1e-6 m <= assertion 1e-5 m, all metres, seeded from one base length. It has PRIVATE fields, exactly one constructor, no setters and no DSL knob. That ladder is the shape #6653 should generalise, and note solver_convergence (1e-6) happens to EQUAL FD_STEP, i.e. the differencing step is the same size as the convergence target.

The engine verdict fold meanwhile uses EXACT f64 equality (reify-expr eval_eq), which is why correctly-solved models report false VIOLATED at ~1e-15 residuals (probe-measured on multi_auto2/multi_auto6/auto_probe). crates/reify-core/src/scalar_tolerance.rs does not exist yet — #6653 creates it.

Completed: Fleet form silently drops a component block's mapping-valued settings: a pv.tilt distribution and battery.grid_charging are ignored by web/fleet_config.py
Description: Agent follow-up found while planning task 441 (escalation id agent-followup-441). OUT OF SCOPE for task 441. That task makes src/solar_challenge/web/fleet_config.py read every number through web.number_fields.as_finite_float. It keeps the extra-settings loop's skip of mapping values as it is.

DEFECT (heuristic 10, informatively enforced, and 12, parse at the boundary; /home/leo/src/dark-factory/docs/code-quality.md). fleet_config._parse_component_distribution copies a pv/battery/load block's settings other than its distribution (azimuth, tilt, max_charge_kw, household_occupants, ...) into the fleet_distribution block that config.parse_fleet_distribution_config reads. Description: Agent follow-up found while implementing task 441 (escalation id agent-followup-441). OUT OF SCOPE for task 441: its plan kept this branch of _parse_component_distribution, and the settings loop's guard, unchanged.

OBSERVED (heuristics 2, 6 and 10; /home/leo/src/dark-factory/docs/code-quality.md). src/solar_challenge/web/fleet_config.py::_parse_component_distribution has a branch for a component block that is itself the distribution. Such a block has no primary field (capacity_kw / capacity_kwh / annual_consumption_kwh) but has a "type" key, e.g. {"pv": {"type": "normal", "mean": 4.0, "std": 1.0}}. The branch builds the primary distribution from the block. The settings loop below it then also copies the distribution's own keys (mean, std, min, max, values, entries) into the grammar block as other settings: its guard skips only the primary field, "type", "enabled" and mapping values. config.parse_fleet_distribution_config refuses those keys as unrecognised. So no form in this shape ever produces a fleet. The fleet page's buildPayload() in src/solar_challenge/web/static/js/fleet-simulator.js never sends it: each block holds only its primary field.

MEASURED 2026-10-06 (CPython 3.12.3, `uv run --locked --extra dev --extra web`). The probe called form_to_fleet_distribution_config, then parse_fleet_distribution_config, on {n_homes: 2, seed: 1, pv: <shape>, load: {annual_consumption_kwh: 3500.0}}:
- main af58bbb, pv {type: normal, mean: 4.0, std: 1.0}: the converted pv is {capacity_kw: {type: normal, mean: 4.0, std: 1.0}, mean: 4.0, std: 1.0}, and config.py raises ConfigurationError "Unrecognised keys in fleet_distribution.pv: 'mean', 'std'; recognised keys: azimuth, capacity_kw, ...".
- main af58bbb, pv {type: weighted_discrete, values: [{value: 4.0, weight: 1}]}: ConfigurationError "Unrecognised keys in fleet_distribution.pv: 'values'; ...".
- task/441 at 108ccc8, where the loop reads every other non-null, non-boolean setting through number_fields.as_finite_float: the normal case is unchanged. The weighted_discrete case is now refused earlier, with ValueError "pv.values must be a finite number, got [{'value': 4.0, 'weight': 1}]". At POST /api/simulate/fleet-from-distribution both refusals are HTTP 400, but the newer message misdescribes the problem.

TO DECIDE (planner): what a block with no primary field should mean.
- Either refuse that shape at the web boundary, naming the missing field (e.g. pv.capacity_kw).
- Or make it work, by having the loop skip the distribution's own keys when the block is the distribution.
Note that the final else-branch (no primary field and no type) passes the whole block on as the primary spec. That is how an empty or null pv/load block reaches config.py's missing-distribution refusal, which tests/unit/web_api/test_fleet_distribution.py::TestFleetFromDistribution::test_null_pv_or_load_component_block_returns_400 relies on.

In test_form_to_fleet_distribution_config_refuses_a_distribution_number_that_is_not_finite_naming_it, the cases are [pv-block-that-is-the-distribution-mean-*]. Either decision updates them.

Decompose/filing gotchas learned on the 2026-09-29 five-PRD batch (tasks 595-662): (a) commit_planning stamps ONE capability-manifest sidecar per call — when a batch spans several PRDs, flip everything once, then re-call commit_planning per PRD with that PRD's ids (statuses are a no-op, the sidecar gets stamped and its mechanical delivered_checks copied); (b) its lint REFUSES to copy a check whose pattern is the NAME of a file the leaf creates ("filename_shaped" — declare it kind: path, expect: present, paths: [the file]) and a presence check whose pattern already matches main ("vacuous_present" — assert something the leaf introduces, or make it kind: manual); (c) it warns "absent_overbroad" when an expect:absent pattern still matches a file outside the leaf's declared files (harmless if an upstream leaf deletes that file); (d) `kind: path` validates against CapabilityManifestDoc; (e) the path-scope lint flags prose too: "scenarios/known_gap/conventions" in a description produced metadata.possible_scope_mismatch (suggested_project solar_challenge) on task 652 — write "the scenario, known_gap and convention entries" instead, and treat any recon gate on that flag as a false positive; (f) update_task title/description/priority are replace-only — append coordination notes to `details` with append=true; (g) a decompose seat can and did find G6 dependency-direction defects the drafters' own DAG missed (12 across five PRDs) — keep the decompose walk even for well-critiqued PRDs.

The /team PRD-batch pipeline that produced the 2026-09-29 demo-gap batch (five PRDs, 68 tasks, ~45 seats, ~12M subagent tokens, one working day) and is worth repeating: lead writes a shared seam table with FIXED leaf labels + one design memo per PRD (owner rulings verbatim, substrate facts, FIXED decisions, seams, out-of-scope) → one drafter seat per PRD (fable for the money/high-ambiguity PRDs, opus otherwise; all at high effort; they verify G3 anchors against main and return open owner questions) → one adversarial critic per PRD (fable for the money path — it found 17 majors the opus critics' style would likely have missed; critics verify third-party API shapes in the installed SDKs) → lead rules on every finding in a rulings-<prd>.md and sends the same drafter (SendMessage continuation keeps its context) to revise → sonnet/medium mechanical verifiers (anchors, task ids, DAG, seam rows verbatim, leaf sizes, stale terms) → one fable global seam-review seat over all drafts + committed siblings (mechanism table, file-contention table, DAG) → C-numbered canonical decisions sent to every drafter → commit PRDs → one decompose seat per PRD (manifests + filing JSON, no MCP) → one sonnet filing seat (planning_mode, deferred, idmap.json written incrementally, edges.log) → lead flips + re-stamps per PRD → fable final coordination review over the filed tasks. Rules that mattered: every leaf ≤ ~14 files (split otherwise), leaf labels stay fixed across splits with an explicit alias map, "second to land rebases" for additive shared files, human-gated leaves filed out-of-plan without prd_task_label.

Decompose-mode lesson (learned on billing-coverage-and-dispatch-hardening, 2026-07-03): before filing any PRD's task batch, sweep the LIVE fused-memory task list (get_tasks + get_statuses over the relevant id range) for in-flight or recently-done tasks that overlap the PRD's leaves. A PRD verified against an older main HEAD can have its premises silently invalidated by tasks that landed after authoring — here a whole leaf (F/expiry) was already done by task 140, and an in-progress task (142) plus a pending task (144) overlapped three other leaves. Getting this wrong means redundant reimplementation, merge collisions on the money path, and cancelling a live agent's work mid-flight. When overlaps are found, surface them as explicit decisions (supersede vs build-on-top vs coexist; drop-redundant-leaf) rather than filing blind — this is a genuine G3/G4 gate that cannot be resolved from the PRD alone because the PRD is blind to sibling task state.

Direct commits to main in the solar-challenge-platform main checkout (project config such as dark-factory-orchestrator.yaml, or docs-only fixes Leo asks for) follow three rules. First, the checkout must be clean before and after: an uncommitted tracked edit trips the merge worker, so a config edit is committed in the same step it is made. The repo has no origin remote, so a commit on main is local. After a config commit, call reload_config and read applied versus restart_required rather than assuming the change is live.

candidates.content: TDD gotcha for RED steps in this repo: when a RED test needs a module-level constant that the GREEN step will introduce (e.g. `from orchestrator.scheduler import _BACKFILL_GRANTS_MAX`), importing it at module scope turns the RED into a pytest COLLECTION error that fails the whole test file — masking every previously-green test in it and destroying the granular red signal TDD depends on. Read the not-yet-existing symbol lazily inside the one test that is about it (`import orchestrator.scheduler as scheduler_module` at top, then `scheduler_module._BACKFILL_GRANTS_MAX` in the body): that yields a targeted AttributeError for that single case. Same reasoning is why asserting on a not-yet-existing METHOD (`scheduler._foo()`) is naturally safe — it fails per-test, not per-file. Hit in task 3823 step-15.

TDD gotcha variant: a RED step whose EXPECTED failure is a collection-time ImportError also MASKS ordinary authoring defects in the same file, because pytest never gets far enough to call anything. Concrete case (task 4215, orchestrator/tests/test_whole_tree_scan_timeout_guard.py): step-1's RED was `ImportError` on two not-yet-existing constants. Both test methods inside its `TestTimeoutConstants` class had been written WITHOUT a `self` parameter. That is invisible at RED -- collection dies first -- and only surfaces at the GREEN step as `TypeError: TestX.test_noself() takes 0 positional arguments but 1 was given` from _pytest/python.py's `testfunction(**testargs)`, since pytest binds a class test as an instance method. Verified in isolation with a two-line synthetic file.

WHAT TO DO: at the GREEN step, before assuming the step's own code is at fault, `git diff` the RED commit for defects the collection error could not have exercised -- missing `self` on class methods, an unreferenced fixture name, a typo'd helper. And when authoring a RED whose expected shape is a COLLECTION error, note that the file's per-test machinery is entirely unproven by that RED; only the first run that actually collects proves it.

RELATED, distinct: memory 9b0d47ae covers a plan-structure trigger (a first RED importing BOTH planned symbols collapses two RED/GREEN cycles because the middle GREEN still dies at collection), and 493aa19f the single-lazy-symbol case. Those are about the RED shape being WRONG; this one is about a CORRECT collection-error RED concealing an unrelated latent bug in the same file.

A RED TEST'S REDNESS IS NOT ITS REASON — read the failure MESSAGE of every parametrized arm, not just the FAILED list. This is the third axis after memory eda2ff76 ("mutation-red at test granularity is not sufficient — check per-CASE") and the vacuity memories (31344c4f, 63bfc367, f9df4219). Those catch a test that never fails, and a test that fails for fewer cases than it appears to. This catches an arm that DOES fail, is counted in your RED, and fails for a reason that has nothing to do with the property under test — so it would never go green either, and the TDD evidence it appears to supply is worthless.

MEASURED INSTANCE (task 5648, 2026-09-21). A step's RED test parametrized a thread-identity probe over three escalation MCP tools — escalate_blocker, escalate_info, promote_to_l2 — and pytest reported `3 failed`, which matched the expectation exactly. Two arms failed on the intended assertion ("_recover_seq_from_disk ran ON the event-loop thread"). The third failed with `TypeError: promote_to_l2() missing 2 required positional arguments: 'evidence' and 'options'` — the tool's signature makes both REQUIRED, and the test had omitted them. The count was right, the commit message would have been wrong, and the arm would have stayed red through the GREEN step. Caught only because the follow-on impl step turned the other arms green and left that one failing with a different traceback.

THE CHEAP HABIT: when a parametrized RED has N arms and pytest says `N failed`, grep the failure output for the assertion text you EXPECT and confirm it appears N times — `pytest -q 2>&1 | grep -c '<your assertion message>'`. A single distinct traceback among them is the tell. Do this BEFORE committing the RED step, because the RED commit message is where the claim "fails today because X" gets recorded as fact.

CORROBORATING MOVE, same task: to prove an arm is red for the right reason after fixing it, re-run it against the PRE-change source without touching HEAD — `git show <prior-sha>:<path> > <path>`, run the single test, restore from a copy. That converted "3 failed" into an observation (all three arms failing on the thread assertion) rather than a count.

TDD RED-verification technique for when the PLAN mandates a module-scope import of a not-yet-existing symbol (so the lazy-access remedy in memory 493aa19f is not available and the whole test file dies at collection with ImportError): after confirming the ImportError RED, temporarily define the symbol in the src module WITHOUT committing (e.g. `sed -i` a `NEW_CONST = 'x'` line in), rerun the suite to read the real behavioural failures per test, then `git checkout <src file>` and `git status --short` before committing the RED. This shows the RED fails for the intended reason (e.g. the ack names the top-1 id instead of the judged one), not just because a name is missing. Used on task 5794, steps 5 and 7.

FALSE-RED GOTCHA: a scoped verify TEST leg can collect ZERO items and exit rc=5 ("no tests ran"), which is classified RED even though the change is correct.

MECHANISM: verify_plan._derive_module_runs FILE-SCOPES a test-only diff to just the touched test files (the `elif collectable_tests:` arm, ahead of the `elif role == 'task':` arm). If EVERY item in those files is marker-deselected by that module's pyproject `addopts -m '<expr>'`, the scoped command collects nothing, pytest exits rc=5, and the task goes RED no matter what its code does.

RECOGNISE IT BY THE SIGNATURE: the task's only collectable .py change is a test file; the scoped pytest command names just that file; output is "no tests ran"; exit code 5. Confirmed on tasks 3292, 3349 and 3494.

CONSEQUENCE WHEN AUTHORING: adding a `-m 'not <marker>'` deselection to a package's pyproject addopts creates a LATENT false-RED for any future task whose sole touched .py under that prefix is a wholly-deselected test file. The trap is armed at addopts-edit time and springs on an unrelated task later.

STEWARD ACTION once recognised: this is a verify-harness artifact, not a task defect -- see the retained steward-disposition peer for the accept-checklist. Structural fix tracked as ticket tkt_0RRZ7PP2M6DCRMG31Z20HZ8SXN via task 3494 (scoping-layer fix).
Worked example: orchestrator/pyproject.toml warm_lane_bash -- see the peer that carries it.

ACCRETION: append here or add a stamped peer under topic `pytest-addopts-marker-deselection-false-red` -- do not write a new unstamped entry.

TDD GOTCHA (click CLIs): a RED test for "this new option REJECTS a bad value" passes vacuously before the option exists, because click's unknown-option error satisfies the obvious assertions. Measured on task 5404 (orchestrator probe-models --budget-usd).

THE TRAP. The natural spelling of such a test is: invoke with the bad value, then `assert result.exit_code != 0`, `assert '--my-opt' in result.output`, and `assert the_fake_was_never_called()`. Before the option is added, click emits `Error: No such option: --my-opt` with exit_code 2 and never reaches the command body — so ALL THREE assertions hold and the test is green. It goes red only if you then break it, which nobody does. The plan for 5404 predicted this test would fail with its sibling two; it was the only one of three that passed.

WHY IT MATTERS. This is a silent-false-green in exactly the step whose job is to prove the assertion is load-bearing. The test then ships asserting nothing about the validation it was written for: delete the `type=click.FloatRange(...)` later and it still passes, because click would... no — it would NOT fail, but the test's whole point (the range constraint fires) is untested from the moment it was written.

THE FIX. Assert the rejection is a VALUE rejection, not an unknown-option one. click prefixes parameter-validation failures with `Invalid value` (`Error: Invalid value for '--budget-usd': 0.0 is not in the range x>0.0.`), which an unknown-option error never carries. Adding `assert 'Invalid value' in result.output` makes the test genuinely RED before the option exists and keeps it load-bearing afterwards.

GENERAL SHAPE, beyond click. Whenever a RED test asserts a NEGATIVE outcome (non-zero exit, exception raised, callee not called) for a surface that does not exist yet, the surface's own absence usually produces that same negative outcome. Always add one assertion that discriminates the intended failure MODE from the not-implemented-yet failure mode, and actually run the test before the GREEN step rather than trusting a plan's predicted RED basis.

TDD VARIANT (dark-factory, task 4777 step-9): a LIVE integration test for a RACE-shaped defect should be written EXPECTED-TO-PASS-ON-INTRODUCTION, and that is not a weak test step — it is the correct one. Do not spend effort trying to make it RED.

WHY. To make a live test fail without the fix you must reliably WIN the race, and a race you can only win sometimes is a flake generator, not a regression test. Concretely here: the FalkorDB post-drop rebuild window opens on roughly 1 in 40-70 single-shot catalog reads at a 1-node fixture size (measured by tasks 4748/4972, not by me), so a "prove it red first" live test would fail intermittently forever. This repo has already rejected that idea twice for the same reason — task 4972 removed exactly that defect from test_drop_vector_indices_integration.py::TestDropRebuildWindow, and test_list_indices_integration.py::TestCallDbIndexesOverRoQuery declines it too.

THE SPLIT THAT MAKES IT SOUND. Give the defect TWO tests with different jobs, and say so in both docstrings:
* the DETERMINISTIC RED is a MOCKED UNIT test where the race is ARRANGED rather than raced for — here `ro_query = AsyncMock(side_effect=[window_rows, settled_rows])` reproduces the window exactly, every run;
* the LIVE test's durable job is COMPOSITION: it proves the fix works against the real system's real column values and real state spellings, not merely against a mock of them, and it fails loudly if the fix is ever removed or disarmed.
Neither substitutes for the other, and the live one is worth having even though it was green the moment it was written.

WHAT TO DO INSTEAD OF CHASING RED, since "it passed" alone is weak evidence for a race test: (a) state EXPECTED TO PASS ON INTRODUCTION in the test docstring together with the reason, so no later reader "fixes" the missing RED; (b) run the new live test standalone several times and report the ratio (I ran 8, got 8/8) — that is evidence of non-flakiness, which is this test's actual risk, rather than evidence of non-vacuity; (c) report the measured call cost against the module's pytest timeout budget (0.14s call under a mark.timeout(30)) so nobody has to guess whether the added barrier made the lane fragile.

DISTINCT FROM the neighbouring "test step that cannot be RED" entries. Memory 3d9cbd3c covers a task with NO production change (a brittleness-reduction guard) and prescribes MUTATION VERIFICATION — inject the regression, watch it fail, revert in the same step. That remedy does NOT transfer here: mutating production to remove the settle barrier would leave this live test still passing ~40-70 runs out of 70, so the mutation proves nothing. When the obstacle to RED is NONDETERMINISM rather than an already-correct codebase, the answer is the mocked-unit/live-composition split above, not mutation.

TDD PATTERN (dark-factory, task 4157): a RED step can legitimately contain a test that PASSES on arrival — the narrowness pin — and mistaking it for a broken RED step is the trap. Both of this task's RED steps had one.

THE SHAPE. When a fix adds a deliberately NARROW `except OSError` (not `except Exception`), the repo's convention is to pair the failure test with a companion asserting a non-caught exception STILL propagates. The idiom is `_raise_emfile_spawn` / `_raise_runtime_error` in orchestrator/tests/test_remove_merge_worktree_guarded.py:100,116. The companion passes before the fix exists, because nothing is being caught yet — it is an INVARIANT THAT MUST SURVIVE the change, not new behaviour. Do not "fix" it, do not drop it, and say so explicitly in the commit message so a reviewer counting failures in a RED step is not left wondering whether the step was under-specified.

WHY THE PIN IS LOAD-BEARING. `DeterministicRunner.run()` deliberately raises `ValueError` (its sole documented `Raises:` entry) and `NotImplementedError` (the "gate resolved but before_done_ran_at is not set" operator guard). "Just make it not crash" is the natural later edit to a function documented as never raising, and widening the clause to `except Exception` would swallow those into a silent BLOCKED escalation — inverting the loud-over-silent-degradation norm with a fully green suite. The pin is the only thing that objects.

VERIFY BY MUTATION — the step that is easy to skip and that makes the pin real. A narrowness pin passes both BEFORE the fix and AFTER it, so a green run proves nothing about whether it constrains anything; inspection cannot distinguish a real pin from a vacuous one. Widen the guard to `except Exception`, confirm the pin goes RED, restore, re-run. Done for both layers of task 4157: Layer 1 (`systemd_inspect.inspect_systemd_unit`) → 'DID NOT RAISE RuntimeError'; Layer 2 (`DeterministicRunner._inspect_unit_guarded`) → same. This is the discipline memory 7b66dee5 prescribes for statement-ordering pins, applied to exception-narrowness pins — the two are the same class of test: their whole value is catching a future refactor that leaves the suite green.

MUTATION-RED AT TEST GRANULARITY IS NOT SUFFICIENT — check per-CASE. The established norm (memory 5188aaf9, adopted as task 4027's acceptance criterion) is "mutation-test a guard before believing it: inject the regression, confirm the test goes RED." Task 4112's review found the refinement that norm misses: a single test can go RED under the mutant while MOST of its loop iterations or parametrized cases are individually non-falsifiable, so the whole-test verdict hides vacuous coverage. Concrete case: test_record_path_for_slug_all_dots_slug_stays_under_sessions_dir (orchestrator/tests/test_session_registry.py) looped over ('.', '..', '...') asserting each sanitized slug's record path stays under sessions_dir. Deleting sanitize_slug's _ALL_DOTS_RE branch DID turn the test red — but only via the '..' iteration. Unsanitized, 'sessions/./record.json' still resolves under sessions_dir, and '...' is a literal POSIX dirname that resolve() leaves in place, so 2 of 3 iterations could never fail and gave the containment assertion more apparent attack coverage than it had. HOW TO APPLY: when a mutation check turns a parametrized/looping test red, confirm WHICH cases went red (pytest reports each param id separately — read the FAILED list, do not stop at "N failed"). Cases that stay green under the mutant are either non-discriminating CONTROLS, which must be commented as such so a reader does not mistake them for attack coverage, or dead weight to drop. Complements the vacuity memories (31344c4f, 63bfc367, f9df4219): those catch a test that never fails at all; this catches a test that fails for fewer reasons than it appears to.

Orchestrator/escalation test pattern for RED-before-GREEN on a fix that threads a NEW keyword arg into an existing dedup/gate call (e.g. workflow.py's has_open_l1(task_id) -> has_open_l1(task_id, category=category), task 2757): a plain MagicMock(return_value=X) MASKS the RED because MagicMock silently ignores the added kwarg and returns X for both the old bare call and the new qualified call. To make the test genuinely fail on old code and pass on fixed code, configure the mocked method with a side_effect FUNCTION whose signature mirrors the real one and returns DIFFERENT values by whether the kwarg is present, e.g. `def _f(task_id, *, category=None): return True if category is None else (category != 'merge_error')`. The old bare call `has_open_l1(task_id)` reads the category=None branch (True -> suppress -> no submit -> RED); the fixed call `has_open_l1(task_id, category='merge_error')` reads the qualified branch (False -> proceed -> submit -> GREEN). Assert both the observable effect (submit happened / escalation row emitted) AND that the mock was invoked with the kwarg (`any(c.kwargs.get('category')=='merge_error' for c in mock.call_args_list)`) so the signature threading itself is locked in.

When a TDD plan's RED test-writing step and its GREEN implementation step land in the same task/pass, reword any 'RED voice' docstrings/comments in the test (e.g. 'today the signature is X, so passing Y raises TypeError') to describe the current invariant instead, once GREEN lands — otherwise the comment misleadingly describes a pre-implementation state that no longer exists to future readers.

TEST RECIPE (dark-factory, task 3592 review remediation, 2026-09-14) — the executable replacement for an `inspect.signature` test, which the "prose-pinning / introspective meta-test" antipattern cluster names as a defect but does not give a fix for.

THE SHAPE THAT GETS FLAGGED. To pin "this parameter is required and has no fallback default", agents reach for `sig = inspect.signature(fn); assert sig.parameters['defaults'].default is inspect.Parameter.empty`. It looks behavioural because it runs, but it freezes the PARAMETER'S NAME: renaming `defaults` to `code_defaults` raises KeyError and fails the test for a change that breaks nothing, while proving nothing about any call.

THE REPLACEMENT, one line: `with pytest.raises(TypeError): fn({'some': 'arg'})` — call it one argument short. This proves the argument is genuinely required, names no parameter, and needs no `import inspect`. CONFIRM rather than assume the raise: a plain positional parameter gives "fn() missing 1 required positional argument: 'defaults'", but a keyword-only parameter, a `*args` signature, or a decorator that repacks arguments can swallow it — run the call once before committing.

SAME MOVE GENERALISES: whenever a test asserts on a signature, a docstring, a name or source text to stand in for a behaviour, ask what CALL the property makes impossible and assert that instead. Here the real invariant was "a failed defaults fetch cannot silently become a stale comparison against a built-in copy"; the call-one-short test states it without naming anything the implementation is free to rename.

TDD gotcha variant for plans that split a SYMBOL PAIR across steps (task 4274: S1/S2 pure predicate `detect_resumable_progress`, S3/S4 session wrapper `resumable_progress_for_session`, both in one new test file). Authoring the FIRST RED's import block with BOTH planned names collapses the two RED/GREEN cycles into one: the S2 GREEN run still dies at collection on the not-yet-written S3 symbol, so the middle step has no observable green and its commit cannot honestly claim one. Remedy: scope each RED step's import to exactly the symbols that step's tests exercise, and let the later RED widen it. This is the same collection-time-ImportError failure mode as memory 493aa19f (which covers the single-lazy-symbol case), but the trigger is PLAN STRUCTURE rather than one symbol — worth checking whenever a plan ships a detector + wrapper pair, a common shape in shared/cli_invoke.py.

VACUOUS-RED VARIANT (dark-factory, task 5374 steps 13/14): before writing a RED test for a defect that lives in a FILTER, COMPARISON or LOOP BODY, check whether an EMPTY fixture short-circuits the path — if it does, a test built on the empty fixture passes GREEN against the unfixed code and proves nothing.

THE CASE. A review reported `escalation/src/escalation/shadow_ruling.py::main` crashing on a naive `--since 2026-09-01` with `TypeError: can't compare offset-naive and offset-aware datetimes`. The obvious RED test — point the CLI at a tmp queue dir and pass the bad flag — RETURNS 0 on the unfixed code and prints the ordinary "no shadow rulings in window" table. The naive-vs-aware comparison sits inside the per-record sweep, AFTER `parse_shadow_ruling(...) is None: continue`, so with no stamped record the comparison is never evaluated at all. The passing test would have been committed as the step's RED, the fix as its GREEN, and neither would have touched the defect.

THE CHECK, and it costs one command: run the reviewer's reproduction against an EMPTY fixture BEFORE writing the test. If it does not reproduce, the fixture is missing the data that reaches the defect — here, a record submitted, stamped AND resolved through the real queue. Reproduce on the FULL fixture first, paste the traceback into the commit message, and only then write the assertion.

DISTINCT FROM THE TWO NEIGHBOURING ENTRIES, and the discriminator is WHERE the vacuity comes from:
* memory c32f8654 (task 4890) — vacuity from the ASSERTION: a test asserting only a NEGATIVE passes when the subject dies before reaching the behaviour. Remedy: add a positive witness that the code was reached.
* memory 56cb045a (task 4777) — vacuity impossible to remove because the obstacle is NONDETERMINISM (a race you can only sometimes win). Remedy: split into a mocked deterministic RED plus a live composition test.
* THIS — vacuity from the FIXTURE: the assertion and the determinism are both fine; the code path is DATA-GATED and the fixture has no data. Remedy: populate the fixture through the real production path until the defect reproduces by hand.

COROLLARY on the fix itself, which is the same defect seen from the other end: the crash existed because the naive-to-aware coercion was written at ONE of the comparison's two sides (`_resolved_at`) and not the other (the CLI's `fromisoformat`). Two copies of a normalisation rule that merely happen to agree is a SPOT violation (heuristic 11) that presents as a type error at the comparison. When fixing one, extract the single rule and call it from BOTH sides rather than adding a second copy.

Verify false-RED gotcha: the FILE_SCOPED pytest leg in orchestrator/src/orchestrator/verify_plan.py (`elif collectable_tests:` ~:555, before `elif role == 'task':` ~:562) narrows verification to just the touched test files. If every item in those files carries a marker that orchestrator/pyproject.toml addopts deselects (e.g. `-m 'not warm_lane_bash'` at :125), the leg collects zero, pytest exits rc=5, and the task goes RED even though nothing is broken — a source-only diff would have gotten FULL_SUITE instead. Touching the deselected test file is what triggers it. Do NOT work around this by editing addopts, verify_classify.py, or verify_plan.py from inside a task lane; escalate it as a scoped-verify false-RED and merge on independently-verified green (post-merge verify runs the module's unscoped command, which does not hit the empty-selection path). Confirmed on task 3292; the real fix is ticket tkt_0RRZ7PP2M6DCRMG31Z20HZ8SXN.

ANTI-PATTERN (dark-factory, task 4561 review remediation): a "drift guard" meta-test that sweeps `globals()` for module-level fixtures by NAME and asserts set-equality against a hand-written tuple. It fails in BOTH directions and is not worth keeping.

THE CASE. `test_pytest_marker_deselection.py` parametrized a family invariant over fixture NAMES (resolved via `globals()[name]` at call time) because the test class sat ABOVE most of the fixtures and parametrize argument values bind at class-creation/import time. A second test then guarded the hand-written name tuple against drift with the rule `name.startswith('_') and 'SOURCE' in name and isinstance(value, str)`.

WHY IT IS NOT THE PROPERTY IT CLAIMS. (a) It does not close the hole: a future fixture named `_CLASS_MARKED_FIXTURE` or `_REAL_CLASS_SHAPE` carries no 'SOURCE' token, so it is invisible to the discovered set AND to the tuple — the drift recurs silently and the guard still passes green. (b) It is a tripwire on cosmetics: a pure rename, or an unrelated `_SOURCE_PATH` helper string, turns the suite RED for a non-behavioural reason. Its assertion targets the names of module-level string literals via introspection, not any behaviour of the code under test. Tightening the regex only deepens (a) while widening (b).

THE FIX, and it is structural not textual: MOVE the parametrized test to the MODULE TAIL, after the last fixture binding, and parametrize over the fixture VALUES directly with an explicit `ids=` list. The name indirection existed SOLELY to work around definition ordering; relocating removes the need for it, and `grep 'globals()'` over the file should then return nothing. Accept the residual — a newly added fixture nobody adds to the list is simply not swept, which costs COVERAGE but can never produce a false RED — and say so in the docstring, including that the fix is not a tightened naming rule.

GENERALISATION: before writing a meta-test, ask what it asserts on. If the answer is identifier names, module structure, or a naming convention rather than a behaviour of the system under test, prefer changing the code's shape so the invariant can be stated on values.

AMENDMENT to topic `vacuous-test-guard` — a seventh shape: THE TEST'S OWN NAME LEAKS INTO THE DATA UNDER ASSERTION, via pytest's `tmp_path`.

MEASURED (task 5361, orchestrator/tests/test_dry_run_unblock.py). A RED test was written to pin that `run_dry_run_unblock`'s investigation prompt carries an explicit marker when the task fetch fails, rather than silently omitting the block:

    async def test_unavailable_task_record_is_marked_not_silently_omitted(self, tmp_path):
        prompt = await _capture_investigation_prompt(tmp_path, scheduler)
        assert 'unavailable' in prompt.lower()

It PASSED against code that had no marker at all. `tmp_path` is derived from the test FUNCTION'S NAME (`/tmp/pytest-of-leo/pytest-N/popen-gwK/test_unavailable_task_record_is0`), and the code under test interpolates the worktree path into the prompt as `Worktree: {worktree}`. So the assertion matched the test's own name, echoed back through the value it was inspecting. Renaming the test to `test_failed_task_fetch_is_marked_...` flipped it to failing immediately.

WHY IT IS ITS OWN SHAPE. The existing peers all describe a discriminator that is weak or short-circuited. Here the discriminator is strong and the assertion is exactly right — the DATA is contaminated by the test's identity. It fires for any test whose name shares a word with its assertion AND whose code under test embeds a tmp path, a fixture name, a node id or a test-id in its output. Prompt builders, log-line assertions, error-message assertions and path-echoing serializers are the exposed surfaces.

THE TELL, and it is cheap: the canonical's universal test caught this for free because the test was written RED FIRST and passed when it must have failed. An unexplained green during the RED step is never "the feature was already there" until you have checked it is not your own fixture talking.

TWO REMEDIES, in order of preference:
1. Assert against the module's own marker CONSTANT (`from ... import _TASK_UNAVAILABLE_MARKER; assert _TASK_UNAVAILABLE_MARKER in prompt`), plus a cheap assertion that the constant itself is non-vacuous. No prose duplicated into the test, and a path can never match it.
2. If a literal must be used, pick a phrase containing SPACES — a tmp path cannot contain them — and keep the test's name disjoint from the asserted words.

Do NOT "fix" it by lowercasing/normalising harder; that widens the collision.

Test-helper extraction convention (from steward triage of esc-1387-155): When a TDD RED/step-1 scaffold and its implementation land in the SAME merged diff, strip the "these tests will FAIL until implemented / ImportError expected" comments before merge — post-merge they assert a non-existent failure mode and mislead debuggers. When a parse/dispatch helper becomes the single source of truth for multiple test suites, validate its mode/kind argument explicitly (raise ValueError on unknown values) rather than using `X if kind=='a' else Y`, which silently mis-dispatches on typos. Document regex limitations (e.g. em-dash truncation) AND raise a clear error at the truncation point rather than relying on a comment alone.

In shared/src/shared/task_metadata.py, TaskMetadata uses model_config = ConfigDict(extra='allow'). This means TDD RED tests for a *new* Literal field must be written carefully: pre-field, TaskMetadata(new_field='some_value').new_field == 'some_value' already PASSES (extra='allow' stores and returns any kwarg as an attribute) — so "valid value constructs/round-trips" assertions are NOT red pre-field. Only these are genuinely red pre-field: (1) TaskMetadata().new_field (AttributeError, since no kwarg means no extra key at all), (2) TaskMetadata().model_dump()['new_field'] (KeyError, same reason), (3) pytest.raises(ValidationError) around an invalid value (extra='allow' silently absorbs it, no raise), and (4) parse_metadata warning-code assertions (pre-field the key is unrecognised -> code='unknown_key', not 'invalid_field'). Confirmed empirically while implementing task 2801 (operational_mode field).

TDD RED against a pre-fix tree, the LATE-STEP case: when a multi-step plan has you demonstrate RED for step N by reverting the SRC files to the pre-task base, an EARLIER step's test-file import blocks collection and you get the wrong RED.

MEASURED (task 4985, fused-memory). Step-13's E2E rows had to be shown RED against base b39a4f57ca. Reverting just the two src files with `git checkout <base> -- <src paths>` (leaving the test file at HEAD) produced only: `ImportError: cannot import name '_implausible_target_reason' from fused_memory.services.memory_service` — a module-level import added by step-7's test commit for a symbol step-8 created. pytest never collected anything, so all five E2E rows reported nothing about their own behaviour.

THE FIX, and why it is not the same as reverting the test file. Back the test file up to /tmp, comment out ONLY the import line(s) naming symbols that post-date the base, run with `-k <YourClass>`, then restore from /tmp and `git checkout HEAD -- <src paths>`. Reverting the whole test file (memory 47b30349's technique) would delete the very rows you are trying to red; reverting only src is what you want, and that one import line is the only thing standing in the way.

WHAT IT BUYS. The isolated run gave per-row causes that could be attributed: two rows `outcome='repaired'` (the live defect), one row failing on a missing kwarg only, one row PASSING pre-fix (the intended no-regression pin), and one failing a layer earlier than the plan predicted (`TypeError: AmbiguousEntityError() takes no keyword arguments`, the structured fields being an earlier step's work) — which is worth recording as OBSERVED rather than as the plan's prediction.

ALSO: to capture concrete pre-fix numbers (nodes_minted, await_args_list) rather than infer them from an assertion that failed early, drop a throwaway `tests/test_zz_probe_*.py` that ends in `raise AssertionError(f'PROBE ...')` and delete it after — plain `print` is swallowed, because this repo's pytest runs under xdist ("bringing up nodes...").

RELATED, distinct: 7687cf77 (extract main's copy of ONE file to /tmp and run a standalone guard script — lint/guard tasks, no package import), 47b30349 (revert the TEST file when tests+impl were authored together as WIP), 0411288f (a collection-error RED masks authoring defects in the same file). This entry is the fourth case: a collection error caused by a PRIOR STEP hiding a LATER step's behavioural RED.

content: TDD gotcha (task 6127, measured): a RED test for strict validation of a NOT-YET-ADDED keyword parameter, written as `pytest.raises(TypeError, match='<param_name>')`, passes vacuously on the old code. The call raises Python's own "f() got an unexpected keyword argument '<param_name>'", which is also a TypeError containing the name. So the RED proves nothing. Match on text only the real validation emits instead (e.g. match=r'OrchestratorConfig\.<param_name>' for verify_spec_shared.py::_validated_field_overrides), and confirm the RED run lists that test as FAILED. The existing parametrized test_verify_spec_shared.py::test_mistyped_field_override_is_rejected_naming_it has the same weakness for any field whose name appears in a signature error.

d9b4d9a6-16f7-4e54-b287-ba4a84516c13.content:
GOTCHA: a guard test can PASS VACUOUSLY -- without ever exercising the assertion it claims to pin. It then provides false assurance, and it keeps passing after the thing it guards is broken.

THE SHAPES OBSERVED, each documented by a stamped peer under topic `vacuous-test-guard`:
  - PARAMETER SUPPLIES THE DISCRIMINATOR. A parametrized test whose discriminating token comes ENTIRELY from the parameter proves nothing about the code's own constant (orchestrator/tests/test_verify_cmd.py, TestChainOperatorTokenCoverage).
  - THE PAIR ONLY PINS TOGETHER, BUT BOTH SIDES DRIFT. A positive/negative pair whose docstring argues they only pin the narrowing jointly (fused-memory path-scope guard, TestProseRightBoundarySignal).
  - AN EARLIER GATE SHORT-CIRCUITS THE ONE UNDER TEST. recon_code_fix_premise_guard's match_candidate requires ALL title_substrings before it ever looks at description_substrings, so a negative test whose title misses an anchor dies at the title gate and says nothing about descriptions.
  - DERIVED CONSTANTS, path_scope_guard._build_pattern, the merge_disposition INTEGRATION_SKEW invariant I7, and a fail-soft variant -- see the peers.

THE UNIVERSAL TEST, and the reason this topic exists: MUTATE THE THING THE GUARD GUARDS AND CONFIRM THE TEST FLIPS TO FAILING. A throwaway rebind is enough -- `import orchestrator.verify_cmd as vc; vc._NON_AND_CHAIN_TOKENS = frozenset()` then re-run the assertions. A guard whose outcome is INDEPENDENT of the constant is vacuous by definition. Repeated green runs prove nothing on their own; only the mutation distinguishes a guard with teeth.

CAUTION (added 2026-09-14, reconciliation run b4fd1c79): peer ordinal self-numbering under this topic has drifted and is NOT reliable. Peers 79625c18 (2026-09-11, "a sixth shape": single-producer test against a shared multi-producer sink) and 95083a87 (2026-09-10, "a SIXTH shape": witness emitted upstream of the claim it defends) both independently claim to be "the sixth shape", describing two DIFFERENT things, because neither queried current topic membership before numbering itself. True membership as of this note: 22 records tagged `topic: vacuous-test-guard` (confirm via `get_memories_by_metadata`/`count_memories_by_metadata`, never by trusting a peer's own ordinal). Read a peer's CONTENT to learn which shape it documents; do not rely on any "sixth"/"seventh"/etc. claim in its text. Same drift pattern independently found and annotated this cycle on the `pytest-xdist-serial-override` canonical (8bb3eb15).

ACCRETION: append here or add a stamped peer under this topic -- do not write a new unstamped entry.

solar_challenge test gotcha, measured 2026-10-14 on main e5d7e80 (task 710 architect, CPython 3.12.3). simulate_home rebuilds every kW series of SimulationResults (demand, generation, grid_import, grid_export, ...) from per-minute kWh flows, as kWh * (1/HOURS_PER_MINUTE). So results.demand is NOT bit-equal to the load profile it was given: in a 1-day run, 453 of 1440 minutes differed by 1-2 ulp, a max relative difference of 2.1e-16. Likewise, results.import_cost only matches grid_import * HOURS_PER_MINUTE * tariff_rate to about 1e-16. Compare such series with pd.testing.assert_series_equal(..., rtol=1e-12, atol=0.0) or np.testing.assert_allclose(rtol=1e-12, atol=0.0), never with exact equality. A home's location timezone shows only in the demand index: the London and Paris load profiles for one day have identical values but different index tz. A test that pins timezone threading must therefore compare the index, which assert_series_equal does.

High-severity findings from review-solar_challenge-20261013 (solar-challenge at 7dfea36e), all open and untriaged:
(1) load.py::generate_load_profile, and ev.py the same way: each day's 1440 one-minute values are laid positionally onto a tz-aware Europe/London index, so demand runs an hour late after any in-window clock change. In a Jan–Dec run every BST minute is shifted while PV is UTC-aligned: PV-direct self-consumption reads -1.87% and Economy 7 cost is off about £6.64/yr for a 4 kWp/3400 kWh home.
(2) flow.py::simulate_timestep: grid_export = excess - post-loss stored charge, so the battery charge loss is booked as SEG-earning export (about 25.8 kWh/yr, 1.6%). Grid import adds only post-loss stored energy, so grid-charge losses are free. The energy-balance check has no loss term, so it passes. A PRD calls it 'phantom export' and puts it out of scope; no task tracks it.
(3) config.py::parse_fleet_config: load_fleet_config never reads a scenario's top-level seg: block, so `fleet run`/`fleet sweep` book £0 SEG revenue on SEG-configured scenarios (bristol-phase1 etc.). Tasks 185/325/542 cover parts.
(4) cli/home.py::home_config_for_run: `home run` reads files through cli/utils.load_config_with_overrides, not config.load_home_config. Flat files and typos silently run the default home, and period: is ignored.
(5) config.generate_homes_from_distribution: some spec types silently produce 0 heat pumps or 0 batteries (task 403 covers part).
(6) PVConfig.module_efficiency and temperature_coefficient have no effect on the default CEC module path.
(7) web/assistant.py::chat persists an empty assistant row after a pre-first-token API error and replays it on the next turn.
(8) web fleet runs above 100 homes 500 (IndexError) on the default 100-value shuffled pools.
(9) finance.project_multi_year: 318 lines, cognitive complexity 78.

The arbitrage home of scenarios/bristol-arbitrage.yaml (built directly: 4 kW PV, LoadConfig(3400, use_stochastic=False), 5 kWh battery at 2.5/2.5 kW, Economy 7, dispatch_strategy tou_optimized) was simulated over 2024-06-21 with synthetic_june_weather('2024-06-21'). At the scenario's grid-charging target_soc_fraction 0.9, overnight grid charging fills the battery, so PV adds only 0.0288 kWh in 33 minutes, against 2.0797 kWh from the grid. A test that needs both charge sources should use target 0.7 (1.0797 kWh from the grid over 27 minutes, 1.0288 kWh from PV over 132 minutes) or 0.6 (0.5797 kWh grid, 1.5288 kWh PV). solar_challenge task 352 premise check (architect, measured 2026-10-02 on main 2bb0402 with a scratch script outside the tree, CPython 3.12.3, scipy 1.17.1). (1) project_multi_year's per-year curve is scipy PCHIP of its node values, and a curve-level test can see it. Setup: an injected simulate with self-consumption 12000*exp(-0.1*age), asset_life 25, and error_target_pct=1e6, which keeps only the seeds, so sampled_ages is (0,12,24). curve.points[y].fleet_self_consumption_kwh then matches PchipInterpolator over the injected node values to 9e-13. Between nodes PCHIP differs from np.interp by up to 935 kWh and from finance._monotone_hermite_interpolate by up to 575 kWh. With sys.modules['scipy.interpolate']=None the curve equals the fallback to 2e-12. So a test against a scipy oracle kills both the fallback and the linear mutant by a wide margin. (2) asset_life_years=1 gives sampled_ages (0,) and one point, so _interpolate_per_year's single-node branch is reachable through project_multi_year. (3) Retiring the fallback is feasible. Locked pvlib 0.15.1 requires scipy>=1.7.2 unconditionally, and uv.lock holds one scipy (1.17.1) for every Python minor. Adding a scipy floor to [project].dependencies then running `uv lock --offline` changes exactly two lines of uv.lock: solar-challenge's dependencies and its requires-dist. scipy ships no py.typed, so its import still needs `# type: ignore[import-untyped]` or a scipy.* mypy override. The PRD's decompose record (review/gap-register.md:91) already said "no fallback needed". (4) No SimulationResults builder exists on main outside tests/unit/test_finance_projection.py, so a curve-level test needs task 349's tests/_finance_builders.py.

candidates.content:
Pre-file owner check, 2026-09-09 instance and the reasoning worth keeping (Mem0 mirror of a decisions_and_rationale entry, since that category distills the rationale away).

Asked to file "ghost reaping on finalize", search_tasks found task 3860 already owned it exactly and no new task was filed for that half; the evidence was appended to 3860 instead. The transferable lesson is about RANKING, not about search: for the query "merge queue snapshot enumerates finalized blocked requests as queued ghost entries never removed", the true owner 3860 scored 0.513 and ranked FIFTH, below task 4582 (0.596) and task 2068 (0.589) which describe adjacent-but-different snapshot defects. Stopping at the top hit would have produced a duplicate. Read the whole result set and compare each candidate's actual defect shape against yours before concluding nothing owns it.

Second transferable point: an ask can be half-owned. The request bundled two symptoms; one (dead entries over-reported as queued) was owned by 3860, the other (a live verify under-reported as not running) was owned by nobody and became task 5245. Splitting on that boundary — dead-over-reported vs live-under-reported — is what made the ownership question answerable, and both tasks now cite the boundary explicitly so a future reader does not re-merge them.

Lesson 2026-09-08: a census taken mid-session goes stale within hours in this fleet, and a final recap must re-check any live state it names. The residual-5050 session's first recap said esc-4314-3 and esc-5131-3 were "not touched" and that the orphan-reaper pattern "has no identified owner". When Leo asked for a brief on those two records, re-reading showed esc-5131-3 had been closed on Leo's own ruling at 21:52Z the previous evening (owner task 5079), esc-4314-3 had meanwhile been inflated to blocking and was pinning a finished branch, and the pattern was partially owned by tasks 3976 (done), 3587 and 4988 plus the 2026-08-10 analysis plan. Two of three claims in one sentence were wrong because they were relayed from an earlier census rather than re-read. Before stating "X is pending / untouched / unowned" in a closing message, re-run the query; and never assert "no owner" without grepping the task store for the mechanism's symbols (here: orphan, reaper, is_actively_held, escalate_info, steward) and plans/ for an analysis.

A task ruling that lives only in an unmerged branch, a sibling task's `details`, and archived L0 resolutions is NOT durable — and the handoff that was supposed to close it can silently evaporate. In the esc-3563-3 case (dark_factory), task 4028's steward ruled for relocation on 2026-08-19 but 4028's own `details` was empty; the ruling existed only in task 4262's details, on branch task/4028, and in dismissed L0 records. Separately, esc-4028-1's resolution rested its plan for closing 4262 on "the still-open esc-4028-2 ... which I am leaving pending on purpose as the post-merge trigger" — but esc-4028-2 was itself resolved six minutes later, so NOTHING was watching for 4028 to land. NORM: write the ruling into the TASK record (details/description), not just the escalation resolution, and do not rely on a deliberately-left-open sibling escalation as a trigger — it can be closed by the next sweep or agent.

Before calling an escalation's question "undecided" or "unowned", read the subject task's OWN details/amendments and the tasks it names, not just the PRD. On 2026-09-11 the L2 watcher wrote an "OPEN DESIGN QUESTION" note on tasks 5097/5053 about verify_cross_check_remote_green, although Leo's ruling R11 (keep the cross-check on for the 3-day parity window, then flip it off by reload) was already recorded in 5053's details. Both notes had to be corrected. Likewise, re-verify a sub-agent's causal claim before recording it: a sub-agent attributed the curator's cold usage gate to a missing check_at_startup call, but that method is a no-op.

CORRECTION 2026-08-12: a task carrying done_provenance has APPEND-ONLY metadata, NOT unwritable metadata. An earlier claim in this session (propagated into task 3936, task 3695 and a markup_tripwire hint string before being caught) said update_task refuses any metadata payload on such a task. That is false and was disproved in the act of writing it: a payload of {'allow_mcp_markup': True} cleared the floor on the done task 3083 and the write returned updated:true. The accurate rule is that the write-authority floor is presence-keyed on done_provenance appearing in the INCOMING payload, so a write-time-only control flag passes. What is genuinely impossible is REMOVING or RENAMING a key: deletion requires metadata_mode='replace', merge mode has no deletion sentinel, and any faithful replace payload must carry done_provenance forward to preserve it, which the floor then refuses. That asymmetry — additive yes, subtractive no — is why leaf eta (task 3697) completed while task 3083's seven non-canonical markup_tripwire_rejections_* keys survived un-migrated, and it is the shape recorded as a known open gap in docs/task-authoring.md.

"NOTHING OWNS THIS" — the check that made task 4953 defensible, 2026-08-30. My own recorded track record is that this is my worst claim class (2 of 4 wrong), so before filing the workflow-less-coalescing defect I searched the task store for the MECHANISM rather than the vocabulary, and read every non-terminal candidate in full.

A broad regex over merge/coalesce/train vocabulary matched 322 tasks — useless. Narrowing to `merge[-_]deferred|train_incomplete|not all members|atomic[- ]train` gave 59, of which 18 were non-terminal. Reading them showed a real owning FAMILY existed and the gap was still genuine:
- 1519-1530 (done) BUILT the atomic-train feature; 1523 is where a member transitions to merge-deferred and 1526 is the all-members-ready GroupMergeRequest enqueue — both workflow-mediated BY DESIGN, which is exactly why a workflow-less entry breaks them.
- 1867 (done) fixes a train that DERAILS after members REACHED merge-deferred, re-driving them to solo merges.
- 4737 (pending) and 4497 (pending) both concern members STRANDED IN merge-deferred — the opposite state to mine.
- 4630 (deferred) is unblock SKILL.md prose about a coalesce non-tip member.
None contemplates a queue entry with NO workflow behind it, so the gap was real.

THE STEP THAT ACTUALLY SETTLED IT was reading the code, not the task titles: grepping for production writers of `merge-deferred` returned exactly two, both TaskWorkflow methods (workflow.py:1515, :1544), and reading `_default_coalesce_exclusion_reason` (merge_queue.py:15097) showed its two signals never ask whether a member CAN reach that state. A task-store search alone would have left the claim as an inference.

GENERALISABLE: when checking whether a gap is unfiled, search the mechanism not the vocabulary, read the non-terminal candidates in full rather than judging by title, and confirm the mechanism in code before asserting nobody owns it.

STEWARD NORM (dark-factory, learned on esc-5029-3, 2026-09-12): before adjudicating an agent's design_concern escalation that asks you to choose between scope arms, CHECK WHETHER THE QUESTION HAS ALREADY BEEN RULED ON -- and check the task's own LIVE record, not the description embedded in the escalation prompt.

THE MECHANISM. An escalation record snapshots the task description AT FILING TIME. A ruling that lands minutes later amends the live task row but does NOT retroactively update the escalation you are handed. So the steward prompt can show an un-amended task while the live record already carries the binding ruling. Measured here: esc-5029-3 was filed 12:27:39 asking the steward to rule on a scope question; task 5029's live record showed updatedAt 12:33:58 with metadata `x_amended_by_ruling` = "esc-5025-2 2026-09-12 option A", a full AMENDED block in the description, a rewritten `user_observable_signal`, and `x_original_user_observable_signal` preserving the superseded one. The escalation prompt showed none of it.

WHY IT MATTERS. Ruling independently would have produced a steward-invented answer competing with a standing decision by Leo -- on a wave where nine sibling tasks were being steered by that same decision. The failure mode is not "wrong answer" but "second answer", which is worse: the siblings diverge.

HOW TO CHECK, cheaply and in this order:
1. `get_task(id, project_root)` on the escalating task, and grep the description and metadata for an amendment block or an `x_amended_by_ruling` / `x_*_owner` / `x_original_*` key. The `x_` namespace is where these rulings get stamped.
2. `search_tasks` with a paraphrase of the ESCALATION'S OWN QUESTION, not of the task. Here that surfaced task 5446 ("Restore the tight bound ... after delta"), filed by the L2 watcher as the backstop for exactly this ruling, plus the amended delta task whose blocking signal had been SUSPENDED.
3. Read a SIBLING task in the same wave. If siblings carry an amendment your escalating task appears to lack, you are looking at snapshot lag or an incomplete sweep, not at an unruled question.

Then relay the existing ruling in the `resolution` text rather than composing a new one -- on the L0 `action='resume'` path the resolution is injected into the agent's briefing, which is what actually repairs the agent's stale premise. Still verify the agent's measurements independently (they may be right, as here, and may even understate the problem); what you are declining to re-derive is the DECISION, not the evidence.

Before filing a fix task in dark_factory from an escalation ruling, ALWAYS run search_tasks to check for an existing owner. Measured across two filing batches on 2026-09-07/08: in the first, 5 of 7 items already had owners (tasks 3353, 4496, 5151, 5055 and a curator-combine into 4862); in the second, 4 of 8 (tasks 3821, 2896, 3154, 4890). Filing blind would have created nine duplicates in two sittings. The escalations themselves are unreliable on this point — esc-4048-4 and esc-markup-guard-5 and esc-4814-3 each concluded "no owning task" or "a NEW remediation task is needed", and all three were wrong; a prior leaf being `done` and closed to appends does not mean the work is unowned. Related trap: when the curator COMBINES a newly filed task into an existing one, the combine's rewrite can DROP the evidence you filed — this happened twice (into 4862 and 3821), dropping measurements, a false-positive-direction warning, and a two-direction test requirement. After any combine, re-read the target and re-append what was lost.

MERGE-QUEUE OWNERSHIP IS INVISIBLE IN THE TASK TABLE — get_task's claimant fields are NOT a check for "is anyone working on this". Observed on dark_factory task 3875, 2026-08-24.

A session was briefed to land task 3875 and told to first confirm no other worker held it. Every task-table signal said CLEAR: get_task returned status='pending', claimant_run_id=null, heartbeat_at=null; `ps` showed no other Claude session referencing 3875; there was no lock. On that evidence the correct-looking next step was to claim the task and submit a fresh merge_request.

That would have been a double-submit. mcp__escalation__get_merge_queue showed task 3875 ALREADY head-of-line in state='verifying', request mr-0ce7a070, enqueued 69 minutes earlier by the orchestrator itself, with an owned merge worktree (.worktrees/_merge-2baccaa7) and a live verify process tree.

WHY THE FIELDS DISAGREE: claimant_run_id/heartbeat_at track the ORCHESTRATOR'S TASK-EXECUTION claim (the workflow that produced the branch). Once that workflow finishes and hands the branch to the merge lane, the claim is released and the task goes back to a claimant-less state while the MERGE WORKER owns it. The two ownerships live in different places by design.

NORM: before concluding a task is unowned — and always before submitting a merge — call get_merge_queue (and merge_status by task_id) as well as get_task. A pending, claimant-less task can still be mid-landing. The corollary bites the other way too: the standing advice that "a formerly-blocked task is DROPPED from the merge queue, so submit fresh" is about tasks the queue dropped, and must not be applied without first LOOKING at the queue.

Related tell: mcp__escalation__get_task_runtime_state showed phase='DONE' for 3875 with has_worktree=true — consistent with "task workflow finished, merge lane now owns it".

TWO DISTINCT FAILURE MODES PRODUCE "A SETTLED QUESTION GETS RE-LITIGATED", and they need opposite fixes — both observed 2026-08-17. (1) RULING-DELIVERY GAP: task 4026's ruling landed correctly but was written only into the escalation `resolution`, never into the task record, so the re-dispatched architect read the unamended task and re-derived the same block. Fix: write rulings into the task's `description`/`details`. (2) AUTHORING-CONSULTATION GAP: task 4363 proposed a rewrite that task 3367 had already adjudicated with measurements AND a guard test (`TestRootTypeCheckCommandPyrightInterpreterPinned`, tests/scripts/test_fallback_verify_config.py:604) — but 4363 was authored by an implementer who never saw 3367, and 4363's description does not mention it at all. The ruling was delivered fine; TASK AUTHORING failed to consult it. Fix: surface prior rulings at authoring time. DIAGNOSTIC TO TELL THEM APART: check whether the new task/record CITES the prior ruling. If it argues against a ruling it never names, it is (2); if it repeats a question the ruling answered and the task record shows no trace of that answer, it is (1). Related signal: a change that would have to defeat an existing GUARD TEST to land is arguing with a settled decision rather than extending one.

GOTCHA (dark-factory): a RULING pasted into a task's Details is a SNAPSHOT, not a live fact, and its git-state claims expire. Task 4666's ruling for task 4925 asserted "the eight `<!-- provenance-guard: negative -->` markers exist ONLY on branch task/4659, which is unmerged — grep on main returns NOTHING", and instructed "Coordinate with 4659 rather than editing main." By the time 4925 dispatched, 4659 had merged (2dfa004857) and all 8 markers were ON main; there was no branch left to coordinate with. The ruling's DECISION (drop the markers, don't build the tier-3 prose grep) survived intact — only its MECHANISM inverted, from "prevent a branch from landing them" to "remove them from main". PRACTICE: when a ruling's instruction is conditioned on a named branch being unmerged or a file being absent, re-measure that condition before planning against it (`git log --all --oneline --grep=<id>`, `git grep -c <string> main -- <path>`), and file an escalate_info recording the correction so a reviewer diffing the frozen ruling text against the change does not read the deviation as the agent ignoring the ruling. Separate the decision from its premise: a stale premise usually does NOT invalidate the decision, so re-derive the mechanism rather than re-opening the question.
