When a long-lived HOLD or gate has drifted, the strongest evidence of what was actually decided is the OPERATOR MEMORY FILE written on the day of the decision — not the task metadata that claims to enforce it. Demonstrated 2026-08-24 while ruling reify task 6488 ("which of 5 divergent statements is the release condition for the 2026-07-28 Mem0 consolidation hold"). The bookmark task reify 5741 carried metadata.external_deps=['dark_factory:3169'], i.e. a scheduler-ENFORCED statement of the condition — and it was wrong. The correct condition sat in /home/leo/.claude/projects/-home-leo-src-reify/memory/project_mem0_consolidation_hold.md, modified 2026-07-28T21:04:43Z (hours after Leo took the decision): "Release condition (mechanical, not a date): dark_factory tasks 3133, 3134, 3112, 3108". reify 6482's metadata.unblock_precondition, derived independently by recon run 5d186c7b 26 days later, named the identical four — two artefacts, no shared derivation, exact agreement. GENERALISABLE RULE: (1) when adjudicating divergent statements of a condition, look for the contemporaneous record first, and prefer it over any later-added mechanical proxy, however authoritative the proxy looks by virtue of being enforced; (2) a proxy that only ONE consumer adopted is not the condition — do not promote it; (3) after ruling, hunt for statements of the condition that are ENFORCED rather than merely retrievable (metadata.external_deps, unblock_precondition, dependency edges) and re-point them in the same sitting, or the ruling will say one thing while the machine does another. In this case the enforced statement was a live SIXTH statement that the gate task enumerating the divergence had not even listed.

SESSION SUMMARY (L2 escalation session l2-df-298963, 2026-08-24, esc-3868-5). Investigated with a 3-agent team including a dedicated refuter, then ruled with Leo. OUTCOME: task 3868 landed and is done; esc-3868-5 and its member esc-3868-4 closed (close_only, actionable); task 4459's description corrected and re-scoped; worktree .worktrees/3868 and branch task/3868 removed after content-proof of the landing. WHAT THE INVESTIGATION OVERTURNED — four load-bearing claims in the escalation chain were wrong or stale: (1) "3868 cannot merge" is false, only the task-role verify blocks (merge role is full-breadth and never file-scopes); (2) the 08-19 triage's correction about task 3513 was doubly stale — 3513 landed on 08-20 AND never touched the marker collection function, Gap 2 went to pending task 4561; (3) "the harness fix is a tracked ticket" badly understated task 4459, whose branch already carries a complete, verified-green, reviewed implementation blocked only on merging; (4) the cited precedent sha bddb9948b6 is a branch commit, not the landing (that is merge 1f2c60c7de). Also corrected the reason option C was rejected: not "it breaks a convention" (no such convention exists) but "task 4459 already implements the durable cure". LEFT OPEN: task 4459's merge phase cancelled at 2026-08-24T10:34 with no merge_queued event, cause undetermined; it is pending with no dependencies and should re-dispatch. Also noted but not investigated: the merge queue reported two two_layer_invariants violations ("frozen-prefix base-chain broken at mr-0ea444e5", "verify-base NOT subset of frozen-tip") from the speculation path during this merge, which completed cleanly regardless.

The escalation-watcher's 2026-08-07 triage note on esc-3841-1 was a model of correctly-bounded evidence, and re-measurement on 2026-08-24 vindicated BOTH halves of it. It probed `grep -rn "x_related_cross_project_tasks" --include=*.py .` and `grep -rn "x_related_task\b" --include=*.py .` -> 0 files each (still 0 on 2026-08-24), but explicitly refused to read that as proof of absence, stating "a code grep cannot see a key written only as mem0 payload data". That caveat was exactly right: the keys DO exist as free-text Mem0 payload — memory c9bcf72a-bf6b-47e9-895d-929fb7cd5177 carries x_related_cross_project_tasks="dark_factory:3833,dark_factory:3839" as a comma-joined STRING, the sibling suppression memory 53236105 spells the same relationship `related_tasks`, and task 3841's own metadata carries x_related_task="598". Three inconsistent spellings across ~2 records, read by no code. So the escalation's recommended anchor was real but unusable, and Leo's 2026-08-17 ruling independently reached the same conclusion, routing to cited_tasks instead: "a plumbing defect, not a vocabulary defect." LESSON: when a probe returns zero, state which channels the probe CANNOT see; a code grep is blind to LLM-authored metadata payloads, and count_memories_by_metadata is blind to Graphiti-stored facts and to nested or differently-spelled keys. The correct follow-up is to read the specific cited records by id via get_memory_by_id, which is what finally settled it.

The "check for an existing owner before filing" rule earned its keep again on 2026-09-21, in a way worth recording because the near-duplicate was BETTER than the proposed new task.

While triaging the over-delivery gap I was about to file a new dark_factory task for "pass plan['files'] to the reviewer prompt so it can flag work outside the task's scope". A non-terminal-tasks-by-symbol query on `build_reviewer_prompt` found task 5369 (pending, high) already owns it and owns it more completely: 5369's Concern 1 wires the task record, THE PLAN, and WHOLE CHANGED FILES into `agents/briefing.py::BriefingAssembler.build_reviewer_prompt`, replacing the `diff[:50000]` truncation outright. It had also independently measured that truncation — 46% of 3,657 persisted reviewer briefings — against my session's 56% of the last 300 landed merge diffs. Consistent, from different populations.

The same query surfaced task 5695 (pending, high), which owns the stale-base half: `_review` and `_run_completion_judge` diff against the STORED creation-time base rather than a re-derived merge-base. And 5695's own "suggested work 2" was the very guard I was about to file, and it named TWO further adjacent owners, tasks 4980 and 3158.

So the correct action was three annotations, not a new task: the guard was homed on 5369 with its wording constraints, 5695 was told its item 2 is ruled and lives elsewhere, and 3918 was told it now has two downstream consumers of the same root cause.

TWO GENERALISABLE POINTS. First, the symbol query must be run against NON-TERMINAL tasks over title AND description AND details AND metadata — 5369 was findable only by the symbol `build_reviewer_prompt` appearing in its details, not by any topic phrasing of "over-delivery" or "scope". Second, a broad topical search is not a substitute: searching for "over-delivery" and "declared minus actual" returned only the two tasks already known, while the symbol query returned four more owners.

A useful corollary about truncation itself, found the same day: git orders a diff by PATH, so when a reviewer diff is cut at 50,000 chars the content that falls off the end is `orchestrator/tests/`, `plans/`, `scripts/`, `shared/` — everything sorting after `orchestrator/src/`. That is exactly where incidental, undeclared files live, so the truncation is biased against noticing precisely the thing a scope check would look for.

Task 'Sitting ownership probe: read x_origin_escalation (canonical) alongside legacy origin_escalation, ahead of the task-4302 corpus x_ sweep' completed. Landed in commit b0e73a9085ec4f00de9c77149e9d5bd77281a894.

When submit_task/resolve_ticket returns status='combined', READ THE FOLDED TASK BACK AND VERIFY YOUR CONTENT PER FIELD — the curator rewrites, and it can replace a verified root cause with a plausible but WRONG mechanism. Observed dark-factory 2026-08-10: a candidate describing L2 co-parent orphaning (mechanism located in escalation/src/escalation/queue.py + server.py) was folded into task 3587, and the curator's rewrite re-attributed it to "the sweep's terminal-subject check is keyed off a co-parent/task-id relationship that doesn't resolve to the true terminal task for L2 records" — a mechanism that does not exist (the escalation's task_id was unambiguous throughout) — while DROPPING both escalation-package files from files_to_modify, so an implementer would have gone straight to the wrong module. Fixed with an explicit update_task carrying a "CORRECTION TO AN EARLIER DRAFT" block plus the restored file list. The combine decision itself was correct (3587 genuinely owned the problem space); it is the rewritten prose that needs auditing. Related: a curator combine can also silently WIDEN a task's charter, which matters because a lock is taken over the declared charter.

Brief an ownership-check seat with SYMBOLS ONLY, never with the current working hypothesis — a seat given the theory searches for the theory. On 2026-09-21 I briefed an ownership seat with my (later refuted) "resumed session replays its transcript" hypothesis for dark-factory esc-5588-8. It ran 11 queries, correctly classified the resume/charter-loss family (3985, 3986, 3991, 3992) as distinct, and concluded owner_found=false. It never surfaced task 5579, which owns the actual trigger and whose own description quotes the exact sentence "that branch restarts from the ORIGINAL prompt, throwing away the transcript and all agent progress". One literal sqlite3 scan over title||description||details||metadata for the symbols `_reset_for_fresh_retry`, `invoke_with_cap_retry`, `original_prompt`, `retrying fresh` found it immediately, and also surfaced task 2136 (the task that ADDED the hook, and therefore the provenance of the gap) — a hit no semantic query produced, because that task is about adding a feature rather than about the defect its narrow scoping caused. The same pattern repeated the next day: a residual I was about to file fresh turned out to be owned exactly by task 3160, again found by literal scan and missed by framing. Semantic search_tasks matches your framing and its corpus excludes deferred/uncommitted tasks; a literal scan matches the code. Run the literal scan yourself alongside any delegated ownership check.

content: The L2 sitting tool refuses a ruling on any task that still carries metadata.x_coalesced_into. scripts/sitting/ownership.py's coalesce_fold probe answers 'owns' whenever subject.metadata.get('x_coalesced_into') is not None, so the item routes to the "owned by" standing footer and resolve-answers refuses the ruling token. This bit esc-5064-3 on 2026-10-16: task 5064 kept an x_coalesced_into marker pointing at task 5293 from the 2026-09-09 backlog sweep even after it was un-deferred to be worked on its own, so Leo's "your rec LGTM" was never applied. When a coalesced task is revived as independent work, clear the marker with update_task(metadata={'x_coalesced_into': None}, metadata_mode='merge'), since the probe checks for None, and fix the owner task's x_coalesced_from. Stamping x_ruling (one of RULING_METADATA_KEYS) records the ruling where the task_ruling probe can see it.

candidates.content: /unblock technique for a systemic fix implemented by hand: submit_task with planning_mode=True creates the task synchronously in DEFERRED status, which the scheduler never dispatches. That gives a real task id for a hand-implemented branch with no dispatch race, and avoids a follow-up briefing off a half-written description. Pair it with mcp__escalation__claim_warm_worktree(slug=<task_id>) to get a CoW-seeded _iact-<id> worktree on task/<id>. Land via merge_request as usual (the queue does not care that the task is deferred), then set_task_status done with kind=merged (deferred→done worked) and release_warm_worktree, which prunes the merged branch. Used for reify task 7691 on 2026-09-19. For ordinary follow-ups that SHOULD be dispatched but build on unlanded code, file normally with dependencies=<the unlanded task id> (7693 depends on 7376, 7695 on 7691).

release_workflow's park is CONDITIONAL on was_active, and the no-park window lets the SCHEDULER re-dispatch the task — filing blocking escalations against work that is already landing successfully.

OBSERVED (reify task 5858, 2026-08-02): an /unblock session called release_workflow(5858) and got {released: false, was_active: false, slot_cleared: true, parked: null} on an in-progress task whose orchestrator lane had already been reaped. No park occurred, so the task stayed non-terminal and scheduler-eligible. ~20 minutes later — while the branch sat head-of-line in the merge queue as mr-774ab2e2, about to land — the scheduler dispatched it and hit "warm-lane acquire fault for branch '5858'", filing a BLOCKING L1 + L2 pair (esc-5858-8 / esc-5858-9). The auto-watcher then re-pended the task blocked -> pending, chasing a phantom. The merge landed cleanly at 30d90a097a regardless; no damage, but two blocking escalations and a watcher rotation were spent on a non-problem.

THE EXPOSURE WINDOW IS THE WHOLE MANUAL MERGE. On a busy fleet that is long: this merge took ~48 minutes end-to-end under host load peaking at 247.

THE DIAGNOSTIC TRAP: a `blocking` escalation naming a warm-lane acquire fault reads like a pool defect. It was not — the watcher independently measured the pool healthy (warm-lane-audit.sh HEADROOM free=11), the seed script present and executable, and the pool enabled. All three of the error message's named causes were ruled out. Before treating an acquire fault as pool health, check whether a concurrent manual landing left the task dispatchable.

THE RUNBOOK STEERS INTO THIS: /unblock's merge procedure says of release_workflow "If was_active is False the orchestrator wasn't running it; you can skip this step in that case." That is backwards — was_active: false on a NON-TERMINAL task is the ORPHANED shape, which is the one MOST in need of the reaper-immune blocked hold, not least. This is the same no-park behaviour already known for the reaper's stranded-in-progress worktree sweep, but the scheduler-redispatch consequence is DISTINCT and bites even when the worktree is already safe (5858's branch lived in a personal warm worktree outside .worktrees/, so the reaper half was already handled).

HOW TO APPLY: on any non-terminal task, if release_workflow returns parked: null, immediately set_task_status(id, "blocked") yourself — regardless of whether you are creating a worktree. Also re-check pending escalations on the task RIGHT BEFORE finishing, not only during triage: both of 5858's blocking escalations were filed mid-session and would have been left pending otherwise.

POSSIBLE UPSTREAM FIX (dark-factory side, not filed): have release_workflow park to blocked whenever the task is non-terminal, regardless of was_active.

reify /unblock triage insight (2026-08-20, task 6128): "/unblock <id>" is not always a blocked-task or escalation case. Task 6128 was `pending` — not blocked, no pending escalations, no worktree at .worktrees/6128, no claimant_run_id, no heartbeat — yet genuinely stuck. The diagnostic that revealed it was reading the orchestrator event history (data/orchestrator/runs.db `events` table) rather than the task record: a task whose LAST event is weeks old while its status is `pending` is silently starved, and the `task_completed` rows carry the reason (here `plan_blast_radius_lock_conflict`, plus two `worktree_quarantined` rows with reason `recovery-identity-mismatch`). Also useful: `phase_skipped` rows with `reason: no_pending_steps` and all step ids in `done_step_ids` mean a resumed run will skip the execute phase entirely and go straight to verify/review on whatever the branch already contains — a stale-complete plan is its own hazard on a rescoped task. Remediation for a stuck-pending task is task-state surgery plus branch disposal, not a merge — there is nothing to merge and no worktree to fix in.

Holding a reify task against orchestrator dispatch: `metadata.do_not_dispatch` and `metadata.claimed_by` are DECORATIVE — grep confirms ZERO readers for either key anywhere in dark-factory. The only ENFORCED hold is the first-class `claimant_run_id`/`heartbeat_at` pair, read via `shared.task_claimant.has_live_claimant` at scheduler.py:4934 with `claimant_dispatch_gate_enabled` defaulting True. Measured failure 2026-08-20 on reify task 6393: an interactive session filed the task with do_not_dispatch metadata AND passed `claimant_run_id` on the `set_task_status` call that moved it pending->in-progress, but never READ THE WRITE BACK — the claimant did not persist (record showed `claimant_run_id: null`). With the decorative flag unread and the real hold silently absent, the scheduler dispatched the human-driven task ~2 minutes later, hit a warm-lane acquire fault, and left it `blocked`; an orchestrator agent would have been dispatched on top of finished human work if the acquire had SUCCEEDED, so the infra fault was luck, not a defense. RULE: after any fused-memory task write that carries a claimant, re-read the task and confirm the field actually persisted before relying on it. The writer-side phantom-contract problem (unenforced holds) is tracked as dark_factory task 4213; DF 2234's deferred_watch gate is the design precedent. Safest pattern for self-implemented work remains submit_task(planning_mode=True) and STAY `deferred` (not dispatchable) through the whole implement phase, flipping to pending->in-progress only immediately before submitting the merge.

A reify task sitting at status `pending` can hide a COMPLETE, unlanded implementation on its task branch. Diagnostic signature, measured on task 6877 (2026-09-01): runs.db shows `task_completed outcome=cancelled` with `agent_invocations=2, execute_iterations=1, verify_attempts=0`, while the branch carries a full RED/GREEN commit series. What happened: the implementer succeeded (2026-08-30T17:02:19Z, 32 turns, $2.47) and rebased, the workflow entered VERIFY, sat ~4 HOURS without ever getting an admission slot (`verify_attempts=0` proves the gate never ran), and an orchestrator restart at 21:01:44Z cancelled the run. Reconcile then logged "task 6877 no-lock but branch task/6877 carries WIP commits — retaining worktree for resume" and "reverted task 6877 to pending" — but the retained lane `_lane-10` was stolen an hour later under pool pressure for task 5711, killing the resume path and leaving only the branch. NEVER read `pending` as "no work exists": check `git log --oneline main..task/<id>` before re-dispatching or coalescing a pending reify task.

PROCEDURE — unblocking a reify task whose `.task/plan.json` was lost to warm-lane reclaim (validated end-to-end on task 5069, 2026-07-28). The correct disposition is FAST-TRACK verify+land, never re-implementation. Steps that mattered:

1. The worktree is NOT at `.worktrees/<id>/`. A warm-lane task lives at `/home/leo/src/warm-lanes/worktrees/_lane-N`. Find it with `git worktree list | grep <id>` — do NOT conclude "no worktree, nothing to unblock" from the missing `.worktrees/` path. The /unblock runbook's Step 0 says to stop in that case, and that instruction is wrong for every warm-lane task.

2. Re-verify the orphan-reaper's done-criteria yourself against the branch rather than trusting the escalation prose — it is cheap, and it is the entire basis for skipping a TDD re-run.

3. `get_task_runtime_state` can report a STALE active workflow. Task 5069 showed `phase: EXECUTE` in that snapshot while `release_workflow` returned `was_active: false` and a /proc cwd scan found zero live processes in the lane. Trust release_workflow plus a /proc scan over the snapshot.

4. If task status is `pending` (not `blocked`/`in-progress`), `release_workflow` will NOT park it — it only parks in-progress tasks. Set it to `blocked` manually before working, otherwise the scheduler can dispatch the task into a fresh lane mid-flight.

5. Do NOT run the runbook's `git worktree remove` / `git branch -d` cleanup on a warm lane. The lane is pool-managed; pool GC reclaims it once the task is terminal and its tip is an ancestor of main. Removing it by hand damages the pool.

6. The reconstructed plan's steps will all read `status: pending`; that is fine and needs no fixing. They become moot once the task goes `done` on merge — mark_step_done reconciliation only matters when RESUMING an implementer, not when landing manually.

Related: [[lane-reclaim-keeps-branch]], [[unblock-wt-outside]], [[lane-force-checkout-gc-clobber]].

UNBLOCK RACE TRAP (task 3112, jun3-4): escalation MCP release_workflow soft-cancel did NOT stop the live workflow. It returned released=true, was_active=true, slot_cleared=false repeatedly (30s+60s timeouts), and because the slot never cleared it never parked the task. When the workflow eventually processed the cancel it exited REQUEUED — resetting the task to pending and overriding the manual set_task_status(blocked) park — and the scheduler RE-DISPATCHED a fresh agent ~4h later (22:18), which reset the branch and re-ran the full TDD cycle while the interactive /unblock session was mid-salvage on the same branch. Lesson for /unblock: if release_workflow returns slot_cleared=false, the workflow is NOT stopped and a manual blocked-park will not survive the workflow's REQUEUED exit; verify no live processes AND expect the task to bounce back to pending. Re-check task status before and after long-blocking operations (merge_request blocked ~9h here due to queue congestion).

A reify task left PENDING with partially-landed work can complete ITSELF via orchestrator re-dispatch while a human/agent session is still deliberating what to do about the residue — so re-read status before acting on any plan premised on "this task is part-done". Concrete case, task 6107: an /unblock session landed most of the work (merge f30d4458fe) but deliberately left the task pending because the description had grown a NEW requirement the diff did not satisfy (an identity-seam stub test). Overnight the orchestrator re-dispatched it — routing history shows implementer 02:09, reviewer_comprehensive 02:25, implementer 03:15, reviewer 03:33, resettled_adjudicator 03:34 on 2026-08-21 — the missing Test 14 was written and landed as merge 955d37c680, and the task was stamped done at 04:14 with done_provenance kind=found_on_main. By the time a follow-up session went to split the residue into a new task, there was no residue: nothing to split, no new task to file, no dependency to repoint. GENERAL LESSON: "task is part-done on main, so split the remainder" is a plan whose premise expires quickly on a live fleet. Re-fetch get_task immediately before executing any split/defer/re-dep sequence, and treat a conditional instruction ("if it is still pending, then...") as a genuine condition to TEST rather than a description of current state.

reify, 2026-09-19 (esc-6583-4 / esc-7692-1): when a task is a verified-superseded duplicate whose own description reserves cancellation for "a human curator decision", the L2 watcher should set it DEFERRED as an interim rather than either cancelling it or leaving it pending. RATIONALE: retitling a task "do not implement" and dropping its priority to low does NOT quarantine it from dispatch — task 6583 was re-dispatched at 06:37 on 2026-09-19, burned a full opus/max ARCHITECT run, exited via report_unactionable_task and fell back to blocked at 06:45:45Z, and would repeat that on every recovery cycle. The status "deferred" is the one status carved out of the stranded/recovery sweeps and out of dispatch, so it stops the waste IMMEDIATELY, is fully REVERSIBLE, and does not pre-empt the ruling the task text reserves (unlike a cancel, which is what the gate was asking a human to authorise). Safe in this case because nothing depended on 6583 (its content lives in #5436) and branch task/6583 carried ZERO commits beyond main, so deferring stranded nothing. If the eventual ruling is to keep the task, it must be UN-deferred explicitly rather than being allowed to drift back to pending.

REAPER GOTCHA in /unblock: release_workflow(task_id) only parks an in-progress task to `blocked` (the reaper-immune state) when a workflow was actually active. If it returns {was_active:false, parked:null} — common when the orchestrator isn't currently running the task — the task STAYS in-progress, and the reconciliation reaper (stranded-in-progress sweep) will remove a `.worktrees/<id>` worktree you create, even mid-session (it swept mine during a user-approval wait). Fix: when release_workflow returns was_active:false/parked:null on an in-progress task, manually `set_task_status(id, blocked)` yourself. After parking blocked, recreating the worktree had no recurrence.

[CURATOR NOTE 2026-08-20, gate 5965 — this entry's trigger is correct but its scope is too NARROW.] As written 2026-07-11 this entry framed the fix as something you do "BEFORE creating/recreating the worktree", i.e. as a worktree-reaper concern. The broadened rule is ratified in b2229c69-9238-467e-a7bf-06ac20827cfc (2026-08-02, task 5858 incident), which is the canonical statement: the same was_active:false/parked:null return leaves the task dispatchable, so it also causes scheduler REDISPATCH and false escalations, and the manual set_task_status(id,'blocked') is required REGARDLESS of whether you are creating a worktree. Read this entry as the original worktree-reaper instance of that general rule; read b2229c69 for the rule itself.

Both entries are retained deliberately — they record different incidents and different consequences of one upstream defect, and neither is a superset of the other's evidence.

candidates.content: Blocked-task re-dispatch ownership across the reify/dark-factory seam: DF's Scheduler._phase_redispatch_stranded_blocked (scheduler.py:6458, registered tick phase at :1887, stranded_blocked_redispatch_enabled defaults True) is the canonical owner of stranded blocked rows — it runs every tick, requires no live claimant plus _deps_satisfied (which accepts BOTH done and cancelled, :4545), and clears the claimant then flips to pending (:6648-6649). It deliberately REFUSES two populations: task_kind == 'deterministic' (:6572, DESIGN GAP carve-out, owned by the deterministic gate flow) and rows with an open pending escalation (:6621, LeaveReason.escalation_pinned). Those refusals are policy, not gaps — docs/task-escalation-state-spec.md S3 says a human-resolved gate record deliberately STAYS PARKED, and RecoveryAction (task_ground_truth.py:143-155) has no cancel member at all. Any reify-side sweep that re-pends or cancels rows in those two populations is a second owner running the opposite policy, not added coverage. This is what reify task 7349 retired from scripts/deterministic-gate-closure-staleness-sweep.sh.

Reconciliation run 64f89bb4-8526-4b3d-b8f5-ea5b1204484e (Stage 2, task_knowledge_sync, 2026-08-12): acted on Stage 1's dead-claimant-PID-sharing and no-claimant-requeue-race systemic findings (mem0 a4f7f292-a271-46e6-81b7-9ccf8675c2bd) by clearing claimant identity on reify tasks 5784, 5344 and 5627 via set_task_claimant, all confirmed with no live-workflow signal that cycle. Separately attempted the documented requeue-race remediation (mem0 0b40556e-3328-4969-8c9a-89df1eb7754f / a7167263-d3fa-48ab-afc7-d73fde91e337) on tasks 5481 and 5623 via set_task_status, but the write tool rejected both calls with an authorization error: the reconciliation actor is not permitted to perform that particular transition under the task-status-authority policy table. Filed a human-operator gate task (reify 6260) covering both 5481 and 5623 so an authorized actor can complete the reset, and to flag that the write-permission gap is new relative to when the 0b40556e/a7167263 playbook was written — a future cycle attempting the same remediation on a task in this shape should expect the same rejection until the policy table is amended or an authorized actor intervenes.

When a blocked task lands through the merge queue, close-out order matters: set the task done BEFORE closing its L2 escalations. Closing the escalations while the task is still 'blocked' re-arms the stranded-blocked sweep, which can re-pend an already-landed task. For task 6082 this was handled by writing an interim result.md handoff naming the finishing steps. The escalation-watcher picked it up after landing, set 6082 done, and closed esc-6082-13/-17 within about 2h. Writing the interim handoff early paid off because the session's fused-memory connection dropped twice during the wait. The later set_task_status(done, merged provenance) returned no_op with done_provenance_repaired=true, so re-stamping provenance on an already-done task is safe.

The merge worker AUTO-FLIPS a task to `done` (with done_provenance) only when a LIVE WORKFLOW exists to flip it. A task that was parked `blocked` and whose merge was submitted BY HAND stays `blocked` after its merge lands, and needs an explicit `set_task_status(id,'done', done_provenance={kind:'merged', commit:<sha>})`. Measured on reify 2026-08-20/21: tasks 5481, 5730, 6353, 5627 and 6107 all auto-flipped on landing, but task 6393 did NOT — it had been parked blocked since a warm-lane acquire fault and its merge was hand-submitted, so it sat `blocked` with its merge already on main until set manually. WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND BOOKKEEPING: an escalation held open as an anti-clobber pin can only be safely closed with `close_only` once the task is TERMINAL — closing while the task is still `blocked` leaves a blocked-task-with-no-open-escalation window that the stranded-blocked sweep can re-pend and re-dispatch into. So the correct sequence for a hand-submitted merge is: merge lands -> set task done -> THEN close_only the pin.

Cancelling a reify task whose warm lane is held by a dead agent releases the lane promptly — the terminal-task lane reclamation path works end to end. Verified 2026-08-05: task 5717 was holding warm lane _lane-27 with a dead owner_pid, zero commits, and null claimant_run_id/heartbeat_at. Within roughly one hour of setting the task to cancelled via mcp__fused-memory__set_task_status, _lane-27 had been reclaimed and reassigned to a different task's branch (task/5284), and the refs/heads/task/5717 branch had been deleted. This is the observable confirmation that DF task 2891's conservative reclaim policy (release ONLY lanes whose assigned task is terminal — done/cancelled — never lanes assigned to pending/in-progress/blocked tasks) fires on the cancelled transition. Practical consequence: when triage identifies a leaked lane held by a task that ought to die anyway, cancelling the task is sufficient remediation; no manual lane reclaim is needed.

SYSTEMIC PATTERN (Stage 1 remediation, run 64f89bb4-8526-4b3d-b8f5-ea5b1204484e, 2026-08-12): stale/stranded in-progress claimant checks on reify tasks have so far been escalation-triggered spot checks on individual tasks, which undercounts. This cycle confirmed TWO distinct mechanisms each recur across MULTIPLE sibling tasks that a single-task check misses:
(1) DEAD-CLAIMANT-PID SHARING — a claimant PID confirmed dead for one task is frequently ALSO the (still-uncleared) claimant PID for one or more OTHER in-progress tasks, because several tasks were dispatched under the same orchestrator run/process before it died. Confirmed this cycle: pid=998922 (run-2f0541d7fcac) was the dead claimant for tasks 6091 and 6093 (cleared) AND ALSO for task 5784 (uncleared at check time); pid=1789361 (run-5142ee1e5f4a) was the dead claimant for task 6128 (cleared, see edge c81833ad-6117-440e-9d2a-7796d4815f77) AND ALSO for task 5344 (uncleared at check time). RECOMMENDATION: once a claimant PID is confirmed dead for any one task, search/sweep ALL in-progress tasks for the same claimant_run_id PID or run-prefix before closing out the check.
(2) NO-CLAIMANT REQUEUE-RACE SHARING — the existing companion pattern (mem0 a7167263-d3fa-48ab-afc7-d73fde91e337, itself companion to 0b40556e-3328-4969-8c9a-89df1eb7754f) recurs across sibling tasks too: tasks 6068 (previously flagged), 5481 and 5623 (this cycle) all show status=in-progress, claimant_run_id=null, heartbeat_at=null, and multi-day-stale updatedAt — the same requeue-race signature. RECOMMENDATION: periodically sweep ALL in-progress tasks for (heartbeat_at older than N hours) OR (claimant_run_id=null AND updatedAt older than N hours), rather than relying on ad hoc discovery per escalation. A project-wide sweep of ALL in-progress tasks (not just escalation-triggered ones) would have caught 5344/5481/5623/5627/5784 in one pass instead of five separate spot checks. Stage 1 holds no task-write tool (set_task_claimant/set_task_status are Stage 2's job) so this sweep's remediation step must still relay to Stage 2/operator, but the DISCOVERY step (searching for shared PIDs / no-claimant staleness across all in-progress tasks) can and should happen proactively in Stage 1/Stage 3 rather than only reactively per escalation.

Stage 2 reconciliation (run 5e5f9dd7-02cd-4dc2-a48d-1a27e2432f8b) added only task 6068 as a companion to human-operator gate task 6260 (which already covered 5481, 5623). Reify /unblock operational facts (observed 2026-06-22): (1) `set_task_status(done, done_provenance=...)` now REQUIRES `done_provenance.kind` ∈ {"merged","found_on_main"}; use kind="merged" with commit=<merge-sha> after a merge_request, or kind="found_on_main" with note=<explanation> when a sibling task already landed it. A provenance dict without `kind` is rejected as done_provenance_invalid. (2) `.worktrees/<id>` in the main checkout is a SYMLINK to the orchestrator-managed warm-lane pool `/home/leo/src/warm-lanes/worktrees/<id>` (same inode) — the worktree the orchestrator compiles/verifies in IS the one you read. (3) Do NOT manually `git worktree remove` a warm-lane-pool worktree during /unblock cleanup; it risks desyncing the pool's lane accounting. Let the orchestrator's GC (scripts/warm-lane-gc.sh, landed as task 4717) reclaim the merged cold worktree. This is a deliberate deviation from the generic /unblock cleanup step for this dark-factory warm-lane setup. (4) A done task's module locks (current_holders in scheduler_state) release on the next scheduler acquire_next tick, not synchronously — reconciliation is async.

This check invalidated the stranding premise (null claimant/heartbeat, no live-workflow signal, as of prior run 0fefde09-fba2-4df4-8071-f9ba5c62ee7a) behind human-operator escalation gate task 5946. At this same check, task 5946 was transitioned blocked→cancelled (set_task_status confirmed newStatus=cancelled), consistent with the resolved pattern for sibling escalations 5928/5916/5902/5871 (each cancelled once the underlying task's stranding premise resolved via scheduler reset). Task 5885's own metadata separately records a resettled-adjudicator conclusion (2026-07-31T17:19, dry_run_proposals) that the earlier merge-verify RED was a false positive caused by an orchestrator-side scope-reaper race, not a defect in task 5885's own commits — so a future merge-verify attempt is expected to pass absent a repeat of that race.

A reify task sitting at status 'pending' while its task/<id> branch carries many unmerged commits is the ORDINARY inter-iteration state of a multi-day WIP task — it is NOT evidence of stranding. Diagnosed wrongly on 2026-08-05: task 5344 was read as "stranded (pending + 20 unmerged commits)" from a 09:48Z snapshot; by 10:13Z the orchestrator had re-dispatched it, rebased task/5344 onto current main, and by 11:19Z it held claimant_run_id=run-.../pid=<live orchestrator pid> with a heartbeat advancing every few minutes. The authoritative liveness oracle is the pair (claimant_run_id, heartbeat_at) on the task record — the same signal DF's shared.task_claimant is_stranded predicate uses — NOT the (status, branch-commit-count) shape. Always re-read the task record immediately before asserting a strand, because status flips between pending and in-progress on every iteration boundary. Acting on the false strand would have been actively harmful here: an agent was live in the lane.

content: /unblock on a PENDING task with a dead claimant (claimant_run_id set, pid gone, absent from get_task_runtime_state): release_workflow returns parked=null (it only parks in-progress tasks). Hold the task and clear the claim in ONE atomic write: set_task_status(status='deferred', claimant_run_id=null, heartbeat_at=null). Clearing the claim alone on a still-pending task would let the scheduler dispatch it out from under the manual merge. solar_challenge test technique (task 768 architect, measured 2026-10-15 on main 0a5ab70).

To drive a degenerate richardsonpy window through load.generate_load_profile without patching solar_challenge.load's private names, run monkeypatch.setattr(ElectricityProfile, "power_sim", fake).
- ElectricityProfile comes from richardsonpy.classes.stochastic_el_load_wrapper.
- fake(_wrapper, irradiation, weekend, day, occupancy) returns a (total, light, appliance) tuple of 1440-element watt arrays.
- The parameter names must match: load._simulate_stochastic_day passes them by keyword.

Facts measured for such tests:
- A real seeded window never reaches zero: seed 42 on 2024-06-21 has a minimum of 0.0379 kW.
- The raw unscaled energy is far from the target: 11.4 kWh against 7.45 kWh for that day.
- Over a window with no clock change, the stochastic profile's energy equals the use_stochastic=False (Elexon) profile's to about 1e-16 relative, e.g. 28.8767 kWh over 2024-06-29..07-02. A test can therefore use the Elexon path as the oracle instead of re-deriving annual/365 x SEASONAL_FACTORS.

solar_challenge gotcha (verified 2026-10-03 at main 684c9ec, task 431): task 285's TMY scaling (weather.get_tmy_data, merge a4bd993) multiplies ONLY ghi/dni/dhi (weather.IRRADIANCE_COLUMNS); temp_air and wind_speed are PVGIS's unchanged values, and heat-pump load is built from weather_data['temp_air'] alone (home.py ~L279), so heat-pump load does NOT move with the scaling — only figures that depend on PV generation do (yields, bills, and solve_cost_recovery_rate on its default simulate=None path: finance.py -> fleet.simulate_fleet -> home.simulate_home -> get_tmy_data). A task text claiming 'heat-pump temperature' changes since the v0.5.0 tag (as task 431's did) is wrong. The v0.5.0 tag fetched via pvlib 0.15.1's unversioned default URL 'https://re.jrc.ec.europa.eu/api/'; main pins weather.PVGIS_API_URL = v5_3, which served the identical TMY when task 285 measured it.

solar_challenge load.py gotcha (measured 2026-10-14 on main e5d7e80, task 711 architect, CPython 3.12.3): both load paths step through the window's days by adding an absolute pd.Timedelta(days=1) to a tz-aware Europe/London midnight. (1) If the window starts in BST and crosses the autumn clock change, every later day is labelled 23:00 on the previous date, so its month (and richardsonpy's day_of_year/weekday) is a day early. A deterministic 2024-07-01..2025-06-30 profile (3,400 kWh) totals 3,323.6 kWh instead of 3,325.0. (2) _generate_elexon_profile's `while current_date <= end_date` drops the last day of a window that starts in GMT and ends in BST, because that day's label is 01:00 BST, after the 00:00 end. The trim/pad block then fills that day with the previous day's mean power: 2024-03-30..04-01 gives 30.3128 kWh, with April 1 at March's seasonal factor. Calendar-year windows (Jan 1-Dec 31) label every day correctly. Review finding R6 (fk-1d920c89e872) covers DST placement in these loops. Cost for test design: a seeded stochastic full calendar year takes about 25 s (365 richardsonpy days); a deterministic Elexon year takes about 0.1 s.

solar_challenge perf fact, measured 2026-09-29 on branch task/150 (base main efe3145), CPython 3.12.3, with the Bristol TMY read from .cache/weather:
- A cProfile of a 1-day simulate_home took 15.8 s. 12.6 s of that was in home._align_tmy_to_demand, which runs DatetimeIndex.strftime('%m-%d %H:%M') over the full-year, 1-minute TMY index (~525,600 stamps) and builds a string-keyed dict from it. That accounts for 8.2 s of strftime and about 3 s of pyarrow string iteration.
- Another 2.2 s was pv.create_pv_system, which reparses the CEC SAM tables through pvlib.retrieve_sam on every call.
- This fixed cost does not scale with the simulated period, which is why one real web job costs about 7-15 s whether days is 1, 7 or 30. Every fleet home pays it.
Follow-up ticket: tkt_0RV7JG7AG13P2DB5WWPDTEV5TG (agent-followup-150).
[Scope note added 2026-09-30 by recon Stage 1 run f8721c18: these figures describe main BEFORE task 164. Task 164 merged as 4c489d531e3861e1dfaeccb77f027df14bde6111 (vectorised _align_tmy_to_demand, CEC SAM caching, characterization tests; see completion memory 05bcadd5-9453-4ab7-8368-ddf0376ab357).]
[Re-measured 2026-09-30 (recon Stage 1 run 2bb6eceb pointer): on main 3a144b1, which includes 4c489d5, a real 1-day home job completes in about 0.6-1.25 s. See memory bfbddbe4-dec2-4cac-b8c4-6be3b8407a07. The 15.8 s / 7-15 s figures above are historical.]

content: solar_challenge test gotcha, measured by the task 794 implementer on 2026-10-17 (CPython 3.12): to simulate a Bristol January week offline with tests/_synthetic_weather.py::synthetic_june_weather, scale the clear June day's irradiance by 0.11. That is Bristol's January GHI (25.8 kWh/m² over 31 days in the TMY get_tmy_data returns: docs/tmy-irradiation-scaling.md's 23.9 raw × 1.078) as a share of the clear June day's 7.43 kWh/m². On the Economy 7 home (4 kW PV, 5 kWh battery, 3400 kWh/yr, seed 42) over 2024-01-15..21, 0.11 gives generation 16.6 kWh, grid_dependency_ratio 0.776 and net £14.62. Scale 0.3 gives gdr 0.359. Scale 0.234, which matches the real week's 40.5 kWh yield, gives gdr 0.494, because the June day's shape puts energy into hours when the January sun is down. tests/integration/test_tariff_integration.py::test_winter_period_costs passes 0.11 through weather_data (branch task/794, not yet merged when this was written).

0145b9b2-8b23-4189-906b-c919f0c2b437.content: solar_challenge test gotcha (measured 2026-10-01 while planning task 237, main bf5fd36, pandas 3.0.3): WeatherCache cannot round-trip a DataFrame whose index spans two UTC offsets. put() writes the CSV with mixed +00:00/+01:00 timestamps, get()'s read_csv(parse_dates=True) returns an object Index, and get() raises AttributeError "'Index' object has no attribute 'tz'". Example: synthetic_june_weather("2024-01-01", irradiance_scale_per_day=(1.0,) * 365), a full Europe/London year. So a test that serves a full synthetic TMY year through set_weather_cache, e.g. for a heat pump, which needs 8760-8784 hourly rows, must index the year in UTC, the PVGIS TMY shape: pd.date_range("1990-01-01", periods=8760, freq="h", tz="UTC"), or .tz_convert("UTC"). A one-day June frame (all +01:00) round-trips fine. Production is unaffected, because get_tmy_data caches only PVGIS TMYs, which are UTC.

75c663e5-6cf6-471b-be93-a70dd81e7340.content: solar_challenge CLI test technique (task 731, measured 2026-10-15 on task/731 at 3d067d2, based on main ece941b, pandas 3.0.3): check what a command simulated through its `-o` CSV, with no seed and no spy on cli.home.simulate_home. LoadConfig's default stochastic load is random minute to minute, but load._try_richardsonpy_profile rescales the window to the sum of annual/365 x SEASONAL_FACTORS[month], so pd.read_csv(csv, index_col=0, parse_dates=True)["demand_kw"].sum() equals generate_load_profile(LoadConfig(...), day, day).sum() under pytest.approx (tests/unit/test_cli_home_quick.py; six repeat runs green; reintroducing the old 3400 default, or dropping the -c value, fails exactly its own case). A time of day on the start timestamp does not reach the CSV: the load generators normalise the window to whole days, and `home quick` mutated to start at 2024-06-01 06:00 still saved a CSV from 00:00.

scripts/legibility/census.py routes every LLM call through the coder invoke seam `invoke(prompt, model)`, which by default is `coder._invoke_cli` bearing `coder._DEFAULT_INVOKE_TIMEOUT_SECS = 120` (sized for one Haiku trickle-coding call). run_census reuses that ONE invoke for the headroom probe AND mining AND (via _build_default_verify_fn / _build_default_synthesize_fn) verification and synthesis. Census verify (one Sonnet CLI call per novel cluster exploring current main) and synthesis (one large Fable call over all clusters) cannot finish in 120s, so a real census fails with 'claude CLI timed out after 120s'. Fix pattern (task 2951): thread per-stage timeouts via functools.partial(coder._invoke_cli, timeout=cfg.timeouts.<stage>_secs) — verify ~900s, synthesis ~1800s, mining/headroom keep ~120s — from a new optional `timeouts:` block in config.py (LegibilityConfig.timeouts). coder._invoke_cli already accepts keyword-only `timeout`; no coder.py change is needed, only the value main() feeds each stage.

Robust membership: enumerate by cheap encoded-prefix pre-filter, then confirm each session by reading its real 'cwd' field from a transcript line and applying Path(cwd).is_relative_to(prefix) path-component semantics — that correctly excludes cockpit and includes .worktrees/.claude-worktrees children. The main dir '-home-leo-src-dark-factory' holds ~18k .jsonl sessions including cross-project reconciliation agents (recon runs with cwd=dark-factory but processes reify/solar_challenge/etc.).

Completed: Grammar has no method-call-with-arguments rule: obj.map(|v| ...) / .filter / .all / .any are parse errors, leaving reify-expr's method arms unreachable from .ri source
Description: Discovered while planning task #5385 (generate-of-geometry silent undef); see escalation esc-5385-1. OUT OF SCOPE for #5385, which delivers only the generate + union_all halves of its acceptance criteria.

OBSERVATION (measured on HEAD 975cbfc301 with target/debug/reify built 2026-08-21): the tree-sitter grammar has NO method-call-with-arguments rule. In tree-sitter-reify/grammar.js, `member_access` (grammar.js:1583-1587) is `prec.left(11, seq(field('object', $._expression), '.', field('member', $.identifier)))` — no callTail. The only argument-taking call rules are `function_call` (grammar.js:1572, bare identifier + callTail) and `trait_method_call` (grammar.js:1642, qualified/instance-qualified callee + callTail).

Consequences measured directly:
- `let ys = xs.map(|v| v + 1)` over `let xs = [1, 2, 3]` => "Parse error: invalid let". Same for `xs.filter(|v| v > 1)`, `xs.all(|v| v > 0)`, `xs.any(...)`, and even `xs.foo(|v| v)` — so the gap is method-ARGUMENTS, not lambdas and not element type.
- `constraint all_pos: xs.all(|v| v > 0)` => "Parse error: invalid constraint" — not let-position-specific.
- Free-function forms `map(xs, |v| v)` / `filter(xs, |v| v > 1)` also fail; no free-function map/filter exists.
- `generate(3, |i| i)` and `flat_map(xs, |v| [v])` DO parse (both `function_call`); `xs.count` parses (bare `member_access`, no parens). So lambdas work and member access works — only method arguments are missing.

DEAD CODE this leaves behind: the `"map"`, `"filter"`, `"all"`, `"any"`, `"generate"` arms of `eval_method_call` in crates/reify-expr/src/lib.rs (lines ~3695, ~3825, ~3714, ~3739, ~3811) are unreachable from .ri source and exercised only by Rust-level tests. crates/reify-expr/src/lib.rs:3798-3810 even documents a deliberate negative-count policy divergence between the free-function and METHOD forms of `generate` — a distinction no .ri program can observe.

WORK TO DECIDE/DO (triage first, this is a design question, not a mechanical fix):
(a) add an `obj.method(args)` rule to tree-sitter-reify/grammar.js plus the corresponding lowering in crates/reify-syntax/src/ts_parser.rs, so the existing evaluator arms become reachable; or
(b) expose the wanted combinators as free functions instead (the shape `generate` and `flat_map` already use) and delete or clearly mark the unreachable method arms; or
(c) accept the gap deliberately and document it, marking the unreachable arms so future readers do not assume surface coverage.

Files: tree-sitter-reify/grammar.js, crates/reify-syntax/src/ts_parser.rs, crates/reify-expr/src/lib.rs.

Rationale for filing: leaving evaluator arms with no surface form is a silent-capability-gap — a design session reading the stdlib docs would reasonably write `xs.filter(...)` and get an opaque "invalid let" parse error rather than an unsupported-construct diagnostic.
Analysis: TRIAGE (the task asks for a design decision first).

That prepend existed because `compile_builder::pre_pass::forward_parse_errors` used to emit parse errors as `Diagnostic::warning`, so tests needed a way to see them as errors.

WHAT CHANGED. Task #5392 promoted `forward_parse_errors` to emit `Diagnostic::error(format!("parse error: {}", err.message))` on the single-module path (crates/reify-compiler/src/compile_builder/pre_pass.rs:37-44), aligning it with the module-DAG path. The remaining call sites still measure through the doubling helper.

SCOPE. Remove the prepend from `compile_source_with_stdlib_allow_parse_errors` so it simply delegates to `compile_with_stdlib`, and check the sibling helper at helpers.rs:344 which calls `parse_errors_as_diagnostics` too. 13 call sites across 6 files: crates/reify-compiler/tests/harness_doc_chunks/angle_crossings_diagnostics_smoke.rs, crates/reify-compiler/tests/harness_doc_chunks/enums_chunk_option_smoke.rs, crates/reify-compiler/tests/harness_modules_ports/sub_placement_lowering_tests.rs, crates/reify-compiler/tests/harness_units_materials/unit_registry_tests.rs, crates/reify-eval/tests/harness_auto_resolution/auto_type_param_determinism_tests.rs, crates/reify-eval/tests/harness_engine/fn_body_separator_value_faithfulness.rs. RELATED. Sibling of #6156 (extend #5392's parse-error-quality treatment to the remaining ERROR arms in ts_parser.rs); #6156's own description already flags this helper as a trap for severity-measuring tests.

Description: Found during printer_v01 dogfood (2026-08-26, O1 round). MINIMAL REPRO: a square-section dims solve `let h = sqrt(sqrt(12 * ixx))` then `solve_elastic_static(material, span, h, h, [load], [mount], ElasticOptions())` — passing the SAME let cell as both width and height. `reify eval` panics the whole process at crates/reify-eval/src/compute_cache_key.rs:99: "compute_cache_key: value_inputs contains duplicate ValueCellId — producer bug".

The panic policy (pinned by task 3503's tests) assumed duplicate value_inputs can only arise from a producer bug — but a user design legitimately passes one cell to two parameters (square sections, symmetric spans, shared dimensions are everyday authoring shapes). WORKAROUND used in prj/printer_v01/printer.ri: clone cells (`let h_eq2 = h_eq * 1.0`) — works but is exactly the kind of incantation dogfooding exists to remove.

Completed: reify.toml [[node_overrides]] parses a commitment policy that nothing enforces
Description: Filed as follow-up from task #7073, which measured this while deciding the fate of `NodePolicyOverrides::resolve` but had no scope to resolve it.

OBSERVATION (measured by grep across crates/ and gui/ on task/7073, and confirmed by `cargo check --workspace --all-targets` exit 0 after #7073's deletion): the whole `reify.toml` `[[node_overrides]]` → commitment-policy pipeline is production-orphaned except for one read-only diagnostic path.

- `NodePolicyOverrides::from_config_overrides` (crates/reify-runtime/src/commitment.rs) — the function that turns `[[node_overrides]]` manifest entries into instance/type overrides — has no production caller. Every caller is a test (crates/reify-runtime/tests/node_overrides_config.rs, plus the unit tests in commitment.rs).
- `check_commitment` and `CommitmentTracker` in the same file — the code that would actually ENFORCE a resolved policy (commit / never-commit / not-yet decisions) — likewise have no production caller.

Hypothesis (NOT verified): this is the same deletion fallout as the gating helpers #7073 re-cited to #5023, so the natural consumer is likely async-recalc Phase A (#5023) or whatever re-introduces a scheduler. Someone should decide deliberately whether to (a) wire the config through to a real enforcement point, (b) delete the config surface and its schema-doc section, or (c) mark it explicitly reserved/not-yet-enforced in docs/notes/reify-toml-schema.md so users are not misled. #7073 deliberately did NOT touch these symbols; it removed only `NodePolicyOverrides::resolve`, which was a true duplicate of `resolve_with_traits` rather than an awaiting-consumer orphan.

Relevant files: crates/reify-runtime/src/commitment.rs, crates/reify-runtime/tests/node_overrides_config.rs, crates/reify-cli/src/dev.rs, docs/notes/reify-toml-schema.md.
Analysis: DECISION: option (c). Keep the `[[node_overrides]]` surface. Mark it explicitly as reserved and not enforced. Correct every pointer that currently lies about it. Do NOT wire it (a) and do NOT delete it (b).

Description: The Rust ShellStress container (pub, re-exported at the crate root) has no production consumer. Outside shell_result.rs's own tests and a lib.rs doc example, nothing constructs or reads it; the DSL-side `structure def ShellStress` in solver_elastic.ri is filled through flatten_shell_channels' four Vec<f64> buffers in reify-eval's compute_targets/shell_solve.rs, not through this type. Completed: Billing push: a provider refusal leaves a dangling Stripe invoice and crashes scp-bill --account; the collected-payment cancel differs between fake and real
Description: FINDING (review 20260928T062907). Traced by a review sub-agent at HEAD 3d74313, with file:line evidence. Re-verify the line numbers before editing.

1. NOTHING CATCHES ProviderRefusal. A repo-wide grep finds no `except ProviderRefusal`. runtime/roles/bill.py::_bill_single_account (≈:327-374) turns ConsentDenied, BillingOrderError and PropertyOfRecordMismatch into tagged `[TAG] … nothing persisted` lines. A refusal from dd.schedule() instead escapes as a raw traceback. The fleet close is fine: fleet_run.py:203-215 catches Exception per account.

2. PUSH ORDER BREAKS "pushes NOTHING". billing/status.py (≈:386-391) creates the Stripe invoice before it schedules the GoCardless DD, and store.put (≈:301-303) comes after both. When the DD is refused, the Stripe invoice already exists but no BillingRun is persisted. One reachable trigger: dd._require_collectable (billing/dd.py:33-40) checks only amount > 0, and the real GoCardless £1.00 minimum is "not modelled" (billing/cassettes/README.md:27-31). A 1-99p amount due therefore passes locally and is refused by the real rail. Suggested fix: check collectability, including a governed or constant rail minimum, before any provider call, and hold or skip with a typed reason. Alternatively, void the Stripe invoice when the DD is refused. Add a fake-lane test showing that a refused DD leaves no Stripe invoice.

3. cancel_payment IGNORES COLLECTED STATUS, AND FAKE AND REAL DIFFER. DirectDebit.recalculate (dd.py:70-96) cancels `current` with no status check. FakeGoCardless.cancel_payment (billing/providers/fakes.py:293-302) quietly turns a CONFIRMED (collected) payment into CANCELLED. The real GoCardlessDirectDebit.cancel_payment (billing/providers/gocardless.py:185-187) lets gocardless_pro InvalidStateError through untranslated, unlike create_payment, which maps errors to ProviderRefusal. Make both refuse a collected payment the same way, through the contract.ProviderRefusal port. Note that recalculate has no production caller: status.py only calls schedule(). Keep it, since task 347 pins it, but its refusal of a negative revision should be a named exception, not a bare ValueError (dd.py:33-40).

Out of scope (latent, noted only): Stripe item, invoice and meter-event keys come from reference_key(account, period) with no revision component (billing/providers/stripe.py:167,172,202,259). A re-price of an already-pushed period would silently reuse the original items. No production path re-prices today.

Completed: Fleet monthly close bills each account from its own last statement (automatic D7 catch-up)
Description: RULING (Leo, 2026-09-27, resolves esc-review-cycle-20260924T054202-3, option A): the fleet runner derives each account's period start from its OWN statement of record (or from opened_on for a first bill), up to the close boundary — automatic D7 catch-up. Do not re-decide this; options B (report-only "needs catch-up" bucket) and C (manual --account catch-up) were rejected.

DEFECT (from code reading, not reproduced end to end):
- billing/fleet_run.py bills ONE shared period P for every rostered account (D9 of docs/prds/scaling-defects-1k-10k.md).
- BillingService.run_billing (billing/statement.py) raises BillingOrderError when a period does not start at the account's statement-of-record period_end (R3 contiguity), and returns SkippedAccount('register_unavailable') without persisting when a boundary register is unreadable.
- So ONE register_unavailable skip in month M makes that account raise BillingOrderError at every later close from M+1 onward: the close reports it failed and scp-bill exits 1, every month, until someone runs a manual --account catch-up.
- Worse, if the skipped month was the account's FIRST month (no statement of record yet), the next close bills it from P's start, so the skipped first month is silently never billed.

REQUIREMENTS
1. For each rostered account, the close computes the start as the statement of record's period_end, or opened_on (clamped to its billing-period start rule) for a never-billed account, and bills [start, close boundary). A normal month is unchanged: start == P.start, one statement, byte-identical to today.
2. Idempotent re-run: a re-run of the same close finds an already-billed catch-up period (via run_billing's idempotent read-through of the statement of record) and REPORTS it as already billed; it never re-bills or re-pushes to Stripe/GoCardless.
3. Back-billing window — DECISION FOR LEO, DO NOT SILENTLY PICK. scp-bill applies no back-billing bound today: BillingService is constructed without as_of, so check_back_billing (billing/tariff.py) and BillingConfig.back_billing_window_months (default 12) never run on the close path. Automatic catch-up makes this matter. PROPOSED bound: construct the close's BillingService with as_of = the close date so the existing 12-month back_billing_window_months guard applies, and report an out-of-window account as a distinct, named class in FleetBillingSummary (never silently dropped, never billed). The implementer must write this proposal into the plan and escalate it (escalate_info / design decision) for Leo's confirmation before shipping any bound; do not choose a different window or skip the guard on your own.
4. Multi-month catch-up presentation: decide and document how a catch-up spanning more than one month is presented (one statement covering the whole gap vs one statement per calendar month), keeping R3 contiguity, the member portal statement list and the Stripe/GoCardless push coherent; record the choice in docs (D9 amendment) and in the close summary (e.g. a catch_up count naming each account and its billed span).
5. The close summary / scp-bill output names each caught-up account and its span; close_succeeded semantics stay honest (a caught-up account is a success, a BillingOrderError is still a failure).

TESTS
- Skip-then-catch-up: an account skipped register_unavailable in month M is billed [M.start, M+2.start) (or per the chosen presentation) at the M+1 close, with no BillingOrderError and scp-bill exit 0.
- First-month skip: a never-billed account skipped in its first month is billed from opened_on at the next close; the first month is NOT lost.
- Re-run idempotency: re-running the same close reports the catch-up as already billed, creates no second statement and makes no second provider push.
- Existing tests/billing/test_fleet_run.py and tests/cli/test_cli_bill_fleet.py stay green; pytest -m 'not slow' + mypy green.

GOTCHA (dark-factory, measured 2026-09-04, task 3517): the orchestrator's per-module verify/debug command passes `-o addopts=`, which WIPES the pyproject `-m 'not integration'` deselection and makes live, paid, OAuth-dependent integration tests RUN inside the verify gate. This contradicts the existing norm that "the pyproject addopts deselects the marked test automatically — no verify-command change needed": that holds for the merge-lane sweep, NOT for the verify/debug path.

MEASURED. Verify cmd: `cd shared && uv run pytest --tb=short -q --timeout=300 -p no:xdist -o addopts= tests/`. shared/pyproject.toml sets `addopts = "-m 'not integration'"` and the repo-root pyproject.toml mirrors it. Collection of shared/tests/test_cli_invoke_integration.py: with default addopts -> "no tests collected (5 deselected)"; with `-o addopts=` -> "5 tests collected". Those 5 make real Claude API calls against real OAuth accounts.

CONSEQUENCE. Task 3517's attempt-1 verify went red on `TestCrossAccountResume::test_invoke_returns_session_id` with `success=False, api_error_status=429, output="You've hit your weekly limit · resets 1pm (Europe/London)"` — an account rate limit, on a branch whose diff touched only two unrelated files. Any shared/-touching or fused-memory-touching task can be turned red this way by an account cap, and no code change in the task's scope can fix it.

WHAT TO DO. If you are debugging a verify failure in a test named *_integration.py or decorated @pytest.mark.integration, check FIRST whether it is a live-service test that the module's own addopts deselects — if so the failure is infra, not your task, and belongs in escalate_blocker with category='infra_issue', not in a code fix. Do NOT "fix" it by adding a module-level pytestmark or editing the test. Note the related, opposite trap already recorded: adding a CLI `-m` to a module test_command also clobbers the ini addopts.

A dark-factory task whose only collectable .py change is a test file wholly deselected by its project's pytest `addopts -m` expression gets a scoped verify command that collects 0 items and exits rc=5 ("no tests ran") — RED no matter what the task's code does. Concretely: orchestrator/pyproject.toml sets `addopts = "... -m 'not warm_lane_bash'"` (landed by task 3349 in merge 8f3f0e4c89), so `pytest orchestrator/tests/test_warm_lane_bash_suite.py` collects "no tests collected (12 deselected)" while `pytest ... -m warm_lane_bash` collects 12 and passes. Diagnose this by re-running the failing verify target with `--collect-only -q` before touching any code; the fix belongs at the verify scoping layer or the module test_command, not in the task's files.

In dark-factory, moving a pytest marker bucket off a package's verify hot path belongs in `<pkg>/pyproject.toml` `[tool.pytest.ini_options] addopts` (e.g. `-m 'not warm_lane_bash'`), NOT in the per-package `<pkg>/orchestrator.yaml` `test_command`. Those per-package yamls are ~8-line verify-scoping configs whose `test_command` is a bare directory-arg pytest with no `-m` of its own, so the pyproject edit covers both the merge-verify invocation and a bare local `pytest` from one place with no risk of two marker spellings drifting apart. This is the shipped `integration` precedent in shared/pyproject.toml and fused-memory/pyproject.toml, and was re-confirmed for `warm_lane_bash` by task 3349.

Correction to the task-5079 peer under topic pytest-xdist-serial-override, which advised deriving the serial-recovery `-o addopts=` from the module's UNSCOPED test_command via the cwd rule. That is insufficient at `orchestrator/src/orchestrator/verify.py::run_verification`'s ENV_TRANSIENT recovery: the command recovered there is often already scoped and cwd-stripped (FILE_SCOPED runs from `_executed_module_configs_from_plan` render `_scope_prefix_to_keyword` output ending in `strip_cwd`; reverse-dependency widening; flake-site commands), and no unscoped command is in scope. The cwd rule then names the repo-root pyproject for `uv run --project orchestrator pytest orchestrator/tests/x.py`, while pytest actually reads `orchestrator/pyproject.toml`. The faithful answer is pytest's own walk (`_pytest/config/findpaths.py::locate_config`): start at the positional args' common ancestor (or the invocation dir when there are none) and walk up. In each directory, check pytest.toml, .pytest.toml, pytest.ini, .pytest.ini, pyproject.toml (only with a non-empty [tool.pytest] table), tox.ini ([pytest] section), setup.cfg ([tool:pytest]), in that order. Measured 2026-10-08 on shared: a blank `-o addopts=` collected 6939 tests, while `-o "addopts=-m 'not integration'"` collected 6928/6939 (11 deselected).

Gotcha for default-ON verify features in orchestrator/verify.py: enabling a new verify knob by default routes the ENTIRE existing verify test suite through the new code path. If the change wraps the pytest command (e.g. `<nice argv> /bin/bash -c <shlex.quote(cmd)>`), shlex.quote mangles substring assertions many verify tests rely on (e.g. test_verify_env_transient.py matches `-o addopts=''`, which stops being a contiguous substring once single-quote-escaped), and a shared /tmp resource (flock slots dir) contends across xdist workers. Clean mitigation: funnel the enable-check through ONE module seam (e.g. verify._verify_admission_active(config)) and add an autouse conftest fixture that monkeypatches that seam to a no-op for every test EXCEPT those with an opt-in marker — mirroring the blessed `_mock_merge_queue_verification` autouse+`exercise_merge_verify` marker pattern (conftest.py:231, marker registered in orchestrator/pyproject.toml markers=[...]). This keeps legacy tests byte-identical without editing dozens of assertions; new-feature tests opt in via the marker. Guard the fixture on hasattr(verify, '<seam>') so it stays inert (green) on commits before the seam lands.

GOTCHA (dark-factory, orchestrator/src/orchestrator/verify.py::_serial_pytest_str, measured 2026-09-04 on the task/4377 worktree): a verify leg can go RED for a reason that has nothing to do with the branch under test, because the SERIAL RE-RUN silently changes pytest's configuration. When you see a verify failure that reproduces only under the recorded verify command and not under a hand-run pytest, check this FIRST.

MECHANISM. _serial_pytest_str rewrites every pytest invocation to `... -p no:xdist -o addopts=`. Its docstring states the intent narrowly — clear the pyproject-level `-n auto`, per task 2045's shared-venv-mutation recovery. But `-o addopts=` is a WHOLESALE BLANK, not a targeted removal, so it drops every other token the root addopts carries. Root pyproject.toml carries two more, BOTH load-bearing:
    addopts = "--import-mode=importlib -m 'not smoke and not integration and not warm_lane_bash'"

TWO CONSEQUENCES, and the second is the one people miss.
(1) COLLECTION MODE. Losing --import-mode=importlib reverts pytest to prepend mode. Any command collecting two directories that share a basename with no __init__.py then dies with "import file mismatch". This is not hypothetical: the `scripts` module test_command is a deliberate UNION of tests/scripts/ and scripts/tests/ (task 3384/3460), which share conftest.py, test_restart_all_orchestrators.py and test_reviewer_redundancy_diagnostic.py. dark-factory-orchestrator.yaml states the union's safety argument and rests it EXPLICITLY on root addopts setting importlib — so the documented invariant and the serial rewrite contradict each other.
(2) MARKER SELECTION. Losing `-m 'not smoke and not integration and not warm_lane_bash'` means the serial re-run COLLECTS AND RUNS the smoke/integration/warm_lane_bash buckets every normal run deselects. A recovery re-run therefore does not execute the same test SET as the run it is recovering, and can go red on tests the primary path never intended to run. cockpit/tests/test_root_config_smoke_deselection.py already names this hazard in a comment: a bare `-o addopts=` "would silently run collection under different semantics than every real root-bound run".

MEASURED, single variable, HEAD=40204bf476:
  `uv run --project shared pytest --tb=short -q --timeout=300 -p no:xdist -o addopts= tests/scripts/ scripts/tests/`
    -> 4197 collected + 2 collection errors, rc=2
  same command + `--import-mode=importlib`
    -> 4218 collected; full suite 4216 passed / 2 skipped, rc=0

HOW TO RECOGNISE IT. The tell is a verify leg reporting COLLECTION errors ("N errors", not "N failed") on files the branch never touched. Confirm with `git diff --name-only main...HEAD` — if none of the colliding files is in the diff, the branch is innocent. Then A/B the recorded verify command against the same command with the missing addopts token restored; that isolates it in one step.

THE CORRECT FIX SHAPE, when you fix it rather than work around it: derive the override from root pyproject.toml and strip ONLY the token you mean to strip, rather than blanking. The in-repo precedent is cockpit/tests/test_root_config_smoke_deselection.py::_addopts_without_marker_filter. Note `-p no:xdist` is appended independently and disables the plugin outright, so removing `-n auto` is already belt-and-suspenders — nothing about task 2045's intent requires the blank.

STATUS as of 2026-09-04: scripts/orchestrator.yaml now pins --import-mode=importlib explicitly on its test_command (steward fix for esc-4377-3, commit 9c657d48ca). That is a per-module unblock for consequence (1) ONLY — it does nothing for consequence (2), and nothing for any other module whose collection or selection depends on a root addopts token. The general fix is filed as a follow-up. So do NOT assume this trap is disarmed fleet-wide.

FIFTH distinct failure mode, stamped peer under topic `pytest-xdist-serial-override` (canonical 8bb3eb15 documents: (1) `-p no:xdist` "unrecognized arguments", (2) silent `worker_id` fixture loss, (3) worker crash under load as a flake; peer 492b6200 documents (4) cross-worker collection mismatch). This one is about the OTHER half of `_serial_pytest_str`'s flag pair — the `-o addopts=` — and it is a defect in dark-factory itself, not a pytest quirk. Task 5079, measured 2026-09-05.

THE DEFECT. `-o addopts=<value>` is a WHOLESALE REPLACEMENT of the ini `addopts`, never a targeted removal. `orchestrator/src/orchestrator/verify.py::_serial_pytest_str` appends a BARE `-o addopts=`, whose docstring states its intent narrowly (clear `-n auto` per task 2045). It also drops every OTHER token the resolved addopts carries. Root pyproject.toml carries two more, both load-bearing: `--import-mode=importlib` and `-m 'not smoke and not integration and not warm_lane_bash'`.

MEASURED, single variable, `uv run --project shared pytest tests/scripts/ scripts/tests/ --collect-only -p no:xdist` (the `scripts` module test_command):
  `-o addopts=`                     -> 4583 collected + 2 "import file mismatch" errors, collection INTERRUPTED (rc=2)
  `-o 'addopts=<root addopts>'`     -> 4594/4604 collected (10 deselected), clean
Cause of the errors: that test_command is a deliberate UNION of two directories sharing three basenames (conftest.py, test_restart_all_orchestrators.py, test_reviewer_redundancy_diagnostic.py) with no `__init__.py` in either — only importlib import mode can collect it. Surfaced as esc-4377-3, which red-legged an unrelated task's verify. The second, wider consequence: dropping the `-m` filter makes a serial recovery run COLLECT AND RUN the smoke/integration/warm_lane_bash buckets every normal run deselects, so the recovery does not execute the same test set as the run it is recovering.

WHY YOU CANNOT JUST USE `-n0` HERE — a boundary on the canonical entry's advice, not a contradiction. The canonical calls `-n0` "the ONE reliably robust workaround", and for a hand-run local invocation it is. It does NOT work for the automated serial-recovery path, because that path exists for task 2045's shared-venv-mutation transient where xdist has VANISHED from the venv (verify.py logs it as "vanished xdist/pip"). With xdist absent, `-n 0` is itself an unrecognized argument. `-p no:xdist` is safe when the plugin is missing — which is exactly why the recovery uses it, and therefore why the addopts override cannot be dropped: with the plugin unregistered, any surviving xdist option in addopts fails the run. The correct shape is `-p no:xdist -o addopts=<resolved addopts MINUS the xdist tokens>`.

To prove a pytest ini setting is non-vacuous (actually changes behaviour, not merely present in the file), spawn a subprocess probe: `[sys.executable, '-m', 'pytest', str(probe_file), '-c', str(target_inifile), '-o', 'addopts=', '-p', 'no:cacheprovider', '-q']`, run twice — once against the real inifile and once against a control inifile written to tmp_path that omits the setting. `-o addopts=` genuinely clears the parent's addopts (verified), which is essential in dark-factory because orchestrator/pyproject.toml's addopts carries `-n auto` that would otherwise make the probe slow and its exit code ambiguous. Strip PYTEST_ADDOPTS/PYTEST_CURRENT_TEST/GIT_DIR/GIT_WORK_TREE/GIT_INDEX_FILE from the child env, because an inherited PYTEST_ADDOPTS overrides the child's `-o addopts=`. The control arm is what attributes the treatment failure to the setting rather than to something ambient — assert on it FIRST with a "CONTROL ARM BROKEN" message so a broken harness is never misread as a real finding.

To re-run a pytest command in load-flake-free isolation in the orchestrator verify layer, reuse verify._force_serial_pytest(cmd) — it appends `-p no:xdist -o addopts=''` to every pytest invocation, clearing pyproject addopts (including `-n auto --dist loadgroup --max-worker-restart=0`). This is the canonical `-n0`/cleared-addopts isolation (proven by task 2045). Combine with verify._scope_command(cmd,'pytest',node_ids) to narrow to specific node-ids. Note: under --max-worker-restart=0 (task 1907) a per-test timeout under CPU oversubscription degrades into a `[gwN] node down: Not properly terminated` worker-down failure that classifies as unknown_test_failure (not pytest_internalerror), so it reaches the sweep alarm path — the isolated serial re-run is what yields a clean verdict.

Orchestrator verify scopes/synthesizes the pytest command for touched-file diffs, and verify._config_test_extras only carries `--extra` flags from config.test_command into that synthesized `uv run pytest` command — NOT `--timeout`. So a per-module orchestrator.yaml `test_command ... --timeout=300` does not reach the SCOPED verify run; those tests fall back to the pyproject `timeout=60` default. Real-git+cargo integration tests (orchestrator/tests/test_atomic_train_merge.py, test_train_integration.py) therefore false-fail with "node down: Not properly terminated" under `-n auto` xdist oversubscription (a starved-but-correct workspace compile crosses 60s → pytest-timeout thread-method os._exit()s the worker). Fix: give such heavyweight modules an explicit module-level `pytestmark = pytest.mark.timeout(300)` (pyproject-sanctioned "slow tests opt out"), which overrides the ini default regardless of whether the verify command carries --timeout.

When writing a behavioral marker-deselection meta-test (mirroring cockpit/tests/test_smoke_marker_config.py) that runs `pytest --collect-only -c <pyproject>` in a subprocess against a config whose addopts contains `-n auto` (e.g. fused-memory), neutralize xdist with `-n0`, NOT `-p no:xdist`: disabling the xdist plugin while `-n auto` remains in addopts makes pytest exit `unrecognized arguments: -n` (documented in orchestrator verify_cmd.serial_pytest). Also: `--collect-only` lists items regardless of skip markers, so a module-level skipif (e.g. qdrant_skipif) does not hide node ids from the assertion; and per-subproject addopts (`-m 'not integration'`) is what governs the DEFAULT verify pass, but the orchestrator recovery/flaky-rerun path applies serial_pytest which appends `-o addopts=''` and clears it — so keep a belt-and-braces skipif on live-service tests for that path.
