THREE things that are not guessable and each of which silently breaks the run:

1. verify_env's PATH entry is LOAD-BEARING. `verify._target_subprocess_env` scrubs VIRTUAL_ENV and drops the venv's bin from PATH so a target resolves its OWN .venv — a tmp tree has none, so a bare `pytest` would not resolve at all. verify_env is overlaid LAST, so it is the supported way to put it back, with no patching of verify internals.

2. The test_command MUST be the bare `pytest` (or `uv run [--project X] pytest`) spelling. `parse_config_command('python -m pytest')` and `parse_config_command('/abs/path/to/pytest')` both return ToolKind.OPAQUE with raw retained, so EVERY mutator (with_junitxml, with_pytest_timeout, apply_pytest_numprocesses, serial_pytest) no-ops and you silently measure nothing. Note also that a structured PYTEST command RENDERS from the canonical head `pytest`, so even if `python -m pytest` parsed structurally the interpreter prefix would be dropped by render().

3. To see the argv, wrap rather than replace: `patch.object(verify_module, '_run_cmd', spy)` where the spy appends `cmd` and then awaits the REAL `_run_cmd`. Replacing it with a fake gives back the very blindness this recipe exists to remove.

WHAT IT CAUGHT: with `--timeout`/`--junitxml` absent from verify_cmd._PYTEST_VALUE_FLAGS the recipe returns `fails_in_isolation` and the captured argv reads `pytest -p no:xdist -o addopts= --timeout --junitxml <path> 300 <node>` (rc=4, `argument --timeout: expected one argument`); with the two flags bound it returns `passes_in_isolation`. Same recipe with call_site='main_probe' is NOT affected — that engine runs role='task', so junit_path stays None and no second parse happens.

GOTCHA (measured 2026-09-04, task 4377 debugger): the orchestrator's SERIAL RE-RUN path silently changes pytest collection semantics, and for the `scripts` module it turns a green suite red with 2 collection errors.

MECHANISM. `orchestrator/src/orchestrator/verify.py::_serial_pytest_str` (:1374) appends `-p no:xdist -o addopts=` to force serial pytest. Its docstring says the `-o addopts=` exists to clear `-n auto` (task 2045's shared-venv-mutation workaround). But root `pyproject.toml:66` is the SOLE carrier of `--import-mode=importlib`, so blanking addopts drops the import mode too — collateral, not intended. Under pytest's default `prepend` mode, `scripts/orchestrator.yaml:22`'s deliberate two-directory union (`pytest tests/scripts/ scripts/tests/`, task 3384) collides on the basenames shared by both dirs — today `test_restart_all_orchestrators.py` and `test_reviewer_redundancy_diagnostic.py` — because neither directory has an `__init__.py`. Result: `import file mismatch`, rc=2, "2 errors", ZERO test failures.

`dark-factory-orchestrator.yaml:105-110` states the dependency outright ("collision across the two directories' few shared basenames is safe because the root pyproject.toml sets addopts = --import-mode=importlib and neither directory has an __init__.py") — so the union command is only collision-free WHILE addopts survives, and the serial re-run is the one path that removes it.

A/B THAT PROVES IT (single variable): the recorded verify cmd `uv run --project shared pytest --tb=short -q --timeout=300 -p no:xdist -o addopts= tests/scripts/ scripts/tests/` → 2 collection errors, rc=2. Same command + `--import-mode=importlib` → 4216 passed, 2 skipped, rc=0 in 290.64s.

HOW TO RECOGNISE IT AS A DEBUGGER. Symptom is COLLECTION errors ("import file mismatch ... which is not the same as the test file we want to collect"), never assertion failures, and the failing leg's recorded `cmd` in `.task/verify/*.summary.json` contains `-o addopts=`. Before touching any code, re-run that exact cmd with `--import-mode=importlib` appended. If it goes green, the defect is the invocation, not your branch — check `git diff --name-only main...HEAD` to confirm your branch touched neither colliding directory, then escalate rather than renaming test files or adding `__init__.py` (the missing `__init__.py` is DELIBERATE and load-bearing per the yaml comment above).

THE CORRECT FIX SHAPE, already precedented in-repo: `cockpit/tests/test_root_config_smoke_deselection.py::_addopts_without_marker_filter` (:202) DERIVES an addopts override from root pyproject.toml and strips only the one token it means to strip, instead of blanking addopts wholesale. That file (:365) had already named this exact hazard in prose — "a bare `-o addopts=` ... would silently run collection under different semantics than every real root-bound run" — a year before it bit a real verify run.

BLAST RADIUS: any task whose scope resolves to the `scripts` module config and reaches the serial confirm re-run hits this deterministically; nothing about the triggering task is special beyond having touched some `scripts/*.py`. Filed as esc-4377-3.

Stamped peer under topic `pytest-xdist-serial-override`. A failure mode NEITHER the canonical (8bb3eb15) NOR the task-5079 peer (2df6373e) covers, because both reason about xdist flags arriving via ADDOPTS. This one is about xdist flags on ARGV, where `-o addopts=` has no reach AT ALL. Task 5408, measured 2026-09-15, fixed in the same task.

THE DISTINCTION THAT MATTERS. `orchestrator.verify._serial_pytest_str` recovers by appending `-p no:xdist -o addopts=`. Read the two flags separately:

Gotcha (orchestrator verify.py isolated re-run gates): `-o addopts=` clears pyproject's `[tool.pytest.ini_options] addopts` but does NOT clear its sibling `timeout` key (orchestrator/pyproject.toml:99 and fused-memory/pyproject.toml:50 both set `timeout = 60`). So every scoped+serial isolated re-run must ALSO inject an explicit generous `--timeout` via `_with_pytest_timeout_str`, or a still-loaded host starves the re-run into a false verdict. verify.py keeps three deliberately SEPARATE constants for this, one per call site, so each is retuned on its own signal: `_MERGE_FLAKE_CONFIRM_TIMEOUT_SECS` (merge gate), `_SWEEP_PREFILTER_TIMEOUT_SECS` (sweep cost pre-filter), and `_SWEEP_CONFIRM_TIMEOUT_SECS` (sweep confirm gate, added by task 3290 — it was the one site missing the injection, so a starved confirm could file a false red-main L1). Follow the per-call-site-constant convention rather than sharing one; a shared constant named for one site becomes a lie at the others.

DARK-FACTORY ALREADY HAS A LIVE, UNUSED PYTEST-XDIST WORKER CAP KNOB that partially pre-empts task 3589 — discovered 2026-08-19 while resolving reify's esc-5984-3.

`verify_admission_pytest_n` (orchestrator/src/orchestrator/config.py, a top-level OrchestratorConfig field, default 'auto' = no-op) injects `-n <N>` into the test leg. It is fully plumbed: verify.py's `_with_pytest_numprocesses_str` -> verify_cmd.py's `apply_pytest_numprocesses`, validated at config load/reload by `_validate_verify_admission_pytest_n` against pytest-xdist's own accepted values (so a typo fails loud at reload, not at verify time), and explicitly listed in RELOADABLE_FIELDS as green tier — it applies with `reload_config`, no restart, and reverts instantly. It was set nowhere in dark-factory-orchestrator.yaml.

`apply_pytest_numprocesses` carries three fail-safe no-op guards: non-pytest tools; a value of '' or 'auto' (the byte-identical guard, since the pyproject `-n auto` addopts already picks a count); and any command already forced serial by `serial_pytest` (`-p no:xdist`), which is what keeps the env-transient and flaky-scoped recovery re-runs from dying on "unrecognized arguments: -n".

CRITICAL SCOPE LIMIT — this knob is NOT a substitute for task 3589. It reaches roles {task, background} ONLY; `merge` is deliberately never -n-capped (it bypasses admission slot-counting and is latency-critical), and it touches nothing outside verify.py — in particular agent-initiated `pytest` runs during the implement phase stay completely ungoverned. Task 3589 edits `addopts` in orchestrator/pyproject.toml and fused-memory/pyproject.toml, which pytest itself reads, and so covers all four spawn paths. CONTRARY EVIDENCE ON RECORD: plans/verify-oversubscription-benchmark-2026-07-14.md (the T6 report) recommended KEEPING the knob at 'auto' for want of a clean idle-window measurement, and nominated -n 16 as the next candidate. 3589's loaded-host ladder postdates it and supports -n 8 on both wall-clock and CPU-seconds, which is why the operator decision went to 8.

To keep a slow real-service test out of dark_factory's merge-lane post-merge full-repo sweep (merge_verify_breadth: full), mark it @pytest.mark.integration. fused-memory and shared pyproject.toml register the `integration` marker and set addopts `-m 'not integration'`; under breadth=full the merge sweep runs each module's per-module orchestrator.yaml test_command IN that module's dir (e.g. `uv run --project fused-memory --directory fused-memory pytest tests/`), so the pyproject addopts deselects the marked test automatically — no orchestrator/verify-command code change. Do NOT add a command-line `-m` to the module test_command: a CLI `-m` OVERRIDES (clobbers) the ini addopts `-m 'not integration'`. The offline-lane home for `-m integration` runs is git.offline_lane_commands (task 2789).

Gotcha 2026-09-23: in the dark-factory orchestrator package `pytest -p no:xdist` fails with `unrecognized arguments: -n --dist --max-worker-restart=0` because orchestrator/pyproject.toml addopts pass xdist flags; to run a subset serially use `-n0` instead. A cold `_iact-*` worktree has no .venv; `env -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --project orchestrator pytest ...` builds one (~99 packages, well under a minute) and resolves the WORKTREE's source, matching how verify runs.

Task verify's fallback config derives its pytest scope from plan.json['files'] (via artifacts.read_plan()), not from the live `git diff`. If a debug/steward fix expands the actually-touched file set beyond the original plan.json['files'] (e.g. a live-test task whose debug fix lands in a different module), plan.json['files'] must be updated to match `git diff --name-only <base>...HEAD` or verify can scope to a stale subset. Concretely: task 2300's original 3-file scope (all under cockpit/tests/smoke, 100% @pytest.mark.smoke, default-deselected via addopts="-m 'not smoke'") produced 0 selected tests (rc=5) after a legitimate debug-fix expansion to 5 files, because the fallback config never saw the newly-touched non-smoke test file. Fix was to realign plan.json['files'] to the true diff. Durable follow-up (not yet applied as of task 2300): pin cockpit/orchestrator.yaml's test_command to the full tests/ tree (mirroring shared/orchestrator.yaml's integration-marker precedent), and/or treat pytest rc=5 ("no tests selected") as pass/neutral in verify._summarize_checks rather than a failure.

content: In dark-factory, orchestrator/src/orchestrator/verify_plan.py::governing_addopts(cmd, worktree_reader) resolves the [tool.pytest.ini_options].addopts that pytest will apply for a parsed verify command. Measured 2026-10-14 against the live module test_commands: it returns orchestrator's and fused-memory's addopts, ('-m','not integration') for shared, () for sampler, and the worktree-root pyproject for a bare `pytest tests/`. Use it to ask whether a verify leg already runs xdist; verify.py itself never reads addopts otherwise.

candidates.content: When adding a new CompiledExprKind variant in crates/reify-ir/src/expr.rs, do NOT use TAG byte values 20-23: the header comment on the TAG_* block reserves those for CachedResult::content_hash's distinct hash domain (reify-eval/src/cache.rs) to avoid reader confusion, and explicitly directs new variants to the next sequential free byte (was [28] for task 4118's TAG_RESOLVE_SELECTOR; bump the header's "use [N]" hint when you take it). The tag only seeds the content hash so structurally-distinct kinds don't collide — any unique value works, but follow the in-code convention. Adding a variant forces a passthrough arm into ~9 exhaustive matches: reify-ir expr.rs (walk, map_value_refs, collect_value_refs_inner, remap_entity, remap_cell), reify-expr eval_expr, reify-compiler guards.rs+type_resolution.rs, reify-eval engine_purposes.rs, gui/src-tauri/src/engine.rs format_expr, plus test walkers (type_error_propagation_tests.rs, boundary2_producer.rs). cargo build catches lib/bin sites; cargo test --no-run is REQUIRED to catch test-file matches (build alone misses them).

Reify test-harness pattern for source-text → Value round-trips (crates/reify-compiler/tests/ri_literal_roundtrip.rs, task #5095): splice every case into ONE `structure def S { param x0 : T0 = <lit0> param x1 : T1 = <lit1> ... }`, call `reify_test_support::eval_source(&src)` ONCE, then `cell_value(&result, "S", "xN")` per case — a 260-case sweep runs in ~0.3s, whereas per-case compiling does not scale. Evaluate rather than inspecting the compiled expression, because a negative literal is a `unary_expression` over the quantity and its compiled shape depends on constant folding. Two non-obvious facts: (1) plain `eval_source` deliberately does NOT seed the stdlib unit registry, which is exactly what proves bare built-in unit symbols (mm/deg/kg/s/K) parse in a module that imports nothing, via the unconditional `unit_to_scalar` fallback; (2) type names `Length`/`Angle`/`Mass`/`Time`/`Temperature`/`Real`/`Int`/`Bool`/`String` all resolve with no stdlib import. Such a test cannot live in reify-ir: `crates/reify-ir/tests/dag_invariant.rs` text-scans reify-ir's whole Cargo.toml including dev-deps and rejects any `reify-*` dep beyond reify-core/reify-ast, so it must go in reify-compiler's test tier (which already dev-deps reify-ir + reify-eval + reify-test-support{eval-helpers}).

reify-expr carries VERBATIM local mirrors of four type-predicate helpers from reify-compiler's private `mod type_compat` (`heads_unifiable`, `type_carries_trait_object`, `type_carries_type_param`, `type_carries_dim_param`), because reify-compiler is only a `[dev-dependencies]` entry of reify-expr and so cannot be imported. MEASURED 2026-08-08 on task/5685: three pairs are byte-identical modulo comments/whitespace, but `type_carries_dim_param` is NOT — the compiler and eval copies list the same 22 leaves in a DIFFERENT order inside the same `=> false` arm, so they are behaviourally identical yet textually divergent. Consequence: a drift guard for these mirrors must be a BEHAVIOURAL differential (run both impls over a per-arm corpus, assert verdict-for-verdict agreement), never a source-text comparison — a text diff would fire on that pre-existing cosmetic reorder. Task #5689 tracks deleting the mirrors by hoisting all four into reify-core (already a real non-dev dep of both crates).

Reify code discovery (2026-05-26, reify-types pre-split): the reify-types → {core,ast,ir} partition is acyclic with exactly THREE misfiled simple types/consts that must relocate downward. (1) QuantifierKind is defined in expr.rs (compiled-IR module) but imported by ast.rs:28 (`use crate::QuantifierKind`) — the only real ast→ir back-edge; used by both parsed ExprKind::Quantifier and compiled CompiledExprKind::Quantifier, so it belongs in reify-ast. (2) PortDirection is a trivial In/Out/Bidi enum living in traits.rs (which as a whole pulls ty+value), but referenced by the declaration AST (port decls) and traits — a meaning-free tag → reify-core. (3) annotation name-constants (TEST_ANNOTATION, OPTIMIZED_ANNOTATION, SHELL_ANNOTATION, ...) live in annotation.rs but are used by both the parser and the compiler → reify-core; the compiled Annotation struct stays in ir. Everything else partitions cleanly by whole-module. The declaration AST (in reify-syntax/lib.rs) references ONLY core+ast types (verified: no EnumDef/TraitDef/TypeParam/Type/Value refs), so reify-ast stays core-only.

reify: crates/reify-test-support already exports byte-identical equivalents of helpers that reify-eval's tensegrity integration-test modules hand-roll privately in 8+ files — `values::point3(x,y,z)` (values.rs:361) == the copied `node()`, `values::meters(v)` (values.rs:89) == the copied `length()`, and `value_decompose::read_f64(v,label)` (value_decompose.rs:4) covers the copied `coord()`/`force_val()` (but note read_f64 ALSO accepts Value::Int, a widening on the panic path). All are glob-re-exported at the crate root. reify-ir and reify-core are UNGATED non-optional deps of reify-test-support, so a Value-only fixture needs no Cargo.toml change and no `#[cfg(feature = "eval-helpers")]`; `tolerance_fixtures.rs:119` (make_provenance_value) is the ungated `Value::StructureInstance` builder to model new ones on. Check these before writing another private Value helper in a test module.

Reify IR: a cross-`sub` field reference in a `.ri` constraint (e.g. `constraint shuttle.stroke >= capstan.band` on an assembly) does NOT compile to a single `ValueRef`. It compiles to `CompiledExprKind::IndexAccess { object: ValueRef(<Assembly>.<sub>), index: Literal(Value::String("<cell>")) }` (crates/reify-ir/src/expr.rs:81). Consequence for anyone writing a Rust gate over compiled constraints: `CompiledExpr::collect_value_refs` reports which SUBS a constraint touches but not which of their CELLS, so it cannot tell one assembly-scoped constraint from another. Re-pair them by walking with `CompiledExpr::walk` (expr.rs:570) and matching that IndexAccess/ValueRef/Literal triple to recover `(entity_path, cell_name)`. Relatedly, the evaluated `ValueMap` carries a contained structure's scalar cells under BOTH spellings — the bare template (`Capstan.band`) and the instance-scoped composition (`CapstanDrive.capstan.band`) — and a DSL constraint resolves against the INSTANCE form, so a test reading the template form is only checking the same number while `sub` constructor overrides remain dropped (task 4147). Worked example: crates/reify-eval/tests/harness_sweep/capstan_groove_e2e.rs (`sub_cell_reads`, `sub_entity`).
In-scope files include crates/reify-types/src/expr.rs, crates/reify-compiler/src/expr.rs, crates/reify-compiler/tests/constructor_hash_tests.rs

Reify pattern for an end-to-end .ri→eval integration test that reads back a named value cell (used in crates/reify-eval/tests/relational_selectors_v2.rs Assertion 3): `let compiled = compile_source_with_stdlib(&source);` then `let kernel: Box<dyn reify_ir::GeometryKernel> = Box::new(reify_kernel_occt::OcctKernelHandle::spawn()); let mut engine = Engine::new(Box::new(SimpleConstraintChecker), Some(kernel)); let result = engine.build(&compiled, ExportFormat::Stl);` then `result.values.get(&ValueCellId::new("<StructName>", "<member>"))` returns Option<&Value> (e.g. match Value::List(items) and assert items.len()). BuildResult fields: `values: ValueMap` and `diagnostics: Vec<Diagnostic>`. Imports: reify_constraints::SimpleConstraintChecker, reify_core::identity::ValueCellId, reify_eval::Engine, reify_ir::{ExportFormat, Value}. Gate the assertion on reify_kernel_occt::OCCT_AVAILABLE (topology selectors need a real kernel to hydrate handles).

reify gotcha for lockstep-gating two copies of a .ri structure that must legitimately differ in a few cells (e.g. printer.ri vs dev_capstan.ri Capstan): the TopologyTemplate.content_hash cannot match, but each CompiledExpr.content_hash (crates/reify-ir/src/expr.rs) is structural and carries no span or doc — the template hash is built from these same per-member hashes (reify-compiler/src/entity.rs ~L4813). Compare value_cells[].default_expr hashes plus sorted constraints[].expr hashes (ContentHash(pub u128) has no Ord, so sort by .0) for a comment-blind, per-cell-localised fork check.

Reify core crate-layering refactor (core-ast-ir-layering, landed by 2026-06): the former monolithic reify-types crate is GONE, split into three layers — reify-core (primitives: DimensionVector, Type, SourceSpan, Diagnostic, ContentHash, annotation-name constants), reify-ast (source-as-written AST: identifiers unresolved, operators as strings — where Declaration/Expr/StructureDef/FnDef live), and reify-ir (compiled runtime: Value enum, geometry handles/Mesh, CompiledExpr, solvers, warm-state). Dependency arrows: reify-core ← reify-ast ← reify-ir; reify-syntax (the tree-sitter parser, sole module ts_parser.rs) PRODUCES reify-ast. The ONLY legal back-edge is the 'deferred-code pattern': an IR node embedding an unevaluated reify_ast::Expr by value (e.g. AnnotationArgValue::Expr) — reify-ast may NEVER name a reify-ir/reify-syntax type (any dep kind). Enforced machine-checked: per-crate crates/reify-{core,ast,ir}/tests/dag_invariant.rs + workspace scripts/assert-crate-dag.sh (B1–B6; B5 is the load-bearing 'reify-ast must not depend on ir/syntax'). NAMING TRAPS: reify-expr is the expression EVALUATOR (consumes CompiledExpr from reify-ir), NOT the expression AST (that's reify-ast). reify-syntax still carries a TRANSIENT `pub use reify_ast::*` re-export pending a test-import sweep (labeled for removal, not a permanent façade). Correct core-pipeline test target: cargo test -p reify-core -p reify-ast -p reify-ir -p reify-syntax -p reify-compiler -p reify-expr -p reify-eval. Motivation: before the split, touching reify-types::value.rs (8.4k lines) rebuilt all 23 dependents; the split isolates blast radii and makes 'meaning never depends on surface syntax' a compile+test-time guarantee.

The reify precedent commit a307bf98 (replacing 33 dimension match-arms with the static NAMED_DIMENSIONS table in reify-core/src/dimension.rs:479) did NOT preserve a compile-time exhaustiveness guarantee — it deliberately traded it for a CI completeness TEST (resolve_type_name_round_trips_all_named_dimensions, type_resolution.rs:3939) that iterates the whole table. That test is arguably STRONGER than the old match: it catches name-mismatch and over-match too, not just a missing arm. The table is a plain `static &[(DimensionVector, &str)]` with linear-scan lookup (not phf, not inventory, not build.rs codegen), and it has absorbed 17+ append-only additions since the commit with the parity test still green. This is reify's accepted pattern for "append-only data + CI invariant" replacing an exhaustive match.

Reify's compiler test suite has THREE distinct shapes of the "find a value cell by id.member and take its default_expr" helper, and reify-test-support only covers one of them. The shared helpers `get_let_expr`/`get_let_expr_in` (crates/reify-test-support/src/helpers.rs) take a `&CompiledModule`, but `compile_first_template`/`compile_template` return an OWNED `TopologyTemplate` (the module is consumed), so files using those compile entry points structurally CANNOT use the shared helpers — which is why the suite independently reinvented 14 private template-scoped copies, including six BYTE-IDENTICAL `fn require_default<'a>(template: &'a TopologyTemplate, member: &str) -> &'a CompiledExpr` clones (solver_elastic_tests.rs, buckling/flexures/trajectory stdlib compile tests, modal_options_validation_tests.rs, multi_load_case_stdlib_tests.rs; ~45 call sites). Before declaring such a private copy "not substitutable by get_let_expr", check whether the obstacle is merely template-vs-module scoping rather than genuinely different semantics.

Reify gotcha — a `reify-stdlib` VALUE-DIMENSION retype is NOT verified by `cargo test -p reify-stdlib --lib` plus `cargo test -p reify-eval --lib`. Both can be fully green while `crates/reify-eval/tests/harness_fea_solver_e2e/kinematic_stdlib_smoke.rs` fails, because that e2e harness drives builtins through the full parse -> compile_with_stdlib -> eval pipeline and then asserts the DIMENSION TAG of each returned component via its local `assert_vec3_dim(value, DimensionVector::X, label)` helper (12 call sites as of 2026-08). It is the only place in-tree that pins SO(3)/SE(3) builtin output dimensions end-to-end, and it lives in an INTEGRATION-test target, so `-p reify-eval --lib` never compiles it. Measured on task #6080 (rotation vectors retyped Dimensionless -> Angle): reify-stdlib --lib 2151/0, reify-expr --lib 335/0, reify-eval --lib 2324/0, reify-cli harness_cli 323/0, clippy clean — yet `cargo test -p reify-eval` (ALL targets) surfaced 245 passed / 1 failed at kinematic_stdlib_smoke.rs:382 (`twist.angular dim` expected DIMENSIONLESS, got ANGLE). Rule: when a change alters what `DimensionVector` a builtin EMITS, run `cargo test -p reify-eval` with all targets, not `--lib`. Corollary for task planners: measuring "blast radius" as `.ri` corpus call sites plus in-crate reify-stdlib unit tests systematically misses this file.

Reify gotcha: reify-compiler depends on reify-expr ONLY as a dev-dependency (Cargo.toml dev-dependencies), so production compiler code cannot call reify-expr::calculus helpers (scalar_dimension/domain_dimension/dim_quotient_type, calculus.rs). Any compile-time mirror of field differential-op codomain typing (gradient scalar→vector with quantity = codomain_dim/domain_dim) must duplicate those tiny dimension helpers into reify-compiler (units.rs), or they must be lifted to reify-core (shared by both). Both crates depend on reify-core + reify-ir.

Reify: `crates/reify-compiler/src/builtin_signatures.rs` is NOT the name→result-type registry despite being cited that way in several PRD capability-manifest `delivered_check` rows — it is only the arg-slot DIMENSION checker (`builtin_arg_slots(name, arity)`, `ExpectedArg::{Scalar{dimension,type_name}, Int}`; no Point/Vector variant, so Point-vs-Vector is eval-only). For an Orientation/Frame/Transform-returning builtin the real registration site is `crates/reify-compiler/src/orientation_signatures.rs`: add the name to `ORIENTATION_TYPED_FN_NAMES`, add a `orientation_typed_fn_result_type` match arm, AND bump the independent hand-derived `EXPECTED_NAMES: [&str; N]` test fixture (it deliberately does not import the slice, so it is the drift guard) plus the `..._are_exactly_the_N` test name. `expr.rs`'s `NoUserFunctions` ladder needs no edit — it already gates on `is_orientation_typed_fn`. Registering only the eval arm compiles and passes CI but silently mistypes every call site via the first-arg fallback (`expr.rs:3614-3631`), and nothing catches it: reify-compiler has no dep on reify-stdlib even at dev scope (documented at orientation_signatures.rs:179-188). Adding a key to `builtin_signatures.rs` also requires listing it in `tests::NON_SELECTOR_ARG_SLOT_KEYS` with a justification unless it is a topology selector — that invariant rejects dead entries too.

Reify's `TopologyTemplate.content_hash` (crates/reify-compiler/src/types.rs:714) and `CompiledExpr.content_hash` are SPAN-independent and DOC/COMMENT-independent, which makes them a ready-made semantic lockstep gate for a structure duplicated across two `.ri` files (v0.1 has no cross-file import, so duplication is common — e.g. `IdlerPulley` in both prj/printer_v01/printer.ri and dev_capstan.ri). Measured on task #6135: both files' `IdlerPulley` template hash was bit-identical (`1bd04c25a2a11a58b2c0ffe0ee309f95`) despite different file paths, different line numbers, and deliberately differing comments; a one-line change to the `body` geometry tree in one file moved that file's hash and the `body` `CompiledExpr` hash while the other held. Asserting equality of the two templates' `content_hash` therefore pins every cell expression, every constraint expression and the whole geometry tree including argument order, in one assertion — strictly stronger than comparing evaluated cell VALUES, which is blind to the geometry tree entirely (a cell keeps its value whether or not `body` reads it). Reach it via `compiled.templates.iter().find(|t| t.name == ENTITY)`; per-cell trees are at `template.value_cells[i].default_expr: Option<CompiledExpr>`, and `CompiledExpr::collect_value_refs()` (crates/reify-ir/src/expr.rs:1008) gives the read-set when you want to pin ONE file's tree rather than mirror two. Do NOT hard-code an expected hash as a literal constant — it is opaque to reviewers and breaks on unrelated compiler hashing changes.

reify has TWO user-observable eval-time channels for asserting a builtin's VALUE-level dimension from a .ri fixture, both requiring zero compiler/registry work — useful whenever a task changes what dimension a builtin's result carries but cannot reach the check-time static-type layer. (1) PRINTED VALUE CARRIES THE DIMENSION: `Value::Scalar` Displays as "{si_value} {dimension}" (crates/reify-ir/src/value.rs:3912-3916) while `Value::Real` prints a bare number, and `DimensionVector` Display names slot 7 "rad" (crates/reify-core/src/dimension.rs:667). So `reify eval` output for a let-binding flips from e.g. `vec(0, 0, 1.5707963267948963)` to `vec(0 rad, 0 rad, 1.5707963267948963 rad)` the moment the builtin switches from Value::Real to Value::angle(...). The existing probe fixture docs/prds/v0_6/fixtures/iso_it_out_of_envelope.ri uses this same channel (documents "prints 'TolProbe.t = undef'", exit 1). (2) POST-Undef DIAGNOSTIC HOOKS: `emit_undef_builtin_diagnostics` (crates/reify-expr/src/lib.rs:1965) dispatches per-family `<family>_diagnose(name, &[Value]) -> Option<Diagnostic>` hooks to turn a silent Value::Undef into a spanned error + exit 1. Five precedents are already wired and re-exported from crates/reify-stdlib/src/lib.rs as `pub use <module>::diagnose as <family>_diagnose`: stackup_diagnose (:20), tolerancing_diagnose (:46), fea_diagnose (:54), geometry_diagnose (:63), dynamics_diagnose (:105). (Separately, flexure_diagnose and dfm_diagnose fire on BOTH the success and Undef paths, via their own emit_* functions.) Adding a new family arm is mechanical. A task whose metadata.files includes crates/reify-expr/src/lib.rs alongside reify-stdlib files is very likely there to wire exactly this hook.

In reify-compiler, adding a new `CompiledExprKind` variant (e.g. ResolveSelector, task 4118) requires explicit match arms in only a small set of files — guards.rs, type_resolution.rs, and reify-eval/src/engine_purposes.rs (plus cross-crate reify-expr/src/lib.rs, reify-ir/src/expr.rs, gui/src-tauri/src/engine.rs). Many compiler files that reference CompiledExprKind (functions.rs, entity.rs, compile_builder/entities_phase.rs) use wildcard `_ =>` matches and need NO edit. Selector→List<Geometry> coercion-node insertion at all three sites (param-binding, single()/list-helper, IndexAccess-object) centralizes in crates/reify-compiler/src/coerce.rs + the call sites in expr.rs — NOT in functions.rs/list_helpers.rs. When planning such tasks, treat those spread-out files as speculative and confirm against `cargo build` non-exhaustive-match errors rather than declaring them up front.

Docs-truth substrate survey facts (verified 2026-07-24, reify repo): (1) crates/reify-compiler/src/units.rs holds 8 name-only builtin registries — GEOMETRY_FUNCTION_NAMES (:21), GEOMETRY_QUERY_HELPER_NAMES (:102), GEOMETRY_KINEMATIC_QUERY_NAMES (:130), GEOMETRY_TOPOLOGY_SELECTOR_NAMES (:215), AFFINE_MAP_CONSTRUCTOR_NAMES (:551), TOLERANCING_MARKER_NAMES (:674), GEOMETRY_QUERY_NAMES (:803), DYNAMICS_QUERY_NAMES (:873) — names only, no arities; real builtin arities are buried in match arms in geometry*.rs with ad-hoc error strings. (2) crates/reify-compiler/src/builtin_signatures.rs is NOT a general signature registry: it is a partial per-argument dimension checker for the topology-selector family (task 4493), deliberately leaving most slots unchecked. (3) The language chunks are include_str!'d at compile time in crates/reify-mcp/src/tools/language_chunks.rs, and reify-mcp does NOT depend on reify-compiler — so any chunk-vs-compiler test must live in reify-compiler and read chunks by relative path. (4) reify-audit also does NOT depend on reify-compiler; its per-pattern module layout (crates/reify-audit/src/{ptodo,pdead_dead_code,p1_producer_orphan,...}.rs) means a new drift pattern text-scans both chunks and the units.rs string literals. (5) crates/reify-compiler/tests/ contains ZERO harness_*.rs consolidated units — every new standalone top-level test binary there trips the C1/C2 kloc-cap ratchet (tests/infra/test_harness_kloc_cap.sh, reason=unsanctioned-standalone), empirically demonstrated by task #5364's merge_verify_red; the sanctioned shape is harness_<subsystem>.rs declaring subdir modules. (6) reify-doc = serde-only doc model + formatters; reify-doc-build lowers CompiledModule → doc model (build_stdlib_doc_model) but only covers .ri-defined stdlib items, not Rust builtins.

Reify: to keep a test's coverage list over @optimized stdlib fns from rotting, ENUMERATE the fn->target map at test time instead of hardcoding or grepping stdlib .ri text: `reify_test_support::prelude_backed_functions(&reify_test_support::compile_source_with_stdlib("structure def Probe {}"))` returns Vec<CompiledFunction> with the stdlib merged in exactly as Engine::with_prelude_and_kernels does, and `.optimized_target` is Some(target) for each annotated fn (16 distinct targets as of 2026-08; overloads such as displacement_at x2 / solve_elastic_static x3 / solve_load_cases x2 collapse to one target each). Pair it with a hand-rolled caller detector over examples/** — strip `//` line comments, then require the char before the fn name to be non-alphanumeric/non-underscore AND the next non-whitespace char after it to be `(` — the `(` is what stops `form_find` matching `form_find_free(` and what stops `worst_buckling_case` reading as a `solve_buckling` call. reify-eval has NO regex dev-dependency; do not add one for this. Pattern in use: `build_surface_survey_is_exhaustive` in crates/reify-eval/tests/no_stale_undef_invariant_gate.rs (task 5578).

content: Reify test-fixture gotcha: before writing a test-local CompiledExpr constructor, check reify-ir's own `impl CompiledExpr` (crates/reify-ir/src/expr.rs). It already provides canonical `CompiledExpr::index_access(object, index, result_type)` (~:1253) and `CompiledExpr::match_expr(discriminant, arms, result_type)` (~:1867), which hash with the real TAG_INDEX_ACCESS / TAG_MATCH tags. Several test files hand-roll copies hashed with ad-hoc `ContentHash::of(b"index_access")` / `b"match"`. The same applies to `reify_ir::dimension_of` (constraint.rs:175, the canonical Type→DimensionVector projection) and `Type::dimensionless_scalar()` (reify-core ty.rs:667).

candidates.content: solar_challenge Plotly gotcha, measured 2026-10-14 by task 691's architect on main ad42de8 (Plotly 2.27.0 CDN, headless Chromium, e2e probe on seeded_home_run): Plotly.relayout(gd, {font: {color}, xaxis: {gridcolor}, yaxis: {gridcolor}}) REPLACES each nested container wholesale. chart-renderer.js's theme-changed recolour therefore wiped the visible charts' axis titles ('Date', 'Energy (kWh)'), reset the tick font from 'system-ui, sans-serif' to Plotly's '"Open Sans", verdana, arial, sans-serif', and turned chart-daily-balance's category x-axis into a date axis with nonsense ticks. On a hidden chart recoloured that way it also dropped chart-power-flow's range slider. Passing dotted attribute paths ('font.color', 'xaxis.gridcolor') sets only those leaves and keeps the rest of the layout.

solar_challenge technique for checking a painted colour without PIL (used 2026-10-02 to plan task 235):
1. Take a small screenshot clip with Playwright, e.g. `page.screenshot(clip={"x": cx-2, "y": cy-2, "width": 5, "height": 5})`.
2. Base64 it and decode it in the page: `new Image()` from a `data:image/png;base64,` URL, `await img.decode()`, drawImage onto a canvas, then `getImageData` at the centre.
3. Serve the app as tests/e2e/conftest.py does (tests._web_app.build_test_app plus werkzeug make_server); for dark mode, set localStorage theme=dark and reload.

Headless Chromium returns exact sRGB values: #f59e0b reads as rgb(245,158,11). A range thumb (1rem) sits at the input box's x+8px, vertical middle, when the value equals min. Sampling the same point before and after a CSS refactor proves a visual no-op without committing colour literals to a test.

solar_challenge e2e technique (task 637 implementer, measured 2026-10-13, playwright 1.61, headless Chromium): to see how a page's own JS handles a modified page without editing src/, fetch the live page with page.request.get(url), edit its HTML text (assert the anchor you replace occurs exactly once), then serve it with page.route(url, lambda route: route.fulfill(status=200, content_type="text/html; charset=utf-8", body=html)) before page.goto(url). Build the modified HTML in the test body, not inside the route handler: an exception raised in a handler surfaces only as a hung navigation. tests/e2e/test_results_page.py's undrawable-chart test injects a chart container whose data-chart-figure is not JSON this way.

solar_challenge convention (task 235, task/235 commits 44aa38c..3378155, 2026-10-02): tailwind.config.js is the one home of the dashboard's theme colours, and two guards run in every verify.
(1) tests/unit/test_web_theme_colours.py fails when any template (templates/**/*.html) or static/style.css writes a six-digit hex colour that tailwind.config.js defines. Matching is case-insensitive and includes comments; an 8-digit alpha copy counts through its prefix. Fix: name the colour through a Tailwind utility (on a pseudo-element, an arbitrary variant such as [&::-webkit-slider-thumb]:bg-primary-500), rebuild dist/style.css, and delete commented-out copies and both the :root and the html.dark copy of a variable. dist/style.css (derived from the theme) and static/js scripts (chart libraries need colour strings) are deliberately not checked.
(2) tests/unit/test_web_range_inputs.py fails when any template other than components/macros.html writes an <input type="range">. Draw every slider with {{ range_input(id=..., model=..., min=..., max=..., step=..., name='', width_class='w-full') }} from components/macros.html, which binds x-model.number and owns the class list, including the four thumb-fill utilities (primary-500, dark primary-400). static/style.css shapes the thumb but gives it no fill, so a slider written out by hand shows a hollow thumb with the track showing through.
tests/_dashboard_sources.py now also holds tailwind_config_source() and HAND_WRITTEN_STYLESHEET_KEY ("static/style.css"); import the key rather than writing the path.

solar_challenge e2e locator facts (Playwright 1.61, headless Chromium, measured 2026-09-30 while planning task 214):
- On /history/compare, get_by_role("columnheader", name="Delta", exact=True) and name="% Change" match, even though the th cells are CSS `uppercase`. Playwright's accessible name is the DOM text, not the transformed text.
- The fleet distribution editor's type selects have no accessible name. A role handle that selects exactly those three is get_by_role("combobox").filter(has=page.get_by_role("option", name="Normal (Gaussian)", exact=True)); pending task 227 names them.
- A toast raised with page.evaluate("() => Alpine.store('toast')...") right after page.goto needs no wait. goto waits for load, and the deferred Alpine CDN script has registered the store by then (60/60 repetitions). The toast element is page.get_by_text(message, exact=True).locator("..").

solar_challenge e2e gotcha (measured 2026-09-29, task 134): Plotly.js sets its chart background rect's colour (document.querySelector('.plot-container .bg')) as an inline style, not a `fill` attribute. rect.getAttribute('fill') returns null even when the chart has rendered; read rect.style.fill (e.g. 'rgb(255, 255, 255)') or getComputedStyle(rect).fill instead. tests/e2e/test_dark_mode_pages.py::test_dark_mode_results_page_charts reads the attribute and so always skips with a false 'No Plotly .bg element found' (follow-up ticket tkt_0RV7AS7WNX7MR20ZACS10MCQ4M).
[Scope note added 2026-09-30 by recon Stage 1 run 8b59f58e: a later probe (memory 93152815-64ed-4986-b89f-9257e4109ee2, task 155) found that on the home results page the '.plot-container .bg' rect is the daily-balance LEGEND's background, not the chart background. Plotly paints each chart's paper_bgcolor as the inline CSS background of its first svg.main-svg, and it omits the plot-area rect.bg when paper_bgcolor == plot_bgcolor. To assert chart colours, read getComputedStyle(svg).backgroundColor. The inline-style-not-attribute point above still holds. Task 155, filed for the always-skip, is status=done.]

solar_challenge e2e accessibility facts (Playwright 1.61, headless Chromium, vendored Alpine 3.14.8; measured 2026-10-05 while planning task 420 on main 31d8a36).
- Alpine's :aria-expanded="expr" renders aria-expanded="false" instead of removing the attribute. Its bind keeps a falsy aria-pressed, aria-checked, aria-expanded or aria-selected. So get_by_role("button", name=..., expanded=False) matches collapsed headers.
- page.expect_file_chooser() fires when keyboard Enter or Space activates a <button> whose @click runs $refs.<input>.click() on a display:none <input type="file">. chooser.set_files(path) then triggers its @change handler.
- A native <button> focused by Tab shows the browser's focus ring: computed outline-style auto 1px, :focus-visible true. The dashboard's Tailwind preflight keeps it. static/dist/style.css has sr-only and focus:ring-* but no focus-within:, peer-focus: or focus-visible: utilities.
- page.locator("id=<id>") resolves an aria-controls target without CSS escaping. get_by_role(role, name=..., include_hidden=True) still names a hidden control through its <label for>.

solar_challenge results-page gotcha (task 636 architect, main b74e0f9, 2026-10-11; headless Chromium, playwright 1.61.0). It refines memory 937efa46: chart-renderer.js defers EVERY chart on /results/home and /results/fleet, the opening tab's included. Every chart panel carries x-cloak ([x-cloak] {display:none !important} in static/style.css). Alpine loads with defer in base.html's <head>, and the pages call renderChart from {% block scripts %} at the end of <body>, so each target has offsetParent === null when renderChart runs. Each chart is therefore drawn later, in renderChart's ResizeObserver callback, outside its try/catch. MEASURED with a throwaway probe: serving chart-renderer.js with a throw appended to _doRender, the page_errors fixture held raw pageerrors ('probe-636: chart-sankey', 'probe-636: chart-daily-balance') on load, never renderChart's 'renderChart: failed to draw the figure for id' console error. Each other tab's charts added theirs only once that tab was shown. So an e2e no-JS-errors test on a results page must show every tab, and renderChart's catch reports only a figure that is not JSON (follow-up ticket tkt_0RVNE79AD77RZ76PRNY65TRXMH).

candidates.content: solar_challenge: a fast, browser-free check for web/static JS (measured 2026-09-29, task 123). tests/e2e sits outside verify, and Playwright needs a workaround to launch. Node v22 is at /usr/bin/node. Run `node --check <file>.js` for syntax. Then pipe a harness to `node -` so nothing is written: it reads the script, runs it with vm.runInContext in a context stubbing document (getElementById, addEventListener, documentElement.classList), Plotly (newPlot/purge/relayout recording calls) and ResizeObserver, then calls renderChart and friends and asserts on the recorded calls. Top-level `var`/`function` names in chart-renderer.js become context globals, e.g. vm.runInContext('_CHART_REGISTRY', ctx). Piping `git show HEAD:<path>` in instead gives a before/after comparison.

In fused-memory, get_tasks/get_task MCP tools (server/tools.py) and the SqliteTaskBackend carry NO project provenance, while task IDs are per-project autoincrement and collide across projects (reify#1654 ≠ dark_factory#1654). Both tools funnel through the same _normalize_project_root → interceptor path, so they cannot diverge for the same project_root; cross-project 'contamination' (e.g. Stage 3's bulk get_tasks dump showing reify titles for dark_factory IDs) is therefore a CALLER passing the wrong project_root, silently undetectable because results aren't self-describing. The reconciliation harness fetches the task tree once per cycle (_fetch_filtered_task_tree, correct root) and injects it into Stage 1/2 only; Stage 3 (IntegrityCheck) does not fetch tasks in Python — its LLM agent calls get_tasks via MCP itself. fused-memory GOTCHA (write-authority floors): TaskInterceptor provenance/reopen/repair unit tests use a bare AsyncMock `taskmaster` (test_task_interceptor.py:23-34) whose update_task/stamp_audit_metadata never enforce the SqliteTaskBackend done_provenance floor. SECOND HAZARD IN THE SAME AREA: `SqliteTaskBackend.get_tasks(<any project_root>)` AUTO-CREATES `.taskmaster/tasks/tasks.db` and returns `{"tasks": []}` without raising, and `EscalationQueue.__init__` does `mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)` on its queue_dir. So a test (or a real run) pointed at a task worktree — where neither `.taskmaster/` nor `data/reconciliation/` exists — silently manufactures an empty store and reports a clean, empty result. `TestRunCliWiring` currently passes the literal `project_root='/proj'` at four call sites and passes only because the auto-create hides the miss. Use `tmp_path`-based roots in new tests, never a literal path. Task 2738 hit the same auto-create as a "false census" in `reconciliation/stages/task_knowledge_sync.py`.

Reconciliation gotcha (fused-memory): the Stage-2 TaskKnowledgeSync `self.taskmaster` is an in-process SqliteTaskBackend, NOT the MCP tool surface. SqliteTaskBackend.get_tasks(project_root) does NO git-worktree resolution — for ANY project_root it auto-creates an empty tasks.db (mkdir parents + CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS) and returns {'tasks': []}, never raising. So a misconfigured/non-git project (e.g. my_solar_challenge, no .git) is indistinguishable from a genuinely-empty project at the get_tasks level; both render as a 0-count tree. The "not inside a git working tree" ValueError from resolve_main_checkout (scope.py) is reachable ONLY at the MCP boundary (server/tools.py _normalize_project_root), which reconciliation bypasses — and even there it is caught and returned as an error dict. Implication: any recon-side "detect a get_tasks read failure" logic cannot rely on an exception; use an explicit resolve_main_checkout git-tree check instead.

Task 'Priority overrides MCP tools: fused-memory surface + audit writes (1229b)' completed. Companion to task 1229 (orchestrator-side `OverrideStore` + scheduler integration). Add the four fused-memory MCP tools that let a user manage priority overrides from the dashboard / CLI, and emit the `decisions_and_rationale` audit memory on each write.

## Scope

Four new tools registered inside `create_mcp_server` in `fused-memory/src/fused_memory/server/tools.py`, all following the existing `@mcp.tool()` pattern (see `get_tasks`/`set_task_status` at `fused-memory/src/fused_memory/server/tools.py:1480-1629` for the canonical shape, including `_normalize_project_root` and structured error returns):

1. `set_task_priority_override(project_root, task_id, boost_tier=None, pinned=None, reserve_now=None, ttl_secs=None, pin_order=None)`
2. `clear_task_priority_override(project_root, task_id, field=None)` — `field in {None, 'boost_tier', 'pinned', 'reserve_now', 'ttl'}`; None deletes the whole row
3. `reorder_pin_queue(project_root, ordered_task_ids)` — accepts CSV string OR list; rejects if the supplied set differs from the currently-pinned set
4. `get_pin_queue(project_root)` — read-only, returns `list[dict]` in `pin_order ASC`

## Cross-process design (per task 1229 plan)

fused-memory has no orchestrator dependency in `pyproject.toml`. The MCP tools open the SAME SQLite file (`<project_root>/data/orchestrator/scheduler_overrides.db`) as the orchestrator's `OverrideStore`, using `aiosqlite` directly inside the tool handlers and running idempotent `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS overrides (...)` on first touch. This duplicates the schema/SQL — mirrors the established `TERMINAL_STATUSES` precedent at `fused-memory/src/fused_memory/reconciliation/stages/task_interceptor.py:107` of duplicating ossified contracts rather than coupling packages.

Schema (must be kept in lockstep with `orchestrator/src/orchestrator/overrides.py` — task 1229 owns the canonical definition):

```sql
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS overrides (
  project_root TEXT NOT NULL,
  task_id      TEXT NOT NULL,
  boost_tier   TEXT,
  pinned       INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  pin_order    INTEGER,
  reserve_now  INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  ttl_until    TEXT,
  created_at   TEXT NOT NULL,
  updated_at   TEXT NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (project_root, task_id)
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_overrides_pinned ON overrides(project_root, pinned, pin_order);
```

## Audit writes

Each successful write tool MUST emit a `memory_service.add_memory` call with `category='decisions_and_rationale'`, `project_id=<derived-from-project_root>`, `agent_id='scheduler-overrides'`, and a structured `metadata` dict containing `task_id` and the changed fields. See the existing `add_memory` `@mcp.tool()` at `fused-memory/src/fused_memory/server/tools.py:429-485` for the call shape. `get_pin_queue` is read-only — no audit write.

VERIFY A FOLLOW-UP TASK'S PREMISE AGAINST LIVE STATE BEFORE PLANNING IT. CANONICAL (curator gates 6025 AND 6284, jointly ruled 2026-08-20).

THE LESSON: an agent-followup / reviewer-spawned / split-out task's description routinely narrates a parent or sibling task's NOT-YET-LANDED work in the PAST TENSE, as if complete. The follow-up branch is cut from main and therefore does NOT contain the parent's unmerged artifacts. Planning against the narrative instead of against live state produces a task whose premise is false from the first commit.

THE PROCEDURE, before trusting any such description:
1. `git merge-base --is-ancestor task/<parent> main` — did the parent actually land? Do not infer it from the parent's status alone.
2. `git diff` against the SPECIFIC claimed change — does the symbol/file the description says exists actually exist on your base?
3. `get_task(<parent>)` — current status, and whether done_provenance names a real merge commit.
Only then plan. If the parent has not landed, the follow-up needs a real dependency edge, not a hopeful assumption.

WHY THIS KEEPS HAPPENING (the structural cause, worth knowing): the agent-followup auto-filer commonly files with `dependencies=[]`, so the scheduler is free to dispatch the follow-up before its parent lands. The missing dependency edge is the defect; the false narrative is the symptom.

Conveniently, the branch's own self-correction is usually strong evidence for the decision the follow-up asks you to make: #6095's review had already chosen the answer in practice.

EVERY terminal cite occurrence in a marker body is flagged independently (ptodo.rs:1037), so multi-cite markers (e.g. `#3541/#3582` plus a repeated `#3541`) need `(done)` after EACH occurrence. Decision rule: DELETE the marker if the symbol now has a real traceable non-test caller in crates/reify-*/src (wiring landed); else ANNOTATE `(done)` (genuine in-scope orphan by design, e.g. consumer lives in gui/ outside the crates/reify-*/src audit scope). Completed: Bristol PVGIS TMY irradiation is below every PVGIS-SARAH2 year 2005-2020 (GHI 992 vs mean 1072 kWh/m²), so Bristol PV yields read 7-9% low
Description: Agent follow-up found while planning task 252 (escalation id agent-followup-252). It is OUT OF SCOPE for task 252, which only adds system losses to the PV model in src/solar_challenge/pv.py.

OBSERVED on 2026-10-01 at base 18a3394, with CPython 3.12.3 and pvlib 0.15.1.
- The Bristol TMY that solar_challenge.weather.get_tmy_data(Location.bristol()) returns is cached as tmy_5dc8c8bca218: UTC, 1990-indexed, 8760 rows, location 51.45 / -2.58.
- Its annual GHI is 992.3 kWh/m².
- PVGIS v5_2 MRcalc at the same point (horirrad=1, PVGIS-SARAH2) gives annual GHI 1006.7-1150.6 kWh/m² for 2005-2020, with a mean of 1072.3. The lowest year is 2008. The TMY is below every single year.
- In-plane irradiation for south, 35°, as computed by the pvlib ModelChain from the TMY: 1143.7 kWh/m². PVGIS PVcalc H(i)_y for the same orientation (2005-2020): 1256.15 kWh/m² (−9%).
- At other UK sites the TMY and PVcalc in-plane totals agree within ±3% (London 1255 vs 1268; Plymouth 1345 vs 1348; Glasgow 1064 vs 1053). Penzance is −7%, and Eastbourne and Belfast are −4%.
- Consequence: every Bristol PV yield and £ figure (finance calibration scenario, fleet runs) is computed from irradiation about 9% below PVGIS's long-term mean. With task 252's losses, Bristol 4 kW reads 927 kWh/kWp against PVGIS-14%'s 1021. The performance ratio itself agrees (0.811 vs 0.813), so the gap is the weather data, not the loss model.

TO DECIDE (measure first):
- Why the TMY is low. Hypothesis: TMY month selection (Finkelstein-Schafer statistics on several variables) does not preserve the annual irradiation total.
- Whether simulations should use a multi-year PVGIS hourly series (pvlib.iotools.get_pvgis_hourly), a TMY rescaled to the long-term mean, or should keep the TMY and document the bias. Record the decision in docs/, e.g. alongside docs/pv-system-losses.md, which task 252 creates.

candidates.content: solar_challenge_platform gotcha, checked by task 1032's architect on 2026-10-14 at main e4f2a2b. Before you reword or remove text in a src module, look for capability-manifest YAML grep checks on it. Running `git grep -n <module path> -- 'docs/prds/*.capability-manifest.yaml'` is not enough: it misses every delivered_check whose `paths:` lists a PARENT directory of the module, and those checks still match the module's text. Examples: fleet-dispatch-policy-and-config-freshness's 'provenance: CommandProvenance \| None' expect: present over src/solar_challenge_platform/control, and collection-mechanics's expect: absent checks over src/solar_challenge_platform such as 'def handle_event\(' and 'recon_collected'. Instead, yaml.safe_load each docs/prds/*.capability-manifest.yaml, walk it for delivered_check entries with kind: grep, and keep those whose paths name the file or any ancestor directory.

Decompose/filing gotchas learned on the 2026-09-29 five-PRD batch (tasks 595-662): (a) commit_planning stamps ONE capability-manifest sidecar per call — when a batch spans several PRDs, flip everything once, then re-call commit_planning per PRD with that PRD's ids (statuses are a no-op, the sidecar gets stamped and its mechanical delivered_checks copied); (b) its lint REFUSES to copy a check whose pattern is the NAME of a file the leaf creates ("filename_shaped" — declare it kind: path, expect: present, paths: [the file]) and a presence check whose pattern already matches main ("vacuous_present" — assert something the leaf introduces, or make it kind: manual); (c) it warns "absent_overbroad" when an expect:absent pattern still matches a file outside the leaf's declared files (harmless if an upstream leaf deletes that file); (d) `kind: path` validates against CapabilityManifestDoc; (e) the path-scope lint flags prose too: "scenarios/known_gap/conventions" in a description produced metadata.possible_scope_mismatch (suggested_project solar_challenge) on task 652 — write "the scenario, known_gap and convention entries" instead, and treat any recon gate on that flag as a false positive; (f) update_task title/description/priority are replace-only — append coordination notes to `details` with append=true; (g) a decompose seat can and did find G6 dependency-direction defects the drafters' own DAG missed (12 across five PRDs) — keep the decompose walk even for well-critiqued PRDs.

How to validate a PRD capability-manifest sidecar locally (verified 2026-10-14): `cd /home/leo/src/dark-factory/shared && uv run python`. Then call shared.capability_manifest.load_capability_manifest(path) for the schema, and shared.delivered_check_polarity.lint_delivered_checks(checks, files=None, repo_root=<repo>, ref="main") per task. Pass each check as its delivered_check.model_dump(exclude_none=True) plus a "name" key, skipping kind=manual. With files=None, every expect=absent check yields a non-blocking 'absent_overbroad' WARN; that is expected at author time, before metadata.files exists. Real rejections are vacuous present/absent checks. The sidecar's delivered_check has no 'name' field (the capability name is used). YAML gotcha: a plain multi-line scalar containing ": " (e.g. "render the value: G6") raises "mapping values are not allowed here"; quote it or reword.

Procedure used 2026-10-14 to validate a PRD capability-manifest YAML sidecar outside a decompose pass. From /home/leo/src/dark-factory/shared, run `uv run python`:
- CapabilityManifestDoc.model_validate(yaml.safe_load(...)) from shared.capability_manifest checks the schema.
- shared.delivered_check_polarity.lint_delivered_checks(checks, files=<task metadata.files or None>, repo_root=<project>, ref='main') checks polarity.

With files=None, every expect=absent check reports a non-blocking 'absent_overbroad' warning, because the matches fall outside declared files. That is expected at author time. At decompose, each leaf's metadata.files must contain every file its absent-checks currently match.

Polarity rule: a check that already passes on main (present already present, absent already absent) gates nothing and is flagged. Verify each check fails on main before filing.

Sidecar verdicts are PASS|FAIL|OPEN. OPEN fits a producer in another stream whose task id is not yet known, e.g. S26's time leaf. The kinds are grep|script|path|manual; use path for file existence, never grep.

Capability-manifest gotcha (task 779 architect, main bd71483, 2026-10-05). Decompose sessions commit docs/prds/*.capability-manifest.md straight to main and never run this repo's pytest (e.g. 32477ca, 048ff26), so any new test that rejects the form today's /prd decompose writes would redden main at the next decompose. In particular, do not add a guard that rejects bare unbackticked grep: text in tests/docs/test_capability_manifest_pointers.py until dark-factory's /prd emits backticked repo-root-relative grep: spans (ticket tkt_0RVF029VB6TGV8FJ7PEYYT89A7). So mirror a CLAIM amendment into both twins, but keep pointer-FORM edits (backticks, repo-root prefixes) .md-only.

Convention established for solar-challenge-platform PRDs: they live at docs/prds/<slug>.md with a committed companion docs/prds/<slug>.capability-manifest.md (mirroring the my-solar-challenge sim repo). The manifest binds each leaf task's asserted capabilities to evidence (verified-import / grep:file:line / producer:task-N upstream / active-rejection-mechanism) and must read PASS with no FAIL bindings before the task batch is queued.

Validating a /prd capability-manifest YAML sidecar against dark-factory's schema from the solar-challenge-platform repo. Run from /home/leo/src/dark-factory/shared with /home/leo/src/dark-factory/.venv/bin/python (there is no shared/.venv):
`import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'src'); from shared.capability_manifest import load_capability_manifest; load_capability_manifest('<abs path>.capability-manifest.yaml')`.
It accepts the review-all sidecar format (prd, schema_version: 1, tasks[label, task_id, title, note, capabilities[name, binding, verdict PASS|FAIL|OPEN, delivered_check{kind grep|manual|script, pattern, paths, expect present|absent | reason}]]).
Pitfall: a grep delivered_check pattern such as `a\.tariff_id` false-fails on any loop variable named `a`. Anchor absent-checks on distinctive text, e.g. `ON a\.tariff_id = t\.id`.

GOTCHA (delivered_check multi-path greps, found by task 344 on 2026-09-26): a kind:grep delivered_check with several `paths` runs as one `git grep -E -e <pattern> <ref> -- <paths...>`. It passes when ANY path matches. A pathspec for a deleted file matches nothing and raises no error. So when a later refactor retires one listed file, the check does not fail: it silently narrows to the surviving paths, and it only starts failing (holding dependents with dep_capability_not_delivered) when the last surviving match moves too. GOTCHA (dark-factory, measured while planning task 3327): adding a config leaf to `RELOADABLE_FIELDS` does NOT make it hot-reloadable if its consumer COPIES the value at construction. `apply_reload`/`_set_leaf` (orchestrator/src/orchestrator/config.py::_set_leaf) mutate the config submodel IN PLACE, so any consumer that re-reads `self.config.<block>.<leaf>` per call sees the new value — that is why the house convention (stated at scheduler.py:1912-1935) is to read config leaves at CALL time and never capture them at construction. But a collaborator object built FROM config at startup breaks that chain: `ApiHealthGate.__init__` (shared/src/shared/api_health.py:224-227) assigns `self.window_secs = window_secs` etc., so a green-tier retune of `api_health.min_failures` reaches the config object and never reaches the live state machine. `diff_config` still reports the leaf under `applied`, so the reload looks successful — the disposition report cannot detect this.

The codebase already names this failure mode "reloadable-in-name-only" at harness.py:6896 (for StormCounter), so it has bitten before.

CHECK, don't assume: for any new green-tier leaf, ask whether a long-lived object copied it. If so, add an explicit re-sync on the reload path (assign the leaves onto the live instance) — and do NOT reconstruct the object, which would discard accumulated state such as a rolling window or a tripped-breaker state, silently reverting the behaviour the operator was retuning.

To make a nested orchestrator config field hot-reloadable (green-tier): add the field to its submodel and rely on `_submodel_leaf_paths('<block>', <SubmodelCls>)` already in RELOADABLE_FIELDS (config.py) — no RELOADABLE_FIELDS edit needed. `_iter_leaves` descends exactly one level into BaseModel-valued fields and yields list/dict-valued leaves (e.g. routing.rules, routing.per_model_daily_ceiling_usd) WHOLE as atomic leaves compared by equality, so a `list[SomeModel]` field reloads atomically. Closed-vocabulary enforcement on reload is free: apply_reload re-runs `OrchestratorConfig.model_validate` post-apply with rollback, so a nested model using `ConfigDict(extra='forbid')` makes an unknown key fail the reload closed (and it also fails when the fresh config is constructed from the new YAML).

TESTING A PER-FIELD RANGE BOUND ON A GREEN-TIER OrchestratorConfig LEAF (dark-factory, measured while planning task 4063 in .worktrees/4063 @ de0773fb04, using the existing `ge=1` on psi_admission.min_inflight_floor as a live stand-in).

There are TWO structurally different rejection points for "an out-of-range value must not survive a hot-reload", and neither subsumes the other. Assert both.

1. LOAD PATH (the realistic operator scenario). `Harness.reload_config()` calls `load_config()` with ZERO arguments off-thread (harness.py) so it can only re-read this process's own ORCH_CONFIG_PATH; ANY exception is caught by its `_load_failure_report` and converted to a fail-closed `{'reloaded': False, 'error': str(exc)}` with `self.config` left untouched. So "rejected at load" and "rejected at hot-reload from edited YAML" are the SAME mechanism. Test it directly: `yaml.dump({'<submodel>': {'<leaf>': <bad>}})` into `tmp_path/'config.yaml'`, `monkeypatch.setenv('ORCH_CONFIG_PATH', str(p))`, then `pytest.raises(ValidationError): load_config(p)`. MEASURED: raises. A YAML containing only the submodel dict is sufficient — `project_root` is NOT required.

2. APPLY PATH (defence in depth). `apply_reload`'s I5 post-apply `OrchestratorConfig.model_validate(live.model_dump())` DOES catch a field-level ge/le violation and rolls back byte-for-byte. MEASURED report shape: `reloaded=False`, `error` starts `'hybrid-invariant: 1 validation error for OrchestratorConfig'` naming `<submodel>.<leaf>`, `applied == {}`, `live.model_dump()` identical to the pre-call dump.

THE NON-OBVIOUS PART. The three existing hybrid-rollback precedents (TestApplyReloadHybridRollback in test_config.py, TestS5HybridRollbackLock in test_config_reload_integration_gate.py, the routing analogue in test_routing.py) all reach that path by combining two INDIVIDUALLY-VALID configs into an invalid hybrid under a synthetically narrowed `allowlist=` argument. That idiom only works for CROSS-FIELD invariants. A per-field range bound can NEVER be violated by combining two valid configs, so copying the precedent will not reach the path — you will just write a passing test that proves nothing. Instead build a valid `fresh` and then assign the bad value straight onto the submodel instance (`fresh.<submodel>.<leaf> = <bad>`). That works because submodels deliberately carry no `validate_assignment` — stated in `config.py::_set_leaf`'s own docstring, which is also exactly WHY apply_reload needs the post-apply re-check. So the bypass is not a test hack; it reproduces the real reason the defence exists.

Distinct from the RELOADABLE_FIELDS-registration entries (aa77b0e6, ec5f137d) and the reloadable-in-name-only entries (a1667f1a, c154847f): this is about validating a CONSTRAINT, not about registering or wiring a leaf.

Adding a field to an OrchestratorConfig submodel already registered in `RELOADABLE_FIELDS` makes it green-tier hot-reloadable for FREE — no allowlist edit. `orchestrator/src/orchestrator/config.py::_submodel_leaf_paths` generates `'<group>.<leaf>'` paths from the submodel class's own `model_fields` at import time, so groups registered that way (models, budgets, max_turns, effort, timeouts, backends, unblock_auto, psi_admission, routing, chronic_flake, ...) grow automatically. The matching reload tests are parametrized over `list(<Submodel>.model_fields)` too, so disposition coverage is automatic as well. Adding a knob to a NON-registered submodel still requires an explicit RELOADABLE_FIELDS entry — check for the group before assuming.

[CORRECTED 2026-08-23 (recon Stage 1, run cd53b227-18ac-4432-b22f-2b5ac0913cf2) — the "disposition coverage is automatic as well" clause above is NOT reliable, and acting on it will surprise you.] Mem0 entry ec5f137d-f6e9-4ba6-baca-c4463ac35b14, written the same day ~7h later and more specific, reports the opposite practical outcome: `orchestrator/tests/test_config.py` pins each whole-submodel reload group's leaves as a LITERAL tuple in a `test_leaves_in_reloadable_fields`-style test, so a newly-added field WILL fail that one test until the tuple AND the surrounding "all N leaves" docstring prose are extended. Both can hold at once — some reload tests do enumerate `model_fields` dynamically while a separate membership test pins a literal tuple — but the actionable expectation is ec5f137d's: EXPECT exactly that literal-tuple test to go red, and read the red as confirmation that the dynamic-enumeration property held, not as an obstacle. Related but distinct: FLAT top-level OrchestratorConfig fields cannot use the `_submodel_leaf_paths` idiom at all and must be added as explicit string literals — see ef838943-0ae8-4571-ae7d-4bd8e99c2caf.

In orchestrator/src/orchestrator/config.py, adding a field to a submodel registered as a WHOLE-SUBMODEL green-tier reload group (via _submodel_leaf_paths, e.g. RoutingConfig / DeliveredChecksConfig / SessionResumeConfig) needs NO edit to RELOADABLE_FIELDS — the generator enumerates model_fields dynamically, so the new leaf is hot-reloadable for free. But orchestrator/tests/test_config.py pins each such group's leaves as a LITERAL tuple in a test_leaves_in_reloadable_fields-style test, so a new field WILL fail that one test until the tuple and the surrounding "all N leaves" docstring prose are extended. Expect exactly that test to go red, and read it as the assertion that the dynamic-enumeration property actually held rather than as an obstacle.

Recipe for a green-tier hot-reloadable orchestrator config submodel (dark-factory orchestrator/src/orchestrator/config.py): (1) define a BaseModel subclass near the sibling scheduler submodels (~line 452, ABOVE the RELOADABLE_FIELDS definition at ~2621 so it can be referenced there) mirroring StarvationWatchdogConfig/WarmBaseHardDownConfig — enabled: bool = Field(default=True) + Field-bounded numeric fields; (2) attach on OrchestratorConfig as `name: NameConfig = Field(default_factory=NameConfig)` (pattern at ~2202-2212); (3) register every leaf as green-tier by adding `_submodel_leaf_paths('name', NameConfig)` to the RELOADABLE_FIELDS frozenset().union(...) at ~2621. Gotcha/bonus: test_config.py::test_every_path_resolves_on_default_config loops over ALL RELOADABLE_FIELDS paths and requires each to resolve via getattr on a default OrchestratorConfig — it silently goes RED if you register a submodel group without attaching the field (or on a name mismatch), so it's a free attachment↔registration consistency guard. diff_config's _iter_leaves descends exactly one level into BaseModel-valued fields, so submodel leaves diff/apply identically to fairness.*/starvation_watchdog.*.

fused-memory's config hot-reload engine (fused_memory/config/reload.py, task 2718) is a near-verbatim port of the orchestrator's apply_reload/diff_config/_iter_leaves/_set_leaf, exposed via the no-args reload_config MCP tool in server/tools.py. GOTCHA when extending RELOADABLE_FIELDS: FusedMemoryConfig has NO validate_assignment=True (unlike OrchestratorConfig), so _set_leaf's in-place setattr of an out-of-bounds submodel leaf succeeds silently — the ONLY authoritative check is apply_reload's post-apply FusedMemoryConfig.model_validate(live.model_dump()) hybrid re-validation, which rolls back all applied leaves on failure. Only add a leaf to RELOADABLE_FIELDS if EVERY consumer reads it live from the shared memory_service.config object (verified live-read: reconciliation.stale_run_recovery_seconds by the reaper; procedural_knowledge_near_dup_guard_enabled/_threshold by near_duplicate_guard.py resolvers). Knobs captured by value at construction (e.g. reconciliation.buffer_size_threshold into the event buffer) must stay restart-only.

Adding a config leaf to RELOADABLE_FIELDS is necessary but NOT sufficient for it to be hot-reloadable: apply_reload mutates the live OrchestratorConfig in place via _set_leaf/object.__setattr__ (config.py), so only consumers that re-read self.config.X AT CALL TIME actually retune. Any value captured at construction (e.g. passed into a collaborator's __init__ and stored) silently ignores the reload while reload_config still reports the leaf under 'applied' with reloaded:true — a fail-soft that reads to the operator as success. When reviewing or adding a green-tier leaf, trace every consumer to a call-time read; if a collaborator must own the value, pass a zero-arg provider callable it resolves per use rather than a captured scalar, which also keeps that collaborator free of any config import. Found in orchestrator task 3823 (Scheduler to HoldHistory min_samples).

Task 'Config-reload α: allowlist + diff_config + apply_reload with hybrid-rollback (config.py)' completed. Pure synchronous reload machinery in orchestrator/src/orchestrator/config.py per plans/config-hot-reload-prd.md §Contract:

1. RELOADABLE_FIELDS — code-owned constant of dotted leaf paths per PRD §Allowlist (v1): all fields of models/budgets/turns/effort/timeouts/backends submodels, steward_completion_timeout, steward_lifetime_budget, fairness.skip_threshold, starvation_watchdog.{enabled,skip_threshold,idle_secs}, idle_poll_secs, orphan_l0_timeout_secs, watcher_rotation_escalations, watcher_rotation_hours (+ the crashloop-window params read live per rotation), review.{enabled,interval,full_review_on_complete,full_review_min_interval_secs,full_review_min_tasks}, unblock_auto.* , verify_env, git.offline_lane_test_threads, git.offline_lane_poll_interval_secs, git.offline_lane_red_advances_before_blocker. PRD Open Q1 suggested resolution: generate per-submodel from model_fields at import time; unit test asserts non-empty and that every path resolves on a default OrchestratorConfig.

2. diff_config(live, fresh) -> every differing dotted path categorized into (allowlisted, restart_required) + unchanged count. Walk the full model dump; EXCLUDE private attrs (_module_configs) — module configs are out of scope (PRD decision 7).

3. apply_reload(live, fresh) -> report dict per PRD §Contract tool schema. Invariants: I2 (only allowlisted paths ever written; restart_required reported, never mutated), I3 (leaf mutation only — NEVER replace submodel objects; GitOps holds config.git and UsageGate holds config.usage_cap by reference), I5 (after apply, re-validate live's full dump via OrchestratorConfig.model_validate; on failure roll back every applied field to its old value synchronously in the same call and return reloaded=false, error='hybrid-invariant: ...'), validate-then-copy (values come only from the fully-constructed fresh instance — never raw YAML; nested submodel assignment skips validation since only the top-level model has validate_assignment=True).

Unit tests: allowlisted-change apply; restart-required categorization; mixed; no-op; submodel identity preserved after apply (id(config.git) unchanged); hybrid-rollback with a SYNTHETIC allowlist {timeouts.steward} that omits steward_completion_timeout (PRD boundary scenario 5 — unreachable end-to-end with the v1 allowlist since both invariant sides are allowlisted; this is the honest unit-level premise); verify_env dict replacement (fresh value already carries the sccache fold applied by load_config).

User-observable signal: intermediate — unlocks β (Harness.reload_config consumes diff/apply).
