To add a green-tier hot-reloadable orchestrator config knob: define it as a top-level OrchestratorConfig Pydantic Field in config.py (near merge_verify_max_concurrent_modules ~line 1799), add its dotted name to the RELOADABLE_FIELDS explicit set literal (~line 2811), and READ IT FRESH off req.config at the point of use in the worker (NOT as a SpeculativeMergeWorker constructor kwarg — construction-time values like speculation_depth are frozen and restart-only). apply_reload mutates the live config in place preserving submodel identity, so held req.config references observe the update. GitConfig leaves are NOT auto-reloadable — they need explicit 'git.<leaf>' entries.

GOTCHA — the free-green-tier mechanism has a DOCS cost that nothing catches. Existing entries (aa77b0e6, ec5f137d, c79f398c) explain the code side: registering a submodel via `config.py::_submodel_leaf_paths` makes every leaf green-tier hot-reloadable with no RELOADABLE_FIELDS edit. The unrecorded consequence is that the OPERATOR-FACING lists never learn about it. `OPERATIONS.md` §6's "Green tier (hot-reloadable)" bullet list and `skills/orchestrate/SKILL.md`'s "Reload vs restart" table are hand-maintained prose with no generator and no test tying them to RELOADABLE_FIELDS, so a new submodel is reloadable in code while both docs still imply it is restart-only.

MEASURED 2026-09-16 at main 8650fcbb02: `merge_deep` has been in RELOADABLE_FIELDS since task 3183 (config.py, `_submodel_leaf_paths('merge_deep', MergeDeepConfig)`), yet `grep -rn 'merge_deep|chain_cap' *.md` outside `plans/` returned exactly ONE hit in the whole repo — an unrelated prose mention of the `--chains` report flag. Task 3193 exists to repair that gap.

WHY IT BITES: the omission inverts the operator's conclusion in the direction that matters. `merge_deep.chain_cap=0` is a KILL SWITCH, and green-tier is deliberate because a kill switch you can only pull by restarting is not one. An operator reading §6's list mid-incident concludes the opposite — that killing the feature costs a fleet restart.

PRACTICE: when you add a submodel to RELOADABLE_FIELDS, the code test that goes red (`test_config.py`'s literal-tuple `test_leaves_in_reloadable_fields`, per ec5f137d) is NOT the whole checklist — also add a bullet to OPERATIONS.md §6's green tier and a row to skills/orchestrate/SKILL.md's reload table. Conversely, do NOT read either doc as exhaustive: §6 says so itself and points at `plans/config-hot-reload-prd.md` as the authoritative allowlist. Treat RELOADABLE_FIELDS as the source of truth and the docs as a lagging index.

Do NOT "fix" this with a doc-grep test asserting the lists match RELOADABLE_FIELDS: §6 is explicitly non-exhaustive by design (it also documents fused-memory's separate allowlist in the same section), so such a test would pin prose that is deliberately partial. The `scripts/tests/test_merge_state_vocabulary_consistency.py` docs-vs-source precedent does not transfer — that one guards a CLOSED vocabulary.

orchestrator RELOADABLE_FIELDS (config.py): FLAT top-level OrchestratorConfig fields cannot use the _submodel_leaf_paths idiom — they must be added as explicit string literals inside the flat `{...}` set block near the end of the frozenset (the backfill_* group at ~config.py:5167 and the digest_* group added by task 4559 are the precedents). _submodel_leaf_paths only generates '<group>.<leaf>' paths for BaseModel submodels. The reload suite that covers this is orchestrator/tests/test_config.py::TestConfigReload: test_every_path_resolves_on_default_config getattr-walks every path (so a typo'd literal fails there, not silently at reload time), and membership is pinned by parametrized test_representative_reloadable_members_present / test_restart_only_members_absent lists.

Hazard inventory for anyone extending config hot-reload beyond the green-tier allowlist (df 2005-2009) — why yellow/red fields stay restart-only (surveyed 2026-07-02): (1) lock_depth is read at try_acquire AND again at release_subset (scheduler.py ~:893/:923) — a mid-flight change makes the re-normalized module keys miss the held set → PERMANENT lock leak; full release() uses the stored set and is safe. (2) max_per_module / module_overrides limits are memoized per-module in LockTable._limits at first acquire and never re-read — a live change would half-take (only never-yet-locked modules). (3) MergeRequest.config is a REFERENCE to the single shared OrchestratorConfig, not a copy — in-place mutation reaches already-enqueued merge requests mid-merge, which is why git.branch_prefix/main_branch/persistent_merge_worktree are restart-only (their start-time fail-closed guards enforce_merge_liveness_margin / enforce_persistent_worktree_serial_lane also only run at merge-worker start). (4) Background-loop intervals and *_enabled gates are captured into locals at loop entry; the existing test idiom (e.g. test_harness_warm_lane_gc mutate-field-then-call-_start_X) is the manual reload recipe for those. (5) Only the top-level OrchestratorConfig has validate_assignment=True — assigning to a nested submodel field (config.timeouts.steward = x) bypasses ALL validation including parent cross-field validators; any programmatic config mutation must validate via a full fresh construction first (the validate-then-copy pattern in the reload PRD).

Fact (dark-factory config hot-reload, confirmed 2026-07-08 for L3b DA2): to make a new tunable green-tier (hot-reloadable via mcp__escalation__reload_config), add a pydantic submodel and register it in RELOADABLE_FIELDS (config.py:2621) via `_submodel_leaf_paths('<field>', <Config>)` (config.py:2600) — the same generator used for fairness/starvation_watchdog/warm_base_hard_down. Submodels attach to OrchestratorConfig as `name: NameConfig = Field(default_factory=NameConfig)` (pattern at config.py:2202). The reload disposition machinery is diff_config (config.py:2693) → apply_reload (config.py:2755), bucketing each differing leaf into applied vs restart_required; test_config_reload_integration_gate.py is the scenario harness to mirror (its Scenario 3 asserts max_concurrent_tasks is restart-only / red tier). So a new scheduler-tuning threshold config is green-tier by adding one _submodel_leaf_paths line; max_concurrent_tasks itself stays red-tier (restart-only) because it sizes the semaphore at startup.

Verifying a green-tier config hot-reload in dark-factory: budgets.* and max_turns.* are confirmed hot-reloadable IN CODE, not just in CLAUDE.md prose — orchestrator/src/orchestrator/config.py:4955 builds RELOADABLE_FIELDS from _submodel_leaf_paths('budgets', BudgetsConfig) and _submodel_leaf_paths('max_turns', TurnsConfig) as whole-submodel groups, so every role leaf is covered automatically as those classes grow. Mechanical caveat that determines WHERE to make the edit: mcp__escalation__reload_config re-reads that process's own ORCH_CONFIG_PATH — i.e. the project's dark-factory-orchestrator.yaml — whereas defaults.yaml is package code loaded at process start, so a defaults.yaml edit alone does NOT hot-apply and needs a redeploy. The 2026-08-17 reviewer cap raise was therefore made in both files. The reload returned applied={'budgets.reviewer': {'old': 5, 'new': 12}, 'max_turns.reviewer': {'old': 30, 'new': 60}} with restart_required={} and 370 leaves unchanged; the `applied` map was read rather than the top-level `reloaded` flag. Crucially the change was then confirmed LIVE IN DISPATCH rather than merely present in the config object: task 3271's very next reviewer invocation ran to turns=40, which was structurally impossible under the old cap of 30. Note also that the known "hot-reload applies the RUNNING code's defaults" hazard did not apply here, because both keys were explicitly present in the project YAML rather than falling through to a default_factory (which fires only when the key is ABSENT).

Adding a leaf to an existing orchestrator config submodel requires TWO edits, not one: the `Field(default=...)` in config.py AND a matching key in the `<section>:` stanza of orchestrator/src/orchestrator/defaults.yaml. YamlSettingsSource layers defaults.yaml UNDER the project YAML, so the STANZA — not the Field default — is what actually applies at runtime; a Field with no stanza key is silent drift. test_config.py's per-section `test_defaults_yaml_block_matches_the_field_defaults` exists to catch exactly this and must be extended with the new keys. Green-tier hot-reloadability, by contrast, needs NO edit when the section is registered via `_submodel_leaf_paths('<section>', <Model>)` in RELOADABLE_FIELDS — new leaves are covered automatically, and the sibling `test_leaves_are_green_tier_hot_reloadable` test iterates `<Model>.model_fields` so it keeps passing for free.

Testing a green-tier hot reload against a LIVE Scheduler whose config a test has mutated (e.g. park_world sets config.fairness.skip_threshold = 1 after construction): build the fresh config as `scheduler.config.model_copy(update={'<leaf>': value})` and pass it to the real `apply_reload(scheduler.config, fresh)`. Then exactly that leaf differs. A fresh `OrchestratorConfig(max_per_module=1, <leaf>=value)` instead also diffs every other test-mutated green-tier leaf and silently re-applies it, e.g. resetting skip_threshold back to its operational value mid-test. Used in orchestrator/tests/test_scheduler_pin_reservations.py::_reload (task 6040).

CONFIG-RELOAD TIER, CLI AND EventType SUBSTRATE, measured on main 2026-09-11 while gate-walking plans/live-shadow-eval-prd.md. Three facts, each of which is a place where a plausible assumption is wrong and nothing catches it.

1. GREEN TIER IS OPT-IN PER SUBMODEL, AND COPYING A FIELD'S "PATTERN" DOES NOT COPY ITS TIER. orchestrator/src/orchestrator/config.py::RELOADABLE_FIELDS is a module-level frozenset[str] of dotted leaf paths, built by unioning _submodel_leaf_paths(field_name, submodel_cls) calls (which auto-generate every leaf of a submodel from its model_fields) with a trailing hand-written set of individual literals. CONSEQUENCE: a new field on an ALREADY-registered submodel needs no RELOADABLE_FIELDS edit, but a brand-new submodel needs exactly one _submodel_leaf_paths(...) call added, or it is silently restart-only. `routing` (RoutingConfig) and `unblock_auto` (UnblockAutoConfig) are registered as whole submodels; `verify_env` is a single flat literal; and `review` is only PARTIALLY green — five explicit literals (review.enabled, review.interval, review.full_review_on_complete, review.full_review_min_interval_secs, review.full_review_min_tasks) out of ReviewConfig's seven fields, with review.briefing_path and review.reports_dir restart-only. SPECIFIC TRAP MEASURED: OrchestratorConfig.auto_eval_redo_budget_usd (float, default 50.0) is NOT in RELOADABLE_FIELDS — it is restart-tier. A design that says "copy the auto_eval_redo_budget_usd pattern" for a hot-reloadable budget copies a restart-only field and gets no hot reload.

2. AN UNKNOWN TOP-LEVEL CONFIG KEY IS SILENTLY IGNORED, WHICH IS WHY check-config EXISTS. OrchestratorConfig is a pydantic-settings BaseSettings with extra='ignore' (the BaseSettings default; no local override), so a misplaced or misspelled key is dropped without error — the 2026-07-22 incident where `spare_warm_lanes` sat under the wrong block for weeks. orchestrator/src/orchestrator/cli.py::check_config therefore does NOT validate via model_validate; it walks the raw YAML through config.py::census_config_keys(config_path) -> ConfigKeyCensus, deliberately so it still reports phantom keys when the file has an unrelated value-level validation error. Exit codes: 1 = genuinely unknown key or unparseable file, 2 = only ignore-entry findings, 0 = clean. A key can be excused with an `x_`/`x-` prefix or a config_key_census.ignore glob entry with a reason. PRACTICAL UPSHOT: "check-config accepts my new block" is a REAL signal for a new config block, not a tautology — an unregistered block exits 1.

3. EventType ADDITIONS ARE COMPLETELY UNCHECKED. orchestrator/src/orchestrator/event_store.py::EventType is a StrEnum (90 members as measured), lowercase snake_case, with member value asserted equal to member name. There is NO registry, allow-list or ALL_EVENT_TYPES constant a new member must join. The dashboard (dashboard/src/dashboard/data/scheduler.py) DELIBERATELY hardcodes plain string literals in _RECOVERY_EVENT_TYPES rather than importing enum members, with an explicit comment that importing a member that does not exist yet would fail at import and take the whole dashboard down since the emitter can be a sibling deploy. And NO test pins the member set: test_event_store.py::TestEventStore::test_all_event_types_valid iterates `for et in EventType` but asserts only isinstance(et.value, str) and et.value == et.name, so it cannot fail on an addition; TestSchedulerOverrideEventTypes::test_override_event_types_are_present uses a SUBSET check (expected <= actual), guarding only against removal. So adding an EventType member is free — and a typo'd or duplicate member name has no automated backstop, which means a new closed vocabulary must carry its own uniqueness assertion.

BONUS, same sweep: orchestrator/src/orchestrator/cli.py::main is a CLICK group (not argparse, not typer), and EVERY existing eval command — eval_cmd ('eval'), eval_ofat_cmd ('eval-ofat'), eval-list-fixtures, eval-sample, eval-matrix, eval-confi…[truncated, 4463 chars total]

GOTCHA for anyone ASSERTING on a reload_config disposition (dark-factory, measured 2026-09-11 while planning task 5379): the report's `unchanged` is an INT COUNT of equal leaves, never a key map. `orchestrator/src/orchestrator/config.py::ConfigDiff` declares `unchanged: int`; `config.py::diff_config` computes it as a bare `unchanged += 1` counter; `apply_reload` and `harness.py::reload_config` pass that scalar through verbatim (the load-failure report hardcodes `'unchanged': 0`). So `tool['unchanged'][KEY]` raises TypeError and `KEY in tool['unchanged']` is permanently false — write neither.

CONSEQUENCE. When a leaf's live value ALREADY equals the file's, the only signal on the wire is the ABSENCE of that leaf from `applied`. A deploy script that asserts `applied[leaf]['new'] == target` therefore FAILS on an idempotent crash-resume against an already-converged process, even though the deploy succeeded — exactly the task-5379 defect in scripts/merge-pytest-n-ab-switch.sh, which re-escalated a live, correct arm.

ABSENCE IS NOT SELF-CORROBORATING, so do not just widen the assertion to "absent ⇒ success". The same absence is produced by (a) a reload that FAILED — `apply_reload` rolls every leaf back, leaving the live config untouched — and (b) a reload of a DIFFERENT orchestrator, which any script taking a caller-supplied escalation port can hit. Require two corroborators, both already on the wire: `reloaded` truthy, AND the report's `config_path` resolving (os.path.realpath, both sides same host) to the file you just edited. `config_path` is reliably non-null even for a `--config`-launched unit with no ORCH_CONFIG_PATH= Environment line, because `config.py::load_config` writes `os.environ['ORCH_CONFIG_PATH'] = str(config_path)` on load and the harness injects it into every report.

Note also that a dict/list/set-valued field (verify_env, verify_runners, …) is an ATOMIC leaf compared by equality (`config.py::_iter_leaves`) — it is reported whole or not at all, never per-key, so you cannot ask "did MY key change" for one.

dark-factory config placement rule discovered while planning task 3136: a knob read ONLY by a per-run script (a systemd-timer job, a sweep CLI) must NOT be registered in fused_memory/config/reload.py::RELOADABLE_FIELDS, even though the task spec asks for a "green-tier hot-reloadable knob". reload.py's own docstring states the safety rule — a leaf is green-tier only if EVERY consumer reads it LIVE off the shared FusedMemoryConfig object apply_reload mutates in place — and tests/test_config_reload.py's convention (TestTopicAnchoredRecallReloadTier) requires a green-tier classification to be PAIRED with a live-read test that earns it. A fresh per-fire process constructs FusedMemoryConfig() at startup, so there is no live read inside the running server to earn the tier; registering it asserts a property that does not exist. The requirement is satisfied more strongly by construction: the next timer fire re-reads the YAML, so a knob edit needs no code change, no restart and no reload_config call. Two further structural constraints from the same module: _iter_leaves descends EXACTLY ONE level, so a reload leaf path is at most `section.leaf` — a nested submodel cannot be addressed, and a map of weights must be one atomic dict leaf (the write_triage.t_high_by_category precedent). And FusedMemoryConfig sets extra='ignore', so a YAML block with no matching schema field is silently dropped with no error — always pair a new config section with a shipped-YAML parse test (the test_config_yaml_enables_require_done_provenance pattern) or the block can read as present while being invisible.

content: GOTCHA (orchestrator config, found re-planning task 3819): a green-tier (RELOADABLE_FIELDS) config SUBMODEL must stay a plain pydantic BaseModel. Do NOT give it `validate_assignment=True` to enforce a cross-field invariant on reload. `config.py::_set_leaf` writes submodel leaves one at a time with a plain setattr, and `apply_reload`'s post-apply `OrchestratorConfig.model_validate(live.model_dump())` is the single authoritative check: it re-runs every submodel `@model_validator` and rolls back all applied leaves on failure. Per-write validation would wrongly refuse a valid multi-leaf retune that is only transiently invalid mid-apply (e.g. moving budget between two leaves under a sum cap). It could also raise during the leaf-by-leaf rollback and leave the live config half-mutated. Test the invariant on reload by driving apply_reload, not by assigning.

candidates.content: reify-cli's integration tests live under crates/reify-cli/tests/harness_cli/*.rs (a single harness binary via tests/harness_cli.rs), not as loose tests/*.rs files — so a task description citing e.g. `reify-cli/tests/cli_build_fea.rs` actually means `reify-cli/tests/harness_cli/cli_build_fea.rs`. Private items in main.rs (a binary crate) are unreachable from there; unit-test them in one of main.rs's own `#[cfg(test)] mod <topic>_tests` modules instead.

In crates/reify-compiler/tests, many test files do NOT compile as their own integration-test binary: they live in a subdirectory (e.g. tests/harness_doc_chunks/geometry_chunk_smoke.rs) and are pulled into an aggregator binary by a #[path] attribute in a sibling tests/harness_doc_chunks.rs. Consequence: `cargo test -p reify-compiler --test geometry_chunk_smoke` fails with "no test target named ..." — you must pass the HARNESS name (--test harness_doc_chunks) and optionally filter by test-fn name. The same shape exists for harness_cli (reify-cli), harness_geometry_solver, harness_geometry_kinds and harness_langcore/harness_patterns. Task descriptions written before a file was relocated into a harness subdir will cite the old flat tests/NAME.rs path, so `git ls-files` returning nothing for the cited path does NOT mean the artifact is missing — grep for a distinctive symbol before concluding a dependency has not landed.

reify: adding a NEW standalone `crates/<c>/tests/<file>.rs` is BLOCKED at source for five "consolidatable" crates — reify-cli, reify-syntax, reify-kernel-occt, reify-eval, reify-compiler. `scripts/check-harness-baseline-registration.sh` (diff-scoped, task 5300) emits `HARNESS_BASELINE_REG FAIL crate=<c> file=<path> reason=unregistered-standalone` and exits 1 for any test file ADDED in your diff under those crates, and `tests/infra/test_harness_kloc_cap.sh` rule (b) is the whole-tree twin. Adding a row to `tests/infra/harness-layout-baseline.manifest` LOOKS like the fix but is explicitly SUPERSEDED (Leo 2026-07-22, esc-5056-11: "actually start using the ratchet" — the manifest is a shrinking ratchet). The sanctioned remedy is to fold the new test into an existing `crates/<c>/tests/harness_<subsystem>/<file>.rs` declared from the harness root with a MANDATORY `#[path = "harness_<subsystem>/<file>.rs"] mod <file>;` — a bare `mod <file>;` in an integration-test crate root resolves against `tests/` and silently binds the wrong file. Seven override stems stay standalone forever (determinism, analytical_validation, modal_benchmarks, buckling_smoke, fea_diagnostics_e2e, tensegrity_t0a, representation_within_assertion) and the harness unit is subject to a raw-`wc -l` kLOC cap that counts the root PLUS its module dir PLUS externally-included files such as `tests/common/`. Crates OUTSIDE those five (e.g. reify-expr, reify-ir, reify-core) are unaffected — a new standalone tests/*.rs there is fine. Plan for this BEFORE proposing "add a per-crate test" in reify-eval or reify-compiler; it changes the shape and cost of the work.

Moving Rust tests from crates/<c>/src/ into crates/<c>/tests/ in reify trips gates that key on the file path. (1) tests/infra/test_no_new_wallclock_rust_deadlines.sh scans crates/*/tests but not src/, so a moved Instant/elapsed upper bound becomes new debt. (2) PLINECITE (crates/reify-audit/plinecite-baseline.txt) scans crates/*/src only, so a moved `file.rs:NNN` comment cite leaves a stale ledger row; convert it to a symbol cite and run plinecite-baseline-gen in shrink-only mode. (3) crates/reify-cli/tests/harness_cli/units_length_boundary_ledger.rs pins named test fns to a source file by text (its OCCT_KERNEL const), so it must be repointed when those tests move.

In reify, a shared Rust test helper that has an OUT-OF-CRATE `#[path]` includer belongs in `crates/<c>/tests/common/`, never in `crates/<c>/tests/harness_<sub>/`. The C1 harness-layout contract (tests/infra/test_harness_kloc_cap.sh) moves files INTO `harness_<sub>/` and splits them back OUT (harness_cli_surface is one such split), so a relative cross-crate `#[path]` at that address breaks with a bare `error: couldn't read ...`; the same contract names `tests/common/` as the retained sibling it deliberately never moves. The move is cost-free on the gates: `harness_layout_unit_lines` re-attributes the file's lines from the unit's `module` component to its `external` one (measured on #6759: external 312/1 file -> 448/2 files, delta exactly the moved file), so the unit total is unchanged and the kLOC cap is not evaded; and `harness_layout_in_scope_standalone` rejects any path nested below `tests/`, so the re-accretion / baseline-registration gates report violations=0 for the new path. Do NOT declare such a file from `common/mod.rs` — a `pub mod` there compiles it into every harness that uses `common`.

reify test-file location gotcha: task #5695 folded 23 standalone `crates/reify-compiler/tests/*.rs` binaries into consolidated harness compile units, so paths cited in older task descriptions are stale. `crates/reify-compiler/tests/forall_statement_lower_tests.rs` is now `crates/reify-compiler/tests/harness_statement_semantics/forall_statement_lower_tests.rs`. Before concluding a referenced test file is missing, check `crates/<crate>/tests/harness_*/` for the same stem. Adding tests to an existing harness member needs no `tests/infra/harness-layout-baseline.manifest` entry (that manifest lists only grandfathered standalone binaries); only the 20000-line per-unit cap in `tests/infra/test_harness_kloc_cap.sh` applies.

In crates/reify-compiler/tests/, files under the harness_*/ subdirectories (e.g. harness_traits/fn_generic_call_inference_tests.rs) are NOT their own cargo test binaries — they are `#[path]`-included modules of a consolidated harness root such as tests/harness_traits.rs (task #5283 merge-gate compile-cost consolidation). To run one, use `cargo test -p reify-compiler --test harness_traits <module_stem>::`; `--test <module_stem>` does not exist and fails with "no test target named ...".

In reify, `crates/reify-compiler/tests/` is organised into harness sub-directories, and many doc comments still cite the pre-move flat paths. `struct_ctor_field_conformance_tests.rs` is at `tests/harness_structure_declarations/`, `examples_smoke.rs` and `ctor_conformance_corpus_survey.rs` at `tests/harness_compilation_surface/`, and the math-signature result-type tests at `tests/harness_constructor_typing/`. Run these with `cargo test -p reify-compiler --test <harness_name>` (the harness aggregator is the test target, not the individual file). When a task description or doc comment cites a flat `tests/<name>.rs` path that `git ls-files` cannot find, check the harness sub-directories before concluding the file is missing.

reify's two harness-layout gates have DIFFERENT scopes and the asymmetry is easy to get wrong. `scripts/check-harness-baseline-registration.sh` + `tests/infra/harness-layout-baseline.manifest` are scoped by `_HL_CRATES` to five consolidatable crates only (reify-cli, reify-syntax, reify-kernel-occt, reify-eval, reify-compiler) — a `tests/*.rs` in any other crate is structurally out of scope and needs no baseline row. But `tests/infra/test_harness_kloc_cap.sh`'s Section 6 live scan iterates `crates/*/tests` UNSCOPED and keys on the `harness_*.rs` stem, so naming a test target `harness_<something>.rs` in ANY crate opts it into the `#[path]`-declared-submodule mandate and the kLOC ceiling. For a small standalone integration test in a new crate, use a plain descriptive stem (e.g. `fixture_tree.rs`), not a `harness_` prefix — `crates/reify-kernel-conformance/tests/*.rs` is the precedent.

reify test-path drift: task descriptions written before #5281 name reify-eval integration tests as `crates/reify-eval/tests/<name>.rs`, but that consolidation folded whole subsystems (fea_/tensegrity_/stress_/objective_/multi_/process_/as_printed_/kinematic_) into single harness binaries — the file now lives at `crates/reify-eval/tests/harness_fea_solver_e2e/<name>.rs` as a `#[path]` module. Always resolve the real path with `git ls-files` before planning. This matters beyond cosmetics: the harness binaries are OCCT-only, and `solve_elastic_static_body_e2e.rs` documents that referencing any `reify_kernel_gmsh` symbol from a non-gmsh reify-eval test binary pulls gmsh's `inventory::submit!` into it and breaks its `kernel_count`/registry-size assertions. Gmsh-requiring tests must go in a standalone gmsh binary that carries the `extern crate reify_kernel_gmsh as _;` anchor.

In reify, `crates/reify-eval` is one of the 5 consolidatable crates (tests/infra/harness-layout-lib.sh:123, alongside reify-cli, reify-syntax, reify-kernel-occt, reify-compiler), so adding a NEW top-level `crates/reify-eval/tests/*.rs` file trips scripts/check-harness-baseline-registration.sh (task #5300). Sanctioned placements for a new integration test there: add a fn to an already-grandfathered top-level binary, or add a `#[path]`-registered module under an existing `harness_*/` root (subject to the 20000-line rule-(a) cap in tests/infra/test_harness_kloc_cap.sh). Pure-Rust logic with no kernel dependency is better placed in the crate's own `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` — it needs no binary at all and runs in stub builds where `#[cfg(has_gmsh)]` tests are compiled out.

In crates/reify-compiler/tests/, many individual test files have been folded into 14 aggregate "harness" test binaries: a harness_<topic>.rs aggregator plus a harness_<topic>/ directory holding the member files (harness_compilation_surface, harness_geometry_solver, harness_units_materials, harness_langcore, etc.). Consequence: `cargo test -p reify-compiler --test <filename>` FAILS for any folded file — you must use `cargo test -p reify-compiler --test <harness_name> <filename>`, e.g. `--test harness_compilation_surface meta_compile_tests` for crates/reify-compiler/tests/harness_compilation_surface/meta_compile_tests.rs. Older task descriptions and follow-up tasks often cite the pre-fold flat path (crates/reify-compiler/tests/meta_compile_tests.rs); resolve the real path with `git ls-files | grep <name>` before assuming a file is missing.

Reify gotcha when verifying that a cited test really runs: a `#[cfg(not(debug_assertions))]` `#[test]` does not exist in a debug build, so a name-regex nextest filterset silently matches ZERO for it and the run looks like the test was deleted. Measured 2026-09-21: `occt_release_armed_bare_length_reports_without_panicking` (crates/reify-kernel-occt/src/lib.rs) and `fidget_release_armed_bare_length_reports_without_panicking` (crates/reify-kernel-fidget/src/kernel.rs) are both release-only this way — they execute only under the merge gate's `--profile both`. A registry/ledger that binds tests by SOURCE-TEXT definition (grep for `fn <name>(`) still covers such a row in a debug run, whereas one that binds by observed execution cannot.

Gotcha: task descriptions that cite flat reify-compiler integration-test paths like crates/reify-compiler/tests/<name>_stdlib_compile.rs are often stale — task #5694 (merge-gate-compile-cost consolidation) folded those binaries into crates/reify-compiler/tests/harness_<subsystem>/<name>.rs as #[path] modules of one harness_<subsystem>.rs binary. Locate the real file with `git ls-files | grep <name>` before planning; also note that any 'separate crate, can't share helpers' rationale in such files is now false for siblings in the same harness.

Two reify test-infrastructure constraints that bind any new cross-driver gate, confirmed at main 9a992fc2f2. (1) A NEW STANDALONE TEST BINARY IN crates/reify-cli IS FORBIDDEN: the harness-layout ratchet (tests/infra/test_harness_kloc_cap.sh + tests/infra/harness-layout-baseline.manifest) records that grandfathering a new standalone binary in reify-cli/-syntax/-occt/-eval/-compiler is SUPERSEDED (Leo 2026-07-22, esc-5056-11); the sanctioned remedy is consolidating into a harness_<subsystem>/ compile unit. reify-cli's integration tests live in one binary, crates/reify-cli/tests/harness_cli.rs, with ~76 `#[path = "harness_cli/<stem>.rs"] mod <stem>;` declarations and shared helpers in tests/common/mod.rs (fixture_path, run_subcommand, run_args using CARGO_BIN_EXE_reify). (2) Any new gate-resident test owes its DRIFT-GUARD REGISTRATIONS IN THE SAME DIFF — a bucket row in tests/infra/run-all-classification.manifest for a new tests/infra/test_*.sh, the wallclock-bounds registration for any elapsed-time assertion, and nextest heavy/smoke partition entries where applicable. The cautionary case is esc-4914-162, where a gate-resident smoke binary landed without them and turned main RED for every subsequent merge because its registration leaf was ordered by PRD prose rather than a real dependency edge.

In reify, you cannot add a new standalone `tests/<name>.rs` integration-test binary to the 5 consolidatable crates (reify-cli, reify-syntax, reify-kernel-occt, reify-eval, reify-compiler — the `_HL_CRATES` array in tests/infra/harness-layout-lib.sh). tests/infra/test_harness_kloc_cap.sh enforces that every top-level tests/*.rs is either a sanctioned `harness_<subsystem>.rs`, one of 7 named override binaries, or grandfathered in tests/infra/harness-layout-baseline.manifest; anything else fails the merge gate with `HARNESS_KLOC_CAP FAIL ... reason=unsanctioned-standalone`. The reify-kernel-occt grandfather baseline is fully drained (zero entries), so ANY new standalone binary there fails. Per docs/prds/merge-gate-compile-cost.md an over-cap harness is resolved by SPLIT into another harness_*, never by raising CAP_LINES (currently 20000 raw lines). Consequence: "give this flaky test its own test binary for isolation" is not an available fix in these crates — fix the shared state instead. [Corrected 2026-09-16 by the curator sitting per gate task #7568, checked at main 2b9b48e241: the crate set was cited as harness-layout-lib.sh:60-62; it is the `_HL_CRATES` array, at line 123 in that commit.]

candidates.content: Reify gotcha: crates/*/tests/harness_<subsystem>.rs roots do NOT contain all of their compile unit's code — the absorbed former-standalone test files live in the sibling harness_<subsystem>/ module directory, and some roots additionally pull in shared helpers from OUTSIDE that directory (e.g. crates/reify-eval/tests/harness_topology_selector.rs declares `#[path = "common/differential.rs"] mod differential;`, 2,128 lines; harness_cli/harness_occt/harness_fea_solver_e2e use a bare `mod common;`). Any tool that sizes or audits a harness compile unit must walk the module dir, and decide explicitly whether to attribute the shared tests/common/ includes — a top-level `wc -l` of the root file reports 15-170 lines for units that are actually 1k-21k.

Gotcha (measured 2026-10-13 on main 3ff216c467): reify-syntax's `crates/reify-syntax/tests/harness_syntax.rs` compile unit is 17994 lines including its 70-line `tests/common/mod.rs` charge — 6 lines under `tests/infra/test_harness_kloc_cap.sh`'s 18000-line WARN line (90% of CAP_LINES=20000). A unit newly crossing that line is RED in the guard's Section 5d unless added to `_KLOC_WARN_KNOWN` with a split cite, so new reify-syntax integration tests should go in `harness_syntax_lowering.rs` (5354 lines; membership rule = `harness_syntax_lowering/*_lowering_tests.rs`) or another unit, not `harness_syntax/`.

Reify gate-resident-test rule: adding a test to an existing `crates/*/tests/harness_<subsystem>.rs` as a `#[path = "harness_<sub>/<stem>.rs"] mod <stem>;` submodule requires NO drift-guard registration at all — `harness_*` units are excluded from `tests/infra/harness-layout-baseline.manifest` by construction, and `run-all-classification.manifest`, the nextest binary selectors in `.config/nextest.toml`, the wallclock-bounds guard, and the THROUGHPUT-COUNTS sentinel (`docs/notes/verify-scope-throughput.md`) all apply only to NEW top-level standalone `crates/<c>/tests/*.rs` binaries. Only the `CAP_LINES=20000` per-compile-unit budget in `tests/infra/test_harness_kloc_cap.sh` applies. Explicit `#[path]` is mandatory, not stylistic: a harness root is an integration-test crate root, so a bare `mod x;` resolves to the sibling `tests/x.rs`, not the subdir.

In crates/reify-compiler/tests/harness_doc_chunks/, cite sibling modules by SYMBOL or TEST name, not by line number: the merge-gate-compile-cost PRD keeps absorbing standalone tests/*.rs suites into consolidated harness roots, which shifts every line number in the absorbed file at once. Measured instance — all six of fence_gate.rs's line citations into geometry_chunk_smoke.rs (:617, :661, :704, :333, :105) were stale after task 5759's absorption grew that file to 2609 lines, and the resulting comments confidently described a floor and a failure mode that did not exist. A stale line number reads as authoritative while pointing at unrelated code; a symbol name degrades to a compile error (if imported) or a failed grep (if prose).

Its consts (e.g. OCCT_KERNEL = "crates/reify-kernel-occt/src/lib.rs", FIDGET_KERNEL, GEOMETRY_OPS) are read by every_cited_test_fn_is_defined_in_its_file, which looks for `fn <name>(` with #[test] in that file. c89fec13-0300-41ec-b72d-121cc5edddaa.content: To measure a reify test harness against HARNESS_KLOC_CAP, use the guard's own measure — `source tests/infra/harness-layout-lib.sh` then `harness_layout_unit_lines crates/<c>/tests/harness_<subsystem>.rs`, which prints `<total> <root_lines> <module_lines> <module_files> <external_lines> <external_files>`. Do NOT use `cat harness_X.rs harness_X/*.rs | wc -l`: it omits the external `tests/common/` attribution the cap actually charges (rustc compiles a separate copy of an included helper into every binary), and in a Claude Code session the cargo/skim PreToolUse wrapper intercepts multi-file `cat` and returns 0 lines. Two task descriptions have quoted wrong harness sizes from that `cat` form.

candidates.content:
Task 'Grid-services-at-events β: compute_fleet_spare_capacity_kw (firm spare at events, net of own use)' completed. Implement the core physics: firm spare dispatchable capacity per event window, summed across the fleet, derived ONLY from observable per-timestep SOC + discharge (no purpose-attribution exists — see PRD decision 2).

PRD: docs/prds/enhanced-grid-services-capacity-at-events.md task β (unlocks γ). §Sketch + §Contract (I1, I2).

Work (src/solar_challenge/gridservices.py):
- compute_fleet_spare_capacity_kw(fleet_results, windows) -> tuple[float, ...] (one avail_kW per window).
- Per home, per window w=[t0,t1] with event_hours=t1-t0:
  P_spare = max_discharge_kw - max_{t in w} battery_discharge(t)   # inverter headroom, firm
  E_spare = min_{t in w} (battery_soc(t) - min_soc_kwh)            # smallest above-floor buffer, firm

candidates.content: G6 premise error found in grid-services-pricing-model PRD §9 P8 (displaced self-use), corrected on task 837. P8 extends the P6 fixture, in which home A sits at its SOC floor for one minute on day 1, so A's day-1 availability is 0 and A displaces nothing that day. The fleet's daily displaced energies are therefore (1.5, 3.0) kWh, a mean of 2.25 kWh per event, not the PRD's "1.5 kWh per home per event × 2 homes" (3.0). The PRD's figure holds only on a fixture without A's floor minute. Displaced self-use per home-day is min(avail × h, post-window discharge energy), so it is zero whenever that day's availability is zero.

Process lesson from the 2026-10-16 solar_challenge grid-services firmness investigation: a /prd G6 measurement on a small slice can mislead. The S9 PRD's §2.2 probe (first 3 battery homes of the board scenario, two January weeks) reported £0 event income and the PRD framed the whole stream around it; the full 100-home, full-year measurement found three homes that never touch the floor (£3/yr) and, more importantly, that 64% of event days never reach the floor in-window, which changed the modelling conclusion (an artefact of the firmness rule, not an absence of capacity). Norm: when a PRD's premise rests on a measured figure for "the board scenario", measure the actual board fleet over the actual window population (all homes, the whole season), and report the distribution (fraction of days/homes affected), not only the aggregate. A 100-home full-year run costs ~11 min here, which is cheap against a mis-framed stream.

Root cause is NOT a bug: under Economy-7 peak-arbitrage dispatch the battery is already fully discharging into the evening peak (16:00-18:00) at exactly the hours winter DFS events fire, so there is zero spare capacity for grid services. Arbitrage and grid-services flexibility CANNIBALISE the same battery at the same hour — they are not additive. Consequence: the consulting model's headline "£280/home/yr (£250 arbitrage + £30 grid services)" cannot be simply summed in practice; to earn grid-services revenue you must reserve battery headroom at event times, trading off arbitrage. This is hard-physics confirmation of the value+buildability model §1.1 warning "do not simply add the column maxima".

Description: Follow-up filed by task 1243's implementer (claude-task-1243-implementer) on 2026-10-15, from code reading on branch task/1243 (base main b9a80a4). Idempotency key: agent-followup-1243. There is no escalation record.

CONTEXT. Task 1243 (S11·θ; PRD docs/prds/review-all-shared-frontend-layer-and-generated-wire-types.md F16, ruling R11) gives frontend/src/components/RunsPanel.tsx a fallback for a run state outside the BillingRunState union. Before the fix the panel crashed and the one ViewErrorBoundary blanked Fleet Health. The task's plan also rejected a calm fallback because "calm would hide the skew". The frontend tsconfig lib is ES2020, so Object.hasOwn fails tsc, and both `in` and `TABLE[key] ?? fallback` read Object.prototype members such as 'constructor'. Render an unknown state in the attention tone (ATTENTION_TONE in frontend/src/components/tones.ts) with its raw text, and decide how LivenessPanel's summary should count such a device. candidates.content: Cockpit (cockpit/src/cockpit) TUI poll pattern: CockpitApp.refresh_registry originally ran scan_sessions()+list_decisions() synchronously on Textual's event loop, freezing input ~4.5s at 10k session dirs (esc-2303-1 F1). Fix pattern (task 2513): keep refresh_registry synchronous for the initial on_mount paint + direct-call tests, split it into _scan_registry() (I/O) and _apply_scan() (UI), and drive the recurring set_interval poll through a @work(thread=True) worker that runs _scan_registry off-thread and marshals _apply_scan back via self.call_from_thread. Use a main-thread-set/cleared _scan_in_flight flag (NOT @work exclusive) for drop-tick backpressure, since a scan (~4.5s) is slower than poll_interval (1.5s) and exclusive would cancel-restart-starve.

CORRECTION (task 5839, commits 8eb3298d4d / 4b1dbbddbb): the claim that the cockpit stale-scan race is "unreachable in production, a test-only race" was FALSE.
- The mechanism: CockpitApp._apply_boost and action_drop re-read decisions after their own write WITHOUT a scan seq. So a poll scan issued before a b/x keypress could land after it and revert the write. The boosted row fell back, a dropped decision reappeared, and the next 'b' persisted a stale boost, losing a press.
- How it surfaced: as a passes_in_isolation flake of TestBoostReordersAndPersists.
- The fix: CockpitApp._reread_decisions, a SEQUENCED read. It takes a seq from _next_scan_seq() and advances _applied_scan_seq, so the existing guard drops the earlier-issued scan.
- RULE: any adoption of registry state outside _apply_scan must be sequenced the same way.
- A cockpit test that flakes under a live poll may be exposing such a production race. Do not mask it with poll_interval=60. Instead, replay the interleaving deterministically by hand-driving _next_scan_seq, _scan_registry and then a late _apply_scan, as cockpit/tests/test_app.py::TestInFlightScanCannotUndoAKeypressWrite does.

In cockpit/src/cockpit/app.py (CockpitApp), the F1 non-blocking-poll fix (esc-2303-1) split refresh_registry into _scan_registry() (pure I/O: scan + list_decisions) and _apply_scan(records, decisions) (the UI half). The session-table/decision-queue rebuild (order_sessions -> self._records, table.replace_rows, _sync_detail_pane, _rebuild_queue) plus the snapshot short-circuit now live in _apply_scan, NOT in refresh_registry. Both the synchronous path (on_mount/refresh_registry) and the threaded poll path (_scan_registry_worker via @work(thread=True) + call_from_thread) funnel through _apply_scan, so any "what renders in the session table" change should hook _apply_scan to cover both.

In cockpit's test_app.py, CockpitApp._apply_scan has no protection against a stale scan result being applied after a fresher one: if a real background poll tick (set_interval -> _poll_registry -> threaded _scan_registry_worker) reads the registry before a test's on-disk write, but its call_from_thread(_apply_scan, ...) hand-off lands after the test's own direct refresh_registry() call, the stale result silently clobbers the fresher state (e.g. table.row_count regresses from 2 back to 1). This is unreachable in production (on_mount calls refresh_registry() directly exactly once, before set_interval is even registered), so it's a test-only race. Any pilot test that calls app.refresh_registry() directly must use a large poll_interval (e.g. 60) to keep the real timer from firing during the test -- this idiom is already established in TestNonBlockingPoll/TestThreadedScanReachesUI/TestScanBackpressure. TestPollRefresh's two tests (test_new_record_appears_and_orders_blocked_first, test_mutated_status_reflected_after_poll) were missing this and were fixed under task 2517. Note: dozens of other tests in test_app.py still use poll_interval=0.05 with a direct refresh_registry() call and carry the same latent (very low-probability) race -- not fixed project-wide, only the two that had actually flaked.

Fleet Cockpit performance fact (measured 2026-07-13): cockpit.app.refresh_registry runs scan_sessions() SYNCHRONOUSLY on Textual's main event loop via set_interval, so at 10,258 session dirs each poll blocks the UI for ~4.5s (operator saw the cursor line take ~5s to update when moved during a scan, instant between scans). The in-memory snapshot short-circuit only skips the RE-RENDER, not the disk walk — the full directory scan is paid every tick regardless of whether anything changed. This is PRD open-Q5 ("ship the poll; optimize only when measured — decide in C5a"), now measured. Fix filed as task 2513 (thread-worker scan + mtime/inotify short-circuit). Workaround for a live demo: launch with a high poll_interval (e.g. 120).

(2) reap_answered_decisions syncs exactly one field, one direction (escalation resolved→answered / dismissed→dropped), and runs only while a watcher session loops — a stopped watcher silently stops reaping, with no liveness check; dangling ids stay open forever. Task 2606 ('Cockpit: harden _apply_scan against stale-scan regressions with a monotonic scan-sequence guard') is done, merged via commit d5c745af887c2e980616ea6b1030f796e421fcab. Follow-up from esc-2517-1 (task 2517 verify). Added a monotonic scan-sequence counter so CockpitApp._apply_scan (cockpit/src/cockpit/app.py) drops any scan result whose sequence is older than the newest already-applied, preventing a stale background-poll result from regressing a fresher direct refresh_registry() call. This was a latent test-harness hazard (unreachable in production, since on_mount calls refresh_registry() once before set_interval is registered) affecting ~27 call sites in cockpit/tests/test_app.py that combine a short poll_interval (0.05s) with a direct refresh_registry() call. AMENDMENT to the task-5449 cockpit Textual probe note (6ac903a0-3854-40b6-ac39-353067f7aeec). Two updates: its fact 1 has LANDED, and its fact 2 is only HALF of the vacuity problem.

1. THE `prevent` FIX IS NOW LANDED, not planned. Task 5449 shipped it (commit aa091035d5, cockpit/src/cockpit/app.py::CockpitApp._rebuild_session_table): `with self.prevent(DataTable.RowHighlighted): table.replace_rows(...)`, plus a new `_resync_session_detail(slug)` that assigns `self._selected_slug` UNCONDITIONALLY but re-renders only while `DetailPane.source is DetailSource.SESSION`. Full cockpit suite green (387 passed), ruff + pyright clean. So the parent note's "as of 2026-09-13 only planned (task 5449 steps 13/14)" caveat is now stale. Note this is NOT a replacement for task 4439's `_persisted_selected_slug` debouncing — 5449 left that path untouched and suppresses the reposts for a different reason (pane ownership, not write churn); the two are complementary, and the parent note's framing of `prevent` as "a candidate alternative to the 4439 fix" was not how it landed.

2. THERE ARE TWO WAYS A COCKPIT PILOT CURSOR-MOVE TEST GOES VACUOUS, and the parent note names only the first. Both were hit for real writing test_app.py::TestDecisionQueueDetail.
   (a) THE EVENT NEVER FIRES — the parent's fact 2: move_cursor onto the already-highlighted row posts nothing.
   (b) THE EVENT FIRES, THE HANDLER RUNS, AND THE ASSERTION PASSES ANYWAY, because the pane ALREADY displayed the target's content for an unrelated reason. Measured: a test moved the QUEUE cursor onto a `session:<slug>` row and asserted that session's question rendered — but that session was AWAITING_INPUT, so order_sessions had already made it the session TABLE's row 0, and the mount-time session sync had rendered it before the move. The test passed against code that had no session branch at all. Fix: seed a second awaiting session with an older start_ts to take table row 0, and self-check with a NEGATIVE assertion that the target's text is NOT in `detail.rendered_text` before the move. (a) is caught by asserting on highlighted_key() before the move; (b) is not — only a pre-move assertion on the PANE catches it.

3. order_queue's SCORE TIEBREAK IS NOT REACHED AS OFTEN AS IT LOOKS. `sorted(items, key=lambda i: (-i.score, i.key))` tiebreaks by key only at EQUAL score, and severity feeds the score: a DecisionRecord with `severity='blocking'` outscores one left at the default `severity=''`. Measured — two decisions with identical filed_at and manual_boost=0 did NOT order by key, because one carried severity='blocking' and took row 0. To place a decision at a known non-row-0 position in a pilot test, give the OTHER row an explicit `manual_boost` (TestDecisionQueueRender's existing idiom) rather than relying on the key tiebreak.

CORRECTION, task 4439 (2026-09-04, commits d02c316d81 + f9b4fb0028) — SUPERSEDES two now-stale cockpit memories: bb5b54d9-44e5-4c2d-a107-10ff52e84761 ("CockpitApp writes cockpit-ui.json on EVERY SessionTable RowHighlighted") and 536c8ef6-a1fb-4c7a-8dc2-e1a9ae1d349a ("cockpit-ui.json's mtime can churn on every refresh_registry() tick"). Both describe the pre-4439 write path. I could not amend them in place: update_memory's content_amend arm is restricted to recon-stage-*/curator-* agents.

WHAT IS TRUE NOW. cockpit-ui.json is written on a DEBOUNCED schedule. on_data_table_row_highlighted -> CockpitApp._sync_detail_pane only MARKS _ui_config_dirty, and only when the slug actually CHANGES. CockpitApp._flush_ui_config does the write, called as the FIRST statement of _poll_registry — deliberately ABOVE the `if self._scan_in_flight: return` drop-tick guard, because a ~4.5s 10k-session scan outlasts the 1.5s poll interval and a flush below the guard would be starved for as long as scans overlap. CockpitApp.on_unmount still calls _persist_ui_config UNCONDITIONALLY (not the flush), which is what keeps the file created even for an app that mounts over an empty registry.

THE TEST GOTCHA THIS CREATES. With poll_interval=60 (the standard cockpit test idiom, so no tick fires), a Textual pilot test that merely moves the cursor now has NOTHING on disk — cockpit-ui.json does not exist until unmount. Any test that assumed "move the cursor, then read the file" breaks. Either drive an explicit `app._poll_registry()` tick, or let the app unmount first (the two-sequential-mounts restore-seam recipe still works unchanged, because the unmount write is what lands the selection between mounts).

TO COUNT WRITES, patch `cockpit.app.save_ui_config`, NOT `cockpit.ui_config.save_ui_config`: app.py binds the symbol at import time and resolves it from module globals at call time. See test_app.py::_count_ui_config_writes, which delegates to the real function so the on-disk half of an assertion stays genuine. Counting at the seam is necessary rather than nice-to-have — an mtime/bytes diff cannot tell one write from four when every write carries identical content inside one mtime granule.

MEASURED, and worth knowing before you write a test: SessionTable.replace_rows posts TWO RowHighlighted messages per rebuild with DIFFERENT row keys when the cursor is parked on a non-row-0 row — clear() resets the cursor to row 0, then the cursor is restored. Pre-4439 that was two cockpit-ui.json writes per rebuild, not one. Post-4439 it means a rebuild still leaves the dirty flag set (parked -> row-0 -> parked contains a real change), so a tick on which a rebuild happened still costs ONE redundant write of the identical slug; over a STATIC registry, where _apply_scan's snapshot short-circuit prevents the rebuild entirely, the app converges to zero writes per tick. Residual recorded in esc-4439-2, deliberately not fixed (it would mean changing replace_rows' cursor restore).

STILL VALID from the superseded entries: a write-discipline test that snapshots the tmp_path tree MID-lifecycle must scope byte-identity assertions to sessions/ and decisions/ only; tests that snapshot BEFORE the app ever mounts avoid the issue since they only assert cockpit-ui.json is an allowed NEW path.

DE-FLAKE DIAGNOSTIC for a SELF-HEALING race (dark-factory, task 5839, measured 2026-09-24): when the system repairs the bad state on its own a moment later, repetition barely shows the red. Measure the HAZARD, not the failures.

THE CASE. cockpit/tests/test_app.py::TestBoostReordersAndPersists reddened once under load (passes_in_isolation). The defect: CockpitApp._apply_boost/action_drop re-read decisions after their write WITHOUT a scan seq. So a poll scan issued before the keypress could land after it and revert self._decisions, and the next 'b' built on the stale boost (a lost update). The next 50 ms poll tick healed the view, so the test only failed when a keypress or assertion fell inside that window.

MEASURED. The unmodified test body passed 120/120 at -n 24, loadavg ~84. Repetition alone would have 'proved' it fine.

THE TECHNIQUE. Wrap the state-adoption seam (here app._apply_scan) in a spy. For each landing, record the value the landing READ plus the in-memory value BEFORE and AFTER it; flag any landing where after < before. Result: 22/120 runs hit a regressing landing before the fix, 0/120 after it at a heavier load (~150). This gives a before/after metric for the fix that does not depend on catching the red. It also proves the mechanism before any fix is written.

THEN pin it deterministically by ARRANGING the interleaving through the seams (issue seq + read, then write, then late apply) rather than racing the timer. See memory 56cb045a for the mocked/arranged-RED vs live-test split, and 3f3123e4 for process-concurrency reproduction. Here the replay went red on the first run: `assert 1 < 0` (view reverted) and `2 == 3` (press lost).

COCKPIT GOTCHA (task 4056): `registry_reader.build_snapshot` is not just a re-render trigger — it is the WAKE-UP TRIGGER for every consumer that runs inside `CockpitApp._rebuild_queue`, including `_prune_overlays`. `_apply_scan` early-returns on an unchanged snapshot, so anything keyed on state the rebuild resolves is silently never evaluated on a tick the snapshot calls a no-op.

THE INVARIANT: a change-detection snapshot must be AT LEAST AS STRONG as any identity keyed off state the wake path resolves. Violating it fails silently and permanently, not loudly — nothing errors; the consumer simply never runs.

THE CONCRETE BUG: `_ask_identity` keys a session overlay on `(question.text, question.asked_at)`, but `build_snapshot` appended only `question.text`. An AWAITING_INPUT(Q1) -> AWAITING_INPUT(Q2) re-ask with IDENTICAL text and a fresh `asked_at` produced a byte-identical snapshot, so the drop-overlay prune never ran and the operator's stale drop suppressed a brand-new live ask for the process's whole lifetime. Identical text is the COMMON case: `orchestrator.session_hooks._extract_question` sets `text=str(message)` verbatim from the Notification hook's canned message and `asked_at=datetime.now(UTC).isoformat()` fresh on every hook — a repeated permission prompt differs ONLY in `asked_at`. Fix was one line: append `question.asked_at` to the per-session tuple.

DO NOT "FIX" IT BY MOVING THE CONSUMER AHEAD OF THE SHORT-CIRCUIT. Running `_prune_overlays` before `_apply_scan`'s early return is actively wrong: the prune resolves liveness through `self._records`/`self._decisions`, which `_apply_scan` assigns only AFTER the return, so it would judge every overlay against the PREVIOUS tick's records and could expire a live overlay on stale data. Strengthen the trigger, don't reorder the pipeline.

DISTINGUISH TWO KINDS OF TIMESTAMP. The standing snapshot rule excludes `start_ts`/age to keep a quiet poll a no-op diff, and that rule is about values that MOVE ON THEIR OWN — not about timestamps as such. `asked_at` is an on-disk stamp written only when a new Question is stamped, so including it reintroduces no flicker. Both no-flicker guards (`test_excludes_start_ts_and_age`, `test_only_wall_clock_age_differing_is_unchanged`) stay green. Read the two "(never start_ts/age)" blurbs with that distinction in mind.

The decision side has no analogous hole: `_DECISION_SNAPSHOT_FIELDS` already carries text, filed_at AND state — a strict superset of the `(text, filed_at)` decision identity plus its OPEN liveness gate.

WHEN ADDING ANY NEW `_rebuild_queue` consumer: check its key against the snapshot's field set first, and pin it with a test at BOTH levels. A test that varies the identity field AND some other snapshot field (e.g. the question text) cannot detect this class of bug — the other field moves the snapshot by itself. Vary ONLY the identity field.

Cockpit Textual gotcha, MEASURED on task 5449 against the real Textual version in a worktree (three headless-pilot probes). Extends the two existing notes on SessionTable.replace_rows reposting DataTable.RowHighlighted (the 4439 "it's a PAIR, away-and-back" note and the earlier cockpit-ui.json churn note) with three facts neither covers.

1. THE REPOSTS CAN BE SUPPRESSED AT THE CALL SITE. Wrapping the rebuild from the APP side — `with self.prevent(DataTable.RowHighlighted): table.replace_rows(...)` inside CockpitApp._rebuild_session_table, where `self` is the App and the posting widget is its child — suppresses exactly the rebuild-generated events. A genuine operator `move_cursor` afterwards still posts normally. Measured: a changed-registry refresh that shifts the session cursor's index went from 3 handler events (DecisionQueue, then the SessionTable away-and-back pair) to 1 (the DecisionQueue's alone). Textual's `prevent` is ContextVar-scoped, so it reaches a child widget's posts without needing to be called on the widget itself. Nothing is lost by suppressing them: _rebuild_session_table already performs its own explicit _sync_detail_pane(table.highlighted_slug()) immediately after the rebuild, precisely because the reposts are unreliable (a same-row-different-content rebuild posts nothing at all). This is a candidate alternative to the _persisted_selected_slug debouncing fix from task 4439 — it removes the transient excursion at the source rather than making a latch immune to it — but as of 2026-09-13 it is only planned (task 5449 steps 13/14), not landed.

2. move_cursor ONTO THE ALREADY-HIGHLIGHTED ROW POSTS NOTHING. `table.move_cursor(row=N)` where N is already the cursor's row emits no RowHighlighted at all. A pilot test that seeds one queue row and then "moves the cursor to it" is therefore VACUOUS — the handler never runs and the assertion passes for the wrong reason. Seed >= 2 rows and target a row that is not row 0 at mount, and self-check with an assertion on highlighted_key() BEFORE the move.

3. AT MOUNT BOTH TABLES POST, DecisionQueue FIRST, SessionTable SECOND — even though CockpitApp._apply_scan calls _rebuild_session_table BEFORE _rebuild_queue. Consequence: whatever the SessionTable's handler branch does wins the detail pane at startup, so wiring a DecisionQueue branch into on_data_table_row_highlighted does not change post-mount behaviour. (Note this ordering is the opposite of the FOCUS ordering already in memory, where the DecisionQueue being first-composed means it holds keyboard focus and wins Enter/RowSelected.)

Cockpit DecisionRecord sweep, 2026-09-16: open dark_factory rows went from 34 to a handful in one sitting, and the mechanics are worth knowing. There is NO CLI verb that closes a decision by id — session_registry.py offers write-decision and reap-decisions, and reap-decisions only closes rows whose escalation_id resolved. Rows filed deliberately WITHOUT an escalation_id (so they could not be auto-closed) need the Python API: `sys.path.insert(0,'orchestrator/src/orchestrator'); import session_registry as sr; sr.update_decision_state('<id>', 'answered'|'dropped')`, which runs from the repo root under plain python3 (stdlib only), is fail-soft and locks per id. What the sweep found: most rows were July/August questions Leo had ALREADY ruled on and that had already been carried out (concurrency cut to 24, xdist capped at 8, a 7th account added, the veto-streak alarm silenced, the metadata vocabulary reconciled), or situations that no longer existed (an orphaned watcher lease, a 26h-stale fleet, merge-worktree husks, task 3082's thrash counter). Every close was backed by a fresh probe; age alone was never treated as evidence. Two seat recommendations were overridden after measuring: task 3002's orphan-reaper false-positive class has NOT recurred in the retained archive since 08-17, so no priority bump was warranted, and the "reset task 3105" row asks for the one action Leo has forbidden.

AMENDMENT to the task-5449 cockpit Textual probe note (6ac903a0-3854-40b6-ac39-353067f7aeec). Its fact 1 says the RowHighlighted reposts "CAN BE SUPPRESSED AT THE CALL SITE" from the APP side, and its landed amendments generalise that to both tables. That framing has a hole this note closes: it silently assumes every rebuild is initiated by the app. A rebuild the WIDGET initiates has no app call site to wrap, and the suppression must then live in the widget.

MEASURED 2026-09-16 in .worktrees/5450 (Textual 8.2.8, real CockpitApp, headless pilot), while planning task 5450 (deriving the decision-queue question column's width from the terminal instead of a hardcoded 60). That task needs DecisionQueue.on_resize to re-render its own rows at a new column width — a clear(columns=True) + add_row + move_cursor rebuild originating INSIDE the widget, on a path CockpitApp._rebuild_queue's `with self.prevent(DataTable.RowHighlighted):` does not enclose.

THREE-WAY MEASUREMENT, operator parked on a session row (_detail_owner=SESSION_TABLE, detail pane showing that session's question, queue cursor deliberately on row 1 so the rebuild's cursor excursion is real):
- NO prevent  -> _detail_owner flipped to QUEUE and the pane's contents were replaced. A terminal resize would STEAL the detail pane from the session table.
- queue.prevent(DataTable.RowHighlighted) (WIDGET-level, `self` is the DataTable subclass) -> owner stayed SESSION_TABLE, pane kept its contents, cursor still restored to row 1 by key.
- app.prevent(...) (APP-level) -> identical to widget-level.

So widget-level `self.prevent(...)` is sufficient, which follows from `prevent` being ContextVar-scoped (the parent note's own observation, read in the other direction: it reaches DOWN from app to child widget, and works just as well when called ON the widget that posts).

WHY THIS BITES QUIETLY. As of 2026-09-16 no cockpit test calls `pilot.resize_terminal` at all, so the full 390-test suite passes with the hazard present — the regression is invisible to the existing gate and only a purpose-built test catches it. Any future widget-originated re-render (resize, a CSS/layout reaction, a widget-owned timer) inherits the same trap.

RULE OF THUMB: ask who INITIATES the rebuild. App-initiated -> keep the `prevent` at the app call site, where _rebuild_queue/_rebuild_session_table already pair it with an explicit _resync_*_detail in the suppressed reposts' place. Widget-initiated -> the widget suppresses for itself, and do NOT push that suppression down into replace_rows/_reflow shared with the app path: that would silently take over a policy the app makes explicitly and leave a future caller who WANTS the event no way to opt in. Note a resize needs NO _resync counterpart — it changes column widths only, never the underlying records, so leaving the pane untouched is the correct outcome.

content: Cockpit poll-race replays, as of task 5851 (commits 76f98913ee / 6d1454426a on task/5851): CockpitApp takes a `decisions_reader` constructor kwarg (default registry_reader.scan_decisions), which is the app's ONLY decision read, used at both _scan_registry and _reread_decisions. To replay a poll scan landing after a keypress write or after a fresher scan, do NOT hand-drive the private halves _next_scan_seq / _scan_registry / _apply_scan (the advice in the task-5839 correction, which this replaces). In tests/infra/run_all.sh's Phase-1 pool worker subshell (~:685-698), slot_acquire runs BEFORE the `bash "$INFRA_DIR/$name" ... > "$WORKDIR/$i.out" 2>&1` line, and that `> .out 2>&1` redirect is scoped to the `bash <test>` command ONLY. So slot_acquire's stderr (and any @@REIFY_CLOCK_*@@ markers from its 4th REASON arg) goes to the worker subshell's inherited FD 2 = run_all.sh's real stderr — the stream dark-factory's clock-stop parser reads UNSANITIZED. It is NOT captured into the per-member .out that _RA_CLOCK_SANITIZE (:217/:223-226) rewrites in Phase 3. Consequence: to make a contended pool wait pause DF's wall-clock budget you only pass the REASON token; no redirection change is needed.

Bash gotcha in reify's tests/infra/*.sh hermetic test harnesses: capturing a script's stdout via command substitution (`OUT="$(bash "$SCRIPT" ... )"`) blocks until EVERY process holding the pipe's write end closes it — including any backgrounded grandchild (`{ cmd; } &`) that inherited stdout and hasn't exited yet, not just the direct child. This masks bugs where a script is supposed to return control before a background job finishes (e.g. an FD-hygiene/lock-leak test). Fix: capture stdout via a real file redirect (`bash "$SCRIPT" ... >"$OUT_FILE" 2>"$ERR_FILE"; OUT="$(cat "$OUT_FILE")"`) instead of `$(...)`, matching how stderr is typically already captured via a real ERR_FILE in these harnesses. File redirects have no EOF-on-all-writers semantics, so the capture returns as soon as the direct child exits (like a plain `wait`), independent of detached grandchildren. Fixed in tests/infra/test_seed_warm_lane.sh's run_helper_real (task #5223 step-3, commit f22f51b770).

In tests/infra/run_all.sh's concurrent pool, the per-member `.out` sanitizer (_RA_CLOCK_SANITIZE / _ra_emit_sanitized, rewrites @@REIFY_CLOCK_ -> @@REIFY_QUOTED_CLOCK_) applies ONLY to the Phase-3 re-emission of captured `.out` files. The worker subshell's slot_acquire call (line ~868) runs BEFORE the member `bash ... > .out 2>&1` (line ~869), and that redirect is scoped to the member command only — the worker subshell `(` has no redirect and its sole exec is `exec 9>&-` (FD-9 mgmt). So slot_acquire's clock markers go to the worker's inherited PARENT stderr = the DF-visible, UNSANITIZED stream. Consequently, giving the pool slot_acquire a 4th REASON arg (e.g. test_slot_starvation) is sufficient to surface live @@REIFY_CLOCK_STOP/START@@ markers to DF — no stream re-routing needed. Intra-invocation the pool never waits (worker-shell throttle == slot count N), so markers appear only under cross-invocation contention on a shared host-global lock; tests force this by externally pre-holding `${LOCK}.slot-1` via `( flock -x 9; sleep N ) 9>>"${LOCK}.slot-1" &`.

reify run_all.sh has a "pool ambient-state normalization" seam (around the `_RA_INBOUND_ROLE` snapshot + `export DF_VERIFY_ROLE=task`) that is the canonical chokepoint for neutralizing merge-gate ambient env for ALL ~103 infra pool members. It covers all five member-launch sites at once, and per-command assignments still override it (so a test that legitimately needs the var sets it inline). Precedents living there: DF_VERIFY_ROLE=task normalization (its comment documents the meta-test plan-collapse failure: "throughput 24/14, scope 72/33"), `env -u REIFY_RUN_ALL_MEMBER_SUBSET` on the subset re-launch, and (task 5280) `export REIFY_RELEASE_DELTA_SKIP=0`. When a new verify_env knob leaks into pool members, this seam is the first place to look — not per-test env prefixes.

In reify's tests/infra, any test that forces a finite-WAIT slot_acquire deadline (rc=75) MUST redirect the child's stderr to a temp file. Since task 6024, scripts/lib_slot_acquire.sh emits a column-0 `@@REIFY_SLOT_TIMEOUT@@` sentinel on every such deadline, and run_all.sh's Phase-3 re-emission sanitizer (_RA_CLOCK_SANITIZE, run_all.sh:368) is prefix-scoped to `@@REIFY_CLOCK_` only — so an unredirected sentinel survives verbatim into the merge-gate verify log and makes dark-factory's line-anchored classifier mark the ENTIRE merge verify as SEMAPHORE_TIMEOUT. Two leak channels exist: an unredirected child stderr, and an assert description interpolating an unfiltered `$(cat "$X_ERR")` (test_helpers.sh prints $desc raw, so line 2+ of a multi-line interpolation starts at column 0 — on PASSING asserts too). Indenting is NOT a defence; the consumer's anchor is `^[ \t]*`. The sanctioned escape hatch when you must dump a capture is the prefix filter `$(sed 's/^/  | /' "$X_ERR")` — `| ` is non-whitespace and breaks the anchor. When writing a test that handles the sentinel, assemble the token at runtime (`SP='@@REIFY_SLOT_'` then "${SP}TIMEOUT@@") so the literal never appears in the file. Guards: Sections D and E of tests/infra/test_slot_timeout_marker.sh.

In tests/infra/run_all.sh the concurrent-POOL path runs under `set -euo pipefail`; any unguarded command in the post-INFO discovery/partition block (lines ~371-421) — most reproducibly the workdir `mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/reify-run-all-pool.XXXXXX"` — dies silently with exit 1 right after the `INFO: run_all.sh pool: N=` line (esc-5080-9 signature). A deterministic hermetic way to force that block to fail in a test is to invoke run_all.sh with a poisoned TMPDIR pointing at a nonexistent NESTED path (mktemp won't create parents → exit 1) while overriding REIFY_RUN_ALL_POOL_LOCK to a good temp path. GOTCHA: mktemp's own stderr already contains "mktemp"/"No such file or directory", so a RED test proving a new discovery/partition diagnostic must assert on guard-specific markers (e.g. `ERROR: run_all.sh pool: discovery/partition`, `loadavg=`, PSI `avg10=` value) that are absent from mktemp's native error, not on the injected command's text.

(3) test_verify_semaphore_e2e is host-isolated (exports REIFY_PSI_GATE_DISABLE=1, REIFY_COMPILE_GATE_DISABLE=1, per-test REIFY_TEST_SEMAPHORE_LOCK, stubs cargo via REIFY_E2E_CARGO_SLEEP); its only shared-within-lane resource is parser.c regen via tree-sitter-generate.sh.

content: reify tests/infra/run_all.sh gotcha (task #8681): the serial branches (--scope host-infra, REIFY_RUN_ALL_MEMBER_SUBSET, REIFY_RUN_ALL_POOL_DISABLE=1 legacy) run each member in `_ra_run_member ... stream` mode, `member 2>&1 | tee <out-file> | sed -u`. A member that leaves a background child holding its inherited stdout therefore stalls run_all until that child exits, and the child's late output lands inside that member's block. The pool's capture mode (`> file`) does not wait. This is deliberate and pinned by test_run_all.sh Test 35, so redirect a member's background holders' stdio (e.g. `>/dev/null 2>&1 &`) rather than leaking them.

candidates.content: When cancelling a task as superseded at a /prd decompose, also look for tasks that DEPEND on it and re-point their edge to the superseding leaf. At the S7 decompose, task 610 (web/CLI input for PVConfig.system_losses) depended on task 283. Before task 283 was cancelled, task 610 was given a dependency on task 914 (S7 β, which makes system_losses a pv: YAML key) and its edge on task 283 was removed. A quick way to find dependents: get_tasks with a statuses filter (the result is saved to a file when large), then jq for .dependencies containing the target id. The supersession rulings in the program doc do not list dependents, so the decompose session has to find them.

In the dark-factory orchestrator, a local dependency on a CANCELLED task counts as satisfied (scheduler.py dependency-satisfaction logic). The only exception is when the cancelled dep carries metadata.delivered_checks that are not green. So cancelling a task as superseded silently releases every task that depended on it. When superseding, re-point the dependents whose need moves to the superseding task (add_dependency dependent -> superseder) BEFORE cancelling. In the S21 decompose (2026-10-16): 133 and 140 got edges to 835, because they were waiting on the sweep chart that cancelled 123 would have built; 654 got an edge to 834, because it was waiting on 565's typed radar. 152 and 153 depended on 123 only to serialise edits to api.py, so they were left without a new edge.

When cancelling a task as superseded in a dark-factory project, first check its dependents: the orchestrator scheduler counts a cancelled LOCAL dependency as satisfied (only cancelled EXTERNAL/cross-project deps escalate), so a pending dependent becomes dispatchable the moment the upstream is cancelled. Transfer the edge to the superseding task (add_dependency dependent -> superseder) before setting the cancel, or the dependent can run before the work it was waiting on.

A lead's supersession ruling written at PRD-authoring time ("cancel pending task X at decompose") can be overtaken by the orchestrator before decompose runs: in the review-all program, tasks sat pending for days and were dispatched in between (742 and 121 went in-progress on 2026-10-17). Before acting on any cancel-at-decompose ruling, re-read each target's status, claimant_run_id and heartbeat_at right before the cancel. Cancel only pending/deferred targets, and turn an in-progress target into a dependency edge plus a note for the lead.

content: Cancelling a superseded task releases every task that depends on it. Cancelled counts as satisfied, so a dependent is dispatched within about a minute. At the S8 decompose on 2026-10-17, cancelling task 350 released task 582, whose only dependency was 350 and which was itself on the supersession list. 582 went in progress (claimant run-30159b979da7) about a minute later, before its own cancel. So it took edges instead (task 928 and task 930 depend on it), and the lead was asked to stop it. Rule for decompose supersessions: before cancelling, query the reverse dependencies of every target. One way is get_tasks(statuses=[pending, deferred, blocked, in-progress]); the result is written to a file you can jq. Then cancel the dependents that are themselves targets first (581 and 582 before 350). Never cancel a dependency while a target that depends on it is still pending.

solar_challenge PV ageing gotcha (task 284 architect; measured 2026-10-09 on main 9ef24ad with pvlib 0.15.1; holds on main once task/284 merges):
- The model chain's DC losses step multiplies each array's p_mp and i_mp by (1 - system_losses) x calculate_degradation_factor(age, rate). So simulate_pv_output's AC for an aged PVConfig is NOT the degradation factor times its new AC.
- Through the CEC Sandia or PVWatts inverters, a 0.90 factor keeps 0.8975-0.8991 of annual Bristol AC for unclipped default sizes. Inverter-limited arrays keep more: 6 kW on 3.68 kW 0.9151, 8 kW on 3.68 kW 0.9332.
- A test that needs an exact aged/new AC ratio uses create_simple_inverter_params, which is exactly linear below its rating (Pso and C0-C3 zero), as tests/unit/test_pv.py's LINEAR_INVERTER_CONFIG does.

solar_challenge web storage seam after task 446 (planned on task/446 at base 51edc0f, 2026-10-04; it holds once task 446 merges).

RunStorage in src/solar_challenge/web/storage.py is the one reader of a runs row by id:
- run_record(run_id) -> RunRecord | None. RunRecord is a frozen dataclass with one field per runs column, under the column's name. config_json and summary_json stay raw JSON text. dataclasses.asdict(record) reproduces the old dict(row).
- latest_run_named(name) -> RunRecord | None.
- update_run_labels(run_id, labels: Mapping[RunLabel, str | None]) -> RunRecord | None. RUN_LABELS = ('name', 'notes'). An absent key is left unchanged, None is written as NULL, and a non-label key raises ValueError before any write.
- run_name delegates to run_record.

api.py, history.compare_page and assistant.get_run_results call these instead of SQL. assistant.get_run_results now takes a RunStorage, not a db_path.

api.history_patch_run checks in this order:
1. request_json_object;
2. 404 when run_record is None;
3. labels = {label: data[label] for label in RUN_LABELS if label in data};
4. 400 'No fields to update';
5. update_run_labels.

Task 331's 'name/notes must be a JSON string' 400 belongs on the label values between steps 4 and 5.

The list and aggregate reads, and jobs.py's run-row writes, still use get_db directly. Follow-up ticket tkt_0RVDC3RASSWP4NBT3J87JMT39A moves them.

939af9fc-a18f-4c60-ad3b-098797557110.content: solar_challenge / dark-factory ordering gotcha (task 273 planning, 2026-10-01): a follow-up filed via submit_task with spawned_from=<parent> gets no Taskmaster dependency on its parent. So when an orchestrator restart cancels the unmerged parent back to pending (task 263 was cancelled at 04:54Z with all 5 plan steps committed), the follow-up can take the shared file locks first (273 did at 04:55Z). When the follow-up must edit lines the parent rewrites, have its architect call report_blocking_dependency on the parent rather than plan on main, because whichever task lands second then hits a guaranteed merge conflict. While the parent is non-terminal, dark-factory's workflow.py _handle_blocking_dep_report registers the dependency and requeues the follow-up; if the parent is cancelled, the follow-up dispatches again.

solar_challenge_platform test gotcha, measured on task 516's probes at main 40a6556, 2026-10-13. To make the database reject ONE statement for one home, attach a before_cursor_execute(retval=True) listener to the test's engine. It replaces the first statement whose bound values equal the home's UUID with "SELECT * FROM no_such_table" and returns type(parameters)().
- Match the UUID against a tuple of (uuid, str(uuid), uuid.hex) using ==. Do not use a set: some bound values are unhashable. psycopg binds uuid.UUID values in dicts, while SQLite binds 32-char hex strings in tuples.
- SQLite raises OperationalError; Postgres raises ProgrammingError (UndefinedTable) and aborts the transaction.
- On Postgres, without a savepoint (session.begin_nested()) the next home's read in the same Session fails with InFailedSqlTransaction. SQLite never aborts the transaction, so only a timescale-lane test can prove a per-home savepoint.

solar_challenge_platform test gotcha (verified 2026-10-09, task 209): tests/test_sqlite_engine_home.py only flags create_engine calls that build the shared StaticPool in-memory SQLite engine (in-memory URL + poolclass=StaticPool + a connect_args that may disable check_same_thread); those must come from tests/_sqlite_engine.make_in_memory_engine. A plain sa.create_engine("sqlite://") is allowed, and is the house way to give a SQL store a database with NO tables, so its write raises sqlalchemy OperationalError ("no such table"). Use it for a "store raises the DB error and logs nothing" test. make_in_memory_engine always runs create_all, so it cannot serve there.

solar_challenge_platform gotcha (read 2026-10-10 at main 1b4b448): SQLite enforces no foreign keys unless `PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON` runs on the connection, and the suite's StaticPool in-memory SQLite engine may be built only in tests/_sqlite_engine.py (tests/test_sqlite_engine_home.py fails any other create_engine of that shape). So a test that needs a real FK violation (the IntegrityError Postgres raises) must take its engine from that helper with the PRAGMA registered as a "connect" listener before create_all, not build its own. With FKs on, an FK violation surfaces at the first flush, not at commit: consent/store.py record_event and the config stores (set_finance/set_battery/set_coverage) flush inside the route handler, before commit_or_409 runs.

solar_challenge_platform gotcha (measured 2026-10-06, base 7fcfeac): the dropped-readings drill's raw-row helpers (validation/drills/dropped_readings.py _read_raw_rows / _delete_rows) bind raw uuid.UUID values through sqlalchemy text(). SQLite rejects that bind with "sqlite3.ProgrammingError: Error binding parameter 1: type 'UUID' is not supported", so those helpers only run on Postgres. Hermetic SQLite tests cannot reach them. The one real check is the slow Docker capstone test_dropped_readings_drill_recovers_against_real_docker_and_flows_into_bundle (about 93 s).
