Completed: Customer portal: a tab at the sign-in form does not join a sign-in made in another tab, so separate sign-ins in two tabs keep signing each other out
Description: Follow-up spawned from task 924 (architect; escalation id agent-followup-924). This is the behaviour task 924's plan leaves on purpose, on branch task/924, once it lands.

WHAT TASK 924 DOES. When another tab forgets or replaces scp_portal_auth_token, a tab that is signed in, or still checking its stored token, returns to the sign-in form. The form says "You were signed out from another tab — please sign in again.", and the tab leaves the store as the other tab left it (frontend-portal/src/auth.ts onSignedOutFromAnotherTab; frontend-portal/src/App.tsx endSession). A tab already at the sign-in form ignores storage events: endSession leaves a 'signed-out' Session untouched.

THE GAP.
- Tabs A and B both show the sign-in form, for example after a session expiry or after opening two portal tabs before signing in.
- The member signs in in tab A, then switches to tab B. B still shows the form, so the member signs in there too. That replaces A's token, so tab A returns to the form saying it was signed out from another tab.
- Signing in again in tab A does the same to tab B, and so on.
- Reloading a form tab joins the stored sign-in, because restore-on-mount reads it, but nothing tells the member to do that.

- When a storage event stores a token while this tab is at the sign-in form with no sign-in attempt in flight, run the restore again (fetchMe → admitToPortal), so the tab joins the device's sign-in. firstRun stays false, as on a reload.
- Restore runs must then cancel each other:

  - an older run's answer must be dropped (task 924 already drops an answer for a token no longer stored);
  - admitToPortal calls logout() for an unknown role before it throws, so a token-identity check alone cannot guard the .catch.
- Task 924's plan records this as a rejected alternative, for that reason.

candidates.content: When a fused-memory test asserts an owner released its SDK clients using task 4412's census (tests/_fm_helpers.py: track_async_httpx_clients -> await reap_leaked_async_httpx_clients() to flush -> build -> _leaked_async_httpx_clients()), keep the pre-close list in a local (`built = _leaked_async_httpx_clients(); assert len(built) == N`) until after the post-close `assert _leaked_async_httpx_clients() == []`. The census is a WeakSet, and an owner's close() typically drops its references (GraphitiBackend.close clears self.client and _group_clients). Without that strong ref, an UNCLOSED client can be refcount-freed out of the WeakSet, and the "none left open" assertion passes vacuously against unfixed code. Asserting the exact pre-close count also guards against a build that silently made nothing. Pattern used in fused-memory/tests/test_sdk_client_release.py (task 4417).

Task 4412 (fused-memory caplog flake, fixed at root) measured three things that refine the AsyncHttpxClientWrapper gotcha and should govern any future leaked-async-client work. (1) "GC-finalised while unclosed" is NOT the danger metric — __del__ only resurrects when a loop is RUNNING at finalisation (asyncio.get_running_loop() raises otherwise and the wrapper's bare `except Exception: pass` swallows it). Measured over the 7 leak-cohort modules: 38 of 40 wrappers finalised unclosed, but only 2 were real resurrections. To count them directly, wrap openai/anthropic._base_client.AsyncHttpxClientWrapper.__del__ and record whether get_running_loop() succeeds. (2) A WeakSet-based autouse teardown reaper structurally cannot reach a client that dies by refcount at test-function exit — the SYNC cohort (test_graphiti_llm_client_construction.py) is already gone from the WeakSet by teardown. Those are harmless (no loop running at exit); the reaper's real coverage is async tests, where the client survives to teardown inside a still-open loop. (3) httpx.AsyncClient.aclose() (0.28.1, _client.py:1978) sets self._state = ClientState.CLOSED BEFORE awaiting self._transport.aclose(), so is_closed flips True even when the transport close raises under a foreign/already-closed loop — which is why closing from a throwaway asyncio.run() loop still disarms __del__'s `if self.is_closed: return` short-circuit. Single patch point for tracking every such client: wrap httpx.AsyncClient.__init__ (both library wrappers chain to it); select the dangerous subset with hasattr(type(c), '__del__'), which is False for a bare httpx.AsyncClient.

GOTCHA — the recurring `ERROR asyncio: Task exception was never retrieved ... coro=<AsyncClient.aclose()> exception=RuntimeError('Event loop is closed')` caplog flake (tasks 1851/2819/3510/3927/4329/3765, fixed at the root by 4412) is NOT caused by a bare `httpx.AsyncClient`. Grepping for `httpx.AsyncClient(` finds nothing in fused-memory/src or /tests — that is why six tasks missed it. Both `openai._base_client.AsyncHttpxClientWrapper` and `anthropic._base_client.AsyncHttpxClientWrapper` SUBCLASS `httpx.AsyncClient` and define `__del__` that does `asyncio.get_running_loop().create_task(self.aclose())` unless `self.is_closed` — so any unclosed AsyncOpenAI/AsyncAnthropic resurrects itself at GC time onto whatever loop is running, and the inherited coroutine's qualname is `AsyncClient.aclose`. Search for the LIBRARY wrappers, not for httpx.

Task 4412 landed: the fused-memory caplog flake class (ERROR asyncio "Task exception was never retrieved ... coro=<AsyncClient.aclose()>") is now fixed at its source rather than armored at a seventh call site. Three files under fused-memory/tests/ only, no product-code change: _fm_helpers gains track_async_httpx_clients() (wraps httpx.AsyncClient.__init__, one patch point that catches openai/anthropic/graphiti_core alike, WeakSet-tracked), _leaked_async_httpx_clients() (unclosed AND hasattr(type(c),'__del__')), and reap_leaked_async_httpx_clients(); conftest calls the tracker from pytest_configure (session start, before collection) and adds two autouse teardown arms — a plain-def one declared FIRST and a pytest_asyncio one declared SECOND so the async arm tears down first and reaps inside the test's own still-open loop; test_async_httpx_leak_isolation.py mirrors orchestrator/tests/test_aiosqlite_leak_isolation.py. Evidence: a control/treatment A/B over the 7 leak-cohort modules took real resurrections from 2 to 0, and the full suite ran clean at three orderings (-n auto / -n 8 / -n 16, --dist loadgroup), 14564 passed each, with zero hits for "Task exception was never retrieved", "AsyncClient.aclose" and "Event loop is closed". Production-side close() gaps (GraphitiBackend, TaskCurator, ReadRouter/WriteClassifier, judge.py, agent_loop.py) are deliberately NOT in this task — they are task 4417.

fused-memory gotcha (measured for task 4417 against graphiti_core installed in the main .venv): graphiti_core's Graphiti.__init__ builds its OWN OpenAIClient() / OpenAIEmbedder() / OpenAIRerankerClient() for any sub-client passed falsy. Each holds an AsyncOpenAI on `.client`. GraphitiBackend.initialize passes llm_client=None when no LLM api_key is configured, and embedder=None when no embedder key is configured. So the base client and every per-group Graphiti built by GraphitiBackend._client_for can each hold up to 2 extra SDK clients that no fused-memory attribute references; they are reachable only via graphiti_instance.llm_client / .embedder / .cross_encoder. fused-memory has NO HTTP-mock library installed (respx, pytest-httpserver, aioresponses and responses are all absent from uv.lock; only pytest, pytest-asyncio, pytest-timeout, pytest-xdist). To prove that a configured base_url actually receives traffic, use the dependency-free recording server at fused-memory/tests/_mock_openai_server.py (task 3715): `with mock_openai_server() as srv` yields a handle with .base_url (carrying the /v1 suffix, matching OpenAIProviderConfig.api_url), .requests (recorded {path, method, headers, json_body}) and .requests_to(suffix). It serves POST /v1/chat/completions and POST /v1/embeddings on a stdlib ThreadingHTTPServer bound to 127.0.0.1 port 0. A REAL socket is required rather than httpx.MockTransport or a mocked AsyncOpenAI: graphiti's OpenAIEmbedderConfig is a pydantic model with the default extra='ignore', so a misspelled base_url kwarg is dropped SILENTLY and every constructor-kwarg assertion still passes while traffic goes to api.openai.com (the graphiti-#912 failure class); transport injection shares that blind spot because it intercepts before URL resolution matters. Always pair it with the negative guard: monkeypatch OPENAI_BASE_URL / OPENAI_API_BASE / OPENAI_API_URL to an unroutable sentinel (http://127.0.0.1:1/v1) so any env-var fallback fails loudly, and assert EXACT request counts so a plumbed-but-ignored base_url cannot pass. Bind port 0 once and read server_address back — probing then rebinding is a TOCTOU race against other xdist workers.

So a test needing a fake HTTP endpoint has two in-repo options: inject an `httpx.MockTransport` (precedent: fused-memory/tests/test_cgl_eta_scheduler_gate.py:68,137) or hand-roll a stdlib `http.server.ThreadingHTTPServer` in a daemon thread. Prefer a real server when the thing under test is URL ROUTING (e.g. proving a configured base_url actually receives traffic) — transport injection intercepts before URL resolution matters, and pydantic client-config models like graphiti's OpenAIEmbedderConfig default to extra='ignore', so a misspelled base_url kwarg is dropped SILENTLY and every constructor-kwarg assertion still passes while traffic goes to api.openai.com. Always bind 127.0.0.1 port 0 (ephemeral) — the default addopts is `-n auto`, so a fixed port collides across xdist workers, and a test that assumes nothing is listening on a well-known port inverts on any host running the fused-memory MCP server. Test gotcha (mcp SDK 1.27, anyio 4.13): a real mcp.server.session.ServerSession(read, write, InitializationOptions(...), stateless=True) built from anyio.create_memory_object_stream pairs creates its own internal _incoming_message_stream pair in __init__. If the test only constructs it, those streams emit 'Unclosed MemoryObject*Stream' ResourceWarnings at GC, and they get attributed to LATER tests. Enter it as `async with ServerSession(...) as session:` (its receive loop closes the internal and passed streams), and close your own four stream ends in a finally. Worked example: fused-memory/tests/test_task_write_agent_id.py::_stateless_ctx (task 5241).

To attribute a leaked async client to the test that created it in a large pytest suite, patch the class's `__init__` to record `traceback.format_stack()` plus a `weakref.ref`, tag it with the current nodeid from `pytest_runtest_setup`, and dump each instance's end-state at `pytest_sessionfinish`. This beats tracemalloc for this class of bug (the finalisation stack is just GC and useless; the allocation stack names the test) and costs nothing. Do NOT scan `gc.get_objects()` per test — on a large heap that is ~100ms each, which is hours over a 14k-test suite. Task 4412 used this to find all 40 leaked openai wrappers in fused-memory in one 22-minute run.

candidates.content: A closure-local dependency inside `create_mcp_server` (fused-memory/src/fused_memory/server/tools.py) can be made observable to a tool-level test WITHOUT weakening the production wiring, provided it is constructed zero-arg: monkeypatch the class name in the tools module namespace with a factory returning your instance — `monkeypatch.setattr(tools, 'TriageFailOpenCounter', lambda: counter)`. The zero-arg construction IS the seam. This keeps the per-server isolation (nothing bleeds between servers or tests) that motivated the closure-local binding in the first place, while letting an assertion read the state. Used in tests/server/test_add_memory_write_triage_gate.py for the write-triage fail-open counter.

GOTCHA (measured task 3778, 2026-09-01): when you make a FAIL-OPEN function async, sync monkeypatch fakes at that seam do not fail loudly — they degrade SILENTLY, and some tests keep passing FOR THE WRONG REASON. A green run is therefore not evidence you finished the async propagation.

THE MECHANISM. `is_workflow_live_for_task` / `detect_live_workflow` are wrapped by callers in `try: ... except Exception: treat as not-live` (harness.py integrity gate; task_knowledge_sync._render_live_workflow_section). Task 3778 made them coroutines. A leftover sync fake `def _fake(_tid, _pr, **kw): return True` is still CALLED fine — the failure is one line later, when `await <bool>` raises TypeError. That TypeError is swallowed by the deliberate fail-open handler and becomes "not-live". So:
- A test asserting live/suppressed FAILS loudly. You find it.
- A test asserting NOT-live / "section absent" / "escalation fires" PASSES — because fail-open produces exactly the expected answer by accident. You do not find it.
The second class is the dangerous one: it survives the refactor as a test that no longer tests anything, and it will not re-redden when the behaviour it guards actually breaks.

CONCRETE INSTANCES FOUND. After merging main into the 3778 lane, main had contributed test classes written against the PRE-async contract:
- test_stage1.py TestStage1RemediationPayloadLiveWorkflowSection (main task 3839): 3 sync `_fake_detect`. ONE failed; TWO passed vacuously (both assert "### Live-Workflow Signals" absent). One of those two even sets is_live=True and would have passed no matter what.
- test_harness.py TestRemediationSnapshotClockPinnedToTreeRead (main task 2964): 1 sync `_fake_is_live`. Failed loudly only because it asserts SUPPRESSION.
Ironically the lane's own helper `_async_is_live` (test_harness.py:38) documents this exact hazard — "a sync fake would still be CALLED, but awaiting its bool return raises" — and the merge reintroduced it anyway.

PRACTICE.
1. Do not audit by running the suite. Audit by GREP: `grep -n "def _fake_is_live\|def _fake_detect" <testfile> | grep -v async` enumerates every unconverted fake in one shot, passing or not. That is the only check that sees the vacuous ones.
2. Re-run that grep AFTER every merge from main, not just after your own edits. A long-lived lane that changes a function's sync/async contract has an ONGOING conflict with main: main keeps adding call sites and fakes against the old contract, and git merges them cleanly because there is no textual conflict. The 3778 merge was clean and still landed three broken seams.
3. The same reasoning applies to any await-a-coroutine seam guarded by a broad `except Exception` fail-open — this is a property of fail-open + async, not of this detector. Consider an `inspect.iscoroutinefunction` assertion on the patched attribute (test_harness.py:13916 already does this) so the seam's contract is pinned by a test rather than by convention.
4. Sibling defect from the same merge: `_assemble_remediation_payload` (sync) called the now-async `_build_live_workflow_section` without await, interpolating a literal `<coroutine object ...>` into an LLM prompt payload. This one only surfaced as a RuntimeWarning plus a content assertion — no exception. When converting a method to async, grep for ALL its callers, including sync ones that merely f-string the result.

To test an MCP JSON-RPC handshake with no server and no socket, stub `_post` on the CLIENT INSTANCE (an instance attribute shadows the class method) and call `asyncio.run(client._initialize())`, collecting the payloads. Construct the client directly, never via `async with` — `__aenter__` is the only thing that builds the httpx.AsyncClient, so skipping it means the real `_post`'s `assert self._client is not None` never runs. Used in tests/scripts/test_migrate_metadata_modules_to_files.py and test_repair_wiped_metadata_files.py (task 3437).

fused-memory enforces a repo-wide AsyncMock assertion-style convention (task 525) via tests/test_check_asyncmock_assertion_style.py::TestRealTestsDirectoryIsClean, which scans the whole fused-memory/tests/ tree: a single test function must not mix assert_not_called() and assert_not_awaited() on mock attributes — use assert_not_awaited() only. The check fails as a normal test, so it surfaces only on a full-suite run, not on a targeted one.

GOTCHA (dark-factory, measured 2026-08-31, task 3790): a test that drives a FAILING TASK CLIENT cannot verify anything about `flake_recorder`'s per-test guard structure, because `flake_ledger.open_debt` is fail-soft and swallows client failures internally.

MEASURED, not reasoned. `record_merge_flake_suppression` loops `await _guarded_async('debt', lambda: open_debt(...))` once per carried test_id, and the source comment claims "ONE GUARD PER TEST, not one for the batch: a filing that fails for one must not cost the other its owner". I wrote a test driving a client whose `submit_task` raises for the FIRST test_id only, then MUTATED the source to collapse the loop into a single shared guard around the whole batch. The test still PASSED. Reason: `open_debt` catches the client failure inside its own `_ensure_owner_task` guard and returns normally, so `_guarded_async` never sees an exception and the loop continues either way. No client-driven test can distinguish the two shapes.

THE TEST THAT ACTUALLY BITES monkeypatches `orchestrator.flake_recorder.open_debt` itself to raise for one id and delegate to the real one for the others. Re-run against the same mutation, it fails with the second test losing its debt row entirely — the regression the claim is about.

GENERAL LESSON, which is the reusable part: when the code under test sits BEHIND a fail-soft callee, the callee's guard absorbs the fault you were trying to inject and your test silently verifies nothing. Inject the fault at the seam the guard under test actually wraps, and CONFIRM BY MUTATION that the assertion fails when the property is removed. Inspecting the test and concluding it must bite is not sufficient — this one looked correct and did not.

VACUOUS-TEST-GUARD — a shape the peers do not cover: THE SWALLOWING `except` IS NOT IN THE CODE UNDER TEST, IT IS IN THE LOOP THAT CALLS YOUR TEST DOUBLE. Distinct from peer 17b9914a ("assertion delivered by raising from inside a try/except Exception block is unreachable"), whose case is a function whose OWN contract is catch-and-degrade, so the hazard is visible at the call site you are testing. Here nothing near the double has a try/except at all, and the double reads as an ordinary recording fake.

MEASURED (task 4427, orchestrator/tests/test_eval_driver.py + test_runner_matrix.py, amendment commit 7de1eda252). A fake eval executor asserted AT CALL TIME that the campaign UsageGate was not yet shut down — `assert self.gate.shutdown.await_count == 0` — with a docstring claiming it was "the only way to distinguish torn down once after the fan-out from torn down between cells". But the fake runs as a CELL inside `_bounded_fanout` / `run_eval_matrix`, both of which log-and-continue on every non-cancel exception (runner.py:1964-1967, :2021-2024), three frames above the fake. Mutation: replacing the guard with `assert False` left ALL SIX campaign-gate cases in test_eval_driver.py green, and `TestRunEvalMatrixCampaignGate::test_one_gate_serves_every_cell` green.

THE SECOND HALF, which is what makes this worse than a merely-inert assertion: the swallow also DROPS that cell's result. So the test does not just fail to fail — it still looks HEALTHY. `len(probe.seen) > 1` holds (the fake appended before raising), the same-object check holds, and `shutdown.assert_awaited_once()` holds, because every one of those reads the probe's own records rather than the loop's output. Nothing in the assertion set was sensitive to results going missing.

THE REPAIR, in two parts.
(1) OBSERVE IN THE FAKE, ASSERT IN THE HELPER — the peer's recording-double rule, applied one frame out. The fake appends `gate.shutdown.await_count` per cell to a list; the helper asserts `== [0] * len(seen)` AFTER the stage returns, outside the swallowing loop. Verified by the OPPOSITE mutation (a gate torn down between cells), which now fails all three stage cases with the intended message.
(2) COUNT THE RESULTS, because (1) alone only protects the assertions you thought to move. Have the fake record which cells raised DELIBERATELY (`fail_on`/`cancel_on`) and assert `len(results) == len(seen) - len(raised)` in every helper. The naive `len(results) == len(seen)` is wrong for any case that fails a cell on purpose — in the OFAT fan-out `fail_on='df_task_a'` drops 6 cells (3 candidates × 2 trials), not 1.

DIAGNOSTIC, generalizing past this case: when a test double is invoked by a bounded fan-out, a task group, a retry wrapper, an `asyncio.gather(return_exceptions=True)`, or anything else that OWNS exception policy for its callees, treat every `assert` inside that double as unreachable until a mutation proves otherwise. The question is not "does the code under test catch exceptions" but "does ANY frame between my double and pytest catch them".

NOTE, stated as its own scope: a heuristic scan of `*/tests/*.py` for asserts inside `async def fake*/stub*` bodies found 23 sites repo-wide. They were NOT checked for a swallowing caller and most probably propagate normally — this is a diagnostic to apply when you next touch such a double, not a sweep to schedule.

In fused-memory, when you add a NEW service read to an existing MCP tool in server/tools.py, every pre-existing test that builds `mock_service = AsyncMock()` without stubbing that new method will silently exercise the new code path with a truthy auto-created AsyncMock instead of a realistic value — so an "unchanged response shape" assertion stops testing what it claims. Explicitly pin the new method in those tests (e.g. `mock_service.count_memories_by_metadata = AsyncMock(return_value=0)`). Observed in task 3129 wiring grouped reads into get_memory_by_id: the child-count probe made test_happy_path_found take the grouped branch until the zero-child corpus was pinned.

MEASURED 2026-08-17 (task 3857 re-spec, positive-control validated): the dark-factory dashboard's CLOSE-WAIT sockets are NOT a leak, by any mechanism. This EXTENDS the 2026-08-08 refutation (mem0 eb3c5348-ecf3-448f-ae9c-7ac4831930ae), which killed only the cancellation half of the claimed root cause.

Three findings, on httpx 0.28.1 / httpcore 1.0.9:

(1) CLOSE-WAIT against escalation ports appears reliably after an idle gap exceeding the SERVER's timeout_keep_alive (>4.9s vs uvicorn's 5s default), and is FULLY REAPED on the next pool use (4 -> 0 in a single poll). It is transient, not cumulative. A large flat census is a STEADY STATE, not accumulation.

(2) It cannot starve the pool. httpcore's AsyncConnectionPool._assign_requests_to_connections does its cleanup pass — removing connections that is_closed(), has_expired(), or are surplus-idle — BEFORE it evaluates max_connections, and its third assignment case explicitly closes an idle connection to make room. So a CLOSE-WAIT socket cannot hold a pool slot "permanently". This refutes the SECOND clause of task 3857's root cause independently of cancellation, which is why no re-scope could rescue the original framing.

(3) has_expired() detects the server-side close via `self._state == IDLE and self._network_stream.get_extra_info("is_readable")`, which is how the reaping in (1) happens at all.

Re-confirmed the cancellation half directly: 15/15 probes cancelled via asyncio.wait_for left ZERO CLOSE-WAIT sockets.

CONSEQUENCE: CLOSE-WAIT count on this client is a GAUGE of (idle pooled connections) x (poll gap > server timeout_keep_alive) — i.e. a host-load indicator — not a defect and not a correctness signal. Do not treat it as one.

This also CORRECTS the prescription in mem0 74095f83-cbb9-459c-9c3f-83c56d5eafc1 ("any explicit httpx.Limits must set keepalive_expiry strictly below 5.0"): that entry's keep-alive topology facts are right, but its prescription does not work — see the companion memory on keepalive_expiry being inert.

content: In fused-memory tests, the task-4412 census (tests/_fm_helpers.py::_leaked_async_httpx_clients) lists only clients that are still OPEN. So it cannot prove that a no-op close() built nothing: a close() that wrongly builds a client and then closes it passes `_leaked_async_httpx_clients() == []`. To assert "nothing was constructed", monkeypatch httpx.AsyncClient.__init__ with a wrapper that calls the original and appends self to a list held by strong reference, then assert that list is empty. This catches AsyncOpenAI, AsyncAnthropic and graphiti_core wrappers at one patch point. Pattern: fused-memory/tests/test_sdk_client_release.py::async_httpx_clients_built (task 4417).

GOTCHA: a guard test can PASS VACUOUSLY -- without ever exercising the assertion it claims to pin. It then provides false assurance, and it keeps passing after the thing it guards is broken.

THE SHAPES OBSERVED, each documented by a stamped peer under topic `vacuous-test-guard`:
  - PARAMETER SUPPLIES THE DISCRIMINATOR. A parametrized test whose discriminating token comes ENTIRELY from the parameter proves nothing about the code's own constant (orchestrator/tests/test_verify_cmd.py, TestChainOperatorTokenCoverage).
  - THE PAIR ONLY PINS TOGETHER, BUT BOTH SIDES DRIFT. A positive/negative pair whose docstring argues they only pin the narrowing jointly (fused-memory path-scope guard, TestProseRightBoundarySignal).
  - AN EARLIER GATE SHORT-CIRCUITS THE ONE UNDER TEST. recon_code_fix_premise_guard's match_candidate requires ALL title_substrings before it ever looks at description_substrings, so a negative test whose title misses an anchor dies at the title gate and says nothing about descriptions.
  - DERIVED CONSTANTS, path_scope_guard._build_pattern, the merge_disposition INTEGRATION_SKEW invariant I7, and a fail-soft variant -- see the peers.

THE UNIVERSAL TEST, and the reason this topic exists: MUTATE THE THING THE GUARD GUARDS AND CONFIRM THE TEST FLIPS TO FAILING. A throwaway rebind is enough -- `import orchestrator.verify_cmd as vc; vc._NON_AND_CHAIN_TOKENS = frozenset()` then re-run the assertions. A guard whose outcome is INDEPENDENT of the constant is vacuous by definition. Repeated green runs prove nothing on their own; only the mutation distinguishes a guard with teeth.

CAUTION (added 2026-09-14, reconciliation run b4fd1c79): peer ordinal self-numbering under this topic has drifted and is NOT reliable. Peers 79625c18 (2026-09-11, "a sixth shape": single-producer test against a shared multi-producer sink) and 95083a87 (2026-09-10, "a SIXTH shape": witness emitted upstream of the claim it defends) both independently claim to be "the sixth shape", describing two DIFFERENT things, because neither queried current topic membership before numbering itself. True membership as of this note: 22 records tagged `topic: vacuous-test-guard` (confirm via `get_memories_by_metadata`/`count_memories_by_metadata`, never by trusting a peer's own ordinal). Read a peer's CONTENT to learn which shape it documents; do not rely on any "sixth"/"seventh"/etc. claim in its text. Same drift pattern independently found and annotated this cycle on the `pytest-xdist-serial-override` canonical (8bb3eb15).

ACCRETION: append here or add a stamped peer under this topic -- do not write a new unstamped entry.

(1) Lower-bound claims (max>=2) can never be vacuous, because the counter reaches 2 only through a real overlap. A barrier miss only MISATTRIBUTES the red.
(2) Upper-bound claims (==1) are vacuous whenever a member's window is zero or shorter than the launch skew.

Completed: Collapse 31 skip-mirror else-branches in tests/infra/test_run_all.sh into one precondition
Description: Each of 31 test blocks is wrapped in `if [ -f "$RUN_ALL" ] ...; then ... else` and the else-branch hand-mirrors that block's assertion list as '(skipped - run_all.sh missing)' false-asserts. Test 1 already asserts that run_all.sh exists. The mirrored lists account for 233 of the file's 646 assert lines.

Measurements: skip-mirror asserts = 233 of 646 assert lines (36%), across 31 guarded blocks (rule: grep -c '(skipped - ' vs grep -cE '^\s*assert ').

Next-change scenario: An agent adding an assertion to any Test must also add a mirrored false-assert in that Test's else branch. Nothing checks the two lists agree, so they drift silently, and the else branch never runs in practice.

Proposal: Replace the 31 guards with one precondition after Test 1 that fails and calls test_summary when run_all.sh or load_tolerance_lib.sh is missing, and delete the else branches.

Finding fk-4229ece8d26d from /review-all run review-all-reify-20261010 (anchor verified at a030ee7528). Freshness clause: before building on this, git diff a030ee7528..main -- tests/infra/test_run_all.sh and re-read the symbol.
Analysis: PREMISES (verified at e217c0f30b, which is also main's tip, so the branch carries no commits): `git diff a030ee7528..HEAD -- tests/infra/test_run_all.sh` is empty. The file has 3597 lines and 646 `^\s*assert ` lines. There are 233 `(skipped - ` lines, made of three variants: 96 `(skipped - run_all.sh missing)`, 135 `(skipped - run_all.sh or load_tolerance_lib.sh missing)` and 2 `(skipped - guard missing)` (Test 12).

GUARD INVENTORY (top-level `if/elif/else/fi`, all at column 0):
- 13 run_all-only blocks: Tests 2, 3, 4, 7, 8, 14, 15, 16, 17-continued, 28, 29, 30, 31.
- 14 run_all + lib blocks, keyed on `[ -f "$RUN_ALL" ] && [ -f "$LOAD_TOLERANCE_LIB_T9" ]`: Tests 9, 10, 11, 13, 17, 18, 19, 20, 21, 22, 24, 25, 26, 27.
- 2 three-way jq blocks: Test 23 (if :1982 / elif :2200 / else :2208) and Test 27-continued (if :2889 / elif :2950 / else :2952). Each has the shape `if run_all && lib && jq; then BODY; elif run_all && lib; then echo SKIP-jq; else MIRROR; fi`.
- Test 12 (:688) has its own `[ -f "$GUARD_T12" ]` guard over scripts/verify-pipeline-guard.sh, with 2 mirrored asserts.
That gives 29 `if` lines plus 2 `elif` lines, i.e. the task's 31 guard conditions. A heredoc-aware awk scan confirmed that every top-level else-branch holds ONLY mirrored `assert "... (skipped - ...)" false` lines (2-line `\ false` forms included), so deleting them loses nothing. The column-0 `if/else/fi` inside the MOCKBODY heredocs (e.g. :1341-1345) are mock-script bodies, NOT guards.

LOAD_TOLERANCE_LIB_T9 is assigned inside Test 9 (:359) but is used as a suite-wide guard input and is sourced again by Test 25 (:2416). It is also baked into the Test 9 probe-mock writer (:408).

DE-INDENT HAZARD: unwrapping the 28 two-way guarded blocks (27 plus Test 12) leaves ~2,700 body lines at 4-space indent, so they must be de-indented to column 0 to match the unguarded Tests 1/5/6. Whitespace matters only inside heredoc bodies. All heredocs are plain `<<'DELIM'` (no `<<-`). Inside de-indented ranges, the heredocs whose bodies carry leading spaces are Test 9 MOCKBODY :410-440 (16 indented lines), Test 18 MOCKBODY :1334-1346 and Test 27 MOCKBODY :2715-2727 (2 each). Every other multi-line construct is a `"$( ... \` command-substitution continuation, where whitespace is insignificant. The two jq blocks KEEP an `if command -v jq` wrapper, so their bodies are not re-indented.

CROSS-FILE COUPLING CHECKED:
- test_slot_timeout_marker.sh Section G statically scans test_run_all.sh. Its site target is `"$RUN_ALL"` behind an exec-position anchor (it explicitly never matches `test -f "$RUN_ALL"`), and this change adds or removes no exec site.
- test_run_all_ambient_isolation.sh drives the real test_run_all.sh and reads only its exit code.
- No ptodo, wallclock, cited-path or harness-layout baseline keys on this file's lines.
- Sibling tasks on the same file are all pending: #8692 ζ₁ and #8696 ζ₂ list #8535 as a prereq, and #8726 π and #8678 α also touch it. In-progress #8536/#8538 touch other files.

APPROACH:
- Hoist the lib path into the preamble as LOAD_TOLERANCE_LIB, and have Test 1 assert both prerequisites.
- Add one precondition right after Test 1, using the sibling-suite idiom: test_summary, then exit 1 when either file is missing.
- Delete every guard line and every mirror else-branch. Reduce the two jq blocks to `if command -v jq ...; then BODY; else echo SKIP; fi`, and drop Test 12's guard: its two asserts already FAIL on their own when the guard script is absent (bash exits 127, and the --list pipeline fails).
- De-indent the unwrapped bodies in a separate, whitespace-only commit.

EXPECTED END STATE:
- 0 `(skipped - ` lines; assert lines 646 + 1 - 233 = 414.
- Real-tree run: rc 0, PASS = baseline + 1, FAIL 0.
- ~3,270 lines. The heuristic-14 split belongs to ζ₂ (#8696).
Key decisions: Do not land a self-invoking meta-test of the precondition. Validate it with a throwaway hermetic fixture run, recorded in the step-2 commit message.; Rename LOAD_TOLERANCE_LIB_T9 to LOAD_TOLERANCE_LIB and define it in the preamble beside RUN_ALL. Test 1 asserts both prerequisites; the precondition reads both.; Keep the jq gate on Tests 23 and 27c as `if command -v jq; then BODY; else echo SKIP; fi`. Drop only the run_all/lib conjuncts and the mirrored else-branch.

candidates.content: merge_queue.py gotcha: `MergeResult` (git_ops.py:368; fields success/conflicts/details/merge_commit/pre_merge_sha/merge_worktree) has NO `branch_tip` field. The branch-tip SHA lives only on `MergedOk` (merge_types.py) produced by the single-branch `classify_and_merge` path (which rev-parses HEAD in the request worktree). The train path `_do_train_merge` uses a raw `MergeResult` from `git_ops.merge_to_main`, so it has NO pre-captured branch tip — resolve it via the public `git_ops.resolve_branch_sha(branch_name) -> str | None` (git_ops.py:3952, `git rev-parse --verify refs/heads/{branch}`). There are exactly two `git_ops.advance_main` call sites in merge_queue.py: single-branch `_finalize_inflight` (~8814, inside a `while True` CAS-retry loop where current_sha mutates on rebased_pending_reverify) and train `_do_train_merge` (~2975).

merge_to_main uses `git merge --no-ff` (git_ops.py:3293), so the merge commit's second parent `git rev-parse <merge_sha>^2` is ALWAYS the exact branch commit that was incorporated — the authoritative, drift-proof "tip actually merged." advance_main already uses this idiom (git_ops.py:3911-3922, verified_branch_tip). Prefer advanced_sha^2 over the live worktree HEAD when validating post-merge content equivalence; the worktree HEAD can drift to an orphaned/rebased lineage on a warm lane and false-positive a "dropped work" divergence (root cause of reify task 4071 stranding).

_check_post_merge_equivalence (orchestrator/merge_queue.py) has exactly ONE caller: _finalize_advanced_merge (line ~1180). When its merged_tip kwarg is None it falls back to `git rev-parse HEAD` in the task worktree — the drift-prone read that task 1917 (merged e0af36b36f) introduced merged_tip to bypass. MergeWorker (non-speculative, ~5324) passes merged_branch_tip directly and does NOT use reverify_on_rebase, so the 1917 hole is fully closed there; only SpeculativeMergeWorker's reverify/CAS retry loop re-opens it.

The orchestrator merge lane integrates a task branch with `git merge --no-ff <branch-tip>` into a throwaway detached worktree at main HEAD (`_run_no_ff_merge`, orchestrator/src/orchestrator/git_ops.py:10700-10711; merge_source is the branch tip at :10761), then moves main by ref CAS in `advance_main`. It is NEVER a squash or a cherry-pick and it does NOT filter by task id, so the ENTIRE `merge-base(main, branch)..branch` range lands. `_classify_branch_presence` (merge_queue.py:4330) checks only ref existence, already-merged markers and worktree misroute; the drop-guard and post-merge-equivalence gates (merge_gates.py:996, :1629) run post-merge, anchor on merge-base, and are fail-open. Consequence: there is no guard that rejects a stale merge-base or a branch carrying another task's commits — a mis-based branch will silently land foreign, unmerged work on main.

GOTCHA (task 5618): 'git merge-base <branch> main' can never equal an UNLANDED sibling's tip, because a merge-base with main is by definition an ancestor of main. To find a branch stacked on an unlanded predecessor you need the predecessor TIP as the replay base (git merge-tree --merge-base=<pred_tip> main <tip>, or git rebase --onto main <pred_tip>). The topology probe 'git for-each-ref --merged=<branch> --no-merged=main refs/heads/task/' is direction-blind: a sibling stacked ON the branch looks identical. Over the ~1069 task refs it costs well over 0.3s per branch.

Root cause of a "durable false already_merged" from the merge queue (reify task/5026, 2026-07-06): the merge worker's already-merged short-circuit in classify_and_merge (orchestrator/src/orchestrator/merge_queue.py) trusted `is_ancestor(effective_tip, main)` alone, where `effective_tip = req.snapshot_tip or worktree_HEAD`. A branch cut from main has a base commit that is trivially an ancestor of current main. task/5026 was born a ZERO-COMMIT branch (architect refused the task, base 88a8eeab / rebased 8318de471c — both ancestors of main) before it gained its real commit at 13:28. When effective_tip resolves to that stale base — via a snapshot_tip captured in the zero-commit window, OR a None snapshot falling back to a recycled-lane worktree HEAD (the task's lane _lane-10 had been reused by another task and sat at/under main) — is_ancestor returns True and the worker emits a TERMINAL already_merged that ejects the task from the queue with its real commit still unmerged. Git was authoritative: 5026 was never on main; the candidate merge commit 9816107 was built for verify but never landed. This is the SAME degenerate-zero-commit-branch trap the reconciler already guards (harness Guard-2, #1823, via find_task_citation_commit) — the merge worker simply lacked that parity.

GOTCHA (dark_factory, hit 2026-08-03): the merge worker REBASES the branch, so a `git merge-base --is-ancestor <pre-merge-tip> main` check returns FALSE for work that has already landed, and reads as "never merged". Task 3042's branch tip was 77ae9f35a9 before submission; the work landed under new SHAs topped by f4b03f36a6, and a background poller watching the pre-rebase SHA reported "not landed" for 30 minutes after `merge_status` had already returned `state: done, finished_at 11:01:55Z`.

VERIFY BY CONTENT, NOT BY SHA. For task 3042 the decisive check was `git show main:<file> | grep <symbol>`; for task 3214 it was `git ls-tree -r --name-only main -- <fixture dir> | grep '\.gz$'` returning nothing plus the new call site being present. Alternatively poll `mcp__escalation__merge_status(request_id=...)`, which is authoritative and unaffected by rebasing.

Not every merge rebases: task 3214's second attempt (mr-2b826e02) landed with its original SHAs 21a87902df / a6a54244da intact because the branch was already current. So SHA-based checks fail INTERMITTENTLY, which is worse than failing always — do not rely on them.

Task 1658 fixed the stale branch-tip race in advance_main (git_ops.py). The fix: capture verified_branch_tip = M^2 at advance_main entry; in the re-merge fallback use verified_branch_tip instead of the moving full_branch ref; add _last_remerged_branch_tip side-channel and a divergence WARNING when the live ref has moved past M^2. All changes are centralized in advance_main — no worker-loop edits.

GOTCHA, measured 2026-08-30 (task 4925): when validating that a captured sha IS the merge commit you just created, the discriminator must be "second parent EQUALS the branch tip", not "second parent exists" and not containment. Both of the weaker checks pass in exactly the case they are meant to catch.

THE SETUP. A hand-merge workflow captures the sha at the moment of the merge: `git merge --no-ff task/<id> && MERGE_SHA=$(git rev-parse HEAD)`. The unstated assumption is that a merge which exits 0 created a merge commit. It does not. When the branch tip is already an ancestor of main, `git merge --no-ff` prints "Already up to date." and exits 0 having created NOTHING, so `git rev-parse HEAD` returns whatever is on main's tip — which on a machine-operated checkout with a live merge worker can be an unrelated task's merge. The `&&` chain does not protect you: only a CONFLICTED merge short-circuits.

WHY THE OBVIOUS GUARDS FAIL (measured in a scratch repo, all four cases):
- `git merge-base --is-ancestor task/<id> "$MERGE_SHA"` PASSES — the branch IS an ancestor, which is precisely WHY git said "Already up to date". The condition that makes the capture wrong is the same condition that makes containment true.
- `[ -n "$(git rev-parse -q --verify "$MERGE_SHA^2")" ]` PASSES — on any repo whose merges are all `--no-ff` (dark-factory's are), main's tip is nearly always itself a merge commit, so `^2`-exists is almost always true and proves nothing about WHICH branch it brought in.
- `[ "$(git rev-parse -q --verify "$MERGE_SHA^2")" = "$(git rev-parse task/<id>)" ]` is the one that works: it accepts a genuine fresh merge, accepts the benign re-run where main's tip IS this task's merge (correct — that is the right sha to stamp), and rejects the unrelated-merge case.

THE CASE EQUALITY STILL CANNOT CATCH, and why it needs a separate guard: merging while NOT on `main`. There the merge genuinely succeeds and MERGE_SHA is a real, correct merge commit of this branch that simply is not on main (`git merge-base --is-ancestor "$MERGE_SHA" main` rc=1). Second-parent equality passes because it IS a bona-fide merge. So a branch guard must run BEFORE `git merge` — `[ "$(git symbolic-ref --quiet --short HEAD)" = "main" ]` — since merging onto the wrong branch is itself the damage, not merely a bad capture.

GENERALISATION. "Command exited 0" and "command did the thing" are different propositions for git porcelain, and `merge`/`pull` are the ones where they most often diverge. When a downstream consumer (here, a `done_provenance` stamp whose only server-side backstop is `is-ancestor <sha> main`, which passes for every recent commit on main) cannot detect a substituted sha, prove the positive structural fact rather than checking a necessary-but-not-sufficient condition.

Complements the existing entry on `<merge_sha>^2` as the drift-proof "tip actually merged" (git_ops.py advance_main / verified_branch_tip): that one says the second parent is authoritative; this one records which COMPARISON against it actually discriminates, and the two weaker spellings that look sufficient and are not.

Gotcha (dark-factory merge lane): `git merge --no-ff <ref>` is a NO-OP when <ref> is already an ancestor of HEAD — git prints "Already up to date.", exits 0, and leaves HEAD unchanged (--no-ff only forces a merge commit for fast-forwards, not for already-contained refs). GitOps.merge_to_main (git_ops.py:9213) reads its result back with `git rev-parse HEAD` in the merge worktree, so for a degenerate/zero-commit task branch it returns MergeResult(success=True, merge_commit=<UNCHANGED main HEAD>) — a plausible-looking foreign SHA that becomes a `done` outcome and gets stamped as done_provenance. Consequence: never "fix" a phantom-done by making the worker's already-merged guard fall through to a merge for a zero-commit branch; that trades an already_merged/commit=None for a done/foreign-SHA (strictly worse) and burns a head-of-line verify slot. Verified empirically 2026-08-16 while remediating task 3103.

Reconciling a long-lived task branch: when N of its commits touch a conflicting file, MERGE main into the branch rather than rebasing. Task 3133's branch was 41 commits ahead / 1371 behind with conflicts in CHANGELOG.md and a 1100-line-modified tools.py; 19 of the 41 commits touched tools.py, so `git rebase main` would replay each and re-hit that conflict up to 19 times. `git merge main` from inside the worktree resolved it ONCE. The merge queue does not require linear branch history (merge_gates._commit_is_linear checks the LANDING commit on main, not the branch's own shape), so a merge commit inside the branch is fine. AUDIT THE RESULT with `git merge-tree --write-tree <branch> <main>` recomputed independently, then `git diff <that-tree> <your-merge-commit>` — anything outside the conflicted files being byte-identical proves the rest is lossless by construction and reduces the audit to the hunks you actually resolved. Then enumerate every REMOVED line in both directions (`git diff main <merge>` and `git diff <old-branch-tip> <merge>`) and classify each as a deliberate rewrite; unclassifiable removals are the signal of lost work.

GOTCHA (dark-factory merge lane, planning task 6647, read 2026-10-10): to make a rebased merge candidate keep its exact git tree in a test, commit onto main a patch IDENTICAL to one of the branch's commits. git_ops.py::GitOps::advance_main rebases with a plain `git rebase main` on top of the --no-ff merge commit. That linearises, drops the merge commit, and skips any branch commit whose patch-id is already upstream, so `<rebased>^{tree} == <merge_commit>^{tree}`. This is the follower-stacked-on-a-landed-head case. Separately, the single-branch gate re-verify (_finalize_inflight → gates.py::_reverify_rebased_tree → _run_post_merge_verify) runs PRODUCTION_VERIFIER rather than the lane's injected FakeVerifier (task 6344). Lane tests must therefore patch orchestrator.merge_lane.worker.run_scoped_verification to observe or answer that re-verify, and a held FakeVerifier verify needs make_lane(clock=healthy_verify_clock()).

In a multi-step runbook that captures a git tip variable at one step and consumes it several steps later (e.g. skills/unblock/SKILL.md's D1 re-verify terminator: capture <old-main-tip>, fetch, capture <new-main-tip>, diff between them), never capture the "before" tip via `git rev-parse main` (the local `main` ref) — `git fetch origin main` and `git rebase origin/main` never move `refs/heads/main`, only `refs/remotes/origin/main` and the current branch's own history, so the local `main` ref can be stale by an arbitrary, silent amount and the diff against it over-reports. Derive the "before" tip instead from the branch's own ancestry: `git merge-base HEAD origin/main`, computed BEFORE the next `git fetch origin main` moves origin/main forward. Fixed in task 3115's amendment pass (2026-07-30); same fix applies to any other runbook that does an analogous before/after main-tip diff.

MERGER GOTCHA (dark-factory, measured 2026-09-14, task 5031 / mr-9f92d235): a merger dispatch can carry a conflict that does NOT exist against main. The merge lane merges SPECULATIVELY on the verify frontier (`merge_to_main(..., base_sha=<predecessor's unlanded merge commit>)`), and when that conflicts the workflow's `_resolve_and_resubmit` rebases the task branch onto REAL main (cleanly, if main is not the problem) and then invokes the merger with the speculative hunk. The merger then finds a clean worktree, no MERGE_HEAD, and conflict blob ids that match no ref.

HOW TO TELL, in ~4 commands: (1) `git cat-file -t <blob>` on both index ids from the `diff --cc` header — they exist but `git log --all --find-object=<blob>` may list nothing (it only lists commits that INTRODUCE the blob, and merge commits are skipped; it is not a containment test — do not conclude 'dangling'). (2) `mcp__escalation__get_merge_queue` → for each `_merge-*` worktree / queued predecessor, `git rev-parse <sha>:<path>`; the HEAD-side blob will equal the predecessor's merge-commit version of the file. (3) `git merge-tree --write-tree main HEAD` → clean, vs `git merge-tree --write-tree <predecessor-merge-sha> HEAD` → CONFLICT reproduces the report. (4) The task-side blob is usually the PRE-rebase tip: `git reflog show <branch> --date=iso` shows the workflow's `rebase (finish) onto <main>` a few seconds before the merger dispatch.

DISPOSITION: `submit_merge_disposition(blocked=false)` — 'blocked' means the merge should be blocked, and a branch that merges cleanly with main should not be parked behind a steward. Do NOT pull the predecessor's content into the branch to pre-empt the conflict (if the predecessor bounces, the branch carries unlanded work; for the ratchet baseline it turns the gate red). Record the analysis with `escalate_info(category=risk_identified, severity=info)` carrying the merge-tree results as evidence so the NEXT merger (dispatched once the predecessor lands and the conflict becomes real) has the mechanical recipe.

SPECIFIC INSTANCE: `orchestrator/tests/merge_lane_ratchet_baseline.json` is a sorted per-path map, so two sibling γ-groups whose keys are adjacent lines (γ8's test_merge_guard_pipeline.py directly above 5025's test_merge_item_union.py) conflict textually even though neither touches the other's key — git treats adjacent-line edits from two sides as a content conflict. Resolution when real: keep both lines (each group's own key), then run orchestrator/tests/test_merge_lane_ratchet.py.

Gotcha for anyone writing/reviewing "is this branch's merge on main" prose in skills/merge-queue/SKILL.md, skills/unblock/SKILL.md or similar merge-authority docs: never prescribe an unfiltered `git log main --oneline --merges | head -5` (or `--oneline | head -5`) as the rc=128 (deleted-branch-ref) fallback search. It takes no task argument, so on any repo with real merge history it prints something unconditionally — "a hit" becomes always-true and "no hit" unreachable — silently attributing an unrelated task's merge SHA as done_provenance. The server's only backstop, `git merge-base --is-ancestor <sha> main`, passes for any recent commit on main and won't catch the error. The correct, task-scoped check mirrors the in-repo authority `GitOps.find_merge_marker` (orchestrator/src/orchestrator/git_ops.py:7862-7905): `git log main --fixed-strings --grep="Merge task/<TASK_ID> into main" --max-count=1 --format=%H` — non-empty output is the true merge-commit SHA (landed), empty means not landed. `--fixed-strings` against the exact `_merge_subject` output (git_ops.py:1874, canonical form `Merge <branch> into <main-branch>`) gives substring safety (`task/1` cannot match inside `task/10`, since the digit-vs-space differs right after the shared prefix). Do not substitute a bare `--grep="task/<TASK_ID>"` either — that's BRE, unrestricted to merge commits, and matches any commit merely mentioning the task, reopening the same collision. Found and fixed on task 3281 (final commit f694fc3beb, on top of 374468dbad which introduced the vacuous check) — the third of three consecutive self-inflicted blocking-review-finding cycles on the same doc region, each one tightening a predicate without checking what it actually returns in the ordinary case.

STAMPED PEER under topic `git-rebase-defeats-ancestry-check` — the PARTIALLY-LANDED subcase, which is the FALSE-NEGATIVE direction the canonical does not yet cover.

`git merge-base --is-ancestor HEAD main` -> rc=1 does NOT mean "this branch never merged". It proves only that the EXACT TIP is not on main. A branch can have been merged normally at an earlier commit and then had more commits added afterwards — the tip is then correctly not-an-ancestor while most of the work IS on main.

OBSERVED on task 3465 (2026-08-25): main carried `af73e791a3 "Merge task/3465 into main"` (committed 10:23:34 +0100, second parent 8dd3e6fc15, itself committed 10:22:47 — the lane took the then-current tip 47s later, correctly). A steward then committed 156419b8e2 at 10:51:34, i.e. 28 min AFTER that merge had already landed. The steward measured `--is-ancestor HEAD main` -> rc=1 and concluded "Branch task/3465 is NOT on main", which read as "nothing landed" when in fact everything except two commits had.

THE DISTINGUISHING CHECKS (either one, both cheap):
  - `git merge-base main HEAD` — if this returns a commit ON your branch that is NOT the base you branched from, the branch already merged at that point.
  - `git log --oneline main..HEAD` (what is unlanded) together with `git log --oneline HEAD..main` (whether main moved / you have diverged). Two non-empty outputs = diverged, so the next landing is a true merge, not a fast-forward.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND BOOKKEEPING: this state strands the residual commits. `report_ready_to_merge` requires main to be an ancestor of the branch tip, which is FALSE once diverged, so the desync fast-path cannot land them; and if the task is marked done on the strength of "it already merged", the post-merge commits are lost silently while main keeps whatever defect they fixed. Check task status is still non-terminal and get a second merge enqueued.

GENERAL RULE, consistent with this topic's canonical: ancestry rc is a claim about ONE sha, never about "the work". Confirm landing by CONTENT on main (`git show main:<path>`), not by testing a ref.

Coalesce-train non-tip members leave `task/<ID>` PERMANENTLY stale-by-rebase, so `git merge-base --is-ancestor task/<ID> main` returns rc=1 forever on work that DID land. Mechanism: the train merges only the tip branch (`tip_branch=tip_req.branch`; `_do_train_merge` step (c) — the tip "by stacking, already carries all member commits") and step (b) rebases that tip onto main first, rewriting every stacked commit's SHA; the member's own ref is never advanced to the rewritten commits. rc=128 never fires for such a member either, because `GitOps._delete_branch_if_on_main` retains any branch carrying commits beyond main. The correct landing test is CONTENT, not ancestry: `git cherry main task/<ID>` → landed iff the output is NON-EMPTY and every line starts with `-`. The non-empty conjunct is required — a zero-commit branch prints nothing, so `git cherry ... | grep -q '^+' || echo landed` falsely reports it landed. In-repo authority for both the test and the conjunct: `GitOps.rebase_preserving_task_commits` in orchestrator/src/orchestrator/git_ops.py (`bool(cherry_lines) and all(line.startswith('-') ...)`). Verified specimen 2026-08-22: task 4104 (train coalesce-4181-b2a290cd, tip merge d25b24468c) — no own merge marker, ref alive at dc82a17583, ancestry rc=1, yet all 5 commits marked `-` by git cherry.

Verifying an UNCOMMITTED merge in a task worktree produces false-red tests that read git HEAD, because HEAD is still the pre-merge branch tip: fused-memory tests/arm_harness/test_lme_control_artifacts.py::test_every_run_is_pinned_to_one_code_sha_and_the_committed_corpus (git merge-base --is-ancestor <pinned main sha> HEAD returns 1) and scripts/tests/test_repaired_delivered_check_descriptors.py::test_resynced_sidecar_descriptor_delivers_at_head[*] (delivered_checks evaluated at ref=HEAD 'evaluates fail at HEAD, but its producer is done'). Observed in the 4448 unblock on 2026-10-08: all of them passed once the merge was committed. Confirm by checking that the pinned sha is an ancestor of MERGE_HEAD; don't chase them as real failures.

Git gotcha in merge primitives: `git merge --no-ff <ref-already-an-ancestor-of-HEAD>` prints "Already up to date.", exits **rc=0**, and creates **NO commit** (verified on git 2.43; HEAD byte-identical, no MERGE_HEAD). So an rc==0 check alone is NOT sufficient to conclude a merge commit was created — a caller that reads `git rev-parse HEAD` afterwards gets the PRE-merge sha back and can report it as the item's merge commit. Any merge helper whose destination worktree is REUSED (e.g. `GitOps.merge_branch_into_worktree`, whose lane HEAD advances per chain item) must compare the post-merge sha to the pre-merge sha and treat equality as a distinct not-success outcome. `merge_to_main` is exempt only because its destination is a fresh `_merge-<hex8>` at main HEAD where the case cannot arise. Detect by sha equality, not by scraping the "Already up to date." string, which is locale- and version-dependent.

⚠️ CONTESTED as of 2026-08-18 (recon Stage 1, run ab330f59-7335-4962-b9a8-e2fdaa96d3e9) — the `merge_to_main` exemption clause above is directly REFUTED by memory ea8f48d8-f698-48dc-8cf1-c4b360703156 (2026-08-16, task 3103), which measured the degenerate/zero-commit case firing at exactly this call site: GitOps.merge_to_main (git_ops.py:9213) reads its result back with `git rev-parse HEAD` in the merge worktree, so for a zero-commit task branch it returns MergeResult(success=True, merge_commit=<UNCHANGED main HEAD>) — a plausible-looking foreign SHA that is then stamped as done_provenance. The later record is empirically verified and GOVERNS; treat the exemption sentence above as false. The rest of this entry (the rc=0 / no-commit mechanism, and the detect-by-sha-equality rule) is unaffected and still correct — and in fact the refutation strengthens it: the sha-equality check is required at merge_to_main too, not just at reused-worktree helpers. See open task 3103 for the code-side fix.

=== CORRECTED 2026-08-20 (curate-fused-memories batch sitting, gate 4423 cluster 8) — THE EXEMPTION CLAUSE BELOW IS WRONG, AND ITS REASONING IS INVERTED. READ THIS FIRST. ===
This entry states that `merge_to_main` "is exempt only because its destination is a fresh `_merge-<hex8>` at main HEAD where the case cannot arise". That is FALSE, and the stated reason is backwards: a fresh destination at main HEAD is the PRECONDITION for the failure, not protection from it.

VERIFIED IN SOURCE 2026-08-20 (orchestrator/src/orchestrator/git_ops.py, GitOps.merge_to_main): after a `rc == 0` no-ff merge the method does `git rev-parse HEAD` in the merge worktree and returns MergeResult(success=True, merge_commit=<that sha>) with NO equality check against pre_merge_sha — even though pre_merge_sha is right there in the same MergeResult. For a DEGENERATE / ZERO-COMMIT task branch whose tip is already an ancestor of main, git reports "Already up to date" with rc=0 and leaves HEAD UNCHANGED, so the method returns the UNCHANGED MAIN HEAD as the merge commit: a plausible-looking foreign SHA that becomes a `done` outcome and gets stamped as done_provenance.
WHY THE EXISTING UPSTREAM GUARD DOES NOT COVER IT: worktree_head_beyond_main() is consulted only on the branch-ref-ABSENT fallback path (`resolved is None`). When the branch ref EXISTS but is degenerate, `resolved` is non-None, that helper is never called, and the merge proceeds straight into the Already-up-to-date case.
SO THE SHA-EQUALITY CHECK IS REQUIRED HERE TOO, not only in helpers with a REUSED destination worktree such as GitOps.merge_branch_into_worktree. The correct account is memory ea8f48d8-f698-48dc-8cf1-c4b360703156 (2026-08-16, verified empirically while remediating task 3103).
Everything else in this entry — the sha-equality requirement for reused-destination helpers — stands. Only the merge_to_main exemption is struck.

Merge-lane test GOTCHA (task 5447 planning, 2026-10-05): on a single-host public lane drive (MergeLane.run, no _host_allocator write), production keeps item.base_sha == real main at dispatch — Mechanism 2 re-merges a stale non-speculative item and a speculative item dispatches only after its predecessor lands — so a test of 'the verify uses the FROZEN base, not a fresh get_main_sha()' is vacuous unless main moves INSIDE the verify before its facts resolve. The ratchet-clean way: persistent_merge_worktree=True plus a GitOps subclass overriding the public reset_persistent_merge_worktree to land an outside commit on main first (the warm swap runs before _run_inflight_verify resolves main_sha), and assert main actually moved.

content: Gotcha (merge lane, measured 2026-10-13, task 3962): RealMergeItem.merged_branch_tip and MergedOk.branch_tip are `git rev-parse HEAD` in the TASK WORKTREE, read before merge_to_main (merge_lane/worker.py::classify_and_merge). They are NOT the commit that was merged. merge_to_main merges the named ref refs/heads/<branch> --no-ff, and uses the worktree HEAD only when that ref is absent. The two can differ permanently (the recycled-lane HEAD shape in _already_merged_is_genuine, or a detached HEAD). So never compare merged_branch_tip to the live branch ref to decide "the branch moved": it never converges and livelocks any void/remerge loop. Compare `<candidate merge commit>^2` with refs/heads/<branch> instead.
