Gotcha for any reify tests/infra gate that greps the tree for a string pattern the gate itself must quote: exclude the gate's OWN artifacts via git pathspec magic (`git grep ... -- . ':(exclude)<own path>'`). This bites hardest when the gate ships a baseline manifest whose every row ENDS in an instance of the scanned pattern — an unexcluded scan harvests its own baseline as fresh findings and regeneration folds the baseline into itself. Canonical in-repo instance of the idiom: `tests/infra/test_orchestrator_config_canonical_path.sh` (`assert_no_legacy_config_refs`).

CORRECTED 2026-09-22 (task 7788, see peer memory 29ba91db-b6c8-48a9-84bc-66bfb85d9a1d): do NOT append `|| true` to the scan. A no-match `git grep` exits 1 (which is meant to abort under `set -euo pipefail`), but git grep ALSO exits 128 on a bad pathspec magic, an unenterable root, or a `-P` search on a git built without PCRE — and `|| true` launders all of those into a vacuous "no matches" PASS. Measured in task 7788 (git 2.43.0): with `|| true`, the canonical-path absence check passed on a root git could not even enter. Instead capture the status (`... || rc=$?`), accept only 0/1 as a real result, and let any other status fail the assert loudly.

Mechanics of the reify/dark-factory `kind: grep` delivered_check, measured 2026-08-07 — two traps worth knowing before diagnosing one. The runner executes exactly `git -C <project_root> grep -E -e <pattern> <ref> [-- <paths...>]` (`_run_grep_check` in orchestrator/src/orchestrator/delivered_checks.py); rc 0 = matched, rc 1 = no match, rc >= 2 = ERRORED. (1) A DEAD PATH DOES NOT ERROR. `git grep` returns rc 1 — indistinguishable from "pattern not found" — with empty stderr, for a path that does not exist, never existed, or is a whole missing directory. Measured: 0 of 340 checks across all 25 manifests ERRORED. So for `expect: present` a dead path is INERT (repointing it changes no verdict), but for `expect: absent` a dead path is a SILENT FALSE PASS — the dangerous direction and a real vacuity vector. As of 2026-08-07 zero such cases existed (all 16 dead-path checks were `expect: present`), and the orchestrator has no guard against it. (2) MULTI-PATH IS OR, NOT AND — `git grep ... -- pathA pathB` matches if EITHER hits, so one live path can satisfy a check whose other path is dead, masking the dead one entirely. (3) The `-E` means patterns are EXTENDED REGEX, so a literal string containing `(`, `)`, `|`, `+`, `?`, `{`, `[` silently means something else. A full sweep of all 340 patterns found exactly ONE genuine escaping bug: reify task 5261's `INTERRUPTED (worktree removed)`, where ERE reads the parens as a group and searches for `INTERRUPTED worktree removed` (0 hits repo-wide) while the literal has 3 hits in tests/infra/run_all.sh — a false FAILED on delivered work. Fixed on main 2026-08-07 (commit 16cfb015bc) by escaping to `INTERRUPTED \(worktree removed\)`. 18 other patterns carry unescaped metacharacters but are deliberate regexes. Two latent unescaped-`.`-as-literal cases do not misfire today: tasks 5259 and 5453.

grep exit code 2 means the SCAN ERRORED, not "no matches" — absence of matches is exit 1. Treating exit 2 as evidence a symbol does not exist is unsound, and in the reify worktrees a repo-root recursive `grep -rn <sym> --include=*.rs .` intermittently exits 2 with empty stdout while the identical search scoped to `grep -rn <sym> crates/` returns real hits (observed 2026-08-25 in _lane-18: `try_angle_eq` reported absent twice, then found at crates/reify-constraints/src/solvespace.rs:224 on a scoped retry). Before concluding a symbol is dangling, re-run scoped to `crates/` or use the Grep tool, and check the exit code is 1 rather than 2.

Git pathspec `*` is NOT path-boundary-aware (no FNM_PATHNAME): `git ls-files 'gui/src-tauri/*.rs'` recursively matches tracked .rs at every depth INCLUDING the top-level build.rs (37 files in reify), reproducing `find -name '*.rs'`. The double-star `'gui/src-tauri/**/*.rs'` requires an intermediate dir and DROPS top-level build.rs (36 files). When porting a `find`-based scan to git ls-files, use the single-star form to preserve the set. Also: `git ls-files` in a non-git dir exits 128 with empty stdout — any test fixture passed via a --repo-root flag must be a real git repo (git init + git add, no commit needed since ls-files reads the index) for tracked-enumeration code paths to be exercised.

In reify, `git ls-files 'crates/*/tests/*.rs'` silently INCLUDES harness members like crates/reify-eval/tests/harness_geometry/foo.rs — git pathspec wildcards match `/` (wildmatch without WM_PATHNAME), unlike a shell glob. Enumerating top-level integration tests vs consolidated harness members requires an anchored regex filter (`^crates/[^/]+/tests/[^/]+\.rs$` vs `^crates/[^/]+/tests/harness_[^/]+/[^/]+\.rs$`), not a pathspec. Measured 2026-09-15: the naive pathspec reported 1294 "top-level" files where the anchored filter reports 546, silently folding in all 712 harness members.

In reify task worktrees, `rg` (ripgrep) is NOT on PATH — `which rg` returns empty. For live-corpus sweeps from Bash (e.g. PTODO/audit FP reviews), use `git grep` instead: `git grep -i -I -c -e "<pat>" -- '*.rs' '*.ri' '*.sh' '*.py' '*.ts' '*.tsx' '*.js' ':!crates/reify-audit/*' | awk -F: '{s+=$NF} END{print s}'` sums per-file match counts over the PTODO swept extension set while excluding the allowlisted detector crate. (The Claude Grep tool is still ripgrep-backed and works fine; this only affects shell invocations.)

reify — FIFTH variant of the self-matching-grep hazard class (siblings: a56545ed manifest-vs-meta-test, 07b67efe same-file static source scan, bc2826b0 parent-greps-child-script, a97e85e2 sub-shell assert-description self-match). Here the self-match is in a MEASUREMENT quoted inside a comment: crates/reify-audit/src/ptodo.rs's `prd_relative_cite_negatives` documented "family 1 has ZERO live four-digit exposure" and quoted `git grep -nEi '(§[0-9.]*|\b(OQ|DD|Q|T))#[0-9]{3,}' -- '*.rs'` as the proof — but the five synthetic controls sitting directly beneath that comment (`§7#4553`, `T#4553`, `Q#4553`, `OQ#4553`, `DD#4553`) ARE tracked source, so re-running it in Aug 2026 returned 5, not 0. RULE: any `git grep` corpus measurement about PTODO/marker/cite grammar must add `':!crates/reify-audit/*'` — that crate is the detector's own §6.8 ALLOWLIST_PREFIXES entry, so its fixtures and test string-literals are invisible to the live sweep but fully visible to a bare `git grep`, i.e. the grep and the detector disagree by construction. Same trap applies to `crates/reify-test-support/src/ignore_hygiene.rs` and `crates/reify-test-support/tests/ignore_reason_hygiene.rs`, the other two allowlist entries. Corollary: prefer the file path WITHOUT a line number in provenance comments (`// crates/reify-eval/src/detectors.rs`, not `:671`) — nothing verifies a line number and no test enforces it; task #6103's own diff shipped a `:671` citation whose quoted text that same branch had already rewritten.

Reify Bash-tool grep gotcha, EXIT-CODE discriminator (measured 2026-08-12, task 6230, lane worktree _lane-17): a recursive `grep -rn "<pat>" <dir>/` can return **exit status 2 with completely empty stdout AND empty stderr** — even when matches exist. Verified by redirecting each stream to its own file: exit=2, 0 stdout lines, 0 stderr bytes; yet the SAME pattern/dir piped as `grep -rn "<pat>" <dir>/ 2>&1 | head` printed the real matches, and a single-FILE `grep -n "<pat>" <file>` returned them normally at exit 0. WHY IT MATTERS: empty output from `grep -r` is what an agent reads as "the string is absent", so this silently yields a FALSE-CLEAN blast-radius/scope check — the exact check that bounds a targeted fix. THE TELL IS THE EXIT CODE: genuine "no matches" is exit **1**; exit **2** means grep/the wrapper errored and the empty result is meaningless. Never conclude "no hits" from `grep -r` without checking `$?`. Reliable alternatives: the dedicated Grep tool (ripgrep-backed, returned all 13 hits here where bash `grep -r` returned none), `git grep` (memory 88ff8de8 — bare `rg` is not on PATH in task worktrees), or per-file `grep -n`.

REFINEMENT (measured 2026-08-21, task 6108, lane _lane-6, HEAD efe4acf1d9): the original hypothesis that interception keys on "the directory-recursive form" alone is FALSIFIED by a control set run back-to-back at the same HEAD: (a) `grep -rn "leodearden" crates/reify-audit/src/bin/` -> exit 2, empty stdout, empty stderr, though a match exists at bin/reify-audit.rs:1109; (b) `grep -n "leodearden" crates/reify-audit/src/bin/reify-audit.rs` — single file, SAME token -> exit 0, prints the match; (c) `grep -rn "usage_text" crates/reify-audit/src/bin/` — SAME directory, RECURSIVE, different token -> exit 0, prints matches; (d) `grep -rn "fn main" crates/reify-audit/src/` -> exit 0. So the failure tracks the PATTERN TOKEN combined with recursion, NOT recursion alone. Hypothesis (unverified — no hook/wrapper config inspected): a harness guard keys on the specific token and swallows both streams while surfacing exit 2.

NEW CONSEQUENCE CLASS: this corrupts CAPABILITY-MANIFEST conformance verdicts, not just ad-hoc scope checks. A `delivered_check` of `kind: grep ... expect: absent` (e.g. the jcodemunch-substrate-restoration manifest's `legacy-git-identity-default-removed` row) evaluated with the common shorthand "exit != 0 means absent" records PASS from this error path without having searched at all — on exactly the rows that exist to prove an absence. Require exit **1** specifically; treat exit **2** as ERROR/INDETERMINATE. Filed as esc-6108-5. Verification instrument that worked: the dedicated Grep tool (ripgrep-backed) returned correct ground truth for all three of the task's manifest predicates where bash `grep -r` returned exit 2.

TOOLING CAUTION (observed 2026-08-19, not root-caused): in this Claude Code harness, a RECURSIVE `grep -rn '<string>' <dir>/` returned EMPTY output for a string that demonstrably exists, twice in a row. Specifically `grep -rn 'reset_session_start' gui/src-tauri/src/` and `grep -rn 'reset_session_start' gui/src-tauri/` both printed nothing, while `grep -c 'reset_session_start' gui/src-tauri/src/debug_server.rs` returned 4 and a python regex scan located all four occurrences (lines 1286, 1295, 1315, 1344).

A positive control on the SAME single-file invocation worked correctly, so single-file grep is fine; the failure was specific to the recursive form. The harness is known to condense some tool output (CLAUDE.md documents a cargo test/build condensation wrapper, and `git log` / `ls` output visibly renders as summaries like "[log] 1 commit" / "LS: ls | 3 entries"), so output swallowing is the leading hypothesis — but it was not confirmed.

Practical rule: never treat an empty recursive-grep result as evidence of ABSENCE. Pair it with a positive control (the same pattern that must match somewhere) and prefer a python scan or a single-file `grep -c` for any absence claim that will end up in a PRD, a task description, or a manifest binding. This is the same discipline as the existing empty-db-scan-needs-positive-control rule, applied to grep.

In reify, a repo gate that checks "every cited crates/<c>/tests/<stem>.rs path in prose resolves on the tree" is UNUSABLE as stated: of 820 distinct cited test paths, 230 do not resolve, and 108 of those are hermetic fixture strings living inside existing test source (crates/alpha/tests/foo.rs, crates/foo/tests/bar.rs, crates/beta/tests/thing.rs, ...) plus deleted files and illustrative examples. Only the harness-consolidation move class is actionable: cited path unresolved AND exactly one crates/<same crate>/tests/harness_*/<same basename> exists. Phrase the predicate that way rather than "flat path moved under harness_", so it also catches harness-to-harness re-moves from the #5620 over-cap SPLIT (live example: harness_fea_solver_e2e/stress_error_messages.rs is cited but the file now lives in harness_stress_scenarios/). A single `git grep -nIoE` pass over all 4161 tracked files costs ~1.1s, so whole-tree prose scanning is cheap enough for a merge gate.

In reify, `git ls-files -- 'crates/*/tests/*.rs'` already matches BOTH flat (crates/<c>/tests/<f>.rs) and nested (crates/<c>/tests/harness_<s>/<f>.rs) paths, because a git pathspec wildcard crosses `/` unless `:(glob)` magic is used. Measured on the live tree: that one pattern yields 1304 units = 549 flat + 755 nested. Adding a second `'crates/*/tests/**/*.rs'` pattern DOUBLE-COUNTS every nested unit rather than widening coverage — it produced exactly 1304 again only because dedup hid it. Also measured and relied upon by tests/infra/cited-test-path-lib.sh: (crate, basename) is a unique key across the whole tests tree (0 duplicates).

GOTCHA for Reify's grep-based source gates (the two tests/infra wallclock guards, scripts/check-nan-safe-ordering.sh, check-compute-trampoline-registration.sh and friends): `grep -rn` WITHOUT `-a` silently drops any file GNU grep classifies as binary — one NUL byte is enough. On grep 3.11 the note "grep: FILE: binary file matches" goes to STDERR and the matching LINES never reach stdout, while rc stays 0. So a gate that captures stdout (`hits="$(grep -rnE ... )"`) reports "we looked and found nothing" about a file it never read, with no failure anywhere. Verified first-hand in task 6597: a .rs fixture holding a NUL plus a real violation emitted ZERO records at rc 0, and adding `-a` fixed it. A non-vacuity floor built on `find -name '*.rs' | wc -l` CANNOT catch this — find still counts the file grep refused to read, so the two disagree silently. Always pass `-a` (or `--binary-files=text`) in a scanning gate, and note the direction of harm differs per gate: a skipped violation is a missed red, but a skipped ESCAPE lowers an escape count that is often compared for EQUALITY against an allowlist constant, so two cancelling skips can read as correct.

CORRECTION to the reify tests/infra self-excluding git-grep gate idiom: do NOT end the scan with `|| true`. A no-match `git grep` exits 1, which does abort under `set -euo pipefail`, but git grep also exits 128 on a bad pathspec magic (e.g. `:(exclud)`), an unenterable root, or a `-P` search on a git built without PCRE. `|| true` turns all of those into a vacuous "no matches" PASS. Measured in task 7788 (git 2.43.0): with `|| true`, the canonical-path absence check passed on a root git could not enter. Capture the status (`|| rc=$?`), accept only 0/1 as a result, and return any other status so the assert fails loudly. Canonical instance once task 7788 lands: `tests/infra/test_orchestrator_config_canonical_path.sh::legacy_config_refs`, whose Section (D) pins that a scan which cannot run fails the check. Before that, main's `assert_no_legacy_config_refs` still shows the old `|| true` form.

GOTCHA when writing a live-corpus sweep over `git ls-files -s` in reify (verified task 6068, 2026-08-21): always parse with `-z` + `awk 'BEGIN { RS = "\0"; FS = "\t" }'` and take `$2`, NEVER a whitespace-splitting `awk '{print $4}'`. `git ls-files -s` emits "<mode> SP <sha> SP <stage> TAB <path>", so a whitespace split truncates any tracked path containing a space. Two distinct failure modes, and the second is EXTENSION-SPECIFIC and worse. Measured in a scratch repo tracking `docs/notes.md`, `data/report v2.csv`, `docs/foo.bar baz.qux`: the tab-split form emits {csv, md, qux} (correct) while the whitespace form emits {bar, md}. (1) PHANTOM: `docs/foo.bar baz.qux` truncates to `docs/foo.bar`, whose post-dot token `bar` names an extension existing nowhere — a loud RED sending the reader hunting a nonexistent file. (2) SILENT MISS: `data/report v2.csv` truncates to the now-DOTLESS `data/report`, so a dotted-segment branch DROPS it and the real `csv` is never checked — the alarm quietly weakens instead of failing. Mode (2) cannot arise on an extensionLESS sweep (a truncated path stays dotless and is still swept), so an extension-side sweep depends on the parse shape MORE, not less. reify tracks zero paths containing a space today (`git ls-files | grep -c ' '` -> 0), so both are latent — but a standing alarm exists precisely to outlive today's corpus. Also pass `--` to grep (`grep -cxF -- "$tok"`) when the swept token could begin with a dash, else grep parses it as an option bundle and the assertion errors instead of answering. Live instances: Cycles 9 and 10 of tests/infra/test_lock_charter_guard.sh.

In a reify warm lane, the root is almost entirely target/: measured 2026-09-27 on _lane-41, 141 GB apparent in ~85k files vs 122 MB for everything else and 4,402 tracked files. A recursive `grep -rn <pat> .` from the lane root reads all of it: still running at 20s, and it hits the Bash tool's 120s cap, which auto-backgrounds rather than kills it. `git grep` (0.18s, `-P` supports look-around) or the Grep tool, which honours .gitignore's /target and .task/, finish instantly. GNU grep 3.11 ignores GREP_OPTIONS, so no env-level exclude is possible.

Gotcha (reify): a task's `delivered_checks` grep with `expect: absent` passes VACUOUSLY once a file move deletes its path. `git grep <pat> <rev> -- <deleted-file>` prints nothing and exits rc=1, which the delivered-checks runner reads as "absent" = PASS. So when you move or partition a file, also grep docs/prds/**/*.capability-manifest.yaml and the pending tasks' metadata.delivered_checks for the old path, and repoint them to a directory pathspec (e.g. `crates/reify-lsp/src/references`) on the same branch. Task #8757 found this against #8910's rename-gate check.

Gotcha when writing a workspace-MEMBERSHIP check against `cargo metadata --format-version 1 --locked --offline --no-deps`: `--no-deps` restricts the top-level `packages` array to workspace members, but each member object still carries its own nested `dependencies` array whose entries also have `"name":"..."` keys. So `grep '"name":"<crate>"'` over the raw JSON is NOT a membership test — it passes for any crate merely REFERENCED as a dependency. Measured in task 7096: a grep for `"name":"serde"` passes on reify's --no-deps metadata even though serde is not a member, so a name dropped from the root Cargo.toml `members` list but still dep-referenced would pass a grep-based guard silently. Parse the `packages` list instead: `python3 -c 'import json,sys; meta=json.load(sys.stdin); sys.exit(0 if sys.argv[1] in {p["name"] for p in meta["packages"]} else 1)' "<crate>"`. That set is exactly what a cargo `-p <crate>` selector resolves against, so it is also the honest check for "will this emitted -p flag resolve". Cost measured at ~0.13s warm, cheap enough for an infra-test assertion. Complements memory e0eaecac (the python3-not-jq metadata technique) and d9c0cfca (deriving member ROOT DIRS); this entry is about the grep-vs-parse hazard on the name field specifically. Worked example: `_check_gate_crate_is_workspace_member` in tests/infra/test_affected_crates_lib.sh.

Reify Bash-tool GREP output is condensed by a wrapper (distinct from the well-known cargo/rustc skim wrapper) that has TWO artifacts which read as real findings. (1) SILENT TRUNCATION: it prints headers like `GREP: grep | 6 entries (showing 5)` / `6 matches in 1 files (showing 1)` and drops the rest — a `grep -rn` whose matches all get truncated can render as EMPTY OUTPUT, which looks like "the string is absent" and can wrongly convince you a citation/symbol was deleted. (2) LEADING-CHARACTER STRIPPING on some context lines — a well-formed `// ("...")` Rust/`.ri` comment renders as `/ ("...")` and a `//!` renders as `/!`, which looks like a malformed comment that would break a parse. Both are DISPLAY artifacts only; the bytes on disk are fine. Confirmed 2026-08-09 during task 6046 against crates/reify-compiler/stdlib/modal_analysis.ri, where each artifact triggered a separate false alarm. Do not conclude "string absent" or "comment malformed" from condensed grep output: re-check with the dedicated Grep tool, an explicit `Read` of the line range, or `grep -c` / `git diff --numstat` for a count. Note the dedicated Grep tool exhibited artifact (2) as well, so an exact `Read` of the line range is the reliable arbiter.

reify: when writing a tests/infra structural guard that greps for a bare CLI invocation, discriminate by COMMAND POSITION, not by mere mention. Measured for `tree-sitter parse` at main 2227f36c4d: a whole-repo literal grep hits 170+ tracked files (PRD prose, .ri fixture header comments, Rust doc comments), but the ERE `^[[:space:]]*(\$ )?([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*=[^[:space:]]+[[:space:]]+)*<cmd>` hits only 7 lines in 4 files. Also exclude docs/prds/**/*.capability-manifest.{md,yaml} by SCOPE: their command lines are archival evidence of probes executed on a stated date, so "fixing" them falsifies a measurement record. House conventions for such guards: POSIX ERE only (grep -P is silently broken on BSD grep and makes negated assertions false-positive), bracketed char-class self-avoidance (`tree-[s]itter`), plus a not-vacuously-green enumeration check and a synthetic positive control — skeleton at tests/infra/test_no_prebuilt_reify_bin_spawn.sh, assertion shape at scripts/test_tree_sitter_generate.sh:166.

esc-6108-5 investigated and REFUTED (2026-08-21, steward): there is no hook/wrapper that intercepts recursive `grep` for the operator-handle token `leodearden`. Reproduction against the exact byte-identical file content from HEAD efe4acf1d9 (`git cat-file -p efe4acf1d9:crates/reify-audit/src/bin/reify-audit.rs` into a tmpdir) gave `grep -rn leodearden <tmpdir>/` -> exit 0 with the match printed. grep is /usr/bin/grep (GNU 3.11), no alias/function shadow. The originally reported exit-2-with-empty-stdout-and-stderr was a one-off, non-reproducible environmental artifact, not a token-keyed behaviour. Do not re-chase the interception hypothesis. Separately: no automated runner for capability-manifest `delivered_check` entries exists in either reify or dark-factory today — `shared/src/shared/capability_manifest.py` only validates the schema; execution is agent-driven via the /prd skill. The error-vs-absent discrimination the escalation asked for is already specified in dark-factory `plans/capability-delivered-checks-prd.md` §5 "Fail-safe runner semantics" (a check that ERRORS -> dep not satisfied this tick, no streak bump; only a check that RAN AND FAILED bumps the streak) and scenario row 7 "Runner error".

candidates.content:
What a real Victron GX returns in an FC6 (write single register) response. Read from Victron's published source on 2026-10-13 by task 988's architect; NOT tested on a real GX.
(1) The normal FC6 response echoes the REQUEST byte for byte, never the stored or clamped value. This holds for every register, including 2700, 2901, 37, 2704 and 2705. Source: victronenergy/dbus_modbustcp at d7baaefbee5a (master, 2026-10-12):
- backend.cpp Backend::modbusRequest puts the request's two value bytes into the mapping request's data().
- mappings.cpp Mappings::setValues reads that data through a const reference and never rewrites it.
- Backend::requestCompleted copies it into the reply with setReplyData(request->data()).
- adu.cpp ADU::toQByteArray writes the address plus that data.
So comparing response.registers with the word written can never fail against a conforming GX. The comparison only catches a non-conforming server, such as the pre-739 FrontingDeviceContext, which answered every FC6 with [0].
(2) An FC6 success does NOT mean the GX stored the value.
- victronenergy/veutil at d84fdf334568, src/qt/ve_qitems_dbus.cpp: VeQItemDbus::setValue sends D-Bus SetValue asynchronously and returns 0. setValueDone discards the reply.
- victronenergy/localsettings at 3aac232f99b1, localsettings.py SetValue: a value below min or above max is REJECTED, not clamped (it returns DBUS_ERR and keeps the old value). int() truncates a fractional value for an 'i'-typed setting.
- So on a GX an out-of-range settings write is silently dropped: the FC6 response echoes the request while the setting keeps its old value.
- An FC3 read-back serves VeQItemDbus::getValue, which returns the cached mValue, not mPendingSetValue. A read-back therefore shows the old value after a rejection.
- Hypothesis: a read-back issued immediately after an accepted write can race the asynchronous PropertiesChanged update and still show the old value.
(3) FC6 exceptions a GX does return:
- 0x02 IllegalDataAddress: the register is unmapped or read-only, or /Settings/ModbusServer/ReadWrite = 0.
- 0x0A GatewayPathUnavailable: the service is offline, setValue returned -1, or the word did not convert.
- 0x0B GatewayTargetDeviceFailedToRespond: the unit id is unknown.

Facts established about the Victron contract code (main 89a2a4a) that affect any future change to GX settings:
(1) contract.from_registers deliberately ignores unknown register keys. This is a recorded amendment pinned by tests/control/test_contract.py::test_from_registers_ignores_unknown_keys. Only ModbusTcpTransport refuses addresses outside VICTRON_REGISTERS. Making the double refuse unknown keys is a policy change for Leo to decide, not a fix.
(2) VictronRegister.service is read by no src code. A real-GX transport that routes by unit id (settings on unit 100, vebus on the VE.Bus unit; register-contract diff row (e), deferred to 699) will be its first consumer.
(3) The real wire path writes 2700/2901/2704/2705/37 uniformly (transport/modbus.py ~572). Only the double distinguishes persisted settings from watchdog-covered registers.
(4) The pair rule (2704 and 2705 written together) is a platform invariant, not a Victron one. On a GX the two are independent settings.
(5) docs/victron-register-contract.md's feedback-frame row says 40 registers, but FEEDBACK_LEN is 42.

Victron GX FC6 write response: re-verified 2026-10-18 by task 988's architect at newer source commits, with the same conclusions as the 2026-10-13 note. A GX echoes the FC6 request byte for byte, and an FC6 success does not mean the value was stored.
Commits: dbus_modbustcp master 205bf75 (2026-10-13, v1.0.104); veutil master 70b1a39; localsettings master c0b65b3 (2026-10-16).
Additions and one correction:
(a) veutil's VeQItemDbus::setValueDone does NOT discard the D-Bus reply. It reports it through reportSetValueResult (VE_QITEM_SETVALUE_RETVAL / VE_QITEM_BUS_ERROR). But dbus_modbustcp has already sent the Modbus reply by then, so a Modbus client never sees it.
(b) dbus_modbustcp app.cpp registers add("ModbusServer/ReadWrite", 0, 0, 1) (path, default, min, max). So a stock GX refuses every Modbus-TCP write with 0x02 IllegalDataAddress until /Settings/ModbusServer/ReadWrite is set to 1.
(c) The cached mValue that an FC3 read serves changes only through the service's PropertiesChanged/ItemsChanged (onPropertiesChanged → produceValue) or a GetValue. setValue stores mPendingSetValue only.
(d) The Modbus spec V1.1b3 §6.6 says verbatim: "The normal response is an echo of the request, returned after the register contents have been written."
  - modbus.org/docs/Modbus_Application_Protocol_V1_1b3.pdf answers curl with a web-application-firewall block page.
  - https://www.modbus.org/file/secure/modbusprotocolspecification.pdf works: V1.1b3, sha256 f80d0d7132fd035104c3f21b01026470e3310ca3d8d493d9a9737d0d32ad2eb1.

VICTRON REGISTER FACTS (verified 2026-09-29 by task 598 / P-Fleet·γ1 architect against primary sources). Published CCGX Modbus-TCP register list, both the repo copy (victronenergy/dbus_modbustcp CCGX-Modbus-TCP-register-list.xlsx @ dddf4b8a06, Rev 54) and the website's latest copy (CCGX-Modbus-TCP-register-list-3.80.xlsx): 2705 /Settings/SystemSetup/MaxChargeCurrent (int16, ×1, A DC) says "-1 Disables." (no-limit = raw -1). 2704 /Settings/CGwacs/MaxDischargePower (int16, ×0.1, W) gives NO no-limit value; its remark is only "similar to 2702, but as an absolute value", and the int32 ×1 twin 2720 is silent too. Only the separate ESS Mode 2 & 3 manual says "register 2704: -1: No limit". The ×0.1 scale is the trap. dbus_modbustcp mappings.cpp sets dbus = raw / scale on a write, so raw -1 lands as -10 W, and the settings-service min that must accept it is unverified (hub4control is closed source). On a read it returns round(dbus × 0.1), so a GX at -1 ("no limit") reads back raw 0, the same raw as a 0 W limit. gui-v2 treats MaxDischargePower < 0 as "not limited". dbus-systemcalc-py registers MaxChargeCurrent with default -1 and min -1.

Completed: Modbus register-write responses: ModbusTcpTransport checks them, and FrontingDeviceContext echoes the written word on FC6
Description: Both sides of the Modbus write-response contract. (1) Client side: `ModbusTcpTransport.write_setpoint` in src/solar_challenge_platform/control/transport/modbus.py discards its register-write responses, so a rejected write is invisible. (2) Server side: `FrontingDeviceContext` in src/solar_challenge_platform/control/testing/modbus_harness.py answers an FC6 single-register write with value 0 instead of echoing the written word, which a stricter client would reject. Found while planning task 598 (P-Fleet·γ1) and by task 826's architect.

OBSERVATION A (code read at main 2ee902c): `ModbusTcpTransport.write_setpoint` calls three writes and discards each response:
- `self._client.write_registers(SELECTOR_BASE, ...)`;
- `self._client.write_register(addr, ...)` for each Victron register;
- `self._client.write_register(CHARGE_LIMIT_REG, ...)`.
Only the final WRITE_TRIGGER read is checked with `response.isError()`. `read_delivered`'s selector write is unchecked too.
Hypothesis (not verified against pymodbus): a Modbus exception response from the device (e.g. a GX rejecting a setting write as out of range or read-only) comes back as an error PDU, not a raised exception. The rejection would then be invisible. The transport would read feedback as if the write had landed, and the actuation would be logged ok=True.
Why it matters: P-Fleet γ2a/β3b will write limit registers 2704/2705 (idle/restore). A silently rejected limit write would leave a home un-idled or un-restored with no signal (design invariant no-silent-fail-soft).

OBSERVATION B (measured on main ab544aa, pymodbus 3.13.1, worktree .venv): with a SimModbusServer(PhysicsDeviceEnd()) and a raw pymodbus ModbusTcpClient, `client.write_register(2901, 200, device_id=1)` returned WriteSingleRegisterResponse(address=2901, registers=[0]) with isError() False. The Modbus spec says the normal FC6 response echoes the request, so the expected echo is registers=[200].
Code reading: in pymodbus 3.13.1, pdu/register_message.py::WriteSingleRegisterRequest.datastore_update calls context.async_setValues and then builds the response from context.async_getValues(device_id, fc, address, 1). `FrontingDeviceContext.async_getValues` returns [0] * count for every address other than WRITE_TRIGGER and READ_TRIGGER, so every FC6 echo carries 0, including CHARGE_LIMIT_REG 50008 and each VICTRON_REGISTERS address. The datastore is served both by SimModbusServer (src/solar_challenge_platform/simulator/modbus_server.py), which task 489's scp-sim-modbus role will deploy, and by ModbusConformanceHarness.
Impact today: none observed, because the transport ignores FC6 echoes (on main) or checks only isError() (_require_accepted on this branch).

Completed: ModbusTcpTransport wraps a DVCC charge_limit_kw of 65.535 kW or more silently into CHARGE_LIMIT_REG, and admits NaN past its pre-I/O check
Description: Found while planning task 739 (ModbusTcpTransport register-write response checks). Out of that task's scope, so it is filed here. Follow-up id: agent-followup-739.

OBSERVATION (measured 2026-10-04 on main 2838c8a, pymodbus 3.13.1, Python 3.11):
src/solar_challenge_platform/control/transport/modbus.py::ModbusTcpTransport.write_setpoint encodes the DVCC charge limit for the auxiliary register CHARGE_LIMIT_REG (50008) as `round(charge_limit_kw * 1000) & 0xFFFF`. SetpointCommand (control/contract.py) bounds charge_limit_kw only from below (>= CHARGE_LIMIT_MIN = 0.0), and the transport's pre-I/O check is also `val < CHARGE_LIMIT_MIN`. Measured with SetpointCommand(mode=MODE_2, min_soc_pct=20, charge_limit_kw=X) then to_registers:
- X = 65.535: the command is accepted and the word is 65535 = 0xFFFF = ABSENT_CHARGE. The fronting server (control/testing/modbus_harness.py::FrontingDeviceContext) reads that as "no charge limit", so the limit is silently dropped.
- X = 70.0: the command is accepted and the word is 4464. The server reads 4.464 kW, a silently different and much lower limit.
- X = NaN: the command is accepted (NaN < 0 is False), and the encoding raises ValueError('cannot convert float NaN to integer'). On main this raise happens after the selector and Victron register writes have already gone out on the wire.

The comment in encode_feedback already notes that the valid domain is [0, 65.534] kW, but nothing enforces it. This is the silent-clamp class that task 598 removed for VICTRON_REGISTERS (contract.encode refuses a value its wire type cannot carry).

WORK:
- Refuse a charge_limit_kw outside [0, 65.534] kW, or not finite, before any I/O. Name the value and the home. Raise ValueError, as the other pre-I/O refusals do.
- Ideally define the bound once in control/contract.py (next to CHARGE_LIMIT_MIN). Use it from SetpointCommand._validate_value_ranges and from the transport's defense-in-depth check, so the two layers cannot drift (heuristic 11).
- Test (default lane, no socket): mirror tests/control/test_modbus_binding.py::test_write_setpoint_refuses_an_unencodable_register_before_io, using ModbusTcpTransport('127.0.0.1', free_tcp_port()) so that reaching I/O would raise ConnectionError instead. Also add SetpointCommand construction tests in tests/control/test_contract.py.

GOTCHA — `orchestrator/tests/test_merge_lane_ratchet.py` takes ~215 SECONDS to run (measured 2026-09-15: 214.48s, 215 tests passed, on base f7f6c8f89a). At the Bash tool's 120000ms DEFAULT timeout it is SIGTERM'd mid-gate (exit 143) and reads as a hang. Pass an explicit `timeout` of at least 600000ms. The module is xdist_group-pinned and does whole-tree scans, so its cost is structural, not incidental.

Any task editing a merge-lane cluster path must budget against TWO independent zero-slack axes, not one. Measured on that same base, both EQUAL to the committed baseline (`check_against_baseline` reports 0 violations, i.e. no headroom anywhere):
- `orchestrator/src/orchestrator/merge_queue.py` — lines 21572, prose_lines 12288, cognitive 2132, function_local_imports 16, reexport_names 60. `lines` is the RAW physical count (`len(source.splitlines())`, blanks included) and `prose_lines` is the union of docstring-spanned lines and tokenize COMMENT lines — so a rewritten comment must occupy EXACTLY the line count of the one it replaces, and a new kwarg must stay on its existing line. `orchestrator/pyproject.toml` ignores E501, so no wrap is ever needed.
- The DERIVED `total:private_reads` — 7212 summed across 231 lane-importing test files. `derive_totals` sums the WHOLE current `tests` map and `_check_totals` fails on any rise, so ONE new private attribute access — read, write OR call, receiver-agnostic — in ANY lane-importing test file reddens the gate. This is what makes a brand-new white-box test file importing `orchestrator.merge_queue` un-GREENable: it also adds a `tests` entry, which independently breaks `test_baseline_matches_a_fresh_measurement` (a byte-identity comparison against the committed baseline).

Consequence worth planning around: when the ratchet forbids a wiring test for a merge_queue call site, `[tool.pyright] include = ["src", "tests"]` in `orchestrator/pyproject.toml` is the available substitute — a REQUIRED keyword-only parameter makes a forgotten argument a `reportCallIssue` error on every pre-commit and verify.

Do NOT regenerate the baseline to make a gate pass — `scripts/merge_lane_metrics.py::BASELINE_README` forbids it; regenerate only in the SAME commit as a change that genuinely LOWERS a measure.

Operational timing calibration for dark-factory merge-queue landings, measured 2026-08-10 across three consecutive landings (tasks 3764, 3763, 3404) on a single local merge host.

MERGE-WORKER FULL GATE: roughly 35-45 minutes wall clock per landing, end to end from merge_request to the branch becoming an ancestor of main. The worker re-runs the whole 7-package test_command fan-out against the merged result regardless of what verified_green claimed. Observed verify_age_secs peaked around 2100s (35 min) before finalizing. eta_seconds from merge_status is unreliable — it returned 424, then 109, then 9, then null, while the verify continued for another ~20 minutes.

LOCAL SCOPED VERIFIES (for comparison, when deciding whether to pre-verify):
- `uv run --project shared pytest tests/scripts/ scripts/tests/` — about 3.5 minutes, ~3026 tests.
- `cd orchestrator && uv run pytest tests/` — 13.5 to 16.5 minutes, 16008 tests.
So pre-verifying a scripts-only branch costs ~4 minutes against a ~40 minute gate; pre-verifying an orchestrator branch costs ~15 minutes. Both are cheap enough to be worth doing for an honest verified_green.

HOW TO TELL A LONG VERIFY FROM A WEDGED ONE: get_merge_queue reports waiter_alive and the owning worktree path (e.g. .worktrees/_merge-<hex>). `pgrep -fa <that worktree basename>` shows the live pytest leg, and `find <worktree> -type f -printf '%T@ %p\n' | sort -rn | head` shows the newest write. On all three landings the worker was demonstrably on its final `tests/scripts/` leg with file writes under a minute old. A merge that looks stuck at 35 minutes is usually just slow — check for a live pytest child before escalating.

QUEUE SNAPSHOT NOTE: get_merge_queue's frozen_prefix.tip_merge_commit predicts the merge commit the landing will produce; on all three landings it matched the eventual main tip exactly (497e5eba05, 1f2c60c7de, a15c8e446f). Useful for confirming which landing you are waiting on.

INCIDENT 2026-09-18, a new instance of the known merge-lane ratchet trap (see the task-5033 gotcha and topic merge-lane-ratchet-private-reads-new-test-rows): DELETING tests trips it just like adding them. Task 5578 removed four tests from orchestrator/tests/test_verify_env_transient.py that called the private verify._is_bare_xdist_worker_crash, dropping that file's row in orchestrator/tests/merge_lane_ratchet_baseline.json from private_reads 35 to 31 without regenerating the baseline. test_verify_env_transient.py is a verify test, not a merge-lane test, yet it has a row: the baseline carries a per-file row for every file under orchestrator/tests/, so 'I did not touch merge-lane code' is not a reason to skip the check. The author had run only the 38 test_verify*.py modules (3578 passed), which cannot see it; only tests/test_merge_lane_ratchet.py does. Cost: the red surfaced inside a 3-member coalesce train (coalesce-5578-462b8bbb) after a ~50 min union verify, then a ~57 min main probe, then a derail that re-pended two unrelated tasks (5461, 5237). Cheap proof before committing any diff under orchestrator/: run `uv run --project shared python scripts/merge_lane_metrics.py --write-baseline orchestrator/tests/merge_lane_ratchet_baseline.json` and check `git status` — an empty diff is the proof. scripts/merge_lane_metrics.py::test_file_measures admits an orchestrator/tests file to the baseline's `tests` map iff `imports_lane_module(source)` — i.e. it imports orchestrator.merge_queue, orchestrator.merge_lane, or any other CLUSTER_PATHS module. Consequences for a NEW test file:
- It gains a `tests` entry, which ALONE stales the committed baseline and reddens test_baseline_matches_a_fresh_measurement (byte-identity).
- Its private_reads feed derive_totals, which sums the WHOLE current tests map (baseline 7847 over 229 entries) and _check_totals fails on any rise. _check_tests iterates BASELINE keys only and skips absent paths, so the per-file arm does NOT protect you — the totals arm does the failing. The ratchet's own seeded self-test pins a brand-new file with private_reads:1 as a total:private_reads violation.
- private_reads is deliberately RECEIVER-AGNOSTIC: any `x._foo` (non-dunder) counts, including writes (`worker._host_allocator = a`) and calls (`await worker._dispatch_item(i)`), and chains count per hop. Bare self./cls. receivers are excluded, but `self.worker._x` counts. No helper, fixture or naming trick avoids it.
- patch_targets is a UNION across all tests entries, so reusing a leaf already in the baseline's 83 is free; a brand-new leaf is a violation.

Practical upshot: a test file that imports only orchestrator.verify_runner or orchestrator.config is INVISIBLE to both gates (neither is a cluster path) and can use unrestricted private access and length. orchestrator/tests/test_host_allocator.py is the worked example — absent from the baseline, module-level imports are pytest only. Keep new merge-lane-adjacent tests lane-import-free on purpose when you can.

When you genuinely cannot test the wiring (e.g. a new config knob threaded into merge_queue.py), pyright is the available substitute: orchestrator/pyproject.toml [tool.pyright] includes both `src` and `tests`, so making the new parameter REQUIRED keyword-only turns an unwired call site into a reportCallIssue on every pre-commit and verify. Task 5097 took that route after confirming no test anywhere drives the real SpeculativeMergeWorker._dispatch_item.

PROCEDURE (dark-factory, task 5021, HEAD cd2bf4de31) — how to PROVE, before reporting a branch ready to merge and WITHOUT rebasing, that the committed merge-lane ratchet baseline will survive the lane's rebase. This is the PREVENTIVE counterpart to memory 7a853852 (the three-step proof once the freshness test is already RED) and 2d500bdc (residual trigger rate). Those are reactive; this one runs while the gate is still green and costs ~50s.

WHY IT IS WORTH DOING. `test_baseline_matches_a_fresh_measurement` compares committed bytes against a fresh measurement of whatever tree it runs on. The merge lane rebases onto main and re-verifies (merge_gates._reverify_rebased_tree), so a baseline that is fresh in the worktree but stale against main produces a GUARANTEED bounced merge cycle, not a possible one — the worktree's own verify stays green throughout and tells you nothing about it.

STEP 1 — narrow the candidates. `git diff --name-only $(git merge-base main HEAD)..main`. Only two classes of file can move the baseline: (a) a path in `merge_lane_metrics.CLUSTER_PATHS`, or (b) a test file under orchestrator/tests for which `imports_lane_module(src, path=...) is True`. Everything else — non-lane tests, docs, YAML, other packages — is invisible to the stored baseline after the esc-5021-7 lane-scoping fix. In a live check, 6 files had changed on main and only 1 was even a candidate. Note `imports_lane_module` covers ALL cluster modules, so grepping for merge_queue/merge_lane alone UNDER-counts — git_ops.py is a CLUSTER_PATHS entry too.

STEP 2 — for each candidate, measure both versions rather than eyeballing the diff. `git show main:<path>` and `git show HEAD:<path>` into temp files, then call `patch_targets(src, path=P)` / `private_reads(src, path=P)` / `imports_lane_module(src, path=P)` on each and compare to the entry in the committed baseline's `tests` map. A candidate file can change a LOT and still be measure-neutral: the live instance had ~50 lines added on main (a new format constant, a tightened regex) and produced patch_targets=[] / private_reads=1 on BOTH versions, identical to the baseline.

STEP 3 — the end-to-end probe, which is the part reasoning cannot substitute for. Copy main's versions of the candidate files INTO the worktree, run `pytest orchestrator/tests/test_merge_lane_ratchet.py -k "baseline_matches_a_fresh_measurement or denominator_covers"`, then `git checkout -- <paths>` and confirm `git status` is clean. Green means the rebase is baseline-safe. This is reversible, touches only tracked files, and needs no rebase — which matters because a task agent should not rebase (steward ruling, esc-5021-9).

GOTCHA that invalidates all of the above if ignored: run every one of these under the WORKTREE's own venv (`env -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --project orchestrator ...`). An agent Bash session inherits the MAIN checkout's VIRTUAL_ENV, which resolves complexipy 7.0.1 against the instrument's pinned >=6.2,<7 — measured live in this worktree: inherited python reports 7.0.1, `.venv/bin/python` reports 6.2.0. Do NOT pass `-p no:xdist` to narrow the run; orchestrator/pyproject.toml puts `-n`/`--dist` in addopts and pytest then aborts on unrecognized arguments.

MERGE-LANE RATCHET (scripts/merge_lane_metrics.py) — the working procedure for a γ test-seam migration task, learned on task 5027.

THE HARD CONSTRAINT. test_merge_lane_ratchet.py::test_baseline_matches_a_fresh_measurement asserts the committed baseline is BYTE-IDENTICAL to a fresh measurement, so a commit that lowers a measure must regenerate that entry in the SAME commit. `--check` (exit 1 = ratchet violation, 2 = instrument failure) is separate from that byte test; both must be green.

EDIT PROCEDURE that keeps parallel γ branches conflict-free: run `python3 scripts/merge_lane_metrics.py --write-baseline /tmp/fresh.json`, then splice ONLY your own group's single `tests` lines into the committed file by exact line match. Never regenerate wholesale onto the committed file, and never touch `enumeration` / `params` / `files` / `functions`. render_baseline emits one line per entry and is idempotent; totals are DERIVED by derive_totals, so there is no totals line to hand-edit.

KEEP EVERY MIGRATED FILE LANE-IMPORTING — do not drop its `orchestrator.merge_queue` / `orchestrator.merge_lane` import — or `enumeration.resolved` changes and the diff stops being confined to single `tests` lines.

MEASURING LOCALLY without running the script (useful mid-edit): private_reads is every single-underscore non-dunder ATTRIBUTE access on any receiver except a bare `self`/`cls`, and it counts WRITES too. So `worker._inflight`, `fake._calls` and `obj._replace` all count, `self._x` does not, and a bare underscore-prefixed NAME call is an ast.Name not an ast.Attribute — `_RecordingEventStore(...)` and `from _workflow_helpers import _bind_landed_row` are free. patch_targets counts DISTINCT leaf names patched through orchestrator.merge_queue or orchestrator.merge_lane only; a patch of an `orchestrator.merge_liveness.*` or `orchestrator.workflow.*` name does not count.

TO STAGE A RED COMMIT AFTER you have already migrated the file in the working tree: `cp` the migrated file to /tmp, `git checkout --` it, run `--check` to MEASURE the rise, `git add` the lowered baseline alone and commit (the tree then holds lowered-baseline + unmigrated file, which is exactly the RED state), then restore both files from /tmp for the GREEN commit. Do NOT use `git stash` — refs/stash is shared across every dark-factory worktree.

DANGER, cost a full redo once: never chain `git checkout -- <file>` after a command that might fail for an unrelated reason (e.g. a pytest invocation rejected for bad args). The checkout runs anyway and silently discards uncommitted migration work.

The baseline's tests section has a row for every file under orchestrator/tests that imports a cluster module (orchestrator.offline_lane, orchestrator.git_ops, anything under orchestrator.merge_lane), including rows whose measures are all zero (66 such rows that day), so a NEW test file that imports one of those modules changes the baseline even with no private reads. New source modules such as offline_lane_*.py are not in CLUSTER_PATHS and are not measured. Consequence for task authoring: any leaf whose new tests import a cluster module must list both ratchet json files, and two such leaves must be serialised by a dependency edge.

GOTCHA for any plan that adds or removes a SYMBOL in the merge-lane source set: orchestrator/tests/merge_lane_ratchet_baseline.json must be regenerated in the SAME change, or verify fails with category test_failure. Architects routinely miss this because the baseline is a generated artefact nobody edits by hand, so no TDD step naturally covers it.

WHAT MOVES. Adding one method to a port moves TWO kinds of entry at once: (a) the file's row — `lines` and `prose_lines` both change (measured on task 5485: orchestrator/src/orchestrator/merge_lane/ports.py went 255→274 lines, 47→59 prose_lines for a single `wait_for_any` on the Protocol plus its production adapter); and (b) a new per-symbol cognitive row per definition added, e.g. `...ports.py::ClockPort::wait_for_any": 0` and `...ports.py::ProductionClock::wait_for_any": 0`. A plan that only expects the line-count row to move will still leave the baseline stale.

HOW IT SURFACES, and why it is expensive. It does NOT fail the merge-lane test files an architect naturally runs while validating a design — task 5485's design measured 1014 tests green across 13 merge-lane files and was still wrong. It fails only in tests/test_merge_lane_ratchet.py, which the full-suite verify runs: four failures (test_merge_lane_ratchet_holds, test_baseline_matches_a_fresh_measurement, and both TestCheckCli rows) inside a 21400-test run that cost 63 minutes of wall clock to reach.

PRACTICE. When a plan's `files` list includes a merge-lane source file AND the change adds/renames/removes any def, put the baseline regeneration in the plan as an explicit impl step, and validate it cheaply with `uv run --directory orchestrator pytest tests/test_merge_lane_ratchet.py -q` (~96s, 287 tests) rather than discovering it from a full verify. Note the baseline is also a frequent rebase-overlap file — many merge-lane tasks touch it — so re-run that ratchet suite after any rebase, not just after the original edit.

RECURRENCE: seen on task 5485 (verify attempt-1, repaired by commit 490273c2ec) and independently on commit b5bf73106e (2026-09-18).

Merge-gate parallelism gap (measured 2026-09-10): pytest `-n` is injected only for role in {task, background} by orchestrator/src/orchestrator/verify.py::_with_pytest_numprocesses_str and verify_cmd.py::apply_pytest_numprocesses, never for the merge role. Per-module addopts and type_check_command are re-discovered from the worktree on every verify (orchestrator.config::_discover_module_configs; hot-reload PRD decision 7 excludes module configs), so a committed addopts edit takes effect on the next verify of a tree containing it, with no reload or restart.

(3) Git facts relevant to the rename gates: - An explicit -M overrides diff.renames=copies, so `git diff -M --name-status` never emits C lines. - With diff.renames=false, `git show -m` reports D/A, but -M still reports R. - `git ls-tree HEAD --` lists the repo root identically for '.', './', 'pkg/..' and 'nonexist/..'. - A rename cycle (x→a→b→a) that _resolve_renamed_plan_path's `seen` guard can see is reachable only through merge history. `git log --diff-filter=D -1 --

` follows the TREESAME parent, so different branches can supply a→b and b→a. In linear history the guard cannot be reached.

Task 'reify-audit: jcodemunch-unreachable hard-fails the WHOLE sweep (exit 125), killing P2/P5' completed. WHAT'S WRONG: The recent P1-jcodemunch wiring (task 4101/4107) made the default audit sweep depend on a live jcodemunch connection. `needs_jcodemunch` (crates/reify-audit/src/bin/reify-audit.rs:412-417) returns true for the no-pattern default sweep and for `--pattern P1`/`--pattern PDEAD` (`args.pattern.is_none_or(|p| p=="P1"||p=="PDEAD")`). In main() (reify-audit.rs:500-519), when that is true and `--no-jcodemunch` is not passed, `RealJCodemunchOps::new` opens an MCP handshake and ANY failure returns `ERROR_EXIT` (125) BEFORE the detector dispatch at :542-571. Net effect: when jcodemunch-serve is down — the documented common case (PyPI quarantine #308; jcodemunch-mcp is NOT in reify .mcp.json per project memory) — a bare `/audit` default sweep dies at exit 125 and ALSO loses P2 (consumer-stub) and P5 (phantom-done), which do not use jcodemunch at all. Previously P1 was inert (NoopJCodemunchOps) so the sweep always ran. The /audit skill (.claude/skills/audit/) documents only P1/P2/P5 and contains ZERO references to the `--no-jcodemunch` escape hatch or to provisioning jcodemunch, so the production consumer will routinely fail.

SUGGESTED APPROACH: Make the default/P1 sweep fail-soft on an unreachable optional substrate: on a non-pre-done sweep, if `RealJCodemunchOps::new` errors, fall back to `NoopJCodemunchOps` with a `tracing::warn!`/stderr breadcrumb and continue so P2/P5 still run (P1 degrades to zero findings, mirroring the existing corpus-overflow-blind handling). Reserve exit-125 for genuine arg misconfiguration, not a down substrate. (Alternatively/additionally: teach the /audit skill to pass `--no-jcodemunch` by default and branch on exit==125; but fail-soft in the binary is the robust fix.)

SECONDARY (same crate, minor): RealJCodemunchOps::get_changed_symbols suppression enrichment at jcodemunch_client.rs:919-923 does `std::fs::read_to_string(&path).unwrap_or_default()`, silently swallowing a file-read error into empty lines so `#[allow(dead_code)]`/`#[cfg(test)]`/`// G-allow:` markers are lost and the symbol can be FALSELY flagged as a P1 orphan. When planning a reify-audit detector task (crates/reify-audit/src/p*.rs), do NOT add every file in the detector's SCAN scope to the plan's `files` list. The scan scope (files the detector lints) is broader than the EDIT scope (files the task modifies). A scoped source file only needs editing if the detector would actually flag it AND it's a legitimate KEEP site needing an allowlist comment. Example: task #4650's PDSSENTINEL detector scopes {entity,functions,traits,expr,conformance/*}.rs, but traits.rs needed no edit because its dimensionless_scalar() sites (language defaults at far line distances) fall outside the detector's WINDOW=16 of any UnresolvedType error-push. Over-declaring scan-scope files in `files` triggers phantom-done narrowing flags at the pre-merge gate.

reify-audit design gotcha — a fail-safe's SAFE DIRECTION inverts when a read-only detector is reused as a blocking gate. Every git seam in crates/reify-audit fail-safes to false/empty on error (path_tracked_on, is_ancestor, diff_*). In the periodic P5 sweep that converges on "no finding" — safe. On the `--pre-done` hook path (reify-audit --task N --pre-done, fired by fused-memory task_interceptor.py step "2d" inside the per-project write lock, 30 s cap) the IDENTICAL defaults converge on a High that REFUSES the done-transition, so an infra hiccup becomes indistinguishable from a genuine phantom-done and wedges the pipeline. Task 6345's fix: before emitting a refusal, prove the evidence was actually gathered — a one-fork probe that main resolves at all (`git merge-base --is-ancestor main main`, run only AFTER something is already absent so the healthy path pays nothing), plus a truncation flag on the sibling-scan cap. Either downgrades the refusal to an advisory Low (exit 0) carrying its reason, so it stays visible but cannot block. Rule of thumb: when reusing a detector as a gate, re-derive which direction each fail-safe points — and never let "we failed to look" read as "we looked and found nothing wrong".

In reify's two-mode audit scripts (scripts/task-branch-contamination-sweep.sh, scripts/warm-lane-degenerate-ref-check.sh), fleet/--audit mode pre-filters candidates against the non-terminal task map BEFORE calling the per-target measurement function, while single-target/--task mode calls it directly. Degradation tests (unreadable store, wrong --tag, terminal id) written only against fleet mode therefore pass VACUOUSLY — the pre-filter emits no row at all, so the untested single-target path can fail OPEN and report a positively benign verdict on a contaminated branch. When testing these scripts, cover both modes' degradation paths, and assert a good-store positive control on the SAME fixture first so the degraded assertions cannot pass against a fixture that was benign anyway.

solar_challenge test-fixture gotcha for project_multi_year battery SOH (measured 2026-10-01, task 271). The seed forward-march snapshots cumulative battery throughput BEFORE each node and accumulates it AFTER, so SOH lags one seed. With seeds (0, 12, 24) the age-12 node sees zero throughput, and only age 24 sees discharge × 12 years (trapezoid over 0→12). compute_soh = clamp(1 − calendar_fade − cycle_fade, soh_floor). With calendar_fade_rate_per_year=0.02, year 24 is already at the 0.60 floor, which hides any throughput difference: 800 vs 6.6 kWh/yr both gave 0.76 at year 12 and 0.6 at year 24. To make discharge visible in a test, use a low calendar fade (0.005/yr with cycle fade 0.0002/EFC and 800 kWh/yr on a 10 kWh battery gives 0.76 at year 24), and assert the final SOH is above soh_floor as a precondition.

solar_challenge test-design gotcha (task 295 amendment, mutation-verified 2026-10-02). battery.compute_soh sees throughput only as EFC = T / (2 × usable_kwh). So a multi-home project_multi_year SOH test that gives each home a discharge proportional to its usable capacity gives every home the same SOH. Then the fleet mean equals each home's SOH, and mutants that read only home 0, swap homes, or average the wrong home all stay green. Give the homes different kWh-per-usable-kWh discharge ratios, and assert as a premise that their SOHs differ. The canonical case is tests/unit/test_finance_projection.py::TestBatterySohCountsThroughputToEachAge::test_each_home_counts_its_own_discharge_and_battery_soh_is_their_mean: a 10 kWh battery at 800 kWh/yr and a 5 kWh battery at 200 kWh/yr, keyed on capacity_kwh. It caught all 5 per-home mutants, which the one-home tests missed.

Task 'Battery SOH and nominal usable capacity have several copies: project_multi_year's _simulate_age recomputes the SOH _aged_homes injected, and capacity × (max_soc − min_soc) is written out three times' completed. Landed in commit 2bb0402ff9c3f9de988c512e1260d90e13ca894b.

Key technical insight from W2 design: a combined calendar+cycle battery SOH model is consistent with hybrid representative-age sampling (which skips intervening years) via a FORWARD-MARCH. Cycle-fade needs cumulative throughput from year 0→N, which is the integral of per-year throughput — and per-year throughput is an already-existing aggregate (SummaryStatistics.total_battery_discharge_kwh). So the projection visits age nodes in ascending order, accumulating throughput into the next node's SOH. This means NO dispatch-loop instrumentation is needed for cycle counting, resolving the usual tension that cycle-fade presupposes per-year simulation.

solar_challenge code fact (measured 2026-10-01 on main ce0d099, for task 323's nominal-usable-capacity SPOT refactor): Battery.__init__'s nominal_usable (battery.py:264) is capacity_kwh × (resolved_max_soc − resolved_min_soc). Those are the constructor-resolved SOC limits, which a caller can override per Battery; they are not necessarily BatteryConfig.max/min_soc_fraction. It is passed to compute_soh with cumulative_throughput_kwh=0.0, and compute_soh's EFC term is 0 whenever throughput is 0, so a BatteryConfig-level nominal-usable property at that site leaves the SOH result unchanged even when the limits are overridden. The finance.py sites (_aged_homes, project_multi_year's _simulate_age) read the config fields directly.

Completed: The real alert path can alter the dark-factory escalation project's environment, and the test that exercises i (src/solar_challenge_platform/ci/cadence_alert.py::EscalationCli.submit_argv)
Description: The real alert path can alter the dark-factory escalation project's environment, and the test that exercises it deliberately does not. submit_argv (cadence_alert.py:239-262) runs `uv run --project /home/leo/src/dark-factory/escalation escalation submit ...` without --no-sync, --frozen or --locked. The test covers a different invocation from the one production uses.

Proposal: Add --no-sync (or --frozen) to submit_argv, or UV_NO_SYNC=1 to the alert service's Environment. Have the slow test run the exact argv and env the unit uses. Mechanical.
