candidates.content: The dark-factory plan-revalidation trigger (TaskWorkflow._plan(), orchestrator/src/orchestrator/workflow.py:4289-4762) decides revalidate-vs-architect purely on: an existing plan + `_session_id` + `_old_plan_base` + files changed on `main` between the plan base and current main overlapped with plan.files (:4359-4364). THE TASK TEXT PLAYS NO PART. Worse, "Lever B" short-circuits even that pass when `not overlap AND _can_skip_revalidation(plan)` (:4377-4388), removing the last opportunity to re-read the task record. `_can_skip_revalidation` (:4764-4830) already receives the plan and can read self.task, and has four conjuncts none of which touch task text — it is the natural seam for a fifth. Note `updated_at` is NOT a usable trigger: sqlite_task_backend.py:2761-2762 "updated_at always advances, even on a no-op write". `candidate_key` is also blind — recomputed only if title or metadata changed (:2719-2721), so a description-only amendment leaves it byte-identical.

Orchestrator plan reuse after a task-description rewrite (measured on reify task 7874, 2026-10-05):
- Nothing compares a saved plan.json against the task's description, candidate_key or a hash. `_plan()` (workflow.py ~:4839-4941) decides only from what is on disk.
- Revalidation can SKIP the architect entirely when no changed file overlaps the plan and the plan is under 24h old (max_revalidation_age_hours=24, config.py ~:3772). It never looks at the description.
- So rewriting a task's scope does NOT by itself invalidate an existing plan. The only lever is the lane's `<worktree_base>/.task-meta/<_lane-N>/plan.json`.
- Plans are LANE-keyed (warm_lane_pool). A pool "reclaim-on-exhaustion" steals a non-dispatched task's lane, and the recycle (_reset_warm_lane / _clear_foreign_meta_root, git_ops.py) deletes that lane's .task-meta, destroying the victim's plan. That happened to 7874 (_lane-36 stolen for 8036 at 08:10 local).
- The task's `details` field goes into the fresh architect prompt verbatim (_format_task, briefing.py ~:1444). A HOLD note describing an old plan will anchor the new architect, so rewrite it when rescoping.
- metadata.files seeds the scheduler's first-dispatch lock set.
Related: DF task 3157 (lane-keyed plan loss).

Architect plan-revalidation, FOURTH subcase — THE ARCHITECT MAY NOT BE INVOKED AT ALL (Lever B revalidation skip). Stamped peer to canonical f7021be8 under topic `architect_plan_revalidation`.

The existing three subcases (plan_json_gitignore_wipe, lost_plan_reconstruction, task_text_rewrite_invisible_to_revalidation) all share an assumption: the architect IS invoked and simply cannot see what changed, so the prescribed fix is "before confirming a plan, re-read the live task via get_task and diff description/metadata.files". This subcase DEFEATS that fix, because there is no confirming agent to run it.

MECHANISM (read off workflow.py::_plan at main 49e9b5c1e6). _plan picks its branch from the plan file: completion-pass needs `not _finalized_at and not _session_id`; REVALIDATION needs `steps and _session_id and _old_plan_base`; fresh planning is reached ONLY when `existing_plan` is falsy, i.e. when plan.json is ABSENT. Inside the revalidation branch sits Lever B, which stamps `_revalidated_at`, bumps base_commit and returns PLANNED **without invoking the architect** when `revalidation_skip_enabled and not overlap and _can_skip_revalidation(plan)`. Defaults: `revalidation_skip_enabled=True`, `max_revalidation_age_hours=24.0` (config.py). `_can_skip_revalidation` additionally requires `_schema_version == PLAN_SCHEMA_VERSION` and every plan file to exist in the worktree.

WHY THIS COMPOUNDS THE OTHER SUBCASES. `overlap` is computed from files changed on main — the very signal the other three subcases establish is blind to task-record rewrites. So a task whose description/metadata was corrected while its plan sat idle has overlap=0 by construction, which is exactly the condition that ENABLES the skip. The blind spot doesn't just mislead the architect; past 0 overlap it removes them.

MEASURED on task 4762 (2026-08-28, from task 4822): its finalized 24-step plan had all Lever B conditions true simultaneously — skip enabled, schema 1==1, all 8 plan files present, age 15.06h under the 24h bound, and 0 commits on main touching any of the 8 files. A dispatch would have handed an implementer a plan whose step 2 encoded a measurably false requirement, with the corrected task description read by nobody.

PRACTICE. (1) Correcting a task's description/metadata is NOT sufficient to retire a stale finalized plan — the correction is only read if an architect runs, and Lever B may mean none does. To force re-planning you must make plan.json ABSENT (archive it aside and remove it); absence is the only thing that selects the fresh-planning branch. (2) The 24h age bound is a timer, not a fix: past it you get a full architect revalidation, but build_revalidation_prompt still hands over the superseded plan to "confirm, update, or recreate", anchoring the architect on the wrong steps. (3) If you cannot remove plan.json (a task lane cannot write a sibling task's .task-meta/ — see the scope_violation escalation pattern), keep the task frozen behind dependency edges until someone can, and say so in the record.

ACCRETION: append here or add a stamped peer under topic `architect_plan_revalidation` — do not write a new unstamped entry.

Architect plan-revalidation gotcha: a requeued task's plan can be invalidated WITHOUT any file on main changing. The revalidation prompt only lists files changed on main, so a plan whose source files are all untouched looks trivially confirmable — but a PRD-decomposition session can reassign a task's scope purely in Taskmaster metadata. Always re-read the task's OWN live record with get_task before confirm_plan() and check metadata.files (may have been emptied), metadata.x_amended_by, and metadata.files_correction_note. Task 3423 hit this: all 6 of its plan files were untouched on main, but a state-graph PRD (D11) had moved the strand-fix scope to tasks 3536/3542, emptied 3423's metadata.files, and adjudicated a DIFFERENT design — so confirming the plan would have implemented a rejected design on files the task no longer owned, colliding with pending high-priority task 3536.

PROCEDURE for plan revalidation after a requeue (architect role): lead with `git diff --quiet <old_plan_base>..HEAD -- <each planned file>` per file, NOT with re-reading the files. A file that reports IDENTICAL gives you a stronger guarantee than any re-read: every line pin your plan carries for it is provably still exact, and you can skip re-verifying those premises entirely. Measured on task 4890's revalidation — 5 of 6 planned files were byte-identical, collapsing the whole revalidation to one changed file.

For the file(s) that DID change, check `--stat` for the deletion count first. A purely-additive diff (+N/-0) means nothing you planned against was edited; only line numbers moved, so the fix is re-pinning, not re-planning. Task 5137 added +518/-0 to tests/scripts/test_spawn_claude.py and shifted every symbol below its insertion points by ~+145 — the function body task 4890 planned to promote was character-for-character unchanged.

DESIGN LESSON worth carrying into planning, not just revalidation: prefer refactors whose correctness is independent of call-site COUNT. Task 4890's step to de-duplicate a helper rebinds the shared function under the SAME module-local name via an import alias (`from shared_mod import f as _f`), so every existing call site keeps working untouched. Between the plan being written and revalidated, that helper's call sites grew from ~10 to 22 — the step needed no change. Had the plan instead renamed call sites, the requeue would have silently invalidated it. When a plan step must quote a count of anything in a file, treat that count as a revalidation hazard and prefer a formulation that does not depend on it.

Also re-check, cheaply, the things a plan reasons about but does not list in `files`: conftest.py bindings, the module's orchestrator.yaml `test_command`, and any `.task-meta/<id>/reviews-*/` artifact the analysis cites. These are not in the plan's file list, so the revalidation briefing's "overlapping files" section will not flag them.

CANONICAL — architect plan-revalidation, third subcase: TASK-TEXT REWRITE INVISIBLE TO THE REVALIDATION PROMPT.

TRIGGER-TAGGED: this subcase fires when the TASK ITSELF was rewritten while the plan sat idle — not when files moved. It sits alongside the other two subcases under this topic (plan_json_gitignore_wipe, lost_plan_reconstruction).

THE BLIND SPOT: the architect's revalidation prompt shows only "Files Changed on Main". It NEVER shows that the task's own description or metadata was rewritten. So a plan can be invalidated with ZERO files changing on main, and the prompt renders that as "nothing changed" — the plan looks safe to confirm when its scope has moved underneath it.

TWO OBSERVED TRIGGERING MECHANISMS, same blind spot:
  - CURATOR `combine` (metadata.curator_action='combine') silently RESCOPED the description and metadata — task 3568.
  - PRD DECOMPOSE reassigned scope purely via Taskmaster metadata, touching no file — task 3423.

THE FIX, same for both: before confirming a plan, ALWAYS re-read the LIVE task via get_task and diff its description and metadata.files against what the plan was built for. Do not rely on the revalidation prompt's file list — it cannot see this class of change by construction.

ACCRETION: append here or add a stamped peer under topic `architect_plan_revalidation` — do not write a new unstamped entry.

What a re-dispatched task with a complete plan actually runs (traced 2026-09-11; orchestrator workflow._drive). Order: setup, _recover_if_already_merged, _resume_merge_retry_if_pending, the SIMPLE-TASK check, _plan(), then execute/verify/review.
- Simple-task check runs FIRST and ignores any existing plan. It fires when simple_task_enabled is on, the task has complexity='simple', no auto_eval_redo, no force_full_path and is not simple_saturated. If that agent falls through, plan.json and plan.lock are deleted and a fresh architect plans from scratch.
- Revalidation skip (Lever B) needs ALL of: no overlap between the plan's files and files changed on main since the plan base, plan age <= max_revalidation_age_hours (default 24h), matching schema, all plan files present. It is the only place besides simple-task that stamps metadata.optimistic_path ('revalidation_skip'), the auto-eval trigger.
- EXECUTE is skipped when no steps are pending. VERIFY is skipped only with a green checkpoint at the current HEAD.
- The review cache is keyed by committed TREE hash plus reviewer-config fingerprint, so any merge of main forces a full re-review.
- Worktree reuse (GitOps.create_worktree) runs rebase_preserving_task_commits, i.e. a plain `git rebase main`. That linearizes merge commits; on a conflict it aborts and carries on at the old HEAD, which is only a log warning.

Architect plan-revalidation gotcha: the revalidation prompt shows only "Files Changed on Main", never that the TASK DESCRIPTION itself was rewritten. A curator `combine` action (metadata.curator_action='combine', with a `combined_at` timestamp) silently rescopes a task after its plan was written — task 3568 was combined on 2026-08-06 and flipped from a "seed the episode node" fix to a "guard the uuid= param" fix, invalidating the stored plan on grounds the changed-files list did not reveal. When revalidating, always re-read the live task via get_task and diff the description/metadata.files against the plan, not just the overlapping source files.

Bug — architect "no plan.json produced" loop bypasses the revalidation mechanism by design. Order in workflow._plan(): architect invoked → no-plan / no-steps / invalid-prereqs / no-files checks (workflow.py:997, 1011, 1023, 1034, 1056) → `stamp_plan_provenance` (workflow.py:1038). When the architect returns subtype=success but writes no valid plan (commonly: it called `escalate_blocker`/`terminate_cleanly` for a task needing human input — operator action, design-pick, missing prerequisite), control returns through `_handle_no_plan_failure` BEFORE stamping. Any plan.json the architect wrote sits unstamped; on the next pass workflow.py:897-900 unlinks it. Net effect: revalidation can never engage for these tasks; every requeue runs full Opus planning. The cycle counter at workflow.py:1230,1248 is keyed on `current_main_sha` — when main advances between attempts (busy days), the counter resets to 1 and the ≥2-failure escalation never fires. Task 917 alone consumed 16 architect invocations (~$13 of Opus) on a task its own description states needs human design pick A/B/C/D. Same pattern: tasks 948 (operator restart task), 1043 (cancelled-then-reopened guardrails task).

CORRECTION to the belief that resolve_issue's 'restart' is a plan-eraser (dark_factory, verified 2026-09-03 against main ad616c0265). The disposition string 'restart_from_scratch' is only a LABEL: repo-wide it appears solely at escalation/src/escalation/action_effects.py::WORKFLOW_RESTART and in resolve_issue's own docstring table. NOTHING in the orchestrator consumes it, and nothing deletes plan.json on the strength of it. All 'restart' actually does is set the task status to pending and stamp the disposition — so where metadata.merge_retry_pending is unset, a plain set_task_status(id, 'pending') reaches the identical end state.

What actually decides whether a re-pended task gets a re-plan is orchestrator/src/orchestrator/workflow.py::TaskWorkflow._plan, which branches on plan.json's provenance: steps present but no _finalized_at and no _session_id -> COMPLETION PASS (architect finishes the partial); _session_id present AND _old_plan_base set (read from .task-meta/<id>/metadata.json's base_commit via artifacts.py::read_base_commit) -> REVALIDATION; otherwise -> FRESH PLANNING.

THE REAL HAZARD IS LEVER B, not restart. workflow.py::_can_skip_revalidation plus _apply_revalidation_skip can skip the architect ENTIRELY when no file changed on main overlaps the plan's files — stamping _revalidated_at and returning PLANNED — which would send a stale plan straight to an implementer. Its guards are: _schema_version must match PLAN_SCHEMA_VERSION; every plan file must still exist in the worktree; plan provenance age must be within config.max_revalidation_age_hours (default 24.0, no dark_factory override); and it declines if the prior block was at REVIEW. So an OLD plan always gets a genuine architect revalidation, and a RECENT one on untouched files may silently get none.

Lever B (revalidation skip) pre-flight checks gate the optimistic short-circuit in workflow._plan(): (1) prior plan has provenance (_session_id) and old base_commit, (2) overlap of plan.files with diff main has gained == 0, (3) revalidation_skip_enabled config flag, (4) plan._schema_version == current PLAN_SCHEMA_VERSION, (5) every plan.files entry exists on disk in worktree, (6) plan age <= max_revalidation_age_hours (default 24h), (7) prior block was NOT at REVIEW phase (read from task.metadata.last_block_phase/last_block_outcome). Any failure falls through to the architect-driven revalidation path. Side-effects on success: artifacts.bump_revalidation_stamp(session_id, base_commit=current_main) writes _revalidated_at + _revalidated_by_session and updates metadata.json:base_commit; phase_skipped event emitted; metadata.optimistic_path='revalidation_skip' stamped for auto-eval.

DEFECT, measured 2026-09-15 on task 5027 (filed as task 5516, high): `resolve_issue(action='restart')` CANNOT force a fresh architect plan, and fails silently when you try. `restart` only flips the task blocked→pending — it is not a plan-eraser and nothing deletes plan.json (fused-memory procedural_knowledge 5f185347). On the re-dispatch, `orchestrator/src/orchestrator/workflow.py::TaskWorkflow._apply_revalidation_skip` (~:5120-5191, "Lever B") compares the finalized plan's files against what changed on main and, on ZERO overlap, short-circuits straight to PLANNED without invoking the architect at all. When the block reason is "plan files not touched", that overlap is empty BY CONSTRUCTION — no commit touched those files, which is the entire complaint — so Lever B fires every time and the stale plan is reused. Live trace: watcher resolved with restart + a RE-PLAN DIRECTIVE in task details at 00:1xZ; 01:15:49Z `phase_skipped reason='revalidation_skipped_no_overlap' plan_session_id=5027-8d624b6c`; then `no_pending_steps`; then `durable_verified_green`; the one architect run that did fire (01:33Z) died `error_max_budget_usd` after 1 turn; 01:33:26Z the identical block. Eighteen minutes, nothing re-planned, and the directive appended to `details` was read by nobody because no agent was invoked. WORKAROUND that worked: archive plan.json aside (rename, never delete) so `_plan()` takes the fresh-planning branch. Adjacent pending task 4031 gates the same Lever B skip on a task-text fingerprint — it would NOT have fired here (the trigger is file overlap, not text), but whoever takes 5516 should read 4031 first since they touch the same function.

CANONICAL — architect plan-revalidation after requeue: plan.json gitignore-wipe on a 0/0-diverged branch (recreate, don't confirm). `.task/plan.json` was removed from git tracking (commit 95347ac64c "fix: remove .task/plan.json from git tracking") and is now untracked/gitignored — so a requeue rebase wipes any locally-created plan.json from the worktree (look for "chore: save WIP before requeue rebase" commits), even when branch task/<id> is 0/0 diverged from main. The revalidation prompt STILL shows "Your Previous Plan" JSON and offers confirm_plan() as option (a), but plan-tools' confirm_plan()/update_plan_metadata operate on the on-disk file and have nothing to act on when it is absent. Always `ls .task/plan.json` at the START of a revalidation session before choosing confirm vs recreate. When absent: re-verify all premises against current main and RECREATE via create_plan()+add_plan_step()+confirm_plan() — even when the plan content is unchanged and fully re-validated. Distinct sibling sub-cases: branch carries committed TDD steps → lost-plan reconstruction canonical; prior commits already merged to main → report_task_already_done (bc9388ab-45a7-4642-9eab-a913b3d54085).

Substrate facts verified on main @ 8eeb862fa5 (2026-08-12) while G3-checking plans/task-amendment-delivery-prd.md, several of which correct stale anchors circulating in older task text. `TaskWorkflow._reconcile_done_step_commits` is at orchestrator/src/orchestrator/workflow.py:8440 with EXACTLY ONE call site at :7976 (inside the implement loop) — task 3157's 2026-08-05 addendum cites :7915 and call site :7451, which are STALE; trust 8440/7976. `_can_skip_revalidation` workflow.py:4764 (four conjuncts, reads no task text). `_apply_revalidation_skip` :4832. `BriefingAssembler._format_task` agents/briefing.py:1467. `stamp_plan_provenance` artifacts.py:978 with 5 production callers (workflow.py :2637, :4705, :5030, :7652, :8052); `bump_revalidation_stamp` artifacts.py:944. `GitOps.find_equivalent_commit` git_ops.py:8855. The async git subprocess runner is MODULE-LEVEL `_run` at git_ops.py:1726 (wrapping asyncio.create_subprocess_exec) — there is no `GitOps._run` method, so "git_ops._run" means the module function. `_check_plan_files_touched_in_branch` lives in merge_gates.py:1333 (NOT workflow.py) and is called from workflow.py:10090 with the `_try_narrow_plan` remedy-and-recheck at :10108. `UpdateTaskResult` fused-memory/src/fused_memory/backends/task_backend_types.py:18. `should_reembed` task_interceptor.py:4467. Combine execution predicate task_interceptor.py:2144; selection-side `combine_eligible=(status == 'pending')` task_curator.py:2793. `_normalize_content_description` flag_dedup.py:1375. Events `EventType.plan_revalidated` event_store.py:334 and `EventType.phase_skipped` :363, with `reason='revalidation_skipped_no_overlap'` emitted at workflow.py:4894 and `_stamp_optimistic_path('revalidation_skip')` at :4886. `revalidation_skip_enabled` config.py:3237 (RED tier today). `plan_tools._create_plan` writes `'steps': []` at plan_tools.py:997.

Architect plan-REVALIDATION ordering gotcha (hit 2026-08-16 on task 4006): plan steps execute in the order added and `add_plan_step` only APPENDS — there is no positional insert. So when revalidation finds the task gained a NEW requirement (e.g. a ruling amended into the description after `_finalized_at`), do NOT append a new test/impl pair: it lands after the plan's final step, which is typically the artifact-regeneration/full-verify step, so the committed output ships without the thing the new requirement asked for. Instead fold the requirement into the existing step(s) whose position is already correct, using `replace_plan_step` (it preserves position, status and commit). Check the task's Details for dated amendments vs plan.json's `_finalized_at` — a requirement added in between is invisible to a plan that otherwise still validates cleanly.

Architect plan-revalidation gotcha, the SIBLING-side complement to the "re-read your own task record" entry (33d219a4): a plan can be invalidated by another OPEN task being rescoped, with zero signal in git and zero change to your own task record. Two compounding blind spots, both hit on task 4590 (2026-08-28).

(1) THE REVALIDATION BRIEFING ONLY SHOWS FILES CHANGED ON MAIN. Task 4590's plan (authored 08-22) centered on a new sweep script. On 08-24 an L2 rescope (esc-4545-2) widened sibling task 4545 to include a sweep with the same corpus, same tasks.db read, and same modelling on the same reference script — making the planned deliverable a straight duplicate. Nothing on main changed to say so. Worse, task 4590's OWN description contained a disambiguation paragraph ("4545 is scoped to two descriptors plus an authoring-time dry-run, not this") that was written 08-21 and silently went stale — a task description's own claim about a sibling has a timestamp and expires.

(2) AN IMPLEMENTED-BUT-UNMERGED SIBLING IS INVISIBLE TO `git ls-files`. 4545's script did not exist on main, so every git check said "free to build it". The tell was indirect: two agent-followup tasks (4782, 4731) filed "while implementing 4545" cited that file's INTERNALS concretely — a specific helper at a line number, a named function, a CLI flag, a COVERAGE line — and one said "REPRODUCE ... after 4545 lands". Follow-up tasks quoting internals of a file absent from main are strong evidence the file exists in an unmerged worktree.

PRACTICE when revalidating (and when first planning anything that adds a file to a shared family like scripts/audit_*.py): query the task store for NON-TERMINAL tasks whose metadata.files intersect your planned files, and read the descriptions of any whose title is topically adjacent — not just your own record. On 4590 this surfaced three collisions the git-diff view could not: 4545 (duplicate deliverable + owns a sidecar in its metadata.files), 4782 (declared 3 of the plan's 7 files for the same shape of consolidation refactor), and 4628 (fixing at SOURCE the very defect class the plan proposed to build a standing detector for). The correct outcome was to narrow the task to its literal ask, not to build the script.

GENERALIZATION: before adding a new member to an established script/module family, check whether an in-flight task already owns that family. The cost of missing it is not a merge conflict — it is landing a duplicate implementation that a consolidation task then has to delete.

PLAN REVALIDATION (architect role): when a requeued task's plan is revalidated after main moved, expect the drift to be almost entirely in LINE PINS, not logic — and prefer create_plan (recreate) over replace_plan_step (patch).

MEASURED, task 4932 at HEAD adbc2d6636 vs. the plan's base 09e589e0a1. Four "overlapping" files were flagged. Every semantic premise held; the churn was orthogonal (server/tools.py +152 was confined to add_memory's dup-guard widening, task 3430; config/schema.py +74 and config/config.yaml +9 were llm.max_tokens COMMENTS, task 3864; tests/_fm_helpers.py +385 was httpx-leak tracking). But essentially every line pin in the plan had moved: tools.py shifted every seam by +1..+65 (_claim_task_statuses 1744->1758, update_memory 4816->4877, the four entity tools ~+59), graphiti_client.py's ensure_entity_node 3265->3305, canonical_labels.py's parse_node_name 278->346.

WHY RECREATE, NOT PATCH. plan-tools exposes replace_plan_step but NO replace_design_decision and NO replace_reuse_item — those are add-only. A plan whose stale pins live in design_decisions/reuse (the immutable half) cannot be corrected in place at all. Patching only the steps leaves the implementer reading correct steps beside decisions that point at wrong lines in a 9000+ line file. Recreating is safe whenever no step is status=done (a requeued-for-locks task typically has none — check first; the instructions forbid removing/replacing done steps).

WRITE PLANS IN `module.py::symbol` FORM FROM THE START. dark-factory's CLAUDE.md already mandates this for code comments/docstrings; it applies with more force to a plan, which is read once, later, by a different agent. Keep line numbers only as explicitly-disposable "currently ~:N" hints. This makes a future revalidation nearly free.

VERIFY BY EXECUTION WHERE CHEAP. canonical_labels.py had gained 87 lines; rather than reading the diff and reasoning, running parse_node_name over the plan's twelve guard-3 cases classified all of them in one shot and turned "assumed" assertions into measured ones. It also surfaced the one real semantic change (digit captures narrowed \d -> [0-9], so non-ASCII Unicode digits now yield None) — which became a free extra test assertion rather than a surprise for the implementer.

RE-READING BEATS TRUSTING YOUR OWN PRIOR PLAN. Three factual refinements only surfaced on the second pass: _resolve_or_create_entity has a FOURTH defensive branch the prior plan never mentioned; _claim_ticket_rows does not itself hold the UNRESOLVABLE sentinel (the function encodes key->None vs. absent, and the sentinel is applied at its CALL SITE); and of four sibling entity MCP tools only reassign_edge calls _known_project_gate. Each would have read as a plan/code mismatch to the implementer.

PLAN REVALIDATION GOTCHA (dark-factory, measured task 4201, 2026-08-29): the requeue briefing's "Files Changed on Main / Overlapping with your plan" list is computed against `plan.files` ONLY. `plan.files` is scoped to what the task WRITES (it drives concurrency locks and the phantom-done gate), but a plan's correctness usually also rests on files it merely CITES in its analysis, design_decisions and step rationale — and those get zero overlap coverage. So a plan can be reported as overlapping in one harmless file while a load-bearing citation silently rots.

MEASURED. Task 4201's plan declared 2 files (task_curator.py, test_task_curator.py). The briefing flagged only test_task_curator.py, whose real diff was 13 deleted lines in an unrelated class — cosmetic, a −14 line shift in the region the plan pinned. The file that actually mattered was task_interceptor.py, which is NOT in plan.files (the task never writes it) and so was buried among "518 more" other changes: it had grown ~498 lines, moving `TaskInterceptor._get_curator` 1380→1531 and `_curator_lock` 2386→2773. A plan step instructed the implementer to write a NEW docstring citing both by their old line numbers. Unrevalidated, that ships a docstring stale on the day it lands — the same defect task 4091's amendment #4 had to fix by hand.

PRACTICE. On revalidation, do not stop at the briefing's overlap list. Run `git diff <plan_HEAD>..HEAD --stat -- <every file the plan reasons about>`, where that set = plan.files ∪ every file cited anywhere in the plan text. Three outcomes, and only the third needs work: absent from the stat output = byte-identical, premises hold with no re-reading; present with a small diff = read the diff, then re-pin; present with a large diff = re-verify the CLAIM at its new location, not just the line number. The claim usually survives — here "one memoized curator shared across projects vs. a per-project lock" still held verbatim at the new lines — but confirm it by reading rather than assuming, because a moved symbol is also the shape a refactor takes.

SECOND-ORDER FIX, not just a re-pin: when a revalidation catches a bare line pin destined for shipped prose (a docstring or comment the plan tells the implementer to WRITE), convert it to CLAUDE.md's `path/to/module.py::symbol` form rather than updating the number. A pin that went stale in nine days will go stale again before the task merges. Bare pins already IN the tree are tolerated drift and must not be swept (CLAUDE.md, CONTRIBUTING.md §2); this is only about prose your own change introduces.

When revalidating a plan for a task whose description has multiple numbered items, always cross-check the plan title against the task title. Task 1089's prior plan title was narrowed from "Promote Scheduler._dispatch_tool to public Protocol method and fix FakeScheduler stub fidelity" to just "Improve FakeScheduler stub fidelity in test_workflow_e2e.py", and accordingly addressed only item 4-5 of a 5-item task while adding speculative capture infrastructure. Title drift between plan and task is a strong signal that the prior architect collapsed the scope and the plan should be recreated, not confirmed.

The recurring orphan-reaper "plan.files ⊋ metadata.files divergence" L2 escalation has TWO DISTINCT root causes, often conflated: (1) a PERMANENT reconcile gap — workflow.py::_replan (blocking-review path) widens plan.files via the architect's plan rewrite but the post-replan block (_execute_verify_review_loop ~5759-5776) never routes it through the scope-reconcile choke point, so metadata.files stays a durable strict subset; fixed by task 2874 (done, deployed 2026-07-22 01:54Z). Tasks 2505 (steward resume/grant path _set_task_scope) and 2868 (Scheduler.handle_blast_radius_expansion pure-widen persist) cover the other two choke-point callers; _replan was the uncovered third. (2) a TRANSIENT stale-snapshot RACE — the orphan-reaper decides "no active workflow" from a ~650s-old sweep snapshot that races the batch-redispatch tick, flagging a LIVE holder-active task mid-reconciliation-lag; fixed by task 2878 (orphan-reaper should re-check live current_holders before flagging). To distinguish benign-vs-real: check get_scheduler_state().current_holders — if the task is actively holding its metadata.files locks it is holder-live (benign FP), not stranded. A pre-redeploy STRAGGLER (a long-in-progress task that diverged under old code before 2874 deployed) will keep tripping until it completes; only a divergence appearing AFTER a post-fix-deploy _replan would disprove 2874.

content:
The orchestrator's plan-revalidation path (orchestrator/src/orchestrator/workflow.py, the existing-plan branch and _can_skip_revalidation / _apply_revalidation_skip) re-runs the architect only when main has changed files in the saved plan's `files`, the schema version differs, or the plan exceeds max_revalidation_age_hours. Edits to the task's OWN description, details or acceptance are never considered, so a pending task whose text gains scope after planning can dispatch on its stale plan.
2026-10-16 instance: task 6820 gained WORK item 4 while holding a 10-12 6-step plan. To force a re-plan, the watcher moved the real plan file aside. plan.json in the worktree is a symlink to .worktrees/.task-meta/<id>/plan.json; it was renamed to plan.json.stale-pre-item4-20261016, which was safe because there were 0 commits beyond main and nothing live was in the worktree.
Leo asked for a trigger on task-text changes; the curator combined it into task 4031 (Amendment trigger α: task-text fingerprint gating the Lever-B skip, from plans/task-amendment-delivery-prd.md). 4031 has been pending since 2026-08-28 and never dispatched.

candidates.content: Reify compiler root cause for prelude-typed sub member mistyping (#5867): crates/reify-compiler/src/entity.rs:1754 populates scope.sub_member_types via find_template(compiled_templates, ..) — module-local templates ONLY, never the prelude — even though a prelude-inclusive entity_template_registry is built 830 lines earlier in the same function at entity.rs:918-931. For a prelude-typed sub (e.g. `sub tol = DimensionalTolerance(...)`), sub_component_types IS set but sub_member_types is NOT, so scope.rs:399-411 sub_member_is_cross_sub_geometry_or_forward_declared() returns forward_declared=true for EVERY member name, geometry.rs:441-467 misclassifies `self.tol.tolerance_band` as a cross-sub geometry alias, entity.rs:3842 emits a RealizationDecl for the let, and eval's engine_build.rs:9987 mint_symbolic_geometry_handle_for_cell stamps a GeometryHandle over it. Every other prelude-consulting site (check_sub_structure_existence, phase_sub_override_autos, phase_connect_auto_params, member_access_on_structure_like) uses prelude ∪ local; the sub pre-pass at entity.rs:1754 and its mirrors (1617, 1809, 4851) are the only module-only outliers.

Reify compiler (verified 2026-10-05 at main b2abf18f25): the MemberDecl::Sub arm in crates/reify-compiler/src/entity.rs consumes from a specialization body (`sub x : T { … }`) and from keyed entries (`"k" => { … }`) ONLY param assignments (spec_param_overrides / keyed param_overrides) plus a W_SUBBODY_OBJECTIVE_IGNORED scan for minimize/maximize. Every other MemberDecl in sub.body / keyed_members[].overrides — let, constraint (e.g. a false `constraint w > 100mm` still prints 'All constraints satisfied.'), likely connect — is silently dropped. Loud-rejection passes for such members belong in crates/reify-compiler/src/compile_builder/ and should reuse specialization_scope_check::for_each_specialization_member, as sketch_unsupported.rs does, so that body-form, keyed, where-guarded and nested scopes are all covered.

Reify compiler gotcha: SubComponentDecl (crates/reify-compiler/src/types.rs) carries CompiledExprs that two exhaustive template walkers must enumerate by hand. They are compile_builder/entities_phase.rs::for_each_template_root_expr (call-site fn-arg conformance, which emits diagnostics) and reify-eval engine_build.rs::module_binds_selector (a fail-closed selector gate). Neither walker is compiler-checked for completeness, so any new CompiledExpr-bearing field on SubComponentDecl must be added to BOTH, or that carrier silently escapes conformance and the selector gate. Also note that eval applies a sub's ctor args only in engine_eval.rs's Phase-2 sub elaboration (elaborate_child_instance(..., args)); graph.rs stamps child DEFAULTS for single, keyed and collection subs alike.

reify-compiler silent-wrong-type cascade (tasks #5867, #5903): when the Sub pre-pass in entity.rs cannot find a sub's target template, it still inserts `scope.sub_component_types` unconditionally but skips `sub_member_types`. That makes `CompilationScope::sub_member_is_cross_sub_geometry_or_forward_declared` (scope.rs) true via its `forward_declared` disjunct, so `geometry.rs::is_bare_cross_sub_geometry_alias` classifies a reading `let r = self.k.m` as GEOMETRY — emitting a spurious RealizationDecl and typing the cell `Type::Error`, with ZERO diagnostics. Two distinct triggers hit the same cascade: a PRELUDE-typed sub target (#5867) and a LOCAL FORWARD-DECLARED one (#5903, since `compiled_templates` is appended only after each entity compiles). Populating `sub_member_types` drives the disjunct false and fixes it — but you must first ensure `sub_realization_names` is populated too, or genuine cross-sub GEOMETRY reads silently regress the opposite way.

reify compiler: to answer "which template does `sub x : Foo` / `sub x = Foo()` point at?", ALWAYS route through `find_template_with_prelude` (crates/reify-compiler/src/types.rs:939) — module-first, prelude-fallback, UNFILTERED by EntityKind (a sub target may be an occurrence), and suppressing the prelude fallback for names the module declares itself. Do NOT use `CompilationScope::template_registry` for a sub-target question: that map is the `PreludeRegistries::ctor` composition, deliberately `EntityKind::Structure`-FILTERED for `Foo()` constructor lowering only (types.rs:873-887). Mixing them up is the exact asymmetry tasks #5867 / esc-5360-9 fixed. Practical consequence for anyone adding a cross-sub lookup: the entity Sub pre-pass (entity.rs ~2303-2410) already resolves each sub's `child_tmpl` once via the correct resolver and fans it out into sibling side-maps on `CompilationScope` (`sub_structure_traits`, `sub_assoc_fn_keys`, `sub_member_types`, `sub_realization_names`, `sub_match_arm_groups`) — add a new side-map there rather than re-deriving resolution at the consumer.

reify-compiler: every arm of a match-arm decl cluster declares the SAME logical sub name, so the `CompilationScope::sub_*` side-maps populated in the match-arm Sub pre-pass (entity.rs, the `MemberDecl::MatchArmDeclGroup` -> `MemberDecl::Sub` arm) are all keyed on that one name and are LAST-WRITE-WINS across arms — `match_arm_group_arm_member_types` exists precisely because `sub_member_types[group]` retains only the final arm's members. When adding a new side-map there, ask what the map is READ for: last-write-wins is tolerable for maps read to RESOLVE a name (a wrong answer degrades to an "unknown member" diagnostic), but not for a map read to REJECT source, where the last arm's answer becomes a hard error on code that is legal under the selected arm. `sub_port_directions` (task #7175) is the second kind and folds arms to their INTERSECTION via `merge_arm_port_directions`, dropping any port the arms disagree on back to "unresolvable". Note the two Sub pre-pass sites are separate code paths — a map added to the plain-`Sub` pre-pass (~entity.rs:2360) is silently absent for match-arm subs unless it is added to the match-arm pre-pass (~entity.rs:2190) too.

Reify IR: a cross-`sub` field reference in a `.ri` constraint (e.g. `constraint shuttle.stroke >= capstan.band` on an assembly) does NOT compile to a single `ValueRef`. It compiles to `CompiledExprKind::IndexAccess { object: ValueRef(<Assembly>.<sub>), index: Literal(Value::String("<cell>")) }` (crates/reify-ir/src/expr.rs:81). Consequence for anyone writing a Rust gate over compiled constraints: `CompiledExpr::collect_value_refs` reports which SUBS a constraint touches but not which of their CELLS, so it cannot tell one assembly-scoped constraint from another. Re-pair them by walking with `CompiledExpr::walk` (expr.rs:570) and matching that IndexAccess/ValueRef/Literal triple to recover `(entity_path, cell_name)`. Relatedly, the evaluated `ValueMap` carries a contained structure's scalar cells under BOTH spellings — the bare template (`Capstan.band`) and the instance-scoped composition (`CapstanDrive.capstan.band`) — and a DSL constraint resolves against the INSTANCE form, so a test reading the template form is only checking the same number while `sub` constructor overrides remain dropped (task 4147). Worked example: crates/reify-eval/tests/harness_sweep/capstan_groove_e2e.rs (`sub_cell_reads`, `sub_entity`).

In reify-compiler's connect path, a collection or keyed sub used as an endpoint WITHOUT an indexer (`connect vents.outlet -> hub.feed` where `sub vents : List<Vent>`) compiles clean and emits a `connect_compat_vents.outlet_hub.feed` constraint reported Satisfied — over a node that does not exist, since the real instances are `vents[0].outlet`/`vents[1].outlet`. Cause: `endpoint_direction` (crates/reify-compiler/src/connect.rs:294-305) strips the indexer at the first `[` and looks the port up under the bare SUB name in `CompilationScope::sub_port_directions`, which scope.rs:197 populates for collection and non-collection subs alike, so the direction check passes and nothing downstream requires the endpoint to denote one instance. `collection_sub_names` (scope.rs:26) and `keyed_sub_keys` (scope.rs:31-38) already carry what a gate would need — keyed subs have `is_collection == false` and are deliberately absent from the former, so any such gate must consult BOTH. Measured 2026-09-18; follow-up ticket tkt_0RTS2C5PFH8RVAEYB8WJCK398N.

In reify-compiler, `CompilationScope::sub_port_directions` carries a deliberate ABSENCE CONTRACT (scope.rs): a missing sub key OR a missing port key within a present sub means "not resolvable at this point in the compile" — never "no such port", never a default direction. The trap is that the two population sites differ in shape: the plain-`Sub` pre-pass (entity.rs ~2382) SKIPS the insert when the child template does not resolve, while `merge_arm_port_directions` (entity.rs ~5076) is called UNCONDITIONALLY for match-arm cluster subs and leaves an EMPTY-but-PRESENT entry. So for an arm cluster the inner map is an INTERSECTION over arms, and any consumer that iterates it as a complete port list reads a fold as an exhaustive enumeration — which is how task 7376 shipped a false "chain element has no port usable as 'out'" plus a silent wrong port pick. Ask the map only about a NAMED port (present ⇒ authoritative in every arm); never enumerate it to conclude a port is absent.

Measured on reify main 2151ed59c5 (task/5867 lane, zero src changes): the two-level instance-scope chain `Parent { sub m = Mid(); let echo = self.m.relay }` where `Mid { sub k = Kid(); let relay = self.k.off }` yields Parent.echo = Undef, Parent.m.relay = Undef, and Parent.m = StructureInstance{fields:{"relay": Undef}} with ZERO diagnostics — for a plain USER-MODULE sub, not just a prelude-typed one. Template scope is fine (Mid.relay = Scalar). So on main the instance-scope half of any nested-sub member-read acceptance criterion is unreachable regardless of whether the sub's target is prelude- or module-typed; that half is task #5360's territory (eval-side unfold.rs/engine_eval.rs), not a compiler-side typing fix.

Reify has TWO template namespaces that must both be searched when resolving a structure name: the local module's CompiledModule::templates and Engine::prelude (stdlib templates are deliberately NOT merged into CompiledModule::templates — io-export delta / esc-4287-15). A bare module-only lookup is a recurring latent-defect shape: it produced esc-5360-9 on the eval side (fixed by unfold::find_template_in_scope) and #5867 on the compile side. In the compiler the miss is silent-wrong-type rather than not-found: entity.rs's Sub pre-pass inserts scope.sub_component_types unconditionally but scope.sub_member_types only inside `if let Some(child_tmpl) = find_template(...)`, so a miss makes CompilationScope::sub_member_is_cross_sub_geometry_or_forward_declared fire its forward_declared disjunct and the reading let is emitted as a geometry RealizationDecl. Before adding any structure-name lookup, check whether prelude fallback is needed.

Reify compiler/eval prelude-resolution asymmetry is a RECURRING defect class (esc-5360-9 on the eval side, task #5867 on the compile side). Stdlib templates live in `Engine::prelude` and are deliberately NOT merged into `CompiledModule::templates` (io-export delta / esc-4287-15), so any bare `find_template(templates, name)` is MODULE-ONLY and silently misses every stdlib type. Two single-source-of-truth resolvers now exist and every sub-target lookup must route through one of them: `reify_eval::unfold::find_template_in_scope` (eval side) and `reify_compiler::types::find_template_with_prelude` (compile side, pub(crate)). Two gotchas: (1) the compile-side prelude registry passed in must be UNFILTERED by EntityKind — do NOT reuse `entities_phase.rs`'s `prelude_template_registry`, which is EntityKind::Structure-filtered for ctor lowering, because sub targets may be occurrences (`sub o = STLOutput(...)` is a shipped shape); (2) the failure is SILENT, not a diagnostic: a missed lookup leaves `sub_member_types` unpopulated while `sub_component_types` is populated, which is exactly the `forward_declared` disjunct of `scope::sub_member_is_cross_sub_geometry_or_forward_declared`, so a relaying `let x = self.sub.member` lowers to a RealizationDecl and evaluates to `GeometryHandle { kernel_handle: None }` instead of the member's real value. When adding a prelude fallback to one resolver, grep for sibling `find_template(compiled_templates, ...)` call sites and fix ALL of them — the asymmetry (one resolver fixed, its sibling not) is what caused esc-5360-9.

content: reify-compiler gotcha (measured 2026-10-18, lane HEAD baff3ed38b): in a structure's CompilationScope, `sub_component_types` is the complete DECLARED-sub set. The entity.rs Sub pre-pass (plain subs ~2413, match-arm subs ~2243) inserts every sub name BEFORE child-template lookup, so it includes forward-declared children (#7374), trait- or type-param-typed subs, and match-arm cluster names. By contrast, `sub_port_directions` and `sub_declared_member_names` are absent whenever the child is unresolvable. Use `sub_component_types` to tell "no such sub" from "sub whose child is not resolvable here". Before #9323, `connect ghost.outlet -> hub.feed` with no sub `ghost` compiled to a phantom "All constraints satisfied".

candidates.content: solar_challenge_platform test-typing procedure: tests sit outside the src-only mypy gate and already carry mypy errors. So check a test-typing fix against the pre-edit version, and you can get that baseline even after editing, with no stash or checkout (the stash is shared across worktrees): run `git show HEAD:<test file> > /tmp/old.py`, then `uv run --extra dev mypy --shadow-file <test file> /tmp/old.py <test file>`, which type-checks the old text in the file's own place. Task 734 used it to show that tests/validation/test_run.py's old DispatchRun(command_log=tuple(object() ...)) helper was flagged ("Generator has incompatible item type "object"; expected "ControlCommandLog"") and the ControlCommandLog-row version was not.

solar_challenge_platform typing gotcha (verified with mypy --strict and pydantic-settings 2.14 on 2026-10-04, task 512 architect):
- mypy types a BaseSettings subclass's constructor keywords from its field annotations. So `Settings(field="timescale")` against a `(str, Enum)`-typed field is an [arg-type] error, which breaks every src caller that passes a string.
- A `Literal["memory", "timescale"]` field instead accepts literal strings and is still refused at load time by pydantic: errors() gives loc=(field,) and input=<value>, type literal_error.
- mypy narrows such a Literal on `==`, so an assert_never exhaustive branch type-checks, and it flags a typo'd comparison as [comparison-overlap].
- Also: under Python 3.11, f"{member}" on a `(str, Enum)` member prints "ClassName.MEMBER", so messages must use .value.

solar_challenge_platform gotcha, measured 2026-10-10 (task 864 amendment), with pydantic 2.13.4, pydantic-settings 2.14.2 and mypy 2.1.0 --strict. (1) An exception raised inside a Settings field_validator is treated by type. A TypeError passes through unwrapped. A ValueError or AssertionError becomes a ValidationError at the field's loc, which reads as the operator's value being refused. So signal a caller's programming error on a validator path with TypeError, never with assert or ValueError. settings.py::_closed_set_refusal does this when its closed_set argument is not a Literal. (2) A parameter cannot be statically typed as 'takes a Literal'. When a Literal alias is passed as a value, mypy types it as typing._SpecialForm, which a type[str] parameter rejects. typing_extensions.TypeForm needs --enable-incomplete-feature=TypeForm, and TypeForm[str] still accepts plain str. Check at runtime with get_origin(x) is Literal instead. A non-empty get_args(x) check is not enough, because Optional[SomeLiteral] also has non-empty args.

In solar_challenge_platform the mypy gate covers only src/ (verify runs `uv run --extra dev mypy src/solar_challenge_platform`; tests/ are not type-checked). Test modules that follow the `object`-returning-helper + `# type: ignore[...]` convention carry pre-existing mypy errors: tests/billing/test_reducer_reconciliation.py had 13 as of task 182. So `mypy tests/<file>` output is only a regression signal against a baseline taken before your edit, not in absolute terms.

Gotcha (solar_challenge_platform tests, measured at d563dfc): tests are outside the mypy gate, which type-checks src/ only, and test files already carry mypy errors (49 in tests/billing/test_telemetry_register_source.py). mypy reports a multi-line call's arg-type error on the argument's own line, so a `# type: ignore[arg-type]` on the call's opening line is reported as an unused ignore and the error stays. To check that a test edit adds no type errors, compare the error count from `uv run --extra dev mypy <test file>` before and after the edit, rather than expecting a clean run.

solar_challenge_platform gotcha (task 443, 2026-10-10): under `mypy --strict` over src (no pydantic mypy plugin configured), `SomeSettings(_env_file=path)` fails with "Unexpected keyword argument '_env_file'" because mypy uses the __init__ that pydantic's dataclass_transform synthesises from the fields. Without an ignore or a cast, read the file through an explicit source and pass its values: `cls(**DotEnvSettingsSource(cls, env_file=path)())` (see instance/spec.py::InstanceSpec.from_directory). Note that pydantic-settings' dotenv reader calls dotenv_values with interpolation ON, so a `${VAR}` value expands from os.environ.

solar_challenge_platform mypy/review gotcha, measured 2026-10-15 by the task 1160 architect. mypy (strict) checks a **-argument's value type against EVERY parameter it may fill, so a dataclass that mixes datetime and int fields cannot be built from **dict[str, object] (two arg-type errors: expected "datetime", expected "int"). Reviewers BLOCK annotating the dict as dict[str, Any] to silence that (INV-12 blocker 3, type contortion; cast and Callable[..., T] aliases count too). The accepted form is the honest dict[str, object] plus a scoped `# type: ignore[arg-type]  # debt: ticket tkt_<id>` on the one-line call, citing the branch's one follow-up ticket, never the task under review. The INV-12 marker regex (dark-factory shared/governed_exceptions.py: ^#\s*debt:\s*ticket\s+(tkt_...)\s*$) ends the comment at the id, so no prose may follow it. No lint gate runs here (lint_command "true"), so line length does not block the long marker line.

solar_challenge_platform gotcha: pandas (3.0.3) ships no py.typed marker, pandas-stubs is NOT installed, and there is NO [[tool.mypy.overrides]] for it — so ANY module under src/solar_challenge_platform that imports pandas MUST write `import pandas as pd  # type: ignore[import-untyped]` or `uv run --extra dev mypy src/solar_challenge_platform` fails with [import-untyped]. Established convention: simulator/profiles.py:58. With the ignore, pandas resolves to Any so `pd.Series` annotations pass --strict. Note the mypy command checks only src/, so test modules under tests/ that import pandas need no such guard.

Gotcha, measured 2026-10-14 by task 890's amendment pass on branch task/890 tip 0bda660: strict `uv run --extra dev mypy --config-file pyproject.toml tests` exits 1 with 2357 errors in 167 of 411 files, all under tests/ (910 no-untyped-def, 575 no-untyped-call, 298 arg-type, 285 unused-ignore). solar_challenge_platform mypy gotcha, measured 2026-10-09 with pydantic 2.13.4 under `mypy --strict` (task 864): in a Settings field_validator, ValidationInfo.field_name is typed `str | None`. So a validator shared by several Literal-typed fields cannot do `cls.model_fields[info.field_name].annotation` without a narrowing step; mypy reports it as an [index] error. Pass each field's Literal explicitly to a shared helper instead. Declaring `frozenset[SomeLiteral] = frozenset({"a", "b"})` type-checks cleanly.

solar_challenge_platform TDD gotcha (task 599, 2026-10-03): control/contract.py::SetpointCommand is a pydantic v2 model with ConfigDict(frozen=True) only, so extra='ignore' — an unknown kwarg (e.g. a not-yet-added field) is silently DROPPED, and a RED test that merely constructs a command with it passes vacuously; assert on the attribute or on from_registers' returned key instead. Also, str(ValidationError) echoes the whole input dict, so `'field_name' in str(exc)` is vacuously true; check the messages via `' '.join(e['msg'] for e in exc.errors())`.

solar_challenge_platform typing gotcha, measured 2026-10-11 by the task 890 architect with mypy 2.1.0 strict and SQLAlchemy 2.0.51 on scratch probes. A Protocol slice of sa.engine.Connection must declare `dialect` as a read-only `@property`: a plain annotation (`dialect: SomeDialectProtocol`) is a settable member, which mypy checks invariantly, and it rejects the real Connection (whose `dialect: Dialect` is a plain annotation) and simple fakes alike. Keep the test fakes STRUCTURAL: a fake that explicitly subclasses such a Protocol and assigns `self.dialect = ...` fails mypy ('Property "dialect" ... is read-only') and fails at runtime ("AttributeError: property 'dialect' ... has no setter"). mypy 2.1.0 also ignores positional parameter names on non-__call__ protocol members, so a fake's renamed `stmt` parameter still matches.

solar_challenge_platform typing gotcha (measured 2026-10-07, mypy 2.1.0 strict, task 761): mypy rejects a TypeVar-typed parameter with a concrete default, e.g. `factory: DeviceEndFactory[T] = ReferenceDeviceDouble`, reporting 'Incompatible default for parameter' [assignment]. A PEP 696 `TypeVar(..., default=ReferenceDeviceDouble)` from typing_extensions 4.15 does not fix it. What passes strict mypy is two @overload __init__ stubs: the first with `self: Cls[ReferenceDeviceDouble]` and no factory parameter, the second requiring `factory: DeviceEndFactory[T]`. The implementation then types the parameter `DeviceEndFactory[Any] = ReferenceDeviceDouble`. Cls() then infers Cls[ReferenceDeviceDouble], and a subclass `Sub(Cls[PhysicsDeviceEnd])` calling super().__init__(..., factory=PhysicsDeviceEnd) types Sub().device_end as PhysicsDeviceEnd.

mypy in solar_challenge_platform is invoked ONLY as `uv run --extra dev mypy src/solar_challenge_platform` (fixed in orchestrator.yaml type_check_command, CLAUDE.md, README). Root-level modules (e.g. a bare `ci/` or `scripts/` dir) are NOT type-checked by the orchestrator verify, so any importable tooling whose task requires "mypy --strict green" should live UNDER the package (e.g. `src/solar_challenge_platform/ci/`) to get genuine coverage and clean test imports — otherwise the mypy signal is vacuous. solar_challenge_platform GOTCHA (task 1067, 2026-10-16): mypy runs only on src (CLAUDE.md `mypy src/solar_challenge_platform`; orchestrator verify = pytest -m 'not slow' + that mypy), never on tests/. Mypy checks the HEAD copy under the real module name, so the file's own `tests.…` imports still resolve. Strip line numbers from the before/after logs (`sed -E 's/:[0-9]+:/:/'`) and diff them. mypy is gated over src only, so tests/api/test_billing_api.py carries about 45 old messages and only the delta matters.

Typing gotcha (verified 2026-09-30, task 400): the orchestrator's type_check_command covers only src (uv run --extra dev mypy src/solar_challenge_platform), so tests are never mypy-gated, and tests/billing/test_pipeline.py already carries stale or mismatched `# type: ignore` comments. solar_challenge_platform conventions confirmed while planning P1·β (S7 models): (1) the orchestrator verify runs `mypy --strict` on src/solar_challenge_platform ONLY — test files under tests/ are NOT type-gated, so test code can be loosely typed but every src/ symbol must be mypy-clean. (2) Cross-module SQLAlchemy 2.0 ORM relationships should use TYPE_CHECKING imports + string forward refs (Mapped[list['Account']]) and declare FKs via 'table.id' strings — SQLAlchemy resolves targets from its class registry, so no runtime imports between mutually-referencing entity modules are needed (avoids import cycles) while staying mypy --strict clean. models/__init__.py must import every entity module so Base.metadata is fully populated for create_all and Alembic autogenerate. UUID PKs use sqlalchemy.Uuid + default=uuid.uuid4 (portable SQLite/Postgres); money uses Numeric/Decimal.

HOW to measure dark-factory verify and throughput from artifacts (worked out 2026-09-30).
- **Merge-gate leg durations:** `run_verification` archives a junit report ONLY for role=='merge' at full breadth (`orchestrator/src/orchestrator/verify.py::_archive_junit_report`). `data/verify-logs/<task>/attempt-N.<module>.junit-<UTCstamp>.xml.gz` therefore holds merge-gate legs only; the testsuite `time` attribute is the leg's wall time.
- **Task-role leg durations:** no junit exists. Parse the pytest summary line ("N passed … in Xs") at the end of `.worktrees/<id>/.task/verify/attempt-N.orchestrator.test.log`. More than 20k tests means a full suite. This only covers surviving worktrees; reaped ones are gone.
- **Admission-slot wait:** approximately the test.log birth time (`stat -c %W`) minus the same attempt's type.log mtime.
- **workflow_verify events carry NO duration**, so task-lane slot-hours can't come from runs.db (task 5798 owns that gap). Pair `phase_enter`/`phase_exit` rows with phase='verify' per task for the verify-phase wall time, including slot wait. `rebase_verify_cost` rows carry `next_verify_wall_secs`.
- **Landings:** `merge_finalized` state='done' plus `train_merged.member_task_ids`. Compare against the same clock window on prior days to control for time of day.
- **Timestamps:** runs.db is UTC; the journal is BST.

To count dark-factory bare xdist worker crashes on the task lane: grep -F 'bare pytest-xdist worker crash detected' (plus 'VerifyInfraError escaped run()' for the merge-phase escapes) across /var/log/syslog, syslog.1 and zcat syslog.N.gz. The log line's own timestamp is local time (BST = UTC+1). That detection line has only existed since 2026-09-25 07:51Z. A crashed attempt is never archived to data/verify-logs, because run_verification raises VerifyInfraError before persisting logs, so counting verify logs or junit misses the class. For the denominator, use the archived task-role orchestrator full-suite summaries (data/verify-logs/*/attempt-*.orchestrator.summary-*.json; n_flag '8' = task role), which are complete from 2026-10-01. Read host load at each sighting from data/load-samples.db, metric runqueue_ratio (= procs_running/nproc).

dark-factory verify.py gotchas, observed 2026-09-27 while planning task 5671. (1) Task-path summary.json files are never archived. _archive_attempt_log copies only the .log files, so every data/verify-logs/*/attempt-*.summary-*.json is a merge-path record, written by _archive_merge_verify_logs. (2) <worktree>/.df-verify-junit/ (the merge junit dir) is NOT gitignored, so a junit report in a live task worktree belongs under the gitignored .task/verify/. (3) VerifyResult.failing_test_ids must stay None on the task path: verify_failure_is_preexisting_on_main and its role='task' main probe branch on `failing_test_ids is not None`, so populating it from a task-leg junit would change pre-existing-on-main adjudication.

In dark_factory worktrees, .task/verify/attempt-N.<module>.summary.json (e.g. .task/verify/attempt-2.orchestrator.summary.json) records the exact verify-pipeline commands (test/lint/type) used for that task, including the precise `uv run --project <module> pytest|ruff check|pyright <files...>` invocations. Reading this file is the fastest way to reproduce a task's verification in an amendment pass without guessing the toolchain (e.g. orchestrator uses ruff for lint and pyright for type-checking, run via `uv run --project orchestrator`).

Measurement notes for verify-host utilisation (how the 2026-10-08 study got its numbers). Ground truth for "is the laptop running a verify" is the laptop's own user journal: ssh leo-laptop 'journalctl --user -o short-iso --no-pager --since "2026-10-01 05:00" -g df-verify' takes about 3 min for a week (18k lines); a journalctl over the whole journal without -g or a tight --since/--until hung for more than 5 min. Each verify leg is a transient scope df-verify-<project>-<hash>-<id>.scope with a "Started" line and a "Consumed ... CPU time" line (systemd only logs Consumed when the scope used at least 1 s CPU, so short ruff legs and the bash -c true probes have no terminal line; treat them as zero wall). One merge verify spawns about 10 scopes on DF (per module x leg); use the interval union, not scope counts. Exclude test-fixture scopes with prefixes proj-, sibling-, test-task-. In runs.db, merge_verify.timestamp is the END of the verify and data.duration_ms its length (the row's own duration_ms column is NULL); rows exist only for completed, parsed verdicts (cancelled, voided, unparseable runs leave none). merge_heartbeat is emitted every 300 s only at depth>=1, and hosts[].slot_state='busy' means LEASED, not running. merge_queued.data.queue_depth is the external asyncio queue (reads 1), not the pipeline depth. Orchestrator start times are in the runs table (started_at), not in events; journalctl -u orchestrator-X with -g over 8 days also hangs. Seat scripts for all of this are in plans/laptop-utilisation-study-2026-10-08/seat{A,B,D,E}/.

Diagnostic facts for reading dark-factory merge-lane state, gathered 2026-09-06/09.

MERGE VERIFY TAKES ~50-56 MINUTES on this repo, measured from merge_verify duration_ms: task 4374 3078643 ms (~51 min), task 4360 3391920 ms (~57 min). So a merge sitting in 'verifying' for 25-45 minutes is normal, not hung — do not escalate on that alone. Verify proceeds module by module (cockpit, dashboard, escalation, fused-memory, orchestrator observed in that order).

A MERGE/TRAIN VERIFY WRITES NOTHING TO data/verify-logs/. Its junit lands in the merge worktree at .worktrees/_merge-<id>/.df-verify-junit/report.<module>.xml, and watching those file mtimes is the reliable way to see live progress and which module is running. data/verify-logs/<task>/ is populated by the TASK workflow verify, so the usual "check verify-logs" habit comes up empty for an in-flight merge and can be misread as "nothing is running".

data/orchestrator/merge_queue.json IS NOT THE LIVE QUEUE. It is the durable journal and holds a SUBSET: on 2026-09-06 it contained 2 records while the live snapshot enumerated 9 entries. Read get_merge_queue() for live state; merge_queue.json only tells you what would survive a restart.

TO CONFIRM A VERIFY IS GENUINELY LIVE rather than an orphaned survivor process, walk the pytest process's parent chain to the orchestrator PID (ps -o ppid=). A merge verify's chain is `uv run pytest` -> pytest -> the orchestrator process; a process reparented to init is a survivor from a dead run.

Where the dark-factory orchestrator's log lines actually are (2026-09-03): the daemon runs as the SYSTEM unit orchestrator-dark-factory.service, so `journalctl --user -u orchestrator-dark-factory*` returns nothing; use the system journal (retention reached back to about 08-24 on 09-03) or /var/log/syslog and its rotated .1/.2.gz/.3.gz siblings (reach back to about 08-02). Syslog is SHARED with the reify orchestrator and both log "Task <id>: ..." lines, so task ids collide across projects; confirm a df line by checking the task id exists in df's runs.db before counting it. The disjoint-delta gate's skip branch logs at DEBUG and therefore appears in neither sink; the overlap branch logs at WARNING ("rebased tree overlaps intervening delta ... triggering re-verify") and advance_main logs "returning rebased_pending_reverify" at INFO, so (reached minus fired) is the only way to count skips. The verify plan logs "Verification mode: fallback-scoped (N files)" for file-scoped merge verifies and "across 9 subprojects" for full-breadth ones, which is how the rehydration door was spotted.

ORCHESTRATOR FULL-SUITE VERIFY HAS ONLY ~13% WALL-CLOCK HEADROOM, so `infra_timeout` on task verify is usually the budget, not the task's diff. Distinct from the existing per-test load-flake entries (test_spawn_claude.py, test_scheduler_state_tools.py): this is about the WHOLE-SUITE budget, and the diagnostic below applies to any task.

MEASURED (task 4405, 2026-09-06, HEAD c3afe1d767). The orchestrator suite is ~15016 tests and took 3142.41s to complete under `cd orchestrator && uv run pytest --tb=short -q --timeout=300 -n 8 tests/` against a 3600s wall-clock budget = 87% utilised, ~458s of slack. THE DIAGNOSTIC THAT SETTLES IT FAST — compare COMMIT timestamps against ATTEMPT timestamps first. If every verify attempt post-dates every commit on the branch, all attempts ran an IDENTICAL tree; N attempts on an identical tree failing N DIFFERENT ways is the signature of infra, not a bug. Task 4405 saw exactly this across 3 attempts:
  - attempt-1: teardown ERRORs only, from the deploy-clock guard reporting data/fused-memory/last_redeploy_fused_memory.json rewritten mid-run (stamps ~9h apart, matching the 8h fleet clock). That guard's own message names a real fleet redeploy as the benign, non-test-bug cause — READ IT before debugging.
  - attempt-2: suite COMPLETED — "1 failed, 15014 passed, 1 skipped in 3142.41s".
  - attempt-3: pure 3600s timeout at 83% with an unbroken run of dots and ZERO failures.
A completing attempt like #2 is the most valuable artifact in the set: it proves the tree passes. Read every attempt log before concluding, not just the newest.

NEW MEMBER OF THE LOAD-SENSITIVE FLAKE FAMILY: orchestrator/tests/test_verify.py::TestRunCmdProcessGroup::test_run_cmd_killpg_on_cancellation failed under `-n 8` as "[gw4] node down: Not properly terminated / worker 'gw4' crashed", and passed standalone in 12.18s at the same HEAD. A test that killpg's a process group is inherently timing-sensitive under xdist; suspect flake before regression, and check whether the branch even touches verify.py.

PRACTICE. Before debugging an orchestrator infra_timeout: (1) diff commit vs attempt timestamps; (2) grep every attempt log for a completing run; (3) run `uptime` and `nproc` and count concurrent `[p]ytest --tb=short` masters; (4) run only the task's own test files to confirm the diff is green. Do NOT add a 6th concurrent full suite to a host already at load 150 just to reproduce — it degrades every lane including your own, and the completing attempt already answers the question. There is no code fix for this; file escalate_blocker with category infra_issue and let the handler re-run.

A test-infrastructure speed-up in dark-factory's orchestrator suite reaches TASK-role verifies only once each task's branch contains it. A task verify runs the tests from the task worktree's own tree, and only the merge gate runs on current main. Measured after task 5677 landed (2026-09-29): task 5308's and task 4023's branches contained the landing, and their full-suite task-role orchestrator legs took 1,346 s and 1,712 s. Task 5460's branch predated it, and its two legs took about 4,500 s each, no better than the pre-landing median of 5,249 s. Old-base branches keep hogging the single task-verify slot, so slot waits and verify-phase times lag the merge-lane improvement until in-flight tasks rebase. Note also that task-role legs run niced (tier 15) with a capped `-n` (`verify_admission_pytest_n`). candidates.content: In reify, the compiler builtin-family name slices (PARSE_FN_NAMES, ANALYSIS_FN_NAMES, MATH_*, JOINT_*, FIELD_OP_NAMES, etc.) cannot be deleted or moved without breaking the whole reify-compiler test module compile: crates/reify-compiler/src/units.rs holds 13 hand-written *_are_disjoint_from_other_families test ladders (no central list-of-all-families helper), and the references are ASYMMETRIC — ANALYSIS_FN_NAMES alone is asserted against by ten sibling family tests, while PARSE_FN_NAMES is referenced one-directionally only. When migrating a family to the reify-builtins registry (PRD docs/prds/v0_6/builtin-signature-registry.md), keep the slice alive as a one-line registry-derived shim (`pub const X_FN_NAMES: &[&str] = reify_builtins::X_FN_NAMES;`) rather than deleting it; disjointness-test retirement is scheduled for the λ integration leaf, not per-family.

Reify fact (units.rs name-family disjointness tests, observed 2026-06-14): crates/reify-compiler/src/units.rs's test module pins each compiler name-family (geometry x5, dynamics-query, math-construction, math-operation, joint, dynamics-constructor, analysis, field-op, relation) disjoint from the others via per-family *_disjoint_from_other_families tests. The substantive guard for a NEW family is a single comprehensive forward sweep (iterate the new slice, assert each name absent from every other family) — this catches a colliding name added to EITHER side, so it fully establishes the partition. The additional converse asserts (re-checking from each existing family's test) are convention/redundancy only (a reviewer explicitly flagged them as duplicate maintenance burden), not required for correctness. AFFINE_ALGEBRA_NAMES (affine_compose/affine_inverse/determinant) and LIST_HELPER_NAMES (single/flat_map) have no public single-source slice — they are local const fixtures mirroring hardcoded match arms in affine_map_algebra_result_type / infer_list_helper_return_type. determinant is the ONE intentional overlap (math-operation vs affine-algebra, arg-type disambiguated).

Correct resolution: keep #5344's module and extend it with orient_to_euler only — the decomposer #5344 disclaims — since orient_euler's Orientation<3> return type is already delivered by #5344. Filed as esc-6082-8. Before adding a new `*_signatures.rs` result-type family, grep every existing family slice in units.rs for the names you intend to claim.

Reify compiler: when you add or widen a builtin classification family slice (e.g. in orientation_signatures.rs / units.rs), you must also do three things in crates/reify-compiler/src/unresolved_function.rs. Add the slice to the `is_known_builtin` union. Add it to the test module's `ALL_FAMILY_SLICES` table. Remove its names from `EVAL_DEFERRED_BUILTIN_NAMES`. Otherwise the name is silently double-owned (family + "unclaimed" manifest), and `eval_deferred_names_are_disjoint_from_every_registered_family` cannot detect it. Task #6082's ORIENTATION_EULER_FN_NAMES missed this; task 6306 fixes it.

In crates/reify-compiler/src/units.rs, builtin name-families (AFFINE_MAP_CONSTRUCTOR_NAMES, FEA_ENVELOPE_NAMES added by task 4629) now carry a `*_names_are_disjoint_from_other_families` in-module test asserting cross-family name disjointness. GOTCHA for task 4387 (η datum constructors): the `offset` name is an INTENTIONAL cross-family overlap — `offset/3` is a relation (relation_signatures.rs RELATION_FN_NAMES) while `offset/2` is the new datum constructor — resolved by arity, NOT by name. A naive datum-constructor disjointness test mirroring the fea-envelope one would FAIL on `offset`; the test must exclude `offset` or assert the intentional arity-resolved overlap.

candidates.content: Reify compiler gotcha — giving one builtin family a real static return type can turn a NEIGHBOURING family's silent first-arg-fallback mistype into a hard compile error, in crates OTHER than reify-compiler. Mechanism: `expr.rs::resolve_function_overload`'s `NoUserFunctions` ladder ends in a fallback that silently adopts the first argument's type. While two interacting builtins BOTH fall through, their wrong types often stay mutually compatible and nothing fails. The moment one gets a correct nominal type, `type_compat.rs` starts judging a real-vs-fallback pairing and emits E_ArithOperandKind. Task 5344 hit this exactly: typing `transform3(..)` as Type::Transform(3) made `let t2 = t * origin` fail with "operator `*` is undefined for operand kinds `Transform3` and `Scalar[m]`", because `point3(..)` still fell through to its first arg's Scalar[m]. The `(Transform(n), Point{n}) => Point` Mul rule already existed in type_compat.rs AND had a passing unit test — it was simply unreachable from any call site, so the unit test gave false assurance. Consequences for future ladder work: (1) a green `cargo test -p reify-compiler` is NOT sufficient — the 10 failures all landed in reify-eval (m10_geometric_types, m8_m11_regression_checkpoint) and reify-compiler's own examples_smoke; run a full `cargo nextest run --workspace --no-fail-fast` baseline BEFORE the change and diff it against the after-run, since a pre-existing-failure baseline is the only way to tell new breakage from old. (2) When a type_compat rule exists but its operand can only be produced by a builtin that is still unclaimed by the ladder, that rule is dead code wearing a passing test. (3) Name-family slices in math_signatures.rs/units.rs are pinned disjoint by generic `.contains` loops in units.rs's test module, so adding a name to a slice is auto-covered — but `datum_constructor_result_type` is a RESOLVER, not a slice, and no `.contains` assert can cover it; double-classification there must be pinned by probing the resolver directly.

The decisive argument against a SEMANTIC resolver is that it cannot catch the motivating defect: 5854 found `dimension.rs:1259` cited for a test actually at :1447, where line 1259 exists and sits inside an unrelated Momentum assert, so a resolve-and-check-bounds detector passes it. Rationale lives in `docs/prds/reify-audit-stale-line-cite-detector.md`; do not re-derive from scratch.

Reify: the "unrecognised function name compiles silently / green check" defect (a bareword call to a nonexistent name with >=1 arg gets ZERO diagnostics; expr.rs terminal first-arg-type fallback, ~expr.rs:3851) is ALREADY OWNED by a three-task chain — #5371 (warn-mode closed-world manifest, in flight on branch task/5371, creates crates/reify-compiler/src/unresolved_function.rs), #5997 (flip Warning -> Severity::Error), #6014 (delete the fallback). Reify: `crates/reify-compiler/src/builtin_signatures.rs` is NOT the name→result-type registry despite being cited that way in several PRD capability-manifest `delivered_check` rows — it is only the arg-slot DIMENSION checker (`builtin_arg_slots(name, arity)`, `ExpectedArg::{Scalar{dimension,type_name}, Int}`; no Point/Vector variant, so Point-vs-Vector is eval-only). For an Orientation/Frame/Transform-returning builtin the real registration site is `crates/reify-compiler/src/orientation_signatures.rs`: add the name to `ORIENTATION_TYPED_FN_NAMES`, add a `orientation_typed_fn_result_type` match arm, AND bump the independent hand-derived `EXPECTED_NAMES: [&str; N]` test fixture (it deliberately does not import the slice, so it is the drift guard) plus the `..._are_exactly_the_N` test name. `expr.rs`'s `NoUserFunctions` ladder needs no edit — it already gates on `is_orientation_typed_fn`. Registering only the eval arm compiles and passes CI but silently mistypes every call site via the first-arg fallback (`expr.rs:3614-3631`), and nothing catches it: reify-compiler has no dep on reify-stdlib even at dev scope (documented at orientation_signatures.rs:179-188). Adding a key to `builtin_signatures.rs` also requires listing it in `tests::NON_SELECTOR_ARG_SLOT_KEYS` with a justification unless it is a topology selector — that invariant rejects dead entries too.

In crates/reify-compiler, the explicit `use crate::<x>_signatures::<X>_FN_NAMES;` lines in the units.rs `mod tests` import block (units.rs:~1759-1810) are a CONVENTION, not a compilation requirement — every family slice is already in scope without them. units.rs:1 is `use super::*;` and lib.rs (~:104) glob re-exports each signature module as `pub(crate) use <x>_signatures::*;`, so the names reach `mod tests`'s own `use super::*`. MEASURED on task 6306: deleting the import for a brand-new slice still built cleanly (`cargo test -p reify-compiler --lib --no-run`) and all 17 `*_are_disjoint_from_other_families` tests passed. Consequence for planning: do NOT write a plan step whose RED signal is "compile failure until the units.rs import lands" — it will be green immediately and the step's TDD framing is false. The real RED/GREEN signal for a disjointness-matrix step is whether the reciprocal ASSERTS hold. Keep the explicit import anyway (it is the block's documented style, and it makes the dependency deliberate so removing the lib.rs glob fails loudly rather than silently un-pinning the matrix); an explicit import shadows the glob and produces no unused-import warning.

Reify gotcha (verified 2026-10-07, task 5476): when you add a NEW compiler builtin-name family slice (e.g. FLEXURE_CTOR_FN_NAMES), also register it as a row in ALL_FAMILY_SLICES in `mod tests` of crates/reify-compiler/src/unresolved_function.rs, and OR it into `is_known_builtin`. Without the ALL_FAMILY_SLICES row, nothing detects that the same names are still parked in EVAL_DEFERRED_BUILTIN_NAMES. The double owner compiles and every test passes. Adding the row makes eval_deferred_names_are_disjoint_from_every_registered_family fail with "... is now claimed by <FAMILY> — remove it from the manifest". Then delete the manifest entries.

Reify has NO gate for stale prose path references to moved integration tests: the CMP-*/C-eval-* harness-consolidation series git-mv'd crates/<c>/tests/<stem>.rs into crates/<c>/tests/harness_<subsystem>/<stem>.rs, silently orphaning every doc-comment/PRD/manifest citation of the old flat path, and crates/reify-audit/src/ (p1/p2/p5/pdead/pdoccover/pdssentinel/player/ptodo/puntested) plus tests/infra/ contain no path-resolution check. Correction has been by manual sweep only — task #6214 (commit 276d32f025, 123 files) then task #6468 (60 files / 69 occurrences for the basename examples_smoke.rs alone) — and manual sweeps demonstrably do not converge: #6214 fixed tree-sitter-reify/test/corpus/io-formats.txt line 5 while leaving the same defect on line 7 of that header block, and fixed a capability-manifest .md without its .yaml twin. The sweep convention both tasks used is a pure path-segment insertion that preserves trailing :LINE numbers and ::selector suffixes verbatim, with a never-edit exclusion set of docs/architecture-audit/findings/*.md, docs/notes/*-2026-*.md and docs/legibility/confusion-codebook.yaml. The citation surface is wider than .rs/.md/.sh — live references also sit in .ri example header comments, .yaml capability manifests and tree-sitter .txt corpus headers — so any future scanner must be extension-agnostic over tracked files.
