candidates.content: When cancelling a task as superseded in a dark-factory project, first check its dependents: the orchestrator scheduler counts a cancelled LOCAL dependency as satisfied (only cancelled EXTERNAL/cross-project deps escalate), so a pending dependent becomes dispatchable the moment the upstream is cancelled. Transfer the edge to the superseding task (add_dependency dependent -> superseder) before setting the cancel, or the dependent can run before the work it was waiting on.

solar_challenge architect exception to the followup-dispatched-before-parent rule (task 504, 2026-10-15, main 0fcef8b): when the parent was CANCELLED rather than left unmerged (504's parent 195 was cancelled at 20:26Z, superseded by the S14 PRD), report_blocking_dependency(<parent>) is wrong, because dark-factory's scheduler._deps_satisfied counts a cancelled dependency as satisfied and re-dispatches the follow-up (504 was dispatched 9 minutes after 195's cancellation). If the follow-up's subject exists only on the cancelled branch, also do not report_task_already_done citing some other main commit that merely touches the same file, since that anchors found_on_main provenance on another task's work; instead amend the reconciler's pending orphan L1 ('Task N orphaned: parent P cancelled', expand_scope|abort_task) with first-hand checks and exit with report_unactionable_task recommending abort_task.

solar_challenge / dark-factory ordering gotcha (task 273 planning, 2026-10-01): a follow-up filed via submit_task with spawned_from=<parent> gets no Taskmaster dependency on its parent. So when an orchestrator restart cancels the unmerged parent back to pending (task 263 was cancelled at 04:54Z with all 5 plan steps committed), the follow-up can take the shared file locks first (273 did at 04:55Z). When the follow-up must edit lines the parent rewrites, have its architect call report_blocking_dependency on the parent rather than plan on main, because whichever task lands second then hits a guaranteed merge conflict. While the parent is non-terminal, dark-factory's workflow.py _handle_blocking_dep_report registers the dependency and requeues the follow-up; if the parent is cancelled, the follow-up dispatches again.

DISCOVERY (M1 validation 2026-07-03, findings F2+F3, fixed by tasks 133/134/141): three unattended-failure modes witnessed on real infra. (1) scp-ingest crashed on broker disconnect (aiomqtt MqttError propagated out of the subscriber's async-for; no reconnect loop) — root disconnect cause was keepalive starvation: blocking synchronous DB writes inside the asyncio event loop starved PINGREQ during a sustained drain, mosquitto k60 dropped the client. (2) The clean-session subscription (auto client-id, c1) meant mosquitto discarded the queued QoS-1 backlog on disconnect — recovery in validation was only possible because the simulator replay is deterministic and store writes are ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING idempotent; real edge data would have been lost. Unbatched per-message commits drained at only ~90-170 msg/s (fine at production's ~1.7 msg/s, ~50x too slow for backfill). (3) A dispatch process wedged silently mid-tick on a half-dead Postgres socket — main thread epoll-parked, DB sessions idle 15+ min, process alive so systemd Restart=on-failure could never fire; only the device-side 60s watchdog protected the fleet (bare create_engine had no connect_timeout/keepalives/statement_timeout/pre-ping).

Discovery (operations-assurance, verified with Docker probes 2026-10-13 at 40a6556) about the scp-deploy instance render (instance/, task 443).
- **Placeholder infrastructure:** the rendered caddy and mosquitto services are stock images with default config. Caddy serves a static page on :80, so nothing listens on the published 443 and nothing proxies to the API. Mosquitto starts local-only on 1883, so ingest configured for 8883/TLS cannot connect. The broker durability settings the README calls REQUIRED are not rendered. Roles cannot read /run/secrets, so they refuse to start (task 444 pending).

The fleet registry's last-known-good YAML is therefore never written, and a dispatch restart during a DB outage would load an empty fleet. The existing test checks only the path.
- **No alert hooks:** every job row defaults alert_on_failure=True, but OnFailure hooks render only when the topology has a WATCH row, and there is none, so no unit carries an alert hook.

Pydantic 2.12.5 behaviours measured in /tmp during task 6524 planning:
- A stdlib @dataclass(frozen=True) used as a model field has its __post_init__ run, and a ValueError raised there surfaces as a ValidationError (type 'value_error').
- PydanticCustomError('<code>', msg) surfaces with error type == '<code>', so validators can emit domain reason codes directly.
- RootModel[Annotated[Union[...], Field(discriminator='kind')]] accepts the parse_metadata splat Model(**raw) when the variants use Literal[StrEnum member].
- Frozen models dumped with model_dump(mode='json') round-trip to an equal instance, and UTC datetimes serialize with a 'Z' suffix.

GOTCHA (pydantic 2.12.5, measured 2026-10-09 in task 6524): a stdlib @dataclass used as a BaseModel field cannot be made strict the obvious ways. Annotated[DC, Field(strict=True)] fails at class creation with "RuntimeError: Unable to apply constraint 'strict' to schema of type 'dataclass'". Model-level ConfigDict(strict=True) makes a dict input fail with dataclass_exact_type, because strict python mode needs a DC instance. Lax mode silently coerces the inner fields (pid True→1, '42'→42). One way that works and keeps the field list in one place: a BeforeValidator that, for a Mapping input, runs TypeAdapter(hint).validate_python(value[name], strict=True) for each name/hint in typing.get_type_hints(DC), then returns the mapping for the normal lax DC build. A ValidationError raised inside it surfaces at the field's loc with the inner error type (e.g. int_type). See shared/src/shared/task_deferral.py::StoredHolder.

Pydantic 2.12 gotcha (verified by probe in dark-factory, 2026-10-10): pydantic_core.PydanticCustomError(type, message_template, ctx) substitutes only bare {name} placeholders from ctx — format specs like {kind!r} are NOT applied and render literally. Render the message in Python first and pass ctx only for structured consumers (errors()[i]['ctx']). Also: a mode='before' field_validator's return value becomes the error 'input' when the inner (e.g. Literal) validation fails, and model_validate(raw, context={...}) reaches a mode='after' model_validator via its info: ValidationInfo parameter.

Pydantic v2 gotcha: `model_dump(exclude_none=True)` drops REQUIRED-but-nullable fields (e.g. `alpha: float | None` with no default), so a model that writes with exclude_none and reads with `model_validate` breaks its own round trip whenever such a field is legitimately None. Measured on `shared.memory_eval_limits.LimitsArtifact`: exclude_none dropped `alpha` for an all-scalar eval run and `load_limits_artifact` then raised on a file the writer had just emitted. The safe convention is "omit None-valued OPTIONAL fields; always emit REQUIRED fields even when null" — dump with exclude_none, then restore any `model_fields[name].is_required()` key missing from the payload as None (derive the set from model_fields rather than hardcoding the field, so it survives a later schema addition).
Pydantic field default is None for backward compatibility

Pyright (basic mode, as configured per-package in dark-factory) rejects extra keyword arguments to a pydantic v2 model even when the model sets `model_config = ConfigDict(extra='allow')` — it synthesizes __init__ from the declared fields via dataclass_transform and reports `error: No parameter named "x" (reportCallIssue)`. Passing such a key in a test (e.g. `TaskMetadata(human_curator_gate=True)`) needs a `# type: ignore[call-arg]` on the offending kwarg's own line. Pyright treats any `# type: ignore[...]` as a blanket line suppression regardless of the code inside the brackets, so the mypy-style bracketed form already used across shared/tests works.

GOTCHA (dark-factory, measured on task 4676): when adding a new `shared.task_metadata` submodel, two pydantic defaults will silently weaken the contract you think you wrote. Both bit a reviewed, verify-green implementation.

1. `Field(gt=0)` on an int runs pydantic v2's LAX coercion. Measured against the worktree venv: `interval_secs=True` yields 1, and `'86400'` / `86400.0` also coerce. For a cadence field that means a stray boolean mints a chain with a ONE-SECOND interval — silently wrong, not a crash. Metadata arrives from JSON where an int is already an int, so nothing legitimate needs the coercion: write `Field(gt=0, strict=True)`. This is the same defect class the sibling guard already defends against with its `always_escalates is True` IDENTITY check rather than a truthiness test, so the codebase had already ruled on it once. Test rows for bool/numeric-string/float ACCEPT without the flag, so they pin the flag and not merely the sign check.

2. A field declared `x: T | None = None` makes KEY PRESENCE useless as a discriminator for "the author omitted this". `parse_metadata` + `model_dump` materialises an explicit `'x': None` on the way back out, so a value the author never wrote comes back as a present key. Any consumer testing `'x' in slice` classifies every round-tripped record as though the field had been set. Write the contract as `x is None` in the docstring AND in docs/task-authoring.md, and assert the trap explicitly in the round-trip test (absent as authored, present as dumped, None either way) — otherwise the prose and the code state opposite contracts and the next implementer follows the prose. Note this is the MIRROR of the already-recorded `model_dump(exclude_none=True)` gotcha (drops required-but-nullable fields): the two failure modes point in opposite directions, so do not "fix" one by reaching for the other.

3. Copying a shape constraint from another module copies only what you transcribe. `Recurrence.key` mirrored `fused_memory.topic_slug::TOPIC_SLUG_RE` but not its companion `TOPIC_SLUG_MAX_LEN`, leaving a key documented as "the same shape as a memory topic slug" accepting 500 characters. When a comment claims a mirror, check what every real consumer of the original pairs it with — for that module it is `is_valid_topic_slug`, which applies regex AND cap together.

orchestrator/tests/_orch_helpers.py:pydantic_spec now enumerates user-defined @property descriptors in addition to model.model_fields, while filtering out BaseModel-inherited ones (model_extra, model_fields_set, __fields_set__). Implementation pattern: build basemodel_props set via `inspect.getmembers(BaseModel, lambda v: isinstance(v, property))`, then iterate the user class's properties and skip names in that set. Co-located test contracts live in orchestrator/tests/test_conftest_helpers.py: (a) test_pydantic_spec_exposes_user_property_descriptors pins read+write of overrides_db_path, (b) test_pydantic_spec_excludes_basemodel_inherited_members pins task-1064's invariant. Also: mock_orch_config now seeds `overrides_db_path = tmp_path / 'overrides.db'` so OverrideStore.__init__ can call .parent.mkdir() and sqlite3.connect(str(...)) without leaking literal-MagicMock-named files to disk.

In the orchestrator project, pydantic BaseModel subclasses get a strict, per-field synthesized __init__ under pyright (via dataclass_transform), NOT the runtime `**data: Any` signature. A helper that forwards a generic `(kind: str, **fields: object)` bag into `SomeModel(kind=kind, **fields)` will fail pyright with reportArgumentType even though it works fine at runtime — the fix used in deterministic_runner.py's `_build_done_provenance` (task 2167) is a `# type: ignore[arg-type]` on the construction line with a docstring note, matching the codebase's established `# type: ignore[code]` convention (mypy-style codes, ~176 uses) rather than inventing per-field typed overloads. orchestrator/orchestrator.yaml's `type_check_command` runs `pyright src/ tests/` as a real verify gate — pytest-only runs will not catch this class of error, so WIP/auto-commits should be pyright-checked, not just pytest-checked, before trusting them.

GOTCHA — two pyright patterns that fail DF's type gate from inside TEST code, both hit on task 3195. (1) A deliberately misspelled keyword arg used to prove a Pydantic model's extra='forbid' rejects typos is a STATIC error ("No parameter named ..."), so the type gate fails before the runtime assertion can run; splat it through a dict instead — cls(**{'enfroce': True}) — to keep the check runtime-only. (2) Splatting a dict literal into a Pydantic model's __init__ (FusedMemoryConfig(**{'section': {...}})) makes pyright widen EVERY sibling field to the dict's value type, producing one reportArgumentType error PER SECTION — 17 errors from one line on FusedMemoryConfig. Use Model.model_validate({...}) instead, which takes Any and is also how a loaded config.yaml actually reaches the model. Separately, fused-memory's ruff config selects SIM (pyproject.toml select = E,F,UP,B,SIM,I), and SIM300 fires on `CONSTANT == frozenset({...})` in tests; `ruff check --fix` flips the operands, which is semantics-preserving for equality and keeps per-key comments attached.

shared.task_metadata gotcha: when a WHOLE-MODEL cross-field invariant on TaskMetadata raises (pydantic loc == ()), parse_metadata's error handler takes its `else:` branch and returns `TaskMetadata.model_construct(**parsed)` — which skips validation entirely, so typed sub-model fields stay RAW DICTS (before_done is a dict, not a BeforeDone). Calling model_dump() on that instance emits a benign pydantic UserWarning "PydanticSerializationUnexpectedValue(Expected `BeforeDone` ...)"; it still returns every key, but a test asserting round-trip via model_dump() will BREAK under `-W error`. Assert on model.model_extra[...] and model.before_done instead. This is distinct from the per-field `invalid_field` branch, which pops the offending keys, re-validates the remainder, and reattaches raw values via __pydantic_extra__. Measured against the existing _deterministic_invariants rule while planning task 3369.

Gotcha (dark-factory config models): do not name a pydantic BaseModel field `register`. BaseModel's metaclass inherits ABCMeta.register, so `register: str` emits "UserWarning: Field name "register" ... shadows an attribute in parent "BaseModel"". That warning becomes an error under -W error / filterwarnings=error. Measured 2026-10-12 while planning task 6877, which uses `register_function` instead.
Believes Pydantic models should enforce their own invariants via field_validator

Confirmed empirically in shared/task_metadata.py: pydantic v2 BaseModel.model_dump() recursively serializes a nested BaseModel instance stored in another model's __pydantic_extra__ (extra='allow') back into a plain dict — I1 round-trip preservation holds for TaskMetadata's W10 registered sub-model slices (e.g. a future 'deploy_state' key) without any extra handling needed in parse_metadata.

Config-state test gotcha (dark-factory orchestrator, measured 2026-09-23, task 2915): never check a raw YAML config sub-block by feeding it through its pydantic submodel and reading values back (e.g. `SandboxConfig(**block).enabled is True`). The submodel's Field default applies where the real loader would have deep-merged defaults.yaml's value underneath, and plain BaseModel submodels silently ignore unknown keys. Concretely, `SandboxConfig(**{'enabld': False, 'backend': 'landlock'})` gives enabled=True because the model default is True, but load_config deep-merges the project block over defaults.yaml's `sandbox: {enabled: false}` (config.py::_load_defaults + ::_deep_merge), so at runtime that block resolves DISABLED. The check false-passes exactly the typo/omission it should catch. Instead: (1) compare the raw block by whole-mapping equality, e.g. `block == {'enabled': True, 'backend': 'landlock'}`; (2) prove every declared key is a real field with `Submodel.model_validate(block).model_fields_set == set(block)`. An ignored typo is absent from model_fields_set, so this also catches a model-side field rename that leaves committed keys inert. Related: memories 6d8d0439 (extra='ignore' makes kwarg tests vacuous) and 3303832a (defaults.yaml shadows Field defaults).

In the dashboard package (which declares only escalation + dark-factory-shared as deps, not pydantic directly), wire-decode failures from `SharedModel.model_validate(...)` can be caught with `except ValueError` — pydantic v2's ValidationError subclasses ValueError (verified pydantic 2.12.5). This lets per-project MCP fan-out helpers (clones of data/merge_halt.py) degrade a malformed payload to that project's offline marker without adding a direct pydantic import/dependency. merge_halt's except tuple already lists ValueError for this reason.

dark-factory canonical fix for bare `config = MagicMock()` lint violations (reaffirmed 2026-06-14): use MagicMock(spec_set=pydantic_spec(<Model>)) where pydantic_spec is at orchestrator/tests/_orch_helpers.py (exposes a pydantic model's fields + @property + methods + PrivateAttr for spec_set, excluding BaseModel API); OR for test methods needing a full Harness config, add the mock_orch_config fixture (orchestrator/tests/conftest.py) as a parameter. spec_set is STRICT — it raises AttributeError on any attribute not on the model, which surfaces dead/non-existent fields the test was setting. Concrete dead fields found and dropped on 2026-06-14: `config.merge_timeout_seconds` (not on OrchestratorConfig, never read in src) in test_harness_train_callbacks.py; `config.max_post_merge_verify_timeouts` / `config.max_post_merge_verify_enospc_retries` (lowercase; not OrchestratorConfig fields — reverify_member_solo uses hardcoded max_timeouts=3/max_enospc=3) in test_merge_queue_train_attribution.py. Prefer a real spec over a `# noqa: bare-magicmock — <reason>` exemption (exemption must be on the PRECEDING non-blank line; inline same-line is intentionally ignored).

Concrete case of `Mocks must match real wire shape`: 2026-05-28, adding `instance_id=self.buffer.instance_id` to TargetedReconciler.reconcile_task's `ReconciliationRun(...)` constructor broke 49 tests in fused-memory/tests/test_targeted.py because `mock_event_buffer` was a bare `AsyncMock()` — `.instance_id` returned an auto-spawned MagicMock attribute, which Pydantic v2's `ReconciliationRun.instance_id: str | None` rejected with `Input should be a valid string`. Fix: add `buf.instance_id = 'mock-buffer-instance'` to the fixture. Lesson: when a Pydantic model has a strict scalar field and your test passes a Mock, the mock's auto-attribute will fail validation — pre-populate the attribute as a real value of the expected type. Pydantic v2 does NOT coerce Mock to str even in lax mode.

GOTCHA (dark-factory, measured 2026-09-08, task 5216): pyright FAILS a test helper that builds a kwargs dict and splats it into a dataclass constructor, even when every value is correct at runtime. `fields = dict(cpu_some10=0.0, ..., own_cgroup='/df.slice/df-x.slice', ...)` infers as `dict[str, float | str]`, so `PsiSample(**fields)` reports one `reportArgumentType` error PER FIELD — a 10-field dataclass produced 10 errors all anchored to the same single line, which reads at first glance like ten separate defects.

FIX: annotate the dict `fields: dict[str, Any]` (and give any `vars_of`-style helper that returns such a dict an explicit `-> dict[str, Any]`). `dict[str, object]` does NOT work — `object` is not assignable to the concrete parameter types. This is a pure annotation change; no runtime behaviour moves.

WHY IT BITES LATE: `uv run pytest` and `ruff check` are both clean on this code, so the failure only appears at `cd <pkg> && npx pyright`, which in the factory is the pre-commit hook (Python-staging commits only) and the verify leg. Budget for it: run pyright BEFORE committing a test helper of this shape, not after. Note the hook skips pyright entirely for docs-only commits, so a green pre-commit on an earlier commit tells you nothing about this.

WHEN THE SHAPE IS WORTH KEEPING: a `_healthy_sample(**overrides)` helper that defaults every field and lets each test raise only the one arm under test is genuinely good for a wide dataclass — it keeps each test's intent to one line. The annotation is the whole cost.

content: Pydantic 2.12 gotchas measured in the dark-factory .venv (task 6717): a plain `int` field accepts True (as 1) and '4' (as 4) in lax mode, so use StrictInt where a bool must never read as a number. model_dump(mode='json') renders a UTC datetime with a 'Z' suffix, not datetime.isoformat()'s '+00:00', so add a field_serializer when the wire string must stay identical. With extra='ignore', an unknown constructor kwarg is dropped silently at runtime (only pyright's dataclass_transform check catches it). A BaseModel is not a collections.abc.Mapping, so a reader still guarding with isinstance(x, Mapping) silently takes its empty branch when handed a model.

Completed: Grammar has no method-call-with-arguments rule: obj.map(|v| ...) / .filter / .all / .any are parse errors, leaving reify-expr's method arms unreachable from .ri source
Description: Discovered while planning task #5385 (generate-of-geometry silent undef); see escalation esc-5385-1. OUT OF SCOPE for #5385, which delivers only the generate + union_all halves of its acceptance criteria.

OBSERVATION (measured on HEAD 975cbfc301 with target/debug/reify built 2026-08-21): the tree-sitter grammar has NO method-call-with-arguments rule. In tree-sitter-reify/grammar.js, `member_access` (grammar.js:1583-1587) is `prec.left(11, seq(field('object', $._expression), '.', field('member', $.identifier)))` — no callTail. The only argument-taking call rules are `function_call` (grammar.js:1572, bare identifier + callTail) and `trait_method_call` (grammar.js:1642, qualified/instance-qualified callee + callTail).

Consequences measured directly:
- `let ys = xs.map(|v| v + 1)` over `let xs = [1, 2, 3]` => "Parse error: invalid let". Same for `xs.filter(|v| v > 1)`, `xs.all(|v| v > 0)`, `xs.any(...)`, and even `xs.foo(|v| v)` — so the gap is method-ARGUMENTS, not lambdas and not element type.
- `constraint all_pos: xs.all(|v| v > 0)` => "Parse error: invalid constraint" — not let-position-specific.

Completed: ts_parser.rs import_declaration dispatch bypasses check_and_lower!, silently swallowing nested parse errors
Description: Discovered while planning task 5931 (canonical destructured-import syntax). OUT OF SCOPE for 5931, which deliberately declined to widen into a shared lowering path.

DEFECT. In crates/reify-syntax/src/ts_parser.rs, the source_file dispatch loop's "import_declaration" arm (lines 337-345) calls `self.lower_import(child)` DIRECTLY, bypassing the `check_and_lower!` macro (lines 13-25) that essentially every other declaration arm routes through. That macro is what turns `child.is_error() || child.has_error()` into a pushed parse error. Because imports skip it, a tree-sitter ERROR node nested INSIDE an import_declaration subtree never becomes a diagnostic: the import lowers silently and `parsed.errors` stays empty.

MEASURED IMPACT (this is not theoretical — it masked a real bug for ~5 months). Before 5931, `import a.b.{C, D}` did not match the tree-sitter rule (which lacked the '.' separator). tree-sitter error-recovered the stray '.' into a sibling ERROR node inside the import_declaration, leaving the `path` and `items` fields intact:

    (import_declaration
      path: (import_path (identifier) (identifier))
      (ERROR [0, 15] - [0, 16])
      items: (import_items (identifier) (identifier)))

`lower_import` collects only `identifier` children of the path node plus the `items` field, so it produced a clean, CORRECT AST from an erroring CST. Four tests across reify-syntax, reify-compiler and reify-lsp therefore passed green on main while the grammar officially rejected the very form they exercised. Task 5931 fixes the grammar; it does NOT fix this bypass.

WORK TO DO.
1. Determine whether the bypass is deliberate (e.g. imports intentionally tolerate partial parses for LSP/incremental-edit reasons) or an oversight. Check git history for the dispatch arm and for any test that depends on a malformed import lowering silently.
2. If an oversight, route the arm through `check_and_lower!` like its siblings.
3. Expect fallout in tests that feed malformed or partially-typed imports — crates/reify-syntax/tests/harness_syntax/cfg_import_attachment_tests.rs is the most likely, and reify-lsp paths that parse incomplete buffers mid-keystroke are the main risk area. Each fallout site needs a judgement call, which is why 5931 did not absorb this.
4. Audit the other dispatch arms in the same loop for the same bypass — imports may not be the only one.

RATIONALE FOR SPLITTING. 5931's mandate was to settle which destructured-import spelling is canonical. Fixing this bypass changes error reporting for unrelated malformed-import inputs across three crates, which is scope 5931 neither asked for nor bounded. After 5931 lands, the canonical form parses cleanly, so this bypass no longer masks anything for that spelling — but it remains latent for every other malformed import.

Description: FILED by the /unblock session on 5470 (esc-5470-5), ruling G (Leo, 2026-10-07): high priority.

DEFECT. `@` is both the annotation prefix (grammar.js `annotation`, ~:2190) and the ad-hoc port-selector operator (`ad_hoc_selector: expr @ ident(args)`, grammar.js ~:2049, prec.left 10). So an annotation on the line after ANY member that ends in an expression is joined onto that expression as a selector.

MEASURED 2026-10-06 on main fca4a9ad5f, fresh `reify eval`. These all FAIL with "Parse error: <L>:5: ambiguous member continuation: ... the grammar joins it onto that member's expression ...":
```
structure S {
    param a : Length = 5mm
    @solver_hint("discrete_set", standard_bolt_lengths)
    param b : Length = auto
}
```
- the same with `let sizes = [22mm, 24mm, 26mm]` before the annotation;
- the same with `constraint a >= 1mm` before it.

These succeed:
- the annotation as the FIRST member;
- the annotation after a `param x : Length = auto` line (the shipped examples/m11_annotations.ri BoltedPanel shape).

#7094's member_continuation guard (crates/reify-syntax/src/member_continuation.rs) is what turns the silent join into this error. Before #7094 the join compiled to "unknown selector kind '@solver_hint'".

CONSEQUENCE. That pre-#7094 error was misread on 2026-07-24 as "local-let discrete_set catalogs are compile-rejected" (docs/prds/v0_6/discrete-cost-minimisation.md §2.3, line ~81, and §9). The misreading became a scope restriction that Leo has now ruled lifted. More generally, a user cannot put `@solver_hint`, `@deprecated`, or any annotation on a member that follows an ordinary valued param, let or constraint. That is the normal layout of any realistic structure, and the new catalog-membership PRD's examples and ε's stock-cost example will hit it.

FIX (design call for the implementer; record it):
- (a) An annotation at the START of a member line (at or left of the member column) always begins a new member. This is newline-sensitive, so it probably belongs in the external scanner (tree-sitter-reify/src/scanner.c), the same place the member-continuation reading lives.
- (b) OR an ad-hoc selector's `@` must be on the same line as its base expression.
Either way:
- keep #7094's guard semantics for genuine continuations;
- regenerate the parser;
- add parse tests for every member kind before an annotation (valued param, auto param, let, constraint, sub);
- add an e2e `reify eval` on the three repros above (expect exit 0 and the hint attached to the right cell);
- check that existing `expr @selector(...)` uses that break across lines still parse, or are deliberately rejected with a clear diagnostic.

ACCEPTANCE: the three repros compile clean with the annotation attached to the following member; `git grep`-located ad_hoc_selector tests stay green; tree-sitter corpus tests green.
Analysis: ROOT CAUSE (verified in grammar.js on base eeb3590096). The literal `'@'` token is shared by two rules: `annotation` (grammar.js ~:2190, `'@' immediate_identifier ...`), which is a member via `commonMembers()` and a declaration via `_declaration`; and `ad_hoc_selector` (grammar.js ~:2050, `prec.left(10, seq(field('base', _expression), '@', field('selector', identifier), callTail))`). Extras include `/\s/`, so the grammar is newline-blind. After any member that ends in an `_expression`, the LR state has a shift/reduce choice on `@`. prec 10 makes the shift win, so the next line's annotation is absorbed as a selector. `= auto` is immune because `auto_keyword` is not an `_expression`.

REPRODUCED with the lane's built `target/debug/reify eval`:
- repro 1 (`param a : Length = 5mm` + `@solver_hint(...)` + `param b = auto`), repro 2 (`let sizes = [22mm, 24mm, 26mm]` + `@solver_hint("discrete_set", sizes)`) and repro 3 (`constraint a >= 1mm` + annot…[truncated, 10565 chars total]

Completed: Doc-chunk harness: make geometry.md's fence-arity cross-checks bidirectional and compile its prose .ri idioms
Description: This task holds the leftover scope of retired task #5926. The 2026-08-28 backlog sweep folded #5926 into #6956, but #6956's text kept only a one-line "derive coverage from chunk content" stub. Its in-flight branch (task/6956, checked 2026-09-30) does not deliver the items below. All facts were measured on main 89c8ccbbed.

1. ONE-DIRECTIONAL ARITY CROSS-CHECKS (the main item).
Two tests check fence call arity: `documented_oracle_arities_are_exercised_by_a_compiling_fence` (crates/reify-compiler/tests/harness_doc_chunks/geometry_chunk_smoke.rs:1621) and its twin `documented_measurement_arities_are_exercised_by_a_compiling_fence` (:1696). They are the ONLY checks of fence call arity. Each asserts only that every DOCUMENTED arity is exercised by a compiling fence (`in_fences.contains(arity)`). Neither checks the reverse, so a compiling fence can call a documented op at an arity the docs never state and nothing catches it.
Make both checks bidirectional. Each must fail if a documented arity has no compiling fence, OR if a compiling fence exercises an arity absent from the documented signatures. Diff the two sets from ONE derived source; after #8036, the fence side comes from doc_forms::call_forms.

2. PROSE .ri IDIOMS ARE NEVER COMPILED.
The harness compiles only the ```reify-tagged fences of crates/reify-mcp/src/tools/chunks/geometry.md (`reify_tagged_fences` on main). The .ri idioms written in prose or inline code elsewhere in the chunk are never compiled, so they go stale silently. Task 5623 hand-patched three such instances without fixing the cause.
Derive a compiled set from the chunk's actual content, not a hand-maintained list, so that a stale idiom goes RED. Choose the extraction rule and state it in the harness; for example, inline code spans that parse as a reify call form (chunk_prose.rs / doc_forms.rs hold the existing span machinery). Keep docs/reify-stdlib-reference.md in sync wherever it mirrors the same content.

3. NURBS CURVE FORM.
#6956's branch pins `nurbs_surface` in a compiling fence (commit a80377ce3f) and lists `nurbs(` as a sentinel. Confirm that a plain `nurbs(...)` curve call also compiles from a fence, and add a fence if it does not. If it is already pinned when this task runs, record that and skip.

Mutation-verify every new check. For example, add a test-local fence that calls a documented op at an undocumented arity: the check must go RED, and GREEN again once the fence is removed. Do not assert absolute counts.

ORDER: this task depends on #6956, which moves chunk I/O and fence parsing into shared modules. It also depends on #8036, which moves the fence side of both arity checks onto doc_forms::call_forms. That way the bidirectional diff is built on the single AST-derived source instead of the text scanners #8036 deletes.

Verify: cargo test -p reify-compiler --test harness_doc_chunks; cargo clippy -p reify-compiler --test harness_doc_chunks -- -D warnings.
Analysis: PREMISES (measured 2026-10-07 on branch base 757458f51b, which contains both dependencies: #6956 merged at 24eb34d148, #8036 at a61a1169fc).

ITEM 1 — bidirectional fence-arity cross-checks — IS ALREADY ON MAIN, delivered by #6956 after this task was filed against 89c8ccbbed. Commits 234b113fbf (test) and 1771f3fdad (feat) replaced the one-directional `documented_*_arities_are_exercised_by_a_compiling_fence` with `oracle_signature_arities_match_the_compiling_fences` / `measurement_signature_arities_match_the_compiling_fences` (geometry_chunk_smoke.rs:815/:881). Both route through `arity_drift` (:770), which diffs the documented set against the exercised set in BOTH directions and is hermetically unit-tested per direction (:1294-1345). #8036's b9ef237f94 then moved the fence side onto `doc_forms::fence_call_forms`, which goes through `call_forms` (the AST walk), so the diff is built on the one AST-derived source the task asks for. Architect mutation check: adding `let gap3 = distance(housing, bracket, housing)` to the FORM B fence and `let v2 = volume(plate, plate)` to the measurement fence turned both tests RED with "a ```reify fence ... calls `distance` at 3 argument(s), but no `distance(…) -> <Type>` signature documents that arity (documented arities: [2])" and the same message for `volume`. Restoring the file turned them GREEN again. No steps are planned for item 1.

ITEM 3 — the plain `nurbs(...)` curve form — IS ALREADY PINNED. geometry.md:226 sits inside the LENGTH-ARGS ```reify fence and calls `nurbs(1, 2, 0mm, 0mm, 0mm, 10mm, 0mm, 0mm, 1, 1, 0, 0, 1, 1)`. fence_gate::every_reify_tagged_fence_compiles_clean compiles that fence. `nurbs` is a sentinel in two tests: geometry_reify_fences_call_every_worked_example_form (:714) and documented_call_names_in_the_length_section_are_real_registry_entries (:1023). All three tests pass on the base. Recorded and skipped, as the task allows.

ITEM 2 — prose .ri idioms are never compiled — IS OPEN, and is this plan's scope. Today the harness compiles ```reify fences (fence_gate) and requires signature-shaped prose spans to be called by a fixture (unfenced_signature_gate, via doc_forms::doc_form_of_span). A CONCRETE idiom written in inline code is compiled by nothing. Examples: `translate(cylinder(r, h), 0mm, 0mm, -h/2)` and `intersects(box(10mm, 10mm, 10mm), bracket)`. doc_form_of_span deliberately reads such spans as "not a signature".

A throwaway probe (deleted, never committed) compiled each candidate span as `structure def ProseIdiom { let idiom = <span> }`. Its free identifiers are metavariables and each raises Error `UnresolvedName`. The compiler POISONS each one (expr.rs make_poison_literal, an anti-cascade fix), so no follow-on diagnostic results. Real defects still surface with poisoned siblings: `translate(cylinder(r, h), 0, 0, -h/2)` gives ArgTypeMismatch on dx/dy, `translate(cylinder(r, h), 0mm, 0mm)` gives "expects 4 arguments, got 3", and `helixx(…)` gives an UnresolvedFunction warning.

Extraction rule: a code span of unfenced prose that (1) opens call-shaped, i.e. a lowercase snake_case identifier directly followed by `(`; (2) is not a signature per doc_form_of_span; and (3) elides nothing, i.e. contains no ASCII `...` and no U+2026 `…`. Over the whole 17-chunk corpus this rule finds 11 idioms in geometry.md and 8 in units.md, and none anywhere else. In geometry.md, 10 compile clean modulo metavariables and ONE is stale: geometry.md:129 `translate(z=-height/2)`, which does not parse because translate has no keyword arguments. docs/reify-stdlib-reference.md:555 mirrors it verbatim. units.md's 3 non-clean idioms (`box(20, 20, 10)`, `box(0, 0, 0)`, `translate(g, 0, 0, 5)`) are forms that chunk quotes in prose on purpose as REJECTED. Gating units.md therefore first needs a notion of an idiom documented as rejected, so this task gates geometry only. This follows schematic_listing_gate.rs's LISTING_GATED_CHUNKS precedent, and the corpus widening is filed as a follow-up.

APPROACH. Add a new sibling module, prose_idiom_gate.rs. It follows the shape of unfenced_signature_gate.rs / schematic_listing_gate.rs: a pure violations function over `(stem, markdown)`, hermetic controls, and one real-chunk test over IDIOM_GATED_CHUNKS with a sentinel for anti-vacuity and no absolute counts. It reuses chunk_prose's unfenced prose and code spans. doc_forms gains a shared `span_callee`, the one definition of a call-shaped opening, which doc_form_of_span is refactored onto. signature_fixtures exposes its "discredits a call" diagnostic predicate, so the idiom gate and the fixture gate share ONE compile criterion; the idiom gate additionally exempts UnresolvedName by DiagnosticCode. TDD order: span_callee, then the hermetic gate logic, then the real-chunk wiring. That wiring goes RED on the live stale idiom. The fix lands in geometry.md and its stdlib-reference mirror. Afterwards the implementer mutation-verifies the live gate (re-introduce a bare `0`, see RED, restore). The hermetic tests also carry a stale/repaired mutation pair for the gate itself.

Verify: env cargo test -p reify-compiler --test harness_doc_chunks; cargo clippy -p reify-compiler --test harness_doc_chunks -- -D warnings; rustfmt --edition 2024 --check on the touched .rs files only (no cargo fmt — CLAUDE.md "Formatting").
Key decisions: Items 1 (bidirectional fence-arity cross-checks) and 3 (plain `nurbs(...)` curve fence) are already satisfied on main, so no steps are planned for them.; Extraction rule for a prose idiom: a code span of unfenced prose that OPENS call-shaped (`span_callee` is Some), is NOT a signature (`doc_form_of_span` is None), and elides nothing (no `...` and no `…`). "Parses as an expression containing a call" was rejected as the rule.; Metavariables are handled by exempting DiagnosticCode::UnresolvedName by its code. Free identifiers are not bound by guessed `param` types, and messages are not parsed.
Steps completed: 6/6
Modules: crates/reify-compiler/tests/harness_doc_chunks.rs, crates/reify-compiler/tests/harness_doc_chunks/doc_forms.rs, crates/reify-compiler/tests/harness_doc_chunks/geometry_chunk_smoke.rs, crates/reify-compiler/tests/harness_doc_chunks/prose_idiom_gate.rs, crates/reify-compiler/tests/harness_doc_chunks/signature_fixtures.rs, crates/reify-mcp/src/tools/chunks/geometry.md, docs/reify-stdlib-reference.md

solar_challenge config.py fact, read 2026-10-09 at main 3b788bb (task 561 architect): a fleet_distribution component's fixed value has two spellings, a bare number (int or float; bool counts too, read as 1.0 or 0.0) and {type: fixed, value: V}. _parse_distribution_spec turns both into one float spec, and _sample_from_distribution returns it with no RNG draw (pre_sample and prepare skip it).
