candidates.content: GOTCHA (INV-8 loop-blocking gate, dark-factory): shared/tests/loop_blocking_scan.py scans fused-memory/src ONLY, so a coroutine that calls a blocking helper living in another package (e.g. shared.safe_io.atomic_write_text) is invisible to it. If you migrate an allowlisted inline write in a fused-memory coroutine to such a helper WITHOUT an asyncio.to_thread hop, the site's shared/tests/loop_blocking_allowlist.py rows go stale (test_no_stale_blessings goes red) and the gate then reads clean, though the I/O still runs on the loop thread. The site is hidden, not fixed. Offload first (asyncio.to_thread(fn, ...), with fn as arg 0), migrate inside the hop, and delete the rows in the same change. Found planning task 5276 (manifest_stamping).

GOTCHA (task 3377) — an AST-based guard test that DISCOVERS its target modules by walking the suite must text-prefilter before parsing. Measured 2026-08-02 in fused-memory/tests: 249 `**/test_*.py` files totalling 9.8MB cost ~14-17s to `ast.parse` in full, and because pytest collects once per xdist worker (`-n auto`, 16 workers here) that cost is paid ~16x at collection. Fix: gate on a cheap `'<identifier>' in path.read_text()` substring check first, then parse only the survivors — 249 files scanned in ~30ms, 7 candidates parsed in ~100ms. This is safe (not a regression to string-grep) when the prefilter token is a strict SUPERSET of the AST criterion: an `ast.Call` to `select_graph` cannot exist without that identifier appearing literally in the source, so nothing can hide from it; every actual assertion stays AST-based. Two companion rules for derived-module-set guards: (1) keep a hand-verified floor set plus a test asserting discovery still finds it, else a criterion broken by a rename parametrizes over the empty set and reports green having checked nothing; (2) prove the guard by probe — drop a temporary module matching the criteria without the required call, confirm it fails, then delete it. See fused-memory/tests/test_falkor_index_barrier_guard.py.

GOTCHA (task 3288): fused-memory/tests/test_gather_convention_guard.py::DRAIN_ALLOWLIST keys each allowed `gather(..., return_exceptions=True)` site by (file, enclosing FUNCTION NAME) with an exact count, e.g. ('fused_memory/reconciliation/harness.py', 'run_loop'). If you extract or rename a function that holds an allowlisted gather, such as moving run_loop's body into a helper, the guard goes red: the moved gather is unallowlisted and the old entry is stale. To leave the allowlist untouched, keep the gather in the named function and extract the code AROUND it instead (task 3288 moved run_loop's startup prologue into _start_up()).

GOTCHA (dark-factory, measured 2026-09-26, task 5920): an "X does not block the event loop" test that asserts a FLOOR on ticker wake-ups (e.g. a 10ms `asyncio.sleep` ticker, `assert ticks >= 5` across a 200ms stub) is load-flaky mainly from IN-PROCESS GIL contention, not from host CPU load. Same-process CPU-bound threads compress it: 1 thread gave min 10 ticks, 2 gave min 7, 4 gave min 3 with 3/30 runs under 5. Cross-process load barely moves it: 12 CPU hogs pinned to the same core still gave min 16, and host load avg 213 on 32 cores gave min 11, because CFS favours the mostly-sleeping process on wakeup. Fix the oracle, not the window. For an AWAITABLE stub, use a loop-turn oracle: queue a marker via `loop.call_soon_threadsafe` on the test's loop, yield `await asyncio.sleep(0)` a bounded number of times, and assert the marker ran. Task 5920 adds this as `LoopFreedomProbe` in fused-memory/tests/_fm_helpers.py. For a SYNC blocking call offloaded via `asyncio.to_thread`, assert `threading.get_ident()` differs from the loop thread (task 5147 precedent in orchestrator/tests/test_verify_ruff_config_boundary.py).

GOTCHA (dark-factory, measured 2026-09-06, task 4592): PRODUCTION code that calls a method on a value which may be a mock ATTRIBUTE takes a silently-wrong branch AND leaks a coroutine. Distinct from the existing AsyncMock memories, which are all about test-side mock CONFIGURATION (side_effect shapes, pyright narrowing of .await_args); this one is about defensive shape checks in production code.

THE SHAPE. `recon_config_base_dir(data_dir)` guarded with `if not base.is_absolute(): base = Path.cwd() / base`. The recon stage suite drives BaseStage with an `AsyncMock` journal, so `journal.data_dir` is an AsyncMock, and `AsyncMock().data_dir.is_absolute()` returns a COROUTINE — not a bool. Measured: truthy, so `not <coroutine>` is False and the branch is skipped. Two consequences, only one visible:
- The branch decision was made by the truthiness of a coroutine object, not by any property of the path. It happened to select the safe branch here; nothing guarantees that in general, and an inverted guard would silently do the wrong thing.
- The coroutine is never awaited, so CPython emits `RuntimeWarning: coroutine 'AsyncMockMixin._execute_mock_call' was never awaited`, pointing at the PRODUCTION line, not the test.

Note MagicMock does NOT reproduce it (`MagicMock().data_dir.is_absolute()` returns a MagicMock, no coroutine), so a test parametrized only over MagicMock — the convenient default — cannot see this at all. Parametrize over `(MagicMock, AsyncMock)` when the suite actually uses AsyncMock.

THE FIX SHAPE: type-guard before calling, `if isinstance(base, PurePath) and not base.is_absolute():`. Verified `isinstance(AsyncMock(), PurePath)` is False, so a duck type is left uncoerced AND uncalled. This is strictly better than `Path(base)` coercion, which is worse than useless here: MagicMock and AsyncMock both implement `__fspath__`, so `Path(mock)` silently yields the RELATIVE path `AsyncMock/mock.data_dir/<id>` which downstream `mkdir(parents=True)` then really creates, littering the repo on every suite run.

DETECTION: `pytest <file> -W "always::RuntimeWarning" 2>&1 | grep "never awaited"`. `orchestrator/pyproject.toml` promotes this exact warning to an error in `filterwarnings`; `fused-memory/pyproject.toml` has NO filterwarnings (measured: grep -c == 0), so fused-memory leaks scroll past silently. Four pre-existing fused-memory sites were found this way and filed as follow-up ticket tkt_0RTB9Q8ZDQS85ZS2PZ2H0PRM20.

GOTCHA (dark-factory orchestrator tests, measured task 3790): changing a function from sync to async in `orchestrator/src/orchestrator/` forces a MECHANICAL but easy-to-miss migration in its test module, because `orchestrator/pyproject.toml` runs pytest-asyncio in STRICT mode (it sets no `asyncio_mode`; the repo-root `pyproject.toml`'s `asyncio_mode = "auto"` does NOT apply to the orchestrator package) AND promotes the warning "marked with '@pytest.mark.asyncio' but it is not an async function" to an ERROR-level filterwarning.

CONSEQUENCE: a sync `def test_` inside an `@pytest.mark.asyncio` class is a COLLECTION FAILURE, not a warning. So the sync/async split across test CLASSES is structural, not stylistic — you cannot simply mark the whole module. `test_flake_ledger.py` and `test_flake_recorder.py` both state this in their module docstrings; follow the same shape: put the newly-async tests in their own `@pytest.mark.asyncio` class and leave any class that drives still-sync helpers directly (e.g. `TestSuppressionStormStreak`, which calls `_bump_suppression_streak_and_maybe_escalate`) sync and unmarked.

THE FAILURE MODE THAT ACTUALLY BITES, and it is not the collection error — that one is loud. It is a caller you forgot to `await`: the call silently creates a coroutine, does nothing, and the test still passes if it only asserts on things the old sync path already did. Verify the RED phase fails with `TypeError: object NoneType can't be used in 'await' expression` (the test awaiting a still-sync function) BEFORE writing the implementation; that error is the proof the test is actually reaching the new colour.

RELATED, in production code: when adding an async side-effect beside existing sync ones under a `_guarded(what, fn)`-style per-signal isolation helper, add a separate `_guarded_async` rather than teaching `_guarded` to sniff its return value with `inspect.isawaitable`. A missed awaitability check drops the coroutine with NO log at all — a lost measurement that is invisible, which is the exact failure such helpers exist to prevent. See `flake_recorder.py::record_merge_flake_suppression`.

GOTCHA — "make it async" is NEITHER NECESSARY NOR SUFFICIENT for keeping work off the asyncio event-loop thread. Established 2026-08-06 (session deb-df-4070020, tasks 3778/3779) while designing a fix for fused-memory's loop stalls.

NOT NECESSARY: `asyncio.to_thread(subprocess.run, ...)` is blocking IO on a worker thread, not async IO, and it is the sanctioned house pattern in this repo — see middleware/task_interceptor.py:946 (wraps `recon_write_policy.check` with an explicit comment that inline git "would both block the event loop and hold this project's write lock for however long git takes") and middleware/task_curator.py:1622. A rule demanding native async would flag correct code.

NOT SUFFICIENT: `asyncio.create_subprocess_exec` still performs the fork/exec INLINE on the event-loop thread; only the subsequent I/O wait becomes awaitable. This was measured directly — sampling /proc/<pid>/task/<pid>/wchan through a live stall showed repeated `kernel_clone` (fork) on the loop thread. So converting a ~500-item subprocess fan-out to "async git" and changing nothing else would keep /health responsive while still burning 29-43s of wall clock and ~1,500 forks per reconciliation cycle.

The term that actually dominates is per-item cost x item count: 40 ms/call passes any "is this fast enough?" eyeball test, 514 x 40 ms does not. So the correct design predicate is BOUNDED OCCUPANCY of the loop thread — offload AND hoisted/bounded fan-out — not the IO modality.

GOTCHA (fused-memory reconciliation, discovered task 4723): adding an EscalationQueue call to any code path reached by `_on_task_done` silently turns existing tests into shared-filesystem writers. Two facts combine: `EscalationQueue.__init__` does `mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)` on `<project_root>/data/escalations`, and `test_targeted.py::_run_done_transition` defaults `project_root='/tmp/test'`. So a new escalation on a reconciliation path makes every pre-existing test that drives that verdict create `/tmp/test/data/escalations/` — cross-developer FS pollution plus a race under fused-memory's baked-in `-n auto --dist loadgroup` addopts. Nothing fails loudly; the pollution is invisible until two runs collide.

TWO THINGS TO DO. (1) Construct the queue LAZILY, inside the branch that actually files, never hoisted — `_escalation_pin_index_for` already documents this rule and is the in-file precedent. The strong test for it is `assert not (tmp_path / 'data' / 'escalations').exists()` on the negative verdicts: asserting merely "no escalation is pending" passes even when an eagerly-built queue left the directory behind. (2) grep for existing callers of the shared-root test helper and re-point the ones that now reach the new code at `tmp_path` — in task 4723 exactly one did (`test_every_verification_outcome_records_a_row[contradicted]`).

RELATED SHAPE, same file: `_sweep_escalate_l1` calls the blocking queue inline, `_escalation_pin_index_for` offloads through `asyncio.to_thread`. The offloaded one is the current rule (EscalationQueue is synchronous blocking FS I/O and these coroutines run on the shared fused-memory event loop); the inline call is older and should not be copied for new code.

REFINEMENT of the dark-factory norm "an AST source-introspection guard is rejected by reviewer_comprehensive even when it asserts over CODE structure" (mem0 08e278e7). That entry's bar — use an AST guard ONLY when the property has no runtime observation at all — has an established, ACCEPTED counterexample class in fused-memory that the entry does not name: the MIGRATION ROUTING GUARD family, built on the shared primitives in `fused-memory/tests/_ast_guard.py` (`parse_python_module`, `calls_named`). Four members as of task 3895: `test_falkor_probe_routing_guard.py`, `test_falkor_index_barrier_guard.py`, `test_gather_idiom_helper_routing.py`, `test_script_loader_routing_guard.py`.

THE DISCRIMINATOR, which matches 08e278e7's own blessed example (`test_the_reader_never_touches_the_producer`, "a negative over the whole module"): a routing guard asserts a NEGATIVE over a whole module — "this module contains no hand-rolled copy of shared helper X" — for a property whose runtime manifestation is COLLECTION-ORDER DEPENDENT and therefore has no stable runtime observation. The rejected task-4182 guard was the opposite shape: a POSITIVE structural proxy (count `_issue(...)` call sites, assert an `eval_id=` kwarg appears) standing in for something directly observable in a returned payload, and it was strictly weaker than the behavioural test that replaced it.

Concretely for task 3895: 42 test modules under `fused-memory/tests/` each carried a private `importlib.util.spec_from_file_location` loader, four sys.modules keys were installed by 2-7 modules apiece, and WHICH module object a given test saw depended on pytest collection order. No runtime assertion can pin that without importing sibling test modules (itself the interface smell the standing instructions warn about), and a fork that happened to win the ordering race in one run would pass anyway.

TWO CONSTRUCTION RULES, both already learned the hard way here:
1. Parse, never grep. These modules' docstrings must NAME the idiom to explain it — a grep over `fused-memory/tests/` for `spec_from_file_location` overcounts by 3 because `conftest.py` (x2) and `test_fm_helpers.py` (x1) only discuss it in prose. Same reason `test_falkor_probe_routing_guard.py` documents for parsing.
2. Exemptions belong in the scan DOMAIN, documented at the exemption — the general rule from the task-4345 gotcha (mem0 6a1903d3) — and their granularity must be `(module, enclosing function)`, not whole-module. `test_bake_off_storage_shape.py` needs both treatments at once: its module-level loader must migrate, while two of its tests deliberately load a `tmp_path` COPY of the script under a throwaway name and pop it in `finally`. A module-level carve-out would have silently excused the fork in the very file the guard claims to cover.

Also worth knowing: this repo writes forward-referencing directives into code naming not-yet-executed tasks. `conftest.py::_integration_collection_lease` already read "Via ``load_script_module`` -- do not add another local ``spec_from_file_location`` loader (tasks 3738/3895)" before task 3895 was ever dispatched. Grep for your own task id before assuming nothing in the tree anticipates you.

Asyncio test-harness gotcha (dark_factory, task 5939, measured): a harness that does `reader = asyncio.create_task(...)`, then `await asyncio.wait_for(gate_event.wait(), timeout=GUARD)` in a try/finally, has two failure-path defects. First, if the child raises BEFORE setting the event, the harness sits out the whole hang guard and reports a bare TimeoutError that hides the child's real error. Second, if the harness body raises, the un-awaited tasks leak 'Task exception was never retrieved' noise. Wrap the tasks in `async with asyncio.TaskGroup() as tasks:` and read `task.result()` after the block. A failing child then cancels the parent at once, so the real error surfaces in 0s. A failing body cancels and reaps the children. The happy path is unchanged. The failures come wrapped in an ExceptionGroup. Working example: shared/tests/test_async_sqlite_base.py::_collide_with_a_pinned_read.

GOTCHA (dark-factory shared/tests, task 5094): a "this scan reads nothing and parses nothing" test that monkeypatches the PUBLIC `ast.parse` to RAISE must scope that patch with `with monkeypatch.context() as patched:` around the call under test. It must not be a test-wide `monkeypatch.setattr`. pytest's own failure rendering calls `ast.parse` while the monkeypatch fixture is still active: `_pytest/_code/source.py::getstatementrange_ast`, and CPython's `traceback._should_show_carets`. So ANY failure in the test, including the intended RED (e.g. a TypeError), re-enters the raising stub and crashes the whole session with INTERNALERROR. A counting/delegating wrapper (like test_tree_scan_sharing._WorkCounter) is safe test-wide. A raising one is safe only inside the context, which undoes on exception before pytest renders the report. The same applies to a raising `pathlib.Path.read_text`.

GOTCHA (dark-factory, measured task 4484 amendment pass): an AST guard in shared/tests that resolves a BARE CALLEE NAME must honour Python scoping, or it manufactures false REDs on a merge-blocking gate. The house idiom of indexing defs with `ast.walk(tree)` into a `{name: [defs]}` map collects class methods and nested closures — names a bare `foo(...)` can never refer to from outside their scope — and then resolves any unbound Name against that map, including names that are the calling coroutine's own PARAMETERS or locals.

MEASURED, not hypothetical. loop_blocking_scan.py did exactly this and it produced a live blessed ledger row: `_verify_task(claim, probe)` in fused-memory/src/fused_memory/services/completion_claim_gate.py has a `probe` PARAMETER, which resolved to the unrelated nested `make_commit_probe.probe` (same file, line 717) that shells out to `git cat-file`. The sweep therefore reported `server/tools.py::create_mcp_server._completion_claim_gate -> verify_claims` as reaching subprocess.run, and a human blessed it as a real defect and filed a ticket for it. It reaches no primitive at all.

THE FIX SHAPE, which keeps the legitimate cases: (1) index only MODULE-LEVEL defs for the bare-name map — that is also exactly what `from X import Y` needs, since Y is by construction module-level in X; (2) for closures, walk the CALL's own enclosing-function chain via the parent map and look up defs bound directly in each scope (this is what makes `server/tools.py::create_mcp_server`'s 22 nested MCP handlers still resolve their sibling `_normalize_project_root`); (3) before resolving, treat the name as shadowed — and therefore silence — if any enclosing function binds it to a non-def: parameters plus every Store-context `ast.Name` (assignment/unpacking/walrus/for/with-as/except-as). Attribute and subscript targets bind no bare name, so check the Name node's own `ctx` rather than walking the target blindly.

Side effect worth knowing: restricting the index to module level made the whole-tree sweep ~2.5x faster (10.2s -> 4.0s over 167 files), because most spurious resolutions were dead-end recursions.

RELATED, same file, same class of defect but failing the other way: matching an OFFLOAD hop by attribute name alone (`<anything>.to_thread(x, ...)`) causes a MISS rather than silence — any object with a `to_thread` method exempts its argument from the sweep. Resolve the receiver (`asyncio.to_thread` / `anyio.to_thread.run_sync`, after `import X as Y` and `from X import Y` substitution) instead.

GOTCHA (CPython 3.13 asyncio): a cancellation that lands while `await asyncio.create_subprocess_exec(...)` is suspended after the fork (connecting pipes in _make_subprocess_transport) is handled by asyncio itself: `transp.close()` SIGKILLs only the DIRECT child, so a start_new_session child's group and grandchildren survive. `await transp._wait()` then waits for every pipe to close, so the cancelled call can HANG while a survivor holds stdout/stderr. The caller never gets a Process to group-kill. Fix pattern (task 6346, shared/src/shared/git_async.py::_spawn_session_leader): run the spawn as its own task and `await asyncio.shield(spawn)`. On BaseException, wait the spawn out with `asyncio.wait((spawn,))`, suppressing further CancelledError and never re-awaiting it, so a spawn failure cannot replace the interrupting exception. Then group-kill and reap any Process it produced, and re-raise. To reproduce deterministically in a test, condition-poll with sleep(0) until the child appears in /proc with ppid == os.getpid(), block the loop thread synchronously, then cancel.

GOTCHA (dark-factory, task 4484, measured 2026-09-03): a defect-class census must enumerate CALL SITES (callers), not the primitive's DEFINITION sites. Task 3778's INV-8 "blocking work on the event loop" census did the latter and its central claim was already false when written.

WHAT IT SAID (the census artifact is task 3778's own task DESCRIPTION, final paragraph "SCOPE OF THE DEFECT CLASS" — there is NO plans/ document, so search the task record, not the plans dir): "only 7 sync `subprocess.run` sites exist in the whole fused-memory server, across 3 modules — live_workflow_detector.py (3), recon_claim_verification_guard.py (3, already offloaded at its call sites), models/scope.py (1)".

TWO INDEPENDENT GAPS, both needed to explain the misses:
1. DEFINITION-SIDE ENUMERATION. It counted where the primitive is WRITTEN, then made a per-MODULE offload claim. One caller wrapping the helper makes the whole module read as clean and every other caller is invisible. The right question is "which callers reach this primitive with no intervening asyncio.to_thread/executor hop", which is the inverse traversal.
2. ONE-PRIMITIVE VOCABULARY. It enumerated `subprocess.run` ONLY, while INV-8's own Rule names "subprocess, network, filesystem, lock, sleep". `read_text`/`read_bytes`/`write_text`, `yaml.safe_load`/`safe_dump` and `fcntl.flock` were never in scope. Note pure-Python `yaml.safe_load` measured 8.15 ms for an 11 KB doc (task 4201) — comparable to a subprocess spawn, so it is NOT "just parsing".

COST OF THE GAP: tasks 4091 and 4201 each rediscovered one site by hand. A caller-side re-run (AST, fused-memory/src only) found 64 candidate sites across 14 modules / ~26 root causes, including TWO in task_curator.py that nobody had filed — `_maybe_blocklist_drop`->`load_blocklist` and `_maybe_route_deterministic`->`load_operational_registry`. All four un-offloaded task_curator.py sites are the SAME shape: an `async def _maybe_*` guard lazily loading a YAML registry from disk on the loop thread. A per-site census cannot see a shape; a caller-side one names all four at once.

TWO TRAPS WHEN BUILDING THE CALLER-SIDE SCAN. (a) Resolve callees through the calling module's `from X import Y` bindings, never by bare name — a common name like `check` or `run` binds to an unrelated module and a false RED in a whole-tree gate is worse than a miss, because it blocks every merge until someone blesses a non-defect, which trains reviewers to bless rows unread. Unresolvable must be silence. (b) Triage severity before filing: many hits are legitimately fine — `server/tools.py::_normalize_project_root`'s 22 async callers reach a CACHED `scope.resolve_main_checkout` (cold-miss only), and `server/main.py::run_server` runs before the loop serves traffic.

The repo already has the machinery: shared/tests/silent_fallthrough_scan.py exports `iter_first_party_files` (sentinel-validated, raises rather than scanning nothing) and `reconcile_against_allowlist` (Counter MULTISET, so a second site in an already-blessed function cannot pass silently). As of 2026-09-03 NO static guard for asyncio.to_thread / loop-blocking existed anywhere in the repo — all coverage was behavioural thread-identity tests on individual already-fixed sites, which by construction cannot find a site nobody thought to test.

GOTCHA (task 3271): when copying dark-factory's transcript-archival producer-hook shape into a new `finally`, check WHERE in the finally it lands. The shape's `except asyncio.CancelledError: raise` is load-bearing, but it only costs nothing at the END of a finally (as in TaskWorkflow._invoke). Placed ABOVE existing teardown it introduces the first await point, and under loop teardown/SIGTERM the re-raise skips everything below it — in run_dry_run_unblock that stranded a TaskConfigDir containing .credentials.json which was previously always reaped. Nest the archival in its own `try: ... finally: <teardown>` so cleanup runs either way. Note asyncio.to_thread does propagate a CancelledError raised inside the worker as a normal exception, so a MagicMock(side_effect=asyncio.CancelledError()) on the archiver is a faithful test driver for this.

GOTCHA (dark-factory): a fan-out of git calls through shared.git_async.run_git (default bounded=True) is ALREADY capped. Its per-event-loop semaphore MAX_CONCURRENT_SPAWNS (8) limits how many git processes are in flight. So an asyncio.gather over 50 per-branch probes runs at most 8 at a time. Do not add a second semaphore around such a gather, because it would restate that bound (SPOT). Do not cite "N concurrent git spawns" as a defect without checking whether the caller uses run_git. Verified for task 4874's landed_on_main.py own-commit fan-out on 2026-10-02.

dark-factory has a SECOND family of AST structural guards, in `shared/tests/`, distinct from the orchestrator/tests "chokepoint guard" family documented in memory 93690770 — reach for this one when the invariant spans PACKAGES rather than living inside orchestrator/src.

THE TRIAD CONVENTION: `<name>_scan.py` (pure scanner) + `<name>_allowlist.py` (dispositioned baseline) + `test_<name>_gate.py` (assertions). Live instances: `silent_fallthrough_*`, `loop_blocking_*`, `config_dir_archival_*`. The scanner takes a `{relpath: source}` MAPPING and does no filesystem I/O, so unit tests feed synthetic modules directly; the gate test supplies real files. A single-file variant (visitor + allowlist + tests in one module) is the right size for a small site population — precedent `fused-memory/tests/test_gather_convention_guard.py`.

THE ENUMERATOR: `shared/tests/silent_fallthrough_scan.py::iter_first_party_files(repo_root)` yields first-party non-test source across 7 scope roots, excluding path components `mem0`/`graphiti`/`tests` and files `test_*.py`/`conftest.py`. It validates repo_root against `shared/src`+`orchestrator/src` sentinels and RAISES rather than yielding a vacuously empty scan, so you must hand it the repo root — narrowing the scope is done by FILTERING its output on a relpath prefix, never by passing a narrower root (`test_loop_blocking_gate.py:955-975` states this explicitly). Reach the root from `shared/tests/` as `Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]`; `shared/tests/conftest.py` appends REPO_ROOT to sys.path (append, never insert(0), or subprojects resolve as namespace packages).

TWO STANCES WORTH COPYING VERBATIM, both from `loop_blocking_scan.py`'s docstring: "an unresolvable name is silence, never a finding" — a false RED in a merge-gating whole-tree sweep "trains reviewers to bless rows unread and destroys the gate's value"; and a `SyntaxError` in one module contributes nothing and never raises, so a mid-edit file cannot turn the gate red. The dual is also true and less often stated: shipping a guard whose allowlist already contains a live unfixed instance of the defect it guards does the same damage. Always pair with a non-vacuity floor set BELOW the measured file count, whose failure message says the SWEEP is broken, not the tree (`test_loop_blocking_gate.py::TestSweepIsNotVacuous`).

CORRECTION to memory 93690770, which claims "No test in the tree uses ast.NodeVisitor/visit_Call — the convention is plain ast.walk plus hand-rolled iter_child_nodes recursion." That holds for orchestrator/tests only. `fused-memory/tests/test_gather_convention_guard.py` defines `_GatherSiteVisitor(ast.NodeVisitor)` with a parent-map for enclosing-function attribution, and `silent_fallthrough_scan.py` exports `_build_parent_map` / `_compute_qualname` / `_content_hash` / `violation_key` for reuse by sibling scanners. Verified 2026-09-19 at task/3288 base c4b3a2f033. Also note `silent_fallthrough_scan` keys findings on `(relpath, qualname, content_hash)` and NEVER on lineno, which drifts on every unrelated edit above the site.

GOTCHA (asyncio, Python >= 3.12): this applies when a test wraps a call in its own real-clock `asyncio.wait_for(..., N)` guard and production code inside has its own `wait_for`/`timeout` budget B. If the host stalls for at least N-B seconds (xdist CPU starvation, a GC pause), both deadlines come due in the same event-loop pass. asyncio then turns the cancellation into TimeoutError only for the OUTERMOST expired scope, which is the test's guard, so the test fails even though production timed out correctly. Measured on task 6482: `tests/test_index_provisioning_wiring.py::TestStartupSweep::test_a_hung_falkordb...`, with N = 3*B = 0.3s. A cheaper permanent armor than a host-stall wrapper is to assert `loop.time() - started == pytest.approx(B)` under `shared.testing_virtual_clock.virtual_clock_test`. That check is exact on the virtual clock and fails on every run on a real loop, so removing the decorator goes RED deterministically.

GOTCHA (measured task 3778, 2026-09-01): when you make a FAIL-OPEN function async, sync monkeypatch fakes at that seam do not fail loudly — they degrade SILENTLY, and some tests keep passing FOR THE WRONG REASON. A green run is therefore not evidence you finished the async propagation.

THE MECHANISM. `is_workflow_live_for_task` / `detect_live_workflow` are wrapped by callers in `try: ... except Exception: treat as not-live` (harness.py integrity gate; task_knowledge_sync._render_live_workflow_section). Task 3778 made them coroutines. A leftover sync fake `def _fake(_tid, _pr, **kw): return True` is still CALLED fine — the failure is one line later, when `await <bool>` raises TypeError. That TypeError is swallowed by the deliberate fail-open handler and becomes "not-live". So:
- A test asserting live/suppressed FAILS loudly. You find it.
- A test asserting NOT-live / "section absent" / "escalation fires" PASSES — because fail-open produces exactly the expected answer by accident. You do not find it.
The second class is the dangerous one: it survives the refactor as a test that no longer tests anything, and it will not re-redden when the behaviour it guards actually breaks.

CONCRETE INSTANCES FOUND. After merging main into the 3778 lane, main had contributed test classes written against the PRE-async contract:
- test_stage1.py TestStage1RemediationPayloadLiveWorkflowSection (main task 3839): 3 sync `_fake_detect`. ONE failed; TWO passed vacuously (both assert "### Live-Workflow Signals" absent). One of those two even sets is_live=True and would have passed no matter what.
- test_harness.py TestRemediationSnapshotClockPinnedToTreeRead (main task 2964): 1 sync `_fake_is_live`. Failed loudly only because it asserts SUPPRESSION.
Ironically the lane's own helper `_async_is_live` (test_harness.py:38) documents this exact hazard — "a sync fake would still be CALLED, but awaiting its bool return raises" — and the merge reintroduced it anyway.

PRACTICE.
1. Do not audit by running the suite. Audit by GREP: `grep -n "def _fake_is_live\|def _fake_detect" <testfile> | grep -v async` enumerates every unconverted fake in one shot, passing or not. That is the only check that sees the vacuous ones.
2. Re-run that grep AFTER every merge from main, not just after your own edits. A long-lived lane that changes a function's sync/async contract has an ONGOING conflict with main: main keeps adding call sites and fakes against the old contract, and git merges them cleanly because there is no textual conflict. The 3778 merge was clean and still landed three broken seams.
3. The same reasoning applies to any await-a-coroutine seam guarded by a broad `except Exception` fail-open — this is a property of fail-open + async, not of this detector. Consider an `inspect.iscoroutinefunction` assertion on the patched attribute (test_harness.py:13916 already does this) so the seam's contract is pinned by a test rather than by convention.
4. Sibling defect from the same merge: `_assemble_remediation_payload` (sync) called the now-async `_build_live_workflow_section` without await, interpolating a literal `<coroutine object ...>` into an LLM prompt payload. This one only surfaced as a RuntimeWarning plus a content assertion — no exception. When converting a method to async, grep for ALL its callers, including sync ones that merely f-string the result.

GOTCHA (dark-factory, measured task 4722): in an async test that drives a never-returning production loop with a poll-and-cancel driver, a spy's signal must denote the EFFECT, not the call's ENTRY — otherwise the driver cancels the very work it is waiting for, and the test blames correct production code for a slow host.

MECHANISM. `fused-memory/tests/test_harness.py::_drive_project_loop_until` polls its predicate every 10ms and cancels the driven `_project_loop` on the first tick where it holds. The deferred-write ordering tests spied `EventBuffer.mark_run_complete` with `signal.append(True)` BEFORE `await original(...)`. That method is `async with self._txn() as db: await db.execute('DELETE FROM reconciliation_locks ...')` with the commit in `_txn`'s exit — at least two awaits after entry — and `EventBuffer._txn` catches `BaseException` deliberately (so cancellation cannot leave sqlite's writer lock open), which means it ROLLS THE DELETE BACK. The lock row survives, and the test fails with its own ordering-bug diagnostic. Measured window: entered t=18.8ms, returned t=24.3ms — ~5.5ms against a 10ms tick, so it only loses under the 32-worker parallel suite.

FIX SHAPE, and why it generalises. Append the signal AFTER the await, and deliberately NOT in try/finally: a call that RAISED did not have its effect, so it must not be reported as complete. Extract it into a factory (`_make_completion_spy(original) -> (spy, signal)`) rather than fixing inline — the defect is a shape, not a typo, and a factory makes the property unit-testable with NO clock (assert the signal is unset at entry, set after return, the return value is forwarded, and a raising call leaves it empty). An inline fix is correct today and unverifiable tomorrow.

REPRODUCING/GUARDING a race like this: do NOT rely on host load. Inject an explicit `await asyncio.sleep(0.05)` (5x the poll tick, three orders of magnitude inside the driver's 15s failsafe) into a NEW test and leave the original running at natural speed — a guard that only fires sometimes is a second flake, not a regression guard.

REJECTED ALTERNATIVE, with the reason: making the predicate awaitable and polling the LEVEL (`not await is_full_recon_active(pid)`) instead. The invariant is an EDGE (this call released it), and the level is re-entered when the loop re-claims via `mark_run_active`, so a 10ms poller can miss the window and report "never released" for a lock that was released and legitimately retaken.

VERIFY BY MUTATION, not by the green run: re-inject each bug and confirm the intended assertion message fires. Here all three held — entry-signalling -> "Lock was not released after replay raised"; bare reorder (inner try/finally dropped) -> "mark_run_complete was never called"; release-before-replay -> call_order ['complete', 'replay']. That last one is what proves moving an ordering spy's append after its await keeps the ordering test load-bearing (under the bug the call both starts and returns before the other spy is entered, so the recorded order is unchanged).

content: GOTCHA (dark-factory, new async code in fused-memory/src): two whole-repo AST guards catch it that a targeted pytest run never reaches. (1) shared/tests/test_loop_blocking_gate.py lives in the SHARED package (run it from shared/), so even a full fused-memory suite misses it: any Path.mkdir / is_file / open inside an async def needs asyncio.to_thread, or a row in shared/tests/loop_blocking_allowlist.py. (2) fused-memory/tests/test_gather_convention_guard.py rejects raw asyncio.gather(..., return_exceptions=True) outside utils/async_utils.py and its DRAIN_ALLOWLIST. Route result-bearing fan-outs through gather_collect / gather_or_raise. A teardown that cancels its OWN tasks must not use gather_collect, which re-raises the children's CancelledError; use `if tasks: await asyncio.wait(tasks)` instead. Found on task 6137 (services/overreach_shadow.py).

candidates.content: In reify, `reify check` renders only the diagnostic MESSAGE on stderr (e.g. `error: unresolved type: obj.width`) and never the `DiagnosticCode` — measured against target/debug/reify, and `check` has no `--verbose` flag to expose more. Consequence for test design: a CLI-level regression test in crates/reify-cli/tests/harness_cli/ can only pin diagnostic PROSE plus the exit code, even though the compiler-level house convention (crates/reify-compiler/tests/unresolved_diagnostic_code_audit_tests.rs) deliberately pins `d.code == Some(DiagnosticCode::UnresolvedType)` rather than message text because prose goes stale on rewording. Note also that code coverage is uneven at the source: `unresolved type: {}` attaches DiagnosticCode::UnresolvedType (reify-compiler/src/guards.rs:175, entity.rs:1962) but `sub-component "{}" references unknown structure "{}"` (reify-compiler/src/conformance/sub_component_validation.rs:88) attaches NO code at all, so a code-based pin is unavailable for the sub-position diagnostic at any level.

Reify CLI diagnostics: `report_eval_output` (crates/reify-cli/src/main.rs) prints only `"{severity}: {message}"` and DROPS `diag.code`, and `DiagnosticCode` (crates/reify-core/src/diagnostics.rs) has no `as_str()`/`Display` impl at all — its only stable string form is the serde/Debug variant name. So a typed `DiagnosticCode` is INVISIBLE on the CLI surface: a `reify check`/`build`/`eval` integration test cannot assert code identity unless the mnemonic is ALSO embedded as a literal prefix in the message text (the `E_DUP_MEMBER_KEY` / `I_DISPLAY_OUTPUT_DEFERRED` / `W_STEP_AP242_FALLBACK` pattern). To satisfy INV-SF-6 end-to-end, set `.with_code(..)` for engine-level assertions AND embed a `pub const E_*` marker for CLI-level ones.

The reify CLI prints diagnostics as `{severity}: {message}` and never prints a DiagnosticCode name (DiagnosticCode has no Display/as_str; verified 2026-10-06 against FeaUnderConstrained, which is coded yet only its message reaches stderr). So a PRD leaf signal or a D3 probe binding `stderr_contains <CodeName>` can never match; user-facing signals must assert the MESSAGE text, and tests assert the code by identity (`code == Some(DiagnosticCode::X)`). Also: `reify check` never dispatches FEA compute trampolines (it prints `no registered compute trampoline (falling back to body-inlining)` and exits 0), so an FEA Error-severity exit is observable only through `reify eval`/`build`; and a warm persistent-cache hit replays NO diagnostics while the in-process cache re-emits no structured_detail, so CLI Warning/Info signals hold only on a cold cache (fresh REIFY_CACHE_DIR) and e2e tests must read the first eval.

A `DiagnosticCode` on a reify diagnostic makes it EXEMPT from CLI deduplication: `dedup_diagnostics` (crates/reify-cli/src/main.rs:3222-3285) short-circuits on `d.code.is_some() || seen.insert(...)`. So any coded diagnostic reaches the user unfiltered, and volume must be bounded at the PRODUCER — one diagnostic per declaration naming the full affected set (the #5014 collateral-observability pattern), never one per trial/component/relation. Separately, `reify check` does NOT fail on Error-severity diagnostics: `check_fails` (main.rs:2843) keys only on `ConstraintOutcome`; `cmd_eval` (:2209) and `build_is_success` (:2834) are the surfaces that do gate on `Severity::Error`. Assert Error-severity acceptance signals through `reify eval`/`build`, not `reify check`, until task #5403's exit-gate leaf lands.

Reify CLI diagnostic mnemonics (E_*/W_*) must be embedded as a prefix in the Diagnostic.message string to be user-visible: `reify check`/`parse_and_compile` render diagnostics as `eprintln!("{}: {}", severity, message)` (crates/reify-cli/src/main.rs:174) and never print the typed Diagnostic.code field. Precedent: E_MODULE_PATH_MISMATCH / W_MODULE_DECL_MISSING in crates/reify-compiler/src/compile_builder/pre_pass.rs build `Diagnostic::error(format!("E_MODULE_PATH_MISMATCH: ..."))`. Attach `.with_code(DiagnosticCode::X)` ALSO, for structured LSP/MCP consumers. cmd_check exits non-zero whenever any compiled.diagnostics entry has Severity::Error.

In reify, `reify check`/`reify eval` render diagnostics as `eprintln!("{}: {}", diag.severity, diag.message)` (crates/reify-cli/src/main.rs:211 and :284) — the CLI prints NEITHER the DiagnosticLabel text NOR the SourceSpan NOR the DiagnosticCode. So a tests/prd-gate probe-set `stderr_contains` predicate can only match the message string; anything carried in a label (e.g. the ctor-conformance `expected 'X', got 'Y'` detail) or a span is unobservable at the CLI and must be asserted at the Rust level instead. Diagnostic mnemonics like `E_CTOR_UNKNOWN_FIELD:` are matchable only because they are baked into the message text as a prefix, not because the code is printed.

Reify CLI diagnostic rendering: `reify eval`/`check` print diagnostics as `severity: message` only (report_eval_output at reify-cli/src/main.rs:2493, plus the compile-diag loops at :206/:279/:1417) — the typed `DiagnosticCode` is used for internal logic (exit codes, GD&T gating) but is NEVER rendered to output. Consequently, to make a `W_*`/`E_*` PRD-prose mnemonic user-observable on the CLI, it must be embedded in the Diagnostic MESSAGE text (the established W_DFM_MIN_WALL prefix pattern in reify-stdlib/src/dfm.rs:1223, asserted via stderr.contains in cli_dfm_thickness.rs). The enum variant itself stays PascalCase (e.g. GeometryUnbounded↔E_GEOMETRY_UNBOUNDED).

reify-core DiagnosticCode is a fieldless Copy enum (~212 unit variants) and Diagnostic carries only severity/message/labels/code/candidates, so a PRD cannot specify payload-carrying codes like `E_X { requested, max }`. The CLI (reify-cli main.rs report_eval_output) prints `{severity}: {message}` and never renders the code, so `error[E_CODE]:` output does not exist. Convention used by implicit-solids (following W_MODULE_DECL_MISSING): attach the code with .with_code(..) AND put the E_/W_ SCREAMING_SNAKE mnemonic as the message prefix; tests assert code identity at engine level and the prefix at CLI; numeric payloads are asserted through typed Rust returns, never parsed from text.

Reify DiagnosticCode (crates/reify-core/src/diagnostics.rs) is #[non_exhaustive] with no code->severity or Display match anywhere: adding a variant needs NO match-arm updates, severity is set at the Diagnostic::warning()/error() call site (not derived from the code), and the user-facing `W_*`/`E_*` mnemonic lives only in the message-text `format!`, not on the enum. So a new diagnostic = add a doc'd variant + emit `Diagnostic::warning(format!("W_FOO: ...")).with_code(DiagnosticCode::Foo)`. Coupling-style diagnostics surface on `reify check` because engine.check() routes through eval(); eval() extends result diagnostics from resolve_order's `ro` OUTSIDE the has_active_solver gate (engine_eval.rs ~4613), while eval_cached() deliberately does NOT re-emit them (eval owns emission).

Reify diagnostic codes are a typed `DiagnosticCode` enum in crates/reify-core/src/diagnostics.rs (#[non_exhaustive], PascalCase serde wire format), NOT string codes. PRD-prose mnemonics like `E_GEOMETRY_UNBOUNDED` map to a PascalCase variant (`GeometryUnbounded`). Attach via `Diagnostic::error(msg).with_code(DiagnosticCode::X).with_label(DiagnosticLabel::new(span, msg))`. Convention: tests assert on `Diagnostic.code` (typed), never on message substrings, so rewording messages doesn't break tests. `reify_core` re-exports Diagnostic, DiagnosticCode, DiagnosticLabel, Severity.

Reify fact (2026-06-19): How to add a new compiler diagnostic code. `DiagnosticCode` lives in crates/reify-core/src/diagnostics.rs as a `#[non_exhaustive]` PascalCase enum (serde rename_all=PascalCase for the wire format). Variants carry a doc comment naming their PRD-prose mnemonic, e.g. the variant `GeometryUnbounded` ↔ mnemonic `E_GEOMETRY_UNBOUNDED`. A diagnostic attaches a code via the builder `.with_code(DiagnosticCode::X)`. NOTE: the current empty-collection-literal warnings (reify-compiler/src/expr.rs, "cannot infer element type of empty list literal, defaulting to Real" etc.) carry NO DiagnosticCode — they are bare `Diagnostic::warning(...)`, so tests must match on message text unless a code is added. Reify functions support type parameters (`fn ident<T>(xs: List<T>) -> ...` parses and works); empty set/map literals use the keyword-prefixed forms `set { }` / `map { }` (bare `{}` is a parse error). `Type` (List/Set/Map/Option/TypeParam/Error/dimensionless_scalar) lives in crates/reify-core/src/ty.rs; there is no `Type::Unknown`.

In reify-compiler, diagnostic message prose is NOT a structured contract — `crates/reify-compiler/tests/unresolved_diagnostic_code_audit_tests.rs` pins only `DiagnosticCode` (e.g. UnresolvedType) via `.with_code(...)`, and explicitly disavows asserting on message text. So you can safely reword a diagnostic's top-line `Diagnostic::error(format!(...))` message as long as the `.with_code()` is unchanged. The one exception: `type_expr_kind_dispatch_tests.rs` does `.message.contains("unresolved field type")` but only for the DimensionalOp field-domain arm, not other arms.

reify's DiagnosticCode enum (crates/reify-core/src/diagnostics.rs) has NO strum derive and NO exhaustive match anywhere, so adding a variant touches only diagnostics.rs — it is #[non_exhaustive] with feature-gated serde rename_all="PascalCase". The E_*/W_* names in PRDs are prose mnemonics, NOT machine-generated: serde renders a variant as its bare PascalCase identifier (e.g. "CtorUnknownField"), so an E_* code is only observable in `reify check` stderr if the mnemonic is embedded as a message prefix (precedents: E_TYPE_ARG_ON_TRAIT at type_resolution.rs:1792, E_EXPR_NESTING_TOO_DEEP, W_MODULE_DECL_MISSING). The repo's completeness discipline is a hand-written per-variant serde-PascalCase + with_code round-trip test pair in diagnostics.rs's inline mod tests, which only run under `cargo test -p reify-core --features serde --lib` — the serde feature is off by default, so a bare --lib run silently skips every one of them.

Gotcha: reify-core Diagnostic::error/warning/info set code:None and `.with_code()` is optional, so a stdlib `diagnose` classifier can emit a CODE-LESS Severity::Error Diagnostic without adding a DiagnosticCode enum variant. Adding a variant would expand scope to crates/reify-core/src/diagnostics.rs AND its exhaustive code-enumeration tests (~diagnostics.rs:2702-2758). Also: stdlib's `*_diagnose` re-export only becomes user-observable once reify-expr/src/lib.rs (~:1271, the builtin-fallthrough sink) calls it — re-exporting alone (like stackup_diagnose/fea_diagnose) does not surface the diagnostic end-to-end.

When emitting a Diagnostic in Reify whose failure mode is well-typed, attach a DiagnosticCode via .with_code(...) and write tests that match on d.code == Some(DiagnosticCode::Variant) instead of d.message.contains("..."). The wire identifier on the MCP boundary is the variant name (PascalCase); the mapping happens in crates/reify-cli/src/mcp_context.rs. Do not collapse Diagnostic.code (typed enum, internal) with DiagnosticInfo.code (String, wire) — they serve different layers.

Reify: to cheaply validate a candidate .ri fixture shape during planning (no cargo build), a warm lane's prebuilt `target/debug/reify` can run `reify check <file>.ri` and `reify eval <file>.ri` on a scratch file under /tmp. It prints per-constraint OK lines, warnings and exit status. Caveat: the CLI never renders a DiagnosticCode; a code is visible only when its mnemonic is spelled into the message text (e.g. W_MODULE_DECL_MISSING). So CLI end-to-end tests (crates/reify-cli/tests/harness_cli/cli_check_*.rs) must assert stderr text, while compiler-level tests assert `d.code == Some(DiagnosticCode::…)`.

reify-core's `DiagnosticCode` enum (crates/reify-core/src/diagnostics.rs:156, ~202 variants, `#[non_exhaustive]`) has NO `impl` block anywhere in the workspace — no as_str/Display/FromStr/ALL const/severity map, and zero `DiagnosticCode::X =>` match arms repo-wide. Its LSP wire string comes free from `serde(rename_all = "PascalCase")` (reify-lsp/src/convert.rs:203), so a variant is added by appending it at the END of the enum with a doc comment and nothing else. `W_*`/`E_*` tokens are PRD-prose mnemonics carried in the doc comment and as the message-text prefix, not the wire string. Precedent to copy: `SubbodyObjectiveIgnored` (:3945), emitted at reify-compiler/src/entity.rs:3767 as `Diagnostic::warning(format!("W_SUBBODY_OBJECTIVE_IGNORED: ..."))`.with_code(..).with_label(..). Keep `.with_code(` tight to the constructor: reify-audit's PDIAG scanner only looks 15 non-comment lines ahead and the widest landed gap is already exactly 15.

reify-cli is BIN-ONLY (no lib.rs), so `reify check` must be mirrored, not imported. Its in-process sequence (crates/reify-cli/src/main.rs parse_and_compile_with_cfg): (1) reify_compiler::parse_with_stdlib(src, ModulePath::single(file_stem)); any ParsedModule.errors stops the run, and ParseError carries NO DiagnosticCode. (2) reify_compiler::module_dag::compile_entry_with_stdlib_cfg_checked(&parsed, &ModuleResolver::new(parent, parent.join("crates/reify-compiler/stdlib")), &CfgSet::host_default() + --cfg, &reify_constraints::SimpleConstraintChecker); any Severity::Error stops before eval. (3) reify-eval Engine::check plus CLI post-processing (drop_falsified_indeterminate_diagnostics, CHECK_ERROR_EXIT_ALLOWLIST). Diagnostic has no phase field: the phase is whichever stage produced it. W_MODULE_DECL_MISSING / E_MODULE_PATH_MISMATCH are uncoded (message prefix only).

reify CLI diagnostics drop the SPAN as well as the code, so `reify check` cannot be the instrument for any corpus sweep that needs positions. Every print site is `eprintln!("{}: {}", diag.severity, diag.message)` (crates/reify-cli/src/main.rs:283-285 in parse_and_compile_with_cfg, :210-212, :2851-2853 in report_eval_output) — it reads neither `diag.code` NOR `diag.labels[].span`, so there is no file, line, column or caret in the output, and no `--json`/`--format` flag exists on `check` (CHECK_USAGE at main.rs:446; unknown flags hard-error at :509-513). No subcommand takes more than one file. Two consequences for mechanizing a sweep over many `.ri`: (1) the in-process API is the right instrument — `reify_compiler::parse_with_stdlib(&src, ModulePath::single(stem))` then `compile_with_stdlib(&parsed)`, reading `CompiledModule.diagnostics` (crates/reify-compiler/src/types.rs:454) and converting `labels[0].span.start` with `reify_core::byte_offset_to_line_col`; prior art is `ctor_conformance_one`/`ctor_conformance_corpus_walk` in crates/reify-compiler/tests/harness_compilation_surface/examples_smoke.rs. (2) The ONLY structured CLI-adjacent surface that does carry position+code is `reify mcp-server`'s `DiagnosticInfo` (file_path/line/column/severity/message/code — crates/reify-cli/src/mcp_context.rs:241-251), but it needs a JSON-RPC session per file. Caveat when comparing to CLI behaviour: `reify check` uses `module_dag::compile_entry_with_stdlib_cfg_checked` (follows #cfg-gated user imports, SimpleConstraintChecker), whereas `compile_with_stdlib` is single-file with CompileTimeIndeterminateChecker — that difference is why multi-module examples sit in examples_smoke's SKIP_SET. Measured 2026-08-27 at main 271e76a577.

Reify diagnostics: the `Parse error: ` prefix is CLI presentation, NOT parser output. `crates/reify-cli/src/main.rs:195` (and :254) does `eprintln!("Parse error: {}", err.message)`, while `reify_syntax` / `reify_compiler::parse_with_stdlib` put only the bare message (e.g. `syntax error: rad`, built at `crates/reify-syntax/src/ts_parser.rs:511` and sibling ERROR arms) into `ParsedModule.errors[].message`; `reify-test-support::parse_errors_as_diagnostics` (helpers.rs:261-270) forwards it verbatim with no prefix. A library-level test asserting the CLI-rendered `Parse error: <msg>` is therefore unsatisfiable — reconstruct it from a documented prefix constant, or assert the bare message. Separately, parse errors are a channel distinct from compile diagnostics: `CompiledModule.diagnostics` never contains them, and `compile_source_with_stdlib` PANICS on parse errors, so use `compile_source_with_stdlib_allow_parse_errors` to observe one as a `Severity::Error`.

content: reify gotcha: `reify check` prints compile diagnostics as only `"{severity}: {message}"` (crates/reify-cli/src/main.rs parse_and_compile_with_cfg) — the DiagnosticCode is never rendered. A CLI-level test or PRD signal that must observe a specific code (e.g. "E_SKETCH_* fires at reify check") therefore relies on the house convention of prefixing the message with the mnemonic (`E_DUP_MEMBER_KEY: …`, `E_OBJECTIVE_INERT: …`, `E_PRIV_REDUNDANT: …`) in addition to `.with_code(...)`; compiler-level tests should still assert the typed code.

candidates.content:
solar_challenge pytest-xdist gotchas (task 847, measured 2026-10-18 at task/847 a7ae4f4).
- `UV_OFFLINE=1 uv run --locked --extra dev --extra web --with pytest-xdist pytest ... -n N` resolves pytest-xdist 3.8.0 from uv's cache with no network.
- tests/unit/web_jobs/test_job_manager.py::TestJobManagerUnrecordedFailures::test_a_failure_whose_message_sqlite_cannot_store_is_logged_for_each_table_and_still_reported deterministically crashes its xdist worker. execnet raises UnicodeEncodeError on a lone surrogate '\udcff' while sending the test's report; the session ends INTERNALERROR (exit 3) and the rest of that worker's queue never runs. It passes serially. To time the suite under -n, --deselect that node-id; follow-up ticket tkt_0RVXZBQ7ZP0QS2AX1TM04XK4JE (escalation esc-847-1).
- A throwaway profiling plugin under xdist must write per process: every worker and the controller load it, so key its output directory on os.environ.get('PYTEST_XDIST_WORKER', 'controller'), or the workers clobber one file.
- Each worker collects every item: ~4.3-5.7 s CPU per worker, the same as one serial collection.

solar_challenge gotcha, measured 2026-10-03 on main fbfee17 (task 383 architect): pytest-xdist is not in uv.lock or pyproject.toml. So `uv run --locked --extra dev --extra web pytest ... -n 4` exits 4 with "unrecognized arguments: -n" after about 4 s, having run nothing. Run the verify selection serially instead: `-m 'not slow and not e2e' --ignore=tests/e2e --ignore=tests/interpreter_matrix` gave 3021 passed, 105 deselected in 8m33s, max RSS about 1.1 GB.

solar_challenge pytest gotcha (task 952 architect, measured 2026-10-18 at base ede1d99, pytest 9.0.3). For every test phase, pytest's LoggingPlugin attaches caplog's handler AND a separate report handler to the ROOT logger (_pytest/logging.py, _runtest_for). The report handler's text becomes the report's 'Captured log <when>' section, even for a passing test, with the formatted traceback of every logger.exception record. So any record caplog sees also lands in the report, and caplog's API cannot keep it out. To keep a record's text out of the report, e.g. a traceback holding a lone surrogate that a pytest-xdist worker cannot send, collect it with a handler of the test's own on the source logger with propagate=False for the block; task 952's plan does this for tests/unit/web_jobs/test_job_manager.py.

solar-challenge: the full verify (`uv run --locked --extra dev --extra web pytest -m 'not slow and not e2e' --ignore=tests/e2e -p no:cacheprovider -q`) runs serially, because pytest-xdist is not installed. On 2026-10-06 at main 291cf22 (task 441 architect), 3995 tests took 18m24s wall clock; on 2026-10-04, 3466 tests had taken about 10.3 min. A foreground run with a 15-min Bash timeout is now killed with exit 143 before it finishes. Background it (run_in_background) and Read its log until the run's summary line appears, or give a foreground run at least 25 min (1500000 ms).

Amendment (task 466 architect, measured 2026-10-05 at main de882d7) to the solar_challenge construction-probe recipe, memory a9c4d620. Wrap the probed class's __init__ with functools.wraps(original): inspect.signature follows __wrapped__, so test_public_api_surface's FROZEN_SURFACE check passes and the recipe's expected false failure does not appear. With no pytest-xdist installed, sync the venv once (uv run --locked --extra dev --extra web), then run ~6 background `.venv/bin/python -m pytest` shards over the 139 test files: ~6 min, against ~20 min sequential. At host load ~100, tests/unit/test_cli_web.py::test_stopping_the_server_drops_the_jobs_still_queued hit its 60 s subprocess timeout, then passed alone in 2 s, so re-run it alone before treating it as a failure.

solar_challenge gotcha (measured 2026-10-01): the project's pytest addopts make `pytest --collect-only -q` print a <Module>/<Function> tree, not one node id per line. Grepping for '::' therefore counts 0. To compare test counts across branches, e.g. to check that an auto-merge lost no tests, read the 'N tests collected' summary line from `uv run --extra dev --extra web pytest <files> --collect-only -p no:cacheprovider`.

solar_challenge procedure, measured 2026-10-06 by the task 419 architect (uv, main 568edab): to try a pytest plugin or another pytest under the project's pytest ini without editing pyproject.toml or uv.lock, put the scenario in a /tmp directory together with a copy of pyproject.toml, then run from the worktree `UV_OFFLINE=1 PYTHONPATH=<worktree> uv run --locked --extra dev --extra web --with 'pytest-rerunfailures==16.7' [--with 'pytest==9.1.1'] python -m pytest <tmp-dir> -p no:cacheprovider`. The --with packages come from uv's cache and shadow the locked ones (the header read pytest-9.1.1). The copied pyproject.toml makes the run read task 490's `filterwarnings = error::pytest.PytestDeprecationWarning`.

solar_challenge: to test pytest fixture/teardown behaviour that only a later test can observe (e.g. tests/conftest.py::_shutdown_job_managers), run the scenarios as an inner session with pytester (`pytest_plugins = ["pytester"]` in the test module; pytester.makeconftest(<real tests/conftest.py text>) + runpytest_subprocess). Use the SUBPROCESS runner, not the in-process one: pytester's in-process run restores sys.modules to its pre-run snapshot, dropping modules first imported during the run, and it shares the JobManager registry with the outer session. Also chdir to request.config.invocation_params.dir before the run: pytester moves cwd into an empty tmp dir, but solar_challenge.weather caches PVGIS data at the cwd-relative Path(".cache/weather"), so a web job would otherwise fetch from PVGIS. Measured on task 131, pytest 9.0.3: about 4 s of subprocess overhead.

solar_challenge verify-suite timing (measured 2026-10-17 at main ede1d99, task 778 architect): the orchestrator's verify command runs serially, with no xdist in the lock: `uv run --locked --extra dev --extra web pytest -m 'not slow and not e2e' --ignore=tests/e2e`. It collected 5,455 tests (72 deselected) and took 12m23s. That is past the Bash tool's 2-minute default timeout. Run it with run_in_background and redirect it to a log file, then Read that file until the pytest summary line appears. Do not pipe it through tail.

solar_challenge test gotcha (task 309, measured 2026-10-02): pyproject's pytest addopts carry `-v`, and at verbosity >= 1 pytest's assertion introspection prints the FULL repr and diff of both operands of a failed `==`. A failed `assert path.read_bytes() == snapshot` on uv.lock (~470 KB) produced a 9.1 MB log for three failures. Compare a compact proxy instead, e.g. hashlib.sha256 digests (tests/unit/test_stale_uv_lock.py::_lock_digest); the custom assertion message then carries the useful detail.

solar_challenge mypy gotcha (measured 2026-10-10, task 374, base aca7236): run mypy the way the orchestrator's type_check_command does, `uv run --locked --extra dev --extra web mypy src/solar_challenge`. Without `--extra web` it reports 5 errors that are not real defects: four 'Unused "type: ignore" comment' in web/history.py and anthropic import-not-found in web/assistant.py. With the web extra it is clean. Also, pytest-xdist is not a dev dependency, so `pytest -n 4` fails with a usage error; shard by directory instead.

solar_challenge scratch-prototype gotcha (task 667 architect, measured 2026-10-13 on a git-archive copy of main 1fb95da, run with the worktree's .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/unit and PYTHONPATH=<copy>/src). Running the WHOLE unit suite from such a copy gives 7 false failures plus 7 setup errors, none caused by the change under test:
- tests/unit/test_per_task_verify.py (2)
- tests/unit/test_offline_lane_contracts.py::test_the_job_collects_its_suite_and_nothing_else (4 ids)
- tests/unit/test_interpreter_matrix_lane.py (1)
These tests shell out to `uv run --locked ...` inside the copy, which has no .venv. uv then tries to build one from PyPI and fails behind the sandbox proxy with "tunnel error: unsuccessful". They pass in the real worktree. Read them as artefacts of the copy, and exclude them when listing what a change breaks. The rest of the serial run took about 14 min (4,796 tests).

solar_challenge review procedure (verified 2026-10-02, HEAD 0669545): when review Phase 1 reports "Failed to spawn pytest/mypy", get a real baseline by running the orchestrator's configured commands verbatim in a detached scratch worktree (git worktree add --detach /tmp/<id>-wt HEAD; uv builds its own .venv there). Measured cost: mypy strict ~1 min (47 files); test_command `uv run --extra dev --extra web pytest -m 'not slow and not e2e' --ignore=tests/e2e` ~8.5 min serial (2783 tests, ~1.1 GB RSS); the e2e lane command ~3.2 min (147 tests, chromium_headless_shell-1228 already in ~/.cache/ms-playwright). pytest-xdist is NOT a dev dependency, so `-n` errors out with "unrecognized arguments". Exclude .mypy_cache/build/.venv when grepping the repo root: .mypy_cache JSON lines are huge.

solar_challenge survey technique (task 238 planning, 2026-10-01): to learn which keys the test suite actually feeds into config.py's parsers, without editing the worktree:
1. Write a throwaway pytest plugin, e.g. /tmp/x/survey_plugin.py, that imports solar_challenge.config and replaces each parser attribute (setattr(cfg, name, wrapper)) with a wrapper that logs out-of-set keys plus os.environ["PYTEST_CURRENT_TEST"] to a JSONL file, then calls the original.
2. Run `PYTHONPATH=/tmp/x uv run --extra dev --extra web pytest tests/unit tests/integration -m 'not slow and not e2e' -p survey_plugin -o addopts= -q`.
Why it works: a -p plugin loads before conftest and test collection, so config.py's internal calls (resolved through module globals at call time) and later `from solar_challenge.config import X` imports in cli/web both get the wrappers.
Cost: 2663 tests in ~9 min. pytest-xdist is not installed, so run it backgrounded to a log file.

solar_challenge per-task verify timing, measured 2026-10-12 on task/641 (base main 5da62aa, CPython 3.12): `uv run --locked --extra dev --extra web pytest -m 'not slow and not e2e' --ignore=tests/e2e -p no:cacheprovider` collected 5216 items (5109 selected) and gave 5107 passed, 2 skipped in 657 s (10m57s), still serial. Backgrounding it with output redirected to a log and reading the log until pytest's summary line appeared worked cleanly; a foreground run needs an explicit Bash timeout of about 1500000 ms.

solar_challenge measurement gotcha (task 847 architect, 2026-10-17): to learn what a child pytest process imports or costs, check sys.modules and os.times() rather than `python -X importtime -m pytest ...`.
- Collecting tests/css_build with -X importtime listed no pandas, pvlib or tests.conftest import at all.
- Yet running pytest.main(['--collect-only', 'tests/css_build']) in-process and then reading sys.modules showed tests.conftest, pandas, pvlib and solar_challenge.weather all loaded, at 3.3 s CPU for 3 tests.

To census every child process a test run starts:
1. Put a sitecustomize.py whose atexit hook appends argv, os.times() and sys.modules flags to a JSONL file in a /tmp dir.
2. Prepend that dir to PYTHONPATH.
pytester's runpytest_subprocess, run_collect_only and uv-run children all inherit PYTHONPATH, so all of them are recorded.

solar_challenge pytest node-id listing, an addition to memory d1bc03b3. That entry gives PYTEST_ADDOPTS="--collect-only --verbosity=-1" and notes that a plain -q prints a tree. Passing `--collect-only -qq` on the command line also works: two -q against the ini's single -v net to -q, which prints one `path::test` node id per line. That line is followed by a 'N tests collected in Xs' line whose timing varies between runs. So filter with `grep '::'` before diffing a before/after listing, as in `uv run --locked --extra dev --extra web pytest <file> -m 'not slow and not e2e' -p no:cacheprovider --collect-only -qq 2>/dev/null | grep '::'`. This was measured on pytest 9.0.3 at main 0017651 on 2026-10-05, by the task 458 architect. It proved a behaviour-preserving import hoist across three test files left their 187 node ids identical.

solar_challenge procedure (task 555 step-1, 2026-10-08, commit 00b24e6; complements the architect's scratch-copy entry on the same topic): to record OLD vs NEW for a characterization pin that passes on its first run, drive the transient mutations from a script under /tmp. For each mutation it writes the mutated module into the worktree, runs ONE pytest call over the edited test file plus an untracked copy of HEAD's version (git show HEAD:<file> > tests/unit/<name>_old<task>.py, unlinked in a finally block), then restores the module with git checkout -- <module>. OLD shows no failure and NEW shows exactly the named test, with the summary count ('1 failed, 109 passed' = 56 edited + 54 old tests). Pass --tb=line to get each failure's file:line and message on one line. Gotcha: on this host `uv run` prints a 'VIRTUAL_ENV ... does not match the project environment path' warning on stderr, so with stderr merged into stdout the last output line is that warning, not pytest's summary; take the summary with a regex such as r'^=+ (.*?) in [0-9.]+s'.

pytest collection-hook gotchas, probed 2026-10-17 on pytest 9.0.3 by the task 873 architect.
(1) Session.perform_collect calls pytest_collection_finish from a `finally` block. So a plugin that writes a report there writes one even when collection stops: a missing path argument (UsageError, exit 4) still wrote an empty test list, and a module that failed to import (exit 2) wrote the other modules' items. A written collection report says what was collected; only the exit code says whether collection succeeded.
(2) A conftest that calls pytest.skip or pytest.importorskip at module level gives a skipped CollectReport for the Dir collector, whose node id is the directory, not for each module under it. solar_challenge's tests/e2e/conftest.py does this with importorskip("werkzeug"). A check of skips at collection that keeps only Module collectors misses such a directory.

solar_challenge architect probe technique (task 660 planning, main 5da62aa, 2026-10-12): to measure a construction-time invariant's blast radius over the full verify without editing the worktree (the architect session has no Edit tool), write a pytest plugin outside the tree whose pytest_configure wraps the class's __post_init__ and appends each violation, with os.environ['PYTEST_CURRENT_TEST'], to a log. 80bcb526-f2f9-4e70-b385-da182f290f14.content: pytest 9.0.3 gotcha (measured 2026-09-29 for task 149 with throwaway /tmp trees): a module-level `pytest.importorskip(...)` or failing import in a SUB-DIRECTORY conftest.py skips that directory cleanly only when a parent directory is being collected. Pass that directory, or a file inside it, directly on the command line and pytest treats it as an initial conftest: it aborts with an uncaught Skipped traceback, exit 1. So a solar_challenge test-directory conftest whose tests must skip without the optional web extra must not import flask at module level. Annotate with TYPE_CHECKING-only imports, import create_app inside the fixture, and let each test module call pytest.importorskip('flask'). Exit codes of that shape with flask blocked via sys.modules['flask'] = None (re-measured 2026-09-29): collecting the PARENT directory exits 0 because other tests run. Running the directory itself, or one file in it, directly reports 'N skipped' and exits 5 (NO_TESTS_COLLECTED), because every module skipped at import. Today's single tests/unit/test_web_assistant.py behaves the same: '1 skipped', exit 5. A 'skips cleanly without the web extra' check must therefore expect exit 5 and no traceback. Exit 1 with a `raise skipped` traceback is the real failure signal: a conftest that imports flask or calls importorskip at module level.

candidates.content: Operator-console frontend/ (vitest + jsdom) has no @testing-library/jest-dom, so there is no toHaveStyle. To assert that a rendered inline colour equals a shared source constant (e.g. ATTENTION_TONE.color from frontend/src/components/tones.ts), normalise the expected value with the DOM's own CSS parser: `const probe = document.createElement('span'); probe.style.color = c; return probe.style.color` turns '#e6b95c' into 'rgb(230, 185, 92)'. Then compare it to `element.style.color`. No hand-written hex→rgb converter and no accept-both-forms logic is needed. Memory 9ccf9bbe has the underlying normalisation facts, including the box-shadow exception. Precedent: RunsPanel.test.tsx's inlineColour helper (task 589).

Operator-console (frontend/) vitest + jsdom 29 fact, measured 2026-09-28 by task 429's architect: inline colours come back normalised as rgb()/rgba() through element.style and in the style attribute (e.g. '#e6b95c' reads 'rgb(230, 185, 92)'). The exception is box-shadow, which keeps raw hex ('inset 3px 0 0 #e5484d'). A React style that sets both `border: '1px solid <colour>'` and a separate `borderStyle` loses the colour from getAttribute('style') ('border: 1px solid;'), while element.style.borderColor still returns it. A test that inspects colours should therefore read the style properties (color, backgroundColor, borderColor, boxShadow) and accept both rgb() and #rrggbb, not scrape the style attribute.

GOTCHA (solar_challenge_platform frontend-portal vitest, jsdom 29, measured 2026-09-30 by task 712's architect): getComputedStyle(el).color reports colours as 'rgb(r, g, b)' — an inline '#4b5563' reads back 'rgb(75, 85, 99)', and it resolves INHERITED colour, so text with no colour set anywhere reads 'rgb(0, 0, 0)'. SVG stroke/fill ATTRIBUTES read back verbatim ('#4b6fa9') via getAttribute. A test comparing HTML text ink against a chart line's stroke, or feeding it to EnergyChart.test.tsx's '#rrggbb'-only relativeLuminance/contrastOnWhite, must first normalise the rgb() form to '#rrggbb'.

Frontend convention (lands with task 435, 2026-09-28): the operator console's design-spec §6 attention tier ("needs a look", never alarm red) is ONE constant, ATTENTION_TONE {color, background, borderColor} in frontend/src/components/tones.ts, worn by LivenessPanel's stale tile and DispatchLivenessPanel's degraded summary. Any new panel state §6 rules attention-worthy (e.g. a future platform-process heartbeat tile such as the ingest tile) should import it rather than copy the amber literals. The same '#e6b95c' hex in StatusBanner (a separate "dashboard data is stale" class), RunsPanel's arrears cell and the dispatch skip-reason chips is deliberately NOT bound to it, because §6 does not rule those attention-worthy.

GOTCHA (frontend-portal vitest + jsdom 29, measured 2026-09-30 by task 702's architect): SVG presentation attributes read back RAW through getAttribute (stroke '#abc', stroke-dasharray '8 4', a <line>'s y1 '104.5'), and an attribute React omits (strokeDasharray undefined) reads null. That is unlike inline style colours, which normalise to rgb(). An inline clip 'rect(0 0 0 0)' (the VISUALLY_HIDDEN technique) reads back as style.clip === 'rect(0px)', and getComputedStyle(el).clip is 'auto', so to detect visually-hidden text test `el.style.clip !== ''` over the element and its ancestors, with the hidden element as positive control. SVGLineElement and similar per-shape interfaces are NOT defined in jsdom (ReferenceError), so never use instanceof on them. getByText does find SVG <text> (it is an SVGElement, not an HTMLElement).

To make a test FAIL when a wait opens no act() scope, draw the change as a Suspense reveal from a lazy child: `lazy(async () => { const said = await readSaid(reply); return { default: () =>

{said}

} })` inside ``, rendered with RTL's ordinary render(). Outside act(), React puts off committing that retry with setTimeout until about 300 ms after the fallback appeared; inside act() it commits at once. Over 40 runs, the real settle() drew it 40/40 and a bare setTimeout(0) wait 0/40, with no warnings. Plain updates only race React's scheduler; drawn without act(): setState from an effect 39/40, an effect chained after it 16/40, a startTransition update 38/40. Both SPAs (frontend/ and frontend-portal/; vitest 5, jsdom 30, React 19.2), measured 2026-10-11 by task 949's amendment. render() and renderHook() flush everything inside act(), so a test cannot otherwise land a `storage` event between a component's commit and its useEffect flush. To land one there:
- Wrap the tree in a component whose useLayoutEffect sends the event. React runs a parent's layout effect after its children's, and before any useEffect.
- Send it with window.localStorage.setItem plus window.dispatchEvent(new StorageEvent('storage', { key, newValue, storageArea: window.localStorage })).
- Do NOT use changeInAnotherTab or fireEvent there. Their act() re-enters React's flush, and React logs 'A component suspended inside an act scope, but the act call was not awaited'. The same warning appears when they are called from a useEffect.

Two agent claims were in tension (one said an unaccompanied park is safe, the other that workflow_cancel_recent protects it); resolving that tension by reading harness.py:10509-10529 myself is what surfaced the missing-grace-stamp gap that became requirement 2 of task 3724.

A DEFENSIVE HOLD PLACED MID-TASK MUST BE LIFTED WHEN ITS CONDITION CLEARS — otherwise it silently becomes a decision nobody made. On 2026-08-05 task 3404 was set `deferred` for one specific reason: an escalation close had unexpectedly released it to `pending` while three recovered commits were still missing, and a dispatch would have merged the branch incomplete. Once the recovery landed and verified, that reason was gone — but the hold was left in place through the end of the session out of generic caution about releasing work to the autonomous fleet. Leo had to ask "why is 3404 deferred?" to surface it. The hold was not wrong to place; leaving it was. PRACTICE: when you park a task defensively, state the lift condition at the moment you park it (write it into `reopen_reason`), and re-check that condition before ending the session. If the condition has cleared and releasing is genuinely the human's call, say so explicitly and ask — do not leave the park standing as an unexplained default, because a parked task reads to the next session as "something is still wrong here".

When a long-lived HOLD or gate has drifted, the strongest evidence of what was actually decided is the OPERATOR MEMORY FILE written on the day of the decision — not the task metadata that claims to enforce it. Demonstrated 2026-08-24 while ruling reify task 6488 ("which of 5 divergent statements is the release condition for the 2026-07-28 Mem0 consolidation hold"). The bookmark task reify 5741 carried metadata.external_deps=['dark_factory:3169'], i.e. a scheduler-ENFORCED statement of the condition — and it was wrong. The correct condition sat in /home/leo/.claude/projects/-home-leo-src-reify/memory/project_mem0_consolidation_hold.md, modified 2026-07-28T21:04:43Z (hours after Leo took the decision): "Release condition (mechanical, not a date): dark_factory tasks 3133, 3134, 3112, 3108". reify 6482's metadata.unblock_precondition, derived independently by recon run 5d186c7b 26 days later, named the identical four — two artefacts, no shared derivation, exact agreement. GENERALISABLE RULE: (1) when adjudicating divergent statements of a condition, look for the contemporaneous record first, and prefer it over any later-added mechanical proxy, however authoritative the proxy looks by virtue of being enforced; (2) a proxy that only ONE consumer adopted is not the condition — do not promote it; (3) after ruling, hunt for statements of the condition that are ENFORCED rather than merely retrievable (metadata.external_deps, unblock_precondition, dependency edges) and re-point them in the same sitting, or the ruling will say one thing while the machine does another. In this case the enforced statement was a live SIXTH statement that the gate task enumerating the divergence had not even listed.

Leo's ruling, relayed by the L2 escalation watcher on 2026-09-16: when an interactive or /unblock session hand-submits a task branch to the merge queue (mcp__escalation__merge_request), the task's scheduler status must be `merge-deferred` while the request is queued, not `blocked` or `pending`.

WHY: if the lane coalesces the request into a train, `_redrive_coalesce_members` only re-drives members whose status is merge-deferred. A pending or blocked member is skipped without any signal, and the train strands (task 4953's class; 11 tasks were stranded that way on 09-16).

HOW: two set_task_status calls, blocked → in-progress → merge-deferred. in-progress → merge-deferred is the only legal edge into merge-deferred. Both transitions were accepted for task 4926. Afterwards, merge-deferred → done with done_provenance was accepted as usual. Do not resubmit the queued request when making this change.
