THERE IS NO RELEASE-AND-RETRY PRIMITIVE for a running dark-factory task, verified 2026-09-06 against shared/src/shared/task_transitions.py::TRANSITIONS across all five actor classes (orchestrator, escalation, deterministic, human, reconciliation).

Only `done` and `cancelled` free a live workflow's dispatch slot and module locks: harness.py::Harness._scan_for_terminal_active_tasks opens with `if status not in TERMINAL_STATUSES: continue`, and TERMINAL is exactly {DONE, CANCELLED} (shared/task_statuses.py).

BOTH OF THOSE ARE ABSORBING: there is NO transition out of `done` and NO transition out of `cancelled`, for any actor class. So releasing a slot is necessarily an abandonment — the task must be re-filed under a new id, losing its history and escalation trail. "Set it done/cancelled then re-open it" is not implementable; there is no re-open.

`deferred` and `infra-hold` ARE reversible (`in-progress -> deferred -> pending` and `in-progress -> infra-hold -> pending` are all legal) and neither arms dependents, but both are NON-TERMINAL, so setting one on a LIVE workflow releases nothing — it only desynchronises the task row from the harness's in-memory slot/lock state, and the workflow later writes its outcome against a parked row. `infra-hold` is semantically ideal for "parked by infrastructure, not its own fault" and is the natural status for a future reaper to use, but today it has no release path.

PRACTICAL CONSEQUENCE: an operator facing a saturated fleet has exactly two options, both bad — abandon-and-refile, or a full fleet restart that also destroys every healthy in-flight task. This is why the ~8h fleet restart was load-bearing in a way nobody designed: it was the only mechanism that could free a slot without abandoning the task. Task 5153 asks for the missing primitive.

Note `deferred` IS the right tool for parking PENDING work (what the 2026-08-28 backlog sweep did with 340 members) — it simply cannot evict anything already running.

The mechanism agreed: track the declaration rate from day one (declared / metadata-bridged / derived / none buckets), and file a DELAYED task, dated roughly +7 days after landing, that reports the undeclared fraction over real production data and drives a tighten-or-hold decision. This is the INV-7 holds-owned-and-bounded pattern applied to a transitional design state: the hold has a named owner and a deadline rather than drifting indefinitely. Filed as leaves iota (task 3674, telemetry) and lambda (task 3676, the dated census). The generalizable principle: when shipping a permissive fallback to avoid a breaking change, bound it with a dated task that forces the tightening decision, rather than relying on someone noticing later.

Norm (dark_factory, established 2026-08-11): when a ruling produces a follow-up task whose correctness DEPENDS on another task landing first, make the relationship enforceable rather than advisory. Four concrete levers, all used together when filing task 4013 against task 3980:

1. STRUCTURED DEPENDENCY, not prose. `add_dependency` writes the real `dependencies` field; a sentence in the description gates nothing. VERIFY IT afterwards — read the task back and confirm `dependencies` contains the id. (This repo has been burned by a "dependency" that was prose while the structured field was `[]`.)

2. PRIORITY PARITY. A gate at lower priority than the task it gates can be scheduled after it, which defeats the gate. 3980 was medium while 4013 was high; 3980 was promoted to high.

3. WIDEN THE GATE TASK'S LOCK CHARTER to cover where the fix will actually have to reach. 4. NAME THE CHEAP CLOSE AND FORBID IT. State explicitly what would look like a fix but isn't — here, "bump MERGE_RESULT_TIMEOUT and declare victory", which is precisely what an earlier task in the same lineage already did before the constant starved again. Also state that scoping a half out must be an explicit escalation, not a silent omission, and say WHY (dropping the vacuity half un-gates the dependent task without fixing what the gate exists for).

Process lesson (2026-10-14): a task deferred 'until Leo releases it' needs an objective release condition and something that fires when the condition is met. On 2026-10-13 I filed reify task 8887 deferred with x_deferral.until_condition = 'Leo explicitly releases this task'. That record named no criterion, and nothing would ever have reminded Leo. When he asked what the release condition was, the honest answer was that there was none.

Two better shapes:
- If the task's dependencies already sequence it and every failure mode is cheap and revertable, recommend releasing it now. The scheduler holds a pending task behind its dependencies anyway.
- If Leo really wants to approve at activation time, file a human-gate task: task_kind deterministic with always_escalates, depending on the prerequisites. Make the held task depend on that gate, so Leo gets an escalation exactly when the prerequisites land.

Also: do not record your own option wording as Leo's words. The hold reason 'nothing changes the live queue without his go' came from my option text, which he selected; he did not say it.

It enforces the per-kind fields (grep needs pattern+expect; path needs expect+non-empty paths; manual needs reason and no pattern/expect/paths; script needs script+timeout_secs). Author-time sidecars use task_id: null and verdict OPEN with kind: manual for capabilities produced by another stream's unfiled leaf.

Validating a /prd capability-manifest YAML sidecar against dark-factory's schema from the solar-challenge-platform repo. Run from /home/leo/src/dark-factory/shared with /home/leo/src/dark-factory/.venv/bin/python (there is no shared/.venv):
`import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'src'); from shared.capability_manifest import load_capability_manifest; load_capability_manifest('<abs path>.capability-manifest.yaml')`.

The legibility trickle's `outcome` field in ~/.local/state/dark-factory/legibility/<project>/trickle-state.json is a TERM OF ART, not a health verdict: classify_run (scripts/legibility/trickle_state.py:136-140) keys solely on `selected_count > 0` for `productive`, `(budget_skipped + below_sampling_cut) > 0` for `barren`, else `quiet`. exit_code is NOT a parameter of classify_run at all — record_run (trickle_state.py:340-362) stores it alongside the outcome and never consults it. This is deliberate and argued at nightly.py:870-876. So a run that fails at every post-sampling stage still records `outcome: productive` with `exit_code: 1, applied: 0, commit_made: false` — that is CORRECT per contract, not a mislabel; do not re-file it as one. The real hole is that the three-value vocabulary has no term for "signal flowed in, the pipeline broke downstream": a permanently broken coder would record productive + consecutive_barren_runs 0 + a fresh last_productive_at every night forever (trickle_state.py:337-338 restamps on productive, :350-352 resets the streak for anything not barren), and check_trickle_progress.py would print "OK ... productive 0h ago" and exit 0 indefinitely — the same silent-degradation shape as the 2026-07-16..29 incident (task 3270) the module was built to end. Filed as dark_factory task 4514, which also covers the second half: NOTHING currently runs either check_trickle_progress.py or check_trickle_liveness.sh — no timer, no cron, no config binding. Their only bindings were one-shot before_done delayed-milestone predicates on tasks 2587 (kappa) and 2615 (kappa-prime), both done, and a completed milestone predicate never runs again. That makes nightly.py:872-873's claim ("crashes are already caught loudly by check_trickle_liveness.sh") stale as an operational statement, even though that script's own logic is correct.

Task 3340: `nightly.run_nightly` now records per-run state (productive/quiet/barren + a consecutive-barren streak) via `trickle_state.record_run` on EVERY exit path, so any `scripts/tests/test_legibility_nightly.py` test reaching `run_nightly` writes to `${XDG_STATE_HOME:-~/.local/state}/dark-factory/legibility/<project_id>/`. That file carries a module-scoped autouse fixture pointing XDG_STATE_HOME at tmp_path; keep it, or test runs will pollute the operator's real XDG state dir with the synthetic project_id 'testproj' and break WARNING-count assertions.

The legibility trickle's run-state classifier cannot see a post-sampling failure, so a night that produced NOTHING is recorded as "productive" and the health probe reports OK. `trickle_state.classify_run` branches only on the sampling stage (`selected_count > 0` -> productive; `budget_skipped + below_sampling_cut > 0` -> barren; else quiet) and never consults the coding stage. `record_run` stores `exit_code`, `applied` and `commit_made` in the document but the classifier ignores all three.

MEASURED, not inferred (2026-08-24 storm, both projects). State files at ~/.local/state/dark-factory/legibility/<project>/trickle-state.json read:

and running the real probe returned exit 0:

    OK: legibility trickle for reify last run was productive 19h ago, consecutive_barren_runs=0 ...
(same verdict for dark_factory). The probe checks only missing / malformed / `recorded_at` freshness / barren streak — note it takes positional args `<project_id> <max_barren_runs> [max_age_hours]` and prints a usage error with just a project id.

So a capped or broken night both restamps the freshness clock AND holds the barren streak at 0, disarming the streak escalation. This is the same silent-degradation shape as the 2026-07-16..29 fourteen-night episode the module was built to end, entered through a different door.

BACKFILLING A LOST LEGIBILITY TRICKLE NIGHT (recipe + the two traps), proven 2026-08-25.

WHY it is ever needed: `nightly.py run` defaults `target_date` to yesterday-UTC — a ROLLING WINDOW, not a cursor — so a night whose run failed is never retried and its signal is dropped permanently. systemd `Persistent=true` buys exactly one catch-up attempt per missed night; if that attempt fails, the date is gone. Two nights are now confirmed lost this way (2026-08-17, 2026-08-23).

TRAP 1 — the census. Do NOT just run `nightly.py run --date <d>`. dark_factory task 3269 (census launcher passes no `--project-root`) is still merge-deferred, so a fired census trigger launches `census.py` against the INHERITED CWD — a real-money, tens-of-minutes operation aimed at whatever project the cwd happens to be. Neutralise it. There is no CLI flag (`--dry-run` is explicitly "not yet wired to any behavior change") and `run_nightly` has no `launcher` seam, but `evaluate_census_step` is resolved as a module global at call time, so a driver can stub it:
    nightly.evaluate_census_step = lambda cfg, **kw: ('census: SKIPPED (manual backfill)', False)
    nightly.run_nightly(project_id=<id>, target_date=date(Y, M, D))

TRAP 2 — sys.path. `coder.py` does a bare `import codebook`, so BOTH scripts/ and scripts/legibility/ must be on sys.path; adding only scripts/ (what PYTHONPATH in the systemd unit sets, because nightly.py self-bootstraps the rest) fails with ModuleNotFoundError. Run under `uv run --frozen --project shared` from the dark-factory root and set LEGIBILITY_CLAUDE_BIN=/home/leo/.local/bin/claude.

TRAP 3 — the state file. A backfill overwrites ~/.local/state/dark-factory/legibility/<project>/trickle-state.json with the OLD target_date and a fresh recorded_at, so the health record stops describing the last SCHEDULED run. Back both files up before and restore after, then re-run check_trickle_progress.py to confirm.

The run commits `docs/legibility/confusion-codebook.yaml` to the target project's repo via `git commit --only <path>` (hook-gated, docs-only, direct on main — the trickle's normal nightly path). 2026-08-25 backfill of 2026-08-23: reify applied=38 -> commit 1040b07fe3; dark_factory applied=43 -> commit f3880fedba.

OBSERVABILITY DEFECT in the legibility trickle, filed as dark_factory task 4511: a failed nightly run leaves a journal showing `status=1/FAILURE` with NO cause logged. scripts/legibility/coder.py contains ZERO logging calls (`grep -c 'logger\|logging'` returns 0) and accumulates per-digest failures silently into run.failures. All four of run_nightly's decision-8 fail-loud branches then build a summary+detail, POST them to the escalation server, and return exit_code=1 WITHOUT any logger.* call: extractor crash (nightly.py ~1151-1162), coder storm (1186-1200), validation failure (~1276-1290), commit failure (~1304-1314). main() (nightly.py:1452) returns result.exit_code straight into SystemExit. This is asymmetric with _report_sample_outcome (nightly.py:847) and _escalate_barren_streak (nightly.py:1000), which DO log the same summary/detail pair. Consequence on 2026-08-18: the diagnosis ("coder storm: 6/6 digests failed ... [Errno 2] No such file or directory: 'claude'") existed ONLY inside data/escalations/archive/2026-08-18/esc-legibility-trickle-reify-1.json, and the resulting L2 escalation plus its spawn brief both reasoned from a journal that showed a causeless failure. Recommended fix is to log at ERROR inside post_escalation (nightly.py ~482-515) on entry, before the POST — so no future fail-loud branch can forget, and the journal carries the reason even when the escalation server is unreachable (today a POST failure loses the diagnosis entirely).

In scripts/tests/test_legibility_nightly.py, a run_nightly e2e test that needs TWO coded records must give each fixture transcript a DIFFERENT first user turn (`_write_transcript(..., user_text=...)`). sampling.dedupe_shapes fingerprints on (stratum, boolean signal-shape, normalized first-turn text), so two transcripts differing only in session_id collapse to one and the test silently degrades to a single-record night — which is how a batch-continuation test can pass while a `continue`→`break` mutation goes undetected.

DISCOVERY 2026-09-21 (legibility trickle): `scripts/legibility/nightly.py::run_nightly` has FOUR early `return result` sites (extractor crash, coder storm, codebook validation failure, commit failure) before it reaches `evaluate_census_step`, and no `except` — only a `finally` that calls `nightly.py::_record_trickle_progress`, which its own comment calls the ONE recording point for all five return sites and an unexpected raise. So a step hooked "after evaluate_census_step" runs only on clean nights; anything that must run every night hooks the `finally`. `evaluate_census_step`'s never-raises discipline is per-function (it guards its own decide/launcher calls), not inherited. Also: every pydantic model in `scripts/legibility/config.py` sets `model_config = ConfigDict(extra='allow')`, so a NEW block added to docs/legibility/legibility.yaml is accepted as an untyped raw dict with zero validation or defaulting — the `census:` block's validation lives in `census_trigger.CensusConfig.from_mapping` (validated-never-coerced, one WARNING per block), and any new block needs its own equivalent. `census_trigger.Decision` is `fire: bool` + `reasons: list[str]` only — no evidence field.

scripts/legibility/nightly.py test-safety gotcha: any test that drives run_nightly/main() to a census FIRE must monkeypatch `nightly._default_census_launcher` (and/or `nightly._default_entrypoint_exists`). On FIRE, evaluate_census_step's default launcher subprocess-runs scripts/legibility/census.py — real LLM spend plus git writes — and `_default_entrypoint_exists` is true in any real checkout, so nothing stops it. Related seam fact (task 4148): `status_fetcher` was the one DI seam in run_nightly whose None meant "no implementation" rather than "the real one" (committer/recorder/poster all default to the real thing), which is why the production systemd path `nightly.py run --project-id %i` reached compute_tasks_landed with None and the census tasks-landed condition (b) could never fire — invisible to 78 green tests because they all enter below main().

GOTCHA (scripts/tests/test_legibility_nightly.py): `_run_e2e_nightly` and `_run_one_digest_night` build their repo via `_init_e2e_repo`, which seeds the codebook by calling `codebook.dump` itself. A budget-suppressed legibility trickle night is indistinguishable from a genuine no-change night at every observable layer, which is why the zero-digest bug survived 14 nights undetected. Three gaps compose: (1) SampleResult.budget_skipped is computed correctly every night and observed by nobody — nightly.select_digest_sessions returns only stratified_sample(...).selected and discards the rest of the SampleResult, even though budget_skipped's own docstring says it exists so an operator can tell "there was nothing to sample" from "the budget cut off real signal" (it was deliberately added under task 2573, commit 20d2d4bd97, then dropped by task 2581's consumer); (2) run_nightly's no-change message is logger.info and scripts/legibility/nightly.py never calls logging.basicConfig, so root level stays WARNING and the line never reaches the journal at all; (3) the run exits 0, so systemd and check_trickle_liveness.sh both see health. PRD decision 8's fail-loud contract is wired only to the three exceptional triggers (extractor crash, coder storm, commit failure) — a green run that silently selects nothing was never covered. Filed as dark_factory task 3270.

GOTCHA (dark-factory, task 3789): grouping N independent "never raises" side-effects under ONE try/except silently makes them order-dependent, and the docstring claiming independence will be wrong for every effect after the first. In `flake_recorder.record_merge_flake_suppression` a single try wrapped ledger-write + event-emit + INV-4 storm-streak bump; an `event_store.emit` that raised (locked/closed sqlite) jumped to the catch-all so the streak bump never ran — a broken event store switched OFF the storm detector whose whole job is to fire when something is going wrong. Fix pattern: a local `_guarded(what, fn)` helper giving each effect its own try/except and tagging the warning with which signal was lost. Also guard the DISCRIMINATING read itself (here `s.verdict`, on an un-validated wire object) and default it to the fail-safe branch, since a raise there decides all downstream effects. Rule of thumb: one try block per effect that the docstring claims is independent.

Debugging census-trigger tests in scripts/legibility: since task 4085, nightly.evaluate_census_step wraps its `decide` call in a never-raises try/except that converts ANY exception into one WARNING plus a synthetic `census trigger: NO-FIRE -- trigger evaluation failed (<type>: <msg>)` line. A broken test fixture (mis-shaped fake MCP response, bad census-state.json) therefore presents as a quiet NO-FIRE with an unfired launcher, never a traceback. When a census-fire assertion fails unexpectedly, grep caplog for 'census trigger evaluation failed' and for compute_tasks_landed's own fail-safe warnings before suspecting the wiring.

GOTCHA (asyncio tests, task 4530): to assert that a raising Task's exception WAS consumed, install a recorder via loop.set_exception_handler, drop the last reference to the task, gc.collect(), and assert nothing was reported (a weakref to the task confirms it was really finalized). The recorder must keep only (context['message'], context.get('exception')), NOT the whole context dict: the "Task exception was never retrieved" context carries 'future': <the task>, so storing it resurrects the task during finalization. The weakref then stays alive and an untracked-task control test fails for the wrong reason. Working example: shared/tests/test_asyncio_tasks.py::_recorded_loop_errors.

GOTCHA (dark-factory tests): a test that exercises a timeout path by killing a recording fake CLI written as a Python script (#!sys.executable) must not use a sub-second timeout. The scripts/ and orchestrator suites run with -n auto (addopts), and under that load the fake's interpreter start can exceed 0.5s. It is then killed before it writes its call record or stream tails, which fails as 'expected exactly one claude invocation, got 0'. Measured on task 5376's scripts/tests/test_sitting_nightly_prepare.py: 2 failures in 10 runs at 0.5s, 0 after raising it to 3s (the fake sleeps 30s, so the timeout path is still exercised). Pick a timeout of several seconds, well below the fake's sleep.

GOTCHA (dark-factory, measured 2026-09-01 on the task-3169 write_triage flip gate): in a before_done predicate script, a WARN emitted on a PASSING run is invisible by construction, so it is never an adequate mitigation for a known-weak pass. The mechanism: DeterministicRunner files a milestone_check_failed escalation (carrying the script's stdout) ONLY when the predicate exits non-zero; on exit 0 nothing is filed and the script's stdout is forwarded nowhere, so no operator ever reads the warning. Two consequences worth reusing: (1) if a gate accepts something on weaker evidence than it would like — e.g. scripts/check_write_triage_attach_target.py forgiving an echoed argument because the PARAMETER'S NAME designates the attach target — give the acceptance its own machine-detectable marker (there: a `PASS-NEEDS-CONFIRMATION` line the shell greps for as PROBE_PENDING_MARKER) and have the caller report it as satisfied-pending-eyeball, rather than relying on prose. Downgrading it to a FAIL is usually wrong: it re-blocks the dependent task against a valid fix. (2) Pin the marker string from BOTH ends in tests (the gate's constant and the probe's emitted line), exactly as PROBE_PASS_MARKER already is — a silent reword turns the demand for confirmation back into an ordinary PASS with no test failure anywhere, since both spellings still exit 0.

GOTCHA (dark-factory, measured 2026-09-01): a before_done predicate's report has a hard 2000-character budget that is spent from the TAIL — DeterministicRunner._default_run_script returns only the last 2000 chars of stdout and _run_predicate feeds exactly that into the milestone_check_failed escalation's detail. So running a child process with `2>&1` inside such a script silently donates part of that window to whatever the child's imports write to stderr. MEASURED: scripts/check_write_triage_flip_preconditions.sh item 1 executes the ref's own fused_memory tree, whose import emits 405 bytes of PydanticDeprecatedSince20 from graphiti_core on every run — ~20% of the operator's whole window, on a report whose actionable guidance was already being truncated. FIX PATTERN, now in that script: capture stderr to a file (`2>"$PROBE_TMP/probe.stderr"`), quote back only a bounded tail (last 10 lines) and only on the branches where stdout carried no verdict, and put anything that MUST survive at the very end of the report (that script's `FAILING ITEMS: ...` summary line). Corollary: once the caller stops folding stderr in, a child's own `logger.warning` reaches nobody — collect WARNING+ records with a logging.Handler and append them to the child's STDOUT report instead.

dark-factory `scripts/` has TWO distinct CLI conventions, and picking the wrong one is a real review finding. (1) BEST-EFFORT SWEEP family — dry-run flag is `--check`, and `main()` returns 0 UNCONDITIONALLY, deliberately, so a cron/watchdog hook does not alarm on routine per-item hiccups; the failure signal rides in the JSON report's `failed`/`failed_paths` instead of the exit code. Exemplars: scripts/gc_agent_transcripts.py (:371 --check, :469 the single `return 0`), scripts/reclaim_orphaned_worktrees.py (:49-51 states the posture verbatim and names gc as its model), scripts/drain_check.py. (2) MUTATOR / one-off MIGRATION family — dry-run is the DEFAULT and `--apply` opts INTO mutation, with NAMED exit-code constants where each code denotes exactly one outcome. Exemplars: scripts/repair_wiped_metadata_files.py (:840-844 EXIT_OK/EXIT_WRITE_FAILED/EXIT_NO_ROOT/EXIT_NOTHING_SCANNED/EXIT_SERVER_UNREACHABLE, :924 --apply, :1044-1058 argues why 0 must not cover both "nothing to do" and "examined nothing"), plus ~18 fused-memory/scripts migrations (migrate_cross_graph_leak.py:45 states "Dry run is the DEFAULT (no --apply)" as contract). A `--dry-run` flag that defaults to MUTATING is the rare minority (only scripts/migrate_metadata_modules_to_files.py:261) — do not copy it for anything destructive. Shared across both: a `_LOG_PREFIX = '<script_name>:'` greppable prefix as the first positional arg of lazy %-formatted log lines (NOT `extra={...}` — structured-logging `extra=` has zero uses anywhere in scripts/), machine-readable JSON as one line on stdout, LOUD human logs to stderr via basicConfig, a factored `build_parser()` for isolated unit testing, and `sys.exit(main())`. Tests invoke these CLIs via subprocess (not in-process main()) precisely so `json.loads(stdout)` sees pure JSON — see scripts/tests/test_gc_agent_transcripts.py:417-432.

content: GOTCHA (scripts/legibility, task 5783): trickle_state.record_run's keywords are deliberately REQUIRED with no default (exit_code, and since 5783 census). nightly._record_run_state wraps the recorder call in a never-raising try/except, so a caller that omits one does NOT crash: it logs one WARNING ('could not record run state') and records NOTHING. Completed: census.main files an escalation only inside one try; its prelude fails silently while nightly logs that census (scripts/legibility/census.py::main)
Description: census.main files an escalation only inside one try; its prelude fails silently while nightly logs that census escalated: The catch-all that files 'legibility census run failed' wraps only the run_census call. Everything before it is outside the try: the `--project-root`/config/identity/harness-config `return 1` paths (stderr only), census_identity.resolve_as_of_sha, census_identity.allocate_run_identity (raises RuntimeError), codebook.load (only FileNotFoundError is caught, so a YAML error propagates), construction of census_window.WindowBatchSource, and the `with session_runner.open_pooled_runner(...)` entry (for example an empty or capped pool at open). Any of these exits 1 with a traceback or stderr line and no escalation. nightly._default_census_launcher then logs 'census filed its own escalation for the failing stage; the nightly trickle's own commit work is unaffected' for every non-zero exit. For those failures the claim is false: the launcher uses check=False, and nothing else records the failure. This is the 2951/2952 silent-failure class re-entering through the part of main that fix did not cover. run_nightly has no outermost except either: its try has only a `finally`. An unexpected raise, such as codebook.dump hitting a missing parent directory, escapes as a bare traceback after recording the run as failed, with no escalation. The module's own docstring promises 'never an uncaught traceback'.

Proposal: Wrap the body of census.main after config load, and the body of run_nightly, in the shared fail_loud_boundary from the previous finding. Drop the launcher's unconditional claim that census filed an escalation, or make the launcher read the exit code and call raise_alarm itself when census exits non-zero without a filing marker. Add a regression test that forces codebook.load, allocate_run_identity and open_pooled_runner to raise and asserts one escalation per case.

candidates.content: reify-audit ratchet ledgers (pdoccover-baseline.txt, plinecite-baseline.txt) are read ONLY when git-tracked: check() and baseline_ledger() test membership in `git ls-files` (the index). So after seeding a NEW ledger with `<x>-baseline-gen --admit-new > <ledger>`, you must `git add` the file BEFORE the shrink-only re-run/diff freshness check; otherwise the committed set reads as empty, Ledger::kept() is empty, and the default generator renders the header alone, which looks like a wipe rather than a fresh ledger.

PLINECITE ledger (crates/reify-audit/plinecite-baseline.txt) freshness is NOT tested: committed_ledger_is_tracked_and_in_generated_form checks form only. A rebase that pulls in de-numbered cites (e.g. #8528) leaves stale rows that only surface as stale-baseline-entry findings at /audit time. After any rebase of a branch touching the ledger, run the header recipe `cargo run -p reify-audit --bin plinecite-baseline-gen -- --project-root . | diff -u crates/reify-audit/plinecite-baseline.txt -` on a clean tree and re-seed with the default (shrink-only) generator, never --admit-new. Exact dated landing counts live only in docs/prds/reify-audit-stale-line-cite-detector.md §5 (742 rows over main 4a0d1687df, 2026-10-14).

reify-audit's tree-coupled baseline manifests (crates/reify-audit/pdiag-baseline.txt, ptodo-baseline.txt) pin per-file counts against the WHOLE worktree, so they go stale on every rebase of a long-lived branch — and the always-on Rust test tiers do not catch it. Staleness surfaces only in the #[ignore]d whole-repo ratchet (`cargo test -p reify-audit --test pdiag_baseline -- --ignored`) and the infra shell gate (`bash tests/infra/test_reify_audit_pdiag.sh`, scenario (a)). Fix by regenerating with the canonical generator — `cargo run -p reify-audit --bin pdiag-baseline-gen -- --project-root . > crates/reify-audit/pdiag-baseline.txt` — never by hand-editing rows, which is what keeps generation and enforcement structurally in sync. Critically, a row that ROSE must be attributed before it is blessed: if `git diff <merge-base> HEAD -- <file>` is EMPTY the drift arrived from main and absorbing it is sanctioned (PRD §6 decision 3 makes backlog migration opportunistic; enforcement is only for sites the diff itself adds), but if it is NON-EMPTY the branch added a code-less Diagnostic::error/warning and that is a real INV-SF-6 violation to remediate per docs/notes/diagnostic-severity-policy.md §3. A bare regenerate blesses both cases identically, which is why the attribution check cannot be skipped. Cheap pre-check before a full verify: `cargo run -p reify-audit --bin pdiag-baseline-gen -- --project-root . | diff - crates/reify-audit/pdiag-baseline.txt`.

reify-audit PDIAG (task #5405, crates/reify-audit): the two whole-repo ratchet checks in crates/reify-audit/tests/pdiag_baseline.rs — `live_counts_are_within_the_committed_baseline` and `regenerating_the_committed_baseline_is_a_no_op` — are `#[ignore]`d as on-demand checks that need a real git checkout. So a plain `cargo test -p reify-audit` reports FULLY GREEN (79 lib + 69 cli + 22 pdiag_baseline passing) while the committed crates/reify-audit/pdiag-baseline.txt is stale against the tree. You must run `cargo test -p reify-audit --test pdiag_baseline -- --ignored` to see it. The merge gate does catch it, via tests/infra/test_reify_audit_pdiag.sh scenario (a), which runs `reify-audit --pattern PDIAG` and expects exit 0 — but only after a release build, so the fast feedback loop is the `--ignored` run. Measured 2026-09-10 on task/5405 rebased onto main b42c7dd: six baseline rows had drifted from main's movement alone (auto_type_param_phase.rs 1->2, geometry_ops.rs 136->138, modal_ops.rs 21->25 up; engine_admin.rs 3->2, engine_compute.rs 2->1, engine_eval.rs 23->21 down), none of those files touched by the branch. This is the esc-5405-17 bootstrap drift and is self-limiting once PDIAG is enforced on main. Remedy is always regeneration, never a hand-edit: `cargo run -p reify-audit --bin pdiag-baseline-gen -- --project-root . > crates/reify-audit/pdiag-baseline.txt`.

reify PTODO gotcha — re-seeding `crates/reify-audit/ptodo-baseline.txt` DISARMS the very ratchet that validates the re-seed, unless you rebuild afterwards. `tests/infra/test_reify_audit_ptodo.sh` gates its (a)+(b) ratchet block on `reify_audit_guard`, an mtime freshness check over the reify-audit crate; the baseline file lives INSIDE that crate, so writing it makes the already-built binary look stale. With `REIFY_AUDIT_NO_COLD_BUILD=1` (the budget-safe mode used in warm lanes) the guard then SKIPS the block rather than failing: the run still prints `0 failed`, only the assertion COUNT drops (observed 25 → 21), so a green-looking run silently asserted nothing about the baseline you just changed. Fix: `touch crates/reify-audit/src/lib.rs && cargo build -p reify-audit --bin reify-audit --bin ptodo-baseline-gen` before re-running, and confirm the "(a) Ratchet" and "(b) Scenario 13" sections actually appear in the output — never trust the `0 failed` summary alone. Observed first-hand on task #6103 (2026-08-29).

reify-audit PDIAG ratchet: `pdiag::BASELINE_HEADER` (crates/reify-audit/src/pdiag.rs) and the committed `crates/reify-audit/pdiag-baseline.txt` are byte-coupled — the always-on test `the_committed_baseline_carries_the_generated_preamble` in crates/reify-audit/tests/pdiag_baseline.rs compares the committed file's prefix against the constant. Editing the preamble constant WITHOUT regenerating the manifest in the same commit turns that test RED even though no diagnostic count changed. Regenerate only via the canonical binary (never hand-edit): `cargo run -p reify-audit --bin pdiag-baseline-gen -- --project-root . > crates/reify-audit/pdiag-baseline.txt`. reify gotcha: tests/infra/test_reify_audit_ptodo.sh defaults to target/release/{reify-audit,ptodo-baseline-gen}, and its freshness guard compares binary mtime against the last COMMIT epoch of crates/reify-audit. In a warm lane, after a debug-only build (`cargo build -p reify-audit --bin reify-audit --bin ptodo-baseline-gen`), running it with REIFY_AUDIT_NO_COLD_BUILD=1 still SKIPS the (a)/(b) ratchet blocks and prints '0 failed'. Point it at the fresh debug build via the testability seam instead: `REIFY_AUDIT_NO_COLD_BUILD=1 REIFY_AUDIT_BIN=$PWD/target/debug/reify-audit REIFY_PTODO_GEN_BIN=$PWD/target/debug/ptodo-baseline-gen bash tests/infra/test_reify_audit_ptodo.sh`. Then confirm the '--- (a) Ratchet' section appears in the log (observed task #6816: 30 → 36 assertions once it ran).

Extension of the reify-audit freshness/ratchet-skip trap (mem 517045fa, 14567ba5) to the NEW PDIAG gate landed by task #5405. tests/infra/test_reify_audit_pdiag.sh has its own run-count marker: 6 passed at FULL strength vs 4 passed when the ratchet skips — and it exits rc=0 either way, so the count (or the stderr line "skipping the precision-sensitive ratchet (a)") is the only signal that scenario (a) was dropped. Measured 2026-08-26 on task/5405 in _lane-12: committing a merge that touches crates/reify-audit/** advances the guard's epoch (git log -1 --format=%ct -- crates/reify-audit) past a binary that was built moments earlier from that very tree, so a content-CORRECT binary is judged STALE and the gate silently degrades 6→4. Same remedy as the PTODO case: build the release binary AFTER the last commit touching crates/reify-audit, forcing an honest relink with `touch crates/reify-audit/src/lib.rs && cargo build --release -p reify-audit` (~16s), then re-run and require 6 passed plus all three @@PDIAG_HARDGATE_{A,B,C}_PASSED@@ sentinels. crates/reify-audit/ptodo-baseline.txt fingerprints are line-number-erased and deduped (format "{path} :: {kind} :: {text}", separator is space-colon-colon-space), so ONE baseline entry can stand for MANY source lines — the 5 entries seeded by task #6087 cover 14 lines, and the T12 layer-B seam entry alone covers 8 identical lines that must ALL be fixed or the entry survives. The section 6.6 ratchet is a SUBSET oracle (comm -23 live baseline), so shrinking SOURCE keeps it green while shrinking the BASELINE first turns it red: always land source fixes BEFORE regenerating the baseline. Regenerate only via target/release/ptodo-baseline-gen with REIFY_PTODO_TASKS_DB pointed at the real tasks.db (a DB-present run is a strict superset of the degraded run the ratchet performs); never hand-edit or sed it. An empty 0-byte baseline is the valid PRD section 6.4 zero-residual-debt end state, pinned by tests/ptodo_baseline.rs validate_accepts_empty_baseline, but the file must stay tracked and present because baseline_is_well_formed asserts path.exists().

Completing a PTODO lane delta-A burndown task requires a SECOND edit that no gate catches: after removing the offending marker from source, you must also delete that fingerprint's line from crates/reify-audit/ptodo-baseline.txt. The §6.6 ratchet (tests/infra/test_reify_audit_ptodo.sh) is a one-directional SUBSET oracle — it reds only when live-minus-baseline is non-empty — so a baseline entry whose marker is gone passes silently forever. crates/reify-audit/tests/ptodo_baseline.rs:11-23 states the contract: the 5 grandfathered entries "can only be burned down". Delete the single line surgically; never regenerate the file with ptodo-baseline-gen, since a regeneration can silently ADD entries and the ratchet is shrink-only.

Verifying reify-audit PTODO findings in a warm lane requires a DB-PRESENT sweep, which the infra test does NOT give you. `tests/infra/test_reify_audit_ptodo.sh` scenario (a) runs `env -u REIFY_PTODO_TASKS_DB ptodo-baseline-gen --project-root "$REPO_ROOT"`, and warm lanes have no `.taskmaster/` (seeded tracked-files-only), so that sweep runs DB-ABSENT: the liveness lane is skipped entirely and the ratchet only proves `live ⊆ baseline` — it cannot confirm an `orphaned`/`unknown-id` finding is actually produced. To verify a liveness finding, snapshot the real DB (`cp /home/leo/src/reify/.taskmaster/tasks/tasks.db{,-wal,-shm} /tmp/snap/`, read-only, avoids racing fused-memory) and run `REIFY_PTODO_TASKS_DB=/tmp/snap/tasks.db ./target/release/ptodo-baseline-gen --project-root "$PWD"`, then diff against `crates/reify-audit/ptodo-baseline.txt` in BOTH directions (`diff <(sort live) <(sort baseline)`) — never the one-way `comm -23` subset oracle, which is blind to a LOST finding. Baseline fingerprints are `path :: kind :: text` and so are line-number independent; a finding's cited line number drifts as the file grows while its fingerprint does not.

content: reify-audit ratchet-ledger regenerators (plinecite-baseline-gen, pdoccover-baseline-gen): NEVER redirect stdout into the ledger (`... > crates/reify-audit/<lane>-baseline.txt`). The shell truncates the file before the run reads its committed rows from the working tree, so a shrink-only render keeps zero rows. Before task #6935's fix (commit 2ac5377074) that run exited 0 and silently wiped the ratchet. Regenerate with `cargo run -p reify-audit --bin <lane>-baseline-gen -- --project-root . --write`, which replaces the file in place through a temp-file rename. To re-verify, pipe stdout to `| diff -u <ledger> -`. Since that fix, a shrink-only run refuses a zero-byte ledger with exit 3 (restore it with `git checkout -- <ledger>`).

395d6a09-665a-419c-b255-40f64e3e0d37.content: Regenerating crates/reify-audit/ptodo-baseline.txt is asymmetrically expensive by DB mode. `ptodo-baseline-gen --project-root <root>` under `env -u REIFY_PTODO_TASKS_DB` (degraded/structural-only, the mode the ratchet gate runs in) finishes in seconds; the same binary with REIFY_PTODO_TASKS_DB pointed at a real tasks.db exceeded 5 minutes without completing, because the ζ inverse lane walks git history per finding (51 task-cites-deleted-path findings on main as of 2026-08). Budget a long foreground timeout or background+poll for a correct (DB-present, superset) regen — and note that a task worktree has no .taskmaster/, so a correct regen is not available there at all: regenerating in a lane silently drops the DB-dependent `orphaned` fingerprints, yielding a baseline that then fails the `comm -23` subset check wherever the DB IS present.

3c58aef6-7664-4541-9313-dded8592ce38.content: PDOCCOVER's ratchet baseline (crates/reify-audit/pdoccover-baseline.txt) is INERT until `git add`ed: pdoccover.rs's `load_inputs` gates every read — units.rs, the chunks/*.md corpus and the baseline itself — on `ctx.git.ls_files()` membership, reading content from std::fs only for tracked paths. Writing the file and re-running `reify-audit --pattern PDOCCOVER` without staging it looks exactly like the file having no effect. Same trap applies to any hermetic tempdir fixture for this detector: `git init` plus `git add -A` is mandatory, not decoration.

4ec04e82-a134-46ab-91dc-30f6bc960b8f.content: Reify PTODO baseline seeding: regenerate `crates/reify-audit/ptodo-baseline.txt` WITH the task DB set (`REIFY_PTODO_TASKS_DB=/home/leo/src/reify/.taskmaster/tasks/tasks.db target/release/ptodo-baseline-gen --project-root . > ...`), never in degraded mode. A cited line yields an `orphaned` fingerprint only when the DB is reachable, so degraded_live is a strict subset of db_present_live; `tests/infra/test_reify_audit_ptodo.sh` scenario (a) runs the generator under `env -u REIFY_PTODO_TASKS_DB` (task worktrees have no `.taskmaster/`) while `/audit` runs in the main checkout WITH the DB. Seeding from a DB-present run makes the baseline a superset of both so `comm -23 live baseline` stays empty in either context; seeding from a degraded run leaves the main-checkout ratchet red.

d0dcf25a-0d12-4ae6-9355-cadd8e82de49.content: PTODO ratchet gotcha: `target/release/ptodo-baseline-gen` run WITHOUT `REIFY_PTODO_TASKS_DB` degrades its liveness lane to structural-only, so it emits a strict SUBSET of the real fingerprint set — `orphaned` / `unknown-id` kinds are simply not classified and silently vanish from the output. Never regenerate `crates/reify-audit/ptodo-baseline.txt` wholesale from a DB-less run: that drops live orphaned grandfather entries and hands future findings free immunity. For a targeted burndown, delete only the one line you resolved, and only if its kind is structural (`untracked` / `malformed-cite` / `bare-ignore` / `phantom-tracking`), whose absence from a DB-less live set IS conclusive. Point it at the real DB with `REIFY_PTODO_TASKS_DB=/home/leo/src/reify/.taskmaster/tasks/tasks.db` when you need the liveness lane.

candidates.content: The capability-manifest sidecar for a solar_challenge PRD can be validated before filing from the dark-factory checkout: `cd /home/leo/src/dark-factory && uv run --project shared python -c "from pathlib import Path; from shared.capability_manifest import load_capability_manifest; load_capability_manifest(Path('<abs sidecar path>'))"`. A pre-filing polarity check (every grep delivered_check must be red on HEAD: an expect=present pattern has 0 hits, an expect=absent pattern has hits) can be run with `git grep -n -E <pattern> HEAD -- <paths>`. Doing both catches what commit_planning's DeliveredCheckPolarityViolation gate would otherwise reject the whole batch for.

The dark-factory capability-manifest sidecar schema (shared/src/shared/capability_manifest.py, DeliveredCheck) accepts four check kinds: grep, script, path and manual — `kind: path` (with paths + expect present/absent) is valid even though the /prd decompose-mode reference text mentions only grep/script/manual. Mechanical kinds (grep, script, path) are copied into the producer task's metadata.delivered_checks by commit_planning; manual stays sidecar-only. commit_planning's polarity gate rejects a batch whose checks are already satisfied on main, so verify each check fails on main before committing (git grep -E -c <pattern> main -- <paths>; git ls-tree main -- <path>).

PRD sidecar authoring tip (from authoring solar_challenge's errors-leaf PRD, 2026-10-14). Validate a capability-manifest YAML sidecar before decompose by running dark-factory's own code from /home/leo/src/dark-factory/.venv/bin/python:
- shared.capability_manifest.load_capability_manifest(path) checks the schema.
- shared.delivered_check_polarity.lint_delivered_checks(checks, files=<task metadata.files>, repo_root=<target repo>, ref="HEAD") checks polarity. Each grep/path check must FAIL on main now and PASS after its producer lands.
An `expect: absent` grep whose matches lie in files outside the task's declared files yields a WARN (absent_overbroad). It clears once the task's metadata.files lists those files. A 'path' kind check is the way to assert a new file exists; a grep cannot.

Capability-manifest sidecar validation recipe used for solar-challenge PRDs: load the YAML with dark-factory's loader via /home/leo/src/dark-factory/.venv/bin/python, with sys.path including /home/leo/src/dark-factory/shared/src, calling shared.capability_manifest.load_capability_manifest(path). Then check polarity by running `git grep -qE <pattern> -- <paths>` in the target repo for each kind: grep delivered_check, confirming it FAILS on current main: an expect:present pattern is absent now, an expect:absent pattern is present now. A check that already passes on main delivers nothing. The S11 sidecar (5 tasks, 22 grep checks) passed both.

Validating a /prd capability-manifest YAML sidecar for solar_challenge before decompose: from /home/leo/src/dark-factory run `uv run --directory shared python` with shared.capability_manifest.load_capability_manifest(<sidecar>) for schema, and shared.delivered_check_polarity.lint_delivered_checks(checks, files=<task files or None>, repo_root=/home/leo/src/solar-challenge) per task for polarity (a check must fail on main and pass after the leaf). With files=None every expect=absent check reports a non-blocking 'absent_overbroad' warning because nothing is declared in scope; those clear once metadata.files lists the edited files. Vacuous checks (expect=present already matching main, expect=absent already absent) are the blocking class.

To verify before filing, run shared.delivered_check_polarity.lint_delivered_checks(checks, files=<the leaf's declared files>, repo_root, ref='HEAD') from dark-factory's .venv. With files=None every absent check reports absent_overbroad, which is a warning artefact.

dark-factory fact for solar_challenge gate decisions, verified by task 631's architect in /home/leo/src/dark-factory at 3a81fad94f on 2026-10-11. type_check_command (like test_command and lint_command) is NOT in RELOADABLE_FIELDS (orchestrator/src/orchestrator/config.py ~5818-6095), so an edit to it is inert until the next orchestrator restart. git.offline_lane_commands is hot-reloadable. verify.py's _build_fallback_config scopes a type_check_command only if it contains 'pyright', so solar_challenge's mypy command always runs unscoped. The interpreter-matrix and newest-releases lanes run only test_command (tests/_verify_suite.py), never type_check_command. So a new static-check gate belongs in a test module under tests/, not in the YAML commands. docs/lint-gate.md §3 gives the reasons: it is in force from the first verify after merge, it cannot fail a branch verified on an old base, and it can carry probes of known verdict.

dark-factory verify scoping, read in /home/leo/src/dark-factory on 2026-10-01 by the task 309 architect.
- Per-task verify: if the plan's `files` list has no .py or .rs path, the verify is TRIVIAL and runs NO command (verify_plan.derive_verify_plan, _has_source_files). So a task listing only pyproject.toml and uv.lock skips its whole per-task verify.
- Merge verify: INV-1 in verify.run_scoped_verification escalates such a no-source diff to the global full gate (test_command, lint_command, type_check_command). It runs in an ephemeral worktree of committed state, so the merge gate still checks it.
- solar_challenge's verify commands parse as OPAQUE in verify_cmd.parse_config_command, because a flag follows `uv run`. They therefore run verbatim and are never file-scoped.
- lint and type start together; test starts after them.
So list a .py test file in any dependency-bump plan if you want the per-task verify to run.

(2) Rebasing a branch that earlier integrated main by merge drops its merge commits. Map the plan steps that recorded them to the replayed commit carrying their effect.
(3) If the branch holds a doc-only commit that a later commit reverts, and the doc has since been rewritten on main, `git rebase --skip` the doc commit and resolve its revert's doc hunk to main's copy.
(4) `git rebase --continue` opens an editor unless GIT_EDITOR=true. Pass `-c rerere.enabled=false` so no recorded resolution applies.

content: You can pre-check a capability-manifest sidecar before commit_planning, so a polarity violation does not reject the whole batch. Load it with dark-factory's shared.capability_manifest.load_capability_manifest. For each label, build its mechanical checks as DeliveredCheckMeta(name=cap.name, kind, pattern, expect, paths, ...).model_dump() plus 'manifest_path', then call shared.delivered_check_polarity.lint_delivered_checks(checks, files=<the task's metadata.files>, repo_root=<project>, ref=GATE_REF). Run it with /home/leo/src/dark-factory/.venv/bin/python -I. An empty findings list means commit_planning will copy every check. kind 'path' (expect present/absent on a file) is a valid mechanical kind beside grep and script. For a held leaf left out of commit_planning, the block keeps task_id: null in the sidecar until the releasing stream's commit stamps it (S10's η and S2's ε both do this).

candidates.content: Diagnostic for the recurring "### Live-Workflow Signals over-reports per-task liveness" class (task 4430, verified first-hand 2026-08-18): the task-2963/2964 corroboration gate IS wired into the render path — it is IN-PROGRESS-ONLY by construction, so it structurally cannot fire for a PENDING task holding a leftover worktree registration. Two deliberate guards: the renderer's `if task.get('status') == 'in-progress':` (task_knowledge_sync.py:~2806) leaves `corroborated=None` for every other status, and detect_live_workflow's gate itself requires `status == 'in-progress'` (live_workflow_detector.py:~555). Trace for dark_factory task 3254 (get_task: status=pending, claimant_run_id=null, heartbeat_at=null, live worktree registered, project lock held): worktree_registered=True; NONE of `_orchestrator_signal_ineligible`'s five rules fire (rule 1 = deferred/done/cancelled, rules 2-3 = blocked-only, rule 5 = pending+deterministic+pure_gate, rule 4 requires `not worktree_registered`), so orchestrator_live=True; the task-3947 stale-worktree gate requires orchestrator_live False so it cannot fire; the 2963 gate requires in-progress so it cannot fire. Result `is_live=True`, rendered `- task/3254: worktree, orchestrator`. So this class of false positive is NOT a missing gate and NOT unreached wiring — do not re-open 2963/2964 looking for a broken gate. Also note the same in-progress-only scoping is deliberately mirrored in `recon_write_policy._corroboration_verdict` (`live_status != 'in-progress'` guard) to preserve task 2964's "the gate and the render must never disagree" invariant, so widening one requires widening the other.

All reconciliation live-workflow gates funnel through fused_memory.services.live_workflow_detector (detect_live_workflow / is_workflow_live_for_task): Stage-2 _render_live_workflow_section (task_knowledge_sync.py), Stage-1 _build_live_workflow_section (memory_consolidator.py, which reuses the Stage-2 renderer), the harness integrity-escalation gate (harness.py), AND the hard write guard recon_write_policy.py Gate 2 that emits ReconLiveWorkflowWriteRejected on set_task_status. So a single detector change propagates to every gate with zero consumer edits. Note Gate 2 calls is_workflow_live_for_task with status= but NOT task_kind, so any new suppression rule that must unblock a recon status write has to be status/task_kind-agnostic.

`live_workflow_detector.detect_live_workflow` has THREE production consumers that must pass an IDENTICAL kwarg tuple (status, task_kind, pure_gate, corroborated) or they silently diverge: `_render_live_workflow_section` (reconciliation/stages/task_knowledge_sync.py), `recon_write_policy.check()` Gate 2 (middleware/recon_write_policy.py), and the integrity-escalation suppression loop (reconciliation/harness.py). Each new detector kwarg has historically been wired at only some of them — task 2963 added `corroborated` to the renderer only, task 3751 added `pure_gate` to the renderer and the policy gate but not the harness — and each gap produced a deterministic (not intermittent) disagreement in production: the renderer stops reporting a task live while Gate 2 keeps rejecting its re-pend write (tasks 599/600, 5 consecutive cycles) or the harness keeps suppressing its stranded escalation. When adding a detector kwarg, wire all three call sites in the same change.

There are three live-workflow gates in dark-factory and they consult DIFFERENT sources — do not conflate them when debugging a liveness decision. (1) `_render_live_workflow_section` (task_knowledge_sync.py) runs the detector to build the prompt payload. (2) The harness integrity-escalation gate (`reconciliation/harness.py` `_run_remediation_pass`, ~L4834-4913) RE-RUNS `is_workflow_live_for_task` per cited task rather than consulting the payload the stage was delivered, so it cannot detect a stale/cross-run citation. (3) `middleware/recon_write_policy.py` Gate 2 blocks `set_task_status` writes against a live task. All three must pass the identical status/task_kind/pure_gate/corroborated tuple (task 2964 invariant).

fused-memory's live_workflow_detector suppression rules (_orchestrator_signal_ineligible) are only as reachable as the kwargs each CALL SITE forwards. Before task 3751, recon_write_policy.check() Gate 2 forwarded only `status` and never `task_kind`, so task 2067's rule 2 and task 2409's rule 3 had never once fired at the one gate that actually blocks a recon-stage write — the rules looked implemented but were dead there. When adding or debugging a detector rule, verify all three production call sites forward the inputs it keys on: recon_write_policy.check() Gate 2, _render_live_workflow_section() in reconciliation/stages/task_knowledge_sync.py (the Stage-2 display path), and reconciliation/harness.py's is_workflow_live_for_task call. A detector-only change fixes the Stage-2 display symptom while the write rejection persists.

Blast radius of making fused_memory.services.live_workflow_detector async (measured for task 3778, 2026-08-17): fused-memory/tests/test_live_workflow_detector.py is 2221 lines / 113 tests, and 85 of them patch `subprocess.run` GLOBALLY (`with patch('subprocess.run', side_effect=...)`) rather than a module-level seam — so any change routing the three probes through a helper silently stops every one of those seams from intercepting. Six further test files patch at their CONSUMER's `from X import Y` binding: test_stages.py and tests/reconciliation/test_stage1.py both at `tks_module.detect_live_workflow` (test_stage1 patches there, not at memory_consolidator, because memory_consolidator imports the RENDERER not the detector), test_harness.py at `harness_module.is_workflow_live_for_task`, plus test_recon_write_policy.py, test_live_task_write_guard.py and test_recon_reliability_integration.py at `recon_write_policy.is_workflow_live_for_task`/`.corroboration_for_task`. Switching any consumer to qualified `module.symbol` calls leaves ~40 patches applying cleanly but no longer intercepting — the tests still PASS while exercising the real git-shelling detector. Also: test_recon_write_policy.py::TestInterceptorSetTaskStatusReconCheckOffload asserts the `asyncio.to_thread` hop around `recon_write_policy.check` BY NAME, so it must be replaced (not migrated) if check() becomes natively async; and test_harness.py::TestIntegrityGateInputParityWithRenderer pins that all three consumers forward an identical status/task_kind/pure_gate/corroborated tuple (task 2964's invariant).

Adding an in-progress liveness input (task 2964's `corroborated`) to a live_workflow_detector consumer will break pre-existing tests that seeded an in-progress task with NO claimant_run_id/heartbeat_at — that fixture shape IS the killed-by-fleet-redeploy case the corroboration gate downgrades. Fix by giving such fixtures a fresh claimant + heartbeat (what a genuinely dispatched task always carries), not by weakening the gate. Hit at test_recon_write_policy.py's task-3751 SCOPE PIN test_non_blocked_normal_task_is_still_rejected.

THE LIVE-WORKFLOW-SIGNALS OVER-REPORTING PATTERN NOW HAS AN OWNING TASK: dark_factory 4430, filed 2026-08-18 by recon Stage 2 (run f3ee5713-3e2a-4dca-9640-3c9e89e6036b).

WHY THIS ENTRY EXISTS RATHER THAN A FOURTH RESTATEMENT OF THE LESSON. At least three prior memories each independently re-derived the same discipline — that the recon payload's "### Live-Workflow Signals" block over-reports per-task liveness and must not by itself justify suppressing a write — and none of them had an owning task. So the lesson kept being rediscovered and re-paid-for every cycle, roughly three weeks running. The durable new information is that the re-derivation loop is now closed by an owner, not the lesson itself. Before re-filing anything in this area, check 4430 first.

THE STRUCTURAL ARGUMENT (independent of any point-in-time reading, which is why it is worth storing). The block ORs three signals and renders them as one comma-separated per-task line, but they are not of equal kind:
- recent-commit is genuinely task-scoped — a commit on the task's own branch.
- a registered worktree is NOT — a leftover worktree survives task completion, so the signal outlives the work.
- the orchestrator signal is NOT — it is a project-wide lock-holder check, so it fires for essentially every task in the project at once, long-terminal ones included, and therefore carries no discriminating information about any individual task.
A line reading "worktree, orchestrator" can thus be composed entirely of non-discriminating signals while looking like positive per-task evidence.

THE TIE-BREAKER. The authoritative liveness test is the TASK RECORD, read via get_task: a live claimant together with a fresh heartbeat. The signals block is a HINT that should TRIGGER that check — never a substitute for it, and never on its own sufficient grounds to skip a write. Any conclusion about a specific task's liveness is a point-in-time observation that can be stale by the next cycle, so re-read rather than carrying a prior cycle's verdict forward.

DIAGNOSTIC-FIRST CAUTION FOR WHOEVER TAKES 4430. Tasks 2963, 2964, 2031 and 2767 are all recorded done, and all four addressed detector-, renderer- or policy-side corroboration for exactly this defect class — yet it still reproduced. Do not assume a gate is missing and write a new one. Establish first whether the existing corroboration gate actually reaches the Stage 2 / memory_consolidator render path; the fault may be wiring rather than absence. Note also that task 3937 (separate) covers Stage 1 asserting a signal absent from its own delivered payload — related but a different defect, do not fold them together.

GOTCHA (found while planning task 3751): recon_write_policy.check()'s Gate 2 (fused-memory/src/fused_memory/middleware/recon_write_policy.py:334-336) calls is_workflow_live_for_task(task_id, project_root, status=live_status) — it forwards ONLY status, never task_kind. So every task_kind-scoped suppression rule in live_workflow_detector._orchestrator_signal_ineligible (rule 2, blocked+deterministic/task 2067; rule 3, blocked+normal-bare/task 2409) has been UNREACHABLE from the gate that actually rejects recon writes with ReconLiveWorkflowWriteRejected. Only the status-keyed rule 1 and the status-agnostic bare-branch rule 4 ever fire there. The other detector call site, _render_live_workflow_section (reconciliation/stages/task_knowledge_sync.py:2621), DOES pass task_kind — so the Stage-2 "Live-Workflow Signals" display and the Gate-2 write decision can disagree for the same task. When adding a detector rule intended to unblock recon, check BOTH call sites; a detector-only change is inert at Gate 2. The interceptor call site (middleware/task_interceptor.py:946) already holds the full `before` task dict under the write lock, so metadata is available there at no extra I/O cost.

Task 'Live-workflow-signal false positive: project-wide orchestrator_live fires for deferred/terminal tasks' completed. Reconciliation's "### Live-Workflow Signals" section (fused-memory/src/fused_memory/reconciliation/stages/task_knowledge_sync.py:_render_live_workflow_section, and its memory_consolidator.py mirror) checks every task in `filtered_task_tree.active_tasks` via `live_workflow_detector.detect_live_workflow()`. That function ORs three signals: worktree_registered, recent_commit, and orchestrator_live. `orchestrator_live` comes from `orchestrator_detector.is_orchestrator_live_for(project_root)` — a PROJECT-WIDE PID-lock check (reads `<project_root>/data/orchestrator/orchestrator.lock`) with NO task-id scoping. Per the module's own docstring, this is intentional for pending/in-progress tasks (avoid racing live dispatch) but the consequence is undocumented-as-a-bug for terminal-ish statuses: `active_tasks` apparently includes `deferred` status, so a deferred (non-dispatchable) task gets `is_live=True` — and thus appears in Live-Workflow Signals — purely because *some other task* in the project is being actively worked by the orchestrator, or even just because the orchestrator process happens to be up.

Concrete evidence: autopilot_video task 452 has been deferred (terminal, human-review-pending) since 2026-04-27T08:33:57Z. It has NO git branch `task/452` (confirmed via `.git/refs/heads` and `.git/packed-refs`), NO registered worktree, and NO recent commit on that branch (branch doesn't exist). Yet it has shown "task/452: orchestrator" in Live-Workflow Signals across 8+ consecutive Stage-2 reconciliation cycles (2026-06-05 through 2026-07-02), purely because the autopilot_video orchestrator has been alive/busy landing unrelated tasks (607-637). A prior investigation (Stage 1, run 853ef190) incorrectly hypothesized an orphaned escalation lock file (data/escalations/esc-452-86.json.lock) as the cause — that hypothesis is REFUTED by reading the actual detector code: `is_orchestrator_live_for` only reads `data/orchestrator/orchestrator.lock`, never touches `data/escalations/*`.

Recommended fix: exclude non-dispatch-eligible statuses (at minimum `deferred`; consider `cancelled`/`done` too, though those likely aren't in active_tasks already) from the live-workflow-signal check — either filter `filtered_task_tree.active_tasks` before calling `_render_live_workflow_section`, or add a status guard inside `detect_live_workflow`/`_render_live_workflow_section` so `orchestrator_live` (the project-wide signal) is not applied to tasks that can never be dispatched. This causes real downstream harm: Stage 2 reconciliation cycles have repeatedly (8+ times) treated a genuinely-stuck, human-review-needed task (autopilot_video 452, missing deliverable docs/mass-task-reset-2026-04-21-findings.md) as having an active live pipeline, which — per the Live-Workflow Authority guardrail — suppresses the human-review escalation it actually needs.

The reconciliation "Live-Workflow Authority" policy (fused_memory reconciliation prompts stage1/stage2, live_workflow_detector.py; signals: task/<id> worktree registered, recent branch commit <6h, orchestrator project-lock held) is a CROSS-PROCESS policy for the reconciliation service deciding whether to touch tasks the orchestrator may be driving. Its orchestrator_live signal is project-wide and trivially true inside the running orchestrator, so it cannot be applied verbatim inside the orchestrator scheduler (it would mark every task live). The scheduler-internal equivalents of "actively driven" are self._dispatched (a slot this run holds) + dispatch/requeue cooldown; the human-handoff signal is the open L1. The Scheduler does NOT hold escalation_queue or git_ops — inject the escalation queue via attribute injection mirroring harness.py:6868 (review_checkpoint.escalation_queue).

Task 3947 (add staleness/expiry detector for the worktree_registered signal in fused-memory/src/fused_memory/services/live_workflow_detector.py) was fully implemented across all 6 plan steps and committed to branch task/3947 (commits 4fdc249dbf, 1a6bf2c547, fb395d35c8, 8cfa86dba4, 01995a5f96, b06c5788f0). No consumer wiring was needed — all three production callers (task_knowledge_sync.py, recon_write_policy.py, harness.py) read only `is_live`. Final verification: tests/test_live_workflow_detector.py (142 tests) plus the three consumer regression suites test_stages.py/test_recon_write_policy.py/test_harness.py (1127 total) all green, `ruff check fused-memory` clean, `pyright` in fused-memory 0 errors.
