Every "chore: save WIP before warm-lane reclaim (task 1933)" commit in the reify repo is MISATTRIBUTED. The trailing "(task 1933)" is a HARDCODED STRING LITERAL in dark-factory at orchestrator/src/orchestrator/git_ops.py:5762 — introduced by DF commit ba92ca6f26 "feat(1933 step-4): GREEN — wire reclaim-on-exhaustion safety valve in git_ops". It is authoring provenance for the DARK-FACTORY task that built the reclaim valve; it is NOT derived from the task whose WIP is being saved, and there is no id-reading logic at that site at all.

This corrects a hypothesis that recurs in escalations (esc-5344-3, esc-5937-5/-6): agents repeatedly guess that the committer "reads a task id from stale lane state" or "uses the reclaiming task's id". Both are wrong; a single constant explains every observation.

CROSS-REPO ID COLLISION makes it worse than a stale label: 1933 is a dark-factory task id, but the commit lands in reify, where readers and any commit-to-task attribution tooling resolve it against REIFY's task 1933 — an unrelated GUI Editor-debounce test consolidation from April 2026.

MEASURED IN REIFY ON 2026-08-19: 6 such commits on main, belonging to tasks 6181, 5937, 5894, 5360, 5729 and 5596 (each identified by the merge that brought it in); 33 across all refs. A prior count on 2026-07-31 was 11 across all refs, so the population roughly tripled in three weeks.

Other WIP-saver variants carry NO task id and are therefore harmless: "chore: save WIP before inter-iteration rebase" (837 on main) and "chore: save WIP before requeue rebase" (266 on main). Only the warm-lane-reclaim site embeds an id.

TRACKED AS dark-factory task 3105, which already contains the full diagnosis and a prefix-preserving fix (derive the id from `victim_branch`, already in scope two lines above the call; the classification contract is prefix-based via WIP_SAFETY_COMMIT_PREFIXES so the suffix is free to change). Re-query its status before acting — as of 2026-08-19 the literal was still present at git_ops.py:5762, i.e. the fix had not landed. Rewriting the already-landed reify commits is explicitly out of scope there; the reify-main residue is permanent.

A `chore: save WIP before warm-lane reclaim (task NNNN)` commit on a reify task branch carries a MISLEADING task id: NNNN names the dark-factory reclaim machinery's own task, not the reify task whose work the diff contains. Seen on task/6315, whose sole commit beyond main was titled "(task 1933)" while `git show` proved it was 6315's own comment-only edit to gui/src/stores/unitLadder.ts (dark-factory 1933 is the spare_warm_lanes/reclaim work). Always `git show` such a commit to identify its real owner — never trust the parenthesized id, and never conclude the branch carries a foreign task's WIP from the message alone.

A commit on a reify task branch titled `chore: save WIP before warm-lane reclaim (task <OTHER-id>)` is NOT necessarily throwaway WIP: the reclaim sweep stamps that generic message over whatever was uncommitted at reclaim time, which can be a complete, green TDD step implementation. On task/6560 the commit a9bee09ba387 carried the whole GREEN body of `Engine::realize_solid_sdf_at`, with the sweep naming an unrelated task (1933) as the reclaimer. Always `git show` such a commit before judging it, and note the cited task id identifies the RECLAIMER, not the author.

In reify warm lanes, a commit subject "chore: save WIP before warm-lane reclaim (task NNNN)" can carry a DIFFERENT task's complete, green implementation — the reclaim sweep stamps whichever task id it is running under, not the one that authored the diff. On task/6560, commit 849f01b8b907 was labelled "task 1933" but was in fact the full GREEN half of 6560's final TDD pair (renaming Engine::realize_solid_sdf to realize_solid_sdf_at and threading VoxelResolution). Always `git show` a WIP-labelled tip and judge it by its diff, not its subject, before assuming the branch is unfinished or that foreign work leaked in.

Warm-lane reclaim can commit a task's real work under the generic message "chore: save WIP before warm-lane reclaim (task NNNN)", where NNNN is a DIFFERENT task than the branch's own. MECHANISM: the WIP-save is attributed to the RECLAIMING task — the task that next acquired the lane — not to the task that authored the diff, so the subject-line id is systematically wrong rather than occasionally wrong. THREE confirmed instances, all naming task 1933 as the reclaimer: (1) on task/5788 the branch-tip commit a12ef7072ad4 was messaged as task 1933 WIP but its diff was 5788's own S2 fix (dimension.rs to_display_units AREA/VOLUME arms); (2) on task/6093 the commit b46852a7395c reads "chore: save WIP before warm-lane reclaim (task 1933)" but its entire content is 6093's own RED test (+84 lines to crates/reify-compiler/tests/modal_options_validation_tests.rs, the test `rayleigh_damping_fields_propagate_declared_dimensions`, whose doc comment says "task-6093" throughout), sandwiched chronologically between 6093's other commits; (3) on task/5711 the tip commit 956358856b46 is titled "(task 1933)" while its content is task 5711's own esc-5711-3 fix (folded in from mem 35c6058e, 2026-08-26). When re-planning or auditing a branch that already carries commits, always run `git show <sha>` on every commit and classify it by DIFF CONTENT plus its position in the chronology, never by the task id in its subject — a foreign-looking task id does not mean the diff is foreign work, and treating it as such drops a completed TDD step back to pending or gets a legitimate step wrongly reverted as contamination. Do not rewrite the mismessaged commit itself; record the correction in a later commit message and in plan.json instead.

A commit on a task branch titled `chore: save WIP before warm-lane reclaim (task NNNN)` names the RECLAIMING lane's task, not the task whose work the commit contains — the id in that subject line is misleading provenance. On task/6120 the commit `5c9bbd5219ff` was labelled "(task 1933)" but actually carried task 6120's complete GREEN implementation. When following the architect "Already-Committed Work" protocol, always `git show` such a commit and judge it by its DIFF (which files, matching the task's FILES list), never by its subject line.

Warm-lane reclaim can leave a commit on YOUR task branch titled "chore: save WIP before warm-lane reclaim (task NNNN)" where NNNN is the RECLAIMING task's id, not yours — the message names a foreign task while the content is entirely your own uncommitted work. Seen on task/6181, which carried "…(task 1933)" holding only 6181's own files. Do not read that label as a cross-task scope breach: verify by content with `git show --stat <sha>` before escalating. Likewise, `git diff --stat <old-main-tip>..HEAD` inflates a branch's apparent scope with commits main has since gained; use the three-dot `git diff --stat main...HEAD` for the branch's true diff.

GOTCHA CLUSTER (topic='warm-lane-reclaim-wip-commit-caution'): a `chore: save WIP before warm-lane reclaim (task NNNN)` commit on a reify task branch has UNRELIABLE provenance — NNNN is typically the RECLAIMING task's id (often 1933), not the branch's own task, and the commit can also silently REVERT prior commits or add throwaway debug/probe code instead of just adding new WIP. Never trust the subject line, and never assume the branch is foreign work, unfinished, or green on the strength of it — always `git show <sha>` and judge by diff content and direction before acting. See same-topic peers for confirmed per-task instances (5429, 5711, 5788, 6093, 6120, 6178, 6181, 6315, 6560) and the misleading-id / silent-revert / leftover-debug-code sub-variants.

A `chore: save WIP before warm-lane reclaim (task NNNN)` commit on a task branch can cite a task id UNRELATED to the work it actually carries — the reclaim WIP-saver stamps whatever id it has to hand, not the branch's task. Observed on task/6178, where commit 100cdae94e0a was labelled "task 1933" but its diff touched only 6178's own four surfaces with unmistakably 6178-specific content. Do NOT treat such a commit as foreign WIP or a scope breach on the strength of its subject line: diff it first (`git show <sha>`) and judge by content. Discarding it would have silently dropped real, higher-quality work — in this case a correction that superseded the task description's own framing of the defect.

Cross-repo seam fact (measured 2026-09-17, reify task 7244): dark-factory consumes reify's warm-lane-degenerate-ref-check.sh verdict in two places, and `degenerate` is read as "this branch carries ZERO task work":
- orchestrator/src/orchestrator/harness.py (~6287): `_branch_is_degenerate(...) or git_ops.warm_lane_ref_is_degenerate(tid)` downgrades a MARK_DONE recovery to revert-to-pending, which re-dispatches a task whose work already landed.
- orchestrator/src/orchestrator/git_ops.py `_abort_lane_acquisition`: deletes the branch (retention-biased — it only deletes what it can prove degenerate).

Script resolution order is PROJECT OVERRIDE FIRST (`_resolve_warm_lane_script`): reify's own scripts/ copy wins for reify, and dark-factory keeps its own relocated copy at orchestrator/scripts/warm-lane/warm-lane-degenerate-ref-check.sh for projects without an override. Those two copies can therefore DRIFT silently — as they now do, since reify's fix landed and DF's copy still carries the old `#N`-only grammar (dark_factory task 5566, external dep reify:7244).

Also note the verdict's real meaning: `landed` proves the tip CITES task N, not that the tip is task N's own work. A foreign commit whose subject names the task — or a sanctioned docs-only commit made directly on main such as `docs(7305): …` — makes a zero-commit ref parked on it read `landed`.

reify warm-lane hazard class (discovered 2026-08-20 during /unblock 6128): a leftover `task/<id>` branch carrying commits beyond main is NOT fail-safe on reify's dispatch path. dark-factory has two different behaviours and only one of them refuses. `create_worktree` -> `_cleanup_leftover_branch` (orchestrator/src/orchestrator/git_ops.py:7948) raises RuntimeError rather than deleting a branch with commits beyond main. But reify dispatches via WARM LANES, and `acquire_warm_lane`'s gamma-reattach route (git_ops.py:6570) does the opposite: `_orphan_has_commits(full_branch)` True -> `git worktree add <lane> <branch>` WITHOUT -b -> `_reuse_warm_lane` (commit-WIP -> rebase_onto_main -> re-provision). The agent is then handed the leftover branch's content as an already-rebased, clean starting state. Consequence: for a task whose premise was RESCOPED or whose prior work was REJECTED by a ruling, the stale branch is a live landmine — a resumed agent can build the new scope on top of the rejected implementation and land both. Do not assume "the orchestrator will refuse to touch a branch with WIP"; that is only true on the create_worktree path. When rescoping/rejecting a task's prior approach, explicitly dispose of its branch.

Reify task-branch tips whose HEAD is a `chore: save WIP before warm-lane reclaim (task N)` / `chore: save WIP before requeue rebase` commit can carry a STALE working tree that silently REVERTS earlier commits on that same branch — and the WIP-save can name a different task (N) than the branch it lands on. Measured 2026-08-27 on branch task/6178 in _lane-7: HEAD fe36a407c503, subject "…(task 1933)", diff was 2 lines in gui/src/debug/bridge.ts undoing type guards added by ancestor commits c3fefbb60015/713e97b106 on the same branch; the whole frontend suite was 2 failed / 5363 passed, and the only signal was those 2 red tests. Consequence for a re-invoked architect or implementer: never infer a branch is green from its commit log or from "verify passed earlier" — run the suite on the actual tip before calling `mark_step_committed` / `report_ready_to_merge`. `git show <tip>` on a WIP-save commit is the cheap first check: a reclaim-time save that only DELETES lines from your own recent work is a revert, not a save.

Warm-lane WIP safety-commits can sweep a FOREIGN file from an unrelated task onto your branch. The harness auto-commits uncommitted work before a rebase/requeue/reclaim with a subject like "chore: save WIP before requeue rebase" — that subject names the RECLAIMING task, not the owner of the swept file. On task 5784 (lane _lane-37, commit adc99655ef) such a commit carried in crates/reify-compiler/tests/zz_probe2_6862.rs, a temporary probe belonging to still-pending task #6862, which would otherwise have landed on main as two permanently-running print-only #[test] fns that assert nothing. This applies whether you are the implementer reporting pre-committed WIP, or a re-planning architect/reviewer inspecting an already-committed branch before pre-satisfying steps or recommending merge: run `git show <sha>` (or `git show --stat <sha>` for a quick file-list-only pass) and check every file against the task's own scope — not just whether it satisfies the next pending step. Confirm safe deletion with `git branch --contains <sha>` (only your task branch = no other branch loses work) and `git grep <name>` (no tracked references; a bare tests/*.rs file is an auto-discovered cargo integration target with no registration to clean up), then verify with `git diff --name-only main..HEAD` that only in-scope files remain.

In a reify warm lane, the reclaim-time "chore: save WIP before warm-lane reclaim (task NNNN)" safety-commit can be the branch tip and can leave the tree NON-COMPILING (it snapshots mid-edit — e.g. a const moved between modules with the `use` not yet added), and its message may name an unrelated task id even though the diff is entirely the owning task's files. Always run a `cargo check` on the touched crates at session start before assuming the branch is green, and read the WIP commit's diff rather than trusting its message for provenance (task 6672 / esc-6672-4).

Gotcha when re-planning a reify task branch after a warm-lane reclaim: the reclaim's auto-WIP commit ('chore: save WIP before warm-lane reclaim (task NNNN)') can carry a WRONG task id in its message. On task 6653's branch it said 'task 1933' but contained 6653's own step-6 solver.rs work. Judge such a commit by `git show <sha>` content plus a first-hand test run, never by the id in its message. Then pre-satisfy it with mark_step_committed and record the mislabel as a plan design decision, so reviewers do not flag it as a scope breach.

Reify warm lanes: a lane reclaim can COMMIT a task's uncommitted working-tree WIP onto that task's branch as `chore: save WIP before warm-lane reclaim (task NNNN)` — where NNNN is the *reclaiming* task's id, NOT the branch's owning task. Observed 2026-08-11 on task/5429 (tip a13f164727 labelled "task 1933" but adding a throwaway `tmp_probe2` debug test to 5429's own test file). Consequence: a resumed task branch can carry throwaway debug/probe code at its tip that verify will happily pass (a test with `println!` and no assertions is neither a clippy nor a test failure) but review will flag as leftover debug code — the same finding class that already blocked 5429 once (esc-5429-1 issue 3). When resuming a task whose branch already has commits, always `git show` the tip and grep the branch diff for `println!|dbg!|_proto_|tmp_probe` before assuming the branch is merge-ready.

Reify task 5181 ("Reconciliation found_on_main check: compare current-HEAD tracked state, not just ancestor-of-cited-commit (post-hoc-revert blind spot)") was CANCELLED 2026-07-12T17:42:24Z — not abandoned, but re-scoped: the fix touches dark-factory's own fused-memory reconciliation code (orchestrator/src/orchestrator/{git_ops,harness,config}.py), which reify cannot land itself. It was cleanly re-filed as dark_factory task 2500 (identical title, status=pending, priority=high) at 2026-07-12T17:42:39Z — ~15s after the reify cancellation, confirming this was a deliberate cross-repo re-scope via the standard "mis-scoped to reify" pattern, not a dropped effort.

Prior reify-side partial work is already captured in mem0 31e0649c-1ab8-4b63-b6cb-57028f253393: an agent had added git_ops.commit_effect_reverted_at_head(sha) (a fail-soft revert detector) and wired it ONLY into the reconciliation sweep (Harness._reconcile_one_stranded). Three other found_on_main chokepoints remain unfixed: Harness._already_landed_dispatch_gate (live dispatch gate), SpeculativeMergeWorker._redrive_coalesce_members (merge queue), and workflow._recover_before_execute/_merge (workflow recovery) — plus the kind='merged' analog merge_queue.reconcile_landed_row. These are now in scope of dark_factory task 2500, not a new reify task.

Reconciliation note: reify's "Tasks Needing Memory Hint Attention" list (Stage 1 snapshot) still showed 5181 as in-progress and flagged it for a memory_hints read-modify-write — that snapshot was stale by the time Stage 2 ran; the task had already gone terminal (cancelled). No memory-hint update was made (hints on terminal tasks are static) and no duplicate reify task should be re-filed for this lineage going forward — dark_factory:2500 is the sole live tracker.

Reify task branches: if the harness "chore: save WIP before requeue rebase" commit has tracked `tree-sitter-reify/src/.generated_outputs.stamp` (a generated sha256 manifest main gitignores), the safe fix is `git rm --cached` PLUS copying main's ENTIRE tree-sitter ignore block verbatim into the branch's .gitignore (.gitignore:48-57, header "# Tree-sitter generated (regenerate via scripts/tree-sitter-generate.sh)").

Two tempting variants are wrong, both measured: (a) `git rm --cached` ALONE leaves the ignore gap open, so the NEXT requeue sweep re-adds the file — this is why branches 6164, 6638 and 5415 each needed multiple "re-untrack" commits; (b) adding just the single missing `.generated_outputs.stamp` line CONFLICTS with main, because main added two lines at that anchor (`.generated_outputs.stamp` and `.tmp-*`), so it is not a same-line add.

Root cause (verified 2026-09-18 by reading the implementation, not inferred): dark-factory `orchestrator/src/orchestrator/git_ops.py` `GitOps.commit` (:8697) stages with `git add -A -- . ':!.claude'`, and both requeue WIP-sweep call sites (:4410, :7634) use it. A whole-tree add honours only the worktree's OWN .gitignore, never the merge target's, so any branch whose merge-base predates main commit 7104ff4b5b (2026-09-08, which added the ignore rule) re-captures the artifact on every requeue. At least nine tasks have hit it: 5385, 5415, 5417, 5931, 6080, 6164, 6231, 6615, 6638.

Tracked as reify task 7538 (the class fix — repo-side guard and/or dark-factory-side staging change). Do not file a new task for a fresh sighting; add the sighting to 7538.

In reify, a task's .task/plan.json step->commit shas can ALL become unreachable from its own branch tip without any work being lost: when a warm lane is reclaimed mid-task and the branch is later replayed onto a newer main, every commit gets a fresh sha while plan.json keeps the pre-replay ones (observed on task/5937: 13/13 recorded shas dangling, `git for-each-ref --contains <sha>` empty, yet 13 subject-identical twins present on the branch and `git diff <old-lineage-tip> <new-tip>` showing only unrelated files from the newer base). So a phantom-done check based on sha REACHABILITY yields false positives; confirm by diffing the old lineage tip against the branch tip and checking the task's own files are absent from that diff. Related artifact: the reclaim WIP-saver commits the interrupted step's work under the RECLAIMING task's id ("chore: save WIP before warm-lane reclaim (task NNNN)"), so git blame can attribute one task's change to another.

A warm-lane reclaim can leave a commit on a task branch whose message names a DIFFERENT task than the work it contains — e.g. task/5711 carries `chore: save WIP before warm-lane reclaim (task 1933)` (956358856b46), which is entirely task 5711 code (esc-5711-3's `params_in_underivable_constraints` abstention). The id in that message is the task whose dispatch triggered the reclaim, NOT the author of the parked WIP. When auditing branch provenance, read the DIFF, not the subject line: treating such a commit as cross-task contamination and reverting it destroys real, green work.

content: In reify, a branch commit titled "chore: save WIP before warm-lane reclaim (task 1933)" is written by dark-factory's warm-lane WIP-save sweep. "task 1933" names that dark-factory mechanism, not a reify task. As of 2026-10-16, 119 such commits existed across refs and 64 had landed on main. Its content may be legitimate in-scope task work, so `git show` it before planning. For a re-dispatched task, treat it as committed work you can pre-satisfy and reword with `git commit --amend` if a commit-message obligation must be met.

candidates.content: solar_challenge storage seam, amended by task 577 (branch task/577, commits 27ba3f9 and 7b17f19; holds once 577 merges): RunStorage.save_home_run and save_fleet_run build their RunRecord with _saved_run_row BEFORE they create the run directory or write any file, and call _upsert_run_row(row) last. A run id the store refuses, or a status outside RUN_STATUSES, raises ValueError with nothing written; tests/unit/test_web_database.py asserts storage.data_dir is empty after such a save. _saved_run_row reads the clock once, so a completed run saved with no created_at has created_at == completed_at, both stamped when the save starts, not after its files are written. For task 468 (JobManager's 'running' placeholder row): build it as a RunRecord and write it through _upsert_run_row, as the saves do.

solar_challenge test seam for seeding web runs. Re-checked 2026-10-12 at main 5da62aa by the task 425 architect; it replaces 20fac469 and holds once task 425 merges.
(1) RunStorage.__init__ creates no schema, so a bare RunStorage needs solar_challenge.web.database.init_db(storage.db_path) first, as tests/unit/test_web_jobs.py::_run_storage does. app.extensions['storage'] is already initialised.
(2) save/load round trips compare == EXACTLY for FleetSummary, the per-home SummaryStatistics and HomeConfig, so no approx is needed. To check a saved run's row, read it with RunStorage.run_record(run_id), which returns a frozen RunRecord with typed type/status Literals, rather than list_runs' dicts.
(3) tests/_web_runs.py is the one test-side home of 'save a run as a finished job does':
- store_fleet_run(storage, run_id, fleet_results, *, name=None, created_at=None);
- store_home_run(storage, run_id, config, results, *, name=None, status: RunStatus = 'completed', created_at=None).
Task 425 moves every unit-test copy onto it: test_web.py, test_web_history.py, test_web_fleet_charts.py, test_web_run_badges.py, test_web_results_chart_targets.py and test_web_heat_pump_results.py. After that, only the storage-level tests (test_web_database.py and test_web_storage_roundtrip.py) call RunStorage.save_home_run or save_fleet_run directly, with hand-made summaries on purpose. A new web test that seeds a run should call these helpers rather than derive summaries itself. Task 438 moves the e2e conftest onto them; task 439 gives production one save function the helpers can delegate to.

solar_challenge, task 627 amendment pass (branch task/627, commits c08ef33 and 0c37031; holds once 627 merges), superseding the failure-path behaviour in memories e8755bed, 75d59c76 and 7384fcd3. JobManager._record_failed_job no longer runs both UPDATEs in one try and one commit. It calls module-level _record_failed_job_row(state, error_traceback, completed_at, conn), then _record_failed_run_row(state, completed_at, conn), each inside `with _best_effort_failure_record(<table>, state, conn):`, a context manager that gives the block a transaction of its own and logs an ERROR from solar_challenge.web.jobs instead of raising. So a refused jobs write still leaves the run failed and a refused runs write still leaves the jobs row failed; the helper name _record_failure_in_table in the plan no longer exists. TestJobManagerUnrecordedFailures asserts the accepted table's content, not only its status (jobs: message, error_traceback, completed_at; runs: error_message, completed_at): with status-only assertions, 3 of 4 wrong-binding mutants left the class green. Task 468 (runs write into RunStorage) and task 646 (exceptions escaping _run_job) edit the same code and must keep that rule.

solar_challenge web storage seam after task 446 (planned on task/446 at base 51edc0f, 2026-10-04; it holds once task 446 merges).

RunStorage in src/solar_challenge/web/storage.py is the one reader of a runs row by id:
- run_record(run_id) -> RunRecord | None. RunRecord is a frozen dataclass with one field per runs column, under the column's name. config_json and summary_json stay raw JSON text. dataclasses.asdict(record) reproduces the old dict(row).
- latest_run_named(name) -> RunRecord | None.
- update_run_labels(run_id, labels: Mapping[RunLabel, str | None]) -> RunRecord | None. RUN_LABELS = ('name', 'notes'). An absent key is left unchanged, None is written as NULL, and a non-label key raises ValueError before any write.
- run_name delegates to run_record.

api.py, history.compare_page and assistant.get_run_results call these instead of SQL. assistant.get_run_results now takes a RunStorage, not a db_path.

api.history_patch_run checks in this order:
1. request_json_object;
2. 404 when run_record is None;
3. labels = {label: data[label] for label in RUN_LABELS if label in data};
4. 400 'No fields to update';
5. update_run_labels.

Task 331's 'name/notes must be a JSON string' 400 belongs on the label values between steps 4 and 5.

The list and aggregate reads, and jobs.py's run-row writes, still use get_db directly. Follow-up ticket tkt_0RVDC3RASSWP4NBT3J87JMT39A moves them.

solar_challenge seam for runs-row writes (planned by the task 577 architect on 2026-10-08 at main 264ded0; holds once task 577 merges). src/solar_challenge/web/storage.py gets these:
- `_saved_run_row(*, run_id, name, run_type: RunType, config, summary, status: RunStatus, error_message, created_at, duration_seconds, n_homes) -> RunRecord`: the save policy. created_at defaults to now; completed_at is now only when status is 'completed'; notes is None.
- `RunStorage._upsert_run_row(row: RunRecord)`: executes `_RUN_ROW_UPSERT`, an INSERT ... ON CONFLICT(id) DO UPDATE built from dataclasses.fields(RunRecord) and `_COLUMNS_A_RESAVE_KEEPS = ("id", "created_at", "notes")`, with named parameters bound from asdict(row).
save_home_run and save_fleet_run both call `self._upsert_run_row(_saved_run_row(...))`. A save given a status outside RUN_STATUSES then raises ValueError (RunRecord's refusal) instead of sqlite3.IntegrityError.

For task 468 (moving JobManager's run-row writes into RunStorage): the 'running' placeholder row from jobs.py::_record_new_job can be built as a RunRecord and written through _upsert_run_row, or through a plain INSERT derived from the same fields if a duplicate id must fail. Description: FINDING (review 20261003T162726, runtime seam; verified by `grep -rn configure_logging src` at HEAD 386b2b2). Heuristic 10 (uniformly enforced).

WHAT'S WRONG: runtime/logging.py::configure_logging is called only in src/solar_challenge_platform/runtime/roles/ingest.py (~L37) and runtime/roles/dispatch.py (~L56). Task 160 wired just those two roles. The api, bill, settle, migrate, seed and validate roles, and runtime/asgi.py, never call it. Under systemd/journald their root logger has no handler, so:
- INFO lines are dropped.
- WARNING and above reach stderr only through Python's lastResort handler, with no timestamp, level or logger name.

CONCRETE LOSS: TimescaleStore's INFO line "requested window … widened to …" (timeseries/timescale_store.py ~L749-760) exists so an operator can see the size of a `scp-settle --refresh-cas` recompute. It never appears under scp-settle. scp-bill's per-account diagnostics are likewise invisible, which hurts monthly-close troubleshooting.

FIX:
- Call configure_logging() at the start of every role's main(), honouring LOG_LEVEL.
- For scp-api, make sure uvicorn's own log config does not override or duplicate it (e.g. configure first and pass log_config=None, or merge).
- Add one parametrised test over every console-script role in tests/runtime/test_logging.py, asserting the root logger carries the configured handler and level after the role's setup. A new role then cannot ship silent.

Role module file names below are from the review's read. The architect should confirm the exact list under src/solar_challenge_platform/runtime/roles/.
Analysis: Call configure_logging() as the first statement of every run_<role> (api, bill, settle, migrate, seed, validate, deploy; ingest/dispatch moved ahead of parse_args for uniformity) and at the top of runtime/asgi.py; scp-api passes log_config=None to uvicorn so uvicorn's dictConfig neither overrides nor duplicates the root handler. One parametrised test over the console-script roles drives each with --help and asserts the root logger carries the configured handler and LOG_LEVEL.
Steps completed: 1/1
Modules: src/solar_challenge_platform/runtime/asgi.py, src/solar_challenge_platform/runtime/logging.py, src/solar_challenge_platform/runtime/roles, tests/runtime/test_logging.py

Completed: Cross-run merge_finalized reads plus durable alias resolution
Description: PRD: plans/merge-status-durable-non-landed-prd.md task label gamma. Capability manifest: plans/merge-status-durable-non-landed-prd.capability-manifest.md and its YAML twin. Prereqs: none. INTERMEDIATE - unlocks beta. Runs in parallel with alpha (disjoint files).

WHY THIS EXISTS. EventStore.latest_merge_finalized filters every query to `run_id = self.run_id`. Measured 2026-08-28 on the live store: runs.db holds 2,620 merge_finalized rows across 228 run_ids spanning 80 days, of which the CURRENT run can see 17 - 0.65%. 885 of those rows are non-done (blocked 699, superseded 86, conflict 35, unknown_branch 17, abandoned 11, wip_halted 3) and become permanently unreachable the moment their run ends. Runs last ~8h (median 8.26h over the last 7 days), so the durable tier's memory window equals one run. This task makes those rows reachable.

WORK.
1. Add an EXPLICIT cross-run mode to latest_merge_finalized (e.g. a cross_run flag), returning the matched row WITH its own run_id so the caller can always tell whether it is current. Do NOT change the default: the existing run-scoped behaviour stays the default for every current caller.
2. Add a superseded_by reverse index: given a `coalesce-*` train id, find the rows whose superseded_by equals it, so a train id resolves to its members instead of resolving through no tier at all.
3. Add absorbed_request_ids to the merge_finalized event payload at the finalize site in merge_queue.py, so an attach/door-coalesced loser's request_id resolves to the primary's outcome durably and across restarts.

DO NOT SIMPLY DROP THE RUN FILTER. Its docstring states the reason it exists: it "prevents merge_status from silently surfacing stale prior-run terminal outcomes". That hazard is real - a branch resubmitted this run whose PRIOR run finalized conflict must not read as conflict now. The PRD's decision D2 is what keeps the guarantee: a cross-run row may only ever populate a labelled last_outcome block and may NEVER set an outcome state. Preserving that property is task beta's job, but it is only possible if this task returns the run_id alongside the row - so returning it is mandatory, not decorative.

ALREADY PRESENT, NOT YOUR WORK. The merge_finalized payload ALREADY carries request_id, branch, state, snapshot_tip, merge_sha, superseded_by, generation, reason and landed_via_chain. Item 2 therefore needs NO new write - it is a read-path index over data already on disk. Only absorbed_request_ids (item 3) is a new write, and it is the single new write in the whole PRD. A superseded member already emits its own row carrying superseded_by, so it is resolvable cross-run once item 1 exists.

COST IS NOT A CONCERN HERE, MEASURED. idx_events_type ON events(event_type) already covers the predicate and merge_finalized is 2,620 of 364,134 rows (0.7%). Measured 2026-08-28 on the live 161 MB store: cross-run 0.0 ms vs run-scoped 0.2 ms. Do not add an index without first reproducing a problem.

TACTICAL, DECIDE HERE: whether absorbed_request_ids should be backfilled for existing rows or written forward-only. Suggested forward-only - the reverse index covers superseded members historically, and door-coalesced losers are a narrow class.

Completed: Rebuild merge_status's read path: epistemic states, reason codes, journal tier
Description: PRD: plans/merge-status-durable-non-landed-prd.md task label beta. Capability manifest: plans/merge-status-durable-non-landed-prd.capability-manifest.md and its YAML twin. Prereqs: alpha and gamma (in-batch) plus OUT-OF-BATCH tasks 4649 and 4498. INTERMEDIATE - unlocks delta and epsilon.

WHY THIS EXISTS. merge_status has exactly one run-spanning tier (git-authority) and it can only ever prove `done`. Every not-landed proposition therefore degrades to `unknown` the moment the observing run ends - and runs last ~8h. `unknown` today conflates at least five distinct propositions: never submitted, finalized in a previous run, journaled and awaiting recovery, a coalesce/train id that resolves through no tier by construction, and landed-but-unattributable. Agents read `unknown` as "not landed" and re-submit work already on main.

WORK. Rebuild the read path per the PRD's contract section.
1. Tier order (decision D5): live snapshot -> event store current-run -> git-authority -> durable journal -> event store cross-run -> no_record. Ordering is by STRENGTH OF CLAIM, not cost: putting a cheap tier ahead of git would report a landed branch as stale_record, recreating the exact task 6873 failure this PRD exists to fix.
2. Emit the new epistemic states from alpha's MergeState: no_record, stale_record, journaled. Narrow `unknown` to ONE meaning - the probe itself failed.
3. Add a required `reason` enum on every epistemic response, and a `source` field naming which tier answered.
4. Make `hint` DERIVED from `reason` through one table. It is a module constant today; it must stop being one.
5. Add the durable-journal tier reading data/orchestrator/merge_queue.json via MergeQueueStore - the same file recover_pending_merges already reads at startup.
6. Attach `last_outcome` as an ALWAYS-ON ENRICHMENT (decision D4), not a tier: whenever any durable row exists, regardless of which tier set `state` - so even a state=done response carries the history. One pass, one place.
7. Wire alias resolution from gamma: train ids via the superseded_by reverse index, door-coalesced losers via absorbed_request_ids.

THE INVARIANT THAT MUST NOT BE BROKEN (decision D2). A prior-run row may populate last_outcome but may NEVER set an outcome state. Concretely: state is in OUTCOME_STATES implies source is live, event_store or git; and last_outcome carrying is_current_run=false must never equal `state`. This preserves in full the property the run_id filter exists to protect - a prior run's conflict can never appear as present truth. `stale_record` is an assertion about our RECORDS, not about the merge. Do not "simplify" this by letting the cross-run tier set an outcome state.

DO NOT DERIVE A LANDING VERDICT HERE (invariant I5). This module consumes whatever the git tier returns. It must make NO is_ancestor, find_merge_marker or patch-id call of its own. The landed half belongs to docs/prds/landed-not-done-recovery.md (tasks 4647/4648); growing a second landing authority beside branch_work_landed is the INV-5 shape that PRD's own design rejects.

FILE SERIALIZATION IS LOAD-BEARING. escalation/src/escalation/server.py is the collision surface: out-of-batch 4649 (extracts the git-authority tier into an importable module) and 4498 (the Tier-3.5 call sites) both own it and are wired as hard prereqs so three claimants never contend. Consume 4649's extracted module - do not re-extract it.

NOTE ON 4498. Its scope item 2 asks whether `unknown` remains the right degradation. That decision is now THIS PRD's (decisions D1/D2) and 4498 has been amended to retain only its delivered_checks wiring. Do not re-litigate it.

INV-8 NOTE. This adds a synchronous sqlite read and a small atomic JSON read inside an async MCP tool. Measured: the cross-run query is ~0.05 ms and the journal is a single small file, so this is affordable today. Keep the journal read a bounded single-file load;…[truncated, 10900 chars total]

Measured 2026-10-15 (task 6927 architect) on a backup-API scratch copy of dark-factory's data/orchestrator/runs.db: 478,825 events and 4,310 merge_finalized rows, with no sqlite_stat1. Host load was 112-194 on 32 cores. Each query was a miss run 200 times on one persistent connection.

Today the EventStore merge_finalized reads plan as SEARCH idx_events_type plus a per-row filter, for cross-run and run-scoped alike, at 17-23 ms p50. Partial indexes ON events(json_extract(data,'$.<key>')) WHERE event_type='merge_finalized' bring those misses to about 0.005 ms p50. The absorbs read additionally needs a json_array_length(data,'$.absorbed_request_ids') > 0 guard in BOTH the query and the partial-index WHERE; without it, it keeps scanning idx_events_type at about 22 ms p50.

Two traps: SQLite uses a partial index only when the query's WHERE implies the index's, so the event_type term must stay a literal; and plans are heuristic, identical on a 1-row tmp store and the full copy.

Through EventStore, which opens a new connection per read, connect + select 1 alone was p50 0.44 ms, p99 4 ms. A single indexed read showed a p99 tail of 46 ms from host scheduling noise. That tail matters for any p99 < 50 ms latency pin, such as task 4834's B10.

Completed: Unblock whole-blob metadata repair on done tasks: update_task's done_provenance floor makes metadata_mode='replace' structurally unusable
Description: Split out of task 3697 (esc-3697-4) by the steward on 2026-08-06. 3697 is rescoped to ship its documentation + tested migration script; THIS task provides the write path 3697 needs, then executes the live migration 3697 could not.

OBSERVED, first-hand code reads (not inferred):

1. sqlite_task_backend.py:2575-2591 — update_task raises DoneProvenanceWriteAuthorityError
   for ANY metadata payload that parses to a dict containing 'done_provenance'. The check
   is PRESENCE-ONLY: no value-unchanged carve-out, no metadata_mode carve-out. It fires
   before _resolve_metadata_mode, before ensure_connected(), before the row SELECT.

2. _merge_metadata has no deletion sentinel (merge is shallow {**old, **new}), and there is
   no task-level metadata_delete_keys — that API exists only for MEMORIES
   (memory_service.py / update_memory). backend.set_task_status
   (sqlite_task_backend.py:1938-1947) accepts no metadata argument.

3. The privileged non-protocol seam stamp_audit_metadata (sqlite_task_backend.py:2835,
   added by task 2201) also hardcodes _merge_metadata(mode='merge'), so it cannot retire a
   key either, and it is not reachable over MCP.

4. Single enforcement point: the interceptor does NOT pre-check independently — it catches
   the backend exception at task_interceptor.py:4366 and converts via .to_error_dict().
   Task 2203 deliberately deleted the duplicate guard copies. So a fix has ONE code site,
   not several.

CONSEQUENCE (the generalization worth fixing): every done/merged task carries
done_provenance, so metadata_mode='replace' is structurally unusable on ALL of them — while
task_backend_protocol.py:209 and server/tools.py:5956 both document replace mode as
"the sanctioned repair path". That doc claim and this floor are in direct tension. Any
task needing a key RETIRED (not just added) from a done task's metadata is currently
unfixable through public API.

CANDIDATE DESIGNS (architect decides; do not assume):
  (A) Identical-passthrough carve-out — permit a payload whose done_provenance is
      byte-identical to the stored value, on the reasoning that an unchanged passthrough is
      not a write of that key. Smallest change, preserves the floor's actual intent
      (set_task_status remains the only thing that can CHANGE done_provenance), and unblocks
      whole-blob repair on every done task. Must compare against the STORED value read under
      the same txn, not trust the caller.
  (B) Task-level metadata_delete_keys on update_task, mirroring the memories API. Most
      general, largest blast radius, and needs its own write-authority thinking (deleting
      done_provenance must stay forbidden).
  (C) Widen the privileged stamp_audit_metadata seam to accept a mode/deletion argument and
      expose a narrow operator-only path. Follows the existing 2201 precedent.

WHATEVER IS CHOSEN, also reconcile the docstrings at task_backend_protocol.py:209 and
server/tools.py:5956 so "the sanctioned repair path" is either true or qualified.

Completed: Adopt the atomic SQLite access primitive in fused-memory's remaining persistent shared-connection stores (task backend, tickets, write journal, durable queue, planned-episode registry)
Description: Leo ruled D2 = B + low-priority C on 2026-09-17 (RCA at /home/leo/src/dark-factory/plans/recon-sqlite-database-locked-rca-2026-09-16.md, UNTRACKED — read it from the main checkout).

The prerequisite task adds a shared primitive in `shared/src/shared/async_sqlite_base.py`: single-hop reads plus write units serialised per connection. None is a regression against pre-4926 main: every failure mode below falls through to the citation gate and never produces a wrong stamp.

(1) SHOULD-FIX: skills/_shared/deriving-landed-sha.md, rc=0 arm, the paragraph "`$c^1` is main-just-before-the-merge only when `$c` was created ON main". Its confirmation step cannot detect the hazard it names. The step reads: "`git rev-list --parents -n 1 "$c"` — the first parent listed must itself be on main before `$c`; if it is the branch side, read `$c^2`".
- Take a merge built on the branch side (an integration branch cut from task/T merges main, then main is fast-forwarded to it). `$c^1` is the task tip, yet `git merge-base --is-ancestor $c^1 main` exits 0 and `--is-ancestor $c^1 $c` exits 0.
- `$c^1` even sits on `git rev-list --first-parent main`, because the fast-forward makes the branch side main's first-parent chain. After a fast-forward, git keeps no record of which side was main.
- Separately, `rev-list --parents -n 1` prints `$c` itself first, so "the first parent listed" is ambiguous.
Failure: an agent on a target project that merges branch-side runs the check and sees it pass. It then trusts `contained-before rc=0` and skips a merge sha it could have stamped, degrading to the citation gate. Fix direction (the architect decides, after validating against real git):
- EITHER discriminate on something the graph does record. For example, in the pinned shape `$c^1` equals or descends from `git rev-parse task/<TASK_ID>`.
- OR say plainly that parent order is not recoverable, and treat rc=0 on a project with unknown merge direction as undecided, deferring to the citation gate.
Pin the chosen rule with a real-git test in orchestrator/tests/test_group_merge_candidate_ordering.py. The existing branch-side test only reads `^2` because it built the merge itself; nothing exercises the remedy the prose prescribes.

By default, rebase, am and cherry-pick set the committer date to now, so on a single machine they never make a later commit older than an earlier one. The realistic single-machine cause is several commits sharing one committer-date second. The reviewer reproduced this: with every commit in one second and no skew, the default order picked an unrelated side-branch merge (contained-before rc=0) and --topo-order picked the right one. For a file that neither parent changed relative to the other, a merge commit's combined diff is silent - the same semantics that make `git show --stat <merge> -- <path>` print nothing. So the guard cannot distinguish "the branch dropped planned work" from "the branch never owned this file and main supplied it".

Completed: Index the cross-run merge_finalized lookups so merge_status's durable history meets INV-8 (prerequisite of 4834's B10)
Description: Prerequisite for task 4834 (merge_status boundary suite, PRD plans/merge-status-durable-non-landed-prd.md leaf ζ), whose row B10 requires the cross-run lookup on a production-sized store (at least 300k events, at least 2,500 merge_finalized rows) to stay under p99 50 ms. Filed on Leo's ruling of 2026-10-13 (esc-4834-2, sitting item 367 = B1): keep B10 as written and make the lookup meet it.

MEASURED 2026-10-13 (L2 watcher pre-investigation, read-only; experiments on a scratch copy of the live runs.db, 470,625 events / 4,228 merge_finalized, host load 52-61 on 32 cores, 300 iterations each):
- orchestrator/src/orchestrator/event_store.py::EventStore._select_merge_finalized runs `SELECT run_id, task_id, data, timestamp FROM events WHERE event_type = 'merge_finalized' AND <key> ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 1`, where <key> is `json_extract(data, '$.request_id' | '$.branch' | '$.superseded_by') = ?`, `task_id = ?`, or `EXISTS(json_each(... '$.absorbed_request_ids'))`.
- The events table has four indexes (run, (run, task), type, ts). EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN shows only `SEARCH events USING INDEX idx_events_type (event_type=?)` followed by a per-row filter over every merge_finalized row, so cost grows with history (2,620 rows on 2026-08-28, 4,228 now).
- Misses: wall p99 21-33 ms, CPU p99 19-26 ms; the absorbs miss: wall p99 105 ms; the 3-read _durable_history miss path: wall p99 117 ms, CPU p99 78 ms.
- This is not a regression: task 4830 (b0dc465bc6) implemented the PRD base's (516ab65125) query shape. The PRD's '0.0 ms' achievability basis matches a hit on the newest row (query-only 0.005 ms), not a miss.

WORK. Add partial indexes WHERE event_type = 'merge_finalized' on json_extract(data, '$.request_id'), json_extract(data, '$.branch'), json_extract(data, '$.superseded_by') and (task_id), plus one supporting the absorbs lookup; add a `json_array_length(data, '$.absorbed_request_ids') > 0` guard to the absorbs query so it can use it. Create them idempotently (CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS) where the store creates its schema, so existing stores gain them at startup. On the scratch copy this brought every miss to wall p99 1.1-2.5 ms (CPU <= 0.8 ms) and the 3-read path to 6.0 ms; each index built in 0.1-0.16 s. Re-measure on your own copy; do not trust these figures.

CONSTRAINTS.
- INV-8 (docs/legibility/design-invariants.md) bounds WALL time on the event-loop thread, and _durable_history runs synchronously inside the async resolver; that is why the bound is not restated as CPU time.
- An 'uses an index' assertion alone passes on today's slow plan; any plan assertion must name the specific new indexes.
- Do not change the query's semantics (newest matching row per key; run-scoped and cross-run tiers).
- The absorbs guard's long-run cost is unmeasured: the live store has 0 rows with absorbed ids today.

TESTS. A query-plan test asserting each cross-run key lookup uses its partial index; existing event-store and merge_status tests stay green. Task 4834's B10 is the latency pin and depends on this task.
Analysis: PREMISES VERIFIED on base 877b58678c. orchestrator/src/orchestrator/event_store.py (1,320 lines) holds `_SCHEMA` (events table + idx_events_run/task/type/ts), `_ensure_schema` (executescript of _SCHEMA, failure logged as 'event_store: schema init failed'), `_MergeFinalizedKey(Enum)` whose values are fixed SQL predicates (request_id/branch/superseded_by = json_extract(data, '$.<k>') = ?, task_id = ?, absorbs = EXISTS(json_each(events.data, '$.absorbed_request_ids') ... = ?)), and `_select_merge_finalized`, which composes `SELECT run_id, task_id, data, timestamp FROM events WHERE event_type = 'merge_finalized' [AND run_id = ?] AND <key> ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 1 | ORDER BY id`. Readers: latest_merge_finalized, merge_finalized_superseded_by, merge_finalized_absorbing. Callers: escalation/src/escalation/server.py::_durable_history (cross_run=True, 3 reads on a miss) and ::_current_run_answer (run-scoped), merge_lane/worker.py (run-scoped branch read). `_MergeFinalizedKey` is referenced only inside event_store.py. The writer (merge_lane/worker.py, the merge_finalized emit) always writes absorbed_request_ids as a list ([] when nothing was absorbed).

MY OWN MEASUREMENT, 2026-10-15. Scratch copy made with sqlite3's backup API from data/orchestrator/runs.db (source opened read-only) into /tmp/arch-6927/. Python's SQLite is 3.50.4. Host load was 112-194 on 32 cores. The copy holds 478,825 events, 4,310 merge_finalized rows and 323 runs. There is no sqlite_stat1, and nothing in the repo runs ANALYZE or PRAGMA optimize. 0 merge_finalized rows have invalid JSON. 203 rows carry absorbed_request_ids, all empty, so 0 rows have non-empty absorbed ids. Query-only timings below are misses on one persistent connection, 200 iterations.
- BEFORE: every key, cross-run and run-scoped alike, plans as `SEARCH events USING INDEX idx_events_type (event_type=?)` plus a per-row filter. The one exception is run-scoped task_id, which uses idx_events_task. Cross-run miss p50 is 17-23 ms; p99 is 36-226 ms; absorbs p99 is 104 ms.
- AFTER, with partial indexes idx_mf_{request_id,branch,task_id,superseded_by} and idx_mf_absorbs: cross-run plans are `SEARCH events USING INDEX idx_mf_<key> (<expr>=?)` or `(task_id=?)`, and the run-scoped plans use them too (task_id stays on idx_events_task). Neither ordering needs a temp B-tree. Every key's miss is p50 0.005 ms, p99 at most 0.18 ms. The UNGUARDED absorbs query still plans on idx_events_type (p50 22 ms, p99 236 ms). With the json_array_length guard it uses idx_mf_absorbs (p50 0.005 ms, p99 0.011 ms). Each index built in 0.11-0.22 s.
- Through EventStore, which opens a new connection per read: connect + select 1 alone is p50 0.44 ms, p99 3.97 ms. The 3-read _durable_history miss was p50 108 ms, p99 488 ms before. With the indexes but the absorbs read still unguarded it was p50 32 ms, p99 202 ms; the unguarded absorbs read alone was p50 30 ms, p99 335 ms. So the guard is what clears the 3-read path.
- WORST CASE FOR THE GUARD: I added 4,310 synthetic absorbing rows, as if every merge_finalized row had absorbed something. The guarded miss was then p50 5.2 ms, p99 25.5 ms at load 186.
- The plans are identical on a fresh one-row DB and on the live copy (no stats, so the planner is heuristic). A small tmp_path test store therefore reproduces the production plan.
- OBSERVATION FOR 4834 (not this task's to fix): on this host, oversubscribed about 6x, a single indexed read through EventStore showed a p99 tail of 46 ms against a p50 of 0.62 ms. That tail is host scheduling noise, not query cost.

APPROACH. Make each merge_finalized lookup key one definition, rendered to two things: the partial index that serves it and the statement that reads it (heuristic 11, SPOT). Concretely, `_MergeFinalizedKey` becomes public `MergeFinalizedKey`. Each value is a small frozen `_Lookup(indexed, match, narrowing=None)`. The enum has an `index_ddl` property (`CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_mf_<name> ON events(<indexed>) WHERE event_type = 'merge_finalized'[ AND <narrowing>];`) and a pure `select(value, *, run_id, latest_only) -> (sql, params)`. That method holds the composition that `_select_merge_finalized` does inline today; `run_id=None` means cross-run. The absorbs key indexes `event_type` narrowed by `json_array_length(data, '$.absorbed_request_ids') > 0`, and its select repeats that narrowing. `_ensure_schema` runs `_SCHEMA` followed by every key's index_ddl, so existing stores gain the indexes at the next construction. `_select_merge_finalized` keeps the execution, the fire-safe warning and the projection, and takes its statement from key.select(...). The public reader signatures and semantics do not change: newest matching row per key, oldest-first for superseded_by, run-scoped by default with cross_run as the opt-in.

TESTS. They go in orchestrator/tests/test_event_store.py, new class TestMergeFinalizedIndexes; the file grows from 1,228 to about 1,300 lines. They EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN the exact statement production runs, via the public `MergeFinalizedKey.select`, against a real EventStore-created DB. Cross-run plans must name `USING INDEX idx_mf_<key> (`. Run-scoped plans must not rely on idx_events_type. A store whose idx_mf_* indexes were dropped (simulating a pre-task store) must regain them on EventStore construction and keep answering. The existing TestLatestMergeFinalized, TestMergeFinalizedSupersededBy and TestMergeFinalizedAbsorbing classes are the regression net for semantics. The escalation merge_status tests must stay green. The p99 latency pin is task 4834's B10 and is NOT re-pinned here.

Heuristic 14: event_store.py goes from 1,320 to about 1,370 lines, below the 1,500 soft ceiling, so no split is warranted.
Key decisions: Partial expression indexes scoped to the merge_finalized rows (WHERE event_type = 'merge_finalized'), one per lookup key, named idx_mf_<key>. The alternative, full-table expression indexes, was rejected.; Each key's index DDL and its SELECT are rendered from one MergeFinalizedKey/_Lookup definition. The `event_type = 'merge_finalized'` term is a shared literal constant, never a bound parameter.; The key enum becomes public, with a pure `select(value, *, run_id, latest_only) -> (sql, params)`. The plan test EXPLAINs exactly that statement. Rejected alternatives: a copy of the SQL in the test, private-name access, and patching sqlite3.connect to trace statements.

TWO COUNTERINTUITIVE PERFORMANCE MEASUREMENTS on dark-factory's merge/event substrate, taken 2026-08-28 on the live stores. Both overturned an assumption that was about to be designed around.

1. A CROSS-RUN merge_finalized query is NOT more expensive than the run-scoped one — it measured FASTER. On data/orchestrator/runs.db (161 MB, 364,134 rows in `events`): run-scoped lookup 0.2 ms, cross-run lookup 0.0 ms (sub-0.05 ms). Reason: `idx_events_type ON events(event_type)` already covers the predicate and merge_finalized is only 2,620 of 364,134 rows (0.7%), so the scan is tiny either way; adding the run_id term buys nothing. CONSEQUENCE: an INV-8 (loop-thread-occupancy-bounded) concern about widening this query inside an async MCP tool evaporated on measurement — no new index is warranted, and anyone proposing one should reproduce a problem first. The run_id filter is there for CORRECTNESS (staleness), never for cost.

2. A find_merge_marker-shaped full-history scan costs 0.84-1.11 s on this repo. Measured with `git log main --fixed-strings --grep="Merge task/NNNN into main" --max-count=1` over 62,928 commits, three trials, on a MISS (a miss scans the whole history). This independently corroborates a separate 2026-08-28 finding that the scheduler's per-candidate find_merge_marker call is the dominant term in its tick.

WHY BOTH ARE WORTH KEEPING: they point in opposite directions and it is easy to guess the wrong one. The sqlite tier looks expensive (a 161 MB file, 80 days of history) and is essentially free; the git tier looks cheap (one `git log`) and costs ~1 s per call. When ordering lookup tiers, the sqlite/event-store tiers can be ordered purely on correctness, but any git tier placed ahead of them imposes a real ~1 s floor on every answer that falls through to a later tier — which is affordable for an interactive probe on a 15-60 s poll backoff, and NOT affordable in a per-candidate loop.

SpeculativeMergeWorker.snapshot() AS A MIGRATION TARGET — what it genuinely reaches, and three MEASURED blind spots that make a "migrate the private read onto snapshot()" plan step unsatisfiable. Measured on task 5028 (γ5), 2026-09-12.

WHAT IT REACHES. `snapshot()['entries']` stamps every pipeline item with task_id, branch, state, position, lane, request_id, waiter_alive, worktree — and it is SOURCED FROM THE REGISTRY, not only from containers: `_lifecycle.non_terminal_items()` surfaces an item that was merely `_register_item`-ed and never queued. So `worker._lifecycle.current(rid)` and `worker._lane_buffers` membership BOTH migrate onto one read of the entry list, and the result is stronger than either: a request wrongly appended to a lane buffer enters `_container_ids`, drops out of the registry section, and therefore surfaces as `queued` instead of its registry state. Proven non-vacuous by mutation: planting a twin straight into `_lane_buffers['normal']` flips the census from [('verifying','normal')] to [('queued','normal')]. Also real: `snapshot()['owned_merge_worktrees']` is the resolved-string view of `_owned_merge_worktrees` (`_register_owned_merge_worktree` memoises `str(wt.resolve())`), so membership tests migrate exactly.

BLIND SPOT 1 — QUEUED and LANE_BUFFERED share the single wire string `queued` (`merge_queue.py::_REGISTRY_STATE_TO_WIRE`, whose own docstring says snapshot() has never distinguished lane-buffered-but-undispatched from freshly-queued). Any test whose subject is the QUEUED->LANE_BUFFERED hop CANNOT migrate: the assertion would pass whether or not the hop fired. Four rows in test_merge_queue_duplicate_submission.py are residual for exactly this.
BLIND SPOT 2 — there is NO liveness key. `worker._running` has no public accessor and no snapshot field (esc-5028-2).
BLIND SPOT 3 — OBJECT IDENTITY is not observable. snapshot() reports task_id, branch and request_id; a journal-recovery twin shares all three with the original by construction, so `_live_items[rid] is original` has no public equivalent.

ALSO: snapshot() reports the lane buffers AND the undrained outer `_queue` under the same `queued` string, so a migrated "queue untouched" row sees a REQUEUED item at the tail that the lane buffer alone could not report. Two γ groups hit this and both amended the expectation upward (it is a strengthening, not a break) — expect it rather than treating it as a regression.
