candidates.content: pytest gotcha (dark-factory, task 4030, MEASURED on pytest 9.0.3 + pytest-timeout 2.4.0, orchestrator's resolved versions): when TWO `@pytest.mark.timeout(...)` decorators are stacked on the same test function, the one pytest-timeout actually enforces is the one CLOSEST to the `def` line (the innermost/bottom decorator, which Python applies FIRST), not the outermost/top one. Mechanism: `_pytest.mark.structures.store_mark` does `obj.pytestmark = [*existing, mark]` — each newly-applied decorator's mark is appended to the END of the list, and decorators apply bottom-up, so `pytestmark[0]` is always the closest-to-def mark. `_pytest.python.PyobjMixin.obj` builds `own_markers` via `own_markers.extend(get_unpacked_marks(self.obj))`, preserving that same order. `Node.get_closest_marker(name)` returns `next(self.iter_markers(name=name), default)`, and for a single function node `iter_markers` yields `own_markers` in list order — so `get_closest_marker` resolves to `own_markers[0]` == `pytestmark[0]`. `pytest_timeout._get_item_settings` calls exactly `item.get_closest_marker("timeout")`. Net effect: for code introspecting `fn.pytestmark` to find "the" timeout value (e.g. a guard test correlating a marker to a computed worst-case bound), use `markers[0]`, not `markers[-1]` — `[-1]` would pick the marker pytest-timeout does NOT actually enforce when two are stacked. A code reviewer suggested `[-1]` as "matching pytest's closest-marker resolution" for exactly this reason and was backwards; verify against the installed library source rather than trusting that intuition.

dark-factory pytest norm (task 4215, MEASURED on pytest 9.0.3 + pytest-timeout 2.4.0): a module-level `pytestmark = pytest.mark.timeout(N)` is the preferred way to opt a whole test file out of the 60s pyproject default, and it is SAFELY ADDITIVE to files that already carry per-test decorators. With pytestmark timeout(300) plus @pytest.mark.timeout(7) on one test, get_closest_marker('timeout').args is (7,) for the decorated test and (300,) for an undecorated one — the decorator still wins, the module mark is only a floor for tests lacking one. (Complements the task-4030 entry on STACKED decorators, which is a different question.) Design consequence for guard tests: only the module-level form is a statically SOUND lower bound over every collected item — that is the documented contract of orchestrator.pytest_markers.module_level_marker_names, which walks tree.body rather than ast.walk. A decorator sweep such as test_marker_registration_drift._applied_marker_names is an explicit UPPER bound, so a file with 3 tests where only 1 is decorated reads as "has timeout" while the other 2 remain at the 60s cliff. Also verified safe against verify_plan's deselection detector: expression_definitely_deselects("not warm_lane_bash", {'timeout'}) is False, identical to the empty-set result, so adding these marks cannot flip a module to "definitely deselected".

Gotcha (measured 2026-10-07, task 6157): the shared timeout-mark coverage helper test_merge_queue_concurrent_verify.py::_timeout_mark_offenders reads only CLASS-level pytestmark, but pytest applies the closest timeout mark, so a METHOD-level @pytest.mark.timeout replaces (can tighten) its class mark. orchestrator/tests/test_merge_queue.py is the one guarded-family module that carries method-level marks (13 at base 08fd381ca1), so a class-only TestTimeoutMarkCoverage there would pass while a 300s method mark os._exit()s the xdist worker on a 360s wait_responsive bill. Separately, the AST wait-budget engine bills a wait inside a loop or nested def ONCE, and bills run.outcome()/merge_through_lane() at 0, so over-mark such classes by hand.

GOTCHA for tests that run a nested pytest via subprocess.run(..., text=True, timeout=N) (task 6384, measured CPython 3.13, pytest 9.0.3). (1) On timeout, TimeoutExpired.stdout/.stderr are BYTES or None even with text=True. Decode them first (bytes -> .decode('utf-8', errors='replace'), None -> ''); see tests/scripts/test_timeout_method_policy.py::_text. (2) The partial output is useful without PYTHONUNBUFFERED. A pytest child killed mid-run hands back its full header and its progress characters, because pytest flushes its terminal writes. A child killed within its first ~1-3s may have printed nothing yet. (3) To read the timeout marks of every test in the current module, -k-deselected ones included, read `pytestmark` off request.module and its test_*/Test* objects (test_timeout_method_policy.py::_timeout_marks). Use mark.kwargs.get('timeout'), because a method-only mark has no 'timeout' key. Do NOT call Module.collect() again: in pytest 9 it re-runs parsefactories and the xunit-setup registration, so it registers the module's fixtures a second time. (4) subprocess.run's timeout SIGKILLs only the child controller. With `-n N`, a worker blocked in a test outlives the controller for a while (it exited on its own later, as measured). A test that deliberately times out a child should run it with `-n 0`.

GOTCHA (dark-factory, measured 2026-09-06 on task 4176): TWO facts about pytest-timeout under xdist that existing memory does NOT cover. The known part — thread method os._exit()s the worker, shows as 'node down' — is already recorded; these two are the parts that mislead a debugger.

1. A @pytest.mark.timeout(N) MARKER CLAMPS DOWN a LARGER --timeout on the command line. pytest_timeout.py:388-410 `_get_item_settings` resolves the marker FIRST and falls back to `item.config._env_timeout` (the --timeout value) only when the marker is None. Precedence is marker-wins, NOT max-wins. Orchestrator verify runs `uv run --directory orchestrator pytest tests/ --tb=short -q --timeout=300`, so every test gets 300s EXCEPT any carrying a marker below that. Measured case: test_aiosqlite_leak_isolation.py::test_a_thread_exception_actually_fails_a_test_under_this_projects_inifile carries @pytest.mark.timeout(120) and therefore ran with a budget 2.5x TIGHTER than the rest of the same run — while being one of the suite's most load-sensitive tests (it spawns two full pytest subprocesses; measured 15.42s/30.74s/31.46s across three isolated runs, a 2x spread from ambient load alone). Every such marker was authored as an UPWARD opt-out from the ini's `timeout = 60`; that intent silently inverts under a harness that raises the run-level budget. When auditing timeouts, compare each marker against the HARNESS --timeout, not just against the ini default.

2. A worker death TRUNCATES the run, so the pass count in a red verify log is NOT the suite. orchestrator/pyproject.toml pairs `timeout_method = "thread"` with `--max-worker-restart=0` (the latter deliberately, to avoid a restart/re-collect/re-die hang — see its comment). Consequence: os._exit() of one worker ENDS the session. Measured on the same run: the red log read "1 failed, 728 passed, 1 skipped in 209.67s" while a clean re-run of the identical command read "19622 passed, 17 skipped in 953.70s". The red run recorded 3.7% of the suite. "728 passed / 209.67s" reads like a completed fast suite and is neither — do not conclude from a red verify log that the other tests passed, and do not use its duration as a suite baseline.

Corollary for diagnosis: pytest-timeout's "+++ Timeout +++" stack dump is written to `item.config.get_terminal_writer()` INSIDE the xdist worker, which is not forwarded to the controller. So the one artifact naming the cause is absent from the controller log BY CONSTRUCTION; its absence is not evidence against a timeout reading.

REMEDY CONSTRAINT: do not answer any of this by raising the number. plans/flake-ledger-prd.md:221 — "do not widen a timeout as a fix for anything" — with the task-1836 precedent where a 10s->30s widening masked a real SIGHUP bug for a day. The sanctioned verdict vocabulary is `passes_in_isolation`; record the evidence and leave the diagnosis to a de-flake task.

GOTCHA (dark-factory, confirmed against installed pytest_timeout source, task 5147): a `@pytest.mark.timeout(N)` marker OVERRIDES the `--timeout` CLI value in BOTH directions — it is never a floor. `pytest_timeout.py::_get_item_settings` reads the marker first and consults `item.config._env_timeout` (which `get_env_settings` fills from CLI `--timeout` -> `PYTEST_TIMEOUT` env -> ini `timeout`) ONLY when the marker yielded None. So a marker WINS even when the CLI value is larger.

THE INVERSION BAND. Two budgets bracket every orchestrator test: `orchestrator/pyproject.toml [tool.pytest.ini_options] timeout = 60` (what a bare local `pytest` gives) and `--timeout=300` (what verify passes — orchestrator/orchestrator.yaml:5 and all 8 segments of dark-factory-orchestrator.yaml's fleet chain). That yields three regimes, and only the middle one is a defect:
* N <= 60 — tightens under BOTH. Deliberate tight bound; leave alone. test_verify_clock_stop.py carries 13 markers at 15s because those tests assert a watchdog fires FAST.
* 60 < N < 300 — INVERTS. The author wrote N > 60 intending to LOOSEN against the ini default in front of them, and under verify it silently TIGHTENS 300 -> N. This is the accident.
* N >= 300 — loosens under both. Safe.

WHY IT COSTS THE WHOLE RUN, not one test: `timeout_method = "thread"` means a breach `os._exit()`s the xdist worker, and `--max-worker-restart=0` declines to replace it — the session truncates and blames whatever innocent test shared the dead worker. This mechanism blamed tasks 4176, 4384 and 4405 in a single day via test_aiosqlite_leak_isolation.py's `@pytest.mark.timeout(120)`.

MEASURED CENSUS (AST over orchestrator/tests/**/*.py, 2026-09-06): 150 marker sites — 62 in the inversion band, 36 at <=60, 17 at >=300, 35 symbolic. Every symbolic constant resolves safely (WHOLE_TREE_SCAN_TEST_TIMEOUT=300, HEAVY_BARRIER_TEST_TIMEOUT=300, PYTEST_TIMEOUT=960).

DO NOT reason about this as "raise every marker below 300" — that sweeps 98 sites across ~35 files and is actively wrong for the lower 36. The band, not the threshold, is the hazard.

WHAT IS ALREADY GUARDED (so you do not rebuild it): the CONFIG side is fully pinned by tests/scripts/test_fallback_verify_config.py (`--timeout > 60` on the fleet chain, `--timeout >= 300` on every per-module orchestrator.yaml). test_whole_tree_scan_timeout_guard.py enforces >=300 but ONLY on module-level `pytestmark` of whole-tree rglob scanner files. test_marker_registration_drift.py checks marker NAMES only. `orchestrator.pytest_markers` is names-only and has NO value extractor — the only value-resolving AST helper is `_module_level_timeout_ceiling` (test_whole_tree_scan_timeout_guard.py:328, module-level only).

pytest gotcha (dark-factory, task 4203, verified on task/4203 @ 9055fcf397): a `@pytest.mark.timeout(N)` override in this repo must budget REAL-GIT FIXTURE AND TEST-BODY SUBPROCESS WORK, not just the test's bounded `asyncio.wait_for` waits. pytest-timeout 2.4.0 installs its timer in `pytest_runtest_protocol` whenever `func_only` is False, and `timeout_func_only` is set NOWHERE in this repo, so the per-test budget covers fixture setup/teardown too. Concretely, in the offline-lane integration modules: the `repo` fixture's `_setup_repo` costs 5 git spawns (`init`, `config` x2, `add`, `commit`), and `_drive_advance` costs 5 more — `harness.git_ops.get_main_sha()`, `_advance_main`'s `add`/`commit`/`rev-parse`, and `harness._note_merge_all` -> `get_merge_diff_files`' `git diff` (unconditional, `harness.py:10377`). Two landed docstrings undercounted `_drive_advance` as "4" and as "3+" because they omitted the opening `get_main_sha`; at task 3451's measured worst-case 4.71s/spawn that error understated `test_b7_stall_promotes_to_blocker`'s out-of-bound cost by ~24s. Lesson: when sizing or reviewing a timeout override, count spawns from the real call path (or instrument the shared `orchestrator.git_ops._run` seam with a delegating counter) rather than trusting an adjacent comment — these hand-maintained counts have drifted more than once.

Gotcha when auditing orchestrator test files for pytest timeout breaches: a class-level `@pytest.mark.timeout(N)` applies to EACH test method independently, never to the class total. So the budget that matters is max-over-methods, not the class-wide sum. Summing per class errs both ways — in test_merge_queue_concurrent_verify.py, TestRunInflightVerifyAbortPoll sums to 180s across four methods but never exceeds 45s in any single one (false positive), while one heavy method among many light ones can be diluted below the 60s pyproject ceiling and missed. Also count hidden default-arg budgets: a bare `_await_outcome(fut, label=...)` call contributes MERGE_RESULT_TIMEOUT (45s) and is invisible to a `timeout=` grep. That term is what reproduces the documented 225s worst case for the two cascade classes (135s explicit + 90s hidden).

PATTERN (dark-factory, task 4972 amendment pass, measured 2026-08-31 on fused-memory/tests/test_drop_vector_indices_integration.py): when a test RETRIES around a barrier, an attempt-count bound does NOT bound wall clock, and raising the @pytest.mark.timeout to cover the product is the wrong fix.

THE TRAP. A retry loop multiplies its per-attempt budgets: 5 attempts x 4 re-opens x 2 await_index_operational barriers x 30s = 240s of budget that can be spent without any single barrier ever raising. This is the multiplicative sibling of the existing "compute a class's worst-case budget as the SUM of its sequential waits" note — summing is right for a straight-line test and wrong for a retried one. Worse, the dangerous case is the barrier that runs LONG BUT SUCCEEDS (25s inside a 30s budget): it never produces the clean AssertionError the mark's comment predicts, it just walks the clock into timeout_method='thread', whose handler ends in os._exit(1) and kills the whole xdist worker with unrelated tests aboard.

THE FIX that keeps the mark small. Take a wall-clock deadline ONCE before the retry, pass it into the reopen callable, and have each barrier there request min(full_budget, deadline - time.monotonic()), refusing outright when nothing is left. The retry phase is then bounded by one constant regardless of attempt count, and the class mark becomes checkable ARITHMETIC over named constants (here: 30 seed + 30 fixture barrier + 100 retry + 2 last observation + 30 final barrier = 192, mark 240) instead of a guess. Write the sum in the comment and say the invariant is the arithmetic, not the literal.

Give the exhausted-budget path its OWN diagnosis. "Ran out of wall clock" means the backend is contended; it is NOT the "the transient no longer happens" failure the test also reports. Collapsing the two into one message is the same two-modes-one-string defect IndexHeaderError exists to prevent.

MEASURED COROLLARY on the pytest-timeout clock, which cuts the OTHER way from the known "budget fixture setup too" gotcha: pytest-timeout installs its timer in pytest_runtest_protocol, so it covers fixture setup/teardown but NOT interpreter startup or conftest import. One trial in a 25-run batch took 42.59s of WALL clock against 3.23s of pytest-reported in-test time — 39s of import under loadavg ~148, entirely outside the per-test clock. So a wall-clock stopwatch on a heavy-conftest module (fused-memory imports graphiti_core) overstates the budget consumption by tens of seconds on a loaded box. Size marks against pytest's reported duration, not `time` on the pytest invocation.

GOTCHA for tests that run a nested pytest via subprocess.run(..., text=True, timeout=N) (task 6384, measured CPython 3.13, pytest 9.0.3). (1) On timeout, TimeoutExpired.stdout/.stderr are BYTES or None even with text=True, so formatting them with an f-string prints the repr b'...\n...' and None. Decode them first (bytes -> .decode('utf-8', errors='replace'), None -> ''); see tests/scripts/test_timeout_method_policy.py::_text. (2) The partial output IS useful without PYTHONUNBUFFERED. A pytest child killed mid-run hands back its full header and its progress characters (e.g. '......'), because pytest flushes its terminal writes. A child killed before ~1-3s may have printed nothing yet. (3) To read the timeout marks of every test in the current module even when -k deselected them, re-collect via request.node.getparent(pytest.Module).collect(). request.node.parent.collect() fails pyright, because parent is typed Node | None and Node has no collect().

In orchestrator tests, WIDENING a wall-clock timeout without also adding a class-level @pytest.mark.timeout is actively harmful, not merely insufficient. orchestrator/pyproject.toml sets timeout=60 with timeout_method="thread" and --max-worker-restart=0, so a test exceeding its per-test timeout does not fail — pytest-timeout os._exit()s the whole xdist worker. Compute a class's worst-case budget as the SUM of its sequential waits (task 3492's _worst_per_method_wait_budget in test_merge_queue_concurrent_verify.py:281 does this from source text and is reusable on foreign files); if it reaches 60s, the class needs @pytest.mark.timeout(HEAVY_BARRIER_TEST_TIMEOUT) (:185, derived as 5*MERGE_RESULT_TIMEOUT+75=300). Measured 2026-08-11: five late-arrival classes in test_merge_speculation.py already sat at 105s-125s with ZERO marks.

TEST DESIGN (dark-factory, task 5488): when the defect under test is an UNBOUNDED RETRY LOOP that records state each pass (appends to a calls list, allocates a lease, logs), `@pytest.mark.timeout(N)` is a backstop, not the guard. The loop reaches no assertion at all — it grows those lists until the host runs out of memory, and at ~10µs/iteration a 15s timeout is a million iterations, which on a loaded 32-core box can take the whole xdist worker (and its innocent neighbours) down before pytest-timeout ever fires.

THE GUARD THAT ACTUALLY WORKS: make the injected stub fail at the moment the loop repeats itself, not after the fact. In scripts/tests/test_legibility_account_pool.py the stub `_NeverTwice` asserts the account token it is handed was not used earlier in this digest, so a non-terminating rotation fails in ~1s with one line naming the account served twice, instead of hanging. The RED run for the fix measured 1.28s for four such tests. Keep the timeout marker as well — it is the backstop for a regression that spins WITHOUT repeating the observable.

This complements the task-4788 entry ("do not rely on pytest-timeout as the backstop when the failure mode is 'the handler never returns'"), which is about a DIFFERENT mechanism: there the signal-method timeout could not unwind a blocked starlette TestClient thread. Same conclusion from the other direction — a hang needs an assertion that trips on the first repetition, not a clock.

COUNTER-INTUITIVE MEASUREMENT (task 5442, 2026-09-17, 32-core host at loadavg 67-365): a SERIAL root-bound pytest run is SLOWER per test than the same tests under their own member's `-n auto` (32 workers), not faster. The same three unmarked tests measured 1.3x to 1.7x longer serially — test_every_scanned_tests_directory_exits_zero 41.76s -> 61.52s, test_no_scanned_file_outside_the_baseline_carries_a_violation 42.63s -> 54.52s, test_hard_v2_fixture_pool's test_reference_unavailable_only_when_no_landing_merge_exists 27.13s -> 45.48s. The natural expectation (a serial run contends with itself less, so per-test wall clock is bounded above by the parallel figure) is therefore FALSE here, and acting on it would have under-derived dark-factory's per-test timeout: the mode that until this task had no cap at all is also the mode producing the largest per-test wall clock in the corpus. Practical consequence for anyone sizing a per-test budget, a verify timeout, or a `@pytest.mark.timeout(N)`: measure BOTH inifile-resolution modes, and take the worst RUN rather than the mean or the freshest — the same file re-measured minutes later on an unchanged tree spanned a ~1.6x band. Full corpus and arithmetic: plans/pytest-per-test-timeout-measurement-2026-09-17.md.

The escalation package's pyproject.toml does NOT declare pytest-timeout (only pytest, pytest-asyncio, pyright), unlike shared/fused-memory/orchestrator which all have pytest-timeout>=2.4.0 plus a [tool.pytest.ini_options] timeout default. Any escalation test using @pytest.mark.timeout(N) (e.g. subprocess concurrency fixtures) must first add the dep + config, else the marker is an unregistered no-op and a hang won't fail fast. escalation runs no pytest-xdist, so timeout_method="signal" (like shared) is correct, not "thread".

When picking a bounded-wait constant in an orchestrator test, check the SUM of waits that stack within one test, not just the single value, against pyproject.toml's global 60s pytest-timeout. Waits inside a shared contextmanager helper are the trap: test_lane_lock_leak_guard.py's foreign_lane_lock_holder runs its startup and attribution polls back-to-back and unconditionally, so two innocuous-looking 30.0s bounds summed to 60s (70s with teardown) before any test body ran. Exceeding the cap is worse than a slow failure — timeout_method=thread makes pytest-timeout os._exit() the xdist worker, so the helper's own pytest.fail diagnostics never print. Rule of thumb: keep a helper's unconditional stack at or below roughly 60 percent of the global timeout, leaving the rest for real-git fixture work.
Uses pytest-timeout with pytest-xdist

orchestrator pytest global config (orchestrator/pyproject.toml:88-89) is `timeout=60` + `timeout_method='thread'` — on breach pytest-timeout's thread method os._exit()s the whole xdist worker (shows as 'node down'). Heavy async test classes opt out via `@pytest.mark.timeout(N)`. Gotcha: when widening in-test wall-clock deadlines whose sum exceeds the enclosing class/function `@pytest.mark.timeout` marker, the marker must be raised too, or it kills the test before the widened inner deadline can help.

Widening a shared TEST-HELPER's `timeout` DEFAULT (fixed literal -> load-scaled resolver) silently re-budgets every caller that relies on the bare default, so it breaks `@pytest.mark.timeout` marks written as LITERALS — a stricter variant of the known "raise the mark when you widen an in-test deadline" rule, because here no call site is edited and nothing flags it. Two lessons from task 4014 (orchestrator/tests/test_laptop_warm_verify_boundary.py): (1) a guard test asserting only on the derived CONSTANTS (mark >= ceiling) does NOT see call sites — Row 5 kept a literal `@pytest.mark.timeout(120)` while two bare-default discovery waits grew to 2x120s; enumerate call sites by parsing the module's own AST (idiom already used by test_marker_registration_drift.py / test_git_repo_isolation_guard.py) and additionally reject `ast.Constant` mark arguments, since a literal is what no re-derivation can reach into. (2) When summing a test's bounded work, check whether a helper spends its `timeout` more than once: `wait_for_marker_stable` passes `timeout` to the `wait_for_marker` existence gate and then starts a FRESH deadline for the settle loop, so its worst case is 2x the argument.

MEASURED per-test pytest duration distribution under real host load, 2026-09-17, taken by task 5442's architect on task/5442 @ 832d6faf16. Host: 32 cores, loadavg 103 falling to 80 across the runs (real fleet load, not synthetic). Command per member: `cd <member> && env -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --project . pytest tests -q --durations=0 --timeout=0 -p no:cacheprovider` — `--timeout=0` disables the cap so true durations are observed instead of truncated at 300.

RESULTS (per-member mode, each member under its OWN addopts/xdist):
- escalation, -n auto --dist loadgroup: 1841 passed / 2 xfailed in 61.96s. call phase p50 0.090s, p90 0.540s, p99 1.850s, p99.9 4.570s, MAX 5.37s.
- shared, serial: 5495 passed / 14 skipped in 209.09s. MAX 13.22s — and it is a SETUP, not a call (test_loop_blocking_gate.py::TestSweepIsNotVacuous::test_scanned_file_floor); slowest call was 9.91s.
- dashboard, -n auto --dist loadgroup: 2470 passed / 1 skipped / 1 xfailed in 75.57s. MAX call 3.76s.
- orchestrator and fused-memory NOT measured (the long poles; left to task 5442's implementer).

TWO FINDINGS THAT CHANGE HOW YOU READ THIS DATA.

1. SETUP CAN BE THE LONG POLE, so a duration corpus built from `call` rows alone understates the worst case — shared's worst datum is a 13.22s setup against a 9.91s slowest call. pytest-timeout caps the whole test including setup and teardown, so setup/teardown rows must stay in the corpus. This is not hypothetical for this repo: the documented dashboard failure mode from task 3431 / esc-3216-2 was 178.5s spent in TEARDOWN.

2. THE MEASURED WORST CASE IS FAR UNDER THE CAP, so the 300s interim looks generous rather than tight. Worst unmarked datum across the three suites measured is 13.22s; x8 headroom = 106s, well under 300. The plausible outcome of the full measurement is therefore that it VALIDATES 300 rather than replacing it — which is a real result, not a failure to find one. Note the slowest orchestrator tests are largely the whole-tree AST scans, which already opt up via `@pytest.mark.timeout(WHOLE_TREE_SCAN_TEST_TIMEOUT)` and so are excluded from the governing set by design; the ini default only has to cover UNMARKED tests.

ALSO CONFIRMED, the root-inifile gap: running `pytest escalation/tests` from the REPO ROOT resolves rootdir to the repo root, reads the root `[tool.pytest.ini_options]`, and therefore ran serial and UNCAPPED — 111.83s versus 61.96s for the same suite per-member. pytest reads exactly ONE inifile and never merges across pyproject.toml files.

The derivation rule task 5442 adopts is `max(300, round_up_60(worst_unmarked_wall_clock * 8))`, reusing the already-justified 8x factor from `orchestrator/tests/test_whole_tree_scan_timeout_guard.py::_REQUIRED_HEADROOM_FACTOR` (8x rather than 2x because xdist worker deaths were observed at loadavg 250-423, one inflation step past any measurable load). Full derivation lands in `plans/pytest-per-test-timeout-measurement-2026-09-17.md`.

GOTCHA (dark-factory, measured 2026-08-28, task 4023) — DISTINCT from the pytest-xdist serial-override topic: this is about caching and per-test timeouts, not about forcing serial execution.

`@functools.lru_cache` on an expensive helper shared by two tests buys nothing under the orchestrator suite's parallel default, because ungrouped tests are spread across WORKER PROCESSES and each pays the full cost — a per-process cache cannot cross a process boundary. To make it pay, co-locate the callers with `@pytest.mark.xdist_group('<tag>')`, the same mechanism test_cargo_scope.py uses for its module-level cache. Measured: second call 0.000004s instead of a ~20s tree walk.

The failure this hides behind is invisible to a single-file test run. orchestrator/pyproject.toml sets `timeout = 60` with `timeout_method = "thread"`, which os._exit()s the worker on expiry; the suite then reports only `worker 'gwNN' crashed while running <test>` — no traceback, no assertion text. A whole-tree scan (read + ast.parse over 553 files: ~13s of work, 20.5s wall on a loaded machine) passed cleanly file-alone and killed a worker on the full run.

PRACTICE: any test walking the whole tree needs BOTH an xdist_group tag and an explicit `@pytest.mark.timeout(N)` well above 60s, set generously — a static scan running slow is contention, not a hang, so a tight bound buys only flakiness. And run the FULL suite before calling such a test done.

content: pytest gotcha, measured on pytest 9.0.3 with pytest-timeout 2.4.0 (task 5571): for a test class, pytest collects class marks from EVERY class in the MRO, BASE CLASS FIRST (`_pytest.mark.structures.get_unpacked_marks` with consider_mro=True reads each class's `__dict__['pytestmark']` in reversed MRO order). `get_closest_marker('timeout')` then takes the first timeout mark in that list. So with `@timeout(10)` on a base class and `@timeout(20)` on the subclass, the subclass's tests run under 10s, not 20s. Also, a plain `getattr(cls, 'pytestmark')` sees only the nearest decorated class's list, so a subclass decorated with `@pytest.mark.asyncio` hides its base class's timeout mark from it. pytest-timeout then reads only that closest mark. Seconds <= 0 disable the timeout. A mark with no seconds (`method=` alone, or `timeout=None`) falls back to the ini/CLI timeout, not to a farther mark's seconds.

candidates.content: Fact (reify infra, 2026-10-13): tests/infra/adoption-ratchet.manifest (engine tests/infra/adoption_ratchet.py, gate member test_infra_adoption_ratchet.sh, from S19) is the existing home for INV-candidate-5 'extract-with-ratchet' rows: `pattern-id | ERE | path-glob | ceiling | owner leaf`. The engine skips only lines whose first non-blank character is '#', so Rust `//` comment lines DO count — each ERE must be anchored on the code construct (e.g. `^\s*pub fn diagnose\(`), and the path must be one repo-root glob that matches at least one file. A row reds only when a count EXCEEDS its ceiling; extract leaves add their row at the post-extraction count.

reify tests/infra/adoption-ratchet.manifest gotchas (adoption_ratchet.py, task 8716 planning).

1. Escape a literal `$` (and `(`) in a row's ERE, e.g. write `_PARENT="\$\(mktemp` and not `_PARENT="$(mktemp`. An unescaped `$` is an end anchor in both POSIX ERE and Python re, so the row silently matches nothing and its ceiling is vacuous.
2. The path column is ONE Python Path.glob, with no {a,b} brace expansion. To cover several files, widen the glob (e.g. tests/infra/test_*.sh) and shape the ERE to exclude false hits, or add separate rows. Remember that test_*.sh also matches test_helpers.sh.
3. Pin each new row with a shape test in test_infra_adoption_ratchet.py: a historical line must match, and the replacement must not.

reify-solver-elastic adoption ratchets (crates/reify-solver-elastic/tests/adoption_ratchets.rs, task 8614, PRD solver-crates-layering D20/BT14) are STRICT-equality: a row passes only when its measured count equals `baseline:` in the RATCHETS table, so a leaf that migrates a copy must lower its own row in the same diff (the red message says "lower the baseline to N"). The host file itself is left out of every measurement (`read_crate_tree` skips HOST_PATH), so its seeds, doc comments and generic helper names never count and a new tests/ file may reuse them. Every other src/ and tests/ file is lexed; the real-tree test goes red naming file and line (`UnsupportedTestCfg`) on any `cfg(..)` naming `test` other than the bare `#[cfg(test)]` (all/any/not, inner `#![cfg(test)]`). The mpc-row-literals row also counts `MpcRow {` inside doc comments (`///`, `//!`, `/** */`, `/*! */`) of those other files, by design (the lib.rs doctest). Supersedes the 2026-10-12 note that said the binary counts its own file.

tests/infra/adoption-ratchet.manifest (S19 α, task #8678; the repo's INV candidate 5 adoption-ratchet engine) has these quirks. Rows are `pattern-id | ERE | path glob | ceiling | owner leaf`. The engine (tests/infra/adoption_ratchet.py) expands globs with pathlib root.glob, so `*` does NOT cross `/`: use `crates/<crate>/src/**/*.rs` for any ratchet that must survive a later file split into subdirectories. A glob that matches no file reds the gate. Lines whose first non-blank char is '#' never count, so Rust `#[…]` attribute lines are invisible to it, and such ratchets must be Rust tests. The ERE must be POSIX-compatible: no \b, \d, (?…) or lazy quantifiers.

reify-solver-elastic tests/adoption_ratchets.rs lexer-health defects (task 8614 amend): besides `UnsupportedTestCfg`, the real-tree test goes red with `OutOfLineTestModule { line }` on any `mod name;` declared inside a `#[cfg(test)]` item (including an ungated `mod x;` nested in a gated inline module), because that module's file would be counted as production by every production row; keep such test modules inline, or extend the host to resolve the file. Reify convention for guard-integrity asserts on a SHRINKING RATCHET (harness-layout-baseline.manifest, ptodo-baseline.txt, the planned pdoccover-baseline.txt): assert the baseline EXISTS and is WELL-FORMED, never that it is NON-EMPTY and never a `rows >= N` floor. An empty baseline is the ratchet's designed terminal state, so a non-emptiness floor REDs the merge gate as a reward for finishing the consolidation the guard protects — invisible while the row count is high, firing only at the finish line. Non-vacuity must come from hermetic must-fire fixtures driving the same code path as the live scan, not from a live count. Canonical precedent: crates/reify-audit/tests/ptodo_baseline.rs::baseline_is_well_formed ("An empty baseline PASSES … asserts existence + well-formedness, NOT non-emptiness"); same reasoning recorded in tests/infra/test_harness_kloc_cap.sh's Section 8 note (#5938) and Section 5 (#5983). Non-emptiness IS still correct for a permanently GROWING registry such as run-all-classification.manifest — the rule is about ratchets, not manifests in general.

Adding a row to `tests/infra/harness-layout-baseline.manifest` LOOKS like the fix but is explicitly SUPERSEDED (Leo 2026-07-22, esc-5056-11: "actually start using the ratchet" — the manifest is a shrinking ratchet). The sanctioned remedy is to fold the new test into an existing `crates/<c>/tests/harness_<subsystem>/<file>.rs` declared from the harness root with a MANDATORY `#[path = "harness_<subsystem>/<file>.rs"] mod <file>;` — a bare `mod <file>;` in an integration-test crate root resolves against `tests/` and silently binds the wrong file. Crates OUTSIDE those five (e.g. reify-expr, reify-ir, reify-core) are unaffected — a new standalone tests/*.rs there is fine. Plan for this BEFORE proposing "add a per-crate test" in reify-eval or reify-compiler; it changes the shape and cost of the work.

reify harness-layout gate — SCOPE AND EXEMPTIONS: what the C1 contract does NOT govern. Rule (b) of tests/infra/test_harness_kloc_cap.sh: a top-level `crates/<c>/tests/*.rs` is sanctioned iff it is a `harness_*.rs` root (governed by the kLOC cap instead) OR one of the 7 permanently-standalone override stems (determinism, analytical_validation, modal_benchmarks, buckling_smoke, fea_diagnostics_e2e, tensegrity_t0a, representation_within_assertion) OR listed in tests/infra/harness-layout-baseline.manifest — which is why the guard was green on the pre-consolidation tree. The guard is classified `pool` in tests/infra/run-all-classification.manifest and runs in the merge-tier run_all suite on every merge_request; its diff-scoped sibling scripts/check-harness-baseline-registration.sh --from-git is wired into scripts/verify.sh as an early preflight tool. Verified at main efbc0932bd, 2026-09-08.

tests/infra/harness-layout-lib.sh:61 scopes the harness-layout baseline-registration gate (scripts/check-harness-baseline-registration.sh, verify plan entry #2) to exactly five crates: reify-cli, reify-syntax, reify-kernel-occt, reify-eval, reify-compiler. A new crates/<other-crate>/tests/<file>.rs — e.g. under crates/reify-audit/ — needs NO tests/infra/harness-layout-baseline.manifest row and must not be given one (the gate's own hint calls that manifest "a shrinking ratchet, not an allow-list to grow"). Corroborating evidence: all 24 existing crates/reify-audit/tests/*.rs files have zero rows among the manifest's 603 entries. Relatedly, the THROUGHPUT-COUNTS sentinel in docs/notes/verify-scope-throughput.md counts verify PLAN LINES (`verify.sh ... --print-plan | grep -cE '^[^#]'`) for four fixture shapes, not test binaries — adding a cargo test binary or a tests/infra script does not move it, since tests/infra runs as a single wholesale run_all.sh plan line.

Design convention from S12 (2026-10-14): when a ratchet row's counted construct lives in files that sibling streams' already-filed tasks will rewrite or move before this stream reaches them, do NOT baseline that row in the stream's ratchet-member leaf (a sibling landing would turn it STALE or over-baseline and red the sibling's merge). Instead the leaf that lowers the construct ADDS the row at its target in its own diff, as a regression guard; only rows over files no other task touches are baselined up front. Also: every row names explicit production files (never a directory glob), because rust_construct_ratchet's production view skips inline #[cfg(test)] modules but counts external test files under src/ (S27 τ/ω move test literals into src/ files). A not-yet-existing file in a row's path list globs to nothing, so destination files of planned moves (e.g. S25's gui engine/*.rs) can be listed ahead of time.

In reify, a NEW integration test for crates/reify-eval must be added as a `#[path]`-declared MODULE under an existing consolidated harness (e.g. tests/harness_kernel_realization.rs, tests/harness_tolerance.rs, tests/harness_cache.rs), NOT as a standalone `crates/reify-eval/tests/<name>.rs` binary. A standalone new test file hard-fails the merge gate via `scripts/check-harness-baseline-registration.sh --from-git`, wired into `scripts/verify.sh` as an early preflight tool. The consolidation is a shrinking ratchet (task #5278/#5282, PRD merge-gate-compile-cost.md §5 C1). Whole-harness size is additionally capped by tests/infra/test_harness_kloc_cap.sh rule (a), so check headroom before adding a large test body.

[CORRECTED 2026-09-09] This entry originally qualified that hard-fail with an escape hatch — the gate fires "unless a matching row is added to tests/infra/harness-layout-baseline.manifest in the same diff". That mechanism claim is WRONG and is withdrawn. A baseline-manifest row is NOT a sanctioned mechanism at ANY row count: Leo SUPERSEDED the "check the crate's COUNT first, then maybe add a row" grandfather branch on 2026-07-22 (esc-5056-11, "actually start using the ratchet"). The manifest is a SHRINKING ratchet whose grandfathered rows are an origin snapshot to ratchet toward empty — not an allow-list to grow — and a same-diff row addition is precisely that superseded branch restated. The sanctioned remedies are consolidation only: a `#[path]`-declaring `harness_<sub>.rs` root, or folding the new tests into an existing already-grandfathered file or subsystem harness in the same crate. See the canonical index under topic `harness-layout-gate-decision-rule`, and that topic's anti-refold ledger, which records this exact restatement as Error B.

Also corrected: this entry cited the gate's wiring as `scripts/verify.sh:2542`. That line anchor has rotted (the `add_tool "./scripts/check-harness-baseline-registration.sh --from-git"` call sits elsewhere in the file at main 415d95bb79). Anchor by the tool invocation, not the line.

For a C1 harness-consolidation task, tests/infra/test_harness_kloc_cap.sh IS the RED/GREEN oracle — no bespoke layout test is needed. Deleting a file's row from tests/infra/harness-layout-baseline.manifest while the file is still a top-level tests/*.rs makes the guard exit 1 with `HARNESS_KLOC_CAP FAIL crate=<c> file=<path> reason=unsanctioned-standalone`; moving the file under crates/<c>/tests/harness_<subsystem>/ (declared with a mandatory `#[path]`) turns it green. Dry-run a ratchet shrink without dirtying the tree via `REIFY_HARNESS_LAYOUT_BASELINE=<tmp-manifest> bash tests/infra/test_harness_kloc_cap.sh` — the override is honored through tests/infra/harness-layout-lib.sh by both this guard and scripts/check-harness-baseline-registration.sh. SEQUENCING: do RED first — delete the grandfather rows before moving the files. Moving the files first and removing rows second passes at every intermediate point and proves nothing, because the guard's live scan walks the FILESYSTEM (`$REPO_ROOT/crates/<c>/tests`), not `git ls-files`, so both the RED and GREEN verdicts reproduce even on an uncommitted working tree.

reify gotcha: tests/infra/adoption_ratchet.py (adoption-ratchet.manifest, #8678) treats only lines whose first non-blank char is '#' as comments. That rule is shell-only, so it is unfit for Rust-source ratchets: it counts `//`/`///` prose as code and drops `#[cfg(..)] foo!(..)` lines as comments. A Rust grep-style gate should read source through scripts/lib_rust_production_view.sh's RUST_PRODUCTION_VIEW_AWK (one awk process per file, escape matched via `comment_tail`), as check-nan-safe-ordering.sh and task 7556's tests/infra/reify_lsp_stderr_scan.py do.

content: In reify, tests/infra/adoption_ratchet.py (the #8678 infra-harness engine behind adoption-ratchet.manifest) checks a ceiling only. It reds only when a count rises above the ceiling, and it scans whole files with no #[cfg(test)] cut. It therefore cannot express S5 analysis-stratum ratchet rows, which must red on a fall without a baseline edit and count only production code, cut at the first column-0 #[cfg(test)]. S5 rows (wire-codec-copy, then catch-unwind-guard, target-string-routing, shell-value-decoder, eval-imports-analysis) live in tests/infra/test_analysis_stratum_ratchet.py, created by task #8984. Each row is a Row constant with one test method.

1b0e5c7f-8f45-4d33-8b46-a8a46bcfb5fb.content: Reify's grep-based source gates (scripts/check-nan-safe-ordering.sh, scripts/check-compute-trampoline-registration.sh) share a hand-ported awk Rust lexer, `_AWK_PRODUCTION_PROLOGUE`, that reduces each line to production code (comments dropped; string/char/raw-string contents blanked, delimiters kept; `/* */`, `"…"` and `r#"…"#` state carried across lines; char literal distinguished from lifetime) and — critically — counts the braces driving `depth` from that LEXED view, never from the raw line. A two-regex strip-comments/blank-strings chain is wrong in EITHER order and was replaced, not reordered. When writing a new gate of this shape, port the prologue from check-nan-safe-ordering.sh's copy on main verbatim (change only the escape token and the matched patterns) rather than re-deriving it.

candidates.content: solar_challenge e2e technique, measured 2026-10-08 by task 512's architect (playwright 1.61, pytest-playwright 0.8.0). To see a page as it renders before Alpine starts, open it in a context from pytest-playwright's new_context fixture with java_script_enabled=False. The fixture is typed pytest_playwright.CreateContextCallback and closes the context at teardown. Locators still work with JavaScript off. After page.goto's load event, static/style.css's [x-cloak] rule has hidden every cloaked element, so get_by_role(...).is_visible() reads what the page shows until Alpine starts. tests/e2e/conftest.py's network-change rerun hook watches only the default `context`, so keep a test's request-heavy JS-on half on the default `page`.

solar_challenge e2e fixture gotcha (verified 2026-10-03, task 250 planning): tests/unit/test_e2e_job_wait.py copies tests/e2e/conftest.py into a pytester session in the per-task verify env, which has no pytest-playwright. So never add an autouse fixture to tests/e2e/conftest.py that requests a pytest-playwright fixture (page, context, browser): every test in that copied session would error with "fixture not found". To apply something to every browser test, override the function-scoped `context` fixture by name instead, e.g. `def context(context, live_server, request): ...; yield context`. pytest-playwright 0.8.0's page fixture requests context, so the override runs for exactly the tests that open a browser, and it is never set up in the copied session. A prototype that aborted other-origin requests this way passed test_e2e_job_wait.py and added about 5% to e2e run time (17.17 s → 18.07 s).

solar_challenge e2e technique, measured 2026-10-12 by task 649's implementer (playwright 1.61, headless Chromium, task/649 at 10d04c1). (1) An unhandled promise rejection on the page arrives as a Playwright 'pageerror' whose text is the bare Error message, e.g. 'this browser opens no event streams', with no 'Uncaught (in promise)' prefix. So tests/e2e/conftest.py's page_errors fixture catches an unawaited async call whose rejection nothing catches. (2) To reach a page's handling of a throwing EventSource constructor without editing src/, call page.add_init_script("window.EventSource = class { constructor() { throw new Error('...'); } };") before page.goto. progress-tracker.js, which base.html loads on every page, constructs its EventSource only on demand, so pages still load. Route the submit POST too, e.g. test_parameter_sweep.py's sweep_jobs fixture, so no job reaches the live server. test_the_page_says_why_it_lost_track_of_a_sweep_it_cannot_follow uses both.

solar_challenge e2e procedure (task 376 architect, 2026-10-04, main cfbbbbd): the Playwright suite runs inside task worktrees on this host, e.g. `uv run --locked --extra dev --extra web --extra e2e pytest tests/e2e/test_fleet_interactions.py -p no:cacheprovider` (about 20 s for 4 fleet-page tests). So a planner can check a browser test's RED premise with a scratch tests/e2e/test_zz_*.py, which gets the live_server fixtures, then delete it. To show a JS form refuses a submission without a fixed sleep: page.route the endpoint to a recorder that aborts, assert a visible refusal message, then assert the recorder saw no request. page.expect_request waits its 30 s default before failing when nothing is sent.

candidates.content: solar_challenge e2e convention (task 138, 2026-09-30): to control the Run History page's runs list in a Playwright test, reuse the shared fixtures in tests/e2e/conftest.py via @pytest.mark.usefixtures rather than an inline page.route stub. `runs_api_returns_no_runs` fulfils every GET /api/history/runs with the API's empty-database JSON. `runs_api_never_answers` holds those requests for the whole test, asserts at teardown that it held at least one (a non-vacuity guard: with a broken matcher it errors "the page made no runs-list request..."), then aborts them. solar_challenge e2e probe gotchas (task 415 architect, main 953f4dd, 2026-10-05).
(1) A scratch tests/e2e probe module must set `pytestmark = pytest.mark.e2e`. Unmarked, the root conftest's offline guard ERRORs each test at teardown, with 'reached the network (cdn.plot.ly:443)', once any page it opens loads Plotly, e.g. a /results page; the test body itself passed.
(2) To test a modified click on a link: `with page.context.expect_page() as new_tab: locator.click(modifiers=["ControlOrMeta"])`, then `expect(new_tab.value).to_have_url(...)`. This opens a new tab in chromium-headless-shell v1228 (playwright 1.61.0). If the click also starts a navigation in the current tab, click() waits for it, so `page.url` already shows the new URL when click() returns, and a following `expect(page).to_have_url(old)` fails deterministically.
(3) The dashboard lists only the 10 newest runs (list_runs(limit=10)), and later e2e tests save runs of their own, so a session-scoped seed such as seeded_home_run can drop off it depending on test order. A dashboard test should save its run in a function-scoped fixture.

solar_challenge e2e technique (task 637 implementer, measured 2026-10-13, playwright 1.61, headless Chromium): to see how a page's own JS handles a modified page without editing src/, fetch the live page with page.request.get(url), edit its HTML text (assert the anchor you replace occurs exactly once), then serve it with page.route(url, lambda route: route.fulfill(status=200, content_type="text/html; charset=utf-8", body=html)) before page.goto(url). Build the modified HTML in the test body, not inside the route handler: an exception raised in a handler surfaces only as a hung navigation. tests/e2e/test_results_page.py's undrawable-chart test injects a chart container whose data-chart-figure is not JSON this way.

solar_challenge e2e procedure (task 412 architect, measured on main c386a34, 2026-10-03): to prove a 'no JS errors' e2e test can see an Alpine expression error without editing src/, run the unchanged node under a throwaway /tmp pytest plugin. Command: PYTHONPATH=/tmp/ uv run --locked --extra dev --extra web --extra e2e pytest -p -p no:cacheprovider. - The plugin's autouse fixture calls request.getfixturevalue('page').route('**/*', handler) whenever 'page' is in request.fixturenames. - The handler calls route.fallback() for any request whose route.request.resource_type is not 'document'. - For a document it calls route.fetch(), drops content-length from the headers and fulfils with '
' inserted before . Result on c386a34: the tests using page_errors (test_fleet_page_no_js_errors, test_fleet_results_page_shows_every_tab_without_errors) failed with ['undefinedComponentXYZ is not defined']. The console-only ones (test_sweep_no_js_errors, test_builder_no_js_errors, test_no_js_console_errors_on_static_pages) passed. Task 412's plan converts those three. solar_challenge e2e order-independence gotchas, measured 2026-09-29 while planning task 134.
(1) tests/e2e uses ONE session-scoped DB. The session seeding fixtures (seeded_home_run, seeded_home_runs_pair) leave runs in it, so any test that asserts DB-wide state, such as an empty history list, depends on suite order. Control the premise inside the test: either page.route(...).fulfill(json=<the real API's response shape>), or filter the list to a seeded run's unique name.
(2) CSS locators match display:none elements, but get_by_role skips them. On /simulate/home, button[role="switch"] matches 4 switches across hidden tabs (a strict-mode violation). After opening a tab, get_by_role('tabpanel').get_by_role('switch') resolves the one visible switch.
(3) To prove a test is order-independent, run it both alone and after `tests/e2e/test_compare_page.py tests/e2e/test_history_interactions.py` on the same pytest command line; pytest keeps argument order.

solar_challenge e2e: the live_server fixture (tests/e2e/conftest.py) serves the Flask app from a thread of the pytest process, so server behaviour can be mutated for a RED demonstration with NO file edit. Run `uv run --extra dev --extra web --extra e2e python - <<'EOF'` that imports the module, replaces the name where the route code looks it up, then does sys.exit(pytest.main([...])). Patch the importing module, e.g. solar_challenge.web.simulation_params.resolve_seg_tariff, because it imports the function by name, so patching solar_challenge.seg would do nothing. Use it when the task's file lock covers only the test file, as in an amendment pass. Verified 2026-09-30 (task 173): refusing SEG presets whose name has a space failed seg-British_Gas and seg-Scottish_Power with `assert 400 == 201` while seg-Octopus passed.

solar_challenge e2e technique (measured 2026-10-09 by task 533's architect, playwright 1.61.0, pytest-playwright 0.8.0, base 39635d0), for tests that hold an SSE progress stream and end it later. (1) After `with page.expect_request(url): button.click()` returns, the page.route handler for that request may not have run yet: the 'request' event precedes 'route', so a list of held routes can still be empty (seen on /simulate/fleet). Make the route fixture register each job's ending, answer an already-held route at once, and answer a route that arrives later on arrival. (2) Response.finished() leaves a watcher task that logs 'Task exception was never retrieved ... Target closed' at page teardown. Instead, `response = route.request.response()` (None if the page dropped the request) then `response.body()`: it waits for the request to finish without that noise. After it returns, the page's EventSource handlers have run, so a negative expect is meaningful. (3) route.fulfill() on a request the page already cancelled (EventSource.close()) is silently ignored.

solar_challenge e2e procedure (task 412 amendment pass, 2026-10-03): you can measure an e2e test as if its fixed sleeps were deleted without editing the file, for example when the file is outside your task's locks. Load a throwaway /tmp pytest plugin with PYTHONPATH=/tmp/<dir> ... pytest -p <module>. Its autouse fixture runs request.getfixturevalue('page').wait_for_timeout = lambda timeout: None whenever 'page' is in request.fixturenames; Playwright's sync Page accepts the instance attribute. Combine it with other -p mutation plugins as needed. On test_fleet_page_no_js_errors the call phase took 0.74 s, under the 1 s its sleep alone would take, so the no-op took effect.

solar_challenge e2e, Playwright 1.61.0, measured by task 298 on 2026-10-07: how to test a debounced Alpine action without sleeping. The example is tests/e2e/test_scenario_builder.py::test_a_refusal_stays_in_the_preview_over_the_preview_an_earlier_edit_queued.
1. Call page.clock.install() before page.goto. The fake time still advances with real time, so the page behaves normally.
2. Do the user actions.
3. Call page.clock.run_for(5_000). It fires the pending setTimeout, here the builder's 500 ms preview, at once.
4. To show that no request was made, record page.on('request'), do one round trip such as Validate, and only then assert.

Separately, avoid Response.finished() in the sync API: it leaves an asyncio task that logs 'Task exception was never retrieved ... Target closed' at teardown. Reading the body with response.json() or .text() also waits for it, without that noise.

solar_challenge test convention from task 347 (branch task/347, commits e8f6ec0 and 165ecf4; in effect once 347 merges), superseding memory fcff94f0's pattern. tests/conftest.py's autouse fixture _run_offline_unless_slow_or_e2e runs every test not marked slow or e2e inside tests/_network_guard.py::refusing_network(). It gives each such test an empty WeatherCache of its own, the public `weather_cache` fixture, installed with set_weather_cache. Any name lookup or connection off this machine, including one from a JobManager job thread (the drain runs before the check), fails the test at teardown with "<nodeid> reached the network (host:port)".
- To give a test weather, seed `weather_cache.put(synthetic_june_weather(day), "tmy", Location.bristol())`, or pass weather_data. Do not write a fixture that installs its own cache.
- The web API's days windows start on 2024-06-01, so seed that date for /api/simulate/home jobs.
- A pytester scenario that copies tests/conftest.py inherits the guard. One that copies tests/e2e/conftest.py does not: seed it with a session-scoped set_weather_cache and point its HTTP proxy variables at a dead port, as tests/unit/test_e2e_job_wait.py does.

solar_challenge: tests/unit/test_e2e_job_wait.py is in the orchestrator verify and runs a verbatim copy of tests/e2e/conftest.py, so any playwright import added to that conftest turns the per-task verify red. To prove the rule holds despite a worktree .venv that kept playwright (inexact sync, memory 8602bf4c), run the real guard in a fresh env: `uv run --isolated --extra dev --extra web pytest tests/unit/test_e2e_job_wait.py -p no:cacheprovider`. solar_challenge gotcha (task 508 amendment, measured 2026-10-06 on task/508 over main e037ca0, Jinja2 3.1.6): a unit guard over EVERY dashboard template cannot render each one with render_template(name) inside app.test_request_context(). 4 of the 27 raise UndefinedError without their view's context: results/home.html and results/fleet.html ('summary'), history/compare.html ('charts') and dashboard.html ('stats'). tests/unit/test_web_page_scripts.py instead reads each template's own source: app.jinja_env.loader.get_source, then env.lex keeping 'data' tokens and the variable_begin..variable_end text verbatim while blanking statements and comments, then tests._html_page.element_attributes over that markup, then render_template_string(src) per <script src> so url_for resolves. solar_challenge e2e procedure, measured 2026-10-12 by task 649's architect on main 5da62aa (playwright 1.61, chromium-headless-shell 1228). Some effects need requests that really hold a browser connection, such as Chromium's 6-connections-per-host HTTP/1.1 limit for SSE streams. Show those with server-held jobs, not page.route. A progress request held unanswered by page.route takes no connection: 8 held sweep streams left another tab loading in 0.31 s. To hold real streams, install JobManager(simulate_home=<function that waits on a threading.Event>) as _e2e_app.extensions['job_manager'] for the test. At teardown, set the event, wait_until_idle, and put the session manager back. Task 649's plan adds this as the tests/e2e/conftest.py fixture release_held_simulations. Gotcha: on this host a request still waiting for a socket is often failed by a Docker veth event with net::ERR_NETWORK_CHANGED before any timeout. That triggers the conftest's one rerun, so a connection stall shows as 'Page.goto: net::ERR_NETWORK_CHANGED' plus '1 rerun', not a 30 s timeout. The captured werkzeug log shows which requests reached the server, e.g. 6 of 8 progress GETs.

content: solar_challenge e2e convention, from task 250's implementer (branch task/250 at 2359229, 2026-10-19; in effect once task/250 merges). tests/e2e/conftest.py overrides pytest-playwright's new_context. So every browser context, including the page and context fixtures' and any a test opens itself (e.g. new_context(java_script_enabled=False)), routes a regex matching every URL outside the live server's origin to route.abort('internetdisconnected'). The test then ERRORS at teardown with '<nodeid> requested other origins (<urls>)'. A test whose page needs an off-origin resource must fulfil it with its own page.route, which takes precedence over the context route. A page's own scripts must come from the app: plotly.js is served from the installed plotly package at url_for('plotly_js.script') (src/solar_challenge/web/plotly_js.py), and tests/unit/test_web_page_scripts.py fails any template script that is off-origin or answers non-200. This refines memory 06c00874: override new_context, not context, so contexts a test opens itself are covered too. Keep it a plain override, never an autouse fixture, and use a regex, not a predicate (a predicate makes Playwright stop every request to ask the test process).

solar_challenge e2e gotcha, measured 2026-10-03 by task 409's architect on main bdb831a (Playwright Python, headless Chromium).
- An uncaught page exception reaches page.on('pageerror') ONLY, never page.on('console').
- An Alpine expression error, e.g. an x-data component function that is not defined, arrives as a console message of type 'warning' ('Alpine Expression Error: ...') plus a pageerror. It never arrives as console type 'error'.
- Only an explicit console.error(...) arrives as console type 'error'.
So a 'no JS errors' e2e test must also collect pageerror events, and Alpine warnings if wanted; collecting console messages of type 'error' is not enough. ef9bcbe7-4ed6-49d8-aea1-6a515a58e5ed.content: solar_challenge web-test technique (measured 2026-09-29 on task/156, base efe3145): to hold a submitted web job deterministically in 'running', install JobManager(simulate_home=<gated fake>) via app.extensions["job_manager"]. The fake sets a 'started' threading.Event, then waits on a 'released' Event. After 'started', GET /api/jobs/<id>/results is always 409 with status 'running', because _run_job sets the status to running before it calls the simulation. Release the gate in a yield-fixture's TEARDOWN, not in the test body. pytest tears down the root autouse drain (tests/conftest.py::_shutdown_job_managers, shutdown(wait=True)) last, so the release runs before the drain waits, and a failing test cannot hang the suite. A planning prototype passed 40 of 40 runs, with every teardown at or under 0.21 s. For jobs whose result the test never reads, a real JobManager(simulate_home=_RecordingSimulation()) finishes in milliseconds instead of 7-29 s of teardown drain.

candidates.content: Task 2418 made scheduler PSI-gate + snapshot-write tests hermetic under `pytest -n auto --dist loadgroup`. Two seams were added: (1) Scheduler(state_snapshot_path: Path | None = None) constructor kwarg — when set, _write_snapshot_best_effort writes there directly, bypassing both the _project_root-derived path and the no-project-root guard. (2) A suite-wide autouse conftest fixture _hermetic_psi_reader that monkeypatches orchestrator.scheduler.read_psi_sample to _orch_helpers.idle_psi_sample, so every Scheduler's _read_psi_sample defaults to a non-saturating sample regardless of host load. This transitively fixed ~10 flaky test_scheduler.py tests without editing them, plus one test_scheduler_state.py test that was hardened directly to pass state_snapshot_path. Full orchestrator suite (8133 tests) verified green after the change.

The Scheduler dispatch-admission gate (PsiAdmissionConfig, default enabled=True, mem_some_avg10=15.0 threshold) samples REAL host /proc/pressure/memory unless a test injects `scheduler._read_psi_sample`. On a heavily-loaded shared dev box (load avg 100+), real mem_some_avg10 easily exceeds 15%, causing non-deterministic dispatch-admission deferrals in any scheduler test that doesn't mock it. `_write_state_snapshot_raw` also hard-codes writes under `<project_root>/data/orchestrator/...`; when a test sets `scheduler._project_root = '/proj'` (a fake path), the write throws PermissionError/FileNotFoundError — but this is caught and merely logged (`_write_snapshot_best_effort` swallows it), so it shows up as noisy "Captured log call" traceback in pytest output, NOT as the actual test failure/cause. Task 2418 ("Make scheduler PSI-gate + snapshot-write tests hermetic", in-progress as of 2026-07-14) owns fixing exactly this via an autouse `_hermetic_psi_reader` conftest fixture + configurable snapshot path; task 2413 (done, merged 93578876fe) already hardened a related-but-distinct aiosqlite event-loop-teardown xdist flake in the same test files. Any agent hitting a PermissionError('/proj') traceback in scheduler test failures should look for the REAL assertion failure elsewhere in the pytest output (it's almost always a few lines earlier, e.g. an unrelated AssertionError) rather than treating the PermissionError as the cause.

In the orchestrator scheduler (orchestrator/src/orchestrator/scheduler.py), `config.psi_admission.enabled` defaults to True, so EVERY `Scheduler.acquire_next()` tick calls `self._read_psi_sample()` which reads real `/proc/pressure/*`. Under parallel `pytest -n auto` load, `mem_some_avg10` crosses the 15.0 default threshold and the dispatch-admission gate defers non-deterministic candidates (scheduler.py ~line 4567), making any scheduler test that drives acquire_next() non-hermetic unless it injects `scheduler._read_psi_sample`. The seam is the module-level `orchestrator.scheduler.read_psi_sample` bound in __init__ (scheduler.py:1298); monkeypatching it before construction defaults all schedulers to a deterministic sample.

GOTCHA when debugging orchestrator scheduler dispatch tests: a test that sets `scheduler._project_root` to a synthetic path (e.g. '/proj', the house pattern in test_scheduler.py's pin tests) will print a full `PermissionError: [Errno 13] ... '/proj'` traceback to stderr whenever a task actually DISPATCHES. That traceback comes from `_write_snapshot_best_effort` -> `_write_state_snapshot_raw` (scheduler.py), is swallowed by design, and is NOT the test failure — pytest's real failure is the assertion further up. Grep the output for the `assert` line before chasing the PermissionError; a dispatch-path change can otherwise look like an unrelated filesystem bug.

GOTCHA (measured 2026-09-14, task 3353): `shared.psi.parse_pressure_file` extracts ONLY the avg10 window, even though every `/proc/pressure/*` line the kernel emits carries `avg10= avg60= avg300=`. Its `_AVG10_RE` matches `avg10` alone and its return is the two-key `{'some_avg10', 'full_avg10'}` dict. So `read_psi_sample()` / `PsiSample` cannot give you avg60 or avg300 today, and any task whose spec asks for a longer PSI window must EXTEND that one reader rather than parse /proc/pressure a second time — `shared.psi` is the single PSI reader by design (INV-5, DA-D9), re-exported into `sampler.metrics` and guarded by an object-identity test (`sampler/tests/test_load_metrics.py::TestParserRehomedToShared`). Blast radius if you do extend it, measured: `sampler.metrics.collect_psi` selects keys explicitly (`parsed['some_avg10']`), so its six-key contract and the identity guard both survive ADDITIVE keys; what breaks is `shared/tests/test_psi.py`, which pins the return by EXACT dict equality at three sites (~L43/49/55). `PsiSample` itself is safe to grow — task 5216 took it from 5 fields to 10 and its docstring states the rule: new fields go LAST with the "component absent" value as default, so every shipped keyword construction stays valid. Do NOT add a telemetry field to `shared.psi._ARMS`: that tuple is the dispatch gate's saturation truth table, ranked by the load-throttle PRD's D10, and adding to it silently changes `saturated()`/`tripping_metric()`.

Session 2026-05-11 (claude-interactive): Diagnosed file-lock starvation of a high-priority wide-lock task in the orchestrator scheduler. Audited scheduler.py and found root cause: default `skip_threshold=4` arms parks too late, letting adversaries acquire contested modules during the skip-accumulation window. Designed Scheduler v2 with five interlocking changes — per-tier skip thresholds {critical:0, high:1, medium:2, low:4, polish:9999}, eager full-set parks (scheme b), lease removal with owner-state-coupled GC, `max_per_tier` removal, cross-tier preemption with preserved skip_count. Also designed a priority override mechanism (Boost/Pin/Reserve-Now) backed by dedicated SQLite (NOT task metadata to dodge the set_task_status metadata-wipe foot-gun), with multi-pin user-reorderable queue. Designed dashboard /scheduler page as new surface (not active-tasks extension) with heatmap, modules-tab, drawer for overrides, active-pins strip. Queued four PRs as tasks via planning_mode (1228 sched core → 1229 overrides backend → 1230 state endpoint → 1231 dashboard page), committed to pending. Saved design rationale to local memory at decision_scheduler_v2_design.md. User then started the orchestrator. Open thread: the user's referenced "reify 3399" task id couldn't be located in any project store.

GOTCHA (orchestrator tests, task 5311): when a Harness path starts reading a NEW boolean Scheduler property (e.g. `scheduler.is_paused`), every fixture with a bare `MagicMock()` scheduler silently takes the TRUE branch, because an auto-mock attribute is truthy. No test fails; the branch just fires spuriously. Pin the default in `_orch_helpers.wire_scheduler_liveness_mock`, which now sets is_paused=False and pause_reason=None. Two fixtures bypass that helper and need their own pin:
- test_harness_deterministic_dispatch.py's `harness` fixture: use `MagicMock(is_paused=False, pause_reason=None)` rather than assigning through `h.scheduler.<property>`, which pyright rejects because the property is read-only;
- test_deterministic_task.py's hand-rolled `_StoreScheduler`, which instead raises AttributeError.
To find spurious hits, add a temporary file-append probe line inside the new branch, run every suite that greps for the call path, read the probe file for MagicMock-typed hits, then delete the probe line.

RESOLVED (follow-up to the data/orchestrator/scheduler_state.json test-pollution note): traced and fixed 2026-05-27 (merge f8cf8b9408). Mechanism — OrchestratorConfig is a pydantic BaseSettings whose settings_customise_sources falls back to the RELATIVE Path('config.yaml') when ORCH_CONFIG_PATH is unset. The orchestrator's autouse test fixture deleted ORCH_CONFIG_PATH, which is exactly what triggers that fallback; running `cd orchestrator && pytest` then loads the tracked orchestrator/config.yaml (project_root → real repo root /home/leo/src/dark-factory). Many scheduler tests build a bare OrchestratorConfig() and drive acquire_next(), which calls _write_snapshot_best_effort() and writes <project_root>/data/orchestrator/scheduler_state.json into the live tree (read back by the dashboard as real state). Fix: the autouse fixture (orchestrator/tests/conftest.py _isolate_orch_config) now also pins project_root to the test's tmp_path via ORCH_PROJECT_ROOT. env_settings overrides only project_root (other config.yaml values like lock_depth still load); explicit project_root= init kwargs still win. Gotcha worth remembering for any package that builds OrchestratorConfig() in tests: isolate project_root or the cwd config.yaml will be silently loaded. Verified: full 2460-test suite passes with zero writes to <repo>/data/orchestrator/.

Orchestrator plan gotcha: adding a method to the Scheduler protocol (e.g. Scheduler.set_task_claimant in task 2188) or changing TaskWorkflow's constructor requires updating the shared test fixture orchestrator/tests/_workflow_helpers.py (FakeScheduler) AND any private scheduler stubs in sibling tests (e.g. test_workflow_dry_run_hook.py's _Scheduler). These collateral test files must be listed in the plan's files parameter or the concurrency-lock/phantom-done gate misses them.

Gotcha in orchestrator/deterministic_runner.py's `_file_*_and_block` escalation-filing methods (verified first-hand, task 4102): every collaborator attribute read used to BUILD the `detail` string executes BEFORE `escalation_queue.submit()`, so an AttributeError raised while formatting runbook PROSE does not merely skip the BLOCK — it loses the durable on-disk safety escalation entirely and propagates, which is exactly what those methods' docstrings forbid. Measured: a duck-typed scheduler stand-in without `.config` gave `AttributeError` and 0 pending records filed. This matters because the runner's `scheduler` collaborator is duck-typed and unannotated (Harness._run_deterministic_slot builds it "with only the minimal dependencies needed"), so an attribute CHAIN off it is a real production failure surface. Discipline: read such values through a small guarded helper that falls back to a VISIBLE placeholder (e.g. `_snippet_project_root` -> `'<project_root>'`), accepting the value only when it is a non-empty str/Path that is not the literal `'None'` — the `'None'` check mirrors the scheduler's own project_root guard against values that bypassed pydantic, and the isinstance check stops a test double's Mock reaching an operator as `<MagicMock id=...>`. Use two `getattr` defaults plus isinstance, never a broad `except Exception`. As of task 4102 all five `_file_*_and_block` methods hold this invariant (zero pre-submit scheduler attr-chain reads).

GOTCHA (orchestrator tests, task 4737): to give a Harness a hand-written fake scheduler WITHOUT a new `# type: ignore[assignment]` (INV-12 makes every new inline suppression need a debt/ratified marker, and scripts/inline_suppression_baseline.json ratchets the count), hand it in at construction: `patch('orchestrator.harness.Scheduler', return_value=fake)` while building `Harness(mock_orch_config)`. h.scheduler is then the fake and is never assigned, so pyright has nothing to flag. Assigning `h.scheduler = fake` after construction fails pyright (incompatible with the declared Scheduler). For the merge worker slot, use `MagicMock(spec_set=SpeculativeMergeWorker)`. It is assignable to `_merge_worker`, restricts the double to the worker's real interface, and auto-makes its async methods AsyncMock. Example: orchestrator/tests/test_harness_abandoned_merge_deferred_wiring.py.

A test-isolation fix prescribed as "mechanical" can silently inert the very behaviour the tests exercise, when the same change also alters a default. dark_factory task 3590 (leaf beta of load-throttle-harmonisation) carried an instruction to give the 16 bare `OrchestratorConfig(` constructions across three scheduler test files an explicit `psi_admission=PsiAdmissionConfig()`, described as "ACCEPTANCE IS MECHANICAL". But that same task's D1 change makes `PsiAdmissionConfig().cpu_some_avg10` default to None, so the CPU arm can never trip — and those files depend on the 85.0 default making it trip: test_scheduler_dispatch_admission.py carries the comment "cpu_some10=90 is OVER the default cpu_some_avg10=85 threshold" plus ~11 `_psi(cpu_some10=90.0|99.0, ...)` sites, and test_scheduler_psi_saturation_transition.py has 3 `feed.set_saturated(cpu_some10=90.0)` sites. A blanket sweep would leave ~17 sites asserting nothing and invert TestDispatchAdmissionMetricRanking. Corrected prescription recorded on 3590: for any construction whose test exercises the CPU arm, pass `psi_admission=PsiAdmissionConfig(cpu_some_avg10=85.0)` — an explicit fixture value rather than a default — and the acceptance criterion gains a second clause: the three files must pass with a non-default block present AND still be testing what they were testing before. Related: the manifest's "default-85 pins: 3 sites" binding was an UNDERCOUNT because it counted `== 85.0` greps rather than behavioural dependence on the default.

Task 2335 (milestone β scheduler time-gate) debugging session: the only verify failure was 9 pyright errors, all pre-existing test/lint gates were already green. Fixed by (1) adding isinstance guards for `milestone.get('at')` (str) and `milestone.get('after_secs')` (int) in Scheduler._milestone_time_gated before passing to datetime.fromisoformat/timedelta — this both satisfies pyright's Unknown|None narrowing and correctly implements the spec's "unparseable at"/"non-int after_secs" fail-safe-withhold requirement; (2) adding `# type: ignore[attr-defined]` to 7 AsyncMock assertion call sites in TestStampMilestoneDepsSatisfied. Also discovered (and filed as a separate non-blocking infra_issue escalation, not fixed under this task) that orchestrator's full `pytest tests/` suite has ~11 pre-existing flaky tests under parallel xdist load, tied to real PSI memory-pressure sampling and a hard-coded `/proj/data/orchestrator` snapshot-write path that doesn't exist in this sandbox — unrelated to milestone work, all pass in isolation.

When extending the `_SchedulerLike` Protocol in orchestrator/src/orchestrator/workflow.py, do NOT add positional-only `/` markers to the new method signatures if any caller uses kwargs. Discovered: adding `update_task(self, task_id, metadata, /)` made pyright reject the existing `await self.scheduler.update_task(self.task_id, metadata=new_metadata)` call site. Fix was to drop the `/`. Same for `_dispatch_tool` — the real Scheduler accepts kwargs (e.g. `timeout=15`), so the Protocol must too.

In orchestrator/tests/test_scheduler.py, when an AsyncMock is assigned to a Scheduler instance attribute (e.g. `sched.update_task = AsyncMock(...)`) inside a pytest fixture rather than inside the test function body, pyright cannot narrow the attribute's type across the fixture/test-function boundary — `scheduler.update_task.assert_awaited_once_with(...)` then fails with reportAttributeAccessIssue ("Cannot access attribute ... for class MethodType"). The established fix in this file is a trailing `# type: ignore[attr-defined]` comment on the assertion call (see line ~4175 precedent); pyright treats any `# type: ignore[code]` comment as a full line-level suppression regardless of whether the bracketed code matches one of its own rule names. When the mock assignment happens in the SAME function as the assertion, pyright narrows correctly and no ignore comment is needed (see TestMilestoneSweepDrivenByAcquireNext for a working example).

Before adding a new public accessor to `Scheduler` just so a collaborator can read a config-derived value, check whether it is already reachable via `scheduler.config` — `Scheduler.__init__` assigns `self.config = config` (public, no underscore) and `scheduler.config.<field>` is an established two-hop reach-through in-tree (e.g. `harness.scheduler.config.max_external_dep_unresolved_cycles` in test_cross_project_dispatch_integration.py). The task-1327 `parked_live_count` precedent only compels an accessor for genuinely PRIVATE state (`_blocked_task_ids_in_window`), not for config fields. This matters beyond style: a plan's `files` list drives concurrency locks, and scheduler.py is the repo's highest-churn file, so listing it can get a task requeued for lock contention (task 4102 was requeued once, then dropped scheduler.py + test_scheduler.py from its plan on revalidation by reading `scheduler.config.project_root` instead — 6 files to 4, 10 steps to 8, identical behaviour). Caveat from task 1447 (memory 3de4db37): when the collaborator is duck-typed and its tests use a bare MagicMock, a missing/renamed attribute silently yields a Mock rather than failing — so guard the read with `isinstance` and cover a genuinely attribute-less stand-in in the tests.

Gotcha (task 2470, eval-revival δ): the eval-mode `_StubMcpSession` (orchestrator/src/orchestrator/evals/runner.py) must have a `call_tool` branch for EVERY string literal the real Scheduler dispatches via `dispatch_tool('<literal>', ...)` in scheduler.py — a missing branch raises NotImplementedError at eval runtime, swallowed and logged as heartbeat WARNING spam (the D2/B9 failure: set_task_claimant heartbeats every ~60s). As of 2026-07 the dispatched literals are: get_tasks, set_task_status, set_task_claimant, get_task, get_statuses, get_external_statuses, update_task. Task 2470 added branches for set_task_claimant and get_external_statuses (the latter had silently drifted in via the cross-project-deps feature, dispatched at scheduler.py:2525) and added a CI tripwire, orchestrator/tests/test_scheduler_dispatch_literal_tripwire.py, that AST-scans scheduler.py for every dispatch_tool string-literal first arg and behaviorally probes that `_StubMcpSession().call_tool(name, {})` does not raise NotImplementedError (any other exception, e.g. KeyError from empty args, counts as branch-present). `add_dependency` is NOT dispatched by scheduler.py — it was added to the stub defensively per spec and is covered by a unit test, not the tripwire. Use AST, not regex/grep, to enumerate dispatch_tool call sites: most put the literal on a line separate from the call, so regex/grep would miss them. When adding a new tool dispatched by the Scheduler, ALSO add a stub branch or this tripwire goes red.

GOTCHA when adding an MCP call to dashboard/src/dashboard/data/scheduler.py's `_one_project`: ~10 tests in dashboard/tests/test_scheduler_page.py build their fake with a FIXED-LENGTH `AsyncMock(side_effect=[snapshot, events])` list, which silently encodes the exact number of MCP calls made per project. A third call makes every one of them raise StopIteration, and test_collect_scheduler_state_retries_whole_pair_on_second_url_when_events_fail additionally asserts the exact call sequence `[url1, url1, url2, url2]`.
