psi_admission yaml leak, re-reproduced 2026-09-08 on main (commit a24b1fb665 era): adding `psi_admission: {cpu_some_avg10: 70.0, min_inflight_floor: 3}` to dark-factory-orchestrator.yaml makes 9 of 18 tests fail across orchestrator/tests/test_scheduler_dispatch_admission.py, test_scheduler_psi_saturation_transition.py and test_scheduler_hermetic_psi.py (control without the block: 18 passed) — the same signature as the 2026-08-03 red main (9cec63e10e, reverted eeb4ad9000). Mechanism: the autouse orchestrator/tests/conftest.py::_isolate_orch_config deliberately pins ORCH_CONFIG_PATH at the LIVE yaml so tests see operational values, and 16 bare OrchestratorConfig(...) constructions in those three files (3 already pass psi_admission=) therefore inherit any psi_admission block. Consequences: no psi_admission tuning can land via the yaml until fixed, and reload_config re-reads the same file so there is no hot path either. Minimal fix: pass explicit psi_admission=PsiAdmissionConfig() at the 16 sites (the empty-ORCH_CONFIG_PATH pattern in test_config_psi_admission_reload.py::test_defaults_on_bare_config also works). Do NOT use conftest.py::code_default_config for this: it skips the project yaml entirely, dropping the operational values (lock_depth, merge_verify_breadth='full', trains) those scheduler tests run under. Rejected workaround: ORCH_PSI_ADMISSION__CPU_SOME_AVG10 in the unit env (OrchestratorConfig has env_prefix ORCH_ and env_nested_delimiter '__') would not leak into verify legs (verify.py::_target_subprocess_env scrubs the whole ORCH_ prefix) but DOES leak into agent shells (agents/invoke.py passes dict(os.environ) unscrubbed), so implementers running these tests would hit the same failures; it is also restart-tier and invisible to check-config. How to reproduce a suspected config-only red safely: git worktree add --detach a throwaway, edit the yaml there, run the files with main's venv python, -n 0, nice 19, then remove the worktree.

Reify module-SCC ratchet (INV-ARCH-1, scripts/assert-module-scc.py) counts only TOP-LEVEL crate modules. If you extract code from a member of a baselined SCC (e.g. reify-eval's unfold or engine_eval) into a new top-level module that still imports SCC members and is still imported by one, the ratchet reds GREW, and moving an import cannot fix it. Nest the new file as a submodule of its origin instead (e.g. crates/reify-eval/src/unfold/<new>.rs, declared `pub(crate) mod <new>;` in unfold.rs). Its edges then count as the parent's existing intra-SCC edges. Also rename its row in crates/reify-audit/pdiag-baseline.txt by regenerating with `cargo run -p reify-audit --bin pdiag-baseline-gen -- --project-root .` (§3(d) move case). Applied in task 6586.

That trips GREW, and `cargo test -p reify-build-utils --test module_scc_ratchet` (workspace_module_sccs_match_the_committed_baseline) goes red. The tool counts every src/geometry/** file as node `geometry`, so this adds no edge. Discovery (reify INV-ARCH-1, 2026-10-14): before S3 β #8687 lands, reify-eval's baselined module SCC is the 24-module one and contains cache, deps, demand, journal, warm_pool, observed_demand, realization_content, engine_compute and engine_fixpoint — the home modules of CacheStore, WarmStatePool, EventJournal, DemandRegistry, DependencyTrace, ComputeDispatchRegistry and BuildScheduler. Any NEW reify-eval module that names one of those types and is imported by engine_admin/engine_* closes a cycle and GROWs the baseline (module_scc_ratchet reds). After #8687 the expected residual is {engine_admin, engine_build, engine_edit, engine_eval, geometry_ops} plus a separate {cache, deps} 2-cycle, which a new module may import without joining. So any leaf adding sub-struct modules below the engine must depend on #8687 (S1 α #9036 does), and the rule is 'imports nothing in the SCC as baselined at landing'. The SCC tool sees only crate::m paths, so new modules also get an 'engine-free-<module>' adoption-ratchet row counting `Engine` mentions at 0.

INV-ARCH-1's checker scripts/assert-module-scc.py counts only explicit `crate::<module>` edges (and names inside `crate::{…}` lists that are modules). An import through a crate-root `pub use` facade such as `use crate::{Finding}` adds NO edge, so a real module cycle can hide behind a re-export facade. It also files a nested path (src/foo/bar.rs) under its first segment, and treats src/bin/ as separate crates. crates/reify-audit has no SCC row in scripts/module-scc-baseline.json, so any new cycle there reds the merge. Design new reify-audit modules to import downward in fact. Example: S24 put every kind enum, and Pattern itself, in a lower crate::kind module, so model and the detectors never import each other.

Reify's INV-ARCH-1 module-SCC ratchet (`python3 scripts/assert-module-scc.py check`, baseline scripts/module-scc-baseline.json) fails with exit 1 when an SCC grows or merges (GREW). It also fails when a baselined SCC shrinks or dissolves (STALE), so a refactor that breaks an intra-crate module cycle must lower the baseline row in the same diff. Lower it by regenerating the file: `print > /tmp/x.json && mv /tmp/x.json scripts/module-scc-baseline.json`. Crates with no SCC are omitted from the file. Per-task lanes run the gate test (crates/reify-build-utils/tests/module_scc_ratchet.rs) only when reify-build-utils is affected, while the merge gate always runs it, so run `check` by hand after moving any `crate::` import.

Key asymmetries: cmd_build has kernel+trampolines but NO solver and NO FEA cache; cmd_report/cmd_explain have solver+trampolines+cache but NO kernel; cmd_eval never calls ensure_openvdb_kernel (only cmd_check for thickness-DFM and cmd_build for isosurface do); only cmd_check ever calls set_capture_repr_tol; the GUI has kernel+solver+trampolines but NO persistent cache; the CLI mcp-server has the cache but neither solver nor trampolines; cmd_doc constructs no engine at all. CRITICAL INSIGHT: four of the seven axes are gated on MODULE CONTENT (module_has_geometry, module_has_isosurface, module_has_thickness_dfm_rule, module_has_representation_within, and the Conforms||ReprWithin||DFM disjunction), not on driver identity, and those predicates are hand-rolled at seven call sites. That predicate duplication — not the capability list — is the real duplication, and it is why the divergences are content-dependent and therefore invisible until a user writes the file that trips one.

Reify kinematics/dynamics structure facts measured 2026-10-13 (S6 seat maps, main e217c0f30b):
- **Relations.** RelationInstance is defined in reify-constraints relate_solve.rs and built at exactly one site, reify-eval relate_solve::relation_instance, from the compiled call's name. It is NOT built in the compiler, and ResolvedFunction carries only name/qualified_name strings.
- **Mechanism record:** {body_id, closing_joint, kind:loop_closure, path_a, path_b}. append_body appends the pose link to path_b for parent-conflict (tie/brace) closures but appends `at` itself for cycle (ring) closures.
- **Dead wrapper.** loop_closure_solver::mechanism_loop_closure_chains has zero production consumers. solve_loop_closure_with_diagnostics has one caller (snapshot), which discards its diagnostics and re-runs the plain solve, so its count-against-6 DOF policy has no production effect.
- **Diagnostic channels.** The snapshot diagnose hook receives (name, args, result) on both paths, but sweep calls snapshot via eval_builtin, so the hook only sees name="sweep". engine_eval::detect_error_map_diagnostics reads top-level cells only.
- **Module SCC.** scripts/module-scc-baseline.json records the reify-stdlib SCC {dynamics, joints, mechanism, snapshot}. Its edges: joints→dynamics::spatial (pure math), snapshot→dynamics (center_of_mass mass reads), dynamics→snapshot (make_binding).

DISCOVERY (jun7, red-team of Option A, verified main + task/3205): two engine mechanics that surprised the design and had to be corrected. (1) A sibling geometry `let` referenced by a bare identifier (e.g. `let filleted = fillet(b, edges, r)` where b is a prior let) is INLINED into the consuming realization's op list as GeomRef::Step (resolved against per-realization step_handles), NOT as GeomRef::Sub through named_steps. GeomRef::Sub is EXCLUSIVELY the self.<sub>.<member> cross-component handshake. So for esc-3205 the load-bearing cross-node dependency is the SELECTOR VALUE CELL (the edges_at_height let, which needs a new realization_reads=[body] edge), not a GeomRef::Sub edge. (2) The claimed "deps.rs:279 realization_ref fallback" edge does NOT exist as a static edge: deps.rs:279 is geometry_cell_realization_reads (a realization -> its OWN output cell, intra-template), and realization_ref is a RUNTIME GeometryHandle field (geometry_ops.rs ~4192), not a reverse-index edge. (3) try_eval_topology_selector and try_eval_geometry_query are called ONLY from the whole-template post-process passes (engine_build.rs:5436 / :5305); execute_realization_ops takes values: &ValueMap READ-ONLY and neither hydrates output cells nor resolves selectors — so "fold P3/P4 inline" is genuinely NEW per-node executor work (three first-class executors: per-realization output-cell hydration, per-cell selector/query resolution, the realization), not a body-unchanged re-dispatch.

Adding a NEW leaf crate to reify can silently red tests/infra/test_engine_hash_closure.sh WITHOUT any edit to crates/reify-eval — an addition to the known registration points, and a correction to the claim that the OCCT pair (occt-touching-crates.txt + .config/nextest.toml) is the only same-diff registration that can red the gate. Mechanism: crates/reify-eval/Cargo.toml depends NORMALLY on both reify-compiler (:15) and reify-stdlib (:51, promoted by task 3819), so wiring a new crate as a non-dev dep of EITHER puts it in reify-eval's build+normal closure, and the drift guard's manifest ⊇ live-closure assertion then fails with the new crate as the sole missing member. Remedy is one sorted line in crates/reify-eval/engine_hash_closure.txt (precedent: 7ce5b632ad, 1 file, 4 insertions). TRAP for task-scoped agents: that manifest is a reify-eval path, so it is usually absent from an architect's declared `files` scope even when the task legitimately requires it — budget a scope escalation rather than discovering it at merge-verify. Confirmed NOT needed for such a reify-core-only leaf: occt-touching-crates.txt, release-sensitive-crates.txt, harness-layout-baseline.manifest (test_occt_gated_scope 61/61, test_release_scoped_scope 33/33, check-harness-baseline-registration PASS).

solar_challenge_platform gotcha (task 350, branch task/350 at 5c85f3f, pending merge): a billed statement's money_carry_in is its statement of record's money_carry_out AS FILED in Numeric(18,10), read by billing/statement.py::_money_carry_in. A test comparing next month's carry-in with the previous FRESH Statement must quantize with tests/_statement_round_trip.STATEMENT_GBP_QUANTUM, because a fresh carry-out is the unquantised amount due. Also, from_statement on a statement with money_carry_in > 0 raises ValueError until the CARRIED_FORWARD draft exists (plan step 12): StatementView.build refuses drafts that miss total_minor by a penny or more.

solar_challenge_platform test gotcha (billing provider bridge): StatementView.build (billing/contract.py) raises ValueError when its drafts' ideal sum misses to_minor_units(total) by 1 minor unit or more. So taking a statement with no fraction of a penny (e.g. exactly 99p) and lowering its amount_due by exactly 1p fails inside from_statement, before R2 ever runs. To test R2 on such a statement, pass contradicting StatementFloats straight to billing.status.run, as tests/integration/test_s5_p7_to_provider.py's TestNothingDue and TestCarriedForward do. Also, the frozen pydantic models there (ReconciliationView, StatementView, BillingRun) keep pydantic's default extra='ignore': a constructor keyword the model lacks is dropped without error. A RED test for a new field must read the attribute itself; comparing two models proves nothing.

solar_challenge_platform test gotcha (task 350, branch task/350, pending merge): Statement.__post_init__ now runs MoneyCarryMismatch.check (B23), which requires money_carry_out to be 0 or exactly amount_due. A fresh sub-£1 statement's money_carry_out is the unquantised amount due, while its read-back is quantised to Numeric(18,10). So any helper that rebuilds a Statement with dataclasses.replace(fresh, amount_due=read_back.amount_due) must also replace money_carry_in and money_carry_out from the read-back, as tests/_statement_round_trip.py::as_stored does. CONSUMER CONSTRAINTS for solar-challenge v0.5.0 (tag solar-challenge-v0.5.0 = commit 03af26e2d8138fa1a728dfd4c12d404b83db8b7b, pushed to github.com/leodearden/solar-challenge on 2026-09-21). Binding on platform tasks 186 (P-Invoice·λ2 re-pin / Statement.amount_due) and 187 (λ3 two-line invoice).

1. DO NOT hard-assert the PRD U1 literal. cbs-invoice-own-use-only.md §10 U1 states `cbs_amount_due_gbp == 70.308`, but that literal is NOT representable as the computed float. MEASURED in CPython 3.12: 12.0*558.0/100.0 -> 66.96 (bit-equal); 0.05*66.96 -> 3.348 (bit-equal); 66.96 + 3.348 -> 70.30799999999999 (~7.1e-15 low, NOT bit-equal to 70.308); 66.96*1.05 -> 70.30799999999999 (identical — the gap is a property of the value's decimal rendering, not of the sum-vs-product choice §4 E3 legislates). A test transcribing U1 verbatim as `assert stmt.amount_due == Decimal("70.308")` WILL FAIL, and will look like a library bug rather than a float-rendering artifact. Assert the STRUCTURAL identity instead — `Statement.amount_due == Σ Decimal(str(li.cbs_amount_due_gbp))`, which IS exact — and quantise or use a tolerance for any U1-style decimal figure (e.g. Decimal(str(round(x, 2))) == Decimal("70.31")).

2. BillBreakdown gained TWO REQUIRED keyword fields with NO defaults: own_use_vat_gbp and cbs_amount_due_gbp. Every platform fixture or helper that CONSTRUCTS a BillBreakdown must supply them.

3. BillBreakdown now VALIDATES in __post_init__: it raises ValueError when cbs_amount_due_gbp != own_use_payment_gbp + own_use_vat_gbp (bare float equality). So constructing fixtures must DERIVE the values — own_use_vat_gbp = vat_rate * own_use_payment_gbp, cbs_amount_due_gbp = own_use_payment_gbp + own_use_vat_gbp — never transcribe decimal literals from PRD §2/§9. Hardcoding cbs_amount_due_gbp=70.308 now raises at construction.

4. UNAFFECTED: the R2 float->Decimal seam (billing/from_statement.py::statement_floats_from, eps=1e-9 GBP per segment) still clears by six orders of magnitude. Read-only consumers walking the dataclass (dataclasses.fields()/asdict(), web.storage) need no change — the two fields were deliberately kept fields()-visible rather than derived @property.

(1) R3 CONTIGUITY — run_billing raises BillingOrderError (billing/statement.py) unless period.start equals the account's latest persisted statement's period_end. Any test that bills TWO periods on ONE account must make them adjacent (or use two accounts); three tests had to be fixed for this (tests/billing/test_coverage_integration.py's two comparison tests moved to consecutive DAYS, and test_run_billing_governed_finance.py::test_run_billing_is_period_anchored_across_rate_change moved its second 28-day period from April to March so the rate change lands on the seam). (2) D5 NO STATEMENT WITHOUT REGISTERS — a hermetic fixture that seeds only power metrics (grid_import_power/load_power) now returns SkippedAccount("register_unavailable"); it needs tests/register_seed.py::seed_registers (for a TelemetryStore) or registers_at / registers_from_hh_reads (for a StaticRegisterSource). Related arithmetic trap: a register delta and the priced half-hour stream differ by exactly one trailing sample, because trapezoidal integration over 60s samples has no successor sample to bridge to in the final bucket — tests/integration/test_billing_boundary.py::test_timescale_in_db_settlement_read expected 35.9975 from the stream and now gets exactly 36.0 from the register.

`orchestrator.yaml` is an OVERLOADED filename in dark_factory with two unrelated meanings, and conflating them silently breaks things. (2) MODULE config at <module>/orchestrator.yaml (e.g. shared/, fused-memory/, dashboard/, escalation/) — a COMPLETELY different concept where the file's DIRECTORY is the module prefix; _discover_module_configs (orchestrator/src/orchestrator/config.py, rel = yaml_path.parent.relative_to(project_root)) walks for that literal filename, and each carries per-package verification commands scoping pyright/ruff/pytest to that package's own venv. Moving/renaming a MODULE config makes it silently stop applying — verification falls back to root commands against the wrong venv, no error. dark_factory has 8 module configs; know-live has 2. When a task says "move all orchestrator config files", it means TOP-LEVEL only — never touch module configs.

Before adding ANY new key to dark-factory-orchestrator.yaml whose pydantic/defaults.yaml default differs from the value you are declaring, grep orchestrator/tests for bare `OrchestratorConfig()` constructions asserting that field's default. conftest.py's autouse `_isolate_orch_config` pins ORCH_CONFIG_PATH at the operational yaml, so a bare config in ANY orchestrator test reads the live operational value — declaring a previously-absent key silently falsifies every `assert config.<field> == <shipped default>` in the suite. Measured on task 3886 (wiring git.merge_config_only_full_gate_globs): a one-line yaml addition turned orchestrator/tests/test_verify.py::TestMergeConfigOnlyDiffForcesFullGate::test_empty_globs_default_config_returns_false red (17964 passed/17 skipped -> 1 failed/17966 passed/16 skipped). Note WHERE it landed: the three obvious candidates in test_config.py all survived (two construct GitConfig() directly, one does monkeypatch.delenv('ORCH_CONFIG_PATH') + chdir), and the breakage was in test_verify.py instead — so a targeted pre-check of the "obvious" config tests is not sufficient; run the full orchestrator suite. The correct repair is `@pytest.mark.usefixtures('code_default_config')` — the sanctioned opt-in hatch conftest.py ships for tests asserting CODE DEFAULTS — never pinning the new operational value into the test.

candidates.content: reify gui flake reporter: vitest 3.2.4's run-level unhandled errors reach a custom reporter's onTestRunEnd second argument as SerializedError objects whose `.message` is UN-PREFIXED — the `Error: ` seen in vitest's console output is the printer's `${name}: ${message}`, not part of the message. So an anchored regex like /^\[vitest-worker\]: Timeout calling "([^"]+)"/ matches real vitest errors directly. Verified end-to-end on 2026-09-20 (task 7724, tests/infra/test_gui_vitest_rpc_hardening.sh Section D Phase 5) by driving REAL vitest, not synthetic {message} fixtures. To reproduce a run-level unhandled error deterministically in a vitest fixture: inside a test, `setTimeout(() => { throw new Error(...) }, 0)` then `await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 50))` — the throw lands inside the run as an Unhandled Error while the test itself still PASSES, giving the "N passed (N) / Errors: 1" shape.

vitest 3.2.4's worker->host RPC starvation flake has TWO distinct shapes, and the second was invisible to task 7630's classifier. Shape 1 (failed SUITES, zero failed tests): a `fetch`/`transform` timeout kills a suite before collection. Shape 2 (ZERO failed suites, zero failed tests, run-level "Errors N errors"): `snapshotSaved` is issued AFTER a file's tests have already passed, so its timeout surfaces as an unhandled error vitest cannot attribute to any module — observed in data/verify-logs/7600/attempt-1.test-20260920T053235_446545Z.log as 174/174 suites + 5707/5707 tests passing with 2 `Timeout calling "snapshotSaved"` errors. Both are built by `new Error(...)` at node_modules/vitest/dist/chunks/rpc.*.js:49-53, so `.message` starts at `[vitest-worker]:` — the `Error: ` seen in logs is the reporter printing `${name}: ${message}`, NOT part of the message, so a `/^\[vitest-worker\]:/`-anchored regex matches both suite errors and SerializedError unhandled errors.

ROOT CAUSE (measured, task 7630) of the recurring GUI-vitest merge-gate flake `[vitest-worker]: Timeout calling "fetch"` — supersedes the "suspected/unverified" note in the esc-7431-3 triage memory. The bound is birpc's DEFAULT_TIMEOUT = 6e4 (60s) on the WORKER->HOST channel (vitest/dist/chunks/index.*.js:3, armed only when `timeout >= 0`), NOT testTimeout — which is why 3185's and 4856's per-test-site bumps could never fix it. It is UNREACHABLE by config in vitest 3.2.4: createForksRpcOptions returns only {serialize,deserialize,post,on}, and the public type excludes it deliberately — `WorkerRpcOptions = Pick<BirpcOptions,"on"|"post"|"serialize"|"deserialize">` (dist/workers.d.ts:23). No VITEST_* env var covers it; the worker module path is hardcoded (`resolve(vitest.distPath,"workers/forks.js")`), so the only injection point (createRuntimeRpc spreads `...options` LAST, so `timeout: -1` would win) needs a custom pool — and createForksPool is NOT exported from vitest/node. Chunk filenames are content-hashed, so always glob them, never hardcode a hash. KEY NEW FACT: in all 5 occurrences (5982, 5757, 6478, 6094, 7431) the timed-out `fetch` is the SAME module, gui/vitest.setup.ts — which is 65 lines with ZERO imports, so it is the victim by FREQUENCY, not cost: `isolate ?? true` gives every test file a fresh fork with a cold vite-node module cache, so the single setupFiles entry is fetched once per test file (173x), always first, before any test runs. That explains the "random subset of failing suites". Transform time across the five ranges 37.16s-166.57s with NO correlation to failure, ruling out transform cost; the real invariant is wall-clock dilation 186-474s vs a 51s idle baseline. `onQueued`/`snapshotSaved`/`onUnhandledError`/`resolveSnapshotPath` time out in the same runs — all share the one 60s bound — so the common cause is host unresponsiveness, not any one method or suite.

GUI vitest 3.2.4 worker-RPC starvation flake: which lost call produces which failure shape. Every worker→host birpc call carries a 60 s timer in the worker. (a) A `fetch` lost during a module's import fails that whole file before any test runs, as a failed suite. (b) A `snapshotSaved` or `onTaskUpdate` lost after a file's tests passed reaches main as a run-level "Unhandled Error" with no file named, and vitest exits 1 with all tests green. (c) If the lost call is a file's CLOSING `onTaskUpdate`, main never learns the file finished, so the module is left 'pending'/'queued' ("unfinished") even though all its tests passed. Worked example, task 8828 (2026-10-14, 00:00 BST): 187/188 files and 6113/6113 tests passed (6113 is the whole suite, so Editor.test.tsx's tests all passed), with 4 unhandled errors (1 onTaskUpdate, 3 snapshotSaved). src/__tests__/Editor.test.tsx was the only file without a result line. The verify failed with zero failing tests. Correct log grep: `[vitest-worker]: Timeout calling "` (vitest's onTimeoutError text), NOT birpc's own `[birpc] timeout on calling`, which never appears in reify logs.

In the reify GUI (gui/), running vitest under host over-subscription (loadavg >> ncores, e.g. 300+ on 32 cores with swap thrashing) can make the default forks worker pool crash with EXIT 1 and ZERO output — a single newline, no error text, no assertion. This is an environmental worker crash, NOT a test failure. Recover by re-running the file isolated: `CI=1 npx vitest run --reporter=dot --pool=forks --poolOptions.forks.singleFork=true <file>`; the test then passes cleanly in well under a second. Distinguish env-crash from real failure by: empty output + exit 1, vs. the same file passing in single-fork mode. Also: the default vitest reporter can emit zero captured output when multiple file-path args are piped non-TTY; use --reporter=dot for reliable captured output.

vitest 3.2.4 attributes a throw during a spec's top-level module evaluation to the MODULE (it surfaces via TestModule.errors(), making the suite 'failed'), NOT to onTestRunEnd's run-level unhandledErrors array. To produce a genuine run-level unhandled error in a test fixture you must throw from a timer (setTimeout(() => { throw ... }, 0)) and then await long enough for it to land inside the run — that is the shape a post-test RPC like snapshotSaved produces. Measured on task 7724 against tests/infra/test_gui_vitest_rpc_hardening.sh Section D, whose Phase 1 (module-load throw => failed suite) and Phase 5 (timer throw => run-level error, zero failed suites) are the two fixtures demonstrating the distinction.

Writing a vitest reporter that decides anything from a finished run must check module STATE, not just the failed set: vitest's TestModuleState is "skipped"|"pending"|"failed"|"passed"|"queued" (gui/node_modules/vitest/dist/chunks/reporters.d.*.d.ts:270-271), so a pool that dies partway leaves suites in 'pending'/'queued' that never ran, and a reporter reasoning only over failed modules will call the run explained while suites were silently skipped. onTestRunEnd's third argument is the run's TestRunEndReason ("passed"|"interrupted"|"failed", ibid.:556, hook signature :598) and is the other completeness signal. Only 'passed'/'failed'/'skipped' are terminal. Chunk filenames are content-hashed — always glob, never hardcode a hash.

vitest 3.2.4 reporter gotcha: a failed describe-level beforeAll/afterAll hook puts its error on the nested TestSuite (read via module.children.allSuites()[].errors()), NOT in TestModule.errors(), and marks that suite's tests skipped (@vitest/runner runSuite). A test that exceeds its it() timeout fails with a message starting 'Test timed out in <N>ms.' (hooks: 'Hook timed out in <N>ms.'), which is how GUI worker-RPC starvation surfaced inside Editor.test.tsx's ?raw import (esc-7094-6), rather than as a '[vitest-worker]: Timeout calling' message.

[SUPERSEDED 2026-09-17: task 7630 landed a source fix (commit 728b40ea8c4eb230673eb6c404eca71defd87834) that hardens the vitest worker RPC channel. Root cause (mem0 a935f42b) is birpc's DEFAULT_TIMEOUT=60s on the WORKER->HOST channel, not merely host resource contention — it IS fixable at the code level. Before following the "do not attempt a source fix / escalate as infra_issue" guidance below, check whether task 7630's fix is present on your branch; if it is and the timeout still recurs, treat it as a new/different failure, not this one.]

When `gui/` npm test (vitest) reports failed test files with errors like `[vitest-worker]: Timeout calling \"fetch\"/\"onQueued\"/\"onUnhandledError\"/\"snapshotSaved\"/\"resolveSnapshotPath\"` but the run summary still shows all individual Tests passed (e.g. \"Tests 3846 passed (3846)\", only Test Files show N failed), this is a vitest worker-RPC communication timeout caused by host resource contention (high load from concurrent warm-lane cargo/npm/vitest processes), not a code defect. Confirm by re-running just the reported-failed files in isolation from gui/ (e.g. `npx vitest run <file1> <file2> <file3>`) once node_modules already exists — they pass cleanly (no timeouts) once contention subsides. Do not attempt a source fix in this situation; escalate as infra_issue and recommend a verify retry.

GUI-vitest worker-RPC starvation flake, occurrence #6 (2026-09-19, seen from task 7094): task 7630's bounded retry in scripts/gui-vitest-run.sh can be SILENTLY VETOED, and the tell is the ABSENCE of any `@@REIFY_GUI_FLAKE@@` marker in the log. gui/vitest-worker-rpc-flake-reporter.ts's classifyWorkerRpcFlake returns null at its first guard, `if (summary.failedTestCount !== 0) return null`, so a single failed TEST anywhere in the run suppresses the retry even when every failed SUITE carries the `[vitest-worker]: Timeout calling "fetch"` signature. The known offender is gui/src/__tests__/Editor.test.tsx's `await import('../editor/Editor?raw')` (the 'imports reifyEditorTheme and reifyHighlightStyle' test): it resolves through the same worker->host `fetch` RPC that starves for gui/vitest.setup.ts, but is awaited inside a test body with its own 60s `it()` timeout, so starvation surfaces as "Test timed out in 60000ms" — a failed TEST — instead of an RPC-timeout suite error. Discriminator for "is this the flake or my code": compare gui vitest wall clock against the ~51s idle baseline (measured here 53.60s green at loadavg 32 vs 265.34s red at loadavg 187 on 32 cores), and check whether the same tree passed the gate earlier. Do NOT fix this by widening the failedTestCount veto — that rule is what stops a real defect being absorbed by the retry; take the assertion off the RPC path instead. Lineage 3185,4856,7630; root cause record is mem0 a935f42b.

In GUI vitest, the 'Error: [vitest-worker]: Timeout calling "snapshotSaved"' unhandled errors are NOT caused by app snapshots (gui has zero toMatchSnapshot usages). snapshotSaved is vitest's internal per-file snapshot-state save RPC (worker->main); it times out only because cross-worktree cargo compiles starve the Node main process beyond the birpc timeout, and vitest then exits 1 ('might cause false positive tests'). Mitigate by raising the worker RPC/teardown timeout or capping per-file worker concurrency (gate on process.env.DF_VERIFY_ROLE, which verify.sh sets to task|merge but is unset in local dev), not by touching any test.

Task 'GUI vitest flake RECURRED past 3185/4856: harden the vitest worker RPC channel (module-load `Timeout calling "fetch"`), not per-test testTimeout' completed. Landed in commit 728b40ea8c4eb230673eb6c404eca71defd87834.

Reify gui vitest convention (since task 7642): fork workers are reused (root poolOptions.forks.isolate=false). A test file is routed to the 'fresh-modules' project (fresh module graph per file) only if its OWN source calls vi.mock/doMock/unmock/doUnmock/resetModules/importMock/importActual — a vi.mock inside a shared helper module is invisible to the classifier (gui/vitest-project-partition.ts). Ad-hoc globals (window.foo = ...) must be deleted in teardown, and a synthetic event's overridden `target` must be defined configurable:true or solid's delegated listener throws "Cannot redefine property: target". Full rules: docs/notes/gui-vitest-shared-workers.md.

Verify-failure triage discovery (esc-5283-12, 2026-07-23): reported test FAILURES that are actually exit-127 'No such file or directory' on the test binary (via run-with-occt.sh) are NOT semantic failures — they are the warm-lane target/ artifact-vanish family (canonical memory 8287c8d8). [SUPERSEDED 2026-09-17: task 7630 (mem0 a935f42b) established that raising vitest's testTimeout/hookTimeout — task 3185's approach, described below as "the pragmatic fix" — CANNOT fix the `[vitest-worker]: Timeout calling ...` flake class: the bound is birpc's WORKER->HOST RPC channel DEFAULT_TIMEOUT (60s), not any per-test timeout. The actual fix hardens the worker RPC channel itself (commit 728b40ea8c4eb230673eb6c404eca71defd87834). The jobserver-contention diagnosis below may still be a contributing factor but is not sufficient on its own.]

GUI vitest cargo-concurrency flakes in Reify are caused by cross-worktree contention on the shared rustc jobserver (CARGO_MAKEFLAGS=--jobserver-auth=fifo:/tmp/reify-jobserver, 32 tokens) saturating CPU and starving the Node event loop. Root cause is NOT within-task contention: orchestrator.yaml's test_command already chains `cargo test ... && cd gui && npm test` so within ONE task the GUI tests wait for cargo. Lowering vitest's pool/maxThreads doesn't help (no internal CPU contention). Gating GUI tests on cargo build completion in orchestrator.yaml doesn't help either (cargo of OTHER worktrees is the contender). The pragmatic fix is raising vitest's testTimeout/hookTimeout so tests tolerate the temporary slowdown — this is what task 3185 implemented.
Notes that the alternative (Vitest pool: 'singleFork' via poolMatchGlobs) requires vitest.config.ts changes and is more invasive

GUI vitest flake shape that the gui-vitest-run.sh retry does NOT cover (seen 2026-10-13 on task 8828): "Test Files N-1 passed (N)" with every test passing, plus run-level `[vitest-worker]: Timeout calling "onTaskUpdate"/"snapshotSaved"` unhandled errors and no @@REIFY_GUI_FLAKE@@ marker. classifyWorkerRpcFlake (gui/vitest-worker-rpc-flake-reporter.ts) deliberately returns null when unfinishedSuites is non-empty, so the run reds the gate. A plain re-run of the gui block was green. Recorded at esc-8828-1.

Recurring merge-gate FLAKE, not a defect: the gui vitest block in scripts/verify.sh intermittently fails with `[vitest-worker]: Timeout calling "fetch"` on a RANDOM subset of suites, plus unhandled `Timeout calling "onQueued"/"snapshotSaved"` errors. Recognise it by three signs together: (a) the failure is COLLECTION-phase — the Summary reads "Test Files N failed | M passed" with ZERO test-level failures (e.g. "Tests 5626 passed (5626)"); (b) the failing suite set differs on every occurrence, so no single suite is implicated; (c) the run's phase times are load-skewed (transform/collect/environment each dwarf actual `tests` time). Observed on 5 unrelated tasks in 4 weeks: 5982 (2026-08-20), 5757 (08-26), 6478 (09-09), 6094 (09-10), 7431 (09-17), always in the _merge-verify lane. Triage recipe: confirm the task's `git diff main...HEAD` touches no gui/ files, then re-run `scripts/gui-test.sh --no-typecheck` in the task worktree — it has passed clean every time (7431: 173/173 files, 5652 tests, 51s). If clean, resolve the post_merge_verify escalation with action='resume', resolution_class='benign' and retry the merge unmodified; change no code. Note the gui block runs EARLY in verify.sh, so this failure ABORTS the run before the Rust nextest phase ever executes — a task's actual Rust deliverable is unverified after such an attempt, which is a further reason to retry rather than dismiss. [UPDATED 2026-09-17, recon consolidation] Root cause now MEASURED (task 7630; full mechanism in mem0 a935f42b-cae4-4d5b-9e4f-29bdfd76de3b) — the earlier "CPU/IO contention" guess below is WRONG, not merely unverified. The actual bound is birpc's hardcoded 60s DEFAULT_TIMEOUT on the WORKER->HOST channel, which is unreachable via testTimeout or any vitest 3.2.4 config; the timed-out fetch is always gui/vitest.setup.ts, refetched once per test file because isolate-per-fork gives each file a cold module cache (173 fetches per run). The fix is no longer unowned: task 7630 (harden the RPC channel) and task 7642 (poolOptions.forks.isolate=false to cut the refetch ~40x) are both filed and in-flight.

bash 5.2 gotcha (verified on the reify host, task 5129): a real async `( ... ) &` fork() EAGAIN is UNCATCHABLE and fatal — bash prints `fork: retry: Resource temporarily unavailable` then exits 254, regardless of `set +e`, `|| rc=$?`, or fork-free control flow. You cannot catch it in-process to degrade gracefully. Consequence for tests/infra/run_all.sh Phase-1 pool: the fork-storm abort (esc-3848/esc-5029) is only fixable by PREVENTION (a `wait -n` worker-shell throttle capping live shells to W=N=_H2_POOL_N), not by catching the failure; the "degrade one member, don't abort" contract must be tested via a deterministic fault-injection seam (REIFY_RUN_ALL_POOL_FORK_FAIL_MEMBER) because reproducing real EAGAIN needs per-uid process-limit exhaustion that also kills the test harness.

content: vitest 3.2.4 attributes only SOME unhandled errors to a test file. Worker-side unhandled rejections go through execute.*.js listenForErrors/catchError, which sets error.VITEST_TEST_PATH (and VITEST_TEST_NAME); they print with an "Unhandled Rejection" banner and "This error originated in <file>". Pool-level failures print with an "Unhandled Error" banner and lose the file. In createForksPool's runFiles (dist/chunks/coverage.DL5VHqXY.js), `paths` is in scope when pool.run rejects, but the error is rethrown bare and then aggregated into an AggregateError. So a reporter can attribute the rejections via VITEST_TEST_PATH today, but attributing the pool-level ones needs a vitest patch. Separately, timeouts cascade under starvation: a timed-out onUnhandledError is itself reported through another onUnhandledError, which also times out. Task 7270's 2026-10-15 run had 84 such nested errors (28 reported unhandled errors).

e306a7fe-5b15-4196-b090-2e2cc34c0431.content: Reify GUI testing (vitest jsdom, @solidjs/testing-library): jsdom does not implement Element.prototype.scrollIntoView — any code that calls it from a reactive effect must guard with optional chaining (el?.scrollIntoView?.()) or it throws across the whole suite; tests stub it via `Element.prototype.scrollIntoView = vi.fn()`. CSS-module class names are hashed and computed styles are unavailable, so assert on data-testid/data-* attributes (e.g. data-selected) or Three.js mock objects, never computed CSS. No global vitest setup file exists (gui/vitest.config.ts has no setupFiles).

fused-memory MCP gotcha seen 2026-09-27. The session's MCP client can drop (ECONNREFUSED) around fused-memory server restarts and not reconnect for a while, even though the server is back on :8002. Right after a restart, submit_task and resolve_ticket can time out while the curator works through a backlog, yet the ticket may still be created: task 408 was created despite a submit_task timeout. Check list_tickets(project_root, since=...) or tasks.db before resubmitting; never blind-retry. A fallback that works: a small urllib streamable-HTTP JSON-RPC client POSTing initialize, then notifications/initialized, then tools/call to http://127.0.0.1:8002/mcp with Accept: application/json, text/event-stream and the Mcp-Session-Id header. It still routes task ops through the MCP server.

Merge throughput observation (solar_challenge_platform, 2026-10-06 ~11:00Z): 12 tasks were parked in the orchestrator's merge phase (oldest 765 since 2026-10-04, 821 since 2026-10-05) behind a single local verify host, with roughly one landing every 1-2 hours; tasks in merge phase do not appear in get_merge_queue until submitted. Find them with runs.db: latest phase_enter phase='merge' with no later phase_exit per task. A manual merge_request from an /unblock session entered the queue directly at position 2 and landed in ~20 minutes (task 585), i.e. it did not wait behind the merge-phase backlog. Gotcha: if the fused-memory MCP server restarts mid-session (ECONNREFUSED), this session's mcp__fused-memory__* tools do not come back, even though ToolSearch finds nothing and port 8002 listens again within seconds. Workaround: drive it over raw streamable HTTP. Replies arrive as SSE 'data:' lines. Also check list_tickets after a timed-out submit_task: one timed-out call had in fact persisted and created its task (353), and a ticket filed just before the restart came back failed/server_restart and had to be re-filed.

Operational quirk of the solar_challenge_platform escalation MCP merge queue (port 8107): merge_request PREPENDS the git branch_prefix "task/" to the branch argument. Passing branch="task/129" fails with status "unknown_branch" / reason "branch 'task/task/129' not found". Pass the BARE task id — branch="129" — which resolves to task/129. (The /unblock skill's documented example branch="task/<TASK_ID>" is wrong for this server.)

Procedure for landing a small manual change directly on main while the dark-factory orchestrator is LIVE and actively merging (learned during /unblock of task 2, 2026-06-23): the repo has NO git remote, so the merge worker advances the LOCAL refs/heads/main and the primary working tree (/home/leo/src/solar-challenge-platform) is kept in sync by the orchestrator — meaning a direct `git commit` to the primary tree can race the worker's CAS ref-advance / working-tree sync and is hazardous. Safe sequence used: mcp__escalation__halt_merge_queue(reason=...) → make edits → verify locally → `git commit -o <explicit files>` → mcp__escalation__unhalt_merge_queue(reason=...). Caveat: halt_merge_queue KILLS and re-queues the in-flight post-merge verify (cost: one task re-verifies), so it's a real but bounded cost — acceptable for a tiny isolated change. get_merge_halt_status should show owner_esc_id=null so unhalt is clean. Commit only your own files explicitly (pathspec), not `git add -A`, because the primary working tree can carry unrelated drift from other processes.

Observation, 2026-10-08: an orchestrator dry-run proposal (risk medium) and the L2 escalation for SCP task 599 both read two get_merge_queue rows (mr-ad70eecc, mr-fea72d42, state queued, waiter_alive=true, head_of_line=599) as live duplicate requests to cancel. They were DF task 3860 ghosts. merge_cancel returned "Request already finalized; cannot cancel." (state blocked), and runs.db had merge_finalized state=blocked for them. A fresh merge_request got a new request_id and landed without being coalesced onto them. SCP task 762's mr-15f8811a, queued about 9.4h, was likewise a ghost (merge_finalized blocked at 2026-10-08T01:39:58Z), even though merge_status still answered queued with a position. Check runs.db merge_finalized before treating a queued row as live; recurrence 9 is recorded on DF 3860.

Merge-queue ghost mechanics, verified from dark-factory code on 2026-10-02. When suffix_graph.py::SuffixConflictTracker.bounce_conflicting_suffix_items bounces a request (real-conflict or cap-exceeded arm), it removes the request from _lane_buffers and resolves req.result to 'blocked', but it never calls SpeculativeMergeWorker._retire_item. The request therefore stays non-terminal in the ItemLifecycle registry, and snapshot()'s registry-sourced section keeps rendering it as 'queued', waiter_alive=true, head_of_line, until an orchestrator restart. merge_status(request_id) also answers 'queued' (live tier wins). merge_cancel answers "Request already finalized; cannot cancel." because it only consults the escalation server's _waiters map, which only MCP merge_request submissions populate; workflow-path requests are never there. KEY SAFETY FACT: InFlightMergeRegistry.acquire registers a done-callback on the request future, so the branch slot auto-releases the moment the bounce resolves it. A later workflow or MCP resubmission for the same branch therefore gets a fresh request_id and does NOT attach/coalesce onto the ghost. The display artifact is harmless to throughput; other landings proceed past it. This is tracked by dark_factory task 3860 (recurrence 7 = SCP task 696 / mr-7e9fa668).

A ghost "queued" merge-queue entry does NOT by itself mean the task is stuck. On 2026-10-02 the escalation-watcher read the ghost mr-7e9fa668 as wedging task 696 and spawned /unblock. In fact the task's orchestrator workflow was still live and landed the task on its own (797071d) while the unblock session was presenting options. Check these signs of a live workflow before taking over: (a) task heartbeat_at is fresh and claimant_run_id names the running orchestrator pid; (b) metadata.merge_phase_liveness / merge_retry_pending are set; (c) the orchestrator journal shows "steward resolved blocking escalation, caller will retry merge in-place" / "retrying merge (attempt N/3)" / "main moved during pre-merge rebase, retrying". If all hold, the workflow owns the slot and will resubmit with a fresh request id. Taking over via release_workflow then only throws away its place in line. Under memory pressure (PSI dispatch-admission gate, about 21 in flight) the in-workflow pre-merge verify waited about 11h and then 7h for admission, with no visible process, which looks like a hang but is not.

Why SCP tasks sit for hours in workflow phase "merge" without a merge_queued event (measured 2026-10-10 to 10-12). Before submitting a merge, the workflow rebases and re-runs the full test suite, and that run needs the single per-project task verify slot (dark-factory shared/verify_admission.py acquire_task_slot; verify_admission_task_slots defaults to 1 and SCP does not override it). Every ordinary task verify contends for the same slot, and waiters poll every 0.1 s, so admission is neither first-come nor priority-ordered. With about 15 waiters and a suite of roughly 23-25 minutes under host load 107-125, the mean wait was about 6 hours with a long tail (one task waited 35 hours, then 13.5 hours more after a redeploy reset it). Tasks with no Python tests to run skip the slot and queue in about a second. Such a task is alive, not stuck: its tasks.db heartbeat is fresh and the orchestrator holds .worktrees/<id>.lock. Do not hand-submit a merge for it, because that races the live workflow's own submit. Leo ruled no platform-side action (fixes are queued in dark-factory).

Escalation MCP resolve_issue mechanics observed 2026-07-04: action='resume' on a BLOCKED task flips it blocked→pending and the running scheduler re-dispatches it (observed pending→in-progress within seconds) — this is the standard "hand back to orchestrator to finish remaining plan steps" move; it preserves the existing task branch commits because the re-dispatched steward re-reads plan.json + the worktree and continues at the first pending step. action='close_only' dismisses an escalation with NO task-status effect — correct for closing stale L2 cluster/wrapper records (used on esc-150-3 and esc-150-5) without disturbing the underlying tasks. Resolution text only injects into the agent briefing on the L0 path, but plan.json is the durable source of truth the steward reads regardless of level. resolution_turns = count of user messages since the /unblock invocation.

TOOL FACTS (escalation MCP, learned 2026-09-27): mcp__escalation__resolve_issue rejects free-text resolution_class values; the only accepted values are 'actionable', 'benign', 'moot-terminal-subject', 'stale-strand' (a "risk accepted" ruling is resolution_class='benign'). Resolving an L2 cluster record cascades to its member L1 records (the member's resolved_by becomes "l2-cascade:<l2-id>"), but resolving the member explicitly with action='close_only' first is harmless. action='resume' on a BLOCKED (not in-progress) task whose code is complete flips it back to in-progress on its merge path (task 204 went blocked → in-progress within seconds); action='restart' resets a task with no commits to pending so the scheduler re-dispatches it once new dependencies are satisfied — wire add_dependency BEFORE resolving with restart so the re-dispatch cannot race the new prerequisite. mcp__fused-memory__commit_planning on a single extra task filed after the batch reports manifest_stamping missing_labels for its label unless the sidecar YAML already carries an entry for it (add the entry by hand, then the label matches).

If the fused-memory MCP client drops mid-session (ECONNREFUSED; ToolSearch then finds no mcp__fused-memory__* tools) but the service is back on 127.0.0.1:8002 (`systemctl --user status fused-memory`), you can call its tools directly. POST JSON-RPC to http://127.0.0.1:8002/mcp with headers Content-Type: application/json and Accept: application/json, text/event-stream, body {jsonrpc:'2.0', id:N, method:'tools/call', params:{name:'submit_task', arguments:{...}}}. The server runs in stateless JSON mode, so no session id or initialize handshake is needed. It worked for submit_task, search_tasks and add_memory on 2026-09-24.

content: To use ANOTHER project's orchestrator merge queue from a session whose escalation MCP points elsewhere (e.g. the solar_challenge_platform session is wired to port 8107), call that project's escalation server directly as streamable-HTTP MCP. Sequence: POST initialize to http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp with headers 'Accept: application/json, text/event-stream' and 'Content-Type: application/json'; read the Mcp-Session-Id response header; POST notifications/initialized; then POST tools/call with that session header. Responses may arrive as SSE, so parse the last 'data:' line. Use an HTTP timeout of at least 150 s when calling merge_request with wait_secs=100. dark-factory's escalation MCP is on port 8102 (solar_challenge on 8106). This worked on 2026-10-13 for merge_request, merge_status and get_merge_queue, using a ~40-line stdlib urllib client.

0f8367ea-ae1b-45de-9c2d-f01bed840b34.content: Rationale behind Leo's 2026-10-11 rulings on SCP merge throughput and the starvation clock. Merge waits: a workflow's pre-merge rebase and full-suite re-verify needs the one per-project task verify slot, which every ordinary verify also contends for by polling, so admission is neither FIFO nor priority-ordered; mean wait was about 6 hours with a long tail (task 600 waited 35h before a redeploy reset it, then landed 13.5h later). Leo declined a platform-side change because dark-factory already has fairness and verify-throughput improvements queued; a second slot would only help new waiters and would compete with the merge-gate verify for CPU. Starvation clock: the watchdog's idle clock is anchored to orchestrator start, so a mass fire lands 3 days after a restart; with redeploys back to roughly daily the window keeps moving, so the risk is accepted until dark-factory fixes the clock properly. A watcher seeing long merge-phase waits or a 3-day-uptime orchestrator on SCP should treat both as known and ruled, and raise them again only if the premise changes (redeploys stop, or the dark-factory fixes land and waits persist).

candidates.content: How a machine-filed task is actually deduplicated in dark-factory's fused-memory (read from code 2026-09-18) — it is NOT "identical title". Three mechanisms sit on the `submit_task` (planning_mode omitted) path: (i) a store-level UNIQUE index `ux_tasks_candidate_key ON tasks(tag, candidate_key) WHERE candidate_key IS NOT NULL AND status != 'cancelled'`, where `fused_memory/middleware/candidate_key.py::compute_candidate_key(title, files)` hashes the normalised title AND the sorted files_to_modify; a collision raises a typed DuplicateCandidateKeyError. Consequences: changing the file list changes the key, and because only `cancelled` is excluded, a finding closed as `done` can never be re-filed with the same title+files even if the condition persists. (ii) `task_curator.py::TaskCurator._pre_llm_exact_match` consults the same key only through an in-process `_recent_creates` cache with a 600-second TTL, so a nightly filer never hits it. (iii) the LLM curator itself, best-effort (any failure degrades to `create`), whose candidate pools exclude only `cancelled` and whose `_STATUS_RANK` ranks `done` — so a `drop` can legally target a DONE task; only `combine` is restricted to pending. A sweep that files "owner task N is dead" findings can therefore have the finding dropped onto the very done task N it reports, leaving no task and a silent violation. Design consequence adopted for the INV-12 owner-liveness sweep: a periodic filer must carry its OWN idempotence key in task metadata (Tier-C `x_` key, accepted by `shared/src/shared/task_metadata.py`) and look it up read-only before filing, treating the curator as a backstop only. Also: `submit_task` returns a ticket (`tkt_…`), not a task id, unless planning_mode=True; no agent role in `orchestrator/src/orchestrator/agents/roles.py` holds `resolve_ticket` (architect, implementer, steward and deep reviewer hold `submit_task`; debugger, judge, merger, simple-task hold neither), so an agent can never learn the id of a follow-up it files. Tickets persist indefinitely (`ticket_store.py` has no delete path; expires_at is a 365-day placeholder), but a ticket can resolve `failed` with no task_id — `flush_pending_on_startup` fails every pending ticket with reason `server_restart` on each fused-memory restart.

Root cause of the offline-deep lane's repeated fix-task refiles (measured 2026-10-11, dark-factory): the lane's own dedup memory has never been written in production. orchestrator harness.py::_OfflineLaneTaskClient.submit_fix_task reads a task id with Harness._extract_task_id, which returns None for every production response shape of fused-memory submit_task (the ticket shape {'ticket': 'tkt_...'}, the planning-mode create shape and the planning-mode collision shape), so it returns an empty string and offline_lane.py::_file_new_fix_task returns before recording the fingerprint. In the orchestrator journal 2026-09-19 to 2026-10-11, 59 of 59 confirmed lane reds logged 'submit_fix_task returned no task id' and the success line 'filed INFO escalation' appeared 0 times; no offline_lane_*.json guard file exists. Consequently open_fix_tasks, the red-advance counter, the L0 info escalation and the staged L2 blocker were dead code. Swapping in chronic_flake.py::extract_task_id would not fix it: that returns the ticket id as if it were a task id. Task 6050 and task 5423 each own a copy of this defect.

Run search_tasks BEFORE submit_task, even when you believe you already know the filing state — and treat a memory's BODY as capable of lagging its own index line. Burned 2026-08-12: a task was filed for the five silently-no-opping MCP POST sites while task 4023 already existed for exactly that defect (high priority, operator-ruled critical, filed the previous day with per-site line numbers and delivered_checks). The stored memory's index hook had been updated to say "FILED -> 4023", but the memory FILE's body still read "No task filed as of 08-11 -- needs operator decision", and the body is what got read. The duplicate ticket was caught only because resolve_ticket timed out (the curator was paused on HTTP 403) and the pending-ticket check surfaced it before any task was created; it was then cancelled via cancel_ticket rather than allowed to reach the curator, since a curator COMBINE can rewrite the surviving task's text. Two rules: (1) submit_task is cheap to precede with a search_tasks pass at score_threshold ~0.5 on the defect's distinctive symbol, and (2) when a memory records a filing decision, the actionable state belongs where a reader will hit it first, or the two halves drift. The salvage move when a duplicate is caught: cancel the ticket and instead AMEND the surviving task with whatever the second investigation learned that the first lacked.

FACTS/quirks discovered while filing tasks via fused-memory (2026-07-13): (1) submit_task metadata.files rejects extensionless file paths as "directory declarations" (LockCharterViolation) — hooks/project-checks was refused; use files=[] to defer scope to the architect for extensionless scripts (extension matching is case-sensitive lowercase). (2) The curator's dedup is genuinely good when descriptions carry precise context: it combined our claimant-dispatch-gate candidate into existing task 2408 with correct reasoning (complementary halves of one feature, same module locks), and dropped our /unblock-guardrail candidate because in-progress task 2509 already targets the same incident — write rich descriptions and let it route. (3) resolve_ticket can time out (~115s MCP cap) while the curator still creates the task — retrying resolve_ticket on the same ticket returns the terminal result (created id 2555 recovered this way); don't re-submit on timeout. (4) search_tasks is permanently blind to planning_mode-created tasks (curator corpus never indexes them at submit or commit_planning — verified in task_interceptor.py:2029 + tools.py:3287) — this is the root cause behind the "verify a batch with get_task, not search" rule; fix filed as task 2562.

TRAP discovered 2026-08-27: pre-task-3446 (which landed done 2026-08-03) the curator's _execute_combine used metadata_mode='replace' and overwrote the combine TARGET's whole metadata blob, wiping its metadata.files — which then made that task eligible for the LLM module tagger, since the tagger only touches tasks whose files is falsy. Consequence for any tagger-debris repair: a stamped task whose created-ticket declared a NON-EMPTY files list is a WIPE VICTIM, not a deliberate-empty filing. Restoring [] there DESTROYS real author scope; the correct repair is to reinstate the ticket's declared list from data/reconciliation/tickets.db candidate_json. 6 dark-factory tasks (2979, 3071, 3093, 3174, 3354, 3419) and 4 reify tasks (5207, 5598, 5682, 5948) were identified in this class and excluded from the 2026-08-27 restore. A further 11 tasks were left UNDETERMINED because a curator combine interacted with the stamp in a way that made the original filing state unrecoverable: dark_factory 3157, 3321, 3158, 3358, 3821, 3853, 4002 and reify 5470, 6446, 6509, 6432.

SESSION SUMMARY 2026-08-20 (claude-interactive, dark_factory) — merge-lane accessibility audit and two filed tasks.

QUESTION ASKED: can the high-priority merge lane be reached through the fused-memory MCP interface?

ANSWER ESTABLISHED (main @ 5bd7fd8489): no merge tool exists on fused-memory at all — the whole merge surface is on the escalation MCP. `metadata.merge_lane`, writable via fused-memory `submit_task`/`update_task`, is the only lane lever in existence, but it is read at exactly one site (workflow.py:10306) and is ignored by `merge_request`, so every MCP-submitted merge silently lands in the normal lane. Traced the full picture: six MergeRequest construction sites and only one sets `lane=`; dispatch-time task snapshot (workflow.py:1201) means the key must be set before dispatch; `append=True` would silently fail to change it (additive mode keeps OLD on scalar collision); `_normalize_lane` silently downgrades typos; `get_merge_queue`'s snapshot is the only lane observability; the restart-restore journal path handles lane correctly.

FILED (both pending):
- 4531 (medium) — add an explicit lane parameter to `merge_request` and fall back to `metadata.merge_lane`. Framed as an under-delivery of task 1689, whose own design named `escalation merge_request` and a "manual operator bump" and shipped neither. Two further defects in fused-memory's reconciliation flag-dedup subsystem, measured 2026-08-24 on main 1cc7c3f3c6. (A) LEXICON GAP — filter_already_tracked_systemic_patterns is the ONE cross-project fix-task check that needs no citation pointer (it queries every known project's non-cancelled tasks), but its candidate gate is a fixed 5-phrase lexicon _NEVER_TRACKED_PHRASES = {'no tracked task', 'was never converted to a task', 'never converted to a tracked task', 'never filed as a task', 'never tracked'}. Tracked as task 4711. (B) TITLE-CONTRACT CONTRADICTION — ReconReportState.cite_task (server/recon_report.py:2020-2030) documents "first-cited title wins ... Titles are cosmetic display text" and never refreshes a stored title, while _cited_task_corroborated (flag_dedup.py:2846-2856) makes normalised title EQUALITY load-bearing identity. So renaming a fix task permanently and silently blinds the cross-project suppression gate, signalled only by an INFO-level near-miss line (reconciliation.cross_project_fix_task_present_but_uncorroborated, flag_dedup.py:3099). Two more live routes to the same failure: recon_report.py:2133-2135 writes title='' when get_task returns no title, and _sanitize_cited_tasks truncates titles at 200 chars (flag_dedup.py:740-748), both producing permanently un-corroboratable citations. Tracked as task 4713.

FACTS about the fused-memory task tooling, learned 2026-07-27 while filing DF 3081/3082.

1. THE CURATOR COMBINES CONCURRENT NEAR-DUPLICATE TICKETS AND REWRITES RATHER THAN DROPS. Two agents independently filed the same merge_queue stranding defect ~2 minutes apart (tkt_0RRRB06C… at 07:48 from an /unblock triage, tkt_0RRRB1TE… at 07:50 from a /deb root-cause). The curator resolved the second as status='combined' onto task_id 3082 and REWROTE 3082 to fold in the candidate's more precise root cause, explicitly reasoning that "rewriting rather than dropping preserves the more precise root-cause detail the candidate contributes; rewriting rather than creating avoids a duplicate architect cycle on the same defect." The merged result was materially better than either input. PRACTICAL UPSHOT: do not pre-emptively suppress a filing because another agent might be working the same defect — file it with your distinct evidence and let the curator merge. But DO check `list_tickets` afterwards to see whether yours was combined, and verify the rewrite kept your evidence.

2. `update_task(append=True, details=...)` APPENDS TO `details` WITHOUT TOUCHING `description`. This is the safe way to add field corroboration to a long, well-formed task: it avoids retyping (and risking mangling) a multi-thousand-character description. Verified: after the append, `description` was byte-unchanged and `candidate_key` stayed b691b7821100d5b1 — so it does NOT trip the candidate_key recomputation that a description rewrite causes. `append` is documented as "the only knob that governs details/prompt append".

3. `add_dependency` takes `depends_on` (snake_case), not `dependsOn` — the camelCase form fails pydantic validation.

4. `get_statuses` requires `ids` as a real JSON LIST, not a comma-separated string.

5. `resolve_ticket` can time out at the MCP layer while the curator STILL creates the task. Two consecutive timeouts on tkt_0RRRB06C… masked a successful creation (task 3082). Do not re-submit on timeout — poll `list_tickets` instead and read the ticket's status/task_id.

CURATOR SEMANTIC DEDUP WAS DEAD FOR THREE DAYS (2026-08-15 to 08-17) AND LEFT NO TRACE. Discovered 2026-08-24 while investigating why tasks 4236 and 4240 were both filed for the same follow-up. Filed as task 4718 (high).

THE SIGNATURE, from data/reconciliation/tickets.db (combines detected via reason/result_json LIKE '%combine%'):

174 tickets over three days, ZERO combines, 3.0-4.7s mean resolve. A resolve that fast cannot have made a Claude CLI subprocess call — the curator was short-circuiting straight to `create` via one of the paths at fused-memory/src/fused_memory/middleware/task_curator.py:1339-1449 (`zero-output-breaker-open` / `llm-failed` / `corpus-failed`). 2026-08-11 shows the identical signature (27 created, 0 combined, 4.6s). USE THE PAIR (combine rate, mean resolve latency) AS THE HEALTH GAUGE. Zero combines alone is ambiguous on a low-volume day; zero combines AT 3-5s resolve is diagnostic, because the latency floor is set by the subprocess the curator must spawn to dedup at all. A healthy same-day control was observed live: a ticket submitted on 2026-08-24 took over 115 seconds to resolve (it exceeded resolve_ticket's default timeout and needed a retry), which is exactly what a working LLM dedup call costs.

dark_factory task-filing norm (used 2026-06-15): to file a single, precisely-scoped standalone task without risking the curator COMBINING it into a semantically-adjacent existing task, use submit_task(planning_mode=True) (synchronous, curator-bypassing, lands deferred, returns task_id directly) then flip it to pending with set_task_status — after doing your own dedup via search_tasks first. This is the same mechanism PRD-decomposition uses, applied to a one-off. Example: task 1756 (in-flight slot release bug) was filed this way to keep it from being merged into adjacent task 1749.

W11-δ (task 2257) makes warm-lane crash recovery record-driven: harness._recover_crashed_tasks reads .lane-state/<lane>.json via git_ops._lane_lifecycle.read(), verifies git reality (_is_registered_worktree + lane_branch_checkouts vs record.branch), and ADOPTS only on an exact match (registered + branch match + task non-terminal), else QUARANTINES. The historical bugs 2097 (orphaned admin entry), 2098 (stale plan.json re-pin), and 2062 (detached-HEAD stale-branch collision) all collapse to ONE divergence cell → QUARANTINE. A lane with NO durable record (pre-W11 seed) is recovered-but-not-pinned (left FREE), never silently re-pinned (PRD decision 5, invariant I3).

MEASURED 2026-09-21 and it invalidates every frequency figure ever quoted for task-lane xdist worker crashes: the system is BLIND to that class on every channel, so no archive- or ledger-derived rate for the task lane can be correct — neither "~7 occurrences" nor "zero".

THE THREE BLIND CHANNELS (verified by a 7-seat /team investigation of esc-5580-4):
1. reclassified-as-infra — the raise precedes _persist_attempt_logs / _archive_attempt_log, so nothing is written.
2. left as test_failure — CATEGORY_POLICY sets archive=False for TEST_FAILURE.
3. the flake ledger — all 368 rows carry call_site='merge_gate'; there are ZERO task-lane rows, because the task lane has no isolated-rerun call site registered at all (that is task 5089, which was sitting DEFERRED and was un-deferred on 2026-09-21).

CENSUS: 0 of 212 archived task-lane test logs carry a crash literal, against 12 of 219 merge-lane logs. That asymmetry is the mechanical explanation for why this class has recurred in six different apparent shapes across tasks 2365, 2619, 3000, 4066, 5333 and 5580 — each fix addressed the shape that happened to be visible.

CONSEQUENCE FOR COST ARGUMENTS: a "merge lane is hit 3.2x harder" style ratio computed from these archives is INVALID — it divides a complete count by a floor. The honest gap is <=1.4x with direction unknown. Corrected task-lane figures: >=0.50 occurrences/day, unit 2839s / $2.81 mean, ~$513/yr, 144 slot-hours, 3.76 delayed merges = 0.070% of throughput.

ALSO SETTLED: verify.py::_is_bare_xdist_worker_crash's docstring points at _main_probe_failure_is_isolated_flake (task 3597) as "the downstream confirm gate that catches it instead". For this shape it does NOT — that gate fires only when the MAIN PROBE is also red with a matching signature, so against a green main the caller returns early; and when it does fire it returns "not inherited", which sends the task TO the debugger. It guards against falsely blaming main; it was never a debugger suppressor.

content: How lane-filed fix tasks were actually deduplicated in dark-factory before the 2026-10-12 PRD: only by fused-memory, in two layers. The task curator (an LLM decision, median 70 s) runs first; the partial UNIQUE index ux_tasks_candidate_key (WHERE status != 'cancelled') is a backstop. Both treat a cancelled task as covering nothing, so cancelling a lane fix task as a false premise re-arms the next identical filing; the curator's recorded reason for creating task 6782 was that the identical-title task 6501 and task 5756 were cancelled. The index is not a general backstop either: the candidate key is recomputed when the files tagger stamps metadata.files, so after dispatch a fresh title-only submission no longer collides (16 of 24 lane tasks across three projects had a shifted key). Over 120 lane tickets in three projects: 24 created, 66 curator drops, 26 index collisions, 4 curator combines.

reify docs/architecture-audit/findings/*.md are DATED snapshots (each carries `**Auditor:**` + `**Date:**`) and are annotated by appending a `> **CORRECTION <date> (<cite>) — <verdict>.**` blockquote, never by rewriting an Evidence bullet, State line, or Top-concerns bullet. Two traps found while doing this on composite-laminated-shells.md (task 6987): (1) SCOPE CREEP IN PRESENT TENSE — an overlay written to record ONE delta will happily restate the snapshot's other claims as still-current ("No `Orthotropic`/`Laminate`/`Ply` symbol exists today", "M-001 stays FICTION"), and those restatements are new present-tense assertions that must each be re-grepped. Here they were false: `OrthotropicMaterial`/`TransverseIsotropicMaterial` had shipped in crates/reify-compiler/stdlib/constitutive.ri two weeks AFTER the audit date. Fix pattern: verify every present-tense sentence, keep each delta in its OWN separately-cited blockquote (different commits/dates must not be conflated), and add an explicit "NON-EXHAUSTIVE — this overlay re-verified M-00x and M-00y ONLY" clause naming the rows you did not measure. (2) READER NEVER SCROLLS — a per-mechanism overlay does not protect the Top-concerns summary at the top of the file; add a short dated pointer under the header block (after `**Gap count:**`, before `## Top concerns`) when a summary bullet is partly superseded. Also: word-bound your absence greps — `hashin` matches "hashing" and `X_T`/`X_C` match `READY_TIMEOUT`/`FIX_CHUNK`, so a naive grep both over- and under-reports. candidates.content: /prd decompose mechanics that worked this session (my_solar_challenge / fused-memory): file each subtask via submit_task with planning_mode=true (lands directly as `deferred`, returns {task_id} synchronously — no resolve_ticket needed, curator bypassed so siblings aren't recombined). Then wire deps via add_dependency(id, depends_on) while still deferred. Then flip the whole batch deferred→pending in ONE bulk set_task_status(id="35,36,37,38,39", status="pending") call (comma-separated ids supported). Cancel a superseded placeholder via set_task_status(id, "cancelled"). Task ids are global and sequential — P1 got #35-#39 (the prior P2-P5 batch ran #16-#34). PRD files must be committed to main BEFORE/at decompose time because task agents run in worktrees branched from main. get_tasks output is large (~87k chars, exceeds tool limit) — query it with jq on the saved tool-results file instead.

PRD sidecar authoring tip (from authoring solar_challenge's errors-leaf PRD, 2026-10-14). Validate a capability-manifest YAML sidecar before decompose by running dark-factory's own code from /home/leo/src/dark-factory/.venv/bin/python:

candidates.content: solar_challenge_platform GOTCHA for task 526 (clock_skew) and task 1013 (β): since task 1067 (S19·α), ops/contract.py has no LIVENESS_FRESH_MAX_S / LIVENESS_AGING_MAX_S. The liveness window is Settings.liveness_stale_after_seconds, passed in by api/routers/ops.py::_read_liveness. The signatures are classify_liveness(age_s, bands: LivenessBands) and read_fleet_liveness(session, last_seen, *, now, bands), neither with a default. Build bands with liveness_bands(stale_after_s): fresh_max_s is stale_after_s / LIVENESS_FRESH_DIVISOR (3), and anything not > 0, NaN included, raises ValueError. The tests build default bands with a module helper, `_default_bands()`, in tests/ops/test_classification.py and tests/ops/test_reads.py, and pin the default-window boundaries as literal 30/90 values. Per PRD D8, task 526 maps a negative age to clock_skew inside classify_liveness(age_s, bands), before the band tests.

solar_challenge_platform (task 1099 amendment, 2026-10-15) CORRECTS two earlier task 1099 gotchas about tests/test_private_names.py's instance rule. A call is a lookup only when it is made by getattr, hasattr, setattr, delattr or object (so monkeypatch.setattr/delattr and patch.object), not any call whose second positional argument is a private string; the _AWAITING_PUBLIC_READ keys are therefore spelled positionally, InstanceReach("tests/x.py", "_optimiser"), with no keyword arguments, and a constructor or pytest.param handed a private-named string looks nothing up. The rule also reads a string constant that mentions `solar_challenge_platform` as source, so `patch("solar_challenge_platform.x.Svc._method")` is a reach reported on the line the string starts, and a reader-table row must spell such a target with a stand-in package. hasattr(obj, "_x") and lookups inside f-string expressions still count; the real-tree reaches were identical before and after (13 groups, 30 sites).

Python compares and subtracts two aware datetimes that share a tzinfo on their wall clock, ignoring fold. On 2026-10-25 at 01:00Z London's clocks go back, so its wall clock reads 01:00-01:59 twice. Rows written in Europe/London (one ZoneInfo) across that change are therefore mis-ordered, and rollups._settle_flow subtracts them on the wall clock.
- Input: 121 pv_power rows, 1000 + 10*m W at minute m from 2026-10-25T00:00Z, each written with .astimezone(ZoneInfo('Europe/London')). Compared with the same instants written in UTC, settlement_hh at the UTC hh_starts 00:00Z, 00:30Z, 01:00Z and 01:30Z gave [equal, NOT equal, equal, equal]. DEBUGGER GOTCHA (measured task 4246, 2026-09-05): a verify red whose `cause_hint` IS the pytest PASS line means no test failed — the leg was killed by an external signal and misclassified. Read the cause_hint before reading any code.

THE SIGNATURE, exactly as it appears in .task/verify/attempt-N.<module>.summary.json:
  "category": "unknown_test_failure",
  "cause_hint": "18619 passed, 1 skipped, 246 warnings in 418.65s",
  "rc": 143, "timed_out": false
The log ends at the pytest summary with no traceback and no failing test id. rc=143 is 128+15, i.e. the SHELL reporting that its child was SIGTERM'd; the shell itself survived, which is why the status is POSITIVE.

WHY IT IS NOT CLASSIFIED AS A KILL. verify_classify.py::is_external_kill_rc is `rc < 0 and -rc in _EXTERNAL_KILL_SIGNALS`, and its docstring says a shell-reported 128+N status is DELIBERATELY not treated as a kill ("must not guess at shell conventions"). asyncio reports a NEGATIVE returncode only when our own direct `start_new_session=True` child is signalled. A SIGTERM landing on the pytest GRANDCHILD is reported by the shell wrapper as positive 143, the predicate rejects it, and it falls through to unknown_test_failure — which is is_infra_transient=False, so it gets NO infra retry and instead dispatches a DEBUGGER against a suite that fully passed. verify_categories.py already documents the mirror-image residual for positive 137/OOM; 143 is the same mechanism on a signal no branch can deliver to itself.

In dark_factory worktrees, .task/verify/attempt-N.<module>.summary.json (e.g. .task/verify/attempt-2.orchestrator.summary.json) records the exact verify-pipeline commands (test/lint/type) used for that task, including the precise `uv run --project <module> pytest|ruff check|pyright <files...>` invocations. Diagnostic facts for reading dark-factory merge-lane state, gathered 2026-09-06/09.

MERGE VERIFY TAKES ~50-56 MINUTES on this repo, measured from merge_verify duration_ms: task 4374 3078643 ms (~51 min), task 4360 3391920 ms (~57 min). So a merge sitting in 'verifying' for 25-45 minutes is normal, not hung — do not escalate on that alone. Verify proceeds module by module (cockpit, dashboard, escalation, fused-memory, orchestrator observed in that order).

A MERGE/TRAIN VERIFY WRITES NOTHING TO data/verify-logs/. Its junit lands in the merge worktree at .worktrees/_merge-<id>/.df-verify-junit/report.<module>.xml, and watching those file mtimes is the reliable way to see live progress and which module is running. data/verify-logs/<task>/ is populated by the TASK workflow verify, so the usual "check verify-logs" habit comes up empty for an in-flight merge and can be misread as "nothing is running".

data/orchestrator/merge_queue.json IS NOT THE LIVE QUEUE. It is the durable journal and holds a SUBSET: on 2026-09-06 it contained 2 records while the live snapshot enumerated 9 entries. Read get_merge_queue() for live state; merge_queue.json only tells you what would survive a restart.

TO CONFIRM A VERIFY IS GENUINELY LIVE rather than an orphaned survivor process, walk the pytest process's parent chain to the orchestrator PID (ps -o ppid=). A merge verify's chain is `uv run pytest` -> pytest -> the orchestrator process; a process reparented to init is a survivor from a dead run.

DISCOVERY (2026-08-24, measured in-process during esc-3868-5, and it ANSWERS the open question in task 4378): a pytest rc=5 "no tests collected" false RED on a task's verify does NOT block that task from merging, because the merge lane never emits the file-scoped command. Driving orchestrator.verify_plan.derive_verify_plan against the real loaded config with a diff of two test files under the tests/scripts module: role='task' -> [file_scoped] `uv run --project shared pytest <the two files>` (arm 4b of _derive_module_runs, rc=5); role='merge' -> [full_suite] `uv run --project shared pytest --tb=short -q --timeout=300 tests/scripts/` with reason "pytest: merge role, full breadth — registered-module full suite" (rc=0, 1212 collected). dark-factory-orchestrator.yaml:890 sets merge_verify_breadth: "full", so derive_verify_plan's merge_full branch routes to _derive_full_suite_runs, which never file-scopes and never consults which files the diff touched, and effective_merge_module_configs expands the set from the one touched prefix to all 9 registered modules. PRACTICAL CONSEQUENCE for anyone triaging this defect class: submitting the branch to the merge queue is sufficient and weakens no gate — it gives the branch MORE verification than the task-role gate would have, not less. Do not describe such an escalation as needing a "verify-gate override".

To count dark-factory bare xdist worker crashes on the task lane: grep -F 'bare pytest-xdist worker crash detected' (plus 'VerifyInfraError escaped run()' for the merge-phase escapes) across /var/log/syslog, syslog.1 and zcat syslog.N.gz. It takes about 2 min. `journalctl --user -u orchestrator-dark-factory.service -g ...` did not finish in 10 min, and the journal only reaches back to about 2026-09-27. The log line's own timestamp is local time (BST = UTC+1). That detection line has only existed since 2026-09-25 07:51Z. A crashed attempt is never archived to data/verify-logs, because run_verification raises VerifyInfraError before persisting logs, so counting verify logs or junit misses the class.   FIX=""; make_fixture FIX; plan_for staged <paths...>; echo "$PLAN_OUT"

EXTRACTING the two functions with `sed` (rather than retyping them) is the load-bearing part: make_fixture's copy list is long and drifts, and it runs assert_source_closure_copied, so a hand-rolled clone silently rots the moment verify.sh gains a new sourced lib. Note make_fixture also copies scripts/verify-pipeline-infra-tests.txt into the fixture, so manifest-row experiments work by appending to "$FIX/scripts/verify-pipeline-infra-tests.txt".

For rename/delete scenarios plan_for is not enough — it only stages NEW files. Seed and commit the file in the fixture first (`git -C "$FIX" -c commit.gpgsign=false commit`), then `git mv` / `git rm` and capture the plan, so the diff carries a real R/D entry.

Read the result from two places: the `# scope decision — RUN_RUST=… RUN_GUI=… RUN_OCCT_GATE=…` line, and plan_count_noncomment_lines "$PLAN_OUT" for the emitted command count (a docs-only stage legitimately yields 0 and `# (no commands — nothing to verify for this action/scope)`).

This is strictly better than reasoning from verify.sh's source or from a script header: hooks/project-checks' own header claims a docs-only stage "produces an empty plan and exits 0", which is true today but says nothing about which manifests can still inject a pole — the measured plan does.

Reproduced defects in reify scripts/verify.sh's bash executor (scout seat, bash 5.2.21, 2026-10-14). (a) A failing plan line exits 1 whatever the child's code: errexit is inherited into the reaper's backgrounded `eval "$_cmd" &` (lib_proc_reaper.sh::reaper_run_in_pgroup), so steps exiting 75 or 124 make verify exit 1. Only the semaphore-acquire failure path preserves its code. (b) For the same reason, the offline confirm wrapper `( cmd; _confirm_rc=$?; recorder; exit $_confirm_rc )` never runs its recorder on a red nextest pass. (c) The background sweep ledger records verdict pass / exit_code 0 for failed runs whenever the node-lane plan step has replaced the EXIT trap: the trap's leading `if kill …; then :; fi` resets $? before _verify_cleanup reads it. (d) The `# narrowing —` print-plan header spans several physical lines because the affected-crate lists are newline-separated.
