Measured properties of `scripts/verify.sh --print-plan` as a cheap in-process oracle (taken 2026-08-24 on task 6426, so other automation can reuse it instead of re-measuring). The canonical widest invocation `DF_VERIFY_ROLE=merge REIFY_NEXTEST_PROBE_RETRY_SLEEP=0 bash scripts/verify.sh all --scope all --profile both --include-infra --print-plan` costs 0.18-0.43s, exits 0, writes ZERO files (the nextest config is a `<print-plan-placeholder>` in print mode, not a real temp file), emits nothing on stderr, and works from a FOREIGN cwd because SCRIPT_DIR/REPO_ROOT are self-resolving. Two caveats. (1) The nextest probe runs UNCONDITIONALLY in print mode and is explicitly OUTSIDE the "hermetic oracle" guarantee — see verify.sh's own scope note at :1702-1714 — so worst case it forks cargo up to 4x and sleeps 2x the retry interval; any automation invoking --print-plan repeatedly must set REIFY_NEXTEST_PROBE_RETRY_SLEEP=0. (2) Bound it with `timeout`: a wedged build_plan otherwise blocks the caller indefinitely. GNU coreutils `timeout` (no --foreground) signals the whole PROCESS GROUP, so a `sleep` or other child spawned inside the timed-out verify.sh dies with it and leaves no orphan — verified against a deliberately blocking fixture, which matters in this repo given the orphaned-test-binary reaper. Separately measured: the set of *.sh gate paths that invocation resolves is byte-identical both to a source-text grep of verify.sh's add()/add_tool() statements and to the union over a 4-action x 3-scope x 4-role 48-invocation matrix, so one fork is the exact superset; each widening is load-bearing (plain `all --scope all --profile both` resolves only 6 of 12 gates, --include-infra reaches 11, role=merge adds tests/infra/run_all.sh).

reify tests/infra plan-oracle asserts: never hard-code the literal `cargo nextest run` when asserting on scripts/verify.sh --print-plan output. verify.sh emits the test pass from one of two branches — verify.sh:1659 (`cargo nextest run ${selector}${rel} ... --config-file`) and :1685 (`cargo test ${selector}${rel} -- --test-threads=N`) — which SHARE the `${selector}${rel}` fragment, so `--workspace`, `-p <crate>`, `--release` and the outer `timeout --kill-after=60 <n>m` wrapper are byte-identical across runners; only --config-file / -E / `-- --test-threads=N` differ. Use the ERE alternation `cargo (test|nextest run)` instead (works in plan_capture_lib.sh's plan_has/plan_lacks, whose plan_match is ERE, and in `grep -qE` — but a plain `grep -q` matches the group LITERALLY, so widen `-q` to `-qE` at the same time). Two failure modes on a nextest-less host (plan header `nextest=0`, reproducible via the harness in test_verify_nextest_absent_suites.sh): POSITIVE asserts go spuriously RED, and — easier to miss — NEGATIVE asserts (`plan_lacks 'cargo nextest run --workspace.*--exclude'`, `! grep -qE 'cargo nextest run ...'`) pass VACUOUSLY because their needle matches nothing, silently asserting nothing. Widening a negative grep is a strict strengthening (rejects a superset), so it never flips an ambient pass. The structurally vacuity-proof shape, used by test_occt_gated_scope.sh Tests 5-8, is: EXTRACT with the alternation into a var, `assert ... test -n "$VAR"`, THEN negative-grep the extract. Reserve an explicit `PLAN_HAS_NEXTEST` guard (test_occt_gated_scope.sh Test 9) for properties that are GENUINELY nextest-only, i.e. --config-file / -E, which cargo test has no equivalent for. Runner identity itself is pinned separately by the `nextest=N` plan header (test_verify_nextest_probe.sh), so widening these asserts loses no coverage. Verified in task 5604: widening 19 needles in test_verify_scope.sh and both halves of 2 compound asserts in test_verify_failfast_order.sh took them from 143/10 and 38/2 under the harness to 153/0 and 40/0, with ambient counts byte-identical.

You can test a reify verify.sh selective-infra plan leaf (`( for _vt in tests/infra/<glob>; do ... bash "$_vt" ...; done )`) BEHAVIOURALLY, not just by grepping --print-plan text. The method:
1. Build a branch fixture: copy scripts/ and .config/, create a git repo on main, and commit a one-line edit to scripts/verify.sh on a task branch.
2. Run `verify.sh test --scope branch --print-plan` with DF_VERIFY_ROLE=task and REIFY_INFRA_SUITE_ACTIVE unset. This emits the `tests/infra/test_verify_*.sh` leaf.
3. Write a probe member such as tests/infra/test_verify_zz_probe.sh into the fixture. The leaf's glob expands at execution time under CWD, so only the probe matches.
4. Run the captured line with `bash -c "$LEAF"` from the fixture dir.
The probe then observes the member's real spawn environment and exit-status propagation. Measured 2026-10-15 (task 8919): it ran in about 3 seconds.

content: reify convention (task 9105): read verify.sh --print-plan header fields with tests/infra/plan_capture_lib.sh's `plan_header_field <dump> <plan|scope|narrowing|heavy> <NAME>`. It returns rc 0 when the field is present, even with an empty value, rc 1 when absent and rc 2 for an unknown kind, and it never depends on field order. Read step order with `plan_step_index <dump> <ERE> [<from>]`, which counts only non-comment lines after `# --- commands` and prints -1 when absent. "X after every Y" is `plan_step_index "$d" Y "$i_X"` == -1. Do not add new ordered `RUN_RUST=… RUN_GUI=…` substring greps: the adoption-ratchet row `ordered-scope-grep` caps them at 82 code lines (all in test_verify_scope.sh), and ξ #9113 lowers that cap to 0.

9e05621e-be1b-429f-83db-7af83c52f83b.content: Decoding hermetic nested-verify.sh failures in tests/infra/test_verify_semaphore_e2e.sh: verify.sh's executor propagates each plan command's exact rc (verify.sh:1553-1557), so nested exit codes map to a root cause. Rule: (1) exit 1 = the real-repo hermetic path — the nested verify's `./scripts/tree-sitter-generate.sh` post-check failed because the GITIGNORED outputs tree-sitter-reify/src/{parser.c,grammar.json,node-types.json,.grammar_hash.stamp} (.gitignore:48-51) were absent/0-byte (a fresh worktree has NONE until generated); (2) exit 127 = an EXECUTED plan-command SCRIPT FILE was absent — the _merge-verify "vanished-worktree race" (DF-side) or a sandbox copy-list drift, NOT a stub-not-found (apply_hermetic_env prepends the stubdir so cargo/npm/tree-sitter stubs are always found); (3) a missing SOURCED lib = exit 1 (verify.sh guards each source with [ -f ]||exit 1). tree-sitter-generate.sh's own failures are all exit 1 (its internal 127 from an undefined portable_timeout is caught by `|| GEN_EXIT=$?` → exit 1). The per-section make_stub_bin real tree-sitter pre-gen is the load-fragile step: interrupted regen trips _cleanup_partial_outputs (rm -f parser.c) and cascades every later section. Nested stderr sinks into runA*.err/$MERGE_ERR/$C_ERR/$F_ERR and was never dumped, which is why exact codes were historically undiagnosable — surface them on section failure.

solar_challenge gotcha (task 627 architect, measured 2026-10-10 on main 86eb58b, CPython 3.12.3, SQLite 3.45.1), extending memory e8755bed.
[PRE-TASK-627 HISTORY, annotated 2026-10-16: the failure-path paragraph and bullets below describe main 86eb58b and are NOT current. Task 627 merged at c5ef7787. On main, src/solar_challenge/web/jobs.py records each failed row in a transaction of its own under _best_effort_failure_record, which logs an ERROR from solar_challenge.web.jobs instead of raising, so a refused write leaves only its own table 'running'. The current behaviour is amendment e7298ef8. The trigger recipe below still refuses the failure-path write on main.]
JobManager._run_job's failure path runs its jobs UPDATE and then its runs UPDATE on the job's own connection as ONE transaction, committed only after both. So a database that refuses EITHER write leaves BOTH rows 'running'. A refused runs write, the second, skips that commit, so the jobs write before it is never committed either. In both cases:
- get_job_status reported 'failed' with the simulation's message;
- the jobs row kept the progress message 'Running home simulation...' and a NULL completed_at;
- a root log handler at DEBUG captured 0 records.
Reproduce with a simulate_home that raises plus `CREATE TRIGGER refuse_failed_<table> BEFORE UPDATE ON <table> WHEN NEW.status = 'failed' BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, '<message>'); END` on jobs or runs; the progress writes (status 'running') pass it.
Read from jobs.py at 86eb58b, not measured: _schedule's done callback ignores the Future. So an exception that escapes _run_job, e.g. from the sqlite3.connect that runs before its try, stays in the Future and is never logged, and get_job_status keeps reporting the job's last status.

So you cannot narrow a merge-role verify by passing fewer ModuleConfigs; call run_verification per ModuleConfig instead. (2) _aggregate_results flattens per-module junit failing_test_ids into one union, so VerifyResult carried no id->module attribution before task 5627. All five run_scoped_verification spawns in orchestrator/src/orchestrator/merge_queue.py run on the freshly-created merge worktree with is_merge_verify=True and pass role='merge'. DISCOVERY (2026-08-24, measured in-process during esc-3868-5, and it ANSWERS the open question in task 4378): a pytest rc=5 "no tests collected" false RED on a task's verify does NOT block that task from merging, because the merge lane never emits the file-scoped command. Driving orchestrator.verify_plan.derive_verify_plan against the real loaded config with a diff of two test files under the tests/scripts module: role='task' -> [file_scoped] `uv run --project shared pytest <the two files>` (arm 4b of _derive_module_runs, rc=5); role='merge' -> [full_suite] `uv run --project shared pytest --tb=short -q --timeout=300 tests/scripts/` with reason "pytest: merge role, full breadth — registered-module full suite" (rc=0, 1212 collected). dark-factory-orchestrator.yaml:890 sets merge_verify_breadth: "full", so derive_verify_plan's merge_full branch routes to _derive_full_suite_runs, which never file-scopes and never consults which files the diff touched, and effective_merge_module_configs expands the set from the one touched prefix to all 9 registered modules. PRACTICAL CONSEQUENCE for anyone triaging this defect class: submitting the branch to the merge queue is sufficient and weakens no gate — it gives the branch MORE verification than the task-role gate would have, not less. Do not describe such an escalation as needing a "verify-gate override".

The verify breadth semantics are easy to misread; an opus critic caught the lead's misreading on 2026-10-15.

Under merge_verify_breadth 'scoped' (the shipped default until task 7008), the merge-role verify keeps the legacy FILE_SCOPED/SKIPPED shape (verify_plan.py::_derive_module_runs):
- Pytest runs only the test files the merging diff touches, and a source-only diff runs NO pytest at merge (arm 5 is reachable only at role='merge').
- Lint is file-scoped. Pyright is file-scoped unless a structural file is touched.

The task-role VERIFY, run before rebase, is different: a touched source or structural file runs the owning module's FULL suite (the floor added by an earlier task, arm 3), and a test-only diff stays file-scoped.

Under 'full', merge-role verify runs every registered module's full suite on the merged tree. Merge junit archives also exist only under 'full'.

Independently of breadth, main_tip_sweep (default on, every 1800 s) runs the full suite on the main tip and escalates L1 on drift. It is not a merge gate.

As specified, the tree-tier key is merge tree OID + spec hash + toolchain fingerprint. It names neither DF_VERIFY_ROLE nor verify_cold_preprovision_command:
- the spec hash renders PlannedRun, whose env is the command's own parsed env (verify_plan.py::_verify_cmd_to_dict), not the role stamp verify.py::_resolve_verify_env injects;
- the preprovision is in no key.

A target whose test outcome depends on the role or the provisioned environment can therefore get a task-role green replayed as its merge verdict. Concrete case: solar_challenge_platform's frontend tests run only at merge role (its task 382). SCP has no module configs, so its task-role and merge-role test commands are identical, and a branch rebased onto main tip M has the same tree as its merge into M. dark-factory's own `uv sync --all-packages && npm ci` preprovision is the analogous exposure.

Remedy options recorded on 5652: (a) the role always in the key; (b) the role in the key only for targets declaring role-sensitive tests. (b) preserves cross-role reuse for role-independent suites.

candidates.content: Reify warm lanes: a lane reclaim can COMMIT a task's uncommitted working-tree WIP onto that task's branch as `chore: save WIP before warm-lane reclaim (task NNNN)` — where NNNN is the *reclaiming* task's id, NOT the branch's owning task. Observed 2026-08-11 on task/5429 (tip a13f164727 labelled "task 1933" but adding a throwaway `tmp_probe2` debug test to 5429's own test file). Consequence: a resumed task branch can carry throwaway debug/probe code at its tip that verify will happily pass (a test with `println!` and no assertions is neither a clippy nor a test failure) but review will flag as leftover debug code — the same finding class that already blocked 5429 once (esc-5429-1 issue 3). When resuming a task whose branch already has commits, always `git show` the tip and grep the branch diff for `println!|dbg!|_proto_|tmp_probe` before assuming the branch is merge-ready.

Warm-lane WIP recovery mechanism (reify): uncommitted WIP left in a warm-lane worktree (/home/leo/src/warm-lanes/worktrees/_lane-K) is NOT lost when a task's worktree appears "missing" — it persists in the lane until the next re-seed. But it is VOLATILE: per the D10 warm-lane contract, acquire_lane re-seeds via git reset --hard <branch-tip> + git clean -xfd -e target, which wipes any uncommitted changes. To make WIP survive a re-dispatch, COMMIT it onto the task branch (a WIP checkpoint commit) — then a lane re-seed resets to the new branch tip and the WIP is included. This is the concrete mechanism behind the /unblock "preserve WIP first" step. Find the lane holding a branch with: git worktree list | grep <branch>.

Warm-lane branch-reaping rarely loses code, despite field RCAs claiming it does. When release_warm_lane deletes a task branch mid-flight, the committed work survives as the lane's DETACHED-HEAD commit / dangling object and is recoverable (a steward recovered task 4760's work this way; 4760 ultimately landed on main at commit 44558ade01). Work becomes truly lost ONLY after the lane is re-acquired and re-seeded/reset (git checkout -f -B + git clean + seed-warm-lane --fresh-checkout), which moves HEAD and makes the dangling commit GC-eligible. So under heavy restart/churn the recovery WINDOW is short but real. Lesson: when an escalation-watcher claims "warm-lane work is lost and must be redone," verify first — check the lane's reflog / `git log <work-sha>` for the dangling commit and whether the deliverable already landed on main, before redoing anything.

A git branch that a reify warm lane once held survives independently of that lane — the lane can later be reclaimed and checked out on a completely different task's branch (observed 2026-09-03: lane _lane-9, which held task/6362's 5 commits as of 2026-08-30, was later found checked out on task/6596's branch instead), but the original branch ref (e.g. task/6362) remains fully intact in the shared .git regardless. So if a task's branch went stale behind a dispatch-path fault (warm-lane acquire, verify/merge lane), the work is recoverable purely from the branch ref (`git branch -a` / `git log <branch>`), even after the lane that produced it is long gone and reused.

A warm lane can hand an agent a DIRTY working tree carrying uncommitted WIP from an interrupted earlier run of the SAME task (observed 2026-08-01 in _lane-16/task 5921: examples_smoke.rs modified, mtime ~2 min after lane creation, zero commits on the branch and an empty .task/iterations.jsonl). Lane reseed does not always clear it. Run `git status --short` at plan/implement start; if a target file is modified with no matching commit, treat the diff as an untrusted earlier draft — read it for signal, then `git checkout --` it and rebuild from the base rather than committing it, since a killed run's partial edit can encode the very anti-pattern the task exists to fix.

reify warm-lane hazard class (discovered 2026-08-20 during /unblock 6128): a leftover `task/<id>` branch carrying commits beyond main is NOT fail-safe on reify's dispatch path. dark-factory has two different behaviours and only one of them refuses. `create_worktree` -> `_cleanup_leftover_branch` (orchestrator/src/orchestrator/git_ops.py:7948) raises RuntimeError rather than deleting a branch with commits beyond main. But reify dispatches via WARM LANES, and `acquire_warm_lane`'s gamma-reattach route (git_ops.py:6570) does the opposite: `_orphan_has_commits(full_branch)` True -> `git worktree add <lane> <branch>` WITHOUT -b -> `_reuse_warm_lane` (commit-WIP -> rebase_onto_main -> re-provision). The agent is then handed the leftover branch's content as an already-rebased, clean starting state. Consequence: for a task whose premise was RESCOPED or whose prior work was REJECTED by a ruling, the stale branch is a live landmine — a resumed agent can build the new scope on top of the rejected implementation and land both. Do not assume "the orchestrator will refuse to touch a branch with WIP"; that is only true on the create_worktree path. When rescoping/rejecting a task's prior approach, explicitly dispose of its branch.

Warm-lane reclaim does NOT lose a task branch's commits (verified 2026-07-27 by reading dark-factory orchestrator/src/orchestrator/git_ops.py). When a blocked/escalated reify task's lane has been reclaimed and reassigned to a different task, flipping that task back to `pending` for re-dispatch is SAFE — its `task/<id>` commits survive.

Mechanism: two γ reattach guards in `acquire_warm_lane`, both gated on `_orphan_has_commits(full_branch)` (a rev-parse existence gate plus `_branch_has_commits_beyond_main`, which fail-safe returns True on any git error):
- `CREATE_ONCE_REATTACH` → `git worktree add <lane> <branch>` (note: no `-b`)
- `RESET_IN_PLACE_REATTACH` → `git checkout -f <branch>` (no `-B`)
Both then route through `_reuse_warm_lane` (commit WIP → `rebase_preserving_task_commits` onto main → re-provision debug port). The destructive `_reset_warm_lane` (`git checkout -f -B <branch> <main_tip>`, which WOULD orphan the commits) is only reachable when the branch has NO commits beyond main. On the cold `create_worktree` path, `_cleanup_leftover_branch` likewise RAISES rather than deleting a branch carrying commits (raise-not-destroy, inv.10 fail-safe-retain), so the failure mode is a blocked task with an L1, never lost work.

Practical consequence for /unblock: do not leave a task `blocked` out of fear of branch loss, and do not hand-copy commits to a rescue branch.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY LOST on reclaim: the lane's untracked `.task/` directory — `plan.json`, `iterations.jsonl`, `reviews/`. The re-dispatched architect re-plans from scratch. Therefore any decision reached during an /unblock session MUST be written into the durable task record (description/details) or the PRD; a decision left only in `plan.json` will not survive the reclaim.

In reify warm lanes, a commit subject "chore: save WIP before warm-lane reclaim (task NNNN)" can carry a DIFFERENT task's complete, green implementation — the reclaim sweep stamps whichever task id it is running under, not the one that authored the diff. On task/6560, commit 849f01b8b907 was labelled "task 1933" but was in fact the full GREEN half of 6560's final TDD pair (renaming Engine::realize_solid_sdf to realize_solid_sdf_at and threading VoxelResolution). Always `git show` a WIP-labelled tip and judge it by its diff, not its subject, before assuming the branch is unfinished or that foreign work leaked in.

Warm-lane reclaim can commit a task's real work under the generic message "chore: save WIP before warm-lane reclaim (task NNNN)", where NNNN is a DIFFERENT task than the branch's own. MECHANISM: the WIP-save is attributed to the RECLAIMING task — the task that next acquired the lane — not to the task that authored the diff, so the subject-line id is systematically wrong rather than occasionally wrong. THREE confirmed instances, all naming task 1933 as the reclaimer: (1) on task/5788 the branch-tip commit a12ef7072ad4 was messaged as task 1933 WIP but its diff was 5788's own S2 fix (dimension.rs to_display_units AREA/VOLUME arms); (2) on task/6093 the commit b46852a7395c reads "chore: save WIP before warm-lane reclaim (task 1933)" but its entire content is 6093's own RED test (+84 lines to crates/reify-compiler/tests/modal_options_validation_tests.rs, the test `rayleigh_damping_fields_propagate_declared_dimensions`, whose doc comment says "task-6093" throughout), sandwiched chronologically between 6093's other commits; (3) on task/5711 the tip commit 956358856b46 is titled "(task 1933)" while its content is task 5711's own esc-5711-3 fix (folded in from mem 35c6058e, 2026-08-26). When re-planning or auditing a branch that already carries commits, always run `git show <sha>` on every commit and classify it by DIFF CONTENT plus its position in the chronology, never by the task id in its subject — a foreign-looking task id does not mean the diff is foreign work, and treating it as such drops a completed TDD step back to pending or gets a legitimate step wrongly reverted as contamination. Do not rewrite the mismessaged commit itself; record the correction in a later commit message and in plan.json instead.

Warm-lane leaked-checkout mechanism (DF release-leak), traced in orchestrator/src/orchestrator/: warm_lane_pool.py is a PURE IN-MEMORY FREE/ASSIGNED state machine with a branch->lane _assignments reuse map (acquire_for returns the SAME lane if the branch is still mapped, line ~136). The git worktree removal only fires on terminal outcomes: harness.py:4391-4397 calls release_lane_for_terminal_task ONLY when report.outcome in (DONE, CANCELLED) and not synthetic_cancel. A BLOCKED outcome (any unhandled slot exception, harness.py:4348) NEVER releases -> the worktree persists with the task branch checked out -> the next acquire_for collides ("already checked out") or reuses a now-deleted lane. Comments at harness.py:4338-4340/4375-4383 note the branch-preservation guard in release_warm_lane is task 1912 (α, NOT yet landed) and task 1913 (β, landed, only delays deletion). An orchestrator restart wipes the in-memory _assignments (disk-backstop via each lane's .task/plan.json is supposed to restore it but didn't across the specific restart). Symptom: task-SPECIFIC DETERMINISTIC acquire faults (same tasks re-fault every dispatch while others run fine) — NOT "transient".

In a reify warm lane, the reclaim-time "chore: save WIP before warm-lane reclaim (task NNNN)" safety-commit can be the branch tip and can leave the tree NON-COMPILING (it snapshots mid-edit — e.g. a const moved between modules with the `use` not yet added), and its message may name an unrelated task id even though the diff is entirely the owning task's files. Always run a `cargo check` on the touched crates at session start before assuming the branch is green, and read the WIP commit's diff rather than trusting its message for provenance (task 6672 / esc-6672-4).

CORRECTION (verified in dark-factory source 2026-09-12): a warm-lane re-dispatch does NOT orphan a task branch's unlanded commits. The widely-repeated claim — "a lane reset runs `git checkout -f -B task/<id> <main>` with no WIP guard, a sibling worktree does not block it, so only a backup branch protects a strand" — is true of the RAW GIT PRIMITIVE but false of the orchestrator's acquire path. `GitOps._orphan_has_commits` (orchestrator/src/orchestrator/git_ops.py:8285 = `git rev-parse --verify` existence gate + `_branch_has_commits_beyond_main`, fail-safe True on git error) gates all three γ reattach sites: `acquire_warm_lane`'s create-once site (~7030), its reset-in-place site (~7209), and `create_worktree`'s cold path (~4440). When task/<id> carries commits beyond main they are PRESERVED and rebased; if reattach itself cannot proceed (e.g. the branch is live in another worktree — precisely the "sibling worktree" case) it RAISES rather than destroying. Owner: dark_factory task 1914 (done 2026-06-25, PRD plans/warm-lane-branch-lifecycle-decouple-prd.md), tested by 1915's test_gamma_reattach_preserves_commits. NARROW RESIDUAL, unverified beyond a read: git_ops.py:~6902-6904, the in-memory identity-MISMATCH RECYCLE route, calls `_reset_warm_lane` with no guard; it reads as a lane-identity collision rather than same-task re-dispatch. CONSEQUENCE for triage: a stranded finished task left dispatchable is a WASTE hazard (a fresh dispatch re-plans finished work, since the plan usually died with the lane), NOT a data-loss hazard. Park it and land it by hand for that reason, and stop telling people their commits are about to be destroyed. On 2026-09-11/12 three reify tasks (6038 with 15 commits, 6830 with 6, 6410 with 1) sat dispatchable after their escalations closed; two sessions plus the L2 watcher described this as near-destruction, and a dark-factory task was nearly filed on that false premise before the guard was found.

Warm-lane task worktrees can be rebased by the orchestrator MID-SESSION (between iterations): HEAD moves to new SHAs with the same commit messages, `git merge-base HEAD main` advances, source line numbers shift (unevenly), and `.git/AUTO_MERGE` + `.git/MERGE_RR` appear (rerere leftovers, harmless). Symptom: grep line numbers stop matching Read offsets, or an Edit's old_string won't match. Recovery: re-run `git rev-parse HEAD` and `git merge-base HEAD main`; if HEAD changed, DISCARD all pre-rebase reads and re-grep/re-Read fresh before editing (a stale pre-rebase old_string can fail or mis-target an Edit). Confirm no rebase is in-progress via `.git/rebase-merge`/`.git/rebase-apply` before proceeding.

A warm-lane reclaim can leave a commit on a task branch whose message names a DIFFERENT task than the work it contains — e.g. task/5711 carries `chore: save WIP before warm-lane reclaim (task 1933)` (956358856b46), which is entirely task 5711 code (esc-5711-3's `params_in_underivable_constraints` abstention). The id in that message is the task whose dispatch triggered the reclaim, NOT the author of the parked WIP. When auditing branch provenance, read the DIFF, not the subject line: treating such a commit as cross-task contamination and reverting it destroys real, green work.

Warm-lane reclaim leaves two recoverable signatures on a task branch, and both look alarming but are benign. (1) `.task/plan.json` is a symlink into `/home/leo/src/warm-lanes/worktrees/.task-meta/<lane>/plan.json`; when the lane is reclaimed that target is deleted, so a re-dispatched architect finds a DANGLING symlink — the plan is genuinely lost and must be re-authored over the already-committed work, not repaired. (2) The reclaim WIP-save commits as `chore: save WIP before warm-lane reclaim (task NNNN)` stamping the RECLAIMING task's id, NOT the branch's — e.g. task/6672 carries a commit subject naming task 1933 while its diff touches only 6672's own files. Check the diff before treating such a commit as foreign WIP injected into the branch; it is the lane's own uncommitted work being parked, not the shared-stash hazard.

reify warm lanes (/home/leo/src/warm-lanes/worktrees/_lane-N) and the persistent merge lane (_merge-verify) are git worktrees of the SAME repo — their .git files point to /home/leo/src/reify/.git/worktrees/<name>. They therefore SHARE refs/heads/main (and all refs/heads/*). Consequence: any operation that rewrites the shared main ref (git commit --amend / rebase / backward reset) — even one done manually in the main checkout while the orchestrator runs — silently strands whatever a concurrent task-lane rebase-onto-main had built on the pre-rewrite tip. Task branches with no own commits are especially exposed because _reuse_warm_lane's rebase-onto-main fast-forwards them to exactly equal main's current tip; if main is later rewritten they become 1-commit-beyond-main orphans. This is the mechanism behind esc-5279-3.

In reify, a task's .task/plan.json step->commit shas can ALL become unreachable from its own branch tip without any work being lost: when a warm lane is reclaimed mid-task and the branch is later replayed onto a newer main, every commit gets a fresh sha while plan.json keeps the pre-replay ones (observed on task/5937: 13/13 recorded shas dangling, `git for-each-ref --contains <sha>` empty, yet 13 subject-identical twins present on the branch and `git diff <old-lineage-tip> <new-tip>` showing only unrelated files from the newer base). So a phantom-done check based on sha REACHABILITY yields false positives; confirm by diffing the old lineage tip against the branch tip and checking the task's own files are absent from that diff. Related artifact: the reclaim WIP-saver commits the interrupted step's work under the RECLAIMING task's id ("chore: save WIP before warm-lane reclaim (task NNNN)"), so git blame can attribute one task's change to another.

Warm-lane reclaim can leave a commit on YOUR task branch titled "chore: save WIP before warm-lane reclaim (task NNNN)" where NNNN is the RECLAIMING task's id, not yours — the message names a foreign task while the content is entirely your own uncommitted work. Seen on task/6181, which carried "…(task 1933)" holding only 6181's own files. Do not read that label as a cross-task scope breach: verify by content with `git show --stat <sha>` before escalating. Likewise, `git diff --stat <old-main-tip>..HEAD` inflates a branch's apparent scope with commits main has since gained; use the three-dot `git diff --stat main...HEAD` for the branch's true diff.

During /unblock of a blocked task living in a WARM LANE (e.g. _lane-11) while the reify orchestrator is LIVE, commit any uncommitted working-tree fix IMMEDIATELY to protect it. Rationale: the orchestrator can reclaim a warm lane for another task via acquire_lane → seed-warm-lane → `git reset --hard && git clean -xfd`, which would WIPE uncommitted WIP. A blocked task is off the dispatch path, so its own lane won't be re-acquired for it, but the lane CAN be grabbed for a different task. Committing to the task branch (reversible via soft-reset) is the durable protection — do it before spending time on analysis or waiting on the user. Also: do NOT `git worktree remove` a warm lane or `git branch -d` a branch checked out in one after merge — the branch is checked out there (branch -d fails) and lane cleanup is the orchestrator pool's job; manual removal breaks the pool. Relates to [[feedback_missing_worktree_may_be_warm_lane]] and [[feedback_unblock_worktree_outside_warm_lanes]].

Warm-lane escalation handling: resolving a blocking escalation with action='resume' does NOT trigger an orchestrator inter-iteration rebase of the task branch onto main for warm lanes (observed for lane _lane-25 / task 5118, 2026-07-21). The agent re-dispatches on the SAME (stale) branch tip it was on, so a task that is blocked pending a rebase-onto-main will loop and re-file the same blocker. Do not assume 'resume' or 'restart' auto-rebases. When a task-branch rebase onto current main is the actual blocker, the escalation handler should perform the rebase directly: the L1/handler agent has whole-tree filesystem write access (unlike the implementer, which is landlock write-scoped to its declared files and will hit the scope wall on the whole-tree checkout). Procedure that worked: `git rebase main`; the branch's net diff touched only its 3 in-scope files so the single conflict was in-scope (engine_eval.rs); resolve by adopting the sibling task's migrated shape verbatim (take main's side of the hunk); rerere (enabled repo-wide) auto-applies the resolution across remaining replayed WIP/amend commits; verify with `cargo check -p <crate> --tests`; then resolve_issue action='resume' with the remaining implementer steps in the resolution text (injected into the agent briefing on the L0 resume path). This is a normal task-branch rebase (branch history rewritten forward onto main), NOT a move/rewind of main, so it does not trip the reference-transaction main-gate tripwire.

content: After an orchestrator restart, a reify task may resume in a DIFFERENT warm lane (e.g. _lane-5 → _lane-6), with its branch rebased onto new SHAs. Uncommitted edits from the old lane arrive only as a harness tip commit "chore: save WIP before warm-lane reclaim (task 1933)", and a tool call interrupted mid-session may be missing from it. On resume, `git show` that WIP commit and diff it against what you intended before continuing; the old lane path may already belong to another task.

candidates.content: A bash script that shells out to python3 to import `orchestrator.*` must prefer the checkout's own `<repo_root>/.venv/bin/python3` over PATH `python3`, not merely set PYTHONPATH. `orchestrator.git_ops` transitively imports `orchestrator.config` and hence pydantic, so a dependency-less system interpreter cannot run the import at all: verified on dark-factory task 3074 that `env -i PATH=/usr/bin:/bin` makes the bridge fail with ModuleNotFoundError, while `<worktree>/.venv/bin/python3` succeeds (the workspace venv carries an editable install pointing at that same worktree). This matters because `PATH=/usr/bin:/bin` is the shape a systemd unit's environment actually has — a bridge invoked from a timer would fail-open on EVERY run, which for a warn-and-degrade design means permanently degraded while training operators to read `[warn]` as noise. Testing trap: pytest subprocess cases inherit the pytest venv on PATH, so a happy-path test and a stub-python3 failure test can BOTH be green while the realistic middle case (a real interpreter without the deps) is uncovered — pin it explicitly with `PATH=/usr/bin:/bin` and a skipif for hosts whose system python does have the deps.

To import the dark-factory `shared` package from a script, use the repo-root virtualenv at /home/leo/src/dark-factory/.venv/bin/python — NOT system python3 with sys.path.insert('shared/src'). The path-insert approach fails at import time because shared/src/shared/__init__.py eagerly imports shared.async_sqlite_base, which imports aiosqlite, so any use of the package (e.g. validating a capability-manifest sidecar via shared.capability_manifest.load_capability_manifest, or reading _BLESSED_METADATA_KEYS from shared.task_metadata) dies with ModuleNotFoundError on a bare interpreter. There are no per-package .venv directories under fused-memory/, orchestrator/, shared/ or escalation/ — the single repo-root .venv is the one that resolves. Verified 2026-08-06. Workaround when a venv is unavailable: parse the source statically (e.g. regex the _BLESSED_METADATA_KEYS frozenset literal) rather than importing, but prefer the root .venv since it exercises the real pydantic validators.

Gotcha, 2026-09-30: running a DF suite as `env -u VIRTUAL_ENV .venv/bin/python -m pytest` leaves .venv/bin OFF the PATH. About 7 orchestrator tests that spawn a bare `python3` then fail with "No module named 'shared'": test_merge_lane_ratchet_commit_gate.py (5), test_lane_state_lib.py::TestLaneProtectGlobBridge, and test_warm_lane_bash_bucket_placement.py.

This is an invocation artifact, not a regression. Run suites the way the gate does: `cd <module> && uv run pytest ...`, or prepend .venv/bin to PATH. The pre-commit hook likewise refuses to run with a python3 that cannot import shared.

Related: `git worktree move` leaves the worktree's .venv dangling, because the shebangs and editable .pth files keep the old path. Re-run `uv sync --all-packages` after moving a worktree if you will run code from it.

Environment note (2026-05-27): the dark_factory worktree uv venv resolved to CPython 3.14.0+freethreaded, while the prod .venv at /home/leo/src/dark-factory/.venv is now Python 3.13.9 (NOT 3.12 as older memory states). The 6 pre-existing scheduler.get_status mock failures reproduced under BOTH 3.14-freethreaded and 3.13.9, which is how I ruled out 'Python-version artifact' and traced them to a stale worktree base instead. For running the orchestrator suite faithfully against prod, use /home/leo/src/dark-factory/.venv/bin/python with PYTHONPATH prepending the worktree's orchestrator/src:shared/src:escalation/src and --override-ini="addopts=" (the addopts bakes in -n auto --dist loadgroup).

dark_factory scripts/tests CLI harness interpreters are NOT interchangeable (measured 2026-09-28, task 5085 planning): scripts/drain_check.py and scripts/recon_busy_check.py are stdlib-only and production invokes them as bare `python3` (restart-all-orchestrators.sh, restart-fused-memory.sh), so their tests spawn `python3`; scripts/scan_task_toolcall_leaks.py bootstraps shared/src and imports `shared` (drags in aiosqlite), so a dependency-free python3 cannot run it and its test must spawn sys.executable. Under `uv run --project shared` (the scripts gate) `shutil.which('python3')` is the venv's own python3, so the difference only shows in ad-hoc runs outside uv. Also measured: pyright resolves a bare `import <sibling>` of a non-test helper module in scripts/tests/ with 0 errors even without a pyright extraPaths entry.

Prod venv at /home/leo/src/dark-factory/.venv/ is Python 3.13.9 as of 2026-05-11 (earlier auto-memory notes said 3.12; reality drifted). Diagnostic signature, measured 2026-10-17 (task 7077). Moving a directory that holds a uv venv leaves the venv's console-script shebangs pointing at the old path. `uv run --extra dev pytest` does NOT repair this: the packages count as installed, so uv only rebuilds the editable project. It then fails with "error: Failed to spawn: `pytest` / Caused by: No such file or directory (os error 2)", because execve hits ENOENT on the missing shebang interpreter. `head -1 .venv/bin/pytest` reveals the cause.

This is why solar-challenge's review Phase 1 (which runs in the main checkout, moved from /home/leo/src/my-solar-challenge) was red for 7 checkpoints while worktree verifies stayed green. "Failed to spawn" with the tool present in .venv/bin means a stale shebang, not dropped --extra flags or a leaked VIRTUAL_ENV.

Run `uv sync --all-packages` in the worktree before a hand-run wide sweep; after that, the same sweep was 7703 passed.

dark-factory dev-env fact (observed 2026-05-27): The repo's only Python venv is the ROOT `.venv` (Python 3.13.9) — there is no separate orchestrator/.venv and no prod 3.12 venv in this checkout. This root .venv is an EDITABLE install whose `orchestrator` package resolves to /home/leo/src/dark-factory/orchestrator/src/orchestrator (the main checkout's src). Consequence: working on a feature branch DIRECTLY in the main checkout (git checkout -b, not EnterWorktree) lets `.venv/bin/python` pick up your edits immediately — no PYTHONPATH/editable-.pth gymnastics, no venv rebuild. This is a clean low-friction alternative to a worktree WHEN no dark-factory orchestrator is running to stash/sync the tree. (Contradicts the older "prod 3.12 venv" assumption in some memories — this checkout is 3.13.9.)

Because verify._target_subprocess_env scrubs UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT, when an eval fixture's setup_commands do `cd <subproject> && uv sync` (e.g. df_task_12: `cd orchestrator && uv sync`), uv creates the venv at `<worktree>/<subproject>/.venv`, NOT the top-level `<worktree>/.venv`. Any check for the implementer venv (e.g. scripts/eval_bootstrap_smoke.sh) must resolve the actual location: direct `<wt>/.venv/bin/python` first, else the one-level subproject match `<wt>/*/.venv/bin/python` (task 2875).

On this host /usr/bin/python3 is CPython 3.12.3 while the dark-factory uv venv is 3.13.9, and an agent shell's bare `python3` resolves to the venv. setup-host.sh runs the check_*_unit_parity.py checkers, scripts/systemd_unit_parity.py and render_systemd_unit.py as bare `python3` (system 3.12). Tests like test_check_dashboard_unit_parity.py::test_checker_subprocess_runs_without_third_party_imports also run plain `python3`, and that can be the system 3.12 once verify strips the venv from PATH. So anything added to those stdlib-only scripts must stay 3.12-compatible. Probe with `/usr/bin/python3 <script> --help`, not with bare `python3`.

GOTCHA (merged from four near-duplicate entries): a test that spawns a child interpreter — via subprocess.run/Popen or asyncio.create_subprocess_exec (e.g. `sys.executable -m <workspace_pkg>`, `python -m escalation ...`) — gets NONE of conftest.py's sys.path injection: the repo's root conftest.py and per-package conftest.py (e.g. orchestrator/tests/conftest.py, which inserts escalation/src, shared/src and orchestrator/src) do this IN-PROCESS only, so a fresh child interpreter sees just site-packages plus cwd. In a worktree venv missing an editable install (e.g. only `_editable_impl_dark_factory_shared.pth` present), the child then resolves the repo's `<pkg>/` directory (e.g. `escalation/`) as an implicit NAMESPACE package with no `__main__` (`__file__ is None`) and dies — while every in-process import in the same test file still works, so the failure looks isolated to the subprocess call. This made task 3404's test_handler_executes_on_failure_path non-hermetic: green in a fully uv-synced venv, red in a worktree venv holding only the editable-shared stub. Diagnose with `<worktree>/.venv/bin/python3 -m <pkg> --help` and by listing `.venv/lib/python*/site-packages/_editable_impl_*.pth`. Fix such tests by explicitly injecting the src roots into the CHILD's env (`env['PYTHONPATH']`, with injected roots taking precedence and inherited PYTHONPATH appended, not clobbered), never by skipif. The injection cannot mask a genuinely unsynced venv: third-party deps still resolve from site-packages only, so a bare `/usr/bin/python3` + PYTHONPATH still fails (verified: ModuleNotFoundError: aiosqlite). Worked example / reference implementation: `_run_wrapper_payload` / `_child_env` / `_assert_submit_cli_invokable` in orchestrator/tests/test_deterministic_runner.py (task 3404) — verified this makes a stripped venv run the CLI at RC=0.

Gotcha for any dark-factory test in tests/scripts/ that shells out to a subprocess: the root conftest.py fixes sys.path for the IN-PROCESS pytest run only (it appends the repo root and inserts each `<member>/src`), and a subprocess inherits none of that. Measured 2026-08-23 in .worktrees/3959: when this suite's own test_command (`uv run --project shared pytest tests/scripts/`) has to CREATE the worktree .venv it installs only shared's closure — 87 packages, with `shared` editable and no `orchestrator`. A subprocess `python -c 'import orchestrator; print(orchestrator.__file__)'` there does NOT fail loudly: the repo root is on sys.path for a `-c`, so the `orchestrator/` DIRECTORY is picked up as a namespace package and `__file__` prints None. Probe `shared` (the one member that command guarantees is installed editable), and always assert the resolved path exists so a namespace-package resolution surfaces as a loud red rather than a plausible-looking string.

Test/tooling fact (dark_factory orchestrator): the prod venv at /home/leo/src/dark-factory/.venv is now Python 3.13.9 (the old "prod 3.12" memory is stale — the principle stands: use the MAIN repo's prod venv, not a worktree's uv venv). To run orchestrator tests against worktree changes: from the worktree's orchestrator/ dir, `PYTHONPATH="$PWD/src:$PWD/tests:$PYTHONPATH" /home/leo/src/dark-factory/.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_merge_queue.py --override-ini="addopts=" -q` (the addopts override strips the baked-in `-n auto` xdist loadgroup; prepending worktree src/tests beats the editable .pth that otherwise resolves to main). For pyright on worktree source: `PYTHONPATH="$PWD/src:$PYTHONPATH" /home/leo/src/dark-factory/.venv/bin/python -m pyright --pythonpath /home/leo/src/dark-factory/.venv/bin/python src/orchestrator/<file>.py` — WITHOUT `--pythonpath` pointing at the venv interpreter, pyright fails to resolve pydantic/pydantic_settings imports (false-positive reportMissingImports).

In the dark-factory worktrees, the repo-root .venv does NOT have per-package runtime deps like psutil installed, so `python -m pytest sampler/tests/...` from the repo root spuriously fails sampler's psutil-dependent tests with ModuleNotFoundError. Use `cd <package_dir> && uv run pytest` (e.g. `cd sampler && uv run pytest`) to run against that package's own uv workspace venv, which has its declared dependencies installed.

In dark-factory tests, a `subprocess.run([sys.executable, '-c', ...])` probe does NOT inherit the per-subproject conftest's sys.path pinning (e.g. shared/tests/conftest.py inserts `<worktree>/shared/src` at sys.path[0] precisely because the venv's editable install may be pinned to the MAIN tree). Such a subprocess can therefore import a DIFFERENT copy of the package than the rest of the suite tests, producing an environment-dependent false pass or spurious failure in a worktree. If a subprocess probe is unavoidable, pass the same src dir through `env={**os.environ, 'PYTHONPATH': ...}`; prefer reading/AST-scanning the source of the already-imported module (anchored on `<module>.__file__`) instead.

A `before_done` deterministic script (and any stdlib-only script) that needs an AUTHORITATIVE value out of a first-party package has a third remedy beyond the two already in memory (b8271996 "use <repo_root>/.venv/bin/python", 38e2f5b3 "prefer the checkout's own .venv/bin/python3 over PATH python3", 31bfeba5 "__file__-relative sys.path bootstrap"): shell out to `uv run --frozen --no-sync --project <member> python -c ...` and parse its stdout. Measured on dark-factory task 3592, 2026-09-13.

WHY THE QUESTION ARISES. `deterministic_runner.py` launches a before_done script with `create_subprocess_exec(script, *args)` — straight through the shebang, inheriting the orchestrator's own environment. The live orchestrator itself runs under `uv run --frozen --project orchestrator ...`, and its /proc/<pid>/environ carries NO `VIRTUAL_ENV` and no venv `bin` on PATH (confirmed by reading the live process's environ, not assumed). So `#!/usr/bin/env python3` in such a script resolves to /usr/bin/python3 (3.12.3 on this host), which HAS `yaml` but NOT `shared`, `sampler` or `orchestrator`. That is the constraint that decides the script's whole import policy, and it is the same shape as the systemd `PATH=/usr/bin:/bin` case in 38e2f5b3.

WHY `--no-sync` IS LOAD-BEARING, NOT DECORATION. It is the join between this and the sibling-uninstall cluster (211d8b9d / 1d0552c5): a plain `uv run --project shared` was measured REMOVING `orchestrator` from the shared root venv, because uv syncs exact-by-default. A helper script that shelled out without `--no-sync` would intermittently break running orchestrators and concurrent verify runs as a side effect of merely reading a default. With `--frozen --no-sync` the same command returns the value from a clean env and mutates nothing.

WHEN TO PREFER IT over the .venv/bin/python remedies: when the value you want is a CODE DEFAULT that must not be transcribed (a pydantic model's field defaults, say), the script must stay runnable from a bare interpreter, and you want the member's OWN resolved environment rather than whichever checkout an editable install happens to point at. The subprocess boundary also keeps the caller stdlib-only and testable by injection — the parsed mapping goes in as an argument, so tests never need the member importable at all.

Gotcha (dark-factory task worktrees): running the scripts gate as `uv run --project shared pytest tests/scripts/ scripts/tests/` in a worktree that has no .venv yet makes uv create a worktree .venv holding only `shared`'s dependencies, so complexipy and radon are absent. About 120 tests in tests/scripts/test_quality_metrics_snapshot.py and test_source_measures.py then fail with "complexipy is not installed", which is an environment fault, not a code failure (measured on task 6612). Verify is unaffected because it runs `uv sync --all-packages` first. Locally, either run `uv sync --all-packages` in the worktree first, or use the main checkout's venv interpreter (`python -m pytest ...`), which has complexipy 6.2.

fused-memory/tests/test_predicate_contradiction.py::TestReconPredicateCheckScript::test_pytest_passing_exits_0 spawns a bare `python -m pytest` through PATH. If the suite is run as `<venv>/bin/python -m pytest` without the venv's bin dir on PATH, the spawned python is /usr/bin/python and the test fails with "No module named pytest". This is environmental, not a code fault.

Measured 2026-10-10 from an un-synced scratch worktree using main's .venv. The fix is `PATH=<venv>/bin:$PATH VIRTUAL_ENV=<venv> python -m pytest tests/ -n auto`. With that, the full fused-memory suite ran 28,785 passed in about 4m41s. The failing invocation had taken about 9m53s to reach the failure under -x.

content: In a dark-factory test that builds a fake venv on disk and then EXECUTES its scripts, the venv's pyvenv.cfg `home` must name the running base interpreter's bin dir (Path(sys.base_prefix)/'bin'), not /usr/bin. With `home = /usr/bin` and bin/python symlinked to the test interpreter (uv CPython 3.13), startup fails with 'Fatal Python error: Failed to import encodings module'. Python resolves the stdlib from pyvenv.cfg home, and /usr has no 3.13 stdlib. orchestrator/tests/_venv_fixtures.py::make_venv already does this correctly (task 7077).

candidates.content: tests/infra/adoption-ratchet.manifest (S19 α, task #8678; the repo's INV candidate 5 adoption-ratchet engine) has these quirks. Rows are `pattern-id | ERE | path glob | ceiling | owner leaf`. The engine (tests/infra/adoption_ratchet.py) expands globs with pathlib root.glob, so `*` does NOT cross `/`: use `crates/<crate>/src/**/*.rs` for any ratchet that must survive a later file split into subdirectories. A glob that matches no file reds the gate. Lines whose first non-blank char is '#' never count, so Rust `#[…]` attribute lines are invisible to it, and such ratchets must be Rust tests. The ERE must be POSIX-compatible: no \b, \d, (?…) or lazy quantifiers.

Fact (reify infra, 2026-10-13): tests/infra/adoption-ratchet.manifest (engine tests/infra/adoption_ratchet.py, gate member test_infra_adoption_ratchet.sh, from S19) is the existing home for INV-candidate-5 'extract-with-ratchet' rows: `pattern-id | ERE | path-glob | ceiling | owner leaf`. The engine skips only lines whose first non-blank character is '#', so Rust `//` comment lines DO count — each ERE must be anchored on the code construct (e.g. `^\s*pub fn diagnose\(`), and the path must be one repo-root glob that matches at least one file. A row reds only when a count EXCEEDS its ceiling; extract leaves add their row at the post-extraction count.

reify tests/infra/adoption-ratchet.manifest gotchas (adoption_ratchet.py, task 8716 planning).

1. Escape a literal `$` (and `(`) in a row's ERE, e.g. write `_PARENT="\$\(mktemp` and not `_PARENT="$(mktemp`. An unescaped `$` is an end anchor in both POSIX ERE and Python re, so the row silently matches nothing and its ceiling is vacuous.
2. The path column is ONE Python Path.glob, with no {a,b} brace expansion. To cover several files, widen the glob (e.g. tests/infra/test_*.sh) and shape the ERE to exclude false hits, or add separate rows. Remember that test_*.sh also matches test_helpers.sh.
3. Pin each new row with a shape test in test_infra_adoption_ratchet.py: a historical line must match, and the replacement must not.

tests/infra/adoption_ratchet.py (INV candidate 5 adoption ratchets) skips every line whose first non-blank character is '#', so a ratchet row whose subject is a Rust attribute (#[serde(...)], #[cfg(...)]) always counts 0 and guards nothing; it also globs one path per row, so a comma-separated path list matches no file and reds the gate. Found by the S26 fold-verifier 2026-10-15 after the draft proposed four such rows. Enforce attribute-level rules with a behavioural test instead (S26 ι uses a gui-feature test asserting each generated X_Serialize/X_Deserialize pair is identical) and measure every proposed row with the real engine, not only git grep.

reify merge-gate tripwires that repeatedly caught stranded branches during the 2026-08-27/28 recovery, worth checking on any branch before submitting it. (1) HARNESS-LAYOUT RATCHET: a new standalone `crates/*/tests/*.rs` in one of the 5 consolidatable crates (reify-cli, reify-syntax, reify-kernel-occt, reify-eval, reify-compiler) must be `#[path]`-declared from a `harness_<subsystem>` root; adding a `tests/infra/harness-layout-baseline.manifest` row is SUPERSEDED as a remedy (Leo 2026-07-22, esc-5056-11 — the manifest is a shrinking ratchet). reify-solver-elastic and reify-eval-fea-tests are deliberately OUT of that contract. (2) `_RUST_COUPLED_RI_FIXTURES` at `scripts/verify.sh:1080`: a new `tests/prd-gate/fixtures/*.ri` that a compiled Rust test READS must be listed there, or `tests/infra/test_verify_scope.sh`'s PG-DRIFT scenario reds. (3) `clippy::neg_cmp_op_on_partial_ord`: `!(x > 0.0)` guards fail the gate's `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`; the in-tree idiom is to bind a bool first (`crates/reify-eval/src/engine_build.rs:12718` names the lint in its comment). (4) PTODO fingerprint ratchet: a literal `TODO(`/`FIXME:`/`HACK(` in a comment with no `#NNNN` cite and no `// ptodo:allow` escape is a NEW untracked fingerprint and reds the severity-blind subset check — note `TODO)` does NOT match the regex, only `TODO(` or `TODO:`. (5) `scripts/release-sensitive-crates.txt`: the FIRST `#[cfg(not(debug_assertions))]` in a crate makes it release-sensitive by grep derivation, and if it is not DECLARED there, `tests/infra/test_release_scoped_scope.sh` Test 3 reds AND the release pass stays `-p`-scoped so the new release-only test never runs anywhere.

Reify's gate-test drift-guard "overlay rule" (.claude/skills/prd/project.md) triggers ONLY on a new `crates/*/tests/*.rs` integration binary or a new `tests/infra/test_*.sh`. A new in-crate `#[cfg(test)] mod foo;` under `crates/*/src/` needs ZERO same-diff registrations: run-all-classification.manifest is shell-test-only; .config/nextest.toml overrides and scripts/heavy-test-filter-lib.sh atoms are keyed on `package(X) & binary(Y)` and their guards require the filter to resolve to a real crates/<pkg>/tests/<bin>.rs on disk, so a lib target cannot be registered even if you wanted to; the two wallclock guards scan only tests/infra/*.sh and gui/src-tauri/src/tests/*.rs. State the N/A explicitly in the module docs rather than defensively registering. Crucially, tests/infra/harness-layout-baseline.manifest is a SHRINKING ratchet over _HL_CRATES=(reify-cli reify-syntax reify-kernel-occt reify-eval reify-compiler) whose growth is superseded (Leo 2026-07-22, esc-5056-11) — so for those five crates a NEW standalone crates/<c>/tests/foo.rs is RED with no sanctioned registration, and the remedies are an in-crate `#[cfg(test)] mod`, or a `harness_<subsystem>.rs` stem (excluded from the re-accretion predicate, governed by the kLOC cap instead). Precedent: task 6001 added seven test compile units and touched none of these four surfaces.

In reify, tests/infra/adoption_ratchet.py (the #8678 infra-harness engine behind adoption-ratchet.manifest) checks a ceiling only. It reds only when a count rises above the ceiling, and it scans whole files with no #[cfg(test)] cut. It therefore cannot express S5 analysis-stratum ratchet rows, which must red on a fall without a baseline edit and count only production code, cut at the first column-0 #[cfg(test)]. S5 rows (wire-codec-copy, then catch-unwind-guard, target-string-routing, shell-value-decoder, eval-imports-analysis) live in tests/infra/test_analysis_stratum_ratchet.py, created by task #8984. Each row is a Row constant with one test method.

reify: adding a NEW standalone `crates/<c>/tests/<file>.rs` is BLOCKED at source for five "consolidatable" crates — reify-cli, reify-syntax, reify-kernel-occt, reify-eval, reify-compiler. `scripts/check-harness-baseline-registration.sh` (diff-scoped, task 5300) emits `HARNESS_BASELINE_REG FAIL crate=<c> file=<path> reason=unregistered-standalone` and exits 1 for any test file ADDED in your diff under those crates, and `tests/infra/test_harness_kloc_cap.sh` rule (b) is the whole-tree twin. Adding a row to `tests/infra/harness-layout-baseline.manifest` LOOKS like the fix but is explicitly SUPERSEDED (Leo 2026-07-22, esc-5056-11: "actually start using the ratchet" — the manifest is a shrinking ratchet). The sanctioned remedy is to fold the new test into an existing `crates/<c>/tests/harness_<subsystem>/<file>.rs` declared from the harness root with a MANDATORY `#[path = "harness_<subsystem>/<file>.rs"] mod <file>;` — a bare `mod <file>;` in an integration-test crate root resolves against `tests/` and silently binds the wrong file. Seven override stems stay standalone forever (determinism, analytical_validation, modal_benchmarks, buckling_smoke, fea_diagnostics_e2e, tensegrity_t0a, representation_within_assertion) and the harness unit is subject to a raw-`wc -l` kLOC cap that counts the root PLUS its module dir PLUS externally-included files such as `tests/common/`. Crates OUTSIDE those five (e.g. reify-expr, reify-ir, reify-core) are unaffected — a new standalone tests/*.rs there is fine. Plan for this BEFORE proposing "add a per-crate test" in reify-eval or reify-compiler; it changes the shape and cost of the work.

reify-solver-elastic adoption ratchets (crates/reify-solver-elastic/tests/adoption_ratchets.rs, task 8614, PRD solver-crates-layering D20/BT14) are STRICT-equality: a row passes only when its measured count equals `baseline:` in the RATCHETS table, so a leaf that migrates a copy must lower its own row in the same diff (the red message says "lower the baseline to N"). The host file itself is left out of every measurement (`read_crate_tree` skips HOST_PATH), so its seeds, doc comments and generic helper names never count and a new tests/ file may reuse them. Every other src/ and tests/ file is lexed; the real-tree test goes red naming file and line (`UnsupportedTestCfg`) on any `cfg(..)` naming `test` other than the bare `#[cfg(test)]` (all/any/not, inner `#![cfg(test)]`). The mpc-row-literals row also counts `MpcRow {` inside doc comments (`///`, `//!`, `/** */`, `/*! */`) of those other files, by design (the lib.rs doctest). Supersedes the 2026-10-12 note that said the binary counts its own file.

reify gotcha: tests/infra/adoption_ratchet.py (adoption-ratchet.manifest, #8678) treats only lines whose first non-blank char is '#' as comments. That rule is shell-only, so it is unfit for Rust-source ratchets: it counts `//`/`///` prose as code and drops `#[cfg(..)] foo!(..)` lines as comments. A Rust grep-style gate should read source through scripts/lib_rust_production_view.sh's RUST_PRODUCTION_VIEW_AWK (one awk process per file, escape matched via `comment_tail`), as check-nan-safe-ordering.sh and task 7556's tests/infra/reify_lsp_stderr_scan.py do.

reify: tests/infra/rust_construct_ratchet.py (task 8730) is the shared Python engine for counting regex occurrences over the production view of Rust files (scripts/lib_rust_production_view.sh's RUST_PRODUCTION_VIEW_AWK, so cfg(test) mods and comments are excluded) against per-row baselines. Import it (sys.path.insert of tests/infra, then rcr.Row/View/evaluate) rather than writing a second lexer driver. View.CODE blanks string contents, so a construct that IS a string literal (e.g. "__connector_) needs View.CODE_WITH_LITERALS. Rows live as Python data in the member (test_compiler_decl_pass_ratchets.py ROWS + FIXTURE_LINES), and a new row needs a FIXTURE_LINES entry or the coverage test reds.

In reify, stale `crates/<c>/tests/**/*.rs` prose path citations are machine-gated by task #7095's one-directional ratchet: tests/infra/test_cited_test_paths_resolve.sh (--gate-only, <1s) against tests/infra/cited-test-path-baseline.manifest, with derivation in tests/infra/cited-test-path-lib.sh (`cited_test_path_scan .` lists every stale cite plus its suggested target). For any citation-repoint sweep, drain the relevant baseline rows first; the gate then reds naming every live site (a free RED test), repointing turns it green, and dead rows can be dropped freely. The regex anchors on `crates/`, so partial forms like `reify-compiler/tests/x.rs` are invisible to it.

reify capability-manifest delivered_check authoring lessons (S5, 2026-10-13):

1. Pin `if target == "..."`-style absent checks crate-wide, not to one file. Another stream may relocate the branch, as S4 η #8864 does with the elastic_static branch into cell_elaboration.rs, and a file-scoped check would then pass while the branch is still alive.
2. Never check a ratchet row by a bare token over tests/infra. A docstring that lists planned rows satisfies it, so make it `manual` and let the ratchet member itself be the enforcement.
3. Do not grep a Cargo.toml for a dependency's absence when the same crate stays a dev-dependency (`faer` in reify-eval); the check wedges.
4. Scope `fn is_opted_in` to its signature `fn is_opted_in\(target: &str`. Unit tests named is_opted_in_* match the bare form.
5. commit_planning's `absent_overbroad` polarity warning is expected and non-blocking for move leaves that declare `files: []`.

Reify gate-resident-test rule: adding a test to an existing `crates/*/tests/harness_<subsystem>.rs` as a `#[path = "harness_<sub>/<stem>.rs"] mod <stem>;` submodule requires NO drift-guard registration at all — `harness_*` units are excluded from `tests/infra/harness-layout-baseline.manifest` by construction, and `run-all-classification.manifest`, the nextest binary selectors in `.config/nextest.toml`, the wallclock-bounds guard, and the THROUGHPUT-COUNTS sentinel (`docs/notes/verify-scope-throughput.md`) all apply only to NEW top-level standalone `crates/<c>/tests/*.rs` binaries. Only the `CAP_LINES=20000` per-compile-unit budget in `tests/infra/test_harness_kloc_cap.sh` applies. Explicit `#[path]` is mandatory, not stylistic: a harness root is an integration-test crate root, so a bare `mod x;` resolves to the sibling `tests/x.rs`, not the subdir.

The drift-guard registration advice in the /prd overlay (and repeated in many PRD task texts) is WRONG for `crates/*/tests/*.rs`, and following it literally HARD-REDS the merge gate. Verified 2026-09-01 with executed injection tests at main 4818478dff.

1. `tests/infra/run-all-classification.manifest` covers ONLY `tests/infra/test_*.sh` — 230 lines, ZERO `crates/` rows; its discovered-set iterates `"$_dir"/test_*.sh` in tests/infra alone. INJECTION TEST: appending a row `boundary_b10_new_test.rs pool` makes `scripts/check-infra-classification-manifest.sh` exit 1 — "manifest declares boundary_b10_new_test.rs but tests/infra/boundary_b10_new_test.rs does not exist" (the ORPHANED-row direction). `verify.sh` runs this gate as the FIRST plan entry when `RUN_RUST=1`, so the red lands before anything compiles.

2. The gate that ACTUALLY fires on a new `crates/*/tests/*.rs` is `scripts/check-harness-baseline-registration.sh` against `tests/infra/harness-layout-baseline.manifest`. INJECTION TEST: `echo crates/reify-eval/tests/boundary_b10_probe_tmp.rs | bash scripts/check-harness-baseline-registration.sh` -> "HARNESS_BASELINE_REG FAIL crate=reify-eval file=... reason=unregistered-standalone", violations=1, exit 1. ITS REMEDY IS SUPERSEDED — the gate's own stderr hint says: "Grandfathering a harness-layout-baseline.manifest row is SUPERSEDED (Leo 2026-07-22, esc-5056-11: 'actually start using the ratchet') — the manifest is a shrinking ratchet, not an allow-list to grow." THE SANCTIONED SAME-DIFF ACTION for a new gate-resident test in reify-eval / reify-compiler / reify-cli / reify-syntax / reify-kernel-occt is to CONSOLIDATE it into an existing `harness_<subsystem>.rs` via `#[path]`, NOT to create a standalone `tests/*.rs`. Plan tests as harness modules from the start.

3. "The wallclock-bounds registration" NAMES A MECHANISM THAT DOES NOT EXIST. tests/infra holds exactly four .manifest files (harness-layout-baseline, run-all-ambient-vars, run-all-classification, run-all-skip-closures). What exists is (a) `tests/infra/test_no_new_wallclock_upper_bounds.sh`, a STATIC-GREP guard over `tests/infra/*.sh` whose only author action is an inline OPT-OUT token `# wallclock:allow — <reason>` on the asserting line, firing only IF the new test contains a wall-clock upper bound; and (b) `tests/infra/test_no_new_wallclock_rust_deadlines.sh`, hard-scoped to `gui/src-tauri/src/tests/*.rs`. Neither is a registration; neither reaches `crates/*/tests/*.rs`.

Note some grandfathered standalones exist (e.g. `crates/reify-eval/tests/printer_z_compliant_mount_e2e.rs`) — copy their ENGINE SHAPE, never their file placement.

Adding a NEW top-level `crates/<c>/tests/<file>.rs` to any of the five harness-ratchet-guarded crates (reify-cli, reify-syntax, reify-kernel-occt, reify-eval, reify-compiler — the list lives at tests/infra/harness-layout-lib.sh:106) requires adding its canonical path as a row in `tests/infra/harness-layout-baseline.manifest` IN THE SAME DIFF, in ASCII sort order. Without the row, `tests/infra/test_harness_kloc_cap.sh` fails with `reason=unsanctioned-standalone` and `scripts/check-harness-baseline-registration.sh` fails with `reason=unregistered-standalone`. Neither guard fires under a branch-scoped verify — they only surface at the `--scope all` merge gate, so the branch looks green until the merge attempt. This is the same invisible-until-merge shape as verify.sh's `_RUST_COUPLED_RI_FIXTURES`/PG-DRIFT allowlist for tests/prd-gate/fixtures/*.ri, which blocked task #5481 across five separate merge attempts.

Adding a new top-level `crates/<c>/tests/<file>.rs` in one of the 5 consolidatable crates (reify-cli, reify-syntax, reify-kernel-occt, reify-eval, reify-compiler) trips `scripts/check-harness-baseline-registration.sh`. The gate is mechanically remedy-agnostic — a grandfather row in `tests/infra/harness-layout-baseline.manifest` clears it too — but its stderr `_hint()` records that grandfathering is SUPERSEDED (Leo 2026-07-22, esc-5056-11: "actually start using the ratchet"); the manifest is a shrinking ratchet, not an allow-list to grow. The sanctioned remedy is a consolidated `tests/harness_<subsystem>/<file>.rs` declared from a `tests/harness_<subsystem>.rs` root via an explicit `#[path]` attribute (a bare `mod <file>;` in an integration-test crate root resolves to the sibling `tests/<file>.rs`, not the subdir). A `harness_*.rs` unit is sanctioned by construction, and no external registry lists harness roots — so creating a new root is cheap. [Corrected 2026-09-16 by recon-stage-memory_consolidator per curator gate task #7568's disposition: the kLOC cap does NOT govern only the root file's raw `wc -l` — `harness_layout_unit_lines` (tests/infra/harness-layout-lib.sh) counts root + module dir + escaping includes.]

Reify convention: the moment ANY tracked `*.rs` names a `tests/prd-gate/fixtures/<name>.ri` path — a doc-comment mention counts, the guard's grep is not scoped to code — that basename MUST be added to `scripts/verify.sh`'s `_RUST_COUPLED_RI_FIXTURES` (:1015, keep the leading/trailing space sentinels) in the SAME commit, or `tests/infra/test_verify_scope.sh` scenario PG-DRIFT goes RED. That guard derives the coupled set behaviourally (`git grep -o 'tests/prd-gate/fixtures/[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+\.ri' -- '*.rs'`) and asserts each hit classifies RUN_RUST=1, because a fixture a compiled test reads must never fall in the no-heavy-checks carve-out (a hook-gated docs commit on `main` has no later gate to catch a bad edit to it). Companion scenario PG-DRIFT-DIR forbids any `*.rs` from naming the fixtures DIRECTORY (read_dir / glob / format!-built leaf) — use a single literal leaf path, the `crates/reify-compiler/tests/harness_units/torque_unit_tests.rs:112-133` idiom. If PG-DRIFT-DIR ever fires, the fix is NOT to extend the list: the carve-out's premise is void and the verify.sh arm has to be re-examined.

reify — FOURTH variant of the self-matching-grep hazard class (siblings: 07b67efe same-file static source scan, bc2826b0 parent-greps-child-script, a97e85e2 sub-shell assert-description self-match). Hit in task #6108. Here the collision is between an in-crate Rust "absence" meta-test and an EXTERNAL machine-checked guardrail: `usage_text_has_no_legacy_repo_default` in crates/reify-audit/src/bin/reify-audit.rs rendered `print_usage`'s string literal and asserted `!usage.contains("leodearden")`, and that needle then became the ONLY occurrence of the token anywhere under `crates/reify-audit/src` — exactly the path covered by the capability manifest's `{kind: grep, pattern: leodearden/reify, paths: [crates/reify-audit/src], expect: absent}` check (docs/prds/jcodemunch-substrate-restoration.capability-manifest.yaml). So the natural hardening — widening the manifest pattern from `<owner>/<project>` to the bare owner token — would have failed the guardrail ON the very test that existed to prove the absence. RULE: when a capability manifest already machine-checks `expect: absent` over a path, do NOT also write an in-source test that spells the forbidden literal inside that path; the manifest grep IS the enforcement and the test only booby-traps it. Keep the behavioural assertions instead — assert the field is `None` (`parse_args_empty_returns_defaults`), and assert the derived value on the wire from an integration test that lives OUTSIDE the manifest's `paths` (crates/reify-audit/tests/cli.rs is not covered by `paths: [crates/reify-audit/src]`, so its `assert_ne!(repo, "leodearden/reify")` is safe). Positive discoverability pins (`usage.contains("--some-flag")`) carry no such hazard and are legitimate API-surface tests.

In reify, adding a test to an EXISTING crates/<c>/tests/harness_<subsystem>/<file>.rs module needs no tests/infra/harness-layout-baseline.manifest row — that manifest is a grandfather baseline of standalone crates/*/tests/*.rs BINARIES (the C1/C2 contract in tests/infra/test_harness_kloc_cap.sh, task #5265). Only a NEW standalone test binary trips the ratchet; adding a new #[path]-declared module under an already-registered harness root adds a module, not a binary.

content: reify tests/infra/adoption-ratchet.manifest engine facts (tests/infra/adoption_ratchet.py, gated by test_infra_adoption_ratchet.sh): pattern-ids must be kebab-case `[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*` (an underscore or `.rs` in the id is a ManifestError); paths resolve with Path.glob, so `crates/reify-eval/src/engine_*.rs` matches direct children only (unlike a git pathspec, whose `*` spans `/`); the engine skips only lines whose first non-blank char is `#`, so Rust `//` comments DO count unless the ERE starts `^[^/]*`; it scans #[cfg(test)] modules too, so a row targeting 0 must also clean in-crate tests; the ERE must be POSIX-portable (no \b, no backslash-letter escapes, no backslash inside [...], no (?...)). A ratchet row can be vacuous: S1's first per-build-reset row (`[.](field)[.]clear[(]`) counted 0 at main because reset_per_build_state clears destructured locals; verify every row is red/at-ceiling before landing.

1b0e5c7f-8f45-4d33-8b46-a8a46bcfb5fb.content: Reify's grep-based source gates (scripts/check-nan-safe-ordering.sh, scripts/check-compute-trampoline-registration.sh) share a hand-ported awk Rust lexer, `_AWK_PRODUCTION_PROLOGUE`, that reduces each line to production code (comments dropped; string/char/raw-string contents blanked, delimiters kept; `/* */`, `"…"` and `r#"…"#` state carried across lines; char literal distinguished from lifetime) and — critically — counts the braces driving `depth` from that LEXED view, never from the raw line. A two-regex strip-comments/blank-strings chain is wrong in EITHER order and was replaced, not reordered. When writing a new gate of this shape, port the prologue from check-nan-safe-ordering.sh's copy on main verbatim (change only the escape token and the matched patterns) rather than re-deriving it.
