candidates.content: Gotcha (solar_challenge_platform, task 688 plan revalidation, 2026-10-07): an architect revalidation session that dies mid-measurement can leave its experiment uncommitted in the task worktree. In that case the branch had been rebased at 18:59, but all five plan files held the full RED+GREEN change set, modified at 19:18-19:20, with no live session in the worktree. Before revalidating, run `git status --short` and compare file mtimes with the branch reflog. If the leftovers match the plan, measure with them, then `git checkout --` the files so the implementer starts on a clean tree.

Dark-factory plan revalidation gotcha (solar_challenge_platform, task 732, 2026-10-06): when the orchestrator rebases a task branch onto a new main ("rebase (pick)" entries in git reflog), the done plan steps keep their pre-rebase commit SHAs, which are no longer ancestors of HEAD. Map them with `git range-diff <old-base>..<old-tip> <new-base>..HEAD` (an `=` row means content-identical), then re-point each step with plan-tools mark_step_done(step_id, <new sha>). mark_step_done changes only the status and commit fields and refuses a SHA that HEAD does not contain.

solar_challenge_platform gotcha (2026-10-12, task 984 architect): a follow-up task may cite commit SHAs from another task's branch that the orchestrator later rewrote when it rebased that branch before verify. For example, task 805's 7dc3b6b and 4251141 became 694febb and 8ad3152. A missing SHA (`git branch -a --contains <sha>` prints nothing) does not mean the work is gone. Find the equivalent commit by subject with `git log --oneline main..task/<id>`. The rebase is logged as a `verify_phase_rebase` event, with old_base and new_base, in /home/leo/src/solar-challenge-platform/.worktrees/.task-meta/<id>/iterations.jsonl.

solar_challenge_platform architect gotcha (dark-factory, measured 2026-10-07): a sibling can land on main after a task's worktree is cut, editing the same lines. If the task branch has zero own commits (`git rev-list --count main..HEAD` = 0), fast-forward it with `git merge --ff-only main` before planning, so the implementer edits current code. Without that, the first EXECUTE iteration runs on the stale base, because the inter-iteration rebase skips iteration 1, and the verify-phase rebase then conflicts. The fast-forward is safe: rebase_before_verify (default true) re-records base_commit to main before verify, so the review diff (`git diff <base_commit>...HEAD`) covers only the task's own commits.

Dark-factory gotcha (solar_challenge_platform, task 309, 2026-10-03): when an escalation handler rebases a task branch onto main, plan.json's step commit SHAs still name the pre-rebase commits, which are no longer ancestors of HEAD. To fix the plan, pair each old SHA with its rebased commit where `git show <sha> | git patch-id --stable` matches, then re-record each step with mark_step_done(step_id, new_sha). The tool accepts already-done steps and checks the SHA is reachable with `git merge-base --is-ancestor`.

solar_challenge_platform gotcha (observed 2026-10-07, task 517): a resumed architect session that hits a usage limit can leave an uncommitted throwaway prototype in the task worktree. The re-dispatched architect inherits those edits, and they would corrupt the TDD RED steps. Run `git status` before planning. If src edits appear that nobody committed, find their origin in the prior session's transcript (.task/claude-config-<task>/projects/*/<session>.jsonl), save `git diff` to /tmp, then revert with `git checkout -- <files>`.

Plan-revalidation gotcha: before re-invoking the architect, the orchestrator may rebase the task branch onto main, which rewrites every step commit, so the plan's done steps point at SHAs that are on no branch (check with `git branch --contains <sha>`; compare old and new with `git patch-id --stable`). Re-point each step with plan-tools mark_step_committed(step_id, <rebased sha>) after replaying it first-hand. You can replay without touching the worktree: `git archive <sha> | tar -x -C /tmp/<dir>`, then run the worktree's `.venv/bin/python -m pytest <test> -p no:cacheprovider` inside that snapshot.

Plan-revalidation gotcha (task 325, 2026-09-25). The revalidation prompt's "Files Changed on Main Since Your Plan → Overlapping" list can name files whose only change came before the plan was written. It flagged models/property.py and api/routers/properties.py for task 304's merge 67375c8, even though the plan had recorded 67375c8 as plan-time main and already planned for it. Hypothesis: the list is computed from the branch's cut point, not from plan-time main. Before rewriting a plan, run `git diff <plan-time-main-sha> HEAD -- <flagged files>`. An empty diff means there is no real drift. Then refresh any stale branch-state wording in the analysis via update_plan_metadata and call confirm_plan; do not rebuild the plan.

Branch-era commit SHAs do not survive the merge flow in solar_challenge_platform: the merge rebases or amends task branches, so a plan or reuse item that cites a branch commit can point at a SHA that main never reaches. Example: task 299's split commits 73139f6 and 2819a85 landed on main as 6e7050b and 5a539d2 (merge 3d74313). Before citing a commit as a model, run `git merge-base --is-ancestor <sha> main`; if that fails, list `git log <merge>^1..<merge>^2` to find the rebased equivalent.

solar_challenge_platform architect gotcha (task 870, 2026-10-07): an agent-followup task (metadata.spawned_from=<parent>) is filed while its parent is still in progress. It carries no Taskmaster dependency on the parent, so it can be dispatched before the parent's branch merges. Before planning one, check that the parent's commits named in its description are ancestors of main (git merge-base --is-ancestor <sha> main). If they are not, and the follow-up describes the parent's new behaviour (e.g. a docstring reworded to match it), call report_blocking_dependency on the parent instead of planning against main.

solar_challenge_platform gotcha: agent-followup tasks (metadata.spawned_from=<N>, source=agent-followup) are filed with NO Taskmaster dependency on the task that spawned them, so one can be dispatched while its parent is still unmerged. Before planning one, check that the parent's artifacts are on main (git cat-file -e main:<path>; git merge-base --is-ancestor <parent sha> main). Example: task 797 was dispatched on 2026-10-06 at main 7fcfeac. It re-points docs to billing/money.py::MONEY_ROUNDING, but that file existed only on the unmerged task/518 branch (fe7dac2), so the planner reported a blocking dependency on 518.

Observed on task 270 (2026-09-26): when the orchestrator rebases a task branch onto a newer main before a plan revalidation, .task/plan.json keeps the pre-rebase step commit SHAs, and those are no longer ancestors of HEAD. During revalidation, confirm each rebased commit has the same `git patch-id --stable` as the recorded one, then re-point it with plan-tools mark_step_done(step_id, full_sha). mark_step_done changes only the status and commit fields. Do not use mark_step_committed for this: it also prepends a [COMMITTED sha] tag to the step description.

Gotcha (dark-factory architect re-dispatch, solar_challenge_platform, task 747, 2026-10-07): an architect can be re-dispatched onto a task whose plan is already complete. In 747's case two earlier architect sessions ended on the infra error "Your organization has disabled Claude subscription access for Claude Code" (one after confirm_plan); the orchestrator logged no invocation_end and retried. Before exploring, check .task/plan.json for `_finalized_at` and read the tails of the prior sessions' transcripts under .task/claude-config-<task>/projects/*/*.jsonl. If the plan is complete, verify it against the moves on main (git diff --stat <metadata.json base_commit> main) and call confirm_plan() again rather than create_plan. confirm_plan's own docstring sanctions this revalidation flow, and create_plan re-initialises the plan.

Plan revalidation gotcha (observed on task 507, 2026-10-07): the 'Your Previous Plan' JSON in a revalidation prompt can be stale. An earlier, interrupted revalidation run had already called create_plan, so .task/plan.json on disk held different design decisions and reuse items, only 2 of the 9 steps, and no _finalized_at. replace_plan_step on a step missing from disk fails with "Step 'step-N' not found in plan." Read .task/plan.json first, add the missing steps with add_plan_step, and align them with the on-disk design decisions, which cannot be removed.

Gotcha (solar_challenge_platform, observed on task 938, main 1b647d3): an agent-followup task filed during a parent task's review/amendment pass is created with dependencies [] even when its description is "measured at" a commit that exists only on the parent's unmerged branch. Task 938 cited 7cb8ba0 (task 892's amend, branch task/892 at 634923f, 892 still in-progress), and the module-level `import pytest` / `from datetime import datetime, timezone` it builds on were absent from main. Before planning such a follow-up, run `git merge-base --is-ancestor <cited sha> main`. A non-zero exit means use report_blocking_dependency on the parent task rather than planning against main. Planning against main would conflict textually with the parent's diff.

AMENDMENT to 01a41fe3 (plan-revalidation overlap-list gotcha): the hypothesis is now MEASURED. On task 252 (2026-09-27), the revalidation prompt listed 87 files in total: 3 overlapping, 30 shown and "54 more". That is exactly `git diff --name-only 887a472 main`, where 887a472 was the branch's merge-base when the plan was last written. The plan had since been revalidated against main 1fa1422, and `git diff 1fa1422 main` touched only 5 files, none of them in the plan. So the list is computed from the plan-time branch cut point and can re-flag changes a prerequisite already integrated. Measure `git diff --name-only <last-revalidated-main> main -- <plan files>` before changing any step.

Plan revalidation after orchestrator rebases: .task/verify/attempt-N.*.summary.json records a started_at time but no commit SHA. To tell which branch tip a green verify ran on, compare that time with the 'rebase (finish)' timestamps in `git reflog show --date=iso task/<id>`. Separately, the step commit SHAs in plan.json become unreachable after every rebase; `git range-diff <old_base>..<old_tip> <new_base>..<new_tip>` maps them to their current equivalents, and `=` marks confirm the task diff is unchanged.

As of 2026-06-21 the solar-challenge-platform repo is far more advanced than a stale git snapshot suggests: P1 (skeleton/S7), P2 (timeseries/S3), P4 (control/S2), and P5 (consent/S8) are ALL authored AND largely built on main; tasks 1-30 are mostly done. When picking up work here, query fused-memory get_statuses and `ls docs/prds/` and probe `src/solar_challenge_platform/` imports rather than trusting the session-start git status block — it lags reality by many commits.

A follow-up task can be filed by its parent's architect while the parent is still only a plan. Its symbols then come from the parent's plan, not from any commit, so `git log --all -S <symbol>` finds nothing. The parent's finalized plan (steps, design decisions, files) can be read at /home/leo/src/solar-challenge-platform/.worktrees/.task-meta/<parent_id>/plan.json, even while Taskmaster reports the parent as 'pending'. Use it to confirm which symbols the parent will add, then route with report_blocking_dependency. Seen 2026-09-25: task 298 (spawned_from=288) names 288's planned _span_from_record and _warn_if_reread_disagrees, and neither is on main 6a23ac1.

content: solar_challenge_platform revalidation gotcha (task 739, 2026-10-12): a requeued task's branch can be recreated from main (reflog 'branch: Created from main'), while its old plan still marks every step done. The old commits then live only on an archive branch named task/<id>-<UTC timestamp>, e.g. task/739-20261011T190218Z, which is not on main. Check `git log main..HEAD` and `git merge-base --is-ancestor <step commit> HEAD` before confirming such a plan. If the commits are absent, re-plan with create_plan and use the archive branch only as reference code to port.

candidates.content: When the plan-tools MCP server is missing from an architect session (ToolSearch finds no create_plan/confirm_plan; tracked by open task 4175, prior repros task 2942/2924/df_task_1993), the plan can still be delivered faithfully WITHOUT hand-writing plan.json: drive the server's own implementation functions in-process. Recipe (verified on task 4274, 2026-08-16): add orchestrator/src and shared/src to sys.path; from orchestrator.artifacts import TaskArtifacts; from orchestrator.mcp import plan_tools as pt; build artifacts = TaskArtifacts(worktree, TaskArtifacts.meta_root_for(worktree.parent, worktree.name)) — this is the identical meta_root the orchestrator and the stdio server both compute; then call pt._create_plan(artifacts, task_id, title, analysis, files), pt._add_prerequisite, pt._add_plan_step(step_id, step_type, description), pt._add_design_decision, pt._add_reuse_item and finally pt._confirm_plan(artifacts), asserting each returns status 'ok'. These are exactly the callables create_server() wraps as MCP tools, so schema validation, markup repair and the atomic writer all run normally. Run it with `uv run --project orchestrator python <script>`. Note _add_plan_step's step_type argument is stored under the key 'type' in plan.json. This supersedes the earlier advice that escalate_blocker is the architect's only channel when plan-tools is absent — escalate_info the infra gap, then deliver the plan this way rather than stalling.

Plan-tools MCP server lives at orchestrator/src/orchestrator/mcp/plan_tools.py — never orchestrator/src/orchestrator/agents/plan_tools.py, which does not exist despite reading as a plausible guess (it was mistakenly cited as "verified in code" in a committed decision record before review caught it). Spawned per-architect-invocation per-worktree as a stdio MCP server; registered at workflow.py:2208-2215. Has TaskArtifacts(worktree) access for atomic .task/<name>.json reads/writes. Exposes plan-construction tools: create_plan, add_plan_step, add_prerequisite, add_design_decision, add_reuse_item, update_plan_metadata, remove_plan_step, replace_plan_step, confirm_plan, mark_step_done. Also exposes DECLINE-protocol tools (verified 2026-08-30): report_blocking_dependency (~:1856), report_task_already_done (~:1890), report_false_premise (~:1986), report_ready_to_merge, report_unactionable_task — each delegating to a writer on orchestrator/src/orchestrator/artifacts.py::TaskArtifacts (write_blocking_dependency ~:443, write_already_done ~:492, write_false_premise ~:578). Use this server for any new architect-only tools that need per-worktree state — adding to fused-memory MCP would be overscoped (it's project-wide and lacks worktree context). CAVEAT: EvalMetrics (orchestrator/src/orchestrator/evals/metrics.py) has no field for the terminal report_* kind, and run_architect_eval reads only artifacts.read_plan() before cleanup_eval_worktree shutil.rmtree's the meta root — so decline artifacts are destroyed unread, and in persisted eval result JSON a deliberate protocol decline is byte-identical to a content failure (outcome == 'done' either way); terminal cause is recoverable only from transcript forensics.

FACTS verified 2026-09-21 on main 2c78539443, each a trap for a design that assumes otherwise: (1) `roles.py::_PLAN_STATUS_TOOLS` (= ['mcp__plan-tools__mark_step_done']) is held by IMPLEMENTER, DEBUGGER AND SIMPLE_TASK — adding a tool there reaches the simple fast path, which has no frozen plan; use a separate list. (2) `escalation/src/escalation/server.py::get_escalation` and `::get_task_escalations` are SYNC `def` tools; `git_ops.py::GitOps.find_equivalent_commit` is async and takes (worktree, base_sha, target_sha) — an archived escalation record carries no base_sha; `GitOps.find_task_citation_commit(tid)` matches a TASK ID in a commit subject, not a cited commit's subject, so it returns one commit per task. (3) `resolution_class='moot-terminal-subject'` has TWO live producers — `harness.py::_ESCALATION_REVALIDATION_RESOLUTION_CLASS` (the L2 revalidation sweep) and `fused-memory/scripts/derive_orphaned_recon_escalations.py::RESOLUTION_CLASS` — so it is never a clean filter key; `escalation/tests/test_models.py::test_resolution_classes_contains_exactly_the_legal_values` asserts SET EQUALITY, making any RESOLUTION_CLASSES addition a two-site edit. (4) `plan_tools.py::_params_of` raises unless the callable's first parameter is named `artifacts`, so it cannot introspect the registered FastMCP tool closures; there is no tool registry (create_server registers all 16 unconditionally). (5) `plan_tools.py::_REPAIRABLE_PLAN_FIELDS`/`_walk_repairable` address exactly one level (plan[collection][i][field]); nested prose gets inbound MarkupGuardMiddleware coverage but no stored-damage repair; `artifacts._normalize_plan` and `_read_plan_repaired` keep unknown step keys. (6) The ARCHITECT prompt contains no suite-outcome forecast solicitation; the RED/GREEN/count predictions in plans are emergent. (7) Task 5637's plan step types are test,impl,test,impl,test,impl,impl — its step-2 'GREEN for step-1' defect is semantic, not a step-graph shape.

GOTCHA when a test DERIVES a candidate set from a module's live surface (dark-factory, task 4176, orchestrator/tests/test_plan_tools_markup_repair.py): deriving "which entry points write X?" by AST-walking each module-level function's body for calls to a mutating method is SOUND but admits too much — an INTERNAL helper can legitimately call the same method without being a callable/probeable entry point. In plan_tools, `_read_plan_repaired` calls `artifacts.write_plan` on its read-repair write-back path (true on main post-c005fabb00) yet returns a bare `(plan, facts)` tuple, not a status envelope; a behavioural probe that then calls it dies on `result.get('status')` with `AttributeError: 'tuple' object has no attribute 'get'` — an opaque crash naming neither the candidate nor a remedy.

FIX, two independent halves, both worth applying:
(1) Intersect the derived set with the surface the server ACTUALLY REGISTERS, itself derived rather than hand-listed: `frozenset(t.name for t in asyncio.run(plan_tools.create_server(TaskArtifacts(Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()))).list_tools()))`. Measured on the live tree: fastmcp 3.2.2, `list_tools` IS a coroutine function, server build ~0.07s, 16 names returned. Wrap in `@functools.lru_cache(maxsize=1)` if the caller re-derives per row. `asyncio.run` is safe in a test file with no `async def` test (`asyncio_mode = "auto"` governs async test FUNCTIONS only, so no loop is already running).
(2) Make the probe assert `isinstance(result, Mapping)` before reading the envelope, with a message naming `impl.__name__` and both remedies (derivation regressed / envelope contract changed). Keep this even after (1): it stays valid however the derivation later changes.

Expose the intersection set as a PARAMETER (`registered: frozenset[str] | None = None`) rather than a hardcoded call, or a test cannot stage a synthetic writer — the honest simulation of "a new tool was registered AND its impl added" is `registered=_registered_plan_tool_names() | {'probe_writer'}`, the exact parallel of the `fn.__module__ = target_module.__name__` forgery such tests already use to defeat a `__module__` guard.

Naming/signature guards (`_`-prefix, first param is `artifacts`) do NOT substitute for either fix — they happened to overlap here, which makes the classification accidentally correct rather than correct.

INFRA INCIDENT (task 2924 architect, 2026-07-22): The repo-defined `plan-tools` FastMCP server (orchestrator/src/orchestrator/mcp/plan_tools.py:501; exposes create_plan/add_plan_step/add_prerequisite/add_design_decision/add_reuse_item/confirm_plan/report_*) was NOT injected into the architect agent's MCP config. The worktree .mcp.json listed only playwright/escalation/fused-memory; ToolSearch across connecting servers found none of the plan-tools; plan.json (symlink to .worktrees/.task-meta/2924/plan.json) was empty. A prior architect session (bc5154d0) for the same task hit the identical absence and stalled SILENTLY (only Bash/Grep/Read/ToolSearch, zero escalations). Lesson: when create_plan is uncallable and writing plan.json directly is forbidden, the architect's only channel is escalate_blocker(category=infra_issue) — the sanctioned rejection tools (report_unactionable_task etc.) are themselves part of the missing plan-tools server. Escalate immediately rather than burning the turn budget re-searching.

GOTCHA (dark-factory, measured 2026-08-30 while planning task 4176): a "completeness" machine-check whose CANDIDATE SET is a hardcoded list does not close the completeness gap — it moves it one level up, and the displaced gap is invisible because the check itself is green.

THE CASE. orchestrator/tests/test_plan_tools_markup_repair.py gained `test_no_plan_writing_tool_is_an_undeclared_alternate` (commit de46b1c153, on main) to prove the converse of a soundness check: whatever is OBSERVED writing a `_REPAIRABLE_PLAN_FIELDS` cell must be declared in that row's `also_written_by`. Sound design, behaviourally probed, mutation-verified in its own docstring. But it iterates `_PLAN_WRITING_TOOL_NAMES` — a hand-written 11-name tuple referenced in exactly two places and tied to NOTHING. A new plan-writing entry point that nobody hand-adds to that tuple is never swept, so its row silently under-reports: verbatim the original defect, one layer out. Grep for "who else reads this constant" is the cheap tell — a candidate set with no derivation and no second consumer is load-bearing on human diligence alone.

THE FIX SHAPE. Derive the candidate set from the live module surface; delete the tuple. Do NOT close it by widening a behavioural probe to every entry point — that couples the harness to signatures it does not own, to observe a provable no-op.

TWO TRAPS when deriving "which functions write X" by introspection:
1. Parse each function's OWN source off the live object (`vars(mod)` + `inspect.getsource` + `textwrap.dedent` before `ast.parse`), NOT the module file. A file-level AST parse cannot see a monkeypatched synthetic writer, which makes the completeness property itself untestable — you lose the one test that proves a new writer gets caught. Also guard `obj.__module__ == mod.__name__` so an imported helper is not mistaken for an entry point (and, in the test, set `__module__` on the injected probe or your own guard excludes it).
2. Use an `ast.Call`/`ast.Attribute` walk, never a substring scan. In this area the docstrings and comments discuss `artifacts.write_plan` in prose repeatedly, so a text match classifies READERS (e.g. `_read_plan_repaired`) as writers.

STRUCTURAL FACT worth keeping: `TaskArtifacts` mutates plan.json through exactly three methods — `write_plan`, `update_step_status`, `mark_step_committed`. The five `report_*` plan-tools entry points call only their own separate-artifact writer (`write_blocking_dependency` / `write_already_done` / `write_ready_to_merge` / `write_unactionable_task` / `write_false_premise`) and provably cannot touch a plan cell — which is why excluding them from a plan-write sweep is a machine-checkable consequence, not a hand-waved exclusion.

Infra observation (2026-07-20, task df_task_1993 architect run in .eval-worktrees): the plan-tools MCP server was absent from the architect's toolset — this run's .mcp.json only wired playwright/escalation/fused-memory, and ToolSearch found no create_plan/confirm_plan. The architect role REQUIRES plan-tools (orchestrator/src/orchestrator/mcp/plan_tools.py, normally stdio-spawned per invocation). If this recurs across architect invocations it is a systemic wiring gap, not eval-specific. The plan was still delivered faithfully via the in-process TaskArtifacts + plan_tools._* code path (see the paired procedural_knowledge note); .task/plan.json for df_task_1993 is finalized and schema-correct.

Completed: _repair_plan_schema shows the architect 6000 chars of a 30k-char plan, tells it to rewrite the whole file from that, then stamps _finalized_at on the result
Description: DEFECT. `workflow.py::TaskWorkflow._repair_plan_schema` builds `plan_dump = json.dumps(broken_plan, indent=2)[:6000]`, instructs the architect to "restructure the existing plan content ... write the result to `<plan_path>` using the Write tool", and emits **no truncation marker**. On the success path it then calls `repaired_plan.setdefault('_finalized_at', ...)` — stamping the plan-completeness marker on a plan the architect reconstructed from a fifth of the original. The sibling `_replan` has the same context problem without the truncation.

MEASURED (sweep F rows S5-4, S7-3, S8-10, S5-10):
- **1,712 of 1,880 live plans (91%) exceed 6,000 chars; mean plan 30,179 chars.** The typical repair sees ~20% of the plan and overwrites the other 80% away.
- Cap set by `9eb2fa888a`, 2026-04-12 — pre-1M-window. The largest briefing this fleet has ever emitted is 26k tokens, ~2.6% of the current window.
- S5-10: `_replan` and `_repair_plan_schema` build raw f-strings that bypass `BriefingAssembler` entirely — **no memory context, no `_agent_identity` block, no task text**. The prior entry lists the test-file edits as _EXPECTED_PAIRS, the literal `len(table) == len(_EXPECTED_PAIRS) == N`, _ORIGINATING_TOOL, _COLLECTION_SCHEMA_TOOL_NAME, and _observed_plan_keys' collection loop plus _seed_plan_through_real_writers. Also present, and easy to miss because NO test fails when you skip them:

1. `_PLAN_WRITING_TOOL_NAMES` — docstring: "Every MCP-registered plan-tools impl that can reach ``artifacts.write_plan`` ... at all — the full candidate set". Consumed only by test_no_plan_writing_tool_is_an_undeclared_alternate, which sweeps each named tool against every table row looking for an UNDECLARED alternate writer. A new writer omitted here is simply never probed; the tuple's completeness claim becomes false silently.
2. `_NON_PROSE_PARAMS` — docstring: "Tool PARAMETERS that name no prose plan key and may therefore NEVER receive a recovered string". Members are enumerated by rationale (task_id/files are not prose; prereq_id/step_id/step_type are stored under different plan keys). A new non-prose parameter (e.g. a `path`) belongs here.
3. `_alternate_writer_changed_the_cell`'s argument synthesizer — a per-parameter-name if/elif chain that RAISES AssertionError on an unrecognized name, with the message "extend the probe rather than silently probing nothing". So edit (1) is INERT WITHOUT THIS: the moment you add a tool to _PLAN_WRITING_TOOL_NAMES, the sweep calls the synthesizer with that tool's parameter names and dies unless you add branches for them. Prose params fold into the existing shared tuple ('description', 'analysis', 'title', 'decision', 'rationale', 'what', 'where', 'how', ...) — giving a prose param its own elif branch is flagged by ruff SIM114 (combine if branches).

TWO SEEDING CONSTRAINTS, if the new writer is a REMOVER rather than a pure appender. `_seed_plan_through_real_writers` is the single fixture for both _observed_plan_keys and the sweep, so the seed must satisfy the new writer's own guards AND leave room for the sweep to call it AGAIN on the same fixture. For task 4807's _drop_plan_file (refuses to drop the last remaining file), that meant seeding THREE files instead of one: one consumed by the seeding drop, one by the probe's drop, one left over. Synthesize the probe's `path` as a path the seed really declares, or the probe bounces off the unknown-path guard, reports changed=False, and passes vacuously.

So a harness-corrupted files argument crashes at the pydantic boundary, unrecoverable by tool code, in two shapes — files as a stringified array -> 'files Input should be a valid list [type=list_type]'; files dropped -> 'files Missing required argument [type=missing_argument]'. The harness (Claude CLI subprocess) is out-of-repo/unfixable; the only controllable, testable surface is the server. Fix: relax files to `list[str] | str | None = None` in create_plan (and update_plan_metadata) so the body runs, add a module-level _coerce_files() that json.loads-then-splits string shapes back into a list, and for a dropped None in create_plan return an actionable status:error naming the split-call workaround. artifacts.write_plan does NO files coercion, so plan_tools.py is the correct layer. Boundary tests MUST use await tool.run({...}) (via create_server+get_tool), NOT tool.fn — only tool.run exercises the pydantic path where the crash lives.

GOTCHA (dark-factory, measured 2026-09-07 while planning task 4597): plan-tools' markup boundary carries FOUR separate byte-equality pins asserting plan.json is unchanged across a refused tool call, and any new write-side channel on that boundary falsifies all four at once. They are in orchestrator/tests/test_plan_tools_markup_guard.py: test_the_tool_body_never_ran (~L337), test_a_rejection_defers_the_stored_repair_and_never_loses_it (~L471), test_the_unrepairable_path_writes_nothing (~L988), and test_a_rejection_still_writes_nothing_to_the_plan (~L1549). The last one is the trap: it was added by task 4744 alongside the markup JOURNAL specifically to catch this, and its docstring says outright that "a new write-side channel is exactly the kind of change that could quietly breach it". Budget for amending them, and amend them deliberately rather than by deleting the assertion.

WHAT THE PINS ACTUALLY PROTECT, which decides whether an amendment is legitimate. They are a PROXY for a property about VALUES, not about bytes. create_server's own comment justifies REJECT_WITH_REPAIR because "forwarding a repair would write a guessed-at document that every later reader inherits", and shared/src/shared/mcp_markup_middleware.py's header says "no middleware-repaired value can ever reach plan.json". So a channel writing GUARD-OWNED bookkeeping that contains zero caller-supplied bytes (tool and param from the invoked tool's own registration and schema, outcome from the guard's closed vocabulary, a timestamp from the clock) does not breach the property; a channel writing anything derived from the caller's payload does. Amend to a content-level invariant — parse before/after, pop the new key, assert the remaining documents are equal — which is strictly stronger in the direction that matters than asserting the file did not change.

TWO ADJACENT FACTS worth having before touching this surface. (1) The middleware accepts exactly ONE fact_sink and its _call_sink wraps the whole sink in a single try/except, so a composed multi-sink MUST isolate each arm itself or one channel's outage silently takes the other down. (2) Anything stored into plan.json must NOT contain the fact record's `pattern` or `misclose` — those ARE envelope markup, plan.json is embedded verbatim into four architect-facing prompts (briefing.py revalidation + completion, workflow._replan, evals/judge) and is edited by agents, and scripts/sweep_toolcall_markup.py walks dead-lane plan.json RECURSIVELY (_repair_dict over list(node.keys()), _string_holes over node.items()), so a stored literal is counted as fresh corruption by the census that exists to measure the leak.

GOTCHA (dark-factory, measured 2026-08-29 while planning task 4807): adding a new PROSE field to plan.json carries two non-obvious obligations that nothing enforces at write time, and both are easy to miss because plan.json has NO schema whitelist at all (artifacts.py::write_plan dumps the dict verbatim; read_plan is json.loads + _normalize_plan, which only renames steps aliases; there is no pydantic model or jsonschema over it, so an additive key silently "just works" and looks finished).

OBLIGATION 1 — REGISTER IT IN THE REPAIR TABLE. orchestrator/src/orchestrator/mcp/plan_tools.py states it outright at the _REPAIRABLE_PLAN_FIELDS declaration: "Adding a prose field to the plan schema means ADDING A ROW HERE — nothing infers the surface." The walk is deliberately table-driven, not a recursive dict walk, so an unregistered prose field gets NO read-time envelope-markup repair. Registering costs a _PlanField row, a MappingProxyType _*_TARGETS mapping, a _COLLECTION_SCHEMA_TOOL entry, AND edits to orchestrator/tests/test_plan_tools_markup_repair.py, whose machine-checks pin the table exactly (_EXPECTED_PAIRS, a literal `len(table) == len(_EXPECTED_PAIRS) == 9`, _ORIGINATING_TOOL, _COLLECTION_SCHEMA_TOOL_NAME, and _observed_plan_keys' collection loop, which asserts each collection came back non-empty and so needs the new writer added to _seed_plan_through_real_writers).

OBLIGATION 2 — THE SHAPE DECIDES WHETHER IT CAN BE REGISTERED AT ALL. _PlanField expresses exactly two shapes: a top-level scalar (collection=None) or a LIST OF DICTS (collection='<key>'); _walk_repairable skips anything that is not a list. So a MAP-shaped field (dict[str, str]) is structurally un-registerable. Today every plan collection is a list and every scalar is a string — there is no map-shaped field in the plan, and the first one would silently fall outside the repair surface. Prefer list-of-dicts for any new prose collection.

THE RELATED TRAP, same family: shared/src/shared/mcp_markup_middleware.py::_first_markup_argument SKIPS NON-STRING VALUES ("the leak is a serialization defect in the caller's own text emission, so it can only ever land in a string"). MarkupGuardMiddleware is live on the plan-tools server and is the designated INBOUND guard for agent prose, but it therefore covers only FLAT STRING tool parameters. Passing agent-authored prose inside a dict- or list-valued argument bypasses it entirely. Two consequences point the same way: a new plan-tools tool taking prose should declare flat `str` params (like add_design_decision(decision, rationale) / add_reuse_item(what, where, how)), not a batch/map parameter — and a later refactor to a batch signature silently drops the guard, so say so in a comment.

Gotcha: test_roles_ancestry_check.py::test_role_holds_every_mcp_tool_its_prompt_names scans only role.system_prompt, so dispatch-time prompts are never checked against a role's tool grants. Task 5356 found that workflow.py's inline _repair_plan_schema prompt told the ARCHITECT to use the Write tool, which ARCHITECT.disallowed_tools forbids, and the _replan prompt asked for a direct plan.json write. Build new architect prompts in BriefingAssembler, and pin their tool contract with a per-builder test like test_briefing.py::TestPlanTighteningPromptToolGrants.

Study-team shape that worked for a decision-ready verify-speed study on reify (2026-09-10, ~2.9M subagent tokens, ~4.5 h wall): phase 1 = five parallel scoped agents (telemetry baseline / opus; build-profile experiments on a personal lane / opus; prior-art + constraints over both repos and both task DBs / opus; web pricing / sonnet; trimming-selection feasibility / opus), each writing a ~500-800-line markdown report to the scratchpad with every number sourced; phase 2 = the parent reads all five reports, then forks three Fable synthesis lenses (reduce demand; add capacity; select/batch/tier) that inherit the full context, then forks a Fable critic that re-derives arithmetic, checks tried-and-rejected registers, verifies ≥10 task ids with get_task, greps mechanism claims in source, and flags double counting. The critic found two BLOCKERs the lenses had missed (a 35%→5% docs-only miscount from DF's .py/.rs-only source classifier, and an offline lane that exits 64 on every run) plus an inverted dependency direction and an already-filed task — a critic pass is mandatory before a report is written. Rules that kept it safe: read-only in both repos, sqlite mode=ro only, never git stash, a personal (non-pool) worktree for measurements with teardown verified, benchmark under load and stamp uptime + PSI per timing, label every estimate and vendor claim, cite prior art by task id and status, and state 'pick up X' rather than 'new' where a pending task exists.

Completed: TimescaleStore.write must slice large batches: a >13,107-row buffered flush exceeds Postgres' 65,535 bind-parameter limit and wedges ingest forever
Description: FINDING (review 20260928T154500, data-plane deep read; CONFIRMED by reproduction on timescale/timescaledb:2.20.0-pg16 at HEAD 417e306).

WHAT'S WRONG: src/solar_challenge_platform/timeseries/timescale_store.py::TimescaleStore.write (~L283-323) builds ONE multi-row `pg_insert(...).values(values)` for the whole row list, 5 bind parameters per row. src/solar_challenge_platform/ingestion/buffer.py flush (~L206) passes the ENTIRE store-and-forward buffer to store.write. Postgres rejects any statement with more than 65,535 parameters, so once more than 13,107 rows are buffered (e.g. after a store outage) every flush attempt fails with "number of parameters must be between 0 and 65535" and the rows stay pending forever — even after the DB recovers. Reproduced: a 14,000-row buffer failed on every retry, all rows pending.

FAILURE SCENARIO: 1k homes x 8 metrics at 1-min cadence: any store outage > ~72 s (10k homes: ~7 s) buffers past the limit. The process stays alive (systemd Restart=on-failure never fires), the buffer grows to its 2M cap and drops the oldest rows; a restart discards the buffer, whose messages were already acked to the broker. This violates the #1 fail-safe/self-heal convention (review/briefing.yaml) and falsifies the scaling PRD's "2M rows ≈ 15 min outage tolerance".

FIX: write in slices of at most batch_max_rows (or ≤ 13,000 rows) per statement, clearing each slice from the buffer once its transaction commits (or use unnest-array / COPY insert as the settlement insert already does), preserving ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING idempotency and WriteResult totals. Add a @timescale test that buffers > 13,107 rows through a simulated outage and asserts all rows land after recovery with no duplicates.

Completed: Settlement HH integration drops the interval straddling each half-hour boundary: interpolate at boundaries so off-grid sample phases don't lose energy/coverage
Description: FINDING (review 20260928T154500, data-plane deep read; CONFIRMED by demonstration at HEAD 417e306).

WHAT'S WRONG: src/solar_challenge_platform/timeseries/rollups.py (~L178-199) integrates FLOW_POWER trapezoidally only between samples INSIDE each half-hour, so the stretch between the last sample before a boundary and the first after it is counted in neither half-hour. The simulator's ticks land exactly on the HH grid, which hides it; a real device's won't.

DEMONSTRATED: constant 2 kW, 60 s samples offset by 30 s → 0.9667 kWh and coverage 0.967 per HH (should be 1.0 / 1.0) against a 0.95 period floor; at 90 s cadence coverage lands exactly on 0.95. Billing energy comes from registers (unaffected), but coverage drives UNDER_METERED holds (until task 221 narrows the gate), the portal coverage note (409) and ops.

FIX: linearly interpolate the power at each HH boundary from the straddling samples (only when the gap is within the 90 s max-gap contract) and split the straddling segment between the two half-hours; bump METHOD_VERSION (persisted rows keep their version — auditable); keep idempotency/byte-identity for re-runs at the new version. Keep the pure reference (rollups.py) and the in-DB materialiser consistent (the reference is what the materialiser is checked against). Tests: phase-offset fixtures at 30/60/90 s cadence give exact 1.0 kWh / 1.0 coverage for constant 2 kW.
Analysis: THE DEFECT (measured at branch base 652c079). rollups._settle_half_hour's FLOW_POWER branch integrates trapezoids only between consecutive samples inside the closed window [hh_start, hh_end]. The interval straddling each half-hour boundary is therefore counted in neither half-hour. At any off-grid phase, constant 2 kW settles every half-hour to energy = coverage = 1 - cadence/1800:
- 0.98333 at a 30 s cadence;
- 0.96667 at 60 s;
- 0.95 at 90 s, exactly the 0.95 period floor.

WHERE THE ARITHMETIC LIVES. There is ONE settlement arithmetic, rollups._settle_half_hour. Both public entry points use it:

- settle_half_hours: the bulk path.

Billing push architecture (review 20260928T062907):
- No flow re-prices an already-billed statement. DirectDebit.recalculate (billing/dd.py) has no production caller; status.py only calls schedule().
- scp-bill's idempotency pre-check returns the existing BillingRun without a re-push.

candidates.content: dark-factory test-infra observations (2026-05-27): (1) The active git hooks path is core.hooksPath=/home/leo/src/dark-factory/.git/hooks, which contains ONLY .sample files — so NO pre-commit/pre-merge-commit hook actually fires right now (the repo's hooks/ dir with pre-commit/pre-merge-commit is NOT the configured path). This contradicts older memory that said core.hooksPath=hooks; commits and direct main merges currently need no --no-verify. (2) The root .venv is Python 3.13.9 (not 3.12 as some plans state), editable to main src — running pytest/pyright with /home/leo/src/dark-factory/.venv/bin/python from the main checkout picks up branch edits with no PYTHONPATH dance. (3) orchestrator addopts bakes in `-n auto --dist loadgroup`; pass --override-ini="addopts=" to run a focused file single-threaded. escalation has no addopts (serial). (4) Standalone pyright on test files reports spurious `Import "pytest" could not be resolved`, and escalation reports fastmcp unresolved, orchestrator reports uvicorn unresolved — all pre-existing env noise, not real errors.

Git hooks DO fire inside dark_factory task worktrees, discovered 2026-09-21 and contrary to the common assumption. `.git/config` sets `core.hooksPath = hooks` — RELATIVE — and git resolves a relative hooksPath against the WORKING-TREE root, so every worktree runs its own checked-out `hooks/pre-commit` rather than the shared `.git/hooks` (which holds only *.sample). Confirmed in `.worktrees/1074/hooks/`: executable pre-commit, pre-merge-commit, project-checks, setup.sh; `git -C .worktrees/1074 config --get core.hooksPath` returns `hooks`; GIT_TRACE on `git hook run pre-commit` shows `run_command: hooks/pre-commit`. `hooks/pre-commit`'s `.task/` strip already runs on EVERY branch. AS OF LATER THAT DAY (task 5722, 2026-09-21; see a0dd1e8b), `project-checks` itself also runs on every branch — only its main-only checks (ruff, the two staged-file style checks, pyright) remain gated behind `[ "$branch" = "main" ]`; the merge-lane ratchet audit inside it is universal. A hook can also read the declaration: `.worktrees/<id>/.task/plan.json` exists as a real readable file from the worktree cwd.

Caveats before building on this: `hooks/` is checked out from the branch's own BASE commit, so a hook change reaches only tasks branched after it lands; and an agent can bypass with `--no-verify`.

This was assessed as a seam for detecting out-of-scope edits at commit time and judged MARGINAL — a bash hook has no judgment and no widen path, so rejecting a commit is strictly worse than detection-plus-briefing (dark_factory task 4371 as re-scoped). It would only be worth it in WARN mode.

Separately and worth recording so nobody re-proposes it as free: `agents/briefing.py::BriefingAssembler.build_completion_judge_prompt` ALREADY receives both the plan and the diff in one prompt — the perfect seam for a judgment-bearing over-delivery check — and is SWITCHED OFF. `judge_after_each_iteration` defaults False and is unset in dark-factory-orchestrator.yaml; runs.db shows ZERO `judge`-role invocation_end events since 2026-09-01 against 963 reviewer_comprehensive and 886 implementer.

dark-factory's git pre-commit hook lives at hooks/pre-commit (core.hooksPath=hooks, NOT .git/hooks). On the main branch it execs hooks/project-checks which runs, in order: ruff check over all 5 packages (shared/escalation/fused-memory/orchestrator/dashboard); an asyncmock assertion-style check on STAGED fused-memory/tests/*.py only; a bare-magicmock check on STAGED tests/*.py only (honors `# noqa: bare-magicmock — <reason>` on the preceding non-blank line, or use the mock_orch_config fixture / MagicMock(spec_set=pydantic_spec(...))); and pyright run per-package from fused-memory, orchestrator, dashboard (the slow "3× pyright" — can exceed the 2-min Bash ceiling). Because of the slow pyright, commit to main via `setsid bash -c '... git commit --only -F <msgfile> -- <paths> ...' &` then poll the log + `git rev-parse HEAD`, rather than a foreground commit. The hook explicitly forbids --no-verify (it also silently strips .task/ from staging). CORRECTED 2026-09-21 (task 5722; see a0dd1e8b): on a non-main branch, hooks/project-checks ALSO runs now, but only its universal merge-lane ratchet audit (a staged-scoped `git diff --cached`, no ruff/asyncmock/bare-magicmock/pyright) — ruff, the two staged-file style checks, and pyright remain main-only.

Cross-project "reify ships primitives, dark-factory wires consumers" (D8) seam pattern: reify-side shell scripts (setup-worktree-debug-port.sh, seed-warm-lane.sh) are invoked by the dark-factory orchestrator RELATIVE TO THE PROVISIONED PROJECT WORKTREE (e.g. `<worktree>/scripts/seed-warm-lane.sh`), not from dark-factory's own tree. The orchestrator wiring must be fail-open when the script is absent (non-reify projects / test repos) — mirror `git_ops._provision_reify_debug_port`. In tests, STUB the script (write a `#!/usr/bin/env bash` file into the test repo's scripts/ dir and commit it); the reify-side script need not exist in dark-factory at all.

Where a repo-wide checker can and cannot be wired into dark-factory's verify (established 2026-09-18 while designing the INV-12 gate). (1) The root `dark-factory-orchestrator.yaml` `lint_command` is effectively never invoked: with `module_configs` non-empty — the normal case, and always under `merge_verify_breadth: "full"` — verify runs each member's own `orchestrator.yaml` lint_command instead; the root one runs only on the module-config-less fallback path. A check added only to the root lint_command does not gate. (2) Lint legs run checkers as bare `python3`. Under `orchestrator/src/orchestrator/verify.py::_target_subprocess_env` (strips VIRTUAL_ENV, drops the venv bin from PATH) that is the system interpreter (3.12), which cannot import first-party `shared` modules: `python3 -c "import shared.task_statuses"` raises ModuleNotFoundError, while a bare `import shared` misleadingly SUCCEEDS as a namespace-package shadow of the member directory. `fused-memory/scripts/check_bare_magicmock_config.py` works there only because it is stdlib-only, a contract `hooks/project-checks` states explicitly; `scripts/check_dashboard_unit_parity.py` is likewise run as bare `python3` by `scripts/setup-host.sh`. Adding a `shared` import to either breaks every lint leg and pre-commit, or host setup. `scripts/merge_lane_metrics.py` already imports `shared.safe_io`, so its documented `python scripts/merge_lane_metrics.py --check` form fails under the scrubbed env; the working form is `uv run --project shared python scripts/<x>.py`. (3) The reliable venue for a tree-pure repo-wide gate is a guard test under `scripts/tests/` or `tests/scripts/`, which run once per merge via `uv run --project shared pytest` under breadth=full — the precedent is `orchestrator/tests/test_merge_lane_ratchet.py` and the silent-fallthrough gate. (4) `scripts/orchestrator.yaml` and `tests/scripts/orchestrator.yaml` have no `check_bare_magicmock_config.py` leg, so "wire it beside that checker" skips `scripts/` itself. (5) lint_command strings are mirrored by live-config drift tests (`_verify_config_corpus.py` with 7 consumers, `tests/scripts/test_contributing_lint_command_drift.py`) and a chain-shape assertion, so editing them is a multi-site lockstep change.

A REPO-WIDE LINT LEG IN dark-factory's `lint_command` IS NEVER DIFF-SCOPED — so any new whole-file check must be green on the ENTIRE existing corpus on the day it lands, or it turns every merge red forever. `verify._scope_to_keyword` / `verify_cmd.scope_to` preserve the `&& python3 ...` tail of a lint chain VERBATIM (`'ruff check'` is in `verify_cmd._TAIL_PRESERVING_KEYWORDS`), and the root `dark-factory-orchestrator.yaml` sets `merge_verify_breadth: "full"`, so a red tail leg blocks every merge repo-wide. Measured while costing a line-pin guard (esc-3815-7, 2026-08-24): a whole-file version would have stood at 1646 violations across 442 files — not "trips sometimes", but permanently red.

TWO MORE FACTS ABOUT THE ENFORCEMENT SURFACE, both counter-intuitive:
  - `hooks/pre-commit` `exec`s `hooks/project-checks` ONLY on branch `main`, and the merge worker lands via `update-ref`, which bypasses hooks entirely. Of the last 200 first-parent commits on main, 85 were merge commits (hook-free). So the pre-commit leg reaches almost NO agent-authored code; `lint_command` is the only enforcement that reaches task branches.
  - The house pattern for a new check is `fused-memory/scripts/check_asyncmock_assertion_style.py` and `check_bare_magicmock_config.py`: stdlib-only, invoked via plain `python3` (not `uv run`, to skip env resolution), `ast`/`tokenize`-based rather than raw regex, STAGED-files-only in the hook ("no repo-wide ambush"), repo-wide leg in `lint_command`, and a `# noqa: <check-name> — <reason>` suppression on the PRECEDING non-blank line (inline trailing is deliberately ignored). A check whose hits are mostly inside DOCSTRINGS cannot reuse that suppression convention, because "the preceding non-blank line" there is prose.
  - The repo also has a ratchet-baseline genre for pre-existing violations: `shared/tests/silent_fallthrough_allowlist.py` and `shared/tests/config_dir_archival_allowlist.py`, both keyed WITHOUT line numbers — the former on `(relpath, qualname, content_hash)` where content_hash = `sha256(ast.unparse(node))[:12]`, explicitly "invariant under pure line-number drift".

Ratchet substrate in dark-factory as studied 2026-09-18: there are two ratchet idioms, not one. SCALAR — `scripts/merge_lane_metrics.py` (1,634 lines, ~40% generic / ~60% bound to the merge-lane cluster: committed JSON baseline, strict `now > was`, equality permitted, derived cluster totals that defeat rename-gaming, ceilings only for paths/qualnames absent from the baseline, params-mismatch and incomplete-enumeration both refuse with exit 2, exit codes 0/1/2) and the in-source per-file budgets in `fused-memory/scripts/check_bare_magicmock_config.py` (`_DATACLASS_DOUBLE_DEBT`, `_WALL_CLOCK_DEADLINE_DEBT`). MULTISET — `shared/tests/silent_fallthrough_scan.py::reconcile_against_allowlist` and the loop-blocking ledger: keys `(relpath, qualname, sha256(ast.unparse(node))[:12])` with no line numbers, `collections.Counter` subtraction so byte-identical duplicate sites are legitimate, mandatory per-entry reason, and ENFORCED stale-entry removal (the scalar idiom has no stale detection). Known hole in the scalar idiom: `--write-baseline` re-measures and writes with no comparison against the committed baseline, so a task that raises a measure and regenerates absorbs its own increase; the only guard is the README text and review of the JSON diff. Task 5406 (in-progress) owns that hole; task 5414 (pending) will widen the module's enumeration for pinning counts. `orchestrator/tests/test_merge_lane_ratchet.py` reaches the module's private names (`_file_complexity`, `_parse`, `_sweep_test_tree`, `_build_parser`, monkeypatches `CLUSTER_PATHS`, `complexipy_version`), so relocating those symbols breaks it. Precedents worth reusing: a `scripts/` module importing another by bare name (`scripts/systemd_unit_parity.py`, imported by three `check_*_unit_parity.py` guards); `orchestrator/tests` importing a `scripts/` module via `sys.path` (pyright resolves it through `extraPaths = ["../scripts"]`); and the rule stated in `tests/scripts/module_budget_family.py` — shared NON-guard helper modules are fine, a guard importing another guard is not.

In the dark-factory orchestrator suite, when a repo-relative fallback path is added to production code (e.g. GitOps._resolve_warm_lane_script's dark-factory warm-lane script dir), it must be seamed through an env var read at CALL time and pinned at a guaranteed-absent directory by an autouse conftest fixture. The established pattern is autouse _isolate_orch_config / _isolate_warm_lane_script_dir for suite-wide isolation plus a named opt-in factory fixture (code_default_config / df_warm_lane_script_dir) for the tests that genuinely exercise resolution. Reading the env at call time rather than import time is what makes monkeypatch.setenv work without a module reload.

candidates.content: reify's `hooks/pre-merge-commit` gates ONLY the `main` branch, exactly like `hooks/pre-commit`: its body is `branch=$(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD); if [ "$branch" != "main" ]; then exit 0; fi` BEFORE the `DF_VERIFY_ROLE=merge verify.sh all --profile both --scope all` call (the hook's own header says so: "Worktree branches skip the gate for speed... the orchestrator's task-branch merges are not main and are gated by the orchestrator's own verify"). CONSEQUENCE for the routine reconciliation merge (`git merge main` FROM a task branch, when main has drifted mid-task): `--no-verify` there bypasses NOTHING — the hook would have exited 0 on that branch anyway — so it is neither a gate skip nor something to caveat in a handoff. Do NOT confuse this with the opposite direction: merging a task branch INTO main (land.sh / manual `git merge --no-ff` while ON main) is where the hook actually runs the full gate, and `--no-verify` there IS the forbidden unsanctioned main move. Complements memory efe6f295-716a-46c2-8196-afa59ed6acc1 (same early-exit shape in `hooks/pre-commit`) and 157cef6e-8fbf-431b-aff4-74f456823345 (the orchestrator merge worker uses advance_main plumbing and never fires this hook at all). Reify OPERATIONAL learning (2026-06-24): how to land a DOCS-ONLY commit on main when the orchestrator is running and the main-gate hook is ENFORCING. The main-gate hook (hooks/reference-transaction + hooks/main-gate-lib.sh) can be in ENFORCE mode EVEN WHEN the shell var REIFY_MAIN_GATE_ENFORCE is unset — it printed 'main-gate ... ENFORCE on — aborting transaction' and aborted a `git merge --ff-only` of a docs commit onto main. WHY ff-merge is rejected: a fast-forward does NOT run the pre-commit hook, so `main_gate_mark` (which sets the one-shot sentinel that sanctions the ref move) is never called → the move is 'unsanctioned' → aborted. THE WORKING PATH for docs: a DIRECT `git commit` on main. pre-commit runs the verify gate (for a docs-only/.md change, affected-crates=none → it prints 'verify.sh: nothing to verify (action=all scope=staged)' and is ~instant), passes, and calls main_gate_mark itself → 'sanctioned main move' → commit lands. This is exactly how recent docs(prd) commits landed (single-parent commits directly on main, NOT --no-ff merges — verify with `git log --first-parent` + `git show --format=%P`). scripts/land.sh is UNUSABLE for this because it refuses on ANY working-tree dirt via bare `git status --porcelain` (counts untracked), and the shared main checkout always has other sessions' untracked PRDs/fixtures present; land.sh also runs the full --scope all gate. IMPORTANT: the temp-branch + `git merge --ff-only` pattern (feedback_ff_merge_vs_orchestrator) does NOT work under ENFORCE — for docs use direct-commit-on-main instead. Concurrent caveat: the shared main HEAD moves under you during a session (other sessions land constantly), so don't capture-then-assume a stale HEAD; commit directly and let pre-commit sanction it.

MAIN-GATE LANDMINE FOUND AND REMOVED (reify, 2026-07-30, esc-5870-3). /home/leo/src/reify/.git/config carried TWO core.hooksPath entries on consecutive lines: "hooksPath = hooks" then "hooksPath = echo". Within a single config file git takes the LAST value, so .git/config alone resolved to `echo` — which turns every git hook into a no-op, including hooks/pre-commit (which marks the main-gate sentinel) and hooks/pre-merge-commit (which runs the full --scope all --profile both verify gate). It was inert ONLY because a third, worktree-scoped value in .git/config.worktree re-asserted `hooks` and wins on scope precedence. That is a single point of failure: CLAUDE.md records that Claude Code's worktree feature clobbers core.hooksPath on every worktree enter, which is exactly why config.worktree exists as a defense — so one clobber would have silently disarmed the gate with reify.mainGate.enforce=true still set. The stray `echo` line was deleted; both remaining scopes now resolve to `hooks`. NOTE for anyone auditing this: merge/warm-lane worktrees have NO config.worktree of their own and inherit .git/config, so before the fix they would have resolved core.hooksPath to `echo` outright. That did NOT break the merge worker — 14 merges landed in the hours after the fix — so the merge worker's CAS path does not depend on those hooks.

LANDED jun8: reify hooks/reference-transaction now gates ONLY genuine main advances — old≠new AND both oids nonzero (hash-agnostic zero check via ${v//0/}). Housekeeping transactions on refs/heads/main are skipped silently before the sentinel/log/enforce logic: no-op (old==new), creation (old all-zero), deletion (new all-zero) — these are gc/pack-refs/fetch/worktree churn, not landings. Commit fbbb3e7180, merged to main as 91a8f0903e via merge queue (zero Rust changes; that landing was itself a --no-ff merge commit, so it was sanctioned). Proven end-to-end with the hook wired + REIFY_MAIN_GATE_ENFORCE=1 in a throwaway repo: `git gc`, `git pack-refs --all`, and a no-op `git update-ref refs/heads/main X X` all exit 0; a genuine UNSANCTIONED advance is blocked (exit 128, main unchanged); the same advance with the sentinel marked succeeds and consumes it; audit log records only genuine landings (zero housekeeping noise). test_reference_transaction_gate.sh: MAIN_LINE retargeted ONE→TWO (genuine), + scenarios g/h/i (no-op/create/delete allowed+silent even under ENFORCE) and j (housekeeping does not consume a pending sentinel). This is the prerequisite that makes ENFORCE safe for routine git maintenance. Supersedes the original Fix-2 hook which gated every main transaction.

GIT ON REIFY MAIN, two mechanics confirmed 2026-08-19.

(1) `git commit --amend` ON MAIN IS REFUSED by the main-gate reference-transaction hook, even when the commit you are amending is the tip and you authored it seconds earlier. The refusal reads: "HISTORY-REWRITE (non-fast-forward) main move <old> -> <new> — REJECTED (rewriting a landed commit strands concurrent task branches that rebased onto it; use REIFY_MAIN_GATE_BYPASS=1 for a break-glass rollback)", and git reports "fatal: ref updates aborted by hook". The working tree and HEAD are left intact. Do not reach for the bypass to fix a cosmetic commit-message defect — the stranding hazard is real because task branches rebase onto main continuously. Get the message right the first time, or land a follow-up commit.

The reify merge queue can land a branch as a LINEAR REBASE with NO merge commit — in which case the standard "did it land?" probes all give misleading answers, and content comparison is the only correct confirmation.

OBSERVED 2026-08-19, task 5623, request mr-f3101d03 (state=done). The queue entry carried `pre_rebased: false`, so the merge worker rebased the branch onto the then-current main ITSELF. Result: the branch's commits landed on main with NEW SHAs and main's tip became the branch's own tip commit. Consequences, all of which look like failure but are not:

  1. `git merge-base --is-ancestor task/<ID> main` -> rc=1. The LOCAL branch ref still points at the pre-rebase tip, which is genuinely not an ancestor. NOT evidence of a failed merge.
  2. `git log main --fixed-strings --grep="Merge task/<ID> into main"` -> EMPTY. There is no merge commit to find. The canonical rc=128 marker search assumes a `--no-ff` merge; a rebase landing produces none.
  3. `git branch -d task/<ID>` -> refuses, "not fully merged". Correct from git's view, misleading from ours. `-D` is required.

CORRECT CONFIRMATION — compare CONTENT, not ancestry:
    FILES=$(git diff $(git merge-base task/<ID> main)...task/<ID> --name-only)
    git diff task/<ID> main -- $FILES        # empty == fully landed
An empty diff over exactly the branch's own file set proves the work is on main, and is immune to SHA rewriting. Do this BEFORE any `git branch -D`.

Beware the naive whole-tree check: `git rev-parse task/<ID>^{tree}` vs `main^{tree}` will DIFFER even on a perfect landing, because main carries other tasks' work the branch never had. Restrict to the branch's own file set.

solar_challenge CLI probe technique (task 541 architect, measured 2026-10-11 on main 6bb51ac): to see which window `optimize configs` or `finance run` simulates, or whether it refuses a scenario before simulating, call tests._cli_fleet_simulator.invoke_cli(argv, simulate) with a simulate that records (start, end) and then raises a sentinel exception. No FleetResults is needed, and each run takes well under a second. The CliRunner result tells three outcomes apart:
- result.exception is the sentinel: the command reached simulation; optimize's first call is asked for the sweep's SimulationPeriod timestamps.
- result.exception is SystemExit(1): handle_errors refused, and its "Configuration error: ..." text is in result.output, stderr included.
- result.exception is a raw exception such as AttributeError: an unhandled crash.
