candidates.content: fused-memory test isolation gotcha (distinct from the dashboard/DashboardConfig one): `fused-memory/tests/conftest.py`'s autouse env fixture scrubs ONLY `CONFIG_PATH` — `DASHBOARD_KNOWN_PROJECT_ROOTS` is left ambient. Any fused-memory code path that resolves a project_root via `build_known_projects_map()` (models/scope.py) and then writes to `{project_root}/data/escalations` can therefore, under an operator shell or systemd unit that sets the var, escape tmp_path and file a real escalation into a LIVE operator queue during a test run. When adding such a path, add a module- or class-level `@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)` doing `monkeypatch.delenv('DASHBOARD_KNOWN_PROJECT_ROOTS', raising=False)` so each test opts in via `monkeypatch.setenv`.

fused-memory builds its project_id→project_root registries by deriving project_id from the directory BASENAME (models/scope.py:resolve_project_id) — used by build_known_projects_map (recon-cadence registry / harness _known_projects) and ProjectPrefixRegistry.from_roots (path-scope guard). The persistent per-project root list is the DASHBOARD_KNOWN_PROJECT_ROOTS env var on the INSTALLED fused-memory systemd unit (survives fused-memory restarts; the committed service templates default to this repo only). Consequence: renaming a project directory so its basename changes breaks recon + path-guard registration for that project_id (recon reads a dead git tree → ValidationError + UNKNOWN task_count_snapshot sentinel; path-guard churns refiles) unless the id is pinned elsewhere. Task 2813 fix: resolve project_id from <root>/dark-factory-orchestrator.yaml's project_id key first (basename fallback), so a rename that preserves the manifest id re-points recon instead of churning. Verified case: my_solar_challenge renamed /home/leo/src/my-solar-challenge → /home/leo/src/solar-challenge.

Until 2026-05-01, fused-memory.service did NOT export DASHBOARD_KNOWN_PROJECT_ROOTS, even though server/main.py reads it on startup. Effect: fused-memory's path-scope-guard / project-prefix-registry was effectively single-project (only dark_factory itself via PROJECT_ROOT) regardless of dashboard config. Fixed 2026-05-01 by adding the env to scripts/fused-memory.service.template AND ~/.config/systemd/user/fused-memory.service. Post-fix log line: "project_prefix_registry: built with 5 project(s); 21 prefix(es) total".

GOTCHA — fused-memory's shared `mock_config` fixture (fused-memory/tests/conftest.py) never populates `taskmaster`, and `FusedMemoryConfig.taskmaster` defaults to None. Any MemoryService code path gated on a resolved `config.taskmaster.project_root` is therefore UNREACHABLE under the `service` fixture in test_memory_service.py: the resolver returns '' and the guarded branch is skipped. That silently makes the positive case fail AND the negative case pass for the wrong reason. Fix in the TEST, not production: assign a real `TaskmasterConfig(project_root=str(tmp_path))` onto `svc.config.taskmaster` during setup (see `_mm_configure_project_root` in test_memory_service.py, task 3195). Note `TaskmasterConfig.project_root` itself defaults to '.', so it is the None SECTION — not the field — that produces the empty root; a configured deployment always has one.

Discovery (2026-04-27): before this session there was NO project_id↔project_root registry anywhere in the fused-memory codebase. event_buffer.get_active_projects() returns just project_ids (not roots); dashboard config had known_project_roots: list[Path] but no mapping to project_ids; the harness only ever knew its single configured project_root. Added build_known_projects_map and known_project_roots_from_env helpers to fused_memory/models/scope.py to fill this gap. Used by the harness (to populate stage.known_projects per cycle) and by server/main.py (to build the multi-project registry passed to TaskInterceptor).

In fused-memory/tests/test_stages.py, TestProjectIdValidation (test_run_allows_matching_watermark_project_id and test_run_succeeds_and_logs_debug_when_watermark_project_id_falsy) asserts MemoryConsolidator.run()'s result.stats via exact dict equality. Any new always-present stats key added to MemoryConsolidator.run() (e.g. task-2312, task-2029, task-2366) must be added to both of these literal dicts or the tests regress. Since that fixture's memory_service is an unconfigured AsyncMock(), any stat value derived from an unconfigured mock call return (e.g. count_memories_by_metadata()'s return) is opaque and must be matched with unittest.mock.ANY rather than a literal value.

Extends mem0 51853e5a (which covers the MANUAL-invocation case) with its unattended twin: when a script resolving the project registry via `build_known_projects_map` (fused-memory/src/fused_memory/models/scope.py:282) runs from its OWN systemd unit rather than an operator shell, a missing `DASHBOARD_KNOWN_PROJECT_ROOTS` fails SILENTLY, not loudly. There is no `unknown --project-id` abort — the map just collapses to `{dark_factory}` and the script processes one project while its logs and per-project census read as if the fleet were covered. Measured 2026-08-21 (task 2917): the var is NOT in /home/leo/src/dark-factory/.env (which these wrappers source), NOT in the systemd user manager environment, and lives ONLY as an `Environment=` line inside the installed ~/.config/systemd/user/fused-memory.service and the dashboard unit. So any NEW unit that needs the registry must import it explicitly — `systemctl --user show fused-memory.service -p Environment` then extract the var — rather than assuming the sourced .env provides it. That import is the right mechanism over hardcoding the 9-root list into a second committed unit, since the value is host-specific and would rot; in-repo precedent at skills/factory-init/scripts/find_escalation_port.py:57-63. Warn loudly when the import yields nothing: a narrowed single-project run must be visible in the journal.

Dashboard test isolation gotcha: setting DASHBOARD_PROJECT_ROOT alone does NOT isolate every DashboardConfig path. reconciliation_db, tickets_db, write_queue_db and write_journal_db resolve through DashboardConfig._runtime_data_dir(), which reads RECONCILIATION_DATA_DIR / QUEUE_DATA_DIR straight from os.environ and WINS over project_root; DASHBOARD_KNOWN_PROJECT_ROOTS separately makes DbPool fan out to extra checkouts. All three are ambiently present in practice (the orchestrator's managed fused-memory spawn injects the runtime dirs; the installed dashboard systemd unit sets the known-roots var). Use apply_isolated_env(monkeypatch, tmp_path) from dashboard/tests/_dashboard_helpers.py, which sets the root and DELETES all three, rather than a bare monkeypatch.setenv.

DASHBOARD_KNOWN_PROJECT_ROOTS is the canonical env var listing active projects for BOTH the dashboard AND fused-memory, despite the misleading "DASHBOARD_" prefix. Dashboard reads it via DashboardConfig.from_env() (dashboard/src/dashboard/config.py:92). Fused-memory reads it via known_project_roots_from_env() defined in fused-memory/src/fused_memory/models/scope.py:19 (constant KNOWN_PROJECT_ROOTS_ENV) and consumed by server/main.py:371 to build the path_scope_guard / project_prefix_registry. Format: comma-separated absolute paths, NO spaces (systemd parses spaces as assignment separators).

dashboard/tests/test_memory_evals_data.py house style (follow it when extending): the file imports no `pytest`, defines no `@pytest.fixture`, and uses no decorators at all — every tmp-tree is built by module-level `_*` helper functions taking `tmp_path`, and production imports happen INSIDE each test body rather than at module top. Route tests use the shared `client` conftest fixture plus `client.app.state.config = _make_config(tmp_path)` and an explicit `_<name>_cache_clear()` before each GET. Builtin fixtures (tmp_path, monkeypatch, caplog) are usable without importing pytest. Gotcha for cache tests: dashboard route builders are invoked via `asyncio.to_thread`, so patch them with a SYNC MagicMock — an AsyncMock will not work.

GOTCHA when adding a new optional dependency to fused-memory's MCP tool layer (dark-factory, found planning task 5151): do NOT reach it via `getattr(memory_service, '<attr>', None)`, even though `set_recon_ledger` / `getattr(self, 'recon_ledger', None)` is an established in-repo precedent. Every `delete_memory`/`consolidate_memories` test builds its service as a bare `AsyncMock()` (see `fused-memory/tests/test_delete_memory_citation_guard.py::_make_service`), so `getattr` returns an auto-attribute Mock rather than `None` — a new gate keyed on "is it wired?" would silently ACTIVATE inside ~40 tests that know nothing about it, holding an unawaitable fake. Add a keyword-only parameter to `create_mcp_server(...)` defaulting to `None` instead: "not wired" becomes unambiguous, every existing test and the reconciliation-disabled server stay byte-identical, and there is exactly one production enable-site (`fused-memory/src/fused_memory/server/main.py`, where the recon journal is already constructed at ~:754 beside the `set_recon_ledger` call). `ReconReportState`'s `journal=None` parameter is the precedent to follow, and its docstring states the property explicitly. Related: those same test files are policed by `tests/test_check_bare_magicmock_config.py` and `tests/test_check_asyncmock_assertion_style.py`, which reject an awaited child left as an auto-attribute — so any fake you do inject must declare its awaited methods as explicit `AsyncMock`s.

Offline/CLI callers of fused-memory internals: FusedMemoryConfig is a pydantic BaseSettings, so the BARE CONSTRUCTOR is the loader (server/main.py:521, maintenance/_utils.py:79) — there is no .load() or .from_yaml() classmethod, and a config path is supplied via the CONFIG_PATH env var that settings_customise_sources reads (config/schema.py:2047). Two adjacent signature traps: SqliteTaskBackend takes NO project_root constructor kwarg — project_root is an argument to get_statuses, which is a COROUTINE (backends/sqlite_task_backend.py:1662) — and TicketStore.get/.initialize are likewise coroutines (middleware/ticket_store.py:90,236). Also note RECONCILIATION_DATA_DIR defaults to './data/reconciliation' RELATIVE TO THE PROJECT ROOT, so a script run from fused-memory/ will not find tickets.db unless it is set absolute. Task 3381 hit all of these: each sat inside an `except Exception: continue` fallback, so the sweep did not crash — it silently resolved every authority to 'unverifiable' and would have reported a clean corpus. pyright caught them; the tests could not, because they inject the probe facade and never exercise the default path.

GOTCHA: `fused_memory.models.scope.build_known_projects_map(primary_root, extra_roots=None)` seeds its candidate list with `primary_root` BEFORE extending with the `DASHBOARD_KNOWN_PROJECT_ROOTS` roots, so an unset/unreachable env var yields a ONE-entry map, never an empty one. Any `if not known_projects_map:` degradation check is therefore unreachable in exactly the failure it looks like it guards — the caller silently narrows to the primary project and exits 0. Detect it instead by comparing resolved project IDS: `missing = [r for r in scope.known_project_roots_from_env() if scope.resolve_project_id_for_root(r) not in resolved_ids]`, and treat "env var unset" (primary-only coverage, expected on a single-project install) as a different, non-fatal case from "env var set but under-resolved". Do NOT compare COUNTS (`len(map) < 1 + len(named_roots)`): the live registry lists the primary root in the env var too, and the builder drops it as a duplicate project_id, so a count check cries degradation on every healthy run. Worked example: `fused-memory/scripts/sweep_orphan_flag_markers.py::_known_projects_coverage_issue` (task 2917).

The "unit reads DASHBOARD_KNOWN_PROJECT_ROOTS but was never wired to receive it" defect recurred on 2026-08-17 for scripts/fused-memory-flag-marker-sweep.service — the same class as the 2026-05-01 fused-memory.service miss. systemd user units do NOT inherit each other's Environment=, so a new per-project sweep/recon unit silently runs single-project (dark_factory only) while its census output reads fleet-green. Note the sweep unit's env cannot simply be copied from the committed template: per skills/factory-init/references/recon-registration.md the real multi-root list is a LOCAL setting on the installed ~/.config/systemd/user/fused-memory.service (9 roots as of 2026-08-17), while committed templates ship only __REPO_ROOT__. When adding such a unit, render its Environment= line at install time from the installed fused-memory.service and log the resolved project list at start-up so a one-project run is legible.

In fused-memory, when you add a NEW service read to an existing MCP tool in server/tools.py, every pre-existing test that builds `mock_service = AsyncMock()` without stubbing that new method will silently exercise the new code path with a truthy auto-created AsyncMock instead of a realistic value — so an "unchanged response shape" assertion stops testing what it claims. Explicitly pin the new method in those tests (e.g. `mock_service.count_memories_by_metadata = AsyncMock(return_value=0)`). Observed in task 3129 wiring grouped reads into get_memory_by_id: the child-count probe made test_happy_path_found take the grouped branch until the zero-child corpus was pinned.

Dashboard service file env var DASHBOARD_KNOWN_PROJECT_ROOTS controls multi-project aggregation scope and is read by both the dashboard and fused-memory (path-scope-guard / project-prefix-registry). Lives in three places that must stay in sync: dashboard/dark-factory-dashboard.service (deployed copy), scripts/dashboard.service.template, and scripts/fused-memory.service.template. As of 2026-05-01 the list is `<repo>,/home/leo/src/reify,/home/leo/src/autopilot-video,/home/leo/src/autotrade,/home/leo/src/know-live`. Comma-separated, no spaces — systemd treats spaces as assignment separators.

Test-environment facts in fused-memory that matter when the tracked embedder identity changes, verified 2026-10-11: (1) fused-memory/tests/conftest.py::_isolate_fm_config is an autouse fixture that re-pins CONFIG_PATH to the tracked fused-memory/config/config.yaml for every test. Pointing CONFIG_PATH at a modified copy therefore tests nothing; to learn which tests are coupled to the tracked identity, edit the worktree's own config.yaml in place, run the suite, then git checkout the file. (2) tests/test_config_schema.py::test_shipped_config_yaml_shares_one_openai_api_url_default requires the llm and embedder api_url defaults to be identical in both config.yaml and config-docker.yaml, so any change that gives the embedder its own endpoint must relax the embedder half of that test. (3) The fused-memory timer jobs do not go through the MCP server: scripts/fused-memory-flag-marker-sweep.sh runs sweep_orphan_flag_markers.py and scripts/memory-metadata-coverage-census.sh runs census_memory_metadata.py and retro_stamp_topics.py, each constructing MemoryService or Mem0Backend from CONFIG_PATH. Any identity that lives outside tracked config.yaml (an overlay set by a unit drop-in) is invisible to them unless their units get the same drop-in. (4) Merge verifies run fused-memory tests against the shared live stores under the tracked config identity, so a period when tracked identity and store width disagree needs a check that the default test selection stays green.

Discovery (2026-09-16): fused_memory MemoryService.initialize() is NOT read-only, so don't use it for dry-run or census scripts.
- It calls graphiti.initialize() with maintenance on: an index-build loop over every graph, plus the W6-epsilon startup identity scan, which REPAIRS dup-uuid edges (a write) and can contend with the live server's sweep.
- It also opens DurableWriteQueue at the cwd-relative ./data/queue and starts workers for any pending groups found there. The live fused-memory.service runs with cwd /home/leo/src/dark-factory, so a script run from fused-memory/ opens a different queue db (fused-memory/data/queue). Check that db has no pending rows before running.
For a truly read-only run: construct MemoryService(FusedMemoryConfig()), call only `await memory.graphiti.initialize(skip_maintenance=True)`, and use memory.mem0._get_async_qdrant() lazily.
Scripts outside the server must load secrets themselves (load_dotenv('/home/leo/src/dark-factory/fused-memory/.env')) and set CONFIG_PATH to the absolute config/config.yaml. Only server/main.py calls load_dotenv.

In fused-memory's server tests, memory_service is built as an unspecced AsyncMock, so any attribute chain you read off it (e.g. memory_service.classifier.classify(...).primary) silently yields a child Mock rather than a real value. Code in server/tools.py that reads a value off the service to make a control-flow decision must narrow it with isinstance() against the real type and treat a non-match as "unresolved", or ~40 pre-existing tool tests will start exercising branches they never configured. near_duplicate_guard.py's resolve_* helpers document this hazard as their motivating case.

GOTCHA (fused-memory tests, measured 2026-10-10, task 5547): passing a DICT-valued field as an init kwarg to FusedMemoryConfig does NOT replace the YAML value — pydantic-settings DEEP-MERGES init_settings over the YAML source. Since the autouse conftest pin makes every test's FusedMemoryConfig() load the tracked config.yaml, `FusedMemoryConfig(write_triage_project_calibrations={'dark_factory': {...}})` merged the test's entry with the shipped dark_factory entry, so a category map gained a key the test never wrote (the test went red only once config.yaml shipped that key). Remedy: key test entries on a name the shipped config can never carry (e.g. 'synthetic_project'), or set the leaf with object.__setattr__ on a constructed config, as the reload-tier tests do.

content: fused-memory test gotcha (task 5263): MemoryService.__init__ now reads DASHBOARD_KNOWN_PROJECT_ROOTS to seed its {project_id: project_root} registry, and the `service` fixture in tests/test_memory_service.py builds the service BEFORE the test body's monkeypatch.setenv runs. A test that needs the env var at construction must call the module helper `_mocked_service(mock_config)` from its body after setenv. The autouse conftest fixture `_no_inherited_project_registry` deletes the var, so every other test sees an empty seed.

candidates.content: GeometryProfileRequired gotcha for .ri sweep/extrude/revolve profiles: the compiler's static profile-precondition check (crates/reify-compiler/src/geometry.rs check_profile_arg) rejects an INLINE transformed profile operand like `sweep(translate(rotate(circle(3mm),1,0,0,90deg),24mm,0,0), helix(...))` with "geometry argument 'profile' must be a 2D Surface profile (Closed, Planar)". Reason: it only inspects operands that are FunctionCall CompiledExprs to a known geometry producer; a transform-wrapped profile's nested Surface is opaque to the static inference so it infers non-Surface and fails. Two things that PASS: (1) a bare direct Surface producer as the profile, e.g. `sweep(circle(3mm), helix(...))` (circle→InferredTraits::surface()); (2) any profile bound to a `let`/`param` — it compiles to a ValueRef and check_profile_arg skips ValueRef operands entirely (documented back-compat escape hatch). So to sweep a POSED profile in .ri, bind it to a let first: `let p = translate(rotate(circle(3mm),1,0,0,90deg),24mm,0,0)` then `sweep(p, helix(...))` (note: each geometry-typed top-level let in a structure becomes its own realization/mesh, so two lets → two meshes). Verified empirically on task 5342. A bare unposed `circle` still sweeps cleanly along a helix at the OCCT layer (MakePipe transports the section along the spine frame) — posing is only needed for an exact Pappus volume, not for sweep success.

Reify DSL gotcha: a sweep/extrude/revolve/loft PROFILE argument must be a `let`-bound binding if it is posed. An INLINE `sweep(translate(rotate(circle(3mm),1.0,0.0,0.0,0deg-90deg),24mm,0mm,0mm), helix(...))` fails to compile with "geometry argument 'profile' must be a 2D Surface profile (Closed, Planar)" — check_profile_preconditions (crates/reify-compiler/src/geometry.rs:1428) inspects FunctionCall operands, and first_geometry_arg_in_env cannot see through the nested combinator, so it falls back to InferredTraits::all() (dimension=Solid). Binding the posed profile to a `let` makes it compile to a ValueRef, which the deliberate permissive back-compat rule skips, and the same expression then compiles and evaluates clean. Note `rotate` on geometry takes 2 args (target, orientation) or 5 (target, ax, ay, az, angle) — never 3.

Reify compiler gotcha, verified 2026-09-03: the `GeometryProfileRequired` precondition (crates/reify-compiler/src/geometry.rs) requires a `sweep` profile operand that is a statically-known Surface producer to be Closed AND Planar, and an INLINE `translate(rotate(circle(...)), ...)` is a known-combinator FunctionCall whose nested profile is OPAQUE to that static inference — so it is REJECTED AT COMPILE TIME. The working spelling is a NAMED BINDING first: `aux let prof = translate(rotate(circle(r), 1,0,0, -90deg), ...)` then `sweep(prof, path)`, exactly as prj/printer_v01/dev_capstan.ri:139-142 does. crates/reify-eval/tests/harness_sweep/helix_sweep_e2e.rs:15-27 documents this as the explicit reason that test uses a bare unposed `circle(3mm)` rather than a posed one — which is precisely why that test is now a silent victim of the sweep-pose defect. IMPLICATION for any diagnostic that tells an author to pose their sweep profile: the message MUST also name the named-binding requirement, or the author who follows the advice inline lands straight in a second, unrelated compile error.

Reify `sweep(profile, path)` transports the profile along the spine EXACTLY AS POSED and never re-orients it onto the path start frame. Measured law (target/release/reify at main abeefbb62e, 2026-09-03): volume = (profile area) x (spine displacement . profile normal). rectangle()/circle() lower to a FACE in the XY plane with normal +Z, so sweep(rectangle(20mm,20mm), line_segment along +X) yields volume 0 m^3 — a CAPPED but zero-thickness body, NOT an open shell; the same call along +Z yields the correct 8e-5 m^3. The degeneracy is CONTINUOUS: 45 deg off-plane gives 5.657e-5, 5 deg gives 6.97e-6, 0.001 deg gives a valid 1.4e-9 sliver with no error, so an exact-coplanarity predicate is evadable by floating-point noise. pipe(path, r) is the contrast that proves it: pipe builds its own circle on the path start frame via wire_start_tangent + make_oriented_circle_face (crates/reify-kernel-occt/src/lib.rs:3296-3317), which is why pipe works and sweep looks broken. query_volume NEVER consults the recorded BRepKind — it calls BRepGProp::VolumeProperties on the TopoDS_Shape unconditionally (occt_wrapper.cpp:3991-3999) — so the hard-coded BRepKind::Solid stamp is causally INERT for volume() and cannot be the cause of any zero-volume sweep. AUTHORING RULE: pose the profile normal to the path start tangent AND bind it to a name first; an INLINE sweep(translate(rotate(circle(r),...),...), path) is rejected at compile time by the GeometryProfileRequired precondition because the nested profile is opaque to static inference. The working idiom is prj/printer_v01/dev_capstan.ri:139-142. TRAP: an unposed circle on helix(r, lead, h) sits only ~3 deg off in-plane and produces a NEGATIVE volume that volume() downgrades to Undef rather than 0. Adjudicated under esc-7248-3 / task 7248 on 2026-09-03: as-posed transport is the INTENDED contract, auto-orienting is REFUSED, and the fix is a typed error on a near-degenerate pose with an angular tolerance band.

Reify's `sweep(profile, path)` transports the profile ALONG the path EXACTLY AS POSED — OCCT's BRepFill_Pipe never re-orients it (unlike `pipe(path, radius)`, which builds its own circle on the path start frame via `make_oriented_circle_face`). So an XY-plane profile swept along an in-plane spine (e.g. `sweep(rectangle(20mm,20mm), line_segment(0mm,0mm,0mm, 200mm,0mm,0mm))`) produces a zero-thickness body and `volume()` reads exactly 0; the same profile against a +Z spine correctly gives 8e-5 m^3. The idiom is a POSED profile: `translate(rotate(circle(r), 1,0,0, -90deg), x0, y0, z0)` (see prj/printer_v01/dev_capstan.ri). Measured 2026-09-03 on task 7248.

Measured 2026-08-19 at main 5df2f9f1f1 with the prebuilt target/release/reify: loft() is still unrealizable from source, both pre-6188 failure modes intact. (a) loft(circle(500mm), translate(circle(250mm), 0mm, 0mm, 800mm)) is rejected at COMPILE time, rc=1, "error: geometry argument 'profile' must be a 2D Surface profile (Closed, Planar)" — despite geometry_traits_inference.rs:823 listing translate in the trait-preserving transform arm, so the inference arm alone does not make the profile precondition at geometry.rs:748 (violates_profile_requirement) pass. reify loft() root causes (verified 2026-10-04 at 107c9016fe): (1) compile-time 'profile must be a 2D Surface profile' for translate(circle(...)) is NOT translate semantics — geometry_traits_inference.rs `first_geometry_arg_in_env` filtered on result_type == Type::Geometry, but expr.rs types every direct geometry-builtin call as a dimensionless_scalar placeholder, so the operand was dropped and all() (Solid) assumed; fix = use `is_geometry_operand` (task #5385's predicate). Geometry profile-trait seam (PRD geometry-primitive-constructors task α / task 4155): extrude/extrude_symmetric/revolve/revolve_full/loft/loft_guided check PROFILE = Surface∧Closed∧Planar; sweep/sweep_guided/pipe check PATH = dimension=Curve (sweep/sweep_guided path is arg[1], pipe path is arg[0]). Reify collision-over-trajectory / swept-volume encoding (established printer_v01 O5 round, 2026-09-03; probe corpus /home/leo/.claude/fleet/sessions/dogfood-reify-1598289/probes/traj-probes/, in-anger use ToolDock in prj/printer_v01/printer.ri). No swept-volume primitive exists (hull/convex_hull/minkowski/extrude_along are silently undef under a green check; sweep/loft reject solids; sweep(2D profile, path) silently yields volume 0; pipe is the only correct swept constructor). The honest two-layer idiom: LAYER 1 (margin, report) `sweep(m, j, range, N)` + `flat_map(snaps, |s| [min_clearance(s, id_a, id_b)])` - exact and cheap but BLIND to full containment on any boolean-derived body (compound shapes), so never the gate. LAYER 2 (the gate) FK-pose the moving body per sample with `apply_transform(body, transform_of(snapshot(m, [bind(j, v_i)]), id))`, `union_all` the N copies into a sampled swept solid, and constrain `volume(intersection(swept, obstacle)) < 1mm^3`; sample pitch must be below the thinnest wall the body could tunnel through. Rules: one snapshot() per sample (sweep()'s result is untyped -> snaps[i] is a compile error); no list min/reduce, so per-sample clearance floors are spelled out as N constraints; every joint must be structurally distinct (identical axis+range joints alias to ONE DOF silently); all bodies top-level geometry lets named verbatim in body(m, "<let>", j) (#5439 sub bodies never reach snapshots); a LEAF sub's body read as `let x = self.leaf.body` (local frame, override honoured) is a valid body/apply_transform/linear_pattern operand, so a tool solid can be single-sourced; mark pose/swept/overlap lets `aux` so they realise hidden. `apply_transform(body, transform_of(...))` is the FK bridge that routes around #6007 without decomposing the Transform. The whole study (kinematic trio + volume) also evaluates on `reify check` with real verdicts (only FEA stays indeterminate). Cost in printer.ri: 9+11 samples of ~8-solid bodies added ~50 s to check and ~60 s to eval.

Wiring the GeometryProfileRequired profile-precondition check into the geometry consumers (task 4155, geometry.rs check_profile_preconditions) flags inline statically-known constructors at profile/path slots. Hex/wedge Phase A gap (found planning task 4746): NO production code converts a swept body (or its profile handle/op) into a `reify_solver_elastic::ProfileBoundary`. Task 2987 ("2D cross-section extraction + Gmsh 2D meshing") is marked done and its description claims it "extract[s] the cross-section profile (curve set)", but its commits only added `mesh_swept_profile_2d`/`mesh_plane_2d` (the ProfileBoundary→2D-mesh CONSUMER half) + re-exports. `GeometryQuery` has no boundary-curve/cross-section extraction variant; `SweptKind` carries only axis/length/angle; `ProfileBoundary{}` is built only in mesher.rs tests. Profile ops DO carry reconstructable literal data (RectangleProfile{width,height}, PolygonProfile{points:Vec<[f64;2]>}, CircleProfile{radius}, EllipseProfile{semi_major,semi_minor}), so reconstruction by walking realization ops/handles (like sweep_classifier::swept_kind_to_sweep_params does for SweepLinear path handles) is feasible but must be built.

Reify 2-D profile constructors (rectangle/circle by task 4160; polygon/ellipse by 4161) all use one pattern: compiler `CompiledGeometryOp::Profile{kind:ProfileKind}` (types.rs), distinct IR `GeometryOp::{Kind}Profile` + `Operation::Profile{Kind}` (reify-ir/geometry.rs), kernel execute arm storing `store_with_repr(BRepKind::Face)`, and a `(ProfileKind, ReprKind::BRep)` entry in register.rs occt_capability_descriptor. Surface inference via `InferredTraits::surface()` (convex=true) or `surface_nonconvex()` (general polygon). GOTCHA: engine_build.rs `compiled_op_repr` BREP_ONLY match (~line 1438) is NON-exhaustive with a conservative `None` catch-all — a new profile/curve Operation MUST get an explicit `=> Some(BREP_ONLY)` arm there or the dispatcher silently won't route it to OCCT. deps.rs and entities_phase.rs match `Profile{args,..}` kind-agnostically (no per-kind edit needed). Numeric profile tests live in reify-kernel-occt/src/lib.rs (real OCCT, OCCT_AVAILABLE-gated); compile→eval pipeline tests use MockGeometryKernel in reify-eval/tests/profile_2d_e2e.rs.

Swept-body → ProfileBoundary cross-section extraction (task 5218, the missing PRD-2987-step-1 producer) is best built by PURE op-stream profile sampling in reify-eval/src/sweep_classifier.rs, NOT a kernel query: all recognized SweptKinds (Extrude/Revolve/SweepLinear) reference a profile OP (RectangleProfile/CircleProfile/PolygonProfile/EllipseProfile, reify-ir geometry.rs:1025-1045) whose 2D geometry is fully in the op-parameter stream. Add `profile: GeometryHandleId` to SweptKind::Extrude/Revolve (SweepLinear already has it), resolve it via the ops/handles linear scan like swept_kind_to_sweep_params, and construct reify_solver_elastic::ProfileBoundary{outer, holes:vec![]} (holes are Phase B). A kernel GeometryQuery cross-section variant is unnecessary and would need new OCCT FFI (BRepAlgoAPI_Section — none exists) plus be an unconsumed orphan.

Three EXISTING in-tree Reify fixtures/tests are silent victims of the sweep as-posed defect (measured 2026-09-03, target/release/reify at main abeefbb62e), and task 7248 owns dispositioning them. (1) tests/prd-gate/fixtures/pnrg_envelope_spline.ri:43 — `sweep(circle(100mm), bezier(0,0,0, 500,800,0, 1000,0,0))`, every Bezier pole at z=0 so the whole spine lies in the circle's own XY plane: measured volume 1.775123576545368e-21 m^3 (numerically zero), area 0.597210694510573 m^2. It is a FLAT RIBBON, not the tube its own header claims ("a circle swept along a cubic Bezier path — the measurable spline surface"). Its chord-deviation numbers (100mm 0.003 / 50mm 0.007 / 20mm 0.013) are COMMITTED to docs/notes/precision-refine-envelope-calibration.md lines 70, 174, 185, 598 — repairing the fixture INVALIDATES those spline-class rows and they must be re-measured. Mitigating: the fixture header says "NOT wired into any probe set or auto-run gate", so no gate reds. (2) crates/reify-eval/tests/harness_sweep/helix_sweep_e2e.rs:45 — `sweep(circle(3mm), helix(24mm, 7mm, 63mm))`, an UNPOSED circle only ~2.7 deg off in-plane: volume() reads Undef because the kernel returns a NEGATIVE volume (self-intersecting body). The test passes today only because it asserts non-emptiness and never volume; its own header concedes "the posed, volume-accurate case ... is covered by the kernel integration test". (3) docs/prds/v0_6/fixtures/helix_sweep_dep_5342.ri:4 — `sweep(circle(0.4mm), helix(2.15mm, 0.8mm, 10mm))`, ~3.4 deg off in-plane, Undef by the same negative-volume route. CONTROL: posing the (2) circle normal to the helix start tangent yields 3.836681796674759e-5 m^3, matching pi*r^2*arc_length — same spine, same profile, orientation is the whole difference. UNAFFECTED and must not regress: dev_capstan.ri:142, printer.ri:279 (|t_hat . n_hat| ~ 0.999), and pnrg_envelope_sweep.ri:36 (measured volume 4.247708123442906e-3 m^3).

Task #5713's containment argument is REFUTED at the TYPE level, not just the repr level (measured 2026-09-03). #5713 assessed its BRepKind::Solid-on-open-SHELL mismatch as "latent, not user-visible" on the reasoning that the compiler requires sweep/loft profile args to be Surface-typed. But `reify check` ACCEPTS `sweep(<Curve>, <Curve>)` at exit 0 ("All constraints satisfied") despite the documented `fn sweep(profile: Surface, path: Curve) -> Solid` (docs/reify-stdlib-reference.md:556): `sweep(line_segment(0mm,0mm,0mm,20mm,0mm,0mm), <+Z spine>)` realizes a single 20mm x 200mm FACE (area 0.004 m^2) labelled Solid. Plain Sweep stamps BRepKind::Solid unconditionally on BOTH entry points — `GeometryOp::Sweep` (crates/reify-kernel-occt/src/lib.rs:3290-3295) falls through to the shared tail `Ok(self.store(shape))` where `store` hard-codes Solid (lib.rs:787-790), and `sweep_with_history` stamps it explicitly at lib.rs:2472 — while SweepGuided (call at lib.rs:3385) and LoftGuided (call at :3416) were fixed to use `brep_kind_of_shape` (lib.rs:660-673) + `store_with_repr`. Related tension to reconcile rather than add a third opinion to: `combine_sweep` (crates/reify-compiler/src/geometry_traits_inference.rs:477-487) already returns `dimension: GeomDim::Solid` together with `closed: false` for EVERY sweep result, so the compiler's static model and the kernel's repr stamp already disagree.

OCCT gotcha in reify (SI metres): at real mm-scale feature sizes (e.g. M5x0.8 thread, 0.8mm pitch), BRepOffsetAPI_MakePipe sweep of a non-circular axial-plane profile along helix() fails ("OCCT make_pipe: "), and Union(cylinder, MakePipeShell-swept helical ridge) returns a face-less COMPOUND with volume 0 — yet the identical composition at 10x/100x scale succeeds. OCCT's absolute sweep/BOP tolerances (~1e-4 m) are commensurate with sub-mm gaps; building at a normalised scale and finishing with a uniform GeometryOp::Scale(1/k) fixes it (measured: watertight solid, downstream 1x booleans consistent to 1.2e-5). For helical sweeps of non-circular profiles use SweepGuided with the Z-axis LineSegment as guide (exact screw frame, Pappus within 0.4%); MakePipe's CorrectedFrenet frame is torsion-minimising, not the helix screw frame.

Task 'Geometry dimensionality refinement (Curve/Surface/Solid) + Planar trait + profile-precondition diagnostic' completed. PRD: docs/prds/geometry-primitive-constructors.md task α (Phase 1 — the profile-trait seam; B+H integration gate).

Extend the SHIPPED geometry-traits framework (do NOT add a new value-type) so profile-consuming ops can reject solids at compile time:
1. Extend `InferredTraits` (crates/reify-compiler/src/geometry_traits_inference.rs:100) with a computed mutually-exclusive `dimension: GeomDim {Curve, Surface, Solid}` enum field + `planar: bool` (+ populate `closed` for profile constructors). Assign dimension in every existing per-op inference arm: curves→Curve, box/cylinder/sphere/tube/cone/torus/wedge + boolean/sweep/pattern/modifier results→Solid.
2. Declare a `Planar` marker trait (and the dimensionality marker names Curve/Surface/Solid) in crates/reify-compiler/stdlib/geometry_traits.ri (the seven markers already live there).
3. Add `DiagnosticCode::GeometryProfileRequired` + an `emit_geometry_profile_required` helper as a sibling of `emit_geometry_unbounded` (crates/reify-compiler/src/conformance/mod.rs:377).
4. Wire the profile-consumer compiler arms — extrude (geometry.rs:999), revolve (:1047), sweep (:1121), loft (:955), extrude_symmetric, loft_guided, sweep_guided, pipe — to check the argument's inferred refinement: extrude/revolve/loft require dimension=Surface ∧ Closed ∧ Planar; sweep/pipe path requires dimension=Curve.

PERMISSIVE BACK-COMPAT (load-bearing): raise the diagnostic ONLY when the operand's refinement is statically-known and mismatched (e.g. extrude(box(...)) — box is statically Solid). An unrefined Type::Geometry whose dimension can't be inferred (e.g. a `param p : Solid`) is ACCEPTED — must not break the ~existing extrude/revolve/sweep call sites.

User-observable signal: `extrude(box(10mm,10mm,10mm), 5mm)` emits error[GeometryProfileRequired] via `reify check`; AND `extrude(p, 5mm)` for `param p : Solid` compiles clean (permissive pin). These are the first + last rows of the PRD boundary-test sketch.
Consumer: tasks ζ, η (intra-batch); follow-up PRD geometry-2d-profile-ops.
Modules touched: crates/reify-compiler/src/geometry_traits_inference.rs, crates/reify-compiler/stdlib/geometry_traits.ri, crates/reify-compiler/src/conformance/mod.rs, crates/reify-compiler/src/geometry.rs

All 8 v0.1 Sweep variants in `reify_types::Operation` (SweepLoft, SweepExtrude, SweepRevolve, SweepSweep, SweepExtrudeSymmetric, SweepSweepGuided, SweepLoftGuided, SweepPipe) are profile-consuming — they take a 2D profile/curve as the geometric input, not a 3D body. Their input is not tracked in the ReprKind lattice (which only classifies kernel families: BRep/Mesh/Sdf/Voxel), so they are dispatched like Primitives: the caller passes `available = {demanded}` and the kernel's declared `(SweepExtrude, BRep)` etc. names only the produced output repr. Do NOT use SweepLoft as a same-repr counter-example (BooleanUnion is the right one). Commit 860c46fc7f specifically replaced SweepLoft with BooleanUnion for this reason.

In reify-compiler's compile_geometry_call (geometry.rs), the profile-precondition permissive seam works because an ident/param/let-bound geometry argument compiles to a CompiledExprKind::ValueRef in `compiled_args`, while an inline constructor like box(...) compiles to a CompiledExprKind::FunctionCall. The op-array geometry linkage (geom_refs/geom_ref(idx)) is a SEPARATE inlining mechanism. So a use-site check that inspects the arg CompiledExpr (statically_known_traits: FunctionCall→Some, else→None) rejects only inline-constructor mismatches (extrude(box(...))) and stays permissive for ValueRef indirection (extrude(p)/extrude(let_profile)) — no let-binding env resolution needed.

Coverage-gap pattern found in crates/reify-kernel-occt/tests/harness_occt: sweep_guided_integration.rs and loft_guided_integration.rs both build their circle profiles from GeometryOp::Arc (0..2pi), which yields a closed WIRE. But the DSL's circle(r) lowers to GeometryOp::CircleProfile -> make_circle_face -> TopoDS_Face, and reify-compiler REQUIRES sweep_guided/loft_guided arg0 to be a Surface (PROFILE_SLOT). So those suites were green while every DSL invocation of the op crashed. When writing kernel integration tests for an op that takes a profile, build it with GeometryOp::CircleProfile (the face the DSL actually produces), not Arc — otherwise the test exercises a shape no user can supply.

content: Since #6188 landed on main (ce2ef856a3, 2026-10-05), an INLINE posed sweep profile compiles and realizes. Example: `sweep(translate(rotate(circle(3mm),1.0,0.0,0.0,-90deg),24mm,0mm,0mm), helix(24mm,7mm,63mm))` gives one body of 3.836681796674759e-5 m^3, the same as the let-bound spelling (measured on a main-built reify at c620c005bd). The older rule that a posed profile must be bound with `let` because GeometryProfileRequired rejects an inline translate(rotate(..)) is OBSOLETE. A Curve profile is still refused at compile time.

candidates.content: solar_challenge mutation-test gotcha (measured 2026-10-09, pytest 9.0.3, task 532 amendment): pytest's --ignore=PATH drops PATH only when collection reaches it by walking a directory argument; a file named explicitly on the command line is collected anyway. So an OLD-vs-NEW script that runs `pytest tests/unit/test_web*.py --ignore=<new test>` still runs the new test, because the shell glob names it, and with -x the OLD run stops at the new test's failure, so the OLD result is contaminated. Build the OLD file list without the new module instead, e.g. `printf '%s\n' tests/unit/test_web*.py | grep -vxF <new test>`, or pass directories and use --ignore. Probe: `pytest A.py B.py --ignore=A.py --collect-only -q` still lists A.py's tests.

In my_solar_challenge, pytest marker deselection (-m 'not e2e') does NOT prevent collection-time ModuleNotFoundError: tests/e2e/*.py and tests/e2e/conftest.py import `playwright` at module top-level, so exclude e2e by PATH (--ignore=tests/e2e), not markers. CORRECTED 2026-09-28 (see 0b4183e0-c58f-42f9-a03c-5c4a487c94b1): the tests/unit/test_web*.py modules now call pytest.importorskip("flask") first, so a dev-only env collects them without error (they skip); `--extra web` is needed only to run them. tests/integration imports neither.

solar_challenge gotcha (measured 2026-10-01): the project's pytest addopts make `pytest --collect-only -q` print a <Module>/<Function> tree, not one node id per line. Grepping for '::' therefore counts 0. To compare test counts across branches, e.g. to check that an auto-merge lost no tests, read the 'N tests collected' summary line from `uv run --extra dev --extra web pytest <files> --collect-only -p no:cacheprovider`.

solar_challenge: to test pytest fixture/teardown behaviour that only a later test can observe (e.g. tests/conftest.py::_shutdown_job_managers), run the scenarios as an inner session with pytester (`pytest_plugins = ["pytester"]` in the test module; pytester.makeconftest(<real tests/conftest.py text>) + runpytest_subprocess). Use the SUBPROCESS runner, not the in-process one: pytester's in-process run restores sys.modules to its pre-run snapshot, dropping modules first imported during the run, and it shares the JobManager registry with the outer session. Also chdir to request.config.invocation_params.dir before the run: pytester moves cwd into an empty tmp dir, but solar_challenge.weather caches PVGIS data at the cwd-relative Path(".cache/weather"), so a web job would otherwise fetch from PVGIS. Measured on task 131, pytest 9.0.3: about 4 s of subprocess overhead.

solar_challenge procedural note (task 489 architect, 2026-10-05, uv 0.11.6). ~/.cache/uv holds the pytest 9.1.1 wheel, so a "newest pytest" check runs WITHOUT network: `UV_OFFLINE=1 uv run --no-project --isolated --with-editable '.' --with 'pytest==9.1.1' --with flask --with plotly --with pyarrow --with anthropic --with pytest-cov pytest <paths> -o addopts= -W error::pytest.PytestRemovedIn10Warning -p no:cacheprovider`. The locked pytest 9.0.3 defines PytestRemovedIn10Warning but lacks 9.1's parametrize-iterator and class-fixture-instance-method checks, so only the 9.1.1 run can show those. Separately: tests/integration/test_cost_recovery_calibration.py mixes in a @pytest.mark.slow class, TestPhysicsReconciliationColumn, that fetches the live PVGIS TMY. Any command naming that file without -m 'not slow' needs PVGIS, and it writes .cache/weather/tmy_*.csv under the cwd (gitignored).

solar_challenge pytest 9.0.3 gotcha (measured 2026-10-15 on main d20b2b6, task 797's architect): a path argument named BESIDE one of its ancestors is not collected when that ancestor's ignore rules exclude it. The explicit-path override of --ignore and collect_ignore holds only when no other argument is its ancestor.
- `pytest tests tests/e2e -m slow --collect-only`, with addopts' --ignore=tests/e2e in force, selected 93 ids and no e2e test (5430 collected). Reversing the order, `tests/e2e tests`, gave the same. `pytest -o addopts= tests -m slow` selected 95, including the 2 slow tests in tests/e2e/test_simulation_workflow.py (5725 collected). `pytest tests/e2e -m slow` alone selected those 2.
- `pytest -o addopts= tests tests/css_build -m slow` collected 0 css_build tests, because tests/conftest.py's collect_ignore names css_build; `pytest -o addopts= tests/css_build -m slow` alone collected its 3.
So to collect every test some mark selects, clear addopts for tests/ (this reaches tests/e2e), and collect each collect_ignore'd suite in its own run.

solar_challenge pytest node-id listing, an addition to memory d1bc03b3. That entry gives PYTEST_ADDOPTS="--collect-only --verbosity=-1" and notes that a plain -q prints a tree. Passing `--collect-only -qq` on the command line also works: two -q against the ini's single -v net to -q, which prints one `path::test` node id per line. That line is followed by a 'N tests collected in Xs' line whose timing varies between runs. So filter with `grep '::'` before diffing a before/after listing, as in `uv run --locked --extra dev --extra web pytest <file> -m 'not slow and not e2e' -p no:cacheprovider --collect-only -qq 2>/dev/null | grep '::'`. This was measured on pytest 9.0.3 at main 0017651 on 2026-10-05, by the task 458 architect. It proved a behaviour-preserving import hoist across three test files left their 187 node ids identical.

solar_challenge pytest gotcha: pyproject's addopts includes `-v`. So `pytest --collect-only -q` cancels out to default verbosity and prints a <Module>/<Function> tree, not node-ids. `-o addopts=` does produce `path::id` lines, but it also drops the ini's --ignore=tests/e2e. To keep addopts in force, use PYTEST_ADDOPTS="--collect-only --verbosity=-1" instead (see memory d1bc03b3-6722-4cd0-b9c0-b806b0e91f11). Separately, collecting the whole tree (2366 items) took about 34-40 s wall on the factory host (measured 2026-09-29), which is too slow for a guard test run in every verify.

solar_challenge test gotcha (task 309, measured 2026-10-02): pyproject's pytest addopts carry `-v`, and at verbosity >= 1 pytest's assertion introspection prints the FULL repr and diff of both operands of a failed `==`. pytest gotcha, verified 2026-10-05 by the task 490 architect (uv 0.11.6, CPython 3.12.3), from the wheels of pytest 7.0.0, 7.4.4, 8.0.0, 8.3.5, 8.4.2, 9.0.1, 9.0.3 and 9.1.1:
- Each PytestRemovedIn<N>Warning class exists only from pytest (N-1).0 through N.0.x. Pytest 8.x lacks PytestRemovedIn10Warning, and 9.1.1 already dropped PytestRemovedIn9Warning, which 9.0.x still had.
- A filterwarnings entry or -W naming a class the running pytest lacks stops pytest at startup with a UsageError, exit 4 (pytest 8.4.2 with error::pytest.PytestRemovedIn10Warning).
- pytest.PytestDeprecationWarning, the base class of every PytestRemovedIn<N>Warning, exists in all of these releases. So `error::pytest.PytestDeprecationWarning` parses on all of them, and on 9.1.1 it still errors on the parametrize-iterator and class-fixture-instance-method deprecations.
- To run solar_challenge's locked environment under a newer pytest without re-locking: `uv run --locked --extra dev --extra web --with pytest==9.1.1 pytest <paths> -p no:cacheprovider`. The --with overlay's pytest takes precedence, and uv.lock is untouched.

solar_challenge convention (task 263, 2026-10-01; on main once task/263 merges): a contract test that runs an orchestrator command verbatim in collect-only mode (dark-factory-orchestrator.yaml's test_command or an offline-lane job) goes through tests/_collect_only.py, not an inline subprocess.run. run_collect_only(command, cwd, *pytest_args, env=None) returns the CompletedProcess, with PYTEST_ADDOPTS=shlex.join(['--collect-only', '--verbosity=-1', *pytest_args]) set in a copy of env (default os.environ; a given env REPLACES os.environ rather than merging, which is how test_per_task_verify.py drops VIRTUAL_ENV). collected_node_ids(stdout) returns the '::' lines in order, and the requires_uv skipif marker goes per test in modules that also hold uv-free tests (module-wide pytestmark otherwise). tests/unit/test_collect_only.py pins the flag choices; the -q vs --verbosity=-1 mechanics are in memory d1bc03b3.

To list flat `path::Class::test[id]` node ids, e.g. to diff a module's tests before and after a refactor, use `pytest <file> -o addopts= --collect-only -q` or `--collect-only -qq`.

solar_challenge survey technique (task 238 planning, 2026-10-01): to learn which keys the test suite actually feeds into config.py's parsers, without editing the worktree:
1. Write a throwaway pytest plugin, e.g. /tmp/x/survey_plugin.py, that imports solar_challenge.config and replaces each parser attribute (setattr(cfg, name, wrapper)) with a wrapper that logs out-of-set keys plus os.environ["PYTEST_CURRENT_TEST"] to a JSONL file, then calls the original.
2. Run `PYTHONPATH=/tmp/x uv run --extra dev --extra web pytest tests/unit tests/integration -m 'not slow and not e2e' -p survey_plugin -o addopts= -q`.
Why it works: a -p plugin loads before conftest and test collection, so config.py's internal calls (resolved through module globals at call time) and later `from solar_challenge.config import X` imports in cli/web both get the wrappers.
Cost: 2663 tests in ~9 min. pytest-xdist is not installed, so run it backgrounded to a log file.

solar_challenge gotcha (measured 2026-10-11, task 652 amendment, pytest 9.0.3, CPython 3.12.3): do not quiet the suite's ~560 UserWarnings with `pytest -W ignore::UserWarning`. PytestDeprecationWarning's MRO is PytestDeprecationWarning, PytestWarning, UserWarning, DeprecationWarning, so the command-line filter swallows it and overrides pyproject's deprecations-are-errors filter. tests/unit/test_pytest_deprecations_are_errors.py::test_a_pytest_deprecation_fails_the_test_that_meets_it then fails with "DID NOT RAISE PytestDeprecationWarning" (rc=1 with the flag, rc=0 without, same tree), and that failure says nothing about the code under test. To read a long run's result, redirect it to a file and read the tail instead of filtering warnings; the full fast suite (`-m 'not slow and not e2e' tests/unit tests/integration`) took ~19 min.

solar_challenge test gotcha, measured by task 471's amendment on 2026-10-07. Pattern: a test proves that a timeout's process-group kill (os.killpg after Popen(start_new_session=True), as in tests/_verify_suite.py) leaves no child of the shell alive. Two traps make such a test pass falsely.
- If the shell hangs in `wait` on its background child, a kill that misses everything lets the shell live until the child exits. The child is then gone when checked.
- If the child inherits the suite's stdout pipe, communicate() blocks until the child exits. Again the child is gone when checked.
The fix: start the child as `sleep 120 >/dev/null 2>&1 &`. Write its pid with `echo $! > f.part && mv f.part f`. Hang the shell in its own shorter `sleep 30`, not `wait`. After the hang, poll os.kill(pid, 0) until ProcessLookupError, with a 10 s deadline. If the pid file is missing, re-run with a longer timeout, since under host load the shell may not yet have started the child.
Teeth, measured: a proc.kill() mutant and a start_new_session=False mutant each fail in about 40 s. tests/unit/test_verify_suite_helper.py::test_no_process_the_suite_started_outlives_a_hang implements this.

content: pytest 9.0.3 facts probed 2026-10-15 for solar_challenge's test harness. (1) The ini option `strict_markers = true` in [tool.pytest.ini_options] makes an unregistered mark (e.g. @pytest.mark.slwo) a collection error (exit 2, "'slwo' not found in markers configuration option"). Being ini rather than addopts, it survives dark-factory's `-o addopts=` reruns. (2) A mark added with item.add_marker in a subdirectory conftest's pytest_collection_modifyitems is seen by `-m` deselection and by get_closest_marker at run time. (3) `subprocess.run(shell=True, timeout=N)` kills only its direct child on timeout, so uv/pytest grandchildren survive. That is why solar_challenge's run_collect_only differs from run_verify_suite, which uses start_new_session + os.killpg.

d1a49ea2-a5f2-45f9-87ff-3b1cf5ba4b86.content: Merge-queue ghost mechanics, verified from dark-factory code on 2026-10-02. When suffix_graph.py::SuffixConflictTracker.bounce_conflicting_suffix_items bounces a request (real-conflict or cap-exceeded arm), it removes the request from _lane_buffers and resolves req.result to 'blocked', but it never calls SpeculativeMergeWorker._retire_item. The request therefore stays non-terminal in the ItemLifecycle registry, and snapshot()'s registry-sourced section keeps rendering it as 'queued', waiter_alive=true, head_of_line, until an orchestrator restart. merge_status(request_id) also answers 'queued' (live tier wins). merge_cancel answers "Request already finalized; cannot cancel." because it only consults the escalation server's _waiters map, which only MCP merge_request submissions populate; workflow-path requests are never there. KEY SAFETY FACT: InFlightMergeRegistry.acquire registers a done-callback on the request future, so the branch slot auto-releases the moment the bounce resolves it. A later workflow or MCP resubmission for the same branch therefore gets a fresh request_id and does NOT attach/coalesce onto the ghost. The display artifact is harmless to throughput; other landings proceed past it. This is tracked by dark_factory task 3860 (recurrence 7 = SCP task 696 / mr-7e9fa668).

   Live console error on the Escalations tab: 'Each child in a list should have a unique "key" prop ... Check the render method of EscalationsTab ... at tr'. Those rows fall back to index keys, so a reorder between polls can hand the row click handler a different row than the one clicked. Fix needs a decision on both ends: why the server emits a null escalation id, and a stable client-side fallback key that does not collide.

2. findEscalationRow returns the first cross-project match.
   tab_escalations.jsx::findEscalationRow searches every subsection and returns the first hit, but escalation ids are only unique WITHIN a project. The live payload has esc-3169-1, esc-7603-1, esc-652-1 and roughly 20 others appearing in two different project subsections. A cross-tab focus link (e.g. from tab_memory_evals.jsx) can therefore open the wrong project's escalation. The lookup key must be (project, escalation_id), not escalation_id alone.

3. tabs.jsx::ChipList calls hooks conditionally.
   `persistKey ? usePersistedState(persistKey, false) : uS(false)` - two hooks on one branch, one on the other. Harmless today only because persistKey happens to be stable per instance. The first caller that makes persistKey conditional gets a 'Rendered fewer hooks than expected' crash. Call the hook unconditionally and branch on the value instead.

4. __DF_PAUSE does not suppress chip-driven refreshes.
   Only data.js::pollTick consults window.__DF_PAUSE. app.jsx's `uE(() => window.DF_REFRESH(win), [win])` calls refreshDFData directly, bypassing the check. Measured: with __DF_PAUSE = true, six window-chip clicks produced two extra full 14-endpoint refreshes. 'Pause live' should mean paused.

5. Unbounded, never-pruned localStorage keys.
   tabs.jsx::usePersistedState (via ::ChipList, ::DepsCell, ::LocksCell) writes one `df.deps.<task_id>` and one `df.locks.<task_id>` key per task row rendered, on MOUNT as well as on change, and never prunes them. QuotaExceededError is swallowed by a bare `catch (e) {}`, so the failure mode is silent loss of every persisted UI preference. Completed: dashboard: active_tasks.collect_active_tasks becomes a test-only wrapper — inline it or keep it deliberately
Description: Filed by task 4889's architect as out-of-scope follow-up (escalation_id agent-followup-4889).

WHAT 4889 CHANGES. dashboard/src/dashboard/data/active_tasks.py::collect_active_tasks is a thin 2-tuple wrapper over collect_tasks_with_counts that discards done_counts, degraded_projects and count_unknown_projects. Before 4889 it had exactly ONE production caller: dashboard/src/dashboard/data/scheduler.py::collect_scheduler_state. 4889 (workstream #4425) switches that caller to collect_tasks_with_counts directly, because the Scheduler tab needs the degraded_projects fact that the narrower wrapper deliberately absorbs — which is precisely the escape hatch collect_active_tasks' own docstring names ("Callers that need to distinguish 'unknown' from 'reachable and empty' must use collect_tasks_with_counts directly").

THE RESULT. collect_active_tasks then has ZERO production callers and remains reachable only from dashboard/tests/test_active_tasks.py, where ~35 tests call it as a convenience 2-tuple form of collect_tasks_with_counts, plus test_active_tasks.py::test_collect_active_tasks_still_returns_two_elements (around :3423), which deliberately pins the 2-tuple arity with a docstring stating the degraded marker "is absorbed by collect_active_tasks, not leaked to it".

A public function kept alive only by its own tests is a well-defined-purpose problem (docs/code-quality.md heuristic 6), and it is exactly the shape the repo's test stance flags: the tests, not the system, are what the entity now serves.

DECIDE, do not default. Either (a) delete collect_active_tasks and migrate the ~35 test call sites to collect_tasks_with_counts with a `_, _, _` tail (or a small test-local helper that does the narrowing, which keeps the convenience where it belongs — in the test file), retiring the arity pin along with it; or (b) keep it, and say in its docstring that it is a deliberately retained narrowing helper with no production caller, so the next reader does not read its survival as evidence of a caller that no longer exists. Option (b) is cheap but must be an explicit written decision, not silence.

Do NOT reverse 4889's change to restore the caller: scheduler.py needs the degraded fact, and reintroducing the wrapper there would re-open the invisible-failure gap #4425 closed.

Files: dashboard/src/dashboard/data/active_tasks.py, dashboard/tests/test_active_tasks.py.
Analysis: DECISION: option (a), delete `dashboard/src/dashboard/data/active_tasks.py::collect_active_tasks`.

CHECKED ON THIS BRANCH (base 85a1e19e1c):
- 4889 has landed (merge 040be27994). `dashboard/src/dashboard/data/scheduler.py::collect_scheduler_state` now calls `collect_tasks_with_counts` directly (scheduler.py imports `_all_project_roots, collect_tasks_with_counts`) and computes offline/degraded itself through `task_snapshot.classify`.
- A whole-worktree grep finds `collect_active_tasks` in no production code outside its own definition. The remaining references are: the import and ~20 call sites in `dashboard/tests/test_active_tasks.py`, including `_one_task_row_with_snapshot` and the arity pin `TestCollectTasksBudget::test_collect_active_tasks_still_returns_two_elements`; prose mentions in `task_snapshot.py::classify`'s docstring, `test_app.py` (~:368) and `test_active_tasks.py` (~:531); a test-name pointer in `test_scheduler_page.py` (~:489); and historical `plans/` records, which are left alone.
- PREMISE CORRECTION: the task description says `collect_tasks_with_counts` returns a wider tuple that needs a `_, _, _` tail. That is out of date. Today it returns a 2-TUPLE, `(active_rows, snapshots_by_label: dict[str, TaskSnapshot])`; its docstring records that the old 5-tuple was retired. So the wrapper's `(active, offline)` and the collector's `(active, snapshots)` have the same arity. Every test call site that writes `active, _ = ...` migrates by changing only the callee name, with the same kwargs (`client`, `config`, `now`).
- The narrowing helper the task suggests already exists in the test file: `test_active_tasks.py::_offline(snapshots)`, built on `_labelled` / `classify`. The one test that reads the offline list (`..._surfaces_offline_projects`) migrates to `_offline(snapshots)`. No new helper is needed.
- The arity pin's substantive claim, that a degraded root is not reclassified as offline, is already covered against the collector by `TestCollectTasksBudget::test_degraded_and_offline_are_disjoint`. Its other claim, that the scheduler unpacks `(active, offline)`, has been false since 4889. Retiring it loses no coverage.
- Deleting the wrapper leaves `SnapshotHealth` and `classify` unused in `active_tasks.py` (line 1226 is their only code use), so they must be dropped from the `task_snapshot` import or ruff F401 fails.
- Baseline: 308 tests passed in test_active_tasks.py, test_scheduler_page.py, test_app.py and test_task_snapshot.py with the worktree's own venv. Run: `cd dashboard && env -u VIRTUAL_ENV ../.venv/bin/python -m pytest <files> -q -p no:cacheprovider`. The Bash session's own `python` resolves to the MAIN checkout's source, so do not use it.

WHY (a) OVER (b):
- Heuristic 6, a well-defined purpose for each entity: the wrapper's only remaining purpose is to be called by its own tests.
- Heuristic 9, deep modules with narrow interfaces: deleting it removes a public name and two imports from `active_tasks.py` and makes `collect_tasks_with_counts` the single row-collection entry point.
- Comments stance: option (b) would need a docstring whose only job is to explain why an unused function exists.
- Migration cost is close to zero because the arities already match.

SCOPE: refactor only, no runtime behaviour change. Every behaviour the wrapper tests asserted (row shape, active-status filter, deps, runtime join, external deps, now threading, offline reporting) is re-asserted against `collect_tasks_with_counts`. Test functions named `test_collect_active_tasks_*` are renamed to `test_collect_tasks_with_counts_*` (heuristic 1, informative names). A collision check found none of the new names already in use.
Key decisions: Option (a): delete collect_active_tasks rather than keep it as a documented narrowing helper (option b).; Rename the migrated test_collect_active_tasks_* functions to test_collect_tasks_with_counts_* instead of keeping the old names.; Retire the arity pin TestCollectTasksBudget::test_collect_active_tasks_still_returns_two_elements outright instead of porting it, and add no 'symbol is absent' test.
Steps completed: 2/2
Modules: dashboard/src/dashboard/data/active_tasks.py, dashboard/src/dashboard/data/task_snapshot.py, dashboard/tests/test_active_tasks.py, dashboard/tests/test_app.py, dashboard/tests/test_scheduler_page.py

Reify plan-authoring norm (task #5714 step-5, esc-5714-3): a plan step of the form "verify no `#NNNN` citation survives anywhere in tracked source, since a cite to a task about to go terminal is an orphaned cite" is OVER-BROAD and must not be written or executed literally. It generalises the PTODO convention from the pattern kinds it actually gates to ALL prose mentions of a task number, and executing it DESTROYS PROVENANCE — the "this code exists because of #NNNN" labels that are the main reason a later agent can reconstruct why a design is shaped the way it is.

THE REAL DISCRIMINATOR IS DEFERRAL LANGUAGE, NOT THE TASK NUMBER. A comment line is only claimed by the δ-B arm when it carries a canonical `#NNNN` cite AND a `DEFERRAL_PROSE` needle on the SAME line (`crates/reify-audit/src/ptodo.rs`: pending / deferred to / not yet / blocked on / awaiting). Classification is FORM BEFORE LIVENESS, so a line claimed by no arm emits no finding no matter what status the cite resolves to. A provenance cite or section label with no needle is therefore permanently safe; stripping it buys nothing.

MEASURED on task #5714 (2026-09-17, worktree _lane-21): 10 `#5714` prose cites across crates/reify-constraints/{src/solver.rs,tests/robustness_floor.rs} and crates/reify-eval/tests/robustness_floor_signal.rs, none carrying a deferral needle and none being a TODO/FIXME/HACK marker, todo!()/unimplemented!() stub, #[ignore] reason or #[allow(...)] rationale — `tests/infra/test_reify_audit_ptodo.sh` green 25/25. DECISION: accepted, no edit. The consistency evidence is overwhelming: those same three files cite 18 other tasks, of which 15 are already `done` (51 cites of #5618, 38 of #5711 alone), all green. Stripping #5714 while keeping ~160 terminal-task cites beside it would be arbitrary. Corroborating: `ptodo-baseline.txt` holds exactly 6 entries and every one is deferral-flavoured ("is deferred to consumer task #3787", "blocked on task #2947"), and the ratchet's own named controls assert the benign direction — (g-benign) "identifier / PRD-relative / uncited / G-allow lines, all cites seeded terminal → exits 0" and (f-benign) "non-deferral rationales → exits 0".

THE CHECK TO RUN INSTEAD, and it is forward-looking rather than a snapshot: do not grep for `#NNNN` and do not trust a green ratchet alone, because a cite ON a needle line classifies `tracked` (invisible) while the task is live and flips to a High `orphaned` fingerprint the DAY it reaches done/cancelled — reddening the gate for an unrelated later task. Grep the intersection: `git grep -nE "#NNNN" -- crates/ docs/ examples/ | grep -E "pending|deferred to|not yet|blocked on|awaiting"`. Empty means terminal status is harmless. Non-empty is the only thing worth fixing, and the fix is to re-word that line (or move the cite off the needle line), never to delete provenance.

solar_challenge Plotly gotchas, measured on plotly 6.7.0 (task 375 architect, 2026-10-03):
(1) plotly.colors.hex_to_rgb('#5e3') returns (5, 14, 3). It splits the digits into thirds, so a three-digit hex comes out silently wrong. Validate #rrggbb first, or use bytes.fromhex.
(2) go.Scatter(fillcolor=None) emits no fillcolor key; to_plotly_json() is {'type': 'scatter'}. Dropping a kwarg that is always None leaves fig.to_json() byte-identical.
(3) A guard that only reads charts.py's figures cannot see a hand-written copy of a COLOUR_PALETTE colour, because the copy equals the palette value. To expose it, recolour every palette entry (monkeypatch.setitem) and check that no figure still draws a shipped colour's RGB. Skip layout.template, which is Plotly's default theme.

solar_challenge gotcha (measured 2026-10-03 while planning task 250, main 8cc1a19): plotly 6.7.0, the version uv.lock pins, makes fig.to_json() write numpy/pandas-backed arrays as base64 typed arrays {"dtype":"f8","bdata":...}. plotly.js 2.27.0, the cdn.plot.ly build results/home, results/fleet and history/compare loaded until task 250, has no bdata decoder. In Chromium it drew a trace with y=[3.5,1.25,7,2,9.5] as its index [0,1,2,3,4], with no error. The plotly.js 3.5.0 that plotly 6.7.0 bundles (package_data/plotly.min.js; plotly.offline.get_plotlyjs_version()) drew the values. web/charts.py avoids this only because every trace passes .tolist(). A chart that passes a Series or ndarray directly will draw wrong data under any plotly.js older than its plotly package bundles.

Plotly figure-JSON gotcha in solar_challenge (task 661 architect, measured 2026-10-12 on main 29e03a9 with the uv.lock plotly):
- fig.to_json() writes NO "annotations" key in layout when a figure has none. Example: web.charts.financial_breakdown on a priced run, whose layout keys are barmode, font, height, legend, margin, paper_bgcolor, plot_bgcolor, template, title, xaxis, yaxis and yaxis2.

candidates.content: solar_challenge_platform convention (task 588, branch task/588; holds once merged). Type every datetime instant a response model serves as schemas.serialization.UtcInstant, an Annotated[datetime, AfterValidator] that reads a naive value as UTC via config.contract.as_utc and converts an aware one to UTC. pydantic-core then serves RFC3339 UTC with a trailing Z on SQLite too, and the OpenAPI schema stays a plain date-time. tests/schemas/test_wire_serialization.py::test_every_instant_the_api_serves_is_utc_with_a_trailing_z walks every router's response models, so a served field left as plain datetime fails there. Request bodies keep plain datetime on purpose: GrantRequest.expiry is task 592's decision, and config POST effective_from is ticket tkt_0RVN69X16QTGE86K7C7X2WEEMB.

solar_challenge_platform gotcha, verified 2026-10-10 on SQLite by task 863's architect: to give a row a controlled age, pass updated_at (and created_at) explicitly. This works either in the ORM constructor on INSERT or as `sa.update(Model).values(updated_at=ts)`. An explicit value overrides models/mixins.py TimestampMixin's default=utcnow / onupdate=utcnow. On SQLite, DateTime(timezone=True) stores an aware UTC value as naive UTC wall time and reads it back naive. A filter like `updated_at >= since` with an aware-UTC `since` still compares correctly, because the bind param is formatted the same way. Non-UTC offsets would not compare correctly.

solar_challenge_platform gotcha (task 208, verified 2026-10-07): SQLAlchemy's SQLite DateTime(timezone=True) drops the UTC offset on write, so an aware non-UTC datetime (e.g. 13:00+01:00) is stored as 13:00 and reads back naive, which the store readers then label UTC: the wrong instant. Convert to UTC before writing, as DispatchLivenessStore.write_tick/write_refresh_tick now do (tick_ts.astimezone(timezone.utc)). Read rows back through dispatch_liveness._stored_utc, which treats naive as UTC and converts aware values to UTC. A since-bounded read is only correct if every writer stored UTC.

solar_challenge_platform SQLite write-side gotcha, measured 2026-10-10 at main 3751150 with TestClient probes on tests/_sqlite_engine.make_in_memory_engine. SQLAlchemy's SQLite DateTime(timezone=True) stores an aware non-UTC datetime at its wall clock and drops the offset without converting. Two cases: a consent expiry sent "2027-06-14T11:02:11+01:00" read back as naive 11:02:11, and a config effective_from sent "2026-09-01T01:00:00+01:00" was served as "2026-09-01T01:00:00Z". So a read-back fix (naive means UTC) alone serves such instants an hour off. Convert request datetimes to UTC before they reach an ORM column. PostgreSQL timestamptz stores the right instant.

solar_challenge_platform gotcha (verified 2026-10-07, task 209 planning): SQLAlchemy's DateTime(timezone=True) on SQLite binds a tz-aware datetime by its wall-clock fields and drops the offset, so a non-UTC instant is stored wrong. Every store converts to UTC before binding (as DispatchLivenessStore.write_refresh_tick does) and re-attaches UTC to the naive values SQLite reads back. The repo had no portable upsert: on_conflict_do_update exists only on the dialect-specific constructs (sqlalchemy.dialects.postgresql.insert / sqlalchemy.dialects.sqlite.insert). A store that must run on both the hermetic SQLite suite and Postgres picks one by session.get_bind().dialect.name.

Gotcha (solar_challenge_platform; task 793's plan, pending merge). Once task 793 lands, TelemetryRow.__post_init__ refuses a naive ts through timeseries.instant.require_tz_aware, where naive means utcoffset() is None. Consequences for tests:
- A test cannot build a naive TelemetryRow to exercise a store's or last_seen_from's at-use refusal. The refusal now happens at construction, and tests/timeseries/test_instant.py's ENFORCEMENT_POINTS table covers it.
- SQLite reads a DateTime(timezone=True) column back naive, so attach UTC before building a TelemetryRow from a read-back. From task 793, validation/drills/raw_telemetry.read_raw_rows does this itself. db/dialects.stored_utc (tasks 453 and 928) is to become the shared helper.
- A new tz-aware check should call timeseries.instant: is_tz_aware, require_tz_aware or instant_in_utc. Add it as a row to that table, not as another `tzinfo is None` test. That test lets through a tzinfo whose utcoffset() is None, which astimezone then reads on the host's zone.

solar-challenge-platform test gotcha (measured 2026-10-01): the factory host runs in Europe/London, not UTC. datetime.astimezone() on a NAIVE value, such as a SQLite DateTime(timezone=True) re-read after session.expire_all(), takes it as host-local time, so in BST naive 2026-09-01 00:00 becomes 2026-08-31T23:00:00Z. Run as_utc (config/contract.py) before astimezone(). A test only distinguishes "as_utc first" from "astimezone alone" when its instants fall in BST (late March to late October); winter dates such as 2026-01-01 pass either way.

solar_challenge_platform gotcha: SQLAlchemy's DateTime(timezone=True) on SQLite drops the UTC offset on WRITE (the string format has no offset), not just on read. A tz-aware non-UTC datetime is stored as its local wall time and reads back as that wall time labelled UTC, which is the wrong instant; the same applies to a non-UTC bound parameter in a >= filter. A store that must round-trip on SQLite converts with .astimezone(timezone.utc) before writing and before filtering. control/dispatch_liveness.py::write_refresh_tick / read_refresh_ticks do this (task 207).

solar_challenge_platform gotcha, measured 2026-10-11 by a probe in task 793's amendment pass. Python compares and hashes two aware datetimes that share one tzinfo object by their wall clock. So two TelemetryRows at 00:30Z and 01:30Z on 2026-10-25, otherwise equal and both written in one ZoneInfo("Europe/London") (01:30 fold=0 and fold=1), are == and hash-equal, and set or dict membership merges them; their in_utc() forms differ. psycopg returns every timestamptz in one cached ZoneInfo per session zone name (psycopg/_tz.py get_tzinfo). So rows read through an engine without db/session.py's "-c timezone=UTC" pin are exposed. One such engine is the dropped-readings drill's bare sa.create_engine(live_config.database_url), whose rows reach dropped_rows' set(survivors). Write such read-backs in UTC (astimezone(timezone.utc)) before comparing, sorting or hashing them, as timescale_store._to_utc does. Follow-up ticket tkt_0RVNM13HJNP7Y8F7ACA453CJWH covers read_raw_rows.

Any other instant gives the date and clock to the second ('2026-10-11 03:07:42 UTC').
