solar_challenge_platform remedy for raw sa.text() reads on SQLite. Measured 2026-10-11 by the task 685 architect at main 6d7c06a, sqlalchemy 2.0.51. Declare result types on the text clause, e.g. `sa.text(sql).columns(hh_start=sa.DateTime(timezone=True), home_id=sa.Uuid())`. SQLAlchemy's SQLite dialect then parses its own stored text ('2026-07-01 08:30:00.000000') into a naive datetime and its hex UUID text into uuid.UUID, while Postgres/psycopg values pass through unchanged, so no fromisoformat or isinstance(str) sniff is needed. The keyword form matches columns by name, so untyped columns and the :since/:limit binds keep working; then apply config.contract.as_utc (naive means UTC) to the datetime.

solar_challenge_platform SQLAlchemy gotcha for telemetry_settlement_hh. It was measured 2026-10-12 by task 698's architect with throwaway probes at main 553f437. On SQLite, a raw sa.text() SELECT returns home_id as 32-char hex text and hh_start as the storage string '2026-07-01 08:30:00.000000'. A typed Core select over timescale_store.settlement_table, or over a Subquery built from it, returns uuid.UUID and a NAIVE datetime holding the UTC wall clock instead. Wrap it in config.contract.as_utc to make it aware. A derived table select(settlement_table).where(...).subquery() names every column, so renaming ANY table column raises OperationalError, even a column the outer query never selects. On the pinned TimescaleDB image, Postgres pulls such a derived table, including a correlated MAX(method_version) scalar subquery, up into its caller. It plans the same index scan on uq_settlement_home_metric_start_version as the flat form, with one Index Only Scan Backward per candidate row, about 4.8 µs each (64,640 rows ANALYZEd).

solar_challenge_platform rollups.settlement_hh (measured 2026-10-05 at 1a8c4a3, task 777 amendment): converting every home×metric row with _as_utc BEFORE the `first <= ts <= last` window test costs 10.07 ms per call against 4.45 ms for the current convert-only-in-window form, over 20,000 UTC-written rows (2.3x), because comparing datetimes that share one tzinfo is a fast path. For London-written rows the two forms cost the same (24.08 vs 24.61 ms), since the mixed-zone comparison already pays utcoffset per row. So a review suggestion to convert before comparing, so that a naive row raises the named ValueError rather than TypeError, slows the common UTC path 2.3x for MemoryStore, which calls settlement_hh once per half-hour with every row of the home; the TypeError is documented and kept by design.

GOTCHA (solar_challenge_platform, found in task 388): dt.strftime(...) + 'Z' formats dt's OWN wall clock, so a non-UTC dt gets the 'Z' stamp of a different instant. A whole-second format also truncates sub-second times onto the key of a different instant. Before stamping 'Z', read a forecast origin through rollups.as_utc_hh_aligned(name, dt): it refuses naive input, converts to UTC and refuses anything off UTC's half-hour grid. Use that, not a bare dt.astimezone(timezone.utc), which reads a naive dt on the host's zone. After task 388, ForecastCache.key_for does this, and it keeps UTC-written keys byte-identical, so the committed fixtures are unaffected.

GOTCHA (solar-challenge-platform frontend-portal vitest; measured 2026-10-11 by the task 428 architect on vitest 5.0.3, host zone BST). A bare wire date such as AccountRead.opened_on/closed_on ('2026-06-01', no time) parses with new Date() as UTC midnight. ISO date-only strings are UTC, unlike zone-less date-times, which parse as local. So a local-getter rendering (getFullYear/getMonth/getDate) shifts the day only WEST of Greenwich. Measured: that mutation passed all 9 AccountScreen tests under the host's BST (+0100) and failed every date case under inTimeZone('America/New_York') (frontend-portal/src/test/timeZone.ts). A test pinning a bare date 'as served' therefore needs a nested describe that calls inTimeZone('America/New_York').

Customer portal convention (utcTime.ts from task 712, applied to the remaining screens by task 721): every wire instant a member sees goes through frontend-portal/src/utcTime.ts. That means formatUtcDateTime ('2025-02-01 00:00 UTC'), or formatUtcDate for a date-only bucket. Never print the raw RFC 3339 string, and never use toLocale*() or the local Date getters. The callers are MeterReadingsBlock, EnergyChart, EnergyDashboardScreen's 'As of' line and ConsentScreen's history rows. Tests pin this with TZ=America/New_York, stubbed only inside a nested describe (vi.stubEnv in beforeAll, vi.unstubAllEnvs in afterAll). The stub is load-bearing: a local-getter formatter with a ' UTC' suffix passes wherever the zone matches UTC, and this host's Europe/London does all winter. AccountRead.opened_on/closed_on and BillingPeriod start/end are `date` on the wire, calendar dates rather than instants, and are shown as-is.

GOTCHA (measured 2026-09-29, task 676 amendment pass): on the default SQLite substrate (Settings.database_url = sqlite:///:memory:), a raw sa.text() SELECT returns a DateTime column as a str such as '2026-07-01 08:30:00.000000' (no result-type processing), NOT a datetime; Postgres/Timescale returns a tz-aware datetime. So ops/reads.py::read_fleet_runs leaks a str into SettlementCoverage.hh_start (declared `datetime`) and api/routers/ops.py::_settlement_coverage_to_dict emits it verbatim (space separator, no Z), breaking the ops design spec's RFC3339-Z wire rule on SQLite only; a test pins that passthrough. This is distinct from the ORM-typed 'SQLite reads DateTime back naive' gotcha. Any new raw-SQL read in this repo should parse datetime columns into UTC datetimes at the read boundary; the fix was filed as follow-up agent-followup-676 (priority low, production Postgres is already Z).

content: solar_challenge_platform convention (task 942, branch task/942; holds once merged): type every datetime a request body or query parameter carries as schemas.serialization.AwareUtcInstant = Annotated[AwareDatetime, AfterValidator(_in_utc)]. A naive value is a 422 whose loc names the field, and an aware one is held in UTC, so SQLite stores the instant it names, per docs/prds/review-all-time-grid-and-utc-home.md D5. UtcInstant, which reads naive as UTC, stays for response models only (D10). After 942 the /config POST effective_from fields and GET /config/audit `since` use AwareUtcInstant; the /ops `since` parameters are follow-up task 1228, and GrantRequest.expiry is removed by S13·β, not retyped.
